default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: A stone got inside the shoe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.sk: N に + N が + Vている（past）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows where the stone is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that appeared or is inside the shoe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 入っていました is the polite past form of 入っている. It describes a state of being inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: The place comes first, followed by the object that is there and a predicate showing its state. The particle が highlights the object that was found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this sentence were changed, it would mean that the subject actively put the object inside the shoe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after a place, but に is usually used for existence or location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vi: Today was really fun, wasn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the degree of the adjective that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 楽しかった is the past form of the い-ending adjective 楽しい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね makes the comment softer and invites agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.why: 今日 は sets the scope of the comment, とても shows the degree, and 楽しかった makes the predicate past tense. ですね comes at the end to make the comment sound like a gentle shared thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 楽しいですね, the sentence changes to the present or to a feeling of having fun now. It no longer focuses on today as a finished day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change 楽しい to 楽しかった when commenting on a finished experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who has the feeling or preference in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: この comes before the noun 味 to specify which flavor it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: In the pattern 好きだ, が marks the object that is liked or preferred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きです is the adjective predicate な. It expresses the speaker's feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q11.kobun.why: わたしは identifies the person who feels something, while 味が is the object used with 好きです. Japanese uses が in the pattern 好きだ, unlike Vietnamese, which uses the verb “like” directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 味を好みます is used, the sentence sounds more formal, and 好む is a verb, so the object is used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q11.kobun.tip: A common mistake is to say 味を好きです. With 好きです, the object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vi: This area is a little inconvenient, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the area being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb softens the degree of the comment 不便.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 不便 is the adjective な used as the predicate to describe the area's feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね makes the comment softer and more like a shared thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.why: The area is stated as the topic first. Then ちょっと adjusts the degree of the adjective な 不便. ですね at the end shows that this is a gentle comment, not a harsh one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 不便ではありません, the sentence becomes negative and means that this area is not inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out です when using the adjective な at the end of a sentence. In a polite sentence, they need to say 不便です or 不便ですね.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the vegetables as the object of cutting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 切って is the て form of 切る. It connects to ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q13.kobun.why: The noun for the object comes before を, followed by the verb in the て form. ください at the end changes the action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence would mean “Please do not cut the vegetables.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the dictionary form before ください. The verb needs to be changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: 以外 shows the excluded range, while は makes that range the topic for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 来ました is the polite past form of 来る and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q14.kobun.why: The phrase 以外は limits the range and excludes Hayashi from the group being discussed. みんな is the understood subject within that range, while 来ました describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, it would mean “only N,” without excluding N.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means excluding N, but it usually connects directly to the rest of the sentence and does not use は in the same way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 以外は as a single subject. In fact, it defines the excluded range so that the remaining part can be discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.vi: I kept looking at the clouds from the window.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the starting point or viewpoint. Here, it is the place from which one looks out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ずっと modifies the action 見ていました and emphasizes that the action continued without stopping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the clouds as the object being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 見ていました is the past form of 見ている. It describes an action that was continuing during a period in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.why: The viewing position is given first with から, and the adverb of duration comes before the verb. The object of 見る goes with を, while ていました shows that the looking continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence would only say that someone saw or looked at something, without emphasizing a continuing process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate から only as “from.” In this sentence, it shows the starting point of the viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q15.kobun.cn: Vている → Vていました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.vi: Please do not photograph or copy this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the object being discussed the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 写さないで is the negative form connected to ください to request that an action not be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ください makes the prohibition polite when it comes after 写さないで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.why: The object that needs protection is made the topic with は. The negative verb form ないで combines with ください to make a polite request not to do the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence would be a stronger rule or prohibition, not a soft request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse ないでください with ないください. The particle で must be kept in this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q17.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: には marks the object or issue being opposed and also adds emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 反対です is a noun predicate that states a position toward the opinion already mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q18.kobun.why: The object of the opposing position goes with に, which combines with は to form には and highlight the object. 反対です uses a noun as the predicate and expresses the attitude politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 反対 is replaced with 賛成, the sentence changes to mean agreement with that opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 反対します, the sentence emphasizes the action of opposing rather than a state or position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 反対. The basic patterns are Nに反対です or Nには反対です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.vi: If it is inconvenient, please call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the inconvenient state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ば connects the condition to the main clause and means “if.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the action of making a phone call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: して + ください creates a polite request meaning “please do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, followed by the requested action. 都合が悪い uses が to state the subject of the condition, while 電話をする uses を to mark the phone call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the nuance changes to “when it is inconvenient,” focusing more on time than on a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle を in 電話をする, but 電話する is not the basic usage in this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q19.tokens.2.m: if it is inconvenient, if you are busy
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: I experienced many things in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where an activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろな modifies the noun that follows and takes the form な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the action しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The place of the activity comes before the modifying phrase and object, followed by the main verb. いろいろな connects directly with the noun, while を marks what was experienced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If にいる is used, the sentence describes a person’s existence in Japan, not an activity they experienced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the place where an action takes place; with しました, the place usually takes で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the object that needs attention or caution.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 気をつける is a fixed phrase in which を marks 気 as the object to be protected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb つける with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to express a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q20.kobun.why: 台風に is the object to be guarded against, while 気をつけてください is a polite request. 気をつける must remain as the phrase used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: The meanings are almost the same, but 注意する is more direct and formal than 気をつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q20.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in 台風に as “to”; here に indicates the object to be cautious about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.vi: There is a geography test tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the test exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 地理 with テスト and shows which subject the test belongs to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is a predicate that indicates the existence of a thing or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.why: The time is stated first, followed by the noun phrase 地理のテスト. Because the sentence describes the existence of a test, this noun takes が and あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes “take a geography test,” focusing on the action rather than existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of が, but the existence pattern あります usually uses が for a thing that is said to “exist.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.vi: Because the road is slippery, please be careful when walking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason with the reminder in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 注意する changes into 注意して to connect the action of being careful with the action of walking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of あるく connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.why: The reason clause with ので comes before the request. The two actions 注意して and あるいて are connected by the て form, and then ください is placed at the end to create a polite reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q22.kobun.tip: Do not incorrectly combine them as 注意してあるいてください in the analysis; recognize that 注意して and あるいて are two consecutive parts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the subject name with the noun 試験.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the English test the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective むずかしい changes to the past tense to describe the feeling after the test ended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q23.kobun.why: The phrase えいごの試験 forms a compound noun meaning English test. は presents this phrase as the topic, while the past-tense adjective acts as the predicate comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence focuses more on the test being difficult instead of presenting the test as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q23.kobun.tip: With adjectives ending in い, the past tense is formed by changing い to かった: むずかしい → むずかしかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 車 with 運転, creating the meaning “driving a car.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the activity that is said to be possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: できます acts as the predicate and expresses the ability to perform the activity 運転.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: か at the end of the sentence changes a statement into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.why: 車の運転 is a noun phrase meaning driving a car. In the pattern expressing ability, the activity takes が and できます; か is placed at the end to ask a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This also asks about the ability to drive, but uses 車を as the direct object of 運転する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only asks whether someone drives a car, without emphasizing ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with できます, but this ability pattern usually uses が: 運転ができます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q25.kobun.vi: If I go to Kyoto, I would like to try staying at a Japanese-style inn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 行ったら uses the た＋ら form to state a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the stay takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてみたいです expresses the desire to try doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q25.kobun.why: The destination is placed first with に, followed by the conditional clause 行ったら. The place where the speaker wants to stay also takes に, and the sentence ends with とまってみたいです to express the desire to try the experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたいです is used instead, it only says that the speaker wants to do something and does not emphasize trying the experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with a place to stay, but a place where something exists or happens usually uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: I asked a store employee where the restroom was.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person being asked or the person receiving the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject whose location is being asked about in the indirect question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates where the restroom exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: か changes the clause どこにある into an indirect question and makes it the content of 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞きました is the main verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The person being asked takes に, while the content of the question is placed before 聞きました. The clause どこにあるか keeps statement word order and uses か to create an indirect question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, this becomes a direct question about location, rather than the content asked through 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: In an indirect question, do not move どこ to the beginning of the clause or add ですか after か.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q3.kobun.cn: 疑問詞・普通形 + か + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: The cafeteria was very crowded today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.sk: N は + N が + Vている（ past）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes today the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the place described as crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: こんでいました describes a crowded state that existed at the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The time is given as the topic first, followed by the place and its state. が identifies the direct object of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would say that someone ate at the cafeteria, focusing on the action rather than the crowded state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: は after a time expression usually gives the background, and is not necessarily the subject of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: The harbor can be seen from this window.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から indicates the viewpoint or the starting place for seeing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the scenery that is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 見えます is a verb that indicates that something can be seen naturally or within one's view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: The place of observation goes with から, while the scenery that is seen goes with が. 見える describes the ability to see something resulting from the viewing position or conditions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 見る, the sentence would emphasize that the subject actively looks at the harbor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 見える; something seen naturally usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate something near the speaker or something already identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the novel the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: おもしろかったです is the polite past form of the adjective い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + かったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: この modifies 小説, while は presents the book as the topic. The adjective おもしろい changes い to かった to express an impression in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with おもしろそうです, it means that something seems interesting, without confirming that it was interesting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with おもしろいです, the sentence changes from a past evaluation to a present one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: When changing the adjective い to the past, remove い and add かった; do not add でした directly after the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: I write in my diary every evening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression shows when an action is repeated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いています describes an action that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The time expression comes at the beginning, followed by the object with を, and then the verb as the predicate. The form Vている emphasizes an action that is being performed or repeated as a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vました, the sentence describes something that happened and was completed, without emphasizing a current habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse を with は; here, を must follow the thing being written, while は is used to state the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.sk: Time + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: This part gives the time when the event occurred and is placed at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the phenomenon that is the subject of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ふりました is the polite past form of ふります, describing rain that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The time is moved to the front and separated from the main clause by a comma. 雨がふりました is a structure that describes a natural phenomenon, in which 雨 is the subject with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 雨がふっています, it means that it is raining now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily add a person as the subject or use を, but natural phenomena usually use Nが + a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: Autumn is coming soon, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This adverb modifies an event that will happen soon, near the present time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun gives the content being confirmed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね shows mild confirmation and invites the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: もうすぐ comes first to limit the time, while 秋 is the noun giving the content of the judgment. ですね at the end creates a friendly confirming tone, as if sharing an observation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with でしょう, the sentence leans more toward a prediction or guess and has less of a shared-confirmation tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ですね as a complete question, but here the speaker is mainly seeking agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with 都合, creating the noun phrase “tomorrow's availability.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes 都合 the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: どうですか asks about the evaluation or condition of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.why: あしたの modifies 都合, then は presents this phrase as the topic. どうですか comes at the end to ask about the situation or level of convenience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 都合 is omitted, the question is directly about tomorrow in general, not specifically about the schedule or availability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 都合 as “schedule” in every case, but this word can also mean availability or circumstances.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q10.kobun.vi: My younger brother has a small face.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is the younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part described as small.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q10.kobun.why: は makes the younger brother the topic, while が marks the face as the body part with the small feature. The adjective 小さい comes at the end to complete the description.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を instead of が in a pattern describing a body part's feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q11.kobun.vi: My father does not like meat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the father is the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: With the adjective 嫌い, が marks the thing that is disliked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: きらいです is a polite predicate that expresses dislike.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q11.kobun.why: 父は is the topic, while 肉が is the object of the feeling of dislike. きらいです comes at the end of the sentence and uses the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q11.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate が as the subject; in the pattern 〜がきらいです, it usually indicates the thing that one dislikes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vi: I am interested in Western culture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 西洋 with ぶんか, creating the noun phrase “Western culture.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that the speaker is interested in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what exists in the pattern 〜に興味があります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: あります completes the pattern expressing interest in an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.why: 西洋のぶんか forms a noun phrase in which 西洋 modifies ぶんか. に marks the object of interest, while きょうみが あります expresses that the interest exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning is still being interested, but the tone is more formal and focuses more on attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place に after きょうみ; in this pattern, に comes after the object of interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vi: I want to become a bus driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person who has the desire in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects バス to the occupation noun that follows, meaning bus driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the occupation or position that the speaker wants to become.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: なりたい is formed from なる＋たい and expresses the desire to become something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.why: バスの運転手 is a noun phrase in which バス modifies 運転手. With the verb なる, に marks the result or position that the person wants to become, and たい expresses the desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern shows the desire to become a specific occupation or role.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with がしたい, the sentence says that the person wants to do an activity or job, without emphasizing becoming a driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out に before なる; the correct patterns are Nに なります or Nに なりたいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.vi: My siblings' house is in the countryside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the house exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows the possessive relationship between the siblings and the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists at that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is used for the existence of objects or places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.why: An existence sentence puts the location with に first, then states the existing thing with が. 兄弟のいえ is a possessive noun phrase meaning my siblings' house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the house becomes a clearly identified topic instead of simply introducing its existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for the place where something exists; with あります, the location usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q15.kobun.vi: Japan imports beef from the United States.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting place or import source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the goods being imported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ゆにゅうします is the main predicate and describes the action of importing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q15.kobun.why: から states the source of the goods, を states the goods affected, and the verb for importing comes at the end. The importer is understood from the context, so it does not appear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If が来ます is used, the meaning is that a person or thing comes from the United States, not that goods are imported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse から with に; から only indicates the source, while を indicates the goods being imported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vi: I underline important parts and memorize them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective な comes before the noun ところ to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the part being presented as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the action ひいて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the action ひく to the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite-form verb ます is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.why: ところは introduces the part being discussed, while せんをひいておぼえます shows two actions happening in sequence. The form て connects underlining with memorizing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ながら, the two actions are understood as happening at the same time instead of one after the other.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と to connect two actions, but this sentence needs the form て to show that the first action happens before the next one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テニス with 試合 and shows that the match belongs to the sport of tennis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 試合 as the object watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 見ました is the polite past-form predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q17.kobun.why: テニスの modifies 試合 to create the noun phrase “tennis match.” This noun phrase goes with を because it is the object of 見ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 試合の is omitted, the sentence means that the person watched tennis in general, not necessarily a match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q17.kobun.tip: Do not translate の mechanically as “of”; in this phrase, テニスの試合 should naturally be understood as “tennis match.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location of the body that was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: けがをする is a fixed combination in which けが goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する in the phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q18.kobun.why: 首に indicates where the injury happened, while けがをしました uses the structure noun + を + する to express being injured. The verb しました comes at the end and has a past meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 首が痛い is used, the sentence only says that the neck hurts, without emphasizing that it was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q18.kobun.tip: Do not say 首をけがしました when you want to state the location of an injury; with けがをする, the location usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vi: Mother is not at home now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 時点 に ＋ 場所 に ＋ いる negative
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that mother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: 今 indicates the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place where mother exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: いません is the polite negative form of いる, used for people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.why: The topic 母は comes first, followed by the time 今 and the place 家に. Because this sentence is about a person's presence, it uses いる, whose polite negative form is いません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ありません, it is used for objects or things, not to say that mother is absent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use あります for people; remember that いる is used for people and animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks これ as the topic being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows the possessive relationship between わたし and the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: だいじな is an な adjective. It comes before a noun and uses な to connect to it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 物です is a noun predicate and uses です to end the polite sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.why: これは introduces the object; わたしの and だいじな modify 物 respectively. 物です creates a noun predicate meaning “is an object.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 大事なもの is used in kanji, the meaning does not change; only the written form of the word is different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な after the adjective な when it comes before a noun, so they must not say だいじ物.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vi: I am looking for a wedding venue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects けっこんしき with 会場 to create the phrase “wedding venue.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 会場 as the object being searched for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of さがす connects with います to create the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: います combines with the て form of a verb to express an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.why: けっこんしきの会場 is a noun phrase serving as the object of さがす, so it goes with を. The form て combines with います to express that the action of looking is ongoing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with さがしました, the sentence only says that the person searched, without emphasizing that they are still searching now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: さがしてあります describes a state in which someone has already searched for something, not that the speaker is searching now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ています only as “already”; in this sentence, さがしています means “is looking for.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vi: In that town, many kinds of fruit are produced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to point to a place or thing far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: では combines with にで to state the place and limit the scope being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: いろいろな modifies the noun くだもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks くだもの as the object of the action of producing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: して is the て form of 生産する. It connects with います to create the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: います shows that the production is happening or is a current activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.why: まちでは identifies the scope and place, while くだものを is the object of 生産する. 生産して＋います describes production that is in progress or is currently a feature of the town.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If では is replaced with で, the sentence only states the place of production, and the limiting or contrasting meaning of は becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 生産しました, the sentence changes to production that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q21.kobun.tip: では does not only mean “in”; は also limits the topic to “only in that town” or “as for that town.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun 洋服 and points to something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the clothes being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects イタリア with an omitted noun and means that it belongs to or comes from Italy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a noun sentence in a polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q22.kobun.why: この comes before 洋服 to modify a noun. は marks the topic, while イタリアのです uses の to replace a known noun and です to give a polite conclusion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning emphasizes that the product was made in Italy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out の and say イタリアです, but that only means “it is Italy.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q23.kobun.vi: This is a good place, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the place being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: いい modifies 所 and forms a noun phrase meaning “a good place.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね ends the comment and invites the listener's agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q23.kobun.why: ここは states the place. Then いい comes before 所 to modify that place. ですね makes the comment sound gentle, with a tone of confirmation or agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with に, ここに only shows where something exists or where someone goes, so it is no longer the topic of a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use いいだ before a noun. いい must come directly before the noun, as in いい所.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.vi: I want to eat the food my mother cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 母 with 料理 and shows that the food was cooked by or belongs to the mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the desired object in the pattern Vたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べたい creates the desire to eat, while です makes the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.why: 母の modifies 料理 to identify the food. With Vたい, the desired object usually takes が, and 食べたいです becomes the predicate expressing a polite wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with を食べます, the sentence only describes the action of eating and no longer means “want to eat.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with Vたい out of habit, but が is usually used to mark the desired object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the little bird as the one performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: ないて is the て form. It connects the main verb with います to create the progressive pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: います in ている shows that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q25.kobun.why: 小鳥が is the subject of the action. ないています combines the て form with います to describe singing that is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, the spelling will sound unnatural because ないく is a verb written only in kana, while the given sentence uses ないています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 鳴きます, the sentence only states an action or habit and does not emphasize that it is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q25.kobun.tip: Do not translate います alone as “have” or “exist.” In Vている, it is part of the meaning “be doing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks today as the time reference and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the wind as the subject that has the strong quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い つよい serves as the predicate, and です makes the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.why: きょうは sets the time context, while 風が is the subject being described. The adjective つよい comes at the end to state the wind's quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 風は is used, the sentence emphasizes or contrasts the wind specifically, instead of simply presenting the wind as the subject of the quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は for both きょう and 風, but が is more suitable for marking the subject that has the strong quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vi: My younger brother is at the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is the younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the subject is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 行って combines with います to create the ている pattern, describing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the predicate of the 行っている pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the place with に. The verb 行く changes to the て form and combines with います to show the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this, the sentence only says that the younger brother goes to the hospital and does not emphasize his current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 行っている as “is going,” but in this sentence it describes the state of having arrived and being there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vi: Last year, I planted a tree in the garden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.sk: N time ＋ N に ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase identifies when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates where the planting took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that was planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: うえました is the polite past form of the verb 植える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.why: The time comes first, the place goes with に, and the object of the action goes with を. The predicate is in the ました form, showing that the planting was completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used instead of に, the meaning focuses more on the place where the action happened. However, with 植える, に is more natural for showing where the tree was planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the place. を marks the tree that was planted, while に marks where the tree was planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vi: Please give me shoes in this color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 色 with くつ to form a noun phrase that modifies the shoes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.why: この modifies 色, and then 色の further modifies くつ. The shoes are the item being requested, so they take を before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If が好きです is used, the sentence says that you like this color, rather than making a request to buy or give you shoes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q6.kobun.tip: You must use の to connect a modifying noun with the following noun. Do not place この directly before the whole phrase in an arbitrary way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vi: I put vegetables in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks what is put in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination where the vegetables are put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 入れました is the polite past form of 入れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.why: The item being moved comes before を, and the destination comes before に. 入れました at the end of the sentence shows that the action is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, this phrase indicates the place where the action happens, without emphasizing that the refrigerator is the destination where the vegetables are put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q7.kobun.tip: With 入れる, remember to distinguish を for the item being put somewhere from に for the place receiving it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to the pond by bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.sk: N で ＋ N へ ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase shows when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past predicate form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.why: The time comes first, the means of transportation goes with で, and the destination goes with へ. 行きました at the end of the sentence completes the movement action in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence still indicates the destination, but に emphasizes the specific destination more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use で to indicate the destination; で here indicates that the bicycle is the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vi: I put my underwear in the drawer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item put in the drawer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination where the item is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 入れました is the polite past predicate, showing that putting the item away is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.why: The structure places the item being put away before を and the place receiving it before に. The verb 入れる in the ました form shows that the action is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 置きました, the sentence emphasizes putting something down or leaving it somewhere, not necessarily putting it inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t10-q9.kobun.tip: 入れる means putting something inside, so the destination usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.vi: If it is this restaurant's lunch set, 1,000 yen is enough for two people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.sk: N の N なら ＋ Number of people で ＋ Amount of money で ＋ 十分だ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun レストラン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects レストラン with ランチ, showing that the meal belongs to the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: なら states the condition or assumed scope being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the number of people doing something together or using something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the amount of money used to judge whether it is enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: 十分です acts as the predicate, judging that the amount of money is enough for the stated condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.why: なら makes the lunch set the condition, and the two phrases で state the number of people and the amount of money in that order. 十分です concludes that this amount of money meets the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 必要です, it means “necessary” and does not directly state that 1,000 yen is enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If では is used, the nuance focuses more on comparison or limiting the topic, so it is less natural than なら in this assumed condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly use で after an amount of money as if it indicated a place, but here で indicates the price or means of payment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.tokens.5.n: noun indicating the number of people
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q13.kobun.cn: N ＋ なら; V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.vi: I am working part-time at a gas station on the highway.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects こうそくどうろ with ガソリンスタンド to identify the gas station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the part-time work happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: しています uses ている to describe work that is continuing or regularly maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.why: の identifies the gas station as belonging to or being on the highway, while で indicates where the action happens. ています comes at the end to describe an ongoing or continuing part-time job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 働いています, it emphasizes being at work, not specifically having a part-time job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with しました, it only says that the speaker worked part-time in the past and does not show a present state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q15.kobun.tip: ています does not always indicate an action happening right now; with work, it often indicates a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.vi: Because I have something to do today, I want to go home as early as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic and time reference of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the task that needs to be done, which is the subject of ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason clause to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: This phrase modifies はやく and expresses the greatest possible degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The はやく form of the adjective modifies the action of returning home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: たい is attached to the continuative form of a verb to express the speaker's wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before the result and is connected by ので. できるだけ modifies はやく to emphasize the earliest possible time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: It is usually used with a negative form and means “not to that extent,” so it does not express the greatest possible degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: It also connects a reason, but its nuance is more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that できるだけ must come before the word for degree or the action it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.vi: It is easier to understand an explanation when it gives examples.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the example being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of giving an example with the action of explaining.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The past form modifies ほう and creates the phrase “the way it was explained.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: ほうが makes the option “explaining by giving examples” the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the predicate that evaluates how easy the explanation is to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.why: て connects two successive actions, while the clause せつめいした modifies ほう. The whole phrase is the subject being compared with が before the predicate わかりやすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means that one should do something, while the current sentence only evaluates the method as easy to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with と, it expresses a condition or natural result and no longer has the nuance of comparing methods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q15.kobun.tip: ほうが in this sentence does not automatically mean “should”; the predicate that follows shows that this is a comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.vi: Because the camera is broken, it is not possible to take pictures.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the camera as the subject of the cause clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the camera being broken with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the photo as the object that cannot be taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: とれません shows that taking a photo is impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.cn: Vて is used to connect a cause or sequence of events; negative potential V: V可能形＋ません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.why: The clause about the broken camera comes first to state the cause. Then, しゃしんが is the object being photographed, and とれません expresses the result that the action cannot be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the cause-and-effect relationship becomes clearer and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, it means “do not take a photo,” referring to an action that is not done, not an action that cannot be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use を with しゃしん, but in the potential pattern, the object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.vi: This is an expensive restaurant, but it is not that tasty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective 高い comes before レストラン to modify “restaurant.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: だが connects two contrasting ideas: it is expensive, but not tasty enough to match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: それほど modifies おいしくない and usually goes with a negative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしくないです is the adjective い in the polite negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.why: The first clause states the feature “expensive,” while だが introduces an unexpected result. それほど combines with the negative form to reduce the degree of the adjective おいしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あまり, it means “not very tasty.” This is usually softer and does not necessarily imply a comparison with the expected level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If とてもおいしくない is used, the sentence can mean “very untasty,” which is stronger and different from reducing the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use それほど with an affirmative sentence, while this pattern usually requires a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q16.kobun.cn: それほど ＋ Vない・Aいくない; それほど ＋ なAではない・Nではない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.vi: I waited for two whole hours, but in the end she still did not come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.sk: Duration も ＋ Vました が、＋ N は ＋ Adv ＋ Vませんでした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes an unexpectedly long period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two clauses whose meaning goes against expectations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes her the topic of the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb emphasizes the final result after the waiting period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: きませんでした is the past negative form of 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.cn: Nも expresses emphasis; Vましたが connects clauses in contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.why: The long period is stated first as the background for the waiting. が creates a contrast, and then とうとう emphasizes the final result that she did not come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence usually suggests a result achieved after difficulty, so it does not fit this negative result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the nuance also tends to mean “finally managed to achieve it,” which differs from finally not coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate とうとう as “finally” in a positive way, but it can also be used for bad or negative results.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q18.kobun.vi: I went to the department store to shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun かいもの goes with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: いきました is the polite past form of いきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q18.kobun.why: The destination comes before へ, the purpose comes before に, and then the movement verb follows. This order shows both where someone went and what they went there to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with で, で usually only shows the place where an action occurs, not the direction toward it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show the destination and で to show the purpose in this sentence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the bus as the subject that carries out the departure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q1.kobun.why: The subject バスが comes before the verb. The verb is in the polite past form to show that the departure has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 出ました is used, it emphasizes that the bus left its position or stop, while しゅっぱつしました emphasizes the act of departing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q1.kobun.tip: Not every case translated as “leave” uses 出る; 出発する focuses on starting a journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents この国 as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks こめ as the object of the importing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: しています shows that the importing action is being carried out or that the state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q10.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the object of the action goes with を, and the main verb comes at the end. This expression directly describes importing rice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that someone is buying rice. It does not clearly state that the rice is being imported from another country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use が for こめ because こめ is the object being imported, so を must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.vi: I accidentally dropped my bicycle key.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects じてんしゃ with かぎ and shows that the key belongs to the bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the key as the object that was dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb おとす with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: しまいました shows that something happened unintentionally and that the speaker feels sorry or regrets it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.why: の identifies the possessive relationship, を marks the affected object, and the two verbs are connected with the て form. てしまいました comes at the end to emphasize that the unwanted event has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means that the key was lost, but it does not clearly say that it was dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If しまいました is omitted, the sentence only states that the object was dropped, and the regretful nuance is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.tip: てしまう does not only mean completion; with an accident such as dropping something, it often includes a sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます／しまった／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.vi: When the work is finished, please contact me immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the work as the subject completed in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a condition or an earlier time with the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: すぐに modifies the action of contacting someone and shows that it must be done immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: てください creates a polite request to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, and the main request comes after it. が identifies the completed thing as the work, while すぐに emphasizes when the contact should be made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with とき, the sentence talks about when the work ends but does not emphasize the condition leading to the request as たら does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with てから, it means after finishing something in sequence; the conditional nuance is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.tip: With a verb, たら must connect to a past form such as おわったら, not おわるら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q12.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら／Aいかったら／Aなだったら・なら／Nだったら・なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.vi: I saw the picture that the teacher took.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the teacher as the person who performs the action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause before しゃしん modifies the picture; とられた is the past form at the end of this clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the picture as the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: はいけんしました is the main predicate and the humble form of 見ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.why: The clause 先生がとられた is placed directly before しゃしん to identify which picture it is. After the modified noun, を marks the object of はいけんしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning may become the teacher's picture or a picture owned by the teacher, without clearly saying that the teacher took it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If とった is used, the meaning is still that the teacher took it, but the respectful nuance toward the teacher is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q13.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a modifying clause comes before the noun, not after the noun as in the usual Vietnamese expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.vi: I will look up nearby restaurants using a computer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the location of the place described in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ある comes before レストラン to modify it, referring to restaurants located nearby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the restaurant as the object being looked up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the means used for looking it up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: しらべます is the main predicate and describes the action of looking up restaurants.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.why: ちかくにある is a modifying clause before レストラン, helping identify which restaurants. を marks the object being looked up, while で states the tool used for the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with の, the sentence is shorter and only says that the restaurants are nearby, without emphasizing the existence structure ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with さがします, it means to search for restaurants, while しらべます focuses more on looking up information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q14.kobun.tip: で indicates the means in this sentence; do not use に for パソコン because に does not mark a tool.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.vi: This mountain is dangerous, so please do not climb it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the adjective な with ので to give the reason for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ないでください expresses a request for someone not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.why: The sentence states the topic with は, gives the reason with なので, and ends with a negative request. Because きけん is a な adjective, な must come before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing なので with だから or なので can make the reason more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If ないほうがいい is used, the sentence changes from a request to advice about what should be avoided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often forget な before ので when connecting it with the adjective な or with a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a noun referring to a time with the noun テスト to modify the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the test is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: でした is the polite past form of the adjective な かんたんだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q16.kobun.why: きのうの comes before テスト to identify which test. テストは is the topic, while かんたんでした is the predicate describing it in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in the sentence, the meaning is still that the test was easy, but it uses the adjective い やさしい instead of the adjective な かんたん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often conjugate かんたん like the adjective い; use かんたんでした, not かんたかったです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q17.kobun.vi: I bought a ring at a department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いました is the polite past form of 買う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q17.kobun.why: The place where the action happens comes first with で, the item bought comes before を, and then the verb comes at the end. This order forms a basic action sentence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of で, に no longer indicates the place where the buying action happens; it usually indicates a destination or a place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use に for every place; with shopping actions, the place should use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before きって to modify the stamp.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the stamp as the item received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました is the polite past form and describes receiving something from someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q18.kobun.why: めずらしい comes before the noun to describe the stamp, while きってを is the object of もらいました. The verb at the end of the sentence shows the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to a stamp that is not rare or special.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often place adjectives after nouns, as in Vietnamese; in Japanese, the adjective must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.vi: No matter how cheap they are, I do not buy things I do not need.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら emphasizes the degree in a concessive clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes to the くて form and combines with も to create the meaning “even if...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: いらない comes before もの to modify the thing that is not needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the things that are not needed the topic of the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: 買いません is the polite negative form of 買う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.why: The clause 安くても comes first to state a concessive condition, while いらないものは identifies the object being negated in the main clause. も in the pattern ても creates the nuance that even if the condition occurs, the result does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 安ければ, the sentence becomes a condition meaning “if it is cheap...”, and no longer means “even if it is cheap, I will not buy it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If 安いのに is used, the sentence usually expresses something contrary to expectations or regret rather than a general concession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often translate ても as “if”; here, it must be understood as “even if...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q19.kobun.cn: Vて・Aいくて・Aな/Nで ＋ も
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: もっと modifies ていねいに and indicates the degree that needs to increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ていねいに is the adverbial form of the adjective な and modifies the action of writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of かく connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q2.kobun.why: もっと and ていねいに respectively modify the way of writing, so they come before the verb. The form て connects かく with ください to create a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 〜なさい, the sentence has a stronger commanding tone, usually used by someone in a higher position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q2.kobun.tip: When the adjective な modifies a verb, it must change to に: ていねいな → ていねいに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.vi: After I come home from school, I will study the lesson in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: かえったら uses the past form of a verb with ら to connect a condition or the time when the following action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content acted on by the verb します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the main predicate and indicates the action of studying the lesson in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.why: 学校から indicates the starting place, while かえったら sets a time condition for the next action. よしゅうをします is the main clause and comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If かえってから is used, the meaning is that the action is done only after returning, with more emphasis on the time order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If かえると is used, the sentence can easily mean “whenever one returns” or “when one returns,” like a rule or a natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use the dictionary form before ら; this conditional pattern needs the past form: かえったら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q20.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aいかった・Aな/Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.vi: Please wait here for a while.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the waiting takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: おまち is a polite and respectful form of the action of waiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed after a verb to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.why: The place comes first, followed by the length of time, and then the requested action. ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the request is still polite but does not show respect toward the listener or the person mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate しばらく as a fixed long period of time, but in this sentence it only means “for a while.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q21.kobun.cn: お ＋ Vます ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks an event that is gradually happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: くれて is the て form, connecting the gradual darkening with きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: きました adds the meaning that the change has been progressing up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q22.kobun.why: だんだん modifies the degree of change, while てくる expresses a change gradually progressing toward the present. が marks a natural event that is changing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes the state of the sky being dark, rather than the process of gradually becoming dark up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit て in くれてきました, but て is the required connecting part between the main verb and くる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q23.kobun.vi: It is okay even if you arrive late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: ても connects a concessive condition with the idea that there is no problem in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: かまいません expresses permission or says that something causes no trouble.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q23.kobun.why: The clause ても states a situation that could cause inconvenience, while かまいません denies that the situation causes trouble. Therefore, the whole sentence gives permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence gives permission more directly and commonly, while かまいません emphasizes that there is no problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form directly before ても; the verb must change to the て form before も is added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q23.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も ＋ かまいません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q24.kobun.vi: This chair is really in the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the chair being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the chair the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: じゃま is an な adjective, used with です to make a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q24.kobun.why: この directly modifies いす, and then は makes the chair the topic. じゃまです comments that the chair is obstructive or in the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes that this chair is necessary, which is the opposite of being in the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand じゃま as “not needed,” but this word emphasizes the feeling of being obstructed or having something in the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q25.kobun.vi: The car suddenly moved and startled me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the car as the subject of the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the car’s movement with the startled reaction in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: びっくりしました describes an emotional reaction that happened after the previous event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q25.kobun.why: くるまが is the subject of the action, and きゅうに indicates how the event happened. The て form connects the car’s movement with the result that the speaker was startled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence specifically says that the car ran, which is narrower in meaning than うごいて, meaning movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with くるま, but when the car moves by itself, が is used to mark the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q3.kobun.vi: My older brother is very good at drawing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that my older brother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object being evaluated as something he is good at drawing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: うまい is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate, meaning skilled or good at something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q3.kobun.why: The sentence places the person being discussed first with は, then states the field being evaluated with が. The adjective うまい comes at the end to conclude the person’s ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it gives the meaning “good” or “skilled” in a more neutral and polite way than うまい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after え instead of が, but ability-evaluation patterns usually use Nが上手です or Nがうまいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes yesterday the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ねぼう combines with する to form a verb, while しました indicates that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q4.kobun.cn: N ＋ する; polite past: N ＋ しました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q4.kobun.why: The time is stated first with は, followed by the verb phrase serving as the predicate. ねぼう is a noun meaning oversleeping and needs する to become an action.
