default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that going to bed or waking up becomes late; it does not directly refer to oversleeping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate ねぼう as an independent verb; remember that it is a noun used with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka was praised by the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Mr. Tanaka is the person affected in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who performs the action of praising in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ほめられました is the polite past passive form of ほめる, showing that Tanaka received the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: remove る, change the final sound to the あ row ＋ れる; group 2: Vる ＋ られる; する → される; 来[く]る → 来[こ]られる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.why: The person receiving the praise becomes the topic with は, while the teacher is the agent and therefore goes with に. The passive form focuses on the person praised rather than the person doing the praising.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The active form makes the teacher the subject and Tanaka the object, so the focus of the sentence changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に in the passive sentence for the person receiving the action; here, に indicates the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.vi: My younger brother is working part-time at that coffee shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates that my younger brother is the subject of the part-time work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content of the action performed with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the ている form of する, expressing an ongoing state or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる; present polite form: Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.why: A workplace location goes with で, while アルバイトをする is a verb phrase with an object. しています shows that the part-time work is continuing in the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that someone did part-time work. It does not stress that the work is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that there is part-time work, but it does not confirm that the younger brother is doing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the workplace; the location where an action takes place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates that I am the person who has the preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that is liked in the structure with すき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: すき is a な adjective. It forms the predicate with です to express a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q7.kobun.cn: N ＋ が ＋ 好[す]きだ; polite form: N ＋ が ＋ 好[す]きです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q7.kobun.why: The person with the preference goes with は, while the thing that is liked goes with が. Because すき is a な adjective, it is not conjugated like an い-ending adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means to swim or practice swimming. It talks about an action, not a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q7.kobun.tip: Do not say すいえいをすきです; with すき, the object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.vi: Hearing that, I was very surprised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of hearing with the reaction that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: びっくりしました is a polite past-tense predicate that expresses a surprised reaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: change the final sound to the て row; 聞[き]く → 聞[き]いて; Vて ＋ following clause
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.why: What was heard comes first with を. Then, the て form connects the cause or event to the reaction. The main reaction comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: ので states the cause more clearly and has an explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: と expresses a reaction that occurs naturally as soon as the person hears that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form 聞く to connect directly with びっくりしました; change it to the て form, which is 聞いて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q9.kobun.vi: That person is beautiful, isn't he?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes あの人 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: です creates a polite tone, while ね is used to seek agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q9.kobun.why: The sentence makes the person the topic with は, then uses the adjective い as the predicate. です and ね at the end create a polite way of speaking and a mild confirmation-seeking tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is still beautiful, but it focuses more on a clean, neat, or good-looking appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t105-q9.kobun.tip: Do not add だ before うつくしい because it is an い adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.vi: When I looked outside, the rain had stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the action of looking with the result noticed immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the rain the topic being observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: やんで is the て form. It connects the main verb with いました to create the ている form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: いました is the polite past form of いる. It shows that the rain had stopped at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と ＋ result; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.why: そとを is the object of みる, while みると shows the result noticed immediately after looking. やんでいました describes the state of the rain having stopped when it was observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If みたら is used instead, the sentence has a stronger conditional or specific-time meaning. It is less natural than と for an immediately noticed result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate みると as “if one looks,” but in this sentence と expresses the result discovered immediately after the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.vi: Mr. Suzuki was asked for directions by a foreigner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ N を ＋ polite past passive verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person affected in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the agent who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what is being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: られました is the polite past passive form of たずねる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.why: The affected person is made the topic with は, while the person who performs the action goes with に. みちを is the object of the question, and the passive verb ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: The active form means that Mr. Suzuki asked the foreigner for directions, which is the opposite direction of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: から can also indicate the agent in a passive sentence, but it usually emphasizes the source from which the action comes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily switch the person asking and the person being asked. Identify who performs the action before using the passive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.tokens.8.m: be done to/be given; passive form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q10.kobun.cn: Vる → Vられる; Vない → Vられない; Vた → Vられた; Vなかった → Vられなかった
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the place being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the place with a noun naming the type of place and creates a polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q11.kobun.why: ここは makes the place the topic, while としょかんです identifies what that place is. です comes at the end to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: が emphasizes that this place itself is the library, rather than simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q11.kobun.tip: Do not translate は as “is”; は only states the topic, while the meaning “is a library” is expressed by としょかんです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the place being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the place with a noun naming the type of establishment and creates a polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q12.kobun.why: ここは is the part stating the place as the topic, while きっさてんです is the predicate part that identifies the type of place. です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: で indicates the place where an action takes place, so this sentence means drinking coffee here, not defining what this place is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q12.kobun.tip: Distinguish ここは, which introduces a place, from ここで, which describes an action taking place at the location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the place being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects a place with a noun naming a facility, forming a polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q13.kobun.why: The sentence uses ここは to make the place the topic, then uses びょういんです to identify it as a hospital. This order is the basic form for introducing or identifying a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence emphasizes that a hospital exists here, rather than simply identifying this place as a hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use あります when you want to say “this place is a hospital”; the identity pattern is NはNです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.vi: This is a place to park cars.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the parking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb phrase before ところ modifies the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ところです forms the predicate, meaning a place for doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.why: The place is introduced as the topic first, followed by the action and the purpose of the place. The clause とめておく modifies ところ, creating the meaning “a place to park in advance.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it, the sentence emphasizes a place where an action is about to happen, rather than a place with a fixed purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q14.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit を before the object or understand ところです simply as “place,” forgetting the modifier before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun くうこう with the topic ここは to form a polite judgment sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q15.kobun.why: The sentence has a direct introduction structure: ここは names the place being discussed, while くうこうです identifies what type of place it is. Therefore, no verb describing an activity is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the sentence describes a place where an action is performed instead of directly naming the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q15.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate ここは as “here” but forget that は turns it into the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q16.kobun.vi: I went to my aunt's house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects おば with うち, showing possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates movement toward the aunt's house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: いきました is the polite past form of いく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q16.kobun.why: おばの modifies うち to identify whose house it is. へ follows the destination, while いきました comes at the end to express a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に still indicates the destination, but に usually emphasizes a specific destination more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q16.kobun.tip: English learners may mechanically use の as the word “of” without noticing that it connects two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the person as the object of knowing or being acquainted with.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: ごぞんじですか is a polite way to ask whether the listener knows that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q17.kobun.why: The person's name comes before を because the person is the object of knowing. ごぞんじですか comes at the end to complete the predicate and form a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with 知っていますか, the basic meaning is still “do you know,” but the tone is more ordinary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may use が with ごぞんじ, but this expression uses を for the person being known.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう states when the meeting happened and does not need a particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person whom the subject met in the fixed expression おめにかかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: に appears in the humble expression おめにかかる and should not be understood separately as an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: かかりました completes the humble expression おめにかかる in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.kobun.why: The time expression comes first to set the time frame. The person met goes with に, while おめにかかりました is a humble expression used to say “meet” when speaking about someone of higher status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with 会いました, the meaning is still “meet,” but the humble tone is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.kobun.tip: English learners may translate おめにかかる word by word and overlook that this is a fixed expression meaning “have an audience, meet.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q18.tokens.3.m: eye; meet face-to-face (in お目にかかる)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.vi: Mr. Smith is teaching English to Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the person doing the teaching the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person receiving the teaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content being taught.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects おしえる with います to form a pattern that expresses an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている and shows that the teaching is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.why: The teacher is the topic, the person receiving the teaching goes with に, and the subject is the object marked by を. The form ている at the end expresses an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with the simple present form, the sentence only says that Smith teaches English; it does not necessarily emphasize that it is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern shifts the viewpoint to the learner: Tanaka is learning English from Smith.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q19.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse に and を, but に is the person receiving the teaching, while を is the content being taught.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle が marks the subject as being in a dirty state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb よごれる in the て form connects with います to express a current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ている describes a resulting state, while よ adds a tone of informing or reminding the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q2.kobun.why: The subject comes first with が, followed by よごれている, which shows that the clothes are in a dirty state. よ at the end tells the listener this information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the sentence emphasizes that the clothes have become dirty, not only their current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may understand ています as only “be doing,” but here it expresses the resulting state “be dirty.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あさ with あいさつ, showing that the greeting belongs to the morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks あいさつ as the object of the verb します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the predicate and expresses a greeting action in the present or as a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q20.kobun.why: あさの modifies あいさつ, then あいさつを becomes the object of します. The pattern をする is commonly used to say that someone performs an action or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the sentence emphasizes the person or object being greeted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may omit を and say あいさつします, but the basic expression here is あいさつをします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the entire speech before it as quoted content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: いいました is the polite past form of いいます and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q21.kobun.why: The speech is placed inside quotation marks and connected to いいました by と. The verb いいました at the end shows that the speaking action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the sentence means that someone said or used to say something like this, with a reporting tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the quotation in this pattern; the spoken content connects to いいます through と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the quoted reminder or request exactly as spoken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: いいました is the main predicate and expresses a completed act of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q22.kobun.why: In the quotation, きをつけてください is a polite request, and the whole request is connected to いいました by と. The verb of speaking at the end of the sentence is in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 頼みました is used, the sentence emphasizes asking or requesting someone to do something rather than simply reporting the words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q22.kobun.tip: For a direct request, と comes after the entire quotation. It is not placed immediately after ください with the rest separated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.vi: It has been a long time since Mr. Tanaka last met Mr. Smith.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action あう in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person whom たなかさん meets, because あう usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the clause あう into a noun, while は makes that act of meeting the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.ch.3.vi: it has been a long time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ひさしぶりです serves as the predicate and evaluates the time since the previous meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.why: The clause たなかさんがスミスさんにあう is nominalized with の, and then は presents the whole act of meeting as the topic. ひさしぶりです comments that it has been a long time since this happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence means “meet someone after a long time,” focusing on the act of meeting rather than commenting on the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 初めてです, the meaning is that it is the first meeting, not that it has been a long time since the last meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q23.kobun.tip: Do not confuse は in のは with a time particle; のは marks the whole clause “the act of meeting...” as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks a spoken comment; ですね adds a slight sense of agreement or admiration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: いいました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q24.kobun.why: いい directly modifies とけい, while ですね makes the comment sound soft and shared. The whole comment is quoted with と before いいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ね is omitted, the sentence simply gives a comment and has less of a sense of seeking agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q24.kobun.tip: The adjective いい comes before the noun とけい; do not place とけい before いい as in the usual word order in English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamashita finishes his work and then leaves the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Mr. Yamashita is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks しごと as the subject of the action おわって.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: おわって is the て form, connecting the end of the work with the following action of leaving the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks かいしゃ as the place from which someone leaves with the verb でます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: でます is the main predicate and expresses the action of leaving the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.why: しごとがおわって comes first and is connected to かいしゃをでます by the て form, showing two consecutive actions. かいしゃを uses を because でる can take a place as the point from which someone leaves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is used, the order “finish the work and then leave the company” is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If たあとで is used, the sentence also indicates the time after the work is completed, with a more formal tone and a clearer separation between the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q25.kobun.tip: With the verb でる meaning to leave a place, Vietnamese learners may easily use に or から, but the basic structure here uses かいしゃをでます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.vi: Please gather in the classroom at 9 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.sk: Time に + Place に + Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the time when the gathering takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the place where people gather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb あつまる changes to the て form to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: てください creates a polite request or instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.why: The two phrases with に respectively indicate the time and the place of gathering. The form てください comes after the verb and turns the content “gather” into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is “try gathering,” so it is no longer a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use で for the location of あつまる; this verb usually uses に to indicate the place where people gather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.sk: N を + Vます-remove ます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the room as the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ましょう attaches to the verb to invite or suggest doing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう expresses a polite invitation to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.why: へやを is the object of the cleaning action and comes before the verb according to Japanese word order. かたづけましょう turns the statement into a suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence asks the listener to clean the room and does not necessarily include the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q4.kobun.tip: ましょう connects with the verb stem in the ます form, so かたづけましょう is used instead of the dictionary form directly before ましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.vi: Mr. Suzuki went instead of Mr. Yamada.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun やまださん with かわり and identifies the person being replaced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: のかわりに indicates doing something instead of or replacing the person mentioned before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いきました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.why: The phrase のかわりに comes at the beginning of the sentence to state who is being replaced. Then, が identifies the person who actually performs the action, while いきました ends the event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is “for Mr. Yamada’s benefit,” not necessarily going in his place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q5.kobun.tip: かわりに in this structure needs の after the noun; do not say やまださんかわりに directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies いす and identifies the chair that has been mentioned or is near the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place or destination of the sitting position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the body part that is placed down in the expression 腰をかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: かける changes to the form て to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: てください makes a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.why: そのいすに refers to the chair as a place to sit, while こしをかける is a fixed expression used を with a body part. The form てください changes the sentence into a polite invitation or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If すわる is used, the basic meaning is still “to sit,” but the fixed expression 腰をかける is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q6.kobun.tip: Do not translate each word of こしをかける as “hang the hips”; the whole phrase means “sit” or “sit down.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.vi: Please be careful not to catch a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb ひかない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The negative clause with ように states the purpose that requires attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 気をつける is a fixed phrase meaning “pay attention” or “be careful.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb つける with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end of the pattern てください and expresses a favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.why: The phrase ひかないように comes before the main action to state the purpose of being careful. 気をつけてください is a polite request pattern in which the verb must be in the て form before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ために emphasizes the purpose, but it is usually used with more intentional actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern directly means “please do not do something”; it does not express purpose like ように.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ように as “like” or “similar to,” but in this sentence it means “in order to achieve a purpose.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ように
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic as the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person whom the speaker consults or asks for advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 相談する changes to the polite past form 相談しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q9.kobun.why: わたしは places the topic at the beginning of the sentence, while せんせいに indicates the person consulted. The verb 相談する ends the sentence and is in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: と emphasizes discussing something together with the teacher, showing a clearer two-way interaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: の only indicates possession or modification, so it does not directly express the object of 相談する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the person being consulted; with 相談する, the object usually takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the object connected with the result おちる, meaning “fail the exam.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes an event that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q1.kobun.why: The noun for the exam comes before に to state the object of failing. おちました comes at the end of the sentence and shows that the event has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence means taking or sitting an exam, without saying whether the result is a pass or a failure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may habitually use を with おちる, but the pattern that shows the result of failing an exam uses しけんに おちる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.sk: N は + Aい (remove い) + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to modify it and indicate a hat that is far from the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the hat the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです attaches to the form of the adjective with い removed to express an appearance or judgment based on what is observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.cn: Vます／Aい (remove い)／Aな + そうだ・そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.why: あのぼうしは states the thing being observed. おおきそうです describes an appearance that looks big, so it is more suitable for a comment based on direct observation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes the guess “it is probably big,” without emphasizing the appearance being seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ようです, the sentence has a more formal, less direct tone of inference based on evidence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q10.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, い must be removed before そうです: おおきい becomes おおきそうです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.vi: Recently, the number of people who play golf has increased considerably.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん indicates the period when the change being discussed occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb する in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause ゴルフをする comes before ひと to modify “people who play golf.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of the increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ずいぶん modifies ふえました and shows that the increase is fairly large.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb ふえる is in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.why: ゴルフをする comes before ひと to narrow the meaning of ひと to “people who play golf.” Then ひとが is the subject of ふえました, while ずいぶん adds the degree of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 人々 is used, the meaning is still “people who play golf,” but the expression emphasizes the group of people more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with している, the sentence emphasizes people who are currently playing or engaging in golf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q11.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a modifying clause comes before the noun, so one must say ゴルフをするひと rather than putting “people” first as in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.vi: Please come as early as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: できるだけ modifies はやく and expresses the earliest possible time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: はやく is an adverbial form that modifies the action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: きて is the て form of くる and connects the verb with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.why: できるだけ sets the degree, はやく indicates the desired manner or time, and きてください creates the request. This order moves from degree to the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vてほしい, the sentence expresses the speaker’s wish and is more familiar, rather than being a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with なるべく, the meaning is almost the same, but the sense of “trying as hard as possible” is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use ください directly after the dictionary form; first change the verb into the て form, such as changing くる into きてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q13.kobun.vi: No matter how many times I read it, I still do not understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら indicates how large the degree or number of times is and modifies the action of reading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: よんでも is the form て＋も and connects to the following clause with the meaning “no matter how I read it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q13.kobun.why: いくら states the degree of the action, while よんでも creates a concessive clause. The main clause わかりません shows that the result remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the meaning becomes more specific: no matter how many times one reads it, rather than emphasizing degree in general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand いくら only as “how much money,” but in the pattern いくら～ても it means “no matter how～much.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q14.kobun.vi: I do not have a single friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object identified as existing or not existing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ひとりも goes with a negative verb to emphasize that the quantity is zero.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: いません is the polite negative form of います and is used for the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q14.kobun.why: ともだちが is the subject whose existence is being discussed. ひとりも combines with the negative いません to express that there is absolutely no one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead would emphasize that there are no friends at all in general, without specifying the unit of one person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use ひとりも with an affirmative verb when you want to say “not even one person”; this pattern must be used with a negative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q15.kobun.sk: Time に + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうべ indicates when the action of coming occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performed the action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q15.kobun.why: ゆうべ is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state the time, then やまださんが identifies the subject. きました comes at the end of the sentence and expresses an event that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Instead of ゆうべ, it still means last night, but the expression is longer and more descriptive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q15.kobun.tip: Do not add に after ゆうべ because time words such as ゆうべ are usually used directly with the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: ちょうど emphasizes the time when the action has just been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: たべおわった uses the past form to modify ところ, indicating the time immediately after finishing eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: Vた + ところです creates a sentence-final pattern that expresses an action just completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q16.kobun.why: たべおわった comes before ところ to identify the time being discussed. ところです at the end of the sentence changes the idea “the time after finishing eating” into “just finished eating.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead in the sentence also means just finished eating, but it emphasizes that not much time has passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ところです when you want to say that an action has just been completed; use Vた形.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the plan as the subject that enters a failed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q17.kobun.why: けいかくが is the subject of the resulting state, while しっぱいしました is the predicate and shows that the failure occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead expresses that the plan did not progress well, with a softer meaning than “failed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q17.kobun.tip: しっぱいする is a verb describing failure, so its subject usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q18.kobun.vi: Clean the top of the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects つくえ with うえ, showing that the top belongs to or is attached to the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the top of the desk as the object that needs to be cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: なさい attaches to the ます form of the verb to create a relatively soft request or command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q18.kobun.why: つくえのうえ creates the noun phrase “the top of the desk,” and then を marks this phrase as the object of かたづける. なさい is placed at the end to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead makes the sentence a more polite request, with less of a guiding or commanding tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse を with に in this sentence; the place or thing being cleaned is the object, so use を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.vi: The bus going to the station is not crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction in which the bus is going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause いく modifies バス, creating the meaning “the bus going to the station.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the bus is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: すいて is the て form of すく, connecting the state with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: います combines with the て form to express a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.why: The phrase えきへ いく comes before バス to modify “bus.” The Vている pattern expresses that the bus is currently not crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に leaves the meaning “going toward the station” almost unchanged, but に usually emphasizes the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate すいています as “open”; in this sentence, it describes a state with few people or plenty of space.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Mr. Tanaka is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where Mr. Tanaka studies or regularly goes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb かよう with います to create a pattern that expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: います combines with a verb in the て form to express an ongoing situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q2.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, and the school or organization attended goes with に. かよって います shows that attending university is an ongoing state, not just a temporary action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that studying takes place at the school, without necessarily saying that the person attends that school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ています as only “is currently,” but with habitual verbs such as かよう, this pattern usually expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q21.kobun.vi: I am working at a hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: に goes with つとめる to indicate the workplace.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: つとめて is the て form, connecting the verb つとめる with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes the state of working at that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q21.kobun.why: The verb つとめる uses に to mark an organization or workplace, unlike the general action of working. ている emphasizes the current work situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: で はたらく describes working at a hospital, while に つとめる emphasizes the workplace where the person is employed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q21.kobun.tip: Do not change に to で when using つとめる; で is more suitable for はたらく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: なにも goes with a negative sentence to mean “nothing” or “do nothing at all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: たべる comes before もの to modify it, creating the meaning “something to eat.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing being discussed as nonexistent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません is the polite negative form of ある, used for objects or things that do not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q22.kobun.why: たべる modifies もの, so the whole phrase means “something to eat.” なにも combines with ありません to create a structure that completely denies the existence of that thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Using は instead of が emphasizes or contrasts the topic “food to eat.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q22.kobun.tip: なにも must go with a negative predicate; do not use it with あります to say “there is something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the party as the event that was held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: ひらきました is the polite past form of ひらく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q23.kobun.why: The event noun comes before を as the object of ひらく. The verb is in the past form because the event has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: しました broadly means to do or hold, while ひらきました emphasizes taking responsibility for organizing an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q23.kobun.tip: Do not translate ひらく as “open” in this context; with パーティー, it means “hold” or “organize.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the train that the speaker needed to catch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: まにあいませんでした is the polite past negative form, expressing that the speaker missed the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q24.kobun.why: に in まにあう marks the object or time that must be reached in time, here the train. The past negative predicate shows that the chance to catch the train has passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: おくれました only means being late compared with the train or train time; it does not directly stress that you did not make it in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q24.kobun.tip: Use まにあう with に; do not use を to mark the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q24.tokens.2.m: to make it in time, just in time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with しゅっぱつ, creating the phrase “tomorrow's departure.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the topic whose time is being identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with the time information politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q25.kobun.why: The phrase あしたの しゅっぱつ is placed first to identify which departure. After the topic comes ７じです, which states the corresponding time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence focuses on the time when the action happens, while は in this sentence states the topic being identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に in every sentence with a time, but this pattern says “A is B,” so は is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the review happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content carried out with the verb しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する, showing that the review was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q3.kobun.why: うちで comes first to state where the action happens, while ふくしゅうを is the noun that is the object of する. This order moves from setting, to content, and then to the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 勉強する, the sentence broadly means studying, while ふくしゅうする stresses reviewing content that was already studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with a place, but an action that happens at home must use うちで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q4.kobun.vi: I graduated from university last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the university that the speaker graduated from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is in the polite past form and expresses that graduation was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q4.kobun.why: きょねん states the time, while だいがくを states the object connected with the graduation action. The main verb comes at the end and is changed to the past tense to complete the meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 大学を出る, the sentence may only mean leaving university or finishing university, with a less direct sense of graduation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with a school in this sentence, but そつぎょうする usually goes with a school + を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this place the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: あんぜんです is the adjective predicate な in polite form, ending the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q5.kobun.why: The place is made the topic with は, followed by the comment あんぜんです. The adjective な comes before です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 危なくない, the sentence expresses the negative meaning “not dangerous,” focusing on denying danger rather than stating safety.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget です after the adjective な when using it as a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the thing that is in an insufficient state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: たりません is the polite negative form of たりる, expressing that the amount of water does not reach the required level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q6.kobun.why: みずが is the subject because water is what is being judged as sufficient or insufficient. たりません comes at the end to state a condition that does not meet the need.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あまりありません, the sentence only says that there is not much water; it does not necessarily imply that the amount is below what is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand たりません as “little,” but its exact meaning is “not enough” compared with what is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q7.kobun.vi: I do the laundry on Sunday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the time when the action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q7.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, followed by the activity being done and then the main verb. The pattern Nをします uses を to mark an activity or task.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used to talk about doing an activity or task, not necessarily about directly acting on an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle を because Vietnamese says “do the laundry” directly, but Japanese requires せんたくをします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q8.kobun.vi: It is getting cold today, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes today the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb ひえます describes the weather becoming colder; ね is used to share the feeling with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q8.kobun.why: きょうは sets today as the scope of the comment. ひえますね ends the sentence with a comment about the weather and a tone of agreement with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence simply says “cold” directly; ひえますね stresses the feeling of the weather becoming colder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q8.kobun.tip: Do not understand ひえます as exactly the same as the adjective さむい meaning “cold”; this word focuses on becoming colder or gradually feeling cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q9.kobun.vi: After hearing the news, I was very surprised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the content that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of hearing with the reaction that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite past-tense verb expresses the speaker's reaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q9.kobun.why: しらせを is the object of the hearing action. The form て connects two events in sequence or through cause and effect: hearing the news first, then being surprised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning stresses “after hearing” more clearly and is less natural than て in this short sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q9.kobun.tip: The form て in this sentence does not mean a command; it is used to connect two actions or events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q1.kobun.vi: My parents will come to Japan next month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q1.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nが ＋ Placeへ ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person carrying out the action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement for the action きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q1.kobun.why: らいげつ is placed at the beginning to state the time. The subject goes with が, while the destination goes with へ before the movement verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に still indicates the destination, but に usually stresses the destination more clearly, while へ stresses the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle after the destination; へ or に is needed before きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.vi: There may not be enough time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object judged as sufficient or insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: たりない is the predicate in the negative form, while かも is a shortened form of かもしれない used to express possibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: しれません completes the pattern かもしれません, expressing an uncertain guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.why: じかんが is the subject being judged for sufficiency. The adjective verb たりない comes before かもしれない, while かも is a shortened spoken form that keeps the meaning of possibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the meaning becomes more supported and certain: the time should or will probably be insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is used instead, this is a relatively soft prediction, usually more certain than かもしれません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that かもしれない must come after the plain form and cannot connect directly to the polite form ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + かもしれない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.vi: I hear that Mr. Yamada is not available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Mr. Yamada the topic of the reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the state or condition related to Mr. Yamada.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: わるい is the predicate of the clause containing the reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです attaches to the plain form to report information heard from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.why: やまださんは is the topic, while つごうがわるい is the information about that person. そうです comes at the end of the sentence to show that the speaker is reporting something they heard, not directly confirming it themselves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in the sentence, the meaning changes to Mr. Yamada directly saying that he is not available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced in the sentence, the speaker is making a guess based on signs or the situation, and it does not have to be information they heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうです as meaning “seems”; after a clause in the plain form, it usually means “I hear that.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.vi: I intend to ask Mr. Nakamura to do this work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun しごと that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes this work the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the person who is asked to do the work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: おねがいしよう is the volitional form, and と marks the content of the intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: おもいます is the main predicate and expresses the speaker’s intention or thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.why: The topic is stated first, the person being asked goes with に, and then the volitional form combines with とおもう to express the speaker’s plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it here expresses a more definite intention, closer to a decided plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に as を after おねがいする, but the person being asked must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q12.kobun.cn: V意向形 + と + 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.vi: Then, I will stop by the research room tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: では is used to move to or continue with an action in a conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: あした indicates the time when the action happens and does not need a particle in this expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action おじゃまします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: おじゃまします is a polite expression used when entering or stopping by someone else’s place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.why: では starts a new turn in the conversation, the time comes before the place, and に marks the destination before the verb for stopping by.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with へ行く only says that the person goes to that place and shows less politeness when entering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand おじゃまします as only meaning “go,” but this pattern also shows politeness when going to someone else’s space.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q13.tokens.5.m: excuse me for disturbing you; stop by
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.vi: I was very surprised to hear that Mr. Ou was getting married.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of getting married in the clause being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content of the information being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: きいて in the て form connects the preceding cause or event with the reaction びっくりしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate and states the speaker’s reaction after hearing the news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.why: The information clause comes before ときく, then it connects through the て form to the reaction that happens afterward; the person getting married is オウさん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with と知って emphasizes knowing the information, not the action of hearing the news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with ので turns the preceding part into the direct cause of the surprise, so it is no longer a structure that quotes heard information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put と after きいて, but と must come immediately after the information being heard and before きく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形 + と + 聞く
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.vi: I hear that Mr. Kato’s son has passed away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かとうさん with むすこさん and shows possession or a family relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the person who has passed away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: なくなった is the predicate of the information clause and uses a polite expression that is less direct than しんだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです at the end of the sentence shows that the speaker is passing on information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.why: The relationship between Kato and his son is connected by の, the person who passed away is the subject with が, and そうです comes at the end to show reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern reports an ongoing state or action, so it is not suitable for a completed event such as なくなった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If this form follows a verb stem, it means “seems about to” or “looks like,” not “I hear that.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse reported そうです with guessed そうです; look at the form before it to tell them apart.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q16.kobun.vi: Tomorrow I will apologize to Mr. Lee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when the apology will be made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person receiving the apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: あやまります is the main predicate and directly means to apologize to someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q16.kobun.why: The time comes first, the person being apologized to goes with に, and then the verb あやまる completes the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means saying “sorry” to someone, while あやまる directly expresses the act of apologizing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with the person receiving the apology, but the object of あやまる must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.vi: My friend gave me a souvenir.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who gives the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the gift being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: くれました expresses that another person gives something to the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.why: The giver is the subject with が, the gift is the object with を, and くれる shows that the benefit is directed to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with もらう, the receiver becomes the subject and the sentence becomes “I received a gift from my friend.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with あげる, the focus is on the person giving something to someone else, without necessarily being directed to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may choose もらう because they think about receiving a gift, but this sentence makes the friend the subject, so it uses くれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q17.tokens.4.m: gave to me or someone on my side
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q18.kobun.vi: I did not arrive in time for the agreed time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause before it modifies じかん, creating the meaning “the agreed time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the time or deadline that one must meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb まにあう is in the polite past negative form and expresses that someone did not make it in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q18.kobun.why: The clause やくそくした modifies じかん, and に then marks the time that must be reached. まにあう is often used with に to say that someone makes it in time for a certain time or deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: The present negative form only says that someone does not or will not make it in time. It does not stress that the event has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with a time expression, but まにあう must be used with に when talking about making it in time for a certain time or deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 人 with なまえ and shows that the name belongs to that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects わすれる with しまいました to create a pattern that expresses something being accidentally or completely done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました follows a verb in the て form and emphasizes that the result has been completed. It often carries a feeling of regret or unintended action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.why: The phrase あの人のなまえを identifies the object as that person's name. わすれてしまいました uses the て form to connect with しまう and express that the forgetting was completed, with a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vています, the sentence only describes a state of currently or still forgetting, without stressing that the action happened accidentally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If the past negative form is used, the sentence means not remembering or having failed to remember. Its meaning is different from “forget completely”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.tip: Do not connect the plain-form verb directly to しまう; first change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q19.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます／しまった／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Eventが ＋ ありました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks an existing or occurring event in the pattern じしんが ありました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ありました is the polite past form of あります and is used for non-living things or events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q2.kobun.why: The time is stated first, and then じしんが is the subject of ありました. For an event such as an earthquake, use ある instead of いる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If います is used, the sentence describes the existence of a person or animal, so it does not fit an earthquake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate this as “there is” and choose います, but あります is used for objects and non-living events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.vi: It is rare for Mr. Tanaka to miss school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action やすむ in the noun-modified clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the place or activity that the subject takes a break from, in the expression がっこうをやすむ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the entire preceding clause into a noun, while は makes that clause the topic for a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な めずらしい acts as the predicate and comments that missing school is rare.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.why: The clause たなかさんががっこうをやすむ is turned into a noun phrase by の. This phrase combines with は to become the topic, and then めずらしいです gives a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のは with ことは still nominalizes the clause, but the expression is usually more general or formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is used after たなかさん, the focus shifts to Mr. Tanaka himself rather than the event of his missing school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.tip: Do not understand は in のは as the subject; のは turns the entire preceding action into the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ のは ＋ Aなです／Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.vi: The director came to the factory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of coming or appearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: おいでになる is a respectful expression; the form ました describes an action that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.why: こうじょうに comes before the predicate to indicate the destination. おいでになりました replaces the ordinary expression when the subject is someone who should be respected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: It can be replaced with いらっしゃいました, which has a similar respectful meaning: came, was present, or went.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 来ました makes the expression ordinary and does not show respect toward the director.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use おいでになる to show respect for yourself; this respectful form is used for another person's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.vi: My younger brother went to the party in my place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects わたし with かわり and identifies the person being replaced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Nのかわりに indicates doing something instead of or on behalf of the person mentioned before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the person who goes to the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the destination or event that the speaker goes to attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: いきました is the main predicate and describes the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.why: Nのかわりに comes before the subject to state the person whom the younger brother replaces. The subject おとうとが performs the action, while パーティーに indicates the place or event toward which he goes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Nのために, it means doing something for my benefit, not necessarily directly going in my place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If Nといっしょに is used, it means going together with me, which is opposite to going in my place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.tip: かわりに must be used with の after a noun when saying “instead of someone”; do not say わたしかわりに directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q22.kobun.cn: Nのかわりに ＋ V／Nのかわりに ＋ NがV
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the person's name with へや and shows that the room belongs to Mr. Sato.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the room the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: よごれています describes the current state resulting from the room having become dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q23.kobun.why: さとうさんの modifies へや to identify which room it is. は makes the room the topic, while よごれています describes the current state after a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with きたないです, the sentence only describes the quality of being “dirty” and does not stress the state resulting from something making it dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If よごれました is used, the focus is that the room became dirty, not its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q23.kobun.tip: With verbs that describe a change of state, Vています usually describes the result that remains, not necessarily an action that is currently happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q24.kobun.vi: My older brother just went out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the older brother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: This word indicates the time when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q24.kobun.why: The topic is stated first, followed by the time, and finally the main action. さっき stands alone to add a time expression to 出かけました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q24.kobun.tip: Do not mistake さっき for a noun that must be used with the particle に; this word usually comes directly before a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of agreeing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the content that was accepted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects しょうちする with くれた to create an expression meaning that someone does something beneficial for another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: くれた adds the meaning that another person did the action for the speaker or the speaker's side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.why: The person performing the action is used with が, while the content that was accepted is used with を. しょうちして connects to くれた in the て form to express help or goodwill toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would only report that she said she was allowed to marry, without emphasizing that she agreed to help the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily overlook くれた, losing the nuance that another person did something for them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q25.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる/くれます/くれた/くれました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.vi: I do not have many chances to speak Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: あまり is used with a negative predicate to express a small amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of はなす.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb はなす comes before きかい to modify a noun and create the meaning “an opportunity to speak.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the noun being described as nonexistent or unavailable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります and serves as the predicate for きかい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.why: にほんごを はなす come before きかい to identify the type of opportunity. The phrase きかいが ありません expresses not having an opportunity, while あまり reduces the degree in the negative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would mean “have never done,” referring to experience rather than a lack of opportunity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand はなす as the main verb, but here it modifies きかい; the main predicate is ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.vi: I plan to return to my country next year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.sk: Nは + Time + Nへ + V辞書形 + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose plan is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates movement toward the speaker’s hometown or country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: かえる in the dictionary form comes before よてい to modify the plan to return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: よていです is a sentence-ending expression that states a planned arrangement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.why: わたしは states the topic, followed by the time and direction of movement. The dictionary-form verb comes before よてい to make returning to the country the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with つもりです, the sentence would emphasize the speaker’s intention more, while よていです emphasizes a planned arrangement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect a noun directly with よてい, but when the content is a verb, use the dictionary form before よてい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + よていです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.vi: I have no experience working at a Japanese company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with かいしゃ to create the phrase “Japanese company.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the action はたらいた takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: はたらいた in the past form comes before けいけん to modify the work experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the experience being described as nonexistent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません denies the existence of the experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.why: にほんの かいしゃで identify the workplace, while はたらいた comes before けいけん to state the type of experience. けいけんが ありません expresses not having that experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern were used, the sentence would emphasize never having done it, while けいけんがありません emphasizes the lack of experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for “Japanese company” and forget that で here indicates the place where the action はたらいた takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q5.kobun.cn: Vた形 + けいけんが ありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.vi: The number of people studying Japanese has increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: This clause comes before ひと to modify which people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects ふえる with くる and expresses an ongoing change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: きました is the polite past form of くる, used as an auxiliary verb to show progress up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.why: The phrase べんきょうするひと forms a clause that modifies ひと. The subject ひとが comes before ふえてきました, and てくる emphasizes the gradual increase up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in the sentence, the nuance would lean toward becoming more crowded or numerous, without directly emphasizing the increasing number of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only indicates an increasing state and places less emphasis on the gradual process leading up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse てくる with simply indicating movement toward a place; in this sentence, くる expresses a change progressing over time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.vi: After reading the letter, I felt relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the letter as the object being read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of reading with the feeling of relief that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: This is the main predicate and expresses the feeling after reading the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.why: The action of reading the letter is placed first in the て form to show the cause or time of the feeling of relief. Japanese often omits the subject わたし when the person performing both actions is the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in the sentence, the meaning would still be “after reading,” but the time order would be stated more clearly and separately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced in the sentence, the focus would shift to the reason: because I read the letter, I felt relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate the て form as only “and,” but here it also shows the before-and-after relationship between the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.vi: I will discuss the school matter with Mr. Tanaka.
