default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person taking part in the discussion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects がっこう with こと to modify the content being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ことを indicates the content or issue being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate; 相談する usually uses と for the person discussing with you and を for the content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.why: The person discussing stands before と, while the discussion content stands before を. のこと changes the noun がっこう into a phrase referring to an issue related to school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in the sentence, the nuance would emphasize discussing together to reach an opinion or decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern being used has the nuance of asking for advice or discussing something to find a solution.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with the listener, but 相談する usually uses と to indicate the person discussing the matter with them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the bus the topic being judged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: もう shows that the expected time has nearly arrived or has arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form くる comes before はず to state what is predicted to be true.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: はずです expresses a well-supported prediction or something considered natural or expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.why: The bus is made the topic with は. The verb くる in the dictionary form directly modifies はず, creating the judgment that the bus arriving is well supported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in the sentence, this would be a softer prediction and would not emphasize firm evidence as はずです does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced in the sentence, the level of certainty would decrease, meaning only that the bus might arrive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand はず as absolute certainty, but this pattern means a prediction based on evidence or a schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.tokens.5.m: to be; is said to be
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t108-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ はずだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.vi: What do you want to become in the future?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.sk: Time reference ＋ N は／なに に ＋ Vますたいですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This word refers to the time or period that the speaker hopes for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the result or destination of なります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: なりたいですか combines the meaning of wanting with the polite form and か to create a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ たいですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.why: しょうらい sets the time context, なにに states the desired result, while なりたいですか is the predicate used to ask about wishes. なります always uses に when talking about becoming a profession or status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the question is more clearly about a definite plan, not only a wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use を before なります when talking about becoming a profession or status; use に instead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.vi: Whenever the teacher meets me, they always ask, “Are you well?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は shows that the teacher is the person who asks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: わたし is the object mentioned in the phrase 会う; in natural speech, に is usually needed after this word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 会うと connects a repeated condition or time with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: いつも modifies the frequency of the asking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the content of directly quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: たずねます is the main predicate and takes the question content through と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.why: The clause 会うと comes first to state the repeated time, and then いつも shows the frequency. The question content is placed in quotation marks and connected to たずねます by と. The given sentence is missing に after わたし; the natural form is わたしに会うと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, it means that it happens every time they meet, emphasizing each meeting more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 聞きます, the tone is lighter and more common, meaning asking or hearing information, than たずねます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle に in わたしに会う; 会う with people who usually use に to mark the person they meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q10.kobun.cn: Vる ＋ と、～; 「～」と ＋ 言う／聞く／尋ねる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.vi: Your Japanese has become better than before, hasn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject being evaluated for ability or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: より gives the comparison point, meaning compared with before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: じょうずに combines with なる to show a change to a better state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, while ね is used to confirm or share an impression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.why: The subject being evaluated comes before が, the comparison point goes with より, and the new state comes before なる. The past form なりました shows that the improvement has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 前より is replaced with もっと, the sentence only emphasizes “even better” without stating a comparison point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から instead of より to mean “more,” but Japanese comparisons use より.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.vi: As for tomorrow’s trip, I will still go even if it rains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow’s trip the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the action connected to ても; in the given sentence, 前 has an unusual form and meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the て form combines with も to express “even if …, still …”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the main clause and states the action that will still happen despite the earlier condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.why: The topic is stated first with は, followed by the concessive clause with ても before the main action. This connection emphasizes that the result 行きます does not change even if the condition occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ても is replaced with たら, the sentence becomes the condition “if it rains, then I will go,” and no longer has the meaning “even if …, still …”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ても as “if,” but this pattern emphasizes that the result stays the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q12.kobun.cn: Vて形・Aいくて・Aなで・Nで ＋ も
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.vi: What do your classmates call you?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects クラス with 友だち, forming the phrase “classmate.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the classmate the subject being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person being called.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: どう modifies よびます and asks how someone is called or what name is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: よびますか creates a polite question about how someone is called.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.why: The possessive phrase クラスの友だち is the topic, the person being called goes with を, and どう stands directly before the verb to ask how. This word order is equivalent to “What way or name do they use to call you?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If どう is replaced with なんと, the question focuses more on the specific name or word used to call someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place どう after the verb, but this adverb usually comes before the verb it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.vi: If I do not leave now, I will be late for the concert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 states the time when the action in the conditional clause occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: This part is used with a negative conditional meaning; the standard form is 出かけなければ, but the given sentence is missing け.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the event toward which being late is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: おくれます is the result that occurs if the earlier condition is met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.cn: Vない形 remove い ＋ ければ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.why: The time expression 今 is placed at the beginning of the conditional clause, and the main result follows. The negative pattern with ければ expresses “if not …, then …”; the given sentence writes 出かけなれば and is missing け compared with the standard form 出かけなければ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If なければ is replaced with なかったら, the condition still means “if not,” but the conversational and hypothetical tone is clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget け in the pattern Vなければ, so remember that Vない removes い and then adds ければ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.vi: It is almost time for the guest to arrive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: そろそろ modifies a time that is about to occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the action 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 来る in the dictionary form comes before the noun じかん to modify “time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: じかんです functions as the predicate and identifies the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.why: The clause おきゃくさんが来る comes before じかん to identify it as “the time when the guest arrives.” そろそろ is placed at the beginning to show that this time is approaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来る is replaced with 来た, the meaning becomes “the time when the guest arrived,” meaning the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 来ます before a noun, but a clause that modifies a noun must use the plain form, such as 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.vi: I usually eat dinner at 7 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes dinner the topic of the habit being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: たいてい is an adverb of frequency that modifies the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the fixed time when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: たべます is the main predicate and expresses the habit of eating dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.why: The dinner topic comes first, the frequency adverb comes before the verb, and the specific time is used with に. This order makes both the habit and the mealtime clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If たいてい is replaced with だいたい, the meaning changes from “usually” to “about/approximately,” which is often used for an imprecise amount or time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に after the time, but a specific time such as 7時 usually needs to be used with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate; です makes the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q17.kobun.why: The topic is placed first with は, followed by the adjective that describes the topic's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q17.kobun.tip: Do not confuse にがい, meaning “bitter,” with あまい, meaning “sweet.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q18.kobun.vi: Please tidy up the pen you used before going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: つかった in the past form modifies ペン, while は states that this pen is the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of tidying up with the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q18.kobun.why: The clause つかった modifies ペン, and then は makes the whole phrase “used pen” the topic. The two actions are connected by the て form, and the sentence ends with a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてから, the sentence emphasizes more clearly that the tidying up must be finished before going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ペン; when modifying a noun, the verb must be changed according to the time you want to express.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q19.kobun.vi: Please do not pollute the water of this river.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the river water as the object being polluted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The ないで form is used to ask someone not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q19.kobun.why: The affected object is used with を. The verb is changed to the ないで form and then combined with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: When this pattern is used, it means asking someone to try to be careful not to do that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q19.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ないでください with なくてください; the correct form is the negative ない followed by でください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: ほとんどの modifies 人 and limits the group of people being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the people who performed the action of attending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the past form and states the subject's main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q2.kobun.why: ほとんどの must come before the noun to modify it, forming the phrase ほとんどの人. This phrase acts as the subject with が and comes before the predicate しゅっせきした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the meaning is that many people attended, but it does not state that the proportion was almost everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q2.kobun.tip: Do not place ほとんどの after the noun; you need to say ほとんどの人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.vi: Let's keep the party ticket price within 3,000 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.sk: N は + amount of money に + Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the party ticket price is what needs to be decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the limit at which the ticket price should be set.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう expresses a suggestion to do or decide something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.why: The topic is the ticket price, while the phrase 3,000円いないに shows the limit to reach. にする shows deciding or adjusting something to the stated state or level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If までにする is used, the sentence emphasizes that the maximum is 3,000 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.kobun.tip: 以内に means “within the range, not exceeding,” not simply “cheaper.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q20.tokens.8.m: within the range, no more than
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q21.kobun.vi: I ate rice instead of bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: Nの代わりに indicates the thing being replaced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the food chosen as the replacement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and expresses a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q21.kobun.why: The phrase Nの代わりに states the food that was not used, while ごはんを is the direct object of the action of eating. This structure clearly shows the replacement relationship between the two foods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Nに代わって, it usually means doing something in place of or representing that person or thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q21.kobun.tip: Do not omit の in Nの代わりに when a noun comes before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 父 with いなか, creating the meaning “father's hometown”; は states that this phrase is the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the topic with the identified place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q22.kobun.why: の shows possession or a relationship between 父 and いなか. After は comes the place used to identify the father's hometown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 父の出身地 is used, the meaning is more precisely “the place where one's father comes from,” with a more formal nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q22.kobun.tip: いなか in this sentence means “hometown”; it should not be understood as a rural area in the geographical sense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.vi: Do you know the person over there?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location where a person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: いる is the predicate of the clause modifying かた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person who is known; かた is a polite way to say person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ごぞんじ is a polite form of 知る, while でしょうか makes the sentence a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.why: The clause あちらにいる comes before かた to identify which person is meant. The known person is the object marked by を, while でしょうか makes the question polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it gives a more ordinary question, without the respectful tone of ごぞんじでしょうか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q23.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に with the person who is known, but in the structure 知る／ごぞんじだ, the object usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.vi: I will stay at my uncle's house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects おじさん with いえ to indicate the house belonging to my uncle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the speaker will stay as a lodger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: げしゅくします is the predicate and describes staying at another person's house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.why: おじさんのいえ creates the noun phrase “my uncle's house,” and then に indicates the location of the action. げしゅくします describes staying with or lodging at someone else's place, not simply living there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 住みます, the sentence only says that the person lives there, without emphasizing lodging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 泊まります, the sentence usually means sleeping over or staying for a short time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q24.kobun.tip: Do not treat げしゅくします and 住みます as the same; this word emphasizes staying at another person's house or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the skirt being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents スカート as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: よごれて is the て form of よごれる, and connects the verb to います to describe a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes a present state caused by a change that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.why: スカートは is the topic, while よごれている describes its current state. ている is used here to express the result “it became dirty and is still dirty,” rather than simply reporting a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only emphasizes that the skirt became dirty, without emphasizing its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes becoming dirty or worse, that is, the process of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate every ている as “be doing,” but with change verbs such as よごれる, it usually indicates the resulting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 父 with いなか and shows that the hometown mentioned is my father's.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents my father's hometown as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with the identified place in a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q3.kobun.why: 父の comes before いなか to create the noun phrase “my father's hometown.” After presenting the topic phrase with は, the place name Hokkaido identifies it with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to the place where my father was born, which is narrower than hometown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q3.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate の as “of” in every case; here, 父のいなか is a phrase referring to my father's hometown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.vi: Do you know the person over there?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.sk: Location に ＋ Vる ＋ N を ＋ ごぞんじでしょうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where the person mentioned is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いる comes before かた to modify the person who is over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the person as the object of knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ごぞんじでしょうか is a polite, softer way to ask whether the listener knows that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.why: あちらにいる is a clause modifying かた, so it comes directly before this noun. The whole person phrase is the object marked by を, and ごぞんじでしょうか is then used to ask politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence still asks whether someone knows, but it is less formal than ごぞんじでしょうか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.tip: Do not separate いる from the noun that follows when translating; あちらにいるかた means “the person who is over there.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q4.kobun.cn: Vる ＋ N; N を ＋ ごぞんじです／でしょうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.vi: I was not available that day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ past negative verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents that day as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject in the fixed expression つごうがつく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: つかなかった is the past negative form of つく in the expression つごうがつく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.why: The day is introduced first with は, and then つごうがつかなかった describes a situation that could not be arranged or was inconvenient. The expression つごうがつく is used as a fixed expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the meaning is that the schedule or situation was unfavorable, with a more direct tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate つく as “go” or “arrive,” but in つごうがつく it means “manage to arrange” or “be convenient.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q5.tokens.5.m: could not arrange; was not convenient
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.vi: I make a habit of drinking milk in the morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N を ＋ V辞書形ことを ＋ N に ＋ しています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: あさ indicates the time when the action of drinking milk takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the drink being consumed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 飲む is followed by こと to turn it into the noun “drinking,” which is the object of しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates a state or goal that is maintained: turning drinking milk into a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: しています describes a habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.why: The action is nominalized with こと, and then combined with にしています to talk about a maintained habit. あさ comes first to identify the time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the focus is on trying to form a habit of doing that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use 飲むを directly; add こと to turn the verb into a noun before using it as an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ことを ＋ N にしています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.vi: Sorry, I am preparing right now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is an apology used at the beginning before explaining the current situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 今 indicates the time when the action is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks preparation as the object of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.ch.3.vi: to be in the middle of doing
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Vているところです emphasizes that the action is happening at the moment of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.why: 今 comes before the verb to limit the time to the present. したくを is the object, while しているところです shows that the speaker is in the middle of preparing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence only says that the person is doing it, with less emphasis on the exact moment in the process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this pattern, the meaning is that the person has just finished preparing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.tip: ところ in this pattern does not mean “place”; it indicates the stage of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q7.kobun.cn: Vている + ところです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q8.kobun.sk: Degree + N をかけて + Vて
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: じゅうぶん modifies the degree of time that needs to be spent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 時間をかける is a phrase that expresses spending a period of time; the form て connects to the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 話して is the て form used as a gentle request: please talk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q8.kobun.why: じかんをかけて comes before 話して to show the manner and duration of the talking action. The form て connects two ideas: spend time, then talk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means arranging or setting aside time, without emphasizing the process of taking time as 時間をかけて does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate をかける literally as “hang up”; 時間をかける means to spend or devote time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.vi: I was invited to a party by Kim.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.sk: N は + N に + N に + past passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person receiving the invitation the topic of the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: In a passive sentence, に marks the person who performs the inviting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination or event that the speaker is invited to attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: されました is the polite past passive form of しょうたいする, expressing that the speaker received an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.why: The affected person is made the topic with は, while the inviter takes に. パーティーに indicates the place or event being approached and comes before the passive verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active sentence is used, the focus shifts to Kim as the person who performed the inviting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 誘われました, it means being invited to go along, with a more casual and broader sense than “being formally invited.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person performing the action usually takes に, not を as in an active sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t109-q9.kobun.cn: N を + Vさせる → N は + N に + V(ら)れる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vi: I have a small dog at home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where a person or animal exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 小さな comes before 犬 to modify the dog.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that exists at the stated place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: います expresses the existence of an animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.why: A place takes に when the sentence talks about existence. 小さな modifies 犬, while 犬がいます is the structure for saying that an animal exists there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 飼っています, the meaning becomes “I keep a dog at home,” emphasizing the action of keeping it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q1.kobun.tip: With います for saying that a person or animal exists, the place takes に, not で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vi: My father goes out at night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states 父 as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 夜 indicates the time when the action 出かけます takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q10.kobun.why: 父は is the topic, and then 夜 adds the time of the action. The predicate 出かけます comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is added, the nighttime is marked more clearly, but the basic meaning does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 夜中に, the time becomes narrower and emphasizes the middle of the night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q10.kobun.tip: Do not read 出かける using the Sino-Japanese sound of 出; this word is read as でかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vi: I am going to buy groceries.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 食料品 as the object of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 買う removes ます and connects to に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.why: 食料品を is the object of 買う, while 買いに states the purpose of 行きます. In this pattern, the verb expressing the purpose uses the stem ます before に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence is more formal and emphasizes the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern modifies a noun and does not directly express the purpose of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use 買うに行きます; remove ます from 買います and change it to 買い before に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q11.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + に + 行く/来る/帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vi: I think about the future by myself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: しょうらいの modifies こと, forming a phrase about the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes こと the topic being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the method or the person who performs the action independently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.why: しょうらいのこと forms the topic and is marked by は. 自分で shows that the speaker performs the thinking action personally, and then かんがえます ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes doing an action personally, emphasizing the method or the person performing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 自分の is used, it must come before a noun to express possession; it cannot directly replace 自分で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse で, which indicates a place, with で, which indicates a method, in 自分で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vi: I was absent from school because I was sick.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause leading to being absent from school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the range or place temporarily left in 休む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 休む changes to the polite past form to express an event that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.why: 病気で places the cause before the action, while 学校を is the object related to being absent. The predicate 休みました comes last and shows that the event was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 病気だから, the cause is stated directly and the conversational tone is clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 病気なので, the expression is softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use に after 病気 to indicate the cause; the cause in this sentence uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.vi: My older brother got married last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: きょねん indicates the time when the marriage took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 兄 as the subject performing the act of getting married.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: けっこんする changes to the polite past form to describe a completed event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.why: きょねん is placed at the beginning to state the time. 兄が is the subject of けっこんしました, and the verb at the end serves as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, 兄 becomes the topic or the subject being compared, rather than simply a new subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: と marks the person one marries, so it cannot replace が in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use は when you only need to introduce the subject of a new event; が is more suitable here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.vi: The air is really fresh here, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object described as fresh.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: きれい is a な adjective used as a predicate and combines with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: ね is used to gently confirm something and seek agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.why: ここは makes the place the topic, and then 空気が is the object being evaluated. きれいです serves as the predicate, and ね creates a casual confirming tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If a noun follows, きれい must connect as きれいなN; do not use きれいですN.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that きれい is a な adjective, so it needs です when used as a predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.vi: A map of a foreign country is stuck to the wall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the map is stuck.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 外国 with 地図, creating the meaning “map of a foreign country.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that has the state of being stuck.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: はって is the て form of はる, connected to あります in a pattern that expresses a resulting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: あります completes the Vてあります pattern and emphasizes that the result of the action still remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.why: かべに states the location, while 外国の地図が is the object in the state of being stuck there. はってあります expresses that the result of sticking it up still remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with はっています, the sentence only describes an action in progress or a current state. It does not emphasize an arranged result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse Vてあります with Vています; てあります usually refers to a result intentionally created by someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.vi: This is an Indian song, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies or introduces the item being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects インド with 歌, indicating origin or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects a noun used as the predicate with the topic これは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ね adds a feeling of confirmation or agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.why: これは is the topic, and インドの modifies 歌 to show its origin. This noun phrase combines with です to form a statement, and then ね softens the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If ね is replaced with でしょう, the sentence sounds more like a guess or a polite confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate の as “of” in every case, but here it also shows the origin of the song.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.vi: From here, we will enter the neighboring prefecture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects となり with 県, creating the phrase “neighboring prefecture.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the action 入ります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 入ります is a predicate that indicates entering a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.why: ここから gives the starting point, while となりの県に gives the destination. The verb 入ります is placed at the end to complete the meaning of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, the sentence still points toward the neighboring prefecture but emphasizes direction more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で for a destination, but the verb 入る needs に or へ to indicate the place entered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.vi: That city is famous for its glass industry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies まち and indicates a city far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes that city the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects ガラス with 産業, indicating the industrial field related to glass.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object described as famous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ゆうめい is a な adjective used as the predicate with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.why: あのまちは is the main topic of the sentence. Inside the comment, ガラスの産業が is the subject evaluated as ゆうめいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the industry becomes a contrastive or emphasized topic, so the meaning is no longer a neutral comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use は for every subject, but が here marks the object being commented on in the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vi: What a beautiful voice, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: きれいな uses the form な to modify 声.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 声 is the main noun in the phrase being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね ends the comment and creates a friendly tone that seeks agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.why: きれいな comes before 声 because the adjective な must connect to a noun with な. The phrase きれいな声 is presented as the comment, and then ですね completes the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced with ですよ, the sentence sounds more like an announcement or statement to the listener than a request for agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out な and say きれい声, but the adjective な needs な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vi: I watched TV while eating dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 夕飯 with とき, creating a phrase that indicates a time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: とき states when the action of watching TV happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb 見ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 見ました is the polite past form of 見る and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.why: 夕飯のとき is a time phrase placed at the beginning to set the background for the action. テレビを is the object, while 見ました ends the sentence and shows that the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is replaced with あとで, the meaning changes to “after dinner,” so it no longer means during dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand とき as “when,” but may forget that the noun before it must connect with の in the phrase 夕飯のとき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the state that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです connects with the adjective stem to express appearance or an inference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q21.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + そうだ／そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q21.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, and then いつも indicates frequency. The adjective いそがしい removes い and connects with そうです to describe an appearance being observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ようです, the sentence has a more inferential or formal comparative tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q21.kobun.tip: Do not connect そうです directly to the adjective い; remove い before connecting them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.vi: Do you have a blue thread?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun 青 with the noun いと to modify the thread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the blue thread is the object being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますか creates a question about whether an object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.why: 青のいと is a noun phrase in which 青の comes before and modifies いと. は makes this phrase the topic, while ありますか asks whether it exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 青い糸, the meaning is still “blue thread,” but the adjective い is used directly instead of the noun 青の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 青の糸 with 青い糸: 青の uses a noun + の, while 青い is a い adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q22.kobun.cn: N + の + N; N は + ありますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.vi: There is a bank over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the place where the bank exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object identified as existing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is a predicate used for the existence of objects or places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.why: The location comes first with に, and the existing object follows with が. あります ends the sentence and is used for things that are not people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with います, the sentence must refer to a person or animal instead of a bank.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is used, the location is understood as the place where an action happens, not the place where an object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.tip: In the existence pattern, use に for a place and が for an existing thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q23.kobun.cn: 場所 に + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.vi: Please give me that brown tie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies the noun immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun 茶色 with ネクタイ to indicate a tie that is brown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object requested by the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed at the end of a sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.why: あの and 茶色の both modify ネクタイ, forming a complete noun phrase. を marks the requested item, while ください comes at the end to express a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with お願いします, the request becomes more formal and has the broader meaning of asking for the item or asking someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.tip: In the phrase NのN, the noun before の modifies the noun after it; the two positions cannot be reversed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q24.kobun.cn: N の + N; N を + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: きれいな directly modifies 着物 and keeps な before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the desired object with ほしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ほしいです is a predicate expressing the desire to possess something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q25.kobun.why: きれいな comes before 着物 to describe the kimono. With ほしい, the desired object usually takes が, followed by ほしいです as the final predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ほしがっています, the sentence expresses another person's desire and uses を for the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use を with ほしい in the basic pattern; the desired object usually takes が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q25.kobun.cn: Aな + N; N が + ほしいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the time when an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of する. It connects with います to express an action that is happening or regularly takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: います follows a verb in the て form to create the ています pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to state the time. Then パートを is the object of する. The て form connects して with います, expressing an activity that is happening or regularly takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with パートをします, it only says that the person does part-time work, without emphasizing that the activity is happening or regular.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit the particle に after a time expression, but a specific time usually needs に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: いっしょに is an adverb that modifies the action of taking a photo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the action とる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう comes at the end of a sentence to invite someone or suggest doing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.why: いっしょに modifies the suggestion, while 写真を is the object being photographed. The verb in the ましょう form creates an invitation to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If とりませんか is used, the invitation becomes softer and sounds more like asking for the listener's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use と一緒に as a required phrase, but いっしょに already means “together” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 英語 with 本, showing the type or content of the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes 本 the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますか creates a question about whether an object exists or is available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.why: 英語の comes before 本 to modify the noun 本. 本は states the exact type of book being asked about, and ありますか asks whether that type of book exists or is available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 英語の本がありますか is used, the question asks more directly whether there is an English book, without making 本 the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate の as “of,” but in 英語の本 it only shows a relationship of type or content: “English book.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vi: I will leave tomorrow at noon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with 昼, forming a noun phrase meaning tomorrow's noon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 昼 combines with あしたの to indicate the time of departure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: しゅっぱつします is the main predicate and uses the polite form to describe the action of leaving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.why: あしたの modifies 昼 to form the time phrase “tomorrow at noon.” The time phrase comes before the predicate しゅっぱつします, so the listener understands that it is the time of departure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is added, the time is marked more clearly. The sentence remains natural but expresses the time more directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often add に after every time phrase, but phrases such as あしたの昼 can come before a verb without に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vi: Her son is a high school student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かのじょ with むすこ, showing possession or a family relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes むすこ the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 高校生です is a noun predicate and uses です to end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.why: かのじょのむすこ creates the complete noun phrase “her son.” This phrase is the topic with は, while 高校生です gives definite information about that topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that the son himself is a high school student, rather than simply stating the son as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand の as only meaning “of,” but here it also shows the relationship between the woman and her son.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vi: Because it was cold outside, I put on a jacket and went out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes 外 the topic for describing the condition outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a reason clause with its result, and さむい is the adjective serving as the predicate of the previous clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks 上着 as the item being worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: きて is the て form, connecting the action of putting on clothes with the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: いきました is the main predicate and shows that the action of going happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.why: 外は gives the situation, and さむいので explains the reason for the following action. 上着を is the object of きる, while the て form connects putting on the jacket with going and places the two actions in order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced by から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 着てから is used, the sentence clearly emphasizes that the person put on the jacket before leaving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use ので after an adjective and forget that な adjectives and nouns must add な before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vi: May I take this sheet of paper?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun （紙） that follows it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the item received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb もらう changes to the て form and then connects with も to create a permission pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: いいですか asks whether the listener approves the previous action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.why: この modifies 紙, while を marks the item received. The pattern Vて もいいですか comes at the end to ask for permission to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If used, the sentence means that receiving this sheet of paper is forbidden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If か is omitted, the sentence becomes permission rather than a request for permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t11-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that the verb before もいいですか must use the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q1.kobun.vi: I did not make it to class on time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time or time target that the action must be in time for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q1.kobun.ch.1.vi: did not make it on time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: まにあう means “to be in time”; its past negative form means “did not make it on time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q1.kobun.why: The noun じゅぎょう goes with に because it is the time target that must be met. まにあいませんでした negates the result, so it means “did not make it on time,” not simply “arrived late.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means “arrived late,” focusing only on being behind schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q1.kobun.tip: Remember that まにあう goes with に to show being in time for a deadline or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.vi: My younger sister has gained weight recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.sk: Time + N は + polite past-tense V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of time showing that the event happened near the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks my younger sister as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb showing a physical change, in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.why: さいきん is placed at the beginning to state the time, then は makes the younger sister the topic. ふとりました ends the sentence and expresses that the change has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes the current state of being fat or having become fat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q10.kobun.tip: Do not translate ふとりました as “has become heavy”; understand it as “has gained weight.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.sk: Demonstrative + N は + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before a noun to modify it and point to an identified object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks that phone number as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The i-adjective い is used as the predicate and ends with です to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.why: その modifies でんわばんごう, forming a complete noun phrase. は makes this phrase the topic, while ただしいです gives a comment about its accuracy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to “not correct,” which negates the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a polite guess, meaning “it is probably correct.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q11.kobun.tip: With the i-adjective い, do not add な before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.vi: I take a walk every day after eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.sk: Frequency + Vた + あと、 + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase acts as an adverb of frequency for the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: A past-tense verb comes before あと to modify the time after the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: あと shows the time after an action and connects to the main clause with a comma.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite-form verb is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.why: 毎日 is placed at the beginning to show a habit. The phrase しょくじしたあと states the earlier action, and then さんぽします expresses the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning becomes “before eating,” reversing the time relationship with the walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence still means “after eating,” but it emphasizes doing the earlier action first and only then doing the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.tip: Before あと, when saying that an action has been completed, use Vた, not the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q12.kobun.cn: Vた + あと、 / Nの + あと、
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.vi: Mr. Muraki introduced me to Mr. Sou.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.sk: N1 は + N2 に + N3 を + polite past passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person affected by the passive sentence as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person being introduced, the object of the introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: されました is the polite past passive form of しょうかいする, showing that I was affected by the introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.why: Because the sentence is passive, the person affected, わたし, goes with は. The person who performs the action goes with に, while the person being introduced goes with を; the passive verb comes at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to the active voice, Mr. Muraki is the subject of the action, and the sentence emphasizes that he made the introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence emphasizes that I received help or a benefit from being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person who performs the action usually goes with に, not が as the subject of an active sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q13.kobun.cn: N1 は + N2 に + N3 を + V受身
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the fax machine as the object that developed a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: こしょうする describes a device developing a problem; しました is the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q14.kobun.why: が identifies which device has a problem. こしょうしました acts as the predicate and describes an event that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning is still “broke down,” but it is a more direct and common way to describe the state of an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q14.kobun.tip: Do not confuse こしょうしました with the meaning “was repaired”; this word means that a breakdown occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.sk: N は + degree + N が + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person experiencing the uncomfortable feeling as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと modifies the state わるい and makes the degree milder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the feeling as the part that has the state わるい in the pattern for expressing feelings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: わるいです acts as the predicate and combines with きもちが to express an uncomfortable feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.why: わたしは states the person experiencing the feeling, while きもちがわるい is a fixed phrase expressing an unpleasant feeling. ちょっと comes before the adjective phrase to reduce its intensity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning stays almost the same but focuses more on the person’s current physical condition or mood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the expression is softer and less direct than わるいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use は after きもち in this pattern; きもちがわるい uses が to connect the feeling with the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q16.kobun.vi: I delivered a magazine to my senior.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the receiver of an action involving giving or sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the item being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb とどける takes the polite past form to express a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q16.kobun.why: The receiver comes before に, while the item being sent comes before を. とどけました is the main predicate and states that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 渡す, the sentence emphasizes handing something over directly rather than bringing or sending it to the receiver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for the receiver, but the receiver usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object that is in a cold state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: ひえる is an intransitive verb describing the juice becoming cold; the て form connects to います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ～ています describes a present state that has already been formed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q17.kobun.why: ジュースが is the object that has the state, while ひえています combines an intransitive verb with いる to describe the present state. This use does not stress who made the juice cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 冷たい is used, the sentence directly describes the cold quality of the juice, without stressing the process of it becoming cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If 冷やしている is used, there is a subject that is making the juice cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand ～ています as simply meaning that someone is doing something, but with state verbs it often describes a result that is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.vi: I was apologized to by Yong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.sk: N は + N に + passive Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person affected by the action the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performs the action affecting the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: あやまる changes to the passive form あやまられる, and then takes the polite past form to say that I received an apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.cn: For V, remove る and add られる; for Group 1 V, change the final sound to the あ row and add れる; irregular V: する → される, 来[く]る → 来[こ]られる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.why: Because the sentence makes わたし the topic affected by the action, it uses は. The person who performs the action goes with に, while あやまられました is the passive predicate, showing that the speaker receives an apology from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active sentence is used, Yong is the person who apologizes, and the sentence does not focus on my experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If the causative-passive form is used, the meaning becomes that I was forced to apologize to Yong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q18.kobun.tip: English learners may mechanically translate the passive as being blamed, but あやまる means “apologize,” so あやまられる means “be apologized to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.vi: We are exporting a lot of fruit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: たくさんの modifies くだもの and indicates the amount of fruit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the goods being exported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ゆしゅつする takes the て form to connect with います in an expression for an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ～ています describes an export activity that is continuing or carried out regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.why: たくさんの comes before a noun to modify its quantity, while くだものを is the object of ゆしゅつする. The phrase ゆしゅつしています places the export action in an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 売っています is used, the meaning is only that someone is selling fruit, without necessarily sending goods abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q19.kobun.tip: English learners may easily place たくさん after the noun because of their first language, but たくさんの must come before the noun when it means “many + noun.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.vi: I prepared a large stereo system for the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects パーティー with ため to form a phrase showing purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ために indicates the purpose of the preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな comes before ステレオ to modify the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing that was prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: じゅんびしました is the polite past predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.why: パーティーのために states the purpose, 大きな modifies ステレオ, and を marks the thing that was prepared. The parts are arranged in this order: purpose → feature of the thing → object → action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If パーティーに replaces it, the sentence may mean preparing at or for the party, but the purpose is not emphasized as clearly as with ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If よういしました replaces it, the meaning is still “prepare,” but the nuance focuses more on preparing the necessary items or conditions in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may omit の in Nのために; a noun before ために usually needs の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q2.kobun.cn: Nの + ために; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the place being discussed the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object whose state changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in な changes to the ～に form to show the state or result that the transportation has become.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: なる takes the polite past form and describes a change that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.why: ここは states the location, while こうつうが is the subject that changes. ふべんに なりました combines the adjective ending in な with に to describe the result that transportation has become inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ふべんです is used, the sentence only describes the transportation as inconvenient and does not stress the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If ふべんにします is used, there is a subject that actively makes the transportation inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use ふべんなになります, but before なる, ふべんに must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q20.kobun.cn: Aな + に + なる; N + に + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q21.kobun.vi: The weather is very bad today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes today the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: ひどい is an adjective ending in い that comes before a noun to modify the weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 天気です serves as a noun predicate and concludes the comment about today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q21.kobun.why: きょうは limits the comment to today. ひどい comes before 天気 to describe the weather, and then noun + です forms the polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 天気が悪いです is used, the sentence describes bad weather in a more neutral way, while ひどい emphasizes how bad or harsh it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may place the adjective after the noun because of their first language, but Japanese adjectives come before nouns when they modify them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q22.kobun.vi: Be careful of cars on the narrow road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective modifies 道 and shows that the road is narrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: では both states the place as the topic and limits the context of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object to watch out for in the expression 注意する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q22.kobun.why: The adjective comes before 道 to modify the place. 注意する usually goes with に to indicate the object to watch out for, while では sets the whole situation as the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: The replacement still means being careful, but 気をつける emphasizes being personally alert and usually goes with に or を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q22.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with 注意する because of their first language, but the correct pattern is Nに注意する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.vi: Ken was thanked by the director.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Ken as the person being talked about in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content spoken in the phrase お礼を言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 言われました is the polite past passive form of 言う, showing that Ken received words from the director.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.cn: Vない形 removeない + れる／られる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.why: Because the sentence makes the person affected by the action the topic, it uses ケンさんは. The person who performs the action goes with に, while お礼を is the content combined with 言う before changing to the passive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: In the active sentence, the director is the speaker, while Ken is the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q23.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse に in the passive sentence with the receiver, but here しゃちょうに is the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the object or field connected to the verb しっぱいする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q24.kobun.why: しっぱいする often combines with に to state what or which field failed. Therefore, しけんに comes before the predicate and means failing an exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression also means failing an exam, but it emphasizes the result of not passing rather than the process of failing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q24.kobun.tip: Do not translate に mechanically as a place; in しっぱいする, に refers to the thing or field in which someone failed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.vi: Please tell me the reason you were absent from work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb 休む in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause しごとを休んだ comes before 理由 and modifies the reason being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 理由 as the information the speaker wants to know.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects おしえる with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ください completes the polite request pattern Vてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.why: しごとを休んだ is the clause before 理由 that identifies the reason for being absent from work. 理由を is the object of おしえる, while Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to provide information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use Nの理由, you only state the reason for a noun and do not clearly mention an action that happened, such as しごとを休んだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the modifying clause after the noun, but in Japanese しごとを休んだ must come before りゆう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.vi: I was scolded by my grandfather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person affected by the passive action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: おこられました is the past passive form of おこる, showing that I received the action of being scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.cn: V受身: Group 1 verbs remove う and add あれる; Group 2 verbs remove る and add られる; する → される; くる → こられる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.why: A passive sentence makes the affected person, わたし, the topic with は. The person who causes the action is そふ, marked by に, and the verb then uses the past passive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to an active sentence, the grandfather is the subject and I am the person being scolded; the focus of the sentence changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with しかられました, it also means being scolded or reprimanded, but the tone is usually stricter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the person who scolds in a passive sentence; the person performing the action usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.vi: I know the director's schedule for tomorrow well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns あす into a modifier for よてい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the schedule is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects しょうちする with います to express a state of knowing or having fully understood something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern しょうちしている and expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.why: The two phrases の modify よてい in order: the schedule belongs to the director and is for tomorrow. は makes よてい the topic, while しょうちしている expresses a state of already knowing the information well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it still means knowing or understanding, but the tone focuses more on natural awareness than on the formal expression of having received information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ている as only meaning 'to be doing', but here it expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.vi: The road in front of the department store is very lively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects デパート with the following noun to create a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 前の modifies とおり and indicates the road located in front of the department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that とおり is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The な-ending adjective にぎやか combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.why: The phrases の come before とおり to narrow the meaning of the road: the road in front of the department store. After the topic, the adjective にぎやか describes the road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 道 replaces とおり, the basic meaning is still road, but it usually refers to a road in general and does not emphasize a street or avenue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that a noun modifying another noun must be connected by の, rather than using a possessive particle in Vietnamese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes しょくじ the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies the predicate to show that the meal has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: すみました is the polite past form of すむ, acts as the predicate, and expresses completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q6.kobun.why: The sentence makes しょくじ the topic and then uses もう to emphasize a completed state. すみました comes at the end because it is the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 終わりました, the sentence directly says that the meal ended; すみました emphasizes that the task that needed to be done has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q6.kobun.tip: Do not understand すむ only as 'to live'; in a work or event context, it can mean 'finished' or 'completed'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 大学 with コンピューター to indicate the computer belonging to the university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the computer as the object being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: りようしました is a polite past predicate that states the speaker's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q7.kobun.why: The phrase 大学のコンピューター forms a compound noun showing belonging. を connects the object with the verb りようしました, so the computer is the thing that was used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 使いました, the basic meaning is still 'used', but the expression is more common and less formal than りようしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を because Vietnamese does not require a separate marker for the object before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.vi: I was asked by the teacher to do some work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person affected by the request to do the work.
