default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who performs the requesting action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the work as the content of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: たのまれました is the past passive form of たのむ, showing that I was affected by the teacher's request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.why: In a passive sentence, the affected person is marked by は, the person who causes the action goes with に, and the requested content still goes with を. The verb たのまれました comes at the end to conclude the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active sentence is used, the teacher is the direct subject making the request and I am the person asked; the tone does not focus on my experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に in a passive sentence with the receiver, but here に indicates the person who causes the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q9.kobun.vi: My grandfather will leave the hospital tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that おじいさん is the person who performs the action being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: あす is a time adverb that indicates when the person will leave the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: たいいんします is a verb in the polite present form, used to talk about a plan or an event that will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q9.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and the time expression あす comes before the predicate to identify when the event will happen. たいいんします uses the polite present form because the sentence is about a future schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 帰ります, the meaning changes to 'return from the hospital', referring to the action of returning without clearly stating that treatment has finished and the person has been discharged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t110-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate します as present tense, but the present form in Japanese often also expresses a future plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q1.kobun.vi: Mr. Honda's house is this way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with おたく, creating the meaning “Mr. Honda's house.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that おたく is the topic whose location is identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q1.kobun.why: ほんださんの identifies who the house belongs to, and then おたくは makes it the topic. こちらです is a predicate showing the location or place identified in the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes that the house exists here, while こちらです has the nuance of pointing to or identifying a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate の as a possessive word placed after the noun; in Japanese, the possessive noun comes before the main noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q14.kobun.vi: I checked the luggage for the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the trip with the luggage, creating a noun phrase that modifies another noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the luggage as the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: This borrowed verb, CHECK, is in the polite past form and shows that the checking action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q14.kobun.why: The phrase りょこうのにもつ forms one noun meaning “the luggage for the trip.” This phrase is the object marked by を before the verb チェックしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If しらべました is used, the nuance is learning about or checking something carefully by examining it, while チェックしました suggests checking against a list or confirming something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q14.kobun.tip: Do not omit の between りょこう and にもつ, because の shows that the luggage belongs to or is related to the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective 新しい modifies the noun コート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that is said to be necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ひつようです serves as the predicate and politely expresses necessity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q15.kobun.why: The phrase 新しい コート forms the noun phrase “new coat,” and then が marks the thing considered necessary. ひつようです is the predicate at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with いる, the sentence still says that a coat is needed, but it uses a verb instead of a noun expressing necessity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use を before ひつようです; a necessary thing usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q16.kobun.vi: The sound of the telephone is very strange.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 電話 with おと and shows that the sound belongs to the telephone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the sound being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: おかしいです is an adjective predicate describing an unusual state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q16.kobun.why: 電話の おと is a noun phrase consisting of an owner and something belonging to it. おとが is the subject of the comment, while おかしいです comes at the end to state its characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If へんな おと is used, the meaning is still “the sound is strange,” but the expression is more direct and へんな modifies おと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q16.kobun.tip: In a possessive structure, の is placed between two nouns; do not put の after おと when you want to say that the sound is the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.vi: I will review the difficult parts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: むずかしい modifies ところ and identifies the difficult parts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects ところ with ふくしゅう, creating the relationship “review that part.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content being reviewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the predicate and combines with ふくしゅう to create the meaning “review.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.why: むずかしい ところ creates the phrase “difficult part,” and then の connects this phrase with ふくしゅう. ふくしゅうを します is a noun + する combination, in which を marks the action being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still to study again, but it emphasizes the act of studying rather than the noun “review.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q17.kobun.tip: With an activity noun such as ふくしゅう, します can be used; ふくしゅう is not conjugated as a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.vi: My little younger brother is being worried about by our mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: 小さい modifies おとうと and identifies the younger brother who is small in age.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes おとうと the topic of the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に identifies the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: されて is the passive form of しんぱいする in the て form, used to connect with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses an ongoing state: the younger brother is being worried about by his mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.why: おとうとは is the topic affected by the action, while 母に identifies the person causing the worrying. The passive form しんぱいされている expresses the state of the younger brother receiving his mother's concern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: In this active sentence, the mother is the person who is worrying, and the younger brother is the person she is worried about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q18.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person performing the action usually goes with に, while the affected person is made the topic with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q19.kobun.vi: I explained the meaning of the word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects ことば with いみ and shows that the meaning belongs to that word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the content being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: せつめいしました is the polite past form and shows that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q19.kobun.why: ことばの いみ is the noun phrase “the meaning of the word.” This phrase is the object with を, while せつめいしました comes at the end to state the completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 教える is used, the sentence focuses more on teaching or giving information; せつめいする emphasizes presenting or explaining something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q19.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ことばのいみ with ことばをいみ; の connects two nouns in a possessive relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q2.kobun.vi: I cleaned up inside the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects つくえ with 中 and identifies the inside as belonging to the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the area that was cleaned up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q2.kobun.why: つくえの中 forms a noun phrase meaning “the inside of the desk.” This phrase goes with を because it directly receives the action かたづける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 掃除する, the meaning is cleaning or sweeping, without emphasizing arranging objects as かたづける does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q2.kobun.tip: English speakers may omit の when describing an inside location, but つくえの中 is needed to express “inside the desk.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.vi: The bus going to the harbor is not crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle へ shows the direction in which the bus is going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 行く in the dictionary form comes before バス to modify the bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes バス the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: すいて is the て form of すく and connects with います to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses the current state that the bus is not crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.why: みなとへ 行く is a clause modifying バス and identifies which bus is meant. After the topic バスは, すいています describes the bus's current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If すくない is used, the sentence says that there are few passengers; すいている emphasizes that the space or vehicle is not crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q20.kobun.tip: すいています does not simply mean “few”; it describes an uncrowded state, opposite to こんでいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q21.kobun.vi: The flowers in this park are very beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun こうえん that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects こうえん with はな, showing that the flower belongs to the park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes はな the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q21.kobun.why: The phrases この and こうえんの modify はな, respectively. は marks the topic, while the adjective うつくしい is the predicate describing that topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence still means beautiful, but it uses the adjective な, which is more common in everyday use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse うつくしい and きれい because both mean “beautiful,” but うつくしい usually has a more formal or emotional tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q22.kobun.vi: I accidentally dropped my bicycle key.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects じてんしゃ with かぎ, showing that the key belongs to the bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks かぎ as the object that was dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The form Vてしまいました describes an action that has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q22.kobun.why: The possessive phrase じてんしゃの comes before the noun かぎ. かぎを is the object of おとす, while てしまいました emphasizes that the dropping happened and that the speaker regrets it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, it means losing something in general and does not specifically show that the key was dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate てしまう as only “already,” but this pattern often also expresses regret or an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.vi: My father is someone who does not apologize very often.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 父 the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり is used with a negative form to express a low degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause あやまらない comes before and modifies 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 人です is the predicate, identifying what kind of person 父 is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.why: After the topic 父は, the phrase あまりあやまらない modifies 人. The negative form あやまらない combines with あまり to say that the act of apologizing happens very rarely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the negative meaning becomes stronger, close to “does not apologize at all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use あまり with an affirmative sentence to mean “very much”; this pattern usually goes with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.vi: At least 50 people came to yesterday’s party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.sk: Nの + Nには + Quantity以上 + Vていました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with パーティー, identifying the party as the one held yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: には indicates the context or place being discussed, while は adds a topic-setting nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ５０人以上 is the number of people who are the subject of 来ていました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ていました describes a state of having arrived or being present at the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.why: きのうの modifies パーティー, while には sets the party as the context. The quantity phrase ５０人以上 comes before 来ていました to state the number of people who came.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes 50 people or fewer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only says about 50 people, without confirming that there were at least 50.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake 以上 for “more than,” but it includes the number before it, so ５０人以上 means 50 people or more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q25.kobun.vi: This animal is rarely seen in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes このどうぶつ the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the location range, while は emphasizes a contrast within Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q25.kobun.why: このどうぶつは is the main topic, while 日本では limits the place being discussed. The adjective めずらしい is the predicate, showing how common the animal is in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is removed, the sentence only states the place and loses the contrast or limited-scope nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out は in では, but は emphasizes “in Japan,” which may imply that other places are not necessarily the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Ron is the topic of the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past passive form of しょうたいする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q3.kobun.why: The person affected is placed before は, while the person who performs the action goes with に. しょうたいする changes to the passive form to show that Ron is the person who was invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, Ron is the person inviting someone else, not the person being invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in a passive sentence with を; に marks the person who performs the action here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q3.kobun.cn: Vれる・Vられる + ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.vi: I am preparing food for the party now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 今において indicates the time when the action is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects パーティー with りょうり to modify the food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: て形 connects よういする with います to create the pattern for an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ています describes an action that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.why: The object りょうりを comes before the verb. よういして connects with います, forming しています to express that the preparation is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If よういします is used, it only states the action of preparing and does not emphasize that it is happening right now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit the particle を or use よういします when they want to express an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.vi: As the number of cars increased, this road became dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the factor whose quantity changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the increase in cars with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: この modifies the noun 道 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: は marks the road as the topic of the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the new state after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました expresses a change to a new state in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.why: The clause 車がふえて gives the reason and connects it to the result clause with て. With an adjective ending in な, add に before なる to express what something becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If the adjective is an adjective ending in い, change い to く before なる, for example あぶなくなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use きけんです, it only describes the road as dangerous and does not stress the change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use きけんくなる; with an adjective ending in な, you must use きけんになる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies レポート that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the report as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: すばらしい is an adjective ending in い and combines with です to form a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q6.kobun.why: このレポート forms a noun phrase, and then は makes this phrase the topic. すばらしいです is the predicate that directly comments on the quality of the report.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with an adjective ending in な, you need the form Aなです, not the conjugation used for an adjective ending in い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add な after すばらしい; an adjective ending in い comes directly before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.vi: Mr. Yang was hospitalized in April.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time に ＋ Nする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Mr. Yang as the person who underwent hospitalization.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the action occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of にゅういんする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.why: The subject goes with は, the time of the action goes with に, and the verb にゅういんしました ends the sentence and shows that the event was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes entering the hospital, while にゅういんしました describes hospitalization as a medical event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate and use に as a preposition for a place, but in this sentence に indicates the time, ４月.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Mr. Ali as the person affected by the greeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past passive form of あいさつする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q8.kobun.why: The sentence makes the person who was greeted the topic, so アリさん goes with は. The person who greets goes with に, while あいさつする changes to the passive form to show that Ali received the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active sentence is used, Machida is the person who performs the greeting, while Ali is the person being greeted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the person who greets with は in a passive sentence; here, the affected person, アリさん, is the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q8.kobun.cn: Vれる・Vられる ＋ ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who enters school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place or destination of entering school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and expresses a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q9.kobun.why: The subject comes before が, and the school comes before に, followed by the verb for entering school. This order makes clear who entered school and where.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入る is used, it means to enter or go inside, without emphasizing the school-entry procedure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q9.kobun.tip: に should not be used as the object; with 入学する, に indicates the school or place entered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.vi: That restaurant is not tasty at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes あの店 the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ちっとも goes with a negative predicate to stress that something is completely not the case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: おいしい changes to おいしくない to form the negative form of an adjective ending in い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.why: あの店は is the topic, and ちっとも modifies the negative predicate to add emphasis. おいしくないです is a negative comment about the quality of the food or drinks at the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the degree is weaker and means that something is not very tasty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.tip: ちっとも must be used with a negative form; it is not used directly with おいしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q1.kobun.cn: ちっとも ＋ Vない／Aいくない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.vi: Please do not smoke on the platform.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place, while の connects the place phrase to the noun おたばこ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes smoking on the platform the topic of the reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ご～ください is a polite request; ごえんりょ means please refrain from or avoid doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.why: The phrase ホームでの sets the place for おたばこ. The topic is marked by は, and the polite request comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence becomes a clearer and more direct prohibition rather than a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is used instead, the sentence asks someone not to perform a specific action, while ごえんりょください sounds more formal and indirect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ごえんりょください as only “must not,” which loses the polite request meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.vi: When you call the pizza shop, they will come within 30 minutes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the target or place receiving the phone call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition or time with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time limit by which the arrival must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 来てくれます expresses that another person does something beneficial for the speaker or someone concerned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.why: The place receiving the call goes with に. The clause 電話すると states the condition leading to the result, while ３０分いないに sets the time limit for the action 来てくれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the condition “after calling, ...,” while と emphasizes a result that usually happens automatically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもらえます is used instead, the sentence changes to asking about or describing receiving help from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand と as only “and,” but in this sentence it connects a condition with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形＋と; Vて＋くれる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle は marks this river as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending い forms the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q12.kobun.why: The topic 川は comes first. Then とても modifies the adjective あさい. The adjective comes at the end of the sentence as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place とても after the adjective, following Vietnamese word order, but it usually comes before the word it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.vi: Please tell me why you missed school yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nを ＋ Vた ＋ わけを ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the place or object connected to the action of missing school in 学校を休む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The past form 休んだ comes before わけ to modify the reason being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: わけ means reason, while を marks what the speaker asks the listener to explain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: てください makes a polite request to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.why: きのう identifies the time, while the clause 学校を休んだ comes before わけ to clarify which reason is being asked about. わけを is the object of おしえてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If わけ is replaced with 理由, the meaning is still “reason,” but the expression is more direct and neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If this question is used, the focus is on directly asking “why,” rather than asking the listener to explain the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the modifying clause after わけ, following Vietnamese word order, but Japanese requires 休んだ to come before わけ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ わけ; Vて＋ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.vi: I was reprimanded by my teacher for being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.sk: Vて ＋ N に ＋ passive verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: Form て connects the action of being late with what happened afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performed the reprimanding action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past form of the passive voice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.why: The clause ちこくして comes first to state the circumstances that led to the reprimand. に marks the person who performed the action in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the cause is stated more clearly, with the meaning “because I was late.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after 先生, but this passive sentence uses に to indicate the person who gave the reprimand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that changes into an available state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: あきました is an intransitive verb that describes something becoming available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q15.kobun.why: Because あく is an intransitive verb, the object that changes state goes with が. The verb is in the polite past form to describe a state that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the restroom is presented as the topic or as a contrast, instead of emphasizing the object that has just changed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use を with あく when meaning “open by itself” or “become available”; use が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が emphasizes the object identified as the venue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun コンサート with the following noun, creating the meaning “the concert venue.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun phrase before です functions as the predicate to identify what これ is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q16.kobun.why: これが is used to identify a specific object. コンサートのかいじょう is a noun phrase in which の shows the modifying relationship between two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the sentence only presents this as the topic; the identifying emphasis of が is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate の as “of” in every case, but here it connects two nouns to form a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.vi: My older sister is good at tennis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the older sister as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object toward which ability or strength is directed in the pattern とくいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.ch.2.vi: good at; have a strength in
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: とくい is an な adjective, used with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.why: あねは introduces the person being described, while テニスが indicates the field in which that person has a strength. The adjective な comes before です to end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with じょうず, the sentence emphasizes being skilled at playing tennis; とくい also suggests a personal strength or something one feels confident about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q17.kobun.tip: The pattern とくいです usually goes with が, not を, to mark a subject or activity in which someone has a strength.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q18.kobun.vi: I go home and then review.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the destination of the action of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: かえって is the て form of かえる, used to connect returning home with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the します form ends the sentence and describes the action of reviewing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q18.kobun.why: いえに indicates the destination. Then the て form connects the two actions in sequence. Only the final action uses the polite form します to end the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is used, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker must finish returning home before reviewing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q18.kobun.tip: The て form in the middle of the sentence does not have a past meaning; here, it is only used to connect two consecutive actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.vi: I am doing research on apples.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person doing the research.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects りんご with けんきゅう to indicate the content of the research.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the activity being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the polite ている form, describing an activity in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.why: りんごのけんきゅう forms a noun phrase showing the content of the research. This phrase goes with を, while しています shows that the activity is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this expression is used, the sentence focuses more on examining or checking apples than on research as a field.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q19.kobun.tip: It is important to distinguish りんごのけんきゅうをしています from りんごをしています; の connects the content with the noun けんきゅう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.vi: Stop bullying people who are weaker than you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the object of the bullying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb いじめる combines with の to turn it into a noun, while は makes it the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: やめなさい is a mild request or command used to tell someone to stop an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.why: The phrase いじめるのは turns the whole action “bullying people who are weaker” into the topic. やめなさい comes at the end of the sentence to give a direct reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the phrase becomes the subject of a comment and no longer has the topic or emphasis expressed in the original sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means “must not bully” and expresses a clearer prohibition than a request to stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit の when they want to turn a whole verb clause into a noun before は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.vi: That person's voice is beautiful, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あの人 with こえ and shows that the voice belongs to that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes こえ the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate and describes the voice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね is used at the end of a sentence to confirm something or seek agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.why: The phrase あの人のこえ comes first to identify the voice being discussed. After the topic こえは, the adjective うつくしい acts as the predicate, and ですね adds a tone of agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence still means beautiful, but the expression is more common and has a broader meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the praise becomes stronger, closer to “wonderful.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may translate うつくしい as only beautiful, but this word often suggests an elegant or highly aesthetic kind of beauty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes these shoes the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: かわいている describes the current state of the shoes after they have dried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q21.kobun.why: このくつは is the topic, while かわいています is the state described about the shoes. The form ています here emphasizes the current state, not only an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to the shoes being wet or having become wet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes that the shoes have dried, meaning that the change of state has just been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may think every form of ています means that someone is doing something, but with verbs showing a change of state, it usually refers to an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this river the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: きけんです is the adjective predicate な and states how safe the river is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q22.kobun.why: After naming a place or thing with この川は, the sentence uses the adjective な きけん to give an evaluation. です comes after the adjective な to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the basic meaning does not change, but this is a more natural and common expression in conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to “this river is safe.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q22.kobun.tip: English learners may mistake きけん for a verb, but it is an adjective な, so it usually goes with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this restaurant the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: こんでいる describes the state of having many people in the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q23.kobun.why: The restaurant is made the topic with は, and then こんでいます describes its current state. The form ています is suitable because the crowdedness is an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to the restaurant being empty or not crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence directly says that there are many people instead of using a verb that describes a crowded state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q23.kobun.tip: English learners may translate こんでいます as “be packed together,” but in a sentence about a restaurant, the natural meaning is “be crowded.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.vi: I do not understand Japanese at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.sk: N が + degree adverb + Vません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is understood or not understood in sentence わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: ちっとも modifies わかりません and emphasizes the degree of not understanding at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: わかりません is the negative predicate and shows that the speaker does not understand Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.why: In the pattern わかる, the thing understood usually goes with が, so 日本語が is the object of understanding. ちっとも comes before the negative predicate to create the meaning “not at all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it also means “not at all,” but the tone is more neutral and common.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the degree becomes weaker: “do not understand very well,” not “do not understand at all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q24.kobun.tip: English learners may use を with わかる because of habits from English, but the object of わかる usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.vi: After looking at the test, I was disappointed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the test as the object being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 見て uses form て to connect the action of looking with the feeling that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: がっかりしました is the main predicate and expresses the speaker's disappointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.why: テストを is the object of the action 見る. Form て connects an earlier action with a later feeling, so the natural order is to look at the test and then feel disappointed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence focuses more on regret or something being unfortunate, which is milder than the disappointment expressed by がっかりしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to being surprised when looking at the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may understand form て here as “and,” but it also shows that looking at the test happened before the disappointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かれ with 話 to show possession or content, while は marks the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the thing that appears in large numbers in those words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 多い acts as the predicate, while です makes the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q3.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to make “his words” the scope of the comment, and then uses が to show the content that appears often within that scope. 多い is an adjective describing quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to this pattern, the sentence emphasizes the action of “telling many lies” instead of the content of the words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may put を before 多い, but a quantity described by 多い usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.vi: If there is a problem, please tell me directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle が marks the subject of the state ある in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: あったら is the conditional form たら of ある, connecting the condition to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ちょくせつ modifies the action of speaking and shows how it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle に indicates the person who receives the message.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: Use 言ってください in the form て together with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.why: The conditional clause 問題があったら comes first to state the situation, followed by the manner ちょくせつ and the person concerned わたしに. The phrase 言ってください ends the sentence with a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ば gives the sentence a more general and slightly more formal conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: へ only points toward the listener, while に emphasizes the person who directly receives the words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place に after わたし, but forget that に here refers to the person being spoken to, not a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.vi: It is impossible to finish this by tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: あした refers only to the point in time used as the reference for a deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: までに refers only to the deadline by which an action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the action やる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: やる combines with の to turn the action into a noun, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: むりです functions as the predicate and describes something beyond one's ability or impossible to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.why: The deadline phrase あしたまでに comes before the action to show when it must be completed. やるのは turns the action into the topic, and then むりです gives the judgment that it cannot be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: こと also turns an action into a noun, but this expression is usually more objective and stiffer than のは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern directly says “cannot do it” and focuses more on the doer's ability than on judging the task to be impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse までに with まで; までに is the deadline, while まで only refers to a period that continues up to that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ のは ＋ Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.vi: Japanese cars are exported all over the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with 車 to show the origin or type of car, while は makes Japanese cars the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に refers to the place or area to which the cars are exported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: されています is the passive form combined with ています, expressing a state or an action that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.why: The topic is Japanese cars, while せかいじゅうに states the destination area of the export. The passive form is used because the cars receive the action of being exported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active form is used, the sentence emphasizes the person or organization exporting the cars instead of emphasizing that the cars are exported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: へ emphasizes direction toward the whole world, while に is suitable for a place or area toward which an action is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the active form when they want to say “are exported”; remember that the affected object usually becomes the topic with は in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q6.kobun.cn: N ＋ される（受身）＋ ている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.vi: Communicating in a foreign language is difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the means or language used during a conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: かいわする combines with の to turn the action into a noun, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: むずかしいです is an adjective predicate that evaluates the action mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.why: 外国語で comes before the verb to show the language used in the conversation. The whole phrase かいわするのは is turned into a noun and made the topic of the comment むずかしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が makes having a conversation the direct subject of the adjective, with less of a topic-setting meaning than は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes using a foreign language to speak, while で expresses the language or means more briefly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 外国語, but when indicating the language or means used to perform an action, they need to use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ のは ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes this pamphlet the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: お～ください is a polite way to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q8.kobun.why: The topic is placed first with は, followed by the part that modifies how to take it. The final phrase uses a polite request pattern to guide the reader's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence is still a request, but the tone is more ordinary and does not use the honorific form お～ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use Vてください directly in every situation without noticing that お～ください is more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.vi: I think Japan is indeed easy to live in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes Japan the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.ch.2.vi: that it is easy to live in
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content of the thought being quoted; すみやすい is the form that connects to やすい, meaning easy to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.cn: Vます形 omits ます ＋ やすい; V普通形 ＋ と ＋ 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.why: The comment about Japan is introduced first with は. The content of the comment comes before と, followed by the verb おもいます, so と connects the whole clause being thought about to the main verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: When used directly after an adjective or verb, this pattern only states an opinion; here すみやすい also contains the meaning of being easy to live in through やすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with そうです, the sentence changes from the speaker's opinion to an appearance or prediction that the place seems easy to live in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t112-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that やすい connects to the verb stem without ます, not to the complete ます form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.vi: My father is opposed to my studying abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes my father the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects two nouns and shows that the study abroad belongs to me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the object toward which the opposition is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: しています expresses a state in which the opposition continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.why: は identifies the person with the attitude, の identifies whose study abroad it is, and に marks the object being opposed. はんたいする combines with ています to express an ongoing state of opposition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence states a condition or opinion of opposition without emphasizing an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence focuses more on an act or decision to oppose at a particular time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 反対する, but the correct pattern is N に反対する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person who has the belief as わたし.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects かれ with 話 and shows that the words belong to him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks 話 as the object of the verb しんじる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: しんじています uses the form ている to express an ongoing state of belief.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.why: The phrase かれの話を forms the complete object of しんじています. The form ている is suitable because belief is an ongoing state, not just an action that happens briefly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence changes to mean that I think something is true, emphasizing the speaker's judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 信じました is used, the sentence only states that the person believed something at a certain time or during a period in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の in かれの話 or use は instead of を before the object of 信じる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this table the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: じょうぶ is an な adjective used as the predicate, combined with です to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q11.kobun.why: このテーブルは identifies the object being discussed. じょうぶです appears at the end of the sentence to state the table's quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 強いです, the sentence emphasizes strength or load-bearing ability, rather than directly describing sturdiness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add な before です, but the な adjective drops な when it appears at the end of a sentence with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q12.kobun.vi: It is almost time for a break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: そろそろ is an adverb that signals that the right time is approaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: きゅうけいしましょう uses the polite volitional form of きゅうけいする to invite or suggest taking a break together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q12.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q12.kobun.why: そろそろ comes before the verb to show that the break time is near. ましょう at the end of the sentence turns the suggestion into an invitation to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ください, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to take a break, without the meaning of doing it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ましょう as only an order, but this pattern usually has the meaning of inviting or suggesting that people do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that creates the liking expressed by すきです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです expresses a state of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q13.kobun.why: The topic comes before は, while the liked object goes with が. すきです is the predicate that expresses liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with すきです, but this pattern usually uses N が すきです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あなた with the noun ゆめ to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes ゆめ the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 何 asks about unknown information, while ですか creates a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q14.kobun.why: あなたの modifies ゆめ, and then ゆめ is made the topic with は. 何 fills the position where the missing information goes and combines with ですか to ask about identity or content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q14.kobun.tip: Do not put は after あなたの; は attaches to the main noun ゆめ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q15.kobun.vi: On days off, I usually go somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: 休みの日は states the general time or situation of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: たいてい modifies 出かけます and shows frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: へ marks an unspecified direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 出かけます is the main verb and receives the direction of movement from どこかへ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q15.kobun.why: The time phrase is moved to the beginning and marked with は. どこかへ indicates movement toward an unspecified place, while たいてい comes before the verb to modify its frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q15.kobun.tip: へ in this sentence indicates direction, not the place where the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: うつくしい comes before 人 to modify that noun directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends the noun sentence and confirms the topic's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q16.kobun.why: きむらさんは is the topic, followed by うつくしい modifying 人. The whole phrase うつくしい人です forms a noun predicate meaning a beautiful person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q16.kobun.tip: The い-ending adjective comes directly before the noun, without adding な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q17.kobun.vi: After reading the letter, I was very surprised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks てがみ as the object being read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 読んで is the て form of 読む, used to connect the action of reading with the event that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: びっくりしました is the main predicate and describes the feeling that occurred after the earlier action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q17.kobun.why: てがみを is the object of 読む. The verb in the て form connects the earlier action with the result or feeling stated in the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use the past form た to connect clauses directly in this pattern; use the て form before the comma.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q18.kobun.vi: The old man next door has passed away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with the noun that follows to modify the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects いえ with おじいさん, forming a phrase for the person belonging to the neighboring house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person as the subject of the event of passing away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: なくなりました is a polite predicate that uses a softer expression for death.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q18.kobun.why: となりのいえの creates a chain of modifiers from left to right for おじいさん. おじいさんが is the subject, while なくなりました is the predicate describing an event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q18.kobun.tip: なくなりました, when referring to a person, is more polite and softer than 死にました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: 言いました is the predicate, using the polite past form of 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q19.kobun.why: The object おれいを comes before the verb 言いました. This structure expresses saying a specific word or piece of content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the exact words spoken, such as a quotation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget を before the verb 言う when they want to say what they said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects a noun アイデア with a polite comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ね。 shows agreement or asks the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q2.kobun.why: いい comes before アイデア to modify the noun. です makes the expression polite, while ね adds a shared-comment feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: When using よ, the speaker emphasizes the information they give rather than seeking agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: When using でしょう, the sentence sounds more tentative, like a guess or a soft confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate ね。 as a required word; it mainly adds a conversational nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.vi: My father gave me a novel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of giving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: くれました describes another person doing something helpful or giving something to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.why: 父が is the giver, しょうせつを is the thing given, and くれました is the predicate showing that the giving is directed toward the speaker. Therefore, the receiver can be omitted when the context makes it clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the subject is the receiver, and に refers to the person who gave the item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: With あげました, the action of giving is viewed from the giver's side, without emphasizing that the speaker is the receiver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q20.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may confuse が and に because Vietnamese often combines the giver and receiver in one sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q21.kobun.vi: I will practice as hard as I can.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action of practicing and shows the degree and attitude of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: れんしゅうします is the predicate and uses the polite present or future form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q21.kobun.why: いっしょうけんめい comes before the verb to modify how the practice is done. The predicate is in the polite ます form, so it can refer to a present action or a future plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Using に after 一生懸命 still expresses doing one's best, but it emphasizes the adverb's role more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a phrase showing manner after the verb, while Japanese usually places it before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.vi: I asked my senior about school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person being asked or the target of the asking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 学校の modifies こと, creating the meaning “about school.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns the content being asked about into a noun, while を marks that content as the object of うかがいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: うかがいました is the humble form of 聞きました when asking another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, while the content being asked about goes with を. 学校の comes before こと to modify it and narrow the content to matters about school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 聞きました, the basic meaning is still “ask,” but the humble and polite nuance is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means asking about N, but it states the topic directly instead of using こと to turn the content into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for both the person asked and the content asked about, but the content usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.vi: When I was a child, I liked swimming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 子どもの modifies とき and identifies the time as when the person was a child.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates a point or period in time and comes after the modifying phrase 子どもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object of liking in the structure 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: すきでした is the past polite form of the な adjective predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.why: The time phrase 子どものとき is placed at the beginning to set the time background. In the pattern 好きです, the thing someone likes goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If using ころ, the sentence refers to the period around a stage of life, with a broader and less definite nuance than とき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This form is more casual because it drops the polite ending でした, but the basic past meaning does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say すいえいをすきでした, but 好きです uses が to mark the thing that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q23.kobun.cn: Nの・V普通形・Aい ＋ とき; Aな・Nの ＋ とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: でも combines with question words to expand the range, meaning “everyone” or “anyone.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary form りようする comes before こと to modify it and turn the action of using into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: こと nominalizes the action, while が marks that action as something that can be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: できます completes the potential pattern Vことができる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.why: りようすること turns the action of using into something that can be done, and then できます expresses ability. だれでも is placed at the beginning to say that there is no limit on who can use it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence emphasizes that the particular action is possible, often in contrast with another action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only says that someone can use it; it does not mean that everyone can use it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use をできます, but the correct pattern is V辞書形＋ことができます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q24.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことができる; 疑問詞＋でも
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.vi: That store is open for business every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ Nをするている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: This word modifies 店 and identifies the store being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the store as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: A time phrase showing that the activity happens every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the ている form of する and describes a continuing state or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.why: 店は places the topic first, and then 每日 adds the time of the activity. 営業しています describes business activity that continues regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the store is open, not its business activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.tip: Do not understand ています as always referring to an action happening right when the speaker talks; here it also describes a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q25.kobun.cn: Nをする: N ＋ を ＋ する; Vている: Vて形 ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.vi: When you have trouble, please call me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The past-form verb modifies とき, creating the meaning “when you have trouble.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates a time or condition, while は makes this situation the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb 電話する with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください expresses a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.why: こまった modifies とき to state a specific situation. After stating the condition with ときは, the verb 電話してください gives the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If using こまっている, the sentence emphasizes the state of being in trouble at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If using こまったら, the sentence has a clearer conditional nuance: if you have trouble, please call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ときに in this sentence, but は makes the whole situation the topic of the advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.tokens.0.m: to have trouble; to be confused
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q3.kobun.cn: Vた形・V辞書形・Nの + ときは; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before the noun to describe the movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: でした is the polite past form of です, used to comment on a movie that has been watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q4.kobun.why: すばらしい comes before えいが to describe the movie. でした shows that this comment refers to a movie watched in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If です is used, the comment has a present meaning or does not stress when the movie was watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If だった is used, the sentence is more casual because the polite form is omitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q4.kobun.tip: Do not add の between the adjective い and the noun; say すばらしいえいが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の shows that the hobby belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the hobby as the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: どくしょ is a noun meaning the activity of reading books. It combines with です to form the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q5.kobun.why: わたしの identifies the owner, しゅみは states the topic, and どくしょです answers what that hobby is. This structure uses a noun to define or introduce a topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes my enjoyment of reading books, rather than defining what the hobby is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence expresses the action of reading books instead of the noun どくしょ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を after しゅみ in this definition pattern; use は to state the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.vi: At this company, I have no job that I dislike.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that the person being discussed is me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the work or state mentioned occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before the noun to describe the job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the object that exists or does not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります, expressing that something does not exist or is not present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.why: このかいしゃで limits the scope to this company. いやな modifies しごと, while が combines with ありません to say that no such job exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning changes to having a job that is not unpleasant or disliked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence emphasizes or contrasts the specific group of jobs that are disliked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for a workplace, but the place where an action or state occurs uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the thing that is in a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb こわれる is in the polite past form and describes the bicycle entering a broken state by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q7.kobun.why: The noun for the thing comes before が to be the subject of the state. The verb こわれる describes the thing as broken, without emphasizing who caused the damage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is that someone broke the bicycle, emphasizing the person who caused the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with こわれる, but こわれる usually goes with が because the thing is the subject of the broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.vi: We held a party with many people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the group of people performing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks パーティー as the object of holding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する, forming パーティーをする, which means to hold a party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.why: おおぜいで comes first to state the number of people taking part in the action. パーティーをする is a verb phrase, in which を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to many people coming to the place where the party is held, without emphasizing that they are holding it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate で as “at,” but in this sentence で indicates the group of people doing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q8.kobun.cn: N + で + N + を + する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes そふ the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective 元気 and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 元気 is an な adjective used as the predicate, and it combines with です to form the polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q9.kobun.why: The topic そふは is stated first, and then とても modifies the state 元気です. Because 元気 is an な adjective, です is used at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 元気な is placed before a noun, this pattern means a healthy or lively noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may see 元気 as an い adjective, but when it is used as a predicate, 元気です is needed, not 元気いです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t113-q9.kobun.cn: N は + とても + Aな です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q1.kobun.vi: This computer is made in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This word modifies パソコン and refers to the computer being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states that the computer is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase is the predicate and states where the computer was made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q1.kobun.why: このパソコンは introduces the object, while にほんせいです gives information about its origin. The sentence pattern has the topic は followed by descriptive information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to a computer produced in Japan, focusing on the act of production.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate 製 as a separate verb; it is an element showing that a product was made or produced in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.vi: I have already prepared the things to take on the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the purpose or context in which the things will be taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause もって行く modifies もの, while は makes the whole phrase the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: もう modifies the action and shows that the preparation was completed before now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb しました describes the completed act of preparing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.why: The clause もって行く comes before もの to identify the things that will be taken. The phrase ものは is the topic, while よういしました is the main predicate about the preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 持って行ったもの is used, it refers only to things taken in the past, not things planned to be taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q10.kobun.tip: A clause modifying a noun must come before the noun, not after it as in the familiar Vietnamese pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.vi: Please do not make noise inside the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 電車 with 中 to indicate the inside of the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where making noise must not be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ないで connects the negative form of the verb with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.why: 電車の中で identifies the place of the action. さわがないでください uses the negative form ないで combined with ください to ask the listener not to make noise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If さわらないでください is used, it means “please do not touch,” which is different from not making noise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern has the meaning of asking someone to try to keep from making noise, so it is longer and more indirect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use ないください; change the verb to the ない form and then add でください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q11.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は indicates the person who performs the action of apologizing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the person who receives the apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q12.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, and the object of the apology uses に. The verb あやまる changes to あやまりました to describe an action that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means speaking to a friend and does not necessarily imply an apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the person who receives the apology; the target of あやまる uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q13.kobun.vi: While traveling, my bag was stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase のとき indicates when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing affected in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb ぬすむ changes to the polite past passive form, describing the speaker having something stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the lost item and the passive action. The passive form highlights that the speaker was affected by the act of stealing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is broader: something was taken or lost, without clearly saying that it was stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q13.kobun.tip: When saying that someone else took your belongings, do not use only the active form ぬすみました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q14.kobun.vi: I did not make it to the appointment on time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the time by which one must arrive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q14.kobun.ch.1.vi: did not make it on time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 間にあう means to make it in time; its past negative form means that the person did not make it on time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q14.kobun.why: The time that must be met uses に and comes before the verb. The past negative form shows that making it on time did not happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the focus is on being late for the appointment, while 間にあわない emphasizes not meeting the deadline.
