default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q14.kobun.tip: 間に合う is a fixed phrase containing に, so do not omit に when saying that someone made it or did not make it on time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q15.kobun.vi: I invited Mr. Yoshida to our party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person who is invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place or event to which the invited person is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb さそう is in the polite past form and describes an invitation that was given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q15.kobun.why: The invited person uses を, while the place or event they are invited to uses に. These two parts come before the verb さそう to create the structure for inviting someone somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 招待する is used instead, the meaning is still to invite, but the tone is more formal and official than さそう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the invited person in this pattern; the invited person uses を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q16.kobun.vi: This school is very active in sports.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は indicates the school being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the field that is described as highly active.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: さかん is a な adjective. It forms the predicate with です to say that a field is very active.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q16.kobun.why: The topic is the school, while が marks the field being described. The pattern Nがさかんです describes activity or a movement in that field as highly developed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that many people play sports. It does not directly comment on how active the sports movement is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q16.kobun.tip: さかん is a な adjective, so it uses です and is not conjugated like a い adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.vi: Before running, you must always warm up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The dictionary form of a verb comes before 前に to indicate that one action happens before another.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb modifies します and emphasizes that warming up is required or must not be forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks what is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the polite present form of する. It describes a habit or rule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.why: The action done first comes before 前に, and the main action comes after it. かならず emphasizes that warming up must always be done before running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the second action is done only after the first action, emphasizing the order in which they happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If かならず is replaced with いつも, the meaning is that the action is often or always done, but the sense of obligation is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q17.kobun.tip: Before 前に, use a verb in the dictionary form, not the て form or the past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q18.kobun.vi: It has started to get dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that is changing into a dark state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: くれてきました describes a change that gradually moves toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q18.kobun.why: 日が is the subject of the change, while くれてきました forms the predicate. The pattern てくる shows that darkness gradually appeared and is now noticeable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence more clearly emphasizes how a state changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate てくる as only showing a direction of movement, but here it describes a change moving toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a person with the following noun, creating the meaning of Mr. Tanaka's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object toward which the action of opposing is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: はんたいします is the main verb and is used with an object preceded by に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q19.kobun.why: たなかさんの modifies いけん, forming the noun phrase “Mr. Tanaka's opinion.” With はんたいします, the object of opposition is marked by に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that two opinions are different. It does not necessarily show opposition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use を before はんたいします; the object of this verb usually uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は indicates that the restaurant is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ていました describes a crowded state that existed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q2.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ いる; polite past: Vて形 ＋ いました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q2.kobun.why: レストランは is the topic, while こんでいました is the restaurant's state at a point in the past. The form ている is suitable for a crowded state, not only a temporary action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence can still indicate that a place was full or crowded, but the meaning is more general and does not directly use the verb こんでいる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q2.kobun.tip: With state verbs such as こむ, ている is usually understood as being in that state, not performing an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の limits テスト to the time period of today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes today's test the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: かんたん is an adjective な, so the polite past form uses でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q20.kobun.why: 今日の modifies テスト, and then は marks the whole phrase “today's test” as the topic. かんたん is an adjective な, so it ends in the past form with でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is still “easy,” but it uses the adjective い, so the past conjugation is different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q20.kobun.tip: The adjective な does not change into かんたんかった; its past form is かんたんでした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes a noun or adjective な into an adverb that modifies studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes studying as an action continuing in the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q21.kobun.why: ねっしんに modifies the way of studying, and 日本語を is the object of べんきょうします. The form ています shows that the studying is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the nuance emphasizes making one's best effort rather than an enthusiastic attitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q21.kobun.tip: Do not omit に after ねっしん when this word is used to modify a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.vi: I have experience working part-time at a restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work experience took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects アルバイト with けいけん, creating the phrase “part-time work experience.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks something that exists, namely part-time work experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: あります describes the existence or possession of experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.why: レストランで identifies the place where the experience exists, while アルバイトのけいけんが あります has a structure that states that the speaker has an experience. The speaker can be omitted because it is clear from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes having done an action before, rather than possessing experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q22.kobun.tip: With あります for expressing experience or an object that exists, a noun usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.vi: This Japanese novel has been translated into English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to point to a specific thing near the speaker or already being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の modifies しょうせつ, showing that the novel is in Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes this novel the topic of the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination or target language of the translation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: されました is the polite past passive form of ほんやくします, emphasizing that the book receives the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.why: この日本語のしょうせつ is a noun phrase in which the parts before it successively modify the head noun しょうせつ. The sentence uses the passive because the topic is the novel that was translated, while に indicates the target language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active pattern is used, the translator becomes the subject and the novel becomes the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q23.kobun.tip: When a passive sentence makes the affected thing the topic, that thing usually goes with は, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.vi: Among the people here, I know only Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the range used to compare or limit the objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 以外は states the part excluded from the range of people known and goes with a negative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: しりません is the negative predicate of 知る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.why: The range phrase comes first, and then は marks “except Tanaka” as the object being negated. Therefore, the whole sentence naturally means that the speaker knows only Tanaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with だけ directly expresses “only N,” with a clearer affirmative nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: しか goes with a negative and more strongly emphasizes that there is no other person or thing besides N.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that 以外は in this sentence must go with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.vi: Mr. Mori went on a business trip instead of Mr. Kimura.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: のかわりに indicates the person replaced or the action done instead of someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who performs the action of going on a business trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に combines with the noun 出張 to indicate the purpose or content of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.why: The person being replaced comes before のかわりに, and the person who actually acts goes with が. The purpose or activity being pursued is marked by に before 行きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used, it means doing something for N's benefit or purpose, not necessarily replacing N.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If といっしょに is used, it means going together with Kimura, not going instead of Kimura.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q25.kobun.tip: Do not confuse のかわりに with “together with”; this pattern emphasizes replacement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.sk: Adverb + N を + Vます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This adverb modifies the action しましょう, showing that the action is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks しょくじ as the content or object of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of する, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.why: いっしょに comes before the verb to add the manner of doing something together. しょくじを is the object of する, while しましょう comes at the end to create an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the invitation sounds softer and more like asking for the listener's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.tip: Do not omit the particle を after an activity noun such as しょくじ when using it with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q3.kobun.cn: Nをする: N + を + する; Vます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This word modifies レストラン and identifies a specific restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the restaurant as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The form ています describes the restaurant's current state of having few customers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q4.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ いる; polite form: Vて形 ＋ います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q4.kobun.why: このレストランは gives the place being described, while すいています gives that place's state. ている is used to show an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to “the restaurant is crowded.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q4.kobun.tip: すく in this sentence does not mean a general decrease in quantity. It only describes a place with few people or customers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.vi: I cut the vegetables into small pieces.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the vegetables as the object being cut.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverbial form of the adjective こまかい modifies きりました and shows how the cutting was done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: This is the main predicate. It describes a completed cutting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.why: やさいを is the object of the action, while こまかく comes before きりました to describe the result or manner of cutting. The adjective こまかい changes to the く form to modify the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes the vegetables' small size more than cutting them into detailed small pieces or crumbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い must change い to く to modify a verb; its basic form cannot be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q5.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ く ＋ V; Vます ＋ ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.vi: I hear that this city is safe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は gives the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: あんぜん is an な adjective, so だ is used before そうです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです at the end of the sentence shows information heard from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.why: The topic is first introduced with は, followed by the topic's safe state. そうです comes at the end to report heard information, so the adjective な needs だ before this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ようです, the sentence focuses on the speaker's judgment and does not necessarily report heard information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget だ after the な adjective or noun before そうです when expressing reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ そうです／Aな・N ＋ だそうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q7.kobun.vi: I threw away the old notebook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before a noun and modifies ノト.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing being thrown away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The ました verb form describes a completed and polite action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q7.kobun.why: 古い comes directly before ノト to describe the notebook. ノトを is the object, while すてました is the main action performed on that object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入れました is used, it means putting something into a place and no longer directly means throwing it away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the affected object; the thing being thrown away must use を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.vi: In large cities, transportation is convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い modifies the following noun まち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the large city the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing described as convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: べんり is an な adjective, and です is used to end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.why: 大きい modifies まち, and then まちは makes the city the topic. In the comment, こうつうが is the subject of the quality べんりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If まちのこうつうは is used, the focus shifts to the city's transportation itself, not the large city.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は for both まち and こうつう; in this sentence, まちは is the topic, while こうつうが is the subject of the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.vi: The next bus leaves at 3 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time に ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the next bus the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the bus leaves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite します verb form describes the bus's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.why: The bus is introduced with は. The time ３時に comes before the verb to specify when the departure occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ３時ごろ is used, it means around 3 o'clock and does not specify the exact time as ３時に does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t114-q9.kobun.tip: に is used for a specific time; に should not be omitted when saying what time an action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.vi: Mr. Kimura has recovered from his illness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject whose condition has recovered or improved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: なおりました is the polite past form of なおる, an intransitive verb showing a recovered state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.why: The person being discussed uses は, while 病気が is the subject whose state changes. Because なおる is an intransitive verb, the illness recovers by itself; do not use を for 病気.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern says that the person's health has improved, while なおりました emphasizes that the illness has been cured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Using を and なおす means that someone treated the illness or made it go away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 病気, but なおる is an intransitive verb, so が is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.vi: Recently, this city's population has increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies まち and identifies the city being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes まち the topic of the comment about the population.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: さいきん modifies the whole event and gives the time when the population increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks じんこう as the subject that increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ふえました is the main predicate and describes an increase that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.why: まちは gives the scope being discussed, while じんこうが is the direct subject of the verb ふえました. さいきん is placed before the subject to add a time reference for the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, it emphasizes that many people began living there, not only the result of an increased population.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は after じんこう, but が is more suitable because the population is the direct subject of ふえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka asked Mr. Suzuki, “What would you like to have?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は shows the person who performs the asking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content being asked about as food or drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.ch.3.vi: what would you like to have
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the entire sentence in quotation marks as quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.why: The person asking uses は, the person being asked uses に, and the question is placed in quotation marks and connected to the verb きく with と. 何を is the object of めしあがりますか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～か聞く is used, the question becomes indirect and no longer keeps the spoken form in quotation marks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～について聞く is used, it means asking about a topic, not directly asking what the person would like to eat or drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake に for a place; in this sentence, に indicates the person receiving the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.vi: Mr. Takahashi is researching Japanese novels.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with the noun しょうせつ, creating a modifying noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being researched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb けんきゅうする with います to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている, expressing an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.why: The phrase 日本のしょうせつ is formed with の to modify the object しょうせつ. The verb けんきゅうして connects with います and shows that the activity is being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vました, it only says that the research was completed and does not emphasize that the action is ongoing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the joined form equivalent to けんきゅうして います, and both express the state of currently researching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ている simply as “did,” but in this sentence it describes an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.vi: I do not know how to drive a car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 車 with うんてん, creating the phrase “driving a car.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun うんてん with しかた and shows the way something is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what the speaker does not know.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.why: The two instances of の connect 車 with うんてん and うんてん with しかた, respectively, creating the phrase “how to drive a car.” This phrase is the subject with が of わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nを知りません is used, it means not knowing information about N or whether N exists, while わかりません emphasizes not understanding how to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: You can say either 車を運転するしかた or 車の運転のしかた; the form with the verb emphasizes the action, while the form in the sentence emphasizes the method.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with わかる, but an object that is understood or not understood usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.vi: This machine is too complicated for children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the machine is the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: には marks the comparison group or the range in which the level of excessive complexity is considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: すぎます follows an adjective to express a level beyond what is suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + すぎる・Aな remove な + すぎる・Vます remove ます + すぎる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.why: このきかい is the topic, while こどもには limits the group being evaluated. The adjective ふくざつ combines with すぎる to say that the level of complexity is beyond what is suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If こどもにとって is used, it means “for children” from their point of view or for their benefit, and does not necessarily emphasize excess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Aなすぎる is the structurally joined form, while ふくざつすぎます is the polite form used in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily keep な before すぎる, but the adjective な must remove な before connecting with すぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.sk: N は + Frequency + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: たまに modifies the verb and shows the frequency of use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the place or service being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.why: The frequency adverb たまに comes before the verb to add information about how often the action occurs. としょかんを is the object of りようします and comes directly before the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with よく, it means using it more often, unlike the irregular sense of たまに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If あまり～ません is used, it emphasizes “not use much” and usually has a negative tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a frequency adverb at the end of the sentence, but たまに usually comes before the verb it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects アルバイト with けいけん and shows the content of the experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks something that exists or is possessed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses existence or possession of an object or concept.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.why: アルバイトのけいけん creates the noun phrase “part-time work experience.” This phrase is the subject with が, while あります expresses the existence of that experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If アルバイトをしたことがあります is used, it emphasizes having had the experience of working part-time, rather than focusing on the noun “experience.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If Nを経験しました is used, it emphasizes the action that was experienced, rather than the state of currently having experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say アルバイトを経験があります, but with あります, they must use a noun phrase and が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q16.kobun.cn: N の + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.vi: Mr. Suzuki does work related to education.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: This word modifies かんけい and limits the field being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the preceding noun with しごと, creating a phrase that modifies the work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks work as the object of the action しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: しています describes current work or the occupation someone is doing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.why: After the topic comes the noun phrase きょういく かんけいの しごと, in which の connects the field to the noun しごと. を marks the work, while しています is the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still work related to education, but the expression is more formal and shows the relationship more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の or use を between nouns, while a noun-modifying phrase here needs to be connected with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q18.kobun.vi: What will you have for dinner tonight?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: This is a greeting used to open the conversation and also sets the time context for the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the dish being asked about as the object of eating or drinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: めしあがります is the respectful form of たべます or のみます; か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q18.kobun.why: The question first sets the context, then states the object なにを, and finally uses a respectful verb. The particle を shows that the thing being asked about is the object of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the question becomes more ordinary and does not clearly show respect toward the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand めしあがる as simply “eat,” but it is an honorific verb used for the actions of a respected person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.vi: I do not know how to practice judo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の indicates しご? No; here, じゅうどう modifies れんしゅう and specifies the content of the practice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects れんしゅう with しかた, forming the phrase “how to practice.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks しかた as the unknown item in the pattern わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりません is a negative predicate. It expresses that the speaker does not know that method.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.why: The two phrases の gradually narrow the meaning from judo to practice and then to the method. The phrase しかたが becomes the unclear item and comes before わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence asks directly how to perform the action, rather than focusing on the noun meaning “method.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with わかりません, but something that is understood or not understood usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.vi: Last week, my older sister left the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 先週 indicates when the event happened and is placed at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who left the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: たいいんしました is the noun 退院 combined with する in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.why: The time expression is placed at the beginning to set the time frame. It is followed by the subject with が and the main action at the end. 退院する describes leaving the hospital after treatment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern only says that someone came back from the hospital. It does not confirm that they completed the hospital discharge procedure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: 入院しました means was hospitalized, which has the opposite direction of meaning from 退院しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate 退院する simply as “go home”; this word is specifically used for leaving the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.vi: Last night, the noise from next door was so loud that I could not sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets “last night” as the time topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects となり with おと and indicates the source or location of the noise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the noise as the subject that has the quality うるさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: うるさい changes to うるさくて to connect the cause with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ねむれませんでした is the negative past potential form. It expresses that the speaker could not sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.why: The sentence gives the time first, then identifies the noise as the subject causing the noisy condition. The form うるさくて connects the cause with the result of being unable to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and more gently than with the connecting form て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect an adjective ending in い with で, but they must change うるさい to うるさくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.vi: This bag has many pockets, so it is very easy to use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to clearly identify the bag being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the bag the topic and describes its features.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks ポケット as the part with the feature described in the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: おおい changes to おおくて to connect the preceding cause or feature with the following comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: つかいやすい is formed from the verb stem つかいます and やすい. It means easy to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.why: After the topic comes the feature of having many pockets, followed by the main comment about ease of use. The form くて connects the two features and creates a natural cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If やすい is replaced with にくい, the meaning changes to difficult to use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If べんりです is used, the sentence only says that it is generally convenient and does not directly emphasize how easy it is to use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate やすい as cheap, but after a verb stem it means easy to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.vi: This is a clock with an unusual shape.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the indicated object the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: This adjective comes before かたち to describe the feature of the shape.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects かたち with とけい and shows that the clock is identified by its shape.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the noun sentence and identifies the object being discussed as a clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.why: これは introduces the object being indicated. めずらしい modifies かたち, while かたちの further modifies とけい, forming the phrase “a clock with an unusual shape.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to a shape that resembles something else, not simply an unusual shape.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place an adjective after a noun as in Vietnamese, but a Japanese adjective must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.vi: The population of suburban towns has increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun with the noun まち to modify まち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects まち with じんこう to form the phrase “the population of the town.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that is increasing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects ふえる with くる and expresses a continuing change up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: くる in the polite past form ends the predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.why: The two N phrases の modify まち and じんこう respectively, forming the subject “the population of suburban towns.” ふえてきました expresses an increase that has continued up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only says that the population increased and does not emphasize the continuing process up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate てくる as “go to,” but in this sentence it only shows a gradual change toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q23.tokens.7.m: has become; has continued until now
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the name Yoko with おかあさん to show possession or a family relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the person being presented or explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the noun かんごし to the sentence and creates a polite noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q24.kobun.why: ようこさんのおかあさん forms a complete noun phrase. Then は makes this phrase the topic. The noun かんごし comes before です to state the occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of は, the sentence emphasizes that Yoko's mother herself is a nurse, rather than simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q24.kobun.tip: Do not translate は as “is”; は only introduces the topic, while the meaning “is a nurse” is expressed by かんごしです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person performing the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the quoted speech content before the verb いいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: いいました is the main predicate, showing that the speaking action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q25.kobun.why: こどもが is the subject of the speaking action. The speech content is placed inside 「」, followed by と and then いいました to form a quoted-speech structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the sentence presents the child as the topic and puts less emphasis on the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit と after quoted speech, but と is required before verbs such as 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.vi: The next lecture starts at 2 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.sk: N は + Time から + です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states which class or lecture is being announced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates when the lecture starts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and confirms the class schedule information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.why: The topic is first stated with は. Then から identifies the starting point of the schedule. です turns this information into a polite schedule announcement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern directly says “starts at 2 o’clock,” while からです emphasizes the starting point of a period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: まで indicates the ending point, so the meaning changes to “until 2 o’clock”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistake から for “because,” but here it indicates the starting point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects being late with the apology, creating a cause or circumstance relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: すみません is a way to apologize at the end of a sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q4.kobun.why: The action or mistake is stated first using て, and the apology is placed at the end of the sentence. In this context, て not only connects two actions but also gives the reason for the apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding しまって emphasizes the regret or unfortunate result of being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Separating them into two sentences makes the report and the apology clearer and more definite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q4.kobun.tip: Do not always translate て as “and”; here it should be understood as “because I was late”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q5.kobun.vi: I prepared my luggage for the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the luggage as the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb よういする is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q5.kobun.why: The noun naming the item being prepared comes before を. Then the verb よういしました functions as the predicate. This word order clearly presents the object before the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this word is used, the basic meaning is still “prepare,” but it has a more common and broader sense than よういする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse を with に when marking the item being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今日 with しゅくだい to modify it and identify the homework as belonging to today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes しゅくだい the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な かんたん combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q6.kobun.why: 今日のしゅくだい is a noun phrase in which 今日の modifies しゅくだい. After stating the topic with は, the sentence uses the adjective な to describe the homework.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning is still “easy,” but it focuses on the feeling that the homework is not difficult, while かんたん emphasizes simplicity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget です after the adjective な when using かんたん as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.vi: Yesterday, the wind was strong, and a lot of rain also fell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.sk: Time は + Nも + Aいく、 + Nも + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes yesterday the time topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: も marks the wind as an additional phenomenon alongside the rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い つよい changes to the く form to connect with the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: も continues to mark the rain as the subject of another phenomenon in the same sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: たくさん modifies ふりました and shows that there was a large amount of rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ふりました is the main predicate and describes rain falling in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.why: The two phenomena, wind and rain, are connected by the く form of the adjective い. The particle も shows that both the wind and the rain were notable features of yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If つよく is replaced with つよくて, the connection is still natural, but the meaning of cause or consecutive states is clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use つよいと instead of つよく when connecting two qualities in the same sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before テレビ to identify the TV being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes テレビ the topic of the comment about its broken condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies こしょうします and indicates how often the TV breaks down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: こしょうします is the predicate and describes the device often having problems.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q8.kobun.why: この modifies テレビ, and は presents the TV as the topic. よく comes before the verb to show how often the problem occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning changes to “is easy to break,” emphasizing a quality rather than the actual frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand よく as indicating a good level, but in this sentence it indicates frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.vi: I go to the dentist once every week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.sk: Time interval おきに + N に + Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: おきに indicates a regular interval between repeated actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place or person the speaker regularly visits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: かよっています describes a habit of continuing to visit a place regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.why: The phrase いっしゅうかんおきに is placed at the beginning to state the cycle, while はいしゃに is the place or person visited regularly. Vています describes an ongoing habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning is also “every week,” but it emphasizes each week as a unit rather than the interval between visits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t115-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse おきに with ごとに; おきに emphasizes the interval between visits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q1.kobun.vi: They are investigating the cause of the traffic accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This noun phrase modifies げんいん and identifies which event the cause belongs to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being investigated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The form ています describes an action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q1.kobun.why: こうつうじこの modifies げんいん, while げんいんを is the direct object of しらべる. ています shows that the investigation is taking place at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence only says that the investigation was completed or carried out in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse を with が in this phrase: the cause is the object being investigated, so it takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q10.kobun.sk: N が + 「Quoted sentence」 と + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q10.kobun.why: The speaker comes before が. The speech is placed in Japanese quotation marks and connected with と. Then, the verb いいました describes a completed speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used in a continuous sentence, it still means “said that,” but it does not show a direct quotation as clearly as quotation marks do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget と after quoted speech when using verbs such as 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q10.tokens.4.m: please go and come back safely
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q11.kobun.vi: I reserved a seat on the Shinkansen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun before it with the noun せき and shows a relationship of belonging or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the seat as the object being reserved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q11.kobun.why: The noun for the train modifies せき with の. Since the seat is the object of the reservation action, を is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is replaced with で, the meaning becomes “by Shinkansen,” showing the means of transport rather than a seat on the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で to mean “on the train,” but the relationship between the two nouns here requires の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の turns おじさん into a modifier for the noun しゅみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the uncle’s hobby the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks fish as the object of the fishing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: つること turns the action of fishing into a noun, while です explains what the topic is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.why: The hobby is made the topic with は. The verb つる is changed into a noun with こと so it can be the explanation after です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことです is replaced with のが好きです, the sentence emphasizes that fishing is a favorite activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: ためです usually gives a reason, so it is not suitable for defining the hobby as fishing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place a verb directly after は, but こと is needed to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I visited my teacher’s home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.sk: Time + N の + N に + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう shows when the action happened and usually does not need a particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects せんせい with おたく and indicates the teacher’s home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the destination of the action うかがいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: うかがいました is the humble form of 行きました or 訪ねました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.why: The time expression comes first. The destination is marked by に. おたく is modified by せんせいの to show whose home it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression is more ordinary and direct, while うかがいました shows humility toward the respected person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: で shows the place where an action takes place, so it is less suitable than に for showing a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に and で. With verbs meaning go or come, the destination usually uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents today as the time and the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the road as the subject in the state of being clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: すいている describes a road with few vehicles or people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q14.kobun.why: Today is presented as the topic, while the road is the subject of the state. すいています describes a continuing state, not just a temporary action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: すきです usually means “to like” or “empty,” so it does not naturally describe a quiet road like すいています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: すきました shows a change to a quiet state, while すいています emphasizes the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may think ています only describes an action in progress, but here it describes a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.vi: I caught a bad cold, but I feel much better now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.sk: Aいく + なる + が + Degree + Aいく + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks かぜ as the object of the phrase かぜをひく, meaning to catch a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: catching a bad cold and then feeling better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: だいぶ modifies the degree of recovery, meaning that the condition has improved greatly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: よく is the continuative form of よい. It comes before なりました to show becoming better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました describes a change of state and uses the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.why: The first clause states that the speaker caught a cold, while が connects it to the contrasting result. よくなる is a structure showing a change to a better state, modified by だいぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If よくなっています is used, the sentence emphasizes that the condition has improved and is still good now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is placed after よくなりました, the sentence opens a following contrasting clause after the idea “has improved.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may say よくなります by translating word for word, but よい must be changed to よく before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q15.kobun.cn: Aいく + なる; Vた + が
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q16.kobun.vi: Mr. Ichiro is Ms. Yoko’s husband.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the person being introduced as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects two nouns to show the relationship between Ms. Yoko and her husband.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q16.kobun.why: The sentence puts the person being discussed first with は. It then uses NのN to show the relationship between the two people. The final noun phrase is the predicate, so it ends with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence emphasizes the state of being married to someone, rather than stating the relationship of being someone’s husband.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may think の only shows material possession, but here の also shows a relationship between people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.vi: He plays the piano very well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the person whose ability is being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the field in which the ability is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: すごく modifies じょうずです and makes the level of skill stronger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: じょうずです is an adjectival predicate な that describes ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.why: With じょうず, が marks the area or object that someone is good at. すごく comes before the adjective to add degree, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence has the verb 弾きます and directly says that someone plays the piano well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: とても also means very, but its tone is more neutral and softer than すごく in spoken language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put を before じょうず, but the ability pattern usually uses Nが上手です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: ちょうど adds the meaning that the action ended at exactly the right time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks work as the subject that completed the action of ending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: おわった is the ordinary past form and modifies ところ in the pattern たところです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: たところです shows that an action has just been completed immediately before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.kobun.why: The clause しごとがおわった comes before ところ to identify the action that has just been completed. The past form おわった connects to ところです, meaning that the action happened just before speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with たばかりです, the sentence still means that the action was done recently, but the time period may be wider and does not have to be immediate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ところ as a place, but in this pattern it only refers to a time or a state that has just occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q18.tokens.5.m: is, is in the state of
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.vi: I went to the seaside yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.sk: Time N + N へ + past Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう only indicates the time when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: へ marks the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: いきました is the polite past form of いきます and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.why: The time expression usually comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the destination with へ. The verb いきました comes at the end and fits an action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 海で遊びました, the sentence says that someone played at the seaside, not only that they went there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: に can also mark a destination and has almost the same meaning in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for a destination, but with 行く they need to use に or へ; で only marks the place where an action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.vi: My future dream is to become a manga artist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しょうらい with ゆめ to show that it is a dream for the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents ゆめ as the topic explained at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the result or point reached by the verb なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the phrase なる into a noun phrase, while です concludes the content of the dream.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.why: しょうらいのゆめは is the topic, and then the content of the dream is presented with the phrase まんがかになること. に goes with なる because it indicates the result of changing into a profession or status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this form, the sentence directly expresses the wish “I want to become a manga artist,” rather than defining what the dream is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.tip: After なる, に must be used, not を; こと turns the whole verb phrase into noun content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ことです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.vi: My teacher introduced me to Yoshiko.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person who performed the action that the speaker benefited from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person introduced in the action しょうかいする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb しょうかいする with いただく to create a pattern for receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ていただきました expresses that the speaker received a beneficial action from the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.why: The person who performs the action goes with に, and the person introduced goes with を. The verb しょうかいして connects in the て form with いただきました to politely show that the speaker received help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with てもらいました, the meaning of receiving help remains, but the polite and respectful tone toward the person who performed the action is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If てくださいました is used, the focus is on the teacher taking the initiative to do it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand いただきました as only receiving an object, but after a verb in the て form, it can also express receiving a helpful action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q20.kobun.cn: Vて + いただく → Vていただきました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q21.kobun.sk: Time N は + N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents tomorrow as the topic and time point of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun おまつり with the topic in a polite noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q21.kobun.why: あすは makes tomorrow the topic, while おまつりです is the noun predicate. The sentence does not need an action verb because it states an event taking place tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あります, the sentence emphasizes that the festival will be held or exist tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily add the verb 行きます, but the noun sentence with です is enough to say that tomorrow is the festival day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.vi: What kind of transport shall we choose?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな modifies the noun のりもの that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the choice being decided in the pattern 〜にしましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょうか is used to ask for an opinion and suggest deciding together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.why: どんな modifies のりもの to ask what type of transport it is. のりものにしましょうか expresses deciding together which transport to choose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the question is more direct and has less of a feeling of discussing it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を, but the choice in 〜にする must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q22.kobun.cn: N + に + する/しましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.vi: My mother said to my grandmother, “I hope you get well soon!”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks はは as the topic, meaning my mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the person who receives the words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content that is spoken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: いいました is the polite past form of 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.why: The speaker is shown with は, the listener goes with に, and the spoken words are placed in quotation marks and connected with と. The verb 言いました comes at the end to finish the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this form, the content after と becomes something the speaker thinks, not direct speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.tip: Do not omit と before 言う when quoting the exact spoken content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.tokens.5.m: take care; I hope you get well soon
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q23.kobun.cn: 引用内容 + と + 言う/言いました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.vi: My wallet was stolen on the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects でんしゃ with なか, creating the phrase “inside the train.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the incident happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the thing that was stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ぬすまれました is the polite past passive form and shows that the speaker suffered a loss.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.why: でんしゃのなかで identifies the location, while さいふを is the object affected. The passive form emphasizes that the speaker suffered a loss because the wallet was stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If an active sentence is used instead, it means that someone stole the wallet and does not emphasize the victim.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern clearly states that the pickpocket is に, while ぬすまれました focuses only on the theft.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence describing a loss, the stolen object still usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q24.kobun.cn: V五段未然形＋れる・V一段語幹＋られる・する→される・来る→こられる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.vi: I think that person will definitely come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks that person as the topic being judged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: きっと is an adverb that modifies the whole judgment that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content of the thought; the verb before と uses the plain form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: おもいます is the main predicate and shows the speaker's thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.why: あのひとは is the topic, and きっと adds a level of certainty. The content of the thought comes before と, while おもいます comes at the end as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with はずです, the sentence shows certainty based more on evidence or a reasonable prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with でしょう, the tone becomes more tentative, close to “will probably.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.tip: Do not connect きっと directly with おもいます; the content must come before と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ と ＋ 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q3.kobun.vi: I was late for the appointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects やくそく with じかん to form the phrase “the appointment time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the point in time that the speaker was late for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: おくれました is the main predicate and describes being late compared with the scheduled time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q3.kobun.why: やくそくのじかん forms a specific time point. With おくれる, に marks the time or schedule that the action was late compared with.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means “waited for the time,” and does not describe arriving late for the appointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q3.kobun.tip: おくれる usually goes with に to indicate a time or event that someone is late for; do not use を for that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q4.kobun.vi: I asked someone to repair the car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun くるま with the following noun and modifies しゅうり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action おねがいしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb おねがいする is in the polite past form and describes asking or requesting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q4.kobun.why: The phrase くるまのしゅうり forms the compound noun “car repair,” and then を marks what was requested. おねがいしました comes at the end of the sentence and describes the request that was made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker received help repairing the car from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically translate の as “of,” but here it connects two nouns to form the phrase “car repair.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.sk: Time point ＋ Nに ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The time expression comes at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the meeting happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object of the verb あう, meaning the person whom the subject met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: あう changes to the polite past form to say that the meeting happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.why: The time expression comes first to give the setting, the person met goes with に, and あいました is the main predicate. With あう, に marks the person met, not the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Using と emphasizes that Yoshiko was the person who took part in the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the kanji spelling of the same structure and does not change the meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を with あう; the person met usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify it and identify the object being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes せつめい the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: すぎる comes after an adjective to show that its degree is beyond what is suitable; the adjective な connects directly with すぎる, without using な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.cn: Aい omit い ＋ すぎる; Aな ＋ すぎる; Vます omit ます ＋ すぎる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.why: この modifies せつめい, while は states the topic. ふくざつ combines directly with すぎます to express the degree “too complicated.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says “complicated,” without the sense of being too much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to “difficult to understand,” focusing on how hard it is to take in rather than on its complexity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q6.kobun.tip: With the adjective な, do not keep な before すぎる: say ふくざつすぎる, not ふくざつなすぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.vi: I was seriously injured while skiing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the situation or activity in which something happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ひどい modifies けが and shows how serious the injury was.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks けが as the object of the phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: けがをしました is the polite past expression for being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.why: スキーで gives the situation in which the accident happened, ひどい modifies けが, and けがをする is a fixed verb phrase. Therefore, しました comes at the end to complete the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression clearly states the action of skiing with をして, instead of using で to state the situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence specifically says that the leg was broken instead of generally saying that the person was seriously injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q7.kobun.tip: けがをする must use を; do not say けががしました when you want to express “was injured.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.vi: No matter how much I searched, I could not find it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら combines with ても to emphasize that no matter how hard someone tries, the result does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb さがす changes to the て form and then adds も, creating the concessive pattern いくら～ても.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: みつかる is an intransitive verb, changed to the polite past negative form to say that the result was not found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.why: The clause いくら～ても states the concessive condition and comes before the comma. The following clause states the actual result, with みつかりませんでした as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the present negative expresses a current situation or habit, without emphasizing an event that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Using が simply connects two contrasting ideas and does not have the sense of “no matter how much one searches.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.tip: Do not connect いくら directly with the dictionary form; this pattern requires Vて＋も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.tokens.0.m: no matter how much one searches
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q8.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も; いくら ＋ Vて ＋ も
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.vi: The son next door is a police officer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies むすこさん and identifies the son who belongs to the neighboring household.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes むすこさん the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the noun けいかん with the topic and creates a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.why: となりのむすこさん is a noun phrase in which となりの modifies むすこさん. は identifies the person being discussed, while けいかんです gives that person's occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes that the son next door himself is a police officer, rather than simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Using でした means that the person used to be a police officer or that this status belonged to the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t116-q9.kobun.tip: An occupation goes with です when introducing or describing it; there is no need to add に after the occupation noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.vi: I beat Hiroshi in the swimming competition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the setting where the victory took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: With 勝つ, に marks the opponent who was defeated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: かちました is the polite past form of 勝つ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.why: で shows that the competition is the setting, while に marks the opponent in the fixed combination 勝つ. The verb 勝ちました comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means competing with someone; it does not confirm that you won.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 負けます is used instead, the result changes to losing to the opponent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.tip: Remember to use に with 勝つ and 負ける; do not use と based on the usual pattern in English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q1.kobun.cn: N に ＋ 勝つ／勝ちます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamada said to Ms. Yukiko, “Please be sure to come!”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は shows the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the recipient of the speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜひ modifies the invitation and emphasizes the speaker's wish for the listener to act.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the entire directly quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 言いました is the main predicate and reports the act of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.cn: 「文」＋ と ＋ 言う; the direct quotation keeps the original sentence form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.why: The speaker is the topic, the listener goes with に, and the spoken content is placed in quotation marks and linked with と. 言いました comes at the end to complete the reported sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence expresses Yamada's thought that Yukiko should come, rather than direct speech sent to Yukiko.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q10.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily leave out と before 言いました, but と must be used to connect the spoken content with the verb 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the object being pointed at the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the topic with a noun used to identify or introduce it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q11.kobun.why: これは identifies the object being introduced, while the noun after です shows what type of object it is. です is placed at the end to finish the noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q11.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily translate これは as “this is,” but は only marks the topic; it is not the verb “to be”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q12.kobun.vi: This box is in the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies the noun はこ that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the box as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: じゃまです is a quality predicate showing that the box causes an obstruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q12.kobun.why: この comes before a noun to identify a specific box. は makes the box the topic, and then じゃまです gives a comment about it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it means “not necessary,” referring only to the need to use something, without emphasizing that it is in the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q12.kobun.tip: English speakers may confuse じゃま with “not needed”; じゃま emphasizes an object that blocks the way or takes up space.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.vi: The room next to my friend's house is vacant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows ownership or a connection with the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: となりの modifies へや and identifies the room's location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the room as the subject in the described state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes the room's current state after becoming vacant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases identify the relationship with the friend and the location next to it. The room goes with が because it is the subject that has the state, while ている emphasizes the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence usually describes something placed or prepared by someone in that state, so it does not fit a room that is simply vacant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q13.kobun.tip: English speakers may understand ています only as “be doing,” but with verbs that show a change of state, it can also describe an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the place being introduced the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the place with a noun that identifies the type of place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q14.kobun.why: ここは identifies the place being discussed, while じんじゃです shows what that place is. The noun pattern は noun です is used to introduce and identify something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q14.kobun.tip: English speakers may confuse ここは with “as for here,” but in this sentence は marks the place being introduced as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q15.kobun.vi: I am sure that person will come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action くる in the smaller clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the clause くる into a noun, while は makes the whole event the topic.
