default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q15.kobun.why: The clause あのひとがくる is nominalized with の to refer to the whole event. は makes that event the topic, and then たしかです comments that it is certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことは is used instead, the basic meaning is still “the act of that person coming,” but the tone is more abstract and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q15.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily omit の when they want to make the whole clause the topic before は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ のは
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q16.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to the barbershop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q16.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N へ ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement toward とこや.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q16.kobun.why: きのう comes at the beginning to state the time, とこやへ marks the destination, and いきました is the main predicate in the polite past. The subject “I” is omitted because it can be understood from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に still indicates the place you are going to, but に emphasizes the specific destination more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q16.kobun.tip: English speakers may confuse へ with を because both can appear before a movement verb, but へ only shows direction toward a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q17.kobun.vi: I bought a toy as a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the purpose of buying this item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q17.kobun.why: おみやげに comes before the object to state how the item will be used. おもちゃを is the direct object of かいました, so を is used to connect it with the verb “buy.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If として is used, the sentence emphasizes the status or role “as a gift” more than the purpose of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q17.kobun.tip: English speakers may translate に as “for,” but in this sentence に expresses purpose, not the recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the state or action of losing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the setting or event where the loss happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q18.kobun.why: ともだちが is the subject of まけました. しあいで shows the situation in which the loss happened, while まけました ends the sentence and gives it a polite past meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: When に is used after しあい, に marks the opponent or competition that the subject lost to; this expression sounds more natural when the focus is on what was lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に with the meaning “in”, but で specifically shows the setting where the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.vi: I work part-time while attending university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vます omit ます ＋ ながら ＋ N に ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks a job done at the same time as attending school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ながら connects two actions that happen at the same time, with the main action in the second part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the destination of going to school or commuting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ています shows an action or state that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます ＋ ながら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.why: しながら connects the part-time job with the main action だいがくにかよっています. The second part is the focus, while ています shows that the state of attending university is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If て is used to connect two actions, the sentence may show only an order or a general connection. It does not clearly stress that they happen at the same time as ながら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily attach ながら after the dictionary form, but they must use the form that omits ます of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q2.kobun.vi: There is a problem with the washing machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects せんたくき with ぐあい, creating the phrase “the condition of the washing machine”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks ぐあい as the thing being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: おかしいです is the predicate adjective ending in い, describing a problematic condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q2.kobun.why: せんたくきのぐあい combine to form the subject “the condition of the washing machine”. が connects this subject with the description おかしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 調子が悪い, the meaning is almost the same, but it emphasizes that the machine is working poorly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate ぐあいがおかしい as “strange condition”; for machines, the natural meaning is “there is a problem”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q21.kobun.vi: Food prices are high these days.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun for food with the noun for price, creating the relationship “the price of...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has the characteristic “high”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q21.kobun.why: さいきん is placed at the beginning to state the time. The phrase follows the structure NのN, and then ねだんが becomes the subject described by the adjective たかい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の and say しょくりょうひん ねだん directly, but の is needed to connect the two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.vi: Yoko entered a famous university and is very happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes ようこさん the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ゆうめいな uses the form な to modify the noun だいがく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the destination or goal of the action にゅうがくする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects entering university with the happy state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: ている describes a state that continues after feeling happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.why: は identifies the person being discussed, while the phrase ゆうめいな だいがくに is the destination of the action にゅうがくする. The form て connects entering university with the continuing happy state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence focuses on Yoko's appearance or signs that she seems happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use にゅうがくて, but the verb にゅうがくする must change to にゅうがくして before being connected with て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q23.kobun.vi: It is okay to keep wearing the hat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item worn with the verb かぶる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたままで describes keeping the state of wearing the hat when doing or judging the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q23.kobun.why: ぼうしを is the object of かぶる. After the verb changes to the past form かぶった, まま describes the state being kept, while かまいません shows that this state is acceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence means that an action does not need to be done. It does not focus on keeping the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand まま as “still” in every case, but here Vたまま must be used to express keeping a state that has already occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the place ここ the topic to explain what kind of place it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q24.kobun.why: ここは identifies the place being pointed to. The noun くうこう comes before です to identify that place as an airport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add に after ここ, but when saying “this is...” with です, use ここは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q25.kobun.vi: I do not usually take that road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the road as the topic and creates a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: とおりません is the polite negative form of とおる, expressing that one does not pass through that road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q25.kobun.why: ふつう limits the frequency of the whole action. あのみちは is made the topic with は, while とおりません is the negative predicate about passing through.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, the sentence only states that the road is the object of the action; は highlights that road for contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with the meaning “go through the road”, but when they want to mention that road specifically as the topic or for contrast, they use は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.vi: It has been a long time since I last met him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に identifies the person the speaker meets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns あう into a noun, while は makes meeting the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ひさしぶりです acts as the predicate and describes a long period during which the event has not happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.why: あうのは makes meeting the topic and comments on it with ひさしぶりです. に marks the person being met, while あう uses the dictionary form because it comes before の to be nominalized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using のが emphasizes that meeting is rare or happens only after a long time, rather than making meeting the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes the action of meeting again soon or now after a long time, not a comment about the act of meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate のは too literally as “still having work,” but in this sentence, the natural meaning is “it has been a long time since I met him.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のは
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.vi: I went to see a painting last week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence to show when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the painting as the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The continuative form み に combines with いく to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いきました is the main predicate, in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.why: えを is the content of the viewing, while みに shows the purpose of going. The movement verb いきました comes at the end to complete the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning focuses on doing an action and then going, not on going for the purpose of seeing a painting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form みるにいきました; before に, use only the verb stem in the ます form, which is み.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q4.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.vi: My translation is still not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし to the following noun to show that the translation belongs to me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes ほんやく the thing being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies the predicate and shows that the condition has not reached the desired level or is not complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: だめです serves as the predicate evaluating the quality of the translation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.why: わたしの identifies which translation, は marks the translation as the topic, and まだ adds the meaning “still not.” The evaluative predicate comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is substituted, the sentence emphasizes an unfinished action instead of evaluating the translation as not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q5.kobun.tip: まだ does not always mean “still”; in negative sentences or negative evaluations, it often means “still not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds the meaning that the action was completed before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes reviewing the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: すみました serves as the predicate and expresses that the review has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q7.kobun.why: もう is placed before the topic to signal completion. ふくしゅうは is the activity being discussed, while すみました ends the sentence with the result that it is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used directly with an action verb, the sentence only says that the action has been completed; すみました emphasizes that the task itself has ended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q7.kobun.tip: すみました does not mean “sorry” here; in the context of work, it means “has been completed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the subject of the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the receiver of the speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the quoted content before the verb いいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: いいました is the main predicate and expresses the speaking action in the polite past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.why: わたしは is the speaker, おじさんに is the listener, and the speech is placed in quotation marks and connected to いいました by と. This order clearly shows who spoke to whom and what was said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If the quoted content is removed, the sentence only means speaking to someone and does not state exactly what was said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, the meaning changes to “was told by someone that…,” focusing on the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.tip: In a quotation, do not use に to connect the speech content directly to いいました; the content must go with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q8.kobun.cn: 引用内容 ＋ と ＋ 言う／思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.vi: I failed at work and made my parents worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に attaches to 失敗する and shows the area in which the failure occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the failed action with the result of making my parents worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person affected by the action させる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: させました is the polite past form of the structure meaning to make someone do something or be in a certain state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.cn: N・Aな語幹 ＋ させる; V1 group 1: remove る, change the final sound from row う to row あ ＋ せる; V2: remove る ＋ させる; する → させる; 来る → 来させる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.why: The expression showing the area comes first, followed by て, which connects the cause with the result. The person made to worry goes with を because they are the object affected by させる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning changes to receiving help or concern from the parents, rather than making the parents worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse が with を before させる; the person affected in this structure usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q1.kobun.vi: These shoes are made in France.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before the noun くつ to identify the shoes being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the shoes as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: せい shows the place of production or the origin of a product.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q1.kobun.why: この must come directly before the noun くつ to modify “these shoes.” After the topic is introduced with は, フランスせいです serves as the predicate showing the product’s origin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand せい as “made of,” but フランスせい mainly says that the product was manufactured in France.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.vi: He must have already arrived in Osaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents かれ as the topic of the judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: もう shows that the predicted event was completed before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of the verb つく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ついた is the past form placed before はずです to say that the event should have been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: はずです expresses a well-supported judgment that the event is certainly true.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.why: かれは is the topic, while ついた is the content being judged. おおさかに goes with つく to show the destination, and the past form shows that the arrival is considered complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with でしょう, the sentence becomes a weaker prediction and does not stress the evidence for something that should certainly have happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with と思います, the sentence becomes the speaker’s personal opinion or thought, weaker than はずです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.tip: はずです is not simply “I think”; this pattern usually has a basis and a high level of confidence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ はずだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.vi: On the way home, I called my friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the time or occasion when the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person receiving the call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the noun as the object of かける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: かけました is the polite past form, showing that the phone call was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.why: かえりに sets the time and context, then ともだちに shows the recipient of the call. でんわを is the direct object of the fixed phrase でんわをかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the meaning is still “on the way home,” but it emphasizes the process of moving rather than the occasion of going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q11.kobun.tip: For the meaning “to call,” remember to use でんわをかける, not でんわをする in this basic structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q12.kobun.vi: I left my textbook on the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the item was left behind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item that was left behind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: わすれました is the polite past form of わすれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q12.kobun.why: テキストを is the item affected by わすれる. でんしゃに indicates the place where the item was left, matching the use of に in the pattern わすれもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use で, でんしゃ is understood as the means of carrying out the action, like “by train,” not the place where the item was left.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q12.kobun.tip: Do not change に to で when you want to say where you left something; に marks the place where the item remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes ちら the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: ほめられました is the polite past passive form, showing that the subject received praise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q13.kobun.why: ちらは is presented as the topic, while ほめられました shows that the subject received an action from someone else. The passive form focuses on the person who was praised, not the person who praised them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with ほめました, the meaning becomes “praised,” with the subject as the person performing the action rather than the person receiving praise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the passive form with the ordinary past tense; られました shows here that the subject “was praised.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.vi: I heard that she moved house last week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Vた + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は shows that she is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to indicate when she moved house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the past form た, showing a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです usually comes after a clause to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the time phrase that modifies the action of moving house. The past-tense clause connects to そうです to show reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.vs.0.t: Vます remove ます + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use it in this sentence, the meaning will be that she seems about to move house or looks as if she has moved house, not that you heard it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use it, the sentence still means “I heard that,” but the sense of guesswork or indirect information becomes clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうです after the ます form with the meaning “I heard that,” but this pattern must connect to the plain form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形 + そうだ・そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.vi: It is already seven o’clock, so I think it is about time to go home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: ですから connects the reason to the intention stated in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content of the thought; かえろう is the volitional form of かえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: おもいます takes the content of the thought before と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before ですから. そろそろ adds the idea that it is almost the right time, while the volitional form + と + 思います expresses the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use it, the intention to go home will sound more certain and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use it, the sentence will become an invitation or suggestion for the listener to go home together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use かえますと思います, but before と 思います, the volitional form かえろう is needed to express an intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.tokens.5.m: will go home, intend to go home
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q15.kobun.cn: V意向形 + と + 思う・思います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.vi: Do you have experience living abroad?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the person being asked the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects がいこくせいかつ with けいけん, creating the phrase “experience of living abroad.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists and combines with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: あります expresses existence or possession; か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.why: The topic あなたは is placed at the beginning, while the experience is the thing whose existence is being asked about, so it goes with が. The phrase がいこくせいかつの modifies けいけん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use it, the sentence will emphasize the experience of having lived abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use it, the sentence asks whether the listener has experienced that event, rather than using the possession structure with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with けいけん, but patterns asking whether something exists usually use 経験があります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.vi: The transportation in this area is inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this area the topic for the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing being evaluated as convenient or inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ふべんです is the adjective predicate な, commenting on the transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.why: このへんは is the scope of the comment, while こうつうが is the subject that has the quality ふべん. Therefore, は and が appear together but have different roles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use it, the transportation is made the topic with は, giving more focus to the transportation in this area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use it, the statement sounds softer and more indirect than 不便です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use こうつうは after このへんは, but this structure uses は for the scope and が for the subject being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.vi: It will probably get cold this evening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.sk: N は + Time から + V + でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the time range of the prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates when the cold state begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: でしょう comes at the end of the sentence to express a prediction with moderate certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.why: きょうは identifies the day being discussed, while ゆうがたから identifies when the prediction begins. でしょう comes at the end of the sentence to turn the statement ひえる into a prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use it, the possibility of cold weather will be expressed with less certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use it, the sentence will simply state a forecast or event more certainly, without the clear sense of uncertainty in でしょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand から as showing a cause, but in this sentence から shows the starting point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.vi: There is a church near my home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the church exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists at that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is the predicate used for things that are not people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.why: The place of existence comes first with に, the thing that exists comes next with が, and the sentence ends with あります. This order is the basic pattern for saying that something exists somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use it, the sentence talks about seeing a church in that area, not about its existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use it, います is incorrect because a church is an object or building, not a living creature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may reverse が and に, but the place goes with に, while the existing thing goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes her the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective that follows and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: まじめです is a polite predicate describing a quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q2.kobun.why: は identifies the person being described, とても comes before the adjective to increase its degree, and まじめです serves as the predicate that concludes the person's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to not very serious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use とても directly with a noun unless that noun has first been changed into an adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.vi: I decided to stay at a boarding house in Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where the speaker stays.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb combines with ことに to turn the action into the content of the decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: ことになりました expresses a decision or result that has been determined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.why: The place is stated first with で, and the action げしゅくする is nominalized with こと. The phrase ことになりました ends the sentence and shows that this has been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker personally decided to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake ことになる for something that happens naturally, but in this pattern it usually means that something has been decided or arranged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ことに ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.vi: There is a match next Sunday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies にちようび and forms a time phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the time when something happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks something that exists or takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate that indicates the existence of something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning of the sentence to show when the event happens. The noun しあい goes with が because it is something introduced as existing or taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence changes from saying that there is a match to saying that someone organizes or takes part in a match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with あります, but something that exists must go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.vi: I have already completely adjusted to life in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: もう shows that a state has been reached by the present time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: すっかり modifies なれました and emphasizes being completely accustomed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: にほんの modifies せいかつ and indicates life belonging to Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the object that the speaker becomes accustomed to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: なれる combines with に to express becoming accustomed to an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.why: The phrase にほんの せいかつ forms a noun phrase naming the object, while に marks the object of なれる. Both もう and すっかり modify the predicate to emphasize that the state has been fully reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is that the speaker understood life, not that they became accustomed to it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say せいかつを なれる, but なれる uses に to indicate the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q23.kobun.vi: Does someone in your family know?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: おうちの modifies かた and creates a polite expression for a family member.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the person being asked about the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ごぞんじですか is an honorific predicate used to ask whether the listener knows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q23.kobun.why: おうちの かた is a noun phrase in which の connects the modifying noun to the person being mentioned. は makes that person the topic, while ですか turns the polite predicate into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence still asks whether the person knows, but it loses the honorific nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ごぞんじですか for themselves, but this is a respectful expression used for other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.vi: I did not make it in time for the appointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: やくそくの modifies じかん and forms an appointment-time phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the time limit by which an action is or is not completed in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.ch.2.vi: did not make it in time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: まにあいませんでした is the polite past negative form of まにあう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.why: やくそくの じかん indicates a specific time with the structure Nの N. まにあう uses に to indicate the time or deadline that must be met, then uses the past negative form to say that it was not met in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only says that the person arrived late; it does not directly emphasize missing a deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate and use まにあう as a verb that goes with を, but the correct pattern is time に まにあう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.vi: Mr. Sato went to Osaka instead of Mr. Nakamura.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Nの かわりに ＋ Place へ ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the person performing the main action of the sentence the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the person being replaced with the noun かわり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: かわりに indicates doing something instead of another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: いきました is the predicate indicating that a movement action took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.why: The person who acts is shown with は, and the person being replaced comes before かわりに with の. The destination goes with へ, and then いきました ends the movement action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it means going together with Mr. Nakamura, not going instead of him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, it means going for Mr. Nakamura's benefit, not necessarily going on his behalf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse かわりに with ために, but かわりに emphasizes replacing a person or thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q3.kobun.vi: Mr. Taro apologized to Ms. Kazuko.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Mr. Taro the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person receiving the apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: あやまりました is a polite past-tense verb that serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q3.kobun.why: The person performing the action is shown with は, the person the action is directed toward goes with に, and the verb あやまりました ends the sentence and shows that the action took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes saying “sorry,” rather than directly emphasizing the act of apologizing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q3.kobun.tip: With あやまる, the person being apologized to usually goes with に, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes him the subject being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb いく combines with の to turn the action into a noun, and then を marks the object that someone is unwilling to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: いやがって is the て form of いやがる. It connects with います to create a structure showing an ongoing attitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: います follows the て form to show an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.why: いくのを turns “going” into the object of いやがる. Because the subject is another person, いやがる describes that person's unwilling attitude, while ている shows that the state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vたがる, the meaning changes to “seems to want to do something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vたくない, the sentence directly expresses the wish not to go, without emphasizing the outward behavior.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use いやがる to talk about their own feelings, but this pattern mainly describes another person's attitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のを + いやがる/いやがっている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.vi: The mathematics test was not very difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects すうがく with しけん, showing that the test is for mathematics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the mathematics test the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: それほど indicates degree and usually goes with a negative form to say “not to that extent.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to むずかしくなかったです to form the polite past negative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.why: すうがくの modifies しけん, and は marks the test as the topic. それほど combines with a negative predicate to limit the degree, meaning that the test did not reach the level of being “that difficult.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is still “not too difficult,” but the expression is more common and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the tone is stronger and implies that the test was not significantly difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use それほど with an affirmative predicate when you mean “not too.” A negative form usually needs to follow it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q5.kobun.cn: それほど + Aいくない/Aいくなかったです; それほど + Aなではない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.vi: I call my family once every week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: おきに shows the time interval between repetitions; here, it sets the cycle for calling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the recipient of the call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the noun as the object of かけます in the phrase でんわをかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: かけます is the polite predicate form and describes an action repeated at regular intervals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to state the cycle. かぞくに indicates the recipient, while でんわをかけます is the verb phrase “make a phone call.” This order goes from time to recipient and then action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ごとに, the sentence emphasizes doing something during every time unit and usually does not suggest a break between repetitions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning clearly becomes “once in N,” focusing more on the number of times than on the interval.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse おきに with ごとに: おきに emphasizes the interval between repetitions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to identify the person being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes せんぱい the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: さびしいです is an い adjective used as the predicate in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q7.kobun.why: あの modifies せんぱい to identify a specific person. は marks that person as the topic, while the adjective い at the end of the sentence describes the person's feeling or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is “looks lonely,” based on observable signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, it only says that the person is alone and does not necessarily feel lonely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q7.kobun.tip: さびしい is an い adjective, so な is not added before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.vi: I did not have enough money to buy a present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb かう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: かう comes before おかね to modify the type of money being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject being described as insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: たりませんでした is the polite past form of たりない and describes insufficiency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.why: The clause プレゼントを かう comes before おかね to identify the amount of money needed to buy a present. おかねが is the subject of the comment たりませんでした, so が is used to state the missing amount of money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the purpose or reason for N. It does not directly modify おかね like the clause かう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q8.kobun.tip: Learners may translate たりない as “do not have,” but it more precisely means “not enough” in amount or degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes ここ the topic being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun りょかん with the topic in a polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q9.kobun.why: ここは states the place being introduced, while りょかんです identifies what type of accommodation it is. The pattern NはNです is used to introduce or identify something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ここに is used, the meaning changes to “here” as a place where something exists or a destination; it is no longer an identifying topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t118-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate りょかん as a general hotel; it is an inn or lodging place in the Japanese style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes これ the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun ガソリン with a polite affirmative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q1.kobun.why: これは indicates the thing being pointed to, while ガソリンです identifies it as gasoline. The pattern NはNです is used to introduce or identify something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes that this particular thing is gasoline rather than simply making it the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q1.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use が because of the habitual translation “this is...,” but ordinary introductions use は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes たなかさん the topic being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: すっかり modifies the change of state and emphasizes that it is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the resulting state after the change with なりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and describes a change into a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.why: たなかさんは is the topic, while げんきに indicates the state reached after the change. なる requires に before the noun or adjective な when describing what someone becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 元気でした, the sentence only says that the person was healthy and does not emphasize the process of becoming healthy again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 元気になっていました is used, the sentence focuses on a state that had already formed before a certain point or when the speaker noticed it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use げんきをなる, but a resulting state with なる must be used together with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q10.kobun.cn: N ＋ に ＋ なる; Aな ＋ に ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.vi: Mr. Yang is doing commercial business.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes ヤンさん the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ぼうえき with しごと to identify the type of work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks work as the object of the verb しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the ている form of する. It describes work that is being done or a job someone currently has.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.why: ぼうえきの and しごと form a noun phrase that shows the type of work. Then, を marks this phrase as the object of する. ている shows that the work is continuing or is someone's current job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しました, the sentence refers to something done once in the past, not a current job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If です is used, the sentence only introduces it as commercial work and does not focus on the action of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を before しています, but a noun used as the object of する usually needs を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる; Nを ＋ する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.vi: This city has a well-developed industrial sector.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes このまち the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the field being described as さかん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: さかんです is the adjective predicate な. It describes the level of development or how active something is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.why: このまちは states the area being discussed, while こうぎょうが is the field being evaluated. さかんです serves as the predicate to say that the field is active or well-developed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 盛んに行われています is used, the sentence emphasizes that industrial activities are being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 工場が多いです, the meaning changes to there being many factories. It does not directly evaluate the level of industrial development.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate さかん as crowded, but here it refers to the level of development or active activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.vi: Please hang the picture up in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the hanging action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 connects the verb かざる with おく to create the pattern ておく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: おく in the て form shows doing something in advance or leaving something in that state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.why: The object comes before the verb. Then, て形 connects with おく to express doing something in advance or leaving it ready. ください turns the whole phrase into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this, the sentence only means please hang it up. It does not emphasize doing it in advance or leaving it ready.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this, the sentence becomes the speaker's promise to do it in advance, not a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand おいて as putting something somewhere, but in this pattern it is an auxiliary verb showing that something is done in advance or kept in a certain state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q13.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ おく; Vて ＋ おいてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun きょうしつ with the topic to create a polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q14.kobun.why: The place is made the topic with は, while the noun きょうしつ gives the identification of that place. です comes at the end to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that this exact place is the classroom, rather than simply introducing this place as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit です after the noun, making the sentence lose its polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person affected by the action of making them worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the noun しんぱい in the fixed phrase しんぱいをかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: かけました is the polite past form of かける, completing the phrase しんぱいをかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.why: The pattern しんぱいをかける uses を for the cause and に for the person affected. The subject is often omitted because it is clear from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, N is the person who worries, not the person who makes N worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 迷惑をかける, the meaning changes to causing trouble or inconvenience for a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use が with ともだち, but に is what marks the person who is made to worry in this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q15.kobun.cn: N に ＋ N を ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.vi: I am studying things from ancient times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before a noun to modify じだい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun じだい with こと, creating a modifying noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the polite ている form. It shows that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.why: ふるい modifies じだい. Then, the phrase じだいのこと is marked by を as the object of けんきゅうする. ている shows that the studying is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with the past form, the sentence only says that the studying was finished or that the study was carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If について is used, the sentence clearly emphasizes that the research topic is the ancient era.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate こと as a specific object, but here こと means things or content related to the era.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q16.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ N; N の ＋ N; Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.vi: My older sister is writing a novel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes my older sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the work as the object of writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: かいて is the て形 of かく. It connects with います in the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: います combines with て形 to show that an action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.why: My older sister is made the topic, and the novel is the object of the writing action. かいています describes an action that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes an action in progress, which matches the fact that she is writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with the past form, it means that she wrote it, but she is not necessarily still writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use かきています, but く must be changed to いて before connecting with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q17.kobun.cn: Vている; Vて ＋ います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the entire quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: いいました is a reporting verb. It shows that someone said the content inside the quotation marks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q18.kobun.why: The speech is placed inside quotation marks and goes with と to show the quoted content. いいました comes after it and reports the speaking action in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 思いました, the meaning changes to thought that, not said that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 答えました, the sentence emphasizes that this is an answer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place と after the verb for speaking, but in Japanese と comes immediately after the quoted content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.vi: At present, you must not eat anything other than foods that are still soft.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: まだ modifies the current state and means “still not yet.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: やわらかい modifies もの, while の connects this noun phrase to いがい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: いがいは states the excluded range: nothing except soft things may be eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: Vては combines with いけません to form an expression that prohibits an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: いけません completes the prohibition pattern Vてはいけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.why: The phrase やわらかいものの いがいは defines the exception, and the pattern たべてはいけません then states what is prohibited. The particle は highlights the range “outside ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しか～ない, the sentence changes to “can eat only soft things,” emphasizing the permitted limit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vないでください is used, the sentence becomes a softer request and does not highlight a prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse いがいは with しか～ない; one emphasizes the excluded part, while the other emphasizes the only part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q19.kobun.cn: Vて + は + いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.vi: It is a little difficult to meet this Sunday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.sk: N の + N に + V辞書形 のは + adverb + Aな です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects こんしゅう with にちようび to modify Sunday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the meeting takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の changes あう into the noun “meeting,” while は makes it the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ちょっと makes the refusal sound less direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: むりです is the predicate and states that meeting is difficult to carry out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.why: The time phrase comes before the verb to identify when the meeting takes place. あうのは changes the whole action into the topic, and then むりです comments on whether it is possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のは with ことは still refers to meeting, but the tone is more general and rigid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.tip: With あう, learners may easily use を, but the place or time of meeting usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes あのひと the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: けっして usually goes with a negative predicate to emphasize an absolute degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks the object being contrasted, instead of the neutral expression うそを.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: つきません is the polite negative form of つく in the fixed expression うそをつく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.why: あのひとは is the topic, けっして modifies the negative predicate, and うそは presents lying with a contrastive meaning. The phrase うそをつく is a fixed combination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 一度も～ない is used, the sentence emphasizes that it never happens even once, focusing on experience or number of times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If あまり～ない is used, the meaning is only “not very ...,” which is weaker than けっして.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate うそをつく word by word; it is a fixed expression meaning “to lie.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the object being pointed at as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the topic with the noun サンダル in a polite statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q21.kobun.why: これは identifies the object, while サンダルです states its name or type. The structure NはNです is used to introduce and identify something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to ではありません, the sentence becomes negative: “This is not a sandal.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit は when translating “this is ...,” but は clearly identifies the object being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.vi: This is a very important letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the object being pointed at as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective だいじな to increase its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: An adjective ending in な uses the form だいじな when it comes before the noun てがみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: です forms a noun predicate and identifies this as a letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.why: とても and だいじな both modify てがみ. とても indicates degree, while だいじな describes a feature. The whole phrase とてもだいじなてがみ forms a noun predicate with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 大切な, the meaning is still “important,” but the tone usually suggests something valuable or worthy of care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If changed to だいじでない, the sentence becomes a negative statement about the quality: “not important.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use だいじい incorrectly; this word is an adjective ending in な, so だいじな must be used before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.vi: Please try not to do things like this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the action しない as the object being mentioned and adds emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the ない form combines with ように to state what one should try to achieve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: してください is a polite request, and together with ように it means “please try not to ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.why: こんなことは identifies the action being warned about, しないように states the goal of not doing it, and してください turns that goal into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vないでください, the sentence only asks “please do not do it,” which is more direct and does not have the meaning “try to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vるようにしてください is used, the meaning changes to a request to try to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ように with ような; before してください here, ように must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.tokens.4.m: so that ... not; in order not to
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q23.kobun.cn: Vない + ように + してください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.vi: This is the company reception desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the place being introduced as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects かいしゃ with うけつけ, showing that the reception desk belongs to the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: です forms a noun predicate to identify the function of the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.why: ここは identifies the place, while かいしゃのうけつけ names it through a possessive relationship. The pattern NのN places the modifying noun before the main noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ここにあります is used, the sentence only says that an object or place exists here; it does not identify it as a reception desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If へ行きます is used, the sentence changes to mean moving to the company instead of introducing a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand の only as “of,” but in NのN it can also show a type or relationship between two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.vi: Thank you very much for coming to listen to the concert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.sk: N を + Vます removes ます に + Vていただいて + ありがとうございました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of listening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vます removes ます + に indicates the purpose of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ていただく expresses gratitude because the listener came; て connects it to the thanks at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The expression ありがとうございました is used to thank someone for something that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.cn: Vます removes ます + に + 来る／行く; Vて + いただく
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.why: The noun コンサート is the object of listening, while ききに states the purpose of coming. The phrase きていただいて comes before the thanks to explain what the listener did.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the tone is more casual and less formal than ていただいてありがとうございました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that に in ききに is に, which indicates purpose, not place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.vi: I intend to decline attending the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects パーティー with しゅっせき to form the phrase “attending the party”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of えんりょする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content of the intention mentioned in おもいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: おもいます is the main verb and takes the preceding intention as what is being thought about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.why: しゅっせきを えんりょする is a verb phrase whose object is attending the party. The volitional form しよう combines with とおもいます to express the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This form focuses more on predicting or thinking that one will decline, rather than directly stating an intention like しようと思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This form expresses a clearer and firmer plan, with less of the meaning “I think I will…”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before とおもいます when expressing your own intention; use the volitional form, such as しよう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q3.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と ＋ 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.vi: What is needed when establishing a new company?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: あたらしい directly modifies かいしゃ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the company as the object of つくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: とき creates a time clause and shows when the necessary action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing being asked about as necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ひつようですか serves as the predicate and turns the sentence into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.why: The clause つくるとき sets the time context before the main question. In the main question, なにが is the thing needed, so が is used, while ひつようです states the requirement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is replaced with なら, the sentence changes from “when establishing” to the condition or assumption “if establishing”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.tip: とき must connect with the appropriate form of the preceding word; before とき, a present-tense verb uses the dictionary form, such as つくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Nの・Aい・Aなな ＋ とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.vi: The grandmother is taking care of a child.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person performing the caregiving action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の indicates the person being cared for and modifies せわ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks せわ as the object of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects する with います to form the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: います indicates that the action せわをする is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.why: こどものせわをする is a noun phrase plus a verb, in which せわを is the object of する. The form しています shows that the caregiving action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This form emphasizes raising a child over a long period, while せわをしています is broader and refers to taking care of someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q5.kobun.tip: せわをする uses を with せわ; it does not change to せわがする because する requires the object to be marked with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.vi: The heating is too strong, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Aい remove い ＋ すぎますね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object whose strong level is being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: つよすぎます combines adjective つよい with すぎる to express a level beyond what is desired, while ね seeks agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます・Aい remove い・Aな remove な ＋ すぎる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.why: だんぼうが is the subject being evaluated for its level. つよい changes to つよすぎます because すぎる attaches to the adjective stem to create the meaning “too…”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This form only says “very strong” and does not necessarily suggest that it is uncomfortably strong or beyond a suitable level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q6.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, remove い before すぎる: つよい → つよすぎる, not つよいすぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.vi: I want to learn about Japanese culture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N について ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with ぶんか to modify the noun ぶんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the topic or object that the speaker wants to learn about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: たい attaches to the ます form of a verb to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.why: The phrase にほんの ぶんか clearly states what is being learned about, while について connects that object to the action しりたい. たい is placed after the verb stem to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with に関して, the meaning is still “about culture,” but the tone is more formal and more common in writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly place について after a verb, but this pattern must come after a noun naming the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.vi: May I try it a little?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: ちょっと modifies the whole action and makes the request sound softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: させて is the て form of the causative and connects the meaning of allowing the speaker to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: させていただけますか is a very polite way to ask for permission to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.why: The action たいけん is put into the causative form to ask the listener for permission to perform it. いただけますか at the end of the sentence turns the request for permission into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with させてください, the request for permission is more direct and less formal than させていただけますか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもいいですか is used, the sentence only asks whether it is allowed and does not clearly show humility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may misunderstand いただく as meaning only receive or eat, but in this pattern it shows humility when asking for permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.tokens.3.m: can receive; may be allowed to
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q8.kobun.cn: V使役形て ＋ いただけますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.vi: My father has finally left the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person performing the action たいいんする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: やっと modifies the action and shows that leaving the hospital happened after a period of waiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: たいいん combines with する to form a verb, which is then changed to the polite past form しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.why: ちちが is the subject of the action, and やっと shows that the result came late but was achieved. たいいんする is the verb for leaving the hospital after treatment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ようやく, the meaning stays almost the same, but the tone is slightly more formal than やっと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If もう is used, the sentence only emphasizes that the event has already happened and does not emphasize the long wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t119-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may simply translate やっと as “already,” but this word always suggests that there was waiting or difficulty beforehand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vi: I do not like this taste very much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets this taste as the topic for evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり modifies the negative predicate and lowers the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ではありません negates the adjective な すき at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.cn: Aな語幹 + ではありません; あまり + negation
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.why: This taste is made the topic with は. あまり comes before the negative predicate to express a low degree, while すきではありません completes the negative comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with すきではないです, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the conversational tone is less formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q1.kobun.tip: あまり usually goes with a negative sentence, so it should not be used with すきです in this basic pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vi: I hear that my friend's house has as many as four toilets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.sk: Nの + N には + N が + Quantity も + V + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 友だち with 家, showing that the house belongs to the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: には combines with に and は, showing both the place and the topic range for that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing said to exist in the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: も emphasizes the number four, suggesting more than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ある is the existence predicate used for objects and things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです comes after the plain form to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 友だちの家には identifies the place, が marks what exists there, and ４つも emphasizes the quantity. そうです is placed at the end to show that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ようです, the sentence becomes a judgment based on signs or observation, rather than simply reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうです, which reports heard information, with そうです, which describes appearance or a prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vi: I buy lunch near the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes lunch the topic of the buying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects かいしゃ with ちかく, forming the phrase “near the company.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.why: Lunch is stated as the topic, while the place of purchase is marked by で. The predicate かいます comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, に is not suitable for marking the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for every place; the place where an action occurs usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes air-mail transport the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective 速い and increases the degree of speed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 速い is an adjective ending in い that serves as the predicate, and combines with です to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.why: After the topic comes the adverb of degree, followed by the adjective as the predicate. です comes after the adjective to give the sentence a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: 速く is the adverbial form, used to modify a verb rather than directly serve as the predicate like 速い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 速くです; before です, the adjective must stay in the 速い form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vi: You can even send a parcel from a convenience store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.sk: N からでも + N が + potential-form V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point, while でも emphasizes that even this place is acceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 荷物 is the item being sent and is marked by が in a potential sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: おくれます is the potential form, expressing that a parcel can be sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.cn: Group 1 verb: change the final sound to the え row + る; Vる + ことができます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.why: からでも states the place of sending and emphasizes the range of choices. 荷物が is the item that can be sent, while the potential predicate comes at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vることができます, it still means that something can be done, but the expression is longer and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may keep を with a potential sentence; in this pattern, the object is usually marked by が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q14.kobun.vi: I do not understand the geography of this city well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object that is or is not understood well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb よく modifies わかりません and shows the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb わかる is in the polite negative form and expresses not understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q14.kobun.why: The phrase このまちの地理 states the object being understood, so it goes with が. よく comes before the verb to show how clearly something is understood, while わかりません serves as the negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 地理 is replaced with 場所, the sentence refers to a place, not geographical knowledge.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with わかる, but the object of わかる usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 電車 with ドア, forming the noun phrase ドア of the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the door as the subject that closes by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 閉まる is an intransitive verb; its polite form ます expresses that the door closes by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q15.kobun.why: 電車のドア is a noun phrase in which の shows possession. Because the door closes by itself, the intransitive verb 閉まる is used, and the subject is marked by が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 閉めます is used, it means that someone closes the door, because it is a transitive verb that requires a person to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse 閉まる and 閉める; use 閉まる when the door closes by itself, and 閉める when someone closes the door.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.vi: There is a chemistry test tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.sk: Time noun + N の + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: A word for a point in time comes at the beginning of the sentence and identifies when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the subject name with テスト and shows the content of the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the test as an existing thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: あります expresses the existence of things that are not people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.why: あした is placed at the beginning to state the time. 化学のテスト forms a compound noun meaning a chemistry test, while があります expresses the existence of the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If the structure is replaced with 化学を勉強します, it means studying chemistry, not having a test.
