default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use います for テスト because います indicates the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.vi: The sky is blue today, and it feels very pleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes today the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the sky as the subject that is blue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective あおい changes to the て form to connect the sky's state with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the feeling as the subject judged to be pleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: いいです serves as the predicate and states that the feeling is pleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + くて
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.why: きょうは sets the topic, and the sentence then describes the sky and the feeling. The くて form connects two qualities or states in the same sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: Using し presents one reason or feature among several, with a clearer listing tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q17.kobun.tip: When connecting an adjective ending in い, change い to くて; do not connect it directly with て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The adverb よく modifies 考えて and shows how to think.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The form てから connects the earlier action of thinking with the later action of writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いて is the て form of 書く. It combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.why: The clause 考えてから comes first to show the action that must be completed beforehand. 書いてください at the end of the sentence states the main request politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 考えたあとで is used, the meaning is still “after thinking,” but it emphasizes the time after an action rather than the order that must be followed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.tip: てから always requires the verb before it to be in the て form; it does not use the dictionary form such as 考えるから.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q18.kobun.cn: Vて + から; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.vi: My younger sister may be a ballet genius.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the younger sister the topic being guessed about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the field of ballet with 天才, making a phrase meaning “a genius in that field.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 天才 is a noun predicate that gives an assessment of the younger sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: かもしれません is placed at the end of the sentence to express an uncertain guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.why: バレエの天才 is a noun phrase used as the predicate, in which の shows the field. かもしれません comes at the end to turn the statement into a guess with a low level of certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If でしょう is used, the guess usually sounds more certain than かもしれません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.tip: Before かもしれない, nouns and な adjectives do not normally add だ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・N + かもしれない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vi: This is the classroom for second-year students.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the place being introduced the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun ２年生 with 教室 to modify the classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends the sentence using a pattern that identifies or classifies something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.why: The sentence makes a place the topic, then uses の to connect the possessor or category with the main noun. です confirms that the place is a specific classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this sentence is replaced with this form, the focus changes from introducing a place to saying that something exists there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の or use 的, but Japanese connects two nouns with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.vi: The bell marking the end of the class has rung.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.sk: N の + N の + N が + past Vます形
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects じゅぎょう with おわり, forming the noun phrase “the end of the class.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects おわり with ベル and modifies the noun ベル.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the bell as the subject producing the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 鳴る changes to the polite past form 鳴りました to describe an event that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.why: The two phrases の successively create modifying relationships among the class, its ending, and the bell. ベルが is the subject, while 鳴りました is the predicate describing the sound produced by the bell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 鳴る because 鳴る is an intransitive verb, and the subject producing the sound goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q21.kobun.vi: I am growing many kinds of flowers in the garden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the place where the action of growing flowers takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the flowers as the object of the action 育てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 育てています uses the ている form to express an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q21.kobun.why: The place にわで comes before the object and the verb, following the natural word order of a Japanese sentence. 花を is what is being grown, while 育てています describes the state of carrying out that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 育てます, the sentence only says that someone will grow or usually grows something; it does not emphasize an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q21.kobun.tip: It is easy to confuse で with に. An action taking place in the garden uses にわで, while に usually shows a destination or a place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.vi: I want a pair of black boots.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before ブーツ to modify the noun directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: With ほしい, が marks the thing the speaker wants to have.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ほしい is an い adjective used as a predicate. です is added to make it polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.why: 黒い comes before ブーツ to identify the boots' color. The pattern ほしいです uses が for the desired thing, unlike action verbs, which usually use を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ブーツを買いたいです, the meaning changes to wanting to buy boots, focusing on the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.tip: Do not say ブーツをほしいです. With ほしい, the desired thing usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q22.kobun.cn: Aい + N が + ほしいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q23.kobun.sk: この N の + N は + Quantity です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the envelope with 重さ, showing the weight belonging to the envelope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 重さ the topic about which information is given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with quantitative information and makes the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q23.kobun.why: このふうとうの重さ is a complete noun phrase, in which の shows possession. は introduces the weight being discussed, while 500 grams is its value.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression treats the envelope as an object that has a weight, while the original sentence directly states “the weight of the envelope.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q23.kobun.tip: Do not omit の in このふうとうの重さ. If you say このふうとうは, the topic will be the envelope, not its weight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q24.kobun.vi: I arranged to meet her at the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: と shows the person taking part in the arranged meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the arranged meeting takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: まちあわせしました is the polite past form of まちあわせする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q24.kobun.why: The person meeting with someone goes with と, while the meeting place goes with で. These two additional phrases come before the verb to state the participant and the place where the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with かのじょに会いました, it means that the speaker met her, without necessarily arranging the meeting in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q24.kobun.tip: と in かのじょと differs from に in かのじょに会いました. と refers to the person carrying out the arranged meeting together, while に usually refers to the person met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q25.kobun.vi: This event has an admission fee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this event the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 有料 is a noun showing a paid status. It combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q25.kobun.why: このイベントは states the object being described. 有料です is a noun predicate that gives information about the event's admission fee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 無料です, the meaning changes to a free event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q25.kobun.tip: 有料 is a noun used as a predicate, so です is needed in a polite sentence; it cannot be used directly as a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vi: If you have a different opinion, please say it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The verb comes before the noun 意見 to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object assumed to exist in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ある changes to the form ば to connect the condition to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 言う changes to the て form to connect with ください and make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ください completes the Vてください pattern, which is used to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.why: The conditional clause あれば comes first to state the situation, followed by the request. The phrase chちがう意見 modifies a noun, so the verb comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたら is used, the condition is more specific. It usually refers to after something happens or to a hypothetical situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vても is used, the meaning becomes that even if there is a different opinion, someone will still say or do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place the subject or the conditional word after the verb, but Japanese places the conditional clause before the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vi: There is an intersection near the elementary school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 小学校 with ちかく to form a phrase referring to the area near the school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists at the stated place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is an existence predicate used for things that are not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.why: The sentence follows the order: the place に comes first, the existing thing が comes next, and the sentence ends with あります. の changes 小学校 into a modifier for ちかく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with います, the sentence refers to a person or animal that exists near the school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use あります for people, but people and animals must use います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vi: In summer, I went up the mountain with my friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time when the act of going takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: と refers to the person who performs the action together with the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: へ marks the direction or destination of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.why: The time comes first, followed by the companion and the destination, and the movement verb comes last. と shows companionship, while へ emphasizes the direction of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 山へ is replaced with 山に, the sentence still refers to the destination, but に emphasizes the destination more than the direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If と一緒に is used, the meaning of going together with friends is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse と with に when talking about going with someone; the companion goes with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vi: I go to church every week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.sk: Frequency + N に + Vて + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase shows frequency and modifies the whole action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place regularly visited by the action 通う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 通う is connected in the て form to combine with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ています describes a repeated action or a state continuing up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.why: 毎週 comes first to state the frequency, 教会に is the destination, and かよっています shows that the visits continue or repeat. に is suitable with the verb 通う when referring to a place visited regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 通います is used, the sentence simply states the habit neutrally, without emphasizing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 教会へ行きます is used, the sentence only says that someone goes to church and does not clearly show that the visits are regular.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ています as meaning only that an action is happening at the moment of speaking, but with repeated verbs it can also describe an ongoing habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vi: This store will be closed tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.sk: Time + この + N は + N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase shows when the state mentioned at the end of the sentence applies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: この comes before 店 to identify the store being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 店 the topic, while この modifies 店.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みです uses the noun 休み together with です to state the store's condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.why: 明日 comes first to identify the time, 店は states the subject, and 休みです gives the conclusion about the store's condition. Japanese uses the polite present tense to talk about a schedule or state planned for the near future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that the store is the place that is closed, rather than introducing the store as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 休みになります is used, the meaning changes to becoming or changing into a closed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may add a future tense, but Japanese often uses the present tense to talk about a future schedule or planned state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes “work” the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the time when an action or event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, followed by the time marked by に, and the predicate おわります comes at the end. This order clearly states what happens and when.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に incorrectly when stating a time; for a specific hour, に is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: はやく is an adverbial form that modifies the act of answering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.why: The adverb はやく comes before the request to state how the action should be performed. The verb in the て form combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vなさい is used instead, the sentence sounds more commanding and less gentle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t12-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change the verb to the て form before connecting it with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before the noun to modify the scenery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: でした is the polite past form of です and ends the descriptive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q1.kobun.why: すばらしい comes before けしき to describe that noun. The whole noun phrase ends with でした to comment on scenery that was seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is still wonderful scenery, but the expression becomes informal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q1.kobun.tip: Do not add だ after the adjective い; say すばらしいけしき, not すばらしいだけしき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.vi: Now, my experience from my previous job is proving useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.sk: Time + N の + N が + N に + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes first to limit the time of the state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: まえの modifies しごと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects しごと with けいけん to form the phrase “work experience.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject that is proving useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: やくにたつ is a fixed phrase in which に refers to a useful state or purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ている describes the present state that has continued since the experience became useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.why: The phrase の arranges the nouns in a modifying relationship: まえのしごとのけいけん. 役に立つ is a fixed phrase, and たっています emphasizes the state of being useful now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is that someone is actively using the experience, rather than simply saying that the experience itself is proving useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate に in やくにたつ as “at”; in fact, it is a particle belonging to the fixed phrase やくにたつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q10.tokens.10.m: stand; be useful in the phrase 役に立つ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the body part that is in a dry state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: かわきました is the polite past-tense predicate, expressing a state that has arisen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q11.kobun.why: Japanese expresses thirst using the subject のどが and the verb かわく. Therefore, the sentence does not need to state “I” directly, but the speaker’s state is still understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes “I am hungry,” because the subject of the feeling is おなか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use を with のど; the natural expression is のどがかわく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of being hospitalized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb しました describes an action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q12.kobun.why: The subject comes first with が, followed by a verb describing an event that happened. にゅういんする changes to にゅういんしました to speak politely about the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the sentence changes from emphasizing the subject to making my friend the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle が because Vietnamese can say “my friend was hospitalized” directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: おっしゃいました is the honorific form of 言いました, used for the teacher’s speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q13.kobun.why: The speaker is marked by が and comes before the predicate. おっしゃいました keeps the polite past form and also shows respect toward the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 言いました is used, the meaning is still “spoke,” but it does not show an honorific expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If お話しになりました is used, the respectful tone remains, but the expression is more formal and different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 言いました for every subject and forget that おっしゃる is an honorific expression used for other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q14.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N が ＋ Vませんでした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうべ indicates when an event happened and does not need an additional particle when it comes at the beginning of a sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject mentioned in the phenomenon of appearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 出る becomes でませんでした in the polite past negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q14.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to show when the event happened. ほしが is the subject of でる, while the form でませんでした expresses that something did not appear in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the stars become the topic and the contrast becomes clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with でる, but the phenomenon of “stars appearing” uses a subject with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the time point that follows and shows that it is approaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 10じです acts as a noun predicate and states the approaching time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q15.kobun.why: もうすぐ comes before the time point to add the meaning “almost.” The sentence uses です after the noun for the hour to announce that the current time is close to that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If もう is used, it means that 10 o’clock has arrived or that it is already 10 o’clock, so it no longer has the meaning “almost.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If ごろ is used, it means around 10 o’clock and does not emphasize that the time is approaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake もうすぐ for “already,” but this pattern means “almost,” while もう is the one related to “already.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the object being pointed to the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun ステレオ combines with です to identify the name or type of the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q16.kobun.why: これは states the object being introduced, while ステレオです identifies what that object is. The pattern NはNです is a basic structure for introducing or identifying something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that this particular object is the stereo, usually when distinguishing it from another object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit は because Vietnamese has no topic particle in introductory sentences.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.vi: This machine is dangerous, so please do not touch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify it and refer to an object near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the machine the topic of the warning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: きけん is the noun-form adjective な, combined with です to create a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Vないでください is used to politely ask the listener not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.why: このきかいは states the object being warned about, and きけんです gives the reason. The next sentence uses さわらないでください to ask the listener not to touch the dangerous object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with さわってはいけません, the sentence becomes a stronger rule or prohibition, not just a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If さわらないほうがいいです is used, the sentence only advises the listener not to touch it, so it is softer than a prohibition or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say さわらないください, but ないでください must be used to connect the negative form with the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q17.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ です; Vない ＋ でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.vi: Recently, I became able to eat sashimi.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that has become possible to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The potential form たべられる combines with ように to indicate an achieved state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました expresses a change that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.why: さいきん states when the change happened, and さしみが is the object that gained the ability to eat. The structure V可能形＋ように＋なる expresses a change into a state in which someone can do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used here, the sentence only states a present ability and does not emphasize the process of becoming able to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it means actively trying or arranging to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse が in this pattern with を, but が marks what has become possible to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q18.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形・V可能形 ＋ ように ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the place being introduced the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun おくじょう with the topic to create a polite judgment sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q19.kobun.why: ここは identifies the place being discussed, while おくじょうです confirms its name or characteristic. This is the noun sentence pattern は nounです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this word is used, the sentence refers only to the roof of the building and does not necessarily mean a place where people can walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit は after ここ, but は is necessary to make the place the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.vi: I said, “My wife passed away last year.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.sk: 「Time ＋ N が ＋ polite past V。」と ＋ 言いました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the clause to show when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the event なくなりました in the quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the whole preceding sentence as the quoted content; ました shows the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: いいました is the main verb of the outer sentence. It shows the act of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.why: The content of what was said comes before と, followed by the verb いいました, which shows the act of speaking. In the quoted sentence, つまが is the subject and なくなりました is the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～そうです is used, the sentence means “I hear that” or “it seems,” not the speaker’s direct words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use と at the beginning of the quoted content; と always comes immediately after the quoted part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.vi: My school rules are very strict.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし to the noun がっこう to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects がっこう to きそく, showing that the rules belong to the school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は marks きそく as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective きびしい serves as the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases come before the nouns and modify the school and the rules, respectively. After stating the topic with は, the adjective きびしい gives an opinion about the rules.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this phrase is used, it means that rules exist at the school, focusing more on the place than on possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate every の as “of,” but they need to identify the noun that comes immediately after it and is being modified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q21.kobun.vi: I have quite a high fever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: だいぶ modifies the degree of the fever, showing that the condition is relatively serious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks ねつ as an existing condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses the existence of ねつ in the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q21.kobun.why: だいぶ comes first to add information about degree, and ねつが is the subject of the existing condition. The pattern ねつがある is used to say that someone has a fever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in the sentence, the meaning becomes “very hot,” which usually describes an object or the weather, not having a fever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ねつをあります, but あります goes with が when talking about the existence of a fever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.vi: I hear that Mr. Yamamoto’s daughter will graduate from university this year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nは ＋ Time ＋ Nを ＋ V尊敬語 ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects やまもとさん with おじょうさん to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the person being discussed as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ことし is a time adverb that identifies when the graduation will take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks だいがく as the object of the graduation action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: なさる is the honorific form of する in そつぎょうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです comes at the end of the sentence to pass on information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.why: The possessive phrase comes before the person being discussed, while the time expression comes before the object and the verb. そうです is attached to a clause in the plain form to show reported information, while なさる shows respect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it comes after a verb stem such as そつぎょうしそうです, it means “seems about to graduate,” based on an observed sign.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence still expresses an assumption based on information, but the meaning is less direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the reporting form そうです with そうです, which only describes appearance; look at the form before it to tell them apart.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.vi: I am preparing to leave the company and go home now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nから ＋ V辞書形 ＋ ところです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: いま identifies the present time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting point of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies ところ and creates a pattern for talking about the time just before an action is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ところです states the time of the action; here, it is just before returning home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.why: いま is placed at the beginning to identify the time, while かいしゃから states the starting place. V辞書形 comes before ところです to show that the action is about to begin or is just about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in the sentence, the meaning becomes that the person is currently returning home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is used in the sentence, the meaning becomes that the person has just returned home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate every ところです as “be doing,” but the form before ところ determines whether the action is about to happen, is happening now, or has just happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q23.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vている・Vた ＋ ところだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.vi: I asked my friend why they went to the airport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the destination of the action いった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb modifies わけ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the content being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.why: The clause いった comes before わけ to modify this noun, creating the meaning “the reason for going.” The first に shows the person being asked, while the second に shows the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 理由 is used instead of わけ, the meaning is still “reason,” but the tone is more direct and neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the two particles に and overlook that いった modifies わけ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the person being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks what is said to exist in a large amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: This word modifies あり and shows the degree of strength.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The form あり＋そうです describes an appearance that suggests strength.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.why: The sentence uses あのひと as the topic and then describes that the person has a lot of strength. そうです follows the stem form ます to express a judgment based on appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: When the plain form is used before そうだ, the pattern usually means “I hear that,” rather than a guess based on appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use あるそうです for both meanings, although ありそうです expresses a judgment from outward signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q25.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.vi: I asked the teacher, “What would you like to see?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action of seeing in the quoted question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ごらんに is the first part of an honorific expression used to describe the teacher’s action of seeing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks a direct question; ごらんになります is the corresponding honorific pattern for 見ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: たずねました is the main predicate and shows the speaker’s act of asking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.cn: お／ご ＋ N ＋ に ＋ なる; 「Question ＋ か」と ＋ 尋ねる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.why: The person being asked is marked by に, and the question content is placed in quotation marks before と. ごらんになります uses a respectful expression because the subject of the action of viewing is the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 見ますか, it still asks what someone will watch, but it loses the respectful tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse ごらんになります with ごらんします; when showing respect for another person's action, use ごらんになります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went drinking with a senior colleague at the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ N と ＋ Vます remove ます に ＋ 行きました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to show when the drinking activity took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects かいしゃ with せんぱい and shows that the senior colleague belongs to the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: と refers to the person who carried out the drinking activity together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: みに is the form made by removing ます from 飲む and combining it with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: いきました is the main predicate and is in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.why: きのう gives the time, せんぱいと gives the person who went together, and のみに gives the purpose of going. The subject “I” is omitted because it can be understood from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the purpose structure itself; if we say 飲みました, it only means that someone drank, without emphasizing going somewhere to drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form のむに; remove ます to make のみ, and then add に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes あのひと the topic of the descriptive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: しっかりした comes before a noun and modifies ひと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ひとです is a noun predicate that identifies that person as a reliable type of person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q5.kobun.why: あのひとは is the topic, then しっかりした modifies ひと to describe a characteristic. です ends the polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しっかりしている人, the meaning is almost unchanged, but it emphasizes the state or quality being shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q5.kobun.tip: When modifying a noun, the adjective な needs な, while しっかりした is already the form of the verb する used before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q5.kobun.cn: N ＋ な ＋ N; Vた ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.vi: This is the gift I received yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ Vた ＋ N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to show when the gift was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense clause modifies プレゼント, creating the meaning “the gift received yesterday.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the noun sentence and identifies the topic as a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.why: これは introduces the item being presented. きのういただいた comes before プレゼント to modify the noun, while プレゼントです forms the noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is still “received,” but the humble and polite tone of いただいた is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese places きのういただいた before プレゼント.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.vi: That person is a respectable person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes あのひと the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な comes before a noun and modifies ひと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ひとです is a noun predicate that completes the comment about あのひと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.why: あのひとは is the topic, and りっぱなひと is the noun phrase that gives the comment. な connects the adjective ending な with the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with まじめな, the meaning changes to “serious/hard-working,” without emphasizing respectability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.tip: Do not omit な before the noun: say りっぱなひと, not りっぱひと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q7.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ な ＋ N; Aな ＋ です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.vi: I decided to wrap the box in yellow paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the item being wrapped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: きいろの modifies かみ and identifies the type of paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the tool or material used for wrapping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb is turned into a noun with こと, and then に marks the content of the decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ことにしました expresses that the speaker decided to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.why: はこを is the object of wrapping, while かみで indicates the material. つつむことにしました turns the action “wrap” into the content of the decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means “was decided” or that the decision was made by circumstances or another person, without emphasizing the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.tip: After ことにする, use the dictionary-form verb when talking about deciding to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことにする／ことにしました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending な changes into the に form to modify the verb しごとします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb phrase is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q9.kobun.why: かれは identifies the subject, while ねっしんに describes how he works. The adjective ending な uses に when it changes into an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning emphasizes making one's greatest effort rather than an enthusiastic attitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t120-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use ねっしんな before a verb; change it into ねっしんに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the item being presented.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q1.kobun.why: これは is the topic, while スーツケースです identifies the name or type of that item. The pattern は＋です is used to introduce and identify something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that this particular item is a suitcase, instead of simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate これは as “this is,” but は mainly marks the topic, not the verb “to be.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: もう shows a state that has been reached by the present time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun wedding with the noun じゅんび to show what is being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the wedding preparations the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: じゅうぶん modifies the prepared state and shows the level of completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: できています describes the present state as the result of finishing the preparations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.why: The phrase NのN identifies the type of preparation, and then は makes this phrase the topic. じゅうぶん shows the level, while できています emphasizes the present state after the preparations have been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If できました is used, the sentence focuses on the completed event; できています emphasizes the state that is complete now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If まだ is added with a negative form, the meaning changes to say that the preparations are still unfinished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand できています as “can do,” but in this sentence it only describes a state that has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the thing being introduced or specified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects a noun with the topic to show the relationship “is.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q11.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the topic これは, and then uses the noun エスカレーター as the information being identified. です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this pattern, the focus shifts to something near the listener or something already mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit は or use を in an identity-introduction sentence, but the pattern “N は N です” requires は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q12.kobun.vi: I was disappointed because I failed the entrance exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the exam targeted by おちる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects failing the exam with the disappointed feeling in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite past-tense verb describes a feeling that arose after the previous event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q12.kobun.why: にゅうがくしけんに goes with おちる to describe failing an exam. おちて connects the previous cause or event with the feeling がっかりしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If たので is used, the cause is stated more clearly and has a more explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with おちる, but an exam goes with に in the expression “fail an exam.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.vi: Tanaka's house is not as spacious as Yamada's house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a person's name with the noun うち to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes Tanaka's house the object being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects a person's name with the noun うち, which is omitted immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ほど marks the comparison standard in the negative pattern “not as ... as.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い changes to ひろくない to form the negative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.why: The two possessive phrases create two objects: Tanaka's house and Yamada's house. ほど combines with the negative adjective to express that N1 does not reach the same level as N2.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with より, the sentence directly says that N1 is greater or less than N2 in the chosen comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget the negative form in ひろくない; in this pattern, ほど usually goes with a negative adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q13.kobun.cn: N1 は + N2 ほど + Aいくない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.sk: N は + Frequency + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person who performs the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the frequency of the action りようします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the library as the object being used or made use of.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb りようします is the main predicate and is conjugated in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.why: A frequency adverb comes before the verb to show how often something happens. としょかんを りようする uses を because the library is the object being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ いきます is used, it means going to the library, without emphasizing the use of the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use へ with りようします; because the place is the object being used, it goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects おなか with ぐあい, creating the phrase “the condition of the stomach.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the condition being described as the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: おかしいです is the adjective predicate that describes an unusual condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q15.kobun.why: The phrase おなかの ぐあい combines a body part with its condition. が marks the condition as the subject, while おかしいです states the feature of that condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this sentence is used instead, the meaning specifically says that the stomach hurts, rather than simply saying that the stomach's condition is unusual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may say おなかをおかしいです, but an adjective describing a state needs a subject marked with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.vi: What kind of outfit do you plan to wear?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな modifies かっこう and asks about the type or style of outfit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the outfit as the object of the action する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before つもり to modify the meaning of intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.ch.3.vi: intend to ...; do you plan to ...?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: つもりですか creates a polite question about the listener's plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.why: どんな comes before a noun to ask about the type of outfit, while を marks the outfit being used. V辞書形 + つもりですか asks about the listener's existing intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定ですか is used, the question focuses more on a scheduled activity or a decided plan and less on personal intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.tip: Do not change する into します before つもり; use the dictionary form する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q16.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + つもりだ／です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q17.kobun.vi: I will go to the art exhibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: えの modifies てんらんかい and shows that it is an art exhibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the place or destination of 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q17.kobun.why: えの comes before てんらんかい to modify this noun. A destination goes with に, and then 行きます serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the verb before に shows the purpose of going, such as going to look at paintings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with a destination, but the verb 行く usually uses に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.vi: Last night, I received a phone call from a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N から ＋ N が ＋ ありました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうべ shows when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the source or the person who made the call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that appears in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ありました is the predicate. It describes the phone call arriving or occurring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.why: ゆうべ is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state the time. With あります, the phone call is treated as the subject used with が, while から shows its source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the focus shifts to the person who makes the call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q18.kobun.tip: Do not translate あります mechanically as “to have”; in this context, it can describe a phone call taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner to the noun しゅみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes しゅみ the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 何ですか forms a question that confirms the content of the hobby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q19.kobun.why: たなかさんの identifies the owner, while しゅみは states the topic. 何ですか asks for the identity or content of that topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the question focuses on the activity that the person likes to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q19.kobun.tip: 何 before ですか is usually read as なん, not なに in this question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q2.kobun.vi: Please take as much as you like.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に changes じゆう into an adverb showing the way of taking something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: お＋the stem form ます＋ください is a polite way to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q2.kobun.why: じゆうに modifies the action of taking and shows that the listener may take as much as they like. おとりください places the request at the end of the sentence and makes it polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If てください is used, the request is still polite but less formal than お＋Vます語幹＋ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand じゆうに mechanically as “freely,” but in this sentence it should be understood as “as you like.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q2.kobun.cn: お＋Vます形の語幹＋ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.vi: What do you need when renting an apartment?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of renting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary form かりる comes before とき to show when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: とき connects the time clause to the main clause that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks what is being asked about as necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ひつようですか is the predicate and asks what is necessary when renting an apartment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.why: The clause アパートをかりるとき gives the time situation first, and then the main clause asks what is necessary. 何が is suitable because the question asks for the subject of the adjective ひつよう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning emphasizes what must be done before renting an apartment, not only the time of renting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence talks about what is necessary after the apartment has already been rented.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.tip: とき does not always go with the past tense; for an action that has not happened yet, V辞書形＋とき is usually used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形 ＋ とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.vi: I buy goods from other countries and sell goods to other countries.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the place or source from which the goods are bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the goods being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The form かったり gives one action as an example and connects it to another action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: へ shows the direction in which the goods are sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the goods being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: The form うったり adds another similar action before します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: します completes the pattern for listing actions たり…たりします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.why: から identifies the source of the purchases, while へ identifies the direction of the sales. The two actions are expressed with たり…たり to give typical examples of business activities.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If the て form is used instead, the sentence connects the two actions more clearly as a sequence or as consecutive actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes a general statement about “doing foreign trade,” with less detail about the separate buying and selling activities.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use たり as if it were て to tell a sequence; たり usually has the meaning of listing examples.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.vi: After we finish eating, let's talk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the meal as the thing that is completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The form すんだら connects a condition or time to the suggestion that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks 話 as the content of the action します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.why: しょくじがすんだら sets a condition or time point first. When that is completed, the speaker suggests doing 話をしましょう together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning simply becomes “after finishing the meal,” with less of a conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the conversation will take place after the meal is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q22.kobun.tip: たら does not always show a hypothetical condition; in this sentence, it also shows the time point “when … is finished.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.vi: I talked with my parents about the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the person who receives the words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the noun しょうらい with こと to modify こと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content being talked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 話しました is the verb 話す in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, the listener is marked by に, and the content of the speech is the object marked by を. The phrase しょうらいの こと forms a noun phrase meaning “the matter of the future.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the listener; the person receiving the words is usually marked by に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.vi: The teacher told me that I did well on the previous test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.sk: N に + 「文」 + と + passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects このあいだ with テスト to modify the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents the test as the topic in the quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies できました and indicates the degree of performance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: できました is the predicate of the quoted speech, while ね adds a friendly tone of confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks all the preceding speech as the quoted content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: いわれました is the polite past passive form of 言う. It shows that the speaker was affected by the words spoken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.why: The speech is put in quotation marks and connected to と. Then the passive form 言われました is used to mean “be told by someone.” The speaker goes with に in the passive structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes “said that...” The subject directly performs the speaking action, so the meaning “was told” is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes being praised, while 言われました only reports the action of being told.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に in this passive sentence with に, which indicates the listener. Here, it indicates the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q24.kobun.cn: 引用内容 + と + 言われる / 言われました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.vi: I went shopping at the food counter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects two nouns and identifies the type of goods at うりば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the shopping takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the noun as the object of the verb しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.why: The place phrase うりばで comes before the action, while かいものを しました form the structure noun + する. の connects two nouns and links them as modifier and modified noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If a specific verb such as 買いました is used, the sentence emphasizes the item bought rather than shopping as a general activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q25.kobun.tip: With activity nouns such as かいもの, をする must be used; do not say かいものをしました by leaving out the particle を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of やすむ in the expression for skipping school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns やすむ into a noun, while が marks that event as something that occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: あります completes the pattern Vることがある and expresses that something occasionally happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.why: The verb やすむ is nominalized with こと to become the subject of あります. The pattern Vることがある expresses something that happens sometimes, not the existence of an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to Vたことがある, the sentence talks about having done something before, so it no longer means that it happens sometimes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: こともある emphasizes that it is also a possible event or case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ことがある as “there is an event,” but after a dictionary-form verb, this pattern usually indicates that something happens occasionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことがある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.vi: The way to use this machine is very complicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the machine being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents the machine as the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the feature of the machine being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending な forms the predicate with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.why: この modifies きかい, forming “this machine.” The structure は + が presents a specific part or feature of the topic. Here, it is the way to use the machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is used, the focus shifts to using the machine being complicated, rather than to the machine’s way of use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put を before ふくざつです, but this adjective needs が to mark the feature being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies ひと and identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: どうも adds an inference based on perception.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: らしい expresses an appearance or typical quality, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.why: The topic is presented first with は. Then どうも gives an inferred judgment. らしい comes at the end to express a quality that seems to fit the image of a man.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with そうだ, the sentence leans toward information heard from someone else, not a perception of manliness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: みたいだ also means “seems,” but it has a more conversational and direct comparison tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse らしい with そうだ, which indicates hearsay, so they need to distinguish the source of the information from the speaker’s perception.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹・N + らしい（です）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the thing in a state or undergoing an action. Here, it is the light.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: つく is an intransitive verb. It describes the light turning on or lighting up by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q6.kobun.why: Because つく is an intransitive verb, the thing that turns on becomes the subject and goes with が. つきました describes an event that has happened and uses the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence changes to a transitive verb and emphasizes that someone turned on the light.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with つく, but が must be used because つく does not directly act on an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.vi: Please tell me why you argued with him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who took part in the argument.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause けんかした comes before わけ to modify the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the reason as the content that must be explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb おしえる with the request ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.why: かれと identifies the person involved in the argument, while けんかした modifies わけ. This reason phrase is the object of おしえて. Then てください turns the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 理由 is used, the meaning “reason” is more direct and formal, while わけ is natural in speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily separate けんかした from わけ in meaning, but this is a clause placed before a noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.vi: Please feel free to share your opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: どうぞ is used to make a gentle invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: じゆうに is an adverbial form that modifies the action of expressing an opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the opinion as the content being expressed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: おっしゃって is the て form of the honorific おっしゃる, connecting to ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: てください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.why: いけんを is the content of the speaking action, while じゆうに describes how it is spoken. おっしゃってください both makes a polite request and uses respectful language toward the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If いってください is used, the meaning is still “please say it,” but the level of respect is lower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use いけんが, but when saying or expressing a specific opinion, they must use いけんを.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q8.tokens.5.m: to say; to express an opinion (honorific)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.vi: I told you that the lecture was canceled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the receiver of the information being communicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the state やすみになる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the result or new state after a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: なった comes before こと to modify the event being communicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: こと turns an event into a noun, while を marks the event as the content being communicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: つたえました is the main predicate and politely describes telling someone the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.why: The receiver of the information goes with に, while the event being reported goes with ことを. The clause こうぎがやすみになった is turned into a noun to serve as the content of つたえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 知らせる is used, the sentence emphasizes making someone know the information rather than communicating the content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 連絡する is used, the meaning is closer to contacting or notifying someone, with less focus on the content being communicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に and を: に is the receiver of the information, while ことを is the content being reported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t121-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形 + ことを + 伝える
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q1.kobun.vi: The sun is about to set.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the whole event and indicates that it will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the state くれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: くれます is the predicate showing the change to a dark sky, used in the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q1.kobun.why: もうすぐ comes before the predicate to show that the event will happen soon. The subject of the natural event is ひ, which goes with が, followed by the predicate くれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 夜になります, the sentence focuses on “the sky becoming night” instead of directly saying that the sun is setting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate くれる here as “give”; in this use, くれる describes the sun setting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q10.kobun.vi: My younger brother said loudly, “I’m home!”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means or manner of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 言いました is the polite past form of 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q10.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and then 大きな modifies こえ. で shows the manner of speaking, while と connects the direct speech to 言いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the way or content that someone is asked to say, rather than simply quoting the exact words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget と after direct speech before verbs such as 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q11.kobun.vi: I looked at the teacher’s photograph.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 先生 with しゃしん, creating the meaning “the teacher’s photograph.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: はいけんしました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q11.kobun.why: 先生の modifies しゃしん, しゃしんを is the object, and はいけんしました completes the predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is “a photograph from the teacher,” emphasizing the source rather than ownership by the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse の, which shows ownership, with から, which shows the source or origin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q12.kobun.sk: Time point + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうべ indicates the time when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the natural event as 雨.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ふりました is the polite past form of ふる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q12.kobun.why: ゆうべ is placed at the beginning to state the time, 雨が is the subject of the natural event, and ふりました ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes that it was raining at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 雨が降る as “rain falls,” but in Japanese this is the natural way to say “it rains.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.vi: I arrived in time for the class to start.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause comes before and modifies 時間, creating the meaning “the time when the class starts.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time point that must be reached in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: まにあいました is the main predicate, meaning that someone arrived in time for a time or deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.why: じゅぎょうがはじまる uses the plain form to modify 時間 directly. The time phrase goes with に as the time point, while まにあいました states the result of arriving in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is “before the class starts,” showing an earlier time rather than emphasizing arriving in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence means “by the deadline when the class starts,” emphasizing the final limit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the particle に directly after the clause じゅぎょうがはじまる, but に must attach to the noun 時間.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that changes to the cured state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: なおりました is the polite past form of なおる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q14.kobun.why: びょうきが is the subject, while なおりました describes the illness changing to a cured state by itself, so を is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is “cured the illness,” with the person who performed the action understood from context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を because they translate it as “treat an illness,” but なおる is an intransitive verb, so it goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.vi: When will the work be finished?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes しごと the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: いつ asks when the work will be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the sentence into a polite question; すみます is the predicate meaning “be finished or completed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.why: しごとは states the topic, いつ comes before the predicate to ask about the time, and か at the end establishes a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 終わりますか is used instead, the sentence still asks when it will end, but it uses a more common expression for “end.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If までに is added, the sentence asks for the deadline by which it must be completed instead of asking generally when it will be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put いつ at the end of the sentence, but question words in Japanese usually come directly before the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q16.kobun.vi: I am free all day today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 一日じゆう refers to a period lasting the whole day; です forms a noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q16.kobun.why: きょうは places the topic first, then 一日じゆう states today's time-related condition. です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 一日中 still means “all day,” but this spelling is more common when kanji is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q16.kobun.tip: Do not understand じゆう here as “free”; 一日じゆう means “all day” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects これ with それ to form a group of objects affected by the same action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks all of これとそれ as the object to be separated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に turns べつ into an adverb that modifies the action してください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to politely ask or request the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q17.kobun.why: The two nouns are connected by と and then marked by を as a group of objects. べつに comes before してください to show how the action is performed, while Vてください creates a polite request.
