default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: The kanji spelling keeps the meaning “please separate them”; only the written form is different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use を immediately after これ if you want both これ and それ to be objects; connect them with と first, then place を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the answer as the object that was made incorrect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: まちがえました is a polite past-tense verb that says the speaker made a mistake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q18.kobun.why: The sentence uses the transitive verb まちがえる, so the object こたえ takes を. The ました form shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern says that the answer itself is wrong, without emphasizing that the speaker made a mistake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q18.kobun.tip: With まちがえる, the object that was made incorrect usually takes を, not が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being described as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun ところ that it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ところです forms a noun predicate and identifies this place as inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q19.kobun.why: ここは is the topic, while ふべんなところ is the noun phrase that describes that place. The adjective な must keep な before the noun, and the whole phrase ends with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to “this is a convenient place”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q19.kobun.tip: Before a noun, the adjective な must have な: ふべんなところ, not ふべんところ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q2.kobun.vi: Mr. and Mrs. Yamada are not at home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states 山田さん as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun るす with a polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q2.kobun.why: The sentence uses the noun るす as the predicate instead of a verb because it describes 山田さん's absence from home. は marks the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes the action of going out and the continuing state, while るすです only indicates being absent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q2.kobun.tip: るすです means “away from home” and does not necessarily say where the person has gone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks cigarettes as the object of the action of quitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: やめました is a polite past-tense verb that describes ending a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q20.kobun.why: たばこ comes before を because it is the object of やめる. The ました form shows that quitting smoking was completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern only says “do not smoke,” and does not necessarily show that the habit has been given up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q20.kobun.tip: やめる goes with を when talking about giving up a specific habit or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes directly before a noun to identify something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は states もんだい as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: かんたんです is the adjective predicate な in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q21.kobun.why: この must stand directly before the noun もんだい to modify it. After stating the topic with は, the adjective かんたんです gives an opinion about the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence also expresses that it is not difficult, but it uses the negative form of the adjective い instead of the affirmative meaning “simple.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q21.kobun.tip: この must always be followed by a noun; do not use この alone before the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The adverb はやく modifies the action かえって and shows the degree or time of going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb かえる takes the て form and then adds も to connect to a pattern for permission or acceptance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: かまいません is a sentence-final expression meaning that there is no problem or that something is allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.why: はやく comes before the verb to modify the action of going home. The structure Vて＋もかまいません expresses permission: it is all right to do that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this sentence keeps almost the same meaning of permission, but the conversational tone is more common.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence changes into a prohibition against doing that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may confuse ても with its usual concessive meaning, but in てもかまいません the whole pattern means permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.tokens.3.m: it is all right; be allowed
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q22.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も ＋ かまいません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.vi: I failed the university entrance exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 大学 with the noun after it and identifies the exam as belonging to the university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the object toward which the action しっぱいする is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: しっぱいしました is a polite past-tense predicate that describes not reaching a goal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.why: 大学の modifies にゅうがくしけん to form the noun phrase “university entrance exam.” にゅうがくしけんに goes with しっぱいする to indicate the object of the failure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means that the speaker passed the exam instead of failing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning remains that the speaker failed the exam, but the expression is more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use を with しっぱいする in this structure; the object usually takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.vi: The store has moved to a new location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks 店 as the subject undergoing a change of location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.ch.1.vi: has moved to a new location
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: うつりました is a polite past-tense predicate describing the store's move to another location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.why: 店が is the subject of the move, while うつりました is the predicate describing the store's movement to another place. が is suitable because the sentence announces a newly occurring change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes that the location or state has changed, rather than directly emphasizing the move to another place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence usually describes a person or household moving house; it is less natural for a store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q24.kobun.tip: Do not translate うつる only as “change”; with 店, this word usually describes moving to another location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks きかい as the subject that is in a faulty state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: こしょうしています uses しています to express the state of the machine being broken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q25.kobun.why: きかいが is the subject of the broken state. こしょうしています expresses a continuing current condition, so it is suitable when saying that the machine is not working properly now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means that the machine has broken down and is still broken, in a more everyday way of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning changes to say that the machine has been repaired and is working again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q25.kobun.tip: ています does not necessarily refer only to an action in progress here; it can also refer to an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.vi: While cleaning the room, I found an old letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the room as the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects かたづける with いる to create the state of cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: いたら creates a conditional or time clause, meaning “while cleaning.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ふるい directly modifies てがみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the letter as the thing that appears as a result of the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects でる with くる, expressing that something appears from inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: きました completes the phrase でてくる and shows that the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.why: The clause へやを かたづけていたら gives the time or condition, and then the main clause states what appeared. でてくる expresses that something came out from inside or from a hidden place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If いたら is replaced with と, the sentence suggests that whenever the action is done, the result usually happens, which is less natural for this accidental event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If でてきました is replaced with 見つかりました, the focus is on “being found,” without emphasizing that the letter came out by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.tip: たら follows いた in this sentence to create the time point “while doing,” rather than only a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q3.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる ＋ たら; Vて ＋ くる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: すごい modifies the noun あめ and describes the intensity of the rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: あめでした is a noun predicate and uses でした to say that the event happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q4.kobun.why: きのうは sets the time as the topic, and then すごい modifies あめ. The structure Nでした changes あめ into a polite past-tense predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes the action of rain falling and the large amount of rain, instead of describing the rain as very heavy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate すごい as “wonderful,” but in this sentence it only means that the rain is very large in amount or very strong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content of the directly quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 言いました is the main verb and expresses a speaking action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q5.kobun.why: The speaker comes first, and the spoken content is inside quotation marks and goes with と. 言いました comes at the end of the sentence to complete the quoted-speech structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 返事しました is used, the sentence emphasizes that this is a reply, not simply a speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q5.kobun.tip: Learners may easily forget と after the quoted content; in this pattern, と is required before 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q6.kobun.sk: N が ＋ honorific V ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the teacher as the subject of the arrival action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: いらっしゃいました is the respectful form of the verb “come,” “go,” or “be,” in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q6.kobun.why: せんせいが states who performs the action, while いらっしゃいました comes at the end as the predicate. The honorific word is used because the subject is someone who should be respected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with きました, the basic meaning is still “has arrived,” but the respectful tone toward the subject is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If いらっしゃいます is used, the action changes from the past “has arrived” to the present or a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q6.kobun.tip: Learners may easily understand いらっしゃる as meaning only “come,” but this word can also mean “go” or “be,” depending on the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being introduced or identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects だんせい with へや, showing that the room belongs to or is intended for men.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: へやです functions as a noun predicate and identifies ここ as a type of room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q7.kobun.why: ここは sets the place as the topic, the phrase だんせいのへや is a noun combined with の, and then です identifies that place as a room for men.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this phrase is used instead, the basic meaning does not change, but the expression is longer and more everyday than だんせい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If the clause だんせいがつかう is used, the sentence emphasizes that men are the people who use the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q7.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use が to connect two nouns, but the relationship of “belonging to or intended for” between the two nouns requires の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the thing being replaced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: とりかえました is a compound verb that expresses replacing an old thing with another thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q8.kobun.why: でんきを is the object before the verb and is marked by を. とりかえました at the end of the sentence shows that the replacement action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あたらしくしました, the sentence emphasizes making it new, without directly emphasizing the action of exchanging the old thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If なおしました is used, the meaning changes to “repaired,” and does not necessarily mean that it was replaced with another thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q8.kobun.tip: Learners may easily separate とりかえる into two separate verbs, but it is one compound verb meaning “change or replace with a new one.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing being evaluated as convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: べんりです is the adjective predicate な, describing the characteristics of traffic at that location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q9.kobun.why: ここは identifies the place range, こうつうが is the thing being evaluated, and べんりです is that thing's quality. The pattern は...が is often used to state a specific feature of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence changes to say that this place is near the station, and no longer evaluates the convenience of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If いいです is used, the tone is broader and more everyday, simply saying that the transportation is good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t122-q9.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use は after こうつう, but in this structure こうつうが is the specific thing described by べんりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before the noun ニュース to refer to news that has been identified in the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes ニュース the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: たしかです functions as the adjective predicate ending in な, expressing the judgment that the news is accurate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q1.kobun.why: その directly modifies ニュース, forming the phrase “that news.” ニュースは is the topic, while たしかです is the comment about the accuracy of the news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes that the news is true, rather than only emphasizing the accuracy of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence means that the news is wrong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q1.kobun.tip: たしか usually refers to information that is reliable or accurate, and is not completely synonymous with ほんとう in every context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: おっしゃる is the respectful form of 言う, while ました expresses an action that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q10.kobun.why: 先生が is the subject of the speaking action and comes before the predicate. おっしゃいました uses respectful honorific language when referring to the teacher's words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this word is used instead, the basic meaning is still “spoke,” but the respectful nuance toward the teacher is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the speaker humbles themself when speaking to a superior. It is not used to show respect for the teacher as the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use おっしゃいました to talk about your own words; it is a respectful honorific for the person being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that 母 is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ゆうはん with したく, creating the modifying phrase “dinner preparation.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks したく as the object of the verb する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する. It connects with います to create the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: います is the auxiliary verb in the pattern ている. It shows an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.why: The phrase ゆうはんのしたく forms the object of する and goes with を. The て form connects して with います to express an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If しました is used instead, the sentence only says that the mother finished preparing, without emphasizing the action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ている for meaning only “already,” but in this sentence it means “is doing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q16.kobun.vi: The steak at that restaurant is delicious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects レストラン with ステーキ, showing a relationship of ownership or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that ステーキ is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしい is an い adjective used as the predicate. です is added to make the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q16.kobun.why: あの and レストランの modify the main noun ステーキ, respectively. After the topic ステーキは comes the adjective predicate おいしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of は, the sentence focuses on identifying the steak as delicious, rather than presenting it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q16.kobun.tip: An い-ending adjective such as おいしい does not add な before a noun and keeps い unchanged when it comes before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks ふく as the object of the washing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: せんたくしました is the polite past form of せんたくする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q17.kobun.why: The noun ふく comes before を because it is the thing affected by the action. せんたくしました is the predicate and shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If せんたくしています is used instead, it means that someone is washing the clothes or is usually in the state of washing them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use に to mark the thing being washed; the direct object must go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.vi: His voice can be heard all the way outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かれ with こえ, creating the phrase “his voice.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that こえ is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: まで shows the range or point that the sound reaches.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: きこえます describes sound naturally reaching the ears, without emphasizing that the listener actively listens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.why: かれのこえ is a noun phrase serving as the topic, while そとまで adds the point that the sound can reach. きこえます is suitable because the sentence describes the natural ability to hear the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 聞きます is used instead, it means that someone actively listens, not that the sound can be heard naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If まで is replaced with にも, the sentence only says that the sound can also be heard outside. It does not emphasize “all the way” outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 聞きます for every meaning of “hear,” but sound that can be heard naturally usually uses 聞こえます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that そのけん is the topic of understanding or acceptance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: しょうちしました is the polite past predicate. It expresses that the speaker understood or accepted the content being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q19.kobun.why: そのけん is made the topic with は, and then しょうちしました serves as the predicate showing the speaker's response. This order sounds natural when the speaker wants to make clear which content they understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If わかりました is used instead, it is a more common and neutral way to say “understood,” while しょうちしました is more polite and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q19.kobun.tip: しょうちしました is often used in polite communication. It should not be understood simply as the past form of a verb meaning “know.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes おたく the topic, while おたく is a polite way to ask about the listener's home or place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: どちらですか is a polite question expression used to ask about a place in a refined way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q2.kobun.why: おたくは states the thing being asked about, while どちらですか asks about its location. どちら is more polite than どこ, so it suits a formal question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the basic meaning does not change, but the expression is simpler and less polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence is more polite and uses a formal expression to ask about someone's residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q2.kobun.tip: どちら can mean “where” in a question about location, not only “which side” or “which one.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q20.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks tomorrow as the topic of the existence sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing or event that exists in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is an existence predicate used for things or events that are not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q20.kobun.why: あしたは sets the time context, while イベントが is the thing that exists in that context. あります comes at the end of the sentence to complete the structure “at a certain time, there is a thing or event.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If the subject is a person or animal, use います instead of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は for イベント, but in the pattern “there is ...,” an existing noun usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.vi: This computer can be used comfortably.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.sk: この N は ＋ Adverb に ＋ Vできます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies パソコン and shows which computer is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks パソコン as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に turns じゆう into an adverb and modifies りようできます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: できます expresses the ability to use something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.why: The sentence makes パソコン the topic and then uses the adverb じゆうに to describe how it is used. できます at the end of the sentence expresses the ability to use the computer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If かってに is used instead, the sentence means using something as one pleases, which may imply that it is not allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand じゆうに as freedom in the sense of doing whatever one wants, but in this sentence the suitable meaning is comfortably, without restrictions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.vi: Before going to bed, I drink milk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The dictionary-form verb ねる comes before 前に to show that an action happens before a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the point in time before which the action of drinking milk happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks ぎゅうにゅう as the object being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: のみます is the main predicate, using the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.why: The clause ねる comes before 前に to create the point in time “before going to bed.” After the time expression come the object ぎゅうにゅうを and the main action のみます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ねたあとで, the meaning changes to drinking milk after sleeping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ねるまでに, the sentence emphasizes that the milk must be finished before bedtime.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q22.kobun.tip: After 前に, use the dictionary-form V, not the past form such as ねたまえに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.vi: In the evening, I always watch TV.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.sk: N は + Adverb + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks よる as the time period chosen as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも is an adverb of frequency that modifies the action of watching TV.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks テレビ as the object of the action of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: みます is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.why: よるは gives the general time frame, while いつも shows the frequency of the action. テレビを comes directly before みます because it is the object of the verb “watch.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If よるは is replaced with まいばん, the meaning becomes more specific: “every evening,” without making the evening the topic with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If よるに is used, に marks the time when the action takes place, giving more focus to the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use を after よる when stating the time; よるは is the topic here, while テレビを is the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies かばん and identifies the bag being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks かばん as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: たかい changes to たかくない to form the negative of the い adjective, and です is then added to keep the polite style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q24.kobun.why: かばんは is the thing being evaluated, while たかくないです is the polite negative predicate describing it. With the い adjective, い changes to くない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with やすいです, the sentence positively states that the bag is cheap, with a stronger meaning than “not expensive.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with たかくありません, the basic meaning does not change, but the expression is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q24.kobun.tip: Do not say たかいじゃないです in this basic pattern; the い adjective must change to たかくない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks きのう as the time put forward as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: でした is the polite past form of はれです, serving as the predicate for yesterday’s weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q25.kobun.why: きのうは puts the time at the beginning of the sentence, while はれでした states the weather at that time. でした shows that the state belongs to the past and keeps the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with はれだった, the meaning does not change, but the expression becomes casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If か is added, the sentence becomes a question about whether it was sunny yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q25.kobun.tip: With a noun such as はれ, it does not change like the い adjective; simply use はれでした to express the polite past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.vi: I said goodbye to my friend at the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of saying goodbye takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates a person who participates in or carries out the action together with someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes an action that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.why: The place 駅で comes first, followed by the person saying goodbye together with the speaker, 友だちと, and then the predicate わかれました. The particle と fits the meaning of saying goodbye to someone together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence can shift to the meaning of saying goodbye to a friend, focusing on the person receiving the words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If と一緒に is used, the sentence emphasizes more clearly that the action is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に to mean “with,” but when talking about saying goodbye to someone, わかれる usually uses と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the work as the object being continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: つづけます is the predicate and describes continuing to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q4.kobun.why: しごとを is the object of the action, while つづけます comes at the end of the sentence to complete the meaning “continue the work.” The particle を connects the noun to the verb describing an action performed on the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is to stop an action rather than continue it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If a verb is used before つづける, the sentence emphasizes continuing to perform a specific action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を because Vietnamese does not require an object marker, but しごとをつづける needs を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.sk: Time + V辞書形 のは + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: あした states the time of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 来る is nominalized with の, and then は makes the whole phrase “coming tomorrow” the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: むりです is the predicate and evaluates coming as impossible or too difficult to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.why: あした adds the time to 来る, while 来るの turns the action “come” into something that can be evaluated. は marks it as the topic, and then むりです gives the judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with のがむずかしい, the sentence emphasizes that coming is difficult rather than stating that it is completely impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことはできない is used, the tone is more direct and emphasizes that the action cannot be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand の as “of,” but in this sentence の turns the verb 来る into the noun “coming.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.vi: The air is very cold today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic and the time being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the air as the subject that is in a cold state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the cold state and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes the current state resulting from the air becoming cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.why: きょうは sets the scope of the comment as today, くうきが is the subject of the state, and とても adds the degree. ひえています describes the air as currently being cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 寒いです is used, the sentence directly says that the weather or a person feels cold, without clearly stating that the air has become cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 冷えました is used, the sentence emphasizes the change to becoming cold, not the continuing current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate ています simply as “be,” but here it mainly describes an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q6.tokens.5.m: is becoming cold; has become cold
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person receiving the congratulations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks おいわい as the content being said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 言いました is the polite past predicate that ends the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q7.kobun.why: The person receiving the congratulations comes first with に, the content of the congratulations comes next with を, and 言いました comes last. This order clearly expresses “say congratulations to someone.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used for a quotation, the sentence gives the exact words or specific content that was said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 祝う is used, the sentence changes to directly congratulating a person or celebrating an event, without focusing on the words spoken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for the recipient, but the recipient of spoken words usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the clothes as the subject that changes into a dirty state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb showing a change of state, meaning that the clothes became dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q8.kobun.why: ふくが is the subject of the change, while よごれました shows the result that the clothes became dirty. が is suitable because the sentence focuses on the change in the clothes' state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 汚す, it means that someone makes the clothes dirty, so a subject performing the action is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 汚い is used, the sentence only describes the clothes as dirty and does not stress the process of becoming dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with ふく, but よごれる is an intransitive verb, so the thing that becomes dirty goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q9.kobun.vi: The wind is blowing very fiercely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: An adjective that modifies かぜ and shows a strong and fierce degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the blowing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb ふく in the ている form describes an action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q9.kobun.why: The subject かぜが comes before the predicate ふいています. The adjective ひどい comes before the noun to describe the strength of the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this word is used instead, the sentence only emphasizes that the wind is strong, with a milder negative and fierce feeling than ひどい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ひどい only as “bad,” but in this sentence it emphasizes how fierce the wind is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem that carries the meaning of the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the ending that forms an い-ending adjective in the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q11.kobun.why: The input is a standalone い-ending adjective. The whole word expresses the feeling that a person, story, or thing is uninteresting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning focuses more on feeling bored or having nothing to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q11.kobun.tip: Do not change ない into ありません when only the dictionary form of the adjective is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the reading of a word describing a step-by-step change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: This part repeats the previous sound to create a gradual, ongoing feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q12.kobun.why: The input is a standalone adverb that usually modifies a following verb or adjective. The repeated sound gives the meaning of changing slowly over time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning emphasizes little by little or in small parts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use だんだん for an action that happens suddenly or only once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem meaning lively and full of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the ending of an な-ending adjective in the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q13.kobun.why: The input is a standalone な-ending adjective. When modifying a noun, this word needs な; when used as a predicate, it usually combines with だ or です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to noisy or annoying, and does not necessarily suggest a lively, crowded atmosphere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q13.kobun.tip: When placed before a noun, do not remove な from にぎやかな町.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the word meaning cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the final part that completes the word's reading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q14.kobun.why: This is a vocabulary entry given as a reading, not a complete sentence, so it has no full subject, object, or predicate relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q14.kobun.tip: Do not confuse げんいん with りゆう; りゆう usually means a reason, while げんいん emphasizes the cause that produces an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the verb describing a tired state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t124-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the dictionary-form ending of the verb.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q2.kobun.why: This is a noun for a feeling of peace of mind. It often combines with する or です to describe the speaker’s state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: 安全 emphasizes the safety of a person or thing, while 安心 emphasizes a feeling of peace of mind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use 安心 to directly say that an object is safe; 安全 is usually used in that case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The two parts combine to form the noun 熱心, which often combines with に to show enthusiasm for something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q22.kobun.why: This vocabulary word describes an attitude or level of dedication. In a sentence, 熱心 usually goes with に to state the object of the person’s focus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: 真面目 generally suggests being serious and hardworking, while 熱心 emphasizes enthusiasm for a specific task or field.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q22.kobun.tip: Do not translate に after 熱心 as 'at'; this particle marks the object that the person is enthusiastic about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q24.tokens.0.m: to get down; to get off a vehicle
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The two parts combine to form the noun 輸入, which refers to bringing goods from another country into one’s own country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q25.kobun.why: 輸入 is a noun for importing and can also be used as a verb when combined with する. In a sentence, imported goods are usually marked with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: 輸出 means export, that is, sending goods abroad, in the opposite direction from 輸入.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q25.kobun.tip: Distinguish the direction of the goods: 輸入 means into the country, while 輸出 means abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the noun こしょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: This part completes the kana spelling of the noun こしょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q5.kobun.why: こしょう is a noun for the condition of a machine or device being broken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this word is used instead, the meaning changes to repairing, not the condition of being broken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q5.kobun.tip: Do not confuse こしょう, meaning 故障, with 胡椒, meaning pepper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the noun げんいん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: This part completes the kana spelling of the noun げんいん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q6.kobun.why: げんいん is a noun for the reason or cause that leads to an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this word is used instead, it means a reason in general and places less emphasis on the cause that leads to a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q6.kobun.tip: Do not mix up the sound order in げんいん; this word is read as げんいん, not げいんん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the first part of the な じょうぶ adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: This part completes the kana spelling of the word じょうぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q7.kobun.why: じょうぶ is an な adjective used to describe sturdy objects or people in good health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: In the negative form, the meaning changes to not sturdy or not healthy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q7.kobun.tip: When modifying a noun, use じょうぶな, not じょうぶ directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the い やさしい adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: い is the ending of the い adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q8.kobun.why: やさしい is an い adjective that describes a gentle, kind, or good-natured personality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If written as 易しい, the meaning changes to easy or simple.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t129-q8.kobun.tip: Use the context to distinguish 優しい, meaning gentle, from 易しい, meaning easy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vi: The bus departed a little late at half past 12.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.sk: N は + Adv + Vて + Time に + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the bus is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the state of being late with the later action of departing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the time when the departure happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of 出発する and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.why: The sentence makes the bus the topic, then adds the degree of lateness and the time using modifying parts. The form て connects the state of being late with the action of departing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with a time, but the time when an action happens usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vi: My husband will come home at around 8 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the husband is the topic of the information about when he will come home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ごろ indicates the approximate time when the action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: かえってきます combines 帰る with くる to express returning toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and the approximate time comes before the predicate. かえってきます emphasizes returning to the point being discussed, usually the speaker’s home or location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used, the sentence means 'come home by around 8 o’clock or earlier,' emphasizing a deadline rather than the expected time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q10.kobun.tip: ごろ indicates an approximate point in time. It is not used to express a period lasting for some time, such as 間.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vi: I want to go to the aquarium that I saw on TV.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means or source of information that the speaker watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause comes before 水族館 to modify this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of 行きたいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: たい attaches to the verb stem to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Vます omit ます + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.why: The phrase テレビで見た comes before 水族館 to identify which aquarium it is. After the place noun, に marks the destination and 行きたいです expresses the desire to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, the main meaning is still going to the aquarium, but the emphasis is more on the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If を見たい is used, the meaning is wanting to look at the aquarium, not wanting to go there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q11.kobun.tip: When saying that you want to go to a place, use place + に/へ + 行きたい, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vi: To stay healthy, I go to school by bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: のために indicates the purpose or reason for going to school by bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means of transport used to go to school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of the action 通っています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 通っている describes going to school repeatedly and continuing to do so.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.why: The purpose is stated first, followed by the means of transport and the destination, and then the main action. 通っている is suitable because going to school is a repeated activity, not a single trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used instead of に, the sentence is still correct but places slightly less focus on going toward the school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 通っています is replaced with 行っています, the sentence only says that someone is going or usually goes, without clearly emphasizing regular commuting as 通う does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q12.kobun.tip: 通う already means going back and forth many times, so it should not be understood as only making one trip to school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vi: My hobby is collecting foreign stamps.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun がいこく with the noun きって, forming the phrase “foreign stamps.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb 集める.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb 集める comes before の to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the content identified as a hobby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.why: The phrase がいこくのきってを is the object of the action 集める. The form 集めるの turns the whole action into a noun, and then が is used to say that this action is a hobby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing の with こと still turns the action into a noun, but the tone is more formal and general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget を after the object and confuse の in this pattern with の, which only shows possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.vi: Shall we go skiing together this winter?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ことし with 冬, identifying the winter being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this winter the time-related topic of the invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: いっしょに modifies the action of skiing and shows that it is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the activity スキーをする being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: しませんか uses a negative question to make a polite invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.why: ことしの冬 identifies the time, and は makes that time the topic. After the adverb いっしょに, the activity スキーをする ends with the invitation しませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ましょうか, the sentence sounds more like a proposal to do something together or a direct request for the listener’s opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate しませんか as an ordinary negative question and miss its meaning as an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.vi: When I do not understand a word, it is very inconvenient if I do not have a dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.sk: Clause とき + N が + Aな でないと + Aな です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object understood in the clause わからない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates a time or situation; the preceding clause modifies とき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject said to be present or absent in this condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: ないと connects the condition “not having a dictionary” with the inconvenient result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends the adjective predicate な 不便 and states the result of the preceding condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.why: The clause わからないとき sets the context first. The condition じしょがないと comes directly before the result 不便です, so the relationship “if there is no dictionary, it is inconvenient” is clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ないと is replaced with なければ, the conditional meaning is similar, but the tone is more formal and less conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ないと here for “must,” but in this sentence it connects a condition with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.vi: I have already forgotten the vocabulary I learned yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the past tense comes before ことば to modify the vocabulary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: もう modifies わすれてしまいました and emphasizes that it has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいました expresses a completed action, often with a feeling of regret or against one’s wishes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.why: きのう identifies the time of 習った. The clause 習った comes before ことば to narrow the meaning to “the words learned,” and then ことばを serves as the object of わすれてしまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If わすれました is used, it only states that the words were forgotten, without emphasizing regret or completely losing them from memory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the modifying clause after the noun, while Japanese always places 習った before ことば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.vi: The color of this bird’s feathers is very beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this bird the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 羽 with いろ, forming the phrase “the color of the feathers or wings.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the predicate きれいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: きれい is the な adjective used as the predicate, ending politely with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.why: このとりは names the general object, while 羽のいろが names the specific part being evaluated. とても comes before きれいです to increase the degree of beauty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If you say 羽がきれいです, you directly comment that the feathers or wings are beautiful, without focusing specifically on their color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use は for いろ, but が is more suitable because いろ is the direct subject of きれいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.vi: Who is the person wearing that white sweater?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: しろい comes before セーター to modify the sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects セーター with 方, identifying the person through the sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 方 is a polite way to refer to a person; は makes the person wearing the sweater the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: どなたですか is a polite way to ask about that person’s identity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.why: あの and しろい identify the sweater, and then セーターの方 uses this feature to refer to the person. は marks the person whose identity is being asked about, while どなたですか forms a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 方 is replaced with 人, the meaning is still “person,” but the expression is less polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand 方 here as “direction”; in the pattern セーターの方, 方 is read as かた and refers politely to a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q19.kobun.vi: The goods in this supermarket are very fresh.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks this supermarket as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the goods as the thing being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q19.kobun.why: The sentence makes the location the topic with は, then states the goods with が, and uses the adjective な as the predicate. が clearly identifies the thing that has the quality of being “fresh”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use を before an adjective; the thing being described usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vi: I am enjoying my daily life.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks daily life as the thing being enjoyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て combines with います to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.why: The object of the action comes before を, while the verb in the form ています comes at the end of the sentence to show an ongoing activity. The phrase の links 毎日 with 生活, creating the meaning “daily life.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q2.kobun.tip: Do not always translate ています as “already”; in this sentence, it emphasizes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.vi: Write “sama” after the other person's name.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あいて with the following noun and shows possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 名まえの modifies あとの, creating the phrase “after the name.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the position or time when 様 is written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the word that is written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 書きます is the predicate and uses the form ます to express a polite action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases gradually narrow the meaning to “after the other person's name.” The phrase showing position goes with に, while 様 is the thing being written, so it goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q20.kobun.tip: に in あとのに shows position or time, not the object marker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q21.kobun.vi: I went to a Thai restaurant with a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と shows the person who performs the action together with someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the phrase タイ料理 with the noun みせ, creating the meaning “Thai restaurant.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of the verb 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q21.kobun.why: The person who went with the speaker is shown by と, the type of restaurant is formed with Nの, and the destination goes with に. 行きました at the end of the sentence carries the main information and shows that the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q21.kobun.tip: と here means “together with,” not と, which is used to quote speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q22.kobun.vi: I will have an examination at a large hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before the noun and modifies 病院.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で shows where the examination takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content or object of the action します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: します is the predicate and combines with the noun けんさ to create the meaning “carry out an examination.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q22.kobun.why: The adjective 大きい comes before 病院 to describe the hospital. The location of the action uses で, while the activity being carried out uses を before します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q22.kobun.tip: Distinguish で, which shows where an action takes place, from に, which shows a destination or a place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q23.kobun.vi: Let's get off at the next station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies えき, creating the phrase “next station.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で shows the place where someone gets off a train or vehicle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 降りましょう uses the base form 降りる, removes る, and then adds ましょう to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q23.kobun.why: The next station is identified by the phrase つぎのえき, while で shows where to get off. ましょう comes at the end of the sentence to make an invitation or suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q23.kobun.tip: 降りる is read as おりる; when it connects with ましょう, use the stem ます 降り-.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.vi: I can clearly hear the voice from the next room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with へや, creating the phrase “next room.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: へやの modifies 声, identifying the voice as coming from the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the sound that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: よく is an adverb that modifies 聞こえます and shows how clearly the sound is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞こえます describes a sound that naturally reaches the ears or can be heard, without emphasizing the intention to listen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases identify the location and source of the voice in order. With 聞こえる, the sound that is heard becomes the subject and goes with が, while よく describes how clearly it is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 聞きます, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker intentionally listens or asks, instead of the sound being heard naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 聞けます is used, the sentence means that the sound can be heard under certain conditions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q24.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 聞こえる, meaning “be heard naturally,” with 聞く, meaning “listen or ask intentionally.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q25.kobun.sk: N は + Location で + Vた + んですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the picture being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the place where the picture was taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: んですか creates a question tone for confirmation or a gentle request for an explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q25.kobun.why: The topic is placed first with は, and then the location with で comes before the verb. とったんですか uses the past form together with んですか to ask about an event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this form, the question becomes more direct and neutral, with less of a confirmation-seeking tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に with the place where a picture was taken, but the place where an action happens must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vi: I want to travel to Thailand during the New Year holiday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.0.vi: as for the New Year holiday
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the New Year holiday the time-based topic of the desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement to Thailand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the purpose or accompanying activity of the verb 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: たい is attached after the verb stem 行き to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.why: は sets a time as the topic, へ shows the destination, and に gives the purpose of going. 行きたいです places the desire at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence still says that the speaker wants to travel, but it emphasizes carrying out the travel activity rather than linking it directly to 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may easily leave out に in 旅行に行く, but に here connects a noun showing an activity with 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vi: I want to try reading a Japanese novel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with 小説, showing that the novel is related to Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the novel as the object of trying to read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 読んでみる expresses trying to do something, while たい turns that desire into the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.why: The phrase 日本の comes before 小説 to modify this noun. 小説を is the object, while 読んでみたいです ends the sentence and expresses the desire to try reading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 読みたいです is used, the sentence only means wanting to read, without emphasizing the idea of trying to read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget て before みる; they must say 読んでみたい, not 読みてみたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vi: Teacher Tanaka's explanation is very easy to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with 説明, creating the meaning “Teacher Tanaka's explanation.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the explanation as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりやすい is an adjective ending in い that serves as the predicate, with the degree strengthened by とても.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.why: The possessive phrase 田中先生の comes before the noun 説明. After 説明 is presented as the topic with は, とても modifies the adjective わかりやすい at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes the explanation as the object with the quality of being easy to understand, instead of presenting it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put の in the wrong position; the owner must come before の, followed by the owned noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vi: That person is Mr. Tanaka's wife.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the identified person as Mr. Tanaka's wife.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 田中さん with 奥さん, showing a possessive or family relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the subject with the noun showing a status or relationship at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.why: が identifies the person being discussed, while 田中さんの奥さん is the noun phrase used for identification. です is placed at the end to complete the polite noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the sentence only presents that person as the topic; が is more suitable when identifying who that person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は instead of が in an identification sentence, making the identifying meaning weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vi: A famous singer lives in the neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the singer lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in な connects to the noun after it and modifies “singer.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject living in the neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 住んでいます expresses the current state of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.why: The place is stated first with に, followed by the subject with が and the state of residence at the end. ゆうめいな comes before かしゅ to limit this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence emphasizes where an action takes place rather than where someone lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で with 住む, but a place of residence usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vi: Many customers have been lining up since morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting time of the line-up state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a quantity word with the modified noun 客.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the people who are lining up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ならんでいます expresses the state of many people having formed a line.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.why: から sets the starting point, the quantity phrase comes before the noun, and が identifies the customers as the subject of the line-up state. The predicate ています is placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used, the meaning becomes lining up until morning, which is opposite to the starting point in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q8.kobun.tip: Do not confuse から, meaning “from,” with まで, meaning “until”; these two particles identify different ends of a time period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vi: The company is located in central Osaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the company as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the company exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is used for the existence or location of objects, places, and organizations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.why: The company is made the topic, and the location is placed before the predicate with に. あります is suitable because the company is presented as an organization existing at that location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to “working in central Osaka,” so it no longer indicates the company's location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t13-q9.kobun.tip: With あります indicating a location of existence, the place usually goes with に, not で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q1.tokens.0.m: go down; get off a vehicle
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q16.kobun.why: This is an adverb showing the result after a long process, and it usually comes before the predicate. It has no particle and does not form a special connecting pattern.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q19.kobun.why: This word indicates a sufficient or just-enough degree. It can be used as the adjective な or as an adverb when に is added. In a sentence, it usually modifies a noun or a predicate expressing quantity or degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: 足りる indicates that the quantity meets the requirement, while じゅうぶん emphasizes a sufficient degree or that nothing more is needed.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: とても indicates a very high degree, while ずいぶん usually suggests a considerable increase compared with before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ずいぶん as “very” every time, but they should notice its sense of a clear change or exceeding expectations.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: お辞儀 is the action of bowing with the body, while 挨拶 is broader and can be a spoken greeting or a greeting action.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: 断念する has a formal tone and emphasizes the decision to give up a plan or goal.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t130-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced by 絶対に, the emphasis is still strong, but 絶対に can also be used with affirmative sentences, while けっして usually goes with a negative form.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t131-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds a time reference, showing that something has already happened or that a time is approaching, depending on the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t131-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: すぐ modifies the following event and expresses a very short period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t131-q11.kobun.why: もうすぐ is an adverbial phrase showing that an event will happen soon. It usually comes before a time noun or before the predicate to add a time reference.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t131-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: 最近 also means recently and is usually more neutral, while このごろ has a natural conversational tone.
