default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q20.kobun.why: さしあげる is the humble form of あげる. It is commonly used with the recipient に and the thing given を. The dictionary form comes before まえに to say “before doing that.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あげる, it simply describes giving or presenting something in the normal way and does not clearly show the speaker’s humility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with くれる, the direction of the action changes to someone giving something to the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q20.kobun.tip: You must identify the direction of giving and receiving before using さしあげる; do not use it for every case of “give.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q20.tokens.0.m: humble form of あげる: humbly give; present
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the word ちゅうし when written in hiragana.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the ending combined with ちゅう to form the noun ちゅうし.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q21.kobun.why: ちゅうし is a noun. In a complete sentence, it can combine with に なります to describe an event changing into a canceled or suspended state. The given word itself is only one vocabulary item, not a complete sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 延期する, it means postponing something to another time, with the plan to hold it again, not necessarily canceling it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with やめる, it describes the subject actively stopping or giving up something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q21.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 中止 with 延期; 中止 usually does not clearly say that it will be held again at another time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the verb あやまる and does not express the complete meaning by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: This part completes the dictionary form of the verb あやまる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q23.kobun.why: あやまる is a verb in its basic form. It often acts as the predicate or comes before another grammar pattern. The dictionary form ends in る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q23.kobun.tip: Do not confuse あやまる with あやしい, because あやまる is the verb meaning “apologize.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the repeated adverb とうとう, which modifies the event being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The repeated part completes the adverb とうとう and shows the result after a process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q25.kobun.why: とうとう comes before the predicate to show that the event finally happened after a period of waiting or a long process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ついに, it also means “finally,” but it more strongly emphasizes an achieved result or an event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use とうとう for an event that happens immediately, because this word usually suggests a process before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q3.tokens.0.m: send; see someone off; take someone somewhere
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: もう is an adverb. When it comes before すぐ, it creates the meaning “soon, before long.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: すぐ modifies the event that follows and indicates a very near time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q7.kobun.why: もうすぐ is an adverbial phrase describing an event that is about to happen. It usually comes before the predicate or the predicted event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with すぐに shifts the meaning toward “immediately” and does not emphasize that the event is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate もう here as “already” on its own, because もうすぐ is a fixed phrase meaning “soon.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q8.kobun.why: This is a vocabulary reading item, so there is no sentence structure to analyze. The two parts are combined in the correct order to form the reading of the word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q8.kobun.tip: Note that けい is pronounced with the double sound え, not as き.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q9.kobun.why: This is a vocabulary reading item, so the first sound and the remaining sound must be combined correctly. じゅつ is pronounced with the combined sound じゅ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t133-q9.kobun.tip: Do not pronounce じゅつ as じゆつ; ゅ must be the small character.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the verb おどろく and does not form a complete predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The ending く completes the dictionary form of the verb おどろく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q1.kobun.why: おどろく is a verb describing the subject’s reaction of surprise. Its dictionary form can act as the predicate or connect to another grammar pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with びっくりする, it still means “be surprised,” but it is more conversational and informal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use おどろく as an adjective; when it acts as the predicate, it must keep the appropriate verb form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: This part carries the main meaning of the verb 行う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: う completes the dictionary form of the verb 行う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q15.kobun.why: 行う is a verb describing the carrying out of an activity, event, or plan. The activity name is often the topic with は, the location uses で, and the action being carried out usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 開催する, the focus is more on organizing an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the place where this action happens; the activity location usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: おもいだ is the stem of the verb おもいだす.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: す completes the dictionary form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q17.kobun.why: This verb expresses restoring a memory or image in the mind. Its dictionary form consists of the stem おもいだ and the ending す.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the meaning is “be able to remember.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate おもいだす as “think of,” but this word emphasizes remembering something already known or experienced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q19.tokens.0.m: indicates the part that comes before
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the beginning of the adverb しっかり and has no separate role when separated from the whole word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: This part completes the adverb しっかり, which is used to modify a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q2.kobun.why: しっかり comes before a verb to show that an action is done firmly, carefully, or completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ちゃんと, the nuance focuses on doing something correctly or as required.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate しっかり only as “strong”; its specific meaning changes according to the following verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: くらべ is the stem of the verb くらべる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: る completes the dictionary form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q21.kobun.why: This verb describes placing two or more objects side by side to examine their similarities and differences. Its dictionary form consists of the stem くらべ and the ending る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the meaning is “be able to compare” or “can compare.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use と after both objects, while くらべる usually uses と to connect the objects being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks けが as the object of the verb する, forming the phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: する completes the noun phrase けが and makes it the verb “be injured” in this usage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q23.kobun.why: けが is a noun and combines with をする to form the expression “be injured.” を connects the noun to する and marks the content of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 傷つく, it emphasizes being hurt or damaged, rather than the fixed phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 病気になる, the meaning changes to becoming ill, not being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q23.kobun.tip: Do not say けががする; the correct phrase is けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: けんきゅう is a noun for the content of research and combines with する to form a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: する changes the noun けんきゅう into the verb “research” in the phrase けんきゅうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q24.kobun.why: けんきゅう is a Sino-Japanese noun that forms a compound verb meaning to carry out research when it comes before する. This structure is common with many action nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 調べる, the meaning is closer to looking up or checking a specific matter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 学ぶ, it emphasizes learning and gaining knowledge, not necessarily doing research.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q24.kobun.tip: When changing tense or form, only change する into している, した, or しない; do not change けんきゅう separately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: ごらん is the respectful vocabulary form corresponding to 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: になる combines with ごらん to form the respectful expression ご覧になる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q25.kobun.why: ご覧になる is a respectful pattern for describing the action 見る of a person who should be respected. になる comes after ご覧 to create a respectful expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 見る, the sentence becomes ordinary speech and does not show respect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 拝見する, it is humble language used for the speaker’s act of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use ご覧になる for your own act of looking in a context that requires humble language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q25.kobun.cn: お／ご ＋ Vます語幹 ＋ になる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: あんない is the noun stem of the compound verb formed with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: する changes あんない into a verb meaning to guide or show the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q6.kobun.why: The pattern Nする is formed by adding する after an action noun. Therefore, あんないする works as a verb and can take an object with を or indicate a direction with へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If あんないになる is used, it means becoming guidance or being arranged as guidance, not directly guiding someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q6.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate する as “do” in every case; with あんないする, the whole phrase means “guide.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the verb いじめる, expressing the action of bullying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The ending る completes the group 2 verb in its dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q7.kobun.why: いじめる is a group 2 verb in the dictionary form, used to describe bullying a person or animal. The affected object usually comes before を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with からかう, the tone is lighter and focuses on teasing, which does not necessarily continue or cause harm like いじめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse temporary teasing with いじめる, which usually suggests bullying or tormenting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: ようい is a noun meaning preparation and combines with する to form a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: する changes ようい into the verb よういする, meaning “prepare.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q2.kobun.why: ようい is an action noun that combines with する to form the verb “prepare.” When changing its form, する is the part that changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 準備する, the meaning is almost the same, but it is more common and more formal in some contexts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 用意がある, it only says that preparation is available, not that someone is preparing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q2.kobun.tip: Do not change ようい into よういて; change する into して, した, or しない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: ほうそう means broadcasting and combines with する to form a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: する changes the noun before it into a group 3 verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q20.kobun.why: ほうそうする is a compound verb made from the noun ほうそう and する. When changing to て, する changes into して, and when combined with います, it describes an action that is being broadcast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 放映する, it still means broadcast, but it is usually used for films, programs, or content that is shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q20.kobun.tip: With the verb Nする, do not put a particle between the noun and する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the verb stem meaning to be mistaken or do something incorrectly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: る completes the dictionary form of the group 2 verb まちがえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q21.kobun.why: まちがえる is a verb in the dictionary form, used to state the basic meaning of the word. In a sentence, the verb can change into forms such as まちがえた or まちがえます depending on tense and style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 間違う, it also means being wrong or making a mistake, but its usage and tone differ from the transitive verb まちがえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that まちがえる usually takes the object marker を, for example 答えを間違える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the verb みつける, expressing the action of finding or discovering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: る completes the dictionary form of the group 2 verb みつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q23.kobun.why: みつける is a transitive verb that usually takes an object with を, such as 鍵をみつける. The dictionary form can come before ことができない to express being unable to do that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 見つかる, the subject is the thing that is found, and the sentence becomes intransitive; it does not use an object with を in the same way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q23.kobun.tip: Do not confuse みつける, “find,” with みつかる, “be found.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem of the verb むかえる, expressing the action of going to pick someone up or welcoming them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: る completes the dictionary form of the group 2 verb むかえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q24.kobun.why: むかえる is a transitive verb, so the person or thing being picked up usually takes を. When combined with ために, the dictionary form むかえる comes before ために to state the purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 出迎える, the meaning focuses more strongly on going out to pick someone up, usually at the place of arrival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit the particle を before the person being picked up, but むかえる usually needs お客さまを迎える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun せんそう provides the meaning of the verb サ変 when combined with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: する changes the noun せんそう into the verb “wage war.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q4.kobun.why: せんそうする is formed by combining the noun せんそう directly with する. It is a サ変 verb, so the whole phrase can change like a verb, for example せんそうした or せんそうしない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 戦争になる is used, the meaning changes to “become a war” or “a war breaks out,” emphasizing a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q4.kobun.tip: Do not add を between せんそう and する when forming a fixed compound verb such as せんそうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun ちゅうしゃ provides the meaning of the verb サ変 when combined with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: する changes ちゅうしゃ into a verb meaning “give an injection.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q6.kobun.why: ちゅうしゃする is a combination of the nouns ちゅうしゃ and する, forming the verb サ変. Before こと, the whole verb becomes a noun phrase used as the object of evaluation or emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 注射を受ける means “receive an injection,” focusing on the person receiving the injection rather than the act of injecting in general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q6.kobun.tip: Distinguish ちゅうしゃする, “give an injection,” from 駐車する, “park a car”; they sound the same but use different kanji and have different meanings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem expressing the meaning of conveying or passing on information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: る completes the verb つたえる in its dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q7.kobun.why: つたえる is a group 2 verb made up of the stem つたえ and the ending る. It usually uses を to state the content being conveyed and に to state the recipient of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 伝わる means “be conveyed or understood,” focusing on information reaching the recipient by itself rather than someone actively conveying it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q7.kobun.tip: With つたえる, the person conveying the information usually uses は or が, the content uses を, and the recipient usually uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the stem expressing the meaning of taking or sending something to a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: る completes the verb とどける in its dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q8.kobun.why: とどける is a group 2 verb in the dictionary form, made up of the stem とどけ and the ending る. In a sentence, the item being delivered usually uses を, while the destination uses に or まで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 届く means “arrive or be delivered,” focusing on the item reaching the destination by itself rather than the sender delivering it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q8.kobun.tip: Distinguish とどける, a transitive verb meaning “to send, transfer,” from とどく, an intransitive verb meaning “to arrive, be delivered.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The part in parentheses is the kanji spelling of the word before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q9.kobun.why: This vocabulary entry includes the kana spelling and the corresponding kanji spelling. The part in parentheses only adds writing information; it does not form a separate clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t135-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 止める with 止まる; 止める needs a person or thing as the object being stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t136-q10.kobun.why: つめたい is an い-ending adjective presented separately to check its reading and corresponding kanji, without any sentence structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t136-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: 冷たい is the kanji spelling of つめたい. It usually describes a cold feeling when touched or cold food and drinks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t136-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: 寒い refers to cold weather or cold air. It is not used to directly describe a cold drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t136-q10.kobun.tip: Use 冷たい for cold objects or drinks, while 寒い mainly refers to the weather and surrounding temperature.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見る is used, the sentence states the action in the dictionary form and does not clearly show a habit or an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を before 見る, but the thing or information being watched must be marked with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vi: Which one is correct among these?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun 中 and indicates the range being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the range of choices and means “among”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 正しい modifies もの, while は makes “the correct one” the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: どれ asks which choice, and ですか forms a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.why: で limits the range of choices. The phrase 正しいもの then states the thing being asked about. は marks that thing, while どれですか asks which one it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If どのN is used, you must ask directly “which noun,” and you do not use もの to turn the quality 正しい into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 中で with 中に; 中で only indicates a range or the place where an action occurs, while 中に usually indicates an inside position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.vi: You do not sleep much, so why not try exercising a little?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: そんなに modifies the state of sleeping and emphasizes its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: Vないで connects to the recommended replacement action and means “do not do V”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: すこし modifies the exercise and shows a small degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたら？ uses a hypothetical condition to give a gentle suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.why: ねていないで connects an action that should not continue with the recommended action. The verb 動く changes to the past form 動いた, and then ら is added to make a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vないほうがいい is used instead, the advice is more direct and clearer, without the gentle suggestion implied by this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand ないで as “not do,” but in this pattern it means “do not do the first action; do the next action instead.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q13.kobun.cn: Vないで + Vた形 + ら？
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vi: I have never ridden a horse.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object or means that the speaker rides or gets on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: のったこと turns the experience of riding into a noun, while は makes that experience the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 一度 indicates the number of times, and も combines with a negative form to emphasize that there was no occasion at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません denies the existence of the experience in the pattern 一度も～ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.why: に attaches to 馬 to mark the object of riding. のったこと turns the completed action of riding into an experience, and then 一度も～ありません completely denies that it happened any number of times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence states that the speaker has ridden a horse at least once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means that someone has never done something, but it is not as strongly emphasized as 一度も～ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use を with 馬, but actions involving riding or getting on a vehicle usually use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q14.kobun.cn: Vた + ことがある／Vた + ことは + 一度も + ありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.sk: Nには + Nが + Number of people + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に refers to the person who exists or possesses something, while は emphasizes the object “I”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who exists in an expression meaning “have”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ２人 modifies います and shows the number of people who exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: います is a predicate that expresses the existence of a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.cn: Nには + Nが + Number of people + います／あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.why: わたしには indicates the owner or related person, while 姉が is the subject that exists. The number comes before います to add information about the number of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes possession, but it is unnatural when talking about the number of people in a family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use あります for people; for people and animals, they must use います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q16.kobun.vi: Please copy this part of the textbook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きょうかしょ to the following noun and shows the part that belongs to the textbook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the part to be copied; この modifies 部分.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q16.kobun.why: きょうかしょの identifies the source of 部分, and この部分を is the object of the action. The verb コピーする changes to the て form and combines with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the request becomes more formal and softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often forget を before the verb meaning copy; the direct object of the action needs を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.sk: Nの + Nを + Quantity + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the denomination with 切手 and shows which type of stamp is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the stamp as what the speaker wants to receive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: １０まい modifies 切手 and shows the number of stamps.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed at the end of a sentence to ask the listener to give or sell the thing mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.cn: Nの + Nを + Quantity + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.why: ８２円の identifies the type of 切手, and を marks the stamp as the object to obtain. The quantity comes before ください to clearly state how many are needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: Without the quantity, it is only a general request meaning “give me N,” without specifying ten items.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often place the quantity after the noun, but in Japanese the quantity usually comes directly before the verb or ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q17.tokens.6.m: sheet, flat item (a counter for thin objects)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q18.kobun.vi: My hometown is a small village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the noun ふるさと to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents ふるさと as the topic to be explained later.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 小さな modifies 村, while です ends the sentence with a polite statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q18.kobun.why: The phrase わたしのふるさと is presented as the topic with は. Then, 小さな modifies 村, and です states that the hometown is a small village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 小さい村 is used, it still means a small village, but the adjective ending in い comes directly before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often confuse 小さな with 小さい and use the wrong form before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.vi: I will go out with a blue polka-dot umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: あおい modifies 水玉, while の connects this phrase to かさ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the umbrella as the object of the action さして.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of raising the umbrella with the following action of going out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 出かけます is the main predicate and describes going out in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.why: The phrase あおい水玉の modifies かさ, and を marks the umbrella used in the action. さして uses the て form to connect raising the umbrella with 出かけます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If かさで出かけます is used, it only states the means or tool and does not clearly express the action of raising the umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often omit の in the phrase 水玉のかさ or use the dictionary form instead of the て form to connect the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vi: Please help me carry this for a moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the phrase 運ぶ into a noun, while を marks that action as the object of 手伝う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: てください is used to make a polite request for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.why: これを is the object inside the action 運ぶ, while 運ぶのを represents the whole action of carrying something and makes it the object of 手伝う. The pattern Vるのを手伝ってください is used to ask someone to help perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes an offer or a statement that the speaker will help, rather than a request for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often omit の when saying “help do something,” but Vるのを手伝う needs の to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.vi: When the traffic light is red, you must not cross the street.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the state of the traffic light in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 赤 with とき to create a time phrase meaning when the light is red.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a point in time, while は sets that situation apart as the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: わたっては creates the conditional part of the prohibition pattern わたってはいけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: いけません completes the Vてはいけません pattern and shows that the action must not be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.why: しんごうが赤のときは identifies the situation and time that form the condition. Then, Vてはいけません states the action that is forbidden in that situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the tone is softer and sounds more like a request not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often translate は in ときは as a separate word, but here it emphasizes the situation as the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q20.kobun.cn: Nの・V普通形・Aい・Aなな + とき（は）; Vて + はいけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.vi: I am researching pharmaceuticals at university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the research activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects くすり with 研究 to indicate the content or field of the research.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 研究 as the object of しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is する in the form ている, expressing an activity in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.why: 大学で shows where the activity takes place, while くすりの研究を indicates what is being studied. しています shows that this activity is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 研究をします, it only says that you will study or usually study, without emphasizing that the activity is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget で after a place when they want to say where an activity is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates せんもん as the topic defined at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects にほん with 文学 to form the phrase “Japanese literature.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 文学です is the predicate used to identify the major.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q22.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to state the topic せんもん, and then places the identified noun at the end. の shows the modifying relationship between にほん and 文学.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use が, the sentence emphasizes the noun chosen as the major instead of stating the topic neutrally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily reverse にほんの文学 into Vietnamese word order, but Japanese places the modifying element before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q23.kobun.vi: I traveled by boat for the first time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: はじめて is an adverb modifying the action りょこうしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means of transportation used for traveling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する, forming the predicate for a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q23.kobun.why: はじめて adds the time of the experience, 船で states the means of transportation, while りょこうしました ends the sentence and shows that the trip happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 船に乗って旅行しました, it emphasizes getting on a boat and then traveling, rather than simply stating the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で, but the means used to perform an action usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.vi: I want to study Japanese history at university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.sk: N place で + N の + N を + Vたいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the study activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with the noun 歴史, creating the meaning “the history of Japan.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what is being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: したい expresses the desire to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the subject of study, while を marks the object of studying. したいです is placed at the end to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence sounds unnatural because に usually indicates a destination or a place where something exists, not the place where studying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で when talking about the place where an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.vi: I grew up in a beautiful natural environment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being discussed throughout the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: きれいな modifies the noun 自然 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 自然 with 中, forming the phrase “inside nature.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the environment or place where growing up takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ました expresses a past action in a polite style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to describe nature. Then の 中で create the range or environment. The past-tense verb at the end completes the main meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence may mean existence or movement toward the inside of nature, without emphasizing the environment where growing up took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な before the noun after the adjective な, such as きれいな自然.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vi: I heard that my father used to swim in a pond long ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Place で + Vていた + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the father is the topic of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: This word indicates when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where swimming took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects およぐ with いた to express a continuing state or activity in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: いた is the past form of いる in the pattern Vていた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです comes after the plain form to convey information that the speaker heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.why: は states the person being discussed, while the time and place add context for the action. Vていた describes an activity in the past, and then そうです shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the sentence only says that someone swam, without emphasizing that the activity was in progress or that such a state existed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the meaning becomes “seems about to swim,” no longer reported information about the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse そうです for reported information with そうです for a prediction, because the reported-information pattern comes after the plain form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vi: If I move, a quiet place would be better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: なら sets a condition or assumption as the basis for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 静かな modifies ところ; the adjective な needs な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the place chosen or wanted in the pattern ところがいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いいです states that the choice is considered suitable or desirable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.why: なら turns moving into a hypothetical condition. The phrase 静かなところ is the chosen subject, while がいい expresses what the speaker wants or considers suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with たら, the sentence focuses more on the time condition “after moving” than on a hypothetical move.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the sentence directly says “want to choose a quiet place,” without using the evaluation pattern がいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q4.kobun.tip: The adjective な must keep な when it comes before a noun, so you say 静かなところ, not 静かところ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vi: There is a cute shop assistant at that store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.sk: Place に + Aい + N が + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where a person or thing exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: かわいい directly modifies 店員.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who exists at the stated place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: います is used to talk about the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.why: An existence sentence places に first, followed by the person who exists with が. The adjective かわいい comes directly before the noun to describe the shop assistant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use で働く, it means that the shop assistant works at the store, emphasizing the action rather than simple existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with は, the sentence becomes a comment about the shop assistant and is no longer the sentence “There is a shop assistant there.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q5.kobun.tip: The existence pattern uses the place に and the person or thing that exists が; in this basic structure, they do not change to で and は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vi: I want to write a letter to him, but I do not know where he lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.sk: N に + N を + Vます remove ます + たいですが、 + 疑問 from に + Vているか + わかりません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person receiving the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of 書きたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 書きたい expresses a desire, while が connects to the next clause with a mild contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the place where someone lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 住んでいる indicates the state of living somewhere; か turns a question into an indirect question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb わかる takes the entire preceding question clause as the content that is not known.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.why: The recipient of the letter goes with に, while the letter is the thing being written, so it goes with を. The second clause uses どこに住んでいるか as the content of わかりません, meaning that the information is unknown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence asks where an action takes place instead of focusing on where someone lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 住むか is used, the sentence refers to where someone will live or to a choice, without focusing on the current state of living there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and で when talking about places; 住む always uses に to indicate where someone lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vi: My mother made me a wool sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who made the sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the material used to make a product.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the product that was made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: つくって is the て form connected to くれました. It expresses an action done for the speaker's benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.why: 母が is the doer, 毛糸で is the material, and セーターうを is the product of the action. The structure Vてくれました adds the meaning that a family member did it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてあげました is used instead, the focus shifts to the speaker or someone else doing something for another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてもらいました is used, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker received help from their mother in making the sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse で and を; the material goes with で, while the thing made goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q7.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる/くれます/くれました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + Nする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this supermarket the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates when the supermarket starts opening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 開店します is the main predicate and describes the store starting to operate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, the specific time goes with に, and then comes the predicate 開店します. 開店 is a noun combined with する to form a verb meaning to open a store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 開く is used instead, the sentence uses an ordinary verb and may emphasize the state of the door being open, rather than the store opening or starting business.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit に after a time expression, but a specific time such as 9 o'clock usually needs に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vi: The shirt you are wearing is very nice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies the adjective きれいな to increase its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: きれいな comes before the noun シャツ to modify the shirt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the shirt as the object of 着ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 着ています expresses the state of wearing something; ね adds a tone of confirmation or a light comment to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.why: とても and きれいな both modify シャツ, so they come before the noun. シャツを is the object of 着る; the form 着ています emphasizes the state of wearing it at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 着ました is used instead, the sentence only says that the shirt was put on, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ね is replaced with か, the sentence becomes a direct question instead of a comment seeking agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may think 着ています only means that the action of putting on clothes is in progress, but in this sentence it expresses the state of wearing them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t14-q9.kobun.cn: Aな + な + N; Vて + いる/います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vi: Next New Year's holiday, I want to go to a hot spring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 来年 with お正月 to identify a specific time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents お正月 as the time or topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of the verb 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きたい expresses the desire to go to a hot spring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.why: 来年の お正月 identify the time, while に is attached to the destination of 行く. The pattern 行きたいです is placed at the end to express a desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, おんせん is understood as the place where an action takes place, not the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で after a place because it translates as “at,” but with 行く they must use に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vi: In Japan, spring is the season of new beginnings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: では limits the scope or context being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents spring as the topic in the context of Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects スタート with 季節, creating the phrase “the season of beginnings.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: きせつです is a noun predicate that explains what kind of season 春 is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.why: では sets the scope as “in Japan,” and then は makes 春 the topic. スタートのきせつ explains the content of 春 and ends with a noun sentence using です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of は, the sentence emphasizes spring as the identified information instead of presenting it as a general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand では only as に, but では also limits the scope and context of the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vi: Japan's economy will probably gradually improve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with 経済, creating the noun phrase “Japan's economy.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes “Japan's economy” the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: だんだん modifies よくなる and indicates a gradual change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: よくなる is the predicate, in which よく is the continuative form of いい before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: でしょう is placed at the end of the sentence to express a prediction or a mild opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.why: The phrase 日本の（経済）は creates the topic, and then だんだん describes the degree of change in よくなる. でしょう comes at the end because the whole sentence is a prediction about the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing でしょう with かもしれない makes the prediction sound less certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: だろう also expresses a prediction, but it usually sounds more written or direct than でしょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change いい to よく before なる and say いいなる instead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vi: I think I would like to try traveling abroad at least once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は emphasizes the experience of “once,” with the meaning of at least once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 海外旅行 is a compound noun meaning traveling abroad, and を marks the action that the speaker wants to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: してみたいと is the quoted content before と; してみたい expresses the wish to try doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: おもいます is the main predicate and takes the whole preceding idea as its content through と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.why: 一度は states the number of times the speaker wants to experience something, while 海外旅行を is the object of the action. The pattern Vてみたい connects with とおもいます to turn the wish into the content of a thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Using Vたい only says that someone wants to do something. It does not emphasize “trying to do it” like Vてみたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Vてみる says that someone will try to do something, while Vてみたい says that the speaker wants to try it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may misunderstand 旅行をしてみたい as two separate actions; here, 旅行をする is one verb phrase, and only then is てみたい added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q12.kobun.cn: Vて形 + みたい; V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + と思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vi: Let’s definitely go out for a drink together at least once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: ぜひ modifies the invitation and shows a strong wish to do the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 一度 states how many times the action of going out for a drink will be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the drink as the direct object of 飲む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲み is the verb stem in the ます form. It connects with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きましょう is an invitation to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.why: おさけを飲む is the main action done at the destination, so 飲みに comes before 行きましょう to state the purpose. ましょう turns the sentence into an invitation to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also expresses purpose, but it is more formal and emphasizes the goal more than 飲みに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Vませんか is a gentler invitation. It is not as strong as the definite feeling of ぜひ and ましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 飲むに行く; they must change 飲む into the stem ます, which is 飲み, before に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q13.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + に + 行く・来る; Vます-stem + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.vi: The Tanaka siblings are very close.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 兄弟 of the Tanaka siblings the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies いい and shows a high degree of closeness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks 仲 as the subject being evaluated in the phrase 仲がいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: いいです is the predicate. It combines with 仲が to describe a harmonious relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.why: 田中さん（兄弟）は is the topic, while 仲がいい is a fixed predicate phrase meaning to have a good relationship. In this phrase, 仲 goes with が because it is the thing being judged as good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing いい with 悪い changes the meaning to a bad or disharmonious relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place は after 仲; the correct phrase is 仲がいい because が marks the subject of the adjective いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.vi: I often shop at the store in front of the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.0.vi: at the store in front of the station
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the shopping takes place; の connects えきまえ with 店.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies かいものします and shows frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: かいものします is the main predicate and describes the action of shopping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.why: えきまえの店 creates a noun phrase meaning the store in front of the station. The particle で selects the place where the action happens, while よく comes before the predicate to show frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the place is more likely to be understood as a place where something exists or as a destination, not as the place where shopping happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に with every place; because the shopping happens at the store, 店で should be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.vi: Tomorrow during the day, I will go out with my mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with 昼間, while は makes that time period the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who joins in the action 出かけます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 出かけます is the main predicate and describes going out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.why: あしたの昼間は sets the time as the topic, and then 母と adds the person who goes along. 出かけます comes at the end to complete the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: 母に usually shows the direction of an action or its object. It does not naturally express “go out with my mother.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 昼間に directly marks the time of the action, instead of making the time the topic as with 昼間は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate と as “and” in every case; here, 母と means “together with my mother.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.vi: There are as many as 23 wards in Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.sk: Nには + Quantityも + Nがあります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle には states the place where something exists and emphasizes that the scope is Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle も follows a quantity to emphasize that the number is higher than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is the predicate showing the existence of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.cn: N + も; quantity + も means “as many as.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.why: The place comes first with には, followed by the quantity emphasized by も. The noun 区 is the thing that exists before あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is replaced with が, the sentence only states the number 23 and no longer has the emphasis of “as many as 23.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may overlook the emphasis of も and translate it simply like the particle が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.sk: Frequency + Nに + Nを + Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The frequency phrase modifies the whole activity that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the time when the activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the ている form of する and describes an activity that is happening now or regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; the polite form is Vています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.why: The frequency phrase comes first to modify the activity. A specific day goes with に, while the sport is the object marked by を before しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If します is used, it only talks generally about playing soccer and does not emphasize an activity that is happening or continuing regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate ています only as the present tense and forget that this pattern can also describe an ongoing state or habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.vi: In Kyoto, yellow flowers have bloomed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where the flowers bloom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: 黄色い is an adjective ending in い and directly modifies 花.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that enters the state of blooming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb さきました is in the polite past form and indicates that the flowers have bloomed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ N; 黄色 becomes 黄色い when it comes before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.why: The place where an event happens uses で. The adjective 黄色い comes directly before 花 to modify it, and then 花が becomes the subject of さきました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 黄色の花 is used, the meaning is still yellow flowers, but the structure changes to the noun 黄色 combined with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 黄色い as an independent noun, but here it must come before 花 to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vi: Tomorrow is Saturday, so the company will be closed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets tomorrow as the time reference of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で is the connecting form of です. It connects the information “it is Saturday” with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 会社 the topic described as being closed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みです functions as a noun predicate and states that the company is closed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.why: The first clause states that tomorrow is Saturday. Then the connecting form で leads to the result that the company is closed. The two は successively mark the time reference and the subject being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If だから is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer and more direct than with the connecting form で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand で as “by” or “at,” but here it connects two clauses with the meaning “because it is.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.vi: I like singing karaoke with my friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と indicates the person who performs the singing action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 歌う combines with の to form a noun, while が marks singing as the object of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, expressing a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ の ＋ が ＋ 好きです; の turns an action into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.why: The person accompanying the speaker uses と, and the place uses で. The action 歌う is nominalized with の and then becomes the subject of the pattern のが好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing の with こと still means liking singing, but the tone is slightly more general and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: Using のは presents singing as a topic and often creates a contrastive or emphatic tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put を before 好きです, but Japanese usually uses が好きです to express preferences.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.vi: Of the four seasons, I like summer the most.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.sk: Scopeで ＋ Nが ＋ いちばん ＋ Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で limits the comparison scope to the seasons in one year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the season chosen as the favorite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies すきです to create a superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです functions as the predicate and states the degree of preference for 夏.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.cn: Nで ＋ Nが ＋ いちばん ＋ Aなです; で indicates the comparison scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.why: The comparison scope is placed first with で. The season is made the subject with が, while いちばん comes before すきです to show the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If いちばん is omitted, the sentence only means liking summer. It does not say that summer is the favorite season.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: 一年の中で also indicates the scope within one year, but it emphasizes the meaning “among the seasons of one year” more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に after the scope, but comparison scopes usually go with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.vi: Here, February is the coldest month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Timeが ＋ いちばん ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the place ここ the topic for a comment about the weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the month being compared within this place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies 寒い to create the meaning “the coldest.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 寒い is the い-ending adjective used as the predicate, and it combines with です to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.cn: いちばん ＋ Aい; the adjective ending in い keeps its original form before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.why: ここは states the place being discussed, while 2月が is the month chosen for comparison. いちばん comes before 寒い because it modifies the adjective and creates a superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 2月は寒いです is used, the sentence only says that February is cold. It does not confirm that it is the coldest month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: もっとも also means “most,” but it has a more formal, written tone than いちばん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put いちばん after the adjective, but in Japanese it comes before the adjective being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.vi: Recently, the number of foreign tourists has been increasing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N からの ＋ N が ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb indicating the time when an event happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: からの connects to the following noun and modifies tourists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that is increasing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ています expresses an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.why: The phrase 外国からの modifies かんこうきゃく and shows that these are tourists coming from abroad. The subject goes with が, while ています expresses an ongoing trend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the meaning is foreign tourists, but the source is less clear than with からの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse からの with からに, but before a noun, からの must be used to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.vi: I forgot to wash my face before going to bed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies まえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time before which the following action must happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being washed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the action あらう into a noun, and then を marks the action that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: ました describes an action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.why: ねる modifies まえ to create the time reference “before going to bed.” The phrase あらうのを nominalizes the whole face-washing action and makes it the object of わすれました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes after sleeping, reversing the time relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use the た form before まえに in this basic pattern; use the dictionary form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q24.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ まえに; V辞書形 ＋ のを ＋ 忘れる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.vi: Since coming to Japan, I have kept writing a diary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction of movement to Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: てから connects the action of coming with the period that begins afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb that emphasizes that the action continues without interruption.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ている describes an action that has continued from the past to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.why: 日本へ来てから sets the starting point, while ずっと書いています shows that writing the diary has continued up to the present. The object 日記 comes before を, and the verb 書く comes at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern only says that the action happens after coming to Japan. It does not emphasize that the action has continued from that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q25.kobun.tip: てから means “after or since finishing an action,” not simply connecting two consecutive verbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vi: I think I want to work at a television station in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.sk: N time ＋ N place で ＋ Vたい ＋ と ＋ 思います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the time when the speaker plans to work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content that the speaker wants to think about or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: おもいます is the main verb and takes the content before と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.why: The place of work uses で, while the content “want to work” is quoted with と before おもいます. おもいます at the end of the sentence shows that this is the speaker’s thought or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If the sentence ends with 働きたいです, it simply states a desire and does not have the meaning “I think that.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit と before おもいます, although と is necessary to mark the content of the thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vi: I will go to a restaurant with a friend tonight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.sk: N time は ＋ N person と ＋ N place に ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tonight the time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who does the action of going with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes going at the present or future time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.why: The sentence gives the time, the person going with the speaker, and the destination in that order, then places the verb 行きます at the end. と shows accompaniment, while に shows direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with のために, the meaning becomes “for the friend” or “for the friend’s benefit,” not going with the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse と and に when saying “with a friend”; the person going together must be marked with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vi: Sending it by ship is cheap but slow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means used for sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a natural condition with a result that usually occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects two contrasting ideas: the price is low but the speed is slow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 遅いです is an adjective predicate ending in い and describes sending by ship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.why: で places the means before the action おくる. The clause おくると gives the condition, and then 安いですが、 gives a result that contrasts with 遅いです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence has a more specific hypothetical meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse と in this conditional sentence with と, which means “and” or is a quotation particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vi: There is a famous temple in this town.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to point to an object near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the temple exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 有名 is an adjective ending in な, so it must connect to a noun with な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists in the place mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate that indicates the existence of an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.why: The place phrase まちに comes first to identify where something exists. 有名な directly modifies おてら, while おてらが is the subject of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 有名な with 有名の would be incorrect because 有名 takes the ending な when modifying a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit な after 有名 and say 有名おてら, but they must say 有名なおてら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vi: In Kyoto, I saw many old buildings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of seeing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 古い comes before 建物 to modify this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies the quantity of 建物 seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 見ました is the verb 見る in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.why: で marks the place of the action, を marks the object, and 古い comes directly before 建物 to form a noun phrase. たくさん adds the quantity before the predicate 見ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of で, the sentence describes existence in Kyoto, not an action taking place there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the place of an action, but the verb 見る requires the place to be marked with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vi: Maria is three years younger than me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N より ＋ Quantity ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents Maria as the person being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the standard of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ３さい indicates the age difference in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 若いです is the predicate describing Maria compared with me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.why: は presents the subject of comparison, より gives the person used as the standard, and ３さい states the difference. 若いです comes at the end to conclude the characteristic being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that the selected person is younger, instead of only stating how many years younger Maria is than me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily reverse より and は; the correct order is the person being compared + は, followed by the standard + より.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vi: You cut vegetables into small pieces very skillfully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action 切る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 細かく is the adverbial form of 細かい and modifies how the cutting is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the phrase きる into a noun, and が marks cutting as the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: じょうずです evaluates the skill of cutting vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.why: やさいを is the object of きる, while 細かく describes how the action is performed. The phrase きるのが turns “cutting” into the subject evaluated by じょうずです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: の can be replaced with こと, but this expression is more formal and objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t15-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 細かいきる, but before a verb, the adjective ending in い must be changed into the adverbial form 細かく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vi: After finishing breakfast, I left home at 7 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 済ます is in the form て to connect finishing breakfast with the action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time when the action of leaving home takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を indicates the starting point when talking about leaving a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 出る changes to the polite past form to end the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.why: The clause 済まして comes first to state the action completed before 出ました. に is connected with a time, while を in いえを shows the place that someone leaves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 済まして is replaced with 済ましてから, the meaning “after finishing breakfast” is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for a place someone leaves, but with 出る, the starting place usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vi: The cow seems to be enjoying eating grass.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: そうに changes an adjective into an adverb and describes how the cow eats.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food as the object of 食べています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ている shows an action that is taking place at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.why: おいしそうに modifies 食べています and shows how the cow looks while eating, not that the cow itself tastes delicious. 草を is the direct object of the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If おいしく is used, it means “eat in a delicious way,” focusing on how the cow eats rather than on the appearance being observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q11.kobun.tip: Do not confuse おいしそうに with おいしいそうに; before そうだ, the adjective い drops い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject whose state changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the degree and timing of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 暗い changes to the く form to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: なる is in the polite past form and expresses the result of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.why: The pattern Aいくなる describes the subject changing to a new state. 暗く comes directly before なりました because the く form is the required connecting form between the adjective い and なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 暗くしました is used, it means that someone made the sky or an object become dark, so there is an active agent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q12.kobun.tip: The adjective い before なる must change い into く, not use 暗いなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vi: My father is working at a car factory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes my father the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 車 with 工場, creating the meaning “a factory related to cars.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the action of working takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes a continuing state of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.why: 車の工場 is a noun phrase in which 車 modifies 工場. で identifies the place where the action of working takes place, while は puts the topic at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence points to the direction or destination of the action, so it is not suitable for showing the place where someone is working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q13.kobun.tip: For an action that takes place at a location, Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies レストラン and refers to one specific restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the restaurant the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 本当に is used as an adverb to emphasize how delicious it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしいです is the adjective predicate い in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.why: レストランは is the topic, and then 本当に modifies the adjective おいしい to increase the strength of the statement. 本当だ changes into 本当に when used as an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 本当に is replaced with とても, the sentence emphasizes only the degree “very delicious,” not the meaning “really.”
