default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q14.kobun.tip: 本当に must stay whole before おいしい; it must not be split into 本当においしい separate pieces that lose characters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the address should be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いてください uses the てください form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.why: ここに identifies the place where the writing is done, while 住所を is the object being written. The てください form comes at the end of the sentence to make the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書きます is used, the sentence only says “I will write the address,” so it is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q15.kobun.tip: に in ここに indicates the place where the content is put or written, while を marks the content itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.vi: Let’s send something that Mr. Tanaka’s husband likes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun before it with the noun ご主人 and shows possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the action 好きな in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 好きな comes before もの to modify the thing being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the action おくりましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ましょう expresses a suggestion or an invitation to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.why: The clause ご主人が好きな comes before もの to identify the thing that the husband likes. ものを is the direct object of おくりましょう, while ましょう changes the sentence into a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If the clause ご主人が is removed, the phrase only means “something I like” or “something that is liked” in general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing が with の in a modifying clause can still be found in spoken language, but が is clearer when marking the subject of 好きな.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 好きなもの as “the thing liked,” but they need to understand the whole phrase ご主人が好きなもの as “the thing that the husband likes.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.vi: Tomorrow I will go shopping with my wife.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.sk: Time は + N と + N に + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は states tomorrow as the time reference and the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the person who does the shopping together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the purpose of 出かけます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.why: あしたは puts the time reference at the beginning of the sentence. 妻と indicates the person going together, while かいものに states the purpose of going out; the main verb 出かけます comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes the meaning “together with my wife” more clearly, while 妻と is already enough to show the companion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes shopping as the purpose of going out instead of using the noun かいもの directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q17.kobun.tip: と in this sentence does not simply mean “and”; it indicates the person doing the action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.vi: I go to school by bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.sk: Means of transport に ＋ Vて ＋ Destination へ ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に combines with 乗る to show the means of transport that the speaker gets on or takes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 乗って is the て form, linking the action of taking a vehicle with the action of 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.why: バスに乗って creates the part showing the way of traveling, then がっこうへ行きます states the destination. The て form links two actions that happen in sequence or combines them to show how the later action is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Use で to say directly “go to school by bus,” without emphasizing the separate action of getting on the bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes two actions happening at the same time, so it is less natural than the て form in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q18.kobun.tip: に is used with 乗る, while で is used to show the means of transport used to perform an action such as 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.vi: Because I am only 19 years old, I cannot drink alcohol.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.sk: まだ ＋ N ですから ＋ N が ＋ negative potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: まだ adds the idea that the current time or level has not yet reached adulthood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから links the cause before it with the result after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object of the potential verb 飲めません in this usage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲めません is the negative potential form, expressing that someone cannot or is not allowed to drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.why: 19さいですから places the reason before the result 飲めません. With a potential verb such as 飲める, the object usually takes が, so お酒が is more suitable than お酒を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still states the reason, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence only says that the person does not drink by choice or habit. It does not clearly say that the person cannot or is not allowed to drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use を mechanically with every verb; potential verbs usually use が to mark the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the postcard is the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the selling takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ている combines with the verb 売る to ask where this item is being sold or is available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.why: The topic ハガキは is placed first, and the place of sale is asked with どこで. 売っていますか asks whether the item is currently being sold or where it is available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 売りますか is used, the question focuses more on who will sell it or on the future action of selling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q2.kobun.tip: で shows where an action takes place, so に is not used to ask the place where goods are sold in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.vi: The wind has blown in from the south.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the starting point or the direction from which the wind blows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the natural subject performing the action 吹く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: ふいて is the て form of 吹く, and connects with 来ました to express wind blowing toward here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ました combines with the preceding て form and shows movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.why: 南から states the wind’s direction of origin, while 風が is the subject. 吹いて来ました combines the action of blowing with movement toward the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern describes the wind blowing and then moving away from the reference point, opposite to 吹いてきました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence only says that the wind blew from the south. It does not emphasize movement toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q20.kobun.tip: てくる does not simply mean “come”; it shows movement toward the speaker or the point being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.vi: How is this Chinese character read?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before the noun 漢字 to identify the Chinese character being indicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the Chinese character as the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content or reading being asked about in the pattern 何と読みますか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: か is placed at the end of the sentence to turn 読みます into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.why: この漢字は states the Chinese character being asked about, while なんと読みますか asks how to read it. The particle と marks the content that is pronounced or called.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: This also asks “how is it read?”, but focuses on the method or reading and does not use the quotation structure 何と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks “what character is it written with?”, so it asks about writing, not reading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q21.kobun.tip: 何と読む is a fixed pattern for asking how to read something; と should not be translated as “and” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.vi: Because I have recovered from a cold, I will go to school from tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Vた ＋ ので ＋ Time から ＋ N へ ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the cause that leads to the recovery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ので links the reason clause with the result and follows the past form 治った.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: から shows the time when the action begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: へ shows the direction of movement of 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the main predicate and expresses the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before ので, and the action being explained comes after it. あしたから identifies the starting time, while 学校へ identifies the destination of the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still shows the reason, but sounds more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place から after the main verb; in this sentence, ので must come after the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.vi: What is this type of alcohol made from?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify おさけ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の links おさけ with 原料, creating a relationship of belonging or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 原料 the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 何ですか creates a question about the identity or content of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.why: このおさけの is a modifying phrase placed before the noun 原料. 原料 is made the topic with は, and then 何ですか is used to ask for the related content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If が replaces は, the focus shifts more toward identifying what the ingredients are rather than presenting them as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate の as “of” in every case, but here it also means “related to” the ingredients of the alcohol.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.vi: I want this coat, but I do not have enough money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun コート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the desired object with the adjective ほしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: けど links two contrasting ideas: wanting the coat but facing an obstacle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject judged to be insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 足りません is the polite negative form of 足りる and serves as the predicate of the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.why: ほしいけど states the desire and then uses けど to shift to the opposite obstacle. In the following clause, お金が is the subject judged as sufficient or insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern expresses the desire to have an object, and the desired object takes が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: 足りない also means “not enough,” but it is the casual form and does not fit the polite style 足りません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with the desired object, but the pattern ほしい requires the object to take が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.vi: After finishing breakfast, I left the house at 7 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that has been completed with 済ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 済まして is the て form, connecting a completed action to the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates when the action of leaving the house took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the place that is left in the use of 出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 出ました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.why: Because the action of eating breakfast was completed first, the て form is used to connect it with the action of leaving the house. The time expression comes before the main predicate, while いえを is the place of departure with 出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is used, the order of events is emphasized more clearly: only after finishing the action does the speaker leave the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for the place of departure, but 出る usually uses を to mark the place that is left.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vi: The convenience store is open even at midnight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.sk: N は + Time でも + Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the convenience store is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: でも attaches to the time expression to emphasize that the store is open even at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes the state of the store being open.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.why: 夜中でも places an unusual time in the sentence to emphasize that the store is still open. あいています describes the state of being open, not only the action of opening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with にも, the meaning is “also at midnight,” which is weaker and does not have the nuance of “even.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q3.kobun.tip: でも means “even” in this sentence, not the verb です in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.vi: Nowadays, we can even send emails to people living in faraway places, so it is convenient, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time and also sets the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the person lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: This clause modifies 人, creating the meaning “people living in a faraway place.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: とも indicates the person being communicated with and carries the nuance “also with.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks email as the object that can be sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects this result or situation to the comment that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: ですね places the comment at the end of the sentence and invites the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.why: The phrase とおい所にすんでいる comes before 人 to modify the person. Then, 人とも states the object of communication, メールができて states the possibility, and 便利ですね gives the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate とも simply as “with,” but in this sentence とも emphasizes the meaning “also with those people.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.vi: The Olympic gold medal is shining.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects オリンピック with 金メダル, showing a relationship of belonging or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the gold medal as the subject that is shining.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 光っている expresses a continuing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.why: の identifies the medal as belonging to the Olympic context, and が marks the object that is shining. 光っている uses the ている form to describe the continuing state of shining.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q5.kobun.tip: ています should not be understood only as “be doing” in every case; with 光る, it can also emphasize a state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.vi: The shoes and handbag cost about 20,000 yen in total.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects the nouns being listed together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the range or items included when stating the total amount of money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 合計 modifies the amount of money that follows and shows that it is a combined amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: くらい expresses an estimated amount, while でした ends the sentence in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.why: と lists two items, and で groups them within the range being counted. 合計 comes before the amount of money to create the phrase “the total was about ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use と to express the total amount of money; と only connects the items, while で shows the range used for the calculation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.vi: I want to learn about the cultures of other countries.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: ほかの modifies 国, creating the meaning “another country.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 国 with 文化, showing that the culture belongs to that country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks culture as the object of the action of learning about it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: しりたい expresses the desire to know or learn about something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.why: ほかの国の文化 creates a multi-level noun phrase: “the cultures of other countries.” This phrase functions as the object with を, and then しりたいです expresses the desire to learn about it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q7.kobun.tip: の must be kept between 国 and 文化; removing this particle would make the relationship “the culture of the country” unclear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.vi: The stars are beautiful tonight, aren’t they?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.sk: Time + N が + Aなですね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: こんばんは states the time setting and is also an evening greeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the stars as the object being described as beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね ends the comment and suggests sharing the feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.why: こんばんは sets the context at the beginning of the sentence. 星が is the subject being evaluated, while きれいですね is a polite comment that suggests shared feelings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q8.kobun.tip: きれい is a な adjective, so it does not conjugate like a い adjective even though its meaning is “beautiful.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.vi: The wind is very strong, so let’s go inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the wind as the subject with the quality of being strong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies 強い, making the degree of the adjective stronger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause clause with the suggestion to go inside that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the direction or destination of the action 入る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ましょう changes a verb into an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.why: かぜがとても強いので states the reason first, and then いえに indicates the destination. 入りましょう gives a suggestion that fits the reason just stated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q9.kobun.tip: With the verb 入る, the destination usually goes with に; do not use を to indicate the place entered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vi: It is very hot today, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.sk: Time point は + とても + Aいかった + ですね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the degree of 暑かった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 暑かった is the past form of the i-adjective い 暑い, serving as the predicate that describes the weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね makes the comment softer and invites the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.why: 今日 is the time topic, とても adds the degree, and the adjective 暑い serves as the predicate. The form 暑かった shows that the state is viewed at a time that has already passed during the day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 暑いですね describes a present comment or a feeling that is happening now, without emphasizing a past state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q1.kobun.tip: The i-adjective い changes to かった in the past; do not use 暑いでした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the money as the object being paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 払います is a polite-form verb and the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.why: The noun お金 comes before を because it is the object of the action 払います. The verb comes at the end of the sentence and uses ます to show politeness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of を before a verb's object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vi: Mr. Satou is wearing a red sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks Satou as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 赤い comes before セーター to modify the sweater, while を marks the sweater as the object of 着ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: きています uses the form ている to express the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.why: The adjective 赤い comes before the noun セーター to form a noun phrase that serves as the object. 着る changes to the て form and combines with いる to express an ongoing state of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 着ました, the sentence only says that someone wore or put something on, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern describes an action in progress or a continuing state, depending on the type of verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand ています as only meaning “is doing,” but with 着る it usually describes the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vi: I will check the things inside the box.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects はこ to the following noun to show possession or scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 中の modifies もの, creating the meaning “things inside.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the things as the objects being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 調べます is the main predicate and uses the polite form ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases identify the source and location of もの in order: the things inside the box. The whole phrase ものを serves as the object of 調べます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If の中に is used, the phrase indicates a place toward which a thing or action is directed, and does not directly modify もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 中の as “inside” and forget that の here connects the location phrase to the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vi: Sorry, I am a little late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し modifies the degree of lateness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 遅い changes to the form 遅く to connect with なる and express the state of becoming late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, describing a change that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q13.kobun.why: 少し indicates degree and comes before 遅く to soften the degree of lateness. The adjective 遅い changes to 遅く and combines with なる to express the state of becoming late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 遅くする is used, the meaning is to actively make something slower or later.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may leave 遅い unchanged before なる, but the adjective い must change い to く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before the noun さら to identify the plate being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the plate as the object of the washing action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 洗った is a clause in the plain form and comes before 人 to modify that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: は marks the person who washed the plate as the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: だれですか creates a polite question about the identity of the person mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.why: The clause 洗った comes before 人 to identify which person, forming the phrase “the person who washed this plate.” This phrase is the topic with は, and the question だれですか asks about the person's identity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 洗う人 is used, the meaning is “the person who washes or will wash,” without confirming that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the same type of modifying clause, in which the object comes before the verb inside the clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may place a relative clause after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese places 洗った before 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q15.kobun.vi: The wind feels very pleasant today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the wind as the subject that feels pleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective describes a pleasant state, and です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q15.kobun.why: 今日 は state the time as the topic, while 風 が are the entity experiencing the state きもちいい. The adjective comes at the end to finish the description.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the sentence shifts to emphasize or contrast the wind specifically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use は for every subject, but が here marks the subject that feels pleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q16.kobun.vi: Shall we go for a walk together?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the manner of doing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.1.vi: shall we go for a walk
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun 散歩 combines with する to form a verb, and the polite negative form with か creates an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q16.kobun.why: いっしょに comes first to indicate doing the action together. 散歩する is a verb formed by combining the noun with する, while ませんか comes at the end to make a polite invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しましょうか, the speech has a more active tone of suggestion or invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q16.kobun.tip: Do not separate 散歩 and する into two separate ideas; together they form a verb meaning to go for a walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Mr. Kawai the topic being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろ modifies the information that Mr. Kawai knows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 知って is the form て used to connect with います, creating a pattern that expresses the state of knowing or having learned something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern 知っている and shows that the state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q17.kobun.why: The topic comes first. Then いろいろ modifies the information that is known. 知って connects with います to express a state of knowing, not just a momentary act of learning something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 知ります, the meaning leans toward coming to know or finding out, not currently being in a state of knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 知っている as “be knowing” in the sense of an action, but in this sentence it mainly indicates a state of already knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q18.kobun.vi: I want to go to a faraway place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before ところ to modify the place the speaker wants to go to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きたい is formed from the verb’s continuative form 行き and たい, and expresses desire; です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q18.kobun.why: 遠い comes before the noun ところ according to Japanese modifier order. The phrase ところへ indicates the destination, while 行きたいです expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に still indicates the destination, but に emphasizes the specific destination more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q18.kobun.tip: Japanese adjectives come before nouns, so you must say 遠いところ instead of placing 遠い after ところ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q19.kobun.vi: Everyone is healthy, so I feel relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks everyone as the subject of the state of being healthy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: 元気 is a な adjective. It changes to 元気で to connect a reason or condition to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 安心 combines with する to form a verb, and the polite past form しました states the emotional result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q19.kobun.why: みんなが元気で states the condition that leads to the emotion. 元気で connects the first clause with 安心しました, showing that the speaker felt relieved because everyone was healthy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If だから is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is expressed more clearly and directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q19.kobun.tip: With the な adjective, you must use で to connect two clauses, not く as with the い adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.sk: N は + Person が + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the owner the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who exists in the pattern います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: います is a predicate that indicates the existence of a person or animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.why: わたしは introduces the related person, while 弟が is the existing person being introduced. For people, Japanese uses います instead of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: あります is used for objects or nonliving things, so it cannot replace 弟.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を to mean “have a younger brother,” but the existence pattern uses が: 弟がいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who receives the phone call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 電話 combines with する to form a verb, and します indicates a polite action in the present or future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q20.kobun.why: 妻に is the object of the phone call, so に is used. 電話する combines a noun with する to form a verb and comes at the end of the sentence as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used, the focus shifts to contacting the wife.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use を after 妻 in this structure; the recipient of the call is marked by に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.vi: A large port can be seen from here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point or the range where something begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: 大きな comes before a noun to modify 港.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that is seen in the pattern 見える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 見えます is the predicate and expresses the natural ability to see something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.why: The phrase indicating the starting point comes first. Then the adjective modifies the noun that is the object seen. With 見える, the object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 見ます, it means actively looking at the port, not being able to see it naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 見える, but the object seen usually uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the bag is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the degree of 軽かった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 軽かった is the past form of the い-ending adjective, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q22.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は. The adverb とても comes before the adjective to increase its degree. The adjective 軽い changes to 軽かった to express a past state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 軽いです, the sentence changes to the present, meaning that the bag is light now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q22.kobun.tip: The past form of the い-ending adjective changes い to かった. Do not add でした directly after 軽い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person with the preference as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing liked in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです is an な-adjective predicate that expresses preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q23.kobun.why: The speaker makes themselves the topic with は. The liked activity comes before 好き and goes with が. 好き is an な adjective, so the polite form 好きです is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 旅行をします is used, it means performing the activity of traveling, not expressing a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q23.kobun.tip: Do not translate mechanically and use を with 好き; the liked object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q24.kobun.vi: I used to live in this village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where someone exists or lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: すんでいました uses the ていた form to express a continuing state of residence in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q24.kobun.why: この modifies 村, and the place of residence goes with に. The form ていました shows that living there continued for a period of time in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で is unnatural with 住む in this sentence; に is what marks the place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q24.kobun.tip: With 住む, Vietnamese learners may easily use で to mean a place, but the standard particle is に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.vi: Mother chose this skirt for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks mother as the person who performed the choosing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: この modifies スカート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the skirt as the object that was chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 選んで is the て form. It connects the verb 選ぶ with くれる to create a structure meaning that someone does something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: くれました is the main predicate and shows that the action was performed for the speaker’s benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.why: 母が is the doer, and スカートを is the affected object. 選んで connects with くれました using the て form to express that mother did it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 選びました, it only says that mother chose it, without emphasizing that she chose it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.tip: The て form in Vてくれる does not simply connect actions. It combines with くれる to express help or a favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q25.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれる／くれます／くれました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective modifies the noun 道具 that follows it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました is the polite past form of もらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.why: あたらしい comes before 道具 and modifies the noun. 道具 takes the particle を because it is the thing received, and the verb もらいました completes the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often put adjectives after nouns, but Japanese puts あたらしい before 道具.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vi: Please get that cup for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the cup as the thing requested to be fetched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 取って is the て form of 取る, used to connect with ください in a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください makes a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.why: そのコップを is the object of the action of fetching. The verb 取る changes to the て form and then combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the request asks whether the listener can do it for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a command with a stronger tone than ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use the plain form 取るください; a request must use 取ってください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vi: My father had surgery on his leg.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks my father as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 足 with 手術 and shows that the surgery concerns the leg.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 手術 as the object of しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.why: 足の手術 is a noun phrase in which 足の modifies 手術. This phrase is the object with を, while しました describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern only says that the leg hurts. It does not describe having surgery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q5.kobun.tip: の here does not only show possession; it also connects nouns and modifies the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vi: I bought cooking oil at the supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the buying action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the oil as the thing bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いました is the polite past form of 買う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.why: スーパーで comes before the object and states where the purchase happens. 油を is the thing bought, and 買いました comes at the end as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, スーパー is usually understood as the destination or direction, not the place where the buying happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q6.kobun.tip: Distinguish で, the place where an action happens, from に, the destination or place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose preference is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing liked in the structure 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies 好き and shows the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, expressing preference politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, while 秋が is the object of the feeling 好きです. いちばん comes before すきです to raise the degree of liking to the highest level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using を here does not fit 好きです; the liked object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If いちばん is removed, the sentence only means liking autumn and no longer has the meaning of liking it the most.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q7.kobun.tip: With 好きです, Vietnamese learners may use を out of habit, but the standard pattern is usually Nが好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vi: The boy is looking up at the sky.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person performing the action of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the sky as the object being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 見ています is the ている form of 見る, expressing an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.why: 男の子が is the subject performing the action, and 空を is the object being looked at. 見ています at the end of the sentence shows that the action is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced with 見ました, the sentence only says that he looked and does not emphasize an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means that the sky is visible or appears, not that the boy is actively looking at it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q8.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 見ています with having looked; the ている form here expresses looking now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: おもしろい is an adjective ending in い that functions as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.why: The noun phrase is made the topic by は. Then the adjective おもしろい describes the topic. です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that the movie itself has the interesting quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t17-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit は or confuse は with が when stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vi: The lake can be seen from here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the lake as the thing that can be seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 見えます is a predicate expressing natural visibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.why: The phrase showing the viewpoint comes first, followed by the visible object and the predicate 見えます. For the object with 見える, use が instead of を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 湖を見ます is used, it means actively looking at the lake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q1.kobun.tip: Distinguish 見える, meaning that something can be seen and usually used with が, from 見る, meaning to look and used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vi: I learned this piece of music at school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the learning activity happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: この modifies the noun immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 習いました is the polite past form of the verb 習う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.why: The place of learning comes before the object and the verb. を shows that the piece of music is what was learned, while 習いました expresses a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, it usually indicates the direction toward or the time of arriving at school, not the place where learning happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for every place, but the place where an action happens usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vi: My younger brother has a strong, healthy body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that my younger brother is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part that has the quality 強い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 強いです is the adjective predicate い in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.why: は introduces the person being discussed, while が identifies the body part with the quality. The adjective 強い directly functions as the predicate and ends with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means that the younger brother makes the body stronger, which is different from describing a body that is naturally strong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q11.kobun.tip: When describing a body part, Vietnamese learners may easily use を, but the body part with the quality usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.sk: N には ＋ N が ＋ Number of people ＋ います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に identifies that an older brother exists for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person being discussed as existing within my scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 一人 indicates the number of older brothers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: います is used for the existence of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.why: The possessor is expressed with に, while the existing person is marked with が. 一人 is placed before います to add the quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This can be understood as saying that I possess an older brother, so it is less natural than the pattern に N が います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use を after わたし when saying that I have someone; the existence pattern uses に for the possessor and が for the person who exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vi: Last night, I was playing a game alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.sk: NのN は ＋ Number of people で ＋ Nを ＋ Vていました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase きのうの夜 states the time, and は makes that time the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the manner or state in which an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the game as the object of していました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: していました is the past form of しています and describes an action that was in progress at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning as the topic, followed by the manner, the object, and the action. していました shows that the playing was in progress last night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ゲームをしました is used, it only states that a game was played and does not emphasize the ongoing process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: 一人に does not show the manner of being alone; the correct expression in this sentence is 一人で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse で and に; when describing doing something in a certain state or manner, use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q13.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる → Vていました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vi: On Sunday, I went to the beach with a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the day chosen as the time reference for the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who performs the action of going with you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行く changes to 行きました to express an action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.why: The sentence pattern places the time first, then gives the companion and the destination, and ends with the verb 行きました. The particle と indicates the person doing the action with you, while に marks the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, the sentence still means going to the beach but emphasizes the direction more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with destinations, but with 行く, use に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vi: My friend appeared on a famous television program.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person performing the action of appearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 有名な modifies the noun テレビばんぐみ that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the program in which the friend appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 出る changes into 出ました to show that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.why: The adjective 有名な comes before テレビばんぐみ to describe the program. The particle に marks the program as the place or object in which the character appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This directly modifies a noun; な cannot be omitted as it can when 有名 is used as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 有名だ is used, it becomes an independent predicate meaning famous and does not stand directly before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q15.kobun.tip: The adjective な must keep な when it comes before a noun; it cannot directly use 有名テレビばんぐみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vi: My older brother got married last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the older brother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: A time noun is placed before the verb to state when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: けっこんする changes into けっこんしました to talk about a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.why: The topic あには is placed at the beginning, followed by the time reference 去年, and then the action of getting married. A time word does not need a particle when it comes directly before the predicate in this sentence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding に is possible in some contexts, but 去年 is usually more natural without に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q16.kobun.tip: Do not automatically add に after every time word; 去年 usually comes directly before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vi: I will give my son the item he likes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects むすこ with the possessed or identified noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: すきな modifies 物, forming the phrase “the item my son likes.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item affected by the action of giving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: プレゼントします is the predicate and describes the action of giving a present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.why: The phrase むすこのすきな modifies 物: it is an item connected with the son and liked by the son. 物を is the direct object of プレゼントします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern uses が to state that the son is the person who likes the item, making the subject of すき clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This phrase means the son's item, not the item that the son likes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q17.kobun.tip: With 好きな in a modifying clause, the person who likes something usually goes with が; の in むすこの mainly expresses possession or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: With 好き, が marks the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです acts as the predicate and politely expresses the state of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.why: The pattern 好き is not used like an ordinary verb: the person who likes something is the topic with は, while the liked object goes with が. Therefore, 黒がすきです means “likes black.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern describes beginning to like an object and emphasizes the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding ではありません changes the sentence to mean not liking N.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the object with すきです; the object of 好き usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q18.kobun.cn: N ＋ が ＋ すきだ／すきです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with 教育, forming the phrase “children's education.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the topic being talked about or discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 話す changes into 話しました to show that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.why: 子どもの教育 forms a specific topic, and then について marks the content being discussed. The topic phrase comes before the predicate 話しました in the natural word order of Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Its meaning is close to について, but it is more formal and has a more written style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This form uses について to modify another noun; it does not end directly with the verb 話しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q19.kobun.tip: について means about or related to; do not translate it mechanically as toward or toward someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vi: My younger brother works at a factory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being talked about in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: はたらいています describes the state of working or the current job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.why: The person being talked about comes at the beginning of the sentence with は, followed by the place of the activity with で. The verb in the ています form describes work that is continuing or a current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, it usually focuses on a destination or a place where something exists. It is less suitable than で when talking about a workplace.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use に with a workplace, but で is usually used for the place where an activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that has the beautiful quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: きれいです acts as the predicate and describes the handwriting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.why: The sentence makes the person being described the topic, then uses が to show the thing that has the quality. The adjective な きれい combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning becomes “write beautifully,” focusing on the action of writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with きれいですが, but here が marks the thing that is being described as beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vi: There is a swimming pool nearby, so it is very convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows where an object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: あるので connects the cause to the result that follows using the pattern ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 便利です acts as the predicate and states the result of having a swimming pool nearby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.why: An existence clause uses に for the place and が for the existing object. The あるので clause comes first to give the reason, while 便利です is the result being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still means “because there is,” but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: あるため has a formal tone and is often used in writing or announcements.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for the place where something exists, but with ある, に must be used to show the location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.vi: When I was young, I had a habit of keeping a diary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: とき shows the time when the habit being discussed occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form clause 書く modifies the noun しゅうかん that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the existing habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ありました acts as the predicate and describes existence in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to set the context. The phrase 書く comes directly before しゅうかん and modifies it, creating the meaning “the habit of keeping a diary”; ありました shows that this habit existed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker used to write a diary regularly, not that a habit existed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese puts 書く directly before しゅうかん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vi: In the late afternoon, I went to the supermarket and bought vegetables and meat to bring home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ N と N を ＋ Vてくる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase states when the action took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of going with the following action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: と connects two nouns of equal status, while を marks the things that were bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 買ってきました combines 買う with てくる and expresses buying something and then returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.why: The time comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the destination of the action of going. The て form connects the actions in sequence, while てくる adds the meaning of doing something and then returning toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買いました is used instead, the sentence only says that the speaker bought something. It does not clearly show that the speaker returned after buying it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes the purpose “go in order to buy,” not the result of buying something and bringing it home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out て in 行って and 買って, but the て form is needed to connect the actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before the noun to modify パソコン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that is wanted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ほしいです acts as the predicate and expresses the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.why: The adjective 軽い comes before パソコン to limit the type of computer the speaker wants. With ほしい, the desired object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence expresses a desire to buy a computer, not a desire to own an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before ほしい, but the basic pattern is Nがほしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q24.kobun.cn: N ＋ が ＋ ほしいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vi: Please show me how to make this dish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to clearly indicate the dish being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 料理 with つくりかた, creating the phrase “how to make this dish.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content for which instructions are requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.why: この and 料理の modify つくりかた in order, identifying it as the way to make this dish. つくりかた goes with を because it is the object of おしえてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern is also a request, but it changes to a question about ability and sounds softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is a very polite request and is more formal than てください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate の rigidly as “of,” but here it connects nouns to create the phrase “how to make the dish.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 座って is the て form of 座る, used to connect with ください in a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: てください creates a polite request or instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.why: The verb changes to the て form and then connects with ください to create a polite request. ください comes at the end of the sentence and determines the requesting tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 座りましょう is used, it means “let's sit together,” with the tone of an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q3.kobun.tip: The dictionary form cannot be used directly before ください; the verb must be changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vi: My older sister is a university student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 姉 the topic; 姉 is the humble way to refer to the speaker's older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects a noun showing a job or status with the topic to create a polite statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.why: The topic 姉 comes first with は, while 大学生 is the noun used as the predicate. です comes at the end of the sentence to give the introduction of the person's status a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, 姉 is emphasized as the identified subject instead of simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q4.kobun.tip: 姉 is used for one's own older sister; when talking about someone else's older sister, お姉さん is usually used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 招待しました is the polite past form of 招待する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.why: The object 友だち comes first and takes the particle を, followed by the verb 招待する. The form しました shows that the action was completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 誘いました, the meaning focuses on inviting a friend to go somewhere or do something together, not simply inviting them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q5.kobun.tip: 招待する is usually used to invite someone to attend or take part in an event, while 誘う usually means inviting someone to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vi: I asked my father to repair my watch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に refers to the person who performs the helpful action for the speaker in the pattern Vてもうらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing being repaired.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 直して is the て form of 直す, connecting the repair action to もらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてもらいました expresses that the speaker receives help from another person's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.why: The helper is marked by に, the affected object by を, and the action is connected using the て form with もらいました. This structure puts the speaker at the center of the benefit received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 父が時計を直してくれました, the sentence emphasizes that the father did it for me, with the father as the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that I received help, so the helper usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.tip: In Vてもらう, the helper uses に; do not mechanically change it to が based on the English wording.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + もらう/もらいます/もらいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vi: I am living in a large room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 広い comes before a noun to modify へや.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place of residence used with the verb すむ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: すんでいます expresses the state of residing somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.why: The adjective 広い comes before へや to describe the room. With すむ, the place of residence uses に, while ています expresses the current state of living there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use へやですんでいます, で focuses on the place where an activity happens, but with すむ, に is the basic way to indicate a place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q7.kobun.tip: Do not habitually use で with every place; すむ usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.sk: Time expression に + Nするしました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when an action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 結婚する changes to the polite past form 結婚しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.why: The time expression comes before the verb and goes with に. 結婚する is changed to the polite past to express an event that already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use で after a month, it is not suitable for indicating the time of marriage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily leave out に after a time expression, but the month when an event happens usually needs to go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks 血 as the subject that is flowing or appearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 出る changes to 出ています to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.why: 血 is what performs the state 出る, so が is used. The form 出ています emphasizes that the blood is flowing now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 出ました, it only says that the blood came out, without emphasizing its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t18-q9.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate ています as always meaning “be doing”; with 出ています, it usually indicates an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな modifies 味, while が marks the object being asked about in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: すきです is the predicate, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.why: どんな味が is the object that is liked, so it goes with が in the pattern 好きです. The predicate すきです comes at the end, with か added to form a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with 何の味, you ask specifically “the flavor of what,” rather than the broader meaning “what kind of flavor.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q1.kobun.tip: Learners may often use を with 好き, but the correct pattern is Nが好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vi: I received a map at a Japanese-style inn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the action of receiving the map happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました is the polite past predicate, expressing that something was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.why: The place where the action happens comes first with で, the received object comes before を, and then the past predicate ends the sentence. This order makes the place and object of the action clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace で with に, 旅館 may be understood as a place where something exists or a destination, rather than the place where the receiving action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q10.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use に for the place of an action, but the place where an action happens usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vi: There is a strange sound from the next room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with へや to form the phrase “the next room.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the place where the sound comes from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: へんな comes before 音 to modify and describe the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound perceived in the pattern 音がする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: します combines with 音が to express that a sound is produced or heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.why: となりのへや identifies the source of the sound, while から emphasizes that the sound comes from there. へんな modifies 音, and then 音がする forms a predicate expressing that there is a sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 聞こえます, the sentence emphasizes that the sound reaches the ears or can be heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 音を聞きます, the subject actively listens to the sound instead of simply noticing a sound being produced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.tip: Learners may easily translate します as “do,” but in 音がします it means “produce” or indicates the sense of a sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q11.kobun.cn: NのN; Aな + N; Nがする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vi: My father is injured and is in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the father as the topic of the two states and actions in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the phrase けがをする, meaning “be injured.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the two clauses in sequence or in a consecutive relationship: becoming injured and then being in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the place where the person mentioned exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: います is used for people and expresses the state of being in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.cn: Vて + V/A/N; Vて can connect consecutive actions or states
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.why: 父は is the common topic for the whole sentence. The phrase けがをして states the earlier condition, and then 病院にいます states where the person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use けがをしたので, the first clause becomes a clear reason for being in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing に with で is unnatural with います, because います expresses a place of existence and requires に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q12.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use で with います, but the place where a person or thing exists must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vi: Would you like to go watch a soccer match?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.sk: N の + N を + Vます-removeます に + 行きませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The form of ます with 見ます removed combines with に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きませんか expresses an invitation or polite suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.why: The phrase サッカーの試合を is the object of watching. 見に行く expresses going for the purpose of watching, while 行きませんか turns the whole sentence into an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only means that someone will go to watch it, without the inviting nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is also a suggestion, but it usually has the nuance of actively proposing to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate に as “come,” but in 見に行く, に only indicates the purpose “to watch.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vi: I will ask Maria directly whether she is going with us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: か is placed after 行く to state what the speaker wants to confirm.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person being asked, while 直接 modifies the way of asking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞いてみます uses the て form together with みます to express trying to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.why: 行くか states what needs to be asked, and the person being asked is marked by に. 聞いてみます expresses the intention to try asking directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 聞きます is used, the sentence only says that the speaker will ask, without emphasizing “trying to ask and see what happens.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes asking beforehand to prepare for what comes next.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 聞くか to mean “whether to ask or not,” but here か marks what needs to be asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this team the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 弱い is an adjective ending in い that serves as the predicate; です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.why: は makes the object of the comment the topic, while the adjective 弱い directly states the team's quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to “not weak.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only guesses from appearance that the team seems weak; it does not state this with complete certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q15.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い keeps い before です; do not add な as with an adjective ending in な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vi: The match was canceled because of the rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that led to the match being stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that enters the state of 中止.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the result or state that something changes into.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました expresses a change that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.why: 雨で states the cause, while しあいが is the subject whose state changes. 中止になりました expresses that the match changed into a canceled state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the subject will be a person or organization that actively cancels something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that something was canceled passively, without focusing on the process of changing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit に before なりました, but the change-of-state pattern requires Nに＋なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: たくさんの modifies the noun for birds that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the action of flying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 飛んで is the て form used to connect with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ています expresses an action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.why: たくさんのとりが is a plural subject, while 飛んでいます shows that the flying is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only says that the birds flew or took off, without emphasizing that they are flying now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern talks about the ability to fly, not an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q17.kobun.tip: The て form in ています does not express a command; here it combines with います to indicate an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vi: There are many cars here, so the air is especially bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that exists in large numbers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause to the result stated in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: に turns 特 into an adverb modifying the degree of 空気がわるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the object being described as bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: わるい is an adjective ending in い that serves as the predicate of the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.why: ここは identifies the place, and 車が多いので states the cause. The main clause 空気がわるいです states the result, while 特に adds the special degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason has a more direct and subjective nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with のに, the sentence means “although there are many cars...” rather than giving a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ので for “therefore”; in fact, ので follows the cause and leads to the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: もう modifies 一度, creating the meaning “one more time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the action of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 言う changes to the て form and combines with ください to make a polite request.
