default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.why: The adverbs come first to add the number of times and the manner of speaking. The pattern Vてください comes at the end of the sentence and turns the utterance into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ゆっくり is omitted, the sentence only asks someone to say it again, without emphasizing a slow speed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ください; they need to use the て form, such as 言ってください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the apple as the object of cutting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 切って is the て form of 切る, which connects with ください to create a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.why: そのりんごを is the object, placed before the verb and used with を. 切ってください is a polite request pattern, so the verb must change to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 切りましょう, the meaning becomes “let's cut it together,” so it is no longer a request to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form 切るください; before ください, you must use the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vi: I will collect the test papers now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the starting point of an action that is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks テスト as the object being collected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 集めます is the main predicate, using the polite form ます of 集める.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.why: The time adverb comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the object marked with を, and then the verb at the end. 集める is a transitive verb, so the object must be stated with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 集まります is used, the test papers gather by themselves; the sentence no longer means that the speaker collects them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 集める “collect something” with 集まる “gather by themselves,” leading them to choose the wrong particle and verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.vi: There is a Japanese test tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.sk: Time の ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates when an event happens and is placed at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本語 with 試験, showing that the test belongs to the Japanese subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 試験 is the thing that exists in an existence sentence with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate expressing the existence of a thing or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.why: The time is stated first. Then の forms the noun phrase 日本語の試験. For an inanimate thing or event, あります expresses the meaning “there is” or “exists.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 受けます is used instead, the sentence changes from announcing that there is a test to saying that someone will take the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate “there is” as います in every situation; あります is used for tests and inanimate things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.vi: The teacher is still in the classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 先生 the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies います, showing that the state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where 先生 exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: います is the predicate indicating the existence or presence of a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.why: 先生 is stated as the topic, while 教室に indicates where the teacher is present. まだ comes before the predicate to show that the state has not changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Using あります for a person is inappropriate; people and animals must use います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で to indicate a place of existence, but with いる, the place of existence usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.vi: Please do not enter the dangerous place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place that the speaker asks someone not to enter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 入らないで expresses a request not to perform the action of entering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.why: The place marked with に comes before the action 入る. The negative form 入らない combines with でください to create a polite request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入らないこと is used, the sentence has the tone of a rule or written command, which is firmer than a direct reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q23.kobun.tip: で must not be omitted in the pattern Vないでください; ないください is incorrect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.vi: I will go to meet my high school friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the phrase 高校時代 with 友だち, identifying the friends from the high school period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object of the action 会う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 会う changes to the continuative form 会い and connects with に to express purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the main predicate and takes the phrase 会いに as the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行く・来る・帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.why: The phrase 高校時代の友だち identifies the friend, に marks the person being met, and 会いに行きます expresses going for the purpose of meeting. The purpose verb comes before に, and the movement verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行きます is omitted, the sentence only says that the speaker will meet the friend, without emphasizing going to the meeting place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 会うに行きます; the correct structure is the form of 会います with ます removed, plus に, meaning 会いに行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vi: Today, the store will close at 9 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Time に ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the general time of the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by the closing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates when the closing action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 閉める uses the polite present form to describe an action that will be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.why: The topic is stated first with は, followed by the object お店を and the time 9時に. The verb 閉めます comes at the end and completes the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, it means starting from 9 o’clock, without emphasizing the exact closing time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に with で when talking about time; a specific time usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vi: I will make a cake and take it with me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the cake as the object of the action of making.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 作って is the て form of 作る, connecting the action of making with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: もって is the て form of 持つ written in kana, continuing the connection with 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the final predicate, showing how the action sequence ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.why: ケーキを is the object of 作って. Two verbs in the て form connect in sequence to express making first and then taking it, while 行きます comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 作ったあとで is used instead, it emphasizes the time “after finishing making it,” rather than naturally connecting the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q3.kobun.tip: The て form here does not mean a command; it connects actions in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vi: Because I am traveling, I will go to the airport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: から connects a cause with a result; here, the polite verb します comes before から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the verb 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main predicate, expressing movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ から／Aな・N ＋ だから; in polite speech, Vます形 ＋ から can be used
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and ends with から. Then comes the destination marked with に, followed by the main action. に is used for a destination; で is not used in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause is presented more gently and objectively than with から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If に replaces へ, the focus shifts to the direction of movement, while に emphasizes the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for every place, but the destination of 行く must use に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vi: A beautiful view can be seen from here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point or viewing position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な comes before 景色 to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object seen in the potential structure 見られます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 見られます is the polite potential form, expressing that the scenery can be seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ N; V一段 remove る ＋ られる; V五段 changes to the え row ＋ る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.why: ここから states the viewing position, while されいな modifies 景色. 景色が is the object that can be seen, and 見られます ends the sentence in the polite potential form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見えます is used, it means that the scenery comes into view naturally or can be seen, without emphasizing the act of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見ます is used, the sentence only says that someone looks at the scenery, without the meaning “can see.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 見られます with the passive voice, but in this sentence it has a potential meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: My school holds a graduation party in March.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.sk: N の + N では + Time に + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with 学校 to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: では shows that the school is the setting of the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the time of the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 開きます is the predicate and is used with を when the subject holds an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: わたしの学校では sets the context, ３月に shows the time, and the graduation party is the object of 開きます, so it goes with を. 開く, meaning to hold an event, uses the reading ひらく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This structure makes the party seem to open by itself or be opened, without clearly saying who holds it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 開く, read as あく when the subject opens by itself, with を, which means to hold an event and is read as ひらく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vi: If it rains, the concert will be canceled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the event that creates the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects the condition to the expected result in the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the concert the topic affected by the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 中止します is the main predicate and describes canceling the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first with 雨がふったら, and the result comes after it. は highlights that the concert is the object canceled when the condition occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence has a hypothetical meaning based on information that has been stated or is already known.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 中止する is replaced with this word, the meaning is to postpone the concert, not to cancel it completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 中止 for “postpone,” but this word means to stop or cancel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vi: My older sister is 17 years old.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Number + さいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows possession or the relationship between the speaker and 姉.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the older sister as the topic whose age is given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase “17 years old” is the predicate and uses です to end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.why: わたしの姉 forms a noun phrase meaning the speaker’s older sister. After the topic comes は, and age is expressed with the structure number + さいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this word is more polite or is used when talking about someone else’s older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q11.kobun.tip: When talking about one’s own family members in Japanese, 姉 is usually used instead of お姉さん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vi: I asked the receptionist where the hat counter was.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun 受付 with 人 and shows that the person belongs to the reception desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who was asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects ぼうし with うりば and identifies the type of sales counter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the information being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞きました is the polite past form of 聞く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.why: The phrase 受付の人 refers to the person being asked, so it goes with に. The phrase ぼうしのうりば is the information being asked about, so it goes with を before 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 聞く with 尋ねる still means asking someone, but the expression is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the person being asked; that person usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person receiving the apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 謝りました is the polite past form of 謝る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q13.kobun.why: The person receiving the apology is marked with に. The verb 謝る changes to the stem form ます, which is 謝り, and then combines with ました to express a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: 謝罪する also means to apologize, but it is more formal and official.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q13.kobun.tip: With 謝る, the person being apologized to uses に, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vi: Today, I informed them that I would be absent from school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object connected with the action of being absent from school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: という turns the clause やすむ into the information being reported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of しました; it is a notice saying that the speaker will be absent from school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.why: The clause やすむ comes before という to clarify the content of 連絡. は sets the time topic, while を after 連絡 marks carrying out the notice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also expresses reporting an event, but it treats the event more like a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern connects the reported content directly to the verb 連絡する and does not emphasize the noun 連絡.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.tip: Do not place という after the noun 連絡; という follows the whole clause やすむ here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形 + という + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.sk: N に + N を + past passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performed the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing taken away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: とられました is the polite past passive form of 取る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.cn: Vない形 remove ない + れる/られる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.why: The speaker is placed in the position of the affected subject, while 泥棒に names the agent that caused the event. Money is the affected object, so it goes with を and combines with the passive form とられました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This active pattern means that the thief takes the money and focuses on the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: The causative pattern means making or letting someone take the money, not having it stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q15.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, do not confuse に, which marks the agent, with を, which marks the affected object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.vi: My younger sister was able to enter a university in Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the younger sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the place とうきょう with the noun だいがく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or goal toward which entering university is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: できました expresses ability or an achieved result in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.why: とうきょうのだいがく forms a noun phrase meaning a university in Tokyo. に marks the place or goal of entering university, while できました shows that this was achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern expresses being able to do an action, while 入学できる is used directly with the noun 入学.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only describes entering university and does not emphasize ability or an achieved result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the name of a school with 入学する; the place or school entered goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q16.kobun.cn: N ＋ できる; Vる ＋ ことができる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.vi: This train is an express train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to refer to a specific thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that this train is the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic to a noun naming the train type and creates a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.why: この must come before でんしゃ to form the phrase “this train.” The structure NはNです is used to identify or explain the type of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes that the thing itself is an express train, instead of only stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: になります describes a change into an express train, so it is not suitable for identifying the current train type.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use この by itself; この always needs a noun after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.vi: I parked the car in the supermarket parking lot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun before it with the noun after it to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the car is placed or parked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object affected by the verb とめました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb とめる is changed into the polite past form とめました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.why: The place where the car is parked comes before the object and the verb. に indicates where the car is placed, while を marks the car being parked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence emphasizes the place where the action happens, but it is less natural than に with とめる when talking about where the car is placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で to mean “at,” but with とめる, に is usually used for the place where the car is parked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.vi: On the way to school, I met my teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of the action いく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: いく in its dictionary form modifies 途中, creating the meaning “on the way.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the time or place where meeting the teacher happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person the speaker meets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: あう is changed into the polite past form あいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.why: へ indicates the direction to school, while いく modifies 途中 to identify the process in progress. で marks the place or time when the meeting happens, and に marks the person met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vている途中で is used, the sentence emphasizes an action in progress more than the shorter form V辞書形＋途中で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If Nの途中で is used, the noun before it is a process or route, not a verb directly modifying 途中.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with the person they meet, but あう usually goes with に to indicate the person met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: Please show me that item for a moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: その comes before a noun to identify the item being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item that the speaker asks to see.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: ちょっと makes the request softer. その modifies 品物, 品物 is the object of 見せる and therefore takes を, then Vてください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This form asks whether the listener can do something for the speaker. It sounds softer and more like asking permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を before the verb, but the noun being shown still needs to be marked with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.vi: Please do not hesitate; please eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: Vないで connects to the following clause and means “do not do V” or “you do not need to do V.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of めしあがる connects with ください to create a polite invitation or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the verb in the て form to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.why: Vないで negates the action of “hesitating” and connects to the invitation to eat. めしあがってください is a polite request in which the verb is used in an honorific form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to Vないでください, the sentence is only a request not to do something and no longer invites the listener to do the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vなくてもいい is used, the sentence means “it is fine not to do it.” It is softer and does not directly connect to the invitation to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ないで as only a negation, but in this sentence it connects two actions and means “do not hesitate; please.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q20.kobun.cn: Vない形＋で; Vて形＋ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.vi: I gave my friend a Hokkaido souvenir.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects Hokkaido with the noun お土産 to show the origin or related place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the gift as the object being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the receiver in the action あげました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: あげる is changed into the polite past form あげました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.why: の identifies the souvenir as related to Hokkaido. を marks the thing given, while に indicates the receiver of the action あげる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If もらいました is used, the subject is the person who receives the gift, and Nに indicates the giver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: くれました describes another person giving something to the speaker or the speaker's side, so the receiver's viewpoint changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse あげる and もらう because Vietnamese can express both as “give/receive,” depending on the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before the noun 洋服 to modify the clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the clothes as the object of the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: かう is changed into the polite past form かいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q22.kobun.why: The adjective あたらしい comes before 洋服 to limit the type of clothes being discussed. を connects that noun to the verb かいました and shows the thing bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nの is used to modify a noun, the part before it is a noun showing a relationship or possession, not a direct description of the feature “new.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the adjective after the noun, following Vietnamese word order, but Japanese adjectives usually come before nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.vi: The meeting room is on the third floor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the meeting room as the topic whose location needs to be identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the location where the meeting room exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is the predicate used for the existence of objects or places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.why: は makes the object whose location must be found the topic. に indicates the place where it exists, while あります ends the sentence with the meaning “is located/exists” for an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence no longer naturally expresses a location because で usually indicates the place where an action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If Nがあります is used, the focus shifts to introducing that there is a meeting room, instead of identifying where the meeting room is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for every meaning of “at,” but for the location where あります exists, に is usually used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects かんじ with the noun after it to modify 辞典.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the item that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb かう is changed to the polite past form かいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q24.kobun.why: The phrase かんじの comes before 辞典 to identify the type of dictionary. This noun takes the particle を because it is the direct object of the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes that it is a dictionary related to Kanji. It is more formal and longer than かんじの辞典.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particles の or を, making the modifying relationship and the verb's object unclear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: きれい is a な adjective, so な must be used when it comes before the noun 音楽.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the sound that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: きこえます describes a sound that naturally reaches the ears, without emphasizing that the listener is actively listening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q25.kobun.why: The adjective きれいな directly modifies 音楽. With きこえる, the sound that is heard usually acts as the subject with が because the event happens naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 聞きます is used, it means actively listening to music, and 音楽 must be used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use きれいの音楽; the adjective な needs な when modifying a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: Sato is a very kind person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Sato is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 親切 is a な-ending adjective, so な is needed before the noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 人です forms a noun predicate and confirms Sato's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: さとうさんは is the topic, and とても modifies the degree of 親切. Because 親切 is a な adjective that comes before 人, it must be connected with な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes negative: the person is not kind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: The adjective な must keep な when it comes before a noun. It cannot be omitted as with the い adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: Recently, hot days have continued, but today is especially hot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.sk: Time + Aい N が + Vているが、N は + 副詞 + Aい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん refers only to the time when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the hot days as the subject of the continuing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two clauses with a mild contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: は shifts the comparison topic to today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 特別 modifies the degree of あつい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: あつい is the い adjective predicate of the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The first clause states that hot days are continuing, and が creates a contrast with today. 特別 comes before あつい to emphasize how hot today is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: 特にあつい also means especially hot, but it usually emphasizes something that stands out within a group or range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Do not always translate が as “but”; here it connects two clauses with a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: Do you have any plans for the summer vacation?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the summer vacation with 計画 to mean plans for the vacation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the summer vacation plan the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 何か acts as the indefinite subject of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ありますか creates a question about whether a plan exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: なつやすみの計画は identifies the topic as the summer vacation plan. 何か comes before ありますか to ask gently whether there is some plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence asks specifically, “What plans are there?” It is more direct and does not have the gentle nuance of 何か.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: 何か means “something” in a gentle question. It is not exactly the same as 何単独, which means “what” specifically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: I often go through this park on my way home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: この modifies the noun こうえん that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: を indicates the place or route through which an action passes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects going through the park with going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action 帰る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: This is the main predicate and describes returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The sentence gives the route with を通って, then states the destination with に. The て form connects going through the park with going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used here, the meaning becomes regularly going to a place, not passing through that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に with 通る, but a route that passes through a place must use を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vi: My younger brother is interested in world news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the younger brother as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 世界 with ニュース, creating the meaning “world news.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the object of the speaker's interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun 興味 and combines with 持つ to form the phrase “be interested.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 持っている describes a state of being interested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.why: N の N creates the noun phrase “world news.” The pattern 興味を持つ uses に to mark the object of interest and uses を for 興味.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is still “be interested,” but the structure changes to use 関心 as the subject with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in 興味を持つ as a place; here に marks the object of interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with the noun 産業 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the topic being researched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ている describes an action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.why: にほんの産業 creates a specific topic, while について connects that topic with the verb “research.” The ている form shows that the research is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the phrase about industry must come before another noun, such as “a document about industry.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の in にほんの産業, making the relationship between the two nouns unclear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vi: What should I prepare for tomorrow's party?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with パーティー to indicate the party taking place tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: には indicates the situation or object being prepared, while は emphasizes the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what needs to be prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: すれば is the ば form of する, used to ask what should be done in this situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Vばいいですか asks about a suitable way to do something or what should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.why: 何を is the content to be prepared and comes before 用意する. The pattern Vばいいですか turns the sentence into a question asking for guidance about what should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, the question still asks what should be done, but it focuses more on advice in a specific situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the sentence asks whether one should do it, rather than what needs to be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t2-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate ば as an ordinary condition; in Vばいいですか, the whole pattern means what one should do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vi: Please take this medicine before the meal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun しょくじ with 前 to form a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time before taking the medicine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: この comes before a noun to specify which medicine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the medicine as the object of the action of drinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 飲む changes to the て form and combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.why: The time phrase しょくじの前に is placed at the beginning to state the time. The object この薬を comes before the verb, while 飲んでください ends the sentence with a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, it means starting before the meal, emphasizing the starting point rather than the time before the meal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may forget that ください must come after the て form of a verb, not directly after the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vi: My older sister always makes a cake for me on my birthday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.sk: N は + time N に + Adv + N を + Vて + くれます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the older sister performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates when the action of making the cake usually occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: いつも is an adverb modifying the action くれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 作って is the て form, connecting the action of making the cake with くれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: くれます shows that another person does something beneficial for the speaker or the speaker's side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.why: The older sister is the topic, the time goes with に, and the cake is the object marked by を. The 作って form connects the action of making with くれます to express that the sister does it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the speaker emphasizes that they or someone does something beneficial for another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the sentence shifts the focus to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q10.kobun.tip: English learners may overlook the beneficiary meaning of くれる and simply understand it as doing an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vi: While the baby is sleeping, I do the housework.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that is sleeping in the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 寝ている expresses an ongoing state and modifies うち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: うちに indicates a period while a state continues; the comma separates the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the action やっています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: やっています is the ている form of やる, expressing an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.why: The clause 赤ん坊が寝ているうちに sets the time condition before the main clause. うちに emphasizes that the housework takes place while the baby is still asleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, it also means during that period, but it is more neutral and does not emphasize the opportunity before the state changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, it means that after the baby falls asleep, the speaker does the housework, emphasizing the order of events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may understand うち as a house; in this pattern, it means while a state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q11.kobun.cn: Vる・Vている・Vない・Aい・Aなな・Nの + うちに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q12.kobun.vi: The moon can sometimes be seen during the day, too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds the meaning “also,” emphasizing that this is one possible case among others.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q12.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning and goes with に. 月がみえる states the phenomenon, while こともある expresses that it sometimes happens as well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing も with が only states that the event sometimes happens, without emphasizing “also.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q12.kobun.tip: English learners may omit に after a noun showing time, or understand もある as “also exists” instead of “there are also cases where it happens.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.vi: I hear that the number of children being born has decreased since 2005.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: This clause modifies 子ども, referring to children who will be born.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 子ども with かず, forming the phrase “the number of children.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the number of children the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: から indicates the starting point of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects the verb 減る with いる to create an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: そうだ usually follows a clause to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.why: The clause 生まれてくる comes before 子ども to modify this noun. から states the starting point, while 減っているそうだ combines the continuing state with reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようだ is used, the sentence expresses an inference based on signs, not reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If てきた is used, it emphasizes that the decrease has continued until now, without stating the source of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse the reported-information form そうだ with そうだ, which shows appearance; before the reported-information form そうだ, the plain form must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q13.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; V普通形 + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.vi: My father's illness improved, so I felt relieved. He had been hospitalized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: して connects the action 入院する with いた in a phrase expressing a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: いた comes after して to form 入院していた and modifies 父.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 父 with びょうき, forming the phrase “father's illness.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the illness as the subject that becomes better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the cause with the result and makes the cause sound softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.why: 入院していた comes before 父 to modify father. The illness is the subject of よくなる, and ので connects the cause, the illness improving, with the result, the speaker feeling relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Using から instead of ので states the cause more directly and sounds more subjective and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with よくなる, but the thing that becomes better must be the subject and go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q14.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; V普通形 + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.vi: I am going to visit my mother tomorrow, so could you let me take one day off?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows the person being visited in the phrase 母の見舞い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.2.vi: to visit someone who is ill
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に comes after a noun showing purpose and goes with 行く to express going to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason for taking leave with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The phrase showing the length of the leave comes before the causative verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: やすませて is the て form of the causative form やすませる, and connects with いただく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: いただけませんか uses humble language to make a polite request for permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.why: 母の見舞いに行く is the phrase “go to visit my mother,” in which に marks the purpose. ので connects the reason with the request for permission, while やすませていただけませんか humbly expresses the request to be allowed to take time off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence is still a request for permission, but it is more casual and direct and does not stress humility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に行く to show the direction of movement, but in 見舞いに行く, に marks the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q15.kobun.cn: Nの + Nに行く; Vさせて + いただけませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.vi: Because of a traffic accident, cars could not pass at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.sk: Nで + Nが + ぜんぜん + past negative potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the cause that prevents cars from passing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks cars as the subject that can or cannot pass.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぜん modifies the negative predicate to stress the degree of being unable to pass.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 通れませんでした is the polite past negative potential form of 通る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.cn: Potential V + ませんでした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.why: で states the cause that prevents passing. The subject くるまが combines with the negative potential form 通れませんでした, while ぜんぜん emphasizes that passing was completely impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 通りませんでした is used, it means that the car did not pass, not necessarily that it was unable to pass.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse 通れません with 通りません; the first means “cannot pass,” while the second only means “did not pass.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.vi: From birth until now, the eldest daughter has needed the least care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the eldest daughter as the topic for comparison among the children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the starting point of the period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: まで shows the ending point of the period being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: いちばん modifies the phrase 手がかかりませんでした to create a superlative comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: In the phrase 手がかかる, が marks care as something that needs a lot or a little effort.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: The past negative form shows that caring for her has not required much effort up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.why: は sets the eldest daughter as the object of comparison, while から～まで limits the period. いちばん combines with the negative form of 手がかかる to express the person who needed the least care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: もっとも also means “the most,” but is more formal than いちばん in ordinary speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If the negative is removed, the meaning reverses to “required a lot of care.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 手がかかる literally as “the hands are stuck,” but the whole phrase means that someone needs a lot of care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q17.kobun.cn: Vてから; Nまで; いちばん + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.vi: Please follow the traffic rules and let us drive safely together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that is followed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 守って is the て form of 守る, used to connect this action with the call that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the action being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう is an inviting form that calls on people to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.why: The two actions are connected by the て form, and then しましょう gives a shared call to action. Each を marks the direct object of its corresponding verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence will only list typical actions and will no longer have the meaning of calling people to do them together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect two verbs with と, but in this sentence the て form must be used to connect the actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.vi: If you have any opinions about the travel plans, please feel free to share them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 旅行 with 計画, showing that the plan belongs to the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: について shows the topic that the opinion concerns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the noun いけん with the clause ある方, forming a modifier for 方.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ある is the predicate in the clause that modifies 方.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: 方 is a polite way to refer to people, while は marks the group of people being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: 言って is the て form of 言う, connecting the action of speaking with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.ch.7.n: Vてください is used to ask or request someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.why: The phrase 旅行の計画について states the topic of the opinion. The clause いけんのある comes before 方 to identify the person who has an opinion, and then は makes that person the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning is still about the plan, but the tone is more formal and written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If 方 is replaced with 人, it refers to people in general and the level of politeness is lower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand のある as a possessive phrase, but here いけんのある is a clause modifying 方.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q19.kobun.cn: N + について; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + N; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before a noun phrase to identify the object being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 昔 with ボタン, creating a noun phrase that modifies the button.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the button as the object of pressing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite imperative phrase comes at the end to ask the listener to press the button.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q2.kobun.why: その昔のボタン is a noun phrase in which 昔の modifies ボタン. After the object ボタンを, the request phrase おしてください completes the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If その is omitted, the meaning is still “old button,” but it no longer has the sense of identifying that particular button.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand の as showing possession only, but here の also connects one noun to modify the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.vi: Because I only joined the company last year, I still cannot do my work well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: 去年 indicates the time when the person joined the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place or destination of the action 入る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 入った is the past form of 入る. It comes before ばかり to show that the action happened recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたばかり shows that an action has just happened, while ので connects the reason to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: は presents the work as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: うまく modifies できません and shows the degree to which the work is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.ch.7.n: できません is the polite negative form and expresses that the person is not yet able to do the work well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.why: The phrase 去年会社に入ったばかりなので gives the reason first, followed by the result concerning work ability. は changes the topic to work, while まだ and うまく modify できません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the action has just happened at the moment of speaking, rather than the state of being a newcomer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and more conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ばかり as “only,” but Vたばかり here means “have just done something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q20.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ばかりだ; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.vi: I looked at the map while searching for the address.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.sk: Nを ＋ Vます omits ます ＋ ながら ＋ Nを ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the map as what is being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: ながら connects two actions happening at the same time, with the main action being さがしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the address as the object being searched for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: さがしました is the polite past-form main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.cn: Vます omits ます ＋ ながら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.why: 見ながら puts the secondary action first and connects it to the main action さがしました. The two を markers respectively show the map being viewed and the address being searched for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes one action happening during the time of another action. The two actions do not necessarily have to be performed by the same subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q21.kobun.tip: ながら must attach to the verb stem in the ます form after omitting ます. It does not attach directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.vi: We gathered at half past six and left immediately, so we arrived at the lake around nine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time of gathering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: あつまって is the て form and connects gathering with what happens next.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason 出発した with the result of arriving at the lake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: ごろ indicates an approximate time, while には emphasizes that time point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the destination of the verb 着く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: 着きました is the polite past-form main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.why: The actions are arranged in order: gathering, leaving, and then arriving. ので connects the reason for leaving early with the result of arriving at the lake, while に marks the time and destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If には is replaced with までに, the meaning changes to finishing before a deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for a destination, but with 着く they must use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q22.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.vi: Please write and submit the essay by next Wednesday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects らいしゅう with 水曜日 and identifies which week the Wednesday belongs to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the essay as the object of both writing and submitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 書いて is the て form and connects writing with submitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: だして connects the verb “submit” with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.why: The time-limit phrase comes before the object to show when the writing and submission must be completed. The two consecutive actions are connected by the て form, and ください comes at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ください is used, the sentence means that the person must write and submit it, so it is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is omitted, まで only emphasizes the end point of the time period and does not clearly state the deadline for completing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 書いてだして for a compound verb, but these are two consecutive actions connected by the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.vi: Besides black and white, this shirt comes in many other colors.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the shirt as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects two nouns of equal status in the color phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 以外 indicates an excluding range, while にも means that there are also other things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: いろいろな modifies the noun いろ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the colors that exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: あります is the predicate that indicates the existence of objects or events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は. Then にも expands the range to colors other than black and white. The noun いろ is the subject that exists, so it goes with が, while あります ends the existence sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 以外にも is replaced with だけ, the meaning becomes “only black and white,” excluding other colors.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: ほかにも also means that there are other things, but it does not clearly emphasize exclusion as 以外にも does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 以外にも for “there are only,” but this pattern means that there are additional things outside the stated range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.vi: Tonight, the moon is bright and beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tonight the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the features of being bright and beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The い-ending adjective changes to the くて form to connect the first feature with the next one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: きれいです is the final predicate and states the moon's second feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning with は, while the moon has two features, so が is used. The two adjectives are connected with the くて form of あかるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If そして replaces くて, the sentence still has the same meaning and is grammatical, but the connection becomes more separate, like two sentences or independent clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: し shows that reasons or features are being listed, giving a broader feeling than くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep あかるい unchanged when connecting words, but the い-ending adjective must change to あかるくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vi: I went to the supermarket to buy food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.sk: N へ + N を + Vます remove ます + に + 行く
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle へ shows the direction of travel to the supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks 食料 as what is bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 買い is the verb stem in the ます form of 買う. It combines with に to show purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate and describes an action that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + に + 行く/来る/帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.why: The destination スーパーへ comes before the purpose 買いに. The pattern verb stem in the ます form, remove ます + に + 行く, describes going somewhere to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 買うために, it also shows purpose, but the tone is more formal and emphasizes the purpose more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q3.kobun.tip: When showing purpose with 行く, do not place the plain verb form directly before に; use the stem ます, such as 買いに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the place where the answer should be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 解答 as the content being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 書く changes to the て form and combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q4.kobun.why: The place where the action happens is introduced with ここに, followed by the content to be written with を.書いてください comes at the end because it is the main request of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence only says where the writing takes place, without emphasizing the place where the answer should be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に and で; for a place that receives or holds content, に is more suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the bus is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: もう adds the meaning that the action happened before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 出発しました is the 出発する verb in the polite past form and shows that the departure has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q5.kobun.why: The topic バスは is stated first, followed by もう to show a completed state. The predicate 出発しました comes last to finish the information about the bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with まだ出発していません, the meaning changes to “the bus has not left yet.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate もう as “already” but forget that it often goes with a completed form to emphasize that something is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the room is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 暗い is an い-ending adjective used as the predicate; です comes at the end to make the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q6.kobun.why: The sentence introduces the topic first with は, then uses the adjective 暗い to describe the topic. です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If inserted, the meaning changes to “this room is not dark.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If inserted, the sentence changes to the past: “this room was dark.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that an い-ending adjective can come directly before です, without adding な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vi: There is nothing in particular that I want to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 特に is an adverb that modifies the negative meaning at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べたい is the want-to-do form and modifies もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: もの refers to an object or dish; は states the group of things being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.3.vi: there is not; do not have
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります and expresses nonexistence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.why: The clause 食べたい comes before もの to modify もの. The pattern ものはありません denies the existence of that object, while 特に emphasizes that there is nothing special.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing は with が only states that the dish one wants to eat does not exist, with less emphasis on the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means not wanting to eat anything at all, which is stronger than the original sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate ものは as an independent noun and forget that 食べたい comes before it to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q7.tokens.5.m: do not have; there is not
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vi: There is an exam next week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.sk: time N + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 来週 shows when the event happens; the comma separates the time adverbial.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists in a sentence using あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses the existence of an object or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.why: The time adverbial comes at the beginning. In an existence sentence, the thing being introduced usually goes with が, and the verb あります comes at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning is that someone will hold or take an exam, focusing on the action rather than existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with 試験, but a sentence saying that an exam exists uses が with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vi: Please wait in front of that flower shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 花屋 with the noun that follows, forming a phrase that identifies a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows where the action of waiting takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: お待ちください is a polite request pattern: お + the verb stem, remove ます + ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.cn: N の + N; お + Vます remove ます + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.why: The phrase あの花屋のまえで identifies the place to wait. In it, の connects the flower shop with the area in front of it. ください comes after the お待ち form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it is still a request to wait, but it is less polite than お待ちください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence is unnatural because に does not mark the place where the action 待つ takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t20-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に and で; an action that happens at a place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamada's jacket on Tuesday seems to have been brown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows possession or a connection with Mr. Yamada.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the time Tuesday with the specified noun 上着.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the jacket is the topic whose color is being guessed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: たしか is an adverb showing incomplete certainty in memory or guesswork.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ちゃいろでした is a noun predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.why: The two phrases with の respectively identify the owner and the time related to the jacket. After the topic comes an adverb showing a guess, followed by a past noun predicate describing the jacket's color at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 火曜日に着た上着 is used, the meaning focuses on the jacket worn on Tuesday, not merely the time when the jacket is identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 上着だった is used to say that something is a jacket, not to describe the jacket's color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically translate the sequence の as several possessive phrases, but の in 火曜日の only shows a time relationship with the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vi: Many cute cats and dogs are being sold on the rooftop of the department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the department store with the rooftop belonging to it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the selling activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective かわいい modifies the animals being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: や connects items in an incomplete list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the objects being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: たくさん modifies the number of items being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: 売っています uses the ている form to describe a selling activity that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.cn: NやN is used for listing; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.why: で identifies the place where the activity takes place, を marks the animals being sold, and たくさん shows the quantity. や indicates that cats and dogs are only examples in the list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ねこと犬を is used, the meaning usually includes exactly these two types in a complete list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 売ります only states the selling action in general and does not stress that it is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q10.kobun.tip: や does not mean “and” in the sense of a complete list; it usually shows that there are other items as well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vi: Because the large store has many goods, I think it will be easy to buy souvenirs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: には states the place and provides the setting for the information that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists in the store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: たくさん modifies ある and shows the quantity of goods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason clause with the result and gives a gentle explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the content of the judgment stated before 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.why: The clause あるので gives the reason first, and the judgment comes afterward. やすい attaches to the verb stem in the ます form to express that something is easy to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If にくい replaces it, the meaning changes to “difficult to buy souvenirs.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is replaced by から, the reason becomes more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that やすい must connect to the verb stem in the ます form, not directly to the dictionary-form verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q11.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + やすい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vi: In Japan, cars must drive on the left side of the road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: では limits the scope of the information to Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents 車 as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 道 with 左がわ to identify the left side as belonging to the road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the route or part of the road on which the car drives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 走らなければ is the conditional form of 走る in the obligation pattern なければなりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: なりません completes the pattern expressing an obligation or requirement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.why: では sets the context, while は states the object subject to the rule. The phrase 走らなければなりません expresses the requirement to drive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced by なくてもいい, the meaning changes to “do not need to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If てはいけません is used, the sentence expresses a prohibition, not an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.tip: Do not translate なければ separately as “if not”; in this pattern, the whole phrase なければなりません means “must.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q12.kobun.cn: Vない形（ない → なければ） + なりません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.vi: Yesterday, after finishing dinner, I went straight to bed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets yesterday as the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks dinner as the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects eating with the sleeping action that happens immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: すぐ modifies 寝ました and shows that the time gap is very short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.why: 食べて comes first to show the earlier action, while 寝ました is the main action that happens afterward. すぐ emphasizes that the two actions happen almost one after the other.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is used, it more clearly stresses that the person must finish eating before going to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If たあとで is used, the meaning is still “after eating,” but the order sounds clearer and more neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q13.kobun.tip: て connects the two actions in sequence in this sentence; it does not simply mean “and.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.vi: When I saw a Western person, I suddenly remembered my parents who are in France.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 西洋 with 人 to form the noun phrase “Western person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person who was seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition or time with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where 両親 is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: いる comes before 両親 to modify “parents” and show that they are in France.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the parents as the object being remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.why: The phrase Vると states the situation that causes the result. The clause フランスにいる comes directly before 両親 to modify “parents,” following Japanese modification order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見ると replaces 見たら, the sentence focuses more on the condition “if/after seeing,” with less of a natural reaction meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 思い出す is used in the present tense, the sentence no longer stresses that the event happened yesterday or in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q14.kobun.tip: A modifying clause always comes before the noun; therefore, いる must come before 両親, not after the noun as in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.vi: At the venue, more than 100 people from a newspaper company had been invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates the location where the invited people are present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 以上の modifies 人たち and indicates a quantity of 100 or more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: の indicates the relationship所属 and shows that these people belong to a newspaper company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject affected in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: 招待されて is the passive form connected to いました and expresses an ongoing state of being invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.ch.5.vi: had been in the state of
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.why: The phrases の modify 人たち in order, showing the number and所属. The subject is the people who were invited, so the passive form 招待され is used. Then, ていました expresses a state of existence in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 招待しました is used, the subject is the person who invited them, not the people who were invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 招待されました is used, it only says that the invitation happened. It does not emphasize the state of being there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.tip: With passive sentences, Vietnamese learners may easily mistake the subject for the person who performs the action. Here, 人たち is the person affected by the invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q15.kobun.cn: N・Vます形の語幹 + される; Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the state or situation in which 生きる is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: こと turns 生きる into a noun, while は makes the whole action of living alone the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q16.kobun.why: で describes the living situation, while こと nominalizes the verb 生きる so that the whole action can be the topic with は. すばらしい is the predicate that evaluates this topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことは is replaced with のは, the basic meaning is similar, but the tone is more conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If のが is used, “living alone” becomes the subject being evaluated or liked, rather than the contrasting topic.
