default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q16.kobun.tip: こと comes after the plain-form verb to nominalize the whole action. Do not always translate こと separately as “thing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q16.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + こと + は + Aい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.vi: I hear that a world skiing competition will be held in a small mountain town.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 山 with the noun phrase that follows, creating the meaning “a town in the mountains.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the competition will be held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies 世界大会 and shows the content of the competition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the event that is predicted to take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 開かれる is the passive form and expresses that the competition will be held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです comes at the end of the sentence to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the subject of the event, while 世界大会が開かれる forms the information being reported. そうです is placed at the end because the whole sentence is information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it expresses a state, the sentence means “it looks as if it is about to be held” instead of “I hear that it will be held.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse そうです, which reports heard information, with そうです, which describes appearance or signs that something is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.vi: My stomach hurts a lot, so I do not feel well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: すごく modifies いたくて and shows the degree of pain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the painful state with the following condition, creating a cause or a sequence of events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the state 悪い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective 悪い is the predicate, while です creates a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.why: The sentence first states the symptom of stomach pain and then connects it to feeling unwell with て. Each state has its own subject, so both おなか and 気分 go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If いたくて is replaced with いたいので, the sentence emphasizes the cause more clearly: “because it hurts, so...”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with a body part, but a state such as おなかがいたい usually uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.vi: This express train does not stop at that station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to point to a specific thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 特急電車 the topic of the negative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the train stops, while は adds a contrastive or emphatic tone to this location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 止まりません is the polite negative form of 止まる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.why: The topic is the type of train, and the stopping place is expressed with に. は after に creates a contrast and emphasizes that the train does not stop at that particular station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is removed, the sentence only gives the neutral information that the train does not stop at that station. It has no contrastive tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate に as “arrive,” but with 止まる, に indicates the place where the train stops.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vi: Although I started in the morning, the work was still not finished by the evening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects an event that has happened with an unexpected result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: になっても expresses that even though the time had changed to evening, the following situation remained the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that the work is the topic of the result being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The past negative verb form shows that the work was still unfinished by that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.why: から sets the starting point, and のに creates a contrast between starting early and not finishing. になっても gives a later time point, but the result remains the same. Then the main clause states that the work was unfinished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with けれども, the sentence only connects two mildly contrasting ideas and does not emphasize that the result was unexpected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 夕方まで is used, it means that the work was unfinished until the evening, without the concessive meaning of “even though that time had come.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse のに with purpose, but in this sentence のに means “although” and connects two clauses with an unexpected contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.tokens.6.m: even after it became, even by the time it became
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.tokens.9.m: was not finished, did not end
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + のに; N・Vて + も; Nに + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the entered data is received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the entering action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: しなければ is the conditional form of the verb in a pattern expressing an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: なりません completes the pattern expressing an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q20.kobun.why: The place for entering comes before the object and the verb. The phrase しなければなりません turns the idea “if you do not do it, it is not allowed” into a required action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 入力してください, the sentence becomes a polite request with a weaker sense of obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand しなければ as “must not do,” but the whole pattern しなければなりません means “must do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.vi: On days off, I usually listen to music, go shopping, or clean my room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 休み with 日, forming the phrase "day off".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the day off as the time and topic of the activities.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 音楽 as the object being listened to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: たり marks one activity listed as an example.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: に shows the purpose of going and combines with 行く to mean "go shopping".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: たり continues listing the second activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks へや as the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.7.n: たり lists the final activity, while して connects the list to います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.ch.8.n: ています describes a continuing state or habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.why: The activities are listed by repeating たり, then ending with して います. に in 買い物に行く shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If the sentence ends with たり〜たりします, it only lists activities that are usually done. It does not stress a continuing state like ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use たり for only one action, but the listing pattern usually needs several verbs in the たり form and ends with します or しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.vi: Tonight is a beautiful night, with many stars in the sky.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は gives the time and topic of the description.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows where the stars appear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that is appearing in large numbers in the sky.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: いっぱい modifies the state of appearing and shows a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: ている describes the state in which the stars have appeared and are still there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: きれいな uses the form な to modify 夜.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: 夜です is the main predicate and concludes that this is a beautiful night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.why: The clause ほしがいっぱい出ている comes before 夜 to modify "night." きれいな also directly modifies 夜, while です ends the main statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 出ます is used, the sentence only says that the stars will appear or usually appear. It does not stress the state of being visible in the sky now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place きれいです before 夜, but before a noun, the きれいな form must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamada's clothes on Tuesday seem to have been a blue jacket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.sk: N の + N の + N は + adverb + N の + N でした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun to the following noun to show possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の modifies 洋服 and shows that the clothes mentioned are Tuesday's clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 洋服 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: たしか is an adverb showing an incomplete memory or an uncertain guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 青色 with 上着 to modify the jacket's color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: でした is the polite past form of です and serves as the predicate concluding the statement about 洋服.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.why: The phrases の successively narrow the scope from the owner and time to the item being discussed. は presents 洋服 as the topic, while 青色の directly modifies 上着.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 青色の is replaced with 青い, the meaning of blue stays almost the same, but the expression changes from a color noun to an adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that の must stand between 青色 and 上着 to form the noun phrase "blue jacket."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.vi: Because there were absolutely no empty seats in the movie theater, I stood at the back and watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.sk: N の + N が + adverb + past negative Vている + ので + N で + Vて + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 映画館 with せき to show that the seats belong to or are inside the movie theater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks せき as the subject of the state 空いていなかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぜん modifies the negative predicate to stress that there were no empty seats.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.3.vi: because there were no empty seats
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 空いていなかった shows a state of being occupied in the past, while ので connects the reason to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: で shows the place where the actions of standing and watching take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: 立って is the て form, connecting standing with the following action of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: 見ました is the main predicate and describes the action of watching in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with ので, followed by the location 後ろで and the sequence of actions 立って見ました. で shows where the action takes place, while the て form connects two consecutive actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 後ろに is used, に only shows direction or a location of existence. It is less natural than で when talking about the place where someone stands and watches.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of で in this sentence, but the place where an action takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.vi: My mother prepared special dishes for the New Year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + Aな な + N を + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 母 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the time when the mother prepared the food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: な connects the adjective ending in な 特別 with the noun 料理.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks 料理 as the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 用意しました is the main verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.why: に sets the time, while 特別な comes before 料理 to describe the quality of the food. 料理を is the direct object of 用意しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If お正月に is replaced with お正月に向けて, the meaning changes to preparing for the New Year, emphasizing purpose rather than time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put な after 特別, but an adjective ending in な needs な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vi: My mother and older sister are preparing to cook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects mother and older sister as people performing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks mother and older sister as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: から shows when the preparation starts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the content of cooking with the noun 用意.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object of the action 用意しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: しています is しています, showing that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.why: と connects the two people participating together, while は makes the whole group the topic. The phrase りょうりの用意 shows preparation for cooking, while を marks it as the object of しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 料理を準備しています is used, the direct meaning is preparing dishes or cooking, without making the noun 用意 the focus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If しています is replaced with 用意しました, the action is complete instead of ongoing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を immediately after 母と姉, but と here connects people doing the action together, and を must come after the object 用意.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q3.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ 用意をする; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vi: When crossing the road, please be very careful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the road that is traveled along or crossed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb clause in dictionary form modifies とき, while は states that situation as the condition for being careful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 十分 modifies 注意, requiring full attention or great care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 注意して is the て form of 注意する, making it the action before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end to turn the preceding action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.why: 道をわたるときは puts the situation and time requiring attention at the beginning of the sentence. Then the adverb 十分 modifies 注意, while 注意してください is a polite request pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ときには is used, the sentence focuses on crossing roads in general, without clearly marking the topic as ときは does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 注意してください is replaced with 気をつけてください, the meaning is still “please be careful,” but the expression sounds more natural in everyday reminders.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate を as “cross,” but in 道をわたる, を marks the road being crossed, not an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた ＋ とき; Vて ＋ ください; Nを ＋ 注意する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vi: I hear that he often goes to the hospital because he is in poor health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun からだ with ぐあい to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that has the condition 悪い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the cause with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: に shows the place or destination of the action 通う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects 通う with いる to form the 通っている form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: いる follows a verb in the て form to show an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: そうです at the end of the sentence shows information that the speaker heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.why: The phrase からだのぐあい is the subject of the condition 悪い. The cause clause comes first, followed by the place 病院に and the ongoing action 通っている; そうです is placed at the end to report heard information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようです is used instead, the sentence expresses a judgment based on signs or observation, not reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に as the object of 通う, but に here shows a place that someone regularly goes to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q5.kobun.cn: Aい・Aなな・Nな・V普通形 ＋ ので; Vて ＋ いる; V普通形 ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vi: Because a large typhoon hit, food became scarce.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective 大きい comes before and modifies 台風.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the event that causes the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the result; きた is the past form of 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that changes into a state of shortage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 足りない changes into 足りなくなる to express a change to an insufficient state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; Aい omit い ＋ くなる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.why: 台風がきたので is the cause clause that comes first. The subject of the result is 食料品, while 足りなくなりました describes the change from enough to not enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives the reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 足りませんでした only says that the food was not enough; it does not emphasize the process of becoming scarce.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q6.kobun.tip: You must distinguish 足りない, which is a state of not being enough, from 足りなくなる, which means becoming not enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vi: The clothing and men's underwear sales counter is where you have just gone down the stairs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a phrase showing intended use with the noun 服.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: や connects nouns listed as examples.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the group of products with the noun 売り場.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that the sales counter is the topic whose location is identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the route or place through which the action 下りる takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The clause 下りた modifies ところ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: に shows where the sales counter exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: あります expresses existence, while よ adds a tone of informing the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ところ; NやN is used to list nouns
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.why: 売り場は is the topic, while 下りたところに identifies the counter's location. The clause 下りた comes before ところ to modify that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 下りるところ is used, it means a place that someone is about to go down or a place for going down, not a place that someone has already gone down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 下りているところ emphasizes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 下りたところ as “went down to a place,” but here the whole phrase means “the place just after going down.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vi: The entrance to the parking lot is at the back of the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a location with a part belonging to that location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the entrance is the object whose location must be identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the building with its back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the location where the entrance exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is used for the existence or location of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.why: The entrance is made the topic with は. The phrase たてもののうらがわに indicates the location, and then あります completes the existence sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replace あります with います only when the subject is a person or animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use います for the entrance or the building because they are an object and a place, not living things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vi: The employee at the nearby vegetable shop seems to be a foreigner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the nearby location with the shop being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the shop with the employee who works there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the employee is the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Nのようです expresses a judgment based on appearance or signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.why: The phrases の indicate a location and a relationship of belonging, respectively. After 店員さん is introduced as the topic, Nのようです is used to make a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Using Nだそうです conveys heard information that the person is a foreigner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Using Nらしいです focuses more on a guess based on known information or characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.tip: With a noun, use のようです, not 外国人ようです directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t21-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ようだ/ようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vi: I hear that Doctor Yamada is a very kind and gentle doctor toward older people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.sk: N は + N を + Vた + N に + adverb + Aな で + Aい + N だそうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 山田先生 the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 年 as the object in the expression 年をとる, meaning to be older.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: とった is a modifying clause for 方. It comes before the noun without a relative pronoun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the people who receive kindness and gentleness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the qualities 親切 and やさしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: 親切で uses the て form of a な-ending adjective to connect it to the next adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: やさしい modifies お医者さん and adds another quality of the doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.7.vi: is said to be a doctor
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: だそうです is placed at the end of the sentence to report heard information that this person is such a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.why: とった comes before 方 to form the modifying clause “a person who is older.” に indicates the person treated well, while 親切でやさしい are two parallel qualities before the noun お医者さん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうな is used, the sentence means “looks kind,” based on a visible impression rather than heard information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 方に is replaced with 方に対して, the target of the action is emphasized more clearly, and the expression is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the clause とった after 方, but in Japanese a modifying clause always comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.tokens.5.m: be of a certain age, grow older
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vi: Next June, I am really looking forward to returning to my home country after a long time and eating my mother's cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.sk: N の + time に + N へ + Vて + N が + Vた + N を + V辞書形のが + N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 来月 with ６月, forming a noun phrase for a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に turns the phrase ひさしぶり into an adverb showing the circumstances of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of the action 帰る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: て-form connects the action of returning with the action of eating the food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject performing 作った in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The clause 作った comes before and modifies 料理.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: を marks the food that is 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.8.n: の turns 食べる into a noun, while が marks eating as the thing being looked forward to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.9.vi: is something I look forward to
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.ch.9.n: です ends the noun sentence and expresses anticipation about eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.why: The time and direction phrases come first, followed by a series of actions connected with て. The whole phrase 食べるのが is turned into a noun to serve as the subject of the noun adjective 楽しみです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence emphasizes the subject's active anticipation of an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is replaced, the sentence expresses a state of looking forward to something rather than an expected pleasure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の before が and say 食べるが directly, which creates an incorrect nominalization structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.vi: When crossing the road, please be very careful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being crossed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: とき creates a time phrase, while は makes that situation the topic of what requires attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 十分 modifies 注意して and indicates the degree of attention required.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: する changes into して to connect the action 注意する with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after the て-form to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.why: The clause わたるときは states the prior situation, while 注意してください is the main request. を marks the road being crossed, and てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of は, the sentence only states the time of the action and does not emphasize the situation requiring attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the reminder becomes stronger and more commanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 注意してください directly after 十分 and forget to change 注意する into 注意して.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.vi: Because I have to finish the research within two months, I am working in a hurry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.sk: Deadline に ＋ N を ＋ V使役形なければ ＋ いけないので ＋ Vて ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 以内に indicates the deadline by which an action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the task being completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 終わらせる in the negative conditional form なければ creates the condition for the required clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.3.vi: because I have to do it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: なければいけない expresses obligation, while ので connects the reason to the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: て-form connects the manner急いで with the action やっています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: ています expresses an action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.why: The deadline and the object of the task come before the obligation structure. ので connects the reason for having to finish it with the result that the speaker is working in a hurry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to not having to finish it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 終わる is used, it means that the research ends by itself, without emphasizing that someone makes it finish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 終わる for completing something, while 終わらせる expresses making that thing finish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q12.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ なければいけない; Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.vi: I do not feel well today, so I will go to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は turns “today” into the time and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 体 with 具合, creating a phrase that describes a physical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the adjective 悪い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason for feeling unwell with the action of going to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: 行きます is the main predicate and expresses the action of going politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.why: The phrase 体の具合が悪い forms a reason clause, and then ので connects it to the result 行きます. へ identifies the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with から, the reason is stated more directly and sounds more subjective and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If て is used, the two clauses are connected more softly, but the reason is less clear than with ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place は after 具合, but here は must connect with きょう to state today’s topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q13.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ ので; N ＋ な ＋ ので; V普通形 ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.vi: Put the letter in an envelope and send it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that is put into the envelope and sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the letter is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: て-form connects the action of putting the letter in with the action of sending it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 出す is the final predicate and expresses the action of sending or taking something out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.why: を marks the letter as the object being handled, while に indicates the destination of putting it in. The two actions are connected in order by 入れて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, it means taking the letter out of the envelope, which is opposite to the direction of the action in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is added, the sentence emphasizes putting it in first and sending it afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for the envelope, but に indicates the destination of the action 入れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.vi: Because there was a large typhoon, yellow water flowed out of the tap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: 大きい directly modifies 台風.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that occurs and causes the stated situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause of the typhoon with the result of water flowing out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: から indicates the source or starting point of the water.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: きいろい modifies 水 and describes the color of the water.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject showing the state 出ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: 出ました is the main predicate and expresses that water flowed out or appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.why: The clause about the typhoon comes first to state the reason, while the following clause describes the source, feature, and appearance of the water. から identifies that the water came from the water system.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is presented more directly and subjectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is used instead of から, the sentence may be understood as water appearing at the tap rather than flowing out of it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use が for a starting place, but the source of the water must go with から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.vi: I hear that trucks carrying goods to faraway places usually leave late at night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being transported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies トラック.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that the truck is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: そうです comes after the plain form to convey information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.why: The clause 運ぶ comes before トラック to identify what kind of truck it is. The phrase 夜おそくに comes before 出発する to indicate the time, while そうです at the end of the sentence shows that the information was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ようです, the sentence changes to an inference based on signs or circumstances, rather than information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places the clause 運ぶ before トラック.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.vi: When I was at university, I especially liked geography and literature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the period as the topic and background of the preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects 地理 with 文学 as two objects that are both liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object liked with the adjective 好き.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 好き is the adjective な, and でした is used to talk about a past state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.why: 大学時代は places the time setting at the beginning of the sentence. The two nouns 地理 and 文学 are connected by と, and then が combines with 好き to mark the things that are liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 好きだった, the tone is more casual, but it still expresses a past preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 好き, but the basic pattern is Nが好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.vi: Because I was having a birthday party, I decorated the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 誕生日 with パーティー to show a modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the place being decorated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 飾った is the past form of 飾る and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.why: Clause するので gives the reason before result 部屋を飾った. Both パーティーをする and 部屋を飾る use を to mark the direct object of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ために is used, the sentence can more easily express a purpose or a more formal reason, depending on how it is connected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ので as “so,” but structurally it comes after the reason clause and before the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.vi: The men's clothing department is where you just went down the stairs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects phrase 男せい用 with 服 to modify clothing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 服 with 売り場, creating the meaning “clothing department.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the place whose location needs to be identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: を indicates the route or place passed through when going down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: 下りた modifies ところ and indicates the place after going down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the location where 売り場 exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: あります describes the existence of a place, while よ is used to give information or add emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.why: The phrase 下りたところ indicates a place created by the action of going down. That place goes with に, and then あります states that the clothing department exists there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 下りるところに, it means the place where someone is about to go down or is preparing to go down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If 下りてから is used, the focus shifts to the time order: after going down, the department is there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で with あります, but the place where an object exists must use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q19.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ところに + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vi: The waves will probably be higher tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets tomorrow as the time reference and the topic of the forecast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 波 as the subject whose state changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 高く is the continuative form of adjective 高い. It connects with なる to show a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: なる expresses becoming high, while でしょう ends the sentence with a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.why: あしたは gives the forecast time, and 波が is the subject of the change. The adjective must change to 高く before なる to express “become high,” and then でしょう adds a guessing nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 高くなるでしょう is replaced with 高いでしょう, the sentence only predicts that the waves will be high. It does not emphasize the change to becoming high.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say 高いなる, but before なる, the adjective ending in い must change to form く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.vi: My mother makes me a lunch box every morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.sk: N が + Time + N を + Vて + くれます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who makes the lunch box.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to show a repeated time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item being made; お is a polite prefix.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the main verb with くれる, creating a structure that means doing something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: くれます shows that the action is done for the speaker's benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.why: 母が is the doer, while お弁当を is the object affected by つくる. Form て connects つくる with くれる to show that the mother does it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つくります, it only says that the mother makes a lunch box and does not emphasize that the action benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If つくってあげます is used, the speaker views the action from the perspective of the person doing something for someone else. It is less suitable than くれます when the receiver is the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the direction of giving and receiving; when someone does something beneficial for you, use Vてくれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q20.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる/くれます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.vi: My older brother has been working as a taxi driver since last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.sk: N は + Time point から + N の + N を + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the older brother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects タクシー with the job or position being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the job that しています shows the person is doing or holding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: しています expresses the continuing state of doing that job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.why: 去年から identifies the starting time, while しています shows that the job is continuing. の connects タクシー with 運転手 to create the phrase “taxi driver.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with まで, it means working as a driver until last year, suggesting that the person may have stopped now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 運転手になりました is used, the sentence only emphasizes becoming a driver and does not confirm that the person continues to work as one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand しています as only “be working” at a certain time, but in a sentence about a job, it usually describes work that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q21.kobun.cn: N + から; Vて + いる/います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q22.kobun.vi: I listen to the correct English pronunciation using a tape recorder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means used to perform the action of listening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 英語 with the noun phrase that follows; 正しい modifies はつおん, while を marks the object of 聞きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞きます is the main predicate and uses the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q22.kobun.why: The phrase showing the means comes first, the object being heard comes next, and then the main verb. Adjective 正しい comes before noun はつおん to clarify what kind of pronunciation it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning focuses more on the accuracy and objectivity of the pronunciation than on “correct” as opposed to wrong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the adjective after the noun, but in Japanese the adjective must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q23.kobun.vi: I change my underwear in the changing room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the action of changing clothes happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: とりかえます is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q23.kobun.why: Use で for the place where the action happens and を for the affected object, followed by the verb. This order forms a basic action sentence in Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of で, the sentence sounds unnatural because に does not mark the place where an action is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the place where an action happens; for an action such as changing clothes, use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.vi: Last week, I lent my friend 10,000 yen, and today they paid me back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence and sets the time of the lending action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who received the money that was lent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: This is the amount of money affected by 貸しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 貸しました is the predicate of the first clause in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The time phrase sets the time of the action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: 返して is the て form, connecting the verb “pay back” with もらいました in a pattern for receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: もらいました acts as the predicate and shows that the speaker received the action of being paid back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.why: The two clauses are connected in time order: lending comes first, and receiving the money back comes later. に marks the person who received the money in the first clause, while Vて＋もらう expresses that the speaker received the action of being paid back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the focus is on the friend doing it for the speaker, showing gratitude more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says “paid back” and does not emphasize that the speaker received this action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse てもらう with てくれる; remember that てもらう is viewed from the side of the person who benefits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q24.kobun.cn: Vて-stem ＋ もらう／もらいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.vi: Everyone is laughing and singing at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the general topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: ながら connects the verb stem without ます to the main action, showing that the two actions happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the song as the object of the verb うたっています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 〜ています describes an action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.why: The secondary action 笑いながら comes first, while the main action うたっています comes later. Since the subjects of both actions are the same group, use ながら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it lists typical actions without emphasizing that they happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If the pattern connected by て is used, the meaning of simultaneous actions is less clear, and it may simply connect the actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q25.kobun.tip: Before ながら, use the verb stem without ます, not the dictionary form such as 笑うながら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vi: Not only income, but land and houses are also taxed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: はもちろん presents the first object as clearly included, while opening the scope to additional objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: や gives an incomplete list of objects of the same type.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: にも adds 家屋 to the range of objects affected by the tax.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks 税金 as the subject to which the tax applies or arises.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: かかる is the predicate and expresses that the tax applies to the objects mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.why: はもちろん presents an obvious object first, then や additionally lists land, and にも emphasizes that houses are also within the scope of taxation. 税金がかかる uses が to state that a tax arises.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If はもちろん is replaced with だけでなく, the sentence still means “not only,” but the tone はもちろん emphasizes more strongly that the first object is naturally included.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 土地や家屋も is used, the meaning “both land and houses” remains clear, but the expanded structure はもちろん is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate かかる as “hang” or “be lost,” but in 税金がかかる, it means that a tax applies or must be paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q3.kobun.cn: N はもちろん、Nも・NやNにも ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vi: Starting tomorrow, I will begin keeping a diary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being written about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: つけよう is the volitional form of つける, expressing an intention or an invitation to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q4.kobun.why: から sets the starting point, then を marks the diary as the object of the writing action. The volitional form at the end of the sentence expresses the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つけます, the sentence becomes a polite statement about the action and no longer has the clear sense of self-determination or invitation found in the volitional form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake つける here for “attach,” but with 日記を it means “write or keep a diary.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vi: It is said that, because washing cleaning cloths makes their hands dirty, more and more housewives dislike cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the cleaning cloth as the object being washed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition with a natural result: whenever the cloth is washed, the hands become dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the body part that experiences the dirty state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the cause clause with the result stated after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks cleaning as the object judged to be unpleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: いやな uses the な form to modify the noun 主婦.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: が marks the subject that is increasing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: 多い changes into 多くなった to express a change to a state of being more numerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.ch.8.n: そうだ is placed at the end of the sentence to report information heard by the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.why: The condition and cause clauses come first, followed by the result: the number of people who dislike cleaning has increased. が mark the hands experiencing the state and the subject that is increasing, respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still states the cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: と here states a natural result after a condition, not simply the meaning “and.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use から in every situation, but ので is usually softer and more objective when explaining a cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vi: He is good at playing musical instruments.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes him the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun 楽器 with 演奏, showing the content or type of performance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what is judged to be a strong point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: とくいです is the adjective predicate な in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.why: は introduces the person being discussed, while の identifies the type of performance. The pattern Nが得意です is used to say that an activity or field is someone’s strong point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 上手です is used, the emphasis is on performing a skill well, while 得意です emphasizes that it is a strong point or something the person feels confident about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q6.kobun.tip: Do not translate 得意 mechanically as “special”; in this structure, it means “good at” or “having a strong point.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vi: Let’s rest for a while at that café.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the resting action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q7.kobun.why: で identifies the place, 少し adds the degree to the resting action. ましょう at the end of the sentence turns it into a polite invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 休みませんか, the invitation becomes a soft question, more like “Shall we rest?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with a place, but an action that takes place somewhere must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vi: This Saturday, I plan to learn how to use the new machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今週 with 土曜日 and identifies which week the Saturday belongs to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the learning is planned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 新しい modifies the noun きかい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects きかい with 使い方, creating the phrase “how to use the machine.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks how to use it as the content being learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: V辞書形 comes before 予定です to express a plan to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.why: The phrases の gradually narrow down the noun, from the time to the machine and then to how to use it. を marks the content being learned, while V辞書形＋予定です expresses a future plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with つもりです emphasizes the speaker’s intention more than a planned schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget の in きかいの使い方, leaving out the relationship “how to use the machine.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ 予定です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vi: When winter comes, strong north winds blow through this area, so there are no people or animals outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the area being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when winter begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 強い modifies the noun phrase 北の風.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 北 with 風 and shows the source or direction of the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the wind as the subject performing the action of blowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: て connects the wind-blowing action with the following result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: には states the place and emphasizes the outside area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: も connects people with animals within the same negative statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: も adds animals to the subjects said to be no longer present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: いなくなる describes people or animals disappearing and no longer being there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.why: は identifies the area, and に＋なると state the time and condition. て connects the wind-blowing event with the result, while 人も動物も combines with いなくなります to negate all the subjects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, it refers only to the condition when winter comes in a specific situation, while と emphasizes a result that happens naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: しか〜ない would mean “only people or animals,” so it does not fit the meaning “neither people nor animals remain.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate も as “also” on its own, but 人も動物も with a negative form means “neither people nor animals.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.tokens.20.m: be absent, no longer be there
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t22-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形・N ＋ になると; Vて ＋ V; Nも ＋ Nも ＋ Vない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vi: The teacher carefully answered my strange question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the teacher is the topic and also the person performing the action of answering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the owner with the noun しつもん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: へんな modifies しつもん and comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the object that the teacher answers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb and modifies the answering action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: 答えて uses the て form to connect the main verb with くださいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: くださいました is the final predicate and shows that the speaker received help, with a respectful tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.why: The possessive and descriptive phrases come before the noun “question,” while に marks the object being answered. The pattern Vてくださる comes after a verb to show that another person does something helpful for the speaker, with a respectful tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the meaning is still that the teacher answered for me, but the tone is more familiar and less respectful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence views the speaker as the person receiving help, instead of showing respect to the person who performed the action as くださいました does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use くださいました directly after a noun; connect it with the verb’s て form: 答えてくださいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q1.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くださる／くださいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.vi: There are plans to hold an international conference at this venue in December this year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the event is planned to take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: V辞書形 comes before 予定です to express a planned schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.why: The time and place come before the event content. The verb 行う in the dictionary form connects with 予定です to turn the action into a planned schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with つもりです emphasizes the speaker’s intention more than an arranged plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 行います予定です; before 予定です, they must use the dictionary form 行う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q10.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ 予定だ／予定です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.vi: Because the luggage was very heavy, I asked Mr. Tanaka to carry it for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject as having the state of being heavy and also gives the reason for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the degree of おもい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the result and gives the reason a soft, objective tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person who performs the action to help the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 持って uses the て form to connect the verb with もらいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてもらいました expresses that the speaker received help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with が and ので, while the second clause states who helped and what action the speaker asked them to do. The て form connects 持つ with もらう to create the pattern for receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If てくれました is used, the sentence emphasizes that Tanaka willingly helped more than that the speaker asked him to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern focuses on the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after a person's name; with てもらう, the person who performs the action usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q11.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ ので; Vて ＋ もらう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.vi: It takes 15 minutes to walk to the station, but it takes only 5 minutes by bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 歩いて uses the て form to state the method or connect to the duration that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: walking takes longer than riding a bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: なら presents a condition or a case for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the amount of time needed to complete the trip to the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: 行けます is the potential form and expresses that one can reach the destination in that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.why: The first clause gives the time needed when walking, while が shifts the sentence to another means of transport. なら selects the specific case of 自転車, and で shows the time needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 場合は, the sentence has a more hypothetical or formal conditional tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: では can state the means of transport in a specific case, but its contrast is clearer than なら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 5分で as the means of transport; in this sentence, で indicates the required duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.vi: I hear that my grandfather leaves late at night to catch fish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who performs the action in the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action とる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: とる in the dictionary form comes before ために to state the action done as a purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ために connects the purpose with the main action 出発する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 夜 indicates the time of departure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: に changes おそく into an adverbial phrase showing a late time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: そうです comes after the plain form to pass on information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.why: The object 魚 comes before the verb とる, and then とるために changes that action into a purpose. After the time phrases, 出発するそうです ends the sentence with a pattern for reporting information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: ようです expresses a judgment based on evidence, not simply information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: そうです at the end of a sentence means “it is said”; unlike そうだ after a verb stem, which expresses appearance or a prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse そうです for reporting 聞 with そうです for expressing appearance; the position and the form before it determine the meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q13.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために; V普通形 ＋ そうだ／そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.vi: Fish are transported to the market by truck early every morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that fish is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎朝 modifies the time of the transport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 早い comes before 時間 to modify this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 時間 indicates the period when the transport takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the means used for the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the fish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: 運ばれています is the passive form combined with ています, expressing a state or an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.why: Fish is made the topic, while the transporter is omitted, so the sentence uses the passive form. The time, means, and destination phrases successively add circumstances to 運ばれています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 運んでいます is used, the transporter is understood to be a person or thing actively carrying the fish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 運ばれました is used, the action was completed in the past, without emphasizing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle で when talking about means of transport; the means in this sentence must go with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.vi: Students are making noise in the neighboring classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies 教室, creating the meaning “the neighboring classroom.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject causing the noisy state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 騒いで connects with います to create the progressive form 騒いでいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.why: となりの教室 creates a noun phrase showing which classroom, while 教室で states the place. The subject 学生が combines with 騒いでいます to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that the students will or usually make noise, without emphasizing that it is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q15.kobun.tip: で should not be translated as “by” in this sentence; here で indicates a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.vi: The camera shop is selling video cameras cheaply now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 states the time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the selling takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 安く is the adverbial form of 安い and modifies 売っています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 売って connects with います to express an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: います creates the progressive form, while よ is used to announce or emphasize information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.why: 今 sets the time, あのカメラ屋で sets the place, and then ビデオカメラを states the product. 安く comes before 売っています to show the way or price of the sale.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 安い modifies ビデオカメラ, it means that the video camera is cheap; it does not necessarily mean that its current selling price is low.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q16.kobun.tip: Distinguish 安く売る, meaning selling at a low price, from 安いビデオカメラ, meaning a video camera that is cheap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.vi: The switch is on the left side of the door.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the switch as the topic whose location is identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ドア with 左側, creating the meaning “the left side of the door.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the location where the switch exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is used for the existence of objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.why: スイッチは is the topic, ドアの左側に is the location phrase, and あります is the predicate used for objects. The particle の shows the relationship “the left side of the door.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If です is used, the sentence only identifies the left side of the door and does not clearly express that the switch exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q17.kobun.tip: For objects, use あります; do not use います because います is for people and animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.vi: Because collecting stamps is my hobby, people often give me stamps.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being collected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の changes the phrase 集める into a noun, while が marks that activity as the subject of しゅみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: なので connects the cause to the result, and なので follows the noun しゅみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: から indicates the person giving the stamps or the source from which they are received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: よく modifies the action もらいます and shows frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: もらいます is the main predicate and expresses receiving something from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.why: The phrase 集めるのがしゅみ changes the action of collecting into the subject of the sentence “is a hobby.” なので connects the reason in the first clause with the result of often receiving stamps in the second clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If こと is used, the basic meaning is still that collecting is a hobby, but the expression is more formal and general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If あげます is used, the direction of giving and receiving is reversed: I give stamps to other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 人からもらう, meaning receive from a person, with 人にあげる, meaning give to a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形 + の; V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.vi: Yesterday, after dinner, I immediately looked up the materials.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that yesterday is the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べてから shows that the later action happens after the earlier action is completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: すぐ modifies 調べました and indicates a very short time gap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the materials being looked up or checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: 調べました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.why: 食べてから establishes the order of the two actions: dinner came first, and then I looked up the materials. すぐ comes before the main predicate to emphasize that the lookup happened immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べたあとで is used instead, it also means after eating, but it focuses more on the time after the action than on the sequence beginning with the earlier action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q19.kobun.tip: 食べてから does not use the past form 食べたから when meaning “after eating.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.vi: Last night, around 11 o’clock, I was woken up by a phone call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.sk: Time + Timeごろ + N で + V受身て + しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうべ states when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ごろ indicates an approximate time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means or agent that caused the speaker to wake up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 起こされて is the passive form て, connected to しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいました expresses that an event was completed and often carries a sense of being unintended or regrettable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.why: The two time phrases are placed at the beginning to identify when the event happened. 電話で states the agent or means, while 起こされてしまいました combines the passive form with てしまう to express being woken up unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If しまいました is omitted, the sentence only states that the speaker was woken up, with less of a sense of regret or unwillingness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 起きました is used, it means waking up by oneself or simply waking up, so it no longer means being woken by someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.tip: Do not translate 起こされる as the active verb “wake someone up”; it is passive and means “be woken up.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q20.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; V受身て + しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.vi: This dish is seasoned with salt, sugar, and soy sauce.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the dish being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects ingredients with the same role.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: と continues connecting the second ingredient with the next one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the means or ingredient used for seasoning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object created or added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb つけます is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, followed by a series of ingredients connected with と. で indicates the ingredient used to perform the action, while を marks what is seasoned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of で, the sentence is no longer natural when indicating the ingredient or means of seasoning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: と only connects nouns of equal status and cannot replace で to indicate the means.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を after an ingredient, but an ingredient or means used to perform an action must be followed by で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.vi: My Japanese pronunciation is fine, but I cannot seem to improve at conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本語 with the noun 発音, creating the meaning “Japanese pronunciation.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 発音 the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects the first clause with the contrasting idea that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: は changes the topic to conversation skills for comparison with pronunciation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: なかなか is used with a negative form to emphasize that achieving the result is difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the state or result that the subject becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: なりません is the negative predicate form of なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.why: The sentence uses two topics with は to compare two different aspects: pronunciation and conversation. ですが creates the contrast, while なかなか combines with the negative form to express a result that is difficult to achieve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ですが with けれども keeps the contrastive meaning but sounds fuller and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: あまり + a negative form means not very or not much, and is milder than なかなか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners easily understand なかなか as “quite,” but with a negative form it usually means “still cannot” or “find it difficult to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q22.kobun.cn: Nの + N・Aな + ですが、; なかなか + Vない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.vi: The phone number I received from Mr. Smith is too long, so I cannot remember it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.sk: N から + Vた + N が + Aい remove い + すぎますから、 + V negative potential form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source or the person who gives something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause もらった comes before and modifies 電話番号.
