default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject described as being too long.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: すぎる is attached after an adjective stem to show an excessive degree, while から gives the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: られません creates the negative potential form of 覚える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます・Aい-remove い・Aな・N + すぎる; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.why: The phrase もらった comes before 電話番号 to describe the phone number received from Smith. The reason clause comes first, followed by the result that the speaker cannot remember it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still gives the reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: 覚えにくい means “difficult to remember,” and does not stress complete inability to remember as 覚えられません does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget to remove い in 長い before すぎる; they must say 長すぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.vi: After hearing the earthquake news, I am worried about my parents who are in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 地震 with ニュース, creating a phrase meaning earthquake news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the news that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞いて connects the action of hearing the news with the worried state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the parents are.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: いる comes before 両親 to modify “parents.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject described as 心配.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: 心配です is the predicate expressing a worried state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.why: The phrase 日本にいる modifies 両親, identifying them as the parents who are in Japan. The part 聞いて comes first to state the event that leads to the state of 心配です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ので makes the cause-and-effect relationship clearer, while 聞いて describes an event that happened earlier or serves as a basis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern makes the worried person the subject and 両親 the direct object of the action of worrying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with 心配, but when saying that “someone is worrying,” use Nが心配です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.vi: At first, because I did not understand how to do the work, I asked my senior colleague many times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は limits the time being discussed to the initial stage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects しごと with 仕方, creating the meaning “how to do the work.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what the speaker did not understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects a past reason with the question in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: も after 何度 emphasizes that the action was repeated many times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the person asked or the person the question is directed to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: ききました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.why: 仕方 is modified by しごとの and serves as the subject of わからない. The reason clause uses ので before it, while asking a specific person uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives the reason, but the expression is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: Using を after 先輩 is wrong when asking a person; the person asked must be marked with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often say 先輩を聞く, but 聞く meaning “ask someone” uses 先輩に聞く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vi: In spring in Japan, small birds sing and flowers bloom, making it very beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with 春, creating a phrase that modifies 春.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that spring in Japan is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that performs the action of singing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: なき is the connecting form of 鳴く, linking it to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks flowers as the subject of the action of blooming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: さいて is the て form of 咲く, connecting the action to the final comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The adjective い in the polite form is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.why: 日本の modifies 春, while は makes 春 the topic. The two clauses use が to mark their separate subjects, then connect with the connective form and the て form before the final comment うつくしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes spring as what is discovered rather than stating it as the general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If なきながら is used, the meaning changes to “sing while doing another action.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use は for 小鳥 and 花, but when each action has its own subject, が is usually needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vi: I have something to do today, so please allow me to leave early.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the time and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 用事 as something that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I have something to do
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason with the action of asking to leave early.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the order or time of leaving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 帰らせて is the て form of the causative, combined with いただきます to express asking for permission to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: いただきます completes the humble expression for being allowed to do something by another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.why: In this clause, 用事があるので comes first to state the reason, followed by the request to leave. 帰らせていただきます combines the causative form with いただく to humbly say that the speaker is asking to leave.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and informal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If you only say 帰ります, the sentence only announces that you will return; it no longer has a humble, permission-seeking tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate させて as being forced to do something; in the pattern させていただく, it usually expresses asking permission to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので; Vさせて + いただく
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vi: The nearby vegetable shop sells fresh vegetables every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 近く with 八百屋, forming a phrase meaning a nearby shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: では states the place where the activity occurs and limits the scope of the description.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: This time expression modifies the action of selling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: な connects the noun 新鮮 with やさい to modify やさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the vegetables as the object being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: うって is the て form of 売る, and it connects with います to express an ongoing state or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: います completes the Vている structure and shows that the activity continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.why: The place is marked by では, followed by the frequency まいにち and the phrase 新鮮なやさい, which is the object of 売る. The form ている shows that the selling activity continues regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 新鮮な is replaced with 新しい, the meaning becomes new vegetables or recently bought vegetables, without emphasizing freshness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 売ります is used, the sentence only states the act of selling in general or a habit, without emphasizing an activity in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q5.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in な must have な before a noun; do not say 新鮮やさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vi: The employee at that ramen shop seems to be a foreigner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the ramen shop with 店員さん and shows a relationship of belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the employee is the topic being guessed about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Nの comes before ようです to form the object of the guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ようです expresses an opinion or guess based on signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.why: 店員さんは is the subject being commented on, while 外国人のようです is the guessing predicate. With nouns, の comes between the noun and ようです to form a comparison or guess pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようです is replaced with みたいです, the meaning stays almost the same, but the tone is more casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If らしいです is used, the sentence leans more toward heard information or a feature believed to be true than a guess based on signs seen at the moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.tip: After a noun, use のようです; do not connect it directly as 外国人ようです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q6.kobun.cn: Nの・V普通形・Aい・Aな + な + ようだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vi: If I do not eat breakfast, I have no energy in the morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that I am the person placed in the hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks breakfast as the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: は limits the time during which the result of having no energy applies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks 力 as something that does not appear in the morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: 出ません is a negative predicate that says energy does not appear or does not become available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.why: The clause 食べないと comes first to state the condition, while 午前中は力が出ません is the result. と is suitable for a natural result or something that happens regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べないと is replaced with 食べなければ, the sentence still means “if I do not eat,” but the condition sounds more formal and intentional.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べないなら is used, the sentence becomes a supposition based on the listener's intention or information, rather than a natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use 食べなくと; before と in this pattern, the negative form 食べない must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vi: I keep cats and a dog at home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of keeping pets takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects ねこ with 犬 in the same object phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the whole phrase ねこと犬 as the object of 飼う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 飼っている describes the continuing state of keeping the dog and cat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.why: で states where the action occurs, と connects the two animals as joint objects, and を comes after the last noun in the list. 飼っている describes the continuing state of keeping them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If や is used, the list means cats, dogs, and other animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 飼っています is replaced with 飼います, the sentence only says that the speaker will keep pets or has a habit of keeping them, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q8.kobun.tip: When listing items with と, use only one を after the last noun in the whole phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.vi: The people here go to the nearby church on Sunday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this phrase with 人たち, creating a modifier for the group of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the phrase 日曜日近く into a modifier for 教会.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.why: The phrase こちらの 人たちは states the topic, and then 日曜日近くの modifies the place 教会. The particle へ connects the place with the direction verb 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence still indicates a destination, but に emphasizes the specific destination more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse へ with に; both can indicate direction, but へ emphasizes the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vi: This overseas trip cost 100,000 yen for food and the hotel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.sk: N の + N は + N と + N で + Amount of money + かかりました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今度 with 外国旅行 and identifies this trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the trip is the topic concerning the amount of money spent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the expenses that make up the total amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The money phrase comes before かかりました to state the amount spent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: かかりました is a predicate indicating the amount of money needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 今度の外国旅行 identifies the trip being discussed. The two expenses are connected by と and combined with で to state the costs that make up the total amount the trip cost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 食事代にすると indicates one purpose or a separate expense, and is less natural than で when grouping several types of expenses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 使いました emphasizes the person who used the money, while かかりました emphasizes the amount needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily reverse this as 10万円をかかりました, but かかる does not use を for an amount of money; say 10万円かかりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vi: The beef at that restaurant is unforgettable after just one taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.sk: N の N は + Number of times + V辞書形 + と + V可能形ません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows the possessive relationship, while は marks the beef as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 一度 adds the number of times the action of eating is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb + と states the natural result after the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: られません expresses negative ability, meaning that something cannot be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.why: あの店の牛肉は is the topic being evaluated. 食べると connects the condition with its natural result, and わすれられません expresses the inability to forget.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べたら is used instead, the sentence focuses more on the specific condition after finishing eating and does not emphasize the natural result as much as と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q10.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily understand と as only meaning “and,” but in this sentence it connects a condition with its natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vi: Because I am not used to it, moving around in a kimono is very difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.0.vi: because I am not used to it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the cause with the result and gives a softer explanatory tone than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 着物 as the object of the action of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition or point in time with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns 動く into a noun, while が marks moving around as the subject being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: たいへんです is the predicate describing how difficult moving around is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.why: なれないので gives the reason first, and then 着ると makes the situation of wearing a kimono the condition. The phrase 動くのが turns the action of moving around into the subject evaluated as たいへん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 動くのは is used, moving around becomes the topic of comparison or emphasis instead of the direct subject of the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily omit の before が, but the verb needs の to become a noun in the pattern Vのがたいへんです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形 + ので; V辞書形 + と; V辞書形 + のが + Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vi: The watch I treasured was unfortunately broken by my younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The modifying clause describes 時計 and shows that the speaker treasured the watch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by the action of breaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に marks the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 壊されて is the passive form combined with しまいました to emphasize that the event happened unwillingly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.why: The clause 大切にしていた comes before 時計 to modify the noun. The passive structure makes 時計 the object that suffers harm, while に identifies the person who caused the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 壊してしまいました is used, the speaker becomes the person who broke the watch, rather than the person affected by it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 壊されていました is used, the sentence only describes a state or an observed event, with less regret than しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q12.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily mistake に for the affected object, but in a passive sentence に identifies the person who caused the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vi: Please send this letter by registered mail.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 手紙 and identifies the letter being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the letter as the object being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means or method of sending the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 出して is the て form, connecting the verb to ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: ください follows the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.why: 手紙を is the object, 書留で is the sending method, and 出してください is the polite request. The additional parts come before the main verb in the usual Japanese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書留で is replaced with 書留に, the expression sounds unnatural because the means of sending requires で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q13.kobun.tip: English speakers may use に to mean “by,” but で expresses the means or method of carrying out an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vi: I think that even in the same place, we can still enjoy ourselves if we change the way we do things a little.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.sk: N でも + N が + Vた + ら + potential V + と + 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: でも follows a noun to express concession: even when it is the same place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し modifies the degree of change in the way of doing things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks やり方 as the subject mentioned in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: たら connects the conditional clause with the result clause that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: 楽しめる is the potential form and serves as the predicate of the result clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the content of the thought or opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: 思います is the main predicate and takes 楽しめると as the thing being thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.why: でも creates a concessive meaning at the beginning, while たら gives the condition leading to the result. The opinion 楽しめる is connected to 思います by と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 同じ場所なら is used instead, it only states a hypothetical condition and no longer clearly expresses the concessive meaning of でも.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: と思います softens the sentence and expresses a personal opinion, while 楽しめます makes a more direct statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily confuse でも with “but”; after a noun, でも can also mean “even if” or “even.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q14.kobun.cn: Vた + ら; 普通形 + と + 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vi: At the weekend, I will stay at that inn with my parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + Person と + Place に + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence, namely the person who will stay overnight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the people who participate or accompany the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the speaker will stay overnight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: 泊まります is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.why: The topic 私は is placed at the beginning of the sentence. The two phrases に indicate the time and place, respectively, while と indicates the person who performs or joins the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding 一緒に makes the meaning “together with my parents” clearer, but と is enough to express companionship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: Using で with 泊まる sounds unnatural; staying at an inn requires the place to be marked with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q15.kobun.tip: English speakers may use で with 泊まる because of the habit of translating “stay at,” but this verb usually uses a place + に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vi: Because my apartment is near the station, I hardly use a car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 私 with アパート to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the apartment is the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the reference point used to judge distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ですから connects the reason before it with the result after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ほとんど modifies the degree of the negative action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the car as the object of use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: しません is the negative predicate in the present tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.why: The first clause, ですから, gives the reason, while the second clause gives the result. から after 駅 identifies the station as the reference point for saying whether the apartment is near or far.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ですから with ので still gives a reason, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: 駅に近い also means near the station; に marks the object used as the comparison standard, while から focuses on the starting point or reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically translate から as “from” in every case; here it only indicates the reference point for determining distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.vi: Because it was cold, my hands and feet became as cold as ice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い changes to the form くて to connect the cause with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: や lists the hands together with another body part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the direct subject of the state of becoming cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: のように indicates a comparison, meaning that the state is like ice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い changes to the form く to combine with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました is the predicate showing a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.why: くて connects the cause, while く＋なる shows a change into a new state. のように is placed before the adjective to compare the degree of coldness with ice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: 氷のような must come before a noun, while 氷のように comes before an adjective or verb to modify the manner or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: 冷たそうに means “looks cold” and does not confirm that it is truly cold as this sentence does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep the adjective い unchanged before なる; they need to change 冷たい into 冷たくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.vi: I opened the window and breathed in the fresh mountain air.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the window as the object that is opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects opening the window with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: おいしい modifies 空気.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 山 with 空気, while を marks the air as the object breathed in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: すいました is the main predicate and shows a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.why: て connects the two actions in order: opening the window first and then breathing in the air. The phrase 山の空気 is placed before を to identify the type of air being breathed in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 開けて with 開けたあとで emphasizes more clearly that the breathing happened after the opening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: で would indicate a means or cause, so it is not suitable for marking the object of 吸う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を for both consecutive verbs; here て connects the first action, while を marks the object of 吸う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q19.kobun.vi: The math exam was very difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 数学 with 試験 to say that the exam was for mathematics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the exam is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 難しかったです is a polite past-tense adjective predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q19.kobun.why: The phrase の modifies 試験 and identifies it as a mathematics exam. は makes 試験 the topic, and then the past-tense adjective acts as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes that mathematics is what was judged difficult, instead of making the exam the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change 難しい into 難しかった when talking about an exam that has already taken place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vi: A lot of people came to the party venue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects パーティー with the place noun that follows, showing possession or a connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates a place, while は emphasizes the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: たくさんの modifies 人, meaning many people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person who performs the action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 来ました is the polite past form of 来る and describes an action that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.why: The phrase パーティーの会場 identifies the place, and then に indicates where the action happened. The people who came are the subject, so が is used, while 来ました is the final predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with で, the sentence focuses on the place where an action occurs, so it is less suitable than に with the verb 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で with every place, but 来る usually goes with に or へ to indicate a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.vi: There was slightly too little time to think about the problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being thought about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies 時間 and creates the meaning “time to think.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject being judged as sufficient or insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing the degree of the shortage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 足りません is the polite negative form of 足りる; でした puts the whole sentence in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.why: 問題を is the object of 考える, while 考える時間 is a noun phrase in which the verb comes before and modifies the noun. The subject is marked by が, and then 足りませんでした acts as the predicate stating that the time was insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 少ない emphasizes that the amount of time was small, while 足りない emphasizes that the time did not meet the need.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly use は instead of が in a sentence that directly comments on whether the time was sufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.vi: I suffered because a thief broke into my home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person who carried out the break-in in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.1.vi: to have one's home broken into
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: 入られて is the passive form て, linking the damaging event to the result 大変でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 大変でした is a predicate evaluating a bad past condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.why: The speaker was affected by the action of 泥棒, so the passive sentence uses に to state the agent. The form て links the direct cause to the feeling 大変でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 泥棒が入って is used, it only says that the thief broke in and does not stress that the speaker was affected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand に as a place, but in a passive sentence it can indicate the agent that caused the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q21.tokens.2.m: to have one's home broken into
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.vi: The carefully preserved document has been dirtied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes 大事 into a state or manner in the phrase 大事にする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: して is the て form of する, connecting to いた in a modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: いた shows that the state of keeping it carefully continued before the document was dirtied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the noun modified by the preceding clause and affected by the following event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: 汚されて is the passive form て, linking the action of dirtying it with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまいました shows that the event was completed and often carries a sense of regret or something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.why: 大事にしていた comes before 資料 to modify the document. After the subject, 汚されてしまいました combines the passive form with てしまう, showing that the document was dirtied against one's wishes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If てしまう is omitted, the sentence only reports that it was dirtied and weakens the sense of regret or an unwanted event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If 大事だった is used, it means that the document was once important, without stressing that it had always been carefully kept.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate していた as a single action, while ～ていた here shows a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q22.kobun.cn: N・Aな語幹・V辞書形 ＋ にする; Vて ＋ いる; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.vi: She had her wallet stolen at that station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 彼女 the topic, meaning the person affected by the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the wallet was lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item taken in a passive sentence showing harm.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 盗まれた is the past passive form, showing that someone else took the wallet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.why: The place where the event happened uses で, while 財布を is the item affected in the passive structure. 彼女は is the person presented as the topic, even though it is not the direct subject of the verb 盗まれた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 財布が盗まれた is used, the focus is only on the wallet being stolen, and it does not clearly state that she was affected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 盗んだ is used, the meaning changes to she stole the wallet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q23.kobun.tip: English learners may mistake 財布を in this sentence for the object of the subject she, but it is the item lost in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.vi: I am working four hours a day at a bookstore to fill in for my friend, for only two weeks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: だけ limits the time period of the work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a noun with 代わり, while に indicates the person or position being replaced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing how often the work is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: A duration phrase adding the amount of work time per day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: で marks the place where the work happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: ～ています shows that the work is continuing during this period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.why: The limited time period is placed at the beginning, followed by the phrase showing replacement. The phrases showing frequency, duration, and place each add information about はたらいています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 友だちに代わって is used, the tone is more formal and stresses acting on behalf of the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 友だちのために is used, it means working for the friend's benefit, without necessarily directly replacing the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.tip: English learners may omit の in の代わりに; a noun before 代わり must be connected with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q24.kobun.cn: N の ＋ 代わりに; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.vi: It is very noisy because construction on a building is being carried out next door.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the construction is happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ビル with 工事, showing that the construction is related to the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the construction as the subject being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 行われて is the passive form て, connecting with いる to create a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the cause with the result うるさいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb showing the degree of うるさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: うるさいです is an adjective predicate with the ending い in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.why: ビルの工事が is the subject of the passive clause 行われている. This clause gives the cause and connects to the result through ので; とても modifies the degree of noise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the reason sounds more direct and subjective; ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If 工事をしている is used, the sentence becomes active and does not stress that the construction is being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may use を with 工事, but when saying that the construction is being carried out, 工事 is the subject, so が should be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q25.kobun.cn: Vて・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vi: Because of the incident, more than 100 people from newspaper companies gathered in the square.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.sk: N で ＋ Quantity 以上の ＋ N の ＋ N が ＋ Place に ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that made many people gather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 以上 shows an amount starting from that number and above, and the whole phrase modifies 人たち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: の shows that these people belong to the newspaper company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the group of people carrying out the action of gathering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the place the group gathered at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: 集まりました is the polite past form of 集まる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.why: 事件で states the cause, while 100名以上の新聞社の人たち forms a long noun phrase serving as the subject. 広場に indicates the destination or gathering place and comes directly before 集まりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほど is used, it means about 100 people and does not state that the number is 100 or more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means there are only 100 people and is usually used with a negative expression, unlike the meaning “more than 100 people.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q3.kobun.tip: 以上 must come after the number and the counting noun, not before the quantity as in the familiar English pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vi: From early morning, the sounds of trains and birds can be heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Time から ＋ N の ＋ N や ＋ N の ＋ N が ＋ Vてきます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 朝 states the starting point of the condition being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point in time; 早く modifies that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 電車 with 音, showing that the sound comes from the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: や lists 音 together with the sound of birds; the whole phrase is the subject that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 鳥 with こえ, identifying the sound made by birds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the sound that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.6.vi: can be heard coming from afar
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: 聞こえる describes a sound entering the ears naturally; てきます shows that the sound is reaching the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.why: The two sounds are joined by や and together become the subject with が of 聞こえる. 朝 and 早くから are placed at the beginning to state the time, while 聞こえてきます ends the sentence by showing that the sound is reaching the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If を聞きます is used, the sentence describes actively listening to a sound, unlike 聞こえる, which means hearing it naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q4.kobun.tip: Do not always translate や as “and”; や usually lists only a few representative objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vi: Autumn is a good season for reading books.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 秋 the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 本 as the object of the action of reading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb 読む combines with のに to state a purpose or a suitable use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いい modifies 季節, showing that autumn is suitable for reading books.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 季節です is the noun part of the predicate, completing the comment about 秋.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.why: 秋は is the topic, while 本を読むのに groups the action of reading books as a purpose for evaluating 季節. The adjective いい comes before the noun 季節 to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ための is used, the sentence emphasizes the purpose “a season for reading books,” with a more rigid and direct tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに follows the past form, the meaning changes to “although someone has read books,” so it no longer expresses purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q5.kobun.tip: のに in this sentence means “in order to do,” not のに, which expresses concession meaning “although.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vi: Because the population has increased, a large supermarket has also opened in my town recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.sk: N が + Aくなったので、 + Time + N の + N にも + Aい + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks 人口 as the subject of the increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 多くなった describes a change to a state of being greater, while ので connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: さいきん modifies the whole event that happened recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 私 with 町, identifying the town being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the place, while も adds the meaning “also” compared with other places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: 大きい comes before スーパー to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: が marks the supermarket as something new that appeared or was built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: できました is the polite past form of できる; here, it means that a new facility was established.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.why: The clause 多くなったので gives the cause first, followed by the result できました. The place uses に, and も adds that the speaker’s town also has a supermarket, like other places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason stays the same, but the expression becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is used, the place is understood as where an action takes place, while に is more suitable for the appearance of a facility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.tip: With ので, the adjective な and the noun need な before ので, while verbs and い adjectives use the ordinary form directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい普通形・Aな語幹 + な・N + な + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vi: Japanese people take very good care of cherry trees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states 日本人 as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 熱心 is a な adjective; adding に changes it into an adverb that modifies 世話をします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects さくら with 木, identifying the type of tree being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 木 with 世話, forming the phrase “care for the tree.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks 世話 as the object in the phrase 世話をする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: します is the polite form of する, completing the fixed phrase 世話をする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.why: 日本人は is the topic, and 熱心に describes how the action is performed. The phrase さくらの木の世話をする consists of nouns joined one after another by の and ends with the verb します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 熱心な is used, it modifies the noun after it and means “an enthusiastic person,” not the manner of performing an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 一生懸命に, the sentence emphasizes making every effort rather than enthusiasm or dedication.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q7.kobun.tip: When the adjective な modifies a verb, it must change to the に form; it cannot directly use 熱心します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vi: 花見 means going to view flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: というのは is used to introduce the word or concept being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: Dictionary-form verb + に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 行く modifies こと, creating the meaning of going to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: こと nominalizes the whole preceding phrase, while です ends the explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.why: というのは makes 花見 the topic to be explained. The phrase 見に行く expresses the purpose of going, and 行くこと turns the whole action into a noun for explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If only は is used, the sentence merely states the topic and does not create as clear a definition as というのは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 見に as “view” and forget that に here only indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q8.kobun.cn: N + というのは + … + ことです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vi: In this town, the machinery industry has been highly developed for a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states この町 as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks a starting point that continues to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the field as the subject of the highly developed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: さかんです is the predicate describing the level of development of the industry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.why: この町は sets the scope of the comment, while が identifies which industry has the state さかん. 古くから comes before the predicate to show that this state began long ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used after この町, this place is understood as the location where an activity happens, rather than the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t24-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は for the subject inside the sentence, but here が is what marks the developing industry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vi: Let us check which explanation is correct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects with 説明 to form the phrase “which explanation.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object being judged as correct or incorrect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the preceding clause into an indirect question and makes it the content of 調べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects 調べる with みる and expresses trying to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: みましょう is the inviting form of the Vてみる pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.why: The phrase どちらの説明が正しいか、 states what needs to be checked. 調べてみましょう places the checking action before みましょう to create a gentle invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 調べましょう is used, it means “please check” and does not emphasize trying it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with かどうか, it fits a yes-or-no question, while どちらの requires choosing one of two options.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that か must come after the whole part that needs to be identified in an indirect question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.vi: According to the plan, this work should be completed by next spring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に combines with よる to indicate a basis or source of information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: によると introduces information based on a source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は presents the work as the topic of the prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle の connects 今度 with 春 and indicates the coming spring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the work must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: A verb in the dictionary form comes before はず to express the content of the prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: はずです expresses a well-founded prediction or something believed to be certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.why: によると gives the basis before the main information. The time limit までに comes before 終わる, while はずです comes at the end to conclude the prediction based on the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a softer prediction and does not emphasize a firm basis as much as はずです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence refers to a fixed schedule or plan, not only a prediction based on evidence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse までに with まで; までに means “must be finished before the deadline,” while まで only means that something continues until that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ はずだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.vi: The building of this shop is dirty, but the food tastes good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は sets the comparison range as this shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The second は separately states the aspect of the building to contrast with 味 in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: きたないけれど connects the negative comment about the building with the opposite positive comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: は marks the aspect of taste and creates a contrast with 建物.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: いいです is the predicate that gives a positive evaluation of the taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.why: The sentence places the two aspects, 建物 and 味, side by side using は for comparison. けれど connects two contrasting comments: the building is dirty, but the taste is good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If けれど is replaced with が, the contrast remains, but the sentence is usually shorter and more neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, the sentence also suggests something contrary to expectations or slightly surprising.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand は as simply “is”; in this sentence, the は are also used to create a contrast between two aspects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ けれど
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.vi: A strong wind has blown in from the sea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point or source of the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the wind as the subject carrying out the blowing movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ふいて is the て form of ふく and connects the blowing action with 来た.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 来た combines with a verb in the て form to express movement toward the speaker or the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.why: から identifies the source of the wind, が identifies the wind as the subject, and 強い modifies the wind. ふいてくる expresses that the wind blows in from the sea toward the speaker or the area being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ふいていく, the movement goes away from the speaker or the area being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If ふいている is used, the sentence only describes the blowing state and does not emphasize the direction of the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate 来る only as “come”; in Vてくる, it also shows movement toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q13.kobun.vi: I am going to buy rice and vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the buying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The polite stem form 買い combines with に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q13.kobun.why: The noun phrase before を is what is being bought. The verb stem ＋ に ＋ いく pattern expresses the purpose of going to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used, the sentence emphasizes the purpose “in order to buy” and sounds more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistakenly think that に in 買いに indicates a place, but here it indicates purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q13.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.vi: There is a very useful map in my room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 私 with 部屋 to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where something exists, while は presents that place as the topic of contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective 便利な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object that exists in the room; 便利な modifies 地図.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.why: The place of existence is stated first with に, and then the existing object is the subject with が. The adjective な comes directly before the noun to describe that object's feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If には is replaced with で, the sentence refers to the place where an action occurs and does not fit the existence verb あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with places, but places where something exists usually go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.vi: I have been doing research at this university since this autumn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: 今年の modifies 秋 and identifies which autumn is meant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of the research activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: この comes before 大学 to identify the university being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the place where the research activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects 研究する with います to create a progressive structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the pattern Vている and shows that the activity is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.why: から is placed after a time point to state the starting point, while で indicates where the activity takes place. 研究している shows that the research activity is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were replaced, the sentence would emphasize starting the research instead of the state of continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ています simply as "did," but this structure usually emphasizes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.vi: I am borrowing three million yen or more from the bank.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source of the money or the place from which the money is borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The quantity phrase ＋ 以上の modifies お金 and indicates that the amount reaches the minimum level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the money as the object of borrowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects 借りる with いる and creates a structure expressing a state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: いる completes the pattern 借りている and shows that the borrowed state remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.why: から indicates the source of the loan, while 以上の comes after the amount and modifies お金. 借りている expresses that the loan still exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 以上 were replaced with ほど, the sentence would mean about three million yen and would no longer emphasize the minimum amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 以上 for meaning "more than" in an absolute sense, but it also includes the exact amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.vi: Every morning I open the window and listen to the birds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも modifies the whole habit described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 朝早く indicates the time and manner in which the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the window as the object that is opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects opening the window with listening to the birds in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 鳥 with こえ to identify the sound as belonging to the birds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the birds' sound as the object that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.why: いつも and 朝早く come before the verbs to state the frequency and time. The form て connects two consecutive actions, and each verb has its own object marked by を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern were used, the sentence would list typical actions instead of emphasizing the sequence of opening and then listening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を before こえ, but 聞く needs to mark what is heard with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.vi: If it happens to rain tomorrow afternoon, let's meet in the gym.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: 万一 warns of an undesirable hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: あしたの modifies 午後 to identify which afternoon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 午後 identifies when the rain occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks 雨 as the subject of the phenomenon 降る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The past form 降った combines with ら to create a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the place where everyone will meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: The volitional form 集まろう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first and ends with 降ったら, followed by the meeting place and the invitation. に marks the destination, while the volitional form expresses a shared decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 降ったら were replaced with 降れば, the sentence would have a more general or rule-like conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were replaced with 降っても, the meaning would become "even if it rains, we will still meet," not "if it rains."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly use the present form before ら, but hypothetical verb conditions usually use the form た ＋ ら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q18.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aいーかった・Aなだった・Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.vi: I do not like working on Sundays.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.sk: N time ＋ N を ＋ Vる のは ＋ Aな です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to state when the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks work as the object of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: するの becomes a noun with の, and then は makes working on Sunday the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 嫌です is the predicate that expresses dislike or hatred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.why: 日曜日 states the time, while 仕事をする forms the specific action. The phrase するのは turns the whole action into a topic for giving the evaluation 嫌です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If が were used, the focus would be on disliking that action, rather than presenting the action as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の when they want to turn the whole verb phrase into the topic before は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vi: My younger sister likes taking care of dogs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the younger sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 犬 with 世話 and indicates taking care of the dog.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks what is liked in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な and expresses a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.why: は makes the person who likes something the topic, while が marks what is liked. 犬の世話 is a noun phrase in which の connects the object with the action of caring for it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 犬を世話する were used, the sentence would talk about the action of caring for the dog, not about a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 世話をする were used, を would be needed because 世話 would become the object of the verb する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q2.kobun.tip: With 好きです, learners may easily use を instead of が because of the habit of their native language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.vi: My school's rules are very strict.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし to the noun that follows to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 学校の modifies 規則, creating the meaning “school rules.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks 規則 as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 厳しい is an adjective ending in い. It acts as the predicate and combines directly with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases gradually narrow the scope from わたし to 学校 and then 規則. After stating 規則 as the topic with は, the adjective 厳しい comments on those rules.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 厳しい is placed before 規則, the phrase only means “strict rules” and does not yet form a complete sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put possessive elements in the wrong order; Japanese places the possessor, such as a person or place, before the head noun with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 規則 the topic of the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: 守りましょう is the ましょう form of 守る, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q21.kobun.why: 規則は states what is being discussed, while 守りましょう is a suggestion to follow it together. は creates the topic here; it does not directly mark the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, 規則 is clearly marked as the object of the action of following, so the sentence is more direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse は and を; は states the topic, while を marks the object of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.vi: Please feel free to express your opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes 自由 into an adverb and modifies how the opinion is expressed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the opinion as the object that is spoken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 言って is the て form of 言う. It connects the verb to ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください expresses a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.why: 自由に modifies how the action 言う is carried out. 意見を is the object, and 言ってください makes a polite request by connecting the て form with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 言ってもいいです is used, the sentence becomes a question or gives permission to speak, so it is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use the dictionary form before ください; the request pattern must use the verb’s て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.vi: There are many beautiful buildings in Europe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.sk: Place には ＋ Aい ＋ N が ＋ Quantity ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates a place and sets the area where the buildings exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 美しい comes before and directly modifies 建物.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the sentence with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies the quantity 建物.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate showing that an inanimate thing exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.why: には states where something exists, 美しい建物 creates a noun phrase with the adjective before the noun. 建物が is the thing that exists, while たくさん states the quantity before あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the focus is on the place where an action occurs; with あります for saying that something exists, に is the suitable particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で for every location, but existence usually uses the place particle にあります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.vi: I studied abroad in the United States for one year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.sk: Destination へ ＋ Duration ＋ Nする しました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of studying abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 1年間 indicates the length of the study-abroad period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 留学しました is the polite past form of 留学する and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.why: アメリカへ states the destination, 1年間 states the duration, and 留学しました expresses a completed action. Place and time adverbials come before the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the place where the action occurs, but the more natural expressions for studying abroad are アメリカへ留学しました or アメリカに留学しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse へ with で; へ indicates the destination, while で indicates the place where the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q24.kobun.cn: N ＋ する; Vます-stem ＋ しました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.vi: I laughed so much that tears came out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.sk: Vます remove ます ＋ すぎる ＋ て ＋ N が ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The verb stem 笑い combines with すぎる to show excess, then uses て to connect to the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 涙 as the thing that appears or comes out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 出ました is the main predicate and describes the result that occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ すぎる; Aい remove い ＋ すぎる; Aな ＋ すぎる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.why: 笑いすぎて states the cause, while 涙が出ました states the result. The form て at the end of the first clause connects the cause to what happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 笑いすぎたので, the cause is stated more clearly and slightly more formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q25.kobun.tip: With verbs, remove ます before adding すぎる: 笑います → 笑いすぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vi: I made a plan to travel in the autumn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the time when the trip will take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before 計画 to modify the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks 計画 as the object of 立てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 立てた is the past form of 立てる and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.why: 秋に indicates the time, while 旅行する comes before 計画 to form the phrase “travel plan.” 計画を立てる is the natural combination of a noun as the object and a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定 is used, the meaning leans toward an intention or schedule and does not emphasize making a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 作る is used, it is still understood as creating a plan, but the more common combination is 計画を立てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate word for word and use 作る with 計画, while Japanese usually uses the fixed phrase 計画を立てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vi: I borrowed a medical book from the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から indicates the starting point of borrowing the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 医学 with 本 and indicates the type of book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks 本 as the thing being borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 借りました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.why: から identifies the source from which the book was taken, の identifies the type of book, and を marks the thing being borrowed. The verb 借りました comes last to complete the sentence in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, it emphasizes the place where the borrowing happened, not the source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If についての is used, it means that the book is about medicine, making the topic relationship clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse から with で: から indicates the source, while で indicates the place where the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vi: My father is researching foods that are harmful to the body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that my father is the topic of the research activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the thing affected by the quality 悪い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 悪い comes after 体に and modifies 食べ物.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の connects 食べ物 with 研究 and indicates the field being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks 研究 as the content of the activity しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: しています is the ている form of する and describes an ongoing activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.why: 体に悪い creates the descriptive clause “harmful to the body” to modify 食べ物. Then 食べ物の研究 becomes the object of しています, showing an activity in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 悪い is replaced with いい, the meaning changes to food that is good for the body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, 体 becomes the subject with a bad condition, not the object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the wrong word order and say 食べ物に体が悪い; the correct structure is Nに悪いN.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.vi: During the summer vacation, get up early and exercise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: には combines に and は to state a time and also emphasize the summer vacation context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The form く of 早い changes the adjective into an adverb modifying 起きて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects getting up with the following action of exercising.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks たいそう as the content of the action する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう is the polite invitational form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.why: には puts the time setting at the beginning of the sentence. 早く modifies 起きる, while 起きて connects to the following action before ending with the invitation しましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 起きたら is used, it means after getting up or if one gets up, emphasizing a condition or time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 起きてから is used, it emphasizes that the exercise happens after getting up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 起きると instead of 起きて, but here the て form is needed to connect the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.vi: People who do not understand how to write an essay should ask questions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の shows that 作文 is the topic being discussed in 書き方.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: について indicates the topic that the learner does not understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative form modifies 人, creating the meaning “a person who does not understand”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は identifies the group of people mentioned in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 質問する changes to the て form to connect with ください and create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.why: The phrase 作文の書き方について states the topic, while わからない人は identifies a person in that group. The verb in the て form connects with ください to turn asking a question into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence means “must ask a question,” which is stronger than the current suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may forget that ください must follow a verb in the て form, not come directly after the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q7.tokens.4.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.vi: My younger brother prepared a delicious fish dish for dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person who prepared the dish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the purpose or occasion for which the dish was prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective directly modifies 料理.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の connects 魚 with 料理, giving the meaning “a dish made from fish” or “a fish dish”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the dish that was prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: 用意する changes to the て form to connect with くれました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: くれました shows that the speaker benefited from the younger brother’s action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.why: The person performing the action is introduced first with は, the dish takes を, and then 用意してくれました expresses that the preparation was done for the speaker’s benefit. おいしい and 魚の modify 料理 respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the focus shifts to the speaker asking the younger brother for help or receiving help from him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the younger brother becomes the person who benefits someone else, and the benefit is no longer directed toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use くれる like the ordinary word “give” and forget that the pattern Vてくれる emphasizes that the speaker receives a benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.vi: I received special help from that doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: には marks the person mentioned in the phrase 世話になる and adds emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 特に modifies the whole idea of receiving help from the doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 世話に combines in a fixed expression with なる in 世話になる, meaning to receive care or help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, completing the pattern 世話になる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.why: The person phrase with には makes clear who helped, while 世話に なりました is a fixed expression for receiving care or support. 特に is placed before this phrase to emphasize the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning changes to “care for N,” so the subject is the person who provides the care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t25-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate なる mechanically as “become”; 世話になる must be understood as “be helped or cared for”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vi: On rainy days, washed clothes are difficult to dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.sk: N の + N は + N が + Vます形 remove ます + にくいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects the noun 雨 with 日 to modify “day.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」 presents rainy days as the scope of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 「が」 marks the object being described as difficult to dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 「乾き」 is the verb stem 「乾く」 connected to 「にくい」 to express difficulty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます + にくい
