default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.why: 「雨の日」 identifies the time and situation, while 「洗濯物が」 is the affected object. The verb stem 「乾き」 comes before 「にくい」 to create the meaning “difficult to dry.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「乾きづらい」 is used, it also means difficult to dry, but it usually suggests difficulty caused by the situation or by the speaker’s feelings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: 「乾きにくい」 focuses on how difficult the event is to occur, so it fits clothes on rainy days.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use the full form 「乾くにくい」; remove ます from 「乾きます」 and then connect 「にくい」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.vi: According to the weather forecast, it is said that a typhoon will come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: によると identifies the information source supporting the statement that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 台風 as the subject of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです follows the plain form to pass on information heard or read from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.why: によると puts the information source first, and the following statement says that 台風 is the subject of 来る. そうです at the end of the sentence shows that the speaker is passing on the forecast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, そうです means that something looks likely to happen soon, not information heard from a forecast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If らしいです is used instead, the sentence expresses a more uncertain guess or impression, without directly indicating the source of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse the two types of そうです: Vるそうです means “it is said,” while Vますそうです means “it looks likely to happen soon.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.vi: Next month, I plan to go on a business trip to Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Nへ + V辞書形 + 予定です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes わたし the topic and the person who will take the business trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 来月 indicates the expected time of the business trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle へ indicates the direction of travel for the business trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.3.vi: plan to go on a business trip
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before よていです to express a planned schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.why: わたしは states who has the plan, 来月 indicates the time, and 日本へ indicates the destination. 出張する comes before よていです to turn the action of going on a business trip into the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with つもりです, the sentence emphasizes the speaker's intention more than a scheduled plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ことになっています, the sentence shows that the schedule or decision has been arranged or officially set.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place 来月 after the verb, but a time expression usually comes before the place and action in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q11.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + 予定だ/です; Nの + 予定だ/です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.vi: Last night, I had a frightening dream and could not sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with the time noun 晩.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 夢 as the object of 見る; 怖い modifies 夢.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the action 見る with the following clause, creating a before-and-after relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 眠れない is the negative potential form of 眠る, expressing that someone could not sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the object of 見る. The て form connects the action of having a dream with the result of being unable to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This is used to say “to dream”; if 夢に見る is used, the nuance and structure will be different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 見る as “look,” forgetting that 夢を見る means “to dream.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.vi: The telephone number for calling an ambulance is 119.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 救急車 as the object of 呼ぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: V辞書形＋ときの modifies 電話番号, indicating the telephone number used when calling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 電話番号 the topic explained at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: です connects the topic 電話番号 with the identifying information that it is 119.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.why: 電話番号は is the topic, while 呼ぶときの is the clause modifying 電話番号. ときの turns a time expression into a modifier for the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: 呼ぶときに emphasizes the time when the action of calling takes place; it does not directly modify 電話番号 as ときの does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の in ときの, causing the clause 呼ぶとき not to connect correctly with the noun 電話番号.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q13.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Nの + とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes この料理 the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: Aな＋な modifies 味; が marks the taste being sensed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 味がする is a structure used to describe what a dish smells or tastes like.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q14.kobun.why: この料理は is what is being commented on, while 変な味がする is the sensory predicate. が marks what is sensed, not the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: 変な味がある indicates the existence of a strange taste, while 味がする emphasizes the taste that is experienced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after 味, but 味がする must be used for tastes and smells.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.vi: While staying at a Japanese inn, I came down with a fever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the accommodation where 泊まる stayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: Vた形＋とき indicates when the main clause takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 熱 as the object of 出す in the expression 熱を出す.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: て形 connects 出す with しまう to form the Vてしまう pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてしまいました expresses a completed event, often with a sense of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.why: The clause 泊まったとき places the time before the main clause. 熱を出す is a fixed verb phrase, and てしまう adds the nuance that the event happened unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: 熱が出ました only indicates having a fever; it does not emphasize regret or an unintended event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: 熱を出しました describes the event simply, with a lighter nuance than 出してしまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 出す word for word as “bring out,” but 熱を出す must be understood as “have a fever” or “come down with a fever.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.vi: In April next year, I will join a financial company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 来年 with 四月, forming the phrase “April next year.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the action 入社する takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or organization that the speaker joins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 入社する is a verb meaning to join a company; します creates the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first, followed by the organization that the speaker joins. The verb 入社する often goes with に to indicate the target company or the place the person joins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: 会社で働く emphasizes the workplace, while 会社に入社する emphasizes joining a company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with 入社する, but に is the one that indicates the place or organization that they join.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.vi: Our company is doing business with the United States.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わが社 the subject of the business activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the partner who carries out or takes part in the activity 貿易.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 貿易 as the content of している.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Vている describes an activity that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.why: わが社は is the topic, アメリカと indicates the partner, and 貿易をする is the content of the activity. ている shows that the commercial activity is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: Using に would not be appropriate because 貿易する usually indicates a business activity with a partner using と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: 貿易をした indicates only a completed activity; it does not express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と with 貿易をする as if と were the object, but と indicates the partner here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.vi: The employee in charge is checking safety at the level crossing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: では indicates the location and sets the context for the safety check.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person performing the action 確認する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 確認している describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.why: The location is stated first with では, followed by the person performing the action with が and the object with を. The ている form shows that the checking is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If では is replaced with に, the sentence only states the location without stressing the context or range of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If 確認している is replaced with 確認した, the meaning changes to having finished the check.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse が and を, but が is the person doing the action, while を is the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.vi: The fire started in the kitchen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the fire the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of the fire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 出た is the past form, describing a fire that started or came out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.why: The topic 火 comes first, while から identifies where the fire started. The verb 出る uses the past form to describe an event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 台所で is used, the sentence focuses on the event happening in the kitchen, without stressing the starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If 台所に出た is used, the meaning may become that it appeared or came out on the kitchen side, which is less natural than から in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for every location, but から is needed when expressing a starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 「を」 marks the object of the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な 「丁寧な」 changes to 「丁寧に」 to modify the verb 書く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 「Vてください」 is used to politely ask or request the listener to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.why: 「字を」 is the thing being written, 「丁寧に」 states how the action is done, and 「書いてください」 creates a polite request. An adverb comes before the verb it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「丁寧な字」 is used, 丁寧 directly modifies the noun 字, meaning careful or beautiful writing, not the way of writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 「ゆっくり」, the sentence stresses writing slowly, not necessarily writing carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.tip: The adjective な must change 「な」 to 「に」 before a verb; do not say 「丁寧な書いて」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q2.kobun.cn: Aな + に; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the baby is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 柔らかい modifies 肌, while を marks the feature described in the pattern 肌をしている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 肌をしている describes an external feature or condition of a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q20.kobun.why: The adjective 柔らかい comes before 肌 to modify the skin. The pattern Nをしている uses を to describe an external feature such as skin, a face, or a facial expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence directly says that the skin is soft, focusing on its quality rather than describing the baby's feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern suggests that the condition has become or changed into that state, so it does not fit an original feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate and use している as “be doing,” but in 肌をしている it describes a feature that the person has.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.vi: The heating system is broken. Could you check it for me?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the device that is in a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: 壊れています describes its current broken state, while ので connects the reason to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.2.vi: could you check it for me
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてもらえませんか is a polite way to ask someone else to do something for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.why: The first clause states the condition as the reason and connects it with ので. The second clause uses てもらえませんか to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is still correct, but the tone becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見てください is used, the request becomes more direct and loses its soft requesting tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand てもらう as “receive,” but in this pattern it means asking someone else to do something for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.vi: The girl has a sad-looking face.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the girl is the person being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 悲しそうな modifies 顔, while を marks the facial expression shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 顔をしています describes a person as having a certain facial expression or look.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.why: 悲しそうな comes before 顔 to form the noun phrase “a sad-looking face.” The pattern 顔をしている describes the expression the girl is showing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 悲しい顔 is used, the sentence states more clearly that the face is sad, while 悲しそうな stresses that it looks sad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, the focus changes to how the girl appears or acts as if she were sad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit な after an adjective ending in そう before a noun, but they must say 悲しそうな顔.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あなた with 健康 to show possession or a related object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks what is wished for; ご is a polite prefix used with nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 祈ります is the polite predicate, stating the speaker's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q23.kobun.why: あなたのご健康 forms a noun phrase meaning the listener's health. This phrase is the object of 祈ります and comes before the verb, following normal Japanese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence more formally and at greater length stresses wishing the listener to be in a healthy state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 願います is used, the meaning is still to wish someone well, but it focuses more on a hope than on a prayer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place the object after the verb, but Japanese places ご健康を before 祈ります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.vi: I am very happy to hear that you passed the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に is used with 合格する to indicate the exam that the person passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 合格する changes to the polite honorific passive form 合格された to describe the listener's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: こと nominalizes the whole previous clause, while を marks the content that is 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い changes to く to modify 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.why: The clause あなたが試験に合格された is nominalized with こと, forming the object of 思います. うれしく comes before 思います to express the speaker's feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことを is replaced with のを, the sentence still only says that you passed, but the tone is more conversational and specific.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change the adjective い into the form く before a verb such as うれしく思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.vi: My jacket was bitten by an insect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.sk: N を + N に + past passive verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the thing affected by the biting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the agent in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: くわれた is a passive past form. It describes the jacket being affected unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.why: In a passive sentence, the affected thing still goes with を, while the agent goes with に. The verb is in the past form because the event has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If we use this active sentence, the focus shifts to the insect as the subject that ate or bit the jacket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 虫が instead of 虫に, but a passive sentence needs に to show the agent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vi: If you make a wrong-number call, please apologize properly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 「を」 marks the wrong-number call as the object of the action of calling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: if you have made a wrong-number call
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 「かけた」 modifies 場合, while 「は」 states that situation as a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies the action of apologizing and shows how it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 「謝りましょう」 uses the form 「ます」 with 「ましょう」 to suggest doing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.why: 「かけた場合は」 places the condition at the beginning of the conclusion. Then the adverb 「ちゃんと」 modifies the advice 「謝りましょう」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「場合は」 is replaced with 「ときは」, it only refers to the time or situation being discussed, so the conditional meaning is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 「かけたら」 expresses “apologize when you have just made a wrong-number call,” so it is closer to a specific situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out 「は」 after 場合, but 「場合は」 needs 「は」 to make that situation the conditional topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q3.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない・Aい・Aなな・Nの + 場合は
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 「は」 makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective いい comes before a noun to modify the type of fortune-telling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 「だけ」 limits the scope, while 「を」 marks the entire object of 信じます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 「信じます」 is the main predicate and expresses present belief.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.why: The topic 「わたしは」 comes first, and then 「いい」 modifies 「うらない」. The phrase 「うらないだけを」 both limits the object with だけ and marks it with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 「いい占いしか信じません」, the meaning is still “believe only good fortunes,” but the negative form 「ない」 is required.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「いい占いも信じます」 is used, it means that the speaker also believes good fortunes, without the limiting meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q4.kobun.tip: 「だけ」 can be used with an affirmative sentence, while 「しか」 must be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vi: If there is no warranty document, you will have to pay a repair fee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 「が」 marks the thing being considered in terms of whether it exists or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 「ない」 comes before 場合 to modify the case of having no warranty document.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 「は」 turns the situation just mentioned into a condition for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 「が」 marks the fee that arises in the result clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 「かかります」 expresses a cost that arises or must be paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.why: The clause 「保証書がない」 modifies 場合 to create a condition. In the main clause, 「修理代がかかる」 uses が because the repair fee is a cost that arises.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「場合は」 is replaced with 「ときは」, it means “when there is no warranty document.” It sounds more natural in speech but places less emphasis on the situation as a case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「保証書がなければ」 is used, it creates the condition directly with a hypothetical form, making the sentence shorter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q5.kobun.tip: For the existence or nonexistence of an object, use 「Nがある/ない」, not 「Nをある/ない」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q6.kobun.vi: Please change this ten-thousand-yen note into one-thousand-yen notes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the amount of money being exchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the form or result after the exchange.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q6.kobun.why: 両替する goes with を to show the money being exchanged and with に to show the type of money received. The verb in the て form combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning is actively changing one object or type of money into another, without emphasizing the act of exchanging money at a counter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before the money received, but the result after the exchange must use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q7.kobun.vi: Have you found the cause of the problem?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the noun 故障 with 原因, creating the phrase “the cause of the problem.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes 原因 the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: わかりました is a polite past form that asks whether the cause has been found or understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q7.kobun.why: The phrase NのN places the problem before 原因 to identify what the cause belongs to. は makes 原因 the topic, while the past question checks whether the result has been achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the focus shifts to which cause has been identified, instead of making 原因 the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate の as “of” a machine, but here it only shows a modifying relationship between two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q8.kobun.vi: Is the preparation for the party progressing?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects パーティー with 準備 and identifies the preparation for the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 準備 the topic being asked about in terms of its progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 進んでいます shows an ongoing process, and か creates a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q8.kobun.why: パーティーの準備 forms a noun phrase, and then は makes this phrase the topic. 進んでいます describes the progress that is continuing at the time of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If the past form is used instead, the sentence only asks whether the preparation progressed, without emphasizing the current process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ています as only meaning “be doing,” but with 進む it also expresses a state of progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.vi: Because I have just woken up, I do not feel hungry yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: さっき shows the time when the action 起きた occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the た form comes before ばかり to show an action that has just been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: Vたばかりです means “have just done something,” while から connects this clause to the reason that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks 食欲 as the thing being discussed in a state of having or not having it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります and expresses that something does not exist or is not present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.why: さっき and 起きたばかり together identify an action that has just happened. から connects the reason before it with the result after it, where 食欲がありません expresses not having an appetite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning emphasizes an action that has just ended at the moment of speaking, while ばかり can cover a slightly wider period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used instead of から, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ばかり with the meaning “only,” but Vたばかり here means “have just finished doing something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t26-q9.kobun.cn: Vた + ばかりだ/です; 普通形・Nな + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 懐かしい comes before a noun to modify むかしばなし.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being enjoyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is in the polite past form and shows that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q1.kobun.why: The adjective is placed directly before the noun it modifies. Then the noun phrase むかしばなしを functions as the object of たのしみました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 懐かしく does not stand directly before a noun; this form usually modifies a verb or describes a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place an adjective after a noun, while Japanese places an adjective before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q1.tokens.3.m: an old story; a fairy tale
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks vehicles as the subject that is passing by.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: たくさん modifies the number of vehicles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 通っている uses the ている form to describe an action in progress; います keeps the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q10.kobun.why: 車が is the subject, たくさん shows the quantity, and 通っています is the predicate. The ている form is suitable because the cars are still passing by.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 通ります, the sentence only states that many cars pass by in general or will pass by. It does not emphasize that the action is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 通って is replaced with 止まって, the meaning changes to “many cars are stopped.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand ています as only the present tense, but in this sentence it emphasizes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective な comes before a noun to modify 運転.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks an action that is or is not performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The form ないで connects with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.why: The adjective な comes before a noun to describe the type of action or event. The object takes を, and ないでください is then used to ask the listener not to do that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a request to drive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistake ないでください for “please do not do,” but its natural meaning is “please do not do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q11.kobun.cn: Aな + N を + Vないで + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q12.kobun.vi: The upper floor is the rooftop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to point to something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents 上 as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: です politely ends a noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q12.kobun.why: この modifies 上 to identify the floor being discussed. The structure NはNです is used to introduce or identify the topic's identity or feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the existence or location of something above.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate この as “this” by itself, but この must come before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.vi: I do not have work today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.sk: Time は + N が + ありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time reference for the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing being said to exist or not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.2.vi: there is not; do not have
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります, used for something that does not exist or is not available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.why: The time reference comes first with は. The thing that exists or does not exist is the subject with が, while ありません is the negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is “not work,” which denies the action rather than saying that there is no work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use を with ありません, but the existence pattern あります／ありません uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q13.tokens.4.m: there is not; do not have
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the departure time or event as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: です politely ends a sentence that identifies a time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q14.kobun.why: The noun for the event is presented as the topic with は. The time phrase comes after it to identify when the event happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence talks about the action of departing rather than stating the departure time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may put に after the time in this pattern, but a noun sentence Nは時間です does not need に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: まっすぐ modifies the verb and shows the direction of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of 進む connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ください expresses a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q15.kobun.why: A directional adverb comes before the verb to describe how to go. The verb uses the て form and combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means “please do not go straight.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may keep the dictionary form before ください, but the verb must be changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q16.kobun.sk: Place が + Nの + N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the place identified as the classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the owner with the noun 教室 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a sentence that identifies the place's identity or feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q16.kobun.why: ここが is the place being identified, while わたしたちの教室 is the noun expressing ownership. です connects the two parts to mean “this is …”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence presents “here” as the topic instead of emphasizing that this is the exact place being identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse の with に, but の shows ownership or modifies a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q17.kobun.vi: That island is south of Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents that island as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with 南, creating the modifying phrase “south of Japan.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate used for the existence of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q17.kobun.why: The phrase 日本の南 identifies the location in relation to “south of Japan.” The particle に follows the place because the sentence describes existence with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: へ shows a direction of movement, so the sentence means going toward the south of Japan, not describing an existing location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use で for an existing location, but with あります they need に to show where the object is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.vi: I want to travel around the world by boat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the means of traveling around.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the range or object that まわる travels around.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: まわりたい is the たい form of まわる, expressing the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.why: The means of transport ふねで comes before the action, while 世界を is the area traveled around. The ending たい attaches to the verb stem to express desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: へ emphasizes movement toward the world and does not clearly express traveling around the whole world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: Without たいです, the sentence only means traveling around the world, with no meaning of desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q18.kobun.tip: Do not attach たい directly to the dictionary form; remove ます first, then add たい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち to 台所, showing possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 台所 the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: せまい is an い adjective used as the predicate, combined with です to make a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q19.kobun.why: うちの台所 forms a noun phrase in which うちの modifies 台所. After the topic comes the adjective い, which describes its feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: が makes 台所 the emphasized subject, instead of simply stating it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: せまくない negates the feature, meaning that the kitchen is not narrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q19.kobun.tip: の must be placed between two nouns; do not use は to connect うち directly to 台所 when expressing possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q2.kobun.sk: Time expression ＋ N が ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence to state when something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the existing thing in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is used for the existence of things that are not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q2.kobun.why: The time expression あした is moved to the beginning to identify the time. 試験 is a thing that exists, so it is the subject with が and goes with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If をします is used, it means that an exam will be taken or held tomorrow, focusing on the action rather than existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use います for every case of “having” or “there is,” but あります is used for exams and things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.sk: Time expression ＋ N の ＋ N は ＋ どうですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence. It does not need a particle when it functions as a time adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects あなた to 都合, showing your circumstances or availability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 都合 the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: どう asks about a state or situation; ですか makes the question polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.why: あした sets the time context, and あなたの都合 is what is being asked about. The pattern Nはどうですか asks about the situation or availability of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: がいいですか directly asks whether it is convenient, with a clearer meaning than どうですか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q20.kobun.tip: どうですか does not only mean “how”; in the context of making plans, it often asks “Is it convenient?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.vi: It was very cold this morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ とても ＋ Aい pastです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this morning the topic of the weather comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective さむかった, showing the degree of coldness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: さむかった is the past form of the adjective い さむい, combined with です to speak politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.why: 今朝は makes the time point the topic, and とても comes before the adjective to increase its degree. The adjective い changes い into かった to describe a state that occurred in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: さむいです is present tense, so it means that this morning is being described as cold now or is generally considered cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q21.kobun.tip: The adjective い changes い into かった in the past; do not say さむいかったです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.vi: I will go to the library now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the starting point of an action that is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement toward 図書館.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the polite form of 行く and serves as the predicate for an action of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.why: これから states the time, 図書館へ states the destination, and 行きます is the main action. The particle へ is suitable because the sentence emphasizes the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: に also indicates a destination and is often more natural when emphasizing the place one will go to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: で indicates the place where an action takes place, so it means studying at the library, not going there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q22.kobun.tip: へ and に can both indicate a destination with 行く, but で is not used to indicate a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective comes before the noun to modify 町.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 町 is the noun expressing the statement, and です ends the polite sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q23.kobun.why: ここは sets the place as the topic, then 小さい modifies 町. 町です forms the predicate, meaning “is a town.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes that this place itself is a small town.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the adjective after the noun, but Japanese puts 小さい before 町.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.vi: I had a child last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.sk: Time noun ＋ N が ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: 去年 indicates when the event happened and stands at the beginning to state the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that was born.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 生まれました is the polite past form of 生まれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.why: 去年 states the time, and 子どもが is the subject of 生まれる. The verb uses the ました form to describe an event completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 産みました is used, the unstated subject is the mother, and the sentence directly says “gave birth to a child,” not that the child was born.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake 生まれる for “give birth to a child,” but it is an intransitive verb: the child is born.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this bag the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 重い is an い adjective used as the predicate, combined with です to make a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q25.kobun.why: このかばんは makes the object the topic, while 重い describes its feature. With an い adjective, keep the 重い form before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 重くないです, the sentence becomes negative: this bag is not heavy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q25.kobun.tip: Do not add な after 重い; an い adjective connects directly to です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vi: The next train is an express train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies the noun 電車.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the next train the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with a noun showing the train type.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q3.kobun.why: つぎの combines with 電車 to form the noun phrase “the next train.” The pattern NはNです identifies the type or feature of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If が来ます is used, the sentence emphasizes that an express train is coming, rather than identifying the train type.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate です as “there is,” but here です means “is.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q4.kobun.vi: I was out during the day yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with 昼間 to modify the daytime period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the period being discussed the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 出かけていました describes a state or action that was continuing at a past time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q4.kobun.why: きのうの昼間 forms a time phrase, while は marks this phrase as the emphasized time point. Vていました shows that the speaker was in the state of being out at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 出かけました, the sentence simply says that the person went out, without emphasizing an ongoing state at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の in きのうの昼間, but の is necessary to connect the two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.vi: Let us try asking that store employee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person whom the speaker will ask.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 聞いてみる uses the form て to connect 聞く with みる and expresses trying to do something; ましょう is an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.why: The phrase あの店員に comes first to state the object of the asking action. 聞いてみましょう expresses a suggestion to try asking that person together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only means “please ask” and no longer has the sense of trying to see what happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence means “be asking” or “usually ask,” not an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle に or use を after the person being asked, but the object of 聞く usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q5.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ みる／みます／みましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to become a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ N に ＋ Vます-removeます＋たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: This time expression modifies the wish to become a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the result or status reached after becoming something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: なりたい is formed from なります by removing ます and adding たい, expressing a wish; です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.why: The topic わたしは comes first, followed by the time expressionしょうらい. 医者になる expresses changing into a profession, while なりたい adds the speaker's wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence refers to a plan or to becoming a doctor, without directly emphasizing a wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the tone is more formal and emphasizes the wish to remain a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 医者をなりたい, but a profession or status goes with になる, so 医者になりたい must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q6.kobun.cn: N ＋ に ＋ なる／なりたい; Vます形の語幹 ＋ たい（です）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.vi: Do you know the name of this flower?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この identifies 花, while の connects 花 with 名前 to form the phrase “the name of the flower.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks 名前 as the information known.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: しっていますか creates a polite question about the state of knowing information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.why: The phrase この花の名前 is formed through the relationship between this flower and its name. 名前を is the object of しっていますか, so を comes directly before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is replaced with は, 花 becomes the topic, changing the structure of “the name of this flower.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If しっていますか is replaced, the question focuses on whether someone understands or can know it, rather than on the state of already knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mechanically translate の as “of,” but here it connects two nouns to form the phrase “the name of the flower.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q8.kobun.vi: I will return home before dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: までに marks the deadline by which the action of returning home must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action 帰る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q8.kobun.why: 夕飯までに places the completion deadline at the beginning of the sentence. いえに states the place of return, while かえります is the main predicate and ends the polite sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If までに is replaced with まで, it means returning home by dinner time or staying until then, without emphasizing a completion deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 夕飯の前に, the meaning is still “before dinner,” but the expression focuses on the time before an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse までに with まで; までに is used for something that must be finished before a deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q9.kobun.vi: It is hot today, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 暑い is an i-adjective used as the predicate; ですね adds confirmation and invites the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q9.kobun.why: きょうは states the time and topic, and then 暑い gives a comment about the weather. ですね turns the comment into a light sharing of feelings or confirmation with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced with ですよ, the speaker confirms or informs the listener rather than waiting for agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ですか, the sentence becomes a question about whether today is hot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t27-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ね as a meaningless word, but ですね often expresses “isn't it?” or a wish for the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.vi: This country has a highly developed industrial sector.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this country is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject being described as highly developed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: さかんです is the predicate and describes the level of development of 工業.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.why: この国は defines the scope of the comment, while 工業が is the field being described. The pattern NはNがさかんです expresses a field that is highly developed in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If を and します are used, the sentence means actively “to make industry develop strongly.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.tip: In a pattern that describes a part or field of the topic, do not use を before さかんです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q1.kobun.cn: N が ＋ Aな です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.vi: Please wait in front of the gate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 門 with 前 to modify 前.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the action of waiting takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: て-form connects the verb まつ with いる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: いて is the connecting form of いる and expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 門の前で identifies the place to wait, and then まっていてください expresses a request to continue waiting. The particle で is used because this is the place where the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only asks someone to wait and does not emphasize the continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit いて and use まってください directly, even when they want to emphasize continuing to wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 光る modifies もの, while は makes the whole phrase the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 何ですか creates a question asking what an object is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q11.kobun.why: The clause 光る comes before もの to identify the type of object being discussed. は marks the whole phrase as the topic, and then 何ですか asks for the corresponding information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning emphasizes an object that is glowing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a modifying clause after the noun, following Vietnamese word order, but Japanese places it before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks 合計 as the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the result or value that the total amount becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: なりますか asks politely about the final value.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q12.kobun.why: The sentence puts the object being asked about, 合計, first using は. いくらに なりますか uses なる to ask how much the total amount will become.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the question directly asks how much the current price is, with less emphasis on the result of adding everything together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use を with なる, but a result after なる usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.vi: There is a sign in front of that store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 店 with 表 to indicate the front of the store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the location where the sign exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the existing object in a sentence that uses あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence of an object that is not a person or animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.why: The phrase 店の表に identifies the location, while かんばんが is the object that exists there. The pattern にあります is suitable for saying where an object is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 表 is replaced with 前, the meaning is only that it is in front of the shop, without emphasizing the outside or front area of the shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は for かんばん, but が sounds more natural when introducing an object that exists in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the goods as the object of the export action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 輸出します is a noun-verb combined with する in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q14.kobun.why: しょうひんを comes before the object of the action. 輸出 combines with します to form a verb meaning to export.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 輸入します, the meaning changes to importing goods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake 輸出 for import because they only remember the Sino-Vietnamese sound and do not distinguish that 出 means out and 入 means in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q15.kobun.vi: I paint the wall with paint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the surface or place receiving the effect of painting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the material that is spread or painted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 塗ります is the polite form of 塗る and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q15.kobun.why: かべに indicates the affected surface, while ペンキを indicates the material used in the action. The verb 塗ります comes at the end to complete the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used with かべ, the wall is viewed as the direct object of painting; the sentence can still be understood, but the material is less clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for both かべ and ペンキ, but に clearly indicates the surface being painted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that was born.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q16.kobun.why: The subject is introduced first with が, followed by a verb expressing birth in the polite past form. This structure is suitable for announcing something that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of が, which removes the focus on the subject that has just been introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q17.kobun.vi: I bought a souvenir at the tourist destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the item that is bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q17.kobun.why: The place where the action takes place comes first and goes with で. The item bought comes before を, followed by the verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence no longer naturally expresses the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse で and に, but the place where an action occurs usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka's house is in the third neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Number + N目 に + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with the noun 家 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the house the topic whose location is identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the location where the house exists; め turns a counting number into an ordinal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is used for the existence of objects or places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.why: The possessive phrase たなかさんの modifies 家. After introducing the topic with は, the location comes before に and the sentence ends with あります to express the existence of the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If only にあります is used without a specific location phrase, the sentence only says that the house exists somewhere without identifying the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の in the possessive phrase and mistakenly think that 家は independently means “as for the house,” separate from the modifier before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I took the express train home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は sets yesterday as the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the vehicle or train that the speaker boards.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: のって is the て form of 乗る, connecting the action of taking the train with the action of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.kobun.why: The time reference comes at the beginning of the sentence and is marked with は. A means of transportation goes with に, while the て form connects boarding the train with the result of returning home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 特急で is used, the focus is on transportation in general, while 特急に乗る emphasizes boarding the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate it as “by train” and always use で, but the verb 乗る usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q19.tokens.4.m: board a train, travel by train
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q2.kobun.vi: The 8th of this month is Saturday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今月 with 八日, creating the phrase “the 8th day of this month.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the 8th day is the topic whose day of the week is identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 土よう日は makes the noun the predicate, and です connects it to the topic politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q2.kobun.why: 今月の八日 creates a noun phrase for a specific date. 八日は makes it the topic, and then 土よう日です identifies that date as Saturday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the phrase only indicates the time when an action takes place, so it does not fit a sentence identifying the day of the week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q2.kobun.tip: 八日 is read as ようか, not by combining the numbers in the usual way as はちにち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.vi: I am reading a book about economics now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.sk: Time + N の + N を + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the action is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the field of economics with 本, showing the content of the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the book as the object of reading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: よんでいます consists of the て form of 読む and います, expressing an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.why: The field of economics modifies the book through の. The book is the object marked by を, while よんでいます shows that the action is taking place now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 読みます, the sentence only says that the speaker will read or usually reads, without emphasizing that the reading is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand の in 経済の本 as possession, but here it indicates the content or topic of the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vi: What do you think of your opinion?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あなた with 意見 to create the noun phrase “your opinion.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that your opinion is the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: どう asks about the condition or evaluation of the topic, while ですか creates a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q3.kobun.why: あなたの意見 is a complete noun phrase because of の. This phrase is placed before は, and どうですか is used to ask for an opinion about it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何ですか is used, the question “What is your opinion?” focuses on the content, rather than asking how it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q3.kobun.tip: どうですか asks about a characteristic or impression, so it should not be translated mechanically as “what is it?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place or location where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb 書く with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of a sentence to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q4.kobun.why: The place comes before the object, followed by the action and the request. に indicates where the action takes place, while を indicates what is being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with this, the sentence will ask for or allow an address to be written, so it will no longer be a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に and で; に indicates a place where something exists or is headed, while で indicates where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は indicates the person being talked about in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: With 好き, the particle が marks the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, which politely expresses liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q5.kobun.why: わたしは sets the topic, while 旅が is the object of the feeling of liking. In the pattern 好き, the object usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with this, the sentence will mean taking a trip, not liking travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with this, the sentence will say that traveling is enjoyable, but it will not directly express the speaker’s preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say 旅をすきです, but 好き usually uses が to mark the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vi: My younger sister is currently in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the younger sister as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 今 indicates the time when the state being discussed applies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of する, connecting the noun 入院する with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ています expresses a continuing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the time 今 adds the circumstances, and then the pattern ています expresses the current state. 入院する changes to the て form as 入院して before います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with this, the sentence will only say that the person was hospitalized, without emphasizing their current condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the full form with the same structure as 入院して います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ています as simply doing something, but with 入院する it usually indicates the state of being hospitalized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.vi: I hear that a new building will be built here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where the new building will appear or be built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 新しい comes before 建物 to modify this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the object that newly appears or is built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: できる acts as the predicate and expresses the formation or appearance of the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです comes after the plain form to report information that has been heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.why: 新しい directly modifies 建物, が marks the thing that will appear, and そうです shows that this is reported information. に identifies where the event takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used after a word stem such as できそうです, it means that something seems about to happen or may happen, not that it is reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with らしいです, the sentence still means that the information is reported, but the nuance is that it is inferred or passed on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the hearsay form そうです with そうです, which indicates appearance; look at the form of the word before it to tell them apart.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.vi: I ate half a loaf of bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the food being eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: だけ limits the amount of bread eaten to half.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べました is the polite past form of 食べる and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.why: パンを is the general object of the action of eating, while 半分だけ limits the amount eaten. The verb is in the polite past form because the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with this, the sentence will emphasize that the person ate only half and imply that this was less than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were replaced with も, the sentence would emphasize eating as much as half.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q8.kobun.tip: だけ has a neutral limiting meaning, while しか always goes with a negative form and often gives the meaning “only that much.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q9.kobun.vi: My younger brother is a company employee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the younger brother as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the topic with a noun showing a job or status and creates a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q9.kobun.why: This simple introduction uses は to state who is being discussed and です to identify that person's job or status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If が were used, the sentence would emphasize that the younger brother himself is the company employee, usually in response to a question or for contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit です in polite speech; in a noun sentence, です creates the polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vi: This country has a long coastline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun or noun phrase that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this country the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks 海岸線 as the subject that has the characteristic of being long.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q1.kobun.why: このくには sets the scope of the statement, while 海岸線が長い states the characteristic of the coastline. が marks the noun that directly has the characteristic 長い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If は were used for 海岸線, the sentence would emphasize a comparison or shift the topic to the coastline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q1.kobun.tip: 海岸線 is a compound word, so you need to understand how 海岸 and 線 combine to mean coastline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vi: This soup has a mild flavor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies スープ and must come before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that スープ is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the specific characteristic of the soup being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: うすい is the adjective い and directly acts as the predicate before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.why: この comes before スープ to identify the specific soup. The structure NはNがAいです uses the first part as the topic and the second part to state the topic's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If スープはうすいです were said, it would still mean that the soup is mild, but it would not clearly state that the flavor is the characteristic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q10.kobun.tip: が should not be translated mechanically as “have”; in this sentence, が marks the part that has the characteristic “mild.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the thing being pointed to is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 歴史 with テキスト, showing the content or field of the textbook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: テキストです is a noun predicate that identifies the thing being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q11.kobun.why: これは is the topic, while 歴史のテキスト is the complete noun phrase used as the comment. の expresses the relationship “a textbook about history.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If これはテキストです were said, the sentence would only identify this as a textbook, without saying that its content is history.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q11.kobun.tip: の in 歴史のテキスト does not express ownership between a person and a thing; it connects a field with the main noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vi: There is a small bird perched on that tree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies 木 and refers to a tree far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 木 with 上, forming a phrase that indicates a position on the tree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the position where the bird is perched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject located there and in the state of perching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: ている describes a state that continues after the action of perching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.why: あの木の上に forms a location phrase and places it before the subject to state the place first. 小鳥が is the subject, while とまっています describes the current continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If とまります is used, the sentence only says that the bird will perch or usually perches. It does not emphasize its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ています as simply “be doing,” but with とまる, とまっています often emphasizes the state of “being perched.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q13.kobun.vi: I want to watch TV tonight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states tonight as the topic or time point of the desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 見たい is formed from the verb stem 見ます and たい, expressing the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q13.kobun.why: 今夜は places the time point at the beginning of the sentence. テレビを is the object, while 見たいです is the predicate expressing the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見たいです is replaced with 見ます, the sentence only means “I watch TV” or “I will watch TV”; it no longer expresses desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q13.kobun.tip: たい usually expresses the speaker’s own desire. It should not be used freely to state another person’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vi: Because it is cold, let’s turn on the heater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: から connects the reason clause to the suggested action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being turned on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう attaches to the verb stem to make an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and ends with から, followed by an action suitable for that reason. 暖房を is the object of つける, while ましょう changes turning on the heater into a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of から, the reason sounds softer and more objective, while から is more direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.tip: When connecting a noun or an adjective な with から, だから must be used. For an adjective い such as さむい, keep it unchanged and add から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + から/Aな・N + だから
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q15.kobun.vi: The first step is very important.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の changes a time phrase into a modifier for 一歩.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the adjective だいじです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q15.kobun.why: The time phrase comes before の to modify the noun 一歩. 一歩が is the subject, while だいじです is the predicate describing the subject’s quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is replaced with に, 最初に usually modifies an action directly, meaning “do something first,” rather than modifying 一歩.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically use に after 最初, although の is needed here to connect with the noun 一歩.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q16.kobun.vi: Because my tooth hurt, I went to the dentist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes to the くて form to connect the reason to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the place or destination that the speaker goes to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q16.kobun.why: The clause 歯がいたくて gives the cause first, and the main clause then gives the result いきました. The particle に identifies the destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 歯がいたいので is used, the sentence still gives a reason, but the explanation sounds clearer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q16.kobun.tip: Do not connect the adjective い with いで; remove い and add くて instead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.vi: I am preparing materials for the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 会議 with 資料, showing that the materials belong to or are used for the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of the verb 準備する and connects with います to form a continuing-action expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: います combines with the verb’s て form to show that an action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.why: 会議の資料 forms a noun phrase that serves as the object of 準備する. The て form connects 準備する with います and describes the preparation as ongoing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 準備します is used instead, the sentence only says that the speaker will prepare or usually prepares something. It does not emphasize that the action is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q17.kobun.tip: The form ている here means “be doing,” not simply “be in a state of” as a mechanical translation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.vi: Because I was careless, I accidentally broke my wristwatch.
