default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause or condition that led to the breakage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object affected by the action of breaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 壊して is the て form of 壊す and connects with しまいました to describe a completed action, often with regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: しまいました adds the meaning of an unwanted completion or regret for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.why: ふちゅういで gives the cause, うでどけいを is the object, and 壊してしまいました is the main predicate. The て form connects with しまう and creates an accidental or regrettable tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 壊しておきました, the sentence means that the speaker intentionally broke it beforehand or left it that way. It no longer has the accidental meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit て in てしまう, but they must say 壊してしまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the written content should be put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content that needs to be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: かいて is the て form of 書く and connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the て form to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q19.kobun.why: ここに identifies the place for writing, while 住所を identifies the content to write. The structure Vてください changes the action かいて into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 書いてもいいですか, the sentence asks for permission to write rather than asking someone else to write.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; change 書く to 書いて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vi: I will show the customer around the factory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person receiving the guiding action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the place or object being shown around.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 案内します is a polite verb expressing the action of showing someone around.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q2.kobun.why: The person being guided goes with に, while the place being guided goes with を. 案内する comes at the end of the sentence as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used with お客さん, the customer becomes the person being guided, not the person receiving guidance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish に as the person receiving guidance and を as the place or object being guided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.vi: There are white clouds in the sky.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where something exists when used with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い comes before 雲 to describe this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the sky.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is an existence predicate for things that are not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.why: そらに sets the location, しろい describes 雲, and then 雲があります states that clouds exist. This order is natural because information about the location usually comes before the thing that exists there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with います, the sentence is used for people or animals, so it does not fit 雲.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for existence, but a location used with あります must use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q21.kobun.vi: I will go to the art museum this weekend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the time presented as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: いきます is the polite form of the verb “to go,” used for the present or future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q21.kobun.why: The sentence puts the time first as the topic, then gives the destination with に. The verb いきます comes at the end to complete the intention to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use で for a destination when saying where someone is going; に marks the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.vi: That person enthusiastically showed me the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the person being discussed as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes the adjective な 熱心 into an adverb, describing how the way was shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content that is shown or explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: おしえて is the て form, connecting the verb for showing the way with くれました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: くれました shows that the other person did it for the speaker’s benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.why: The person performing the action comes before は, while the object being explained goes with を. The て form connects おしえる with くれる to express an action done for the speaker’s benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the focus shifts to the speaker having received guidance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the sentence only says that the other person showed the way. It no longer has the meaning of doing it to help the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that the adjective な must add に when it describes a verb, as in 熱心に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q22.kobun.cn: N は + Aな に + Vて + くれる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: での turns the phrase ここで into a modifier for the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents smoking here as the topic of the reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ご + noun + ください is a polite way to ask the listener not to do that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q23.kobun.why: The phrase ここでのきつえん combines the place and the action into a topic. ご遠慮ください comes at the end of the sentence and creates a polite, formal request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence is still a prohibition, but it is more direct and less formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q23.kobun.tip: Do not translate ご遠慮ください as an invitation; on signs, this pattern usually means please refrain or do not do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.vi: The event venue is near the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects イベント with the noun 会場, creating a relationship of possession or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the event venue the topic for the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the place used as the reference point for comparing distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ちかいです is the polite form of the い adjective predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.why: の creates the noun phrase “event venue,” and then は makes that phrase the topic. With distance adjectives such as 近い, に marks the place used as the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with から, the meaning changes to being near the company or near from the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q24.kobun.tip: When saying that one place is near another, learners may easily confuse に with から; に gives the reference point, while から emphasizes the starting point or the distance measured from it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.vi: A beautiful view can be seen from here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the viewing point or starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: うつくしい comes before 景色 to describe the view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the scenery that is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 見えます describes scenery naturally coming into view from the current position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.why: The sentence gives the viewing point with ここから, then places the adjective before the noun to describe the view. With 見える, the scenery that is seen becomes the subject and goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced with 見られます, the sentence emphasizes the ability or conditions that allow the viewer to see.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q25.kobun.tip: 見える means that something is seen naturally, not that someone actively looks at it intentionally as with 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I stayed overnight at a traditional Japanese inn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.sk: Time は + Place に + past Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the time as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place of accommodation or the place where the overnight action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb とまる is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.why: きのうは makes the time the topic, then に gives the place where the speaker stayed overnight. とまりました comes at the end and takes the polite past form to describe an event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the place is understood as the location where an action is generally performed, without emphasizing accommodation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で instead of に; when とまる means staying or spending the night, the place usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.sk: Time + Hour に + Nする + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to set the departure time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the specific time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form, used to suggest doing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.why: あした gives the day, while ９時に gives the specific hour. 出発する changes into 出発しましょう to make an invitation or suggestion to leave together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, it means starting from 9 o’clock, so the action does not necessarily take place exactly at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out に after the hour; a specific time such as ９時 usually needs to go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q4.kobun.cn: N + する + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vi: What kind of relationship do those two people have?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies ふたり, referring only to the two people identified in the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the two people the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: どういう comes before a noun to ask about that noun's type or content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: what kind of relationship is it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ですか creates a polite question about the relationship between the two people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.why: ふたりは is the subject being asked about, while どういう関係 is the noun phrase asking about the type of relationship. ですか comes at the end of the sentence to turn this phrase into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with どんな関係ですか gives almost the same meaning, but どんな usually asks more directly about the type or quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put どういう after the noun; in Japanese, it must come before the noun being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q5.kobun.cn: どういう + N + ですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vi: Mr. Hayashi is a person who uses polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Mr. Hayashi as the person described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 丁寧 is a な adjective, so な must be used before the noun ことば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the words or speech being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 使う in its dictionary form comes before 人 to modify the person who uses them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 人です acts as the predicate and concludes that Mr. Hayashi is the type of person described earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.why: 丁寧な modifies ことば, forming the ことばを object. The clause ことばを使う then modifies 人, and 人です acts as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 丁寧に is used, 丁寧 directly modifies the verb 使う, meaning to use something politely or carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If you say 丁寧な人, the adjective modifies the person, meaning a polite person, not polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な after the adjective な when the adjective comes before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or an honorific for a person
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q6.kobun.cn: Aな + な + N; V辞書形 + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vi: I had an accident and was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に goes with あう to indicate an unexpected event that the subject experiences.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: あって is the て form of あう, linking having an accident with the result of being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks けが in the fixed phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing the phrase けがをしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.why: 事故にあう is a verb phrase meaning to have an accident, in which に marks the event experienced. The て form connects the cause or earlier event with the result けがをしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If あってから is used, the sentence emphasizes that the following action happened after the accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If あったので is used, the sentence emphasizes the cause: because I had an accident, I was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after 事故, but with あう meaning to experience an event, the correct particle is に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being raised by 育てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the phrase 子どもを育てる into a noun, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: たいへんです acts as the predicate and comments that raising children is hard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q8.kobun.why: 子どもを育てる is a verb clause nominalized by の. のは turns the whole action into the topic for the comment たいへんです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のは with ことは still refers to raising children, but こと has a more general or formal tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 子どもを育てるは directly; to turn an action into a topic, they must add の or こと before は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.vi: Her Japanese pronunciation is very clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies her as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun 日本語 with 発音, creating the meaning “Japanese pronunciation.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object described as きれい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: きれい is a な adjective, used with です at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.why: は sets the topic as かのじょ, while 日本語の modifies 発音 to identify the type of pronunciation. が marks the part being evaluated, and then きれいです acts as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 日本語の発音が is removed, the sentence only directly comments that she is “pretty/beautiful” or “clean.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t29-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of が in 日本語の発音がきれいです, which removes the structure “as for the pronunciation, how is it?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: I decorated the flowers at the entrance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where the decoration is put or takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being decorated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 飾る changes to the polite past form 飾りました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The place where an object is put comes first with に, while the flowers are the object of the action, so they go with を. The verb 飾る comes at the end and has the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the place where the decorating action takes place, which is not necessarily where the object is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for every location, but に is suitable when talking about where an object is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q1.tokens.0.m: entrance hall, entrance to a house
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the exam the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The い-ending adjective やさしい changes to やさしかったです to describe a past state politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: 試験は is the topic, while the adjective comes at the end to comment on the exam. やさしい is put in the past because the exam has already taken place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, やさしい directly modifies 試験, and the predicate is the noun 試験でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add だ after the い-ending adjective, but they must say やさしかったです, not やさしかっただです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vi: Yesterday I went to the zoo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q11.kobun.sk: Time + N に + Vます past
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes an action that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q11.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning, followed by the destination with に, and then the main verb. The いきました form shows that going was completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, the sentence still shows the direction of movement but emphasizes the direction more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle に after a location when saying where they went.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vi: It was a shame that I could not meet Mr. Yamada.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person whom the speaker wants to meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: あえなくて is the て form of あえない, connecting the cause with the regretful comment that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 残念でした is the polite past form of the な adjective predicate, expressing a feeling about the previous event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.why: The person met goes with に. The clause あえなくて comes first to give the reason, while 残念でした is the main comment of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If あえないで is used, the meaning tends to be “not meeting someone and doing something else,” so it is less natural than the cause-linking form in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the reason is stated clearly and has a softer explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate なくて as “without” in every situation, but here it connects the cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vi: It takes about one hour by bus from my house to the airport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.sk: N の + N から + N まで + N で + Duration + くらいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: わたしの modifies いえ, forming the phrase 'my house'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: まで marks the ending point of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the means of transport used for travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The duration phrase shows how long the journey takes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: くらい shows an approximate degree and combines with です to end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.why: The structure から〜まで covers the whole route from the starting point to the ending point. Then で states the means of transport, while the duration combines with くらい to express an approximate period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ごろ is used, it refers to an approximate point in time, not an approximate duration like くらい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is used after バス, the sentence does not correctly express the means of transport; means of transport must be used with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse から with 'because', but in から〜まで it marks the starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vi: This store has both cheap things and expensive things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the store being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: には combines with に to state where something exists and with は to make that place the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 安い modifies もの, while も marks one type of thing in the listed group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 高い modifies もの, and も links it in parallel with the cheap-things group above.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate showing that the things exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.why: The place where things exist is stated with には. Then the two noun phrases are listed in parallel with も〜も. The adjectives come before もの to modify each type of thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence only joins two nouns with the meaning 'and'; it does not create the meaning 'both'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If だけ is used, the sentence limits the range and means 'there are only cheap things' or 'there are only expensive things'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that も must be repeated after each item in the listing pattern も〜も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vi: What kind of house is it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな comes before 家 to ask about the characteristics or type of the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ですか turns the noun phrase into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q15.kobun.why: どんな must come directly before the noun whose characteristics are being asked about. ですか comes at the end to form a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If どう is used, the sentence asks about the condition or evaluation of something. It does not directly modify 家 like どんな.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 何の is used, the sentence asks what type or purpose the house has, not its general characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use どうな家, but the correct form for modifying a noun is どんな家.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object whose singing ability is evaluated as good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: じょうずです is the adjective predicate な, expressing ability or skill level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q16.kobun.why: With ability words such as じょうず, the object being evaluated usually takes が. Therefore, 歌がじょうずです means being good at singing or singing well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 歌を歌う is used, 歌 is the object of the verb 歌う, referring to the action of singing a specific song.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 歌が好きです is used, the sentence only expresses a liking for songs, not the ability to sing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with じょうず, but the ability pattern usually uses が to mark the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 帰る changes to the て form to connect with きてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: きて combines with 帰って to express an action of returning toward the speaker or a reference place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: てください comes after a verb in the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q17.kobun.why: はやく modifies the action 帰ってきて, while 帰ってきてください asks the listener to return. Two verbs in the て form are connected, and then ください adds a polite requesting tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If きて is omitted, the sentence simply means 'please return' and does not emphasize returning toward the speaker or the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means that the speaker will return; it is not a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit きて and use only 帰ってください, losing the nuance of returning toward the speaker or the specified place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: 急ぐ changes to the て form to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: てください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q18.kobun.why: 急いで is the て form of 急ぐ. It comes before ください to make a request. Because the sentence does not state an object or place, the listener understands from the situation that they need to hurry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 急ぎます, the sentence means 'I will hurry' or 'I will go quickly', so it is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is a softer and more polite request. It asks whether the listener could hurry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form 急ぐください; before ください, a verb in the て form must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.sk: Time は + N が + Aい + です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks today as the topic or time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the characteristic of being strong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 強い is an adjective ending in い that acts as a predicate and adds a state to かぜ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: です makes the adjective sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.why: きょうは states the time range, while かぜが is the subject being described. The adjective 強い comes after the subject to describe the wind and ends with です to keep a polite style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used after かぜ, the wind becomes a contrastive topic, which may suggest that other factors are not the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern describes the wind becoming strong, emphasizing a change rather than only its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use きょうが when they want to say 'today'. In this sentence, きょうは is the time topic, while が goes with かぜ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: I look for the program I want to watch in the newspaper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the means or source used to find information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause みたい comes before 番組 to modify which program.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The whole phrase みたい番組 acts as the object, so it takes the particle を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: さがします is the main predicate in the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: The clause みたい comes before 番組 according to Japanese modifier order. The whole phrase is the object being searched for, so を comes after 番組.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Writing 見たい in kanji does not change the sentence structure or nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: When you see a clause before a noun, understand it as a description of that noun. Do not translate it in Vietnamese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: ちょっと modifies the degree of the action 教えて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 教える changes to the て form to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q20.kobun.why: ちょっと is placed at the beginning to soften the request. 教えてください is a structure for asking the listener to tell or explain something, although the object may be omitted when it is clear from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks whether the listener can tell the speaker, so it sounds tentative and softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is a direct command and is much stronger than a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q20.kobun.tip: Do not translate ちょっと mechanically as a small amount. Here, it also helps soften the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before ビル to identify the building being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks ビル as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 近くに indicates the location where the building exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is an existence predicate used for objects and places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.why: その ビル is made the topic, then 近くに states the location and あります expresses the building’s existence at that location. に marks the place of existence, not the object receiving an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If we say 近いです, the sentence only states that the building is near; it does not use an existence structure to identify its location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: へ with 行きます only indicates movement toward a nearby place; it does not express that the building is there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with あります; locations of existence usually go with に, while で mainly marks a place where an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the sky as the thing being seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: きれいに is the adverb form of the adjective な, modifying 見えます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 見えます expresses the ability or natural state of being visible, not the intentional action of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q22.kobun.why: 空が is the thing perceived by the eyes, きれいに describes the sky’s appearance, and 見えます expresses how it appears in one’s field of vision. The adjective な changes to the に form when modifying a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If we use を見ます, the subject is the person actively looking at the sky, unlike the state in which the sky naturally appears before one’s eyes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only states that the sky is beautiful; it does not emphasize how it looks or is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use きれいく; the adjective な must use きれいに when modifying a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q23.kobun.vi: I played tennis with my older brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person participating in the same action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q23.kobun.why: The person acting together comes before と, the activity comes before を, and the verb しました comes at the end of the sentence. This structure describes an action completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If we replace it with と一緒に, the meaning is still “with,” but it emphasizes doing the action together more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse と in this pattern with を, but と indicates the person participating together, while を marks the activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that is running toward us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action はしる with the verb 来る that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: きました expresses movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q24.kobun.why: が states the subject of the consecutive actions. はしって connects to きました through the て form, creating the meaning of running while approaching or running toward us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If we replace it with はしっていきました, the direction of movement is away from the speaker or reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate and use 来る and 行く only with the meanings “come” and “go,” forgetting to consider the direction of movement in relation to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q24.kobun.cn: Vて + くる/きます/きました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.vi: There is old bread in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 古い comes before a noun to modify パン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that is in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 入って is the て form of 入る, connecting with います to express a resulting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the 入っている pattern and expresses the object’s current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.why: The place of existence comes before に, the noun is described by the adjective 古い, and then が marks the existing object. 入っている expresses the state of the bread being inside the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If we replace に with で, the sentence describes an action occurring in the refrigerator, not the existence of the bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If we replace が with は, the sentence makes the bread the topic and creates a contrastive or emphatic nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for every meaning of “be,” but the existence of an object usually uses the location particle に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object that was dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action おとす with the pattern てしまう that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: てしまいました expresses an action that has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or against one’s intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: 財布 is the object affected by おとす, so it goes with を. The て form connects the verb with しまう, highlighting that the action happened accidentally and that the speaker regrets it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence only reports that the wallet was dropped; it does not emphasize the accidental or regretful feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means intentionally dropping something or placing it there in advance, so it does not fit the usual context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Do not connect しまう directly with the dictionary-form verb; use the て form before しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう/しまいます/しまった/しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I visited my friend’s house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.sk: Time + N の + N を + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression comes at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the owner with the noun いえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the place or object being visited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 訪ねる changes to the polite past form 訪ねました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: きのう is placed at the beginning to state the time, then の creates the phrase “your friend’s house.” The house is the object of 訪ねる, so it takes を, while the verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes going to your friend’s house, while 訪ねました emphasizes the act of visiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: 訪ねる in this sentence means “visit” and uses を, not に as when simply saying that someone goes to a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: During the summer vacation, I traveled to Kyushu.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object referred to in the travel action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 旅行する changes to the polite past form 旅行しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, followed by the place or object of the action, and then the predicate comes at the end of the sentence. を marks the place traveled to in the expression 旅行する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If we replace it with へ行く, the sentence emphasizes going to Kyushu and does not directly emphasize the travel activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of を before 旅行する, but this pattern usually uses Nを旅行する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun しごと with 計画, creating the meaning “a plan about work.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the plan as the object being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb たてる changes to the polite past form たてました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: の turns しごと into a modifier for 計画. The phrase 計画を is the object of たてました, forming the common combination Nを立てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This form emphasizes a plan related to the topic of work. It is clearer but longer than 仕事の計画.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の between the two nouns, but Japanese needs の to connect 仕事 and 計画.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: I was injured in an accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that made the speaker get injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks けが as the event affected by しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase けがをする changes to the polite past form けがをしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: で gives the cause before the result. けがをする is a fixed expression in which けが is marked by を and する is the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 事故にあう means having an accident; it does not directly say that someone was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から for every cause, but で is usually used to state the direct cause of an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose feelings or interests are being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that is liked in the pattern 好きだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: だいすきです is the adjective predicate な, expressing the degree of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: わたしは puts the topic at the beginning of the sentence, while 漫画が is the object of the feeling 好き. With 好き and 大好き, the object usually goes with が instead of を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 漫画を読む means reading manga. It describes an action, not a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say 漫画を大好きです, but with 好き・大好き, they must use 漫画が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: On Sunday, I went to see a movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the speaker went to see a movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 映画 as the object of the action of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に follows the linking form み to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: いきました is the main predicate, the polite past form of いく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The time comes first, followed by the object of the action of watching. The form み＋に＋いく shows that the purpose of going was to watch a movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 映画を見ました only means that the speaker watched a movie. It does not emphasize going somewhere to watch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use みに行く as a dictionary-form verb, but み is the form with ます removed from 見ます before に行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.vi: I will welcome the New Year with my family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the person who performs the action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: いっしょに adds the manner of doing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks お正月 as the object being welcomed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: むかえます is the polite form of the verb meaning welcome. It comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.why: The phrase showing the person involved and the manner comes before the object. お正月を is the direct object of むかえます, so を is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 祝います changes the meaning from welcoming the New Year to holding or celebrating the New Year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q1.kobun.tip: と in 家族と means together with, not the particle marking the direct object of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object that the speaker is interested in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: In the pattern 興味がある, 興味 is the subject described as existing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses the existence of interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q10.kobun.why: The pattern 興味がある uses に to state the area or object of interest, and が to mark 興味. あります completes the predicate with the meaning “be interested.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 関心がある still means being interested, but the tone is more formal and focuses more on attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put を after テニス, but the fixed pattern is Nに興味がある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q11.kobun.vi: I will transport the luggage to the new home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the item being transported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 運びます is the predicate and describes carrying or moving something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q11.kobun.why: The item being transported comes before を, while the destination comes before へ. The verb 運びます comes at the end to complete the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に can still indicate the destination, but へ emphasizes the direction of movement more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particles を or へ because Vietnamese does not clearly mark objects and destinations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.vi: My grandmother lives at her parents’ home in the countryside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 田舎 with 実家, creating the meaning “parents’ home in the countryside.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates where the grandmother lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 住んで connects the verb 住む with います in the pattern ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 住んでいます describes the state of living somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.why: The topic is stated with は, the place of residence goes with に, and の links 田舎 and 実家. 住んでいます describes an ongoing state of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern usually describes an ongoing state, unlike Vます, which only describes an action or a general habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: 住みます only indicates that someone will or plans to live somewhere. It does not emphasize the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ています as only meaning “be doing,” but with 住む, it usually means “be living or residing in.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.vi: I pressed the brake to stop the car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the part affected by the pressing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects pressing the brake with stopping the car in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the vehicle being stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: とめました is the main predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.why: 踏んで links two successive actions: pressing the brake first and then stopping the car. Each verb has its own object, so ブレーキ and 車 both go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 踏んでから is used, the sentence emphasizes more clearly that the brake must be pressed before the car is stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 踏んだので is used, the sentence changes to a cause-and-effect relationship: the car stopped because the brake was pressed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で to connect two verbs, but connecting successive actions here requires the form て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.vi: I received an anesthetic injection at the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.sk: N place に ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ますい with 注射 to modify it, while を marks the object of うけました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 受ける in the polite past form means that someone received or had something done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first, followed by the object received, and then the verb at the end. 受ける uses を with an action or service received by the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, it means that the subject performed the injection themselves, without emphasizing that they received one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is replaced with へ, the sentence only indicates the direction toward the hospital, not the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で when talking about where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.vi: She goes to piano class every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ N に ＋ Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that she is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎日 modifies the action and shows how often she goes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に only indicates the destination, while 通っています describes going there regularly and continuing to maintain that routine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the frequency adverb comes before the place, and the predicate ends the sentence. 通う shows that someone goes back and forth regularly, so it is used with ている to describe a continuing habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning focuses more on going to or having gone to the class, without emphasizing regular travel as 通っています does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is replaced with へ, the focus is more on the direction toward the class than on the destination of a regular activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 通っています as meaning that someone is going right now, while this pattern usually refers to going regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.vi: Please do not run in the hallway.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place through which the speaker asks someone not to run.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ないで combines with ください to form a polite request meaning “please do not do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: ください completes the polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.why: を attaches to the area where the movement takes place, while ないでください comes at the end to ask the listener not to perform that action. The verb changes to ない before connecting with でください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning is stronger and expresses a rule or prohibition, rather than just a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is written in kanji, the meaning and structure do not change; only the way the verb is written is different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ないでください with ないください; で is required between ない and ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q17.kobun.vi: The mirror in the restroom broke.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects おてあらい with 鏡, while が marks the mirror as the subject undergoing the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 割れる is an intransitive verb. Its polite past form shows that the mirror has entered a broken state by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q17.kobun.why: The possessive phrase おてあらいの鏡 makes clear which mirror is meant, and then が marks the thing undergoing the change. 割れる is an intransitive verb, so it does not need the object marker を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, it means that someone broke the mirror, so the person who performed the action is clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is replaced with は, the mirror becomes the topic, and the sentence may contrast it with something else or provide information about it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with 割れる, but this intransitive verb usually uses が to mark the thing that changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q18.kobun.vi: My father is a taxi driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents my father as the topic whose occupation is being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects タクシー with 運転手 to express “the driver of the taxi,” while です ends the polite noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q18.kobun.why: The pattern は＋noun＋です is used to introduce or identify an occupation or status. の connects the noun タクシー with the noun referring to a person, 運転手.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, it means that my father drives a taxi. It describes an action rather than stating his occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is replaced with が, the focus shifts to the fact that my father is the person whose job is driving a taxi.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の between タクシー and 運転手, but the two nouns need の to connect their modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.vi: I teach my daughter how to clean.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.sk: N recipient に ＋ N の N を ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person receiving the teaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns そうじ into a modifier for 仕方, while を marks the content being taught.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 教えます is the predicate. It takes the person being taught with に and the content being taught with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.why: With 教える, the person being taught comes first with に, while what is taught comes first with を. の connects そうじ and 仕方 to create a noun meaning how to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the daughter becomes the learner, and the sentence emphasizes that she learns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If 仕方 is omitted, the sentence only says that cleaning is taught in general, without specifying how to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を for the person being taught, but 教える uses に for the recipient and を for the content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.vi: Before cooking, I prepared the ingredients in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb つくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies 前, creating the meaning “before cooking.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates a point in time, while 前に connects it to the clause that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the ingredients as the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 用意する changes to the て form to connect with おく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ておく describes doing something in advance to prepare for another action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.why: The clause つくる 前に states when the preparation is done. The object of 用意する comes before を, and then the て form connects with おく to express prior preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning becomes “after cooking” instead of “before cooking.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If ておきました is replaced with ています, the sentence only describes an action in progress or a present state, without emphasizing that it was done in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that 前に goes with a dictionary-form verb and does not directly use the た form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ 前に; Vて ＋ おく
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q20.kobun.vi: He is not interested in politics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: には marks the object of interest or lack of interest, while also creating a contrastive emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: です politely ends a noun sentence or an adjective ending in な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q20.kobun.why: かれは is the topic, while 政治には is the object judged to be むかんしん. The particle には combines に with は to indicate the object and emphasize the contrastive scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the meaning is that he is interested in politics, which is more positive than むかんしんです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に like に興味がある and forget that むかんしん also commonly goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.vi: I asked the person at the reception desk to pass on a message.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 受付 with 人 to modify the person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the recipient of the request or the person affected by the action 頼む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content or task that is requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: たのみました is the polite past form of 頼む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.why: 受付の人 identifies the person being discussed, に marks the recipient of the request, and 伝言を is the content of the request. The verb 頼む comes at the end of the sentence and uses the polite past form to express a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the meaning is that I directly delivered the message to that person, without the sense of asking someone for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake に for a place; in the pattern Nに頼む, に indicates the person being asked for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.vi: Before leaving home, I reserved a table at the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place that is left in the phrase 家を出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: でる in the dictionary form comes before 前に to create a time clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 前に indicates the point in time before which the following action must occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the action 予約する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of 予約する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.why: 家をでる前に creates a time clause before the main action. In the main clause, レストランを is the object reserved in advance, while しました shows that the reservation has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the reservation takes place after leaving home, which is the opposite of 前に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may change 出る to the past form before 前に, but this pattern uses the dictionary form: Vる前に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.vi: Next year, my daughter will attend the coming-of-age ceremony.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.sk: N time ＋ N は ＋ N を ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: A time phrase at the beginning of a sentence identifies when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the person who will carry out or experience the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the event that the subject will 迎える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 迎えます is the polite present form, used for an event expected to happen in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.why: らいねん sets the time, むすめは is the topic, and 成人式を is the event being welcomed. 迎えます uses the polite form to talk about an event that will happen in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes attending the coming-of-age ceremony, focusing on participation rather than welcoming the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate 迎える as meaning only “welcome” a person, but this verb is also used with times or events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.vi: I will submit the report by the 10th of next month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.sk: N の ＋ Date までに ＋ N を ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects next month with the 10th to identify which month the date belongs to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed, or no later than that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being submitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: だします is the polite form of 出す and describes an action that is planned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.why: らいげつの10日までに identifies the deadline, then レポートを is the object and だします is the action that must be completed. までに differs from まで because it emphasizes completing the action by the deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is that it continues until the 10th, without necessarily emphasizing completion before the deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit に after まで, but までに is what expresses the deadline for an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q24.kobun.cn: N ＋ までに／V辞書形 ＋ までに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.vi: It is dangerous, so please do not touch that machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: ですから connects the reason given first with the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that is touched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: Vないでください is a polite request not to do an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.why: あぶないですから gives the reason first, and the main request appears at the end of the sentence. そのきかいを is the object that must not be touched, while 触らないでください expresses a polite request not to perform that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a stronger rule or prohibition, not just a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 触らなくてください, but the correct pattern for saying “please do not do it” is Vないでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q25.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: たくさんの modifies the noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the people who carried out the action of gathering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 集まって connects with くる and describes gathering toward the speaker or the mentioned point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q3.kobun.why: たくさんの 人が form a subject referring to a large number of people. The て form connects 集まる with くる, so the sentence describes not only gathering but also coming toward the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 集まります is used, the sentence only says that people gathered, without emphasizing movement toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 集まっていきました is used, the gathering is viewed as moving away from the speaker or forward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate てくる as only “come,” but this pattern can also describe a change or an action moving toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q4.kobun.vi: My student days are very nostalgic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 学生時代 is a compound noun referring to a period, and が marks the period being remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective なつかしい acts as the predicate and expresses nostalgia about the subject before が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q4.kobun.why: The phrase 学生時代 is used as one noun and acts as the subject of the feeling. The adjective なつかしい stands at the end of the sentence to give an opinion and express nostalgia.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 恋しい, the sentence focuses more on missing and wanting to see a person or place again, rather than only nostalgia.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand なつかしい as meaning “old,” but this word mainly expresses nostalgia and memories.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q5.kobun.vi: I will deliver the goods by truck.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means used to deliver the goods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the goods as the object being delivered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 届けます is the predicate and describes bringing goods to a place or recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q5.kobun.why: で follows the means of transport, while を follows the item being transported. The predicate 届けます ends the sentence and expresses the act of delivery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 送ります is used, the focus is on sending; 届けます emphasizes bringing the goods to a place or recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse で and に: で indicates the means of transport, while に usually indicates a place or recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q6.kobun.vi: The production of the new product is delayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 新商品 with 生産, forming the phrase “production of the new product.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the production activity as the subject that is delayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes a continuing state of delay.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q6.kobun.why: の turns 新商品 into a modifier for 生産. The whole phrase 生産が acts as the subject, while 遅れています shows that the delay is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 生産 is replaced with 製造, the meaning focuses more on the process of making a specific product, while 生産 is broader.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の between the two nouns, making the relationship “production of the new product” unclear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.vi: I read the passage while underlining it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the line drawn while performing the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 引く changes to the verb stem 引き and connects with ながら to show two actions happening at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the passage as the object of よみます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: よみます is the main action; the action 引きながら happens at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.why: The clause 引きながら states the supporting action that happens at the same time as the main action よみます. Each verb has its own object before を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ながら is replaced with the て form, the sentence usually describes actions happening one after another rather than at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence lists typical actions and does not necessarily say that they happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may divide 引く into 引いてながら, but ながら must connect with the verb stem in the ます form, which is 引き.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q7.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 ＋ ながら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.vi: Yesterday, a fire occurred near this area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の 場所で ＋ N が ＋ ある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the time when the event occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks an event that exists or occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: ありました is the polite past form of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.why: The place with で comes before the event, while the event that occurs is marked by が. あります in the past describes an event that happened or existed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence focuses on the existence of an object at that place, without emphasizing that an event occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for every location, but an event occurring at a place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.vi: Many people go to watch the festival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in its basic form comes before 人 to modify 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the state 多い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い is the predicate and expresses a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.why: The phrase おまつりの見物 indicates the activity being directed toward, so it is used with に before いく. The clause いく modifies 人, and then 人が is the subject of 多い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, 見物 becomes the object of する and requires を, not に as in the structure meaning “go to watch.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に in 見物に行く with を; に here indicates purpose, not an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.vi: My school holds a sports festival every October.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Frequency の + Time に + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち to the following noun and shows possession or a range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes “school” the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects a frequency phrase with the time point of October がつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates when the event is held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the sports festival as the event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: 行います is the polite form of the verb 行う and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.why: The sentence moves from the subject to the time, then to the object and the action: school, every year in October, sports festival, hold. を identifies the event affected by 行います, while に identifies the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is omitted, the time phrase is more natural and concise: simply “every October.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に with を in a time phrase; a time point uses に, while the event being held uses を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.vi: My house is far from the station, so it is very inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the house as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point or reference point used to measure distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects a cause to its result and places the cause clause first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a polite sentence; 不便 is an な adjective used as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.why: えきから provides the reference point for saying that the house is far away, and then ので connects the cause “far from the station” with the result “inconvenient.” Because 不便 is an な adjective, 不便です is used when it functions as a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, the sentence means “although it is far from the station...” instead of showing a cause-and-result relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect the な adjective to ので with 不便ので; 不便なので must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.vi: There are many unusual animals at this zoo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.sk: この + N には + Aい + N が + Quantity + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun どうぶつえん immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place of existence, while は emphasizes that place as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the animals as the beings that exist in the zoo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies the quantity of animals that exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: います is used for the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.why: The pattern にいます places the location first, then states the existing subject with が and ends with います. 珍しい comes before どうぶつ to limit the type of animals being discussed, while たくさん adds the quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If います is replaced with あります, the sentence is unsuitable because animals are living things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If どうぶつは is used, the focus shifts to the animals, and the introductory sense of stating their existence becomes less natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use あります for every meaning of “there is/are”; for people and animals, います must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q13.kobun.vi: I will prepare an ashtray at the smoking area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に indicates the place where an object is put or prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q13.kobun.why: The place where the object is put comes first, followed by the object with を, and then the verb 用意します at the end of the sentence. に emphasizes the place where the object is prepared or put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the meaning focuses on the place where the preparation action takes place, not on where the ashtray is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で to mean “at,” but for the place where an object is put or brought, に is usually used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q14.kobun.vi: I put the bag on the shelf over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the object being placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the destination where the bag is placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 置きました is the polite past form of 置く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q14.kobun.why: The object being placed goes with を, while the place receiving it goes with に. The verb 置きました comes last and shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence only indicates where the placing action takes place, not where the bag is placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q14.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に, which indicates the destination of the object, with で, which indicates the place where the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.vi: While taking a walk, I met someone from the neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The pattern Nのとき indicates the time when an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 近所の modifies 人 and indicates a person from the nearby area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: With 会う, に marks the person whom the subject meets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 会いました is the polite past form of 会う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence and is separated by a comma. 近所の comes before 人 to modify it, while 人に is the object of the meeting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If と会う is used, the meaning emphasizes that the two sides met each other or met together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q15.kobun.tip: With 会う, Vietnamese learners may easily use を because of their Vietnamese habits, but the person being met usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.vi: My older brother is doing work related to trade.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は presents the older brother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase 貿易関連の modifies しごと and shows the type of work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the work being done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する. It connects with います to create the structure for an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the Vている structure and shows an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by a noun phrase that describes the work. している describes work that is continuing or being done now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If に関する is used, the meaning is still “related to,” but the expression is more formal and complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out the particle の in the modifying phrase, but they need to say 貿易関連の仕事.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify an object near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は shows that the bookshelf is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies an adjective and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 丈夫 is an な adjective. When it is used as a predicate before です, it directly uses the 丈夫です form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q17.kobun.why: この modifies 本棚, は makes 本棚 the topic, and とても comes before the adjective to increase the degree. The な adjective used as a predicate connects directly with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If an adjective ending in い is used, the connection is different, for example 丈夫ではなく強いです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q17.kobun.tip: Do not add な before です. Say 丈夫です, not 丈夫なです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: まどの modifies ガラス and identifies the type of glass being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object as being in a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 割れました is the polite past form of the intransitive verb 割れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q18.kobun.why: まどの identifies ガラス, and then ガラスが makes it the grammatical subject of the intransitive verb. 割れました shows that the glass changed into a broken state by itself, without mentioning who caused it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If を割りました is used, it means that someone broke the glass and emphasizes the effect on the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with a broken object, but a sentence describing an object breaking by itself uses が with 割れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.kobun.vi: This machine is broken, so it does not work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the machine the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of 故障する connects the cause to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ません changes a verb into the polite negative form.
