default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は. Then the cause is connected with the て form, followed by the result. The polite negative form shows that the machine does not work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ので, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and softly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate て as and in every situation, but here it connects a cause to a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q19.tokens.5.m: does not run, does not work
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun phrase showing the time when a state occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 眠い changes the ending い to く before なる to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q2.kobun.why: じゅぎょうちゅう states the time, while 眠くなりました describes the change into a sleepy state. An adjective ending in い must change to the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that the speaker is sleepy and does not emphasize the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use 眠いなる directly. An adjective ending in い must change to 眠く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q20.kobun.vi: I went for a drive to change my mood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に comes after a noun to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に in ドライブに行く shows an activity done for the purpose of going for a drive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: いきました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q20.kobun.why: The purpose phrase comes before the verb 行く. The first に states the general purpose, while に in ドライブに行く connects the planned activity with 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used, the purpose is emphasized in a more formal way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に before the activity, but the Nに行く pattern needs に to show the purpose of going to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.vi: This cookie is shaped like a star.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes クッキー the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 星 with 形, while を marks the shape that the cookie has.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する. It connects with います to create a state of having something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: ています describes a present state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.why: The Nの形をしている structure describes an object as having a certain shape. 形を is the part affected by する, while している shows that this feature continues to exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence has a comparative nuance, meaning that it has a shape like a star.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q21.kobun.tip: Do not translate 形をする mechanically as make a shape. The whole phrase 形をしている means to have a shape.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.vi: I have recently been learning judo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん modifies the whole action and shows a time close to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 柔道 as the object being learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ならって is the て form of 習う. It connects with います to show an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ています shows that the learning started before now and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.why: The time adverb comes at the beginning of the sentence to identify the time. 柔道 is the object of 習う, while ならっています describes learning that is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to being about to start learning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that the speaker has learned judo before and does not confirm that they are learning it now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the simple present, but ています here emphasizes that the process is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q23.kobun.vi: The thief was arrested by the police.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 泥棒 the topic of the arrest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に identifies the person who performs the arrest in the passive structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: つかまりました is the polite past form of 捕まる. It describes the subject entering a state of being arrested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q23.kobun.why: The thief is made the topic, while the police are marked with に because they are the ones who made the arrest. The verb 捕まる itself describes the state of being arrested, so を is not needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the police will be the subject and 泥棒 will be the object being arrested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 捕まる. を goes with 捕まえる, while the person being arrested usually goes with は or が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks 春 as the subject of arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 訪れました is the polite past form of 訪れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q24.kobun.why: 春 is the subject undergoing the change meant by spring arriving, so が is used. The polite past verb shows that the event has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the focus shifts to the change into spring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q24.kobun.tip: 訪れる is not used only for people visiting; with seasons or periods, it also describes their arrival or appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q25.kobun.vi: After graduating, I became a civil servant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The て form connects the action of graduating with the change that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the new state or position after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, expressing an achieved result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q25.kobun.why: The clause そつぎょうして comes first to state the earlier action. With なる, the new state goes with に, followed by the past form of the verb, なりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If にします is used instead, the meaning changes to actively making someone or something become a civil servant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with なる, but the pattern for a new state is N に なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vi: Suzuki, my senior, always listens to me and gives me advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Suzuki the topic, and the part in parentheses explains this person's status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb modifies the action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the content or matter that the listener helps with in 相談に乗る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 乗る changes to the て form to connect with くれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: くれます shows that Suzuki's action benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.why: Suzuki is the topic, so は is used. 相談に乗る is a fixed expression, and the て form connects with くれる to show that Suzuki does this to help the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If あげます is used, the speaker is the person who helps someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse あげる and くれる; when another person does something beneficial for you, use くれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vi: There is no need to get angry over something trivial.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the cause or situation that leads to getting angry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The plain-form verb modifies 必要, creating the meaning “the need to get angry.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: は states that 必要 is the content being negated in the pattern 必要はありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません negates existence or necessity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.why: ことで states the cause, while 怒る comes before 必要 to modify this noun. The structure 必要はありません negates the need to perform that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: The basic meaning is similar, but が presents 必要 as the existing subject; は in the original sentence adds emphasis and contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means “must not get angry” or “do not get angry,” which is stronger than “there is no need.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q4.kobun.tip: Do not understand 必要はありません word for word as “there is no necessity”; the whole phrase means “there is no need to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.vi: I contact my parents by international telephone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means used for communication.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who participates in the communication relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb とります in the phrase 連絡を取る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: とります completes the fixed phrase 連絡を取る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.why: で states the means, と states the person participating in the communication relationship, and れんらくをとります is the main predicate. The additional parts come before the final verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If に連絡する is used, the sentence still means contacting one's parents, but it uses the verb 連絡する instead of the phrase 連絡を取る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を in 連絡を取る; it is the required object of とる in this phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.vi: I dyed my hair brown at a hair salon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object whose color is changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the result or new state that the hair is changed into.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する in the pattern NをNにする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.why: The place goes with で, the hair is the object marked by を, and 茶色に states the result of the change. NをNにする expresses that the subject actively makes something become a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence describes the hair becoming brown by itself, without emphasizing that the speaker actively caused the color change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is used when the result is an adjective ending in い; 茶色 is a color noun, so 茶色にしました must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q6.kobun.tip: With a noun for a color such as 茶色, use にする; do not change it to 茶色くする as with an adjective ending in い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.vi: My younger brother came back in the evening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the younger brother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase states when the younger brother came back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects 帰る with the verb 来る to create the meaning “come back.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 来る is in the polite past form and completes the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.why: は makes the subject the topic, while the time phrase comes before the predicate to identify when the event happened. 帰って＋来ました forms a verb sequence expressing a return toward the speaker or a reference location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that the person returned, without emphasizing the sense of returning as in 帰って来ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate 来ました alone as “came” and miss the combined meaning “come back” of 帰って来ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.vi: At the weekend, I clean my room thoroughly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the weekend is the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the room as the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: きれいに is the adverbial form and indicates the state that the room reaches after the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 片付けます is the verb 片付ける in the polite present form, expressing the action of cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.why: The object へやを comes before the resulting state きれいに and the verb. When the adjective な modifies a verb, it uses the form に, so きれい becomes きれいに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If きれいで is used, it usually connects to another clause or quality and does not directly indicate the resulting state of cleaning the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use きれいな before a verb; before a verb, the adjective な must change to the adverbial form きれいに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.vi: I put the puppy in a safe place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the puppy as the object being placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 安全な modifies ところ, forming the phrase “a safe place.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the puppy is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 置く is in the polite past form and shows that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.why: The verb 置く requires an object and a place, marked by を and に, respectively. 安全 is an adjective な, so な must be added when it comes before the noun ところ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 安全な is used instead of 安全に, the meaning becomes “safely,” and it does not directly modify the noun ところ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t31-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit な after the adjective な when it comes before a noun, but 安全なところ must be said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vi: When I turn 20, I will start living alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the age reached in the pattern 20歳になる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: なって is the て form of なる. It connects a point of change with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the way the activity is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.ch.3.vi: will live and carry out daily activities
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.why: The age combines with に and なる to express reaching that age. The て form connects this change with the action of living alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 20歳になったら, the sentence has a conditional meaning: once I turn 20, I will live alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use で to mark age in this pattern; the age reached is used with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q10.kobun.vi: I asked Satoshi the reason for being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に refers to the person who is asked or who provides information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ちこく with 理由 to create a phrase meaning the reason for being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the reason as the information being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きました is the polite past-tense predicate, showing that the asking already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q10.kobun.why: さとしくんに refers to the person being asked. ちこくの modifies 理由 to create the specific content being asked about, while 理由を is the object of 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に and を: に refers to the person being asked, while を refers to the information being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the way the action 騒ぐ is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns 騒ぐ into a noun, while は makes the whole action of making noise the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: です forms the polite predicate, commenting that making noise is annoying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.why: おおごえで adds the manner to 騒ぐ. 騒ぐの turns the action of making noise into a noun, and then は presents that action as the topic to be commented on with めいわくです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is replaced with ことは, the sentence still nominalizes the action, but the meaning is more general and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If のは is replaced with のが, the action of making noise becomes the subject or the object being evaluated. It is no longer presented as a contrasting topic like は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit の when they want to turn the verb 騒ぐ into a noun before は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q12.kobun.vi: I checked the goods that had just arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause とどいた modifies 品物, while を marks the goods as the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: しました is the polite past form of the verb する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q12.kobun.why: The clause とどいた comes before 品物 to identify which goods are meant. 品物 takes を because it is the object of the checking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If the clause とどいた is removed, the sentence only means checking the goods and does not specify that they have just arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often place the modifying clause after the noun, as in Vietnamese, but Japanese always places this clause before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q13.kobun.vi: I will take a break during work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 仕事の modifies 途中, creating a phrase that indicates a point in the middle of the work process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 休憩 as the object carried out with the verb 取ります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 取ります describes the action of taking or spending time on a break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q13.kobun.why: The phrase 仕事の途中 is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state when the action occurs. 休憩を取る is a fixed combination in which 休憩 is the object of 取る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 間 is used, it means throughout the period of work, while 途中 emphasizes the time when the work is still in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q13.kobun.tip: 休憩を取る should not be translated mechanically as taking rest time; the whole phrase means taking a break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.vi: Because it started to rain, I went back to the classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks 雨 as the subject of the phenomenon that begins to occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 降り出したので connects the cause with the result that follows; ので means because, so.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place toward which the action 戻る is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 戻りました is the main predicate and describes the completed action of going back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.why: The clause 雨がふりだしたので gives the cause first, followed by the result 戻りました. The verb 戻る is used with に to indicate the place of return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still means because, so, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, the sentence changes to a contrastive relationship instead of a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget な before ので when the previous clause is a noun or an な adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.vi: Our company has many female employees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with 会社, creating a noun phrase for the company belonging to our side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 会社 the topic being commented on in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 女性 modifies しゃいん, while が marks the group of employees as the subject whose quantity is large.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い is the い adjective used as the predicate to describe the number of employees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.why: うちの会社は limits the scope of the comment to our company. 女性社員が is the subject whose quantity is described, so it is used with 多い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used after 女性社員, the focus changes to female employees being numerous, instead of introducing the company as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 多い; an object whose quantity is large is usually used with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.vi: The man over there wearing a suit is my younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies the phrase referring to the person and indicates someone far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 背広 as the item worn in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects 着る with いる to create a structure showing the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: きている comes before 男 and modifies the man being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks 男 as the subject identified as the younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: です connects the noun おとうと with the subject and creates a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.why: The phrase 背広をきている comes before 男 to identify which man is meant. 男が is the subject of the sentence, while おとうとです is the comment about him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 着た is used, the sentence emphasizes having put the suit on or having finished putting it on, rather than the state of wearing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 背広をきている is removed, the sentence only says that the man over there is the younger brother and gives no identifying feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often place the descriptive phrase after the noun, but in Japanese the phrase 背広をきている must come before 男.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q16.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; V普通形 + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nを ＋ Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎晩 is a time adverb that shows when a repeated action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks えいご as the content being reviewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of 復習する, connecting the verb to います in the structure ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ています describes a state or habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.why: 毎晩 comes at the beginning to show frequency, while えいごを is the object of 復習する. The form ている shows that reviewing is maintained as a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 復習します is used, the sentence only states the action or plan to review. It does not emphasize a continuing habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If てから is added, the sentence means that the speaker reviews first and then goes to bed, emphasizing the order of the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q17.kobun.tip: The verb する must change to して before います. It cannot be connected directly as 復習するいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.vi: He is waiting at the station exit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the waiting takes place; の connects 駅 with 出口 to create the meaning “the station’s exit.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb まつ with います to form the progressive aspect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern Vている and describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は. Then the place uses で, followed by the verb in the て form connected to います. This order creates the pattern “who is doing what and where.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If にいる is used instead, the sentence emphasizes being present at a place, not the action of waiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with an action verb, but the place where an action such as waiting occurs must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.vi: I drank coffee at a coffee shop in front of the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の turns えきまえ into a modifier for the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the drinking takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the object and predicate, matching the order “where someone drinks what.” Particle で shows where the action happens, while を shows what is drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If にある is used, it only states that the coffee shop exists in a place. It does not describe drinking coffee there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show the place of the drinking action; に usually shows a place of existence or a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vi: I sent a telegram to my parents in my hometown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase の modifies the noun りょうしん and identifies which parents are meant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に shows the receiver of the sending action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the item being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: おくりました is the polite past form of おくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.why: The phrase ふるさとの modifies りょうしん before the receiver is mentioned. In the sending pattern, the receiver goes with に, and the item being sent goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に replaces へ, the sentence emphasizes the direction of sending rather than the receiver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q2.kobun.tip: Do not reverse を and に: the receiver is N に, while the item being sent is N を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.vi: I sometimes take a walk in that park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: 時々 is an adverb of frequency that modifies the action of taking a walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: あの modifies 公園 and identifies the park being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the place where the walk takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate of the sentence in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.why: An adverb of frequency often comes at the beginning of the sentence. The place uses で, and the action comes at the end. The subject “I” is omitted because it can be understood from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 公園に行きます is used instead, it means going to the park, without saying that the speaker will take a walk there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q20.kobun.tip: あの comes before a noun to modify it. It does not come after the noun as it commonly does in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.vi: Competition with other companies is very fierce.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: ほかの modifies 会社 and creates the phrase “other companies.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: との shows the opposing party or competitors and connects this phrase with 競争.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject described as はげしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い serves as the predicate and ends with the polite form です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.why: The phrase showing the competing side comes before the noun 競争. The whole phrase then becomes the subject with が. The adjective はげしい comes at the end to describe the competition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence changes to the topic “as for competition with...,” creating a more contrasting or general meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q21.kobun.tip: との does not show possession like の; it only shows a relationship “with/between” the parties.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.vi: She is good at both math and English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose ability is being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects 数学 and 英語 as two items placed side by side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 両方とも emphasizes that both objects just mentioned have the same quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: じょうずです is the な adjective predicate that evaluates the ability of かのじょ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.why: The two subjects are joined by と. Then 両方とも covers both objects. This phrase comes before the predicate to say that the same quality applies to both.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 数学も英語も is used, it also means “both math and English,” but it emphasizes each subject by repeating も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.tip: Do not translate と as “with” in this sentence; と joins two equal nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q22.kobun.cn: N と N ＋ 両方とも
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.vi: Yesterday I held a celebration party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう shows when the party was held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects お祝い with パーティー and shows the type or purpose of the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the party as the object being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ひらきました is the polite past predicate and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.why: The time expression comes first. The phrase お祝いの modifies パーティー, and then the object パーティーを comes before the verb. This order makes “when and what kind of party was held” clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If お祝いをしました is used instead, it means celebrating or holding a celebration, without directly emphasizing the organization of a party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q23.kobun.tip: の connects nouns to modify them; it should not always be translated mechanically as “of.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.vi: I went to my friend’s house, but my friend was not home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 友だち with 家 to create a possessive noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two clauses with opposite meanings: the person went there, but the house was empty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: でした makes 留守 a polite past noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.why: The phrase 友だちの家 shows the location, while に marks the destination of いきました. が connects the expected result with the opposite reality, which is 留守でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with でも, the sentence must be reorganized because でも usually connects two independent sentences with the meaning “but”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 家, but when saying that someone goes to a place, they need to use に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の changes 技術 into a modifier for the noun しんぽ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents しんぽ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 早い is the adjective い used as the predicate, and it keeps the ending い before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q25.kobun.why: The pattern NのN creates the relationship “the progress of technology.” は makes the main noun しんぽ the topic, and then the adjective 早い describes it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 技術が進歩する is used, the meaning changes to “technology progresses,” focusing on the action of changing rather than the speed of progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put an adjective before a noun because of Vietnamese habits, but here 早い is the predicate after the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.vi: I would like to stop by tomorrow. I wonder if it would be convenient for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence to state when the action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: たい expresses a wish, while が gently leads to the following question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes ご都合 the topic being asked about; ご is a polite prefix.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: いかがですか is a polite way to ask about a situation or convenience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.why: The time is stated first, followed by the wish to visit. が makes the opening softer, and then ご都合は いかがですか politely asks whether it is convenient for the other person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If いかがですか is replaced with どうですか, the basic meaning stays the same, but the level of politeness is lower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q3.kobun.tip: たいですが does not necessarily express a strong contrast here; が is often used to begin a polite statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: からの creates a modifier phrase for せつめい, showing the source or person giving the explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the explanation as the topic being concluded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 以上です is placed at the end to show that the explanation is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q4.kobun.why: The phrase からの comes before a noun to identify the source of the explanation. After the topic, 以上です serves as the predicate and concludes that the explanation is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with までです, the sentence emphasizes the range or endpoint, while 以上です is usually used to close an explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q4.kobun.tip: 以上 in 以上です means that the speaking part has ended, not simply “above” or “more than.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka writes in his diary every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person being talked about in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: A frequency expression that adds the repeated time of the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the thing Tanaka writes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: かいて is the て form of 書く. It connects the main verb to います to create ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ています describes an action that is continuing or a habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.why: は states the subject, 毎日 shows the frequency, and を marks the diary as the object of writing. かいています combines the て form with います to express an action that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If かいています is replaced with かきました, it only says that the writing was completed once and does not emphasize a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q5.kobun.tip: ている does not always mean “currently”; with 毎日, it usually describes a repeated habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.vi: I am looking for a job related to education.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the phrase 教育関係 to the noun しごと that follows, modifying the job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the job as the object of the search.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb さがす to います to create the expression for an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern for expressing an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.why: わたしは places the topic first, followed by the phrase 教育関係の that modifies しごと. しごとを is the object of さがす, while さがして います expresses an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget の when they want to connect one noun to a following noun as a modifier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: いい comes before a noun to modify 習慣.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the habits as the object of forming or learning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: みにつけます is the main predicate. It describes making something part of one’s skills or habits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q7.kobun.why: いい comes directly before 習慣 to describe the type of habit. The phrase 習慣を is the object, and the verb みにつけます describes the action affecting that object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of を, but here 習慣 is the object being developed, so を must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q8.kobun.vi: My husband is a kind person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 夫 the topic in order to introduce this person’s characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: やさしい comes before 人 to modify a noun referring to a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the noun phrase やさしい人 to the topic in an introduction or statement structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q8.kobun.why: 夫は is the topic being introduced. やさしい modifies 人, forming the phrase やさしい人, and then です completes the statement about the husband.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put an adjective after a noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese places やさしい before 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.vi: My mother is cooking in the kitchen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the mother is the topic of the action being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the cooking action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food as the object being made or cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects つくる with います to show an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern for expressing a state of currently doing an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.why: 母は identifies the performer, 台所で identifies where the action takes place, while りょうりを is the object of つくる. The form つくって います shows that cooking is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t32-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for a place, but the place where an action takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks かれ as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the specific body part that has the feature ほそながい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ほそながい is the adjective い used as the predicate to describe 指.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q1.kobun.why: は limits the comment to かれ, while が marks the body part described as 指. The adjective ほそながい comes at the end to conclude the feature of the fingers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to 指は細長いです, the fingers become the topic, while the current expression emphasizes that he has fingers like this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after かれ to express “he has,” but the structure for describing a body part usually uses は...が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.vi: My father is doing dangerous work at a construction site.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that father is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 危険な modifies しごと; な is the connecting form of the adjective な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the work being done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: して is the て form of する, connected to います to create a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ています shows that the action is continuing in the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.why: で identifies the workplace, while 危険な comes directly before 仕事 to modify the work. 仕事をしている describes doing that work at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If にいます is used, the sentence only says that father is at the construction site; it does not describe the action of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If the adjective is the い type, it connects directly to the noun, without adding な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な after the adjective な before a noun, or use に instead of で when talking about where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q10.kobun.cn: Aな + N; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q11.kobun.vi: The chemical industry is developing in City A.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that City A is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the chemical industry as the subject that has the feature of developing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ています creates a predicate that describes a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q11.kobun.why: The sentence puts the topic first with は, then uses が to identify the thing that has the developing state. The predicate comes at the end, following Japanese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of が in the middle, the nuance shifts toward presenting the chemical industry as a topic for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with verbs that describe a state, but here the thing that has the state usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きょう to the noun that follows and modifies the homework.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the homework is the topic being defined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the noun 作文 with the topic to create a polite judgment sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q12.kobun.why: きょうの modifies しゅくだい, and then は makes this noun phrase the topic. The noun 作文 comes before です to state the content or type of the homework.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence changes from defining the homework to saying that some homework exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q12.kobun.tip: Do not translate の mechanically as “of”; here it identifies the homework as belonging to today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.vi: I convey my feelings of gratitude to the other person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かんしゃ with きもち to create the phrase “feelings of gratitude.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the feelings as the content being conveyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に identifies the receiver of the content being conveyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 伝えます acts as the predicate and takes the object with を and the receiver with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.why: の creates the noun phrase “feelings of gratitude.” The structure を + に distinguishes the content being conveyed from the receiver, while the verb comes at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is directly thanking the other person, without emphasizing the act of conveying a feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily reverse に and を; remember that the content goes with を, and the receiver goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q13.tokens.4.m: the other person, person opposite you
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q14.kobun.vi: I sent invitation cards to the participants.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に identifies the receiver of the item being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 招待状 as the item being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: おくりました is the polite past form of the verb “send.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q14.kobun.why: The sentence places the receiver first, the item being sent next, and then ends with the verb. に and を mark the receiver and the object of the action, respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used instead of に, the focus shifts more toward sending something to the participants.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the invitation card; the item being sent must go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.vi: I have been married to my wife for 10 years.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: と identifies the person who takes part in the action of getting married.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of getting married with the state that continues afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に identifies the time point reached in the pattern that expresses how long something has become.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました describes reaching the ten-year point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.why: と identifies the person who took part in getting married, while て connects getting married with the result in duration. The phrase 10ねんに なりました expresses that the time reached ten years.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says whom the person married; it does not state how long the marriage has lasted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q15.kobun.tip: The pattern Nに なりました here expresses reaching a point in time, not “becoming 10 years” in the sense of an object changing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.vi: Deep in the forest, there is a mountain cabin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 森 with おく to identify the inside part of the forest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the mountain cabin exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the place mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is used for the existence of objects or places without life.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.why: の creates the place phrase “inside the forest,” and then に states where something exists. In the pattern あります, the existing thing usually goes with が and comes before the verb at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used for やまごや, the sentence emphasizes the already known mountain cabin instead of introducing its existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing あります with います is appropriate only when the existing subject is a person or animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は in a sentence introducing existence, but new information such as やまごや usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.vi: Sato is better at swimming than tennis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the topic being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 水泳 and 方, forming the selected object in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ほうが marks the side judged to be better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: とくいです is the predicate that states ability or a strong point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.why: The sentence puts the standard of comparison first with より, then puts the stronger object with のほうが. The adjective な とくい comes at the end to conclude the statement about ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If より is replaced with と比べて, the comparison keeps the same meaning, but the expression becomes fuller and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often forget の before ほうが when saying which object is better or more skilled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.vi: Everyone will make a plan for next year together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: で refers to the people who participate in carrying out the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects らいねん with the noun 計画, forming a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the plan as the object being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: たてます is the polite predicate that expresses the action of making a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.why: The phrase referring to the people doing the action comes first, followed by the noun phrase らいねんの計画 as the object. を connects the object to the verb たてます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nについて is used, the sentence talks about the topic of the plan, not about making a plan for N.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で when many people carry out an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.vi: Because I did something wrong, I will apologize properly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: 悪い modifies こと, forming a phrase meaning the wrong thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks こと as the object of した.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the cause clause to the action that will follow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ちゃんと modifies 謝ります and shows how to apologize.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: 謝ります is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.why: The cause clause したから comes before the main action and ends with a comma. ちゃんと comes directly before 謝ります to modify how the action is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the sentence still states a cause, but the tone becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with のに, the sentence changes to a contrast and is no longer a direct cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often put the adverb ちゃんと at the beginning of the sentence, making its connection to 謝ります less clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vi: I explained the company rules to the part-time worker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects アルバイト with 人, forming a phrase referring to a part-time worker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who receives the explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 会社 with 規則, forming the phrase “the company’s rules.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: せつめいしました is the main verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.why: The two phrases の identify the part-time worker and the company’s rules, respectively. に refers to the person receiving the action, を refers to the content being explained, and the verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 教えました is used, the meaning is “teach or tell someone,” while せつめいしました emphasizes presenting and explaining something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に or を, but they need to clearly distinguish the person receiving the information from the content of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.vi: I am working part-time at a supermarket during the day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time period as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the work performed with the verb する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects して with います to form an expression for an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている and expresses the state of currently working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.why: The time is made the topic with は, and the workplace uses で. アルバイトをしています is the predicate phrase, in which て connects the verb with います to show continuation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If しています is replaced with します, the sentence only says that someone will work or usually works, without emphasizing that the action is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use に for the place in this sentence, but the place where an action happens must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.vi: I received a beautiful kimono from my grandmother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source or the person who gives something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: すてきな modifies 着物 and keeps the form な before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 着物 as the item received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいました is the predicate showing that the speaker received something from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.why: The source of the gift comes first with から, and the received item comes before the verb with を. The adjective な is placed directly before the noun to describe 着物.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, the sentence can still indicate the giver, but it emphasizes the person involved in the giving and receiving more than the source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If もらいました is replaced with あげました, the subject changes from the receiver to the giver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often confuse receiving and giving, so they should first identify whether the subject is the receiver before choosing もらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.vi: There is a geography class in the afternoon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the afternoon as the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 地理 with 授業 and shows the content of the class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the class as something that exists in the afternoon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate that indicates the existence of a thing or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to state the time, then uses の to identify the type of class. The thing that exists is じゅぎょう, so it goes with が before あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If the structure あります is replaced with Nを勉強します, the sentence says that someone studies geography, not that there is a geography class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use を with あります, but a thing that exists must go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.vi: I gave my daughter gloves as a Christmas present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に indicates the person who receives the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the purpose or role of the item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the item being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb あげる is in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.why: The recipient goes with に, the purpose of the gift also goes with に, and the gifted item goes with を. あげました is placed at the end of the sentence to complete the act of giving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with くれました, the meaning changes to another person giving something to the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with もらいました, the meaning changes to the speaker receiving gloves from their daughter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に, which marks the recipient, with を, which marks the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.vi: I took a boxed lunch and went flower-viewing with a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the item being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The て-form connects the action of taking the boxed lunch with the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indicates the person performing the action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb いく is in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.why: The first clause uses the て-form to connect carrying something with going. と indicates the companion, while に attaches to the activity 花見 to state the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 一緒に is used, the meaning of doing something together is emphasized more, but と is still the particle for the companion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 花見をしに, the purpose is expressed more clearly as going to view flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を after the person they go with, but a companion must go with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.vi: This store has everything from bedding to underwear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify 店.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: には both makes the store the topic and indicates the location of existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the starting point of the range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: まで indicates the ending point of the range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: なんでも refers to the things included in the range being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: あります expresses the existence of objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.why: には makes the location the topic of an existence sentence. The pair から〜まで creates a range from the starting point to the ending point, and then なんでも generalizes the objects within that range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If からだけ is used, the range is limited to the starting point, so it no longer means from the starting point to the ending point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with しかありません, the meaning becomes that there are only those things, with a limiting nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit まで when they want to use the full structure from 〜 to 〜.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vi: I repaired the bicycle using a tool.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item used in the action of つかって.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The て-form connects the action of using a tool with the action of repairing the bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the direct object of しゅうりしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: しゅうりしました is the main action in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.why: つかって connects the method with the main action, so 道具をつかって means “using a tool.” The bicycle is the object being repaired, so it goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 道具で is used, で directly marks the means, making the sentence shorter, while 道具をつかって emphasizes the action of using something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に to indicate a tool, but a tool usually goes with で or をつかって.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vi: When the water boils, I will put in the eggs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that reaches the state of boiling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ら attaches to the past form 沸いた to create the condition “when the water has boiled.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item put into the pot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いれます is the main action that occurs after the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.why: The 沸いたら clause gives the condition first, and then the main clause states the action いれます. が identifies hot water as the subject that boils, while を marks the eggs as the item put in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 沸くと is used, the meaning is closer to “whenever the water boils...,” expressing more of a rule or natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 沸いたあとで is used, it only states the order “after it boils” and does not emphasize a conditional relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use 沸くたら, but before ら in this pattern, the past form 沸いた must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q5.kobun.vi: I attended a lecture focused on the summer vacation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that the speaker attends or receives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q5.kobun.why: The time phrase comes before the object and the action. を connects the object with 受ける, while ました shows that the action has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit the particle を when talking about attending or receiving a lecture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vi: I went to a Shinto shrine for the first shrine visit of the year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.0.vi: go for the first shrine visit of the year
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the purpose or occasion of the shrine visit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.why: に attaches to the activity or purpose of the shrine visit, while へ attaches to the destination. いきました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, に directly indicates the destination, and the sentence does not emphasize the purpose of the shrine visit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is used with 神社, this particle emphasizes the place where the action takes place, not the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use で instead of へ when talking about a destination, but で usually indicates the place where an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q6.tokens.0.m: first shrine visit of the year
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.vi: My father bought me a cute doll.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the father is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: かわいい modifies 人形, while を marks the item bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The て-form connects the action of buying with the pattern くれる that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: くれました shows that another person does something beneficial for the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.why: The item bought comes before を, and then 買って connects to くれました. The Vてくれる pattern adds the meaning that another person did the action for the speaker’s benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the subject will be the person doing something beneficial for someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence will emphasize that the speaker receives help from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse the direction of giving and receiving, so they must identify who performs the action before choosing くれる or もらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.vi: Please come and visit again next time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 今度また modifies the invitation and indicates the time and repetition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に attaches to the noun あそび to indicate the purpose of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 来て is the て form used to connect with ください and create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ください expresses a favor or request, while ね makes the speech softer and more familiar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.why: あそびに states the purpose of 来る, then 来てください creates a friendly invitation or polite request. また and ね make the sentence sound friendly and natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence directly says that the speaker wants the other person to come and visit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes a gentle invitation or suggestion, not a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand あそびに as a place, but in あそびに来る, に only shows the purpose of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.vi: Before getting married, my older sister used to be a nurse.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the older sister is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: けっこんする in the dictionary form modifies 前, creating the meaning “before getting married.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 前 indicates the time before the marriage, while は sets the time as the topic or point of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: でした is the polite past form of です, serving as a noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.why: The clause けっこんする comes before 前 to identify the event used as the time reference. 前は makes that reference point the comparison frame, followed by a noun as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the time changes to after getting married.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning becomes until before or until getting married, emphasizing the time limit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.tip: With verbs, use the dictionary form directly before 前; with nouns, add の, as in Nの前.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t33-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ 前(に／は)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vi: My younger brother left home and made our parents worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that the younger brother is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the action 家出する that was performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: して connects leaving home with the result that happened afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the person affected by the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 心配を is the content or feeling caused for the parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: かける combines with the person marked by に and the feeling marked by を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.why: The two actions are connected by the て form in a natural order: leaving home and then making the parents worry. The pattern Nに Nを かける identifies the affected person and the feeling caused.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 心配させました is used instead, it emphasizes making the parents enter a worried state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 心配 is replaced with 迷惑, the meaning changes to causing trouble for the parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を for the affected person, but that person must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects the noun 技術 with 進歩 to create a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」 states the topic being commented on in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 「はやいです」 is the predicate and describes the speed of progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 技術の進歩 comes before は to form the topic. The adjective はやい comes at the end of the sentence and takes the ending です to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes the fast progress itself instead of stating a general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit 「の」 between the two nouns and incorrectly say 「技術進歩」 in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.vi: After the operation, the illness was cured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: 「を」 marks the operation as the object of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 「して」 is the て form of する, connecting the operation with the result afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 「が」 marks 病気 as the subject that reaches the cured state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 治りました is the polite past form of 治る, showing that the illness was cured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.why: The two actions are connected in order by the て form: the operation happened first, and the illness was cured afterward. The subject of 治る is 病気, so が is used, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding 「から」 makes it clearer that the illness was cured only after the operation was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 「と」 gives the sense that whenever the operation is performed, the result occurs, rather than simply describing one event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 「を」 with 病気, but with the intransitive verb 治る, the illness is the subject and goes with 「が」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.vi: I hear that a new museum will be built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: あたらしい comes before a noun to modify “museum.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 「を」 marks the museum as the object of 建てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.2.vi: hear that it will be built
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 「そうです」 comes after the plain form to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.why: あたらしい comes before はくぶつかん to create a noun phrase. 建てる in the dictionary form combines with そうです to express information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the expression “I hear that it will be built,” not an appearance or sign that construction is about to begin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Leaving out だ after 建てる and connecting 建てそうです creates the meaning “it seems that construction will begin soon,” which is completely different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse 「Vるそうです」 with 「Vます＋そうです」; the two patterns mean “I hear that” and “it seems likely to happen soon,” respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうです（伝聞）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.vi: The factory was moved to the suburbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 「を」 marks the factory as the object being moved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 「に」 indicates the destination of the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: うつしました is a polite past transitive verb and needs an object marked by を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.why: The pattern 「NをNに移す」 describes moving an object or facility to a new place. The factory is the object, so it goes with を, while the suburbs are the destination, so they go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「へ」 emphasizes the direction toward the suburbs rather than a specific destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 「が」 and うつる makes the factory the subject that moved itself, without stating who moved it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse うつす and うつる; うつす needs an object with 「を」, while うつる usually goes with 「が」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q14.kobun.vi: The food counter is on basement level one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase 食料品うりば is the topic, while 「は」 brings that topic forward to state its location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is an existence predicate used for places or things that are not people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q14.kobun.why: An existence sentence places the object as the topic before は, then gives the location with に and ends with あります. Because the counter is a thing, use あります, not います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「で」 is unsuitable for showing a fixed place of existence in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: います is used only for people or animals, so it is not used for the counter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 「で」 out of habit to indicate a place, but for existence with あります, use 「に」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the oranges near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」 states the number of oranges being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 「で」 indicates the quantity or amount used as the basis for the total price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The price phrase at the end of the sentence states the total amount for those oranges.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.why: この modifies オレンジ, then は states the number of oranges as the topic. 八つで shows the quantity converted into a price of 1,500 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: It means that there are eight, stating only the existing quantity and not the price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This sentence emphasizes buying eight for 1,500 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may read 八つ as はちつ; the counter for objects in the form つ must be read as やっつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q16.kobun.vi: My mother is an ordinary housewife.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun 普通 with the noun 主婦 to modify housewife.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: です follows a noun to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q16.kobun.why: 母は sets the topic first, then 普通の modifies 主婦. The noun 主婦 combines with です to identify a job or role.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If な is used, it must connect directly with な, while 普通 is a noun, so の is used in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse の and な; identify whether the preceding word is a noun or an adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.vi: Taro went out to play with a friend from the neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that Taro is the topic of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 近所 with 友だち, forming a phrase meaning a friend from the neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indicates a person who takes part in the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The connective form 用形 of あそぶ combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: いきました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.why: The phrase 近所の友だち forms a friend identified by area. と indicates a companion, while あそびにいく expresses going for the purpose of having fun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is attached directly to another action, it can mean doing something together or quoting something; it does not necessarily indicate a companion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If あそんでいきました is used, the meaning is play and then go, emphasizing the order of the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use を after あそび when expressing the purpose of going to do something; the correct pattern is Vます-stem に 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.vi: A picture is pasted on the wall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the location where the picture is pasted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object as being in a pasted state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb 貼る with あります in a pattern that describes a result that still remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: あります expresses the existence of an object and the fact that the result of the action still remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.why: 壁に indicates where the picture is placed, while 絵が is the object that receives the state. 貼ってあります combines the action of pasting with the resulting state that remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 貼っています is used, the sentence may emphasize an action in progress, not only the result that the picture has been pasted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only says that an object exists somewhere; it does not say who pasted it.
