default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate the whole Vてある as “be doing”; this pattern usually emphasizes a completed result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.vi: I have something important to say.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: 大事 is an な adjective, so な must be used before the noun はなし.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is a predicate that indicates the existence of an object or matter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.why: 大事な comes before はなし to limit the type of matter being discussed. はなしがあります uses が because はなし is the object introduced as existing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If はなし is replaced with こと, the meaning becomes broader: there is something or some matter that is important.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern changes the meaning from having something important to say to carrying out the action of saying something important.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q19.kobun.tip: The adjective な must keep な when it comes before a noun, even though English often has no equivalent connecting word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vi: At university, I majored in Japanese literature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: では states the context or place of study.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the field chosen as a major.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: して combines with いました to describe a major that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: いました completes the structure ていました, indicating a state or activity that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.why: では sets the scope as the time or environment of university. The field of study comes before を as the object of 専攻する, while ていました shows that the major belonged to a period in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 勉強しました is used instead, it only says that the person studied and does not emphasize that it was a major.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 専門にしました is used, it emphasizes choosing a field as a specialty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse 専攻する with 学ぶ, but 専攻する must clearly state the field of study as the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.vi: I planted a tree in the garden and am taking care of it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates where the tree was planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the tree as the object of the planting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て of 植える connects planting with the following action of taking care of it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て of そだてる connects the main verb with います to express an ongoing activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: います after the て form creates the pattern Vている, indicating an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.why: 庭に and 木を indicate the place and object, respectively. 植えて connects planting with taking care of the tree, while そだてています focuses on the activity that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 植えてからそだてています is used, the sentence emphasizes that taking care of the tree began after planting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 植えたあとでそだてています is used, the before-and-after order is stated more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q20.kobun.tip: The form て here does not mean a command; it is used to connect actions and create the pattern ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.vi: I bought beef at the supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks beef as what was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: かいました is the polite past form of 買う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.why: スーパーで states the place where the action occurs, 牛肉を states the object, and かいました ends the sentence with an action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If スーパーに行きました is used, に indicates the destination of going, not the place where the purchase is made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If スーパーから買いました is used, the focus is on the source or place that supplies the goods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q21.kobun.tip: Distinguish で and に: で indicates where an action happens, while に usually indicates a destination or a place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.vi: My house is far from the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with the noun 家.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that my house is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the reference point used to compare distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 遠い is an adjective ending in い that functions as the predicate; です is placed at the end to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.why: The sentence places the topic first with は, then states the reference point for comparison with から, and uses the adjective 遠い to describe the distance. です gives the sentence a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If から近い is used, the meaning changes to being near the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use に instead of から when stating the reference point for distance comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 迷う goes with に to show the place or area where someone got lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: ました is the polite past form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q23.kobun.why: 道に comes before the verb to state where the speaker got lost. The verb is changed to the polite past because the event already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the place where an action happens, while に is the natural combination with 迷う to show the place where someone got lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q23.kobun.tip: に should not be translated mechanically as “into”; in 迷う, に usually shows the place or area where someone got lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q24.kobun.vi: I do my homework in the classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the place where the action of doing homework happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the polite form of する and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q24.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the verb, with で used to state where the action happens. 宿題を is the activity performed by します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: にいます shows existence in the classroom, not the action of doing homework.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse で with に; で is usually used for where an action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q25.kobun.vi: I will return the book to the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the book as the item being returned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the place or recipient that receives the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 返します is the polite predicate form and describes the action of returning the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q25.kobun.why: The book is the object used with を, while the library is the place or recipient used with に. This order makes it clear what is returned, and to whom or where.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: で shows where the action of returning takes place, without emphasizing the library as the recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q25.kobun.tip: When saying that you return or give something to someone, use を for the item and に for the person or place that receives it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vi: Because I stood for a long time, my back began to hurt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ずっと modifies the state of standing and emphasizes that it continues without a break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: たって connects the state of standing with いた to form the progressive expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects a cause with a result and sounds more explanatory and softer than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the body part that undergoes a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective いたい changes to いたく to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました describes a change into a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.why: The cause clause comes before ので, and the result comes after the comma. With なる, the adjective ending in い must change to the く form to show a newly formed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the cause has almost the same meaning, but the expression is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If いたくて is used, it only connects states or events and does not clearly show a cause-and-effect relationship like ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say いたいなる, but before なる, the いたく form must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vi: Because the room is small, there is no space to put a table.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject described as small.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes to 〜くて to connect the cause clause with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item being placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: おく modifies 場所 to form the phrase “space to put a table”; が marks this phrase as the subject of ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります and expresses non-existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.why: せまくて gives the cause first, and then おく場所がありません gives the result: there is no space. The particle が marks both へや and おく場所 in two different clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with せまいので, the meaning of the cause remains, but the connection sounds clearer and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 場所, but here おく場所 is the subject of ありません, so が must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes こうじ the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: うまく modifies 進んでいます; 〜ています describes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q5.kobun.why: こうじは states the topic being evaluated, while うまく modifies 進んでいます. The form 〜ています shows that the process is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 順調です, the sentence only describes a favorable condition and does not emphasize the ongoing progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q5.kobun.tip: 〜ています should not always be translated as “be doing”; with 進んでいます, it emphasizes the current state of progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vi: This morning, I exercised in the park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase shows when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the activity happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.why: The time phrase usually comes first, followed by the place with で, the activity object with を, and then the verb at the end. しました shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of で, the sentence sounds unnatural because に does not mark the place where the activity happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the place of an action; the place where you exercise must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q7.kobun.vi: I am staying in lodgings near the university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects だいがく with ちかく to form the phrase “near the university.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the place where the subject is staying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: しています is the 〜ています form of 下宿する and describes the ongoing state of staying in lodgings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q7.kobun.why: だいがくのちかく forms a noun phrase showing a location, and に marks the place where the subject is staying. 〜ています describes an ongoing current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence focuses more on the place where an action happens, so it is less suitable than に for a state of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q7.kobun.tip: With verbs showing residence, such as 下宿する, the place usually goes with に, not で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.vi: I handed the wallet I found to the police box.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: ひろった is a clause that modifies さいふ and comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the wallet as the item being handed over.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the place or recipient that receives the wallet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 届けました is the main verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.why: ひろった comes before さいふ to identify which wallet. Then さいふを is the item being handed over, こうばんに is the place or recipient, and the verb comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used, the sentence only emphasizes the direction toward the police box, while に is more natural when referring to the place that receives the item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q8.kobun.tip: A modifying clause in Japanese comes before the noun, so say ひろったさいふ instead of reversing it as さいふひろった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.vi: That building over there is our company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あそこ with 建物 to form the phrase “the building over there”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject identified as our company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects うち with 会社 and shows ownership or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a polite judgment sentence following the pattern A is B.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.why: あそこの建物 is the subject being pointed out, while うちの会社 identifies what that subject is. The pattern が〜です is used to identify or introduce a thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the sentence has more of a topic or contrast meaning and focuses less on identifying the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t34-q9.kobun.tip: In a sentence identifying what a specific thing is, が is usually more natural than は when the noun before it is the object being pointed out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vi: Mr. Suzuki is wearing a blue shirt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies Mr. Suzuki as the person being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: あおい comes before シャツ to modify the shirt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the shirt as the object of the action of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes the current state resulting from the action of putting on clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.why: The adjective あおい is placed directly before the noun to describe the shirt's color. きています describes the state of wearing the shirt at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 着ます indicates the action of putting on clothes or a future action, without emphasizing the state of wearing them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q1.kobun.tip: With clothing, 着ている usually means “is wearing,” not simply “has put on.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q10.kobun.vi: Tomorrow evening, I will go out with my family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with よる to form a noun phrase indicating a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person or people who carry out the action of going out together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q10.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to state when the action happens, while かぞくと adds the companion. 出かけます is the main predicate and comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the meaning focuses on a direction or target, so it no longer means “with my family.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q10.kobun.tip: Do not confuse と, meaning “with,” with に when talking about a companion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item requested to be lent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is used in the て form to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ください creates a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q11.kobun.why: かさを is the object of the action of lending. The て form connects with ください to make the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it means “May I borrow an umbrella?”, so it asks for permission instead of asking someone to lend one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the dictionary form before ください, but this request pattern requires the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q12.kobun.vi: There is a soccer match tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents tomorrow as the topic and the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects サッカー with しあい, while が marks the thing that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: あります describes the existence or holding of an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q12.kobun.why: あしたは makes the time the topic. The phrase サッカーのしあい is the thing said to exist, so it goes with が before あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it means “play or hold a soccer match,” focusing on the action rather than the match's existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q12.kobun.tip: With あります, a thing that exists usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.vi: There were many people at the concert hall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates the location and sets it as the place where the people exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects たくさん with 人 to modify the number of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the people who exist at the stated location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: いた is the past form of いる, used for the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.why: The location is placed first with には, followed by the quantity and the subject that exists. いた at the end of the sentence shows that this state occurred in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning emphasizes that the hall was packed with people rather than simply saying that many people were there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q13.kobun.tip: いる is used for people and animals; do not use ある to say that people are present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほんぶんがく with けんきゅう to indicate the subject of the research.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being carried out or studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ている describes an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q14.kobun.why: The noun phrase before を is the object of the action. しています at the end of the sentence shows that the research is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it means “studied,” referring to an action completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q14.kobun.tip: Do not always translate ています as “did”; in this sentence, it describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q15.kobun.vi: Please explain how to use it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the content being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: てください expresses a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q15.kobun.why: The content to be explained comes before を. Then the verb 説明する in the て form combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence becomes a softer and more polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget を before the content being explained or use the dictionary form before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q16.kobun.vi: My opinion and Mr. Kobayashi's are different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q16.kobun.ch.0.vi: the opinions of the two people
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the topic as the opinions of me and Kobayashi.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q16.kobun.why: と connects two people who both own or are related to the opinion, while の connects a person with the noun 意見. This noun phrase is made the topic with は and then ends with ちがいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning changes to “the opinions of the two people are the same.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand と as “and” in every situation, but here it connects two people who are both related to the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.vi: If you take the express train, it takes 20 minutes to get to Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.sk: N で ＋ Vば ＋ N まで ＋ Time です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means of transportation used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 行く changes to 行けば to create a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.cn: V drops る ＋ ば; Aい drops い ＋ ければ; Aな・N ＋ なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.why: The means of transportation comes before で, and the conditional clause 行けば comes before the result. まで marks Tokyo as the final destination, while 20 minutes states the required time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 行ったら, the meaning is “after going / if you go,” and it is more specific to the situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 行くと, the sentence has a more natural or more frequent result meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse で with に; で indicates a means of transportation, while に usually indicates a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies the action of thinking and indicates the degree to which it is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: てから connects two actions in order: do the first action, and then do the second.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: こたえてください is a polite request for the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q18.kobun.why: よく modifies the first action. てから places the action of thinking before the action of answering, while ください turns the following action into a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this form, the sentence only connects the actions without clearly emphasizing their order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate てから as “because,” but in this sentence it only shows the time order: “after doing the first action, …”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.vi: The vegetables at that supermarket over there are cheaper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes vegetables the topic of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: のほうが marks the side chosen as superior in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.why: は states the item being compared, while のほうが selects the supermarket over there as the side with the lower price. The adjective 安い serves as the predicate for the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If より is used, the comparison standard must be stated clearly, such as “this supermarket is cheaper than that supermarket.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 一番安い, the meaning changes to “the cheapest among several items.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の in のほうが or understand は as the only subject, while the selected side is in the phrase のほうが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q19.kobun.cn: N は ＋ N のほうが ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vi: Please tell me the location of the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 会議 with 場所, creating the phrase “the location of the meeting.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the location as the information being requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: おしえて is the て form, which connects the verb with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows the て form to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.why: かいぎのばしょ creates a noun phrase in which the location is identified as belonging to the meeting. This phrase is the object of おしえてください, a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks whether the listener can do something for the speaker, and is more polite and softer than ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use the ます form directly before ください; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: まいあさ indicates the time when the repeated action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The distance phrase adds information to the verb “run.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 走って is the て form, connected with います to show an action that is ongoing or regularly continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ています indicates a state or habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.why: The time and distance phrases come before the predicate to add the circumstances and scale of the action. 走っている shows that running is maintained as a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 走ります, the sentence only states the action or habit neutrally, without emphasizing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes that it is a rule or a personal decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate ています only as “be doing,” but with a repeated habit it can also mean “still usually do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q21.kobun.vi: I always buy the same kind of bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of frequency that modifies the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks bread as the object being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 買います is the main predicate and is used in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q21.kobun.why: The adverb いつも comes before the verb phrase to show frequency. The noun パン goes with を because it is the object of the action 買います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 毎回, the sentence emphasizes each specific occasion more strongly, meaning that the speaker buys it every time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to use を after the noun for the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this seat the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ています describes a current state; か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q22.kobun.why: The topic このせきは comes first, followed by the state of the seat. The form ています is suitable for asking whether the seat is free at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 空きますか is used, the question asks whether the place will become free, not only whether it is free now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ています only as an action in progress, but here it indicates a state of being free.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place or position where the address is written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks 住所 as the content being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence and makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q23.kobun.why: The place ここに comes before the object 住所を, followed by the action 書いて. The Vてください pattern comes at the end to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 書きます, it only states or announces the writing action and is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use the polite form ます directly before ください; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q24.kobun.vi: The high school is quite far from my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から indicates the starting point for comparing distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes 高校 the object being evaluated for distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い serves as the predicate and combines with です to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q24.kobun.why: から identifies the place used as the distance reference point, while 高校は is the object being evaluated. The adjective とおい comes at the end to state the conclusion about the distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 近いです, the meaning changes to “the high school is near my house.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse から in this sentence with a cause meaning; here it only indicates the starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks 料理 as the object of the action of cooking or making.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: つくります is the main predicate in the polite form and expresses the speaker’s action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q25.kobun.why: The noun phrase 料理を comes before the verb because Japanese places the object before the action. The verb つくります ends the sentence and functions as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 料理ができます means that someone can cook or that the dish has been completed; it does not directly state the action of cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を because Vietnamese has no separate particle for marking the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.vi: My house is a five-minute walk from the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.sk: N は + N から + Vて + Time です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with いえ to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents my house as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the starting point for calculating travel time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て of あるく expresses the means of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ５分です indicates the amount of time needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.why: は sets my house as the topic, while から identifies the starting point. あるいて comes before ５分です to state the means of travel used when calculating the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the action of walking to somewhere rather than the travel time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate word for word and place から after the destination, but から must come after the starting point here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.vi: Because a subway was built, everything has become more convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks a newly appearing or newly formed thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the formation of the subway with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the state or result that something becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and expresses a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.why: The first clause states the background event and connects it to the result with て. With the adjective な, 便利 drops な and adds に before なる to express becoming convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 便利で is used, the sentence only connects characteristics or events and does not emphasize a change into a convenient state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep な in 便利になりました, but before に in the pattern 〜になる, 便利に must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vi: Because I was very sleepy, I drank coffee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.sk: Aい past + ので + N を + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies the adjective 眠かった to show a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result; the adjective い changes to the past form 眠かった before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks coffee as the thing being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲みました is the polite past form of 飲む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.why: ので places the cause before the result and gives a gentle explanatory tone. The object コーヒーを comes directly before the verb 飲みました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the causal meaning remains, but the expression becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with のに, the sentence changes to a contrastive meaning, such as being sleepy but still doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect ので directly to the dictionary form, but the adjective い must change into ねむかったので here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q6.kobun.sk: Time は + N が + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks snow as the thing that is falling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ふっています uses the form ている to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q6.kobun.why: は sets today as the topic, while が introduces the phenomenon of snow falling. The form ている shows that the phenomenon is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 降りました is used instead, the sentence only says that snow fell and does not emphasize that it is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は for snow because they want to make it the topic, but in this sentence snow is the subject of the phenomenon, so が is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q7.kobun.vi: I want a pair of black socks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before くつした to modify the noun directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the desired thing in the pattern ほしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ほしい is an い adjective that expresses the desire to possess something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q7.kobun.why: くろい comes before the noun to describe the socks’ color. In the pattern 〜がほしい, the desired thing is marked by が, and ほしい functions as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the desire to carry out the action of buying, not only the desire to have the item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before ほしい because of the influence of verbs, but the pattern 〜がほしい uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.vi: The summer vacation plan has not been decided yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects なつやすみ with けいかく to create the phrase “summer vacation plan.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the plan as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies the negative predicate to show that something has not been completed up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: きまっていません uses ている in the negative form to express a state in which something has not been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.why: The phrase なつやすみのけいかく identifies the type of plan. Then は makes the plan the topic. まだ combines with ていません to express an unfinished state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 決まりません is used, the sentence focuses more on not having a decision or being unable to decide, and does not emphasize the current state as 決まっていません does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate まだ as “still” and use an affirmative sentence, but talking about something not being finished requires the negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.vi: I want to become a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic is the person who wants to become a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the result or state reached after becoming something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: たい attaches to the form without ます to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.why: わたしは places the topic at the beginning of the sentence. The profession is the result of なる, so に is used. なりたいです expresses the desire to become that profession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning will be “I will become a doctor.” It only states a change and does not emphasize desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before a profession, but with なる, に must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t35-q9.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + たいです; N に + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects じぶん with いけん to show possession, while を marks the opinion being stated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: はっきり is an adverb that modifies the way the opinion is stated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: いって is the て form of the verb “to say,” used to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of a sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q1.kobun.why: The phrase じぶんのいけんを identifies what needs to be said, while はっきり shows how to do it. Vてください comes at the end of the sentence to make the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 言います, you only state the speaking action and do not directly ask the listener to speak.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place adverbs incorrectly; はっきり should come directly before the verb it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the book as the object being lent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: かして is the て form of かす, connecting the action of lending with もらいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: もらいました expresses that the speaker receives help or an action from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q10.kobun.why: ほんを is the object of the action かす. The て form connects かす with もらう, creating a structure that expresses that the speaker receives the action of lending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use Vてくれました, you emphasize that someone else did the action for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Vてもらいました emphasizes that the speaker received help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q10.kobun.tip: Do not translate もらいました simply as receiving an object; in the pattern Vてもらう, it means receiving a helpful action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.vi: I am busy every day because I take care of dogs and cats.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects いぬ with ねこ in a group of objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ねこ with the noun せわ, creating a relationship meaning “taking care of cats.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the reason why the speaker is busy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: まいにち adds the repeated time of the busy state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: いそがしいです is the い adjective predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.why: The two objects are connected by と, and the phrase ねこのせわ forms a noun phrase meaning “taking care of cats.” で gives the reason, while まいにち shows the repeated time of the state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use のために, the meaning focuses more on a purpose or a more formal reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q11.kobun.tip: You must distinguish と, which connects nouns, from で, which shows the reason in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the group or method of doing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the song as the object of うたう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the clause うたう into a noun, while は makes singing the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: たのしいです is the predicate that evaluates the topic of singing together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.why: みんなで shows who participates together, and うたを is the object of うたう. の turns the whole singing action into a topic for the adjective たのしい to evaluate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use ことは, the meaning is still “singing,” but the tone is more general and formal than のは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use は directly after a verb; first nominalize it with の or こと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のは + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.vi: There is a hospital near the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects いえ with ちかく, creating a phrase meaning “the area near the house.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the location where the hospital exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the sentence あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is an existence predicate used for objects, places, and things that are not people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.why: いえのちかくに identifies the place of existence, while びょういんが is the thing being introduced. あります comes at the end of the sentence to express that the hospital exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use で, the place becomes where an action happens, not where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Using は refers to a hospital that is already known, instead of introducing a newly mentioned hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q13.kobun.tip: In an existence pattern, the place goes with に, and the thing usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q14.kobun.vi: I carry the luggage on foot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て connects walking with carrying the luggage and also shows the method.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing being carried or transported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb はこびます is the main predicate and describes the action of transporting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q14.kobun.why: The clause あるいて comes first to state the method of carrying out the action はこびます. The noun にもつ goes with を because it is the direct object of the verb はこぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit を or use に before the transported object; the direct object must use を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q15.kobun.vi: My mother is very good at cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes 母 the topic being evaluated in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the area in which the ability 上手 is shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: じょうずです acts as the predicate and evaluates the mother's cooking ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q15.kobun.why: The pattern N は N が 上手です uses は to state the person being evaluated and が to state the area of skill. 料理 is the content of the ability, not the object of を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 得意だ, the sentence still says that the mother is good at cooking, but the tone emphasizes talent or confidence more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use を in 上手です; the area of skill usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person whose feelings or preferences are being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object of the feeling きらい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: きらいです is the な adjective predicate and expresses dislike.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q16.kobun.why: The structure は + が separates the person who has the feeling from the object of the feeling. さかな goes with が because きらい is a な adjective that expresses an evaluation or feeling toward an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 好きです, the meaning changes to “I like fish.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q16.kobun.tip: With 好き and きらい, the object usually goes with が, not を as in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.vi: My older sister will get married next month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.sk: Nの N は + Time + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects わたし with the following noun to show possession or a family relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes あね the topic of information about next month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to identify when the marriage will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: けっこんします is the main predicate and uses the polite present form to talk about a plan or future event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.why: わたしの comes before あね to identify her as the speaker's older sister. らいげつ is a time phrase, so it comes before けっこんします without needing the particle に in this expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 来月に, the sentence is still correct, but it clearly emphasizes next month as the time when the marriage will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q17.kobun.tip: Not every time phrase must have に; words such as 来月 can usually come directly before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q18.kobun.vi: This building is very tall, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies 高い to increase the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い comes before ビル to directly modify the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is placed at the end of a sentence to confirm something or share a feeling with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q18.kobun.why: とても modifies the adjective たかい, while たかい comes before ビル according to the rule that adjective い directly modifies a noun. ですね makes the comment sound like a gentle shared observation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced with でしょう, the sentence focuses on a guess or confirmation based on the speaker’s thoughts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q18.kobun.tip: The adjective い keeps its form before the noun, with no な added between たかい and ビル.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q19.kobun.vi: A ten-year-old is still a child.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the age being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies the predicate to show that the child’s state has not changed yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: こどもです is a noun predicate that gives a conclusion about a ten-year-old.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q19.kobun.why: １０さいは makes the age the topic, and then まだ adds the meaning of still. The noun こども combines with です to form a polite noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If まだ is replaced with もう, the sentence means that the person is already a child or has reached the stated state, so it does not fit the meaning of still.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q19.kobun.tip: まだ usually expresses that something has not changed or is still true; do not confuse it with もう, which means already or no longer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vi: I buy fruit juice and then drink it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun is the object of the following verb, but the particle を comes next.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ジュース as the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The linking verb is in the て form, connecting the action of buying with the action of drinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The final verb shows the action that happens after buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.why: The particle を marks the thing being bought. The て form links two successive actions, while the final action serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてから, the meaning emphasizes that drinking happens only after buying is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use と or そして to link two verbs, but in this sentence Vて is the natural way to link successive actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective modifies the noun むし.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: います expresses the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q20.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to describe the insect. The noun subject goes with が, followed by the existence verb います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 大きい, the meaning changes to “big” or “large”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may easily put the adjective after the noun, but Japanese puts the adjective before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q20.tokens.3.m: exist; there is for living things
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.vi: We talked for as long as two hours.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.sk: Duration も + Vて + いました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: も emphasizes that the period lasted as long as two hours.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the て form combines with いました to express a state or activity continuing in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: いました is the polite past form of います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.why: The duration comes first to state how long the activity lasted. Vていました combines the て form with いました, showing that the activity continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 話しました is used, it only states that they talked for two hours, with less emphasis on the continuing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate も as “also,” but in this sentence も emphasizes the duration “as long as” or “up to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q22.kobun.vi: The weather is bad today too, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: も adds a comparison with other days: today is the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject being described as the weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective states the weather condition, while ね is used to share the observation with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q22.kobun.why: 天気が is the subject being described, so が is used. The adjective comes after the subject to state its condition, while ですね creates a tone of confirmation or agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced with でしょう, the sentence leans toward the guess “the weather is probably bad.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q22.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically use は instead of が when you want to state the direct subject of an observation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.vi: Everything is cheap at this supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate a specific supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は states スーパー as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 何でも refers to all the products being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective serves as the predicate and describes the prices of the products.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.why: この modifies スーパー, and then は makes the supermarket the topic. 何でも covers all the products, while やすい serves as the predicate describing the prices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何でも is replaced with 何か, the meaning becomes “something,” so it no longer covers everything.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q23.kobun.tip: 何でも means “anything; everything,” not just one unspecified item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q24.kobun.sk: Adverb + N を + Vます + か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies the action and indicates how often someone drinks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the drink affected by the action of drinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: か is placed at the end of a sentence to turn a polite statement into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q24.kobun.why: よく comes before the verb to show frequency. The drink goes with を, while か at the end marks a yes-or-no question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 飲みませんか is used, the sentence may sound like an invitation, “Would you like to drink?” rather than a question about a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q24.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit を because English has no particle that marks the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q25.kobun.vi: I want to meet my parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who participates in the action of meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who is the object of the action of meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: たい is attached after the ます of a verb to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q25.kobun.why: と identifies the person met together with the speaker, while に identifies the person toward whom the action of meeting is directed. The verb stem combines with たい to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 会いたがっています is used, the sentence describes another person’s desire rather than the speaker’s own desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q25.kobun.tip: With 会う, the person being met usually goes with に; do not use を to mark that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vi: I sat down in the empty seat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase あいている comes before a noun to modify the seat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the speaker sits down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q3.kobun.why: The phrase あいている comes before せき to identify which seat it is. に indicates the destination or position toward which the sitting action is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If せきで is used, it means sitting at that place as the location of the action, without emphasizing sitting down into the seat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate both に and で as “at,” but に usually indicates the destination or target position of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vi: There is a large road in front of the store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects みせ with まえ, forming the noun phrase “in front of the store”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the location where the road exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists at the location stated earlier; おおきな modifies とおり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate used for things that are not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.why: The pattern Nに Nがあります states the location first and then names the thing that exists there. が marks the thing introduced as existing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If まえで is used, the area in front of the store becomes the place where an action occurs, not the location where the road exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse あります with います: あります is used for objects, plants, and places; います is used for people and animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the clock as the subject that is in a stopped state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: Vている describes the current state caused by the stopping action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q5.kobun.why: The subject of the state is marked by が. The form とまっている does not only say that the stopping action happened; it says that the clock is now in a stopped state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If とまりました is used, the sentence only says that the clock stopped, without focusing on its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand Vている as always meaning “is doing,” but with verbs that change a state, it often means “is in the state that has resulted from the action.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before テーブル to modify the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the table as the thing bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb shows that the purchase was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q6.kobun.why: The adjective あたらしい comes before the noun according to Japanese modifier order. This noun phrase is the object and goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If あたらしく is used, the adjective becomes an adverb and modifies the way of buying, so it does not fit the meaning “new table.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q6.kobun.tip: The adjective い directly modifies the noun, so の is not needed between them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes “the particular problem” the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ありません is the negative form of あります, expressing that the problem does not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q7.kobun.why: The phrase とくべつもんだい is made the topic by は. ありません denies the existence of that problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence simply states directly that there is no problem, with less emphasis on making it the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q7.kobun.tip: When denying existence, use ありません for things or situations and いません for people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.vi: Please throw out the trash on Tuesday and Friday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that trash is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects two days with the same function in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the time when the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: すてます is the main predicate and uses the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.why: The topic ごみ comes first. The days are then joined by と, and the time is marked by に. The verb すてます comes at the end to complete the meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If only one day is used with に, the sentence refers to only one time and does not express a list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget に after a date or day when stating the time an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective that follows and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q1.kobun.why: The noun topic comes before は. Then とても modifies the adjective ひろい. The adjective ending in い keeps its original form and adds です to make a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse とても with たくさん; とても modifies an adjective, while たくさん usually indicates a quantity or a large degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: かんがえて is the て form, connecting the action of thinking with the action of answering; よく modifies this verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: こたえて is the て form, connecting with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ください turns the preceding action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q10.kobun.why: The two verbs in the て form appear in sequence, showing that the first action is done before the second. ください comes at the end and applies to the whole request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding から emphasizes more clearly that you must finish thinking before answering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q10.kobun.tip: The て form in this sentence both connects two actions and connects with ください, so every て should not be mechanically translated as “and.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the method or the person who directly performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action つくります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: つくります is the ます verb form, serves as the main predicate, and expresses a polite action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: か at the end of the sentence creates a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q11.kobun.why: で states the person or method of performing the action, を states the object of the action, and the verb comes at the end. か turns the question about the action into a yes-or-no question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ていますか, the question asks about an action in progress or a current habit, not just the action in general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q11.kobun.tip: で in 自分で does not mean a location; here it refers to the person who performs the action personally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location where the car is stopped or parked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the car as the object of the action とめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: とめないで is the negative form of ないで, connecting with ください to request that the action not be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ないでください is a polite way to ask someone not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.why: The location comes before the object and the verb, following the usual order of a Japanese sentence. The form ないでください makes the action negative while keeping the polite request tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern has a stronger rule-like or prohibitive tone, equivalent to “You must not park here.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Using で emphasizes the place where the parking action takes place, while に fits the point where the car is stopped or parked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q12.kobun.tip: Do not connect ないでください with the ます form; remove ます, change it to ない, and then add でください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing the state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes an event that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q13.kobun.why: The possessive phrase うちの comes before the noun ねこ to identify which cat it is. ねこが is the subject, while しにました comes at the end as the predicate and shows that the event has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the sentence changes from emphasizing the subject to presenting the cat as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q13.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse の with が and put the particle in the wrong position in the noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the place identified in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects わたし with いえ to show whose house it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: です politely ends a noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q14.kobun.why: ここが identifies the place. The phrase わたしのいえ is the noun that says what that place is, and です concludes the sentence using a noun-sentence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, ここ becomes the topic being introduced instead of highlighting the identified place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate の as a separate word and forget that it connects two nouns into one phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The polite-form verb comes at the end of the sentence and describes an action that will be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q15.kobun.why: ９時から places the time point before the verb to say that the action starts at that time. はじめます comes at the end because it is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used, it means that the action continues until 9 o'clock, not that it starts at 9 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake から for a method or a reason, but in this sentence it indicates a starting point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.vi: I am always thinking about you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも modifies the whole action and indicates frequent repetition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects あなた with こと to form a phrase showing the object of thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of 思う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: Vている describes a state or an ongoing action; here, the polite form います is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.why: いつも comes first to modify the action. あなたのことを is the object phrase, while 思っています comes last to express a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 思います is used, the sentence only describes a thought or feeling in general and does not emphasize an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を after こと or understand ています as only the simple present tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.vi: Please give me one more sheet of paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: もう modifies the quantity and expresses a request for one additional sheet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: １まい indicates the quantity and the type of item counted with 枚.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item being requested or supplied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.why: もう and １まい specify the requested quantity. かみを is the object of ください, so this phrase comes immediately before the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If お願いします is used, the request is more general and formal, without directly stating the Nをください pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the wrong counter; paper and flat objects usually go with 枚.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 本 as the item borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: １さつ adds the quantity and the type of item counted with 冊.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and shows that the borrowing has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q18.kobun.why: 本を is the object of the borrowing action, while １さつ shows the number of books. かりました comes at the end to serve as the predicate and show that the action is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If １まい is used, the counted item means a sheet or a flat object, so it is not suitable for a book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 冊 with 枚; books and book-shaped objects use 冊.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.vi: Those who understand, please raise your hands.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: This clause comes before 人 to modify the person who understands.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the person who understands the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase comes before を and serves as the object of the verb あげて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: あげて is the て form and connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.why: わかった comes before 人 to identify the group of people being discussed. Then, the object goes with を, while あげてください makes a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence has the meaning of asking someone to try doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を or use the dictionary form before ください instead of using the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the opening action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb あける changes to the て form and combines with も to create a permission-request pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: いいですか asks whether the previous action is allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q2.kobun.why: The object goes with を and comes before the action. The pattern Vて もいいですか asks for permission to perform that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it still gives a request for permission, but the tone is more formal and rigid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence asks whether the action is forbidden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before もいいですが; this permission pattern requires the verb in the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: やっと modifies the predicate and emphasizes that something happened after a period of waiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: おわりました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q20.kobun.why: やっと comes before the predicate to state the result achieved after a long process. おわりました is at the end because it is the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the tone emphasizes the final result and does not necessarily imply a long wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse やっと with もう; やっと emphasizes that the event happened only in the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.vi: Because it is already spring, it is no longer cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: もう indicates that the current time has changed to a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: だから connects the reason with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the く form to connect with ありません in the negative structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません completes the polite negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.why: もう states that the time has changed, だから gives the reason, and the adjective い changes to く to combine with the negative form ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If だから is replaced with ので, the reason is presented more gently and objectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with のに, the sentence means something contrary to expectation, such as “although it is spring.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep the adjective い unchanged before ありません; 寒い must be changed to 寒くありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.vi: There are few young people in this village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the village being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the village the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the group of people whose number is described in the village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: すくないです is the polite predicate describing a small number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.why: The village is introduced as the topic with は. The group of young people goes with が because it is the group being evaluated in terms of quantity, while すくないです serves as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used after わかい人, the group of young people becomes a contrasting topic, emphasizing that young people in particular are few.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は for わかい人, but the pattern for describing quantity usually uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q23.kobun.sk: Aい + N を + Quantity + V without ます + なさい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before もの to modify it, while を marks the whole phrase as the item to be chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 一つ indicates the number of items to choose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: なさい is attached after the verb's stem form ます to give an instruction or a mild command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q23.kobun.why: The phrase ただしいものを is the object of the action of choosing. 一つ adds the quantity, while えらびなさい comes at the end to give the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If えらびなさい is replaced with えらんでください, the request becomes more polite and softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place 一つ after the verb, but the quantity usually comes before the verb in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.vi: If you do not go quickly, you will be late for the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The adverb form modifies the action of going and shows that the person needs to go quickly or early.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 行かないと states a necessary condition; if the action is not done, the result that follows will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the point or event that the person will be late for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: おくれます is the predicate, while よ emphasizes the reminder or warning to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.why: はやく modifies 行く, and then 行かないと creates a negative condition. に marks the meeting as the point at which someone will be late, while よ makes the warning clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence means that one must go quickly or early.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes “one must go,” rather than stating the consequence of being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand に as a direction of movement; in おくれるに, に marks the point or event that someone will be late for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い changes to the form く to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and expresses a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q25.kobun.why: The subject of the change comes before が. The adjective い changes to the form く and combines with なる to express the state of becoming healthier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only describes the body as healthy and does not emphasize a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use つよいなる directly; it must be changed to つよくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vi: While waiting, I read a magazine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: まっている describes the state of waiting and modifies 間.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 間 indicates the period during which the action in the following clause takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb “read.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 読んで is the て form of 読む and connects with いました to create the polite past progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: いました indicates a continuing state or action in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.why: The clause まっている modifies 間 to specify the period. After the comma is an action that happened during that period, with 読んでいました showing that the person was reading in the past.
