default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 間に is used, the sentence emphasizes an event that happened at a point during the waiting period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ながら is used, the sentence emphasizes two actions performed at the same time by the same subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q3.kobun.tip: Do not omit いる before 間 when you want to clearly express an ongoing state: まっている間.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.vi: About what time do you usually wake up?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも modifies the action and indicates frequent occurrence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 何時ごろ indicates the approximate time being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: おきます is the predicate and uses the polite form to ask about a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: か changes a statement into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.why: いつも comes first to state the frequency, followed by the time phrase 何時ごろ. The verb おきます comes at the end of the content, and か marks the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何時ごろ is replaced with 何時に, the question asks about a more exact time and no longer has an approximate meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q4.kobun.tip: 何時ごろ has ごろ, so に is not needed when asking about an approximate time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: もう indicates that the present time has arrived for the action to be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: かえる changes to the て form and combines with も to create a permission pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: いいですか asks whether going home is acceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q5.kobun.why: もう comes before the sentence pattern to ask whether the present time is suitable for going home. Vて もいいですか is the permission structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the request for permission becomes softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence asks whether it is still not permitted to go home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q5.kobun.tip: もう in this sentence does not mean only “again” or “more”; it indicates that the time has come or that the conditions have been met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: きゅうに modifies the change of state in the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective いたい changes to いたく to connect with なる and express a change into a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and shows a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.why: あたまが is the thing undergoing the change, while いたく comes before なる because the i-adjective ending い must change into the く form. なりました shows that the state of being in pain has appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If いたいです is used instead, the sentence only describes being in pain and does not emphasize the sudden change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If いたくします is used, the meaning is to make someone or a body part become painful, with an active cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q6.kobun.tip: Do not connect いたいなる directly; the i-adjective ending い must change from い to く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q7.kobun.vi: Is it close from the apartment to the university?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the distance; ちかい is the adjective used as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ですか changes a statement into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q7.kobun.why: The distance is presented in the order of the starting point から and then the endpoint まで. The adjective ちかい comes at the end to comment on the whole distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 遠いですか is used instead, the question changes to “Is it far?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use に instead of から when expressing the starting point of a distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q8.kobun.vi: What kind of fish do you like?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな modifies さかな, while が marks the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: すきです expresses a state of liking; が before it states what is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q8.kobun.why: In the pattern 好きだ, the thing that is liked usually goes with が. どんな comes before a noun to ask which kind, so the question phrase is placed before が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何の魚 is used instead, the focus is “fish of what kind,” usually asking more specifically about the type or origin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If を食べますか is used, the meaning changes to “Do you eat fish?” because を marks the food involved in the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q8.kobun.tip: With 好き, Vietnamese speakers may easily use を out of habit, but a noun that is liked usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q9.kobun.vi: Sorry, please say it one more time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies いちど, giving the meaning “again, one more time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: いって is the て form of いう, and it connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q9.kobun.why: もう一度 shows the number of repetitions, while the verb in the て form comes before ください to make a request. This order puts the action to be performed before the request expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks more softly, “Could you say it one more time?” and expresses an indirect request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t37-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form いう directly before ください; change it to the て form, which is いって.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: ちょっと modifies the request, making the sentence softer and more natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the て form connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q1.kobun.why: ちょっと comes before the request to show a small degree. The て form combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it, the sentence becomes a more casual question, suitable for people of equal status or close friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; use the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the thing that exists in a sentence pattern with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: たくさん modifies the number of friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: いますか creates a question about the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q10.kobun.why: In an existence sentence, a noun referring to a person goes with が and the verb います. たくさん comes before います to state the quantity, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If いますか is replaced with ありますか, it is used for objects or things, not for friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Using は makes friends the topic, giving the nuance of asking about a group of friends that has already been mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ある for all types of existence, but people and animals must use いる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.vi: Waking up early in the morning feels good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: あさ indicates the time when the action of waking up takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: はやく modifies おきる, showing that the time of waking up is early.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a natural condition and result, with the verb before と in the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the feeling being judged as good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: いいです is a predicate that describes a state or feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.why: あさ and はやく add the time and manner to おきる. The おきると clause states a natural condition, and then きもちがいい describes the resulting state or result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If おきたら is used, the condition is more hypothetical or connected to one specific occasion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: おきるとき indicates the time of waking up and does not directly state a condition–result relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と as “and,” but in this sentence と connects a condition with a natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q12.kobun.vi: That flower shop has low prices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the flower shop the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective やすい acts as the predicate, while です creates a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q12.kobun.why: あの modifies the noun in the phrase （ はなや ）.は states that the flower shop is the topic, and then やすいです describes the shop’s price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 安そうです, it means that it looks inexpensive, which is only a guess based on its appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate やすい as “easy,” but when talking about prices, やすい means “inexpensive.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.vi: There is a river near the school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: N の connects the noun がっこう with そば, creating the phrase “near the school.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists at the stated place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is a predicate used for things that are not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.why: The phrase Nのそばに puts the place first, while 川があります states what exists there. In an existence pattern, が usually marks the thing being discovered or introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, it refers to a place where an action takes place, not where a river exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use で to mark the place of existence with あります; a place of existence usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: N の modifies べんきょう, showing the content of the study.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes studying Chinese characters the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: In the phrase 時間がかかる, が marks the amount of time needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: かかります combines with 時間 to express that an amount of time is needed or required.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q14.kobun.why: かんじのべんきょう is a noun phrase serving as the topic. The pattern 時間がかかる uses が for the amount of time needed and places かかる at the end of the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 時間を使います, the sentence emphasizes an active subject using time, rather than simply saying that the activity takes a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q14.kobun.tip: With かかる meaning “take time,” learners may easily use を; the standard expression is 時間がかかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: With 乗る, the particle に marks the means of transportation that the speaker gets on or travels by.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of のる connects the action of getting on the train with the following action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q15.kobun.why: のって行きましょう connects two actions in order: get on the train and then go. に goes with 乗る to show the vehicle one gets on, while ましょう creates an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 電車で行きましょう, it only says “let’s go by train,” without emphasizing the action of getting on the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q15.kobun.tip: 乗る goes with に, while 行く used for traveling by a means of transportation usually goes with で; do not change the two particles freely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.vi: It takes 10 minutes to walk from the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.sk: N から ＋ Vて ＋ Duration です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から marks the starting point of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of あるく comes before the duration to add the means of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: １０分です states the time needed for the walking route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.why: から states the starting point, あるいて shows the means of travel, and １０分です states the duration. The parts are arranged in order, from the starting place to the means of travel and then the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 駅から１０分かかります is used, it directly says “it takes 10 minutes from the station,” without clearly stating that the person walks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q16.kobun.tip: あるいて adds the means of travel, so it is usually placed before the duration; do not understand １０分 as a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q17.kobun.vi: I will pay the taxi fare.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the taxi fare the topic and gives the sense of “as for this particular amount”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が identifies the person who directly pays the money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: はらいます is the predicate. It describes the action of paying in a polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q17.kobun.why: タクシー代は states the amount being discussed, while わたしが は らいます identify the person responsible for paying. は and が appear together to separate the topic from the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, the taxi fare becomes the direct object, so the sentence is more neutral and does not emphasize the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use が with タクシー代 when you want to make the amount the topic; は fits the sense of “as for the taxi fare” better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q18.kobun.vi: I do not have any particular questions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb that modifies the whole negative meaning at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は brings “questions” forward as the topic to say that there are no particular questions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります. It is used to say that something does not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q18.kobun.why: The adverb comes before the topic to limit the scope of the negative meaning. N は ありません means “there is no N.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is “not ... much,” not that there is none at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ない with nouns; with あります, they need to use the polite negative form ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks meat as the object of the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: よく is an adverb that modifies 食べます and shows frequency or how often something happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べます is the polite form of 食べる; か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q19.kobun.why: The object goes with を, and the adverb よく comes before the verb to modify its frequency. The polite verb 食べます combines with か to ask a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: たくさん asks whether the amount eaten is large or small, while よく asks how often it happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q19.kobun.tip: Do not confuse よく, “often,” with たくさん, “a lot”; one shows frequency, while the other shows quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being requested for lending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the て form connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q2.kobun.why: The item being lent is the object, so it goes with を. The phrase Vてください comes at the end of the sentence to express a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used instead, the question becomes softer and more indirect. It means asking whether the listener can lend it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q2.kobun.tip: 貸す means lending something to another person, while 借りる means borrowing something from another person; do not mix up these two verbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.vi: I live in a different apartment from last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: とは marks last year as the point of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: 別の directly modifies the noun アパート that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the place where someone lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 住んでいます is the ている form of 住む. It describes the state of living somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.why: The comparison point comes before the noun phrase, while 別の modifies アパート. The place of residence goes with に, and 住んでいます describes the state of being there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: 違うアパート also means a different apartment, but it emphasizes the difference more and does not clearly have the identifying sense of “another apartment” that 別の has.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で with 住む; a place of residence usually goes with に: 場所に住む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q21.kobun.vi: After reading the letter, I felt relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the letter as the thing being read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: 読んで is the て form of 読む. It connects the action of reading with the following state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 安心しました is the polite past form of 安心する. It states the feeling that arose after the previous action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q21.kobun.why: The letter is the object of 読む, so it goes with を. The て form connects two events in order, with the feeling of relief happening after reading the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 読んでから is used, the meaning “only after reading it...” is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q21.kobun.tip: Do not translate every て form as “and”; in this sentence, it also shows the order of events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.vi: Listen carefully to the doctor's words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 医者 with 話 to create the phrase “the doctor's words.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the doctor's words as the content to listen to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies 聞きなさい and asks someone to listen carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: Remove ます from the verb's ます form, then add なさい to make a moderately polite request or command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.why: の creates a possessive phrase or relationship between the doctor and the words. 話を聞く is the fixed combination meaning “listen to words,” while なさい turns the sentence into a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: 聞いてください is softer and more polite, so it is suitable when asking the listener to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 聞く as “ask,” but in 話を聞く, 聞く means “listen.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q23.kobun.sk: Time + N を + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 shows the time or repeated frequency of the action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks 運動 as the content of the action する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: しています is the ている form of する. It describes an activity in progress or a habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q23.kobun.why: The frequency phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to state how often something is repeated. The noun 運動 combines with をする, and then しています describes exercise that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: 毎日運動します shows a habit or regular action, while 毎日運動しています emphasizes the state of maintaining that habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q23.kobun.tip: With an activity noun such as 運動, use 運動をする; do not directly say 運動します when you want to keep the noun + を structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q24.kobun.vi: What kind of music do you often listen to?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな modifies 音楽, while を marks the music being listened to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the action 聞きます and shows frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞きます is the polite predicate form, and か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q24.kobun.why: どんなN creates a phrase asking about the type or quality of a noun. を marks 音楽 as the object of 聞きます, while よく comes before the verb to show frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何の音楽 is used instead, the question asks what type or subject the music belongs to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put を in the wrong position; place を immediately after the object affected by the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.vi: I will go to the company before 9 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.sk: Deadline までに + N に + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: までに shows the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the verb 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.why: The deadline phrase comes first to state the completion point, followed by the destination with に. 行きます takes a destination, not a place of action marked by で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 9時まで is used, it only states the period up to 9 o'clock and does not emphasize that the action must be completed before that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: で with 行きます usually shows a means of transportation; for example, 電車で行きます means going by train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q25.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に, which shows a destination, with で, which shows the place where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vi: Do you have a long pencil?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: An adjective comes before a noun to describe えんぴつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks pencil as the thing whose existence is asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますか politely asks whether an object exists or is available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.why: The adjective comes directly before the noun to identify the type of pencil being asked about. The pattern Nがありますか asks about the existence or availability of an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the question focuses specifically on the pencil as the topic and often has a contrastive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.tip: The adjective い directly describes the noun, with no の between them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q3.kobun.cn: Aい + N が + ありますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the bird as the subject performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the て form connects with います to express an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: います completes the pattern Vています, showing the state of flying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q4.kobun.why: The bird is the subject, so it goes with が. The て form combines with いる to express that the action of flying is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only says that the bird flew or performed the action of flying. It does not emphasize that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q4.kobun.tip: Do not understand います here as “have.” After a verb in the て form, it creates the meaning “be doing something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vi: It has been raining since this morning today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic and time reference of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates when the rain began.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks rain as the phenomenon in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the て form connects with います to create a pattern that expresses an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vています and shows that the rain is still falling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.why: きょうは sets the time range first, and then から gives the starting point. 雨が is the subject of the phenomenon, while Vています shows that the rain is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only says that it rained from the morning. It does not necessarily show that it is still raining now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q5.kobun.tip: から in this sentence only marks the starting point in time. It does not mean “because.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vi: This winter is cold, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今年 to the noun that follows and describes that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this year's winter the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is placed at the end of the sentence to give an observation and wait for the listener's agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.why: 今年の describes ふゆ, while は makes the phrase ふゆ the topic. The adjective さむい is the predicate and combines with ですね to create a casual tone of observation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced with です, the sentence only gives information and no longer asks for agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょう is used, the sentence is more like a guess or a mild confirmation, rather than simply sharing an observation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit は after the topic or translate ですね as a complete question, although it usually only suggests agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.vi: I always shop at the same supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも is an adverb of frequency that describes the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: おなじ comes before a noun to indicate a supermarket that is the same as or familiar from before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the action of buying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: かいます is the polite predicate form and describes a present action or habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.why: いつも describes the action, おなじ describes スーパー, and で marks the place where the action occurs. The verb かいます comes at the end of the sentence to complete the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, it does not fit the meaning of buying something at a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: へ only indicates the direction toward the supermarket, not the place where the buying action is being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q7.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use に for every place, but the place where an action occurs usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て comes before the following verb to connect the way an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the endpoint of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes going to the stated point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q8.kobun.why: あるいて states the way of traveling and connects to 行きます through the て form. 学校まで identifies the endpoint of the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: に only indicates the destination, while まで emphasizes the range or endpoint of the journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: あるいてから means walking is completed before doing something else. It no longer only indicates the means of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q8.kobun.tip: Learners may easily understand て here as past tense, but あるいて is the て form used to connect the way of doing something with the main verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the eyes as the object affected by the action of opening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 大きく is the adverbial form of 大きい and describes how to open the eyes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: あけて uses the て form to connect the verb with ください in a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after the て form to create a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.why: 目を identifies the object to open, while 大きく describes the degree of opening. The structure Vてください places the polite request at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This form only states or describes the action of opening the eyes. It is not a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding ないで changes it into a request not to open the eyes wide.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t38-q9.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use 大きい before a verb, but when it describes a verb, it must change to 大きく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vi: I am doing research at the university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the research activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 研究 as the content of the activity しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: しています is している in the polite form and describes an activity in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.why: 大学で gives the place where the activity occurs, while 研究を is the object of する. The form ～ています shows that the activity is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 大学にいます, it only means being at the university and does not say that the person is doing research.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 研究しました is used, it means that the research was completed and no longer has the meaning of an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q1.kobun.tip: For an activity taking place at a location, use で; do not use に instead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the food affected by the verb たべません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: たべません is the polite negative form of たべる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q10.kobun.why: わたしは makes the speaker the topic, while にくを is the object of the action of eating. The negative form of the verb comes at the end of the sentence to complete the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: わたしが emphasizes that I myself am the person who does not eat, rather than simply making me the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: にくは emphasizes meat as the topic or contrasting object and often suggests that I may eat another food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the subject “I”; わたし is the topic and therefore goes with は, while を comes after the food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: て形 connects with the verb いきます and describes the means or way of traveling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action いきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q11.kobun.why: The clause あるいて comes before いきます to add how the action of going is done. に comes after the destination, so 会社にいきます means going to the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 会社で, it means doing an action at the company, not going to the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に to show a means of transport, but means of transport usually use で; in this sentence, に shows the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes ちち the topic being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that has the quality つよい, meaning that the strength is strong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate and describes the level of the father's strength.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the sentence in a polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q12.kobun.why: The structure は～が～ is used to state a specific quality of the topic. ちからが is the part being described, while つよい is the adjective acting as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with 元気です, it means being healthy or having good energy, which is broader than physical strength.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q12.kobun.tip: Do not translate が mechanically as “is”; here, が marks the noun described by the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the map as the item being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: もっていって is the て形 of もっていく, and it connects with ください to form a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: てください expresses a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q13.kobun.why: The object を comes before the verb to show what is being carried. てください comes after the verb in the て form and turns the action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with もっていってもいいです, the sentence asks about or talks about permission to carry it, so it is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put ください after the dictionary form, but a request pattern must use the verb in the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.vi: That person is not a bad person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents あの人 as the topic being judged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective わるい comes before 人 to modify the noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ではありません is the polite negative form of です and negates the whole phrase わるい人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.why: わるい comes before 人 to form the noun phrase わるい人. は makes that person the topic, while ではありません negates the noun phrase at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use わるくありません, it directly negates the adjective and means “not bad,” rather than emphasizing that the person is not a bad person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.tip: Do not change わるい into わるく when it comes before a noun; the adjective い keeps its original form to modify the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q14.kobun.cn: Aい + N + ではありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.vi: Tomorrow I intend to get up at 7 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.sk: Time に + V辞書形 + つもりです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time when the action おきる is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the dictionary form comes before つもり to modify the intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: つもりです expresses the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.why: The time is placed before the action to show when the speaker will get up. The verb in the dictionary form connects with つもり to express the intention to do something in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use Vる予定です, it means there is a plan or schedule, which is more objective than つもりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.tip: After つもり, do not use a verb conjugated in the past tense when talking about a present or future intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q15.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + つもりだ/です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the pen as the item being requested to borrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: かして is the て form of かす, and it connects with ください to form a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q16.kobun.why: ペンを is the object of the action かす. The verb uses the て form before ください to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 貸してもらえますか, the request becomes a softer question with the meaning “Could you help me...?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q16.kobun.tip: かす means “lend something to another person,” while かりる means “borrow something from another person”; do not mix up these two verbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q17.kobun.vi: Please buy stamps and bring them back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks what is being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the two actions of buying and bringing back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q17.kobun.why: The object comes before the verb and goes with を. The two actions are connected using the て form, and then ください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace it with this form, the request becomes softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that ください must come after a verb in the て form, not after the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: なにか modifies the noun that follows and means “some ...” or “something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes “some question” the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ありませんか is used to ask gently whether something exists or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q18.kobun.why: なにか comes before a noun to limit the object to “something.” The topic is presented with は, while ありませんか politely asks whether it exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the question is more direct and has less of a suggestive tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q18.kobun.tip: Do not translate は as “is”; in this sentence, は only marks the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q19.kobun.vi: Yesterday I went to sleep at 8 p.m.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets yesterday as the time reference for the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the exact time when the action of sleeping happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ねました is the polite past form of the verb ねる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q19.kobun.why: The day reference is placed at the beginning of the sentence and marked with は. The specific time goes with に, followed by a predicate showing a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use ごろ, the time is approximate, so it does not emphasize exactly 8 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for hours; the specific time in this sentence must use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q2.kobun.vi: Thank you very much for your kindness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に connects with ご親切 to state what the speaker is expressing thanks for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: どうも adds emphasis to the expression of thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ありがとうございます is a polite sentence-ending expression used to say thank you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q2.kobun.why: ご親切に is a fixed phrase used to thank someone for kindness or help. どうも comes before the thanks to add emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 親切のおかげで, the meaning changes to achieving a result thanks to someone's kindness, rather than directly expressing thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in ご親切に as a separate preposition; the whole phrase is usually learned as a polite way to say thank you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Tanaka the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the verb into a noun, while が marks running as the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective はやい to show degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: はやい is the predicate commenting on running speed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.why: The action of running is turned into a noun with の so it can be the subject of the adjective. This pattern says that someone is good at or fast in a certain activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to は, “running” becomes the topic being introduced, with a clearer explanatory or contrasting nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.tip: Do not omit の before が; the verb must be turned into a noun to be the subject in this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + の + が + Aい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.vi: We held a party in the student dormitory cafeteria.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun before it with 食堂, showing ownership or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the party takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of organizing or carrying out an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: した is the past form of する in パーティーをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.why: The possessive phrase with の modifies the place. The place takes で because it is where the action happens, while パーティー is the object and takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence points to or describes existence at a place, and no longer emphasizes where the event is held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for every place; the place where an action happens usually takes で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.vi: It is very hot, so let’s turn on the air conditioner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies the adjective 暑い to show how hot it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the result; the い-ending adjective stays unchanged before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the device being turned on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう creates an invitation or suggestion to do an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. The object being turned on takes を, while ましょう makes the suggestion polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is usually more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: With Vませんか, the sentence becomes a softer invitation or suggestion and does not state that we will act together as ましょう does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.tip: With い-ending adjectives, do not add な before ので: say あついので, not あついな​​ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + ので、／Aな・N + な + ので、
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.vi: I asked the staff member whether there was a larger size.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing being asked about as existing or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ないか creates the content of an indirect question introduced into the verb 聞いた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞いた is the main predicate and describes a past act of asking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.why: The phrase 大きいサイズがないか is the content of the indirect question and comes before 聞いた. に marks the person asked, while が marks the thing being checked for existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ないか asks whether a larger size exists, focusing on its existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 聞く when asking about a person, but the person being asked usually takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.vi: Tomorrow, I have to go out during the day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase shows the time period when the action of going out takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative pattern combined with はいけない expresses the meaning of having to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.cn: Vない形 remove い + くてはいけない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.why: あしたは sets a time point as the topic, while （ ひるま ） add a specific time. 出かけなくてはいけない uses the negative form to create the meaning of obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence means that going out is allowed instead of required.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q24.kobun.tip: Do not understand なくてはいけない as meaning that it is forbidden; the whole pattern means that it is necessary to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.vi: Because the door was open, I went inside and called out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the door as the subject in an open state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the result; いた shows that the open state continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place the speaker enters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: 入って is the て form used to connect entering with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object of the action かけた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: かけた is the main predicate in the past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.cn: Vている + ので; Vて to connect actions
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.why: The open state of the door is mentioned first and connects to the result with ので. Then, 入って connects two consecutive actions: going inside and then calling out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still shows a reason, but the nuance is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: 入ると emphasizes that the result happens as soon as one enters, rather than simply connecting two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle に in 中に入る, but に is necessary to show the place entered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vi: The highest mountain in the world is Everest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.sk: Scope で + いちばん + Aい + N は + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で limits the scope of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies 高い to create the superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 高い comes before 山 to modify the noun 山.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes 山 the topic identified at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends a noun sentence and gives the conclusion about the topic 山.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.why: 世界で sets the scope of comparison, and いちばん高い creates a modifying phrase for 山. 山は introduces the topic, while エベレストです identifies that topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 世界の中でいちばん高い山 is used, the expression more clearly means “the highest mountain among the mountains in the world.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: もっとも高い also means the highest, but it is more formal and more common in writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q3.kobun.tip: An adjective modifying a noun must come directly before the noun, as in 高い山.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: わかる usually goes with が to mark the content that the speaker understands.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: わかりますか creates a polite question about the ability to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q4.kobun.why: English is the content being understood, so it takes が in the structure わかる. か at the end of the sentence changes the polite statement into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 英語を理解しますか sounds more active and formal, like asking whether someone understands something clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q4.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically apply を to every verb; わかる is usually used with が for the thing being understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject being judged as the most important.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: です creates a polite predicate that describes a state or evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q5.kobun.why: The noun marked by が is the subject of the evaluation. いちばん comes before an adjective to raise the evaluation to the highest level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing いちばん with もっとも keeps the meaning “most,” but sounds more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は because of the translation habit “health is,” but が is suitable for stating the thing being evaluated in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q6.kobun.vi: Fires often happen because of cigarettes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the cause or factor that makes something happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the event that happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite present form of the verb describes an event that often happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q6.kobun.why: The cause comes first, followed by the frequency and the event that is the subject of the verb meaning “happen.” With おこります, 火事 is marked by が because it is an event that occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: たばこによって emphasizes the objective factor or cause and is more formal in writing than たばこで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q6.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate で as “by”; in this sentence, で means “because of” or “due to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.vi: I was seriously injured and then had to go to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 大きな comes before a noun and directly modifies けが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of being injured or suffering an injury.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of する, connecting the earlier action or event with the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する, creating the main predicate “went to the hospital.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.why: 大きな modifies けが, and then けがをする describes being injured. The て form connects the injury with the result of going to the hospital in a natural order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: けがをしてから emphasizes “after being injured,” making the time point clearer than て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 大きいけが, but 大きな is also a natural form for directly modifying a noun before it in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.vi: Because I do not have enough money, I cannot buy it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.sk: N が + Vない + から + negative potential-form V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the thing that is in an insufficient state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the cause clause with the result and comes after the plain form of たりない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: かえません is the polite negative potential form, expressing that the speaker cannot buy something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.why: The cause clause おかねがたりないから comes before the result かえません. たりない uses が because おかね is the thing being judged as sufficient or insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also means “because,” but is usually softer and more objective than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.tip: Do not confuse たりない with ない; たりない means “not enough” and always implies that a necessary amount is missing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q9.kobun.vi: I do not understand the meaning of this word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ことば with いみ, creating the phrase “the meaning of this word.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that is understood or not understood with わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: わかりません is the polite negative form, expressing that the speaker does not understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q9.kobun.why: このことばのいみ is a noun phrase in which の shows the relationship “of.” The whole phrase is the grammatical subject of わかりません and goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Using は makes “the meaning of this word” the topic, which can create a contrastive or emphatic tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t39-q9.kobun.tip: With わかる, Vietnamese speakers may easily use を following Vietnamese speech patterns, but the thing being understood usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.sk: N は + Time + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes これ the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: きのう shows the time when the studying took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 習いました is the polite past form of 習う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: は states the thing being discussed, きのう adds the time, and the past predicate comes at the end. The object is understood from the context, so it does not need to appear separately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 習います is used, the sentence will refer to the present or future instead of something studied in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put time words at the end because of Vietnamese speech habits, but Japanese usually puts them before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before the noun とけい to modify the watch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q10.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to create a noun phrase, and then を marks the object of the buying action. The verb in the ました form describes an action that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used here, the sentence would describe the existence of a watch rather than the action of buying it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the adjective after the noun, but Japanese puts 新しい before とけい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vi: I can see a blue building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective directly modifies the noun たてもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q11.kobun.why: 青い comes before たてもの to describe the building. With 見える, the thing seen usually goes with が because it is the object that appears before the eyes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If を見る is used, the meaning changes to actively looking at the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 見える when you want to say that something naturally comes into view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before 車 to limit the type of car being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: With 好きです, the object of liking is usually marked with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q12.kobun.why: 赤い modifies 車 to create the phrase “red car.” The pattern 好きです uses が to state the object that is liked, unlike ordinary verbs, which usually use を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes the process of starting to like a car, not only the current preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say 車をすきです, but 好きです usually goes with 車が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で refers to the group of people performing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb modifies the action of running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 走ろう is the volitional form of 走る, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q13.kobun.why: みんなで states who is participating, while いっしょに states how the action is performed. 走ろう comes at the end because it is the main invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to run, with less of a sense of inviting everyone to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q13.kobun.tip: 走ろう is the invitation “let us run,” not a direct command like 走ってください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb that indicates a point in time and modifies the action of sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 送って is the て form of 送る, connected to ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q14.kobun.why: すぐに is placed before the verb to state when the sending should happen. The て form connects to ください and turns the sentence into a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the statement has a stronger commanding tone and is usually spoken by someone in a higher position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form 送るください; before ください, there must be a verb in the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the body part that becomes painful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective いたい changes to いたく to connect to なる and express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, showing that the painful state has begun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q15.kobun.why: 足が is the object that undergoes the change, while いたくなりました expresses becoming painful. The adjective い must change to the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only describes the leg as hurting, without emphasizing the beginning or the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q15.kobun.tip: Before なる, an adjective ending in い must change い into く: 痛い → 痛くなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that is described as having a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 多い is an adjective ending in い that serves as the predicate; です comes after it to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q16.kobun.why: 車が is the object being described, while 多いです is the predicate that describes its quantity. With an adjective ending in い, simply add です to speak politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Changing が to は makes the sentence focus on the topic “cars”, often with a comparing or contrasting tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は instead of が when they only want to say simply that an object has a certain feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: 知って is the て form of 知る, used to connect with います and create the 知っている pattern that indicates the state of knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: いますか creates a polite question; in 知っていますか, いる expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q17.kobun.why: 知って connects to います in the て form to create 知っている, expressing the state of “knowing”, not the action of “knowing” in the usual sense. か at the end turns the sentence into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: 知りましたか asks whether someone has learned or received the information, focusing on the moment of learning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q17.kobun.tip: 知る should not be divided into 知っています based on the mechanical meaning “to be knowing”; it is a pattern that expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: 着いたら is a verb in the past form connected to たら, creating a conditional or time clause meaning “when you arrive”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: でんわして is the て form of でんわする, used to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to make a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.why: The clause 着いたら is placed at the beginning to state when the next action should happen. でんわしてください is the main request, in which the て form connects the verb to ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: 着いたとき only indicates the time “when someone has arrived”; it does not have the conditional or reminder tone of 着いたら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If 着いたら is omitted, only the request to call remains, with no stated time for calling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change the verb to the て form before ください and use the original form, such as でんわするください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q18.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.vi: I eat in the cafeteria at noon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ Place で ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks noon as the time or topic of the eating action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the action 食べます takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べます is the main predicate, using the polite form to describe the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.why: The time 昼は is moved to the front to set the context, followed by the place 食堂で to add where the action happens. 食べます comes at the end as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: 昼に directly indicates the time of eating, while 昼は emphasizes or limits the topic “noon”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for a place, but the place where an action occurs must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: I bought a pair of black shoes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 黒い comes before a noun to modify くつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the shoes as the object that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: かいました is the polite past form of 買う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: An adjective comes directly before a noun to describe it. An object noun uses を, followed by a past-tense verb at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is replaced with が, the black shoes become the subject rather than the object being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the adjective after the noun, but Japanese adjectives usually come before the noun they modify.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.vi: I went shopping with my younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who performs the action together with the speaker, meaning “together with my younger brother”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the purpose of going; かいものに行く means going to shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.why: 弟と states who went together, while かいものに states the purpose of 行きました. The verb 行く comes at the end and takes the past form to describe an action that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence focuses on the shopping action and does not use a structure meaning “go somewhere to shop” such as 買い物に行きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: Using に after 弟 makes the particle relationship incorrect because the person going together must use と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse と and に; と indicates a person who performs an action together, while に in 買い物に行く indicates purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: どの modifies 店, while が marks the store being asked about its low price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: 安い is the adjective serving as the predicate; ですか creates a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q21.kobun.why: どの店が is the subject phrase, in which どの comes before the noun to ask which choice. 安いですか comes at the end to ask which store is cheap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: どれ can stand alone with the meaning “which one”, so it does not come directly before a noun like どの店.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: Using は makes 店 the topic and may create a contrast between stores.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use どれ店, but どの must be used before a noun: どの店.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.kobun.vi: I do not know the way well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object being discussed in the act of not understanding clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: よく is an adverb that modifies わかりません and indicates the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: わかりません is the negative predicate of わかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.kobun.why: 道が is the object that is understood or not understood, so が is used. よく comes before わかりません to add the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あまりわかりません, the meaning is that the person does not understand much, with a weaker tone than よくわかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with わかる, but this verb usually uses an object with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q22.tokens.3.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: たくさん is an adverb of quantity that modifies the action of selling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 売って uses the て form to connect the verb to います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 〜ています indicates a continuing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q23.kobun.why: たくさん modifies 売っています, while 売っています creates a pattern describing something being sold or currently available for sale. The て form connects directly to います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 売ってあります is used, it describes a state prepared by someone, which does not fit the meaning of currently selling goods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ています only as “already”, but here it emphasizes a state that is continuing or exists now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the clothes as the thing being changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: かえました is the polite past form of かえる and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q24.kobun.why: 服を is the object of the changing action, so を is used. かえました comes at the end of the sentence and shows that the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 着替えました is used, the specific meaning is that the person changed into a different set of clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse かえる, meaning “to change”, with かわる, meaning “to be changed or to change by itself”, and use the wrong particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: これは introduces the thing being asked about as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: だれの modifies 物 and asks who owns the thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 物ですか forms a polite question about the identity or ownership of a thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q25.kobun.why: これは makes the thing being asked about the topic, while だれの comes before 物 to form the phrase “whose thing.” ですか ends the polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If どの物 is used, the question asks “which thing,” focusing on a choice rather than the owner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put だれの after the noun, but in Japanese だれの must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vi: What time do you usually go to sleep?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.sk: Frequency ＋ N時ごろ ＋ Vますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも modifies the action of sleeping and shows a usual frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 何時 asks about the time, while ごろ adds the meaning of “approximately.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ねます is the polite verb form, and か turns the whole sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: いつも states a habit, 何時ごろ asks for an approximate time, and the verb for sleeping comes at the end. The particle か forms a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何時ごろ is replaced with 何時に, the question asks about a more specific time and no longer has the sense of “around what time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 何時までに is used, the sentence asks by what time one must go to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit ごろ or use に when expressing an approximate time, but ごろ is what creates the meaning “around.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: I do not have an older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who has or does not have something in an existence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes 姉 the topic being negated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: いません is the polite negative form of います, used for people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: わたしに identifies the person whose existence is being considered, while 姉は is the topic being discussed. いません denies the existence of an older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression also means that I do not have an older sister, but it makes わたし the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with いません, but a pattern that denies existence must use に and は／が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the new state or result after a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and expresses a change into a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: The noun 秋 comes before に to show the state that has been reached, and then なりました expresses that the change has been completed. Therefore, the sentence naturally means that autumn has arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: 秋です simply says that it is autumn, without emphasizing the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle に before なる, but a noun showing the result always needs to go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vi: Everyone, let us collect the trash together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the people who perform the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks ごみ as the object being collected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 集めてください uses the て form with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.why: みんなで shows the group acting together, ごみを shows the affected thing, and 集めてください comes at the end to form a request. The て form connects directly to ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 集めましょう changes the sentence into an invitation to collect the trash together, with a softer meaning than a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern expresses an obligation to collect the trash, not a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say 集めてください as a complete verb, but remember that 集めて is the て form of 集める.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vi: This is quite heavy, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the thing being pointed at the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ずいぶん modifies the adjective 重い and emphasizes its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 重い is an adjective ending in い that acts as the predicate describing this thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね is used at the end of a sentence to express a feeling and seek agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.why: これは introduces the thing being commented on, ずいぶん increases the degree of 重い, and ですね softens the comment and adds a shared feeling. The adjective comes before ですね without changing form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 重いですよ emphasizes the information more strongly for the listener and does not necessarily wait for agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily add だ after an adjective ending in い, but they must say 重いですね, not 重いだですね.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな comes before a noun to ask about its type or characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 色 as the object that is liked in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: すきですか forms a polite question about preferences.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.why: どんな directly modifies 色 to ask about the type of color, while が marks the object of the feeling of liking. すきですか comes at the end to complete the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 何色が好きですか asks specifically what color it is, while どんな色 can ask more broadly about the type or shade of color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 好き, but the object that is liked usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes かれ the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 心 as the subject that has the characteristic やさしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase 心がやさしい modifies 人 and creates a clause describing a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 人です is the main predicate and identifies him as a particular type of person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.why: The clause 心がやさしい comes before 人 to modify 人, like the phrase “a person with a kind heart.” かれは is the main topic, while 人です is the concluding predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: やさしい人です only says that he is kind and does not clearly state that his heart is the characteristic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t4-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese puts 心がやさしい before 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes that athlete the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb modifies the change expressed by the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the く form to connect with なる and show the result of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: なった is the past form of なる and completes the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ く ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.why: きゅうに shows how the change happens. The adjective before なる must change to the く form to connect and state the new condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 強くした means to make someone or something become strong and emphasizes the person causing the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q1.kobun.tip: Before なる, the adjective い must change い into く; do not say 強いなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects アメリカ with the noun that follows and shows that the literature belongs to or is related to America.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: しています expresses an action that is currently being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q10.kobun.why: The phrase アメリカの（ぶんがく） comes before を to clarify the object of study. を connects the noun phrase with the verb けんきゅうしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If アメリカ文学 is used, it forms a compound noun with the more concise meaning of the term “American literature.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget を before the verb 研究する because Vietnamese has no particle that marks the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.vi: This building was built 100 years ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.sk: N は + N から + quantity + N 前に + V受身ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this building the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point for calculating a period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the time when the building action took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: つくられました is the polite past passive form, describing the building as having been built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.cn: V受身形 + ました; N から; quantity + N 前に
