default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.why: 今から１００年前に identifies the time of construction by counting backward from the present. Because the topic is the building affected by the construction, the passive form つくられました is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If １００年前から is used, it means starting 100 years ago, not a point in time 100 years ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If つくりました is used, the person who built it is emphasized, while the current sentence emphasizes that the building was built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake １００年前に for "before 100 years" and forget that に marks one exact point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.vi: Do not ask other people right away. Try doing it yourself first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point of an action or approach.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person the speaker intends to ask.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ないで connects to the following clause, meaning to do the later action without doing the earlier one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the method or the person who directly performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: てみなさい combines the form て with みる to advise or ask someone to try doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.why: Clause 聞かないで states what should not be done first, and やってみなさい then states the recommended action. で in （じぶん）で shows how to perform the action independently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 聞かずに is used, the meaning is similar, but the style is more written and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If やりなさい is used, it only means "do it" and does not emphasize trying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ないで simply as "not do" and miss the meaning of "do not do this, then do something else."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q12.kobun.cn: Vないで; Nで; Vてみなさい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.vi: The shop we were looking for was in the basement of the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the search in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: This clause comes before 店 to describe which shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes 店 the topic of the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the place with 地下, while に indicates where the shop existed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: あった is the past form of ある, used for the existence of the shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.why: わたしたちがさがしていた comes before 店, creating a relative clause that identifies which shop. The phrase ビルの地下に indicates location, while あった is the past predicate showing existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If さがした店 is used, it only shows that the search was completed and does not emphasize the process of searching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, while Japanese always places it before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; Vている + N; N の N; N に + ある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.vi: Because there were children running in the hallway, I warned them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place where the children ran or ran along.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: はしっている comes before 子ども to describe the children who are running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that exists in the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason to the result and gives a softer explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: した is the past form of 注意する and serves as the main predicate for the action that was carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.why: はしっている子ども is a noun phrase in which the clause before it describes the children. いたので states the reason first, and 注意した is the result that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and conversational, and may sometimes sound more subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for places in every situation, but with verbs meaning to run through or along a route, を can mark the place of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q14.kobun.cn: Vている + N; N が + いる; V普通形 + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.vi: I will definitely return the money I borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: かりた comes before お金 to describe which money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the borrowed money the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies かえします and emphasizes certainty or determination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: かえします is the main predicate in the polite form, expressing the intention or action of returning the money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.why: かりた comes before お金 to identify the money being discussed. 必ず is placed before かえします to emphasize how certain the act of returning the money is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If きっと is used, it focuses on a confident prediction or expectation, while 必ず expresses a clearer promise or determination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 必ず as simply meaning "often," but this word emphasizes that something will certainly happen or must definitely be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q15.kobun.cn: Vた形 + N; 副詞 + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.vi: This ring is something my father made especially for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the ring the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who directly made the ring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes a word describing a quality into an adverb that modifies the action of making.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: てくれた expresses that another person did something helpful or beneficial for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ものです is used to explain or confirm the nature of the ring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.why: The sentence makes the ring the topic, then states who made it and how. The form てくれた shows that the ring was made for the speaker's benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with わざと, the meaning is that it was made intentionally, without the sense of making it especially or thoughtfully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may forget that くれた must be understood from the receiver's point of view and often carries a feeling of gratitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした to the noun that follows, modifying the class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the class with the preparation activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content for which preparation was done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q17.kobun.why: The two phrases の narrow the scope step by step: tomorrow → tomorrow's class → preparation for that class. を marks the activity performed with the verb しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 復習 is used, it means reviewing a lesson already studied, unlike 予習, which means preparing before the lesson.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily reverse the order of the phrase の; in Japanese, the modifying part always comes before the main noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.vi: I met my wife at a university in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the person met or the person met with, while は makes this phrase the topic with a contrastive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects にほん to the university being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the meeting took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 出会いました is the polite past form and describes meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.why: The person met is introduced first with とは. Then the place is put before the predicate and marked with で. This order makes the place of the meeting clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is omitted and only 妻と is used, the sentence simply says that the speaker met someone or met their wife, without a topic or contrastive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand と as “and,” but in 出会う, と marks the person the speaker met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.vi: The temperature dropped to 0 degrees this morning, so it was very cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ Quantity まで ＋ Vて ＋ とても ＋ Aい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this morning is the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject undergoing the change: the temperature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: まで indicates the limit to which the temperature dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the temperature drop with the cold condition that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the adjective さむい to show a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the time, then gives the temperature and how far it dropped. The form て connects the change in temperature with the result: feeling very cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 冷たい is used, it usually describes an object or drink that is cold to the touch or taste, not cold weather directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 冷たい instead of 寒い, but 寒い is used for weather or a cold feeling in the body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.vi: There are only three copies of this book in the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Range に ＋ Quantity しか ＋ ない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this book the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the range of existence or distribution.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: しか is used with the negative form ない to limit the remaining quantity to three.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ない is the negative existence predicate and completes the pattern しか〜ない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.why: この本は introduces the object being discussed, while 世界に limits the range of existence. ３さつしか is used with ない to emphasize the small and limited quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: だけある also means that there are only three copies, but it is more neutral than しか〜ない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q2.kobun.tip: しか must always be used with a negative predicate; do not use ３さつしかある to say that there are only three copies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.vi: Clearly state the reason you were late for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に is used with おくれる to show being late compared with the class time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause おくれた comes before the noun and modifies the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the reason that must be stated clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: きちんと modifies 言いなさい and requires the speaker to explain fully and seriously.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: なさい is added after the stem form ます of a verb to give a relatively gentle request or command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.why: The clause おくれた comes before 理由 to identify which late arrival the reason belongs to. After the object 理由を, the adverb きちんと modifies the request 言いなさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 理由 is replaced with わけ, the sentence focuses more on a cause or explanation, while 理由 directly indicates the reason for being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places Vた before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.vi: I ordered food from a staff member at the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the ordering took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who receives the order request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food that was ordered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: ちゅうもんした is the past form of ちゅうもんする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.why: The place is put at the beginning and marked with で. The person receiving the request is used with に, while the food is the object used with を before the verb meaning “order food.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 店員と is used, the meaning may change to ordering food together with the staff member, not ordering food from the staff member.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と for every meaning of “with,” but when speaking to or making a request to someone, に marks the person receiving the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.vi: Only Japanese money can be used here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.sk: 場所 では ＋ N の ＋ N は ＋ negative potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: では indicates the place and emphasizes the scope where the sentence applies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun にほん with お金 to modify the type of money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the object being discussed the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative potential form expresses the inability to use something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.why: The place is stated first. Then the type of money is made the topic, followed by the ability to use it. の shows the relationship “money from Japan,” while は limits the object being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with だけ, the sentence emphasizes that only Japanese money can be used, giving a more direct limiting meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse は in this sentence with が; は indicates the scope or topic, not simply the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.vi: I woke up at noon today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ Time point に ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time reference for the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks when the action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ました is the polite past form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.why: きょうは sets the time context, while に identifies the specific time of the action. The verb is in the polite past form because waking up has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ごろ is used instead of に, the meaning is around noon, not a clearly specified time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out に before a clock time or time of day, but に is necessary when saying when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows possession and modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes Emma's essay the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い acts as the predicate and combines with です to make a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q24.kobun.why: The possessive phrase comes before the main noun. Then は marks the topic for the comment. The adjective い comes at the end of the sentence and takes です to keep the polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the focus shifts to Emma herself doing the main action of writing the essay, rather than simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put の after the possessed noun; in Japanese, the possessor comes first and is connected with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.vi: If you lose your card, please contact us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the card as the object of the action of losing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense verb clause modifies 場合, creating the meaning “the case of having lost the card.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 場合は states a situation as the condition for carrying out the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to complete the polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.why: The object of losing comes first. The past clause modifies 場合 to create the condition. After 場合は comes the action to take, ending with てください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 場合は is replaced with ときは, the sentence can also refer to a time or situation, but 場合は emphasizes a case that needs to be handled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate なくした場合 as two separate sentences; in fact, なくした directly modifies 場合.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vi: Although I was made to wait for a very long time, I still could not meet her.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: although I was made to wait
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects an event that happened with an unexpected result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person the subject wants to meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 会えなかった is the past negative potential form, expressing that the subject could not meet someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.cn: Vた + のに; V可能形 is the past negative form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.why: The first clause states that the subject had to wait for a long time. Then のに creates a contrast with the result of not being able to meet her. に marks the person as the object of meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: のに対して is used to contrast two objects or situations, so it is less natural than のに in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: ても also expresses concession, but it has a more hypothetical or conditional meaning than のに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 会えなかった as “did not meet,” but the potential form shows that the subject was unable to meet her.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vi: Clearly state the reason why you were late for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.sk: Vた + N + を + adverb + Vます omit ます+なさい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase before を modifies the noun meaning “reason.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content that is requested to be spoken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb modifies the verb 言いなさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: なさい follows the stem form ます to create a request or a mild command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Vます omit ます + なさい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.why: The clause before the noun identifies which reason it is. This noun takes を because it is the content of the speaking action, while きちんと shows how to speak.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is replaced with について, the sentence focuses more on the topic being discussed than on the exact content that must be said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that a clause modifying a noun must come before the noun, not after it as in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vi: Large vehicles cannot pass beyond this point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the area ahead as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes large vehicles the objects being considered and creates a contrastive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before こと to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the action into a noun, while が marks the action as being considered in terms of possibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ことができない expresses the inability to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.why: この先は identifies the location range, while 大きな車は states the type of vehicle being considered. The verb is nominalized with こと and then combined with できない to express impossibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vられない is used, the sentence can also mean that something cannot be done, but it usually focuses on the subject's ability or conditions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ことができない with the direct negative of the verb and forget to keep が before できない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる/できない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vi: In winter, it gets dark earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects the seasonal change with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: なる expresses a change, while の turns the whole phrase into a noun and が marks the subject being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: なった is the past form of なる, showing that the change has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.cn: Nに + なる; Aい omit い + くなる; V普通形・Aい・Aなな + の
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.why: 冬になって states the situation in which the change occurs. The phrase くらくなる is nominalized with の and becomes the subject of the comment はやくなった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is used, the action phrase becomes the topic for explanation or comment, rather than remaining the subject with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 暗いなる, but an adjective ending in い must change to く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q7.kobun.vi: I will study hard until the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q7.kobun.sk: N まで + adverb + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: まで indicates the time limit until which the studying continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb phrase modifies the action of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q7.kobun.why: The time expression combines with まで to set the limit of the studying. The adverb comes before the verb to add information about how the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If までに is used, the meaning is to finish studying before or by the time of the exam at the latest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse まで, the time until which an action continues, with までに, the deadline for completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.vi: It looks like a typhoon will come from tomorrow through the day after tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.0.vi: from tomorrow through the day after tomorrow
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: から and にかけて together create a period extending from the starting point to the ending point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the typhoon as the subject of coming toward the area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: やってくる describes a thing or person moving toward the speaker or the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ようだ is placed at the end of a sentence to show a judgment based on signs or available information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state the expected period when something will happen. The typhoon is the subject, やってくる shows the direction it is moving toward, and ようだ makes the statement less certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: When そうだ is used, the sentence usually relies on appearance or direct signs and has a clearer sense that something is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: When らしい is used, the sentence emphasizes heard information or a judgment being passed on to others.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate にかけて as referring to only one point, but this pattern describes a whole period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q8.kobun.cn: Nから + Nにかけて; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ようだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q9.kobun.vi: My father was born in Hiroshima Prefecture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner to the noun 父.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks “my father” as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the place where the birth took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q9.kobun.why: わたしの shows the possessive relationship with 父. The place uses で because it is where the birth took place, and the predicate is then put in the past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: に生まれた can also show a place of birth, but で emphasizes the place where the event took place more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t40-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for every location, but a place where an action or event takes place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.vi: The person over there is my older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.sk: Place に + Vている のは + N の + N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows where the person being discussed exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の nominalizes the clause いる, while は makes the whole phrase the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects わたし to the following noun for a family member.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: です connects the topic to the description and forms a polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.why: に identifies where the person exists. The clause いる is nominalized with の and then uses は as the topic, while です identifies who the person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If のが is used, the focus is on the fact that the person there is my older sister, rather than on the introductory structure “as for the person there...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand のは as a separate word; here, の turns the whole clause いる into a noun, and then は marks the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.vi: I bought a watch in England.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase is the thing being bought, so it functions as the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing affected by the action 買いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 買いました is the polite past predicate and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.why: The place of purchase comes before で, while the thing bought comes before を. The verb 買いました is placed at the end of the sentence and shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence no longer correctly describes the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show the place where an action is carried out; with 買う, the place of purchase usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.vi: My grandfather often tells stories about old times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that my grandfather is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the action します and shows how often it occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 古い is placed before a noun to modify 時代.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 時代 with 話, forming the phrase “stories about that period”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the stories as the object being told.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 話をします is the predicate, in which 話をする describes telling stories or speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.why: よく modifies the action, while 古い comes before 時代 to describe the period. The phrase 古い時代の話 is grouped as the object before を, and then 話をします completes the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 古い時代の is replaced with 昔の, the meaning is still “about old times,” but the expression is shorter and more natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q11.kobun.tip: Place the adjective before the noun and use の to connect one noun with another; do not follow Vietnamese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.vi: I bought clothes at this store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: この is placed before a noun to identify the store being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase is the thing being bought and goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the clothes as the object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 買いました is the polite past predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.why: この modifies 店, forming the phrase “this store.” The place uses で, the object uses を, and the past-tense verb is placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If この店で is replaced with ここで, the meaning changes from “at this store” to “here,” without clearly stating the noun “store.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q12.kobun.tip: この must come before a noun, while ここ can stand alone to show a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.vi: You can see the sea from the rooftop of the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ビル to the following place, forming the meaning “the building’s rooftop.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the viewpoint or the starting point of what is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the sea as what is perceived in the structure 見える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 見えます describes a state in which something can be seen naturally, without emphasizing the person who sees it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.why: ビルの屋上から identifies the viewpoint, while 海が is what appears within the field of vision. 見えます is placed at the end because it is the predicate describing natural visibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見られます is used, the sentence emphasizes that someone can look at or view something, usually with an intentional sense of ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q13.kobun.tip: With 見える, things usually go with が; do not use を based on the usual pattern of the verb “to look” 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.vi: Please bring the bed into the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the bed as the thing being carried or transported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the destination of the action はこぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb はこぶ with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is a polite request pattern placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.why: The thing being transported uses を, and the destination uses に. The verb uses the て form to connect with ください and turn the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If へやに is replaced with へやで, the meaning becomes carrying something out inside the room, not carrying it into the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q14.kobun.tip: With verbs of movement or bringing something to a place, に shows the destination, while で shows where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q15.kobun.vi: It is hot today, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: Adjective い acts as the predicate and describes today's weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is used to confirm or share an impression with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q15.kobun.why: The sentence puts the time topic first with は, then uses an adjective to comment on it. ですね at the end gives a tone of agreement and gentle confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ですよ, the sentence focuses more on informing or emphasizing something for the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit は after the topic, but in a comment sentence, は is needed to state what is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.vi: Last week, I went to the zoo and had a lot of fun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning to set the time for the whole event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 行って is the て form of 行く, connecting the action of going with the comment that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: たのしかった is the past form of adjective い and describes a past experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: です gives the sentence a polite ending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.why: 先週 sets the time, どうぶつえんに states the destination, and 行って connects it to a comment about the result of the experience. The adjective is put in the past form because the event happened last week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 行ったあとで, the sentence would emphasize that the fun happened after going, instead of naturally connecting the two ideas.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use 行いて; verb 行く has the special て form 行って.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.vi: I think this dish is a little spicy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate a dish near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the dish is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 少し modifies からい and reduces the degree of spiciness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content that the speaker is thinking about or judging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: おもいます is the main verb and expresses the speaker's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.why: The dish is made the topic with は, and 少し reduces the degree of からい. The comment comes before と, while 思います follows it to state who gives the opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If 少し is omitted, the sentence states that the dish is generally spicy, without the nuance of being slightly spicy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with からいそうです, the meaning changes to “it seems spicy,” based on observable signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.tip: と in this pattern does not mean “and”; it marks the content of 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ と ＋ 思います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.vi: Please give me the low chair over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あちら with the following noun and forms a phrase referring to the chair over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: Adjective い comes before a noun to modify いす.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the chair as the thing being requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ください acts as the predicate of a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.why: あちらの and ひくい respectively modify いす and form a complete noun phrase. いすを comes before ください because it is the thing being requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あちらにあるいす, the sentence would emphasize that the chair is located over there, rather than only indicating its position with あちらの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q18.kobun.tip: Adjective い directly modifies the noun, so の is not added after ひくい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.vi: This pencil is thick, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate a pencil near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the pencil is the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: Adjective い acts as the predicate and describes the pencil's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね is used to confirm or share a comment with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.why: このえんぴつは creates a complete topic, and ふとい states its characteristic. ですね gives the comment a friendly tone and invites agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced by 太いです, the sentence is only a polite comment and does not ask for the listener's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q19.kobun.tip: Do not change adjective い into ふといなです; before です, it keeps the form い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to identify an object near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the plate as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: An adjective ending in い acts as the predicate and combines with です to speak politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q2.kobun.why: この comes before おさら because this demonstrative always directly modifies a noun. は makes the plate the topic, while the adjective at the end states its characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced by が, the sentence emphasizes that the plate is light, instead of simply describing the plate being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use この alone; この must go with a noun, while これ can stand alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.vi: I am studying because I want to become a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the result or status achieved with verb なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: なりたい expresses a desire, while から connects the reason to the studying action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: べんきょうして is the て form and connects the action verb with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ています expresses that the studying action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.why: いしゃに combines with なりたい to state the desired goal. から puts the reason first, and then べんきょうしています states the action continuing because of that reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced by ので, the reason becomes softer and more objective, but the cause-and-effect relationship remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If べんきょうしています is replaced by 勉強します, the sentence only says that the speaker will study or usually studies, without emphasizing that the studying is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.tip: With なる, a profession or status goes with に; do not say いしゃをなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q20.kobun.cn: N に なりたい ＋ から、; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q21.kobun.vi: This Japanese-style inn is very old.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes this inn the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies adjective 古い and indicates a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: 古い is an adjective ending in い that acts as the predicate; です gives it a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q21.kobun.why: The topic phrase comes before は, followed by the degree adverb and the adjective acting as the predicate. Adjective 古い directly describes the inn's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If とても is replaced by あまり〜ない, the meaning changes to “not very old.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that とても usually goes with an affirmative adjective or adverb to express “very.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.vi: My daughter is wearing a red coat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes the daughter the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun あか with コート to modify the coat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the coat as the object of the action of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects verb きる with います to form a pattern expressing the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes pattern ています and describes the state of wearing the coat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.why: The color comes before の to modify the coat, and the coat takes を because it is the object being worn. きています expresses the state of wearing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 着ました, it only says that the coat was put on and does not emphasize the state of wearing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse きています with “to be coming”; in this sentence, きる means wearing clothing on the upper body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Peter as the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination of the action 出かける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 出かけました is the polite past form of 出かける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q23.kobun.why: The person performing the action comes first, は, the destination comes before に, and the verb comes at the end of the sentence. The form ました shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 出かけました is replaced with 行きました, the sentence only emphasizes going to that place, not the idea of going out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after a place, but with 出かける, the destination usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q24.kobun.vi: This cafeteria is new and clean.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this cafeteria the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 新しくて is the て form of the adjective 新しい, connecting the first feature to the following one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: きれいです is the second predicate, adding another feature of the cafeteria.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q24.kobun.why: Both adjectives describe the same topic, so the first adjective uses the て form to connect to the following adjective. The feature at the end of the sentence serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 新しく、 makes the sentence more formal and more suitable for writing than 新しくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect 新しい and きれい with と, but when connecting two adjectives, 新しい must change to 新しくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.vi: There is a small art museum in that village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: には combines に with は, showing the location and emphasizing the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 小さい comes before a noun to modify the museum.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists at the stated location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: あります expresses the existence of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.why: The location is stated first with には. The thing that exists there goes with が, while あります comes at the end to complete the existence sentence. The adjective 小さい is placed directly before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of には, the sentence sounds unnatural because an existing location usually uses に or には.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use あります with people or animals; this pattern uses あります for objects and places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.vi: Please do not move because I am going to take a picture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb とる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I will take a picture
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the preceding clause to the reason for the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ないで connects the negative form with ください to request that someone not do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.why: The object しゃしん comes before とる and goes with を. The clause とるから gives the reason, and then ないでください makes a request not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a polite request not to do something, and it is softer than a direct prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to a request to do the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate から as only because, but in this sentence it connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.vi: Please gather at the airport at 9 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where everyone gathers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb あつまる with ください to create a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.why: The location and time come before the verb and use に, respectively. The verb あつまる changes to the て form to combine with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes an invitation or suggestion to do something together, rather than a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also expresses a command, but it is stronger and is usually used by a superior toward a subordinate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit one of the two particles に, but に after the location and に after the time have different functions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to specify アパート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes アパート the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ひろい is an い-ending adjective used as a predicate, and it combines directly with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q5.kobun.why: この modifies アパート, while は identifies this noun as the topic. The adjective ひろい comes before です to end the polite comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern is used with な-ending adjectives, while ひろい is a い-ending adjective, so な is not added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If a noun is used instead, the sentence becomes an identification or classification sentence, rather than a comment about a feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add な before です, but an い-ending adjective such as ひろい connects directly with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who has the feeling or preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that is liked in the structure 好きだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: すき is an な-ending adjective used as a predicate and combined with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.why: わたしは identifies the person who has the feeling, while カレーが identifies the object that is liked. 好き is an な-ending adjective, but in a polite sentence, な does not appear before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this verb is used instead, カレー must go with を, and the tone becomes more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 嫌いです is used instead, the structure stays the same, but the meaning changes to not liking or hating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 好き, but the object that is liked must go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q6.kobun.cn: N ＋ が ＋ 好きだ・好きです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.vi: The train has already arrived at the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 電車 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: もう modifies the state and shows that arriving at the station has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the verb つく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ついて is the て form of つく, connecting with います to show an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: ている expresses a resulting state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.why: 駅に is the destination of 電車, while ついています describes the state after the train has arrived. もう emphasizes that this state began before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If つきました is used, it only says that the action happened and does not emphasize the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern usually describes a state intentionally created by someone, so it does not fit a train arriving at a station by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ています as meaning only currently doing something, but with verbs of arrival, it usually indicates an established resulting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.vi: How many countries are there in the world?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.sk: N に は ＋ Number の ＋ N が ＋ あります か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the scope of existence, while は makes that scope the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: いくつの modifies the noun 国 to ask about quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the structure あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate showing that an object or thing exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: か changes a statement into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.why: に indicates the place where countries exist, and は highlights that scope. いくつの comes before 国 to ask about quantity, while が marks the subject that exists with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is omitted, the sentence only states the place where something exists, while に は emphasizes or limits the scope being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: います is used for people and animals, while 国 is used for things or units, so use あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse あります and います; countries, objects, and places use あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the self-introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content being said or the name used to introduce oneself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: もうします is the humble form of 言います, used when introducing oneself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q9.kobun.why: The topic is first stated with は, and then と marks the name being spoken. もうします comes at the end as the predicate and shows humble speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with です, the sentence simply means “I am Yamada,” without the humble tone of a self-introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often place です directly after the name, forgetting that ともうします is the polite and humble way to introduce oneself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t41-q9.tokens.4.m: to be called; to call oneself
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q1.kobun.vi: The moon was very bright yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with 月 to identify the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states that the moon is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: あかるかった is the past form of the adjective あかるい, while です keeps the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q1.kobun.why: きのうの sets the time for 月, and then 月は makes it the topic. Because the sentence describes a past state, the adjective あかるい changes to the form あかるかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あかるいです, the sentence changes to the present: the moon is bright now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often keep あかるい unchanged and only add です, but an adjective ending in い must change to あかるかった to show the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q10.kobun.vi: If you exercise your body, you will lose weight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks からだ as the object being exercised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: やせます is the main predicate, while よ is used to emphasize the information being conveyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q10.kobun.why: The object of the action goes with を, then the condition comes before と and the result comes after it. と is suitable because the weight loss is presented as a natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with うごかしたら, the sentence has a more hypothetical meaning, referring to one event or a specific situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often understand と in this pattern as “and,” but here it connects a condition with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that わたし is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ちり with じゅぎょう, showing which subject is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object evaluated as liked in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, expressing liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q11.kobun.why: The topic is stated with は, the subject is identified by the NのN phrase, and then が marks the object of the feeling 好き. In Japanese, 好き usually goes with が instead of を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Using を before 好きです is incorrect in this basic structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often say じゅぎょうをすきです, but with 好き they must use が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q12.kobun.vi: I borrowed a dictionary at the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the borrowing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks じしょ as the thing borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: かりました is the polite past form of かりる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q12.kobun.why: The place where the action happens comes before で, the object comes after を, and the verb ends the sentence. The past form shows that the borrowing already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the place refers more to where something exists or to a destination, not to where an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse で and に when saying “at” because both can sometimes be translated as “at.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that 母 is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part or aspect described as not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: わるいです is the adjective predicate い in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q13.kobun.why: The sentence makes the mother the topic, then identifies the aspect being evaluated as her health. The adjective わるい comes at the end to conclude that her condition is not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 病気です is used, the sentence states that the mother is sick, which is stronger than saying that her health is not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use からだをわるい, but the adjective わるい needs a subject or aspect used with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.vi: I make jam using grapes and sugar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects ingredients that are used together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the ingredient being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of using the ingredients with the action of making jam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the dish being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.why: The two ingredients are connected by と and together serve as the object of 使って. The clause 使って、 comes first to state the means or method leading to the action つくります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If を使って is replaced with で, the sentence focuses directly on the ingredient used to make jam and sounds shorter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use で in every situation, but を in を使って marks the thing being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.vi: I am copying the passage written by Murayama.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の appears in the modifying clause to indicate the person who wrote the passage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: 書いた is a clause in the plain form that comes before 文 to modify 文.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the passage as the object being copied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: Vている shows that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.why: The clause むらやまさんの書いた comes before 文 to identify which passage it is. Then 文を is the object of うつしています, and ている shows that the copying is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書いた is replaced with 書いている, the meaning changes to the passage Murayama is writing, without emphasizing that it has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.tip: Do not place の after the noun being modified; the modifying clause must come directly before 文.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to refer to a specific classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the classroom the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: さむい is an い adjective used as the predicate describing the classroom's state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: です comes after the adjective い to make the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q16.kobun.why: The noun is presented as the topic with は, and the adjective い directly serves as the predicate. です adds a polite tone at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If さむい is replaced with さむくないです, the sentence means that this classroom is not cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q16.kobun.tip: The adjective い keeps the ending い before です; it does not change to さむいなです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.vi: I have left my family and am living alone in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person or group involved in the separation or distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the act of separating with the state of living alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the state or manner in which the person lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the place where the subject lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: Vている indicates a state of residence that continues up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.why: わかれて、 states what happened first and connects it to the present state. で describes the state of being alone, while に identifies the place where the person lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 別れながら, the meaning becomes that the person is separating from the family while living in Japan at the same time, without clearly stressing the order of events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q17.kobun.tip: に is used for a place of residence with 住む, while で here indicates the state of 一人で, not a location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q18.kobun.vi: The test is about to end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the whole event and shows that it will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the test as the subject that ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q18.kobun.why: もうすぐ is placed at the beginning of the sentence to show that the event will happen soon. テストが is the subject, while おわります is the predicate showing that it ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If おわります is replaced with 終わっています, the sentence describes something that has ended or is in a finished state, not something that is about to end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 終わる in this sentence; the thing that ends is marked with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.vi: I do not understand the meaning of this kanji.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify a specific kanji.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the kanji with いみ, forming a phrase that means the meaning of the kanji.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the meaning as what is or is not understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりません is the polite negative form of わかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.why: このかんじのいみ forms a noun phrase in which の connects an object with something belonging to it. いみが is the grammatical subject of わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 知りません, the sentence means not knowing this kanji, which is different from not understanding its meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q19.kobun.tip: With わかる, the thing understood usually goes with が, not を as when talking about knowing or learning an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.vi: A large building is being built east of the harbor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: みなとの modifies 東 and identifies the harbor whose eastern side is meant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the location where the event is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな comes before the noun ビル to modify the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object being built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The form ている describes an action that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.why: The location phrase comes first, followed by the thing being built and the predicate. を marks the building as the object of the building action, while ている shows that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vました, the sentence says that the building has been completed or that the action has been carried out, without stressing that it is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly think that ています only means doing something now, but with some verbs it also describes a state that has already formed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.vi: I have gradually come to look like my father's face.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing a gradual change over time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 父 with the noun that follows, forming a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the object used to compare similarity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: にて is the て form of にる, connecting with くる to express a gradual change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: きました completes the pattern てくる and puts the sentence in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.why: The phrase 父の（かお）に identifies the object used for comparison, while にてきました describes similarity that has gradually developed up to the present. The adverb だんだん comes before the predicate to show the degree of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used, the sentence emphasizes beginning to reach a new state rather than a gradual change moving toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with にる, but the pattern for similarity uses にる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.vi: I have something to do tonight, so I will go home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the existence of something in the pattern ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I have something to do
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason clause with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: もう modifies an action that is about to happen or will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.why: The time is made the topic, then the reason is given with あるので before the resulting action. が marks ようじ as something that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place は after ようじ, but here は marks the time こんや.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな+な・N+な+ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q22.kobun.vi: There is a law exam tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q22.kobun.sk: Time N + N の + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to identify the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun ほうりつ with the noun for the exam that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks something that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q22.kobun.why: The time phrase あす comes first, followed by the noun phrase ほうりつの（しけん）, which is the subject of あります. The particle の shows the content or field of the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate の as “of,” but here it means “about law” and modifies the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q23.kobun.vi: I received medicine at the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q23.kobun.sk: N location で + N を + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of receiving medicine takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ました shows that the action was completed in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q23.kobun.why: The location びょういんで comes before the object and verb, creating the order “receive what where.” を directly connects the thing received with もらいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of で, the sentence is no longer natural because に does not indicate the place where the action of receiving takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for every location, but the place where an action takes place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.vi: A fire occurred in the nearby neighborhood last night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.sk: N の N + N location で + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with よる, forming a time phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase identifies when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the fire occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks an event that occurred or exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: あります describes an event occurring or existing at that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.why: きのうのよる creates the time reference, きんじょで states where it happened, and （かじ）が is the event being reported. For events such as fires, あります can describe something occurring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with おきました, the sentence emphasizes more clearly that the fire occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate あります only as “there is,” but with an event such as 火事 it can also mean “occur.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies the action of thinking and shows the degree to which it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: Vてから connects two actions in the order of first and then.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb こたえる with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after Vて to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.why: The Vてから clause places the action of thinking first as a condition in the sequence, and only then asks the listener to answer. ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If あとで is used, the sentence only states the time “after that” and does not emphasize a close sequence linked to the previous action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the dictionary form before から, but this sequence pattern uses Vてから.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q25.kobun.cn: Vて + から; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.vi: The wind blowing from the mountain is very strong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ふく is a clause that modifies the noun かぜ that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes かぜ the topic in order to describe the characteristics of that wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: つよいです is an adjective predicate that describes how strong the wind is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.why: The clause ふく comes before かぜ to identify what kind of wind it is. After introducing the topic with は, the adjective つよいです acts as the predicate describing the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this sentence is used, the focus is on the action of the wind blowing from the mountain, not on whether the wind is strong or weak.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 山からふくかぜ in Vietnamese word order and overlook that the clause comes before the noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q4.kobun.vi: I will return to my hometown next week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: 来週 indicates the time when the return will take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination of the return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: かえります is a verb in the polite form and the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q4.kobun.why: The time adverb comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the destination with に, and then the verb describing the action of returning. The subject is omitted because it can be understood from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: へ also indicates movement toward the hometown, but emphasizes direction more than the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で with いなか, but で only indicates the place where an action takes place; a destination must use に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that is in the stated condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: しんでいます describes the current state of being dead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q5.kobun.why: むしが is the subject of the state, while しんでいます is the predicate. With a verb showing a change of state such as 死ぬ, ている usually indicates that the result still exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 死にました is used, the sentence emphasizes that the event of the insect dying has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand 死んでいます as “is dying,” but this sentence naturally means that it is in a dead state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: みじかい comes before スカート to modify the skirt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the skirt as the object being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いました is the polite past form and shows that the purchase was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q6.kobun.why: The adjective comes directly before the noun it describes. That noun goes with を as the object, followed by the past-tense verb to complete the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買っています is used, the sentence means that the speaker is buying it or has bought it and still has the related state, depending on the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the adjective after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese puts the adjective before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.vi: The bird is flying over the sea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the bird as the subject that is flying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects うみ with 上, forming the phrase “above the sea.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を indicates the space or route through which the bird flies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: とんで is the て form, connecting the main verb with います to create the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern とんでいます and describes the flying action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.why: が identifies the subject, の creates the location phrase, and を marks the space through which the bird flies. The て form connects とぶ with いる to describe an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the place where the action occurs, while を emphasizes the space or route of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for every location, but a movement verb such as flying through a space can use を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun before it with 本 and shows the type of book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 本 as the object being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いました is the 買う verb in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q8.kobun.why: The book-type phrase comes first with の, followed by the object with を and the verb at the end. This order clearly shows the thing bought and the completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of の, the ownership or classification relationship is not natural in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の when using one noun to modify another noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.vi: I am working at a watch factory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows that 工場 is a factory that produces or is related to clocks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the action of working takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects はたらく with います to form an expression for an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: います makes it clear that the action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.why: The phrase とけいの modifies the place, while で identifies the workplace. The form Vている describes an action that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence can shift to mean existence or movement toward a place, without emphasizing where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If はたらきました is used, the sentence only says that the person worked, so it no longer means that the person is working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t42-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で when talking about the place where an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q1.kobun.vi: I want to go somewhere far away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q1.kobun.sk: 疑問語 + + Aい + N へ + V without ます + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: とおい modifies ところ, while へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きたい is the form たい added after the stem form without ます of 行く, expressing the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q1.kobun.why: どこか indicates an unspecified place; とおいところ is a noun phrase in which the adjective modifies ところ. The particle へ marks the direction of movement, while たいです is placed at the end to express desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing へ with に is also correct and natural, but に emphasizes the destination more than the direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake たい for “like,” but the pattern V without ます + たい expresses “want to do” at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.vi: I am planning to go flower viewing tomorrow evening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: あしたの modifies 夜, identifying the time as tomorrow evening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 夜 indicates when the flower-viewing action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the purpose of going.
