default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 行こう is the volitional form, and と marks it as the content of a thought or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 思っています expresses a thought or plan that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, 花見に states the purpose of going, and 行こうと 思っています express the content of the plan. The volitional form combines with と to quote what the speaker is thinking or planning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence expresses a clearer and firmer intention, while 思っています focuses more on a current thought or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use 行くと思っています when you want to clearly state your own plan; 行こうと 思っています is more suitable for an active intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where the car is parked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the car as the object of the parking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ないでください forms a polite request meaning “please do not perform that action.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q11.kobun.why: ここに indicates the parking place, 車を indicates the object affected, and ないでください is placed at the end to make a request not to perform the action. Its final position makes clear that this is the main instruction to follow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a stronger rule or prohibition, rather than just a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を after 車, but the verb とめる needs を to mark the object that is parked or stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.vi: I do not use much oil when cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the scope or object to which the use of oil applies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり is used with a negative sentence to express a low degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks oil as the thing being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: つかいません is the polite negative form of つかう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.why: りょうりに states the scope of use, あまり modifies the degree, を marks the oil, and つかいません completes the negative predicate. あまり combines with a negative form to express “not very” or “not much.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If あまり is used in an affirmative sentence, the structure sounds unnatural because あまり usually needs to be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q12.kobun.tip: Do not translate あまり as “very”; in a negative sentence, it usually means “not much” or “not very.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.vi: Since this month, the weather has become cool.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the starting point of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: てから connects the previous action or state with what happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the く form to modify なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: なる expresses a change of state; なりました is the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.why: The time expression comes first with に, followed by てから to state the starting point. The adjective い must change to く before なる to express becoming cool.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is omitted, the sentence only says that the weather has become cool, without emphasizing the starting time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave the adjective い unchanged before なる, but い must be changed to く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.vi: If there is anything you do not understand, ask the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the thing that is not understood the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who receives the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: This noun combines with する to form a verb meaning “to ask.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう is the polite suggestion form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.why: The thing that is not understood is presented as the topic, while the teacher is the person being asked, so it takes に. The noun しつもん combines with する and then changes to しましょう to make a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 聞きましょう means “ask the teacher” or “listen to the teacher,” which is broader than asking a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the person being asked; the receiver of a question usually takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.vi: I like math more than language arts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person expressing the preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: より sets the object as the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the preferred object in the pattern すきです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです is the polite predicate expressing a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.why: より indicates the subject used as the comparison standard, while が marks the subject that is liked. This order creates the pattern “AよりBがすきです,” meaning “like B more than A.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Using のほうが emphasizes the preferred side, equivalent to “like B more.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: Using も changes the meaning to “also like,” so there is no longer a comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q15.kobun.tip: With すきです, the thing that is liked usually takes が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.vi: During summer vacation, I plan to go to the beach.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time or situation of the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb 行く comes before つもりです to express a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.why: Summer vacation is given as the background, and the sea is the destination, so へ is used. The dictionary-form verb connects with つもりです to turn the action of going into a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: 予定です usually emphasizes a decided plan or a more specific schedule than つもりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: たいです only expresses a wish to do something; it is not necessarily a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.tip: つもりです is usually connected to a verb in dictionary form when talking about plans to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Nの + つもりだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.vi: This is a park for local residents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the place being presented.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: This noun combines with の to modify ため.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: のための connects the beneficiary or purpose to the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the predicate that introduces the type of place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.why: The place is stated first, and then the phrase のための modifies こうえん. The relationship の connects the residents with the purpose or the people being served.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: ために is usually connected to a verb to say what someone does for whom or for what purpose. It does not directly modify a noun like ための.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q17.kobun.tip: Before a noun, use ための; before a verb, usually use ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.vi: Is it far from the station to the school?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point of the distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: まで marks the ending point of the distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: とおい is an adjective used as the predicate to comment on the distance between two places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ですか turns the statement into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.why: The distance is presented using the pair of starting point から and ending point まで. The adjective とおい is the predicate, while ですか creates a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the negative form to ask for confirmation that the distance is not far.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 近いですか asks instead whether the distance is close.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q18.kobun.tip: In questions about distance, remember to use から for the starting point and まで for the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q19.kobun.vi: This city has many friendly shops.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective ending in な with the noun みせ to modify the shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い is a predicate that expresses quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q19.kobun.why: The topic is stated first with は. Then the phrase 親切な店 becomes the subject of the quality 多い. An adjective ending in な must use な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な when placing an adjective ending in な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q2.kobun.sk: その + N は + past Aい + です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: その comes before a noun to identify the box being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks はこ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: おもかった is the past form of the adjective ending in い おもい. It combines with です to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q2.kobun.why: その modifies はこ, and then は makes the box the topic. The adjective at the end of the sentence is the predicate and uses the past form to describe a state that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Using おもいです changes the meaning to “heavy” in the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q2.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い changes い to かった in the past. Do not add でした directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q20.kobun.vi: Please deliver it to my home instead of the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: ではなくて negates the noun before it and connects to the place chosen instead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place of receipt or the destination of the delivery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q20.kobun.why: The phrase ではなくて excludes the first place and connects it to the correct place with に. The てください verb is placed at the end to express a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ではなく sounds more formal and written, while ではなくて connects naturally to the following clause in speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use を with the delivery location; に marks the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q21.kobun.vi: Do you know the location of the post office?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun ゆうびんきょく with noun ばしょ to form a possessive phrase or relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb しっています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: しっていますか creates a polite question about whether someone knows the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q21.kobun.why: The noun ばしょ is clearly identified as the post office's location through の, and then becomes the object of 知っています. か at the end turns the sentence into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q21.kobun.tip: しっています describes a state of knowing, not only the act of knowing at one moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.vi: In the evening, when it is cool, I will go for a walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: すずしくなる describes a change into a cool state, while たら connects the condition to the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: This is the main action that occurs when the condition is met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.why: The time is placed first, followed by the conditional clause すずしくなったら. The main action さんぽします comes after the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with なれば makes the sentence sound more hypothetical or formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, change い to く before なる: すずしくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q22.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった + ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.vi: If you take the Shinkansen, you will reach Osaka in about three hours.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the means of transport used in the action 使う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition or method with a naturally occurring result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the time needed to achieve the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the destination of the verb つく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: つきます is the main predicate and describes arriving in Osaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.why: The means of transport comes first and is the object of 使う. と connects the method with a natural result, while で states the time needed and に states the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Using なら gives a hypothetical meaning or a suggestion based on a condition. It does not emphasize an inevitable result like と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q23.kobun.tip: Distinguish を, which is used with the means of transport, from に, which is used with the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.vi: It may be a mental illness rather than a physical illness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.ch.0.vi: rather than physical; compared with the body
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: より introduces the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects こころ with びょうき, forming a phrase meaning related to or belonging to the mind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: かもしれません is placed at the end to express an uncertain guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.why: より sets the physical body as the comparison standard, then の forms the phrase 心の病気. かもしれません comes at the end because the whole sentence is an uncertain guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with はずです changes the meaning to having a stronger basis for believing it is true, rather than making a weak guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.tip: より does not mean “more than” in every independent situation; it needs a side or content to compare.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q24.kobun.cn: N・V普通形・Aい・Aなな ＋ かもしれない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.vi: Autumn in Japan has beautiful red leaves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with the noun that follows, creating the meaning “autumn in Japan”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes autumn in Japan the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing being described as wonderful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.why: The phrase 日本の modifies the topic あき, while こうようが is the subject that has the quality すばらしい. The particle は limits the topic, while が identifies the thing being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with では, the sentence emphasizes the scope “in Japan” more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If こうようは is used, the red leaves become the topic, and the contrast is clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put を before すばらしい, but this adjective is usually used with が to state the thing that has the quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects メイさん with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks じゅうしょ as the object of the action おしえて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request or ask someone for a favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q3.kobun.why: メイさんのじゅうしょ forms a noun phrase in which the address belongs to Mei. This phrase takes を because it is the information being provided, while てください comes at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern becomes a question asking the listener to provide the address, so it sounds softer and more like asking permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use に to mark the thing being mentioned or provided; the direct object of the verb usually takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q3.tokens.1.m: Mr./Ms.; a respectful form of address
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.vi: Please show me that black box.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to point to something far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: くろい modifies はこ, while を marks the box as the object being shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 見せて is the て form of 見せる, used to connect with ください in a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ください completes the 見せてください pattern, meaning that the listener is asked to show something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.why: あの and くろい respectively identify the position and quality of はこ. はこ takes を because it is the thing being shown, while the て form connects the verb with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression asks whether the listener can show it, so it sounds softer and more like asking permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q4.kobun.tip: くろい is an adjective that directly modifies a noun, so だ or の is not added before はこ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.vi: I pass in front of the post office.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ゆうびんきょく with 前 to form the phrase “in front of the post office.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the place or route that the speaker passes through with the verb とおる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: とおります is a polite predicate that describes passing through a place or along a route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.why: ゆうびんきょくの前 is a location phrase in which 前 is identified using the post office. With とおる, を can mark a route or place being passed through, not only an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence keeps the same structure but uses the dictionary form in ordinary speech instead of とおります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Changing とおります to 行きます means going to the area in front of the post office, rather than emphasizing passing by it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を only for objects; with movement verbs such as とおる, を also marks the route being passed through.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.vi: During the summer vacation, I will go to Hokkaido with my family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ Companion で ＋ Destination へ ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates when the action of going to Hokkaido takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the people who participate together or the means used to carry out the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: へ marks the direction of movement to Hokkaido.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the polite form of 行く and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to give the context, followed by the companion and the destination. The particle で indicates the companion, while へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: と also means “together,” but it emphasizes doing the action together with the family more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: に emphasizes Hokkaido as a specific destination, while へ emphasizes the direction of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q6.kobun.tip: で in 家族で does not mean “at” or “by”; here it indicates the person participating in the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q7.kobun.vi: For dinner tonight, I will choose a boxed meal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the phrase “tonight's dinner” the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the result or choice being aimed at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: する in the polite form します expresses a decision or choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q7.kobun.why: The topic phrase comes first, followed by the choice with に and then します. The pattern にします is suitable when the speaker decides to choose a dish or an option.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning changes to “eat a boxed meal,” describing the action of eating rather than emphasizing the decision to choose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before the chosen dish, but the decision pattern uses にします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.vi: I received a letter from a friend in Kyoto.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Nの modifies 友だち, showing that the friend is connected with Kyoto.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から indicates the source or the place from which the letter was sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that arrived, namely the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ました is the polite past form of 来る, describing an event that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.why: Nの modifies a noun referring to a person, から indicates the source, が marks the thing that arrived, and 来ました serves as the main predicate. This order sounds natural when describing something sent by someone and then arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker received a letter from a friend, rather than emphasizing that the letter arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q8.kobun.tip: Do not confuse から, which indicates the source, with に, which indicates the recipient or the target.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.vi: The package arrived one day later than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.sk: N が ＋ N より ＋ Duration ＋ Vて ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the package as the subject of arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle より creates a point of comparison, meaning later than the expected time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: １日 states the amount of difference, while おくれて adds the state of being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: とどきました is a polite past predicate that shows the package arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.why: よていより sets the point of comparison, １日おくれて states how late it was, and then とどきました ends the event. The て form of おくれる connects a state or condition with the action of arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 遅く is used, the sentence focuses on the late arrival time; 遅れて focuses on the condition of being delayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t43-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mechanically translate より as “more than,” but here it creates the point of comparison “than expected.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.vi: Please write the answer with a pencil.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テスト with こたえ, creating the phrase “the answer to the test.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the answer as the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the tool used to perform the action of writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 書いてください uses the て form together with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.why: The answer is introduced first with は. Then the writing tool is placed before the verb with で. The Vてください pattern comes at the end to turn the action of writing into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 書きなさい, the sentence has a stronger command-like tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書いてもいいです is used, the sentence becomes a question or gives permission to write.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate で as “at” in every case; here で indicates a tool or means.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: With きらい, が marks the object that the speaker dislikes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: きらい is a な adjective used as the predicate, so it combines with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q10.kobun.why: わたしは states the person who has the feeling, while すうがくが is the object of that feeling. Words for likes or feelings, such as きらい, commonly use が for the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If をきらいます is used, the sentence uses a verb and sounds more direct; the Nがきらいです pattern is more natural and basic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is used after 数学, math becomes the topic of comparison, which may imply that other subjects are not necessarily disliked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use を because of the verb “hate,” but きらいです usually uses N が for the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.vi: I hear that the weather will be clear tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks tomorrow as the time being predicted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: はれる is a dictionary-form verb placed before そうです in the pattern for reporting information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです at the end of the sentence shows that the speaker is reporting a forecast or information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.why: The time marker あしたは comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the predicted content. Because そうです means reported information, the verb はれる stays in the plain form before this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If はれそうです is used, it means the weather seems likely to clear soon based on current signs, not that the speaker heard it from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If はれるでしょう is used, the sentence expresses the speaker’s guess or forecast and does not emphasize an outside source of information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse そうです for reporting聞 with そうです, which only describes appearance; before a reporting pattern, the verb must use the plain form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.vi: I will study in Japan starting next month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.sk: N time から ＋ N place で ＋ Nをする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the time when the action begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where studying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the polite form of the verb する and forms the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.why: The starting point comes before the place, followed by the main action. The particle で is attached to the place where studying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence sounds unnatural because に is not used to indicate the place where studying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use に for every place; remember that the place where an activity takes place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.vi: I have liked swimming since I was little.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 子どもの modifies とき, creating the meaning “when I was little.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the time when the liking began.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object described as すき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: すき is a な adjective, while でした expresses a past state of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase 子どものときから is placed at the beginning to state the starting point. With すき, the thing that is liked goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the present-tense expression; use でした in this sentence to talk about a past liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Using を with すき is incorrect in this basic structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate “like” as a verb and use を, but すき usually uses N が好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.vi: I am growing many kinds of vegetables at home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.sk: N place で ＋ Aな ＋ N を ＋ Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the vegetables are grown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろな modifies the noun, while を marks the object of つくっています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ている expresses an ongoing action or a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the verb. いろいろな must come directly before the noun to modify it, while を connects that noun to the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Do not use いろいろの in the basic structure; いろいろなN is the correct connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes an action that is in progress or being maintained, unlike つくります, which only describes a general or future action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.tip: Do not omit な before the noun: say いろいろな野菜, not いろいろ野菜.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q14.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ N; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.sk: Time adverb ＋ N が ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the predicate and shows that the event will happen shortly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of starting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ます creates the polite form; the verb はじまる is intransitive, so the concert goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.why: もうすぐ comes first to add a time reference to the action. Because はじまる is intransitive, the event that starts is marked with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If を始めます is used, someone actively starts the concert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ました means that the concert has already started, so it is no longer an upcoming event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q15.kobun.tip: Distinguish 始まる, which goes with が, from 始める, which goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.vi: Can I use a card here?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.sk: N place は ＋ N が ＋ potential V ますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being asked about and creates a contrastive tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that can potentially be used in the potential structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: つかえます is the polite potential form of つかう, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.why: ここは sets the location being asked about, while カードが is the object that can be used. The potential form uses が to mark the object that can perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence asks whether a card can be used, not whether the card is permitted or able to use something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Changing it to the negative means that the card cannot be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q16.kobun.tip: In a potential sentence, learners may easily keep を; at a basic level, remember that the object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q17.kobun.vi: Please do not forget the phone number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: も replaces を and adds the meaning “also/too,” marking something that must not be forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: Vないでください is used to politely ask the listener not to do that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q17.kobun.why: The mentioned object comes before the request pattern at the end of the sentence. も connects to a noun to add the phone number to the things that must not be forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてください, the sentence becomes a request to do that action, which is the opposite of “do not forget.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This form also means “do not do,” but it is more casual and less polite than ないでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q17.kobun.tip: Do not mistake ないでください for “not do”; here, it is the polite request pattern “please do not do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.vi: The movie I watched yesterday was very interesting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.sk: Time expression ＋ Vた ＋ N は ＋ Degree adverb ＋ Aい past tense
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to modify the action of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: A verb in the past tense modifies the noun that follows it and creates a relative clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は marks the movie as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb modifies the adjective おもしろかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い changes to the past tense to describe the feeling after watching the movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.why: The clause きのう見た comes before the noun to identify which movie it is. After the topic は, the adjective in the past tense expresses an evaluation of the movie that was watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, it only describes the action of watching a movie and does not create a clause that modifies a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put a relative clause after the noun, but Japanese always puts the modifying part before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.vi: I want to dye my hair slightly brown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.sk: NのN を ＋ Degree ＋ Nに ＋ Vたいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the noun かみ to the following noun and shows possession or a part-whole relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object whose color is changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing the slight degree of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the state or color reached after the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: する combines with たい to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.why: The phrase かみのけ refers to the hair and is the object of を. The pattern Nにする expresses making the object change to a certain color, while したい expresses the desire to do this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ちゃいろになる is used instead, it means that the hair itself becomes brown, without emphasizing that the speaker wants to change its color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may habitually use に with places, but in Nにする, に only marks the result after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.vi: If you do not practice kanji many times, you will not be able to remember it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 回数も ＋ Vないと ＋ negative potential verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents kanji as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: も after a word showing the number of times emphasizes repeated practice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ないと creates a negative condition, meaning “if one does not do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: られません expresses ability in the polite negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.why: The kanji topic is placed at the beginning of the sentence, while なんかいも modifies the action of practicing. The conditional clause ないと comes before the result, “cannot remember,” and shows a necessary condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vなければ, the conditional meaning is similar, but the tone is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vないといけない is used, the sentence talks about the duty to practice, not only a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ないと in this sentence with と, which means quotation; here, it connects the condition “if not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.vi: What time does the library open?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time point から ＋ Vている か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the library the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the time when the open state begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: あいています describes the state of being open, while か turns the whole sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.why: After stating the library as the topic, the question asks when its open state begins. から comes after the time point, while Vている describes a state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with まで, the question asks until what time the library is open, meaning the ending time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake から for a marker of cause, but here から marks the starting point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.vi: I am washing dishes at a restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.sk: Place で ＋ N を ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the place where the washing action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the plate as the object of the washing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the form ている describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.why: The place where an action happens uses で, while the affected object uses を. The form あらっています shows that the washing is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If レストランで is replaced with レストランに, に only shows a destination or a place of existence, so it is not suitable for showing where the washing action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q21.kobun.tip: A common mistake is to use に for every place, although the place where an action happens requires で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.vi: Let’s take a boxed lunch and go see the flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vて ＋ Purpose に ＋ Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the boxed lunch as the thing being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of carrying the boxed lunch to the action of going in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the purpose or destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: いきましょう is the れんよう form of the verb, used to invite or suggest doing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.why: The action of carrying the boxed lunch comes first and connects to 行く in the て form. お花見に shows the purpose of going, while ましょう creates the meaning of inviting someone to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If いきましょう is replaced with いってください, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to go, rather than an invitation to go together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand に in お花見に as a place, but here it emphasizes the purpose of going to see the flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q23.kobun.vi: I forgot to do my homework.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the homework as the object of the action of doing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the action する into a noun, so the whole act of doing homework becomes the object of わすれました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb わすれる in the polite past tense expresses that the forgetting happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q23.kobun.why: しゅくだいを is the object of する, and then するのを makes the whole action of doing homework the object of わすれる. The two particles を have different functions at the two structural levels.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことを忘れる is used, the basic meaning is still forgetting to do something, but the expression is more general and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out one of the two particles を, but each を marks the object of a different verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action of driving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: して is the て form, connecting the action of driving with the action of going camping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the verb 行く in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q24.kobun.why: The noun 車 goes with を because it is the object used in the action of driving. The て form connects driving with going, while に marks the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out を before the verb because Vietnamese usually says “drive a car” directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.vi: The university cafeteria has many kinds of meals and is inexpensive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 大学 with the following noun to show a possessive relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the university cafeteria the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: いろいろな modifies the noun メニュー.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks what exists in the clause ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: あって is the て form of ある, connecting having meals with the comment that they are inexpensive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: 安いです is an adjective predicate ending in い in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.why: 大学の食堂 forms the noun phrase “the university cafeteria.” After stating the topic with は, the sentence says that the cafeteria has many meals and then describes it with 安いです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If には is used, the emphasis on the place or object “as for the cafeteria” becomes clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use の like the word “of” in every position, but here の must stand between two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.vi: When I was young, I often caught insects in the mountains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with とき, forming a phrase meaning “when I was a child.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates the time when the action in the main clause happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies とりました and indicates the frequency of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the place where the action of catching insects took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks insects as the object of the action of catching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: とりました is the polite past form of the verb とる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.why: The phrase 子どものとき is placed at the beginning to set the time, and then よく indicates frequency. The place uses で, while insects use を because they are the direct object of とる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 山で is replaced with 山に, に usually indicates a direction or a point where something exists, so it is less natural than で for the action of catching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If むしが is used, insects become the subject rather than the object being caught.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the place of an action, but the place where an action happens usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.vi: I can make clothes by myself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で emphasizes that the person does it alone, without asking someone else to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks clothes as the object being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb combines with こと to turn the whole action into a noun, and then が marks the action as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ことができます expresses the ability to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.why: The action of making clothes is nominalized with こと to become the subject of できます. じぶんで adds the meaning of doing it oneself, while ようふくを marks the object of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If the potential form Vられます is used instead, the sentence still expresses ability, but the structure is shorter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてもいいです is used, the sentence means that doing something is permitted, not that it is possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.tip: Before ことができます, the verb must be in the dictionary form, not the ます form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.vi: What time does the bank's ATM operate until?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the bank with the ATM, forming the phrase “the bank's ATM.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the ATM the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: まで indicates the time limit when the ATM's operation ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ですか creates a polite question about the ending time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.why: The possessive phrase NのN comes before the topic ATM. 何時まで asks about the ending time and is placed directly before ですか to form a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is replaced with から, the question asks about the starting time instead of the ending time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This form asks directly “What time does it end?” and focuses more on the action of ending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q5.kobun.tip: まで means “until,” not “from”; “from what time” must use から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.vi: I accidentally wrote down the wrong house number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object that was mistaken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: まちがえてしまいました combines the て form with しまいました to express an action that has happened and carries a sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.why: The thing that was mistaken comes before を, followed by the main verb. The てしまいました form shows that the action has been completed, and the speaker usually feels regret or is apologizing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, it refers to accidentally making the mistake or completing the mistake in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the sentence simply says that a mistake was made, without a clear sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that てしまう means not only “finished” but also often expresses regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう/しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q7.kobun.vi: I will choose an outfit for tomorrow's date.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with the noun that follows and modifies that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the outfit as the object being chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q7.kobun.why: あしたの modifies the noun meaning date, while the noun phrase before を is the object of えらびます. Japanese places the modifying part before the head noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is replaced with に, あしたに does not connect directly with the noun to mean “of tomorrow.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If と is used, the two nouns are usually connected with the meaning “and,” so it does not show a possessive or time-related modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may place the modifying part after the noun, while Japanese places あしたの before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.vi: The map Yuko drew is very easy to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A clause in the past form comes before a noun to modify it; が marks the subject of 書いた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the noun modified by the preceding clause the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective that follows it and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりやすい is an adjective ending in い and serves as the predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.why: The clause ゆう子さんが書いた comes directly before the noun to identify which map it is. After the topic, とても modifies わかりやすい, and the whole phrase ends with an adjective predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書いた is replaced with 書いている, the meaning changes to the map Yuko is drawing or usually draws.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If わかりやすい is replaced with わかりにくい, the meaning changes to difficult to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a relative clause after the noun, but Japanese places it before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q8.kobun.cn: Vた／Vる ＋ N; Vます-stem ＋ やすい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.vi: The Tokyo subway is very complicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects とうきょう with the noun that follows to show possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the Tokyo subway as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.why: とうきょうの modifies the noun meaning subway. This noun phrase becomes the topic with は, and is then described with the adjective な ふくざつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, Tokyo becomes a destination or a place where something exists, rather than a modifier of the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this phrase is used, it means “complicated subway,” with the adjective before the noun instead of serving as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な when the adjective な comes before a noun, but な is not used when it comes at the end of the sentence before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t44-q9.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ N; Aな ＋ です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.vi: What time do you finish work today?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N ＋ Time point に ＋ Vますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: きょう indicates the time point referred to in the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: しごと is the object of the finishing action, with を omitted in natural speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time when the finishing action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ます makes the expression polite, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.why: 何時に comes directly before the verb to ask when something finishes. In spoken language, the noun しごと can appear without を when the listener already understands that it means the work to be finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with から, the sentence asks when the work starts instead of when it finishes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse に and で when talking about time; use に for a specific time point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.vi: Since there are only 5 minutes left, let us run.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: しか goes with the negative form ありません to emphasize that the remaining amount is very small.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.ch.1.vi: because there is not enough left
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects a reason clause to a suggestion in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう attaches to the continuative form of a verb to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.why: しか always goes with a negative form to limit the remaining amount to only 5 minutes. から gives the reason first, and then ましょう gives an invitation to run together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only says that 5 minutes remain, without emphasizing that the time is very short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use しか with an affirmative sentence, but the correct structure is しか together with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q10.kobun.cn: Nしか ＋ Vない; Vます-stem ＋ ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.vi: The mobile phone battery seems about to run out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N が ＋ Vます-removeます ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the preceding noun with the following noun and shows possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the battery as the subject in a state of running out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: なくなりそう uses the connective form of the verb なくなる before そう to express a sign that something is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ そうだ／そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.why: The phrase の identifies the battery as belonging to the phone, while が marks the object that is changing. The verb なくなる connects with そうだ to show signs that the battery is about to run out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence emphasizes that the action is about to begin rather than making a prediction based on signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: そうだ after the plain form can mean “I hear that,” while なくなりそうだ in this sentence means “seems about to run out.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse そうだ; after a verb, the removed form ます must be used, not the dictionary form なくなるそうです, when saying that something seems about to run out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.vi: Tomorrow, the temperature will be 10°C lower than today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets tomorrow as the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: より sets today as the standard for comparing the temperature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the temperature as the object that changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: An adjective ending in い changes to the く form to connect with なる and express a change to a lower state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.why: は sets tomorrow as the topic, while より creates today as the comparison point. Because the temperature changes to a lower state, the adjective い uses the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only describes a low temperature and does not emphasize a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If なる is omitted, the sentence can make a direct comparison but does not clearly show that the temperature becomes lower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q12.kobun.tip: Do not keep ひくい unchanged before なる; the adjective ending in い must change to ひくくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.vi: Because it is still early, the shop is not open yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: まだ modifies the state of being early and shows that the current time is not late yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective ending in い comes before ので in its plain form to create a reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the shop as the subject of the state of not being open yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: あいている indicates the state of being open, while the negative form ていません expresses the state of not being open yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, followed by the result that the shop is not open yet. が marks the shop as the subject of the state described by あいていません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason stays the same, but the tone becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes an action that has not been completed, while あいていません emphasizes the state that the shop is not open yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use ので as a word standing alone; it must be connected directly after the appropriate form of the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.vi: I know a shortcut to the post office.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: への modifies the noun that follows and shows the direction or destination of the shortcut.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the shortcut as the object of knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: しっています indicates the state of knowing information or a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.why: への sets the post office as the destination and modifies the shortcut. The shortcut is the object of しっています, so it takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If への is replaced with までの, the sentence emphasizes the range or endpoint, which is the post office.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern describes something located at that place, not only the direction leading there as への does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.tip: しっています expresses a state of knowing, so use を for the thing known, rather than に as a direct translation from Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q14.kobun.cn: N ＋ へ ＋ の ＋ N; Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.vi: I chatted with a friend while drinking black tea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.sk: N と ＋ Vます-drop ます ＋ ながら ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who takes part in the chatting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ながら connects the secondary action in the dropped form ます with the main action and shows that the two things happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks black tea as the thing being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲みました is the polite past form of 飲む and functions as the main action of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.cn: Vます-drop ます ＋ ながら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.why: と identifies the person being chatted with, while ながら connects the chatting action with the main action of drinking. The object of 飲む is marked by を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If て is used, the sentence focuses on linking actions in sequence or in a connected relationship, without clearly stressing that they happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If も is added, this pattern usually has a contrastive meaning, such as doing one thing while still doing another.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q15.kobun.tip: ながら must connect to the dropped part ます of the verb, so use おしゃべりしながら rather than おしゃべりするながら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.vi: I am studying to enter the medical department.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the department as the place or destination for entering and studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ために connects the goal with the main action; 入る keeps the dictionary form before ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: しています shows that the studying action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.why: The medical department is the destination, so it goes with に. The clause 入るために comes first to state the purpose, followed by the action being done to achieve that purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ように, the sentence fits better with a goal of achieving a state or ability, rather than the direct purpose of entering the department.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern turns the purpose into a modifier for a noun, so it cannot end directly with べんきょうしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.tip: ために expresses a purpose and usually goes with a verb in the dictionary form; the て form or the past form is not used in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q16.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.vi: The director owns as many as 6 cars.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Number ＋ Counter ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the director is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the car as the object being owned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 台 is the counter used to count cars and comes after the number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 持っています expresses the state of having or owning something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.cn: Number ＋ 台; Nを ＋ Number ＋ Counter ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は. Then を marks the thing that is owned. The number of cars is placed before the verb to give the quantity of the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the existence of 6 cars more than the act of owning them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget the counter 台 when counting cars and often use the wrong counter for objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q17.tokens.5.m: unit for counting cars and machines
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.vi: I want to study hard to become a good doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The て form connects the action of trying hard with the following action of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: して、 connects the studying action with the goal stated in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: いい modifies the noun for the profession that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the result or target state of the change with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: なりたい expresses the desire to become a certain professional or enter a certain state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.why: The two actions are connected by the て form and lead to the goal in the following clause. With なる, に marks the desired result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence changes from a simple desire to an intention or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use になる directly with a noun and forget the particle に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q18.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; Vます-stem ＋ たいです; N ＋ に ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.vi: I saw a beautiful bird in the forest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of seeing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な comes before a noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the bird as the object being seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 見ました is the polite past form of 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the verb. きれいな comes directly before the noun to describe the bird.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the existence of the bird in the forest rather than the act of seeing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse で, which indicates the place where an action occurs, with に, which indicates a place of existence or a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q19.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ N; N で ＋ V; N を ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who carries out the buying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: しろい modifies ふく, while を marks the clothes as what is bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies the verb かいます and shows how often the buying happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: かいます is the predicate and expresses a habit or a polite present action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q2.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to describe the type of clothes. よく comes before the verb to add frequency, while を marks the clothes as the object of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 白くない, the meaning becomes “not white,” which negates the clothes' quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often place adjectives after nouns, but Japanese places adjectives before nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a time word with the noun for the exam and modifies that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that yesterday's exam is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective and increases the level of difficulty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: むずかしい changes to むずかしかった to express a quality in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.why: The phrase きのうのしけん combines the time with the noun using の. Because the exam has already taken place, the adjective changes to the past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning becomes that the exam was not difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget to change い into かった when describing the quality of something in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q20.kobun.cn: N の ＋ N; Aい → Aかったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.vi: Of all animals, I like pandas the most.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の中で limits the range used for comparison or selection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the selected object as the most outstanding within that range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies すき to create the meaning “like the most.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, expressing a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.why: の中で sets the range of comparison, が marks the selected object, and いちばん comes before すき to show the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If の中で and いちばん are removed, the sentence only means liking pandas, without the meaning of liking them the most in a group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern uses を with an action verb, so the meaning changes to wanting to eat pandas the most, not liking them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with すき, but すき usually goes with が to mark the favorite object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q21.kobun.cn: N の中で ＋ N が ＋ いちばん ＋ Aなだ／Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.vi: You should properly return the things you borrowed from other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: から only indicates the source or the person who lent something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: A past-tense clause comes before もの to modify the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the borrowed things are the topic of the reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: きちんと modifies the action of returning and shows how it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: なさい attaches to the stem form ます to create a request or a soft command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.why: かりたもの is a noun phrase with a clause before it to identify which things are meant. After the topic, an adverb of manner comes before the request to return them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the request is more polite and has less of the tone of an instruction from someone with higher status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the things must be returned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place a modifying clause after a noun, while Japanese always places it before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q22.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ N; Vます-stem ＋ なさい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.vi: There is a small sofa in my room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし to the noun after it to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the sofa exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 小さな comes before a noun to modify ソファ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate showing the existence of an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.why: The location is stated first with に, the existing object goes with が, and the sentence ends with あります because a sofa is an object. The phrase 小さな comes directly before ソファ to describe its size.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with います, the sentence is used for people or animals, not for a sofa.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で to show where something exists, but the existence pattern uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q23.kobun.cn: N に ＋ N が ＋ あります／います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.vi: When I was young, I wanted to become a flower seller.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects こども with とき to form a time phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the result or occupation after becoming something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: なりたかった is the past form of なりたい, expressing a past desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the person or occupation the speaker wanted to become with に. なりたかったです comes at the end to state a desire that existed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means that the speaker still wants to become a flower seller now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use を with なる; the result after なる must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q24.kobun.cn: N に ＋ なる; Vます-stem ＋ たい → Vたかったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.vi: I often write letters at a coffee shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the action 書きます and shows frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the place where the writing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 書きます is the polite form of the verb 書く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and the adverb of frequency comes before the location and object. The location uses で because it is where the writing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, に shows a direction or destination, not the place where the writing is happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and で; use で for the place where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.vi: Things sent by mail should be made lighter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the means or method of sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: as for the things to send
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: おくる is a clause modifying もの, while は makes the object the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: かるく is the く form of the adjective かるい, combined with する to express making something lighter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ほうがいいです expresses advice to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.why: The clause おくるもの modifies もの, creating the meaning “the thing to be sent.” The adjective かるい changes to the く form to combine with する, and then the pattern ほうがいい gives advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 軽くしてください is used, the sentence becomes the direct request “please make it lighter,” which is stronger than advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 軽いほうがいいです is used, it means “it is better if it is light,” without emphasizing the action of making it lighter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect an adjective directly to する, but an adjective ending in い must change い into く before する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q3.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない ＋ ほうがいいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.vi: I often take children to the park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the children as the people being taken along.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: つれて is the て form of つれる, connecting the action of taking someone along with the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies 行きます and shows how often the speaker goes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: へ shows the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.why: The children are the people being taken along, so they go with を. The form て connects the action of taking them along with 行きます; へ shows the destination, and よく shows the habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 公園で is used, the park will be the place where an action takes place, not the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 子どもと is used, the meaning is going together with the children, without emphasizing taking them along.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use と for every meaning of “with,” but an action of taking someone somewhere uses を with the person being taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.vi: I was made to wait for a very long time at the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates where the forced waiting took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective that modifies 時間 and shows that the time lasted for a long period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase indicates the length of time that the waiting action lasted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: A verb in the polite past form that creates the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.why: で sets the location where the event happened, while 長い modifies 時間 to express the length of the wait. The predicate is in the passive form, making the speaker the person who had to undergo the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would only say that someone was waiting, without emphasizing that another person made them wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for duration; with a long period such as 長い時間, an additional particle is usually not needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.vi: The area in front of the station in this town is very lively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 町 with 前, showing ownership or a related location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the location being discussed the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb that modifies にぎやかです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: An adjective ending in な in the polite form, used as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.why: The phrases この and 町の modify the location 前 in that order. は marks the location as the topic, and then にぎやかです states a characteristic of that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the location would change to behind the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate の as “of” in every case, but here it connects nouns to form a phrase indicating location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.vi: I always listen to music on the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing the frequency of the listening action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means used to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 音楽 as the object being listened to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞いています uses the ている form to express an ongoing action or a habit.
