default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.why: いつも modifies the whole action, 電車で indicates the means, and を connects the direct object with 聞く. The ている form shows that the action is happening or is repeated as a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would only say that someone listened to music, without the sense of listening now or listening regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を because Vietnamese does not require an object marker, but 聞く needs を when stating what is being listened to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.vi: The typhoon may be coming again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that the event may happen again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 台風 as the subject of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb in the dictionary form that comes before a speculation pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: A sentence-final pattern showing possibility without making a definite statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.why: が identifies 台風 as the subject that will come. 来る stays in the plain form to connect directly with かもしれません and create an uncertain prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would still be a prediction, but the sense of expectation or probability would usually be stronger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily change 来る into the polite form before かもしれません, but this pattern requires the plain form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ ＋ かもしれない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.vi: Choose the words with the same meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks いみ as the subject that has the same characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 同じ directly modifies もの, forming a noun phrase for things with the same meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks もの as the object of the verb えらぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.why: The phrase 同じもの is formed by placing a modifier before a noun. を connects that phrase with えらぶ, while てください turns the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning would change to things that are similar in form or quality, not necessarily things with the same meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifier after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese places 同じ before もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t45-q9.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ N; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.vi: Even if I do not have time, I can still send it immediately if it is an email.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: なくても creates a concessive clause, meaning even if there is no time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: なら presents a condition or assumed scope: an email.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: すぐ modifies the sending action and indicates when it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A verb in the polite form, understood from the context as being able to send it immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.why: The clause ても states an unfavorable situation that does not prevent the result. なら limits the condition to email, and then すぐ comes before the predicate to emphasize speed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nでも is used, the meaning is “even if it is an email or some other choice,” so the concessive sense is broader.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is more formal and only discusses the case of email. It does not have the direct hypothetical sense of なら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.tip: Do not understand ても as only “also”; in this sentence, it means “even if... still...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q1.kobun.cn: Vて形・Aくて・Aなで・Nで ＋ も; N ＋ なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.vi: I want to live in a slightly larger place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds the meaning “more” or “in addition” to the desired degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 小し（ひろい） is a phrase that modifies ところ, in which ひろい comes before the noun to describe its characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the speaker wants to live.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたいです expresses the speaker's polite desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.why: The descriptive phrase comes before ところ to identify the place where the speaker wants to live. Then に marks the location, and すみたいです states the desire. もう and 少し both add information about the degree of the adjective ひろい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 広くて, the sentence would connect to another characteristic or action. It would no longer directly express “want to live in a larger place” as Aい does before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the adjective after the noun, but Japanese places the adjective before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.vi: I will go to meet my older sister who is in China.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause 中国にいる comes before あね to modify it and identify which older sister is meant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person whom the speaker will meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The continuative form of あう combines with に to indicate the purpose of going to meet someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: いきます is the main predicate and expresses movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.why: The clause 中国にいる modifies あね, while に after あね marks the person being met. The V-stem＋に行く structure expresses going somewhere in order to perform action V.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 会いに来ます is used, the direction of movement is “come here to meet,” instead of “go to meet.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after the person being met, but 会う goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q12.kobun.vi: There is cow's milk behind the cheese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects チーズ with うしろ to form a location phrase; に marks where an object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: あります is used for the existence of an object, here 牛乳.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q12.kobun.why: The location phrase comes first to state where something exists, followed by the object that exists and あります. The pattern Nの場所にNがあります means “there is N at N’s location.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If チーズの後ろです is used, the sentence only confirms that the location is behind the cheese; it does not say that there is milk there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse あります and います; あります is used for objects, not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.vi: Tokyo is Tokyo-to, while Osaka is Osaka-fu.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes とうきょう the topic for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: ですが connects two clauses with contrasting content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は shifts the topic to おおさか for comparison with Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the sentence by stating Osaka's administrative name.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.why: Both clauses have the same pattern Nは「name」です, connected by ですが to create a contrast. は marks the two place names as the topics in order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If そして is used, the two pieces of information are simply connected in sequence, without emphasizing the contrast between Tokyo and Osaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ですが as “but” every time, but in a contrastive sentence, “while” is often more natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.vi: Sometimes I go to see the nearby harbor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: ときどき is an adverb showing how often the action of going to see the harbor happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ちかく with みなと to form a phrase that describes a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks みなと as the object being looked at or viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 見に shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the main predicate and shows the action of moving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.why: を marks the place or object being viewed, while 見に行きます shows that the purpose of going is to view it. The phrase ちかくのみなと comes before を to clearly identify which harbor it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見て行きます is used, it means “see it and then go,” describing two actions in sequence rather than the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 見に行く for “go and see,” but に shows purpose here: “go to see.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.vi: The sky is very blue today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks today as the time and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks そら as the subject that has the blue color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: とても adds degree to the adjective あおい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: あおい is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate; です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.why: 今日 は states the time, そら が states the subject, and とても modifies あおい, after which the adjective ends the sentence by describing the state. This order follows the pattern NはNがAいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 青くて is used, the sentence is incomplete because 青くて usually needs to connect to another clause or characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may habitually put “very” after the adjective, but in Japanese とても comes before the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun りょうり that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the part that has the bland characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: うすい is the adjective い used as the predicate, and です creates a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q16.kobun.why: The sentence makes the dish the topic, then uses が to identify the dish's taste and uses the adjective い to describe that taste. The natural order is to state the thing being commented on first, followed by the characteristic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If the Nが part is omitted, the sentence directly says that the dish is bland instead of talking specifically about its taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は instead of が in a phrase that identifies the part or property being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.vi: Running every day made my legs slimmer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vていたら ＋ N が ＋ Aいく ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: まいにち shows the time of a repeated action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: Vていたら connects a conditional clause or a process with a result discovered afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the part that changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes い into く before なる to express becoming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました describes a change that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ たら; Aい removes い ＋ く ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.why: The clause はしっていたら puts the condition or process first, while the change in あし is stated afterward. The form ほそく connects directly with なる to create the meaning “become slim.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vていると, the sentence focuses more on a result that naturally occurs whenever one runs, without emphasizing a condition or process that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change the adjective い into the form く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.vi: The wind has gradually become a little weaker than before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: より marks the point used for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し modifies the degree to which the wind has weakened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that is changing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: よわい changes into よわく to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: なってくる describes a change that has gradually progressed toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.cn: Nより; Aい removes い ＋ く ＋ なる; Vて ＋ くる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.why: さっきより sets the comparison point first, and the sentence then states the degree of change in かぜ. The form よわくなってきました combines becoming weak with the idea of gradual change up to the present time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If よわくなりました is used, the sentence only states that the wind has become weak, without emphasizing the gradual process of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate てくる as “come,” but in this sentence it only shows a change gradually progressing toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.vi: Young people do not seem very interested in politics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes young people the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり is used with a negative form to show a low degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the object toward which interest is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks what is said to exist or not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ない denies the existence or possession of きょうみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: ようです is placed at the end of a sentence to make a guess based on signs or available information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.why: わかものは is the topic, while せいじにきょうみがない is the comment about that topic. あまり combines with ない to soften the degree, and then ようです changes the whole comment into a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: ようです usually describes appearance or a well-founded guess, while そうです can focus on a directly observed sign.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: らしいです focuses more on information heard from others or a more typical judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use あまり with an affirmative sentence, although its basic use is with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の ＋ ようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.vi: Whenever I come here, I remember my student days.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the destination of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the action 来る with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the time remembered as the object of 思い出す.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 思い出します is the main predicate and expresses remembering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.why: 来ると creates a time or repeated-condition clause, while the remembered object goes with を. The predicate 思い出します comes at the end to complete the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来たら is used, the sentence emphasizes the condition “after coming,” which does not necessarily happen every time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q2.kobun.tip: With 思い出す, the thing remembered usually goes with を, not が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.vi: Are there any convenience stores around here?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies へん to identify the area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the store exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the object whose existence is being asked about the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ありませんか politely asks whether something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.cn: 場所に ＋ Nが／は ＋ あります／ありません; polite question: ありませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.why: The location is stated first with に, and then the object being sought is made the topic with は. The negative question form ありませんか asks about existence in a polite and softer way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If がありますか is used, the question is more direct and does not have the gentle tone of ありませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for a place of existence, but a place of existence usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.vi: The teacher’s handwriting is very easy to read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 先生 with the noun 字 to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the teacher’s handwriting as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the degree of readability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 読みやすい is formed from the stem ます, 読み, and やすい, and expresses that an action is easy to perform.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ やすいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.why: 先生の字 creates the noun phrase “the teacher’s handwriting,” then は makes that phrase the topic. 読みやすい uses the stem ます of 読む and connects it with やすい to describe how easy the handwriting is to read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 読みにくいです, the meaning changes to difficult to read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect やすい with the dictionary form, but the stem ます must be used: 読み＋やすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.vi: There are many trees near my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with the following noun to create a possessive phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: には states the location as the topic, while に indicates where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object described as numerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い is an adjective expressing a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.why: The location phrase ちかくには is placed first to state the place. The object that exists in large numbers goes with が, and then 多い serves as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes the existence of greenery rather than its large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は after みどり, but in this sentence が marks the object described as numerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q23.kobun.vi: The convenience store is very convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は states コンビニ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the following adjective and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: べんり is an adjective な used as the predicate and ends politely with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q23.kobun.why: The topic is stated first with は, and とても comes directly before the word expressing a quality to increase its degree. です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If な is used before a noun, とても便利な modifies the noun instead of serving as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit な when べんり comes before a noun, but in this sentence べんり comes at the end, so です is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.vi: Even a popular store is quiet in the morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 人気 with みせ to create a phrase that modifies the store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: も means also or even and includes the popular store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: なら sets a condition or assumed range for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: すいています describes the store as being uncrowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.why: 人気のみせ creates a noun phrase, while も emphasizes that even this object has that feature. ごぜんなら states the time condition, and すいています describes the uncrowded state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If なら is replaced with は, the sentence only presents morning as the topic or time, without a conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is used, the sentence only states the time when the state occurs and does not mean “if it is morning.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand なら as only は, but なら also creates an assumed or condition-based limitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.vi: It must be sent urgently by the day after tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: いそいで is the て form used as an adverb to modify おくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ないと begins a required pattern meaning that something must be done or else it is not acceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: いけません completes the pattern ないといけません and expresses the meaning must do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.why: The deadline あさってまでに comes before the action. いそいで modifies おくる, while おくらないといけません creates the structure meaning must send.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this form, the meaning of obligation is almost unchanged, but the tone is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this form, the sentence changes to “do not have to send,” which is the opposite of obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ないと as if not on its own, but here it combines with いけません to create the meaning must.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q25.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ と ＋ いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.vi: This medicine is very easy to take.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to identify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents medicine as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the quality 飲みやすい to increase its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲みやすい is formed from the stem 飲み of 飲む and やすい, meaning that an action is easy to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.why: この comes before the noun to identify the medicine, は makes the medicine the topic, and 飲みやすい states that the medicine is easy to take. とても comes before the adjective to add degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If やすい is replaced with にくい, the meaning changes to “difficult to take.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q3.kobun.tip: When connecting やすい, remove ます from the polite form and use the stem part, such as 飲み.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.vi: I want to become even better at English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of degree that modifies the desire that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that the speaker wants to become better at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な changes to the に form to modify なる and show the state of becoming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: なる in the たい form expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.why: もっと adds degree to the desire. N comes before が as the object of じょうずになる, while じょうずに connects to なる using the adverbial form に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says that someone is good at English. It does not emphasize the desire to become better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q4.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use を before じょうずになる, but the object of ability or improvement usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.vi: If there is any interesting news, please let me know.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before ニュース to modify this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that exists in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ある changes to the たら form to connect the condition to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.why: The clause with あったら is placed first to state the condition. After the condition comes the request, using the てください form to ask the listener to report the news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with なら, the meaning is based on information already mentioned or an assumption being discussed. It is less natural than たら for the meaning “if there is.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily say あればください, but this request needs to connect with the て form: しらせてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q5.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aい・Aなだ／だった・Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.vi: That cloud looks like an animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative comes before the noun to identify the cloud far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents the cloud as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the object used for comparison in the pattern に似ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 似る in the ています form expresses the state of being or seeming similar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.why: The cloud is made the topic by は. The object of comparison goes with に, following the structure に似ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If のようです is used, the sentence means “seems to be an animal” or “looks like an animal,” with a clearer sense of guessing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q6.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use と with 似ています, but the thing being compared must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.vi: This stone is a very rare thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative comes before the noun to identify the stone near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents the stone as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb of degree that modifies めずらしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い modifies もの that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: もの serves as the main noun and combines with です to form a noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.why: は introduces the stone as the topic. とても modifies the adjective, while めずらしい comes before もの to describe the type of object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says that the stone is rare. It does not use もの to emphasize that it is an object or a special thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q7.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily place とても after the adjective, but in Japanese this adverb comes before the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.vi: I want to stay at a hotel near the lake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects みずうみ with ちかく, forming the phrase “the area near the lake.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ちかくの modifies ホテル, referring to a hotel in the area near the lake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place where とまる stays.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: とまる in the たいです form expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.why: The two phrases の in a row create a chain of modifiers: lake → area near the lake → hotel. に marks the hotel as the place where the action of staying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で with 泊まる is unnatural when indicating a place to stay; に is the more suitable particle in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q8.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily understand ちかくのホテル as two separate ideas, but this is one noun phrase in which ちかくの modifies ホテル.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.vi: Work has been very busy lately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.sk: Time point ＋ N が ＋ 程度副詞 ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence to limit the time of the busy state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks work as the subject that has the busy state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb of degree that modifies いそがしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.why: さいきん states the time point for the whole sentence. Work goes with が as the subject of the state, while とても modifies いそがしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the sentence presents work as the topic and may create a contrast with another matter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t46-q9.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use で to say “busy at work,” but 仕事が忙しい describes the work itself as plentiful and busy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.vi: On a birthday, a person feels special.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the birthday as the time or topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な with きもち to modify the feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the state or result that the feeling becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: なります describes a change into the state stated earlier by に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.why: とくべつな comes before きもち to describe the feeling. The phrase きもちになって expresses the state reached, and なります is the predicate showing the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If します is used, the meaning is “make something become special,” emphasizing an active action rather than a natural change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q1.kobun.tip: English speakers may forget な after the adjective な when it comes before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.vi: That supermarket is open until 9 p.m.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes あのスーパー the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase indicates the time used for closing hours.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: まで marks the end point, meaning “until” or “up to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a polite affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.why: The sentence makes the supermarket the topic, then gives the afternoon time and the ending limit of 9 o'clock. まで is placed after the time to show the final point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is replaced with から, it means “from 9 o'clock,” showing the starting point instead of the ending point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If ごろ is used, it means “around 9 o'clock,” without clearly setting an ending time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate まで simply as “until,” but remember that it marks the final limit of a period or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.vi: The snack I wanted has unfortunately sold out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The past adjective ほしい comes before おかし to describe the snack.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object described as sold out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the sold-out state to the pattern しまう that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました shows that an event has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.why: The clause ほしかった describes おかし, forming the subject “the snack that was wanted.” てしまいました comes after うりきれて to emphasize that selling out was fully completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 売り切れました is used, it only reports that the item sold out, with a milder feeling and no strong regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If 売り切れていました is used, it emphasizes the sold-out state as seen at a certain past time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may overlook the regretful feeling of てしまう and translate it mechanically as “finished doing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.vi: My house is large and is right near the road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with いえ to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the house the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きく is the connecting form of the adjective ending in い; this form usually needs a suitable following clause or predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects みち with ちかく to form the phrase “near the road.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: すぐ modifies ちかく and emphasizes the very short distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: ちかくです serves as the predicate and ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.why: わたしのいえは is the topic, while みちのすぐちかくです is the location phrase for the house. However, in the given sentence, 大きく comes before the location phrase without て; a more natural expression would usually be 大きくて or 大きいし.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 大きく is replaced with 大きくて, the two ideas “large” and “near the road” are connected naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes the existence and location of the house near the road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 大きく to connect the two ideas directly; when connecting the adjective い to another clause, 大きくて is usually needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.vi: Because it is hot, I want to cut my hair short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason with the desired action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the hair as the object affected by making it short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: みじかく is the く form of the adjective い, placed before する to show the resulting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: したいです expresses the desire to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.why: あついので gives the reason first, then かみを identifies the object of the action. The Aいくする pattern expresses making something have the state described by an adjective, and then たい adds the meaning of wanting to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If なりたい is used, it means “want to become short,” which does not fit actively making the hair short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If みじかいです is used, it only describes the hair as short and does not express the desire to cut or shorten it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use みじかいする, but before する, the adjective い must be changed to the く form: みじかくする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.vi: Over a period of about 10 years, transportation has become more convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.sk: Period of time に + N が + Aな に + なりました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the period during which the change took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that underwent a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the resulting state before なりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the main predicate and describes a completed change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning to state the period of change. 交通が is the thing that changed, while べんりになりました expresses the result “become convenient.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If べんりになりました is replaced with べんりでした, it only says that transportation was convenient and does not emphasize the process of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If べんりにしました is used, there is an active subject that makes transportation convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse べんりなりました; before なる, べんりに must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.vi: I always eat lunch at the university café.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that lunch is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the action of eating and shows frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 大学 with カフェ, creating the meaning “the university café.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the place where the eating action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite present form and describes a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.why: The topic phrase comes first, followed by the frequency adverb and the place where the action happens. The particle で is suitable because カフェ is where the eating action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence is no longer natural because に usually indicates a direction or a point where something exists, not the place where eating happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に with the place of an action, but で is needed to show where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q16.kobun.sk: Place に + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the snowfall occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks snow as the subject of the falling phenomenon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb ふる is changed to the polite past form to describe snow that has fallen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q16.kobun.why: The location of the phenomenon comes before the subject and predicate. With natural phenomena such as snowfall, 雪 usually serves as the subject together with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で focuses on the place where an action happens, while に is more suitable for the location of snowfall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q16.kobun.tip: Do not automatically use は for every subject; sentences describing a newly occurring phenomenon often use が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.vi: Last year, I climbed Mount Fuji with a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N と ＋ N に ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: と refers to the person who performs the mountain-climbing action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination or target of the climbing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the polite past form to talk about a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.why: A time phrase can come at the beginning of a sentence, followed by the person acting and the destination. のぼる is used with に when stating the mountain or place being headed toward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the meaning changes to an action taking place at Mount Fuji, without emphasizing the destination being climbed to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake と for only “and,” but here と refers to the person participating in the action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.vi: Because I am full, I am very sleepy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the part that is in a full state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: で connects the cause, a state, with the result of feeling sleepy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies the adjective ねむい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate and combines with です to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.why: The first clause states the condition and its cause, while the second clause states the result. The adjective いっぱい connects to the following clause with で to show a softer cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with だから states the reason more directly and conversationally, with a clearer explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with のに creates a contrast, like “although I am full, I still...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.tip: With the adjective い, use くて rather than で to connect two clauses; で here is the connective form for a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q18.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ くて／Aな ＋ で／N ＋ で、
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.vi: I made all of this dish myself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Scope ＋ N で ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this dish the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ぜんぶ modifies the action of making and emphasizes that everything was made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: で refers to the person who performs the action personally, without asking someone else to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the polite past form and describes a dish that has been made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the whole scope and the method or person performing the action. 自分 after で emphasizes making it oneself using one's own ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, 自分 becomes the emphasized subject, while で emphasizes performing the action personally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q19.kobun.tip: Do not translate で here as a place; it indicates the method or the person who performs the action personally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.vi: The baseball game was canceled because of the rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that makes the game stop or be canceled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects やきゅう with ゲーム to identify the type of game.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that changes to the state 中止.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the result or state that ゲーム changes to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました describes a change that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.why: 雨で gives the cause first, and then やきゅうのゲームが becomes the subject. The pattern Nになる shows that the game changed to the state 中止.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the cause keeps the same meaning, but the expression is more formal and clearly written in a written style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes that someone actively decided to cancel the game.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before 中止, but when expressing a change of state, the noun goes with に in the pattern Nになる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I borrowed an umbrella from a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Person に ＋ Object を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the umbrella was borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に refers to the person who lends the umbrella, that is, the person from whom the speaker borrows it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the umbrella as the thing being borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb かりる is changed to the polite past form to describe a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.why: In the pattern for borrowing something, the lender goes with に and the borrowed object goes with を. This order clearly shows the lender, the object received, and the borrowing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: から can also indicate the source, the person who lends something, and emphasizes “from a friend” more than に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: Using が makes the umbrella the subject, so it no longer has the correct structure for “borrow an umbrella.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and から; に is the person directly involved in the borrowing pattern, while から emphasizes the source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.vi: I have liked swimming since I was little.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates a starting point that continues until the present or a later time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object being discussed as すき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: すき is a な adjective, and でした is used to express the state of liking in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to state the starting point. With すき, the object of liking usually goes with が, and then すきでした acts as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ごろ, the meaning changes from “since around that time” to “around that time,” without emphasizing continuation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put を before すき, but the standard structure is Nがすきです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q21.kobun.cn: Nのときから ＋ Nが ＋ Aなです／でした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: あおい comes before ペン to modify this noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the desired object in the structure ほしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ほしい is a い adjective that expresses the desire to own an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q22.kobun.why: The adjective あおい comes directly before ペン to describe the pen's color. ペンがほしい expresses the desire to have the pen, not the desire to do something with it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほしがる is used, it usually describes another person's desire and has the nuance of “appearing to want to have it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q22.kobun.tip: With ほしい, the desired object usually goes with が, not を as with ordinary verbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q22.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ Nが ＋ ほしいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The quantity phrase states the distance to be covered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: はしって is the て form of はしる, and it connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q23.kobun.why: The distance, １００メートル, comes before the action to state how far the person must run. The verb in the て form combines with ください to turn the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vなさい, the sentence has a stronger command-like tone and is usually spoken by someone in a higher position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q23.kobun.tip: Do not connect ください directly to the dictionary form; first change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.vi: Mr. Ueda lives in Chiba Prefecture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Mr. Ueda is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the subject lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: すんでいます describes the state of living in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, the place of residence goes with に, and すんでいます is the predicate. With 住む, に shows the place where someone lives, not the location of a movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with で暮らしています, the meaning is still living there, but it focuses more on life or daily activities at that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use で with 住む to indicate a place of residence; the basic usage is 場所に住んでいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q24.kobun.cn: Nは + Nに + Vている／ています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.vi: Snow can be seen from the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.sk: 場所から + Nが + naturally possible verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the position or direction from which something can be observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that appears within the field of vision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 見えます is the polite form of 見える and describes something naturally coming into view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.why: へやから gives the viewpoint, while ゆきが is the thing being seen. 見える is a verb for naturally being visible, so the thing seen goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Nを見る, the sentence becomes the active action of “looking at the snow,” focusing on the person looking rather than on the thing that appears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.tip: Distinguish 見える from 見る: 見える usually goes with が and means “can be seen,” not actively “look.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q25.kobun.cn: 場所から + Nが + 見えます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.vi: I ate too many cakes, so I accidentally gained weight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 食べすぎて connects the cause to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects this action or result with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました shows that the result has been completed, often with a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.why: ケーキを is the object of 食べる. 食べすぎて gives the cause, while ふとってしまいました describes the unwanted result that occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence only states the cause, “because I ate too much,” without emphasizing the following event through the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that すぎる attaches to the masu verb stem, so they say 食べすぎる instead of 食べるすぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.vi: I want to go to many countries around the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects せかい with the noun phrase 国, creating the meaning “countries around the world.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろな modifies the noun 国.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: たい attaches to the stem of 行き to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.why: せかいの and いろいろな modify 国 respectively. 国へ indicates the desired destination, while 行きたいです is the predicate expressing desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: に also indicates the destination and has almost the same meaning in this sentence, but へ emphasizes the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with a destination; with the verb 行く, the destination usually goes with に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.vi: Today is much hotter than yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes きょう the topic being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: より gives the point used for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ずっと modifies an adjective and emphasizes the difference in degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: あついです is the adjective predicate describing today's weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.why: きょうは is the thing being evaluated, while きのうより is the point of comparison. ずっと comes before あつい to emphasize that today is much hotter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the meaning becomes “not as hot as yesterday,” changing to a comparison of a lower degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse より with ほど; より follows the point of comparison in an affirmative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.vi: Studying abroad in Japan is a very good experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction toward Japan, while の connects this phrase to the noun りゅうがく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes studying abroad in Japan the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies いい to increase the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: いい comes before the noun けいけん to describe the experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: けいけんです is a noun predicate that states the nature of studying abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.why: 日本へのりゅうがく creates a noun phrase meaning “studying abroad in Japan.” This phrase is the topic, and then いい modifies けいけん in the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If での is used, the focus is on the place where the study abroad takes place, not on the direction toward Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often leave out の between 日本へ and りゅうがく; の is necessary to connect the modifying phrase to the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.vi: I have had a headache continuously since yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ずっと modifies the state いたい and emphasizes its continuation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: いたい describes the state, while んです adds an explanatory or emphatic feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.why: きのうから identifies the starting point, and ずっと shows that the state continues. The painful body part is the subject with が, and then いたいんです states the condition with an explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence describes the condition of hurting or injuring the head, not the adjective structure “the head hurts.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use を with あたま; in the pattern あたまがいたい, が marks the body part in the painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.vi: The most important thing is family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: いちばん modifies たいせつな and creates the meaning of the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: たいせつ is an な adjective, so な must be used before the noun もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes もの, meaning “the most important thing,” the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: かぞくです is a noun predicate that identifies it as family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.why: いちばんたいせつなもの is a noun phrase in which いちばんたいせつな modifies もの. This phrase is the topic and is identified by the predicate かぞくです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes family as the answer or identified object, instead of presenting the topic with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget な after the adjective な when it comes before a noun: たいせつなもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.vi: This is the umbrella I forgot yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the thing being introduced or explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the clause that modifies かさ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: This word indicates the time when the action of forgetting occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: A past-tense verb comes before a noun to modify かさ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends the sentence with a polite affirmative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.why: これは is the main topic, while わたしがきのうわすれた is the clause before it that identifies which umbrella. The verb わすれた uses the past tense because the forgetting happened yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this phrase, it means “my umbrella,” without clearly saying that I forgot it yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If もの is used, the meaning is broader: “the thing I forgot yesterday,” which is not necessarily an umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t47-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake が in the modifying clause for the topic of the whole sentence, but here the main topic is これは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to work in politics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.sk: Time ＋ NのNが ＋ Vます-stem ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: しょうらい states the time when the wish is to be fulfilled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects せいじ with しごと, forming the phrase “work related to politics.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that the speaker wants to do in the Vたい structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: したい is formed from the continuative form of する and たい, expressing the speaker’s wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.why: しょうらい sets the time context, せいじのしごと creates a noun phrase, and this phrase becomes the object of the wish. With する, the wish form is したい, not するたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vるつもりです, the sentence expresses a clearer intention instead of only a wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.tip: With たい, the verb must remove ます before adding たい; する changes to したい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q1.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 ＋ たい／たくない／たかった／たくなかった
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.vi: I am very happy because I won against a strong team in a soccer match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects サッカー with the noun しあい to form the phrase “soccer match.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the setting where the winning took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the object that was defeated in the expression チームに勝つ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the action of winning with the happy state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: うれしいです is the predicate expressing the speaker’s emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.why: で places the action in the context of a match, while に marks the team that was defeated. The form て connects a cause or an earlier action with the emotion at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This form cannot be used; with 勝つ, the defeated object usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 勝ったので, the cause-and-effect meaning “because I won” is expressed more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を because of the usual pattern of the verb “win,” but 勝つ usually uses に to indicate the opponent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the teacher the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks cigarettes as the object of smoking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ません is the polite negative form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q11.kobun.why: は introduces the person who performs the action, を marks what is smoked, and ません politely negates the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning would be that the person did not smoke before, emphasizing the past time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget を because Vietnamese has no separate particle for marking the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q12.kobun.vi: This is a good piece of music, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: いい modifies the noun for a piece of music.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the noun phrase with a polite comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ね is used to seek the listener’s agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q12.kobun.why: いい comes before the noun to evaluate the music, then です creates a polite sentence. ね adds the feeling of sharing the comment with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ね is replaced with よ, the sentence sounds more like an announcement or places more emphasis on the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate ね simply as “isn’t it” and forget that it needs a comment or piece of information to confirm together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q13.kobun.vi: My younger sister has a weak body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the younger sister the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part that has the weak state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective acts as the predicate describing the body’s state, while です creates a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q13.kobun.why: は makes the person being discussed the topic, while が identifies the body part with the weak quality. The pattern NはNがAい is used to describe a feature or state of the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If を and します are used, the meaning becomes “the younger sister makes the body weak,” which is different from describing an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before the adjective, but when describing a body part or a feature of the subject, が is usually used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q14.kobun.vi: It is very cloudy today, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes today the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the object described as numerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate and describes the amount of clouds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね is used for gentle confirmation and creates a friendly tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q14.kobun.why: 今日は makes the time the topic, then が marks clouds as the object being described. おおい comes at the end of the content to act as the predicate, while ですね adds a confirming tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は instead of が when stating the object being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: もっと modifies the action and indicates that its level needs to increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q15.kobun.why: もっと modifies the action of hurrying, while the form て combines with ください to form a polite request pattern. ください comes at the end to complete a gentle request or command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this instead would make the request softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change the verb into the て form before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q16.kobun.vi: I live on the eighth floor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は introduces the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the specific place where the speaker lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: すんでいます describes the state of living somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q16.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, the specific place comes before に, and then すんでいます acts as the predicate. With the verb 住む, に indicates a place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This form is not suitable for indicating a specific place of residence in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に, which indicates a place of residence, with で, which indicates the place where an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で marks the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects 働く with います to express the state of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: います completes the pattern for an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q17.kobun.why: 外国で indicates the place where the action happens. Then the form て connects with います. The structure Vている expresses working at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes living abroad, not working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with 働く, but the place where the action of working takes place uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.vi: Reading a thick book takes a lot of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: あつい comes before 本 to modify the noun 本.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the book as the object being read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 読むの turns the clause about reading into a noun, and は marks it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks time as the thing that is needed or used up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: かかります acts as the predicate and expresses the time needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.why: The adjective comes before 本 to describe the type of book, and を marks the object of 読む. 読むのは turns the whole action of reading into a noun, while 時間がかかります expresses that the action takes time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のは with ことは still refers to reading, but the tone is more general and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the adjective after the noun, while Japanese puts the adjective before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the button as the object of the pressing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects 押す with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes at the end to politely ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q19.kobun.why: ボタンを is the object phrase and indicates the thing affected. The verb uses the form て before ください to turn the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the request sounds softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ください, but the request pattern requires the form て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the closing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q2.kobun.why: The object of the action comes before を. Then the verb in the て form combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence means please do not close the door.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ください instead of changing the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q20.kobun.vi: I rented a car and came here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that is borrowed or rented.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects かりて with きました and expresses doing something and then coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q20.kobun.why: 車 を is the phrase for the rented object. The verb in the て form connects with きました to express renting a car first and then coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vていく, the sentence emphasizes finishing the action and then leaving the place of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that て in this pattern connects two actions in an earlier-then-later order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q20.kobun.cn: Vて + くる/きます/きました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to clearly identify the school being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: では states the place and limits the scope of the situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that is provided or appears at the school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 出ます acts as the predicate and indicates that the school meal is served or provided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q21.kobun.why: この modifies 学校 to form the phrase “this school.” では sets the location, while が marks the school meal as the subject being provided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 学校に is used, it only indicates direction or a place of existence and does not emphasize the scope “at this school.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate では as “then” by itself and overlook its meaning of location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that my father is the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with a noun for an occupation in a noun sentence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q22.kobun.why: わたしの modifies 父 to form the phrase “my father.” は makes this phrase the topic, while です confirms the topic’s occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes that the father himself is a doctor instead of stating a general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse の with only a possession particle, but it also connects two nouns into a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q23.kobun.vi: My younger sister is a university student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the following noun to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that my younger sister is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: です is used to identify the status or role of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q23.kobun.why: わたしの modifies younger sister to form the noun phrase “my younger sister.” は makes this phrase the topic, and then です identifies her as a university student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 妹が is used, the focus shifts to the fact that the younger sister herself is a university student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の and say わたし妹 directly, but in Japanese the two nouns must be connected by の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q24.kobun.vi: My mother is a strict person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that my mother is the person being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective comes before 人 to modify the mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 人です creates the predicate, in which the adjective before it describes the type of person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q24.kobun.why: 母は is the topic. The adjective comes directly before 人 to form the phrase “strict person,” and then です completes the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 母は厳しいです is said, it directly describes the mother as strict and does not use the noun 人 to classify her.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the adjective after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese puts the adjective before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Teacher Yamamoto is the person being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: です ends a noun or adjective sentence and な confirms the quality of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q25.kobun.why: The name and title form the topic before は. A word describing personality belongs to the な adjective group, so it ends with です when used as a predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 親切な先生 is used, it means “kind teacher,” where 親切 modifies 先生 instead of acting as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な when placing the な adjective before a noun, but before です, な is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.vi: My younger sister is working at a hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.sk: N は + location N で + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes younger sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で shows where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern ています describes the state of working or the current situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, the location of the activity uses で, and はたらいています describes the current state of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern only shows existence in a place. It does not emphasize the activity of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show where an action takes place; for working, studying, or eating, use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun テストの modifies 時間, forming the phrase “the test time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the quality of being short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: An adjective ending in い changes to かった to describe a quality in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + かった + です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.why: The phrase テストの時間 forms a noun phrase, が marks the subject being described, and the short adjective in the past form acts as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If the present form is used, the sentence only says that the time is generally short or short now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes the change of becoming short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily keep い unchanged when talking about the past, but Aい must change to かった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object that needs attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase してください forms a polite request or reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q5.kobun.why: The object that needs attention takes に, followed by a polite request that reminds the listener to be careful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is almost the same, but the nuance is “please be careful with that object.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q5.kobun.tip: With 注意する, the object usually takes に, not を as when marking an object directly affected by an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.vi: She lives in the same apartment complex as me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes her the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と names the object used for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: おなじ modifies アパート, while に shows where she lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern ています describes her current living situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.why: わたしとおなじ creates a comparison, おなじ comes before the noun being compared, and に marks the place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: When this pattern is used, it emphasizes doing an action together or being together more than being the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means different from me, unlike おなじ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake と in おなじと for “together with” in the sense of accompanying someone, but here it marks the object of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.sk: N は + location N に + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes Mr. Murata the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 住んでいます describes the state of living in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.why: The person's name is the topic, the place of residence takes に, and ています shows the current living situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern says that someone is working in France, not living there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that someone is going or has gone to France. It does not describe living there long-term.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q7.kobun.tip: The verb 住む uses に for a place of residence; it does not use で as it does for the place where an activity occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.vi: This part-time job pays 1,000 yen per hour.
