default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.sk: N は + N が + amountです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は names the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the content identified as １０００円.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.why: は puts the topic first, then が states the specific amount of the hourly pay. です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning becomes broader and refers to wages in general, not necessarily an hourly rate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit が and use は in both positions, making the sentence less natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q9.kobun.vi: A black car came running toward us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before 車 to modify the car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that is running toward us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: きました combines with はしって to describe movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q9.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to describe the car, while が marks the car as the subject of the action. The form てくる shows movement toward the viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the car will be understood as running away from the viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t48-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate てくる simply as “come,” but in this sentence it emphasizes movement toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.vi: My grandmother is very healthy and walks in the park for one hour every morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.sk: N は + state で + time + location を + duration + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は names the grandmother as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で connects the healthy state with the walking action in the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The time phrase comes before the action to show when it takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the place walked through in this expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: This phrase shows how long the action continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The form て connects the verb あるく with います to create a pattern for an ongoing or continuing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: います completes the Vている pattern and describes an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, then で connects the state with the action. The time, location, and duration phrases add information before the predicate Vている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If the simple present form is used instead, the sentence only describes a habit or something that usually happens. It does not emphasize an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to use ている after the verb when they want to say what someone is doing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.vi: I borrowed books and studied at the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the actions take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 本 as the object being borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The form たり states one action from a group of typical actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The second form たり adds another action of the same type.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: しました completes the listing pattern たり、たりしました in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.why: で identifies the place where the activities take place, while を identifies the borrowed object. The two forms たり list typical activities, and しました ends the sentence in the past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: List two actions in a clear sequence, without the meaning of giving examples.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Use the present tense or a habitual action instead of a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.tip: The form たり must be used with the short past form of the verb; it cannot be used directly with the polite form ますたり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q10.kobun.cn: Vた + り、 + Vた + りします/しました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.vi: I learned many things from my teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に refers to the person who gives knowledge in the structure “learn something from someone.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な to the noun こと that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks こと as the content that was learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ならいました is the polite past form of ならう and shows that the learning was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.why: 先生に refers to the teacher, while ことを refers to the content received. The verb ならいました comes at the end because it is the main predicate and is changed to the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: から emphasizes that the teacher is the source of the knowledge.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Emphasize that the teacher taught me as a form of help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q11.kobun.tip: With ならう, the teacher usually goes with に; do not mechanically use を for the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.vi: On days off, I wake up earlier than usual and go to the park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は gives the day off as the background and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: より sets the standard for comparing the state or time of waking up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective はやい changes to the form はやく to modify the verb おきて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects waking up with going to the park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the destination of the verb 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: 行きます is the main predicate and describes an action usually done on days off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.why: 休みの日は sets the background, いつもより creates the comparison standard, and はやく modifies おきて. に marks the park as the destination, and the て form connects the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Emphasize “an earlier time” instead of directly describing how one wakes up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It means doing something as usual, which is different from the earlier meaning in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q12.kobun.tip: When the adjective ending in い modifies a verb, い must change to く; do not use はやいおきて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.vi: If you turn at the corner, you will see a bookstore.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place or point that the speaker turns through.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb + と expresses a result that happens immediately after the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists after turning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate that expresses the existence of something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.why: The phrase かどをまがる is the conditional action, while the following clause states the natural result. A noun referring to an existing thing goes with が before あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this, it means “when turning” and only indicates the time of the action, without emphasizing the natural result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with たら, the sentence has a more hypothetical conditional meaning instead of expressing a result that usually happens automatically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with the meaning “at the corner,” but in this sentence を marks the point passed when turning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.vi: I still have not decided what I want to buy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.ch.0.vi: the thing I want to buy
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: 買いたい modifies もの to form the noun phrase “the thing I want to buy,” and が marks the subject being decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ shows that the decision is still not complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: きまりません is the polite negative form and describes a state that has not been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.why: 買いたい directly modifies もの, so the whole phrase becomes the subject of きまりません. まだ comes before the negative predicate to emphasize the incomplete state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 買うもの, it means “the thing I will buy” or “the thing to buy,” and does not clearly show desire like 買いたいもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 決めていません is used, the subject “I” has directly not decided; きまりません emphasizes that it has not been determined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate たい as an independent verb, but 買いたいもの is a phrase that modifies the noun もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q14.kobun.cn: Vます-stem + たい; V普通形 + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.vi: I asked a store employee where the snacks were.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic being asked about is the location of the snacks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: か is added after the question word to create the content of an indirect question before 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きました is the main predicate and refers to an asking action that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.why: おかしはどこか is the content of the indirect question, while the person receiving the question goes with に. 聞きました comes at the end to complete the asking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If どこですかと聞きました is used, the sentence is more like a direct quotation and keeps the polite question form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If どこにあるか is used, the sentence states more clearly that the question is about where the snacks are located.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を for the person being asked, but the receiver of the question or the person being asked usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.vi: Because work was busy, I could not eat lunch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that has the state of being busy in the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い changes to くて to connect the reason clause with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks lunch as the object that could not be eaten in the negative potential sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べられませんでした is the negative past potential form and means that the speaker could not eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.why: The clause いそがしくて gives the reason before the result of being unable to eat lunch. Work is the subject of the busy state, while lunch is the object of 食べられませんでした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ので, the reason is presented more gently and objectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If the potential form られ is removed, the sentence only says “did not eat,” without emphasizing that the speaker was unable to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 食べられませんでした for “did not eat” instead of “could not eat”; られる expresses ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q16.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくて; Vて-form・Aな/N + で
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.vi: This piece of meat is very tender, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to refer to something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the piece of meat is the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective やわらかい to increase its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: やわらかい is the adjective predicate, while ですね adds a comment-like tone and seeks the listener’s agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.why: この must come directly before the noun to form the phrase “this piece of meat.” After the topic, とても modifies the adjective, and ですね ends a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with やわらかいです, the sentence is only a polite comment and does not seek agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use よ, the speaker emphasizes information for the listener instead of sharing the same feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place この after the noun, but Japanese places この before the noun and does not use の after この.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.vi: Would you like to eat together?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: いっしょに is an adverb showing that an action is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ごはん as the object of the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: Vませんか is used to make a polite invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.why: いっしょに modifies the action of eating, ごはん is the object used with を. The polite negative form ませんか is used as a gentle invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 食べましょうか, the speaker more actively suggests, “Shall we eat?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 食べたいですか, the question directly asks what the listener wants, so it is less natural than an invitation in this context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ませんか as a negative question, but in this pattern it usually means an invitation: “Shall we do … together?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.sk: N は + Time + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who performs the action in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The time phrase comes before the verb to show when the repeated action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べます is the predicate and uses the polite form of 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the time and the object of the action. The verb 食べます comes at the end of the sentence and takes the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace は with が, the sentence emphasizes that I am the person eating instead of simply stating the general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the time phrase after the verb, but Japanese usually places 毎日 before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.vi: There is a new supermarket near my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.sk: N の + location に + Aい + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with the noun for the area that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the supermarket was built or appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase before スーパー modifies that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object that has newly appeared or been formed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: できました is the predicate and describes a supermarket that has been completed or has appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.why: The location comes before に, while スーパーが is the new subject that has appeared, so が is used. The adjective comes before the noun to modify the supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use あります, the sentence only states that the supermarket exists. It does not emphasize that it was newly created or appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of が when introducing a newly appeared object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q20.kobun.vi: My house is quite far from the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: わたしのいえ is the topic being commented on, and は marks the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the reference point used to compare the distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective comes before です as the predicate and describes the state of the distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q20.kobun.why: The sentence makes my house the topic and uses the station as the reference point for judging the distance. から adds the standard or starting point for the adjective とおい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: より can also indicate a comparison point, but it is more formal and more common in writing than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use に after 駅 when expressing distance from a reference point. Use から in this case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the writing should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects じぶん with the following noun and shows possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content that needs to be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 書いてください uses the て form with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q21.kobun.why: The place where the action occurs comes first, followed by a noun phrase modified by の and marked by を. The Vてください pattern comes at the end to express a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vていただけますか, the request becomes softer and more humble, in the form of asking for permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; the verb must be changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who is in the mentioned state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates a place of existence or residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 住んで is the て form. It connects the verb 住む with います to show an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the Vている pattern and describes the current state of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q22.kobun.why: The place of residence goes with に, while the action 住む changes to the て form to connect with います. The whole Vています phrase acts as the predicate showing the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 住みます, the sentence only describes living somewhere or planning to live there. It does not emphasize an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q22.kobun.tip: With state verbs such as 住む, Vています is usually understood as living or residing somewhere. It does not necessarily mean that the action is happening in front of us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.vi: If you go straight up that slope, there is a supermarket on the right.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the route or place passed through during movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary form of a verb connects with と to state a natural result that occurs after the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the location where the supermarket exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is an existence predicate used for things such as スーパー.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.why: を marks the route passed through, then と connects the action with a natural result. The location 右に comes before the existing subject スーパーが, and あります ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with すすんだら, the sentence has a stronger conditional or specific-time meaning and does not emphasize an inevitable result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is similar to the present structure but usually describes a natural result or something that always happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use を to indicate the supermarket’s location. The location of existence must use に, while を here only indicates the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q24.kobun.vi: It is almost time for us to leave.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: This adverb modifies the action and shows that the time for the action is near.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of する, used to invite or suggest doing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q24.kobun.why: そろそろ signals that the suitable time is approaching, while しましょう is placed at the end to invite someone to depart together. The noun 出発 combines with する to form a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 出発しませんか, the sentence becomes a question-like invitation and sounds gentler.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q24.kobun.tip: With an action noun such as 出発, add する to form a verb before changing it into しましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q24.kobun.cn: N ＋ する／します／しましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies この道 as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: です follows an adjective to end a sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q25.kobun.why: この modifies 道, while は makes the whole phrase この道 the topic. くらい is an adjective ending in い that serves as the predicate and ends with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence means that this road is not dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that an adjective ending in い can stand directly before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.vi: My older sister has not been well lately, so I am worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ time ＋ N が ＋ negation ＋ ので ＋ N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the older sister as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase indicates the period of the state being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what the older sister lacks or does not have.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason with the speaker's conclusion that they are worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: This noun phrase gives the main content concluded at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends a noun sentence and gives it a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.why: The sentence first states the topic and then presents the health condition as the reason. ので connects the reason with the feeling or judgment in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with から, the meaning of the reason is almost unchanged, but the expression is usually more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget な before ので when the reason clause ends with a noun or an adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ な ＋ ので; N ＋ な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.vi: I am wearing the sweater my older sister gave me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the giver or source of the item received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause comes before セーター to modify the sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the sweater as the object of the action of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb 着る with います in the pattern describing the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている and indicates the present state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.why: The clause あねにもらった comes before セーター to identify which sweater it is. After を, 着ている describes the current state of the person wearing the sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If あねがくれた is used, the focus is on the older sister giving the sweater; the information source changes from the receiver to the giver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake あねに for the person performing the action, but with もらう, に indicates the giver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q4.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ N; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.vi: I finished cooking and then waited for everyone to arrive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the food as the object being made or cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of cooking with the action of waiting that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the clause 来る into a noun, while を marks it as the object being waited for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: まちました is the main predicate, in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.why: The form て connects two consecutive actions performed by the same subject. The clause about everyone coming is nominalized with の so that it can be the object of 待つ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 待っていました is used, the sentence emphasizes the state of waiting at a point in the past instead of simply saying that the waiting was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の when they want to use a whole clause as the object before を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q5.kobun.cn: Vて、; V普通形 ＋ のを ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.vi: I want to buy new clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.sk: Aい ＋ N が ＋ Vます-removeます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before ふく to modify the clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the desired object in the Vたい pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 買いたい expresses desire, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.why: The adjective 新しい modifies the noun ふく. In the Vたい pattern, the desired object usually takes が, then the verb changes to the form without ます and たいです is added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるつもりです is used, the sentence changes from expressing desire to expressing an intention that has been planned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may habitually use を with たい, but が is usually used to mark the desired object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the object being borrowed; the particle を is omitted in casual speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb uses the て form with もいい to ask permission to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: いいですか creates a question about permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q7.kobun.why: それ states the item to be borrowed, while かりてもいいですか is the permission structure. The て form comes before もいい to express “is it okay to do ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This also asks for permission, but it sounds more formal and rigid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This only expresses the desire to borrow something; it does not directly ask whether the other person allows it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may incorrectly use the dictionary form 借りる before もいい, but this pattern requires the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.vi: The answer to that problem is not A but B.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects そのもんだい with the noun that follows, creating a meaning of possession or relation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the answer the topic being identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: じゃなくて connects the negative part with the contrasting part that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: です concludes the sentence and identifies the answer as B.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.why: The phrase の modifies 答え, and then は makes 答え the topic. The pattern Aじゃなくて、Bです denies A and then affirms B.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is similar, but it is more formal and more common in written language than じゃなくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: It still contrasts A and B, but the full form is used in polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate の as “of” in every case; here it links the problem with the answer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.vi: Every morning, I wake up at 6 o'clock and leave home at 7 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N に ＋ Vて、＋ Time ＋ N を ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the repeated time of the whole action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the person wakes up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects waking up with the next action in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the time of leaving home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the place of departure with the verb 出ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb 出る in the present polite form describes a habitual action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.why: The two に each identify the time of one action. The て form links actions that happen in order in the same sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Emphasizes that the later action happens after waking up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Emphasizes the starting point of the next action from the time of waking up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t49-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で after a time, but the specific time in this sentence must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Number of people ＋ います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who exists in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 三人 is a counter for people. It comes before います to show the number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: います is the predicate showing that a person exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: 妹が states who exists, 三人 adds the number, and います expresses the existence of a person. The natural order is person ＋ number ＋ います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.t: N は ＋ Number of people ＋ います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use は, the sentence emphasizes or contrasts the topic instead of simply stating existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use あります, it is for objects or events, not for talking about a younger sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use あります for every meaning of “have,” but people must use います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: です links the subject being discussed with a noun for a time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q10.kobun.why: いま states the time being discussed, while （四月）です acts as a noun predicate to identify that time as April.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q10.kobun.tip: Do not add は after いま when the sentence uses いま as a time adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.sk: Time から ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the time when an action begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks what has been started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: はじめました is the main predicate in the past polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.why: The starting point comes at the beginning of the sentence with から, followed by the activity that is the object of はじめる. The ました form shows that the start has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use から after a clause, it can mean “because,” not only the time meaning “from.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with 以来, the nuance is “from last month until now,” emphasizing continuation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate から as “from” every time, but after a clause it usually means “because.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the defined topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: です links the topic, today, with the noun for the date.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q12.kobun.why: きょうは makes the current date the topic, while （八日）です identifies it as the eighth.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes that today itself is the eighth, rather than simply stating today as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q12.kobun.tip: Remember that 八日 is read as ようか, not by combining the usual sounds of 八 and 日.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vi: It takes only half the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Quantity しか ＋ Vない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes time the topic and creates a comparison or limitation nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: しか goes with a negative sentence to limit the quantity to half.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: かかりません is the polite negative form that must go with しか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.why: 時間は states the time range being discussed, 半分しか limits the amount of time, and かかりません provides the negative form to complete the pattern しか～ない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace しか with だけ, the sentence still means “only,” but the verb does not need to be negative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 半分も, the sentence emphasizes the surprisingly large amount, “as much as half,” and no longer has a limiting meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use しか with an affirmative verb; しか always needs a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vi: I will read everything before next month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.sk: Deadline までに ＋ Quantity ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: までに marks the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 読みます is the main predicate and shows an intended action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.why: The deadline comes at the beginning of the sentence with までに, followed by ぜんぶ, which states the scope of the reading. The verb 読みます comes at the end to complete the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace までに with まで, the meaning is “keep reading until next month,” without emphasizing completion before the deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use うちに, the nuance is to make use of the remaining time, not to meet a fixed deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse までに with まで; までに means “finish before the deadline,” while まで means “until.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the place identified as the largest classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies 大きい and creates a superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きい comes before 教室 to modify the noun; です ends the noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q15.kobun.why: ここが states the identified place, while いちばん大きい modifies 教室. The adjective 大きい comes before the noun, followed by です to end the polite sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing いちばん keeps the meaning “largest” but makes the tone more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the adjective after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese puts 大きい before 教室.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q16.kobun.vi: I do not have any brothers or sisters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 兄弟 the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: いません is the polite negative form of いる, used for people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q16.kobun.why: 兄弟 is made the topic with は, and then いません expresses that no person exists. The subject “I” is omitted because it is understood from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes not having siblings, rather than stating siblings as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use ありません for people; you need to use いません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to refer to an object near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes まち the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object described as numerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い is an adjective of quantity and the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q17.kobun.why: このまちは sets the scope of the topic, while 工場が is the object whose quantity is being described. With the adjective 多い, a noun with a large quantity often goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes the existence of many factories, while 多い emphasizes the characteristic of the area being “many.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q17.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate 多い as “crowded”; with 工場, the natural meaning is “many factories.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.vi: You will work tomorrow too, right?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.sk: Time noun も ＋ N を ＋ Vますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks tomorrow as a time when the action also applies, like on other days.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 仕事 as the object of the verb します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the polite form of する, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.why: あしたも identifies the time and adds the meaning “also,” while 仕事を is the object of する. か at the end makes the question polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Using は makes tomorrow the topic, without the meaning “also” emphasized by も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q18.kobun.tip: も replaces は or が when expressing “also”; do not use あしたもは at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.vi: If you have a question, please ask.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that exists in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: あれば is the conditional form of ある, connecting the condition “if there is a question” to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞いて is the て form, connecting the verb to ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください expresses a polite request or instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.why: 質問があれば creates the preceding conditional clause, and then 聞いてください is the main request. The ば form of ある expresses the condition “if there is.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Using あったら gives the sentence a more specific hypothetical meaning, such as “if there is a question at that time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: あるなら usually relies on information already mentioned or assumes that the listener has a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.tip: Do not change ある into あればる; the correct conditional form is あれば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q19.kobun.cn: Vば: Vる → Vえば; ある → あれば. Vてください: Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ is an adverb showing that something will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the new state or time after a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: なります describes a change to a new state or time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: もうすぐ refers to a time near the present, while 夏休みになります describes changing into summer vacation. With なる, the changed state or result usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 夏休みにします means that the subject actively decides or makes something become summer vacation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If もうすぐ is omitted, the sentence only says that it will become summer vacation, without emphasizing that it is approaching soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse になる with にする; になる describes a natural change or result, while にする shows active intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 写真 as the object of the verb とる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the phrase とる into a noun, while が marks this activity as the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: しゅみです serves as the predicate and identifies the preceding activity as a hobby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.why: 写真をとる is changed into a noun phrase with の, and this phrase becomes the subject with が. しゅみです is the predicate that states this activity is a hobby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Using は presents “taking photos” as the topic and gives a stronger contrast or emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: こと can also turn a phrase into a noun like の, but it sounds slightly more objective and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.tip: After のが, use a verb in the plain form such as とる, not とりますのが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ のが ＋ N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.vi: What would you like to choose for dinner?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes dinner the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に comes before します to show a choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: しますか creates a polite question about a choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.why: The topic is stated first with は. Then に marks the choice, and します describes the action of choosing. The form か at the end turns the sentence into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the question only means whether you will eat that dish, without emphasizing the choice of dish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the meaning focuses on making a final decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before します, but the choice pattern must use にします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with コート to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the coat the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 茶色です serves as the predicate and states the coat's color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q22.kobun.why: The possessive phrase わたしの comes before the noun コート. After the topic, the color noun combines with です to form a polite noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes that the coat is the thing that is brown, rather than simply making it the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q22.kobun.tip: Do not use な before 茶色 because 茶色 is a color noun and already combines directly with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: しっかり modifies the action of studying and shows how it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: 勉強する changes into 勉強して to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ください creates a polite request after a verb in the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q23.kobun.why: The adverb しっかり comes before the verb to modify how one studies. The verb uses the て form because the polite request pattern てください must connect to this form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence has a more direct and stronger command-like tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the request becomes softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q23.kobun.tip: Do not connect ください directly to the dictionary form; the verb must be changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this exercise the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: むずかしい is an い adjective used as the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q24.kobun.why: この must come directly before the noun 問題 to form a definite noun phrase. This phrase becomes the topic with は, while the adjective むずかしい states the topic's characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes that the noun is the thing that is difficult, rather than making it the familiar topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q24.kobun.tip: The adjective い keeps the ending い before です; it does not change to むずかしいなです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.vi: What kind of food would you like to eat?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな modifies 料理, while を marks the food as the object one wants to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: たい attaches to 食べる to express desire, and ですか creates a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ たいですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.why: どんな comes before 料理 to ask about the type or characteristic of the food. 料理を is the object of 食べたい, while たい expresses the desire of the speaker or the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the question asks what type or topic the food belongs to, without emphasizing its characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only asks whether someone will eat, without the meaning of wanting to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q25.kobun.tip: たい attaches to the verb stem ます, so use 食べたい rather than 食べるたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks 夜 as the subject that has the characteristic 長い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 長い is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate, with です added to make it polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: The noun 夜 is the subject, so it goes with が; 長い is the adjective describing the characteristic of 夜. An adjective ending in い comes before です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using は makes the night the topic and gives a more contrasting or general meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は out of habit, but が is suitable when identifying the subject that has the characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vi: Please stand up for a moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 立つ changes to the て form, becoming 立って to connect with ください and create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: ちょっと modifies the whole request and makes it sound softer. 立ってください is the request phrase, in which the verb must be in the て form before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This means that standing is allowed, not that the listener is being asked to stand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This means “let us stand,” so it sounds more like inviting someone to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: Do not connect 立つ directly to ください; change it to the て form: 立ってください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes スミスさん the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 力 as the direct object that has the quality つよい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: つよいです is an adjective predicate describing Mr. Smith’s strength.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to introduce the person being discussed, then uses が to indicate the person’s body part or ability being described. つよい is the adjective acting as the predicate for 力.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This structure makes 力 the topic and focuses directly on strength instead of mentioning Smith first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: The pattern NはNがA is usually not translated word for word as “as for N, N.” Instead, understand it as “N has a certain quality.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vi: The area outside my house is lively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with 外, showing that 外 belongs to or is connected with my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 外 as the place with the quality にぎやか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: にぎやか is a な-ending adjective, used with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.why: うちの modifies 外 with の to identify which place’s outside is meant. 外 is the subject being described, while にぎやかです is the predicate showing its lively state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using は makes 外 the topic, often giving a comment or contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q6.kobun.tip: A な-ending adjective such as にぎやか does not connect directly to a noun with が; you must distinguish the positions of の and が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 白い comes before 車 to modify the car directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 車 as the subject currently performing the action of running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: はしって is the て form of はしる. It connects with います to show an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the pattern Vている and expresses an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.why: 白い comes before 車, creating the noun phrase “the white car.” 車 is the subject, while はしっています describes the running action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is still “is running,” but the kanji 走る is used instead of the kana spelling はしる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This means “ran,” without emphasizing an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q7.kobun.tip: Do not always translate ている as “did” or “has done”; in this sentence, はしっている only shows an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vi: The school is right next to the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes 学校 the place whose location is being identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 駅 with そば and identifies the reference place used to describe the school’s location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: すぐ modifies そば and emphasizes that the distance is very short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: そばです acts as a location predicate and tells us that the school is beside the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.why: 学校 is the topic whose location must be identified. 駅のそば creates the location phrase “beside the station,” while すぐ emphasizes that the school is right next to that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 近く also means near, but covers a wider area than そば and does not necessarily mean immediately beside it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use に after そば in the pattern 〜は〜のそばです because そばです already acts as the location predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 行った modifies こと and creates the meaning “the act of having gone.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: こと nominalizes an action 行った, while が marks this as the subject of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ことがある expresses the experience of having done something before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.why: The place and purpose come before the verb 行った. The past-tense verb comes before こと to turn the experience into a noun, and then ことがある expresses “have done before.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence means “sometimes do,” not the experience of having done something before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence means “can travel,” referring to ability rather than experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t5-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ことがある with the possessive meaning “have,” but in this pattern it refers to an experience that has happened before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 車 as the object of the action of driving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: する combines with a noun that names an action to create the verb 運転する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns the preceding action into a noun, while が marks that act as something that can be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: できますか creates a polite question about ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.why: 車を is the object of 運転する. The phrase 運転すること turns the action of driving into a noun, allowing できます to express the ability to perform it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence still asks about ability, but it uses the verb’s potential form and sounds more concise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place を after こと, but を must come before the verb 運転する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.sk: N は + Time から + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies tennis as the activity being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of the activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: はじまります is the predicate for an event that starts by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.why: Tennis is the topic, and the 9 o’clock point goes with から to indicate the starting point. Then the verb はじまります ends the sentence. はじまる is an intransitive verb, so it does not need the object を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: に indicates the specific time when something happens, while から emphasizes that the activity starts from that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If おこないます is used, the subject must be a person or organization that carries out tennis, not the activity itself starting on its own.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を after テニス, but in this sentence tennis is the topic of the event, so は is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.vi: Today was a very enjoyable day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective たのしい to increase its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective たのしい comes before the noun to modify the day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: １日でした forms a polite past-tense noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.why: とても modifies たのしい, while たのしい comes before １日 to create the phrase “an enjoyable day.” The whole noun phrase combines with でした to comment on today in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: 楽しくて connects “enjoyable” with a following clause or quality, rather than directly modifying a noun like たのしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If １ is removed, the sentence still means that it was an enjoyable day, but it does not emphasize that it lasted a whole day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place とても after the adjective; in Japanese, とても usually comes before the adjective it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.vi: I lost to my older brother in a game.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person the speaker lost to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で marks the setting or means by which an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of まける connects with しまいました to create the pattern てしまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました describes something that has ended, often with a feeling of regret or that it was unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.why: The person or object involved comes first, the game setting comes next, and the main verb combines with てしまう at the end of the sentence. The particle で is suitable because the losing happened in a game.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence describes a state or an ongoing action, without stressing that it has ended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for a game, but a place or setting where an action happens usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q12.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう/しまいます/しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.vi: When winter comes, I want to travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks a point in time or a state that has been reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The たら form creates a condition or time clause and provides the basis for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks a purpose or an activity directed toward something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きたい expresses the speaker's desire, and です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.why: The なったら clause puts the time condition before the comma, and then states the desire. に in りょこうに goes with a verb for an activity as a destination or goal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used instead, the sentence means that whenever winter comes, the result naturally happens. This fits the speaker's desire less well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If なら is used, the sentence is based more on stated information or an assumption about winter than on stressing the time when winter comes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に in りょこうに with へ, but に here focuses on the activity or purpose of traveling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.tokens.2.m: when it changes, if it comes
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q13.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら; N に + なる; Vます-stem + たい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the cold quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate, and です makes the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q14.kobun.why: A noun for a thing comes before が, while the adjective い comes at the end to describe that thing. This structure is a direct descriptive sentence and does not need a linking verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the sentence makes the wind the topic for comparison or contrast, instead of simply stating the subject of the quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit が or use を, but the adjective つめたい needs its subject to go with が or は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.vi: Even if I am opposed, I will still study abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: されても is the passive form combined with ても, creating the concessive meaning “even if I am opposed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: りゅうがくします is the main predicate and states that the action will still be carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.cn: Vて形 + も; passive V: Vない remove ない + れる/られる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.why: The ても clause comes first to state an unfavorable situation, while the following clause states that the action does not change. The passive form shows that the speaker receives the effect of the opposition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active form 反対しても is used, it means “even if the speaker opposes someone,” not “even if the speaker is opposed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, the sentence focuses more on something contrary to expectations or on complaining than on the intention to continue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand されても as active, but it is passive: the speaker is opposed by other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.vi: I look it up with a dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object used in the act of looking something up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of using a dictionary with the following act of looking something up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: This is the main predicate and describes an action carried out with a dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.why: The object comes first, followed by the て form, which describes the method or an accompanying action. The action しらべます comes at the end because it is the main action of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If you say じしょでしらべます, で directly marks the means of looking something up, without stressing the order of using it and then looking something up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If ながら is used, the two actions are understood to happen at the same time, rather than the dictionary use being the method.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に to mark a tool, but a tool or means in this sentence needs で or the suitable て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q16.kobun.cn: Vて + V; 五段動詞: Vう → Vって
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.vi: Please tell me the meaning of this word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase with の modifies いみ and indicates the meaning belonging to this word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the meaning as the content to be explained or given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb おしえる with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is a pattern for politely asking the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.why: The phrase このことばのいみ is formed with の to identify the meaning of which word, and the whole phrase becomes the object with を. The てください form comes at the end to turn the act of telling into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If てくれますか is used instead, the sentence becomes a gentler request in question form rather than a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもらえますか is used, the speaker emphasizes wanting to receive help from the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put の in the wrong position; の must connect the modifying noun このことば with the main noun いみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q17.kobun.cn: Vて + ください; N の + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q18.kobun.vi: The teacher asked the student a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person receiving the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q18.kobun.why: 先生が is the subject, 学生に is the target of the action, and the final part is the predicate describing an action that happened. The particle に is suitable because the action is directed toward the student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with と, the meaning becomes “ask a question together with the student,” rather than “ask the student.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before the person being asked, but this recipient of the action must take に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.vi: I will explain what needs to be done from now on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: これから marks the starting point of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: する modifies こと and forms the noun phrase “what to do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what will be explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: します is a polite predicate for the action of explaining.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.why: これから comes before the phrase すること to identify what will be done from the present time. This noun phrase comes before を and acts as the object of the explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means “there is something to do from now on,” not “explain that thing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate and arrange this according to Vietnamese, but a modifying clause must come before こと in Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.vi: Let's take a photo here with everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the people who participate in the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the photo is taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks しゃしん as the object being photographed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう attaches to とる to make an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.why: みんなで states who will do it together, ここで states the place, and しゃしんを is the object of とる. These parts come before とりましょう in an order that adds meaning to the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a gentle invitation such as “Would you like to take a photo together?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for a place, but an action that happens at a place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.vi: I am interested in Vietnamese culture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects Vietnam with the noun “culture” and shows a modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object of interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the existence of something, namely interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: あります expresses the existence of interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.why: ベトナムのぶんか forms the phrase “Vietnamese culture.” The pattern に興味がある expresses having interest in an object, so に goes with the object and が goes with 興味.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 好きだ, the sentence leans toward “liking Vietnamese culture,” which is more direct and emotional than “being interested in.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say 興味をあります, but the fixed pattern is Nに興味があります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.vi: My older sister can speak both Japanese and English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.sk: N は + N も + N も + potential-form verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the older sister is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: も marks one item in a list and means “also.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: も is repeated to connect the second item in the meaning “both...and....”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 話せます is the polite potential form of 話す, expressing the ability to speak.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.why: あねは is the topic, and the two languages are listed with も...も to emphasize that both are within the range of ability. 話せます is placed at the end of the sentence as the shared predicate for the two items.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, it simply connects two nouns in a neutral way, with less emphasis on “both” than も...も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は for both languages, but the topic uses は only once; the parallel items use も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.vi: The construction work will be carried out in March.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.sk: Time に + N を + する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the construction work is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 工事 is the object acted on by します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 工事 as the content of the action of doing or carrying out something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: します is a polite predicate indicating an action that will be carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.why: ３月に is placed before the sentence to state the time, while 工事をします is the verb phrase “carry out construction work.” In Japanese, action nouns often combine with する and go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: で is not used to indicate the specific time of the action in this sentence; に is the correct choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を because 工事 already has an action meaning, but 工事する in this pattern usually uses 工事をする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.vi: I will report that the customer has arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.ch.1.vi: the fact that the customer arrived
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 来た modifies こと, turning the fact that the customer arrived into a noun that functions as the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: しらせます is a polite predicate indicating the action of reporting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.why: おきゃくさんが来た is the inner clause, in which the customer is the subject and 来た is the completed action. Adding こと turns the whole event into the content being reported, so this phrase comes before を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern talks about the experience of having done something before. It does not express reporting an event that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place こと after を, but the modifying clause must come before こと, and the whole phrase then takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q24.kobun.vi: I accompanied the customer to the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the person being taken or accompanied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: おくりました is the polite past form of おくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q24.kobun.why: The person being accompanied goes with を, while the endpoint goes with まで. The verb is in the polite past form to express a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is replaced with に, the sentence only emphasizes the destination, not the endpoint of the journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse まで with に; まで emphasizes the range or endpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.vi: Because I was very sleepy, I fell asleep as soon as I closed my eyes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.sk: Aい past + ので、N を + Vた + ら + すぐに + Vてしまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies the adjective and shows the degree of sleepiness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause to the result; ねむい changes to the past form ねむかった before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the eyes as the object of the action of closing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: たら connects an action that has happened with a result that occurs immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: すぐに modifies the action of sleeping and indicates that it happened very quickly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまいました expresses that the sleeping happened completely, with a nuance of being unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.why: The clause with ので states the cause first, and then たら connects closing the eyes with the result of falling asleep immediately. すぐに makes clear that there is almost no time between the two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the result usually has a natural or repeated meaning, so it is less suitable for the one-time event in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: てしまう emphasizes completion or regret, while たら expresses a time or condition relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may forget that たら follows the past form of the verb, not the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.vi: I looked at the map and went to that store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the map as the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the action of looking with the action of going that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement to that store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.why: ちずを is the object of 見る. The form 見て connects two actions in sequence, and then へ marks the direction toward the place mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見て is replaced with 見てから, the meaning emphasizes “going only after finishing looking at the map.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand て as “and” in every case, but here it also shows the order of the actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q4.kobun.vi: The train is not running because of an accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause of the train not operating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 電車 as the subject in the state of not running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ていません expresses the current state of not operating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q4.kobun.why: じこで states the cause, 電車が is the affected subject, and うごいていません describes the state of the train not operating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 事故なので is used, the cause is expressed with a more polite noun clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に to indicate the cause, but the direct cause in this sentence uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.vi: Because I have a headache, I will rest for a while.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that feels pain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause あたまがいたい with the action of resting that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ちょっと modifies the degree and duration of the rest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みます is the main predicate in polite form and indicates an intended action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.why: あたまがいたいので is the cause clause placed first. ちょっと adds a degree to 休みます, so the action of resting is presented briefly and naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still means “because I have a headache,” but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say “I have a headache” using 私は, but for pain in a body part, Japanese usually uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.vi: I was warned: “It is dangerous, so please do not run.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason to the warning that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the entire quoted request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: されました expresses that the speaker received the action of being warned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.why: The clause あぶないので gives the reason, the request is placed in quotation marks, and と introduces that quotation before the passive verb されました. This structure emphasizes that the speaker is the person who received the warning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and informal, while ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a way to ask someone not to do something; unlike なければなりません, which expresses an obligation to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often forget that ので must follow the plain form of the reason clause, and と must come after the entire quotation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q6.kobun.cn: Aい・Aなな + ので; Vないで + ください; 普通形 + と + Vられる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.vi: When school ends, let’s meet at the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that completes the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a condition or an earlier time with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the meeting takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or a suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.why: 学校が終わったら is the time point for carrying out the action 会いましょう. The place of the action comes before the predicate and is used with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is used, the sentence simply says “when” as a time noun; たら emphasizes a condition or an earlier completed time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: あとで means “after” in time order and does not have as clear a conditional meaning as たら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often mistakenly use が as は in a conditional clause, although が here marks the subject that finishes studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q7.kobun.cn: Vた + ら; Aいかったら; Aなだったら; Nだったら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.vi: Sorry, Wednesday is not convenient for me.
