default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が connects a polite opening with the information the speaker wants to give.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes Wednesday the topic and states its specific condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject being described as good or not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: わるいです forms the adjective predicate and says that the day is not convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.why: は limits the scope to Wednesday, while つごうがわるい is the phrase describing the inconvenient condition. The adjective わるい comes before です to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If わるい is replaced with いい, the meaning changes to “convenient” or “I am free.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression only says that there is already a schedule; it does not necessarily mean a refusal because it is inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may say つごうはわるい when they want to describe a subject; in this pattern, が is more natural for describing a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q9.kobun.vi: I will go home early today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time point for the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The form はやく modifies the verb かえります and shows when the speaker will return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: かえります is the polite predicate form and expresses the action of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q9.kobun.why: 今日 identifies the time, はやく comes before the verb to modify the manner or time of the action. The predicate かえります is placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 早いです can be a predicate meaning “early,” while はやく must be used to modify a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t50-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often keep the adjective はやい unchanged before a verb; when it modifies a verb, the い-ending adjective must change to はやく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.vi: I have recently gained weight, so I want to lose weight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.sk: Time + Vてしまったので、Vたいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん indicates the period when something happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: てしまった expresses a completed event, often with an unwanted feeling; ので connects it to the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: たいです attaches to a verb stem to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; Vます remove ます + たい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.why: さいきん is placed at the beginning to state the time, followed by the reason for gaining weight. The result やせたいです uses たい to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If たくない is used, the sentence says that the speaker does not want to do something instead of wanting to lose weight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use たい with nouns; in this pattern, it must attach to a verb stem after removing ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うし with こども, forming the phrase “the cow’s child” or the cow’s young.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that was born.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: うまれました is the polite past form of an intransitive verb and describes the birth of the young animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q10.kobun.why: うしのこども creates a compound noun meaning a cow’s young. Because 生まれる is an intransitive verb, the young animal is the subject with が, and the event is placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 産みました is used, the sentence becomes active and emphasizes the mother cow as the one giving birth to the young.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use を with 生まれる, but this verb usually uses が for a person or animal that is born.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.vi: Recall your childhood and write an essay.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects こども with ころ to modify the period being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ころ with こと to modify what is remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content that the listener is asked to remember.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects recalling with the following action of writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the essay as the object of the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 書く changes to the て form to connect with ください and create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to express a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.why: The phrase こどものころのこと forms the content being remembered and receives を. The two actions are connected by the て form, and then ください is placed at the end to turn the writing action into a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence lists typical actions instead of expressing the sequence of recalling and then writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use を after ころ, but ころのこと is the complete noun phrase that receives を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.vi: He was wearing work clothes stained with oil.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents him as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the cause or agent that made the clothes dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause よごれた modifies the noun 作業着 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the clothes as the object being worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 着る changes to the て form to connect with いる and express the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: いた is the past form of いる and shows that the state of wearing existed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.why: あぶらでよごれた is the clause placed before to describe 作業着. 作業着 receives を because it is what is worn, while 着ていた expresses the state of wearing at a point in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 着た, the sentence only says that the action of putting it on was completed, without emphasizing the state of wearing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate 着ていた as “wore”; here, understand it as being in the state of wearing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q12.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; Vて + いた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.vi: My younger brother’s room window suddenly flew open, and then the sound of glass breaking rang out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の only shows possession and modifies 部屋.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 部屋 and 窓 to form the phrase “the room’s window.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the window as the subject of the opening action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: と follows an onomatopoeic word to describe the manner or sound of the opening action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 開く changes to the て form to connect the window opening with the next event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the glass as the subject of the clause describing the breaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: われる is the predicate of the clause and, together with ガラスが, modifies 音.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: が marks the sound as what is produced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.ch.8.n: する in 音がする describes producing or hearing a sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.why: The two clauses are connected by 開いて、 to describe events that happen one after another. Clause ガラスがわれる comes before 音 and modifies the type of sound produced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 音を聞いた, the sentence emphasizes that the listener heard the sound, rather than describing the sound as occurring by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 音, but the pattern 音がする uses が because the sound is something that is produced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.vi: I was really worried about whether my test score was bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しけん and てん to form the phrase “the test score.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the test score as the subject being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the preceding clause into the content of the worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ほんとうに modifies 心配 and emphasizes the degree of worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: でした ends a noun sentence and describes a worried state in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.why: The phrase しけんのてん is the subject of the indirect question clause. Clause わるくないか gives the content of the worry, while 心配でした is the main predicate at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If かどうか is used, the sentence simply states whether something is bad or not, making it more neutral than the negative question form わるくないか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q14.kobun.tip: か should not be translated as a direct question; here, it is part of an indirect clause meaning “whether it was bad or not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.vi: In Japan, most houses have a bathroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: では both sets Japan as the topic range and indicates the location context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects たいていの and 家 to modify the range of houses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates where the bathroom exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the existing object in the pattern NにNがある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: ある is the predicate that expresses the existence of a non-living thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.why: では sets Japan as the range, and then 家に indicates the place containing or where something exists. Since the bathroom is an existing object, it takes が, while ある comes at the end to complete the existence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence describes an action taking place in the house and does not fit the pattern for expressing existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.tip: With ある, a location usually goes with に and the existing object goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q15.kobun.cn: 場所に + Nが + ある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.vi: By July, Japan becomes very hot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + V辞書形と + 副詞 + Aいく + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents Japan as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when it changes to July.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition or time with a result that usually happens automatically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 暑い changes into 暑く to modify なる, while すごく indicates the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: なる shows a change of state, here meaning “becomes hot.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.why: 7月に identifies the time, while なると connects that time with the usual result that the weather becomes hot. The adjective 暑い must change to 暑く before なる to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with たら, the sentence focuses on a one-time condition or assumption and is less natural than と when describing a regular event linked to time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q16.kobun.tip: Before なる, an adjective ending in い must change い into く; do not say あついなります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.vi: The wind suddenly blows, and the sky becomes dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.sk: Adverb + N が + Vて + N が + Aいく + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: きゅうに is an adverb that modifies the event happening afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the subject performing action ふく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ふいて is the て form of ふく, used to connect the wind blowing with the next event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle が marks the subject that has state くらい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: くらく is the く form of adjective くらい, connected to なる to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.why: The adverb きゅうに comes first to modify an action that happens suddenly. The pattern Aいくなる connects adjective くらい with なる and describes the sky changing to a dark state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern describes a change to a new state, while Aい simply describes a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change くらい to くらく before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.vi: Suddenly, it started raining very heavily.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.sk: Adverb + N が + Aいく + Vて + くる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: きゅうに is an adverb that modifies the intensity and timing of the rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks 雨 as the subject being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: つよく is the く form of the adjective つよい, modifying the verb ふる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ふって is the て form of ふる, connecting with くる to express a phenomenon that begins or progresses toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: きました combines with ふって to form ふってくる, the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.why: つよく modifies ふって to show that the rain is falling heavily. ふってくる combines the て form with くる, emphasizing that the rain is beginning to appear or progressing toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ふっています, the sentence only describes the state of raining and does not emphasize its beginning or progress toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q18.kobun.tip: ふってくる should not be translated mechanically as “fall and come”; the whole phrase describes a phenomenon beginning to occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.vi: The place where I am working is a factory built last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.sk: N ＋ Vている ＋ ところは ＋ Time ＋ past passive V ＋ N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: 今 indicates the present time and modifies the phrase はたらいている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: はたらいて is the て form, combining with いる to create the state of being at work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: はたらいている is a modifying clause for ところ, identifying the place where the person is working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes ところ the topic explained in the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: きょねん indicates the time when the building action occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: たてられた is a past passive clause modifying こうじょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: こうじょうです is the concluding part, identifying that place as a factory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.why: The clause はたらいている comes before ところ to modify the noun “place.” Similarly, きょねんたてられた comes before こうじょう to identify when the factory was built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with はたらくところ, it means “the place where someone is about to work” or “the place where someone will work,” not the place where someone is currently working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with はたらいたところ, the meaning leans toward “the place where someone worked,” emphasizing that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places it before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Nが＋V受身普通形 ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.vi: You can hear the lively voices of children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Aなな ＋ Nが ＋ natural ability V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with the following noun, showing that the voice belongs to the children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 元気 is a な adjective, so な must be used before the noun こえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the sound that is heard in the structure 聞こえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞こえます is a predicate indicating that a sound naturally reaches the ears or can be heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.why: 子どもの and 元気な both modify こえ. With 聞こえる, a sound that is heard usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 聞きます is used, the subject actively listens to the sound, while 聞こえます describes a sound that is heard naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit な after the adjective な when it comes before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.vi: I will attend an English conversation school until March.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time まで ＋ N に ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes わたし the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle まで indicates the ending point of attending school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks a destination or a place that someone regularly goes to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: かよいます is the predicate, describing regularly going to school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.why: わたしは states the person performing the action. The phrase 3月まで sets the deadline, while the school goes with に because it is the place the speaker regularly goes to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is replaced with までに, the sentence means that an action must be completed before or by March.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is replaced with へ, the sentence only indicates movement toward the school and emphasizes direction more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use で to mark the destination with かよう; the destination of this verb usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.vi: He was injured in a traffic accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes かれ the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the cause that led to the injury.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks けが as the noun used with する in the phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of する, completing the verb phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.why: こうつうじこで states the cause, while けがをする is a noun phrase + する, so けが functions as the object of を. しました puts the whole event into the polite past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with こうつうじこにあう, the sentence focuses on “having a traffic accident” and does not directly state the result of being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a form written without spaces, but the structure and meaning remain unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit を because they translate けがをする as a single verb, but けが is a noun that must be used with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.vi: Westerners eat using a knife and fork.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the group of people being discussed the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と connects ナイフ and フォーク as two tools used together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the tool used for eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 食事する is the main predicate, describing the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.why: は states the topic, と connects two equal nouns, and で marks the tool used to perform the action. The tool phrase comes before the predicate 食事する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with や, the sentence means using a knife, a fork, and other tools, not limiting the meaning to the two items.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If フォークで is replaced with フォークを使って, the meaning is still using a fork, but it emphasizes the act of using it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q22.kobun.tip: Here, the particle と means “and,” not a particle indicating a companion or quotation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 学校を is the object of 卒業する, indicating the place from which the speaker graduates.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of graduating with the later action of entering society.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination or target state that the speaker enters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q23.kobun.why: 学校を is the object of the action of graduating. The clause て comes between them to connect the two actions in sequence, while に marks the destination of 出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence emphasizes the result or event that occurs immediately upon graduation, rather than simply connecting two actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle を after 学校, but 学校を卒業する is the correct expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.vi: I was thinking that I wanted to change my way of life.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks いきかた as the object that is wanted to be changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: と quotes the content of the thought, namely the wish to change one's way of life.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects おもう with いた to express an ongoing state of thinking in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.cn: Vたい ＋ と ＋ 思う／考える; Vている is used to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.why: The phrase じぶんのいきかたを is the object of the desire. The content of the desire comes before と, and then 思っていた shows that it was a thought that existed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If と思った is used, the sentence only states a time when the person thought about it, while と思っていた emphasizes an ongoing state of thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use を after かえたい; the content before と is connected to 思う by the particle と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.vi: If someone who does not know how to use the machine touches it, it will be dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the content that is not known, namely how to use the machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause わからない modifies 人, while が marks the person who performs the action in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the condition with the dangerous result that occurs when the person touches the machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.cn: Vる／Vない／Vた ＋ と; NのN が わからない are used with a clause that modifies the noun before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.why: The clause わからない comes before 人 to identify what kind of person is meant. The condition さわると comes before the result あぶないです and shows a result that naturally occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, the sentence has a more specific hypothetical condition, instead of a rule-like result such as と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate がわからない人 as “a person who does not understand people,” but が here marks the unknown thing: how to use the machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q3.kobun.sk: Degree ＋ N が ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 少し modifies the degree of pain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: いたいです is an adjective predicate that describes the state of the head.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q3.kobun.why: When describing symptoms, the body part goes with が, and the adjective describes the state of that body part. 少し is placed before it to reduce the degree of pain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, the structure is unnatural with the adjective いたい because pain is not an action that affects the head.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may easily say 頭を痛い, but 頭が痛い must be used to say “have a headache.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.vi: Please go straight along this road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.sk: この ＋ N を ＋ Adverb ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies the noun 道.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the route or space that the speaker asks someone to travel through.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: まっすぐ modifies the way of moving in the action すすむ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to ask or instruct the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.why: 道を indicates the route to take, while まっすぐ indicates the direction. すすんでください is placed at the end to make the sentence a polite instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is replaced with に, 道に通常 indicates a destination or a place where something exists, so it does not naturally express a travel route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vないでください is used, the sentence becomes a request not to go straight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に with 道, but when talking about traveling along a route, を is the appropriate particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q5.kobun.vi: The teacher’s explanation is very easy to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 先生 with the noun 説明 and creates a possessive relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the explanation the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q5.kobun.why: The phrase 先生の modifies 説明, and then は presents 説明 as the topic. The adjective わかりやすい comes at the end to comment on that topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the emphasized noun is the subject that has the quality of being easy to understand, rather than the general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit の or put の in the wrong position when they want to say “the teacher’s explanation.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q6.kobun.vi: Winter is coming soon, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ですね is used to confirm or share an observation with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q6.kobun.why: もうすぐ comes before a noun to indicate a time in the near future. ですね at the end of the sentence creates a sense of confirming it together with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with そろそろ, the meaning is “it is almost time,” often suggesting that an action or change will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may translate もうすぐ as “immediately,” but this word usually means “soon, before long.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.vi: My child got my clothes dirty, unfortunately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the clothes as the object affected by the action of making them dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に in a passive sentence indicates the person who performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: よごされて is the passive form connected to しまった, showing that the subject was affected unwillingly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまった expresses that something has been completed and often includes regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ しまう・しまった; Vられる・Vされる is used to form the passive voice
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.why: 服を is the object affected, while 子どもに is the agent in the passive sentence. The verb is in the て form to connect with しまった, emphasizing that the event happened unwillingly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this active sentence is used, the focus shifts to the child as the person who made the clothes dirty, without emphasizing the inconvenience to the affected person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If てしまった is replaced with ている, the sentence only describes a state or an ongoing action and no longer has a sense of an unfortunate or regrettable result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse に in the passive sentence with the object and forget that it only indicates the person who caused the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.vi: I said goodbye to Mr. Sato at the station around noon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who takes part in the action of saying goodbye.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ひるごろ indicates the approximate time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the action of saying goodbye takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ました changes the verb into the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.why: と names the person who performs the action together, ひるごろ indicates the time, and えきで indicates where the action takes place. The past-tense verb comes at the end to complete the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 会いました is used, it means that you met Sato, not that you said goodbye.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 離れました is used, the focus is on moving away from a person or place, not necessarily on saying goodbye.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に for the place of the action, but the place where the farewell takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.vi: Please carefully load that glass product onto the truck.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the glass product as the object to be handled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: 気をつけて uses the て form to connect the reminder to be careful with the following request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or position where the product is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.why: は identifies the item to be handled, and 気をつけて is a reminder that comes before the main action. に indicates the destination where the product is placed, while てください comes at the end to turn the action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vなさい, the sentence has a stronger and less gentle command-like tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてもいいです is used, the sentence asks about or gives permission to do the action, so it is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t51-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse に with で; に is where the product is placed, while で usually indicates where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.vi: I felt pain because the person next to me stepped on my foot on the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects でんしゃ with なか to modify the space inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the foot-stepping happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.ch.2.vi: by the person next to me
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the body part affected by being stepped on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form of the passive voice connects the direct cause with the feeling of pain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The past form of the adjective describing the feeling of pain that occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.cn: V受身て ＋ Aいかったです; Vて connects an event with a following feeling or result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.why: で identifies the setting where the event happened, while に identifies the person causing the effect in the passive sentence. あしを is placed before the passive form to state the affected body part, and then connects to the feeling of pain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to the active voice, the focus shifts to the person next to me who stepped on my foot, without emphasizing the speaker's affected experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q1.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person performing the action usually goes with に, not が as when they are the active subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q10.kobun.vi: Let's take a break here for about 10 minutes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the phrase とる, forming the expression 休憩をとる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: とりましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q10.kobun.why: The place is placed first with で, followed by the duration and the object of とる. The とりましょう form at the end of the sentence turns the statement into a polite suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, it means taking a general rest, without emphasizing taking a specific break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate it word for word as take a break, so remember that 休憩をとる naturally means take a break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the sea is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective and shows a very high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: です comes after an adjective to end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q11.kobun.why: は puts the topic at the beginning, and とても comes before the adjective to increase its degree. An adjective ending in い combines directly with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, the meaning changes to the sea is not wide.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q11.kobun.tip: Do not add な after an adjective ending in い before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.vi: I felt very good after fishing in the river.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the fishing action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks fish as the object being caught.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: つって is the て form of つる, connecting the fishing action with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the state よかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: よかったです is the polite past form of よい, describing a good feeling after the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.why: で states where the action takes place, を marks the object, and then the て form connects that action with a result or feeling. In the following clause, が goes with the subject of the feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes that the following clause happens after fishing is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence clearly shows a cause-and-effect relationship: because I went fishing, I felt good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q12.kobun.tip: The て form here does not itself carry past meaning; it is mainly used to connect two clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: にも combines with に and も, indicating the range where something exists and meaning in every country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses the existence of a non-living thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q13.kobun.why: The range phrase with にも comes first, followed by the existing thing with が. あります is placed at the end to complete the existence pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence has the nuance of presenting history as a topic or contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q13.kobun.tip: In the existence pattern, do not use を for the thing that exists; use が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.vi: The machine is broken, so let's ask someone to repair it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the thing that is in a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: こわれている describes the broken state, while ので connects this clause to the reason for the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: なおして is the て form, connecting the verb repair with もらう to express having someone do it for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.ch.3.vi: let's ask someone to do it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてもらいましょう expresses a suggestion to ask someone else to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.why: The first clause states the current condition and uses ので to give the reason. Then, Vてもらう shows asking someone else to do it or having it done for you, and ましょう turns it into a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means let's repair it ourselves or together, without emphasizing asking someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.tip: Vている in this sentence indicates a broken state, not an action of breaking something that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.tokens.6.m: ask someone to do it for you
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q14.kobun.cn: Vているので / Vて ＋ もらう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.vi: When sending an important item, ask the post office to handle it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: おくる modifies とき, forming the time phrase when sending; には emphasizes that situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the request is made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: たのみます is the main predicate and describes the act of asking or requesting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.why: The object comes before the time phrase, while the place of the action comes immediately before the predicate. The dictionary-form verb おくる comes before とき because the sending is viewed as unfinished at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with おくったとき, it means when the item has already been sent, emphasizing that the sending is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is used, the focus is on the post office as the party being asked; で in the current sentence focuses on the place where the request is made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q15.kobun.tip: Do not change おくる into the past before とき if you want to refer to the time before or during sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.vi: My father is working at a factory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action はたらく takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects はたらく with the existence verb います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: います describes a state or an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the place of the action goes with で, and then Vている is used to talk about an action in progress. Here, います adds the meaning of continuation to はたらいて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with にいる, it means being in a place, without emphasizing the action of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a shorter form equivalent to Vて＋います in normal spoken and written language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of で when talking about the place where an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.vi: The air in this area is very polluted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify へん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: へん indicates the area covered, while は makes that area the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the quality きたない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate and combines with です to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.why: このへん is the area presented as the topic, while くうき is the actual subject of the quality, so it goes with が. The adjective きたない comes before です at the end to complete the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If くうきは is used, the sentence focuses directly on the air and no longer clearly presents the area as the range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: Do not put です directly after the adjective い; the correct form is Aいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse が and は, or add な after the adjective い and before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.vi: Because it is raining, please be careful on your way home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: なので connects the reason to the reminder in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 気 as the object of つける, while て connects the reminder to the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of かえる connects the action of returning with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください makes a polite request or asks someone for a favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and is connected with なので. The phrase 気をつけて expresses a reminder, and then かえってください asks the listener to return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: With this form, the sentence becomes a request not to do a certain action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget を in the fixed phrase 気をつける and use the wrong form てください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.vi: The sales plan has already been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects はんばい with けいかく, making the preceding noun a modifier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: けいかく is the main noun, while は presents the plan as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: もう modifies the action to show the time by which it has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: きまった is the past form of きまる and describes a state that has been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.why: はんばいのけいかく is a noun phrase in which はんばい modifies the plan with の. もう combines with Vた to show that the decision has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 販売計画 is used, the two nouns combine directly into one term, giving a more compact meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, the meaning changes to say that the plan has not been decided yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically translate の as "of," although here it means "about" or "related to."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.vi: Because I cannot hear clearly, please speak a little louder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason for not hearing clearly with the request in the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase adds a degree to 大きい and asks for a slight increase in volume.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the method or volume used when speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: お願いします makes a polite request to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.why: The reason is given first with ので, followed by the request. で shows the method or volume to use, while お願いします makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the reason sounds more direct and personal; ので sounds softer and more objective in a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of で in 大きい声で, but で only indicates the method or volume used when speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.vi: The concert has not started yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes コンサート the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies a negative predicate to express that something has not happened up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: はじまりません is the polite negative form of はじまる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and まだ comes before the predicate to limit the state to the present time. The polite negative form shows that the starting has not happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to say that the concert has already started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used with a suitable verb, the focus is on an action that is still continuing, not on one that has not started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake まだ～ません for "still not" instead of "not yet."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.vi: My company is in an inconvenient location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with かいしゃ to show that the company belongs to or is related to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents かいしゃ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: ふべんな modifies ばしょ, while に indicates the place where the company exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: ある is a predicate that indicates the existence or location of an object, place, or organization.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.why: わたしのかいしゃ creates a noun phrase as the topic. The adjective な comes before ばしょ to modify it, and then に marks the location where the company exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ふべんなばしょ is omitted, the sentence only gives the information about where the company is located and does not express the judgment that it is inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If です is used, the sentence introduces or identifies the company as a place, without clearly expressing its location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な after the adjective な when it comes before a noun, and use で instead of に with ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.vi: I do not have time to visit him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: には identifies the person in the situation "for me" and emphasizes that scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action たずねる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb before じかん modifies the type of time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks what is identified as existing or not existing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります and expresses nonexistence or lack.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.why: The object かれ を comes before the verb to form a clause that modifies じかん. Then じかんが ありません expresses that there is no time to do that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used instead, the meaning changes to "in order to visit him," emphasizing purpose rather than a clause modifying time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことができる is used instead, the sentence talks about the ability to visit him, not a lack of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put じかん before the modifying clause, but in Japanese the modifying clause must come before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.vi: This robot can work as a guide.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes このロボット the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: も replaces を, showing that a robot can also take this role.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb that modifies こと in a pattern expressing ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the action into a noun, while が marks an action that can be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: できます completes the pattern ことができます, expressing ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.why: The action つとめる is turned into a noun with こと and combined with ができます to say “can do.” も emphasizes that this is also a role the robot can take on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern describes a change into being able to do something, not just a present ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means deciding to do something, not being able to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use Vます directly with できます; use V辞書形 ＋ ことができます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q23.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ことができる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.vi: The sun rises in the east.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the sun the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the starting point of the sun's rising.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: でる is the main predicate, in the dictionary form to state a general rule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は. Then から states where it starts, and でる describes the direction in which the sun appears. The dictionary form suits a regular fact.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で focuses on the place where the action happens. It is less natural than から when saying “rise from the east.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: へ shows movement toward the east, not the sun's starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で for every place, but から is needed for a starting point or source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.vi: Because it is hot, I do not feel like eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects the hot condition with the result of having no appetite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks what is said not to exist in this condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ありません denies the existence of しょくよく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.why: The adjective あつい changes to あつくて to connect the reason with the following clause. しょくよくがありません describes the state of having no appetite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also gives a reason, but its explanatory tone is clearer and softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: のに shows contrast, creating the meaning “although it is hot...,” which differs from the cause-and-effect relationship in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q25.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い must change to くて when connecting with て. Do not use あついて directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.vi: Because I woke up late, I run to the station when going to work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て connects the state of waking up late with the action of running in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the purpose or direction related to work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: とき creates a time clause that modifies the action of running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: まで shows the endpoint of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.why: The clause て gives the earlier condition. とき identifies the time of going to work, while まで marks the destination of the running action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason for waking up late is stated more clearly. The form て only connects the condition with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に and まで: に shows the direction or purpose of going to work, while まで shows the endpoint, the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q3.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; Vる／Vない／Vた ＋ とき; N ＋ まで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.vi: The other day, I went skiing for the first time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase shows the time when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 初めて modifies the verb した and shows that the action happened for the first time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks スキー as the object of the action した.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: した is the past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first. Then 初めて modifies the action. スキーをする uses を to mark the content of the action する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning becomes “first” or “at the beginning,” without emphasizing a first-time experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse 初めて with 初めに because both relate to “first,” but 初めて usually modifies an action experienced for the first time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.vi: The person wearing those brown trousers is Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the color word with the noun ズボン to modify the trousers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks ズボン as the item being worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: はいて is the て form of はく. It connects with いる to show the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The clause はいている modifies 人, while は makes 人 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: です connects the topic 人 with the identifying part, たなかせんせい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.why: The phrase はいている人 forms a modifying clause before 人. The whole phrase “the person wearing those brown trousers” is the topic, and です identifies who that person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If はいている is replaced with はいた, the meaning focuses on someone who wore or has finished wearing the item, not on the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate はいている as “wore,” but in this sentence it describes the state of currently wearing the trousers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.vi: I prefer Western clothes to kimono.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わたし the topic of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects ようふく with ほう, forming a phrase for the preferred side in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ほうが marks the side judged to be better in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: すきだ is the predicate expressing preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.why: より gives the comparison standard, while のほうが marks the preferred side as better. すきだ comes at the end to give a judgment about preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this pattern changes the sentence into a negative comparison, such as “N2 does not like N1 as much as...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the comparison object in the pattern より. Use N1より N2のほうが to express “N2 is preferred to N1.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q6.kobun.cn: N1より ＋ N2のほうが ＋ Aなだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.vi: That person used to be a principal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks ひと as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: いぜん indicates a time in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the position held in the pattern 〜をする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: していた describes a state or job that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.why: いぜん sets the past context, and the position goes with を in the expression 〜をする. していた shows that holding the position existed during an earlier period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Nだった, the sentence only states a past status and does not stress the meaning of “holding a position” as 〜をしていた does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q7.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate していた as “did”; with positions, it usually means “once held the position” or “once worked in that profession.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.vi: I heard that my mother forgot her wallet in the cafeteria.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 母 the topic of the reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the wallet was left behind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks さいふ as the object that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: わすれた is the past form of わすれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです appears at the end of the sentence to show information heard from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.why: The place に comes before the object を because it shows where the forgetting happened. The past-form verb connects with そうです to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ようです, the sentence expresses an assumption based on signs or the speaker’s judgment, not necessarily something heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.tip: Distinguish そうです, which reports information, from そうです, which describes appearance; after a verb in the plain form, そうです usually means “I heard that.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形 + そうだ（伝聞）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.vi: This office is convenient because it is close to the station and the shopping district.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks じむしょ as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: や connects places given as examples without implying a complete list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the place used as a reference point for the adjective ちかい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the reason clause to the conclusion べんりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: べんりです is the conclusion evaluating the office.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.why: や lists typical places, while に identifies the places near the office. The clause ちかいので gives the reason first, and then the sentence concludes with べんりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced by から, the cause has almost the same meaning, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget な before ので when connecting nouns or な adjectives; however, adjectives such as い, including ちかい, connect directly to ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t52-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + ので／Aな・N + なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.vi: I like a house in the countryside where birds sing and flowers bloom everywhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject performing the action of calling or singing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the image of singing birds with the scene of blooming flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject performing the action of blooming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: いっぱい modifies さく and shows that many flowers are blooming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the plain form stands at the end of the clause that modifies いえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: の connects いなか with いえ, forming the phrase “a house in the countryside.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: が marks the object liked in the main sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: すきです is the main predicate and expresses a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.why: The clause とりがないて はながいっぱいさく comes before いえ to describe the house. In the main sentence, いえが combines with すきです to show the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: ないで means “without singing, ...,” so it negates the bird’s action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: たくさん also means many, but focuses more on quantity; いっぱい creates a feeling of fullness or abundance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.tip: You need to identify いえが as the subject of すきです, while the earlier clauses only modify いえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; Vて + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.vi: It is dark. Could you turn on the light for me?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the light as the object being turned on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: つけて is the て form and connects turning on the light with the request pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: もらえませんか expresses a polite request, meaning that the speaker asks the listener to do something for them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.why: The reason is given first with ので, followed by the object and the requested action. The pattern てもらえませんか makes the request softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with てください, the sentence becomes a more direct request, with less of the meaning “do it for me.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.tip: Do not translate もらう here as “receive”; the whole phrase てもらえませんか means “could you do it for me?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; Vて + もらえませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q11.kobun.vi: A beautiful view can be seen from the rooftop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q11.kobun.sk: Nから + Aなな + Nが + potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the starting point or viewing location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: きれいな modifies けしき, while が marks the scenery that can be seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q11.kobun.why: The viewing location comes first, followed by the scenery and the verb みえる. With みえる, the object seen usually takes が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見る is used, it means that the subject actively looks at the scenery, rather than the scenery simply coming into view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use を with みえる; the object seen in this structure usually takes が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.vi: Now, please open page 10 of the textbook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: それでは moves to the next action based on the situation just described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects テキスト with the page being mentioned, creating a possessive or belonging relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks page 10 as the object of the action of opening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to politely ask or instruct the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.why: The name of the material modifies the page, and the page is the object of the verb “open.” The て form combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 開けてください is used, it usually means opening something that can be closed, such as a door or a box. It is less natural than 開いてください with a book page.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q12.kobun.tip: Distinguish 開く（ひらく）, which is used for books, pages, and meetings, from 開ける（あける）, which is used for doors, boxes, or closed objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.vi: I hear that eating fish and tofu instead of meat is better for the body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: のかわりに indicates the thing being replaced in the choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: や lists examples, while を marks the group of food being eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べるほうが states the choice being compared and marks that choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the object that receives a benefit or is judged positively or negatively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.ch.4.vi: it is said to be good
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです follows the plain form to pass on information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.why: The replacement phrase first states the rejected choice, followed by the food that is chosen. ほうが turns the choice “eating fish and tofu” into the comparison clause, while に indicates that the body is the object receiving the benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 肉より is added, the sentence clearly states that meat is the point of comparison, while ほうが emphasizes the better choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is understood as 様態, the meaning changes to “looks good” and is no longer information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use のかわりで; the replacement pattern is Nのかわりに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q13.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ かわりに; V辞書形 ＋ ほうが; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ（伝聞）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.vi: My parents sometimes took me to an art exhibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the parents the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks me as the person taken by my parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: えの modifies てんらんかい, while に indicates the destination of the action of taking someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: つれて is the connecting form of つれる. It combines with いく to mean taking someone somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: いってくれた shows that the parents performed the action for the speaker’s benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いく; Vて ＋ くれる（past: くれた）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.why: The parents are made the topic, and I am the person taken. The destination goes with に, while the sequence つれていってくれた describes taking me somewhere and doing it for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 連れて行った is used, it only says that the parents took me somewhere and does not emphasize that the action benefited the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 連れて来てくれた is used, the direction of movement is toward the speaker or the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に before a place, but the destination in 連れて行く usually has to go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.vi: I remembered singing with the teacher in a bright classroom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle で indicates the place where the singing took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle と indicates the person who performed the action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the object of the verb うたった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The past form た modifies the noun こと that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: こと turns the act of singing into a noun, and を marks the content being remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.why: The phrase showing the place and the person acting together comes before the content nominalized with こと. The clause うたった modifies こと, and the whole ことを becomes the object of おもいだしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If のを思い出す is used, the expression sounds more conversational but still emphasizes remembering an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake と for a simple “and,” but here と indicates the person who sang together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.vi: Even though I listened to the English in the movie, I still do not understand it well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun えいが with the noun phrase that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: 中の identifies the English as being inside the movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks English as the content being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: Vて＋も creates a concessive clause, meaning that even if one listens, the result does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: まだ modifies the state of not understanding clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: よく modifies わかりません and shows the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.why: The phrase の connects nouns to identify which part of the movie the English belongs to. The clause きいても comes before the result わかりません to show a contrast: the speaker listened but still did not understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: ても expresses concession, while てもなお emphasizes more strongly that the result remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is changed to のに, the sentence has a clearer feeling of regret or complaint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate も as “also,” but in Vても it means “even if one does it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q16.kobun.cn: Vて・Aくて・Aで・Nで ＋ も
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.vi: When I began living abroad, I felt as if I were living in a new world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.sk: Nで ＋ Vます omit ます ＋ はじめると ＋ Aい ＋ Nに ＋ Vているようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle で indicates the place where the living takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: くらしはじめる combines the verb くらす with はじめる to mean beginning to live, while と connects a natural condition or time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective directly modifies せかい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place or state in which the subject is felt to be living.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects いきる with いる to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: ようです expresses a feeling or inference based on the situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます ＋ はじめる; Vる・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ ようだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.why: くらしはじめると states the time or condition leading to the feeling in the following clause. あたらしい modifies せかい, while に combines with いきている to express the state of living in such a world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうです is used, the sentence focuses on appearance or observable signs, not the feeling of “being like.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: みたいです has a meaning close to ようです but is more casual in conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect はじめる directly to the dictionary-form verb; they need to use the form omitting ます, such as くらしはじめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with 試験 to identify the exam held yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に goes with しっぱいする to indicate the object or matter in which one failed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of しっぱいする, linking the failed action with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました describes an action that has been completed and often includes regret or a sense of misfortune.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.why: きのうの試験に identifies the event and object of the failure. しっぱいしてしまいました combines the て form with しまう to express a result that has occurred, with a regretful tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: てしまう can indicate simple completion or regret, depending on the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If only ました is used, the sentence only reports that the person failed and reduces the sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle に after 試験, but しっぱいする usually uses に to mark the event or object of the failure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.vi: I heard that as many as 5 people died in yesterday's fire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nで ＋ Quantityも ＋ Vてしまったそうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the time of yesterday with 火事 being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the event or cause related to the death.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: も emphasizes that the number is higher than expected, while 5人 is the subject of しんでしまった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of しぬ connects with しまった to express an event that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです is attached after a plain-form clause to pass on information that the speaker heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.why: で sets the fire as the background or cause, then 5人も states the subject and emphasizes the number. しんでしまった expresses the regrettable result, while そうです shows that this is information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: そうです at the end of a sentence means hearsay, while Vます＋そうです expresses a prediction based on signs that something is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: らしいです also expresses a guess or hearsay, but it usually shows a clearer level of uncertainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand も as “also,” but 5人も here emphasizes “as many as 5 people.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q19.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.vi: I heard that in the past, people borrowed books, took them home, and copied them by hand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects むかし with 人, creating a phrase meaning people from the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes people from the past the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the book that was borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects borrowing and bringing the book back with the following copying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: の shows a possessive relationship with 手.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: で indicates the tool or method used to copy something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: うつした is the past form of a verb and states that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: そうです follows the plain form to pass on information heard from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.why: かりてきて connects two actions in before-and-after order. 手で indicates the method, while Vたそうです shows that the speaker is reporting information they heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern predicts that an action is about to happen, rather than passing on heard information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern describes an experience of having done something before and does not mean “it is said.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish そうです, which passes on information, from そうです, which expresses a prediction; the hearsay form follows the plain form, including Vた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ（伝聞）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.vi: I have to buy a new suit for my son.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who benefits from the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い modifies せびろ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the suit as the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 買って is the て form, connecting the action of buying with やる to show that the action benefits the son.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: なければならない expresses an obligation that must be carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ やる; Vない removes い ＋ ければならない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.why: 息子に indicates the beneficiary, while せびろを is the thing being bought. 買ってやる shows that the speaker does the action for someone of lower status or someone close to them, and なければならない turns the whole action into an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: 買ってあげる also means buying something for someone, but it is more polite and neutral than 買ってやる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 買わなければならない is used, the sentence only says that the speaker must buy something and does not clearly state that it is for the son.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に as the direct object, but here に marks the beneficiary and せびろを is the actual object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.vi: The staff member in charge is away from their desk right now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase indicates the time when the action is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the seat as the object of leaving.
