default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: はずして is the て form, connecting the verb with おります to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: ております is the polite, humble form of ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the time and the object of the action. The Vております form comes at the end of the sentence to show an ongoing state in a polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this form keeps the meaning of an ongoing action but is less formal than ております.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with this form describes a state intentionally created by someone, so it does not fit the action of leaving one's seat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ております with a verb for an action that has just happened, while this structure emphasizes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.vi: I still do not know how to read Kanji.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun かんじ with the noun よみかた to create a modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks よみかた as something unknown or not understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies the state of わかりません and shows that the matter is not yet complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりません is the present negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.why: The noun よみかた is clearly identified as the reading of かんじ through の. This phrase functions as the subject with が, while まだ combines with the negative predicate to express not knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with は, the sentence gives a stronger contrast or puts more emphasis on the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure means still understanding or already knowing, which is the opposite of the unknown state in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は in every position, but が here marks the specific thing that the speaker does not know.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.vi: I am happily studying English at school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the studying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks English as the content being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: たのしく is the adverbial form of the adjective い, while まなんで is the て form used to connect with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ています expresses an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.why: で states the place of study, を states the content being studied, and たのしく modifies the verb まなんで. The ている form at the end of the sentence shows that the studying is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If まなびます is used, the sentence only says that the person will study or usually studies, without emphasizing that the action is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If たのしそうに is used, the meaning is studying with an appearance that seems happy, without confirming that the way of studying is happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change the adjective い into the く form before a verb to create an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q23.kobun.cn: Aい → Aく + Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.vi: Because I stopped the car in the middle of the way to go shopping, it became dark.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase describes the situation or time when an action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the car as the object being stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects stopping the car with the shopping that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects a cause with a result and shows a relatively mild, objective reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the sun as the subject of the state of becoming dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまいました describes a completed result, with a feeling of regret or something happening unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.why: The form て first connects stopping the car with shopping. The clause with ので gives the reason, followed by the result that it became dark; てしまう adds the feeling that the event happened against expectations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から gives a more direct and subjective reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If くれています is used, the sentence only says that it is gradually becoming dark, without the regret expressed by てしまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.tip: English learners may understand てしまう as only meaning that something has been completed, but this structure can also express regret or an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.tokens.0.m: in the middle of the way
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q24.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; Vた + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that he is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: そうに modifies うたって and describes the appearance or manner of performing an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the song as the object of singing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: うたって is the て form of うたう, and it connects with いる to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ている describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.cn: Aい omit い + そうに; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the outward state, the object, and the verb. ている at the end of the sentence shows that the singing is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If たのしくうたっている is used, the sentence states that he sings happily instead of saying that he seems happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: そうだ at the end of a sentence can describe the subject's appearance, but そうに directly modifies a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use たのしいそうに, but before そう, い of the adjective い must be removed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.vi: This spring, there was little rain, and pleasant days continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase の modifies 春 and identifies which spring it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that spring is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the state すくない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of the adjective い connects this cause or condition with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects the noun きもち with the phrase いい, creating a phrase that modifies ひ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: いい modifies ひ, creating the meaning of days with pleasant weather.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: が marks ひ as the subject of the verb つづいた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb in the past form describes a condition that continued during spring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.why: 春は sets the topic, and then 雨が identifies the subject with a small amount. The phrase きもちのいい modifies ひ, while すくなくて connects the condition of little rain with the result that pleasant days continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is inserted here, the sentence more clearly emphasizes that little rain is the reason for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used instead of の, きもちがいい is a separate clause and does not directly form a short modifying phrase for ひ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use が in きもちがいい and forget that, when modifying a noun, the suitable structure here is きもちのいいひ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.vi: Because the streets were crowded, I did not arrive on time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the street as the subject with the state of being crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result and follows the plain form こんでいた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time by which the speaker needed to arrive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: まにあう is usually used with に to express arriving in time for a specific time or deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.ch.4.vi: did not make it in time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: でした puts the whole event in the past and ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first with ので, and the result follows. The verb まにあう uses に because it describes making it by a specific time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the meaning of the cause is almost unchanged, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: The use of を is wrong because まにあう requires に to mark the time or object that must be reached in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may translate it as “make it in time” and then use を, but the correct pattern is 時間にまにあう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.vi: Drivers should fasten their seat belts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the driver as the person being given advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the seat belt as the object affected by しめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form of the verb comes before べき to create the action that should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: べきだ expresses advice or something that should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.why: うんてんしゅは is the topic, and シートベルトを is the object of the action. The dictionary form of the verb comes before べきだ because this pattern requires the action that should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with なければならない, the sentence changes from advice to obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ほうがいい is used, the advice is softer and more like a suggestion than べきだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may change the verb to the ます form before べきだ, but the dictionary form must be used: しめるべきだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.vi: For young people, America was once a dream country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that America is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: には identifies the people who see America as a dream country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects ゆめ with 国, creating the phrase “dream country.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 国でした acts as the predicate, and でした shows that this is an opinion from the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.why: アメリカは is the topic, while わかものには limits the group of people whose view is described. ゆめの国 is a noun phrase, in which の connects “dream” with “country.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If には is replaced with にとって, the sentence emphasizes the young people's viewpoint or benefit more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If ゆめみたいな国 is used, the meaning is “a country like a dream,” with a more comparative and conversational tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may understand に as only referring to a place, but in には it can also refer to an object or group of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.vi: Recently, the village's population has been increasing.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects むら with じんこう, identifying the population as belonging to the village.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the population as the subject that is increasing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects ふえる with くる in a pattern that describes a change gradually continuing up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: くる works as an auxiliary verb, showing that the increase has continued up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.why: さいきん sets the time point, むらのじんこう creates a noun phrase that functions as the subject. ふえてくる shows that the population increase began earlier and has gradually continued up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ふえています, the sentence only emphasizes the state of increasing and does not highlight the process gradually continuing up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If ふえていきます is used, the direction of change is viewed from the present toward the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate くる as “come” in the sense of movement, but here てくる describes a change that has continued up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.vi: The autumn festival is scheduled to be held next week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: らいしゅう indicates the expected time when the event will take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects あき with まつり, identifying it as an autumn festival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the festival as the object of the action of organizing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies よてい and states the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: よていです ends the sentence with the meaning of an expectation or plan.

default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with つもりです, the sentence focuses more on the intention of a specific person than on a scheduled or planned event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことになっています is used, the sentence emphasizes a decision or schedule that has already been set.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ます before 予定です, but the correct pattern is the dictionary-form verb + 予定です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q9.kobun.vi: The flower petals fell because of the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that made the flower petals fall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject experiencing the state of falling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q9.kobun.why: The phrase showing the cause comes first, followed by the subject and the verb at the end of the sentence. The particle が makes it clear that the flower petals are what fell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 風で is used, the meaning does not change, but it is written in kanji and is more formal in written language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t53-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を instead of が, but an object experiencing the state of falling usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.vi: The person in the middle of the family photo is my older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かぞくしゃしん with the position in the middle, creating a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the position まんなか with the modified noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the person in the middle of the photo the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: の shows the ownership relationship between わたし and あね.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: です connects the topic with a noun that indicates status or a relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.why: The two phrases with の identify the family photo and the middle position of the person being discussed, respectively. After stating the topic with は, the sentence uses わたしのあねです to identify who that person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this structure is used, the meaning emphasizes a person who is at a certain place rather than a person in the middle of the photo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes that the person in the middle is my older sister, rather than simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate and arrange の according to Vietnamese, but in Japanese, the modifying part always comes before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q1.kobun.cn: N の + N; N は + N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q10.kobun.vi: The teacher was waiting for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person performing the action of waiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the person being waited for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: まっていました is the past form of まっています and describes an action that was continuing at a certain time in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q10.kobun.why: The subject comes before が, the person being waited for comes before を, and the verb ends with ていました to describe a state that was continuing in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If まっていました is replaced with まちました, the sentence only says that the person waited and does not emphasize that the action was continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q10.kobun.tip: ていました is not simply the past tense; it often emphasizes a state or action that was happening at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.vi: I met a friend from my school days in front of the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects えき with まえ to create the phrase “in front of the station.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.ch.1.vi: in front of the station from my school days
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the meeting happened; 学生 comes before じだい to modify that period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 学生じだい with 友だち, creating the meaning “a friend from my school days.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: With the verb あう, に indicates the person whom I met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: あいました is the polite past form of あう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.why: The place comes first with で, the phrase 学生時代の modifies 友だち, and に marks the object of あう. This order goes from the place to the person met and then to the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If と会う is used, the sentence more strongly emphasizes that both sides met or arranged to meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q11.kobun.tip: With あう, the person met usually goes with に, not を as with many other action verbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q12.kobun.vi: I lived in the countryside until high school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: まで indicates the ending point of the period of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place where the subject lived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: すんでいました describes a state of living that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q12.kobun.why: The ending point of the time period comes first, the place follows with に, and then the verb ていました describes a state of living that continued until that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If 高校までに is used, it means that an action must be completed before or by high school at the latest, not that someone lived continuously until that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q12.kobun.tip: まで indicates a period continuing until a certain point, while までに usually indicates a deadline by which something must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.vi: Please feel free to ask any question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: なんでも indicates the object of the question and has an unlimited meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: なく changes the noun えんりょ into an adverb and modifies the action of asking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: て-form connects the action しつもんする with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence and changes the verb form て before it into a polite offer or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.why: なんでも states the range of the object, えんりょなく states the manner of performing the action, and then Vてください creates a polite request. The form なく allows the noun to function as an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If して ください is replaced with しなさい, the sentence becomes a stronger and less gentle command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.kobun.tip: Do not connect the noun えんりょ directly to the verb; use えんりょなく to express the manner “without hesitation.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.tokens.1.m: without hesitation; please do not be formal
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q13.tokens.3.m: please do it; carry it out
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.vi: The sign “No entry” means that people must not enter here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place of the entering action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: という quotes the content or meaning of the clause before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the sentence in an explanatory noun pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.why: The topic is stated first, followed by the place and the quoted content. という changes the clause はいらない into a modifier for the noun いみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, it means “is called” or “is said to be,” and it no longer directly modifies いみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes the conclusion or the content understood in that way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate という as “say,” but in this sentence it connects the whole clause to modify a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ という ＋ Nだ／です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.vi: No matter how much I draw, I still cannot draw well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.sk: いくら ＋ N を ＋ Vても、＋ なかなか ＋ Aく ＋ negative potential form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら begins a concessive pattern and signals that the result will not change even if the degree increases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the picture as the object of the drawing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: て-form combines with も to express “even if one does...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: なかなか modifies what follows and is often used with a negative form to express difficulty in achieving something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: うまく is an adverbial form that modifies the verb かけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: The negative potential form expresses that one cannot draw skillfully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.why: The clause いくら...ても states a concessive condition, while the following clause says that the result is still not achieved. うまく is used in adverbial form because it describes how the drawing action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means “no matter how much one does...,” emphasizing that the result does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means “no matter to what degree,” emphasizing degree more than the number of times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use うまい directly before a verb, but it must be changed to うまく to function as an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.tokens.5.m: still; even after a long time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q16.kobun.cn: いくら ＋ Vて・Aくて・N／Aなであって ＋ も
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.vi: Because it has not rained, vegetable prices have risen especially.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks rain as the subject of the falling phenomenon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result; ふらない is the negative form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: とくに modifies the degree of the rise in vegetable prices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects やさい with ねだん to form the phrase “vegetable prices”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the price as the subject that increases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb is in the polite past form and states a result that has already occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.why: The cause comes before the result and is connected by ので. The phrase やさいのねだん is the subject of あがりました, while とくに indicates a notable degree of increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is usually more direct and more subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If ために is used, the cause is presented more formally and objectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ので with のでに; ので is already a pattern that connects a cause and does not need に added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな／だった・Nな／だった ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.vi: I lived with my mother in a house near the sea throughout my childhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who performs the action together; は adds a nuance of singling out or contrasting the mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: いっしょに modifies the action of living and shows how it was done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the location with 家 to modify the noun 家.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the place where the action くらした takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the period spent during the action of living.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: くらした is the ordinary past form of くらす and states that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.why: The phrases for the person acting together and the manner come first. The sentence then identifies the place with で, the period with を, and ends with a past-tense verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If といっしょに is replaced with とともに, the meaning is still “together with,” but it is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This is the kanji spelling of the same structure and does not change the meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q18.kobun.tip: The particle で indicates where the action takes place. に is not used in this sentence because に usually indicates a destination or a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.vi: I returned home at around 6 p.m. to prepare for the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects りょこう with ようい to form the phrase “preparations for the trip.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ようい as the object of the verb する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ために connects the preceding action with the purpose of the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The time phrase indicates when the return happened; ごろ expresses an approximate time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: へ indicates the direction of movement for the action かえりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb is in the polite past form and is the main action of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.why: The purpose is placed first with するために, followed by the time, direction of movement, and main action. へ is used because うち is the destination, while ごろ gives the time an approximate meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is replaced with ように, it usually goes with an ability or a state that needs to be achieved, so it is less suitable here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the sentence gives the reason “because of preparing,” rather than the purpose “in order to prepare.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.tip: Before ために, use only the dictionary form of a verb when expressing purpose; do not use the past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.tokens.5.m: in order to; for the purpose of
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q19.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ために／Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.vi: As I grow older, I find myself wanting to meet friends from long ago whom I have remained apart from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 「を」marks the object of the verb 「とる」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 「Vると」connects a condition or a natural result: when one does V, ...
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The time expression modifies the clause 「わかれた」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 「わかれたままの」modifies 「ともだち」 and expresses a state that remains after parting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: 「Vたい」＋「なる」expresses a change into wanting to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.why: The clause 「としをとると」states the condition that occurs first, followed by the desire that arises. 「わかれたままの」is placed before 「ともだち」to identify them as friends whom the speaker has not met again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 「と」with 「たら」emphasizes a more specific condition or time, and the clear sense of a natural result is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 「Vたいと思う」expresses a present thought or desire and does not emphasize a change in desire like 「たくなる」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 「と」in this sentence for the meaning “and,” but here it connects a condition with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.tokens.6.m: as it is, keeping the same state
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + と; Vた + ままの + N; Vたい + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.vi: Although I bought it at a famous store, the quality is not very good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies “store” and shows that the store is famous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle で shows the place where the action of buying takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb かった in the past form connects with のに to create a contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: あまり usually goes with a negative predicate to express a low degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: Particle が marks quality as the thing being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: よくない is the negative form of adjective いい and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the verb “buy,” and then のに connects it to a result contrary to expectation. あまり modifies the negative predicate よくないです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with けれども, the sentence still has a contrastive meaning, but the conversational tone and connection are slightly different from のに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that あまり usually has to go with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q20.kobun.cn: Vた・Aかった・Aなだった・Nだった + のに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.vi: Yesterday, my younger sister had a fever as high as 40 degrees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は shows that the younger sister is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は emphasizes yesterday as the time point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle が marks the fever as what increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: まで shows the limit reached, while あがりました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.why: The topic and time are stated first, and then が identifies the fever as what increased. まで marks the highest level reached by the temperature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほど is used, the sentence focuses on a level of about 40 degrees and does not emphasize the point reached as まで does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q21.kobun.tip: まで should not simply be translated as “to” in every sentence; here, it shows a limit of degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.vi: I have a personal matter this week, so I cannot go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.sk: N は + Time は + N が + あるので + V辞書形 + ことが + できません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle が marks the personal matter as something that exists or arises.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: ある in the plain form connects with ので to state a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the dictionary form modifies こと and turns the action of going into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern Vことができる uses が to mark an action as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: できません is the polite negative form and serves as the predicate showing ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.why: The clause about having a personal matter comes before ので to state the reason. V辞書形 comes before こと, which nominalizes the action of going, and then ことができません expresses inability to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective, while ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If a negative potential form such as 行けない is used, the sentence is shorter but does not keep the Vことができません structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put ので after a noun and forget that the correct form is Nなので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q22.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる/できない; V普通形・Aい・Aな+な・N+な + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.vi: There was no special dish tonight, but it was a pleasant meal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は presents tonight as the time and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects adjective な with a noun, while では negates noun ごちそう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: なかった is the negative past form of ない and connects with が to shift to a contrasting idea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: Adjective い directly modifies the noun “meal.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: だった is the past form of だ and serves as the noun predicate in the second clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.why: The first clause negates a noun with ではなかった, and then が connects it to a contrasting result. たのしい comes before しょくじ to describe the meal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is used, the feeling of “although..., nevertheless...” is stronger and usually shows clearer surprise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.tip: With nouns, past negation must use ではなかった, not ないでした in this standard structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q23.kobun.cn: N+ではなかったが; V普通形・Aい・Aな+だ/だった+が
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.vi: After leaving the ticket gate, please go down the stairs on the left.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the place or route of exiting with verb 出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: 出る changes into 出たら to connect a condition or the time “after leaving.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects “left” with the noun “stairs” to form a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle を marks the stairs as the object of the action of going down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 下りて is the て form and connects the action of going down with the request ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.why: たら gives the condition or time point before carrying out the request. The phrase の connects “left” with “stairs,” while the て form combines with ください to create a polite instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 出てから is used, the order “after leaving, then...” is clearer and sounds less conditional.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 出ると is used, the sentence focuses on a natural result after leaving, so it is less suitable for a direct instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake を in 出口を出る for an object; here, it shows the route or place of exit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q24.kobun.cn: Vた + ら; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I ate pork shabu-shabu with a friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.sk: Time + N と + N の + N を + Vた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase shows the time when the action of eating took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と indicates the person who performs the action together with someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the ingredient with the name of the shabu-shabu dish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the dish used as the object of 食べた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べた is the usual past form of 食べる and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.why: The time and the person joining the action come before the food being eaten. の connects the ingredient with the dish name, while 食べた ends the sentence and shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 友人で is used, the sentence will not correctly express the person eating together; と indicates companionship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use に to say “eat with a friend”; the natural particle in this structure is と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.vi: This Sunday, I have a personal matter to deal with, so I cannot go to church.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects 「こんしゅう」 with the specific day 「にちようび」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」 makes Sunday the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 「が」 marks the cause or the situation that exists in the preceding clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 「あって」 is the て form of 「ある」 and connects the reason with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 「に」 indicates the destination of the verb 「いく」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: 「いけません」 is the negative potential form of 「いく」, meaning “cannot go.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + following clause; negative V可能形: Vえます／Vられます → Vえません／Vられません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.why: The day is introduced as the topic, followed by the reason 「ようじがあって」, and only then by the place that cannot be reached. 「に」 is used with movement verbs to indicate a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「ので」 is used, the reason is stated more directly and formally, while 「あって」 links the two clauses more gently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing 「に」 with 「へ」 still indicates going toward the church, but emphasizes direction more than the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 「を」 for a destination, but the verb 「いく」 usually uses 「に」 or 「へ」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.vi: This year, the number of people who died in accidents is not small.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression placed at the beginning of the sentence to limit the scope of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 「で」 indicates the cause that led to the death.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 「しんだ」 comes before 「ひと」 to modify the people; 「は」 makes this whole phrase the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 「すくなくない」 uses the negative form of the adjective 「すくない」 to express a considerable number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.why: 「しんだ」 is placed before 「ひと」 because it is a relative clause that identifies the type of people being discussed. The structure 「すくなくない」 negates the idea of “few” to emphasize that the number of people is not small at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「おおい」 is used, it directly says that there are many, with a stronger and more direct tone than 「すくなくない」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: 「すくないわけではない」 only says “it is not necessarily a small number,” which is weaker than the original sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand 「すくなくない」 as “not few at all” in an absolute sense, but its actual tone is usually “not small at all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q4.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Aい → Aくない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.vi: If you go straight along this road, you will see a park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 「を」 marks the route being traveled, not an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb modifying how the action 「行く」 is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 「Vると」 connects going straight with the natural result that there is a park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 「が」 marks the object that is discovered or exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 「あります」 is used for the existence of inanimate things or places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.why: 「を」 after a road name indicates the route of travel. 「行くと」 states the natural result after going straight, while 「こうえんがあります」 describes the park as existing ahead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「行ったら」 makes it more like the hypothetical condition “if you go/after you go.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: 「公園まで行く」 means going all the way to the park, while the original sentence says that a park is seen or exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 「道を行く」 as “go the road,” but 「を」 here only indicates the route being traveled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.vi: In front of the station, shops are lined up in a row.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects 「えき」 with the location 「前」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 「に」 indicates a location where something exists, while 「は」 makes that place the scope being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 「が」 marks the subject in the described state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 「Vている」 describes the state of the shops being arranged in a row.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.why: The place 「駅の前」 is mentioned first, followed by 「みせが」, the things that exist there. 「ならんでいます」 emphasizes the state of the shops already being lined up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「あります」 is used, it only says that the shops exist there and does not clearly show that they are lined up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: 「並べてあります」 means that someone has arranged the shops or objects in a row, emphasizing an intentional action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 「ています」 simply as “be,” but with a verb showing arrangement, it also describes a state that continues to exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.vi: The fire spread faster than I expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects 「火」 with 「まわり」, creating a phrase describing the spread of the fire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 「が」 marks the phenomenon being described as fast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies 「はやかった」 and shows that the speed was greater than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 「はやかった」 is the past form of the adjective ending in い, while 「です」 makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.why: 「火のまわり」 is the subject being described, 「いがいに」 shows the surprising degree, and the adjective is in the past form because the event already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「思ったよりはやかった」 is used, the sentence compares the speed directly with what was expected and expresses “faster than I thought” more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 「速くなった」 emphasizes a change to becoming fast, rather than simply describing speed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may forget to change 「はやい」 into 「はやかった」 when the sentence describes an event that already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q8.kobun.vi: When you open this door, you will immediately see the street.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb combines with と to state the result that occurs immediately after the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: とおりだ is the predicate describing the result noticed after the door is opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q8.kobun.why: The object phrase comes before を, followed by the dictionary-form action combined with と to lead to a natural result. すぐ adds the meaning that the result occurs immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence has a more hypothetical conditional tone and does not emphasize that the result happens automatically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use たら in every conditional sentence, but と is suitable when the first action always leads directly to the following result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.vi: My aunt has a mouth and nose similar to my mother's.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes my aunt the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects くち with the noun that follows to form a parallel subject group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject; くちと and はな together are the subject of にている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the object used as the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 似ている describes an existing state of similarity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は. Next, two nouns are connected by と and both take が. The pattern Nに似ている uses に to indicate the person or thing used as the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If に似ている is replaced with と同じだ, the meaning becomes stronger, closer to being exactly the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the object of comparison in に似ている; the correct particle is に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.vi: Because there was an empty bed, I quickly had my sick mother admitted to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that is in the empty state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て modifies the hospital admission that happens immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the noun びょうき with はは to modify はは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: させました is the polite past form of the causative pattern, meaning to let or make someone do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.why: The reason clause with ので comes first, followed by the manner いそいで and the object ははを of the causative action. The pattern Vさせる is suitable because the subject makes the mother enter the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more subjective and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 入院しました, it means that the mother entered the hospital herself, without the speaker making her do so.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse を with が in the causative pattern because を marks the person who is made to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.vi: If you need a receipt, please go to the staff member in charge.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the thing considered necessary in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ひつような modifies ばあい, so the ending な is used before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents this case as the condition or topic of the instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.ch.3.vi: to the staff member in charge
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person or place to go to ask questions and carry out the next step.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: てください creates a polite request telling the listener to go to the stated place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.why: The conditional clause is turned into a noun phrase with 場合 and placed first with は. In the main clause, に identifies the place or person to go to, while てください turns the action into a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: なら creates a more direct and conversational condition, while 場合は emphasizes a specific case and is usually more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.tip: Before 場合, use な with an adjective and な with a noun の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・Nの ＋ 場合（は）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.vi: Although I studied very hard, my exam score was still not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies 勉強した and shows the level of effort made while studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects the completed studying with the unexpected result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects しけん with てん to identify the type of score being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the exam score the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: よくなかったです is a past negative predicate that states the result was not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.why: The first clause gives a reason that makes the listener expect a good result, but のに signals the opposite actual result. The phrase しけんのてん is made the topic and commented on with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: けど also connects two contrasting ideas, but it is softer and more common in conversation than のに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: ても means even if a condition occurs, with more emphasis on supposition or concession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.tip: In this sentence, のに is a conjunction showing contrast; do not confuse it with のに, which means “in order to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.vi: Because I drank too much coffee, I could not sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks coffee as the object of the action of drinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: のみすぎて consists of the verb stem のみ and すぎて, and connects the cause with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ねむれません is the negative potential form, expressing that one cannot sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.why: Coffee is the object of drinking, so it takes を. すぎて connects an action that exceeds the proper amount with its result, while the negative potential form expresses the inability to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the sentence gives the cause neutrally and does not keep the sense of drinking too much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: から also indicates a cause, but clearly separates the completed cause from the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.tip: すぎる connects with the verb stem ます, so use のみすぎる instead of のむすぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q12.kobun.cn: Vます語幹 ＋ すぎる／すぎて; V可能形 ＋ ません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q13.kobun.vi: Enter the name into the computer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the object or place that receives the data.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the content being entered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: します creates a polite predicate for the action of entering data.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q13.kobun.why: The receiving object comes first with に, while the content being entered comes first with を. The verb します comes at the end of the sentence to complete the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入れる is used, it emphasizes putting or placing something in, and does not specifically mean entering data as in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and を. Remember that the place or system receiving the data takes に, while the data being entered takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.vi: The bread has just finished baking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.sk: Time point ＋ N が ＋ Vた ＋ ところです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: This part states the time when the state occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object whose baking has just been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: Vたところです expresses an action that has just been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.why: The subject of the newly completed state is marked with が. The past form Vた combines with ところです to indicate the time immediately after the action ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means that the baking is in progress and is not yet finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q14.kobun.tip: Do not understand ところ here as a place; Vたところです is the time point immediately after the action is completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.vi: On Sunday, Mr. and Mrs. Sato were away from home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ N でした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes Sato the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: A time noun can stand directly before the predicate without a particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: でした is the polite past form of です and ends the description of the state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.why: The topic is placed at the beginning with は, followed by the time and the topic's state. Because the event belongs to the past, です changes to でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Using いませんでした directly says that the person was not present, while るすでした emphasizes the state of being away from home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q15.kobun.tip: It is not necessary to add に after a day noun such as にちようび when it serves as a time reference in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.vi: The day before yesterday, we arrived in Osaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N は ＋ Place に ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: This part states when the action happened and is separated by a comma.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the person who performs the action as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of the verb つく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ついた is the casual past form of つく and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.why: The time reference comes first, followed by the subject, then the destination with に. The verb is in the past because the arrival in Osaka already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing に with へ still indicates Osaka as the destination, but places slightly more emphasis on the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q16.kobun.tip: With つく, the destination uses に; を is not used to indicate the place reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.vi: I got an injection at the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.sk: Place で ＋ N を ＋ しました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で marks the place where the injection takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the action performed together with しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.why: The place where the action happens goes with で, while the noun for the action goes with を and then combines with しました. This order forms an action phrase that happened at the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the hospital is the destination, not the place where the action directly happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q17.kobun.tip: Distinguish で, which marks the place where an action happens, from に, which marks a destination or a place of existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.vi: Sometimes we also need to let our brain rest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.sk: Frequency は ＋ N を ＋ Vないと ＋ いけない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は gives the special case of “sometimes” an emphasizing effect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the body part affected by やすめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.ch.2.vi: if we do not let it rest
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative form やすめない combines with と to create a required condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: いけない in the pattern ないといけない creates the meaning “must do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.why: The brain is the object of やすめる, so it takes を. The phrase やすめないといけない has a negative conditional structure, but the whole pattern expresses obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in the sentence, it still means “must do,” but the tone is more formal and rigid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If used, the meaning changes to “do not have to let the brain rest.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.tip: Do not translate ないと alone as “if not”; in ないといけない, the whole phrase means “must do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q18.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ と ＋ いけない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.vi: Starting tomorrow, I plan to begin the experiment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.sk: Time から ＋ N を ＋ V辞書形 ＋ Nの予定です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the time when the action begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that is to be started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: はじめる in the dictionary form modifies 予定 and states the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 予定です serves as a noun predicate and expresses a plan or intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to state when the action begins. The object takes を, while the dictionary-form verb comes before 予定です to show the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 予定です with つもりです puts more emphasis on the speaker's intention than on a planned schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of を before an action, but the object of はじめる must take を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q19.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ 予定です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q2.kobun.vi: Please hurry as much as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action いそいで and indicates the fastest possible degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q2.kobun.why: できるだけ comes before the verb to limit the degree of the action. Vてください makes the whole sentence a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vなさい, the sentence has a stronger command-like tone and is usually spoken by someone of higher status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use the plain verb form before ください; change it to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: この comes before a noun to identify the plan being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: には marks the object being commented on and creates a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: はんたいだ is a noun predicate that states the speaker's attitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q20.kobun.why: The topic わたしは comes first, followed by the noun identified by この. には clarifies the object of the attitude, and はんたいだ completes the sentence with a noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 賛成だ, the meaning changes to agreeing with or supporting the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q20.kobun.tip: Do not translate には simply as “at”; in this sentence, it marks the object that the speaker opposes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.vi: Compared with Tokyo, living costs in Osaka are cheaper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: と combines with くらべて to state the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects おおさか with ほう, creating the phrase “the Osaka side.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: ほうが chooses Osaka as the side being compared, and が marks the subject of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks living costs as the object having the feature やすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: やすいです is an adjective predicate that gives the conclusion about the cost level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.why: とうきょうとくらべて places the comparison standard first. The pattern Nのほうが states the side being evaluated, while が after せいかつひ marks the noun that has the feature やすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Using より instead of と比べて is shorter but keeps the meaning “compared with N.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.tip: In comparison patterns, Vietnamese speakers may easily omit が after ほう or mistakenly use を before the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q21.kobun.cn: Nと比べて ＋ Nのほうが ＋ Aい／Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.vi: Please deliver the package by the afternoon of the day after tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.sk: Deadline までに ＋ N を ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the day after tomorrow with ごご to identify which afternoon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the package as the item to be delivered or sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request or ask someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.why: The deadline is placed before the action and goes with までに. The package is the object of とどける, while てください turns the request into a polite favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks for something more softly and humbly instead of making a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q22.kobun.tip: までに means “by or no later than that time,” not that the action continues until that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.vi: My older brother works at the city hall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with あに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the older brother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the workplace used with the verb 勤める.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ている shows that the working state is continuing or is still maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.why: わたしの identifies the possessive relationship, and あには is the topic. The workplace goes with に, while ている shows that the working state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: で働いている also means working at a place, but it puts more emphasis on the place where the activity happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q23.kobun.tip: With 勤める, the workplace usually goes with に, not で as is common in English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.vi: Mr. Sato’s eldest son became a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects Mr. Sato with the son being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the eldest son the topic of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the result or status achieved after becoming something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and describes a completed change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.why: The possessive phrase comes first to identify the son. The noun for the profession goes with に before なる because it is the result of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Using Nです only states the current status and does not emphasize the process of becoming it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q24.kobun.tip: When saying “become a noun,” Vietnamese speakers may easily use で instead of に; the correct pattern is Nに なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.vi: That is a work written by a famous writer in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the thing being presented.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the fame is established.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before a noun to modify the writer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person who performs the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: The past-tense verb clause modifies さくひん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the sentence with a definite and polite meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.why: The topic あれは is introduced first. Then, the information before さくひん describes the origin of the work. The particle が identifies the person who performs the action かいた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 有名だ is used directly before a noun, it must change to 有名な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 書いている, the meaning changes to a work that the writer is writing or usually writes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that the adjective な before a noun must use な, not だ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.vi: My younger brother is someone who thinks carefully many times before stating his opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the younger brother the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: も emphasizes how many times the thinking action is repeated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies かんがえて and describes how the person thinks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: てから connects the earlier thinking action with the later speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the content that is spoken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The clause いう comes before 人 to modify that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: です ends the sentence and identifies the younger brother’s characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.why: The topic おとうとは is described by the clause いう人です. かんがえてから comes before いう to show the order: he thinks first and then speaks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is replaced with たあとで, the time meaning is almost the same, but it emphasizes the time after completion more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with るまえに, the order changes to stating the opinion before thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that the clause modifying 人 must be placed directly before 人; do not use の between the verb and 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.vi: That person’s husband is a famous musician.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies かた and refers to a person far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects かた with ごしゅじん, while は makes this phrase the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before a noun to modify おんがくか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: です connects the topic with the statement at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.why: The possessive phrase かたのごしゅじん is made the topic by は. The adjective な comes before the noun おんがくか to describe that profession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ご before しゅじん is omitted, the possessive meaning is still correct, but the level of respect is lower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If おんがくか is replaced with 有名な人, the sentence only says that the person is famous and does not identify the person as a musician.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place ゆうめいな after the noun, but the adjective な must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.vi: Pay attention to the grammar and think together about the correct answer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the object that the speaker needs to pay attention to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of paying attention with the later action of thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ただしい modifies こたえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the thinking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.why: に marks the object of attention, while を marks the answer being considered. The two actions are connected by the て form and end with ましょう to make a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ましょう is replaced with てください, the sentence changes from an invitation to act together into a request for the listener to act.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を after ちゅういする in this structure; the object usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.vi: Last night, I wrote a letter to my family, put a photo in it, and sent it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.sk: Time expression + N に + N を + Vて + N を + Vて + Vた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: A time expression at the beginning of the sentence identifies the time of all the actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the recipient of the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing that is written and sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the writing action to the following actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the thing put into the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects putting the photo in with sending it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: おくった is the informal past-tense predicate at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.why: The actions are arranged in the correct order: writing the letter, putting the photo in, and then sending it. に indicates the recipient, while を indicate the letter and the photo, respectively, as the objects of the actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたり is used, the sentence only lists typical actions and does not emphasize the order in which they were completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If てから is used between two actions, the before-and-after relationship is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for both the letter and the photo, but an affected object must be used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.vi: Car accidents often happen at intersections.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: では marks the place where the event often happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects くるま with じこ to indicate an accident related to a car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the action おきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies the verb and indicates how often the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.why: The place is put at the beginning with では, and then の identifies the type of accident. The subject of the event is used with が, while よく comes before the verb to modify its frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of では, the sentence only states the place where the event happens, without emphasizing the setting or scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use を for じこ because it is the subject of the event, not the affected object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.vi: This coffee is rich and tastes good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes コーヒー the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: こくて is the て form of the adjective い, connecting the rich quality with the following comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object evaluated as いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: いいです is the main predicate and gives an evaluation of the taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.why: は makes the coffee the topic, while こくて connects the comment about richness with the comment about taste. The element あじがいい forms a subject–predicate phrase for the second evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using し lists reasons or characteristics and gives the sense of stating several causes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q8.kobun.tip: The adjective い changes い to くて when connecting; do not add で directly to this adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.vi: I prepared a meal for the customer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects お客様 with ため to identify the purpose or the person being served.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ために indicates the purpose of the preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the meal as the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past-tense predicate of the preparation action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.why: The purpose phrase comes before the main verb. The meal is used with を because it is the thing being prepared, while しました shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ように is used, the sentence focuses on a goal or a state to achieve, and does not clearly state the purpose of the action as ために does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.tip: After a noun, のために must be used; a noun cannot be connected directly to ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.tokens.2.m: for, for the sake of, to serve
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t55-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.vi: Please help yourself to the meal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: なく changes the noun えんりょ into an adverb meaning that there is no need to be reserved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.why: えんりょなく modifies the invitation, while めしあがってください is the polite request phrase. The て form is required before ください in this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern is also polite, but it has a more respectful and formal tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this form is used, the sentence only states the action of eating or drinking and is no longer an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form directly before ください; change it to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to become a doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person who has the wish the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: A time expression comes directly before the desired content and does not need a particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the result after becoming a profession or position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: たい is attached to the connective form of なる to express the speaker's wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, while いしゃに indicates the desired result with なる. たい changes the action into the subject's wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is substituted, the meaning becomes that the person seems about to become a doctor, not that they want to become one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use を with なる when talking about becoming a profession or status; the result is usually used with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.vi: There is snow in winter, while the maple leaves are very beautiful in autumn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes winter the topic of the first clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: ゆき states the content associated with winter; です is omitted in this short listing style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は shifts the topic to autumn to contrast it with winter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the object described as beautiful.
