default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: きれい is a な adjective and is used with です to end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.why: The two clauses use は to place the two seasons side by side and state a typical feature of each. In the second clause, が marks the maple leaves as the object evaluated by きれいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is used instead of は, the meaning is that the season also has a similar feature, without emphasizing contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q11.kobun.tip: きれい is a な adjective even though it ends in い, so use きれいです instead of conjugating it like a い adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person being talked about in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the content being learned, so it functions as the object of を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the direct object of the action of learning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ならって is the て form of ならう. It connects with いました to express an ongoing action in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: いました is the past form of います in the Vていました pattern. It describes an action that was already in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.why: わたしは sets the topic, and then けんどうを is the object of ならう. The て form connects with いました to describe the learning process that took place in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ならいました, it only says that the person learned, without emphasizing that the action was in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If ならっています is used, the meaning changes to “am currently learning.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ていました as only “already,” and miss the meaning of an action that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q12.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ います／いました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.vi: Black smoke came out of the chimney.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the place where the smoke started to come out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: くろい modifies the noun けむり that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the smoke as the subject that performs the action of coming out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: でて is the て form of でる. It connects the action of coming out with きた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: きた adds movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.why: えんとつから indicates the starting point, while くろいけむりが is the subject that comes out. でてきた combines “come out” with “come,” showing that the smoke came out and moved toward the viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If でていった is used, it emphasizes that the smoke comes out and then moves away from the viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If only でる is used, it only says that the smoke comes out and does not show movement toward a direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand てくる as just two verbs in sequence, but this pattern also shows movement toward a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.vi: Please check whether there are any scratches on the bottle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object being checked, namely the surface or container that needs to be examined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the scratch as the thing whose presence or absence is being confirmed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ないかどうか creates the content to be checked in the form “whether there is ... or not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: たしかめて is the て form. It connects the checking verb with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください is a polite request pattern meaning “please do V.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.why: びんに identifies the thing being checked, while きずがないかどうか is the complete content being confirmed. This clause comes before たしかめてください because it clearly states what needs to be checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If きずがないか is used, it still means “whether ... or not,” but the expression is shorter and shows the two possibilities less clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If きずがないか is used without どうか, the sentence is still natural, but it usually sounds like a direct question or a request to see whether ... or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put どうか at the end of the sentence. In this pattern, かどうか comes directly after the clause being confirmed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ かどうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.vi: I went to the hair salon yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N へ ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう adds the time when the action took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: いきました is the polite past form of いく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.why: きのう places the time at the beginning of the sentence, the destination is used with へ, and the verb いきました comes at the end. Japanese often leaves out the subject when the listener already knows who it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the meaning “go to the hair salon” remains almost unchanged. に emphasizes the destination more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used, the sentence refers to the place of departure, not the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse へ with “return.” In this sentence, へ only indicates direction toward a place and does not necessarily mean going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.vi: This soap has a very pleasant scent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this soap the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies 良い and increases the degree of the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 良い modifies 香り and creates the phrase “pleasant scent.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the scent as a sensation or feature coming from the soap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 香りがします is a way to say “has a scent” or “gives off a scent.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.why: このせっけんは is the topic, while 香りがします is the predicate describing the scent given off by the object. 良い comes directly before 香り to modify the scent, not the soap itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If せっけんの香りがする is used, the sentence emphasizes the soap’s scent rather than judging whether the scent is good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If せっけんは良い is said, it means that the soap is good or nice, so the comment is no longer limited to its scent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 香りをします. For sensations or smells that come from something, Japanese uses 香りがします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q16.kobun.cn: N が ＋ します／する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.vi: I started learning judo when I was in elementary school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しょうがくせい with とき to create a phrase indicating a time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the action began.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks judo as the activity that was started or practiced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: はじめました is the polite past form and describes the time when an activity began.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.why: しょうがくせいのときに sets the time, and then じゅうどうを is the object of はじめる. The particle に makes it clear that the action began at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If しょうがくせいのころ is used, it means “around the time of elementary school,” with less emphasis on one specific moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If しょうがくせいのあいだに is used, it means that the action happened throughout that period, rather than identifying only when it began.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out の in しょうがくせいのとき. A noun before とき usually needs の to connect them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q17.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ ときに／V普通形 ＋ ときに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.vi: Because I was sick, I could not visit today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a noun with ため to create a phrase showing a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: ために indicates the cause that led to being unable to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes today the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before こと to turn the action of visiting into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: こと turns the action into a noun, while が marks it as the thing being considered in terms of possibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: できませんでした is the polite past negative form of できる. It means that the person was unable to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.why: The reason phrase comes first, followed by the time as the topic. The action うかがう is turned into a noun with こと so that it can combine with ことができる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ので, it still gives a reason, but the tone is softer and more explanatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: ためで does not connect directly with ことができませんでした in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ために as “in order to,” but in this sentence it means “because” because it follows a noun expressing a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q18.kobun.cn: Nの・V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ために; V辞書形 ＋ ことができる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.vi: Now is exactly the right season for planting tomatoes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the current time as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the tomato as the object of planting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: のに turns the action of planting into a purpose or an action to be evaluated in the phrase いい季節.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: いい modifies きせつ, judging this season to be suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: きせつです is the predicate, and です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.why: The object being planted comes before を, while the action of planting is changed into the phrase のに to express purpose. The adjective いい comes before きせつ to modify the noun “season.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used, the meaning leans toward “for planting tomatoes” as a purpose, so it is less natural than のにいい for expressing suitability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: のは only turns an action into a topic. It does not create the structure “suitable for...” like のにいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.tip: Do not confuse のに in this structure with のに, which means “although.” Look at the word いい immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q19.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ のに ＋ いい／便利な／必要な ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.vi: Every evening, on my way home from school, I stop by the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ N に ＋ N に ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to state when the repeated action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects だいがく with かえり, showing their relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time or occasion when the stopping by takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination of the stopping-by action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: よります is the main predicate, ending with the polite form ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.why: The time and situation phrases come first, followed by the destination with に. The verb よります describes stopping at a place while traveling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced by で, the library becomes the place where the activity happens, rather than emphasizing it as the stopping destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: へ emphasizes the direction toward the library more than the specific destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q2.kobun.tip: With verbs meaning stop by or go to a place, English learners may easily confuse に with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.vi: Because mornings and evenings become cold, I want to pay attention to my clothes and similar things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.sk: N と N は ＋ V普通形 ので ＋ N など に ＋ Vます形 omitます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects two times, while は makes the whole phrase the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause to the result of paying attention to clothing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the thing that needs attention; など adds the meaning “and so on, such as.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: たい follows the linking form of a verb to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; Vます形 omitます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.why: The two times are joined by と and then made the topic with は. The reason comes first with ので, followed by the thing that needs attention and the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced by から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective, while ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is used, it creates the contrast “although it is cold,” which conflicts with the cause-and-effect relationship in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may use を with ちゅういする, but this verb usually uses に to indicate what needs attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.vi: If you do not diet, you will gain weight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks ダイエット as the content of the action する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.ch.1.vi: if you do not do it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: ないと creates a necessary condition or warning: if you do not do it, the following result will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: よ emphasizes the warning for the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ と ＋ result; V辞書形 ＋ と can also state a natural or inevitable condition
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.why: The object of doing something comes before を. The negative form しない combines with と to create the condition “if you do not do it,” followed by the warned result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced by なければ, the conditional meaning stays the same, but the tone is more formal and less conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: ないなら only makes an assumption based on the information “if it is the case that one does not do it.” It does not have the strong sense of an inevitable warning found in ないと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q21.kobun.tip: Do not understand と here as “and”; しないと is a complete conditional phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.vi: If you turn this, you can adjust the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that is turned or twisted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: V辞書形と connects an action with the result that happens immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks sound as the object that changes or is adjusted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: できます expresses an ability or a possible result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と ＋ result; Vない ＋ と ＋ a negative result or a necessary condition depending on the context
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.why: The affected object comes before を, while と connects the turning action with the result that happens automatically. Sound is made the subject of the adjustable state, so it goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, it only states the condition after turning, without emphasizing the natural action-result relationship as と does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If ば is used, the sentence has a more general conditional tone and is less direct as an operating instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q22.kobun.tip: In instructions for using a device, V辞書形と usually describes the result that occurs when that action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.vi: I want to stay at a hotel near the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N の ＋ N に ＋ Vます形 omitます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects えき with ちかく, creating the phrase “near the station.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ちかく with ホテル and modifies “hotel.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where one stays or the destination of the action とまる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: たい follows the omitます form of とまる to express the desire to stay.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.cn: Vます形 omitます ＋ たいです; Nの ＋ N connects possessive or location relationships
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.why: The two phrases の identify the hotel as being near the station. に indicates the place to stay, while とまりたい expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced by とまりませんか, the sentence becomes an invitation or suggestion to stay, rather than the speaker’s direct desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If とまるつもりです is used, it means that there is already an intention to stay, so it is more certain and planned than たいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q23.kobun.tip: たい always attaches to the stem ます, such as とまりたい, and does not attach directly to the dictionary form とまるたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は presents petroleum as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle で indicates the means used for transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The passive verb form shows that petroleum is the object being transported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q24.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, followed by the means with で and the passive action at the end. The passive form is suitable because petroleum is affected by the transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the tanker becomes the direct subject that transports it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q24.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use はこぶ in the active form and forget that the topic 石油 is the thing being transported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.vi: Please cool the water in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks water as the object of the cooling action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb uses the て form to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください makes a polite request, meaning “please do something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.why: The object comes before を, and the place where the action occurs comes after で. The て form connects the action with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression is also a request, but the form is incorrect because ひやす must change to ひやして before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.vi: My daughter currently lives in Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents むすめ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: いま indicates the current time of the state of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place of existence or residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: すんで is the て form of すむ. It connects with います to express a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vている with the meaning of a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.why: The topic is marked by は, the place of residence uses に, and すんでいます expresses the continuing state of living. This order moves from the object, to the time, to the place, and then to the state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with すみました, the meaning is that the person lived there or moved there to live, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: で usually indicates the place where an activity occurs, so it is less natural than に with すむ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for a place of residence, but すむ is usually used with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the person who has the feeling or preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: やさしい comes before 人 to describe a person with a kind personality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object considered likable in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きです is the adjective predicate な, expressing the topic’s preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.why: やさしい人 forms a noun phrase in which the adjective comes before the noun to describe the person. With 好きです, the liked object usually goes with が, while the person who has the preference goes with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If を好む is used, the sentence has a more formal written style and emphasizes the action of preferring something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is changed to は, the kind person becomes a contrasting topic instead of the direct object of 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say 好きです with を, but the basic pattern is Nが好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.vi: His close friends are all young women.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かれ with ゆうじん to show possession or a relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: したしい comes before ゆうじん to describe how close the friends are.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents ゆうじん as the topic, and the comma separates the topic from the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: わかい modifies the noun for women that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ばかり emphasizes that the group consists only of women, while です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.why: かれのしたしいゆうじん is a large noun phrase, in which の and したしい modify ゆうじん in order. After the topic, わかいじょせいばかりです comments that the group of friends consists only of young women.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ばかり replaces だけ, the meaning is still “only,” but the emphasis on concentration or repetition is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If しか〜ない is used, the sentence must be negative and emphasize that there are no other people besides women.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put ばかり after a verb out of habit, but here it comes after a noun to mean “all are.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.vi: Hanako, an actress, married a musician.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects this noun with the person described as 花子さん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents 花子さん as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indicates the person who participates in the marriage action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 結婚する is changed to the polite past form しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.why: The noun phrase before の modifies 花子さん. と marks the person who performs the action 結婚する, while ました shows that the event has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is dating a musician, not marrying one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the person one marries; with 結婚する, the companion usually goes with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.vi: This building was designed by an Italian person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before the noun ビル to indicate a specific building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents ビル as the topic of the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: によって indicates the agent that performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: されました is the polite past passive form, expressing that the building received the effect of the design action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.why: ビル is the affected object, so it is made the topic with は. The agent is stated after によって, and then the verb uses the passive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If an active sentence is used, the Italian person becomes the subject, and the focus shifts from the building to the designer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse によって in the passive sentence with に, which indicates a place or time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q7.kobun.cn: N は + N によって + V受身形
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.vi: I have already paid this month’s rent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: もう modifies the predicate and shows that the payment was completed before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 今月 with the noun for rent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the amount of money affected by the payment action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate is in the polite past form, expressing that the payment happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.why: もう comes first to show a completed state. The phrase 今月のやちん forms a compound noun, and then を marks the object of the payment action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning changes to “have not paid yet.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q8.kobun.tip: Do not omit の between 今月 and やちん, because の connects two nouns in a modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.vi: The dormitory heating system is broken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects a place with equipment belonging to that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the equipment that is in a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects こしょうする with います to create the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ている expresses a state that is still continuing, not an action currently in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.why: だんぼう is the subject of the broken state, so it goes with が. こしょうしている expresses that the broken result still exists at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern can also indicate an action in progress, but with こしょうする it usually expresses a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t56-q9.kobun.tip: With verbs that show a change of state, such as こしょうする and ている, the meaning is usually that something is in that state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q1.kobun.vi: This is a souvenir from Kyushu.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks this as the topic being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects Kyushu to the following noun and shows its origin or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a noun sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q1.kobun.why: A noun sentence uses は to state the subject, の to show the origin of the noun おみやげ, and ends with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If からの is used, the sentence emphasizes that the souvenir was sent or brought from Kyushu.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate の as only showing possession; in this sentence, it also shows origin or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しょくじ with ようい, forming a phrase meaning meal preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the preparation as the thing that has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: できました is the polite past form of できる and describes something that has been finished or completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q10.kobun.why: しょくじのようい forms a noun phrase showing the content of the task. が marks that task as the subject of できました, because できる in this meaning describes a completed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If しょくじのよういをする is used, the sentence emphasizes the preparation action, not the result of being finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 終わりました is used, it means that the task has ended, while できました emphasizes that the result has been completed or is ready.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with できる, but when saying that a task is complete, a noun usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q11.kobun.sk: 程度副詞 ＋ Aなに ＋ Vます形 removeます＋なさい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: もっと modifies the whole request and shows an increased degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: まじめに is an adverb form that modifies the action はたらきなさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: はたらきなさい is a mild request form of the verb はたらく. It is used to advise or ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q11.kobun.cn: Vます形 removeます ＋ なさい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q11.kobun.why: もっと comes before the adverb まじめに to increase the degree of the action. まじめに comes before はたらきなさい because it describes how the work is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse まじめな and まじめに; before a verb, まじめに must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.sk: N が ＋ 副詞 ＋ Aい removeい＋く ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that undergoes the change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: きゅうに modifies なりました and shows that the change happened unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: くらく is the linking form of an adjective ending in い. It is used before なる to show a change into a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and completes the pattern for expressing a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.cn: Aい removeい ＋ く ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.why: へやが is the changing subject, while きゅうに describes when or how the change happens. The adjective くらい changes to くらく before なる to express “become dark.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence only says that the room is dark. It does not emphasize the change from light to dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is used with adjectives ending in な or with nouns. It is not used directly with くらい adjectives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use くらいなる; an adjective ending in い must change い to く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.vi: There are at least 40 prefectures in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.sk: N に は ＋ N が ＋ Number ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: には states the range or place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: This quantity phrase modifies けん and shows the number of prefectures.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the predicate showing that a thing or place exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.why: には sets the range as “in Japan,” and then が marks the thing that exists as the prefectures. The quantity comes before あります to modify the number of prefectures being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If では is used, the focus is more on the place where an action or event happens. It is less natural than には when talking about existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q13.kobun.tip: In an existence pattern, the place usually goes with に, while the existing thing or person goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.vi: I will return to my country next spring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.sk: N の ＋ Time に ＋ N へ ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 来年 with はる, forming the noun phrase “next year's spring.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the action of returning happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: へ marks the direction of movement for the action かえります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: かえります is the main predicate and expresses the action of returning in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.why: 来年の modifies はる to identify which spring. に shows the time, while へ shows the direction of return; these two particles give different kinds of information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence is still correct, but に emphasizes the destination rather than the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use の between はる and に; の only connects the noun 来年 with the noun はる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the action of buying happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing that was bought, the object of かいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: か at the end of the sentence changes a polite statement into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q15.kobun.why: どこで asks about the place where the action happens, while それを is the object of buying. か is placed at the end to form a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If どこに is used, the meaning is usually “where to go” or “where to put something,” not the place where the buying happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse で and に; the place where an action happens uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.vi: When I looked at the map, I found out the location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the thing that was looked at, the object of 見たら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects the action of looking with the result of finding the location. It means “when or after looking.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the information understood in the pattern 場所がわかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりました is the main predicate in the polite past form and shows the result that was understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.why: ちずを is the object of the action 見る, while 見たら creates a conditional or time clause before it. After the comma comes the result of understanding, with 場所が as the subject of わかりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vて is used, the sentence only connects two actions in sequence. It does not emphasize the relationship “when I looked, I realized.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vと is used, the result is usually natural or automatically happens whenever that condition occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use をわかりました; something understood or known usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q17.kobun.vi: I take medicine before going to bed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: 前に marks the time point before the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks medicine as the object of the verb 飲みます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q17.kobun.why: The time expression ねる前に is placed first to state when the action of taking medicine happens. Medicine goes with を because it is the direct object of 飲みます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would mean taking medicine after sleeping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily think that 前に always comes at the end of the sentence, but this pattern places 前に after an action or a noun showing a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q18.kobun.vi: Who is the person wearing those red clothes?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the clothes as the object of the action of wearing in the relative clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause きた comes before 人 to describe 人; は marks that person as the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: だれですか forms a question asking about identity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q18.kobun.why: The phrase あのあかいふくをきた comes before 人 to identify which person is being asked about. は marks the whole phrase about that person as the topic, and だれですか asks about the person's identity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence emphasizes the person who is wearing the clothes now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the relative clause after the noun, but Japanese places the part きた before 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.vi: A fire broke out in the neighborhood last night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.sk: Time + Place で + Event が + ありました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうべ states when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks an event that exists or happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ありました is the polite past form of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.why: The sentence orders the information from the time, to the place, and then to the event that happened. When describing an event appearing or happening, the event usually goes with が and uses あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 起きました is used, the sentence emphasizes that the fire started or broke out at the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 火事, but an event that happens usually acts as the subject and goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.vi: There was a postcard in the mailbox.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.sk: N に + N が + Quantity + Vて + いた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle に indicates where something is or enters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the postcard as an object existing in the mailbox.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The counting phrase 1まい modifies はがき and shows the number of postcards.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb はいる in the て form connects with いる to express an existing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: いた is the past form of いる and shows that the state existed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.why: The place is stated with に, the existing object is marked with が, and the quantity comes next. はいっていた describes the state of the postcard already being inside the mailbox.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: 入った emphasizes the postcard entering the mailbox, not the state of being inside it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish はいっている, which means being inside, from はいる, which is understood as the action of entering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q2.kobun.cn: Vて + いる・Vて + いた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q20.kobun.sk: N を + Adverb + Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the luggage as what is being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: すぐに modifies the action of sending and shows how and when it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to ask or request that the listener perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q20.kobun.why: The luggage comes before を because it is the object of おくる. すぐに modifies the action, while Vてください gives a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the request would sound more like a strong command and would usually be spoken by someone of higher status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ください, but this request pattern requires the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the speech is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: みじかい modifies ほう; が marks the choice considered better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: ほうがいいです expresses the idea that the option before it should be chosen or followed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q21.kobun.why: The speech is made the topic with は. The adjective みじかい comes before ほう to create the option judged to be better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたほうがいい is used, the sentence advises doing a specific action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out が in ほうがいい, but が is a fixed part of the comparison and advice pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q21.kobun.cn: Aい + ほうがいいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the venue is the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: どこですか asks about a position or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q22.kobun.why: The venue is placed at the beginning as the topic with は. どこですか comes at the end to ask where that venue is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence emphasizes the location where the venue exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で to ask about a place, but when asking where something exists, they should use は with どこですか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle まで indicates the endpoint of walking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb あるく changes into the polite past form あるきました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q23.kobun.why: State the destination first, then use a verb showing movement. まで emphasizes where the action ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead, the sentence states the destination more neutrally and does not emphasize the endpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に in every sentence stating a destination and forget that まで emphasizes the final limit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes this country the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the object that exists in this country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: たくさん modifies 森 in terms of quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is the polite form of ある and is used for nonliving things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q24.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to state the scope as this country, then uses が to identify what exists within that scope. たくさん comes before あります to show a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If います is used, the sentence talks about people or animals that exist, so it is not used for forests.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse あります and います; remember that あります is used for objects, plants, and other nonliving things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes the question the topic of a confirmation question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: ありませんか is the polite negative form of ある combined with か to ask whether the listener has any questions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q25.kobun.why: The noun is first presented as the topic, and then the negative question pattern is used to ask gently whether it exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern directly asks “Is there N?”, while ありませんか has a softer, suggestive question tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q25.kobun.tip: Do not understand ありませんか only as a negation; in polite questions, it often means “Is there no ...?” or “Is there ...?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.vi: The two of them are competing to see who will be promoted first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the two people as the subjects of the whole activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates where the competition takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the person who will carry out the action of being promoted first in the question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 先に modifies しゅっせする and indicates the order of events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: か turns the preceding clause into an indirect question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The noun きょうそう combines with する to form a verb, and the て form connects to いる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: いる in している expresses that the competition is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.why: After the topic and location comes an indirect question clause that gives the content of the competition. している shows that the competition is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: 比べている only means comparing or considering and is weaker than the competitive meaning of きょうそうしている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.tip: か in the middle clause does not have to be a direct question; here, it creates the content being competed over.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ か ＋ Nする ＋ ている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.vi: There is no one suitable for this job except him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies the noun しごと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: には states the range or target being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: かれいがい limits the range to mean except him, while てきとうな modifies ひと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the person being discussed as the subject of the state of nonexistence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: いません is the polite negative form of いる, used for people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.why: The range of the job is stated with には, while the limiting phrase かれいがい comes before the adjective and noun to identify a suitable person. がいません denies that such a person exists within the stated range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: だけが states that only he is suitable; it does not directly express that there is no one else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.tip: 以外 means “except,” so the phrase N以外 usually goes with content that identifies the part remaining outside N.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q4.kobun.cn: N以外（に）＋ Aな ＋ N が ＋ いない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the preceding noun with the noun しな and shows a belonging relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the goods as the subject that was delivered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: とどいた is the past form of とどく and describes the goods arriving at their destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q5.kobun.why: The phrase ちゅうもんの modifies しな and forms the noun phrase “the goods from the order.” しなが is the subject of とどいた because とどく is a verb for something arriving by itself or being delivered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use とどける, you need a person or thing as the object with を, meaning to actively deliver something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly treat とどく as a transitive verb and use を, but when goods arrive, you must use が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that she is the topic and the person carrying out the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects わたし with くつ and shows that the shoes belong to me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the shoes as the object of the polishing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: きれいに modifies みがいて, while みがいて is the て form that connects the action to くれた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: くれた shows that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.why: かのじょは is the subject of the action, くつを is the thing affected, and きれいに indicates the result or manner of polishing the shoes. The て form connects みがく with くれる to express that the action was done as a favor for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use てもらう, the speaker becomes the person receiving help, changing the viewpoint of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use てあげる, the subject does the action for another person, which does not fit the meaning of doing it as a favor for the speaker here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse てくれる and てもらう because both can mean receiving help, but they differ in subject and viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.vi: I did not understand the teacher’s explanation clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 先生 with せつめい and shows that the explanation was given by the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the explanation as the content that is or is not understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies わかりませんでした and indicates the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりませんでした is the polite past negative form of わかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.why: 先生の説明 forms a noun phrase, and then が marks this phrase as the object that is understood. よく comes before わかりませんでした to add the degree of understanding, while the past negative form shows that the speaker did not understand it before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Nを理解する, the sentence emphasizes actively grasping the content, so the particle changes from が to を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may think that the verb needs を, but わかる usually uses が to mark what is understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q8.kobun.vi: A low mountain can be seen over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the state of seeing the mountain occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the mountain as the thing that is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 見えます describes the natural state of being visible, without emphasizing the deliberate action of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q8.kobun.why: あそこに places the location at the beginning of the sentence, and then 山が is the subject of the state 見えます. ひくい comes before 山 to directly modify the mountain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 見られます, the sentence emphasizes a person’s ability or conditions for seeing something, while 見えます emphasizes that the thing naturally comes into view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 見ます or 見られます instead of 見えます, but 見えます describes something that can be seen naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that that person is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the part or aspect used to evaluate that person’s quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: いいです is the adjective predicate and combines with あたまが to mean that the person has a good mind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q9.kobun.why: あの人は makes the evaluated object the topic. The pattern あたまがいい uses が to state a specific aspect, and then いい evaluates that aspect as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If いい is replaced with 悪い, the meaning changes to having a poor mind or not being intelligent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 賢い, the sentence directly describes that person as intelligent without naming the mind as a separate aspect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t57-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may say あの人を頭がいい, but this evaluation pattern uses は for the topic and が for the aspect being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q1.kobun.vi: My older brother is in poor health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the older brother as the person being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the body as the part with the weak condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective よわい acts as the predicate and combines with です to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q1.kobun.why: は identifies the person being discussed, while が identifies the part or quality being described. The adjective comes at the end of the sentence as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 強い, the sentence describes the body as healthy or strong, opposite to よわい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は for both nouns; in this pattern, the first noun uses は, while the described part uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.vi: Because the children were making noise in the library, I warned them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The part before the comma states the situation that leads to the action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person being warned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes an action that already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first to state where the event happened. The object is marked with を, and the verb ちゅういしました comes at the end to complete the main message.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ので, the cause-and-effect relationship is expressed more clearly and gently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse に with で when talking about the place where an action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.vi: After washing it, the sweater became shorter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item that was washed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects the washing action with the result that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the く form to modify なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: なる expresses a change of state and is in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.why: The object of washing comes before を. The たら form connects the washing action with the result, while the adjective changes to く before なる to express the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: と emphasizes a natural or inevitable result that occurs when the condition happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: てから only indicates the order of events after something is finished. It does not emphasize the condition leading to the result as たら does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily keep the plain adjective い before なる instead of changing it to the く form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q11.kobun.cn: Vたら + Aいく + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.vi: After hearing the news, everyone is happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies the noun 知らせ immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of hearing with everyone's state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the subject of the happy state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: ている shows an ongoing or continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.why: The news is the object of hearing, so it goes with を. The て form connects the action of hearing with the subject みんな, and the state is shown at the end of the sentence with ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If てしまう is used, it emphasizes completion or a feeling of regret, so it no longer describes a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Using Vた only says that they became happy; it does not emphasize that the state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ています as meaning only “be doing,” but with state verbs it can also describe a state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q13.kobun.vi: I asked for directions at the police box.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the asking action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ききました is a polite past-tense verb and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q13.kobun.why: The place comes before で, the object of the question comes before を, and then the verb ききました comes at the end to complete the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used after the place, it does not fit an asking action that happens there; で is the one that indicates the place where the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the place where an action is being performed; in this sentence, で must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the speaker's team as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: きのうの modifies the noun 試合 after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に goes with 勝つ to indicate the match that the team won.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: かちました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.why: The phrase きのうの試合 forms a compound noun meaning “yesterday's match.” With 勝つ, the match being won usually goes with に, while the conclusion is expressed by the verb at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Using を here is not the usual combination; 勝つ normally goes with に to indicate the object that was won.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: で emphasizes the place or circumstances of the competition, not the match directly as the thing defeated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate “win a match” and then use を, but 勝つ usually combines with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the spider is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the tool or material used to make the web.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the product that is created.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: つくります is the main predicate and describes a regular action or a general fact.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.why: The subject is stated with は, the material is marked with で, and the created object goes with を. The ます verb at the end fits a fact or a common action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: から emphasizes the source of the material, while で emphasizes the material or tool used directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: によって has a more formal tone and is often used to state an agent or method.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse で with a marker for place, but で is also used for tools and materials.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q16.kobun.vi: In summer, the daytime is long.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents summer as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ひるま with 時間 to form the modifying phrase “daytime hours.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that has the quality 長い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 長い is an adjective ending in い and acts as the predicate; です makes the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q16.kobun.why: The phrase ひるまの時間 is placed before が to identify the type of time being discussed. は sets summer as the scope, while が marks the subject with the quality 長い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use の after ひるま when you want to say “daytime hours,” because の is needed to connect a modifying noun with the main noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.vi: Teacher, thank you for helping me so much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: This is a way to address the listener. It comes at the beginning of the sentence and is separated by a comma.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろと modifies the whole act of helping and shows that it happened in many ways or many times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に combines with おせわになる in a fixed expression that means receiving care or help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and completes the pattern おせわになる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.why: The person being addressed comes at the beginning, followed by the degree いろいろと. おせわになる is a fixed combination in which に connects the noun おせわ with なる to express receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to おNをする, the subject is the person providing care or help, not the person receiving it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を in おせわをなりました, but the correct pattern is おせわに なりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q17.kobun.cn: お + N + に + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means of transport used to return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the action かえりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: かえりました is the polite past form of かえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q18.kobun.why: The means of transport comes before で, while the destination comes before に. The verb かえる comes at the end of the sentence and uses the polite past form to describe a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: When using Nに乗って, the sentence emphasizes getting on or going by that means of transport, instead of only stating the means of transport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use に with taxi when saying “by taxi”; means of transport usually go with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: すこし modifies the tired state and reduces the degree of the adjective or verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: つかれました is the polite past form of つかれる and describes a state that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q19.kobun.why: すこし comes before the predicate to show a mild degree. つかれました comes at the end of the sentence, carries the main information, and uses the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: ちょっと also means “a little,” but it is usually more conversational and natural in dialogue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q19.kobun.tip: Do not place すこし after the verb in this basic structure; adverbs usually come before the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the vegetables as the object of the washing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the verb and shows the degree of thoroughness in washing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: あらって is the て form of あらう and combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q2.kobun.why: The object comes first, and the adverb showing how the action is done comes before the verb. The て form connects with ください to make a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ています, the sentence describes an action in progress instead of making a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q2.kobun.tip: Do not connect ください directly to the dictionary form; first change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents それ as the topic being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ですか creates a polite question about whether ほんとう is true.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q20.kobun.why: それは makes the thing being discussed the topic, while ほんとうですか asks whether that thing is true. ですか comes at the end to create a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If でしょうか is used, the sentence becomes softer and more hesitant, like “I wonder if it is true.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit は after それ, but それは is needed to clearly connect the topic with the confirmation part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to modify かばん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the bag as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: かるい is an い adjective used as the predicate; です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q21.kobun.why: この comes before かばん to create the noun phrase “this bag.” は marks that phrase as the topic, while the adjective かるい comes at the end to state its feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes the bag as the object that has the feature of being light. This is often used when introducing new information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q21.kobun.tip: Do not add な after かるい because this is an い adjective, not an な adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q22.kobun.vi: Please excuse me for leaving first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に creates an adverbial phrase showing order, meaning going first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q22.kobun.why: おさきに is a fixed phrase used when someone asks permission to leave first. しつれいします is the predicate that expresses the polite request for permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, it means inviting someone else to go first, not asking permission to go first oneself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に as a word for a place and forget that in おさきに, に shows the order of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q23.kobun.vi: My older sister is an English teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes あね the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun えいご to the following noun and shows the field or subject taught.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and expresses the relationship “is” politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q23.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to state who is being introduced, and の to connect “English” with “teacher.” です turns the final noun phrase into a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, it emphasizes a teacher who teaches English, focusing on the action of teaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を between えいご and せんせい, but when two nouns modify each other, use の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the person as the object of the verb “know.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: しっています expresses the current state of knowing that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q24.kobun.why: あのひとを is the direct object of しっています. With 知る, the ている form usually indicates the state of “having come to know and still knowing,” not an action of knowing in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, it means having understood or grasped something, so it is not natural for saying “know that person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mechanically translate しっています as “be knowing,” but it should be understood as the state of “already knowing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.vi: Please take care of your health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the body as the object to be cared for, while お adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: たいせつに is an adverbial form that modifies the action してください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください creates a polite request or message meaning “please do V.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.why: おからだを is the object of the action of taking care. The adjective たいせつな changes to the たいせつに form to become an adverb, then combines with してください to give a polite message.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the complete expression with たいせつにする; the given sentence omits する because してください already carries the request meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say たいせつをする, but when the adjective な modifies a verb, it must change to たいせつに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q25.kobun.cn: Aなな + に + Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.vi: Let’s go to the department store to buy clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the clothes as the object of the buying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: かいに is the form of ます with かう omitted, combined with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement to the department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite or suggest going together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.why: The clothes are the object of 買う, while かいに states the purpose of going. へ shows the direction to the place, and ましょう turns the statement into an invitation to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used, the purpose is stated more formally and with more emphasis than with the shorter expression かいに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern can be understood as going to do an activity expressed as a noun, but it does not clearly show the connection using the verb stem, such as かいに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the dictionary form かうに; with a pattern showing the purpose of movement, the ます stem, which is かいに, must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q3.kobun.cn: Vます語幹 + に + 行く・来る・帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.vi: The sky can be seen from the window.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.sk: N から ＋ N が ＋ natural-ability V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: から only indicates the starting point of seeing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 見える describes a state in which something can be seen naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.why: まどから indicates the viewpoint, while そらが is the object that appears within the field of vision. 見えます describes the natural ability to see something, without emphasizing that the subject intentionally looks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 見ます, it means that someone actively looks at the sky.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 見える; things that are seen usually go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects くび with うんどう, forming the phrase “neck exercise.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう is used to make an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q5.kobun.cn: N の ＋ N を ＋ Vます-removeます ＋ ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q5.kobun.why: くびの modifies うんどう and identifies the body part to exercise. うんどうをしましょう uses を because する takes the activity as its object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 運動します is used, it only states that one exercises and does not specify which body part is exercised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use が after うんどう when saying that the activity is performed with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q6.kobun.vi: During the winter vacation, I will return to my parents' home in the countryside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects いなか with じっか, forming the phrase “my parents' home in the countryside.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of the return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q6.kobun.why: ふゆやすみは places the time at the beginning of the sentence. いなかのじっか is a noun phrase, while に marks the place of return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, it still points toward the countryside, but emphasizes direction more than the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q6.kobun.tip: With かえる, a place of return usually goes with に or へ, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q7.kobun.vi: Because I caught a cold, I got a fever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the illness that goes with ひく in the expression かぜをひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 connects a cause or an earlier event with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks a symptom that appears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q7.kobun.why: かぜをひいて places the cause first, and then ねつがでました states the result. ひいて is the て form of ひく used to connect two clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause is stated more clearly and gently: because I caught a cold, I got a fever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate ひいて as “pull”; in かぜをひく, it means to catch a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.vi: A nurse's work is hard but interesting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かんごし with しごと, forming the phrase “a nurse's work.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents しごと as the topic for comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two contrasting comments: the work is hard but still enjoyable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.why: かんごしのしごとは is a noun phrase functioning as the topic. The two qualities, たいへん and たのしい, are connected by が to show mild contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with けど, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the conversational tone is more casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If そして is used, it only adds information and no longer has the meaning of “but.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.tip: たいへん is an な adjective, so before ですが, たいへんですが is used directly, without adding だ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q8.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ ですが、／Aい ＋ ですが、
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q9.kobun.vi: Because I overslept, I arrived at school late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: して connects a cause or an earlier action with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination connected with おくれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q9.kobun.why: ねぼうして states the earlier cause. がっこうにおくれました describes being late for a time or place one must reach, so に is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the cause is stated more directly and clearly: because I overslept, I was late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 間に合いませんでした, it means not making it in time, not simply arriving late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t58-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use で after がっこう when saying “be late for school”; おくれる usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.vi: The clothes washed this morning are still not dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vた ＋ N が ＋ まだ ＋ Vていません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates when the washing took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause modifies the noun ふく, meaning the clothes washed this morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the clothes as the subject in the state of not being dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ shows that the state being discussed is not yet complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: かわいていません expresses the present state in which the result of being dry has not yet been reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.cn: Vている is the polite negative: Vていません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.why: The せんたくした clause comes before ふく to modify “clothes.” まだ combines with Vていません to emphasize that the dry result has still not occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this sentence is replaced, it only says “not dry” or “will not dry,” and emphasizes the present state less than かわいていません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese places せんたくした before ふく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.vi: The package I sent yesterday has already arrived at home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vた ＋ N が ＋ 副 from ＋ N に ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The time expression modifies the act of sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense verb comes before the noun にもつ to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the package as the subject that arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: もう adds the meaning that the action happened earlier than the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the destination where the package arrived.
