default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.why: おくった comes before にもつ to identify which package. After the subject, もう and いえに add the completed state and the destination, respectively, and then とどいた serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If the dictionary form is used, the meaning will be “a package to send” or “a package that needs to be sent,” not a package that has been sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is used, the sentence says that the action happens at home, not that the package arrives home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for a destination, but the verb とどく usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.vi: When I heard that Mr. Sato was injured, everyone became worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the injured person in the clause that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content of the action した in the phrase けがをした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と quotes the content that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects hearing the news with the worried reaction that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.why: The clause さとうさんがけがをした is placed before と to show the content that was heard. 聞いて connects the cause or time with the main reaction of みんな.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と聞くと, the meaning leans toward “whenever someone hears the news” or a conditional reaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with と聞いたので, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer, and the sentence has an explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place と after 聞いて, but と must come immediately after the content that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.vi: I have a dream of becoming a singer in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.sk: N には + Time + N に + なるという + N が あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates the person who owns or has something in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The time expression modifies the content of the dream.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the result or goal of a change with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: という frames the content “become a singer” to modify ゆめ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the dream as something that exists in the pattern わたしにはあります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.why: The phrase かしゅになるという clarifies what the dream is about. わたしにはあります uses には to state who has the dream, while ゆめがあります states that the dream exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If という is omitted, the phrase can still modify 夢, but the meaning is shorter and places less emphasis on the content identified as the dream.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with たい, the sentence emphasizes the speaker’s desire more than the identified content of the dream.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use をあります, but the pattern expressing possession or existence uses があります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形 + という + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.vi: Mr. Lee, please be sure to come to this party too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.sk: N も + N の N に + 副 from + Vてくださいね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: も replaces は or が and adds Mr. Lee to the group of invited people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects こんど with パーティー, creating the phrase “this party.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the place or event that the invited person will go to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ぜひ emphasizes the speaker’s wish for the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 来てください is a polite invitation, while ね creates a friendly tone and shows that the speaker hopes the listener agrees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.why: も shows that this invitation also applies to Lee. The place or event goes with に, ぜひ increases the strength of the request, and 来てくださいね creates a polite but friendly invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the sentence would ask or allow Lee to come, so it would no longer be a direct invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the invitation would sound softer and more hesitant, in the form of a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use へ in every case, but に here emphasizes the target event that the listener will attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.vi: I will explain how to use the machine from now on, so please listen carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.sk: Time + N の N を + Vます から、 副 from + Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the time when the explanation begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects きかい with つかいかた and indicates how to use the machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the reason clause with the request for the listener to pay attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: よく modifies 聞いて and asks the listener to listen carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: 聞いてください creates a polite request by combining the て form of 聞く with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.why: The noun phrase きかいのつかいかた is the object of せつめいします. から gives the reason for the following request, while よく comes before 聞いてください to show how to listen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If the ending is replaced with 聞いてもいいです, the sentence asks for permission to listen instead of asking someone else to listen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate から as “from,” but in this sentence から connects the reason and means “because.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q14.tokens.0.m: from now on / from this point
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.vi: Because my teeth are not healthy, I cannot eat hard food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.sk: N が + Aい + ので + N は + negative potential form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that has an unhealthy condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause clause with the result and means “because/due to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes “hard food” the specific topic being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べられません is the negative potential form and expresses the inability to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. は in the following clause limits the topic to “hard food,” while 食べられません states the restricted ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still expresses a cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after かたいもの, but when stating a contrasting or limited object separately, they use は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.vi: I invited Mr. Mori on a date, but he said he could not go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.sk: N を + N に + Vました が、 + 普通形 と + passive Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person being invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the purpose or activity that the other person is invited to join.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two contrasting clauses; the verb is in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content of the quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 言われました is the polite passive form and shows that the speaker was told this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.why: The person being invited goes with を, while デートに states the activity or purpose of the invitation. The refusal is placed before と and combines with 言われました to form a passive reported sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: けど also connects contrasting ideas like が, but it is more conversational and casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: と言いました simply states directly that someone said something and does not emphasize the meaning “was said to me” like 言われました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use に to mark the person being invited; with 誘う, the invited person usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.vi: In one year, my son grew about 5 cm taller.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Time で + Quantity くらい + N が + Aいくなる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the possessor with the noun むすこ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes my son the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the period needed for the change to be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: くらい comes after a measurement to show an approximate amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the direct object that becomes taller.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: Aい changes into く and then connects with なりました to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.why: で identifies the time needed to achieve the change, while くらい gives the approximate amount of increase. The structure Aくなる expresses the height changing to a taller state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: １年の間に emphasizes that the event happened within about one year, without emphasizing the time needed to achieve the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.tip: With adjectives ending in い, い must be changed to く before なる; do not say 高いなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q17.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくなる・Aくなります・Aくなりました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.vi: I compared three computers at the store and chose the lightest one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.sk: N で + Quantity の N を + Vて + いちばん Aい N を + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the comparison takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the quantity to the modified noun パソコン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the computers as the objects being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the comparison action to the following selection action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: いちばん modifies the following adjective and creates the superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective modifies パソコン and identifies the computer that was chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the computer as the object of 選ぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.ch.7.n: This is the main predicate, stating the result after the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the action. The form て connects two actions in sequence, while いちばん combines with an adjective to choose the one with the highest degree of lightness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: てから emphasizes that the selection happens only after the comparison is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: Nと比べて is used when comparing with a specific object or standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q18.kobun.tip: Do not put いちばん after a noun; いちばん must come before the adjective whose highest degree you want to emphasize.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.vi: The light in Mr. Tanaka's house is not on. It seems that he is away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.sk: N の N が + Vている negative + ね。N は + N のようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner to the noun いえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects いえ with the noun 電気, creating the phrase “the house's light”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the light as being in the state of not being on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ついていません describes the state of the light not being on; ね is used to confirm this with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes Mr. Tanaka the topic of the next statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: With nouns, の is the linking form before ようだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: ようです expresses a judgment based on an observable sign.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.why: The first sentence states the observable sign: the light is not on. Based on this sign, the second sentence uses は to shift the topic to Mr. Tanaka and ようです to guess that he is away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: みたいです also means “seems,” but it is more conversational and informal than ようです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: そうです usually describes appearance or a direct sign, so its meaning is different from the inference expressed by ようです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.tip: After a noun, use のようです; do not connect 留守ようです directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ようだ/ようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.vi: Mr. Smith always studies very hard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.sk: N は + Frequency adverb + Aなに + Vて + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes Mr. Smith the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも is a frequency adverb that modifies the act of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ねっしんな changes to ねっしんに to modify the verb べんきょうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb べんきょうする with います in a pattern that describes an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern ている and describes studying that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.why: は states the topic, いつも shows frequency, and ねっしんに shows the way of studying. べんきょうしています describes studying that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaced this form in the sentence, it would mean “enthusiastic” as a state, rather than directly modifying the way of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep ねっしんな unchanged before the verb, but the adjective な must change な to に when used as an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q2.kobun.cn: Aな + に; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.vi: I am looking for the room key, but I still cannot find it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects へや with かぎ, creating the phrase “room key”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the key as the object being searched for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: さがしています describes an ongoing action; が connects it to a result that has not been achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ modifies the negative predicate to refer to the present time when the result has not yet happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 見つかりません uses an intransitive verb in the negative form to say that the key has not been found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.why: The object being searched for goes with を, while ている shows that the search is still continuing. が connects the ongoing search with the current result: it has not been found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: 見つけられません has a person as the subject who cannot find something, while 見つかりません emphasizes that the object has not been found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q20.kobun.tip: Distinguish 見つける, a transitive verb usually used with を, from 見つかる, an intransitive verb describing an object being found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.vi: When I heard that Mr. Sato had been injured, everyone was worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the injured person in the clause that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb した.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: と closes the けがをした clause as the content that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action of hearing the news with the result that everyone became worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.why: The clause さとうさんがけがをした is placed before と as the content that was heard. 聞いて、 shows the cause or earlier situation, followed by the main clause stating everyone's reaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうだ were used, the sentence would mean “I heard that Mr. Sato was injured,” without emphasizing the action of hearing and then becoming worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit と before 聞く, but と is necessary to mark the content that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + と + 聞く
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.vi: I have a dream of becoming a singer in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: には identifies the person who has or owns what is mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: しょうらい modifies the content of the dream.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination of becoming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: という turns the clause かしゅになる into content that modifies ゆめ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks something that exists in a sentence using あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.why: The structure にはあります expresses that something exists or belongs to someone. The clause かしゅになる connects to という to modify the noun ゆめ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If かしゅのゆめ were used, the sentence would mean a singer's dream, not a dream of becoming a singer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.tip: Do not understand という here as an independent verb; it packages the whole clause as a modifier for ゆめ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + という + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.vi: Lee, please be sure to come to this party too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: も adds Lee to the group of invited people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects こんど with パーティー to modify the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or event that the listener is asked to attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ぜひ emphasizes the wish for the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 来てください is a polite request; ね makes the sentence softer and seeks the listener's agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.why: A place or event is marked by に and comes before the action 来てください. ぜひ modifies the request, while ね creates a friendly tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 来ませんか, the sentence becomes a gentle suggestion or invitation instead of a request to come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 来てもいいです is used, the meaning is that coming is permitted, not a direct invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use へ for every verb of movement, but for an event that someone is invited to attend, に is more natural in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.vi: We will gather in front of the station and then go to see a movie together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 駅 with 前 to create the phrase “in front of the station.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the gathering takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects gathering with the later action of going to see a movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the group or the way the action is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the object of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: The stem form ます of 見ます combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.why: 前に identifies the meeting place, while あつまって、 connects that action with the next plan. The phrase 見に行きます uses the stem form ます of 見ます to state the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見て行きます is used, it means watching first and then going, not going for the purpose of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行きます is omitted, the sentence only means watching a movie and does not express going somewhere to watch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily keep 見ます and add に, but the pattern uses only the verb stem: 見に行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q24.kobun.cn: Vて + V; Vます語幹 + に + 行く・来る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.vi: The energetic voice of the announcer can be heard coming from the television.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source from which the sound comes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows that the voice belongs to the announcer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun こえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects 聞こえる with 来る to express sound coming toward the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: くる adds the idea that the sound is traveling toward the speaker or observation point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.why: から states the source of the sound, while が marks the sound itself. 聞こえてくる combines natural hearing with くる to express sound coming toward the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 聞こえる is used, the sentence only says that the sound can be heard and does not emphasize the direction from which it comes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: 聞いてくる means going to listen and then coming back, or asking and then coming back, which is different from sound naturally coming toward the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate くる as “come” in the sense of a person's movement, but here it only indicates the direction in which the sound travels.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.vi: I am interested in Japanese manga.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects にほん with the following noun and creates a modifying meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the object of interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks what exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses the existence of interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.why: The topic わたしは comes at the beginning of the sentence. The object is marked by に, while きょうみが is the content that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes the active action or state of being interested more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the object, but the pattern 興味があります uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.vi: I do not know the rules of tennis well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects テニス with ルール to indicate rules belonging to tennis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of 知りません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies 知りません and indicates the degree of knowing clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: しりません is the polite negative form of 知る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.why: The object that must be known comes before を, while よく comes before the verb to add a degree. The form ません politely negates the action 知る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means not knowing much or not knowing clearly, and it is often used with a negative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q4.kobun.tip: よく in a negative sentence usually means “not clearly,” not necessarily “frequently.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.vi: Have you finished preparing the luggage for the trip?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects りょこう with にもつ to identify the type of luggage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the luggage the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: もう shows the point in time by which the action is expected to be complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: できました describes preparation that has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: か at the end of a sentence changes a statement into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.why: The phrase 旅行の荷物 identifies the type of luggage, and then は presents it as the topic. もう comes before the predicate to ask whether the preparation has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the question focuses more on whether the preparation is still unfinished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q5.kobun.tip: もう usually goes with the idea of completion, while まだ is usually used to say that something is still unfinished or remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.vi: I discussed it with my younger brother and then chose a gift for my mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と indicates the person who takes part in the discussion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of discussing with the later action of choosing a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the person receiving the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: あげる modifies プレゼント and identifies it as a gift to give to my mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the gift as the object being chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: えらびました is the main predicate and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.why: そうだんして connects two actions in time order. The clause 母にあげる comes before プレゼント to modify the gift, while えらびました is the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the idea of “a gift for my mother” is shortened with の, without emphasizing the action of giving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q6.kobun.tip: When a clause comes before a noun, learners may easily forget that it modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.vi: Please carry this luggage over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to point to a specific thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the luggage as the object being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the carrying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb はこぶ with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.why: The thing being carried is marked with を, and the destination is marked with に. The form てください comes at the end to turn the action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the request becomes more polite and softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; change the verb into the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.vi: This machine is very dangerous if used incorrectly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun for the machine that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents the machine as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the way of using it as the object that is done incorrectly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: と connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the adjective 危険 and shows the degree of danger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: きけんです is the predicate stating the result of the previous condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.why: The conditional clause つかいかたをまちがえると comes before the result. と fits because using the machine incorrectly naturally leads to the result that the machine is dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern keeps the meaning of a result that is certain or usually occurs after the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with たら, the sentence only states a hypothetical condition, so the sense of certainty becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q8.kobun.tip: With the と condition, the verb before it uses the dictionary form, not the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.vi: Please do not park in front of the entrance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 入口 with 前, creating the noun phrase “in front of the entrance.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: には states the location and highlights the place where parking should be avoided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object affected by the verb とめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ないでください creates a polite request meaning “please do not do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.why: The location phrase 前には comes first to identify where the request applies. 車を is the object, while とめないでください expresses a request not to park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence becomes a request to park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that the speaker does not park; it is no longer a request to someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t59-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget を before the verb or use ないください instead of ないでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: Do you often go to the movie theater?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies 行きます and shows how often the person goes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of the verb 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きますか asks politely about going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: よく comes before the verb to show frequency. The destination goes with に, then 行きます expresses going and か creates a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence can sound like going by or at the movie theater, which is unnatural; で usually marks the place where an action occurs or a means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is replaced with へ, the meaning is still going to the movie theater, but the direction is emphasized more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: A destination uses に or へ, not を; を usually marks the place where someone leaves from in patterns such as 家を出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: She is working at a famous restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: 「は」makes 「かのじょ」the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な must keep 「な」when it comes before a noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 「で」indicates the place where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 「ています」describes the state of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: 「有名なレストラン」is a noun phrase in which 「有名な」modifies 「レストラン」. 「で」marks the place where the work takes place, while 「ています」describes the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: This is incorrect because the adjective なuses 「な」, not 「の」, when it directly modifies a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「に」 is used, the phrase usually indicates a destination or a place of existence, so it is less suitable than 「で」for an action of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget 「な」after the adjective なbefore the noun, so they must say 「有名なレストラン」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: If it is next week, I can go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: 「なら」sets a condition or topic limit: if the time is next week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 「行けます」is the polite potential form, meaning “can go.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: 「来週なら」states the time condition, and the main clause 「行けます」states the possibility of going under that condition. 「なら」comes directly after the time noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 「は」, the sentence only presents next week as the topic and does not clearly show the meaning “if the condition is next week.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: 「だったら」also means “if it is next week,” but it has a more conversational and clearly hypothetical tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 「なら」with 「に」, which only indicates time; 「来週なら」emphasizes a condition, while 「来週に」is unnatural in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q11.kobun.cn: N・V普通形・Aい・Aな + なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q12.kobun.sk: Time + Manner adverb + Vます-stem + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 「今度」is a time adverb that adds the time when the action of going takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 「いっしょに」modifies the action 「行く」and shows how it is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 「Vましょう」is used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: 「今度」states the time, 「いっしょに」states how to do it together. 「行きましょう」is placed at the end of the sentence to make a polite invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the invitation becomes softer and takes the form of asking whether the listener wants to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 「今度」as meaning only “this time,” but in an invitation it is often understood as “next time,” depending on the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vi: The bus will leave at 9 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.sk: N は + Time に + N します
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: 「は」makes the bus the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 「に」indicates when the departure action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 「出発します」is the noun 「出発」combined with 「する」in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: 「バスは」states the vehicle as the topic, 「9時に」identifies the time. 「出発します」is the main predicate and describes the bus leaving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「から」is used, the sentence emphasizes the starting time or the point from 9 o’clock, not only the exact departure time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use 「で」to indicate the time in this sentence; a specific time such as 「9時」usually goes with 「に」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective modifies 食堂and shows what kind of cafeteria it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle がmarks the subject that exists in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますexpresses the existence of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: おいしいcomes before 食堂to modify the noun. 食堂がありますuses がto state what exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence means “This is a delicious cafeteria,” and no longer emphasizes existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use はinstead of がwhen introducing a new place or object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vi: Knives and forks came from the West.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: とconnects ナイフwith フォークto form a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: はmarks the whole phrase ナイフとフォークas the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: からindicates the source or starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ましたis the polite past form of 来るand describes something coming from the stated source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.why: とjoins two objects being discussed, while はplaces the topic at the beginning of the sentence. からstates the source, and then 来ましたis the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If でis used, the sentence is easily understood as an event taking place in the West, without emphasizing the source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If へis used, the meaning changes to going toward the West.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse からwith the place where an action happens, but in this sentence it indicates the starting source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: でもcomes after an interrogative word to create the broad meaning “anything.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: にchanges the adjective な大切into a state or manner for the following verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: しますcombines with 大切にto create an expression meaning to value or treat something with care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q16.kobun.why: 何でもis the object affected by the action. 大切にcomes before しますto show how that object is treated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 大事にします, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the conversational tone and vocabulary change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q16.kobun.tip: With the adjective なbefore するto show how something is done, you must use に: 大切にする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.vi: If it is evening, I have time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: ならtakes the noun before it as a condition or hypothetical topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: がmarks what exists under the stated condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますexpresses the presence or existence of free time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.why: ならsets 夕方as a condition, then 時間がありますstates the result under that condition. がmarks the thing that exists as 時間.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If はis used, the sentence only presents evening as a topic and does not clearly create a conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If ときis used, the meaning is “when it is evening,” focusing more on the actual time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q17.kobun.tip: Do not attach ならdirectly to a conjugated verb; with a noun, use Nならdirectly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.vi: I go to work by bicycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: でindicates the means of transportation used for traveling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: にindicates the purpose or destination of the verb 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きますis the main predicate and takes the means and purpose before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.why: でstates the means, while にstates the purpose or destination. These two phrases come before 行きますto add information about going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 自転車に乗ってis used, the sentence emphasizes riding a bicycle before mentioning going to work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If へis used, the sentence only indicates the direction toward the workplace and emphasizes the purpose less than に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q18.kobun.tip: にin しごとに行くdoes not mean time; it indicates the purpose or destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.vi: Is there a library in this city?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: このmust come before a noun to identify a noun near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: にindicates the place where the library exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: がmarks the object whose existence is being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ありますかturns an existence sentence into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.why: このmodifies まちto create the phrase “this city.” The location pattern にobject がありますasks whether an object or place exists somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If でis used, the meaning focuses on the place where an action occurs, so it does not fit an existence sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If はis used, the question becomes specifically about the library, with a contrastive or topic-focused tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q19.kobun.tip: The existence pattern usually uses locationにand objectが, not locationで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi: I am growing flowers on the rooftop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.sk: Location N で + N を + Vて + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: でindicates the place where the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The てform connects the verb そだてるwith いますto express an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: いますcomes after the てform to show that an action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: The location comes first with で, the object uses を, and then the verb in the てform combines with いますto express an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてあるis used, the sentence emphasizes a state that someone has already created, not an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use にinstead of でwhen talking about the place where an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the supermarket as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the type of goods being described as cheap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q20.kobun.why: The sentence makes the supermarket the topic, then uses が to indicate the item being described. The adjective やすい serves as the predicate for that item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the action of selling food cheaply.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 食料品, but in a description pattern such as 食料品がやすい, が marks the item being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the indicated item the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: でした is the polite past form of です, used to state a price in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q21.kobun.why: The item is introduced first with は, while the price follows as a noun predicate. The form でした shows that the price refers to a past time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If です is used, the sentence refers to the current price or gives information without emphasizing the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q21.kobun.tip: Do not translate でした as a separate verb; it is the past form of linking a noun with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.vi: This temple was built about 600 years ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.sk: N は + time ぐらい 前に + V受身ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は introduces the temple as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ぐらい follows a time amount to show an approximation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: に combines with 前 to identify the time when the action occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite past passive form shows that the temple is the object that was built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by a time phrase showing when the action occurred. The passive verb is suitable because the temple received the action of being built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, it means starting about 600 years ago and usually suggests a connection with the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q22.kobun.tip: ぐらい comes after the time amount, while に comes after 前 to create a time point; do not reverse these two particles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.vi: I have worked at this company for 10 years.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.sk: N で + time + Vて + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase shows how long the activity has continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects はたらく with います to create a pattern describing a continuing state or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the Vている pattern and describes work continuing up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.why: The workplace goes with で, the duration follows it, and the verb uses the て form connected to います. This pattern shows that the work started in the past and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If はたらきました is used instead, the sentence only says that the person worked in the past and does not confirm that the work continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use に to mark the place where an action occurs; for work activities, the place usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces Kanji as the item being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The い adjective serves as the predicate and ends with です to keep a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q24.kobun.why: The noun topic comes before は, while the adjective い directly serves as the predicate. です follows the adjective to make the sentence more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes Kanji as the item that has the quality of being difficult rather than making it a contrasting topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q24.kobun.tip: With an い adjective, do not add な before a noun or before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q25.kobun.sk: time + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes first to identify when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing or event said to exist or take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses existence or the occurrence of an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q25.kobun.why: The time is stated first, then the event as the subject goes with が. あります is suitable for announcing that an event will exist or take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence says that tomorrow is the test day or identifies what tomorrow is about, rather than simply announcing that there is a test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q25.kobun.tip: When talking about an event such as a test, meeting, or class, use があります instead of mechanically translating it as がいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: I went to the supermarket by car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.sk: destination N + まで + vehicle N で + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: まで marks the endpoint of a range or the place one travels to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: まで indicates the destination, で indicates the means of transportation, and 行きました serves as the main predicate and shows that the trip happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nに行く is used, the sentence only states the destination and does not emphasize a limit or endpoint as まで does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use に for transportation; a means of transportation goes with the particle で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes beef the topic whose desirability is being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: すきですか creates a polite question about preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The noun naming the object of preference is introduced as the topic with は, then すきですか is used to ask whether the listener likes that object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nが好きですか is used, N is marked as the direct object of preference instead of being introduced as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: 好き is an な adjective, so it is not used like a verb, and one should not say 好きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.sk: location N に + N が + ありますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing whose location is being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ありますか asks about the existence or location of an inanimate thing or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: The existence pattern puts the place first with に, the existing thing goes with が, and then ありますか asks about that thing's location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nはどこですか is used, the question directly asks for N's location without using the existence pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: With あります, a location uses に, not で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.sk: person N は + honorific verb ますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes ご主人 the topic; ご is a polite prefix used in the form of address.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: いらっしゃいますか is a polite way to ask whether a person is present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: The person being asked about is introduced as the topic with は, while いらっしゃいますか uses respectful language to ask politely about the person's presence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If いますか is used, the basic meaning is still presence, but the level of respect is lower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use あります for people; people must use います or the honorific いらっしゃいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: What kind of newspaper are you reading?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: どんな modifies 新聞, while を marks the newspaper being read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of 読む connects to います to create the structure meaning “be reading.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: いますか after a verb in the て form asks about an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: どんな新聞 forms a question phrase meaning “what kind of newspaper,” を marks the object of 読む, and 読んでいます expresses an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 読みますか, the question is about reading in general or a plan to read, and does not necessarily mean reading at this moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If Nのような is used, the sentence means “like N” and is no longer a question about the type of newspaper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: A group 1 verb 読む changes its final sound from む to んで when changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: Please try not to get sick.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 「に」 indicates the state or result that 「なる」 becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 「Vないように」 connects to 「する」 to express an effort to avoid something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 「して」 is the て form of 「する」, and connects the pattern 「ようにする」 with 「ください」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 「Vてください」 is used to make a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: 「病気になる」 uses 「に」 to indicate becoming a state. The negative verb 「ならない」 combines with 「ようにして」, followed by 「ください」, to make a request to try to avoid that situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is simply a request not to do something, without emphasizing the effort to achieve a goal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit 「に」 in 「病気になる」, but 「Nになる」 must be used to express becoming a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ようにする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects 「日本」 with the following noun and creates a modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of 「けんきゅうする」 connects to 「います」 to express an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 「ています」 expresses an action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The phrase 「日本の文学」 is placed before 「を」 to identify the object as Japanese literature. 「を」 goes with the verb “study,” while 「ている」 shows that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence says that the study was completed or took place in the past, without emphasizing that it is still happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate 「の」 as a possessive word in every case; here, it connects two nouns to form the modifying phrase 「日本の文学」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.vi: I accidentally left something on the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 電車 with 中 to identify the inside of the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the item was left behind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item that was left behind in the phrase わすれものをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb する with しまう in a pattern expressing accidentally doing something or finishing it completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました expresses a completed action, often with a feeling of regret or something unwanted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the object to identify where the event happened. してしまいました shows that the item was left behind and that the speaker regrets it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If the present or future form is used, the sentence means that someone will accidentally do something or usually finish it, not that it has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If only Vました is used, the sentence only reports that the action was completed and does not show regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate しまう as “put away,” but after the て form it usually expresses an unwanted completion or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.vi: The clothing counter is on the second floor, so please use the escalator over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the place being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the location where the counter exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects information about the location with the following guidance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects あちら with the noun エスカレーター to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the means of transport that the listener is asked to use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ごりようください is a polite request form used with the noun 利用.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.why: The sentence first introduces the counter’s location, then uses ので to give suitable guidance. あちらの identifies which escalator, while を marks the thing to be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ございます is replaced with あります, the meaning is still “exist,” but the level of politeness is lower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use で to indicate a location where something exists; with ございます meaning “exist at,” use に for the location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.vi: Recently, the computer had not been working well, but it finally broke down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん modifies the whole event that happened near the present time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects パソコン with the noun ぐあい to indicate the computer’s condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject being judged as good or bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects the earlier condition with the later event and creates a contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: とうとう emphasizes a result that happened after a long process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまった shows that the event was completed, often with a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the time and the computer’s condition, then uses が to move to the final result. とうとう emphasizes the result, while てしまった shows that the computer broke down completely and that the speaker regrets it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If こわれた is used, the sentence only says that the computer broke down and does not emphasize the feeling of an unfortunate result or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q11.kobun.tip: Do not omit しまった when you want to show that the event was unwanted or that you feel regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.vi: A: I heard that you were sick, but you look well. B: Yes, thankfully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the content that was heard or passed on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects what was heard with a contrasting comment about the current condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです connects with 元気 to express the appearance of being healthy; ね adds a mild confirmation tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: おかげさまで is a polite reply implying that the good condition is thanks to someone’s help or kindness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.why: The question uses と to report information that was heard, and then が connects it to a comment about the present. そうですね describes the appearance observed by the speaker, while おかげさまで is a humble and polite reply.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようです is used, the judgment is based more clearly on signs or evidence, rather than only on appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.tip: そうだ in おげんきそうですね means “seems,” not そうだ, which means “I hear that.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q12.kobun.cn: N・Aな ＋ そうだ; Vます形 ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.vi: I can eat anything except beef.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: いがいは marks the range excluded from what is stated in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 何でも acts as the object and indicates all items outside the excluded range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べられます is the potential form, expressing the ability or possibility of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.why: は at the beginning of the sentence indicates the person who can eat, while 以外は limits the range by excluding one item. 何でも acts as a general object and combines with the potential form to say that the speaker can eat everything in the remaining range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 牛肉しか食べられません is used, the meaning changes to “can eat only beef,” which is much narrower.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q13.kobun.tip: Do not understand 以外は as “only”; this pattern means “except N,” so it applies to the remaining part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.vi: I thought meeting Mr. Tanaka had happened only recently, but it has already been a year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the object of the action 会う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 会った is nominalized with の, and then は marks the topic to explain when the meeting took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: このあいだの modifies こと and indicates an event that happened recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ことだと introduces the content of the thought, and と marks what was thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: のに connects the earlier thought with the opposite reality that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: もう modifies the time phrase and emphasizes that time has passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: も follows a period of time to emphasize that it is long or a large amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: 前だ serves as the predicate and identifies the event as having happened one year before the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.why: The clause 会ったのは is made the topic, and then the thought is introduced with と. のに connects the past thought with the opposite fact stated at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence only expresses a present thought and does not emphasize that the thought continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If のに is replaced with けれども, the contrast remains, but the feeling of surprise and regret is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that のに here means “even though,” not only a purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q14.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ のは; Nだと ＋ 思っていた; Vていた ＋ のに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.vi: This coffee is quite bitter, isn't it? Let's add a little more sugar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase is presented as the topic through a pause in intonation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ずいぶん modifies the adjective and shows a degree higher than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: にがい is an adjective predicate; ですね is used to confirm the speaker's impression with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: もうちょっと modifies the amount of sugar to be added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the thing being added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: 入れましょう uses the ましょう form to make an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.why: The first sentence states the topic and then comments on it with an adjective. The second puts the amount to be added before the object and uses ましょう to suggest doing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ましょう is replaced with 入れてください, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to add the sugar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入れませんか is used, the suggestion becomes softer and sounds more like asking for the listener's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ましょう like a command; this pattern usually includes the idea “let's do it together.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q16.kobun.vi: This set of clothes was made in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は puts このふく forward as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: にほんせいです serves as a noun predicate and states the origin of the clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q16.kobun.why: The sentence combines the topic structure は with a noun showing the place of origin as the predicate. です comes at the end to close the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 日本からです, the sentence may refer to something sent from Japan or coming from Japan, but it does not directly mean that the item was made in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 製 with から; 製 is attached after a place name to indicate the place of production.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.vi: This is a place I am visiting for the first time, but I feel relieved because my friend will come to pick me up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.sk: V辞書形 ＋ N ですが ＋ N が ＋ Vます remove ます に ＋ Vてくれる から ＋ Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: はじめて modifies 行く and indicates going for the first time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before ばしょ to modify the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects the introduction of the place with contrasting or additional information that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person who will come to pick someone up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: に follows a nominalized purpose phrase and indicates the purpose of 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.5.vi: because someone will come to help
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: 来てくれる expresses that another person does something helpful for the speaker; から connects it as a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.ch.6.n: あんしんです describes a state or feeling that results from the reason stated before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.why: 行く comes before ばしょ to form the phrase “the place I will go to.” Then から states that the friend's coming to pick the speaker up is the reason for feeling relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the focus shifts to receiving help or having someone else come to pick the speaker up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason stays the same, but the expression becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place に after 来る with the meaning of a location; in むかえに来る, に indicates the purpose “come to pick someone up.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q17.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれる; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.vi: Because this bag is very easy to use, I have been using it for more than five years.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.sk: N は ＋ とても ＋ Vます remove ます やすいので ＋ もう ＋ 期間 ＋ Vます remove ます 続けています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は puts the bag forward as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective showing how easy the bag is to use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it is easy to use
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: つかいやすい means “easy to do”; ので connects a cause with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: もう emphasizes that the period of use has continued until now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: This time phrase shows duration; いじょう means from that level upward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: つかいつづけています describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ やすい; Vます remove ます ＋ 続ける; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.why: つかいやすいので gives the reason first, while the continuing action comes after it. 続けています shows that the use began in the past and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 使っています, the sentence only says that it is being used, without emphasizing continuous use over a long period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective, but the cause-and-effect relationship does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may connect やすい directly to the dictionary form; they need to remove ます before adding やすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.vi: Because I have not hung curtains on the window, the inside of the room is very hot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the curtain is hung or attached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the curtain as the object affected by かける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it has not been hung
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: かけていない describes a state in which something has not been done; ので connects this state with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects へや with なか to form the phrase “inside the room”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the inside of the room as the subject that has the hot state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: あつい is a predicate adjective that states the result of not hanging the curtain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.why: The phrases に and を respectively indicate the place of hanging and the thing being hung. The reason clause comes before ので, while the room’s hot state is given in the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with ないから, the reason is stated more directly and subjectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If かけていなかった is used, not hanging the curtain is placed completely in the past, without emphasizing the present state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に and で in this sentence; に indicates the place where something is hung, while で usually indicates where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q19.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いない; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q2.kobun.vi: Japan is importing a lot of food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Japan is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects たくさん with the following noun to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks food as the object being imported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: しています indicates an action in progress or a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q2.kobun.why: The sentence places the topic first, then states the object and the action affecting it. The particle を connects the noun 食べもの with the verb ゆにゅうしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget を before transitive verbs such as ゆにゅうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.vi: Because it is a difficult problem, think carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects a cause with a result and means “because... therefore...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb modifies the action of thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects a verb with ください to create a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to describe the problem. The reason clause comes before から, then the adverb よく modifies the action, and てください expresses the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still means “because... therefore...”, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If かんがえなさい is used, the sentence becomes a stronger command, usually spoken by a superior to a subordinate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place よく after the verb, but in this sentence よく comes before the verb and functions as an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q20.kobun.cn: Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the direct object of the closing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb modifies how the closing action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the て form connects with ください to create a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern てください asks the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.why: The object ドア goes with を, while しっかり shows how to close the door. The verb uses the て form before ください to make the sentence a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: しめなさい has a stronger command tone than しめてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: しめてもいいです asks about or gives permission to close the door, rather than asking the listener to close it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the adverb しっかり; を only follows the object ドア.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.vi: Because the car is broken, I will go by train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject in the broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason with the action in the following clause; している describes a state that is currently happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means used for traveling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the dictionary form is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.why: The clause about the car gives the reason before ので. The means is marked by で and placed immediately before the verb meaning “go.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: こしょうしているから also means “because it is broken,” but usually expresses a more direct and subjective reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: でんしゃにいく is not correct for the meaning “go by train”; に indicates a destination or direction, while で indicates a means of transport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に to indicate a means of transport, but means of transport must go with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.vi: I took my child to a department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the person taken along in the action つれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of taking someone along with the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: いきました is the polite past form of いく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.why: The person taken along is the object of つれる, so it goes with を. The action of taking someone along connects with the action of going through the て form, while へ marks the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: こどもと一緒に emphasizes going together with the child, not that the speaker took the child along.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: デパートにいきました is also correct and has a similar meaning to デパートへいきました; に emphasizes the destination more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use と to mark the person taken along in the pattern こどもをつれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q23.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; N へ ＋ 移動動詞
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.vi: Last year I often played tennis, but recently I have stopped playing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time and topic of the first clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb shows how often the person played tennis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the sport played with しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: は indicates a point in time and creates a contrast with きょねんは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: していません describes the state of not performing an action recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.why: The two time points are both used with は to create a contrast. が connects a past habit with a negative state that has continued until recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: しましたけれども also connects contrasting ideas, but it is more complete and polite in tone than が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: 最近はしません only says that the person does not play now; it does not emphasize a continuing state like していません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate and use は as “is,” but here は is used to state and contrast two points in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q24.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ います／いません; Vました ＋ が
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.vi: I have not met him for a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: と marks the person met together with someone, while は presents the person for contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing the long duration of the state of not meeting someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: あっていません is the negative form of 〜ています and describes the state of not having met someone up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.why: The person met is used with と, while は adds the meaning of presenting this person separately. ずっと modifies the period of time, and ていません describes a state of not having met that has continued until the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: まだ会っていません emphasizes “still have not met,” often implying that the people may meet later.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: 会いませんでした only says that the person did not meet someone at a specific past time or during a specific past period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 会う; the person met together with someone is usually used with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q25.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ います／いません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.vi: Because Mr./Ms. Yamada was ill, I went to visit them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who is in a sick state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects a cause with a result and means “because someone is or is in a state.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.ch.2.vi: to visit someone who is ill
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the purpose of going in the phrase おみまいに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate and uses the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first, while the action caused by it comes after. に in おみまいに行きました indicates the purpose of going to visit someone who is ill.
