default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing なので with から still indicates a cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: ために usually expresses a more objective purpose or cause and is less natural than なので in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use びょうきだので; with a noun or adjective, な must use なので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.vi: I was busy that day, but I will definitely arrive on time for the appointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets that day as the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting clauses and creates the meaning “but.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects やくそく with 時間 to form the phrase “the time of the appointment.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates a point in time, while は emphasizes that time point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: かならず modifies 行きます and expresses certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: 行きます is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.why: The sentence first states an unfavorable situation and then uses が to shift to a contrasting idea. The phrase 時間にはかならず sets a time point and emphasizes definitely going at the right time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: けど also means “but” and is more informal than が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: までに emphasizes a deadline, so the meaning is going before or by the deadline, not merely going at the appointment time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate に as “arrive,” but in 時間には it mainly indicates a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.vi: It is a shame that I could not get a concert ticket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects コンサート with チケット to modify the ticket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the ticket as the object that can or cannot be obtained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: なくて is the connecting form of the negative and links not being able to get the ticket with the feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ざんねんだ is the predicate expressing an evaluation of the whole preceding situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.why: Not being able to get the ticket is placed first as the cause, while the feeling of regret is placed at the end. が marks チケット as the object connected with the ability or inability to obtain it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: ないで usually means “without doing action A, do action B,” so it is less natural than なくて for connecting to an emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: ので would state the cause more clearly, while なくて shows a close connection between the situation and the emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q5.kobun.tip: なくて is not the negative past; it is the connecting form of ない used to link clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.vi: A: Thank you today for inviting me to the party. B: You went to a lot of trouble to come from far away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ いただいて ＋ ありがとうございました。＋ N ＋ Adv ＋ honorific Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the topic of the thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place or event to which the speaker was invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects よんで with いただく to create a structure for receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Vていただく describes the speaker receiving a beneficial action from someone else; the form て continues into the expression of thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ありがとうございました ends the expression of thanks; とおいところ is a shortened expression implying that the person came from a faraway place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.5.vi: went to a lot of trouble
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: よく emphasizes the effort or goodwill involved in the listener's coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: いらっしゃいました is the respectful form of “came.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.why: Speaker A uses Vていただく to humbly say that they received the other person's invitation, and then ends with thanks. Speaker B uses the shortened phrase とおいところ and the honorific いらっしゃいました to welcome the guest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 呼んでもらって also means “be invited,” but it is more informal and does not show the humility expressed by いただいて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: 来てくださって thanks the person for coming because they did something beneficial for the speaker, while this sentence thanks the speaker's being invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.tip: Vていただく is viewed from the receiver's side, so the inviter cannot be the subject of this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q6.kobun.cn: Vて＋いただく; Vて＋いただいて＋ありがとう（ございました）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.vi: Since the beginning of this year, the price of rice has gone down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.ch.0.vi: since the beginning of this year
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: になってから indicates a starting point, meaning from when the current year began.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects おこめ with ねだん to modify the price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the price of rice as the changing subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: さがりました is the main predicate and describes a decrease that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.why: The phrase indicating the starting point comes at the beginning to set the background. The sentence then states that the changing subject is the price of rice. の connects “rice” with “price,” while が marks the price as the thing that decreased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 今年から simply means “from this year” and does not emphasize the change into a new year like になってから.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 今年以来 usually emphasizes a continuing state since this year, while this sentence describes one decrease in price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse おこめのねだんが with おこめを; the thing that “decreased” is the price, so ねだん is used with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q7.kobun.cn: N＋になってから; Vて形＋から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.vi: This lake is shallow, but please be careful for the safety of children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ですが connects two clauses with a mild contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: には identifies the object that needs attention and emphasizes that scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 気をつけてください is a polite request, in which てください expresses the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.why: The sentence states the topic first, then uses ですが to shift to a contrasting reminder. に in には marks the object that needs attention, while を goes with 気をつける in a fixed expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: ですが can be replaced with けれども. The contrast remains almost the same, but the tone is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in 気をつける as a direction of movement; the expression 気をつける means to pay attention or be careful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.vi: It is already late, so let's get ready to go home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the suggested action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb しましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, followed by the suggested action. かえる modifies したく, forming the phrase “preparing to go home,” and this phrase is the object of しましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.tip: Do not confuse かえるしたく with two verbs; かえる modifies the noun したく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t60-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.vi: Translate this English sentence into Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the following noun and identifies a specific object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being translated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に identifies the target language of the translation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb ほんやくする with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ください is placed at the end of the sentence to express a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.why: The object comes first, the target language goes with に, and then the verb in the て form combines with ください to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a polite request in question form instead of a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q1.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use を after the target language, but に identifies the place or language toward which the action is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the curtains as the object being replaced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: とりかえました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q10.kobun.why: The object カーテンを comes before the verb. The verb in the ました form shows that the replacement action was completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 替えました is used, the meaning is still “replaced,” but the expression refers more generally to substitution and places less emphasis on changing an old item to a new one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q10.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily omit を in quick speech, but を is necessary to mark the item being replaced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.vi: While receiving an injection, please do not move.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the injection as the action being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: している modifies あいだ and indicates the period during which the injection is being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the period during which the injection is being given the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The ないで form connects with ください to ask someone not to move.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.why: The clause している modifies あいだ to identify the time period. During that period, the pattern Vないでください asks the listener not to move.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 間に is used, the sentence emphasizes an action that occurs during that period rather than a state that continues throughout the period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q11.kobun.tip: English speakers may confuse 間は and 間に; 間は presents the whole period as the topic, while 間に usually refers only to the time when something happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.vi: I boiled water to make tea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks tea as the thing being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ために turns the action のむ into the purpose of boiling water.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks hot water as the object being boiled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: わかしました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.why: The phrase のむために comes before the main action to state its purpose. The object ゆを comes directly before the verb わかしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ように, the sentence focuses more on a goal or result to achieve, rather than simply the speaker's direct purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily use のんだために here; to express purpose, use the dictionary form of the verb before ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q12.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.vi: I do not like ball sports, such as baseball and soccer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb comes before the noun スポーツ to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: たとえば gives a specific example of the preceding noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: や lists one example together with the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: は makes the group of sports being discussed the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: ではありません creates a polite negative predicate with the noun or adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.why: The phrase つかう modifies スポーツ, forming a noun phrase for sports that use a ball. は marks the whole group of objects, while ではありません expresses a negative preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence states positively that the speaker likes these sports.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning is still “do not like,” but the tone is more casual than ではありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.tip: English speakers may easily place を after スポーツ, but を must come directly after the object ボール of the verb つかう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q13.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ N; Nではありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamada is staying in rented lodging near the university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks Yamada as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 大学 to the noun ちかく and shows possession or location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where Yamada is staying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: しています shows that the state of staying in rented lodging is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.why: 大学の近く forms a location phrase, in which 近くに is where the state 下宿しています occurs. は comes after the topic Yamada to state who has this state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the place where the activity of staying in rented lodging takes place, while に is more natural when talking about a place where someone exists or lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: The sentence would only state that the person stayed in rented lodging or started doing so. It would not emphasize the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use で with the meaning of a place of residence in this sentence; に fits a place where someone is staying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or a polite title
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q14.tokens.7.m: to exist or be present (for people or animals)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.vi: This bread is very soft and delicious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before パン to identify the bread being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes パン the topic of the next two characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective やわらかい and shows the degree of softness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending い changes to くて to connect the characteristics of being soft and delicious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: おいしいです is the final predicate of the sentence and states the second characteristic of the bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.why: このパンは is the topic, and the two qualities are connected equally by やわらかくて. The first adjective changes from the ending い to くて, while the final adjective keeps its polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: し also connects several characteristics, but it often suggests that there are additional reasons or characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: が creates a contrast, as if the bread is soft but still delicious, or delicious in an unexpected way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.tip: Do not connect two adjectives ending in い by leaving い unchanged; the adjective before it must change to くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q15.kobun.cn: Aいくて + Aい; Aいくて + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.vi: The bus will leave soon, so hurry up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the bus as the subject that will soon leave.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: もうすぐ modifies 出発します and indicates that the event will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason clause to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 急いで is the て form. It connects the verb to ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください expresses a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason and is connected by から. The following clause then gives the request. 急いでください uses the て form with ください to politely say “please hurry up.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also gives a reason, but it is usually softer and more objective than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern expresses that something must be done, not a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use the plain form 急ぐください; before ください, you must use the て form: 急いでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q16.kobun.cn: Vますから; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.vi: I do not feel well today, so I will take the day off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time point for the condition and action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 具合 as the subject that has the characteristic わるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I do not feel well
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause to the result and gives a mild, objective explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 休みます is the main action stated after the cause clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.why: 具合が悪い is the cause clause, in which が connects the physical condition to the adjective 悪い. ので comes before the action of taking the day off to explain the reason in a softer way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: から also means “because,” but the explanation is more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: のに shows contrast, so the meaning changes to “although I do not feel well, I still take the day off” or still do something else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use は instead of が in the phrase 具合が悪い, because が connects the subject to its characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q17.kobun.cn: Aいので; V普通形ので; Nな・Aなな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.vi: The miso soup has unfortunately gone cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the miso soup as the thing that has become cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 冷えて is the て form and connects the state of being cold to しまった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 〜てしまった shows that the event has been completed, often with regret or an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.why: The miso soup is the subject of the cold state, so it takes が. The て form connects 冷える to しまう and emphasizes that the soup has become completely cold and that the speaker did not want this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: It only says that the soup became cold, without emphasizing regret or an unwanted event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes the current state of being cold, without focusing on the process that occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.tip: 〜てしまう does not only mean “finish”; in this sentence, it also expresses regret that the soup became cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q18.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; Vてしまった
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being mistreated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern Vてはいけない is used to prohibit an action or say that something must not be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: いけません completes the negative pattern meaning “must not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.why: The verb いじめる takes its object with を, then changes to the て form to connect with the prohibition pattern てはいけません. This pattern comes at the end of the sentence to give a rule or warning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, it would sound softer, like the request “please do not mistreat animals.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the sentence would mean that the action must be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget は in the pattern てはいけません or mistakenly use を after the entire pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q19.kobun.cn: Vて + は + いけない／いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.vi: It was used for ten years, but it finally broke down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.sk: Duration + Vている + が、 + とうとう + Vてしまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The duration phrase states the length of time it was used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the verb to いました and creates a structure that expresses a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: いました expresses a continuing state, while が connects to the contrasting result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: This adverb modifies an event that happens after a long period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects 壊れる to しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: 〜てしまいました shows that the event has been completed and often carries a feeling of regret or an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.why: The duration and state of use come first. が creates the transition to the result, while とうとう emphasizes that the final result is that the object broke down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If しまいました is replaced with ました, the sentence only states that it broke down and has less regret or an unwanted-result feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q2.kobun.tip: Do not understand しまう as only meaning “put away”; after the form て, it often expresses completion or something that happened accidentally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes that matter the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the verb and shows the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: して is the て form of する, used to connect with います in the form 〜ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 〜ています describes the current state of knowing or understanding clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, while よく modifies the action 承知する. The form 〜ている changes a mental action into a state that continues in the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, the sentence still means “know,” but it is more common in everyday speech and does not emphasize confirmation or acceptance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If used instead, the meaning leans toward “understand,” and it does not necessarily have the formal tone of 承知しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate 〜ています mechanically as “be doing,” although with mental verbs it usually indicates an established state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.vi: The number is attached to the athlete's back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks the number as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects せんしゅ with せなか to indicate the athlete's back, while に indicates the location of the attachment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: はって is the て form of はる, connecting the action of attaching with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 〜てあります describes something that someone has prepared, with the result still remaining.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.why: The attachment location is shown by the phrase Nの場所に. The てある form is suitable because the sentence focuses on the result of the attaching action that still exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with はっています, the sentence only describes the state of attaching or being attached, without emphasizing that it was prepared in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If はります is used, the sentence describes an attaching action that will happen or be carried out, not the existing result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse 〜てあります with 〜ています; てある usually implies that someone actively did something and that the result remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q21.tokens.6.m: be ready / already be in place
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.vi: It is impossible to memorize everything by tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.sk: Deadline までに + V辞書形のは + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: あした marks the deadline for the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: までに means completing something before or no later than the stated time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぶ modifies おぼえる, referring to all the content that must be memorized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns おぼえる into a noun meaning the act of memorizing, while は makes that act the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: むりです is the predicate that judges memorizing everything to be too difficult or impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.why: までに sets the time limit, while のは turns the whole action おぼえる into a noun for evaluation. むりです appears at the end as the predicate of that judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes that the action cannot be carried out, rather than judging it to be too difficult or unrealistic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the meaning is softer: it only says that memorizing is difficult, without stating that it is impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.tip: English learners may easily leave out の before は and connect the verb directly to むりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.tokens.1.m: before the deadline; no later than
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Nだ/です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.vi: Three months after moving, I have finally become used to this town.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.sk: Vて + period of time + 副詞 + N に + Vてくる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The て form connects the action of moving with the time that has passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: This time phrase tells us how much time has passed since the move.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: やっと modifies なれてきました and emphasizes a result achieved after some time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place or environment that the speaker is gradually becoming used to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 〜てくる describes a gradual change toward the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.why: ひっこして gives the starting point, while 3ヵ月 shows the time that has passed. なれてきました describes the process of gradually becoming used to something up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with なれるようになりました, the sentence emphasizes achieving a new ability or state, with less emphasis on the process moving toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with なれています, the sentence only states the current condition of being used to something and does not clearly show the process of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.tip: English learners may understand 〜てくる as only meaning "go to," but in this sentence it describes a gradual change toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q23.kobun.cn: Vて + くる/きます; Vて + きた/きました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.vi: I am living with my younger sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.sk: N は + N と + Number of people で + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who participates with or lives with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the number of people who do the action together or share the stated condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 〜ています describes the continuing state of living together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.why: The speaker is the topic, the person living with them is marked by と, and ふたりで shows that there are two people in total. 住んでいます describes the continuing living arrangement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with いもうとと一緒に, the meaning is still "together with my younger sister," but it emphasizes being together rather than the number two.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with いもうとと住みます, the sentence changes to an intention or future event of living together, not the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q24.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に instead of と when talking about someone who lives with them or does an action with them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.vi: Because I caught a cold, I skipped school and slept at home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb ひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result; ひいた is the past form of ひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that is taken a break from in the phrase 学校を休む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the action of skipping school with the following action of sleeping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the place where the sleeping action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects with いました to create a form meaning being or having been in a sleeping state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: いました shows that the sleeping state continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first with ので, and the actions are then connected in sequence using the て form. で identifies the place where the sleeping action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still indicates a cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If ねていました is replaced with 寝ました, it only says that the person slept and does not emphasize a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use で for the cause, but the cause in this sentence must use ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q25.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.vi: There is only one hour left, so it is impossible to finish all this work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.sk: Time limit で + N を + Adv + V辞書形 のは + Aな です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the deadline or the remaining time to finish something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the work as the object of やる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぶ modifies the action and shows that all of it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the clause やる into a noun, while は makes that action the topic for evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: むりです is the predicate judging that finishing the work is not feasible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.why: The time limit is placed at the beginning to state the time condition; the clause やるのは is nominalized and made the topic, and then むりです gives the judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことはむりです is used, the basic meaning is still "impossible," but the tone is more formal and general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q3.kobun.tip: English learners may easily leave out の after the verb, but やるのは is needed to turn "doing that" into the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.vi: I gave my friend a birthday present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.sk: Recipient N に + Object N を + あげました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person receiving the gift in the structure あげる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the gift that is given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: あげました is the polite past form of あげる and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.why: In the structure for giving, the recipient goes with に, the thing given goes with を, and the verb あげる comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with もらいました, the viewpoint changes to the gift receiver: “have received it”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: When くれました is used, the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side is the gift receiver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the receiver; in a sentence with あげる, the receiver usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.vi: I work part-time for two hours every day at a bakery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.sk: N は + Frequency + Duration + N で + N をしている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the whole part-time work activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The duration phrase shows how long the person works each day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the noun that combines with する to form the verb meaning “to work part-time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: して is the て form of する. It connects to います to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: 〜ています expresses an activity that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by frequency and duration. The place goes with で, and the work content goes with を, then combines with しています to say that the work is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 〜で働いています, the sentence emphasizes working there rather than doing part-time work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q5.kobun.tip: で indicates the place where an action occurs, while に usually indicates a place of existence or a destination. Do not switch these two particles freely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.vi: When you meet someone you know, greet them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause しっている modifies ひと, creating the meaning “a person I know.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object of the action あう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The form たら creates the condition “if or when you meet that person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the greeting action being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form of する. It is used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.why: The phrase しっているひと modifies the noun meaning “person,” に marks the person met, and あったら creates the conditional clause before the suggestion to greet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If あったら is replaced with あうとき, the sentence only states the time “when meeting,” without emphasizing a condition like たら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: なら usually depends on information or an assumption already given, so its meaning differs from a condition that occurs when meeting someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q6.kobun.tip: With 会う, the person met goes with に. Do not use を as in the Vietnamese expression “meet someone.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the payment action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb 払う with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q7.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the object and the main action. The pattern Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence becomes a request not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget that ください must come after a verb in the て form. It does not come directly after the plain verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.vi: The television next door is too noisy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects となり with the noun うち to modify “house.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects うち with テレビ to identify the television belonging to that house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects テレビ with おと to form the phrase “the sound of the television.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound as the subject having the noisy quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: うるさい is an adjective ending in い that acts as the predicate. It combines with です to be polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.why: The phrases の are arranged consecutively from larger to smaller scope: next door → house → television → sound. Then, おとが is the subject of the adjective うるさい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence emphasizes the topic of the sound rather than presenting the sound as the thing having the quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate each の as a separate word. Here, the whole chain should be understood as “the sound of the television in the house next door.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.vi: I have just finished calling to book a hotel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.sk: Time + Vて + N を + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The time expression modifies the whole action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て of でんわする connects the action of calling with the action of booking a hotel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the hotel as the object booked beforehand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: よやくしました is the main predicate in the polite past form and expresses that the booking was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.why: さっき is placed at the beginning to state the time. The two actions are connected by the form て in the order of calling first and then booking the hotel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning “after calling, book the hotel” is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t61-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand the form て here as the present tense. In fact, it connects two actions in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.vi: Please call Mr. Tanaka right away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: はやく modifies the action of calling and creates a sense of urgency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person receiving the call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the noun serving as the object in the phrase でんわをかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb かける with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: てください expresses a favor or request for the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.why: The person receiving the call goes with に, while 電話 is the object in the phrase 電話をかける, so it goes with を. てください is placed at the end to turn the action into a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This way is more polite and softer than てください, so it is suitable when asking someone of higher status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This way has a stronger command-like meaning and is often used by a superior to a subordinate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use に for 電話; に indicates the person receiving the call, while 電話 must go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.vi: I prefer watching sports to playing them myself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents sports as the topic being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the subject or method of performing the action する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: よりも marks the side being compared and can follow a verb in the dictionary form directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 見る modifies ほう, forming the watching option.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ほうが marks the side chosen as preferable in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: すきです acts as the predicate expressing preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.why: The two activities are placed on the two sides of the comparison pattern: するよりも is the less preferred side, while 見るほうが is the chosen side. ほうが makes clear which side is considered preferable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it only says that the speaker likes watching sports and no longer clearly compares it with playing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out ほうが, but in this comparison pattern ほうが marks the side that is preferred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I had a meal at a restaurant with Mr. Yamakawa.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N と ＋ Place で ＋ N を ＋ しました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう modifies the whole action and shows when the meal took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person who performed the eating action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the meal took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun しょくじ as the object of しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する and shows a completed action in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, followed by the person joining the action and the place where it happens. The noun phrase しょくじを combines with する to form しょくじをしました, meaning “had a meal.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to “went to the restaurant,” without confirming that the person ate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for a restaurant, but the place where the eating action takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects まど with ガラス, creating the noun phrase “window glass.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ガラス as the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な きれい changes to きれいに to modify the verb みがく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: みがいて is the て form used to connect a verb with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.why: The phrase まどのガラス is placed before を to clarify the object to clean. きれいに comes before みがいて to show how the action is done, while Vてください expresses a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If きれいな is used, it must come before a noun and cannot directly modify みがいて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use きれいなみがいて, but before a verb, the adverb form きれいに must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.vi: After lunch, I drink two cups of coffee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nで ＋ Nを ＋ Quantity ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ひるごはん with 後で to identify the time after lunch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: 後で indicates when the coffee-drinking action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks コーヒー as what is being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ２はい indicates the number of cups of coffee and modifies the action のみます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase 後で comes at the beginning to state the time before the main action. コーヒーを is the object, while ２はい states the quantity of the counted noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 後で is replaced with 後に, the time meaning remains similar, but 後で is more natural for an action that takes place afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget the particle の in ひるごはんの後で when connecting a noun with 後.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.vi: Because the exam is coming soon, I am taking careful notes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks しけん as the subject of the adjective ちかい in the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause with the note-taking action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: しっかり modifies the action とって and shows how the notes are taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks ノート as the object of the phrase ノートをとる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: とって is the て form that connects the verb とる with います in the ongoing-action pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: Vています expresses an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.why: The clause しけんがちかいので gives the reason first, followed by the main action. ノートをとる is a fixed verb phrase meaning “take notes,” and ている shows that the action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ノートをとる as “take the notebook” instead of understanding the whole phrase as “take notes.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.vi: I plan to ask someone to buy clothes for me at the department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action of buying clothes takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ようふく as what is being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: かって is the て form of かう, connecting the action of buying with もらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてもらう expresses receiving help from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: つもりです places the intention to do something at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.why: で states where to buy, を states the item, and Vてもらう shows that the speaker receives help with the purchase. つもりです comes at the end to express an intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買うつもりです is used, the speaker plans to buy the item personally, without the meaning of asking someone else to buy it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 買ってあげるつもりです is used, the speaker is the person who buys something for someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the direction of benefit of てもらう with てあげる; てもらう centers on the person receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.tokens.4.m: receive, have someone do something for you
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q15.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もらう; V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q16.kobun.vi: The food at the supermarket in front of the station is cheap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects えき前 with スーパー, creating the phrase “supermarket in front of the station.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes スーパー the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object described as やすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q16.kobun.why: The phrase えき前のスーパー is made the topic with は. In the comment, しょくりょうひんが is the object with the quality やすい, so が is used instead of を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to を with 安く売っています, the focus changes from the quality “cheap” to the action “sell cheaply.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before やすい, but the adjective やすい usually takes the described object with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.vi: I will work part-time and use the money I receive to go abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks アルバイト as the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: して is the て form connecting the part-time work with the action of going abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: もらった is a clause modifying お金 and indicates the money that was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the means or source of money used to go abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: へ indicates the direction of movement of 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.why: して、 connects two actions in sequence. The clause もらった comes before お金 to modify the money, while で states the means or resource and へ states the direction of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If お金を使って is used, the sentence emphasizes the action of using the money instead of simply stating that the money is the means.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places もらった before お金.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q18.kobun.vi: A concert will be held at the church.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the event takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that is in the state of being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ひらかれます is a polite passive form that describes an event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q18.kobun.why: The location comes first with で, followed by the event as the subject with が. The verb is in the passive form to emphasize that the concert is being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would emphasize the person carrying out the organization or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after the location, but the place where an event takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q19.kobun.vi: Because it was cold, I put on a hat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects a cause with a result and means because or due to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being worn on the head.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: かぶりました is the polite past form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q19.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. The object, hat, comes before the verb かぶる and takes the particle を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and conversational than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the item being worn; the hat is the object, so it takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.vi: There was a letter inside a beautiful envelope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: きれいな directly modifies the noun ふうとう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ふうとう with 中 to form a phrase referring to the inside of the envelope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the location where the letter is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object that exists at the location 中に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 入って is the て form of 入る. It connects with いました to describe a state of already being inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: いました completes the structure for an existing state in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.why: The phrase きれいなふうとうの modifies 中 and identifies the space containing the letter. In an existence sentence, the location comes before に, and the existing object is marked with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 中で is used, the focus is on an action taking place inside, not on the existence of the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: あります says that an object is placed or exists there, while 入っています emphasizes the state of lying inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.tip: For the existence pattern, remember the order: location に first, then object が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q2.kobun.cn: Aな + N; N の + N; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.vi: I brush my teeth in the morning and evening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects two nouns that together form a time expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the teeth as the object of brushing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: みがきます is the main predicate in the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, and the two times are connected with と. The verb's object is marked with を before the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with にも, the sentence emphasizes that brushing the teeth happens at both times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q20.kobun.tip: Do not confuse と in this sentence with the object particle; と connects two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.vi: When you do not understand the meaning of a word, look it up in a dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ことば with いみ to form the noun phrase meaning of the word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the meaning as what is or is not understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: わからない is the predicate of the clause describing the state of not understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: とき indicates a point in time, while は presents the situation as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the dictionary as the item used for looking something up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: てください creates a polite request or instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.why: The clause わからない modifies とき and forms the phrase when you do not understand. After stating the situation with は, the sentence gives a request using てください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 場合は, the sentence sounds more formal and more like an official instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand とき as a verb, but とき is a noun meaning a point in time and can take は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.vi: It seems to be raining. There is someone holding an umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks rain as a phenomenon that is occurring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ている describes a state or action that is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ようです expresses a guess based on signs that have been observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the umbrella as the item used in the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: This clause modifies 人 and identifies the person holding an umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the person who exists in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: います is used to talk about the existence of people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.why: The first sentence uses ようです after the clause to make a guess. In the second sentence, the action かさをさしている comes before 人 to modify the person, and then 人がいます expresses existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with そうです, the sentence focuses more on information heard from someone or on direct appearance, depending on the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence changes from the existence of a person to noticing someone holding an umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q22.kobun.tip: The modifying clause must be placed directly before 人; do not put the person first and describe the action afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.vi: Those who understand, please raise your hands.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: わかった comes before 人 to modify it and refer to people who have understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the group of people asked to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the hand as the body part being raised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: てください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.why: わかった is the modifying clause for 人, so it comes directly before 人. After stating the target group with は, the sentence uses を and てください to request that they raise their hands.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with わかる人は, it means people who understand or can understand, without emphasizing that they have finished understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place a relative clause after the noun, but Japanese places わかった before 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.vi: At the station, I was asked for directions by a stranger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.sk: Nで + Nに + Nを + passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who performs the asking action in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞く changes to the passive form 聞かれる and then takes the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.cn: Vない + N; Nを + passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.why: The location comes before the person performing the action and the object being asked about. The particle に marks the person asking, while を marks what is being asked; the verb uses the passive form to show that the speaker was asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If が and the active voice are used, it means that the person asked for directions, without emphasizing that the speaker was asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is used with 聞きました, it means that I asked that person for directions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and を, but に is the person performing the action in the passive sentence, while を is what is being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.vi: If we take a taxi, we seem likely to arrive in time for the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 行けば forms a conditional clause with the ば form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects パーティー with the noun 時間 to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the time by which something must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.ch.4.vi: seems likely to arrive in time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです is added after the verb stem to express a prediction based on the current situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.why: The conditional clause 行けば comes before the predicted result. The required time is marked with に, while そうです shows that the speaker thinks arriving in time is possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 行くと, the sentence suggests a result that usually occurs or is discovered after the action, rather than only a supposition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょう is used, the sentence gives a mild prediction or asks for agreement. It does not emphasize present evidence as そうです does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q25.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use そうです after the dictionary form of a verb, but a prediction based on appearance must use the stem ます: 間に合いそうです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.vi: I hear that Mr. Yamashita is not in good health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 山下さん the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects からだ with ぐあい, meaning the condition of the body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the adjective わるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: わるい serves as the predicate describing the state of health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです comes after the plain form of a sentence to report information that the speaker has heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.why: は identifies the person being discussed, while が identifies the body part judged to be in poor condition. そうです at the end shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: わるそうです means that something seems not good based on visible signs, not because someone said so.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: ようです expresses a judgment based on evidence, with a clearer sense of inference than そうです hears聞.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.tip: Distinguish わるいそうです, meaning that you hear something is not good, from わるそうです, meaning that something looks not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.vi: It is too dark, isn't it? Please turn on the room light.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: くらいです describes the current state of the room or the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: ね is used to seek agreement or share a feeling with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects へや with 電気, identifying the light as belonging to the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object affected by the action つける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: てください expresses a request for the listener to turn on the light.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.why: The first sentence states a feeling and uses ね to share it with the listener. The second sentence identifies the light with の, marks it with を, and ends with てください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: よ instead of ね emphasizes information that the speaker wants to tell the listener, rather than seeking agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure means that the light is on, not that someone is being asked to turn it on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.tip: つける means to turn on something such as a light. When giving this command, it normally uses 電気を, not 電気が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q4.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ください; Aい ＋ です ＋ ね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.vi: Because I took a bath, my body became warm.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place or destination of the action 入る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a cause; 入った is the past form of 入る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that undergoes a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: An い-ending adjective changes to the く form to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました expresses a completed change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.why: The action of entering the bath comes first and is given as the cause with ので. The thing that changes is からだ, and the adjective い must change to the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This is incorrect because an い-ending adjective must use the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: しました means to make something warm and emphasizes that someone actively causes the change; なりました means to become warm by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.tip: When something changes its state by itself, use が＋Aくなる; do not use を unless you mean to make it change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q5.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; Aい → Aく ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.vi: I want to send a picture postcard, so what value of stamp should I attach?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the thing being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: I want to send it, but
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 出したい expresses a desire, while んですが presents the situation before moving to a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase いくらの modifies きって, while を marks the stamp being attached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: はれば is the ば form of はる, creating a condition for asking about the appropriate way to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: いいですか is used to ask about an appropriate method or choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.why: The opening sentence starts with the thing to be handled, states a desire, and then moves to a question about how to do it. The pattern Vばいいですか asks about the suitable choice or method in this situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this pattern still asks about the method, but its conversational tone is usually more direct and natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may mistake いくらのきって for a quantity phrase, but いくらの only modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.vi: The library is just after you cross the bridge.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the library is the place being pointed out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the bridge as the object of the action of crossing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: わたって is the て form, connecting the action of crossing with the following location information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: すぐです serves as the predicate, showing that the library is just after the place mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.why: は introduces the place being looked for, while をわたって describes the point that must be passed. The て form connects the action of crossing with the location result すぐです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means going past or passing the place, without directly emphasizing crossing the bridge.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may translate すぐ as immediately, but in directions it usually means nearby or just after that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.vi: Please pay at the reception desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the payment takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks money as the object being paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: はらって is the て form, connecting the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください expresses a request for the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.why: The location comes first with で, followed by the object affected by the action with を. The て form of the verb combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If used instead, it makes the request more polite and softer, asking whether the listener can do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may use に to indicate the place of payment, but the place where an action takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q8.tokens.3.m: to pay; to settle a bill
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks hot water as the object being boiled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: わかして is the て form of a transitive verb. It connects with ください to request that someone boil the water.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください makes a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q9.kobun.why: The object is mentioned first with を, followed by the action to be performed. The て form combines with ください to turn the sentence into a favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence has a stronger command-like tone. It is often used by a superior to a subordinate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t62-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake わかす for “to boil by itself,” but わかす means “to make the water boil,” so it needs the object おゆを.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.vi: I borrowed four books from the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.sk: Nで + Nを + Number + counter + polite past V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the borrowing happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the book as the object being borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ４さつ adds the quantity and counting unit for 本.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: かりました is the polite past form of かりる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.why: The place and object come before the main verb. The quantity comes after the noun phrase and before the verb, adding information about the number of books borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買いました is used instead, the meaning changes from borrowing books to buying four books.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the counter, but books must be used with 冊, so you need to say 四冊.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q10.kobun.vi: This is a thread as thin as a hair.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the image being compared with the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ような comes before a noun to create a comparison phrase meaning “like.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: いとです is a noun predicate that concludes that this is a thread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q10.kobun.why: かみのけのような creates a comparison phrase and comes before ほそいいと to describe how thin the thread is. です ends the noun sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ように is used, the phrase usually modifies a verb or adjective. It does not directly come before a noun like ような.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q10.kobun.tip: Before a noun, you must use ような; ように cannot directly replace it in the phrase ようなほそいいと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.vi: It is a little dark, so shall I turn on the light?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is a little dark
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the action suggested in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 電気 as the object being turned on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: つけましょうか uses the volitional form to make a suggestion or ask the listener's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with から, followed by the suggested action. 電気を is the object of the verb つける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので makes the reason sound softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that から must come after a reason clause. It cannot come after a noun without だ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.vi: I will definitely finish this work by tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.sk: N time + までに + Adv + この + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: この comes before a noun to modify it and identify a specific object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the work as the object of おわらせる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.why: The deadline is stated at the beginning with までに, followed by the degree of certainty かならず. この しごとを is a noun phrase functioning as the object of おわらせます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used, the meaning is that the action continues until tomorrow. It does not necessarily have to be completed before that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse までに with まで and lose the meaning “complete it before the deadline” expressed by までに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.vi: Because I was busy, I still have not eaten lunch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.sk: Aい past + ので、 + まだ + N を + Vて + いません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason with the result, and adjective い changes into the past form いそがしかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ is used with a negative form to express that something has still not happened up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks lunch as the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べて connects the main verb with いません in a pattern expressing an action that has not yet been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: いません negates ています, creating the meaning “still have not eaten.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.why: The reason with ので comes first. The result uses まだ + Vていません to say that the action remains incomplete up to the present. ひるごはんを is the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: It means that the speaker has not eaten or does not plan to eat. It does not emphasize the continuing state of not having eaten up to the present as まだ食べていません does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing ので with から makes the reason more direct and stronger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use まだ with an affirmative form, but the meaning “still not” here needs to be used with ていません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので; Vて + いません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q14.kobun.sk: Greeting + Adv + Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: 入って is the て form. It connects the action with ください to create a polite invitation or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q14.kobun.why: After the greeting, どうぞ softens the invitation. The verb 入る changes to the て form and then combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern asks about or gives permission to enter. It is not a direct invitation like 入ってください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ください as coming after the plain verb form. In this pattern, the て form must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.vi: Because I studied very hard, tomorrow's exam will probably be fine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects a past reason with an opinion about tomorrow's exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects あした with しけん to modify the noun “exam.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes tomorrow's exam the topic of the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: でしょう is placed at the end of the sentence to show a soft guess or a moderate level of certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.why: The reason べんきょうしたから comes first. Then は makes the exam the topic. たぶん combines with でしょう to create a prediction that is not completely certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If はずです is used, the speaker shows stronger grounds and greater confidence than with でしょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If かもしれません is used, the possibility is lower or less certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate でしょう as the simple future, but here it mainly expresses a polite guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + から; V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.vi: I'm sorry for being late. The bus took a long time to come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: おそくなって uses the て form to connect the reason with an apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks バス as the subject of not arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: なかなか is used with a negative form to emphasize that something takes a very long time or is difficult to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 来る is an irregular verb. Its past negative form is 来なかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: んです is used to explain a reason or add information to what was said before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.cn: Vて・Aくて・Aなで ＋ すみません; なかなか ＋ V negative; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ んです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the て form to state the situation that led to the apology. The second sentence states バス as the subject and combines なかなか with the negative form to explain that the bus kept not coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression only reports the event, while なかなか来なかったんです emphasizes the explanatory meaning.
