default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If バスが来なかったので is used, the reason is presented more clearly as a complete clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use なかなか with an affirmative sentence, but the pattern meaning “kept not” must be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.vi: I had heard that it would rain from the afternoon, and, as expected, it started to rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: から only marks the starting time of the event being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the weather event ふる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: と introduces the content that the speaker heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb 聞く to the next part and forms a 聞いていました phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: が connects two clauses that contrast a prediction with reality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: やはり modifies the whole following clause and shows that the event happened as predicted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.ch.6.n: はじめる follows the continuative form 用 of a verb to show that an action has started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, followed by the rain event and the content that was heard. が creates the contrast, while やはり emphasizes that the actual result matched what had been heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning is that it looks like rain is about to start based on current signs, not that this is information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the information has the feeling of hearsay or a weaker guess than directly confirming that it was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と as the word “and”, but in this sentence と introduces the content of the verb 聞く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q17.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と; Vて形 ＋ いる; V連用形 ＋ はじめる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.vi: Thank you for always helping me. I will never forget you, Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に goes with おせわになる to indicate help that the speaker received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる in the pattern おせわになる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 田中さん with こと and identifies the object being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes 田中さんのこと the topic of the promise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: けっして usually goes with a negative predicate to emphasize the degree of negation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: ません is the polite negative form and expresses a firm promise not to forget.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the pattern おせわになる to say that the speaker received help. 田中さんのことは makes “the matter concerning Mr. Tanaka” the topic, while けっして combines with the negative form to emphasize the promise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, the sentence focuses directly on Tanaka; 田中さんのことは covers everything related to him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use けっして with an affirmative sentence. This word almost always needs a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.vi: The plane tickets for Saturday are already sold out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a time with the noun 飛行機のきっぷ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a noun for a means of transport with the noun きっぷ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the Saturday plane ticket the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: もう shows that the state occurred before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects なくなる with しまう in a pattern describing a completed event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまいました emphasizes that the tickets ran out completely, with a feeling of regret or something unwanted happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.why: The two phrases の identify the time and the type of ticket. もう comes before the predicate to state an existing condition, while てしまう emphasizes that the event has completely ended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence only reports that the tickets are sold out. It does not emphasize regret or completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand しまう as “put away”, but after the て form it can also show completion or an accidental event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.vi: It is hot, so please open the window.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the reason with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the window as the object that needs to be opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to ask or request that the listener do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.why: The reason あついので comes before the request to explain why. The verb “open” uses the て form combined with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead, the reason is more direct and casual than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If あけなさい is used, the sentence becomes a strong command, suitable for someone with higher status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the dictionary form before ください, but the correct pattern is the verb’s て form＋ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q2.kobun.cn: Aい＋ので; Vて＋ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.vi: Yesterday’s exam was not very difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a time with the noun しけん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes yesterday’s exam the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: あまり goes with a negative form to express a low degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い changes to く to connect with ありませんでした in the negative structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ありませんでした creates the polite past negative form for the adjective before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.why: きのうのしけん is made the topic with は. あまり combines with the negative form, so the sentence means “not very difficult” rather than an absolute negation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the expression is less natural for the meaning “not very difficult”; あまり is more suitable for expressing degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q20.kobun.tip: Do not conjugate あまり like a verb. Put it before the negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.vi: No matter how much I practice, I do not get better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら modifies the practice action and emphasizes the high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 ＋ も creates a concessive clause, meaning that no matter how much one does something, the result remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the resulting state after なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: なりません negates the result stated in じょうずに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.why: The concessive clause comes first to state a condition that does not change the result. With なる, the new state is marked by に, so じょうずになりません is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is still “no matter how much I practice”, but it places stronger emphasis on the amount or degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes the ordinary condition “if I practice”, without the meaning that the result will not change whatever happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で when saying “become skilled”, but with なる, に must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q21.kobun.cn: いくら + Vて形 + も; Aな + に + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.vi: There is still time until the bus leaves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action 出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: まで only marks the time limit, while 出る is in the dictionary form because it describes an event that has not happened yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies 時間がある and shows that the time has not run out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists in the pattern 時間がある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate showing that the time exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.why: The clause バスが出るまで sets the time limit for having time left. In the existence pattern ある, the thing that exists is used with が, while まだ emphasizes that the period of time has not ended yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes “before the bus leaves,” which indicates the time before departure rather than emphasizing the whole period that continues until departure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q22.kobun.tip: Do not use に after まで in this structure; まで already marks the time limit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.vi: I finally finished my homework. It took as long as two hours.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The adverb やっと modifies the whole event and emphasizes that it took a lot of effort to finish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the completed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes homework that has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も after a period of time emphasizes that the amount of time is greater than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: かかる is used to talk about the time needed for something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.why: The first sentence says that the homework was completed, with が marking the homework as the subject of the completed state. The second sentence uses the period of time as an additional element with かかる, while も emphasizes the long duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is replaced with は, the sentence only states the separate period of two hours and no longer emphasizes that it was a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that かかる is used for the time or money needed for something, so it should not simply be translated as “take” in every case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.vi: I still have work to do, so please go home first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies あります and shows that the work has not ended yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists as work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the reason clause to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 先に shows the order of actions, meaning that the action of going home is done first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects the verb かえる with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: Vてください expresses a request for the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with から, and the following clause gives a request. 先に comes before the verb to show the order, while Vてください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason stays the same, but the sentence sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If ください is replaced with ましょう, the sentence becomes an invitation to do something together instead of a request for the listener to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use から at the end of a sentence as a complete sentence, but in this structure から comes after the reason clause and connects to the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q25.kobun.vi: I drew a picture on the wall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where the picture was drawn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of drawing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes an action that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q25.kobun.why: The affected location is marked with に, the thing drawn is marked with を, and the verb かく comes at the end to complete the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, で usually indicates the place where the action happens rather than emphasizing the surface that receives the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で for every location, but for a surface where a picture is drawn, に is more suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.vi: Thank you very much for all your help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.sk: Nに + polite Vて + 、Adv + polite past expression of thanks
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: いろいろと modifies the content of the help received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: になりまして is the polite connective form of になる and connects to the following thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ほんとうに modifies the degree of the thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ありがとうございました is a polite past expression of thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.why: The phrase おせわになりまして states that the speaker received help, followed by thanks. と and に clarify the degree and content of the gratitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If なっています is used, it means that the speaker is currently receiving help and is not limited to help received in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If only ありがとう is said, the tone is more casual and it is less suitable for formal thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate なる as “become,” but in お世話になる, the whole phrase means receiving help from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q3.kobun.cn: Nに + なる → Nに + なりまして
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.vi: Because I turned on the heater, the room became warm.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks 暖房 as the object that is turned on or used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 入れたので connects a past cause to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that undergoes a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending い changes to the く form before なる to express a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.why: The cause, turning on the heater, comes before the result, the room becoming warm. が marks the subject that changes, while the adjective meaning warm must change to the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If あたたかいです is used, the sentence only describes the room as warm and does not emphasize the process of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If あたためました is used, the person or thing that directly makes the room warm is emphasized more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may say あたたかいなりました, but the adjective ending い must change to あたたかく before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q4.kobun.cn: Vた + ので; Aい → Aく + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the thing being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the following adjective and indicates a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い combines with です to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q5.kobun.why: この comes before くすり to specify “this medicine,” followed by は to mark the topic. とても comes before the adjective にがい to emphasize the degree of bitterness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If とても is replaced with あまり～ない, the meaning changes to “not very bitter” or “not very bitterly.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q5.kobun.tip: Do not place とても after the adjective; とても must come before the adjective or adverb that needs emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q6.kobun.vi: I received an interesting book from my teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who gives or the source of the thing received with いただく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: おもしろい directly modifies 本 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: いただきました is the polite past form of いただく, expressing that the speaker received an item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q6.kobun.why: The giver is marked by に, the received item by を, and the adjective comes directly before the noun it describes. いただきました serves as the predicate and humbly expresses a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 先生に is replaced with 先生から, it still means “from the teacher,” but it emphasizes the source of the item more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the giver; the giver goes with に or から, while the received item goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.vi: Because Mr. Oyama has a weak body, he often catches colds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes 大山さん the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the characteristic よわい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause clause to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies ひきます and shows how often it occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object in the fixed expression かぜをひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ひきます is the main predicate and combines with かぜを to mean “catch a cold.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.why: The sentence states who is being discussed with は, then explains the cause with the clause からだがよわいので. The result, よくかぜをひきます, comes after the comma to show a frequent habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate が in からだがよわい as “but”; here, が marks the subject of the adjective よわい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.vi: When I dropped my wallet and was in trouble, a kind person lent me some money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item that was dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of dropping something with the following difficult state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: こまって connects with いたら to express being in a difficult state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: いたら creates a condition or situation meaning “while being in that state.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: しんせつな modifies 人, so the form な is used before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the person who lends the money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the item that is lent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: かして connects the main verb with くれました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: くれました shows that another person did something beneficial for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.why: The two forms て connect the actions and states before the main situation. The clause after いたら states who helped, what was lent, and the action くれる that benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If くれました is replaced with もらいました, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q8.kobun.tip: With くれる, the person performing the action is usually the subject, while the person receiving the benefit is usually the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.vi: When you climb a high mountain, the air becomes thinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 高い modifies 山 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the destination of the action のぼる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition or a naturally occurring event with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object that undergoes the change うすくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The く form of the adjective い connects with なる to show a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: なります completes the pattern Aくなる, meaning “become a certain way.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.why: 高い modifies 山, while に shows the destination when climbing. のぼると expresses a natural result: when you climb a high mountain, the air naturally becomes thinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If のぼると is replaced with のぼったら, the sentence focuses more on a specific condition or time and does not stress inevitability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t63-q9.kobun.tip: When the adjective い comes before なる, い must change to く: うすい → うすくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.vi: I take my dog for a walk every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: A time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence and adds the repeated time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object taken along with 連れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of 連れる connects the action of taking the dog along with the action of going for a walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows the purpose or activity connected with going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the main predicate and expresses a regular action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning to show frequency. The companion is marked with を and 連れる, while the activity of walking uses に before 行きます to show purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the dog is understood as a person or object going together, not as something being led along.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と with 連れる because of the habit of translating it as “go together,” but an object being led along must go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.vi: This area has many restaurants and shops, so it is lively at night too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the area being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: や lists some types of places without implying a complete list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks a thing that exists in large numbers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the cause with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: も adds nighttime to the range being described, with the meaning “also.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: にぎやかです is the polite form of the adjective predicate な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.why: は makes the area the topic, while が marks the places that are numerous. The clause with おおいので gives the reason first, then concludes with the condition at night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から in every situation; ので is usually softer and more objective when explaining a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ ので; Aな ＋ ななので; N ＋ なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.vi: Because Mr. Yamada’s beloved dog has died, he looks very sad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aな ＋ N が ＋ Vた ＋ ので、程度副詞 ＋ Aい remove い ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な comes before the noun and modifies いぬ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the action of dying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: しんだ is the plain past form and comes before ので to give the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The form of the adjective い without い combines with そうです to express the appearance of looking sad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.cn: Vます＋そうだ; Aい remove い ＋ そうだ; Aな remove な ＋ そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.why: The dog is the subject of the event that happened, so use が and the past-tense verb しんだ. The result describes Yamada, so use そうです to say that his appearance shows he is sad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: ようだ is more about a judgment based on a situation or information, not only on appearance like そうだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q11.kobun.tip: Do not keep かなしい unchanged and then add そう; with the adjective い, remove い and change it to かなしそう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.vi: This road is always quiet, and there are not many cars.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 副詞 ＋ Vているて、N が ＋ Aい remove いく ＋ ありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the road the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: すいていて is the て form of すいている, connecting this state to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the object said to be not numerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: おおく is the adverb form of おおい, placed before ありません to create a negative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: ありません completes the polite negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ て; Aい remove い ＋ くありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.why: The two states of the road are connected by て: the road is always quiet, and there are not many cars. The subject of the second part is 車, so use が, while おおくありません negates the large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: あまり～ない emphasizes that the amount is not large, while おおくありません directly denies that there are many cars.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q12.kobun.tip: When the adjective おおい is changed into the negative form, it must become おおくない, not おおいない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.vi: Because this road has many cars, it is very dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the road is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the cause 車がおおい with the result あぶないです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: あぶないです is the polite form of the い-adjective predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.why: The road is made the topic, while 車が多い is the cause of the danger. ので comes after the cause clause, and the result あぶないです comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: から also connects a cause, but it is usually more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.tip: Do not put ので directly after the noun 車; you need to complete the clause 車がおおいので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ ので; Aな ＋ ななので; N ＋ なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.vi: I am shorter than my younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the feature being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ひくいです is the い-adjective predicate describing height.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.why: わたしは is the main person being discussed, and おとうとより is the comparison standard. The feature being compared is height, so せが is the subject and ひくい is the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: わたしはおとうとほどせがたかくない emphasizes that I am not as tall as my younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.tip: より comes after the comparison standard, not after the person being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q14.kobun.cn: N1 は ＋ N2 より ＋ N3 が ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.vi: If it is inconvenient, let us leave it until next week.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject being judged as good or bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective わるい combines with なら to state a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the time or option that has been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form, used to make a suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.why: わるいなら gives a condition about convenience. When that condition is true, らいしゅうにしましょう expresses the decision to choose next week with にする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: ～たら expresses a more specific condition or time, while なら usually responds to a situation that has already been mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: にする refers to an active subject deciding to choose next week, while にになる describes a natural change or result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.tip: Distinguish にする from になる: this sentence involves someone deciding the schedule, so use にする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ なら; N ＋ なら; N ＋ に ＋ する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.vi: That is a very good movie, so please be sure to watch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective いい and indicates a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: なので connects the reason to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ぜひ modifies the request and shows that the speaker wants the listener to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects the verb 見る with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.ch.6.n: ください comes after the て form to express a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.why: あれは states the topic. Then いいえいが is connected with なので to give the reason. At the end, 見てください changes the act of watching into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見てください is replaced with 見ましょう, the sentence becomes an invitation to watch together instead of a request for the listener to watch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget that ください must come after the て verb form, not after the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q16.kobun.cn: N・Aな語幹 ＋ なので; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.vi: One costs 250 yen, so four cost exactly 1,000 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: 一つ is the subject whose price is being calculated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the unit-price information with the result of calculating the total cost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the quantity used to calculate the total.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ちょうど modifies the amount that follows and indicates exactness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: です serves as a noun predicate and concludes the amount to be paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.why: The first clause gives the unit price and uses ですから to show the reason. 四つで identifies the quantity being counted, while ちょうど emphasizes that the result is exactly 1,000 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of ですから, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If 約 is added before 1,000円, the amount means approximately that much rather than exactly that much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.tip: で in 四つで indicates not only a place, but also the quantity or condition used for calculation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q17.kobun.cn: Nですから; Nで＋数量・金額
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.vi: Although it is spring, it is very hot, just like summer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: なのに connects an expected situation with a result that is opposite to reality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies あつい and shows the degree of heat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: あついです is an adjective predicate that states the actual condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the noun なつ with よう, forming a phrase used as the basis for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ようです expresses similarity or the feeling that something is like summer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.why: なのに sets two contrasting ideas: it is spring, but it is hot. Then なつのようです uses よう to compare the feeling of heat with summer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If なのに is replaced with けれども, the sentence only connects two contrasting ideas and has a weaker sense of surprise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ようです is replaced with みたいです, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the expression is more conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.tip: Before のに, with a noun or adjective な, you must use なのに; do not use Nのに directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q18.kobun.cn: Nな＋のに; Nの＋ようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.vi: It is impossible to eat this many dishes alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: こんな modifies the noun phrase that follows and shows its type or degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects たくさん with りょうり, forming a phrase that modifies a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the dishes as the object of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the way or situation in which the eating is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: の turns the clause たべる into a noun, while は marks it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: むりです acts as the predicate and judges eating many dishes alone to be too much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.why: The phrase たくさんのりょうりを is the object, and ひとりで shows how the eating is done. The clause たべるのは is changed into a noun to act as the topic, and the sentence ends with むりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If たべるのは is replaced with たべることは, the sentence becomes more formal and general, but the main idea is still eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If できません is used instead of むりです, the sentence emphasizes that the action cannot be done rather than judging it to be too much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.tip: のは here is not の meaning possession; it turns the whole action たべる into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q19.kobun.cn: V辞書形＋のは; Nの＋N; Nで
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.vi: A very strong wind is blowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: とても modifies the adjective つよい to increase the degree of strength.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective phrase つよい modifies かぜ, while が marks the wind as the subject that is blowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of 吹く connects with います to create a progressive structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ています shows that the action is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to describe the wind. The verb 吹く changes to the て form and combines with います to express that it is blowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vています is used, the sentence emphasizes a continuing state or action, which fits the meaning of the wind blowing now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vました is used instead, the sentence only says that the wind blew in the past and no longer emphasizes continuation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit います after the て form, leaving only a connecting form and failing to express the meaning of “is happening.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.vi: Have you gotten used to life in Japan yet?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: もう modifies the action and asks whether getting used to it has been completed by now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with せいかつ and identifies the life being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the object or environment that the speaker becomes familiar with.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: なれました is the polite past form of なれる, while か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.why: 日本のせいかつに identifies the environment that the speaker becomes familiar with; the verb なれる always takes に for this object. もう combines with the past form and か to ask whether the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 慣れてきましたか is used, the question emphasizes the gradual process of getting used to it up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If か is replaced with ね, the sentence becomes a confirmation that the listener is already used to it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.tip: なれる means to become used to something, so it usually uses the particle に, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q20.kobun.cn: Nの＋N; Nに＋慣れる; Vましたか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.vi: I ate a lot, so I am full now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: たくさん modifies たべて and shows that a large amount was eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of eating with the resulting state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks おなか as the subject that is in a full state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: いっぱいだ acts as the predicate and states the condition of the stomach after eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.why: たべて places the earlier action before and connects it to the result おなかがいっぱいだ. The particle が marks the part that has the state, while いっぱいだ is the predicate showing the full condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If たべて is replaced with たくさんたべたので, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If いっぱいになった is used, the sentence emphasizes the change into a full state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use を with おなか in a structure describing a state; the part that is in the state usually takes が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q22.kobun.vi: I recently started a part-time job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the job that was started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and expresses that the action has started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q22.kobun.why: さいきん states when the event happened. アルバイトを is the object used with はじめる and comes before the predicate はじめました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used, the sentence emphasizes that the action is starting or has started and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q22.kobun.tip: Do not use に after さいきん because this word can directly act as a time adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.vi: There is an empty seat, so would you like to sit down?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the seat as being empty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the suggested action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.ch.2.vi: would you like to sit down?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ませんか creates a polite invitation or suggestion, not just a request for information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and ends with から. Then, すわりませんか uses the polite negative form to give a gentle invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used, the sentence becomes a suggestion to do the action together or a more active proposal by the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is used, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to sit down and no longer has the sense of asking for their opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ませんか as a simple negative question, but in this pattern it is usually a polite invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.vi: Because of the typhoon, many trees fell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the cause or force that makes an event happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: たくさんの modifies 木 and shows the number of trees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that was affected and fell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: たおれた is a past-tense predicate describing a result that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.why: たいふうで places the cause at the beginning of the sentence. たくさんの modifies 木, while 木が is the subject of たおれた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with に, the meaning focuses more on the agent or direction of impact and is less natural than で in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q24.kobun.tip: When the cause is a natural event or situation, Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.vi: Please cut the vegetables very finely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the vegetables as the object of cutting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The く form of the adjective ending in い is used to modify the verb きって.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the cutting action to the request ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: てください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.why: やさいを is the object of きる. こまかく shows the way or degree of cutting, while きってください makes a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence emphasizes making the vegetables small, rather than directly requesting the cutting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q25.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い must change to the く form before a verb when expressing the way or degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.vi: The flowers look as if they are about to bloom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.sk: もうすぐ ＋ N が ＋ V without ます ＋ そうです。
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the whole event and shows that it is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the flowers as the subject of blooming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.ch.2.vi: look as if they are about to bloom
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: そうです follows the verb's connective form to express a prediction based on visible signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.why: もうすぐ comes before the clause to show that the event is about to happen. The verb 咲く changes to the さき form and combines with そうです to express that the flowers look as if they are about to bloom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるそうです is used, it usually means “I hear that they will bloom,” based on information heard rather than an observed sign.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vる予定です is used, the sentence describes a plan or scheduled event, so it does not fit flowers that are naturally about to bloom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうです after a verb with “I hear that,” but Vます without ます ＋ そうです means “look as if it is about to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.vi: Because I cannot handle alcohol, I always drink juice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object toward which weakness or inability is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective よわい connects with ので to give a reason for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the drink being consumed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite-form verb ます is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.why: The object phrase おさけに comes before the adjective よわい to say that the speaker cannot handle alcohol. ので connects the reason with the result: always drinking juice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead, it still means “because,” but its tone is more direct and conversational than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を after おさけ, but the correct pattern is Nに弱い when saying that someone is weak against or cannot handle something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka is the person wearing that red tie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents Mr. Tanaka as the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The word あの modifies the noun that follows and refers to something far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the item being worn in the phrase する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of する connects with いる to create the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: している creates a modifying clause for 人 and identifies who that person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the sentence and confirms that the topic is the person with the feature described earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.why: The phrase あかいネクタイをしている comes before 人 to modify 人. は introduces Tanaka, while です confirms that he belongs to the group of people described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: 着ている usually refers to wearing clothes, while している in this sentence refers to wearing a tie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: かけている is used for items worn or placed, such as glasses, while a tie uses している.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate している mechanically as “doing.” With jewelry or accessories, する means “wear.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.vi: A child fell down the stairs and was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the falling action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting point of the fall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form of おちる connects the falling action with the result of being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: けがをする is a verb phrase in which を marks the noun けが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.why: から identifies where the fall began. The て form connects the two events in order: falling first and being injured afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the stairs are understood as the place where the event happened, without emphasizing the starting point as から does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit を in けがをする, but けがをする is a fixed phrase that must keep を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.vi: A large calendar is hanging on the wall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows where the object is hung and that this state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 大きな directly modifies the noun カレンダー.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the object that is in a hung state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてあります describes a remaining state caused by someone's intentional action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.why: The place かべに comes before the hung object. カレンダーがかけてあります shows that the calendar is currently in a state of already being hung.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Vている describes a state or action in progress, while Vてある emphasizes the result of an intentional action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use で to show where an object exists in this pattern; an existing state usually uses Nにあります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q7.kobun.cn: Vて＋ある（丁寧形：Vてあります）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.vi: Please wait a moment. I will make tea now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ください ends a polite request; おまちください is a polite way to ask the listener to wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 今 shows when the tea-making action will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the thing being prepared or put in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite-form verb ます is the predicate of the clause giving the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: から comes after a clause to give the reason for the preceding request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.why: The request is made first, and then から explains why the listener should wait. 今 comes at the beginning of the clause to clarify when the tea will be made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still gives a reason, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.tip: Do not understand から at the end of the sentence as “from”; after a clause, から usually means “because.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q8.kobun.cn: お＋Vます語幹＋ください; V普通形・Aい・N/Aな＋だ＋から（丁寧体では Vます・です＋から）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.vi: When you have a cold, do not push yourself; rest comfortably.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を goes with the phrase かぜをひく to describe catching a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The plain past form ひいた modifies とき and creates the meaning “when you have caught a cold.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a time, while は makes that situation the topic of the advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the act of pushing yourself in the phrase むりをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Vないで connects an action not to do with the next action that should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: ゆっくり modifies 休んで and shows how to rest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The て form of 休む connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to turn a verb in the て form into a suggestion or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.why: The clause かぜをひいた modifies とき to identify the situation. After that topic, Vないで denies the action of pushing yourself, while Vてください gives the advice to rest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Vないでください directly requests “please do not do it,” while Vないで＋Vてください connects two opposite actions in the same advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Vないと means “if you do not do it...,” so it does not fit the direct advice in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ないで with なくて; ないで connects the actions “do not do A but do B,” while なくて usually connects a cause or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t64-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の＋とき; Vないで＋V; Vて＋ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.vi: I visited my friend because my friend was sick.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person in a sick state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the reason to the action of visiting in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the purpose of going and comes before the verb いきました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: いきました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.why: ともだちが びょうきなので state the reason. おみまいに いきました uses に to show the purpose of visiting, not a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だから, the meaning is still a cause, but the tone is more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with のに, the sentence means “although sick, ...” and no longer expresses a cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q1.kobun.tip: With a noun or an adjective ending in な, use なので to connect the reason in a softer and more polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.vi: Because I am sick, I will take some time off work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に goes with なる to show becoming or falling into a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a past-tense reason with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies the length of the break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks what is being taken a break from, naturally meaning taking time off work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite present-tense verb expresses a decision or plan to take time off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. しばらく comes before 会社をやすみます to limit the length of the break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: から also means because, but it is more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ので as an independent particle, but it must follow a complete clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.vi: Many people are making noise outside. I wonder what happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the place where the noisy action is happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the quantity to the modified noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person carrying out the ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ている indicates an action continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 何か refers to an unidentified event and is the subject of ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: んでしょうか expresses a mild guess together with a question asking for confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.why: で sets the scene. Then the subject 人が combines with ています to describe an action in progress. The next sentence uses 何か as the unidentified subject and ends with んでしょうか to express a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This way asks directly whether something happened and has less of a guessing tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse で and に; for an action taking place at a location, use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ んでしょうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.vi: I told Mr. Tanaka that Mr. Kawamura had called.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the source of the phone call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the event that occurred in the existence clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.ch.2.vi: the fact that there was a call
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns the clause into a noun, while を marks the information being conveyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the person receiving the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The past-tense verb shows that the act of conveying the information was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.why: The source of the call comes first. Then the clause あったこと is turned into a noun as the content of the report. The recipient takes に, while the conveyed content takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If と伝えた is used, the preceding part is treated more like direct quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the content and を for the recipient, but this structure is reversed: the content takes を, and the recipient takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.vi: I showed my foreign friend around Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a noun describing a type of person with the modified noun 友だち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the person being guided or taken around.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the place or object being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form of the verb あんないする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.why: The phrase がいこくじんのともだち identifies the friend, に shows the person being guided, and を marks Tokyo as the place being introduced. The service verb あんないする ends the sentence in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This only says that the person went to Tokyo; it does not show the action of guiding someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may omit the particle に before the person being guided; あんないする usually uses the pattern NにNを案内する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.vi: Close the curtains so that people outside cannot see in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the direction or viewpoint from outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.ch.1.vi: so as not to be seen
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: 見えないように connects a negative purpose with the action that must be taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that needs to be closed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.why: The clause 見えないように states the purpose of closing the curtains and comes before the main action. カーテンを is the object, while しめてください is the polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: ために also shows purpose, but ように is more natural for the goal of avoiding a state such as 見えない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ように after a noun, but in this sentence it connects directly to the negative verb 見えない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q14.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ように
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.vi: I confused the inside and the front of the sheet of paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects かみ with うち and shows a relationship of belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と connects うち with おもて as the two objects that were confused.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb まちがえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb まちがえる with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: しまった expresses something that was accidentally done or happened completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.why: The two nouns うち and おもて are connected by と and together act as the object of まちがえる. The form てしまった adds a feeling of regret because the mistake was made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If the present tense is used, the sentence refers to something that one will accidentally do or often accidentally does, not something that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with Vた, the sentence only states that a mistake was made and reduces the feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget と when connecting two objects affected by the same verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q15.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう（過去: Vてしまった）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.vi: The person next door was making noise until late at night, so I could not sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nが ＋ Timeまで ＋ Vていて ＋ past negative potential form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies 人 and identifies the person as someone next door.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the person who caused the noise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: まで limits the time that the noise continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The form ていて connects the ongoing state of making noise with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The past negative potential form expresses being unable to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ て; negative potential V ＋ ない ＋ かった
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.why: The person causing the noise comes before が, while まで identifies the time when the action ends. The clause さわいでいて states the reason why the speaker could not sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vて, the sentence only connects two actions and does not emphasize an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If the negative passive form is used, the meaning becomes not being allowed to do something or not being affected in another way, not being unable to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate まで as simply “until,” but in this sentence it emphasizes that the action continued until late at night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.vi: In this country, soccer is very popular and there are many teams.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before 国 to clearly indicate the country being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states the topic area, while で indicates where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject described as さかん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な uses the form で to connect the comment about soccer with the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: たくさん modifies the number of soccer teams that exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the subject that exists in clause ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.why: では limits the topic to this country. The two comments are connected by で: soccer is very popular, and many teams exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the meaning changes to contrast or concession instead of connecting two similar pieces of information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If の is added after たくさん, the quantity phrase becomes clearer grammatically: many soccer teams.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse では with で; は states the topic, while で indicates the range or place where something happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.vi: It seems that I am starting to have a fever. My back feels shivery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.sk: Nが ＋ Vてくる ＋ ようだ。 Nが ＋ onomatopoeia ＋ する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the appearance of a phenomenon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The form てきた expresses a change that has begun to appear and is moving toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ようだ is placed at the end of the sentence to give a judgment based on observed signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the body part that has a sensation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The onomatopoeic word ぞくぞく modifies the sensation expressed by する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.why: ねつが出てきた states a symptom that has started to appear, and then ようだ expresses an inference from that symptom. The second sentence uses が to state the body part that has the sensation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vているようだ is used, the focus is on a state that is continuing now, without emphasizing the process of beginning to appear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: そうだ usually describes something that seems about to happen or a direct impression, while ようだ is suitable for an inference based on signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit くる in Vてくる, which removes the meaning of a change moving toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q18.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる; V普通形 ＋ ようだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.vi: The last person to leave the room should carefully check whether it is locked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.sk: Orderに ＋ Nを ＋ V辞書形 ＋ Nは ＋ Nが ＋ Vているか ＋ adverb ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the order of the person who leaves the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the place being left in 出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause 出る comes before 人 to modify it and identify the person who leaves the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the person who leaves the room the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the object checked for being closed or locked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: か creates an indirect question clause that serves as the content of the check.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: しっかり modifies the checking action and asks for it to be done carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.7.n: The form て connects 確認する with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.ch.8.n: ください completes the polite request pattern Vてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.why: The clause へやを出る comes before 人 to identify who must carry out the request. The thing to be checked is placed in a question clause with か, and the sentence ends with Vてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたか is used, the sentence asks directly whether the action has been completed, without emphasizing the state of the door being closed or locked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If どうか is added, the sentence emphasizes whether the checking condition is true or not, but in this sentence か is enough to create an indirect question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the modifying clause after 人, but in Japanese 出る must come before the noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q19.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ N; Vている ＋ か ＋ 確認する; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.vi: Even after graduating from university, I intend to continue studying Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を goes with 卒業する to mark the school or program from which someone graduated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ても connects a concessive condition with an action that still continues in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects にほんご with べんきょう to create the phrase “studying Japanese.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks studying as the object of つづける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: つづける is the main verb of the planned action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: つもりです expresses the speaker’s plan or intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.why: そつぎょうしても creates a concessive clause, meaning that the later action will not change even after graduation. にほんごの べんきょうを form a noun phrase that is the object of つづける, and the dictionary-form verb comes before つもりです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with たら, the sentence only means “after graduating” as a time condition and does not emphasize concession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 続けたいです, the sentence expresses a wish to continue rather than confirming an intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.tip: つもりです usually goes with a dictionary-form verb to express an intended action and is not used directly with a verb in the past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q2.kobun.cn: Vて形・Aくて・Aで・Nで + も
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.vi: Please eat while it is still warm.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: うちに refers only to the period when the warm state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: どうぞ makes the invitation polite and gentle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the food being eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: めしあがる is the honorific form of eat or drink. The form て is used to connect it to ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ください completes a polite invitation or request in the pattern Vてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.why: あたたかいうちに is placed before the invitation to say that the food should be eaten while it is still warm. めしあがってください uses honorific language to invite the listener to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 間に is used, the sentence only states a period of time and places less emphasis on doing something before the state changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べてください replaces it, the request keeps the same meaning but loses its respectful tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 食べてください with everyone, but when inviting someone who deserves respect, めしあがってください should be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.tokens.1.m: while, while there is still a chance
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q20.kobun.cn: Aい + うちに; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.vi: Next time, let us definitely meet in a relaxed way and talk much more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: This part states when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the action of meeting with the suggestion in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks the content of the action 話をする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.ch.7.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.why: Adverbs are placed before the action to add information about time, manner, and degree. The form て connects the action of meeting with the invitation しましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced here, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to perform the action, rather than an invitation to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If ましょうか is used, the sentence sounds more like asking for the listener's opinion or making a gentle request for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use しましょう for every invitation, but this pattern includes the idea that the speaker will also take part in the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q21.tokens.7.m: let us do it, let us do it together
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.vi: People dying is sad, but no one can avoid it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of dying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the verb しぬ into a noun, while は makes the whole event the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects the comment in the previous clause with the contrasting clause that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: だれも combines with a negative predicate to mean that no one does something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the object being avoided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: こと turns さける into a noun, and は presents that avoidance as the topic of ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: できない is a negative predicate showing that avoiding it is impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.why: The clause しぬ is nominalized with の and then made the topic with は for a comment. After が comes the main clause, where さけること is the action being considered in terms of ability and できない negates that ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If は replaces が, dying becomes the subject of an emotion or evaluation, without emphasizing a contrastive topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことができない is used, the sentence still means that it cannot be done, but the structure focuses directly on ability instead of making the action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate のは as a separate word, but here の turns the whole clause into a noun, and then は marks the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Aいことだ/Aなことだ/Nのことだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.vi: I have been busy all this time, but yesterday I finally got a day off after a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: This word modifies the state of being busy and emphasizes that it continued without interruption.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form of the adjective い combines with が to connect two contrasting clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes yesterday the emphasized topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the state or time when getting a day off happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks something obtained or that appeared in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: とれた is the past form, expressing that the speaker requested or obtained a day off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.why: The first clause describes a continuing situation, while が creates a contrast with getting a day off. きのうは identifies the time, and ひさしぶりに adds the circumstances for the result とれた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ひさしぶりに is replaced by たばかり, the sentence emphasizes that the day off was obtained just recently, not after a long period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If ながら is used, two actions or states happen at the same time instead of forming two contrasting clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q23.kobun.tip: に in ひさしぶりに should not be translated as 'at'; the whole phrase expresses doing something after a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.vi: I am the type of person who eats my favorite food last.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.sk: N は + Order に + Aな + N を + V辞書形 + Nだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the order in which the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: すきな modifies the noun もの that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the food being eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies タイプ and creates the meaning of a person who eats their favorite food last.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: だ connects the noun タイプ with the topic わたしは to form a noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.why: わたしは states the person being described. The phrase すきなものをたべる comes before タイプ to modify 'type of person', while さいごに shows the eating order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If てから is used, the sentence says that the favorite food is eaten after another action, not that it is last in the order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If ような is used, the sentence has the softer, more comparative meaning 'the type of person who is like...'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place たべる after タイプ, but a plain-form verb must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.vi: A car and a bicycle had an accident right near the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects いえ with ちかく to indicate the area near the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the accident happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the two objects that collided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject involved in the collision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun for the accident that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the event that happens in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: おきた is the past-tense predicate, showing that the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.why: The location phrase comes first to set the scene. The clause ぶつかる modifies the noun accident, and then おきた serves as the main predicate, showing that the accident happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If にある is used, the sentence describes the existence of something at a location, not an event happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If で起こった is used, the meaning stays almost the same, but the expression uses the verb 起こる more directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the location of an event, but the place where an action or event happens usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.vi: Because the car is almost out of gas, it cannot go far.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.sk: N の N が ＋ あまり ＋ Vないから ＋ N へ ＋ negative potential form of V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is said to remain or not remain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり goes with a negative form to express a small amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.ch.2.vi: because there is not enough left
