default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ないから connects the cause to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: へ shows the direction or destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: いけません is the polite negative form of いける, expressing that someone cannot go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.why: The cause comes first, and the result comes after it. へ marks the direction of travel, while ないから gives the reason why the action cannot be carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので keeps almost the same causal meaning, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after とおく, but a place or destination must use へ or に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.vi: When the test ends, the bell will ring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action of ending in the modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause before とき modifies the time; は emphasizes that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that produces the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.why: おわるときには creates a time phrase at the beginning of the sentence and sets the background for the main event. Since both clauses have their own subjects, が is used in each clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Removing は and using ときに only states the time, without emphasis or contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Using と after おわる emphasizes the natural result that happens as soon as the test ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put は after テスト, but in this sentence テストが is the subject of the verb おわる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の＋とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun まど with noun ガラス to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: This is the subject that is in the broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: われて is the て form, connecting the verb われる with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました expresses that an event has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or something unwanted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.why: The phrase まどのガラス identifies what is broken. われてしまいました combines the broken state with しまう to emphasize that the unwanted event has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing しまいました with います only describes the glass as being broken, without emphasizing the regrettable accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand しまう as meaning only “put away,” but after the て form it can also show completion or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.vi: It is already dark, so let us go home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the state of becoming dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the suggestion in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.why: The reason that it is dark comes first, followed by the suggestion to go home. へ marks the direction, while ましょう expresses an invitation to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Using か instead of ましょう changes the invitation into a gentler question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ましょう as a command, but this pattern usually means doing something together or making an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から；V意向形＋ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.vi: I am a little busy tomorrow, so it is not very convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと makes a refusal or inconvenient statement less direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject being judged as convenient or inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: わるいんです uses an adjective with んです to give an explanation or state a reason gently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.why: Tomorrow is set as the topic, while つごうがわるい is the content of the comment about the schedule. ちょっと and んです make the refusal sound softer and more natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using んですが leaves the statement open, often when asking for a favor or leading into a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Removing ん only reports the situation, without an explanatory tone or a sense of giving the circumstances.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect a noun directly to んです, but the noun needs な to become なんです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋んです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.vi: I am thirsty, so let us have some juice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a thirsty state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the suggested action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the drink being consumed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: のもう is the casual volitional form of のむ, used to invite someone to drink together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.why: The reason, being thirsty, comes first, followed by the invitation to drink juice. を marks the object of のむ, while the volitional form creates a casual inviting tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using のみましょう keeps the meaning of an invitation but is more polite than のもう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で to mark a drink, but the thing being drunk must go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.tokens.7.m: let us drink / let us have a drink
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ＋から；V意向形
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.vi: Walking alone on a dark road at night is very dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates the time when the action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the state or manner in which an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that someone walks on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns a verb into a noun, while は makes the whole action of walking the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: だ concludes that the topic above has a dangerous quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.why: The phrases showing time and state come first to add the circumstances of walking. のは nominalizes the action, making the whole action the topic that is described as dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のは with ことは still makes walking the topic, but the tone is more general and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t65-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may forget that のは must come after the verb's plain form to nominalize the whole action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.vi: I wrapped the gift for my friend in beautiful paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows possession or the relationship between the friend and the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the item being wrapped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な modifies the noun かみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the tool or material used for wrapping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: つつんだ is the predicate in the past tense, showing that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.why: The object プレゼントを comes before the means かみで, followed by the main verb つつんだ. きれいな comes before かみ to describe the type of paper used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used after プレゼント, it may indicate the receiver or the direction of the action, not the wrapping material.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If と is used, the sentence will more likely mean wrapping together with paper or another object, not wrapping with paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse で with に in this sentence; で indicates the material or means, while に does not mean “with”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.vi: I got the front and back of the paper mixed up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 紙 with 裏, creating a relationship of possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と connects the two sides being compared or confused.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the front side as an object of 間違える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the mistaken action with しまった to create a pattern meaning that someone did something by mistake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: しまった describes an action that happened unintentionally or caused the speaker regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう（ past: しまった）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.why: の identifies the two sides as belonging to the paper, と connects the back and front sides, and を marks the whole group as the object of 間違える. てしまった adds the feeling of having done something by mistake or regretting it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: The present form describes something that will be completed or may be done by mistake, while まちがえてしまった clearly shows that the mistake has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means to confuse, but it emphasizes mistaking two objects for each other.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out と between the two objects, but when saying that A and B were confused, Japanese usually connects them with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.vi: Next time, let’s definitely meet in a relaxed way and talk much more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite form て links an invitation to meet with an invitation to talk お会いして.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks 話 as the content of the conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.why: Adverbs come before verbs to show time, manner, and degree. て connects two invitations, while ましょう comes at the end to turn the whole sentence into a suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vませんか, the invitation sounds softer and more like asking for the listener’s opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたいです is used, the sentence only expresses the speaker’s wish and does not directly invite the listener to join.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put もっと after 話を, but an adverb of degree usually comes before the verb phrase it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.vi: A traffic accident involving a car and a bicycle happened very close to the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 家 with 近く, creating a phrase for the area near the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle と connects the two vehicles involved in the collision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the bicycle as the second part of the subject involved in the collision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before 交通事故 to modify the noun for the accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle が marks the traffic accident as the event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb 起きる in the past tense is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.why: The phrase ぶつかるこうつうじこ identifies the type of accident by placing a modifying clause before the noun. で indicates the place, と connects the two vehicles, and が marks the event involving おきた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: The use of て clearly separates two events in sequence: the vehicles collide, and then the accident happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may put the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always puts ぶつかる before こうつうじこ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q13.kobun.vi: Please do not bully my younger sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the younger sister as the object of the bullying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The form ないで connects with ください to create a polite request meaning “please do not do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ください comes at the end of the Vないでください pattern and makes the sentence a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q13.kobun.why: The object of the action goes with を, then the verb in the negative form ないで connects directly to ください. The whole pattern asks the listener not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence sounds more like a rule or a strong prohibition than a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use いじめませんでください, but the correct pattern is the ない form with い removed, followed by でください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.vi: The rain has stopped, so an umbrella is not needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: もう comes before the predicate to show that the state has already occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the rain as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason clause to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the umbrella the topic for judging whether it is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: いりません is the polite negative form of いる, meaning “not needed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.why: The clause やんでいるから gives the reason, while かさはいりません gives the result. は marks the topic in both 雨 and かさ, helping the sentence compare the state of the rain with the need for an umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still expresses a reason, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that から must come after a complete clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.vi: This machine is easy to use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.sk: この + N は + Aなに + potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify it and indicate a specific thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the machine as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in な changes to かんたんに to modify the verb つかえます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: つかえます is the potential form, expressing the ability to use the machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.why: このきかいは is the topic phrase, while かんたんに describes how the action is performed. The potential form つかえます shows that the user can use the machine, not merely that the user uses it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: かんたんな comes before a noun, so if it were used here, it would modify a noun rather than directly modifying a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: やさしく can also mean “easily,” but it focuses more on doing something gently or without difficulty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use the basic form かんたんな before a verb; the adjective ending in な must change to かんたんに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.vi: Before the test, I reviewed the parts I had learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テスト with まえ, forming a noun phrase that indicates a time related to the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the review was done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: ならった modifies ところ, referring to the parts that were learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the learned parts as the object of the review.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する, expressing a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.why: The phrase テストのまえに identifies the time, and ならったところを is the object of ふくしゅうしました. The た form of a verb comes before a noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: When ならったばかり is used, it emphasizes that the learning has just been completed, not simply that the part was learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: あとで means after doing something, so it reverses the time relationship with まえに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q16.kobun.tip: A clause that modifies a noun must come before the noun, not after it as is common in English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.vi: I send an email using a computer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the tool or means used to perform the action of sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the email as the object being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: おくります is the main predicate and expresses the action of sending an email.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.why: パソコンで states the means, メールを states the affected object, and おくります ends the sentence with the main action. Here, the particle で does not indicate a place; it indicates a tool.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If パソコンに is used, に usually indicates a destination or a place where something exists, and does not clearly express the tool used for sending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: パソコンから emphasizes the source of the email or the place it comes from rather than the tool.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に instead of で when talking about means; a tool used to perform an action usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.vi: I will translate the Vietnamese book into Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ベトナム語 with 本, showing that the book is written in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the book as the object of the translation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the target language, meaning the language into which the content is changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ほんやくします is the main predicate and expresses the action of translating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.why: ベトナム語の本 is the noun phrase naming the object, 本を marks the thing being translated, and にほんごに indicates the target language. This order clearly shows the transfer of content from the source language to the target language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: 日本語で emphasizes the language used to perform or present the action, not the target language of the translation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: ベトナム語から日本語へ highlights the direction of transfer from Vietnamese to Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q18.kobun.tip: With the verb “translate,” the target language usually goes with に; do not confuse に with で, which indicates a means.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.vi: I competed with my younger sister, but unfortunately lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person taking part with someone or the opponent in a competition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: して is the て form of する, connecting the competition with the next event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: まけて connects the loss with しまいました in a pattern describing a completed or regrettable event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: しまいました follows the て form to express a completed action, often with a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.why: いもうとと identifies the opponent, きょうそうして connects the competition with the result. まけてしまいました combines the て form with しまう to emphasize that the loss happened and that the speaker did not want it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: ながら describes two actions happening at the same time, so it is not suitable for connecting the competition with the result of losing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: てみる means to try doing something, so replacing it here would mean trying to lose or trying to perform the action, which would completely change the sentence's meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before しまう in this pattern; the verb must change to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.vi: I put the bookshelf in the corner of the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects へや with the noun that indicates a location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where an object is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 置く in the past form expresses a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.why: The location phrase comes before the object and verb to state where the action takes place. The particle に marks the place where something is put, while を marks the object being placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, it usually indicates a place where an activity happens, and is less natural than に for placing something in a location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use で instead of に; for the place where an object is put or the destination of an object, use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.vi: I will take the child to the old man's house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person being taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun おじいさん with the following noun and indicates possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action of taking someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb つれていく expresses taking a person or animal along to another place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.why: The person being taken comes before を, and the destination comes before に. The phrases おじいさんの and いえ form a compound noun meaning the old man's house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means taking someone toward the speaker or to a place currently being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse に, which indicates a destination, with で, which indicates the place where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q21.kobun.vi: My younger sister sings very well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the younger sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the area in which the younger sister is skilled at singing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: うまい is an adjective indicating good ability; です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q21.kobun.why: With ability adjectives such as うまい, the area of skill comes before が. The person being evaluated as the topic comes before は, while the degree word とても modifies the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this structure is used, the focus shifts to singing skillfully as an action, not to general singing ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を after うた, but this ability-evaluation pattern requires が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.vi: My younger brother fell down the stairs and was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the younger brother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から indicates the starting point or the place from which someone fell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of falling with the injury that happened afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object in the phrase けがをする, which means to be injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of します and completes the phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.why: The starting point is marked by から. Then, the action of falling uses the て form to connect with the result. The phrase けがをする is a fixed expression, so けが goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the cause-and-effect relationship more: because he fell, he was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q22.kobun.tip: English learners may translate を in けがをする as “make an injury,” but the whole phrase means “be injured.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.vi: Thank you for always treating me kindly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て of しんせつにする connects the action of treating someone kindly with くださる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてくださる shows that another person does something helpful or kind for the speaker; くださって connects it to words of thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: This is a sentence-final expression used to show gratitude politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.why: An action done by another person for the speaker uses Vてくださる. The form て of くださる connects the clause stating what the speaker received with the expression of thanks at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: When てもらって is used, the speaker emphasizes that they received help or a favor from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.tip: English-speaking Vietnamese learners may easily use してあげる, but くださる must be viewed from the receiver’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q23.kobun.cn: Vて + くださる; くださって、 + 感謝表現
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.vi: My older brother works for an American trading company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the older brother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects アメリカ with the following noun and shows a relationship or origin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun ぼうえき modifies かいしゃ through the particle の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows the place or organization where a person works.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the verb つとめる with います to create an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: います after a verb in the て form shows an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.why: The two Nの phrases successively modify かいしゃ, forming “an American trading company.” The workplace takes に, while Vています shows the state of working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: When で働く is used, the focus is on the action of working taking place at the company; 勤める emphasizes belonging to or working for that organization.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で with 勤める out of habit, but the workplace of 勤める usually takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.vi: Running up the escalator is dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object or route connected with the action of running up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the way of running with the action of going up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The Vると pattern states a condition or a result that naturally follows the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: あぶない is the predicate, while よ emphasizes the warning to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.cn: Vて + V; Vる + と + result
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.why: はしって adds the manner to のぼる. The Vると pattern connects the action with a natural or certain result, which suits a warning about danger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with たら, the sentence becomes a more specific hypothetical condition and does not stress an inevitable result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression is more formal and neutral, while よ creates a direct reminder to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand と as “and,” but here と connects a condition with a natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.vi: My friend did not come even when the agreed time arrived, so I became impatient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who made the appointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause before じかん modifies the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the point in time that was reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: なっても connects a condition with a contrasting idea: even when that time had arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the cause with the result of feeling impatient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: した is the past form of する in a word describing an emotional state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.why: The clause やくそくしたじかん modifies じかん, forming the phrase “the agreed time.” ても states a situation that goes against expectations, while ので connects the cause with the emotion at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is used, the expression emphasizes dissatisfaction or a result contrary to expectations rather than stating a cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used, the reason is more direct and conversational than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.tip: Do not translate ので simply as “because” in every place; in this sentence, it connects the whole cause clause with the emotional result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.vi: The clothes became wet from the rain and still have not dried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the cause that made the clothes wet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause before ふく modifies the clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject in the state of not being dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: なかなか combines with a negative form to express that something is difficult to happen or takes a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 乾く in the negative form shows that the clothes do not dry by themselves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.why: The clause ぬれた comes before ふく to identify which clothes. なかなか combines with the negative form and emphasizes that the clothes take a long time to dry but are still not dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 乾かす is used, it means making something else dry, so a person or another agent is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q4.kobun.tip: Distinguish 乾く, meaning “dry by itself,” from 乾かす, meaning “make something dry”; do not mix up these two verbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.vi: During the vacation, I ate too many snacks and gained weight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 休み with あいだ, forming a phrase for the vacation period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the period during which the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food that was eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies the amount of snacks eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the action of eating with the result that happened afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects the state of gaining weight with しまった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: てしまった expresses a completed result, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended outcome.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.why: あいだに sets the time frame for all the following actions. The two verbs in the て form connect a sequence of actions and results, while しまった shows that the weight gain happened completely and carries a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ておく is used, it means doing something beforehand as preparation, without a feeling of accidentally doing it or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べすぎて太った is used, it emphasizes that eating too much directly caused the weight gain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q5.kobun.tip: てしまう does not only mean “finish”; in a sentence about an unwanted event, it often suggests regret or accidentally doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.vi: When I got lost, a kind person took me to the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: ていたら connects an ongoing situation with an unexpected event that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な with 人 to modify the person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who performs the action of taking someone somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: まで shows the final destination of taking someone somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects 連れて行く with くれる to create a structure showing that help was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: くれた shows that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.why: ていたら provides the background situation, after which the new subject appears with が. まで shows the destination, while てくれた expresses that another person actively did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If てもらった is used, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If てあげる is used, the speaker is the one doing something helpful for someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.tip: With てくれる, identify the performer as someone else, while the person receiving the benefit is usually the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q6.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった ＋ ら; Vて ＋ くれる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.vi: On the way to my friend’s house, I bought a cake as a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 友だち with いえ to show whose house it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 行く in the dictionary form comes before とちゅう to modify the journey being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the time or situation in which the cake was bought during the journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: に shows the purpose of buying the cake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the thing that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: 買う is in the past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.why: 行くとちゅうで creates the phrase “on the way to,” in which 行く modifies 途中. おみやげに states the purpose of buying it, while ケーキを is the direct object bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行きながら is used, it emphasizes two actions happening at the same time, rather than a point during the journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 行っている間に is used, it means “while going,” which is broader and does not necessarily mean halfway along the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.tip: 途中で usually follows a verb in the dictionary form or the noun の. It does not connect directly to a past-tense verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ 途中で
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.vi: I showed the guest to the meeting room and then brought out tea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person being shown the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates where the guest is taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects showing the way with the following action of serving tea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks what is brought out or served.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 出す is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.why: The sentence puts the two actions in order: first showing the guest the way, then serving tea. を marks the objects of the verbs, while に indicates the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence lists typical actions instead of emphasizing their order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に for the object of あんないする, but the person being shown the way must be used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.vi: The package I sent yesterday has already arrived at the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause おくった comes before 荷物 and modifies the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the package as the subject that arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に indicates where the package arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb とどく is intransitive, so the thing that arrives is the subject with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.why: The clause きのうおくった comes before 荷物 to identify which package. Then, 荷物が is the subject of とどいた, while に states the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the package sent yesterday becomes the topic, with a clearer contrast or comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t66-q9.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with とどく, but とどく is an intransitive verb, so the place uses に and the arriving thing uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.vi: Try pronouncing the new English words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun えいご with the noun that follows, showing the relationship “belonging to English.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the action はつおんする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action はつおんする with the invitation or suggestion at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: みましょう is the polite form used to invite or suggest doing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.why: The phrase えいごの 新しい ことば modifies the object ことばを. Then はつおんして connects the pronunciation action with the suggestion みましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to pronounce the words, not an invitation to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q1.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand みましょう as “to see,” but in this structure it means “let’s try doing it together.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.vi: I viewed the picture drawn by the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の identifies the person who performed the writing or drawing action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause comes before え to modify the picture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the picture as the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: はいけんしました is the main predicate and uses a humble expression for viewing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.why: The clause 先生のかいた comes before え to identify which picture. The whole phrase 先生のかいたえを is the object of the verb for viewing at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of の, the meaning is similar, but the subject of the modifying clause is stated more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If かいた is changed to the dictionary form, it means a picture the teacher usually draws or will draw, instead of one already drawn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q10.kobun.tip: Do not separate かいた as the main predicate; here, it modifies the noun え immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.vi: Since we will be late for school, please get ready quickly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object or place connected with being late in the phrase ちこくする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: はやく modifies the action of getting ready and shows how it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of したくする connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.why: The clause ちこくするから gives the reason first, and the request comes in the following clause. はやく comes before したくして to modify the speed of getting ready.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective, while から sounds more direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.tip: The pattern Vてください requires the verb to be in the て form; do not use the dictionary form directly before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ から；Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.vi: The student’s parents came to meet the principal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 学生 with 両親, showing that the parents belong to that student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the parents as the people who came to meet someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the principal as the person being visited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects たずねる with くる, showing arrival while the action of visiting is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: きました indicates movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.why: 学生のりょうしん creates a noun phrase as the subject, while こうちょうを is the object of the action of visiting. たずねてきました combines the action of visiting with movement toward the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to たずねていきました, it emphasizes going to visit in a direction away from the speaker or reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q12.kobun.tip: In Vてくる, くる does not only mean “come” by itself; it adds movement toward the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.vi: The bicycle in front of the gate is in the way, so please move it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase の connects "もん" with the following noun showing location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the location where the bicycle is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun "じてんしゃ".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes the bicycle the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.4.vi: because it is in the way
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: から connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects the verb with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: ください follows the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.why: The clause "もんの 前に ある" comes before and modifies "じてんしゃ". After giving the reason with から, the sentence uses the form て＋ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still states the cause, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern changes the request into a more polite and gentle favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.tip: English learners may forget that the verb before ください must be in the て form, not the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.tokens.0.m: of the gate; of the door
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋です・N＋です ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.vi: Please do not tell everyone yet that Ms. Sabine will return to her country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who performs the action of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle へ shows the direction of the return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies こと, turning the whole action of returning into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: こと nominalizes the preceding clause, while は makes that matter the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: まだ shows that the action of telling should not happen yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に shows the people who receive the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: The form ないで connects with ください to ask someone not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: ください makes the negative request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.why: The clause containing が and へ is nominalized with こと. Then は turns the whole matter into the topic. The recipient of the information goes with に, while ないでください expresses a request not to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes trying to prevent the action from happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression is softer because it changes the request into a question-like favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use に to mark the person returning; に in this sentence marks the recipient of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q14.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Vない形 ＋ こと; Vないで ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.vi: This glass cup is difficult to break, so it can be used safely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the cup being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the material with the noun "コップ".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the cup the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.ch.3.vi: because it is difficult to break
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: にくい follows the stem of the ます form to show that an action is difficult, while ので connects the cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb modifying the following verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The potential form of the verb expresses that the cup can be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.why: ガラスの modifies コップ to state the material. The feature of being difficult to break is connected to the result by ので, while あんぜんに modifies the action of being usable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with われやすい, the meaning changes to “easy to break.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: から also shows a cause, but it is usually more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.tip: にくい must connect with the stem of the ます form, not directly with the dictionary-form verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q15.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ にくい; V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので; Aな ＋ に
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.vi: A new rule was decided at the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows where the decision about the rule took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective comes before a noun and modifies 規則.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the object affected by the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The past passive form shows that the rule was decided by someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.why: 会社で shows the context where the event occurred, while 規則が is the grammatical subject affected by the action. The passive is used to focus on the rule that was decided rather than on the person who decided it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: The active form means that someone decided it and focuses on the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means that something had already been arranged or decided beforehand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the affected object usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q16.kobun.cn: Vる → Vられる; Vない → Vられない; Vた → Vられた; Vている → Vられている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.vi: Because there is no gasoline, the motorbike cannot run.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks what has run out and creates the cause for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: なくて is the て form of ない, connecting the state of lacking or running out with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that cannot operate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite negative verb form says that the motorbike does not operate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.cn: Vない → Vなくて; Aい → Aくて; Aな・N ＋ で ＋ clause
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.why: The first clause gives the cause and is connected by なくて to the result in the following clause. The two clauses have different subjects, so each subject is marked with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: ないので also shows a cause, but it makes the reason-linking pattern clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern does not only show a cause; it expresses the meaning “must do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q17.kobun.tip: なくて in this sentence is the cause-linking form of ない, not the meaning of obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a field or area with the noun "せいじ".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb with います to create the progressive pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: います is an auxiliary verb showing that an action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.why: The phrase アジアの せいじ identifies the field of study, while を marks the object of けんきゅうする. The form ている shows that the study is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: This form only says that someone will study or usually studies; it does not emphasize an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: The past form shows that the study was completed or took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.tip: Do not omit して when using ている with the verb する; you must say けんきゅうしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q18.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる; Vて ＋ いない; Vて ＋ いました; Vて ＋ いませんでした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.vi: I guided the guest to the department manager's room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person being guided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the noun 部長 to the following noun to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the destination of the action 案内する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 案内しました is the polite past form of the verb 案内する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.why: The object goes with を, the destination goes with に, and の connects two nouns to form “the department manager's room.” The verb comes at the end of the sentence and uses the polite past form to show that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, the sentence still shows direction, but it emphasizes direction rather than the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を incorrectly for a destination; a place that someone is guided to must go with に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.vi: I will ask the teacher about the parts I do not understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.sk: V普通形 ＋ N を ＋ Person に ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A clause in the plain form comes before ところ to describe the part or place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content that the speaker wants to ask about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the person who receives the question, namely the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: しつもんします is the main predicate and expresses the action of asking politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.why: わからない comes directly before ところ to identify it as the part that is not understood. ところを is the affected content, while 先生に is the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If について is used, the sentence focuses more on the topic being asked about than on the specific part that is not understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use で for the person being asked; with a verb of asking, the receiver usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being grown or cared for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The form ている expresses an ongoing action or a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q20.kobun.why: A noun showing the object of an action goes with を. The verb そだてる changes to て形 and then combines with いる to express the ongoing action of growing flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with そだてました, the sentence only says that the flowers were grown or raised, without emphasizing that the action is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q20.kobun.tip: Do not put the dictionary form directly before います; change the verb to て形 first, and then connect it to います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.vi: This textbook is suitable for review.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to clearly identify the object being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes this textbook the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern V辞書形＋のに changes an action into a purpose or a use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: てきとうです is the adjective predicate な, which evaluates the textbook's suitability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.why: のに connects the review action with the purpose “for review.” The adjective な comes at the end of the sentence to evaluate the textbook as suitable for that purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with ために, the sentence sounds more formal and emphasizes the purpose more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: When のに follows a complete clause such as 雨なのに, it means “although,” which is different from のに in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand every use of のに as “although”; after a verb in the dictionary form, のに here means “in order to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q21.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ のに ＋ Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.vi: My Japanese is still not very good, so please do not praise me too much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects わたし with 日本語 to show that it is my Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes my Japanese ability the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies the predicate to show that the state has not reached the desired level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.ch.3.vi: because it is not very good
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the reason clause to the request that follows; うまくない is the negative form of うまい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: そんなに modifies the action of praising to show an excessively high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: ないでください creates a polite request meaning “please do not do something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.why: The clause before から gives the reason, while the request comes at the end of the sentence. は states the topic, Japanese ability, and そんなに limits the degree of praising.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason is presented more softly and objectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If ほめすぎないでください is used, the direct meaning is “please do not praise me excessively,” emphasizing praise that goes beyond the limit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that ないでください must follow the negative form ない, rather than connecting directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q22.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ でください; V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.vi: The cake I baked yesterday has all been eaten, so none is left.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう shows the time when the action in the modifying clause occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: A clause in the past form comes before ケーキ to describe the cake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the cake baked yesterday the topic of the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ぜんぶ modifies 食べて to show the whole cake that was eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the action of eating with the result or state that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: もう shows that the state of no longer having something occurred before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: のこっていません describes the present state in which nothing remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.why: The clause きのう やいた comes before ケーキ to identify which cake is meant. After the topic, ぜんぶ and 食べて state the completed action, and then のこっていません states the present result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 食べ終わりました, the sentence emphasizes that the eating has ended rather than the result that no cake remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If まだのこっています is used, the meaning changes to “there is still cake left.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate ている simply as “be doing”; with のこっている, it usually describes a remaining state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q23.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ N; Vて ＋ Vている; Vている → Vていない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q24.kobun.vi: I put the bedding away in the built-in closet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being put away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the place where the bedding is put away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: かたづけました is the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q24.kobun.why: The affected object goes with を, while the place where it is put goes with に. The verb comes at the end of the sentence and uses the polite past form to show that the action is finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, で usually only indicates where an action takes place, not where an object is moved to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use で for every location, but the destination of an action such as putting or placing something uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.vi: Starting next week, I will work part-time at a bookstore.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.sk: N time から ＋ N place で ＋ Nを ＋ します
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the starting point of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the activity that します performs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.why: The starting point comes first, followed by the place where the action occurs, and then the object of します. The particle で identifies the place where the action is performed, while を marks the part-time work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, it is not suitable for showing the place where the work is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for every location, but the place where an action occurs usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q3.kobun.vi: Please throw that ball this way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the ball as the object being thrown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the direction or destination of the ball.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: なげてください consists of the て form of the verb and ください, creating a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q3.kobun.why: その modifies ボール, を marks the affected object, and に identifies the throwing direction. Vてください is placed at the end to turn the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with へ, the meaning of direction stays the same, but the direction is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q3.kobun.tip: に in this sentence indicates the throwing direction, not the person receiving the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.vi: The supermarket closes too early, so it is very inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects スーパー with 時間, showing that the time being discussed is the supermarket's closing time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: しまる in the dictionary form comes before 時間 to modify the closing time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the closing time as the subject being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: Aい removes い and then connects with すぎる; the form て connects the cause to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends the sentence politely and gives an evaluation of that situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.why: しまる modifies 時間, forming “closing time.” はやすぎて gives the reason, while ふべんです gives the speaker's result and evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If はやいので is used, the sentence only says “because it is early,” without emphasizing that it is too early as すぎる does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: はやくて only connects the adjective to the following clause and does not express a level beyond what is suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, remove い before すぎる: はやい → はやすぎる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.tokens.5.n: adjective ending in い + auxiliary verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q4.kobun.cn: Vます語幹・Aい語幹・Aな語幹・N + すぎる; すぎる → すぎて
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.vi: Do not decide matters about the future by yourself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しょうらい with こと, creating a phrase for a matter or thing about the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes “matters about the future” the topic of the advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates how the action is performed, meaning deciding by yourself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: Vないでください is used to make a polite request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.why: ことは places the topic first, and then 一人で states the way of acting that is discouraged. The form ないでください expresses a request not to perform the deciding action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence becomes softer advice, less direct than a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q5.kobun.tip: で in 一人で means “by means of or in a state,” not a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.vi: The bell is ringing very loudly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the state or manner in which the bell is ringing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks ベル as the subject producing the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb なって with います to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: います combines with the て form to describe an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; polite form: Vて + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.why: 大きいおとで describes how the bell rings, ベルが is the subject, and なって います describes the bell continuing to ring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてある is used, the sentence describes a state intentionally created by someone, so it does not fit a bell ringing by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q6.kobun.tip: で here adds manner or state, not a place particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.vi: I will show this picture only to you in a special way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who receives the benefit of the showing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb and modifies 見せる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects 見せる with あげる to express doing something for another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.ch.5.vi: I will do it for you
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: あげましょう shows that the speaker actively does something beneficial for the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.why: The recipient of the action comes before に, while the object being shown comes before を. 見せてあげる expresses the speaker doing something for the listener, so あげましょう is placed at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 見せてくれます, the nuance is that another person shows something to the speaker, with the benefit directed toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見せてもらいます is used, it emphasizes that the speaker receives help or is shown something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q7.kobun.tip: English learners often confuse あげる and くれる because they do not correctly identify who performs the action and who receives the benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.vi: The machine is not working well, so I will try checking it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun for machine with the noun ぐあい, creating the phrase “the machine's condition.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject as being in a bad condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the following action and has a mild explanatory nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of 見る connects with みる in the pattern for trying to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: みます is an auxiliary verb that completes the meaning “try checking.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.why: The phrase きかいのぐあいがよくない gives the condition as the reason, and then ので connects it to the action. 見てみる expresses trying to check it to find out the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見てみます is replaced with 見ておきます, it means checking in advance or checking to prepare for what comes next, not trying to check.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.tip: Do not understand てみる as “see”; this pattern means trying to perform the action before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な・N + な + ので; Vて + みる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.vi: I bought a birthday present for my younger sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the recipient of the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun for birthday with プレゼント, creating the meaning “birthday present.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 買いました is the polite past form of 買う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.why: The recipient comes before に, the gift's description is connected with の, and the gift is the object marked by を. The past-tense verb comes at the end to complete the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing に with へ sounds unnatural when indicating the recipient of a gift because へ mainly indicates a direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t67-q9.kobun.tip: English learners often use を after the recipient, but in this structure the recipient must be used with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.vi: If there is a typhoon, tomorrow's concert will be canceled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun たいふう with とき to create a phrase expressing a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the situation of a typhoon occurring as the topic of the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects あした with コンサート and modifies the concert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object being canceled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.why: The conditional situation is placed at the beginning of the sentence and expressed with ときは. Then, あしたの modifies コンサート, and を connects the object to the verb ちゅうしします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If なら is used, the sentence has a hypothetical meaning based on information or a situation mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the sentence expresses a cause-and-effect relationship, meaning that the concert is canceled because there is a typhoon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ときは with ので; ときは only indicates a time or condition and does not directly mean because.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.vi: I informed the department manager that I would be absent from work because I had a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause of being absent from work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を combines with 休む to indicate the place or work from which the speaker is absent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before こと to turn the action of being absent into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the whole clause 会社を休む into a noun, and を marks the content that was reported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the person receiving the communication.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: しました is the polite past form of れんらくする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.why: 会社を休む is placed before こと to turn the action of being absent into information that can be reported. で states the reason, に states the recipient of the information, and を marks the content communicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If のを伝える is used, the sentence focuses on communicating the content and has a clearer reporting meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 知らせる, it means to inform someone, and usually has more of a meaning of providing information than communicating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit こと and connect the clause directly to を; in this sentence, こと is necessary to turn the whole action of being absent into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.vi: I asked a hotel employee to change my room to a larger one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ホテル with 人, creating the phrase hotel employee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person asked to change the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the action of asking with the result of having the room changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ひろい comes before へや to describe the room's feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the destination or new state after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてもらいました expresses that the speaker receives help from someone else to change the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.why: ホテルの人にたのんで states the person asked and the action of asking first. ひろいへやに indicates the desired result, while かえてもらいました shows that the speaker received this help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If かえてくれました is used, the focus is on the employee changing the room to help the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If かえてあげました is used, the speaker would be understood as the person who changes the room for someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often mistake に in へやに for a place; here, に indicates the state or destination after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.vi: This coffee is black and very bitter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks coffee as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks color as the feature being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to the くて form to connect with the following adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the adjective にがいです and indicates a very high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: にがいです is the main predicate and describes the taste of the coffee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.why: この modifies コーヒー, and then は makes coffee the topic. The two features are connected with the くて form, while とても comes before the adjective to indicate degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If し is used, the sentence has more of a meaning of listing reasons or several features, rather than simply connecting two adjectives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use に to connect two い adjectives; the first adjective must be changed to the くて form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.vi: Please do not collect trash here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where the action must not be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks trash as the object of the action of collecting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern ないでください expresses a request or reminder not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.why: ここに identifies the place, ごみを is the object, and the verb in the ないでください form comes at the end to create a polite negative request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a stronger rule or prohibition: do not collect trash here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ないでください with なくてください; the correct form is the ない form, removing い and then adding でください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q13.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.vi: The house burned down in a fire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the cause that made the house burn down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the house as the object affected by the burning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the verb やける with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: しまいました expresses that an event has been completed and often carries a regretful or unintended meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.why: かじで states the cause, いえが is the subject of the event, and then やけてしまいました shows that the burning was fully completed and regrettable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes a state or event that was in progress in the past, without emphasizing a regrettable result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q14.kobun.tip: しまいました does not only mean had; in this sentence, it also shows an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.vi: I tried very hard to memorize the law, but then I forgot it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the law as the content being memorized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase modifies おぼえました and indicates the manner and degree of effort.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: the speaker tried to memorize it, but the later result was the opposite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects わすれる with しまいました to create a pattern expressing something that happened accidentally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました completes the Vてしまう pattern and adds regret because the speaker forgot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.why: ほうりつを is the object of memorizing, and いっしょうけんめいに indicates the degree of effort. が creates a contrast between having memorized it and then forgetting; Vてしまう emphasizes the regrettable event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence says that something was done beforehand or prepared in advance, without expressing regret about forgetting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q15.kobun.tip: When you want to say accidentally lose or forget something, use Vてしまう instead of only using the ordinary past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.vi: I am studying grammar at university.
