default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where the study takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects ぶんぽう with けんきゅう and shows the content being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the study as the object of しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects する with います to form the progressive tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vています and expresses an activity in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.why: 大学で shows the place, and ぶんぽうの shows the content of けんきゅう. The phrase けんきゅうをしています uses を for the object and ている to express an ongoing activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This is the progressive form; if Vました is used, it only says that the study happened and does not stress the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q16.kobun.tip: The particle で is used for the place where an action happens, while に is usually used for a place where something exists or for a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.vi: After drinking alcohol, you must not drive a car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks alcohol as what is being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: のんだら uses the past form plus ら to state a condition or the time after drinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the car as the vehicle being driven.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Vては places the action of driving within the scope of the prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: いけません completes the pattern Vてはいけません and expresses prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.why: のんだら sets the condition or time first, while じどうしゃをうんてんしてはいけません is the main clause stating the prohibition. を mark, respectively, the drink and the vehicle affected by the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence only emphasizes the sequence “after drinking” and does not have the clear conditional meaning of たら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is used instead, the sentence becomes advice not to drive, which is weaker than the prohibition てはいけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically understand を after じどうしゃ as “drive a car”; in Japanese, うんてんする takes the vehicle with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q17.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった ＋ ら; Vて ＋ はいけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.vi: I promised my friend that I would go to the swimming pool tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who performs the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates direction or a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content that is said or promised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: いう modifies 約束 and creates the phrase という約束.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the object of しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: しました is the polite past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.why: The phrase 行くという約束 states the content of the promise, while を marks the whole promise as the object of する. へ shows the direction to the swimming pool, while と shows the person going together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence emphasizes committing to the action of going and sounds more formal and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use と to indicate a destination; a destination must be used with へ or に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.vi: Look up words you do not know in a dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause before ことば modifies this word.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the unknown words the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the tool or means used for looking something up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: て-form connects the verb with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after the て-form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.why: わからないことば is a noun phrase in which the preceding clause modifies ことば. で indicates the means, while Vてください at the end turns the act of looking something up into a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence means that one must look it up, rather than giving a softer request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate the tool; with a dictionary, the natural particle is で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.vi: Mr. Furuta is taking care of his younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い comes before おとうと to modify “younger brother.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects おとうと with せわ and indicates the person being cared for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun combined with する in the phrase せわをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects して with います to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the pattern しています and indicates an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and the phrase 小さいおとうと is made by placing the adjective before the noun. せわをする is a noun phrase plus する, and ている expresses ongoing care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If しています is replaced with します, the sentence describes a habit or a general action, without emphasizing that it is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If した is used, the caring action is understood as completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ています as the future, but in this sentence it expresses an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.vi: Every souvenir sold at that shop is unusual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies the noun 店 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the selling happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: うっている creates a clause that modifies おみやげ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: いる completes the form ている and expresses the state of being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: は states that the souvenirs are sold at that shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: どれも covers all the souvenirs being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: めずらしい is the い adjective used as the predicate; です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.why: The clause うっている comes before おみやげ to identify the souvenirs as the ones being sold. どれも combines with the affirmative predicate to say that all the items have this feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence changes to the passive voice and emphasizes that the souvenirs are sold rather than the shop being in the state of selling them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q20.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a modifying clause comes before the noun, not after it as in the familiar Vietnamese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.vi: Do not stop practicing singing until you become a little better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the state reached after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: まで indicates the limit; the preceding clause states the condition for reaching that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects うた with れんしゅう to create the phrase “singing practice.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the practice activity as the object of やめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: ないで connects with ください to request that an action not be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.ch.7.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.why: なるまで sets the time reference for the action やめないでください in the main clause. The state after a change uses じょうずに, while を marks practice as something that must not stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If までに is used, the sentence emphasizes reaching a state before a deadline, not continuing until that exact point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use じょうずな with なる; when expressing becoming good at something, use じょうずになる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.vi: I have not recovered from my cold yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person in the described state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ shows that recovery from the illness is not complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the state なおっていません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: なおっていません describes a state in which recovery is not complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.why: は makes the speaker the topic, while が marks the illness as still not cured. まだ combines with the negative form to emphasize that this has still not been completed up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to having already recovered from the illness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q22.kobun.tip: Do not translate まだ alone as “still”; with Vていません, it usually means “still not yet”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.vi: I am carefully using the pen my father gave me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the giving action in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 父がくれた comes before ペン to modify the pen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the pen as the object being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に changes だいじ into an adverb showing how something is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: The て-form connects to います to show an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the Vています pattern and keeps a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.why: 父がくれた is a modifying clause for ペン, so it is placed before the noun ペン. だいじに shows how the pen is used, while つかっています describes an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes taking care of or valuing the pen, not necessarily using it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q23.kobun.tip: Do not put the modifying clause after the noun; 父がくれた must come before ペン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.vi: There are many different kinds of goods displayed on the convenience store shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun コンビニ to the following noun to modify the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: には indicates a place and states where the goods exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: いろいろな directly modifies the noun しなもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the goods as the objects being displayed on the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: ならんで is the て form connected to います to describe the state of being arranged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the pattern describing the existing state of an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.why: The sentence places the location first with には, then states the subject with が. ならんでいます describes the goods as being arranged on the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あります, the sentence only says that the goods are there, without emphasizing their arranged state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for a place, but for existence or a present state, they should use に or には.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q25.kobun.vi: I went to see a piano concert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ピアノ with コンサート, creating the noun phrase “piano concert”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the event or place that is the destination of the action 行きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q25.kobun.why: The phrase ピアノのコンサート is formed with の to modify コンサート. The particle に marks the event as the destination of 行きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the meaning changes to the place where an action takes place at the concert, not the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use で with 行く to indicate a destination; a place or event one goes to usually takes に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.vi: A French doll is already displayed on the table.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects つくえ with 上, creating the location phrase “on the table.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the doll has been put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies にんぎょう, showing its origin or a feature related to France.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object that has been placed in that state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: てあります describes the result of an intentional action and the fact that the state remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.why: The location phrase つくえの上に comes first to identify where the state exists. にんぎょうが is the object in that state, while てあります emphasizes that someone intentionally displayed it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If かざっています is used, the focus is on the action of displaying something or on an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If あります is used, the sentence only says that there is a doll there and does not clearly state that it is already displayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse てあります with ています; てあります usually implies a result intentionally created by a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.vi: The machinery industry in this country is highly developed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before 国 to identify the country being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the country the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects きかい with こうぎょう, creating the phrase “machinery industry.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object evaluated as さかん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: さかんです serves as the predicate and comments on the industry’s level of development.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.why: この modifies 国, while きかいのこうぎょう is the noun phrase serving as the subject of the content being evaluated. The pattern Nは Nが Aです is used to comment on a feature of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nは Aです is used directly, the sentence evaluates the whole country instead of only the machinery industry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 多いです is used, the meaning changes to a large quantity and no longer means highly developed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit が after the object being evaluated, but Nは Nが Aです needs が to mark the part that has the feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.vi: Please do not catch fish in the pond.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects いけ with 魚, identifying the type of fish being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the catching action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ないでください creates a polite request not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.why: The phrase いけの魚 identifies the object, and を connects that object to the verb. The verb in the ない form combines with でください to create a polite negative request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If つかまえてください is used, the sentence becomes a request to catch fish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ください is omitted, the sentence still means “do not catch,” but the tone is more casual and less polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ないでください as a simple negative, but the whole phrase is actually a polite request: please do not do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q5.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.vi: After the water boils, put in the vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that becomes boiled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: てから connects an action that happens first with an action that happens later.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the vegetables as the object being put in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 入れる is changed into the polite form ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.why: The clause わいてから states the time when the first action is completed, and only then does the action 入れます take place. おゆ is the subject that boils, so が is used, while the vegetables are the affected object, so を is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes that the first action must be completed before the second action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It also means after, but it directly emphasizes the time after an action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often mistakenly use を for the subject of boiling; with おゆがわく, hot water is the subject, so が should be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.vi: The studying for the test has been fully prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テスト with べんきょう, creating the phrase “studying for the test.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes studying the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb that modifies the action して.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the preparation action with the state of already being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: てある shows that the result of an intentional action is still maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.why: テストのべんきょう forms a compound noun meaning “studying for the test.” じゅうぶんに modifies して, while してあります shows that the preparation has been completed and the result still remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しています, the sentence only says that someone is studying or usually studies. It does not emphasize that the preparation is already done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with しておきます, the sentence means that someone actively prepares in advance for a purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often understand てあります as simply meaning completion; this pattern also emphasizes a result that someone intentionally created and left in place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q7.kobun.cn: Vたどうしのて形 + ある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.vi: Please show me a nearby place where I can view cherry blossoms.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate a place near the speaker or a place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where flower viewing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the activity that can be performed in the potential clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause 花見ができる comes before ばしょ to modify the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the place as the thing the speaker wants someone to show them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects おしえる with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: Vてください is used to ask the listener to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.why: The clause 花見ができる is placed before ばしょ to identify the type of place being sought. ばしょを is the object of おしえて, while ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 花見をすることができる is used, the meaning is still that flower viewing is possible, but the expression is longer and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks for permission to do something. It is not used to ask someone to show a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often put a modifying clause after the noun; in Japanese, 花見ができる must come before ばしょ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.vi: The news about the accident was broadcast on the radio.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the medium or channel through which the news was broadcast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects じこ with ニュース, identifying the content of the news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the news as the subject affected by the broadcasting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: されました is the polite past passive form of ほうそうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.why: ラジオで states the broadcasting channel, while じこのニュース is the noun phrase identifying the news content. The sentence uses the passive voice because the news is the object being broadcast, not the subject that actively broadcasts it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ニュースがほうそうしました is used, the news is treated as the person performing the action, so it is unsuitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ラジオでニュースをほうそうしました is used, the sentence becomes active and must name the person or organization doing the broadcasting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use the active voice because of Vietnamese sentence patterns; when the subject is an affected thing such as ニュース, consider using the passive voice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t68-q9.kobun.cn: する動詞語幹 + される
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.vi: Please enlarge page 3 of this book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the book being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 本 with ３ページ, indicating the page belonging to the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the page as the object to be copied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 大きく is the adverbial form of 大きい. It modifies コピーして and shows how to make the copy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: して is the て form of コピーする, connecting the copying action with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after the て form to create a polite favor or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.why: The phrase この本の３ページ clearly identifies the object to be copied, and then を marks that object. 大きく comes before コピーして to add the manner of carrying out the action, while てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 大きく is omitted, the sentence only asks for the page to be copied and no longer asks for it to be enlarged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with てもいいです, the sentence becomes a request for permission to copy, not a request for someone else to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q1.kobun.tip: When the adjective い modifies a verb, it must change into the form く, such as 大きい changing into 大きく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.vi: In the afternoon, please take the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.sk: N time + N を + Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: 午後 indicates the time when the action takes place and can stand at the beginning of a sentence without a particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the exam as the object of taking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes at the end of a request and makes the sentence more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.why: The time expression is placed at the beginning to set the context, followed by the object of the action. The form てください changes a statement about an action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with うけなければなりません, the sentence means that one must take the exam, which is stronger than a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q10.kobun.tip: Do not put を after 午後 in a general time expression such as 午後、; を only goes with the object しけん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.vi: Eating alone every day is very lonely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.sk: N time + N だけで + N を + V辞書形 のは + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 indicates the time or frequency of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: だけで expresses the state or manner in which only one person performs the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks ごはん as the object of 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb 食べる combines with の to nominalize it, and then は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: さびしいです is the predicate adjective ending in い, expressing a feeling about eating alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.why: The phrase 食べるのは turns the action of eating into the topic, while さびしいです is the comment about that topic. The particle で in 一人だけで indicates the state or manner in which the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけ is omitted, the sentence only says that someone eats alone and does not emphasize the meaning “only one person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after 一人, but 一人だけで is what expresses the manner or state of being “alone.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.vi: Because there are still people who have not arrived, please do not start the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: まだ modifies the unfinished state of arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 来て is the て form of 来る, connecting with いない to create the state of not having arrived yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: いない negates the existence or presence of the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person who has not arrived and 人がいる forms an existence clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: から connects the reason to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks パーティー as the object of the action of starting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: ないで connects the negative form of the verb with ください to create a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: ください completes the polite request pattern meaning please.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.why: The clause 人がいるから gives the reason first and then makes the request. The phrase 来ていない comes before 人 to modify the person who has not arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a request not to perform an action; if Vてください is used, the meaning changes to a request to start.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing から with ので still states the reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse まだ with もう; まだ来ていない means “still not here yet,” while もう来ている means “has already arrived.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.vi: Because the gate was open, the dog came in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the gate as the subject that is in an open state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: ていた describes a state that already existed, while ので connects that state to the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the dog as the subject of the action of entering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 入って is the て form of 入る, connecting the action of entering with 来ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: きました is 来る in the polite past form, adding movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.why: The gate's state is placed first and connected with ので to give the reason. 入ってきました combines the action of entering with 来る, emphasizing movement toward the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the sentence still means “because the gate was open,” but the reason sounds more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入っていきました is used, the movement is entering and then moving away from the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ている as meaning only “be doing”; with verbs that show a change of state, such as open, ている usually indicates a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: もっと modifies the degree of seriousness in studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な changes to the に form to modify the verb べんきょうして.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: べんきょうして is the て form of べんきょうする, connecting with ください to create a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ください completes the polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.why: まじめに comes before the verb because it describes how to study. The form て combines with ください to turn the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vなさい is used, the request sounds stronger and is usually spoken by someone in a higher position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding みて gives the meaning “please try studying more seriously.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may keep まじめな unchanged before the verb, but the adjective な must change to まじめに when it modifies a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.vi: This steak is hot and delicious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the steak being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents ステーキ as the common topic of the two features that follow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: あつい changes to あつくて to connect the first quality with the second.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: おいしいです is the main comment and ends the sentence in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.why: ステーキは is the topic, while あつくて and おいしいです are the two listed qualities. An adjective ending in い uses the くて form to connect qualities with the same topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Using し presents the features as reasons or notable points instead of directly connecting the two qualities.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: Using が creates a contrast, such as “although it is hot, it is delicious.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may connect two adjectives with と, but an adjective ending in い must change to くて in this connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.vi: I eat bread spread with butter and jam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the surface or object that receives the butter and jam spread onto it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects two equal nouns, while を marks both as the objects of つける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: つけて is the て form of つける, connecting the action of spreading with the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べます is the main action of the sentence in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.why: に indicates the place or object to spread onto, while を marks the butter and jam as what is spread. The form て connects two actions in sequence: spread first, then eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, パン is understood as the means or way of eating, not the surface to spread onto.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Using や only lists butter and jam and may imply that there are other things, without stating that the list is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を after パン, but に is what indicates the surface or object that receives the spread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q17.kobun.vi: I went to see a famous festival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective な modifies the noun おまつり that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the action けんぶつしました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 見物する is changed to the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q17.kobun.why: The phrase ゆうめいな comes before おまつり to describe the festival. おまつり takes を because it is the object being viewed, while けんぶつしました serves as the final predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 見ました, the sentence only says that the speaker saw it, without emphasizing visiting or going to see an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget な after the adjective な when placing it before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.vi: Why are you opposing my opinion?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: どうして is an interrogative adverb that asks for the reason for an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: わたしの modifies いけん and shows that the opinion belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the object toward which the opposing action is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb はんたいする with いる to create a continuous structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: いる indicates an ongoing state, while のですか creates a question that asks for an explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.why: わたしのいけん forms a noun phrase, after which に marks the object of はんたいする. The form はんたいしている expresses an ongoing opposing action or attitude; のですか gives the question a tone that asks for an explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 反対しますか is used, the question asks whether the person opposes it, without emphasizing the ongoing state of opposing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with はんたいする, but this verb usually goes with に to indicate the object being opposed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q18.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; V普通形 + のですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q19.kobun.vi: Because I cannot win the match, it is really disappointing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the setting or scope in which winning takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: かつ changes to the negative past form なくて to connect the reason to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: This is a predicate that states the speaker's feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q19.kobun.why: しあいで states the circumstances, while かてなくて connects the reason to the feeling ざんねんです. The form なくて is suitable when the preceding clause explains the reason for the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 勝てないで, the sentence can easily mean not doing this but doing something else, so it is less natural than なくて when stating a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse で, which marks a place, with で, which marks the context or situation of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.vi: If you find a lost item, please take it to the reception desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item found in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 見つけたら uses the past form together with たら to set a condition that occurs before the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the place where brought items are received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: とどけて is the て form of とどける, connecting the action with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes a polite request after a verb in the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.why: The 見つけたら clause gives the condition first, while the main clause states what should be done when the condition occurs. に marks the reception desk as the place where the item is received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is replaced with と, the sentence has a natural or regularly occurring result, so it is less suitable as an instruction or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: 見つければ also means "if you find," but it focuses more on a hypothetical condition or a logical explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse たら with the simple past; in 見つけたら, たら turns the whole clause into a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q2.kobun.cn: Vたら + …; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.vi: Please write your own opinion in a simple way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects じぶん with the noun that follows and shows possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks いけん as the object of the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: かんたんに is an adverb that modifies how the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: かけてください uses the て form together with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.why: The possessive phrase じぶんの comes before the object いけんを. The adverb かんたんに comes before the predicate to describe how to write, while てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If かいてください is used, the kana spelling shows the verb “to write” more clearly, while the request structure stays the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q20.kobun.tip: The adjective な becomes an adverb by adding に: かんたんな → かんたんに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: どうぞ is an adverb used to invite or make a polite suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the place or position toward which the sitting action is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks こし as the element used with the fixed verb こしをかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The form てください creates a polite invitation or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q21.kobun.why: いすに marks the place where the listener sits, while こしをかける is a fixed expression for sitting down. どうぞ makes the invitation, and together with てください it creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 座ってください is used, the meaning is still “please sit down,” but it is expressed directly with the verb 座る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate and use こし as “chair,” but in this phrase こしをかける is a fixed expression meaning “to sit.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.vi: If it is something you do not like, you do not have to force yourself to eat it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective な modifies もの and refers to something the listener does not like.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: なら is attached after a noun to give a condition or assumption.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The に form of the adjective な acts as an adverb and modifies the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.ch.3.vi: even if you do not eat
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The form なくても expresses a concessive condition and combines with いい to say that not doing the action is acceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: いいですよ ends the sentence and permits or reassures the listener that the previous action is not necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.why: きらいなもの creates a noun phrase, and なら sets a condition for that situation. むりに describes how to eat, while なくてもいい expresses that it is acceptable not to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 食べないでください, the sentence becomes a request not to eat and no longer has the meaning that skipping the meal is allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べなくてはいけません is used, the meaning changes to “must eat.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake なくてもいい for “must not eat,” but this pattern means “it is okay not to eat.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q22.kobun.cn: N + なら; Vない形 + なくてもいい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.vi: I have no special plans tonight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tonight the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: とくに modifies the idea of having no plans and emphasizes the degree of being special.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what is said not to exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります, used for things or plans that do not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to make a time expression the topic, then とくに modifies the noun よてい. In the negative existence pattern, the noun is marked by が and the sentence ends with ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ありません with ない creates a more informal expression, which is less suitable for polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with ありません, but a thing that does not exist must be used with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.vi: I feel sick when I ride in a car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the vehicle or object that the speaker gets on or rides in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the action のる with a result that usually occurs immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the state described as becoming bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: わるく is the く form of the い-ending adjective and connects with なる to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: なります is the polite form of なる and acts as the main predicate showing a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.why: The のると clause states the condition or time that causes the result. The structure Aいくなる uses わるく to express a feeling changing into a bad state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is used, the sentence only states the time when riding in a car, while と emphasizes the result that usually follows the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: Using わるく感じます means directly “feel uncomfortable” and does not emphasize a change of state as わるくなります does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say わるいなります, but the い-ending adjective must change to the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q25.kobun.vi: I invited my friend to my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the person who was invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination or the place where the invitation takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: しょうたいしました is the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q25.kobun.why: The verb “invite” uses を for the invited person and に for the destination. The verb is in the ました form because the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the friend becomes the person performing the action together with the speaker, not the person being invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and で; に only marks the destination, while で usually marks the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.vi: You must not copy your friend's report and submit it to the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 友だち with レポート to show that the report belongs to the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the report as the object being copied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: うつして is the て form and connects the copying action with the submitting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person who receives the submitted report.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 出しては combines with だめです to create a pattern that forbids an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: だめです completes the 出してはだめです pattern and expresses a prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.why: The two actions are connected by the て form in the order of copying the report and then submitting it. The pattern Vてはだめです places the entire 出す action within the prohibited content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is similarly prohibitive, but 出してはいけません is more formal and more regulatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is a direct request saying “please do not submit it,” and is less regulatory than a formal prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.tip: Do not translate ては separately; 出してはだめです must be understood as a whole: "must not submit."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q3.kobun.cn: Vては ＋ だめだ／いけない／ならない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.vi: Please do not plant flowers here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: には indicates the location and states where an action must not be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the flowers as the object of the planting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: うえないで is the negative form connected to ください to ask someone not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ください completes a polite negative request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.why: ここには places the restricted location at the beginning of the sentence, and 花を is the object of うえる. The form ないでください expresses a polite request not to plant flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with うえてはいけません, the sentence has a stronger rule-like or prohibitive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: うえません only says "do not plant" and does not directly ask the listener not to plant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q4.kobun.tip: For a group 2 verb such as うえる, the negative form is うえない, and only then is でください added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q5.kobun.vi: There is a taxi parked over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the taxi is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject as being in a stopped state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ている describes the current state of a vehicle that has stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q5.kobun.why: The location phrase comes first, followed by the subject marked with が. The verb in the form ている is suitable for describing the taxi as being stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with とまります, it means that the taxi will stop or stops habitually, without emphasizing its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate ている as simply "be doing," but with とまる it often describes a stopped state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.vi: Please feel free to use this computer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun and modifies コンピューター.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this computer the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes a word describing a quality into an adverb that modifies how something is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb to ください to form a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.why: The topic is marked with は, the adverb じゆうに shows how to use it, and Vてください creates a polite request. This order moves from the object being discussed, to the manner, and then to the action to perform.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つかってもいいです, the sentence becomes a question or a request for permission, rather than a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; change the verb into the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.vi: Because it was cold, I turned on the heater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the cause さむい with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that was turned on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ました describes a completed action in polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. The object turned on is marked with を, followed by the polite past-tense verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the basic cause remains the same, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.tip: With adjectives ending in い, such as さむい, keep the form い before ので, and do not add な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q8.kobun.vi: I booked a hotel room by phone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means used to make the booking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the booking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: しました is the polite past form of する in the verb よやくする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q8.kobun.why: The means is placed first and marked with で. The noun serving as the object comes before the verb and takes を, creating the structure Nをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If the phrase ホテルをよやくしました is replaced with 電話をしました, it means that I made a phone call, not that I booked a room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q8.kobun.tip: で in 電話で indicates a means, not a place; therefore, it should not be translated as "at the phone."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.vi: I was given an injection at the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.sk: N で ＋ N を ＋ passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the injection took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the injection as the object of the passive action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the polite past passive form of する, showing that the speaker received the effect of the injection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.why: The place where the action occurs uses で, while ちゅうしゃをする changes into the passive form ちゅうしゃをされる. The person affected is omitted because the context already makes it clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ちゅうしゃをしました, it means that I received or gave an injection, without emphasizing that I was given one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t69-q9.kobun.tip: Do not confuse されました here with honorific meaning; the structure Nをされる shows that the subject receives the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object of liking in the pattern 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです is the predicate and expresses an emotion or preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to state the person who has the preference, が to mark the liked object, and places すきです at the end as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with を, the sentence is no longer the standard connection with 好きだ in common Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use を based on the Vietnamese expression "like winter," but 好きだ usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ ability V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces Yamashita as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object of ability in the ability pattern はなせます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: はなせます is the ability form and expresses the ability to speak English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.why: は makes the person with the ability the topic, while が marks the content or object toward which the ability is directed. はなせます is the predicate stating the ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If を話します is used, the sentence only describes the action of speaking English and does not confirm ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If も is used, the sentence also suggests that the person can speak English in addition to another language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with an ability verb, but the ability pattern usually uses が to mark the object of ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the thinking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 考えて is the て form, which connects the action to ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてください is used to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q11.kobun.why: このこたえを is the object placed before the verb. The verb uses the て form and then combines with ください to turn the sentence into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern adds the meaning "please try thinking about it," emphasizing trying to do the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern expresses the meaning "must think," which is stronger than an ordinary request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the dictionary form before ください, but the verb must use the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vi: I want to travel around the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.sk: N を + V without ます + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the range or object of the travel activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: たい attaches to the verb stem to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.why: 世界を is the object or range of the activity りょこうする. Remove ます from りょこうします and add たい to express desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ旅行します is used, the sentence only says that someone travels to the world or somewhere; it does not express desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern expresses a definite and specific plan, stronger than the desire expressed with たい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q12.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily attach たい to the ます form, but ます must be removed before adding たい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.vi: Because there is no time, please hurry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks what is stated to be absent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 急ぐ changes to the て form to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: てください expresses a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason and is connected to the request by から. 急いでください uses the て form with ください to ask the listener to hurry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence is still a request, but its tone is stronger and sounds like an instruction from someone of higher status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q13.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily forget to change 急ぐ into 急いで before connecting it with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q14.kobun.vi: I went to the wrong examination room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun しけん to the following noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 教室 as the object that was mistaken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: まちがえる is the polite past form and describes an event that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q14.kobun.why: しけんの modifies 教室, forming the phrase “the examination classroom.” This noun phrase is the object of まちがえました, so it goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the focus is on the noun itself being different or wrong, not on the speaker’s action of making a mistake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q14.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may mechanically translate の as “ownership”; here, it identifies the type of classroom related to the examination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q15.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamamoto is a convenience store employee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Mr. Yamamoto is the topic being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the workplace with a noun that indicates a profession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with information identifying a profession or status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q15.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to introduce information about Yamamoto. コンビ二の店員 is a noun phrase, in which の shows that this person belongs to or works at the convenience store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes working at the convenience store rather than the job title of employee.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q15.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily omit の when talking about a profession connected to a workplace, but コンビ二の店員 needs の to connect two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.vi: My older sister is 25 years old.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.sk: N の + N は + number + さいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows possession and modifies 姉.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 姉 the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and states the topic’s age.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.why: わたしの姉 forms the phrase “my older sister,” and then は marks this phrase as the topic. The age is stated in the final predicate with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that the older sister is the person who is 25, rather than simply introducing information about her.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q16.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may confuse the order of possession; Japanese places わたしの before 姉.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.vi: My friend made a bag for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who made the bag.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing that was made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 作る changes to the て form to connect with くれました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: くれました expresses that another person did something helpful for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.why: ともだちが is the person who performs the action, while かばんを is the thing affected by 作る. The て form connects 作る with くれる to show that the friend made something to help the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the subject is understood as the person doing something helpful for someone else, not someone doing something to help the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence shifts the focus to the speaker receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q17.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may use てあげる in the wrong direction; when someone does something to help you, use てくれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.vi: My older brother is studying science at university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the older brother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the research activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the field being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 研究する combines with ています to express an ongoing activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.why: The sentence is ordered as topic, place, object, and then predicate. The particle で shows where the activity takes place, while を marks the field that the older brother is studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says that the older brother is at the university; it does not mention the research activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q18.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may use に for the place of an action, but the place where a research activity takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.vi: The wind has been getting stronger and stronger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.sk: N が + adverb of degree + Aいくなる + てくる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: だんだんと modifies the degree of the change in the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: なってきました describes a state that is gradually changing toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.why: 風が is the subject of the change, while だんだんと shows that the change happens step by step. The adjective つよい changes into つよく and combines with なってくる to express becoming gradually stronger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it only says that the wind becomes strong; it does not emphasize the process as it develops.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that the change continues from the present into the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may forget to change the adjective ending in い into the く form before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q19.kobun.cn: Aいく + なる + てくる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: The air here is not good, is it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the place ここ the topic for comparison or comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the characteristic わるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective わるい serves as the predicate and describes the condition of the air.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ですね adds a sense of confirmation or agreement with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: ここは makes the place the topic, while 空気が is the actual subject of the adjective わるい. ですね comes at the end to turn the comment into a gentle confirmation shared with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですね is replaced with でしょう, the sentence focuses more on guessing or asking for agreement and no longer has the clear shared-comment tone of ですね.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Do not connect ですね directly as a word-for-word translation; it is a sentence-final expression used to share or confirm a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.vi: Read the instructions carefully before you begin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects やりかた with 説明, creating a phrase that modifies the explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the content being read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies the action of reading and shows how carefully it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The form てから connects the action of reading with the action that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: てください turns the request to begin into a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.why: The phrase やりかたの説明 identifies the type of explanation to read, and then を marks the object of 読む. てから puts the two actions in order: read first, then begin.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means “read before beginning,” but the focus is more on the time before the later action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means after finishing something, but it does not directly connect the form て with から as the current sentence does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before から in the pattern てから; the verb must be changed to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.vi: Please go to the post office, buy ten stamps, and bring them back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.sk: N で ＋ N を ＋ Number ＋ Vてくる ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: まい is a counter used for thin, flat objects such as stamps.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 買ってくる expresses going to buy something and bringing it back, and combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.why: で identifies where the buying takes place, を identifies what is being bought, and １０まい states the quantity. 買ってくる shows that the speaker wants the listener to go buy the item and bring it back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it only means “please buy it”; it does not clearly state that the bought item should be brought back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes going somewhere to buy something, but it does not necessarily clearly express bringing it back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate てくる as only “go,” but in this sentence it also includes the meaning of returning after buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q21.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.vi: I have just arrived in Japan, so I still do not have any close friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the destination of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたばかりで connects the recently occurring reason with the result of not having close friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ modifies a negative predicate and shows that the state has not changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 親しい comes before 友だち to modify it, while が marks the subject that exists or does not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: いません is the polite negative form of います, used for people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.why: にほんに identifies the destination of 来る, and then Vたばかりで gives the reason: the arrival in Japan happened recently. In the negative existence sentence, the friends are marked by が, and まだ shows that the state of still not having them continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes an action that has just finished at the moment of speaking, while たばかり can cover a longer period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means that since arriving in Japan, the speaker has not had any friends; it does not directly emphasize having just arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q22.kobun.tip: まだ is often used with a negative form to say that something has not happened or has not been achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.vi: There are many picture books for children in that library over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.sk: あの ＋ N には ＋ Nのための ＋ N が ＋ Quantity ＋ ある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to point to a specific place that is far from the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase に は states the location and makes it the scope of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: Nのための modifies えほん and shows the target or purpose of use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists at the stated location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: たくさん modifies ある and shows a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: ある is the existence predicate used for things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.why: に は makes the library the scope of existence, while えほんが is the thing introduced as existing there. The phrase 子どものための comes directly before えほん to specify the type of picture books.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern usually connects to a verb to say what someone does for someone else or for what purpose; it does not directly modify a noun like ための.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means that something is aimed at children, but it emphasizes that the product is designed to suit that group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q23.kobun.tip: Distinguish ための, which comes before a noun, from ために, which usually comes before a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the place where the car must not stop or park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the car affected by the action 止める.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ないでください creates a polite request not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.kobun.why: そこに identifies the prohibited place, and 車を is the object of the parking action. 止めないでください puts the negative form before ください to ask the listener not to perform that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern expresses a rule or stronger prohibition, without the direct polite-request tone of ないでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern asks someone to try to avoid doing something. It is softer and more like a reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use を after 止める to express the parking place; a location goes with に, while the car goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q24.tokens.4.m: do not park, do not stop
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.vi: Today, I would like to hear many different opinions from everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the time the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the source of the opinions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase is the object being heard, so it goes with the particle を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: と quotes the desired content before おもいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: おもいます expresses the speaker's judgment or wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.why: きょうは states the time, followed by みなさんから, which shows the source of the opinions, and then 意見を marks the object of 聞く. The content 聞きたい is placed before とおもいます to express the wish in a softer way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with に, the meaning changes to a request or action directed toward everyone, without emphasizing the source of the opinions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of から when they want to say that they are obtaining or receiving information from someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person whose experience is being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense verb した modifies こと in the pattern for talking about experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns an action into a noun, while が marks the experience being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません denies the existence of that experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: The action 運転する changes to the た form and then comes before こと to become “the experience of having driven.” The phrase ことがありません denies ever having that experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence can mean that something is sometimes done or that someone sometimes has an experience, so it no longer means “have never done it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget to change the verb to the た form before こと when talking about an experience they have had.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: Vた + ことが + ある/ない・ありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: Please say it one more time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 一度 indicates the number of times and combines with もう to mean “one more time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: いって is the て form of 言う. It connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: もう一度 acts as an adverb showing repetition and comes before the action. The verb uses the て form before ください because this is a polite request pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the request will sound more polite and humble than てください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: I will meet my friend and then eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と indicates the person who takes part in the action 会う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 会って is the て form. It connects meeting a friend with the following action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the food being eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: たべます is the main predicate and uses the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: ともだちと identifies the person being met, and 会って connects the earlier action with the main action. ごはんを is the direct object of たべます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence will list typical actions and will not necessarily emphasize their order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: The particle と in ともだちと会う means “with”; it is not an object marker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vi: Because of an accident, the train is not running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the cause of the train not running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the vehicle that is in a non-running state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 動いて is the て form of 動く. It combines with いません to describe a current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: いません denies an ongoing state in the pattern Vていません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.why: じこで gives the cause first, and then でんしゃが is the subject affected by it. Vていません describes the train's current state of not operating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 動きません is used instead, the sentence more easily means that the train does not run or will not run in general, with a weaker sense of its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.tip: Do not understand ています as meaning only “be doing” in every case; with 動く, it can also describe a state of operating or not operating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q6.kobun.cn: Vて + います/いません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vi: I will get up early tomorrow morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with あさ to create a phrase indicating a point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 早く is an adverb modifying おきます. It indicates how or when someone gets up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.why: The time phrase あしたの あさ comes before the adverb 早く to state the time and manner of the action. 早く directly modifies おきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 早い is used, it is an adjective and cannot directly modify おきます like the adverb 早く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 早めに also means earlier than usual and emphasizes doing something before the expected time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep the adjective form 早い before the verb, but it must be changed to 早く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vi: I am living in a large house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where someone lives, while 広い modifies いえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: すんで is the て form of すむ. It connects with います to create a pattern describing the state of living.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: います follows a verb in the て form to describe an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.why: 広い comes before いえ to describe the house. に marks the place of residence, while すんでいます shows the state of living there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 住みます is used instead, the sentence only talks about living in the future or planning to live there, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 住んでいます is the kanji spelling of すんでいます and keeps the same structure and meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に as a word showing direction, but in this sentence に indicates a place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vi: There was a fire nearby yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates where the event happened, while きのう states the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks an event that appears or happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ありました is the polite past form of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.why: きのう states the time, and the phrase 近くで states where the event happened. In sentences about something existing or happening, a newly appearing thing usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 近くに is used, に will indicate a place where something exists or a destination, so it is less natural than で when saying that a fire happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes the action of a fire breaking out, while ありました only reports that the event happened or existed.
