default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t7-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for every location, but the place where an action happens usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.vi: My older sister often argues with my older brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the older sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the action and shows how often they argue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the person who takes part in or interacts in the argument.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する. It connects the main verb with います in the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: います combines with the て form to show an ongoing state or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.why: After the topic and frequency, あにと identifies the person involved in the interaction. The ている form at the end of the sentence shows that the state of arguing is continuing or happens repeatedly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: The simple past only says that they argued; it does not emphasize an ongoing or repeated state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with the person they argue with, but this interactive action uses と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q10.kobun.vi: I will try taking the N4 exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects N4 with the noun “exam” to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the exam as the object of the action of taking it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: うけてみます uses the て form to connect with みます and express trying to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q10.kobun.why: The phrase N4のしけん forms a compound noun. Then を marks the object of うける. The pattern Vてみる comes at the end of the sentence to express the intention to try doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced here, the sentence will say that someone is taking the exam or is in the state of having taken it, and will no longer emphasize trying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form directly before みる; change the verb to the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほんご with ぶんぽう, forming the noun phrase “Japanese grammar.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は shows that Japanese grammar is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective むずかしい to increase its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The い-ending adjective acts as the predicate and adds です to make the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q11.kobun.why: The phrase にほんごのぶんぽう is grouped as the topic, while とても comes before the adjective to modify its degree. The adjective むずかしい keeps the ending form い and adds です at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of は, the sentence emphasizes Japanese grammar itself instead of presenting it as a general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q11.kobun.tip: Do not add な before です with い-ending adjectives such as むずかしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.vi: I sent sweets to my family in my home country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects くに with かぞく, showing that the family belongs to the home country or country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the recipient of the sending action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the sweets as the thing being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: おくりました is the polite past form of おくる, expressing a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.why: In the structure for sending something, the recipient goes with に, and the thing being sent goes with を. おくりました at the end of the sentence shows that the action happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used, the focus shifts to the direction of sending, while に is more suitable when stating the recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the recipient; the recipient usually goes with に, while the object goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.vi: At Christmas, I always give gifts to my family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents Christmas as the topic or time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the action します and shows repeated frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the recipient of the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the gift as the object of the action します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: します is the main predicate; in this context, する combines with おくりもの to express giving a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.why: クリスマスは sets the time context, and いつも modifies the regularly performed action. The recipient uses に, while the gift uses を before します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If します is replaced with あげます, the verb directly means to give and sounds more natural when emphasizing the recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q13.kobun.tip: Distinguish に, which marks the recipient, from を, which marks the gift; do not switch these two particles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.vi: On my birthday this year, I want a new computer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ことし with たんじょうび, forming the phrase “this year’s birthday.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents this year’s birthday as the topic and context for the wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 新しい comes before パソコン to modify the computer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the desired object in the pattern ほしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ほしいです acts as the predicate and expresses the desire to have an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.why: ことしのたんじょう日は sets the time and topic. In the pattern ほしい, the desired object goes with が, while 新しい comes directly before パソコン to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたい is used, the sentence expresses wanting to perform an action; ほしい expresses wanting to have an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.tip: With ほしい, the desired object usually goes with が, not を as with an action verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q14.kobun.cn: N が ＋ ほしいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.vi: Because the weather is good, the train going toward the sea is very crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the cause clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause clause to the result and comes after the adjective いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction in which the train goes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb 行く comes before 電車 to modify the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the train as the entity experiencing the crowded state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: こんでいます describes the train as crowded or packed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.why: The clause 天気がいいので states the cause before the result. 行く comes before 電車 to form the phrase “the train going toward the sea,” while が marks the train as the entity in the state こんでいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the cause has almost the same meaning but sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure means going to the sea by train, not that the train goes to the sea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.tip: Do not mistake 行く電車 for “go by train”; the verb before the noun here modifies that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.vi: Children, let’s play happily under the sunlight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the topic of the invitation to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the nounたいよう with 下, forming a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the place where the playing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.ch.3.vi: in a lively and healthy way
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective なげんき changes into the adverb formげんきに to modify あそぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: あそびます removes ます and adds ましょう to make an invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.why: The topic is stated first, followed by the place and manner of the action. The verb at the end uses ましょう because the speaker is inviting or encouraging everyone to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence becomes a gentle invitation in question form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to play, so the meaning of doing it together is no longer clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that Aな must change to Aなに when modifying a verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q16.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ ましょう; Aな ＋ に
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.vi: Because of the strong wind, the tree in the park broke.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the cause that led to the tree breaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies 木, showing that the tree belongs to or is in the park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks 木 as the entity undergoing the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite past form describes an event that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.cn: N ＋ で for expressing a cause; Vます-stem ＋ ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.why: The cause comes first with で, while the affected object comes before が. おれる is an intransitive verb, so the tree is marked with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the cause has a more negative tone or clearly assigns blame.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence sounds more formal and emphasizes the agent that caused the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 木, but the intransitive verb おれる uses が to mark the thing that broke.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.vi: The match that will decide the top team in Asia is tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: で limits the scope of the comparison or the decision about which team is the best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the phrase いちばん with チーム to describe the team.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object decided in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before しあい to describe the match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: は states that the match is the topic whose time is specified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: です connects the topic しあい with the time information あした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N to create a noun-modifying clause; N の + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.why: The clause きめる comes directly before しあい and describes which match. The whole phrase becomes the topic with は, followed by あしたです, which states when it takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning leans toward a match held for the purpose of deciding which team is the best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes deciding as content or an event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put しあい before the modifying clause, but in Japanese the modifying part always comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.vi: My older sister cut as much as 30 cm of her hair, which surprised everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.sk: N が + N を + quantity も + Vて、 + N + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the cutting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing affected by the cutting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: も comes after a quantity to emphasize a large amount or an amount beyond expectation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: きって is the て form of きる, connecting the previous action with the following result or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: みんな is the subject of the action of being surprised, although the particle が is omitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb is in the polite past form and describes the reaction after the previous action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.cn: Vて + the following clause connects successive actions or events; quantity + も emphasizes the degree
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.why: かみを is the object being cut, while 30センチも adds the amount of hair cut and emphasizes the large number. The て form connects the cutting action with everyone's surprised reaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning is that only 30 cm was cut, emphasizing a small or limited amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly instead of connecting events with the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand も as simply also, but after a quantity it usually emphasizes the meaning of as much as or to the extent of.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.vi: Please put everything unnecessary into that box.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: いらない comes before もの to describe and identify the things that are unnecessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the unnecessary things the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぶ describes the action and requests that everything be thrown away, not just part of it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: あそこの describes はこ and points to the box in that location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the place where the objects are thrown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: すてて is the て form of すてる and connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: ください comes after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.why: The clause いらない comes before もの to limit the objects to be handled. The order is then the rangeぜんぶ, the destinationはこに, and the てください form to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: すてなさい is also a request, but it has a stronger commanding tone than すててください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: すててもいいです asks whether throwing something away is allowed or gives permission; it does not require the listener to throw it away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put ください after the dictionary form, but a polite request pattern must use the verb's て form before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.vi: On my way home from work, I often stop by a department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point, while の connects this phrase with 帰り.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase 帰り states the situation or time when the action of often stopping by the store takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb よく describes how often the action of stopping by occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place or destination of the action 寄る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: よっています describes a habit or a repeated action that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.cn: N からの + N; Vている can describe a continuing state or habit
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.why: かいしゃからの帰り puts the situation at the beginning of the sentence. よく shows frequency, while に marks the place visited with the verb よる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes being in the middle of the return journey rather than the time while going home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning is only going to the store, without the sense of stopping by.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate and use に as a general destination, but with よる, に marks the place visited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.vi: When the color of lipstick changes, my mood changes too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects くちべに with いろ to create a phrase meaning the color of lipstick.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that changes in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the condition with the result and means that when the condition occurs, the result usually occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds mood as another thing that also changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb describes a spontaneous change in mood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + と, used for natural conditions or results that usually occur; N の + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes before the result and ends with と. いろが is the changing subject, while きぶんも is another subject that also changes under that condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used instead, the sentence has a more specific hypothetical meaning, and the result does not necessarily always occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If なら is used, the sentence is usually based on information or an assumption given earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と for every conditional sentence, but と is most suitable for natural or frequently occurring results.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.vi: Since I started playing tennis last week, my physical condition has improved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of はじめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: Vたら connects a conditional or time clause with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 体 with ちょうし to create a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject of the change in state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective よい changes into the adverb form よく to describe なりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: なる describes a change into a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.why: The time expression comes first, followed by the activity performed. The clause はじめたら states the transition point, while 体のちょうしがよくなりました is the result that occurs afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this pattern instead emphasizes that the following action is performed after starting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: Using this pattern instead describes a result that usually or naturally occurs, without emphasizing one specific occasion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use よいなりました, but before なる, よい must be changed to よく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.vi: I like swimming, but I can swim only 50 meters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.sk: N は + Aなですが + Quantity しか + negative potential verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces swimming as the topic for comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting ideas: liking swimming but having limited ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: しか limits the range and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative potential form shows that the ability reaches only 50 meters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.why: The topic is marked by は, and then が creates a contrast between preference and ability. しか comes after the distance to limit how far one can swim.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか is replaced with だけ, the sentence still means only 50 meters, but a negative predicate is not required.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If でも is used, the meaning changes to “about 50 meters is also acceptable” or “at least 50 meters can be swum.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use しか with an affirmative sentence such as およげます; use およげません instead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q23.kobun.cn: N + しか + Vない; Aな + ですが
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.vi: The vacuum cleaner broke, so it is very inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that has entered a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the cause to the result; しまう adds a sense that the event was unfortunate or unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective showing the degree of inconvenience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the comment about the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.why: The broken subject comes first, followed by the てしまって clause stating the cause. The result and the degree of inconvenience are placed in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If しまって is replaced with いて, the sentence only states that the machine is currently broken and reduces the sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated clearly and sounds more gently explanatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.tip: しまう does not only mean putting something away; after the て form, it also describes something that happened accidentally or is regrettable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q24.kobun.cn: Vて形 + しまう; Vて形 + しまって
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.vi: While I was cooking, an earthquake occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: している modifies 途中 and shows that the cooking was in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the time or situation in which another event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the event that occurred in that situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ありました describes the appearance or occurrence of an earthquake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.why: The phrase している途中で sets the time frame, meaning in the middle of an ongoing action. The main event, 地震がありました, is placed after で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes that the event occurred during the whole period of cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If ときに is used, the sentence only generally says that it happened while cooking, without emphasizing the middle of the activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q25.kobun.tip: 途中で must be used with a noun or a Vている phrase to indicate the exact time in the middle of a process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.vi: This country produces delicious coffee beans.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before 国 to identify the country being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place of production, while は limits the scope to this country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: おいしい comes before コーヒーまめ to modify the coffee beans.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the product being produced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: して is the て form of する, and connects to います in the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: います combines with the て form to describe an ongoing activity or a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.why: では defines the production location, and then the adjective おいしい modifies the product. The object goes with を, and the phrase ている forms the predicate describing ongoing production.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, this country becomes the newly emphasized subject, instead of the location range marked by この国では.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 生産しました describes one completed act of production and does not express an ongoing activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the place of production, but the location where an action occurs must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q4.kobun.vi: A pleasant smell is coming from the kitchen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle から indicates the place from which the smell comes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the smell being sensed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: する in the pattern においがする describes having or giving off a smell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q4.kobun.why: The place where the smell comes from is placed first with から, while the sensed smell is the subject with が. いい modifies におい, and then においがする is used to say that there is a smell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is replaced, the sentence only says that the smell exists and does not emphasize the feeling of the smell spreading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で to indicate the source of a smell, but the source in this pattern uses から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.sk: Time + N が + N を + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the person who quit smoking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the object that was given up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: やめました is the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.why: さいきん is placed at the beginning to state the time. The person who quit smoking is 父, so it goes with が, while たばこ is the direct object of やめる, so it goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence emphasizes the current state of not smoking or the continued state of having quit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use に before たばこ because やめる takes the direct object with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q5.kobun.cn: Vます + やめました → Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.vi: My wife is very good at cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は makes かない the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle が marks the area in which ability is evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 上手です is the adjective predicate な, used to evaluate skill or ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.why: かない is the person being described, so it is made the topic with は. りょうりが states the area of ability, while とても modifies the degree of 上手です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says that my wife cooks and no longer means that she is good at cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.tip: With 上手, the area usually goes with が, not を as when describing the action of cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q6.kobun.cn: N は + N が + Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.vi: Please greet people cheerfully in the morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.sk: Time は + Aな に + Nをしますましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は limits the advice to the morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 元気に is the adverbial form of the adjective な and modifies the way of greeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form, used to invite or advise people to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.why: あさは states when the advice applies. 元気に changes the adjective な into an adverb showing manner, and then しましょう creates an invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 元気で is used, the meaning leans toward a state or condition, so it is less natural than 元気に when talking about how to greet someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.tip: The adjective な must change to ～に to modify a verb; it cannot remain in the form 元気な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q7.kobun.cn: Aな + に + Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.vi: I will go to the airport to pick you up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle へ indicates the direction of movement toward 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the person being picked up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: に after an action noun indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 行く is the main verb. Combined with むかえに, it forms the pattern meaning “go to pick someone up.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.why: A destination is used with へ, and the person being picked up is used with を. むかえに states the purpose and comes immediately before 行く in the pattern Nに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only says that someone picks up a guest. It no longer expresses movement to the airport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.tip: In the pattern for expressing the purpose of movement, に follows an action noun such as むかえ. It does not follow を directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q8.kobun.cn: N に + 行く/来る/帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.vi: I want to work not only in Japan but also abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: だけではなく opens the first part of the structure “not only A but also B.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place of work, while も adds this place to the previous range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ～たいです attaches to the continuative form 用形 of a verb to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.why: だけではなく connects the first place with the additional place. で indicates where the work takes place, while も means “also,” creating the relationship “not only... but also....”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning becomes “work only in Japan,” removing the idea of working abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If か is used, the sentence presents a choice between the two places and does not state that both places are included.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.tip: Do not omit も after で, because で only indicates the place, while も expresses the idea of adding something in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t70-q9.kobun.cn: N/V普通形/Aい/Aなな + だけではなく + N/場所 でも
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.vi: I do not throw away the receipt from a purchase; I keep it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the action that has been performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ときの turns the clause した into a modifier for レシート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the receipt that needs to be kept the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ないで connects an action that is not done with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてある describes a state maintained because someone deliberately did something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.why: The clause 買いものをしたときの modifies レシート and identifies what kind of receipt it is. すてないで connects with とってあります to express not throwing it away but keeping it in the same state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ないで is replaced with ずに, the meaning is still that the earlier action is not done, but the expression is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If とっておく is used, the sentence emphasizes keeping something for later use, not only the state of keeping it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.tip: Vてある emphasizes a maintained result. Do not confuse it with Vている, which only describes a state or an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q1.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ときの; Vない形 + で; Vて形 + ある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.vi: This year, I will also go with my family to see the summer festival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: も shows that the activity is repeated this year, as in previous years.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects なつ with おまつり to form the phrase “summer festival.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the event that someone goes to see.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the people who take part in the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: けんぶつします is the main predicate and describes visiting or watching a festival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.why: The time expression comes at the beginning of the sentence. It is followed by the noun phrase for the festival, and を marks the object that someone goes to see. で shows that the family is the group carrying out the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If かぞくで is replaced with 家族と, the meaning is still “with the family,” but it emphasizes the companion more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 家族に is used, this particle usually marks the person affected by an action, so it does not fit the meaning of going to see something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q2.kobun.tip: で in かぞくで indicates the person acting together, not a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.vi: I am hanging a beautiful picture in the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: きれい is a な-ending adjective, so it needs な when it comes before the noun え.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the picture as the object being hung.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place where an object is placed or hung.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes an action in progress or a resulting state that exists now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.why: きれいな modifies え and comes before the noun. を marks the affected object, に indicates the place where it is hung, and ています shows that the action or state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: かけました only says that the picture was hung, without emphasizing its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: かけてあります emphasizes that the picture has been hung and remains there as an intentional result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.tip: The adjective な must keep な before a noun, but な is omitted when it comes at the end of a sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q1.kobun.cn: Aな + N; Vて形 + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.vi: Among accessories, I like rings the best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects アクセサリー with 中 and creates the meaning “among the types of accessories.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 中 indicates the range, while は makes the comparison range the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object chosen as the favorite within the range above.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: いちばん modifies すき and expresses the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: すき is a な adjective and forms the predicate with the polite form です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.why: 中では limits the comparison range, ゆびわが is the object being evaluated, and いちばん adds the superlative meaning to すきです. This order corresponds to the expression “like ... the best among ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 中で is used instead of 中では, the sentence has less of a topic or contrast meaning, but its main meaning is almost unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern compares something with only one specific object and does not clearly show a range of several choices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q10.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use 好きな as a verb, but すきです is a な adjective and needs が to mark the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that ごはん is the topic of the advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies かんで and indicates how thoroughly the food is chewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects chewing with the following action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ゆっくり modifies 食べましょう and shows how to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ましょう creates an invitation or a gentle suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.why: ごはんは shows the object being suggested, and かんで connects chewing with eating. The two adverbs, よく and ゆっくり, modify two different actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 食べてください, the speech becomes more direct and expresses a request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: Using this pattern changes it into a request not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand て as “and” in every situation, but here it also connects actions in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.vi: Because I used the computer continuously, my neck started to hurt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: ずっと modifies the action of using the computer and emphasizes its duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the computer as the object being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 使っていたら combines an ongoing action with たら to state a condition or situation that leads to a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the body part that changes into a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The form く of the adjective い connects いたい with なる and describes a change into a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: なる describes a change of state, and ました shows that it happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.why: The clause 使っていたら describes a continuing situation. Then くびがいたくなりました describes the result: the neck changed into a painful state. The adjective いたい must change to いたく before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と, the result sounds more natural or more likely to happen repeatedly, rather than describing only one specific situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ので emphasizes the reason “because I used it,” instead of the condition or time expressed by たら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily say いたいなりました, but before なる, the form く must be used: いたくなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q12.kobun.cn: Vている + たら; Vた・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.vi: Because I woke up later than usual, I hurried to make breakfast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: より shows the reference point for comparing the time of waking up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The form く of おそい modifies おきた and shows that the waking time was late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason with the action of hurriedly making breakfast that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て of いそぐ modifies the action of making breakfast and shows how it was done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks breakfast as the object being made or cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: つくりました is the main predicate and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.why: いつもよりおそく sets the comparison point, おきたので states the reason, and いそいで shows how the main action was performed. The object あさごはんを comes directly before the verb つくりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is stated more directly and subjectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Using おきたら changes the meaning to “after waking up” or “if I wake up,” so it no longer emphasizes the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may more easily use おそい as an adverb, but before the verb it must change to おそく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + ので（丁寧形:ですので）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.vi: Please take out burnable garbage on Tuesday and Friday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.sk: N は + Time と + Time に + Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic as the type of garbage being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects two time points that both show days.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the day when the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください creates a polite request meaning “please do something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the days when the action is performed. と connects the days equally, while に attaches to the last day before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence expresses an invitation or doing something together, rather than asking the listener to take out the garbage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly use に after each day. When listing several days with the same function, と is usually enough to connect the days, and に is placed after the last day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.vi: I think I will make hamburger steak for dinner tonight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今日 with the noun that follows and creates a phrase modifying dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that dinner is the topic of the intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the dish as the object of 作る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the quoted content of the intention before 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: 思います is the main predicate and expresses the speaker's thought or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.why: The dish comes before を because it is the object of making. The intention uses the volitional form つくろう, and then と connects the intention's content with 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence directly and more firmly states the plan instead of saying that I think I will do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before と 思います when expressing your own intention; the intention must use the volitional form, such as つくろう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q15.kobun.cn: V意向形 + と + 思います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.vi: The old building was demolished, and a new building was built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective 古い modifies ビル immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the old building as the object affected by the demolition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the demolition clause with the next clause in the order of events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective 新しい modifies ビル after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the new building as the subject of the building action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: The past passive form describes the building as having been built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.why: Each noun ビル goes with が to become the grammatical subject of a passive clause. て connects two events that happen one after another: the old building is demolished, and then the new building is built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If て is replaced with てから, the sentence more clearly emphasizes that the new building is built only after the demolition is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Using this pattern lists representative actions rather than showing a complete sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand が as the person performing the action. In a passive sentence, the noun with が is usually the object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q16.kobun.cn: V受身て + V受身ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.vi: Japan's population is more than one hundred million people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 日本 with じんこう to create the phrase “Japan's population.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents Japan's population as the object being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.ch.2.vi: more than one hundred million people
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: より shows the standard used to compare Japan's population.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 多い is the predicate that expresses the result of the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.why: は makes the object being compared the topic, while より places the standard after it. The adjective 多い comes at the end to state the comparison result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence means “about the same as one hundred million people,” not “more than.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: Using this pattern changes the sentence into a negative comparison, meaning it is not as large as the standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.tip: Do not translate より as the word “than” in English. In Japanese, the comparison standard goes with より and comes before the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q17.kobun.cn: N は + N より + Aい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.vi: This shirt is thin but very warm, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to identify the shirt being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the shirt the topic of two contrasting features.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: のに connects an unexpected condition with a result that goes against the prediction; before のに, the adjective い keeps its うすい form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies あたたかい and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ですね is placed at the end to express a feeling and seek the listener's agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.why: The clause うすいのに states something that would normally make people expect the shirt not to be warm. The following clause のに gives the opposite result, emphasized by とても.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with けれども, the sentence still expresses contrast, but the tone is more neutral and places less emphasis on the unexpected result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: のに can also express regret or blame in another context, but here it expresses surprise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.tip: With い-ending adjectives, keep the dictionary form before のに: うすいのに, and do not add な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + のに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.vi: This swimming pool is deep, so it is dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies プール and must come before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the swimming pool the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the result; the adjective い stays in its plain form before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: あぶないです is the main predicate and states the result of the pool being deep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.why: は makes the swimming pool the topic, then ふかいので gives the reason before the conclusion あぶないです. ので creates a soft and objective cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with から, the sentence still means that it is dangerous because it is deep, but the expression is more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with のに, the sentence expresses contrast and no longer means cause and effect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.tip: An い-ending adjective does not use な before ので; say ふかいので, not ふかいなので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.vi: Because I received help, I want to return the favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.sk: Vた + ので + N が + Vます形 remove ます + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object or state toward which 世話になる is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks what the speaker wants to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: たい attaches to the ます form of a verb to express desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, while the desired action comes afterward. おれいがしたい is the が used to mark the object of the desired action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If たいと思います is used, the desire is expressed more softly and tentatively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly think that たい comes directly after the dictionary form, but the ます form of the verb must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.vi: Making so many copies like this alone is too much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a quantity word with the noun コピー.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of やる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the way or scope in which an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: の turns the verb やる into a noun, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: むりです serves as the predicate and evaluates making many copies alone as impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.why: The phrase やるのは turns the action of making copies into the topic, which is evaluated with むりです. で shows how the action is performed, while を marks what is being done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with できません, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker cannot perform the action rather than judging it as too much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget の when they want to turn a whole action into the topic before は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のは + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.vi: Yesterday's test was easy, and many people got 100 points.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a time noun with テスト to modify the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the test the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: で is the connecting form of an な-ending adjective. It connects the first comment to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects １００てん with 人 to refer to people who scored 100 points.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject that exists in いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: たくさん modifies the quantity 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.ch.6.n: いました is the polite past form of いる, used for people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.why: The first clause describes the test, then connects it to the actual result with で、. The following clause uses が to make the people who scored 100 points the subject of いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If し is used, the tone presents one reason or feature among several, rather than simply connecting two equal clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q21.kobun.tip: When an な-ending adjective connects sentences, use で, not くて as with an い-ending adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.vi: It is rude not to say anything after we greeted you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the side that performed the greeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects an event that has happened with the unexpected result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: 何も is used with the negative form 言わない to mean not saying anything at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns 言わない into a noun, while は makes that action the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: しつれいです is a comment about not replying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.why: のに creates a contrast between greeting someone and not replying. The phrase 言わないのは is nominalized to become the topic of the comment しつれいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with けど, the sentence still expresses contrast, but the conversational tone is lighter and more neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.tip: 何も must be used with a negative verb; it cannot be used alone to express the idea of nothing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q22.kobun.cn: Vた形 + のに; Vない形 + のは + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.vi: I hear that there will be an extremely strong typhoon tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.sk: Time + 副詞 + Aい + Nが + V普通形そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when an event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: ひじょうに modifies 強い and indicates a strong degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 強い comes before 台風 to modify the noun 台風.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the typhoon as the subject of 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです is attached after a clause to convey information that the speaker has heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.why: The time comes first, followed by an adverb and an adjective that modify 台風. Clause 台風が来る is placed before そうです to express reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If the Vますそうです form is used, the sentence means that something seems likely to happen soon, not that it is said to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうです, which reports hearsay, with そうです, which describes appearance or a prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.vi: This problem is difficult, so I do not understand it at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to point to a specific problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the problem as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: くて is the connecting form of the い-ending adjective. It connects a feature with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ぜんぜん modifies わかりません and is used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: わかりません is a negative predicate that states the result of the problem being difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.why: The adjective むずかしい changes to むずかしくて to connect a cause or state with わかりません. ぜんぜん combines with a negative form to emphasize the degree of not understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and formally, with a softer tone than the connecting form くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.kobun.tip: ぜんぜん in the basic pattern usually needs to be used with a negative predicate such as わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.tokens.3.m: difficult and; because it is difficult
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q24.tokens.6.m: do not understand; do not know
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.vi: I am working hard to make sure that I pass the N4 exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects N4 with しけん to indicate the N4 exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the goal or target that the speaker is aiming for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: かならず modifies うかる and emphasizes a certain result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ように connects the goal うかる with the action がんばっています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ています describes an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.why: The goal うかるように comes before the main action がんばっています. に marks the exam as the target, while かならず modifies the result of passing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used, the sentence emphasizes the direct purpose more strongly; ように is usually used with a goal or result that must be achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.tip: ように must come after the goal to be achieved and before the main action. It cannot be placed freely like the word for “in order to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q25.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ように + V; Nのように
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.vi: I used money from my part-time job to buy a present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb した.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause comes before the noun to modify お金.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means or source of the money used for the purchase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the item that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: A polite past-tense verb that serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.why: した comes directly before お金 to create a modifying clause, meaning money earned from a part-time job. お金で indicates the means or source of the money, while プレゼントを is the direct object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If お金で is replaced with お金を使って, the use of money is emphasized more clearly with a separate verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used, the sentence is more likely to suggest taking money from a source rather than using money as a means.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places した before お金.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.vi: On weekends, I enjoy sports with my family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time that is presented as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the group of people who perform the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what is being enjoyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: A polite present-tense verb that serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.why: The time is stated first with は. かぞくで shows who participates together, while スポーツを is the object of たのしみます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 家族で is replaced with 家族と一緒に, the meaning of being together with the family is emphasized more clearly, and the expression becomes longer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If に is used instead of は, the weekend is only a time reference and is no longer presented as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use と for every meaning of “together,” but で can indicate a group of people performing an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.vi: My mother's hobbies are traveling and reading books.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 母 with the noun 趣味 and shows ownership or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the mother's hobby as the topic to be explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects two equal nouns in a list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: です connects the topic with the explanation at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.why: 母の趣味 creates the noun phrase meaning “mother's hobby,” and then は introduces this phrase as the topic. The two hobbies are connected by と and together form the content of the pattern NはNです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with や, the list gives examples and suggests that there are other hobbies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If も is used, the meaning is “also” or “both,” not simply a connection between two hobbies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out の in 母の趣味, but の is necessary to connect the owner with the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.vi: Last night, I saw something glowing in the sky.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with よる to modify the time phrase “evening.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase serves as the time reference for the action 見ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the glowing phenomenon exists or occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: か creates an indefinite meaning after a question word and serves as the subject of ひかっている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: の nominalizes the clause ひかっている, while を marks what was seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: 見ました is the main predicate and shows an action that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.why: The time and place are placed before the main verb. Clause 何かひかっている is nominalized with の, and the whole phrase becomes the object of 見ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If のを is replaced with ことを, the sentence sounds less natural because こと usually refers to an event or abstract content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If のが見えました is used, the meaning changes to naturally seeing something or having it come into view, without emphasizing the act of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate のを as a separate word, but here の turns the whole clause about something glowing into the object of 見ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.vi: Many people are viewing the flowers under the cherry trees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a quantity word with 人 to modify the noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject performing 花見.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects さくら with 木 to refer to the cherry tree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 木 with 下 to form the phrase “under the tree.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the place where activity 花見 takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the activity being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: しています shows that the action is happening at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.why: The long noun phrase さくらの木の下で is built with two uses of の to identify the location. The subject comes before が, the activity comes before を, and then しています expresses an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 下で is replaced with 下に, the sentence focuses more on a place where something exists or on a direction toward underneath, so it is less suitable than で for an activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If しました is used, the action is understood as having already taken place, not as happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for the location in every sentence, but the place where an action takes place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.vi: I will have the clothes I bought online delivered on Sunday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means or place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 買った modifies the noun ふく that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the clothes as the object being delivered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates when the clothes will be delivered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern とどけてもらいます describes receiving help from someone to have an item delivered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.why: インターネットで states the means of buying, while 買ったふく is the phrase modifying the object ふく. The time 日よう日に comes before the action とどけてもらいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with とどけてくれます, the sentence emphasizes that another person willingly delivers it as a favor to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: The past form shows that the request to deliver it has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake とどけてもらう for meaning that they deliver it themselves, but this pattern means receiving help from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.vi: Because I want to change my image, I will wear a different color from before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that the speaker wants to change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: かえたい expresses a desire, while から connects the reason to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the standard for comparing the difference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ちがう modifies いろ, forming “a color different from before.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the color as the object of the action of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.why: The phrase かえたいですから gives the reason first, followed by the intended action. ちがう comes before いろ because this verb directly modifies the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective than から, but the main meaning is still wearing a different color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the tone becomes more hesitant, like stating an intention or thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place ちがう after いろ, but in Japanese, a modifier must come before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t72-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から（丁寧形: ですから）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 好きで connects the state of liking with the additional part that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb emphasizes a specific choice within the range of sports.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the object liked in this part of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: 好きです is the predicate at the end of the sentence and expresses a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.why: The two objects come before 好きです and are marked with が. 好きで、 connects the general preference with the emphasized preference in the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 好きな is used, this word must directly modify the noun that follows; it cannot stand at the end of a clause like 好きで、.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 好きですが, but the standard structure usually uses Nが好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q10.kobun.vi: I am the middle child of three siblings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わたし the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the group of three 人きょうだい with the position being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: まんなかです serves as the predicate and identifies the speaker’s position in the family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q10.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic, while the phrase 3人きょうだいの limits the range of comparison. The predicate まんなかです shows the speaker’s position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used, the sentence will refer to the eldest son instead of the middle position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q10.kobun.tip: の in 3人きょうだいの does not simply show possession; it connects the range with the position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.vi: At the company, even being one minute late is not allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.sk: N は + Quantity でも + Vては + いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the company as the scope or topic of the rule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: でも means “even just,” emphasizing that even the minimum amount is not allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ては connects the action with いけません to form a prohibition pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: いけません completes the Vてはいけません pattern and expresses a prohibited action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.why: かいしゃは sets the scope of the rule. 1分でも emphasizes that even a very small amount is prohibited, and then the Vてはいけません pattern states the action that must not be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means that something does not need to be done, which is the opposite of the prohibition in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.tip: Do not translate でも here as “but”; in this emphatic structure, it means “even just.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q11.kobun.cn: Vて + は + いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.vi: There is a meeting from 10 o’clock tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.sk: N は + Time から + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting time of the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks that an event exists or takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: あります is used for an event that is held or takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.why: Tomorrow is stated as the topic, and then から identifies the starting time. The subject is the meeting, and あります describes the event taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with に, the sentence only states when the meeting takes place, without emphasizing its starting time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q12.kobun.tip: For an event such as a meeting, use あります to say that it exists or takes place, not います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person stating the opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun showing the owner with the noun 意見.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the opinion as the object of the action of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: This adverb modifies the verb 言います and shows how the speaking is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q13.kobun.why: The topic is stated first with は. Then, の shows that the opinion belongs to the speaker. The object goes with を, while はっきり comes before the verb to describe how the speaking is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put を after はっきり, but を must come after the noun serving as the object, いけん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.vi: Because I have finished my homework, I will go out to play.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the homework as the subject that has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause with the action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きます is the main predicate and ends in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first, and the result comes after ので. In あそびに行く, に connects the noun showing the purpose with 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still shows a reason, but the meaning is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: ために often shows a formal purpose or reason and is less natural than ので in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand に in 遊びに行く as a place, but here に shows a purpose: going in order to play.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows that 学校 belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the school is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the period of time with 歴史, creating the phrase “a 100-year history.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks history as what exists in the school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses existence and is the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.why: The structure は ... が あります is used to say that something exists or is present in an object. The two phrases の show, respectively, ownership and the content being modified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with N は N です, the sentence expresses identification or equivalence, and does not emphasize existence like あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with あります, but the noun showing what exists in this pattern usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.vi: Please wrap this present in pink paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate an item near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the present as the thing being wrapped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects ピンク with 紙 to modify the type of paper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the tool or material used for wrapping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects the verb with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: ください completes the polite request pattern Vてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.why: The object comes first, followed by the material marked with で. The verb uses the て form and combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Vなさい is also a request, but it has a stronger commanding tone and is often used by someone in a higher position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Vてもいいです asks about or gives permission to do something; it is not a request for someone else to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に to indicate paper, but で is the particle that indicates a tool or material.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.vi: At the party, I will make many other delicious dishes besides cake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the setting or place where the cooking takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: 以外に shows the range of exclusion, while も adds the meaning that there are other things as well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the food as the object being made or cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies ごちそう and shows that the quantity is large.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: つくります is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.why: The setting is placed first with で. The phrase 以外にも limits the range to things besides cake and then adds other dishes. The object and quantity come before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: N だけでなく also means “not only N but also...,” emphasizing addition rather than the meaning “besides N.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: N しか～ない means “only N,” which is the opposite of making many dishes besides cake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out も after 以外に, but 以外にも emphasizes that there are additional objects besides that one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.vi: I am planning a Christmas party with my friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the people taking part in the planning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects クリスマス with パーティー to identify the theme of the party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the party as the object of the planning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: して is the て form of する and connects with います to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern Vています and expresses an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.why: と indicates the person working together, の modifies the noun “party,” and を marks the object being planned. けいかくしています expresses an ongoing process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: けいかくします only says that someone will plan or usually plans something, without emphasizing that the action is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: Vてあります emphasizes a state in which something has already been prepared by someone, not the process of planning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と to mark the object of 計画する, but the object must go with を; と only indicates the person doing it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.vi: My father caught a lot of fish in the sea and brought them back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the fishing took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies the quantity of fish caught.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the fishing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects fishing with 来る.
