default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: きました describes an action moving toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.why: The place comes before the object and the main verb, while つって connects fishing with きました. The Vてくる structure shows that the action was completed and then moved toward the speaker or the present point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes an action in progress or a state, without emphasizing going somewhere and bringing something back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand きました only as "arrived" and miss the combined meaning in つってきました: finishing an action and bringing something back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q19.tokens.8.m: came; did something and came back
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.vi: I gradually came to understand Japanese customs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with the following noun, creating the meaning "Japanese customs."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks what is understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies the process of change in understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ように indicates the state reached before the verb なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and describes a change that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.why: The noun にほんのしゅうかん is placed first as the topic of what is understood. わかるようになりました describes the change from not understanding to being able to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ようになっています is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the state that has formed now, rather than when it changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.tip: Do not translate ように as a separate word; in this pattern, it connects a state with なる to express a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ように ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.vi: Among means of transport, I like buses best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects のりもの with 中, creating the phrase "among the means of transport."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: で limits the range of comparison or choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object chosen as the favorite within that range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: This adverb shows the highest degree and modifies 好き.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 好きです serves as the adjective predicate な and expresses a feeling or preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.why: The phrase の中で sets the range first, and then が marks the most prominent object. いちばん comes before 好き to create the meaning "like best."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with 好き, but 好きです usually goes with が to mark the favorite object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.vi: That man took the money and ran away toward the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who performs the sequence of actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects taking the money with running away in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects えき with ほう, creating a phrase that shows direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: にげました is the main predicate and describes the completed action of running away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.why: とって stands between the two verbs to show that taking the money happened first. The phrase えきのほうへ shows direction and comes directly before the movement verb にげました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the meaning "after taking the money, he ran away" emphasizes the time order more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の in えきのほうへ, but の is necessary to connect the noun for station with the direction word 方.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.vi: In yesterday's earthquake, some people were injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の modifies じしん and identifies the earthquake that happened yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the cause of people being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks けが in the fixed phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: した in the past form comes before 人 to modify the injured person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the person who exists in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: いました is the past form of います and is used for the existence of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.why: The clause けがをした comes before 人 to identify which person is being discussed. で states the cause, while が marks the person who exists together with いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes a person who is currently injured or remains injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand けがをした人 as "a person who injured someone," but けがをする is a fixed phrase meaning "be injured."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.vi: I found the pair of shoes I had wanted for a long time at a department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: ずっと modifies ほしかった and emphasizes the lasting desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form of ほしい comes before くつ to modify the shoes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the shoes that were found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the place where the shoes were found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: みつけました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.why: ずっとほしかった is a modifying clause placed before くつ to identify which shoes. くつを is the object of みつけました, while デパートで indicates where they were found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning changes to shoes that the speaker currently wants, without emphasizing a desire that lasted in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese places ほしかった before くつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋の ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.vi: This shirt has no picture on the front; the picture is drawn on the back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the shirt is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: ではなくて negates the location on the chest and connects it to the opposite location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates where the drawing exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the drawing as already having been drawn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects 描く with あります to express the remaining result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: あります in Vてあります expresses a resulting state that someone intentionally created.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.why: ではなくて creates a contrast between the chest and the back. に indicates the location of the picture, while Vてあります shows that the picture has been drawn and is still on the shirt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence only describes a state or an action in progress. It does not emphasize an intentionally created result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で to indicate a location, but to describe where a picture is in a certain state, they need to use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.tokens.13.m: exist; be placed in a state
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q24.kobun.cn: Nではなくて + Vてある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.vi: I go shopping with my mother, and she buys me many things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who does the shopping with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase modifies the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination or purpose of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the action of going with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: This adverb modifies the act of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: 買ってもらう expresses receiving help or a benefit from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.why: 母と states who goes with the speaker, while に after ショッピング marks the destination of 行く. The two actions are connected by the て form; 買ってもらいます shows that the speaker benefits from the mother buying things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means that the speaker buys something for another person, rather than having another person buy something for them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse the direction of benefit in てもらう and あげる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.vi: Work is busy and difficult, but I will do my best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes work the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of an い-ending adjective connects the feature of being busy with the next feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects an unfavorable comment with the contrasting clause that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: がんばります is the main predicate and expresses the speaker's intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.why: は makes work the topic, and the two qualities are connected by て. が at ですが creates a contrast between the difficult situation and the determination to do one's best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If けど is used instead of ですが, the contrastive meaning stays almost the same, but the tone is more casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used, the sentence expresses a cause: because the work is difficult, the speaker will do their best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.tip: With an い-ending adjective, use くて to connect it; do not connect it directly with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q3.kobun.cn: Aいくて + Aいです・Aなです・Nです + が
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.vi: I definitely want to win tomorrow's match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the time of tomorrow with the noun “match.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes tomorrow's match the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb emphasizes the speaker's level of determination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: たいです attaches to the verb stem to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.why: The phrase あしたのしあい identifies which match is being discussed. ぜったい modifies かちたいです and makes the speaker's strong desire clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If つもりです is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the plan to win rather than the feeling of wanting to win.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If なければなりません is used instead, the sentence means that the speaker must win.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.tip: たい can only attach after a verb stem in the ます form, so use かちたい, not かつたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q4.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹 + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.vi: If you get married, what kind of man would you like?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: なら sets a hypothetical condition as the context for the question that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: どんな modifies a noun phrase and asks about its type or characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects タイプ with 男性 to form a phrase meaning “what type of man.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the person being judged as suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: いいですか creates a question about a choice or preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.why: けっこんするなら gives a hypothetical condition before the question. どんなタイプの男性 is a noun phrase in which the modifiers come before 男性, and が marks the person being chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, the sentence focuses more on the condition that the marriage actually happens or is completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence has a topic or contrastive tone and sounds less natural when asking about a choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.tip: どんな must come before the noun; it cannot be placed after the noun as in the English-style question “what kind of man.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.vi: I am hungry because I have not eaten anything since morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から indicates the starting point of the period without eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: なにも goes with a negative form to mean not eating anything at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 食べていない describes the state of not having eaten, while ので connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject that is in a hungry or empty state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: すいています describes the current state caused by an empty stomach.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.why: The cause comes first and the result comes after, following the natural order of the ので pattern. なにも combines with a negative form to emphasize not eating anything at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the causal meaning remains, but the speech is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If すきました is used, the sentence only says that the speaker has become hungry. It does not emphasize that the hunger is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.tip: なにも must be used with a negative predicate; do not use なにも with 食べました to say “eat something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は emphasizes the time or situation mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: で refers to the person performing the action or the way the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being baked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: やいて is the て form of やく, connected with みましょう to express an invitation or suggestion to try doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q7.kobun.why: A time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the person performing the action and the object of the action. The pattern Vてみましょう expresses a suggestion to try doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only means “do it” and does not emphasize trying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that で here refers to the person doing the action themselves, not a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.vi: The sweets my friend brought as a souvenir were very delicious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with the thing being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun おみやげ with おかし, forming the phrase “sweets as a souvenir.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents おかし as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the adjective おいしい to increase its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: おいしかった is the past form of an adjective ending in い, while です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ かったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.why: The two phrases の modify おかし in order, showing that the sweets were a souvenir from a friend. The topic is stated first, followed by the degree and the comment at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence changes from a past comment to a present one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use です directly after おいしかった because the polite past form is おいしかったです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.vi: Even though I am an adult, my parents sometimes still scold me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.ch.0.vi: even though I have become an adult
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: ても connects a condition with an opposite idea: even though I have become an adult, the following event still happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person performing the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: しかられる is the passive form, placed before こと to modify the event of being scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the action into a noun, while が marks it as something that happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses that an event or experience exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も; plain-form V ＋ ことがある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.why: The clause ても states a condition that goes against expectations. The action of being scolded is turned into a noun with こと, and then combined with ことがある to say that it sometimes happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that even if the condition occurs, the result remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that something sometimes happens. It does not necessarily have a passive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t73-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in a passive sentence with a place, but here it refers to the person affected or the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.vi: Please pay attention to balance in your food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 食べもの with the noun バランス to form a modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that needs attention in 気をつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the fixed object 気をつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください makes a polite request or asks someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.why: 食べものの modifies バランス, forming “the balance of the food.” The structure 気をつける uses を with 気, while てください places the reminder at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes an invitation or suggestion to pay attention together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate 気をつける word for word as “put attention”; this is a fixed phrase meaning “pay attention” or “be careful.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.vi: Because I have just moved, I cannot use my computer, so it is inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.sk: Vたばかりで ＋ N が ＋ negative potential V ので ＋ Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Vたばかりで describes something that has just happened, and で connects it to the next situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks パンコン as the object that cannot be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the result and gives a softer explanatory tone than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ふべんです is a predicate that states the result or feeling caused by the previous reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before the result: moving house has just happened, so the computer cannot yet be used, which causes inconvenience. ので connects the reason with the final comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ばかり is used instead, the sentence only emphasizes that something has just been completed, without clearly stating the situation that caused the inconvenience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used, the reason is more direct and subjective than the softer explanation with ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ので as a separate particle; it must be connected directly after the plain form of the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q10.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ばかりで; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.vi: This road has many cars, so it is dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the road is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks cars as the subject that exists in large numbers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 多い changes to 多くて to connect the cause with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: きけんです is the predicate concluding that the road is dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.cn: Aい: remove い ＋ くて
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.why: このみちは makes the evaluated object the topic, 車が多くて states the cause, and きけんです is the result. The ～くて form connects two clauses with a cause-and-result relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 多くて is replaced by 多いので, the cause-and-result relationship is stated more clearly and has a fuller explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may keep 多い unchanged when connecting sentences; an adjective ending in い must change to 多くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.vi: I cannot go to the party I wanted to attend, so I am very disappointed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The past form of たい modifies パーティー, describing the party the speaker wanted to attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 行けない changes to the て form to connect the cause with the regret in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective な 残念 combines with です to end the sentence and express a feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.why: The clause 行きたかった comes before パーティー to modify this noun. 行けなくて states the cause of the feeling 残念です, while とても modifies the degree of disappointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, it means “the party I want to attend” in the present, without emphasizing a past desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, it means “without going,” usually expressing not doing the action rather than being unable to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake 行けなくて for the ordinary meaning “do not go,” but it is the negative potential form, meaning “cannot go.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.vi: I am very happy because I finally met the star I had liked for 10 years.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle も emphasizes a long period, with the sense of “as long as.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point of a period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: すきだった is a past clause that modifies スター, referring to the star that was once liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 会う is used with に to show the person or thing met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: あえて is the て form of 会う. It connects being able to meet with the happy feeling in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: うれしいです ends the sentence by stating the speaker’s feelings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.why: The phrase 10年も前から marks the starting point of liking. The clause すきだった modifies スター, and then やっと emphasizes that the speaker had to wait a long time before finally meeting that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If やっと is replaced with ついに, the meaning is “finally,” but it emphasizes achieving the result more than the difficulty of waiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If あえて is replaced with 会うことができて, the sentence clearly emphasizes the ability to meet instead of simply connecting two actions with the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that 会う goes with に. を is not used to refer to the person being met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.vi: It is already late, so I will take my leave.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: から follows the clause おそいです to give the reason for taking one’s leave.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: そろそろ modifies the following action and shows that the appropriate time is approaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: しつれいします is a polite expression used when leaving or ending a meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.why: The clause おそいですから comes first to give the reason, while そろそろ is placed just before the main action to show that it is time to leave. しつれいします keeps the polite tone when ending the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of から, the reason sounds softer and more objective, but the sentence still gives the reason before the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If しつれいします is replaced with 帰ります, the sentence only says “I will go home,” so it has less of a polite social tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate そろそろ as “soon,” but in this sentence it means “it is time to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.vi: My monthly part-time job income is about 50,000 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.sk: N は + Time period + 副詞 + Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes アルバイト代 the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: This time phrase shows the period used to calculate the amount of money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the sentence and gives the approximate amount of part-time job income.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.why: アルバイト代は introduces the topic, and 一か月 identifies the time unit used to calculate the money. だいたい comes before the amount to reduce precision and show that it is an estimate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ５万円くらい is used, the sense of “about 50,000 yen” attaches directly to the amount, so だいたい is not needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 一か月 is replaced with 毎月, the meaning changes from “calculated for one month” to “every month,” with a clearer sense of habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place だいたい after the amount, but in this sentence it comes before the amount to modify the estimate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.vi: On a sunny day, Mount Fuji can be seen clearly from here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.sk: N は + Location から + N が + 副詞 + V見える
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the condition or situation はれの日 as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the observation point, or the place where seeing begins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing being seen in the structure 見える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: はっきり modifies 見えます and states how clear the image is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 見える describes the natural state of being visible, without emphasizing the active action of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.why: はれの日は gives the situation, ここから indicates the observation position, and ふじ山が is the object that appears within view. 見える is suitable because the sentence is about naturally being able to see something from a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見られます is used, the sentence emphasizes that the observer can view or actively look at the mountain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If はっきり is replaced with よく, the meaning is “see clearly/well,” but it places less emphasis on sharpness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 見ます in this sentence, but 見える expresses that scenery is naturally visible from a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.vi: I slipped and got injured on a snowy day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.sk: Time に + Vて + Nをしました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form of すべる connects slipping with the result of getting injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks けが as the object of する, while しました describes an event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.why: ゆきの日に puts the time at the beginning of the sentence to clarify the situation. すべって comes before けがをしました and shows that the first action happened before and led to the result of getting injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If すべったので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship “because I slipped, I got injured” is stated more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If すべりながら is used, the sentence describes two states happening at the same time, so it does not fit the relationship of one action leading to a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use すべるとけがをしました, but the て form is more natural for connecting slipping with the result of getting injured in the same sequence of events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q18.kobun.vi: This part-time job is a perfect fit for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: This part is the topic, and the comma replaces は in casual speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person being judged as a good fit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ぴったり describes a perfect fit, while よ emphasizes the information being told to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q18.kobun.why: アルバイト is the topic introduced first, and then あなたに indicates the person whose suitability is being judged. ぴったりですよ comes at the end to give the conclusion and emphasize the opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 向いている is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the job matches your abilities or personality, rather than simply being suitable in general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after あなた, but the pattern for the suitable person uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.vi: I met Mr. Kobayashi at the corner of the post office.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun before it with the noun かど after it to show possession or location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the meeting took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person whom the subject met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 会う changes to the polite past form 会いました to describe an event that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.why: ゆうびんきょくのかど forms a location phrase, while で marks where the action happened. With 会う, the person met goes with に, not with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use と会いました, the nuance is that you met Mr. Kobayashi or had an appointment with him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for the person they met, but 会う uses に for the person being met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.vi: Open the window and let fresh air in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects opening the window with letting air in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before a noun and modifies くうき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the air as the object being let in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The volitional form ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.why: まどをあけて is the preparatory action, followed by くうきを入れます as the main action. The adjective な must keep な when it comes before a noun, while ましょう gives the sentence a suggestion meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use てから, it emphasizes that the later action happens only after the earlier action is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out な in しんせんなくうき, but the adjective な needs な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.vi: Choose the cake you like from these.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the range or source of the choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: すきな modifies ケーキ; the adjective な must keep な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object being chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: えらんでください uses the Vて＋ください form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.why: 中から limits the range of choices, while すきなケーキ is a noun phrase in which すきな modifies ケーキ. The chosen object takes を, and the verb in the て form connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with えらびましょう, the sentence becomes an invitation to choose together instead of a request for the listener to choose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な in すきなケーキ because すき is often remembered as a word expressing feelings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q21.kobun.vi: Please add a little more salt and pepper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects nouns listed together in the same group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the group of spices as the object being added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: たしてください uses the Vて＋ください form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q21.kobun.why: もう少し modifies the action to show the amount being added. しおとこしょうを is one object group made of two nouns connected by と, and both are affected by たしてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use や, the sentence mentions salt and pepper as typical examples, so there may be other spices too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may repeat を after each noun, but when listing items with と, only を is needed at the end of the whole group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.vi: Because I am only 19 years old, I cannot drink alcohol.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.sk: まだ ＋ N なので ＋ N は ＋ negative potential verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I am only 19 years old
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the reason with the result; after the noun １９さい, な is needed before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks アルコール as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲めません is the polite negative potential form of 飲む, meaning that someone cannot drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.why: The reason clause １９さいなので comes before the result 飲めません. アルコールは is presented as the topic, while 飲めません uses the negative potential form to say that the action cannot be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with だから, the reason has almost the same meaning, but the expression is more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use 飲みません, the sentence only says that the person does not drink or does not want to drink. It does not emphasize inability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な before ので after a noun or adjective な, but they must say １９さいなので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.vi: My older brother took her home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of taking her home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person who is taken or brought somewhere else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the destination to which she is taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: つれてくる combines with Vて＋くる to express bringing a person from another place toward the speaker or a designated reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる；Vてくる → Vてきました in the polite past
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.why: あにが is the subject, かのじょを is the person being led, and いえに is the destination. つれてくる uses てくる because the action of bringing someone moves toward the reference location, and its polite past form is つれてきました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with つれていきました, the direction of movement is taking her away from the reference place instead of bringing her there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use かのじょと来ました, it means that the older brother came together with her, without emphasizing that he led or brought her.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse てくる and ていく; identify whether the movement is toward or away from the reference place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.vi: Last week, I went to a hot spring during a family trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N で ＋ N に ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates the time when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the situation or occasion in which the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行く is in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.why: The time and situation come before the destination, followed by the main verb. 行く goes with に to indicate the destination, while で indicates the situation or occasion in which the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing に with へ still indicates movement toward a place, but emphasizes direction more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: Using で after a means of transport means going by that means of transport, not going to that place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may use で for the destination because they are familiar with saying “go at somewhere,” but the destination of 行く usually takes に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.vi: I have finally become used to my work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.sk: Adverb ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ くる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the object that the speaker is gradually getting used to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects 慣れる with くる to express a developing change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: くる adds the meaning of a gradual change reaching the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.why: やっと modifies the whole situation and shows the result achieved after a process. 慣れる takes the object with に, while てくる expresses a gradual change continuing up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use ていく, the change is viewed from the present and continues afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes reaching a new state or ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q25.kobun.tip: Do not translate くる here simply as “come”; it shows that the change has progressed up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.vi: The weather is good, so the washed clothes dry quickly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that has a good state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: よくて is the linking form of よい. It connects a reason or state to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that becomes dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies the degree or manner in which the clothes dry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.why: 天気がよくて gives the reason or favorable condition, and the main clause is about the clothes. Each clause has its own subject, so が appears twice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If よくて is replaced with ので, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used, the reason usually sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use よいで to connect the clauses; the adjective い changes to くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.vi: When cleaning, do not forget to clean the top of the shelf as well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects そうじ with とき to indicate a time related to cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the time of cleaning the topic of the instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects たな with 上 and indicates the top part of the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: も adds the top of the shelf to the places that need cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ないで connects to the main action and means doing something without forgetting that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: きれいに modifies します and indicates the result or state that is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: します is the main predicate. It combines with きれいに to express cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.why: ときは sets the time context, while 上も is the additional object to be cleaned. わすれないで comes before きれいにします to remind the listener to do the main action without missing this place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means “please do not do that action,” which is different from “do not forget to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q4.kobun.tip: わすれないで in this sentence does not independently mean forbidding forgetting; it connects to the action that needs to be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.vi: If you go through this place, you can get to the station faster.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.sk: Nを + V辞書形と + Nに + Aいく + potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the route or place passed through with とおる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition or method with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: はやく modifies 行けます and indicates the manner or speed of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けます is the potential form of 行く and expresses that one can reach the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.why: ここをとおると states a method or condition, followed by the natural result 行けます. を is used for the route passed through, while に is used for the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と replaces たら, the condition becomes more specific and hypothetical. The result does not necessarily always occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ば is used, it emphasizes the hypothetical conditional relationship between passing through the place and being able to reach the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q5.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に with a place passed through, but とおる usually uses を to indicate a route or place that one passes through.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.vi: My hometown has not changed from 20 years ago to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Time も + Time も + Vている negative
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with the following noun and creates a possessive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the hometown is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: も adds the point 20 years ago to the comparison with the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: も shows that the state continues at the present time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ～ていません expresses a state that has not changed up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.why: The two time points both go with も to emphasize that the past and present states are the same. The phrase かわっていません at the end of the sentence is the main predicate and shows that the state is still maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the period from a starting point to an ending point, rather than the similarity between two time points.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand も as simply “also,” but here ２０年まえも今も creates the meaning “both in the past and now.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.tokens.11.m: does not exist / there is not
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q6.kobun.cn: Vている → Vていません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q7.kobun.vi: Even within the same country, there are many different customs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: でも is attached after a noun to express the range “even within...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろな modifies しゅうかん, while が marks customs as things that exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is the predicate used for the existence of things or concepts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q7.kobun.why: The phrase おなじ国でも sets the range at the beginning of the sentence. Then が introduces the object that exists. あります comes at the end to complete the structure “there are many...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If にも is used, the sentence has the sense “even within the same country...,” focusing more on the place or range where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q7.kobun.tip: でも should not be translated here as “but.” After a noun, でも usually means “even/in the range...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.vi: The speeches by the international students were all excellent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Range + Degree + Aい polite past
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the preceding noun with スピーチ and shows that the speeches belong to the international students.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the speech is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: みんな modifies the comment that follows and shows that all the speeches were like this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the degree of the adjective すばらしかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: すばらしい changes to すばらしかった to express an evaluation in the past, then です is added to keep the polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.cn: Aい: remove い + かったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.why: The topic スピーチは begins with the possessive phrase. Then みんな and とても narrow the range and increase the degree of the evaluation. The adjective is in the past form at the end because the comment is about speeches that have already taken place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence shifts to the present or becomes a general comment, without emphasizing that the speeches already took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily forget to change the adjective ending in い to ～かった when talking about a past event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.vi: I prefer strict teachers to kind teachers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person expressing the preference and sets the basis for the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the object used as the standard for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: のほうが marks the side chosen as superior in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きです is an adjective predicate な that expresses the speaker's preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.why: N1より states the comparison standard, while N2のほうが marks the object rated higher. 好きです comes at the end to conclude the speaker's preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence becomes a question asking the listener to choose one of the two objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes not liking N2 as much as N1, which reverses the direction of the evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place より after the object they like, but より must come after the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t74-q9.kobun.cn: N1 より ＋ N2 のほうが ＋ Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.vi: The company's lunch break is from 12 o'clock to 1 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.sk: N の N は ＋ Time から ＋ Time まで ＋ です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 会社 with 昼休み to modify lunch break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes lunch break the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the starting point of the time period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: まで indicates the ending point of the time period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: です concludes that the lunch break lasts from the starting point to the ending point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.why: The phrase 会社の昼休み forms the noun phrase “the company's lunch break”, and then は states the topic. から and まで form a pair showing the beginning and end limits of the time period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This pair indicates a continuous period between two points and can be used for time or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: に indicates one specific point in time and does not fully express a period with a beginning and an end like から〜まで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit から or まで, but to say “from〜to〜”, this full pair is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.vi: I checked the weather forecast, took an umbrella, and went outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the weather forecast as what was viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of viewing with the next action in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the umbrella as what was carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects carrying the umbrella as an accompanying state with going outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 出かけました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.why: The two forms て connect the actions of viewing and carrying the umbrella with the main action of going outside. Both earlier actions have the same omitted subject because it is clear from the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてから is used, it emphasizes that the later action starts only after the earlier action has finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate every form て as “and”; here, て also shows sequence and an accompanying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.vi: After losing 3 kilograms, I was able to fit into the tight trousers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.sk: Quantity ＋ Vたら ＋ Aい ＋ Nが ＋ past potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: A phrase showing the amount of weight lost, modifying the verb やせる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb やせる in the たら form connects a condition or time with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ほそい comes before the noun パンツ to modify the trousers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the object that became possible to fit into.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: はけました is the past potential form of はく and expresses that I was able to wear them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.why: The clause やせたら places a condition or time before the result はけました. The adjective ほそい comes before パンツ, while が marks the trousers as the object that can be fitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with やせると, the sentence leans toward a natural or inevitable result whenever weight is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake はける for “go”; with trousers, shoes, and socks, はく means to wear or put on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q11.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなだ・Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.vi: Because the design of these shoes is very nice, I will buy both the red and blue versions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Nが ＋ Aいので ＋ NとNを ＋ Adverb ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents these shoes as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks design as the element evaluated as good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason with the buying action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: と connects the two colors into a list, while を marks the whole list as the objects being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: りょうほう modifies the buying action and emphasizes buying both colors.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.why: The sentence first presents the shoes, then gives the reason with ので, and only after that mentions the buying action. と connects the two colors, を marks them as the objects being bought, and りょうほう confirms that the range includes both.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the reason becomes more direct and more subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place りょうほう before a noun, but in this sentence りょうほう comes after the object phrase and modifies the buying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.vi: This summer, I want a pair of sandals to wear at the beach.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ことし with なつ to create the phrase “this year's summer”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the time when the speaker wants to use the sandals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause うみではく comes before サンダル to modify the type of sandals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the desired object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: ほしい expresses the desire to have an object and goes with が to mark that object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.why: The phrase うみではく is placed directly before サンダル to specify that these are sandals used at the beach. に indicates the time, で indicates the place of the action はく, and が goes with ほしい to mark the desired object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used, the sentence means wearing the sandals toward the beach, not wearing them at the beach.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with ほしい, but the standard pattern is Nがほしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.vi: Because I am busy and have not eaten much, I look like I am about to collapse.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.sk: Aいくて + あまり + Vていないので + Vるそうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: 忙しい changes to いそがしくて to connect the reason to the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: あまり is used with the negative form 食べていない to express a small amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ている in the negative form describes a state of not having eaten yet or not eating for a period of time, while ので gives the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.ch.3.vi: look like I am about to collapse
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: そうです attaches to the る form of a verb to describe something that seems about to happen based on present signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.cn: Aいくて; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nな + ので; Vますます + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.why: Two reasons are connected in sequence: being busy and not eating enough. They then lead to a prediction that the person is about to collapse. あまり must be used with a negative form, while そうです is based on present signs, not on something heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If たおれるそうです is used, it means that someone says the person will fall or collapse. It is not a prediction based on the person’s present condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse あまり with an affirmative sentence; the pattern あまり～ない means “not very much.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.vi: I hear that onions clean the blood in the body.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes onion the topic of the reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks blood as the object that is cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: きれいに is the adverb form of the adjective な. It shows the resulting state before する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: してくれる describes the cleaning action as being done for the benefit of the speaker or someone on the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです attaches to a clause in the plain form to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.why: Onion is the topic, and blood is the object affected by きれいにする. くれる adds a benefit for the speaker’s side, while そうです at the end shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: In たおれそうです, そうです is a guess based on signs; in this sentence, it reports information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out に in きれいにする; the adjective な must first change into an adverb with に before する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.tokens.7.m: do something for the speaker or the speaker’s side
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q15.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.vi: Sometimes I drop a cup and accidentally break it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.sk: Adverb + Nを + Vて + Vてしまう + ことが + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the cup as the thing that is dropped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: おとして is the て form of おとす. It connects dropping the cup with the following action of breaking it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまう describes an action that has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: こと turns the entire preceding action into a noun, while が marks it as something that happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: ことがあります describes something that sometimes happens or has happened before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.why: The two consecutive actions are connected by the て form: dropping the cup and then breaking it. てしまう emphasizes the unfortunate result, and ことがある then turns the whole event into something that can happen sometimes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If てしまう is omitted, the sentence only says that the person sometimes breaks a cup. The sense of accidentally doing it or regretting it is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ことがあります as “a thing,” but the pattern Vることがあります here means that the event sometimes happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q16.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; Vる・Vない・Vた + ことがある
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.vi: Now, let’s put the clothes that we are not wearing into the closet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the time being made the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.ch.1.vi: clothes that are not being worn
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the clothes as the object being stored.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the place where the object is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects putting the clothes in with putting them away for later.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: ておく describes doing something in advance to keep the needed state; ましょう creates a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first and is marked with は. The object goes with を, the destination goes with に, and then the て form connects to おく to show that something is done in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes that the item has already been put away and is now in that state, rather than emphasizing a suggestion to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate ておく as only “put,” but this pattern also implies doing something in advance to prepare or maintain a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q17.kobun.cn: Vて + おく; Vます-stem + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.vi: I will show my friend from my hometown around Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun くに with 友だち to modify “friend.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who is shown around or guided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks Tokyo as the place being introduced or shown around.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb あんないする is the predicate and is in the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.why: の identifies the friend as being from or belonging to the hometown. The person being shown around goes with に, while the place being introduced or visited goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: It means introducing a person or thing, and does not necessarily mean directly taking that person sightseeing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use を for the person being shown around; that person usually goes with に in the structure 案内する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q18.kobun.cn: N に + N を + Vする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.vi: In a city with a port, you can hear the sound of boats.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the port as the subject that exists in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ある is the predicate of a clause describing existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause みなとがある modifies まち; では identifies where the main sentence takes place and adds a sense of scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects ふね with 音 to show that the sound comes from boats.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks sound as the object perceived through hearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: 聞こえる describes sound entering the ears naturally, without emphasizing that the listener actively listens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.why: The clause みなとがある comes before まち to identify the type of city. After the place is stated with では, the sentence uses 音が聞こえる because sound is something that is perceived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes actively listening to a sound, while 聞こえます describes a sound being heard naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 聞こえる, but the sound object in this pattern goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; Nでは + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.vi: After writing this, please get the section manager’s signature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the thing being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form of 書く combines with たら to state a condition or a time after completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the person from whom a signature is requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the thing received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the verb もらう with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ください changes the previous action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.why: The clause 書いたら gives the condition or time before the main request. The receiver is marked by に, the thing received is marked by を, and もらってください expresses a request for the listener to receive it as a favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あとで, the meaning “after” is clearer and has less of a conditional feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Used directly, it only asks someone to do the action. It no longer has the meaning “please receive it for me” in もらってください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use に for サイン; the thing received goes with を, while the person who gives or receives it usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q2.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.vi: I left something on the bus yesterday, but I got it back today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the item was left behind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object used with the verb phrase わすれものをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 今日 identifies the time of the action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects 帰る with くる to express returning toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: くる completes the action of moving back in the phrase かえってくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.why: The first clause gives the time, place, and item left behind, then が creates a transition. The second clause uses てくる to express returning to the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: It only says that someone returned, without stressing the direction of return or its connection to a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.tip: Do not understand てくる as only two separate verbs; in this sentence, it gives the feeling of “returning here/to this point”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q20.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる; V普通形 ＋ が
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.vi: My older brother plays soccer very well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the older brother the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the sport in which the older brother is skilled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: うまい is the い adjective used as the predicate, while です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.why: The sentence makes the older brother the topic with は, then identifies the area of skill with が. とても modifies the degree of the adjective うまい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means “skilled,” but 上手です is usually more neutral and polite than うまいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes that something is the speaker's or the subject's strong point, not only an evaluation of demonstrated skill.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.tip: With 上手い or 上手だ, the sport or area of skill usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q21.kobun.cn: N は ＋ N が ＋ Aい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.vi: When I had just arrived in Japan, I was very lonely, but now I am fine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 来たばかりの modifies とき and identifies the time immediately after arriving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a time, while は makes that period the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い takes the past form to describe the state at that time, and が connects it to the contrasting present situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: は sets the present as a point of comparison with the time when the speaker had just arrived in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: だいじょうぶです serves as the predicate and states the current condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.why: The phrase 来たばかりのときは identifies the time immediately after arriving in Japan and serves as the topic of the first clause. が connects the past state with the present state, while 今は creates a clear contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: It only means “when I arrived,” without emphasizing that the arrival was recent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: It means “after arriving,” focusing more on the time sequence than on the moment immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ばかり with “only,” but Vたばかり here means “have just finished doing something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q22.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ばかりだ／のN; 普通形 ＋ が; Nは ＋ Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.vi: There is a strange smell from the kitchen, so I will go and check, then come back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates where the smell comes from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: へんな modifies におい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the cause clause with the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects 見る with 来る to express going to check and then returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: きます completes the predicate 見てきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.why: The source phrase uses から before the phenomenon においがします. から gives the reason, while 見てきます expresses going to check and then returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that someone will go and check, without emphasizing the return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand から as a place because it is often translated as “from,” but here it also connects the reason to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.vi: Please feel free to take this book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ Adv ＋ お＋Vますdropます ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects こちら with 本 to modify 本.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the book the topic of the instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: じゆう comes before おとり to modify how the action is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: お comes before the continuative form 取り to create a polite expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: ください changes the phrase おとり into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.cn: Vますdropます ＋ ください; 自由に ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.why: こちらの本は is the topic phrase, followed by the manner じゆう before the request おとりください. The pattern お＋the continuative form of the verb＋ください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the request becomes more formal and emphasizes the listener's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit お in お取りください, but お helps the request keep its polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.vi: I intended to get up early and study, but in the end I could not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: あさはやく modifies the time 起きて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects getting up with studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content of the intention expressed by 思いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects the intention to the opposite result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: でした acts as a polite past predicate, showing that the intention could not be carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.why: 起きて connects two actions in sequence. The intention to study is placed in quotation marks with と after the volitional form, and then が signals that the result was not as planned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes an existing plan or intention, not the thought at that moment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence says that the person tried to start doing something, rather than only having the intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use と思いました with the plain verb form, but the intention that follows needs the volitional form, such as しよう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q25.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と ＋ 思う; V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹＋だ・N＋だ ＋ が
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.vi: I am using a bus to go to school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the means of transport used in 利用する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 利用しています is the ている form of 利用する, expressing current or regular use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.why: 学校まで states the endpoint of the route, while バスを is the object of 利用する. The ています form shows that bus use is continuing or happening regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern directly means “go by N,” focusing on the action of traveling by that means of transport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 使う also means to use, but 利用する often suggests using a service or means of transport for a purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ています as “be doing” in every case; here it can also refer to a habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.vi: This test has not only a front side but also a back side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before テスト to identify the test being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the test the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: だけではなくて connects the limited negative content to the additional part that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も adds the back side to the scope being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate showing the existence of the front and back sides.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: よ tells the listener about information or a discovery that needs attention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.why: は makes the test the topic, then だけではなくて denies the idea of “only the front side.” も adds the back side, creating the structure “not only〜but also〜,” while あります concludes that it exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If only だけ is used, the sentence is limited to the front side and does not add the back side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: も means “also,” and is used to add a similar object to the previous information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use だけではなくて as a separate phrase; this pattern needs an additional part with も in the second clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q4.kobun.cn: N・V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nではなくて ＋ Nも ＋ あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.vi: When I received a ring, I was so happy that I burst into tears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the thing received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the act of receiving something with the emotion that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to くて to connect a cause or state to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of the verb connects with しまった, creating the pattern Vてしまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてしまった describes something that happened completely, often with an unintended feeling or strong emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう; past: Vてしまった
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.why: The actions and emotions are connected in sequence by the て form, with receiving the ring leading to happiness. Vてしまった emphasizes that the result, bursting into tears, happened completely and was difficult to control.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vておく, it means doing something in advance or preparing in advance, without the unintended nuance of bursting into tears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand しまった as only “did,” but the pattern Vてしまう also expresses completion or regret and something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.vi: I drove myself out for a drive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who directly performs the driving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of driving with the action of going out by car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the purpose or activity targeted in the structure ドライブに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.why: The subject is stated with が, and then the driving action comes first to add the means of going. ドライブに行く shows going for a relaxing drive or going out by car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vながら is used, the two actions happen at the same time, emphasizing doing one thing while driving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.tip: を should not be used with わたし in this sentence; the person performing the action uses が, while the affected object uses を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q6.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; N に行く
