default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.vi: Because I walked all day, I will probably sleep well tonight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.sk: Time ＋ V普通形 ので ＋ N は ＋ Adv ＋ potential V ＋ でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the length of time during which the walking continued.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause in the first part with the result or prediction in the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes “today” the topic of the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies ねむれる, indicating how well or how much someone sleeps.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The potential form shows that after walking all day, the person can sleep well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: でしょう is placed at the end of the sentence to express a gentle prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.why: The cause clause with ので comes first, followed by the time topic 今日. よく modifies the ability to sleep, while でしょう turns that statement into a prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is more direct and subjective, while ので is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょう is replaced with かもしれない, the level of certainty is lower and only a possibility is stated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ので after a noun, as in Nので; with nouns and adjectives な, it must be connected with なので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.vi: When I ride a motorcycle, the wind feels very pleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the means of transport used for running.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition or action with a natural result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the wind as the subject experiencing the pleasant feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies 気持ちいい, indicating the degree of pleasantness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective phrase acts as the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.why: で indicates the means of transport, while と connects the action of running with the result that is felt. The wind is the subject of the feeling, so が is used, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたら is used, the condition is more hypothetical and does not emphasize a natural result like と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse で and に; means of transport use で, while に usually indicates a destination or purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.vi: The tallest building in Japan has been completed, hasn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で limits the comparison to Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies 高い to create the meaning of the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 高い comes before ビル to modify “building.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the building as the subject that was built or completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: できました expresses completion, while ね is used to confirm or share an opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.why: で sets the comparison range, then いちばん高い creates a modifying phrase for ビル. ビルが is the subject of できました, while ね adds a friendly tone of confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: もっとも also means “the most,” but it is more formal and more common in writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Nより高い only means higher than one specific object; it does not claim to be the highest in the whole range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place the adjective after the noun, as in Vietnamese; in Japanese, 高い must come before ビル.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t75-q9.kobun.cn: Nで + いちばん + Aい・Aな + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.vi: This bird is said to be the most beautiful in the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies the noun とり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the bird is the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で limits the range of the adjective きれい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: もっとも modifies きれい to create a superlative comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the content that people say.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: 言われています uses the passive and progressive forms to express an opinion that is being passed on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.why: で sets the comparison range, while もっとも comes before the adjective to create the superlative meaning. The content of the opinion is introduced by と and is the subject of the passive sentence 言われています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the tone becomes more cautious, like a guess believed to be true.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate で as “at,” but in this sentence で only marks the comparison range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.vi: After finishing the drink, wash the plastic bottle and throw it away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause with たら states the condition or time for carrying out the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the plastic bottle as the object that is washed and thrown away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects washing with the following action of throwing away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.why: The time clause with たら comes first, followed by the object を and a sequence of actions connected by て. ましょう at the end turns the sentence into a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with てから, the sentence more clearly emphasizes that the drink must be finished before washing and throwing away the bottle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If たあとで is used, it means “after finishing the drink,” but the tone for presenting the time is more neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that たら must attach to the past form of the verb, even though the meaning may refer to the present or future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q10.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら、; Vて + Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.vi: All of us are taking good care of the cat that my father picked up and brought home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who picked up the cat and brought it home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb phrase comes before the noun ねこ to modify “cat.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the cat as the object that everyone takes care of.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the people who carry out the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The form に of the adjective な changes たいせつ into an adverb that modifies しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: しています expresses an action that is continuing in the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.why: The clause 父がひろってきた comes before ねこ to identify which cat it is. After the object を, みんなで shows the people acting together, while ています shows the continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If きた is removed, the sentence only says “the cat my father picked up,” without emphasizing that he brought it home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If します is used, the sentence refers to a shared action or plan and does not emphasize that it is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may misunderstand で as a place, but in みんなで it refers only to the group of people doing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q11.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; Aな + に; Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.vi: I received a watch as a gift to celebrate passing the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects ごうかく with おいわい, creating a phrase for a gift or congratulations on passing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the purpose or occasion for receiving the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the watch as the item received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいました is the polite past form, expressing that something was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.why: The phrase ごうかくのおいわい identifies the purpose of the gift, and に connects this phrase with the action of receiving. The item received comes before を, while the verb もらいました ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If として is used, the sentence emphasizes that the watch was given as a congratulatory gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If で is used, the sentence can more easily mean receiving a gift at a congratulatory occasion or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate に as “for,” but in おいわいに it only indicates the purpose or occasion of receiving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q12.kobun.cn: NのN; Nに + V; Vます → Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.vi: No matter how difficult it is, we have to keep trying...
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: どんなに modifies an adjective to show that no matter how high the degree is, the result does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: でも connects with the adjective な to create a concessive meaning: even if it is difficult, still.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ないと is a shortened form of ないといけない and expresses obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The ellipsis shows that the required conclusion has been omitted but is still understood by the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.why: どんなにたいへんでも creates a concessive clause, stating a difficult situation without changing the requirement that follows. ないと means “must do,” while the rest is omitted with an ellipsis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If なければならない is used, the obligation is expressed more fully and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If てください is used, the sentence becomes a direct request instead of expressing an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit いけない after ないと, but in spoken language this part is often omitted when the context is clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q13.kobun.cn: どんなに + Aいくても / Aなでも / Vても; Vないと + いけない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.vi: I am studying in a university department.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that わたし is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where a learning activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects the noun がくぶ to the following noun, expressing possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: The form ています describes an activity that is being carried out or continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.why: The topic わたし comes first, followed by the place of study with で and the object of study with を. The form ています shows that the studying is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with べんきょうします, it only refers to studying in general and does not stress that it is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q14.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use に to indicate the place of an activity, but the place where an activity takes place must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.vi: I attend classes every day without taking a day off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: も follows a period of time and combines with a negative form to stress that not even one day is missed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ないで connects an action that is not done with the main action, meaning without taking a day off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the object or activity that the speaker attends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: しています describes continuing attendance at class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.why: １日も combines with 休まない to stress a frequency of zero. ないで connects the state of not taking a day off with the main action, while に marks the class as the object attended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern stresses doing the main action without taking a day off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 休まずに is used, the meaning is similar, but the style is more written and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.vs.2.d: If 出ています is used, the sentence focuses on being present in class rather than stressing participation in the lesson.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand も as also, but in １日も休まないで it combines with a negative form to stress that no day is missed at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q15.kobun.cn: Nも + Vない; Vないで; Nに + 出席する; Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.vi: The Japanese language test is held in July and December.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.sk: N と + N に + N の + N が + passive verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects two time points mentioned together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the test is held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects にほんご with しけん, creating the modifying phrase “Japanese language test”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the action being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in a polite passive form and describes the test being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.why: The two time points come at the beginning of the sentence and are connected by と. Then に indicates when the event takes place. しけんが is the grammatical subject of the passive verb おこなわれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q16.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse に, which indicates time, with で, which indicates the place where an event is held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.vi: Because I want to become a teacher, I will enter the education department.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the result or status achieved after なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: たい expresses a desire, while ので connects the reason to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the place or organization that the speaker will enter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.why: Clause なりたいので gives the reason, and the main clause きょういくがくぶに入ります gives the intended action. に appears twice, but the first use indicates the result of なる, while the second indicates the direction toward the place to be entered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use で after 先生, but the correct pattern is Nに なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な＋ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.vi: I want to give my father something that will make him happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs or experiences the action よろこぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before もの to modify もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: もの is modified by clause よろこぶ, while を marks what is given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: たい attaches to the form of the verb without ます to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.cn: Vます形 without ます + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.why: Clause 父がよろこぶ comes before もの to identify the thing that will make the father happy when he receives it. ものを is the direct object of あげたいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If たい is removed, the sentence only says that the speaker will give something and no longer stresses the desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.kobun.tip: English learners may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese places よろこぶ before もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q18.tokens.5.m: want to give, want to offer
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.vi: I want to visit my older sister who lives in France.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the older sister lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: すむ in dictionary form comes before あね to modify older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks older sister as the person being visited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: たい expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.cn: Vます形 without ます + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.why: フランスにすむ is the modifying clause for あね and helps identify which older sister. あねを is the direct object of the verb たずねたいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来た is used, the meaning is “the older sister who came from France,” not “who lives in France.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q19.kobun.tip: English learners may understand にすむ as a phrase describing going to France, but に here indicates a place of residence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.vi: I have a fever and a sore throat, so it seems that I have a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks the first symptom and means also.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: し connects one reason in a series of symptoms.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: も marks the second symptom added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: し continues to connect another reason or sign.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: どうも modifies the statement ようです and expresses a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: の connects the noun かぜ with ようだ in a pattern of comparison or guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: ようです ends the sentence with a guess based on signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.why: し lists several signs as the basis for a conclusion. どうも combines with Nのようです to give a mild guess based on the symptoms.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning of the guess is almost the same, but the expression is more casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the sentence focuses more on information heard from someone or a commonly seen feature than on direct signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use かぜようです, but before ようだ, の is needed when the preceding word is a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ようだ; V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ し
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.vi: I made an appointment with a friend to go and see a movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.sk: N と ＋ N を ＋ Vます形 remove ます ＋ に ＋ V辞書形 ＋ N を ＋ する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: と refers to the person who goes to see the movie with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the movie as the object of 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The remove form ます of 見る combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 行く in its dictionary form comes before やくそく to modify the appointment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks やくそく as the content carried out in しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.cn: Vます形 remove ます ＋ に ＋ V; V普通形 ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.why: 見に行く is the purpose phrase “go to see,” and this whole phrase comes before やくそく to identify the content of the appointment. やくそくをしました is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 映画を見る is used, the sentence only means “an appointment to see a movie,” without emphasizing going together to the place where it is shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 見るに行く, but purpose must use the remove form ます: 見に行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q21.kobun.vi: I bought a ticket for a classical concert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun クラシックコンサート with きっぷ to modify the type of ticket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the ticket as the direct object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q21.kobun.why: The phrase クラシックコンサートのきっぷ is formed with の to identify the type of ticket. This noun phrase is the object of を, while 買いました is the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 行く is used, the meaning is a ticket for going to the concert, not simply a ticket for the concert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の between two nouns, but Japanese needs の to connect and modify nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.vi: It is sad that a war is taking place somewhere in the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects せかい with どこか to modify the place that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows the place where the action せんそうしている takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the clause into a noun, while は makes that action the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: かなしい modifies こと, forming the phrase “a sad thing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: こと nominalizes the previous content, while です ends the polite judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.why: The clause せんそうしている is nominalized with の so that the whole action becomes the topic with は. かなしい modifies こと, and then です ends the polite comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is replaced with ことは, the meaning is still “the act of...,” but the tone is more general and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget の after a clause when they want to make the whole action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q23.kobun.vi: A very large typhoon is approaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the state 来ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: まで shows the limit that the typhoon has reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ています uses the ている form to describe an ongoing process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q23.kobun.why: とても modifies 大きい, and this whole phrase comes before たいふう to describe the typhoon. が connects the subject with 来ています, and まで states the point reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 近くに is used, the sentence only states that something is nearby; 近くまで emphasizes the process of moving closer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use まで as a simple place particle; it emphasizes a limit or a point reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q24.kobun.vi: Because the bag was very expensive, I paid by card.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result, and 高い modifies バッグ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the means used for payment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: はらいました is a polite past-tense verb that states the result of the previous cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q24.kobun.why: とても 高い describes how expensive バッグ is. なので gives the reason first, then カードで states the means and はらいました states the completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced with から, the causal meaning is almost the same, but the expression is more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q24.kobun.tip: With い-adjectives, connect directly to ので; do not add な after 高い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.vi: I always get my hair cut at the same salon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the hair is the object being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies the action きっています and shows frequent repetition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: おなじ modifies びよういん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the place where the hair-cutting action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: きっています expresses a habit or a repeated action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.why: は sets the hair as the topic, while いつも shows a repeated action. で identifies the place, and きっています expresses the habit of getting a haircut.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If びよういんで is replaced with びよういんに, に usually shows a direction or destination, so it is not suitable for showing the place where an action directly takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q25.kobun.tip: When an action takes place at a location, use で instead of に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.vi: Recently, Mr. Hayashi has looked happy; as expected, I hear that he has gotten a girlfriend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 時点 ＋ Aいremoveいそうですが、 ＋ Adv ＋ N が ＋ Vた ＋ そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Mr. Hayashi the topic of both statements.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: このごろ indicates the time when the state is observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: そうだ follows the adjective stem うれし and describes appearance, while が connects to the next information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: やはり modifies the whole statement that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the newly appearing subject in the structure 彼女ができる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: できた is the past form and shows that getting a girlfriend happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: そうです follows the plain form to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.cn: Aいdropい・Aなdropな + そうだ; V普通形 + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.why: The first clause describes appearance with an adjective + そうだ, and after が, it gives heard information using Vた + そうです. やはり connects the following judgment with the earlier feeling that it was as expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: With this form, そうです means that it is said to be happy, not that it looks happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, it means that it seems likely to happen or that something may be possible, not that it is said that he got a girlfriend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the two types of そうです: the first describes appearance, while after Vた it reports information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.vi: The report is due next week, but please try to submit it early.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.sk: N は + Deadline までですが + Adverb + Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the report is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates a deadline, while ですが connects a contrasting idea to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: なるべく modifies the act of submitting and expresses the greatest effort possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: はやく is the adverb form and modifies 出してください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: A verb in the て form combines with ください to make a polite request or ask someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.why: The sentence first states the topic and deadline, then uses ですが to shift to a request. なるべく and はやく respectively modify the act of submitting the report.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the obligation to submit it rather than making a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ください with the simple meaning “for me,” but after Vてください it forms the request “please do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.vi: Because I forgot something, I went back home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action する in the phrase わすれものをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause to the result; した is the past form of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement to the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: もどりました is the main predicate and uses the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first, followed by the result, following the natural order of a Japanese sentence. へ attaches to the destination of the action of going back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から keeps almost the same causal meaning, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を directly with わすれもの to express “forget something”; the natural phrase is わすれものをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + な + ので・N + な + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.vi: Because I like running, I started running marathons.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の turns the verb はしる into a noun, while が marks the thing that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: すきで is the linking form of the adjective な, used to connect the reason to the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks marathon as the object of はじめました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: はじめました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.why: の nominalizes はしる so that the whole phrase “running” can be the subject of すき. After the reason すきで comes the new action はじめました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also expresses liking to do something, but it emphasizes the topic “running” more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.tip: After the verb when saying “like doing something,” Vietnamese learners may forget の before が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + の + が + Aな/Aな + で
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.vi: I always treasure the diamond my mother gave me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source or the person who gives something in an act of receiving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause もらった comes before ダイヤ to modify the diamond.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the diamond as the object being treasured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: だいじに is the adverb form and shows how しています is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: しています describes an ongoing state or habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.why: The clause もらった is placed directly before ダイヤ to identify which diamond it is. だいじに comes before しています to describe the way the object is kept and treasured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes that the mother gave the diamond, while もらった emphasizes that the speaker received it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use 大事なに, but when changing the adjective な into an adverb before する, they must use 大事に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.vi: I sometimes have meals with Mr. Yamada.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.sk: Nとは + Frequency adverb + Adverb + Nします
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: とは marks a person who participates together or the object being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: いっしょに modifies the action of eating and shows that it is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: しょくじします is the main predicate and combines the noun 食事 with します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.why: The person eating together is placed at the beginning and attached to とは. The adverbs たまに and いっしょに come before the predicate to add frequency and manner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Using only と merely states the person acting together and does not create the topic-marking nuance of とは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate とは as one fixed word; in this sentence, it is close to “with Mr. Yamada” or “as for Mr. Yamada.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.vi: Are there any stores nearby that sell food at low prices?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun or noun phrase to indicate something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the location where the store exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks food as the subject described as cheap in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 安い is the predicate of the clause modifying みせ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes the store selling cheap food the main topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: ありますか asks whether the store exists at the stated location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.why: The phrase しょくりょうひんが安い comes before みせ to modify the store. に indicates where the store exists, while は makes the whole store the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: The pattern の can also modify 店, but it is less direct and does not clearly state that the food is the subject of the adjective 安い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t76-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place 安い after みせ, but a relative clause in Japanese must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.vi: Once a year, I have my health checked at a hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.sk: Time period に + Number of times + N で + N を + Vて もらいます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates a repeated time point or cycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: いちど adds the number of times an action is performed during the time cycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the check is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the body as the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: てもらいます expresses receiving help or a checking service from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.why: 一年にいちど places the frequency at the beginning of the sentence. Then で states the place where the action is performed, を marks the body being checked, and てもらいます shows that the speaker receives a service or help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 調べます is used, the sentence only says that the speaker checks something personally or that a check generally takes place. It does not emphasize that another person does it as a service.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q1.kobun.tip: てもらう places the person who receives the benefit as the implied subject, so it should not be translated mechanically as “receive.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.vi: Saying goodbye to a truly dear friend is very painful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と indicates the person who takes part in the farewell; たいせつな modifies 友だち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the verb phrase さよならする into a noun, while は marks this phrase as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb とても modifies the adjective expressing emotion at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: つらい is the predicate and expresses the speaker's feelings about the farewell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.why: The verb phrase is nominalized with の so that it can be the topic with は. とても comes before the adjective to strengthen the emotion, while と identifies the person who is leaving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のは with ことは still refers to saying goodbye, but the tone is more objective and general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の when they want to make the whole verb phrase the topic, which makes さよならするは grammatically incorrect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形 + のは + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.vi: When I asked a stranger for directions, they kindly showed me the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person who is asked; しらない modifies 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the content of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The past form 聞いた combines with ら to create a condition or time point and leads to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な changes to the に form to modify the verb おしえる and show how the directions were given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects おしえる with くれる to create a sequence of actions and express receiving a benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: くれる in the polite past form shows that the stranger did the action for the speaker's benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, while the content of the question goes with を. Vたら sets asking for directions as the starting point, and then Vてくれる describes the action of helping the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to と, the sentence suggests a natural result or something that always happens immediately after asking, rather than one specific occasion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes that the speaker asked for or received directions, instead of viewing the action from the guide's side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for the person being asked, but the person goes with に, while the content of the question goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q11.kobun.cn: Vたら、 + Vて + くれる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.vi: This box is in the way, so please move it to the next room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the box as the topic of the explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is in the way
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the moving action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.why: The sentence first states the condition of the box, then uses ですから to give the reason for the request. に marks the destination, while Vてください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective than the direct tone of ですから.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で for the destination, but with verbs meaning move or carry to a place, the destination usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q12.kobun.cn: N・Aな + ですから、 + Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.vi: Your Japanese has improved a lot in just one year, hasn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the time needed to achieve a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object whose ability has changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb だいぶ modifies the degree of improvement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The に form of the adjective な indicates the resulting state after a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, while ね shows agreement or confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.why: で sets the time limit for the process of change, が marks the object that improves, and に indicates the achieved state. だいぶ adds degree, while ね creates a friendly comment-like tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If じょうずだ is used, the sentence only says that someone is good at Japanese and does not emphasize the process of becoming good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Nにする describes the subject actively making something become that state, not changing by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use じょうずだ after the subject, but before なる, the adjective な must change to the に form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.vi: The bus did not come for a long time, so I ended up being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that has not arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: なかなか is used with a negative form to express that something is difficult to happen or that one waits for a long time without success.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative form なくて connects the cause to the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the action of being late with しまう to create a complete verb phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてしまう in the past expresses a completed event together with regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason that the bus did not come, while the second clause gives the result of being late. なかなか combines with the negative form to emphasize the long wait, and てしまう adds a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あまり～ない, the meaning is that something does not come often or many times, without emphasizing a long wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Using only Vました reports that the event happened, but does not clearly express regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use なかなか with an affirmative sentence, but the meaning “for a long time without” requires a negative verb form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q14.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ なくて、＋ Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.vi: At today's meeting, the director will speak first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: きょうの modifies かいぎ and shows which meeting it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes today's meeting the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: さいしょに modifies the action あいさつをします and shows the order of performance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person who performs the speaking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the content of the action performed by the director.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: します is the predicate and expresses a polite action in the present or future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.why: The phrase きょうのかいぎは puts the topic first, then gives the order, the person performing the action, and the object of the action. The particle が identifies the director as the speaker, while を marks the content of the speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 最初は is used, it means “at first,” focusing on the early stage rather than the order of performance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は for the person performing the action, but in this sentence the person must be marked with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.vi: I heard that he is rich; sure enough, he is wearing things that look very expensive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes him the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content that was heard; だ follows the noun おかねもち in the quotation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 聞きましたが connects the information heard to the following comment with a mild contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: なるほど is an adverb that confirms what was just heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 高そうな modifies もの; を marks the things as the object of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: きています uses the ている form to express the state of wearing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.cn: Nだ ＋ と ＋ 聞く; Aい remove い ＋ そうな ＋ N; Vて形 ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.why: The content that was heard comes before と聞きました, then が shifts to the speaker's comment. The Aそうな pattern comes before a noun to describe how an object looks, while ています expresses the current state of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 高いようなもの is used, the meaning is “things like they are expensive,” which is less natural and does not focus on appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If 高いもの is used, it states that the things are expensive, rather than only saying that they look expensive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 高そうもの, but な must be added before the noun: 高そうなもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.vi: If I get the chance, I want to go to Japan as much as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that exists in the conditional clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form あった combines with ら to create a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase modifies the action 行きたい and shows the greatest possible degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement toward 行きたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The form 行きたい expresses the speaker's desire, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.why: The clause あったら gives the condition first, and then states the desire 行きたい. へ is used because にほん is the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If チャンスがあるなら is used, the meaning is close to “if there really is a chance,” while あったら focuses more on a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use で after にほん when talking about the direction of movement; 行く goes with に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q17.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら; N・Aな ＋ だったら; Aい ＋ かったら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.vi: My dream is to start my own company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects じぶん with かいしゃ and shows that the company belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the company as the object of the action つくる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the phrase つくる into a noun; が marks the whole action of establishing a company as the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects わたし with ゆめ and shows that the dream belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ゆめです acts as a noun predicate and completes the structure “doing ... is my dream.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.why: The phrase つくるのが is nominalized so that the whole action of “starting a company” can act as the subject. Then わたしのゆめです identifies the subject through the structure “is my dream.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is used, “starting a company” becomes the topic, usually when comparing or explaining that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことが is used, the meaning is almost the same, but the tone is more abstract and formal than のが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out の after the verb, but つくるの is needed to turn the action into a noun before using が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q18.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ の ＋ が ＋ Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.vi: This TV drama seems likely to continue for a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies ドラマ to identify the drama being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the drama the topic of the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: まだまだ modifies つづく and emphasizes that it will continue for a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: つづく in the dictionary form comes before ようです to form the content being inferred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ようです comes at the end of the sentence to express a judgment based on signs or circumstances.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.why: The topic ドラマは comes at the beginning of the sentence, while まだまだ adds the degree of continuation. The verb in the plain form comes before ようです because ようだ needs a clause as the basis for the judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If つづきそうです is used, it means “seems likely to continue soon” or “may continue,” focusing on present signs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If つづくでしょう is used, the tone is a light prediction or guess, without emphasizing observed evidence as ようです does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ような at the end of the sentence, but a sentence expressing a judgment needs to end with ようです or ようだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ようだ／ようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.vi: Because I got wet in the rain on a cold day, I caught a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows when the getting-wet event occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects a cause or an earlier event to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks かぜ as the object in the fixed phrase かぜをひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ひきました is the polite past form of the phrase かぜをひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning to set the context. あめにぬれて uses the て form to connect the cause to the result かぜをひきました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of the て form, the causal relationship is stated more clearly and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use を after かぜ in this phrase; the fixed expression is かぜをひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.vi: I do not like meat, but I still try to eat as much as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes meat the topic of the comment about preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: I do not like meat, but I still try to eat it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: できるだけ modifies 食べる, showing the greatest possible effort to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べる in the dictionary form comes before ように to show an action that is maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: ように connects action 食べる with しています, forming a pattern for trying to maintain a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: しています shows that this effort continues in the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.why: The first clause states an opposite preference and is connected by が to the actual action in the second clause. The pattern Vるようにしています shows that the speaker is trying to keep eating meat, while できるだけ limits the amount according to their ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べるようになります is used, it means gradually becoming able to eat it or starting to eat it, without emphasizing the will to make an effort.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べることにしています is used, it means that the speaker has decided for themselves that eating is a rule, so it is stronger than ようにしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say 食べてようにします, but before ようにする in this pattern, the dictionary form must be used: 食べるようにします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ようにする; Vて形 + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.vi: I caught a cold, but I recovered after drinking soup.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action ひく in the fixed expression かぜをひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: catching a cold but then recovering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks soup as the thing that is drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 飲んだら uses the past form + たら to state the condition or time when recovery occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.why: The first clause states the initial condition, and が connects it to the opposite result. The phrase 飲んだら places the action of drinking first, followed by the result なおりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If 飲むと replaces it, the sentence means that drinking always leads to recovery, giving it a more natural-law or rule-like meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 飲んだあとで replaces it, the sentence simply says after drinking, without emphasizing a conditional relationship like たら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use たら for every meaning of "if", but in this sentence it mainly indicates the time after drinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.vi: After adding the salt, lower the heat and leave it as it is for 30 minutes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.sk: N を + Vたら + N を + Aいくして + duration + N に + してください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks salt as the thing that is added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 入れたら uses the past form + たら to indicate the time when adding the salt is complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the heat as the object that is lowered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て of よわくする connects lowering the heat with the following request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: This duration phrase shows how long the following state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the target state in the pattern そのままにする, meaning to keep the state unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: てください creates a polite request to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.why: 入れたら sets the time point, and then the two actions are linked in sequence by the て form. ３０分 comes before そのままにしてください to limit how long the unchanged state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入れたあとで is used, the sentence only says that after adding the salt, another action is done. The time sequence is clearer, but the conditional meaning is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入れてから is used, the sentence emphasizes that the salt must be added before the heat is lowered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に in そのままにしてください, but に is necessary to show the state that is kept unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.vi: I usually eat a sandwich at lunchtime.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes lunchtime the topic and states the eating habit at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: だいたい modifies the whole eating action, expressing a general level or a usual habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the sandwich as the food that is eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 食べています uses ている to express a repeated habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.why: おひるは identifies the topic and time, while だいたい adds the usual meaning. The object comes before 食べています and goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べます is used, the sentence still describes a habit, but it does not emphasize an ongoing or repeated state as 食べています does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 食べています as only "am eating", but with habits, ている can mean "usually eat".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.vi: I contact my family in Thailand every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.sk: N の + N に + time + Vしています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects タイ with 家族, showing that the family is related to Thailand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the recipient of the contact action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase shows the frequency of the contact action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: しています uses ている to express an action that continues or is repeated as a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.why: タイのかぞく creates a noun phrase, and then に marks the person or group receiving the contact. まいにち comes before the predicate to add the frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If と連絡する is used, the meaning is contacting each other or contacting from the same side, instead of focusing on the recipient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If に電話する replaces it, the meaning becomes specifically calling the family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と with 連絡する because of Vietnamese habits, but に is suitable when emphasizing the person being contacted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.vi: My house is in the countryside, and there are both mountains and rivers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with the noun いえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes my house the topic of the first clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: で is the connecting form of a noun with です, linking the description of the place with the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: も replaces は or が, adding mountains to the list of things that exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: も marks rivers as also existing there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: あります is the existence predicate used for things that are not people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.why: いえは states the topic, while いなかで describes where the house is and connects to additional information. The two nouns 山 and 川 both go with も to emphasize that both exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If いなかです is used, the sentence ends with information about the home in the countryside and does not connect naturally with the clause containing a mountain and a river.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If にも is used, the nouns are understood as places or objects where something exists, rather than things that exist in an area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate で as "and", but here で means both "in the countryside" and the connecting form of a noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.vi: I have a cold, a sore throat, and a cough that will not stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb ひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects an action or cause to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of the adjective いたい connects the painful state to the following condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject of とまる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb is in the polite negative form and describes a cough that does not stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.why: The sentence first gives the cause, having a cold, then the symptom, a sore throat, and finally the result, a cough that does not stop. The form て links the states and events in one flow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of て, the cause is stated more clearly and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with のど or せき, but here が marks the painful body part or the subject experiencing the state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.vi: I will put the food left over from dinner in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the situation or time that serves as the basis for the rest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause modifies もの and identifies it as something left over.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what is put in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination of the action 入れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the main verb with おく to create the pattern Vておく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: おく after a verb in the て form expresses doing something beforehand as preparation or maintaining a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.why: のこった directly modifies もの, so it comes before the noun. に indicates the place where it is stored, while Vておく shows that putting it in the refrigerator is done beforehand for storage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If おいています is used, the sentence emphasizes the state of being stored in the refrigerator rather than the preparation of storing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入れてしまいます is used, the sentence has a feeling of something being completely finished or regrettable, and no longer means preparation beforehand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate おく as 'put' in every case; after Vて, Vておく usually means doing something in advance or leaving it in its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.vi: Because dark clouds appeared, I stopped jogging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before a noun and modifies くも.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that appears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 出てくる describes appearing toward the speaker; ので connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the activity that was stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite past form and states an action that was performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.why: くろい modifies くも, forming the subject "dark clouds." The clause with ので comes first to explain the reason for stopping jogging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still states a cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 出ていった is used, the cloud is seen as moving away from the speaker, opposite to the movement toward the speaker in 出てきた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ので and から; ので is usually softer and more objective when stating a cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな+な・N+な + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.vi: When the train door closes, the bell rings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun 電車 with ドア, showing possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that performs the state 閉まる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates the time when the action in the main clause occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that produces the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb なります is the main predicate and describes the bell ringing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.why: The phrase しまるとき indicates the time and comes before the clause about the bell ringing. The particle が is used separately for the door and the bell because each noun is the subject of a different verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If しまると is used, the sentence emphasizes a natural result or something that always happens as soon as the door closes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using しまったとき means when the door has finished closing, unlike the time when it is closing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use は for both ドア and ベル; the two clauses have different subjects, so が makes the structure clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形 + とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.vi: Because I like the sea, I want to live on an island in the south.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.sk: Nが + Aな + なので + Nの + Nに + Vます omit ます+たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: With 好き, が marks the object that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 好き is an な adjective, so な is needed before ので to connect the cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 南 with しま and modifies the noun しま.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where someone wants to live.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: たい attaches to the verb stem to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな+な・N+な + ので; Vます omit ます + たい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.why: 好きなので gives the reason first, followed by the phrase 南のしまに, which indicates the place where the person wants to live. With 好き, a liked noun goes with が, not with を as the verb "like" does in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing なので with だから still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Use 住みたがっています when talking about another person's desire, not the speaker's own desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q7.kobun.tip: A common mistake is to say うみをすき; in Japanese, 好き is an adjective, and its object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.vi: By 2020, the number of tourists from abroad will probably double.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: までに indicates the time limit by which or before which a change will be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: からの modifies かんこうきゃく and indicates where the tourists come from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject whose number increases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the level or result that the number reaches.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: でしょう comes at the end of the sentence to express a prediction without complete certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.why: The time expression is placed at the beginning to set the limit of the prediction. が marks what increases, while に after ばい indicates that the increase reaches double.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ２０２０年まで is used, the sentence only states a period that lasts until that year. It does not stress finishing before the deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing でしょう with と思います makes the sentence express the speaker’s personal opinion or thought more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.tip: Do not omit に after まで or ばい; までに only sets a time limit, while 倍に indicates the level that the number reaches.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q8.kobun.cn: Nまでに; Nに + V; V普通形 + でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.vi: I was very happy because my friends held a birthday party for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who performs an action that benefits the speaker in the pattern Vてもらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the event held by the friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: Vて connects with もらう to express receiving help or an action from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to the past tense by changing い to かった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.why: The phrase Nに indicates the person who performs the action, Nを is what is done, and Vてもらう shows that the speaker benefits from the action. The happy state is stated at the end and put in the past tense because the event has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the friend is the person who does something good for the speaker, instead of stressing that the speaker receives the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in Vてもらう with が, but に indicates the person who performs the action that I receive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t77-q9.tokens.7.m: have someone do something for someone
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.vi: I often ask a kind senior for advice about many things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before a noun to modify せんぱい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person who is asked for advice or consulted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: いろいろ modifies the content being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: しています uses ている to express asking for advice as an ongoing or repeated action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.why: やさしい comes before せんぱい to describe the senior. に marks the person being consulted, while いろいろ adds the range of content before the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If と相談する is used, the meaning stresses discussing something together with that person instead of asking that person for advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If について is added, the phrase clearly shows the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with 相談する because they think “ask advice about what,” but the person being asked usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.vi: Since I was little in my home country, I have watched Japanese anime.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where watching the animated films takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of the period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects にほん with アニメ to modify it and show its origin or attribute.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the verb “watch.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ていました expresses a habit or an action continuing from the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.why: The place and starting point are placed before the object to create the context. にほんの modifies アニメ, while を marks anime as the object of 見ていました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of から, the sentence only states when the person watched something as a child. It does not stress that it started at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見ていました is replaced with 見ました, the sentence only states one viewing or one completed event. It does not stress continuation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake から for showing a cause, but in this sentence から indicates the starting point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q10.kobun.cn: Vた + とき; N + の + N; Vていました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.vi: Because I had a cold, I stayed home from school and made everyone worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the cause that led to staying home from school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of 休む in the expression for staying home from school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of staying home from school with the result stated in the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the people affected by the action that caused worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the noun used with the pattern しんぱいをかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: かけました is the polite past form of かける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.why: The cause かぜで comes before the action of staying home from school. The two actions are connected with the form て; after that, に indicates the affected people, while しんぱいをかける is the verb phrase meaning to make someone worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of で, the cause is stated more clearly in a “because... therefore...” way. The tone is softer and more explanatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If 心配させました is used, the focus is on making everyone worry with a causative structure, not on the fixed phrase 心配をかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate みんなに as the person performing the action, but here に indicates the people who have to bear the worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.vi: My grandfather is very healthy and says that he will live until he is 100 years old.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that he is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective 元気 and shows the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な 元気 changes to 元気で to connect with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: まで indicates the age limit up to which the action of living continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the whole quoted content of the speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: 言っています is the main predicate and expresses speech that is continuing or being repeated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.why: 元気で connects the grandfather’s two characteristics with the で form of the adjective な. The spoken content is placed in quotation marks, and と connects it with 言っています; まで sets the final point of his lifespan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If 言っています is replaced with と思っています, the sentence changes from “is saying” to “is thinking or believing that.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If までに is used, the meaning is to complete an action before or by the age of 100, not to continue living until that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use までに for every time limit, but an action continuing up to a limit uses まで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q16.kobun.cn: Aな + で、; V普通形 + と言っています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.vi: I get up at 5 a.m. and jog for about 30 minutes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ Vて、 ＋ Duration くらい ＋ N を ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time of getting up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects getting up with the next activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: くらい follows a time amount to show an approximation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the activity performed with しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: しています shows an activity that is in progress or continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.why: The time of getting up comes first and goes with に. The form て shows the order of actions, while 30 minutesくらい comes before the object to state the time spent jogging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: With ５時ごろ, the meaning is around 5 o’clock, while ３０分くらい refers to an approximate duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: With おきてから, the sentence emphasizes that jogging happens after getting up, not simply that the two actions are connected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q17.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may confuse くらい with a time point; くらい after a counter expresses an approximate amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.vi: I have to change trains twice to get to the discount supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Number of times も ＋ Vて、 ＋ Aい N へ ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the vehicle being changed or the transfer being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: も emphasizes that the number of times is more than the speaker wanted or expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects changing trains with the purpose of going to the supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 安い modifies スーパー, while へ indicates direction toward a destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.why: 電車を is the object of the action of changing trains. ２回も emphasizes the large number of transfers, and the form て then connects the means or method with the destination marked by へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: With ２回しか, the sentence means changing trains only twice. It is usually used with a negative form and gives a limiting meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence still indicates the destination, but に is more neutral about the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q18.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may leave out the particle を after 電車, but 乗り換える still needs を when talking about changing transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.vi: I always listen to a radio program while cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.sk: Frequency ＋ N を ＋ Vます-stem ながら ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: いつも modifies the whole activity that follows and indicates frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the program as the object of listening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ながら follows the connective form of a verb and shows that two actions happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: しています is the main action; the activity before ながら is the secondary action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.why: In the pattern ながら, the verb before ながら is the secondary action, while the verb after it is the main action. Therefore, listening to the radio comes first, and cleaning is the central activity of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If きいてから is used, it means listening first and then cleaning, so the two actions no longer happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ながらも is used, the sentence has a contrastive meaning like “although…,” rather than simply meaning “while doing….”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q19.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may conjugate the verb after ながら in the polite form; the correct pattern is to remove ます and add ながら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.vi: I want to start my own company and become its director.
