default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the company as the object being established.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects establishing the company with becoming a director in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the position or state reached after なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: たい attaches to the verb form with ます removed to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.why: The sentence uses を for the company being established, then uses the て form to connect two successive actions. With なる, に marks the position or state that someone becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form were used, the sentence would list typical actions rather than emphasize the sequence of establishing a company and then becoming a director.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q2.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may use を before a position with なる, but the correct structure is Nに なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.vi: If you want to stay at that hotel, you should book in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where someone will stay.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: なら connects a hypothetical condition with the advice that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: Vた＋ほうが indicates the choice that should be made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: いい completes the advice pattern Vたほうがいい; よ adds a reminder-like tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.why: The place phrase comes before the condition なら to state the situation. Then Vたほうがいい is used to give gentle advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the condition or intention to do something soon. It no longer has the considered-choice meaning of Vたほうがいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern makes the advice stronger and more connected to responsibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.tip: English learners from Vietnam may mistakenly think that ほうがいい always means comparison, but here it creates advice about what should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N＋なら; Vた＋ほうがいい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.vi: In Tokyo, forms of transportation such as trains and buses are very convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Tokyo the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: や connects one example in an incomplete list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: など shows that the transportation just mentioned is only an example.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject being described as convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: 便利です is the predicate adjective ending in な in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.why: は limits the scope of the comment to Tokyo. The list comes before 交通 to name the types of transportation being discussed, while が marks 交通 as the subject of 便利です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence usually refers only to the two stated items, rather than an example-based list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means “only N,” so it limits the range more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q21.kobun.tip: や does not connect a complete list like と; など or the context is usually needed to show that other things also exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Japanese the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the predicate and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 役に立つ is a fixed verb phrase meaning useful or helpful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q3.kobun.why: The topic comes before は, and then とても adds a degree to the predicate phrase. In 役に立つ, に is a fixed part used with 立つ to express usefulness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence also expresses convenience, but it focuses more on being easy or convenient to use than on being useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q3.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in 役に立つ as 'at'; it is a particle in a fixed phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.vi: I will graduate from university in March next year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.sk: N の + Time に + N を + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the time point with the following month noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when graduation takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the university as the object of graduation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 卒業する uses を to indicate the place or program from which the learner graduates.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.why: らいねんの modifies ３月 to identify which year’s March it is. に indicates the time, while を marks the university in the phrase 卒業する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence may be understood as graduating at that location, while を names the school or program from which one graduates.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q4.kobun.tip: With 卒業する, learners often mistakenly use に for the school; the basic usage is 大学を卒業する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.vi: I joined the soccer club at university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where joining the club takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects soccer with the noun club.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or organization that the speaker joins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 入る is the polite past form, expressing that someone entered or joined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.why: で gives the context or place, の identifies the type of club, and に marks the organization joined. 入る is used with に when entering a place or joining an organization.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, it means doing activities in the club, without emphasizing the act of joining.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use で after クラブ when you mean 'join'; 入る requires クラブに入る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.vi: The watch I received last year has already broken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.sk: Time + Vた + Nが + もう + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: きょねん identifies the time when the receiving action took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause modifies 時計 and tells us when the watch was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the watch as the subject that broke.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: もう emphasizes that the event happened early or has already been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 壊れる is an intransitive verb that describes an object entering a broken state on its own.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.why: きょねんもらった comes before 時計 to form a clause modifying a noun. が identifies the watch as the subject of the broken state, while もう highlights that it has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it means that someone broke the watch, emphasizing an active agent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q6.kobun.tip: Distinguish 壊れる 'be broken' from 壊す 'break something'; an object used as the subject usually goes with が and uses 壊れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.vi: I will buy the gift for my older sister at the cosmetics counter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who receives the gifted item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: あげる modifies もの, while は makes that item the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the buying action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 買おう is the volitional form, showing the speaker’s intention or self-talk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.why: あねにあげる modifies もの, forming the phrase 'the item to give to my sister.' で indicates where to buy it, while the volitional form at the end expresses the speaker’s decision or intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買います is used instead, the sentence only states that the speaker will buy something or politely announces it. It does not clearly show a personal decision like 買おう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 買いましょう is used, the sentence becomes an invitation or suggestion to buy something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.tip: Learners may easily confuse に and で: the recipient goes with に, while the place where the purchase happens goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + N; V意向形: Vる → Vおう・Vよう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.vi: When I ate with everyone, I was so happy that I kept laughing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the group of people performing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: ている describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: とき forms a phrase showing a time point, modified by the clause before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the happy state with the following action and has a causal meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: ていました describes a state or action that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first. Then the happy state is connected with て to explain the continued laughing. ずっと modifies わらっていました and emphasizes continuity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ときに is used, the time point is emphasized more clearly, but the main meaning of the sentence hardly changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If たのしくて is replaced with たのしいので, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.tip: Learners may easily forget to change Aい to Aくて when using an adjective to connect a cause or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.tokens.7.m: because it was fun, and fun
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q8.kobun.cn: Vている + とき; Aい → Aくて; Vている → Vていました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.vi: In summer, there are many festivals in many places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes summer the topic and context of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where an event or existence takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the sentence with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: あります expresses existence or an event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.why: The time topic comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the place with で. The existing thing is marked by が, and the sentence ends with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ところで is replaced with ところに, the sentence focuses more on where the festival exists, but for an event taking place, で is more natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q9.kobun.tip: Learners may use に for every place, but the place where an event takes place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.vi: I am busy today, but I am free tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the topic and time point being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ですが connects two contrasting ideas: today is busy, but tomorrow is free.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: なら limits the condition or time being considered to tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: です forms the polite predicate, while よ emphasizes the information being reported to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.why: The sentence first states today's situation, then uses ですが to shift to the opposite idea about tomorrow. なら is placed after tomorrow to limit the condition, and then ひまです forms the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですが is replaced with でも, the following sentence usually needs to be separated into a new sentence, making the conversational tone clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: ならば also means if it is, but it is more formal and stiffer than なら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use なら as simply meaning “as for,” and forget that it often limits the condition or topic being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.tokens.7.m: if it is/if it is on
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q1.kobun.cn: Aい・Aな・N・V普通形 ＋ ですが; N ＋ なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.vi: I made a lavish meal for my child's birthday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども to the following noun, creating a phrase that modifies the birthday occasion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the time when the meal was cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the meal that was cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: ました shows that the action was completed, with a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 子どものたんじょうびに states when the action occurred. ごちそうを is the object placed before the verb つくりました, following the usual Japanese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If のために is used, the sentence emphasizes the purpose or the person who benefits, rather than simply the time of the birthday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q10.kobun.tip: Do not place the object after the verb as in Vietnamese; ごちそうを must come before つくりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.vi: When I was young, I often argued with my older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with とき, creating a phrase that indicates a period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase 子どものとき indicates the time or period when the argument occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indicates the person who participated together or interacted in the argument.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: This adverb modifies けんかした and indicates how often it occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: した is the past form of する in the noun けんかする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to give the background, followed by the person who interacted with と. よく modifies the past action けんかした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Nの間 emphasizes the whole period of time, while とき usually indicates one time or period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: に対して indicates the direction of an action or attitude toward someone. It is less natural than と when talking about two people arguing with each other.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q11.kobun.tip: With interactive actions such as けんかする, the other participant usually goes with と, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.vi: At Christmas, everyone gathers at my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: には combines with に to indicate the time, and は makes that time the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the person performing the action of gathering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place where everyone gathers or gathers at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb あつまります is in the polite present form and describes something that will happen or usually happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.why: The time is moved to the beginning and marked with には to make it the topic. The subject みんなが performs the action あつまります at the place うちに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If うちで is used, the sentence emphasizes the place where the activity takes place, while うちに better fits the idea that everyone gathers at a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If は is removed from クリスマスに, the sentence only states the time and does not emphasize contrast or the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q12.kobun.tip: Distinguish に, which indicates the place where people gather, from で, which indicates the place where an action takes place; あつまる usually uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.vi: The grandmother who lives with me is my mother's mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the manner of living together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: This clause modifies そぼ and tells us which grandmother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents the grandmother as the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 母 to the following noun and shows possession or a family relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: です connects the topic そぼ with the explanation おかあさん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.why: The clause すんでいる comes before そぼ to modify this noun. After stating the topic with は, the sentence uses NのN to show the relationship of a mother's mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If the dictionary form 住む is used, it only describes the action of living and does not emphasize the current state of living like 住んでいる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used instead of は, the sentence emphasizes the grandmother as the subject, rather than introducing and explaining the grandmother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese requires すんでいる to come before そぼ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.vi: I accidentally made as many as 100 copies incorrectly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.sk: Nを ＋ Quantityも ＋ Vて ＋ しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that was made incorrectly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: も follows a quantity to emphasize that the number is very large.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb しっぱいする with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました indicates that the action was completed, often with regret or an unintended feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.why: コピーを is the object of しっぱいする, while １００まいも adds the quantity and creates an emphatic tone. The form てしまいました describes an action that was fully completed and regrettable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vておく, it means doing something in advance or preparing it, so the feeling of accidentally making a mistake is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: しまう in the present describes something that will or usually finishes, while しまいました identifies something that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q14.kobun.tip: Do not translate も here as “also”; after a quantity, も usually emphasizes “as many as” a large number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.vi: Please write your name at the reception desk on the first floor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the first floor with the reception area that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the writing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the name as the content to be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects 書く with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: ください is placed after the verb in the て form to ask the listener to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.why: １かいのうけつけ forms a noun phrase indicating a place, and then で states where the action takes place. The object お名まえを comes before 書いてください in basic Japanese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the request sounds softer and more humble, in the form of a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with Vなさい, the tone becomes more commanding or forceful, like an instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で to mark the object, but in this sentence で indicates the place, while を marks what is written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.vi: In a test, please check your answers several times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.sk: Nでは ＋ Nを ＋ Number of timesも ＋ Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: では limits the context: in the situation of taking a test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the answer as the object to check.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: も emphasizes that checking is repeated many times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects チェックする with ください to form a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.why: テストでは gives the context, while こたえを is the object of チェックする. The phrase なんかいも adds frequency before the request チェックしてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence means that checking is required, so it is no longer a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence asks whether checking is allowed, which is different from requesting that it be checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q16.kobun.tip: なんかいも means “many times,” not “as many times as you like”; permission is usually expressed with 何回でも.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.vi: I always sit in the seat at the very front.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: This adverb modifies the action of sitting and shows frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the location phrase with 席, forming a phrase that modifies the seat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the speaker is sitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: すわっています describes the continuing state of sitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.why: いちばん前のせき is a noun phrase in which the part before の modifies 席. に marks the location, while すわっています describes the continuing sitting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If すわります is used, it only describes the action or habit of sitting and does not emphasize the current sitting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If へ is used, it emphasizes movement toward the front, not the location where the speaker is sitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q17.kobun.tip: With posture verbs such as すわる, the ている form usually describes being in that posture, not only an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.vi: I still cannot come up with a good idea for a trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective いい modifies the following phrase for the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects りょこう with アイディア and indicates the content of the idea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the idea as something that has not appeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: なかなか is used with the negative form to express that something is difficult to happen or does not happen as hoped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 出てくる describes an idea appearing and coming to the speaker, while ません is the polite negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.why: いいりょこうのアイディア is a noun phrase serving as the subject with が. なかなか combines with the negative form to emphasize difficulty, while 出てくる shows an idea gradually appearing in the speaker’s mind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 出ません is used, it only says that the idea does not appear and lacks the meaning that the idea comes to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If あまりVない is used instead, the meaning is weaker: it only means “not very ...” and does not emphasize difficulty as なかなか does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.tip: なかなか in a negative sentence must be used with the Vない form; it should not be used directly as an adverb meaning “not good.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q18.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる; なかなか ＋ Vない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.vi: I always decorate the table with beautiful flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun 花 to modify 花.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the flowers as the object being decorated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the flowers are placed or decorated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ています describes an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.why: いつも modifies the whole action. 花を is the object, while テーブルに is the place where the flowers are placed; the verb ています shows that the decorating state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 飾ります is used instead, the sentence only says that the speaker will or usually decorates, without emphasizing a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q19.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use で instead of に, but に only indicates where an object is placed or exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.vi: After studying, the number of words I understand increased quickly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: たら connects a conditional clause or an earlier event with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: わかる comes before a noun and modifies the kind of words that can be understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the words as the subject that increases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: どんどん modifies ふえました and describes a continuous increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate. It uses the polite past form to state the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.why: The clause べんきょうしたら describes what happened first, while the increase in understood words is the result. わかる modifies ことば, and が marks the noun phrase as the subject of ふえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Using と emphasizes a natural or certain result whenever one studies, so it is less suitable than たら when describing one specific development.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ば gives the sentence a more general or hypothetical conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may easily place わかる after ことば, but in Japanese, a modifying clause must come before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q2.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋だ ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.vi: I put on the shirt I received and tried looking at myself in the mirror.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: もらった is a clause that modifies シャツ, meaning the shirt that was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the shirt as the object of putting on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects putting on the shirt with looking at or trying to look at oneself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the means used for looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 見てみる describes trying to perform the action of looking, and ました puts the action into the polite past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.why: The clause もらった comes before シャツ to identify which shirt it is. The two actions are connected by the て form, while で shows that the mirror is the means used for looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vている is used, the sentence emphasizes an action in progress and no longer has the meaning of trying to do something as in Vてみる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate てみる as “see,” but this pattern means trying to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.vi: Because we want to play soccer, let us gather everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: With したい, が marks what the speaker wants to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: したい expresses desire, while ので connects the reason to the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the people who will be gathered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ たい; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.why: サッカーが is what is desired when したい is used. The reason clause comes before ので, followed by the object 人を and the suggestion あつめましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason keeps almost the same meaning, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use を with したい, but a desire to do an activity usually uses が before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.vi: When I was a student, I often went to the club to dance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.sk: Nの + とき + 頻度副詞 + Nへ + Vます-remove ます に + 行きました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 学生 with とき to identify the time as when the person was a student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: とき creates a time phrase for the action of going to the club.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: に attaches to the ます-removed form of おどる to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: 行きました is the main predicate and describes going in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.cn: Nの + とき; Vます-remove ます + に + 行く・来る・帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.why: 学生のとき sets the time frame at the beginning of the sentence. クラブへ shows the direction of going, while おどりに shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるために is used, the purpose is expressed more clearly and formally than with the short form Vます-remove ます に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place に after the plain-form verb, but the pattern showing the purpose of going uses the ます-removed form, such as おどりに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.vi: In the news, the truth must be communicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: では states the scope or context being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ほんとう with こと to modify こと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks こと as the content being communicated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: つたえなければ is the conditional form of the negative form and combines with なりません to create a meaning of obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: なりません completes the double negative pattern meaning “must do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.cn: Vない-remove い + ければ + なりません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.why: ニュースでは limits the context of the sentence. ほんとうのこと is the content being communicated, while なければなりません changes communicating into an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vなくてもいい, the sentence means that it is not necessary to communicate it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたほうがいい is used, the sentence is only advice, not an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand なければ as “if not” and leave out なりません, but the whole phrase means “must.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.vi: The soccer team I love very much has lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: な connects the adjective な with サッカーのチーム to modify the team.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects サッカー with チーム to identify the team as a soccer team.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the team as the subject of losing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb まける with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました describes a completed action and often includes a feeling of regret or something unwanted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.why: The two modifying phrases come before チーム to identify which team it is. が marks the team as the subject, while てしまいました emphasizes that the unwanted result has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vている, the sentence only states an ongoing state or action and does not emphasize regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vておく is used, the sentence means doing something in advance or preparing, so it does not fit the team losing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate しまう as “put away,” but after the て form it usually shows completion together with regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.vi: The cause of this fire has still not been identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: A demonstrative that modifies the noun かじ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the event as the subject of おきた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: A past-tense verb comes before a noun to modify げんいん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes the cause the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb showing that the state is not complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: わかっていません describes a state that is still unclear at present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.why: The clause かじがおきた comes before げんいん to identify which cause is being discussed. After the topic げんいんは, the adverb まだ combines with わかっていません to express that it is still unclear up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of は, the sentence only states that the cause is unclear and does not emphasize “the cause” as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a modifying clause after a noun, but Japanese places the clause おきた directly before the noun げんいん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.vi: The last time we met was six months ago, so it has been a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.sk: N + Vた + のは + Period of time も + N ですから + N ですね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase shows the time of the action of meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の nominalizes the action あった, while は makes that event the topic for comparing time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.2.vi: as long as half a year
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: も emphasizes a period longer than normally expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: because it was a long time ago
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ですから connects the reason with the comment ひさしぶり in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.4.vi: it has been a long time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: ですね is used at the end of a sentence to confirm and share a feeling with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.why: The sentence makes the previous meeting the topic and then states the time gap of six months. ですから explains why the speaker feels that this is a meeting after a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ですから with ので makes the reason softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: 以来 emphasizes the period from a certain point up to the present, rather than simply stating a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand も as only “also,” but in 半年も it emphasizes that half a year is a lot or a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形 + の; N + も; N・Aな + ですから; V・Aい + ですから
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.vi: These shoes suit me very well in both design and size.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the shoes the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: も marks design as one of the aspects that fit well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: も forms a parallel structure with デザインも and shows that the size also fits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the person toward whom the suitability is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ぴったりです is the predicate expressing complete suitability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.why: The sentence mentions the shoes first, then lists two aspects with the structure NもNも. わたしに shows the person receiving the evaluation, while ぴったりです is the main comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This structure can be understood as “both A and B,” emphasizing that both parts have the same feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: と simply connects two nouns and does not emphasize that both are true, as もも does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate に as “at” or “in,” but in わたしにぴったりです, に shows the person that the object suits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.vi: Secure the picture firmly on the wall so that it does not fall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 壁 with the picture, forming a noun phrase meaning “the picture on the wall.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the picture as the subject of the clause meaning “does not fall.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: so that it does not fall
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ように connects the purpose with the main clause and uses the negative form to prevent falling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: しっかり modifies とめて and shows how the picture is secured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: てください makes a polite request, asking the listener to perform とめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.why: The clause おちないように states the purpose of securing the picture. しっかり shows how to do it, while とめてください is the main request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with ないために focuses more on a direct purpose, while ように is more natural when referring to reaching or avoiding a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: ないでください means “please do not,” and does not express the purpose of preventing something from happening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ように with ために; ように usually goes with an ability or a state to be reached, such as おちない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q5.kobun.cn: Vない + ように; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.vi: Teacher Yamashita teaches us very enthusiastically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Teacher Yamashita the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies ねっしんに and increases the degree of enthusiasm.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The に form of the adjective な changes it into an adverb that modifies おしえてくださいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: くださいます shows that a person of higher status performs an action that benefits the speaker or the speaker's group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.why: The sentence makes the person performing the action the topic, then states the degree and manner of teaching. おしえてくださいます is both the predicate and a respectful expression for the teacher's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: くれます still means teaching for the speaker's side, but is more casual and less respectful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: おしえます only states the action of teaching and does not clearly show a benefit for the speaker as くださいます does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use ねっしんだ to modify a verb, but the adjective な must change into ねっしんに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q6.kobun.cn: Aな + に; Vて + くださる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.vi: Please stay here a little longer. When the rain stops, let's go out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action いて and shows that it continues for a little longer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates where the speaker exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb いる changes to the て form to connect with the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of the rain stopping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The past form やんだ combines with ら to create the condition “when the rain stops.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.why: The conditional clause やんだら comes before the main action 出かけましょう. に shows the location of いる, while て connects staying with waiting for the rain to stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with と, the sentence would have a more natural or frequently occurring result, so it would be less suitable as an invitation in this context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: たら expresses a specific condition or time and fits the meaning “go out after the rain stops.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may incorrectly use the dictionary form before たら; with verbs, the た form is needed, such as やんだら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.tokens.4.m: be, stay (the て form of いる)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q7.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった + ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.vi: A bag with a small pocket is very useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates where the small pocket exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that exists in the bag.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ある in the dictionary form combines with と to state the natural result of having a pocket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.why: The existence structure uses に for the place and が for the existing object. と connects the condition with a result considered natural: having a pocket is convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, the sentence states a more specific condition, while と emphasizes a result that usually follows naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: なら is based on information or an assumption already mentioned, so its meaning is less natural and general than と in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use を after かばん when talking about where something exists; an existence location usually takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.vi: The water has boiled, so let's have tea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the boiling state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form わいた combines with ので to give the reason for inviting someone to drink tea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the drink affected by the action 飲む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to drink tea together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first with ので, followed by the suggested action. を marks tea as the object of 飲む, while ましょう creates an invitation to act together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: から also indicates a reason, but is more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: たら would change the meaning to “drink tea after the water boils,” focusing on the time rather than the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.tip: Before ので, adjectives な and nouns need な, but the verb わく only needs the plain form, such as わいたので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t79-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vi: My mother is working at a hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with 母 to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 母は makes my mother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates where the work activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 働いて is the て form that connects with いる to show an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: いる completes the pattern Vている and shows that the action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.why: わたしの母は is a noun phrase serving as the topic, and びょういんで shows the place of the activity. The verb in the て form connects with いる to describe an ongoing action or continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If にいる is used, it means that the mother is at the hospital, but not necessarily working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse で and に: use で for an activity's location, and に for a place where someone or something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vi: I lost the important letter I received from my father.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から shows the source of the item received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 父からもらった comes before the noun and modifies the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 大切 is a な adjective, so it needs な when placed before the noun 手がみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the letter as the object that was lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: なくしてしまった combines the て form with しまう and expresses a completed action with regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.why: The clause 父からもらった and the adjective 大切な both come before 手がみ to identify which letter it is. 手がみを is the object of なくす, while てしまった is placed at the end to show that the regrettable action has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If ておく is used, the sentence describes doing something beforehand as preparation, not accidentally losing the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If てある is used, the sentence describes a state intentionally created by someone, which does not fit losing the letter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.tip: The adjective な must keep な before a noun, while the adjective い does not use な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q10.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ しまう／しまった
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vi: People often say that my younger brother and I look very similar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects わたし with 弟 to form a group of two people being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the group わたしと弟 as the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: にている is the predicate of the quoted content and expresses the similarity between the two people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the entire preceding clause as what someone said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 言われる is the passive form and serves as the main predicate, meaning that people comment that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.why: と connects the first two objects, while と introduces the content of the statement. Clause にている comes before と, and then 言われる expresses that the speaker receives this comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If と思われる is used, the sentence focuses on a guess or a general judgment, without stressing people's direct words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If と言われている is used, the sentence stresses that the comment is being passed around or is still widely believed to be true.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.tip: と in わたしと弟 means “and,” but と in にていると言われる is a quotation particle; they must be distinguished by their position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ と言われる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vi: This place is quiet but inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates a place someone moves to or a place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb 引っ越す with the pattern てしまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまった describes a completed action and may sometimes carry a sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.why: The first clause states an advantage, and after が comes the contrasting content. The phrase 不便なところ modifies ところ, while に indicates the place moved to; てしまった shows that the move has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing が with けれども keeps the contrast but makes the tone more complete and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing てしまった with ている only describes the state of being in that place, without stressing regret or completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget な before the noun after the adjective な and use で instead of に when talking about a place they move to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q12.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう（過去形：Vてしまった）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vi: From the garden, I can hear insects making sounds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.sk: N から ＋ N の ＋ modifying-form V ＋ N が ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source or place where a sound comes from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun 虫 with noun 声 to form a modifier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The modifying form of the verb 鳴く comes before 声.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound that can be heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.why: The phrase 虫のなくこえ is a noun phrase in which なく modifies こえ. With 聞こえる, a sound that can be heard usually goes with が, while から indicates where the sound comes from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 聞く emphasizes that the listener listens actively, while 聞こえる describes a sound naturally reaching the ears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 聞こえる, but a sound that can be heard usually uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vi: What is the most important industry in your country?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あなた with the noun 国.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the scope or place where the activity being asked about takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies the adjective じゅうような to create the superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: な connects the adjective 重要 with 産業, while は makes this phrase the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: なんですか is used to ask about the identity or content of the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.why: 国で defines the comparison range. いちばん comes before the adjective to create the meaning “most,” and the whole phrase いちばん重要な産業 is made the topic using は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Using どんな産業 asks what type of industry it is, not necessarily which industry is the most important.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: もっとも also means “most important,” but it is more formal than いちばん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place は directly after 国, but here は must attach to the industry phrase being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vi: No one knows the real reason why he left school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action of leaving school in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of やめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The past form comes before a noun to modify 理由.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 本当 with the noun 理由.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes the real reason the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: だれも combines with a negative verb to mean “no one.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.why: Clause かれが学校をやめた comes before 理由 to explain what kind of reason it is. After は, だれも combines with わからない to negate the entire subject: “no one knows.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 誰にも emphasizes “to no one,” with a meaning close to saying that no one is able to know.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This form is incorrect because 本当 is a noun or an adjective な, which must connect to a noun with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use だれがわからない, but the meaning “no one” requires だれも with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ N; Aな・Nの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.vi: Tomorrow, please be careful not to be late for the departure time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when the reminder applies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 出発 with the noun じかん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the time point at which being late may occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative form expresses something that must be avoided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ように connects the goal to be achieved with the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: してください creates a polite request or favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.why: The phrase 出発のじかんに indicates the time that must be met. Vないようにしてください expresses a request for the listener to do something to avoid an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: Vないでください only requests that someone not do something, while Vないようにしてください emphasizes trying or taking care to avoid it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: Vないために focuses on the speaker's purpose and does not directly carry a polite request meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand ように as “like,” but in this pattern it indicates a goal to achieve or something to avoid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q16.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ ようにしてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vi: I wonder how many people will come to the party on Saturday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the time reference 土よう日 with the noun パーティー.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は shows that the party is the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 何人 asks how many people perform the action 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: のかな changes the question into private wondering or a gentle guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.why: 土よう日のパーティー makes the event the topic. 何人 comes before 来る to ask how many people will come, while のかな adds a gentle wondering tone instead of asking directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: 何人来ますか is a more direct and polite question, without a wondering tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: 何人来るでしょうか expresses a more polite prediction or guess than のかな.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add the particle が after 何人, but when asking about the number of people as the subject, 何人 can come directly before the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q18.kobun.vi: Many people are using the convenience store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the convenience store is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the people performing the action of using it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: している describes an action in progress or a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q18.kobun.why: は puts the topic at the beginning of the sentence, while が identifies the person performing the action. 利用する changes into 利用している to show that the use is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 利用した, the sentence would only mean that it was used, without emphasizing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse は and が, but は states the topic, while が clearly identifies the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.vi: There are many picture books for children in that library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: には marks the place where something exists and also states the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the phrase 子どものため to the noun that follows, modifying the picture books.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists in the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ある is the predicate showing that an object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first with には, followed by the existing object with が and the predicate ある. 子どものための comes before えほん to specify the type of picture books.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 子ども向けの, the meaning is still “for children,” but the nuance is closer to a product designed for children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the subject object after ある because of Vietnamese habits, but Japanese usually states the place first and then the existing object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vi: During the exam, I forgot my watch and had a lot of trouble.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: のとき creates a time phrase showing when the event occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 時計を is the object forgotten in the action わすれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects forgetting the watch with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: こまりました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.why: しけんのとき sets the time background, and 時計を is the object of わすれる. The て form connects the previous cause or situation with the result こまりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If わすれたので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly, and the sentence has a more direct explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate the て form as only “and,” but here it also connects a cause with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.vi: Please do not go into the forest alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the method or circumstances of performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement toward the forest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 行かないで is the ないで form, which combines with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ください makes the prohibition sound like a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.why: で states the way of going alone, while へ shows the direction toward the forest. The verb 行く changes to 行かないで and combines with ください to ask the listener not to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vないほうがいい, the sentence becomes advice not to go, which is softer than a direct request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 行かなくてください, but a request not to do something must use 行かないでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that she is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: な connects the ending-な adjective 有名 with the noun がか that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: がかです serves as the predicate and identifies her occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q21.kobun.why: は puts the described object at the beginning of the sentence. 有名な comes directly before がか because an ending-な adjective needs な when modifying a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 有名な with 有名の is wrong because an ending-な adjective does not connect to a noun with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: 有名で usually connects to another clause or quality, and does not directly modify がか in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な after an ending-な adjective when placing it before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person whose location or position needs to be identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: どちらですか is a polite way to ask about the location or choice of the person mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q22.kobun.why: The noun serving as the topic comes before は, while どちらですか creates a polite question about that person’s location. The specific place is omitted, but the listener still understands that the question asks where the person is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If どこですか is used, the sentence still asks where someone is, but it is less polite than どちらですか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand どちら as only “which side,” but in a polite question it can also mean “where” or “which person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.vi: I went to a restaurant near my home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 近所 with the noun しょくどう to modify it, creating the meaning “a restaurant in the nearby area.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement toward the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and describes an event that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.why: 近所の comes before しょくどう to identify which restaurant. へ marks the direction toward that place, while 行きました comes at the end of the sentence and shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence still shows the destination, but に emphasizes the destination more than the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If 近所の is replaced with 近くの, it means “near” and usually refers to a short distance from an understood place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out の between 近所 and しょくどう, but a noun that modifies another noun must be connected with の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.vi: There is a bird over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.sk: Place に + N が + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: います is the predicate showing the existence of a person or animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.why: In an existence sentence, the place usually comes first and goes with に, while the existing thing goes with が. います is used because the object is a bird, a living thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あります, it is used for objects or non-living things, so it is not natural for a bird.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で instead of に when talking about where a person or animal exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.vi: The tree in the park fell because of the storm.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.sk: Cause で + N の + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the direct cause that made the tree fall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun こうえん with 木 to modify 木.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the tree as the subject affected by the event of falling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb たおれる is in the polite past form and describes an event that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.why: The cause is placed at the beginning of the sentence with で, followed by the noun phrase acting as the subject. たおれる is an intransitive verb, so the tree goes with が and does not need the object を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 台風のせいで emphasizes the storm as a more negative or blameworthy cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 木, but たおれる is intransitive, so 木 must go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vi: Because it was cold, vegetable prices are very high.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the cause in the first clause with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 野菜 with ねだん to form the phrase “the price of vegetables.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks ねだん as the subject being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 高いです is an adjective predicate that states the price level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.why: さむかったので states the reason first, while ねだんがとても高いです is the result being explained. の connects the noun 野菜 with the noun ねだん, and が marks the subject of the adjective 高い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason stays the same, but the tone becomes more personal and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget to change the adjective い into the past form before ので: さむいので is different from さむかったので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q3.kobun.cn: Aいかった + ので; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vi: She is intelligent and also has a good personality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes her the shared topic of the two characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 頭が is the subject in the fixed expression 頭がいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: よくて is the て form of いい, connecting the first characteristic with the next one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: も replaces は or が to add a similar characteristic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: いい is the predicate giving an evaluation of her personality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.why: かのじょは makes her the overall topic, and then the two characteristics are presented in parallel. て connects the two qualities, while も shows that her personality also has a good quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is used in 頭も, the sentence emphasizes that her mind is also good in addition to a characteristic already mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say 頭はいい when they want to express “intelligent,” but the familiar pattern here is 頭がいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vi: During the New Year holiday, I will travel with my family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 正月は presents a time or holiday occasion as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: と identifies the person who performs the action together with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: いっしょに modifies 行きます and emphasizes going together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the purpose or activity aimed at in the phrase 旅行に行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きます is the main predicate and politely describes going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.why: 正月は sets the time, かぞくといっしょに identifies the companion, and りょこうに行きます is the verb phrase showing travel. The particle に attaches to the activity name in the pattern Nに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with へ, the sentence shows movement toward the family, not going together with the family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of と when saying “with someone”; the person acting together must go with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vi: I went shopping for a while in the neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the place where the shopping took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Nに行く uses に to show the purpose of going; 買いもの is a noun meaning shopping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 行った is the past form of 行く and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.why: The place comes before the purpose, and then the verb 行く comes later. The first に shows the place, while に after 買いもの shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If に, which shows the place, is replaced with へ, the sentence emphasizes the direction toward the neighborhood rather than the location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out に after 買いもの, but 買いものに行く is a fixed expression meaning to go shopping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vi: Yesterday’s meeting was shorter than I thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with the noun かいぎ, forming a phrase that modifies the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes yesterday’s meeting the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: より states the comparison standard; the clause おもっていた refers to what the speaker had thought earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 短かった is the い adjective in the past form and states the comparison result for the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.why: The phrase より comes before the adjective to provide the comparison standard, while the adjective at the end of the sentence states the meeting’s actual quality. The past form shows that the meeting has ended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほど is used in a negative structure, the sentence means that the meeting was not as short as expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q7.kobun.tip: より must come after the comparison standard, not after the result as is often arranged in Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vi: Because I have a lot of work, I am very busy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks work as the thing that exists in a large amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: あって is the て form of ある, connecting the cause of having a lot of work with the state of being busy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い at the end of the sentence is the main predicate and describes the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.why: The clause about having a lot of work comes first and is connected with て to lead to the result of being busy. が clarifies that the existing object is 仕事, while いそがしい ends the sentence and states the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more clearly and formally: because there is a lot of work, I am busy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q8.kobun.tip: て should not be mechanically translated as “and” here; in this sentence, it connects a cause with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vi: Mr. Yamamoto plans to arrive at the station at 3 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Mr. Yamamoto the topic of the plan being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the expected time of arrival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle に marks the destination of the verb 着く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary form 着く comes before よてい to modify the planned action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: 予定です is a sentence-final expression that turns the preceding action into the content of a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the time and destination. The verb in dictionary form comes before 予定 to show the action included in the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with つもりです, the sentence emphasizes Yamamoto’s personal intention more than a plan that has already been made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.tip: With 着く, the place usually goes with に. を is not used because the station is a destination, not an object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., Mrs., or a polite title
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t8-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + 予定だ/です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.vi: The skirt is too long, so I often accidentally step on it on the stairs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle が marks the subject that has the characteristic of being long.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb that modifies the adjective 長くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the くて form to connect a cause or condition to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle で indicates the place where the stepping action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form of ふむ connects the action to the auxiliary verb しまいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: しまいます expresses an unintended action or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.why: スカートが states the object with the characteristic of being long, and とても increases the degree of that characteristic. 長くて connects the cause to the action occurring at かいだんで, while ふんでしまいます adds the sense of accidentally or unwillingly doing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 長いので, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer and more formal, but it cannot connect directly in the くて form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If the past form しまいました is used, the accidental stepping is presented as an action that happened and finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use the plain form 長い to connect directly to the following clause; the adjective い must change to 長くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.tokens.3.m: long and; because it is long
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q1.kobun.cn: Aいくて + Vて + しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.vi: Mount Fuji is very beautiful in winter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle の connects winter with Mount Fuji to limit the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle は makes Mount Fuji the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective うつくしい to show a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: An adjective ending in い acts as the predicate and describes the topic’s quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ですよ is used for emphasis and to give information to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.why: ふゆのふじ山 identifies the subject by season, とても shows the degree, and then うつくしい acts as the predicate. よ at the end of the sentence adds a reporting or emphatic tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with きれいな, the meaning is still “beautiful,” but this is an adjective ending in な, so it must use the form きれいな before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If よ is replaced with ね, the sentence changes from a reporting tone to confirmation or a request for agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use きれいい, but きれい is an adjective ending in な and does not have the form きれいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.vi: This chocolate is a little bitter, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before チョコレート to identify the chocolate near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle は makes the chocolate the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ちょっと slightly reduces the degree of bitterness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: An adjective ending in い acts as the predicate and describes the taste of the chocolate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: ですね expresses a mild opinion and invites agreement from the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.why: After stating the topic with は, the sentence uses ちょっと to reduce the degree and then uses にがい as the predicate. ね turns the opinion into a shared comment or mild confirmation with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ね is replaced with よ, the sentence sounds more like a report or assertion to the listener than a shared opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out ちょっと, but this word makes the sentence less strong: it means “a little bitter,” not “very bitter.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.vi: When I was young, I was very afraid to go to the bathroom alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with とき to create a phrase showing a time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the time 子どものとき the background of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the way the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination of 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: の nominalizes 行く, while が marks going as the object that is felt to be frightening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: こわい changes the sentence to the polite past tense to describe a past feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.why: The phrase 子どものときは sets the background first, followed by the way of acting and the destination. The pattern 行くのがこわい makes going the subject of the feeling of fear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used instead of が, the sentence emphasizes or contrasts going itself rather than stating the natural subject of the feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning is almost the same, but こと sounds more general and formal than の in conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 行く, but a destination with 行く must use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.vi: When climbing a mountain, let’s take enough water with us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the destination or place toward which the action のぼる is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: とき creates a time phrase, while は presents that time as the background.
