default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun 水 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks water as the thing being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects the action 持つ with 行く to express taking something along.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: ましょう creates an invitation or suggestion to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning to state the situation, followed by the thing to bring and the action sequence 持って行く. を marks 水 as the object of 持つ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of は, the sentence indicates a more specific time and loses the sense of stating a general background.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 来る is used, it means “let’s bring the water toward the speaker or to the place considered the destination.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily leave out particle を before the thing being carried, but 持つ usually needs Nを.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.vi: When I called the library, they answered very politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object or place that receives the call from 電話する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects an action that has happened with the following result or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies 丁寧に to show the degree of politeness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The に form of the adjective な 丁寧に modifies the way of answering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects 答える with くれる in a pattern showing an action that benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: くれました shows that another person answered in a way that benefited or helped the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.why: たら connects the act of calling with the result of receiving an answer. とても and ていねいに modify the degree and manner of the answering action, respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence emphasizes a result that usually happens immediately or naturally whenever one calls.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもらいました is used, the focus shifts to the fact that someone answered for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate に as “with,” but in 電話する, Nに usually refers to the place or person being called.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.vi: I am busy, but I still meet my university friends from time to time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings: being busy but still meeting friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun 大学 with 友だち to identify the type of friends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the person met, while は adds a contrastive or topic-limiting nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: たまに modifies あいます to show how often the meeting occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.why: が is placed between two clauses to create a contrastive relationship. The phrase 友だちとは names the person met and emphasizes that, although the speaker is busy, meeting friends still happens sometimes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used instead of とは, the sentence simply states the person met in a neutral way and no longer has a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: ときどき also means sometimes, but it usually suggests a more regular frequency than たまに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と to connect two contrasting sentences, but here が is needed after the busy clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.vi: Because work was busy, I could hardly travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the state of being busy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い changes to くて to connect the reason with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: ほとんど modifies できませんでした and usually goes with a negative form to show a degree close to zero.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も means “also,” replaces を, and marks traveling as an action that could not be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: The polite past negative form describes being unable to travel in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくて; past negative potential verb: Vられませんでした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.why: いそがしくて connects the busy state of the work with the result of being unable to do something. ほとんど combines with the negative form to emphasize that traveling was almost impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If いそがしいので is used, the reason is presented more gently and objectively than when it is connected directly with くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q16.kobun.tip: When an adjective ending in い is connected to the following clause, い must change to くて; で is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.vi: The other day, I saw Mr. Kawaguchi at the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: このあいだ modifies the whole sentence to show when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the seeing action occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person seen as the object of 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ました expresses an action that happened in polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.why: The time adverb comes at the beginning, the place comes before the object, and the predicate ends the sentence. で is used for the place where the action 見る occurs, while を marks the person seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If にいました is used, the sentence only says that someone was at the station; it does not express the action of seeing someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If が見えました is used, it means that Mr. Kawaguchi came into view or was visible, without emphasizing that the speaker actively looked at him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for a place in every situation, but the place where an action occurs must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.vi: Because I studied a lot every day, the N4 exam will surely be fine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.sk: N(time) ＋ Adverb ＋ Vたので、 ＋ Adverb ＋ Nの ＋ Nは ＋ Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: This part shows the time or frequency of the studying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: This word modifies the studying action and shows a large amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason with the result; した is the past form of the studying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: This word modifies the whole statement that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects N4 with the following noun to modify the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: は makes the N4 exam the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: This is the predicate and describes the exam as having no problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.why: The sentence first gives the reason and then gives an opinion about the exam. は marks the topic, while ので connects the reason and result naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので replaces から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of ので to connect the reason, which makes the sentence lose its reason–result structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.vi: The homework is almost finished, and it will be complete in five more minutes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.sk: Nは ＋ Adverb ＋ Vている、 ＋ Time periodで ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the homework the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: This word modifies the completed state and shows that it is nearly complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ていて connects the completed state with the following information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the time needed for the task to finish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the predicate and says that the homework will be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.why: The sentence first states the homework's current condition, then adds the remaining time until completion. で combines with the time period to create a completion point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ５分までに is used, it means the task must be completed before or by the five-minute point at the latest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse で, which indicates the time needed for completion, with に, which indicates when an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q19.tokens.4.n: auxiliary verb in the て form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.vi: This pink coat is cute on the inside too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: ピンクの modifies the noun コート in the form NのN.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は marks the coat as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も replaces は and adds the meaning “also,” showing that the inside has the stated feature too.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective い modifies the noun いろ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends a noun sentence and creates a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.why: この and ピンクの modify コート in turn to identify which coat. After the topic コートは, うらも adds the inside; かわいい comes before いろ to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If も is replaced with は, the sentence talks only about the inside and loses the meaning “the inside is also the same.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q2.kobun.tip: も means “also” and usually takes the place of は or が. Do not add は immediately after も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.vi: I still cannot remember the kanji.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.sk: Nが + なかなか + negative potential verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks what can or cannot be remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: This word modifies a negative predicate and emphasizes that the result is difficult to achieve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: This is the negative potential form, expressing an inability to remember.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.why: が marks what needs to be remembered, while the negative potential form shows that remembering cannot be done. なかなか is often used with a negative form to express a continuing situation that has not yet been achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If あまり is used, the sentence only says that the person does not remember much. This is weaker than the meaning of still being unable to remember.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate なかなか as “quite,” but in a negative sentence it usually means “still cannot.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.vi: Because I was in a hurry, I forgot to receive my change at the cashier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.ch.0.vi: because I was in a hurry
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: ていて connects the state of being in a hurry with the later action of forgetting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the action of receiving the change took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the change as the object received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the verb もらう into a noun, while を marks receiving as the object that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.why: The state of being in a hurry comes first as the cause. Receiving the change is nominalized with の and then becomes the object of わすれました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことを is used, the meaning is still that the person forgot to receive the change, but the expression sounds more general or formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit の when connecting a verb with を, but の or こと must be used to turn the whole action into an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.vi: I forgot her birthday, so I was scolded a lot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.sk: Nの + Nを + Vて、 + adverb + passive Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows the possessive relationship between her and the birthday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the birthday as the object that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects forgetting with the later result of being scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: This word modifies the degree of being scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: This is a passive predicate, showing that the speaker received an action from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.why: The sentence places the cause before the result by using the て form. おこられました uses the passive form to emphasize that the speaker was the person who suffered the scolding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If おこりました is used, it means that someone became angry. It no longer means that the speaker was scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse the passive and active forms and understand おこられました as “became angry” instead of “was scolded.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.vi: This type of fruit was imported from Thailand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to point to a specific object near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this fruit the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the starting point of the imported goods.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: This is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.why: The sentence makes the goods the topic, then shows the starting point with から, and only after that gives the action of importing. The importer is omitted because it is not important in this context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If タイで is used, it means that the importing action took place in Thailand. It does not emphasize that the goods came from there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に instead of から, but から clearly shows the starting point “from Thailand.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.vi: This soup tastes a little bland.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the soup the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object whose state is being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: うすい is the adjective い used as the predicate; です creates a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.why: は makes the soup the topic, while が marks the taste being described. ちょっと comes before the adjective to reduce its degree, creating the meaning “a little bland.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If スープはうすいです is said directly, it means that the soup itself is thin or bland, without focusing specifically on its taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure also talks about the taste of the food, but clearly shows the relationship “the taste of N.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after あじ, but the state being described usually uses が: あじがうすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.vi: My dog went missing, so I am worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects うち with 犬 to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the dog as the subject that enters a state of disappearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: いなくなる changes to the て form to connect this state with the following action of worrying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: している shows a state that is continuing at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.why: The phrase うちの犬が is the subject of いなくなる. Then, the て form connects the cause or situation with the state 心配している. ている emphasizes that the worried state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If いなくなったので is used, the cause is stated more clearly, with the meaning “because it disappeared.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If いなくなってしまった is used, it emphasizes that the event happened unintentionally or caused regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q25.kobun.tip: Do not understand ている as always meaning “be doing.” With 心配している, it usually indicates a state of being worried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.vi: For your health, you should exercise every day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.sk: N のために + time + Vた + ほうがいいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ために indicates the purpose or reason for the action 運動したほうがいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: A time adverbial shows when an action should be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb comes before ほう to form a pattern for giving advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ほうがいいです expresses advice about what someone should do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.why: The purpose phrase けんこうのために and the time phrase 毎日 come before the advice. The verb うんどうした uses the た form before ほうがいい to say that the action should be performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If といいです is used, the advice sounds softer and is closer to “it would be good to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with しなければなりません, the meaning becomes a compulsory duty, not just advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.tip: For advice about what someone should do, use the た form before ほうがいい; the ない form has the opposite meaning: someone should not do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q3.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない + ほうがいいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.vi: Athletes always pay attention to their health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: スポーツの modifies せんしゅ and indicates an athlete in the field of sports.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the sports athlete as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the object that needs attention in the phrase 気をつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を is a fixed particle in 気をつける, while ています expresses a continuing state or habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.why: スポーツのせんしゅ creates a noun phrase and then makes that phrase the topic with は. The phrase けんこうに気をつけています uses に for the object being watched and を in the idiom 気をつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 注意しています is used, the meaning is still “pay attention,” but the tone is more formal and suggests always staying alert.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 気にしています is used, the sentence focuses on worrying about or thinking about health, rather than actively taking care to protect it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q4.kobun.tip: Do not say 気をつける健康; the correct pattern is object + に + 気をつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.vi: Every day, let us eat salad and get plenty of vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.sk: Time + Nを + Vて、 + Nを + Quantity + Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The time adverb modifies both actions in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the food that is eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of eating with the next action in the same call to action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the vegetables that are added or taken in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: A quantity adverb that modifies とりましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The form ましょう expresses an invitation or a call to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.why: まいにち is placed at the beginning of the sentence to show general frequency. The two verbs are connected with the て form, and then とりましょう gives a call to perform the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べてから is used, the sentence emphasizes finishing the salad before adding vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べながら is used, the two actions are understood to happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q5.kobun.tip: The form て here connects two successive actions or actions in the same call to action. It does not automatically mean “because,” as から does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.vi: The fish is cooked and gives off a delicious smell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.sk: N が + Vて、 + Aい (remove い) + そうな + N が + する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that is being cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects this state with the clause that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: そうな changes the adjective into a modifier for the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the smell as the subject of the expression します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: します combines with におい to express having or giving off a smell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.cn: Aい (remove い) + そうな + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.why: The clause やけて states the earlier condition, and the result perceived is においがします. そうな comes before におい because it modifies the noun and expresses an appearance of deliciousness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence directly states that the smell is delicious, without emphasizing an uncertain impression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If そうに is used, this word usually modifies a verb and does not come directly before the noun におい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners can easily use the original form おいしいそうな, but with adjectives ending in い, they must remove い before そうな.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.vi: This snack is not a gift; it belongs to me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify an object near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes this snack the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ではなくて negates a noun and connects it to the contrasting information that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の expresses possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: ものです acts as a noun predicate and confirms that the snack belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.why: After the topic おかしは, the sentence rules out the possibility that it is a gift with ではなくて and then gives the correct information. じぶんの comes before もの to show that the object belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ではなく is used, the connection is more formal and concise, while ではなくて has a natural conversational tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If じゃなくて is used, the meaning does not change, but the tone is more casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle の in じぶんのもの, making the possession relationship unclear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q7.kobun.cn: N ではなくて、N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.vi: At the park area, the road divides into a right side and a left side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects こうえん with ところ to modify the location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where a state or event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the road as the subject in the state of dividing into two directions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: と connects the two directions created by the division.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に indicates the directions into which the road divides.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: ている expresses the current state resulting from a division that has already occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.why: ところで identifies where the state occurs, while みちが is the subject of わかれています. と and に respectively connect and mark the two directions into which the road divides.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes an existing state, so it fits a road that is currently divided into branches.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with てあります, the sentence suggests a state intentionally arranged by someone, which is unnatural for a road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate で as “in” in every situation, but here で only indicates where the state occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q8.tokens.11.m: be, exist; be in a state
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.vi: This area is full of buildings, but the suburbs also have mountains and rivers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this place the topic to be described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ばかり shows that there are mostly only buildings, while が connects to a contrasting idea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle には states the location and creates a contrast with ここ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も marks the mountain as something that also exists there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: も is repeated to add the river to the list of things that exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: あります is an existence predicate used for things that are not living.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.why: The sentence contrasts two places: ここ and こうがい. ばかり limits the scenery to buildings in the first area, while も connects things that exist together in the suburbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけ is used, it means there are only buildings. The meaning is more neutral and does not strongly suggest that the whole place is covered with buildings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If しか～ない is used, the sentence must be negative and the limitation is emphasized more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse ばかり with しか, but ばかり does not have to be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t80-q9.kobun.cn: N ＋ ばかりだ・です; N ばかりだが・ですが
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.vi: Both my father and mother raised me with great care.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: も marks the father as one member of the listed group of subjects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: も connects the mother with the father and creates the structure “both father and mother”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the person who was raised by the parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: たいせつに is the に form of the adjective な and modifies the way the raising was done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: そだてる changes to the て form to connect with くれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: くれました shows that the raising was done for the speaker's benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.why: 父も母も become the joint subject through the repetition of も, creating the meaning “both father and mother.” The main verb そだてる connects to くれる with the て form to show an action that benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If そだててあげました is used, the speaker presents themself or their side as the person doing the action for someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If そだててもらいました is used, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving care from their parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may simply translate くれる as “give,” but here it expresses help or a benefit directed toward the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.vi: I came to Japan and made many more friends, so I am very happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the destination of the action 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of coming with the next clause in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the result ふえて with the feeling of happiness in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ the following clause; Vて is used to connect actions or express a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.why: 来て connects the event of coming to Japan with the situation that follows. 友だちがふえて states the direct reason why the speaker feels うれしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 日本に来たら is used, the sentence means “if/after coming to Japan,” so it is no longer a direct account.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 友だちが増えたので is used, the cause is stated clearly and separated into two complete clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use がうれしい to say “I am happy”; with emotion adjectives, the person feeling the emotion is usually understood to be the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.vi: When going out by car, he is always the driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means of transportation used for going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates the time; は states the situation being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the person performing the role of driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends a noun sentence and states his status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.why: 車で indicates the means of transportation, while あそびに indicates the purpose of 行く. The phrase 行くときは sets the time situation before the main part, and then かれが is the subject of うんてんしゅです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, it usually indicates a direction or destination, not a means of transportation like 車で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に instead of で when talking about transportation, but transportation requires で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.vi: Because of heavy rain, the train is stopped now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: で expresses the cause that led to the train stopping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the present time the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that is currently in a stopped state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ています describes a current state that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.why: おおあめで gives the cause first, and then the sentence moves to the time and the subject of the state. とまっています shows that the train is still stopped now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with とまりました, the sentence only emphasizes that the train stopped and does not emphasize the continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q12.kobun.tip: Do not understand ています as meaning only “be doing.” With state-change verbs such as とまる, it usually indicates a state that has formed and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.vi: I heard that a diamond worth one hundred million yen was stolen from the store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the place from which the property was taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the value to the noun ダイヤモンド and modifies it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object affected in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.ch.3.vi: is said to have been stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ぬすまれた is the past passive form; そうです at the end of the sentence indicates reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.why: みせから states the starting place of the loss, while 一おく円の modifies ダイヤモンド. The passive form makes the diamond the subject, so the thief does not need to be mentioned; そうです adds the meaning of hearsay.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is ぬすまれそうです, it means “it seems likely to be stolen soon,” not information heard about an event that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: With this active form, the subject must be the thief, while ダイヤモンド is no longer the subject of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may overlook the passive form and translate ダイヤモンドが as the person who did the action, but here the diamond is the thing that was stolen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ（伝聞）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.vi: Because there was a stranger in front of the house, I called the police.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects いえ with 前 to indicate a location belonging to the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the location where a person exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: しらない comes before 人 to modify that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that exists in the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ので connects the reason いる with the result of calling the police.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the object being called.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: ました describes an action completed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.why: いえの前に identifies the place, while しらない人 is a noun phrase in which しらない modifies 人. The clause いるので comes first to give the reason, and then けいさつをよびました is the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still expresses a reason, but から is usually more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing ので with が changes the reason relationship into a contrast like “there is someone there, but...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put ので after the result, but in Japanese the reason clause usually comes before the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.vi: I have a lot of clothes that I no longer wear, but I still cannot throw them away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: もう adds the meaning that the time has come when the clothes are no longer worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: きない comes before ふく to modify the clothes that are no longer worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in a large quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: あります states existence, while が connects to the contrasting clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: なかなか is used with a negative sentence to emphasize that something is difficult to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: すてられません is the negative potential form, expressing that something cannot be thrown away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.cn: V可能形AませんAるN ＋ られる with group 2 verbs
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.why: きないふく creates the noun phrase “clothes that are not worn anymore,” and then があります states their existence. が connects two contrasting ideas; なかなか combines with the negative form to emphasize the difficulty of throwing them away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If すてません is used, it only means “do not throw away,” and does not necessarily mean that it is impossible to throw something away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This form can mean “was thrown away” or “could be thrown away,” so it is different from the negative potential form in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand られません as passive, but here it is negative potential: cannot throw away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.vi: I will decide whether to buy that bag after looking at the price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the bag as the object of 買う in the choice clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: かどうか changes clause 買う into a choice question; は makes that choice the topic of the decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the price as the object being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects looking at the price with deciding in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: きめます is the main predicate and describes the action of deciding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.why: 買うかどうかは groups the two possibilities, “buy or not buy,” as the topic to be decided. ねだんを見て comes before きめます to show the basis and order: look at the price first, then decide.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If どうか is omitted, the sentence simply asks or states whether to buy, in a shorter way that emphasizes the pair of choices less.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If を is used instead of は, the phrase becomes the direct object of a verb such as 考える or 知る, rather than the topic of きめます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate かどうか as an independent question, but here it is inside the sentence and functions as the “whether...or not” part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ かどうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.vi: Because I stayed outside for a long time on a cold day, my body became cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the time when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb modifying staying outside and emphasizing duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates where the speaker exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form of いる connects the action of being outside with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the direct subject that falls into a cold state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects the verb ひえる with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.ch.6.n: てしまいました describes an event that has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.why: The phrases showing time and place come before the action. The clause いて connects the cause with the result, while Vてしまう emphasizes that the cold state happened completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If only Vます is used, the sentence merely states the event and does not emphasize the unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If ので is used instead of いて, the cause-and-effect relationship is stated more directly and gently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may forget that てしまう can mean not only finishing something but also expressing regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.vi: I have a fever, a stomachache, and have not felt well since yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle も means “also” and adds another symptom to the information already given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: し connects one reason or symptom with the following idea, showing that this is not the final information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: も continues to mark an added symptom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: し connects the stomachache with the general comment at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle から indicates the starting point of the unwell condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject that has the state わるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective わるい functions as the predicate and describes the health condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.why: The symptoms are listed with も and し before giving a conclusion about the health condition. から is connected to the starting point in time, not to the cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used after a clause, the sentence states the reason more clearly instead of listing several reasons like し.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: も〜も only emphasizes that all the components share the same feature; it does not create the meaning of listing reasons like し.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistake から in きのうから for a time expression, rather than “because yesterday.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ し
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.vi: There will be a meeting at the office tomorrow afternoon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects tomorrow with the afternoon, while は makes that time the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the meeting takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the pattern あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: あります describes the existence or occurrence of a non-living thing or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.why: The time is given as the topic, the place comes before the event, and the event is the subject of あります. で is used for the place where something happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with います, the subject must be a person or animal, not a meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: にあります emphasizes the location where something exists, while であります is suitable for the place where an event happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use に instead of で when talking about the place where an event is held or takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.vi: My older brother's family bought a house nearby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あに with かぞく to show that the family belongs to the older brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the older brother's family as the subject carrying out the purchase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the house was bought or where the house is located.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the house as the object of the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 買う is divided into 買いました to show that the action happened in a polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.why: あにのかぞく is a noun phrase functioning as the subject. に indicates the place related to the house, を marks the thing bought, and the verb at the end completes the information about the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If きんじょで買いました is used, the focus is on the place where the buying happens, such as buying at a nearby shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If きんじょに is understood as a destination, a movement verb is needed; with 買う, に here is connected with the location of the house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q2.kobun.tip: Do not assume that every place goes with で; に is often used to indicate where something exists or is located.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.vi: Even after being washed, children's clothes quickly get dirty again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase 子どものふく is the topic discussed throughout the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: Vて＋も creates a concessive condition, meaning that even if the washing is done, the later result still occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The time adverb modifies the action of getting dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects よごれる with しまう in the same pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいます emphasizes that the result happens completely and often has an unwanted meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.why: The topic is placed at the beginning, followed by ても, which states the concessive condition. The adverbs すぐに and てしまう make clear that the clothes quickly reach an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is used, the sentence emphasizes that the result is different from what was expected after washing, rather than expressing a concessive condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If only よごれます is used, the sentence loses the feeling of an unfortunate or unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ても as meaning only but, while here it combines with て to mean even if something is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q20.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ も; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.vi: When the house is empty, please check the lock carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object that is changed into the state of being empty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: にする creates the state of being empty, while ときは indicates the time or situation for carrying out the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverb よく modifies チェックする and shows the degree of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう is the polite invitation or suggestion form of the verb チェックする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.why: The phrase るすにするときは sets the context before the advice. を marks the house and the lock in two different relationships: putting the house into an empty state and checking the lock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If るすになる is used, it means that something becomes empty by itself, without emphasizing an action that puts the house in that state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If るすの場合は is used, the sentence is more formal and means in the case of being away from home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse Nにする with Nになる; にする has a subject that actively makes something change to a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q21.kobun.cn: NをNにする; V辞書形・Nの ＋ とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.vi: The road here is narrow, so please do not park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this place the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the feature せまい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason with the suggestion or request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: Vないでください is used to politely ask the listener not to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.why: The place is stated first, and then the road is described as the reason. から connects the reason with the request not to park, while ないでください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If てはいけません is used, the sentence becomes a stronger rule or prohibition than a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から after every type of sentence, forgetting that with nouns and な adjectives, だ or です is needed before から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ／です ＋ から; Vないでください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.vi: I do not have money now, but I want to become rich in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N が ＋ negative V が ＋ N は ＋ N に ＋ Vたいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time being made the topic of the clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks money as the thing being discussed in the state of not having it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ありません is the polite negative form of ある, while が connects to the contrasting clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: は shifts the time topic to the future to contrast it with the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the state or result reached with the verb なりたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: なりたい is formed from なります in the form without ます, plus たい to express a desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.why: The first clause states the present situation, and then が connects it to the next clause to show a contrast in time and desire. With なりたい, に marks the target state, while たい attaches to the connecting form of the verb to create the meaning want to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence emphasizes wanting to have money, not wanting to become rich.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before a target state, but with なる, に must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q23.tokens.13.m: a person with a lot of money; a rich person
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.vi: A rare bird, even in the world, was discovered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: でも combines with a place to emphasize a wide range, with the sense of even there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective comes before とり to describe the bird.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the bird as the subject that was discovered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 見つかりました is the polite past form of 見つかる, expressing that something was discovered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.why: The opening place phrase defines the range being considered, and the adjective directly before the noun describes the bird. The subject is marked by が and serves as the subject of 見つかりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used instead of でも, the sentence only states the place of discovery or the usual range. It no longer emphasizes even in the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q24.kobun.tip: Do not translate でも here simply as also; it emphasizes the range, even in a place as broad as the world.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.vi: I really love my kind grandmother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the person who has the feeling of love in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the degree of liking stated at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective comes before そぼ to describe the grandmother's personality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: In the pattern 大好きだ, the liked object is usually marked by が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: だいすきです is the predicate that states the speaker's feeling of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.why: The speaker's topic comes first, and the degree とても comes before the description and the predicate. やさしい comes before そぼ to form a noun phrase, while そぼが is the object of the feeling 大好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This substitution is unnatural; with 大好きです, the object usually takes が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may habitually use を, as with the verb meaning like, but 好き and 大好き usually go with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.vi: It will soon be six o'clock, so I will clear the top of the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.sk: Time なので ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it will soon be six o'clock
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the reason to the cleaning action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects つくえ with 上 to form the phrase “the top of the desk.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the top of the desk as the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: かたづけます is the main predicate. Its polite form expresses something the speaker will or plans to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.why: ６時なので gives the reason first and then states the intended action. つくえの上を is the noun phrase referring specifically to the part that needs cleaning, and it is the object of かたづけます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If なので is replaced by だから or なので, the degree of directness in stating the reason changes; から is usually more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This form makes a complete sentence first and then connects it with から, giving the reason a more independent and clearer tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.tip: With a noun, ので requires the form Nなので; do not say Nので in this cause-and-effect structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.vi: My older sister works as a nurse at a hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 場所 で ＋ Occupation を ＋ しています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the older sister the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the occupation performed with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: しています indicates the job the older sister is doing or her current occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.why: は states who is being discussed, で indicates the workplace, and the occupation comes before を to combine with する. しています shows that the work or occupation is continuing at present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 働いています is used, the sentence only says that the older sister is working at a hospital. It does not specify that she is a nurse.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If かんごしです is used, it only confirms the occupation and does not emphasize the action of working as a nurse at a hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate をしています as “doing an object”; with a job name, Nをする means working in that occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q4.kobun.cn: Nを ＋ する／しています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.vi: I went to bed late yesterday, so I overslept today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This is the time point of the sleeping action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: の turns the verb ねる into a noun, while が marks the subject of おそくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective おそい changes to おそくて to connect the reason to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes today the topic and contrasts it with yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects the verb ねぼうする with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: しまいました expresses something that happened unintentionally or caused the speaker regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくて ＋ following clause; Vて ＋ しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.why: The clause おそくて states the reason first, and then the sentence moves to the result that happened today. のが turns ねる into the subject described as おそい, while しまう adds an unintended-result nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If おそくて is replaced by おそいので, the reason is stated more clearly and the explanatory tone is softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ねぼうしちゃいました is used, the meaning stays almost the same but has a casual conversational tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use おそいで incorrectly; an adjective ending in い must change to くて when connecting a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.vi: I want to study law at university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.sk: Nで ＋ Nを ＋ Vます-remove ます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates where the study activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: たい is attached to the verb stem to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ たいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.why: The place comes before the subject of study, followed by the verb expressing the action and たい to state the desire. The particle で is used for the place where an action occurs, while を is used for the subject of study.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If たいです is replaced by つもりです, the sentence changes from expressing a desire to expressing an intention or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If べんきょうすることができます is used, the sentence talks about the ability to study, not the desire to study.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse で with に; because the study activity takes place at the university, 大学で is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.vi: I bought a new textbook for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: のために indicates the purpose of the purchase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective directly modifies テキスト.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.why: The purpose phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the adjective modifying the noun that serves as the object. The verb 買いました at the end of the sentence completes the main idea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 授業で使うように is used, the sentence emphasizes the purpose of use or the desired result more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 授業があるので is used, the sentence changes from expressing purpose to expressing a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place 新しい after the noun; in Japanese, an adjective usually comes before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q7.kobun.cn: Nの・V辞書形 ＋ ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.vi: I will go to the department store to look for a bag to give my older sister.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.sk: Nに ＋ V辞書形 ＋ Nを ＋ Nへ ＋ Vます-remove ますに ＋ 行きます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the receiver of the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before バッグ to modify the bag.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the bag as the thing being looked for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb stem さがし combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.cn: Vます-remove ます ＋ に ＋ 行く・来る・帰る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.why: あげる modifies バッグ, creating the meaning “the bag to give.” After the destination, さがしに行きます expresses going for the purpose of searching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If さがすために行きます is used, the purpose is expressed more formally and is not limited to the pattern meaning “go to do something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: ように is unnatural in this sentence because searching is an intentional purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use さがすに行きます; they must remove ます to form さがし before adding に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.vi: I gave my friend a novel by a famous writer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the receiver of the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な comes before a noun to modify 作家.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 作家 with 小説, showing possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the novel as the thing given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.why: The modifier sequence ゆうめいなさっかの modifies しょうせつ, forming a complete object before を. に states the receiver, while あげました states the act of giving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If the position is changed to 有名な作家の小説, the meaning is similar, but the kanji make the writing clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This structure highlights that the writer is famous, rather than simply meaning a novel belonging to that writer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t81-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often forget な after an adjective ending in な when placing it before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.vi: My pet dog, which was like a member of the family, has died, so I am very sad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: ような comes after の to create a modifying phrase for ペットの犬.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the dog as the subject of the action of dying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: しんで is the て form of しぬ, connecting the dog’s death with the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the degree of sadness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: かなしいです is the predicate expressing the speaker’s feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.why: ような changes かぞくのようだ into a modifier placed before a noun. The て form connects an earlier event with the emotional state stated afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If ように is used, the phrase usually modifies a verb, meaning doing something like a family, and does not directly modify 犬.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q1.kobun.tip: Before a noun, ような must be used; ように usually comes before a verb or adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.vi: I confused salt with sugar, so the food tasted strange.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects the two things confused in the pattern 間違える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object that was confused.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the mistaken action with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な modifies the noun あじ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the result of becoming a certain taste in the pattern なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: なった is the past form of なる, stating the result that occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.cn: N＋に＋なる; Vて connects a preceding cause or development
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.why: The two nouns are connected by と and marked by を to express confusion. へんな modifies あじ, while あじに＋なった expresses the result of becoming a strange taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is substituted, the sentence means that the salt was not confused with the sugar and does not emphasize the cause leading to the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before the thing that was confused and omit と, but this pattern usually uses NとNを間違える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.vi: The company’s autumn trip was decided to be to South Korea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 会社 with the noun phrase that follows, showing belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects あき with りょこう, specifying the time of the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents the company’s autumn trip as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place or option that was decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: きまりました is the predicate, expressing that the decision has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.why: The two phrases の respectively specify that the trip belongs to the company and takes place in autumn. The topic りょこうは is connected to the destination or option by に before きまりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that it has been decided to go to South Korea, while the original sentence focuses on the trip’s decided destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q11.kobun.tip: に should not be understood here as simply indicating direction; with 決まる, に usually indicates the content or option that was decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.vi: I help my mother wash the dishes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the washing action in the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of あらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns あらう into a noun, while を marks the action being helped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: てつだいます is the main predicate and takes あらうのを as its object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.why: The clause 母がおさらをあらう is nominalized with の to become the action that the speaker helps with. が indicates the subject of the washing action, while を after の marks the whole action being helped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: 助ける also means help, but it usually focuses on supporting a person or task, while 手伝う is more natural when doing an activity together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place を after 母, but 母が is the subject of the washing action in the subordinate clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.vi: For my family’s health, I increase the amount of vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かぞく with けんこう, showing that the health belongs to the family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: のために shows the purpose of eating or using more vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object whose amount is increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 多くする means making the amount larger, and しています describes a state or habit that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.why: The phrase かぞくのけんこうのために comes first to state the purpose. やさいを is the object, while 多くしています describes actively making the amount of vegetables larger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes doing something to achieve a state that is good for health, with a clearer goal meaning than ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.tip: Do not translate 多くしています as becoming numerous; する shows that the subject actively increases the amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q13.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい＋ために; Aな＋なために; Nの＋ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.vi: I am often told that I look like my mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the person being described or talked about by someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the person with whom the speaker is compared in 似ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content of the quoted comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: 言われます is the polite passive form, showing that someone else makes this comment about me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.why: わたしは is the topic of the comment, while 母に is the object of comparison because 似ている uses に. The comment comes before と, followed by 言われます to form a passive sentence meaning that someone else says this.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern conveys information that the speaker has heard. It does not emphasize someone directly making the comment about me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means that I am considered to look like my mother, and it focuses more on evaluation or guesswork.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.tip: 似ている goes with に, not with と; と marks the content being said here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q14.kobun.cn: 普通形＋と＋言う; 普通形＋と＋言われる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.vi: My younger brother is still a baby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the younger brother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: まだ modifies the state 赤ちゃん and shows that this state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with a noun showing a state or status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to state the subject, まだ to show that the state has not changed, and the noun あかちゃん as the predicate with です. Therefore, the sentence emphasizes that the younger brother is still small.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed this way, the meaning becomes that he is still not a baby, which is opposite to the original sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern shows that he is no longer a baby, which is opposite to まだ～です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q15.kobun.tip: まだ does not always go with a negative form; in まだNです, it means that the subject is still in that state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.vi: My older sister has studied piano since she was four years old.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time から ＋ N を ＋ Vています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the starting point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ています describes studying that began in the past and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.why: The topic comes first. Then the starting point is shown with から, and the object of study with を. ています shows that the studying is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with まで, the meaning changes to studying until the age of four.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse から, meaning “because of,” with から, which shows the starting point in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q17.kobun.vi: I commute to work by train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the means of transportation used for commuting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the destination of the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ています describes a commuting habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q17.kobun.why: The means of transportation is stated first with で, and the destination follows with に. The verb かよう combines with ています to describe regularly going to the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the focus is on being on the train, not on the habit of commuting by train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show the means of transportation in this sentence; the means of transportation goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.vi: All the senior employees at the company are good people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ Adverb ＋ Aい N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects noun かいしゃ with noun せんぱい to show a relationship of belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the senior employees at the company the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: みんな adds the meaning of the whole group of senior employees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: いい modifies 人, while です ends the polite noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.why: の creates the phrase “the company’s senior employees,” then は makes that phrase the topic. みんな shows the whole subject, while いい modifies the noun 人 in the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence emphasizes that the senior employees are the group with the characteristic, instead of stating them as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q18.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate みんな as a proper noun; here it means “everyone, all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.vi: Let’s review the vocabulary we studied yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Vた ＋ N を ＋ Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう shows the time when the studying took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense clause modifies the noun ことば that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being reviewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: しましょう creates an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ N: the past form comes before a noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.why: きのう identifies the time of studying, while べんきょうした comes directly before ことば to create the phrase “the words studied.” This noun phrase is the object of ふくしゅうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ている, the meaning becomes words that are being studied or are in the process of being studied, without emphasizing that they were completed yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q19.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a modifying clause comes before the noun, not after it as in the usual way of speaking in English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.vi: When going home at night, taking the main road is safer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: よる shows the time when the person goes home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before とき to modify the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the situation of going home as the condition or background for the following comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects とおり with ほう, creating a phrase that shows a side or choice belonging to that road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the choice being judged as safer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: あんぜんです is the predicate that describes the choice just mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.why: よる帰るときは puts the time setting first. The phrase 大きいとおりのほうが is implicitly compared with other roads, and then あんぜんです gives an opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほう is removed, the sentence only says that the main road is safe. It does not stress comparison or choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q2.kobun.tip: ほうが usually implies a comparison; do not understand it as meaning that there is only one road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.vi: I have been interested in Japanese manga since I was little.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with とき to form a phrase referring to the childhood period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point of the state of being interested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: の modifies まんが, referring to manga from Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the object of the interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject that exists in the pattern きょうみがある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: ありました is the polite past form of ある, expressing that there was interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.why: The time phrase with から comes first to state the starting point. The object of interest goes with に, while きょうみがある uses が to mark the existing interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 興味を持つ, the meaning is still being interested, but it emphasizes the action or attitude of directing attention toward the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q20.kobun.tip: With きょうみがある, the object goes with に and きょうみ goes with が; do not use を for the whole phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.vi: Because my friend is getting married, I am thinking about what to give them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of getting married.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.ch.1.vi: because my friend is getting married
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the result and gives a softer explanatory tone than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks what is given in the indirect question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: か turns the question content into a clause that serves as the object of 考える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses an ongoing process of thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. The content being considered comes before 考える, where か marks the indirect question “what to give.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the meaning of the reason stays almost the same, but the explanation sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If かどうか is added, the question becomes whether to give something or not, instead of asking what to give.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.tip: In an indirect question, do not put か at the beginning of the clause; か comes after all the content being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので、; 疑問詞+V普通形+か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.vi: One cup from the pair has broken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ペア with カップ to modify the noun カップ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects カップ with １つ, expressing one part of the cups.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the cup as the object that has entered the broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb われる with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: 〜てしまいました expresses that the event has been completed, often with a sense of regret.
