default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.why: The phrase ペアのカップの１つ expands from the main noun １つ, while が marks the object that is broken. The て form connects われる with しまう to show that the event happened completely and regrettably.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 〜ている, the sentence only describes a state of being broken or having broken. It does not emphasize regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit て when using しまう, but this pattern always requires the て form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q22.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう/しまいます/しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.vi: My younger sister is looking forward to a gift from me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the younger sister is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: から shows the source of the gift, while の connects this phrase to プレゼント.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the gift as the object being looked forward to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: に creates the fixed phrase たのしみにする, expressing that something is regarded as an expectation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 〜にしています expresses a continuing state of anticipation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.why: The phrase わたしからのプレゼント comes before を to clarify who the gift is from. たのしみにしている is a fixed phrase in which に marks the continuing state of anticipation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 期待している, the meaning is still expectation, but the tone is more formal and active.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in たのしみにしている as a place; the whole phrase means “look forward to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q23.kobun.cn: Nを + 楽しみにしている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.vi: As for tomorrow’s picnic, let’s leave at 6 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.sk: N の + N は + Time に + Vます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あした with ピクニック to identify when the picnic takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the picnic is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the time of departure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: 〜ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do an action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.cn: Vます形 omit ます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.why: あしたのピクニック forms a complete topic before は. The time is placed before the verb and goes with に, while ましょう changes a statement into an invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 〜ませんか, the sentence becomes a gentler invitation that asks for the listener’s opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use を for a specific time; the time when an action occurs usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.vi: In autumn, I want to go to the mountains to see the beautiful autumn leaves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.sk: N は + N へ + Aな + N を + Vます omit ます に + Vたいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes autumn the topic and the time setting of the speaker’s wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: へ shows the direction of movement toward the mountains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before a noun and keeps な to modify こうよう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the autumn leaves as the object of viewing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: The ます form of 見る combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: 〜たいです expresses the speaker’s wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.cn: Vます形 omit ます + に行く; Vます形 omit ます + たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.why: 山へ shows the direction of travel, while 見に shows the purpose of going: going to see the autumn leaves. きれいな comes directly before the noun to modify it, while たい at the end of the sentence expresses the speaker’s wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見て行きたい is used, the meaning leans toward wanting to see something and then go, so the pattern “go in order to see” is no longer clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 見に行きます, the sentence only states that the speaker will go to see something and does not express a wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q25.kobun.tip: With the pattern Vます, omit ます＋に行く; do not use the dictionary form such as 見るに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.vi: I wanted to buy a dictionary, but there was no one at a suitable price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks “dictionary” as the object of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 買いたかった expresses a past desire, while のですが connects to a situation contrary to that desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: てきとうな is a な adjective placed before ねだん to modify the price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: の replaces an omitted noun, meaning something with a suitable price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the thing with a suitable price as the subject considered in a state of nonexistence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: ありませんでした is the polite negative past form of ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.why: The first part states the desire to buy, then のですが shifts to the result that no suitable item was found. てきとうなねだんの is an abbreviated noun phrase, while が marks the missing suitable item in sentence ありませんでした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If the full expression もの is used instead of の, the meaning does not change, but the sentence is clearer and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If の is omitted, the sentence can still be connected with が, but the explanatory tone or introduction to the following situation becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q3.kobun.tip: の in 値段の does not simply show possession; it replaces an omitted noun such as もの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q4.kobun.vi: You were off last week. How is your health now?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the time point the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects the situation in the first part with the question in the second part, with a gentle shift in topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes health the topic; いかがでしょうか is a polite way to ask about a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q4.kobun.why: The first part gives the previous time and situation, then が shifts to a caring question. お体はいかがでしょうか uses は to make health the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If いかがでしょうか is used in this sentence, the question is still correct but less formal and less gentle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use どう instead of いかが in a polite caring question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.vi: I studied Italian, but I have completely forgotten it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks イタリア語 as the object of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects having studied with the unexpected result of forgetting it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies わすれてしまいました and shows the extent of forgetting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the verb わすれる with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました shows that an action has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or something having happened unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.why: を marks the language studied, while が connects two contrasting ideas. すっかり comes before the verb phrase to emphasize completely forgetting, and てしまう expresses the fully completed result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 忘れました is used, the sentence simply states that the speaker forgot and has less of a feeling of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit て before しまう and say 忘れしまいました, but the て form must be used for the connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.vi: Compared with the past, it has been raining more recently, hasn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.sk: N に ＋ Vると、＋ Time ＋ N が ＋ 副詞 ＋ Vますね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the point used for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects the comparison phrase with a comment about the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase indicates the time when the phenomenon being discussed occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the phenomenon as the subject of the verb ふります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: This adverb modifies ふります and indicates a large amount of rain or frequent rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: ふります is the main predicate; ね is used to confirm the comment together with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.why: The phrase むかしにくらべると places the comparison standard at the beginning of the sentence. The sentence then states the present time, the rain, and its high amount to make a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If むかしより is used instead, the comparative meaning is almost unchanged, but より directly marks the comparison point and does not create a clause like くらべると.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate と as “and,” but in this structure と connects a condition or comparison point with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.vi: I think that person's name is probably Yamashita...
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あの人 with なまえ to modify the noun “name.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes “name” the topic of the guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: たしか modifies the whole thought that follows and shows that the memory is not completely certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: だと marks the content of the thought; 山下さん is the part judged to be the name.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: が connects an uncertain statement with an ellipsis, making the speaker sound hesitant or as if inviting the listener to continue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.why: The possessive phrase あの人のなまえ is made the topic by は. The guessed content comes before とおもいます, while が and the ellipsis reduce the strength of the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If が．．． is omitted, the sentence becomes a complete statement of opinion and sounds less hesitant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand と in だと思います as “and,” but here it marks the content of the thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.vi: If I could study abroad in Japan, I would be very happy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.sk: もし ＋ N に ＋ past potential V ＋ たら、＋ とても ＋ Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: もし introduces an assumption and usually goes with たら in the condition clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination or place where studying abroad takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: できたら is the たら form, connecting a hypothetical condition with the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies うれしい, while うれしいです is the predicate expressing a feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.why: The condition clause comes first and ends with たら. The sentence then states the feeling if that condition becomes real. に is connected with the place of study abroad, while とても emphasizes how happy the speaker is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with なら, the sentence focuses more on a condition based on information or a topic already mentioned. It does not emphasize a hypothetical event as たら does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use できるたら, but it must be changed to the past form できた before adding ら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q8.kobun.cn: Vた・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.vi: I want to try playing this game, but I do not understand the rules well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the game as the object of trying to play it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: やってみたい expresses the wish to try doing something; が gently connects the opening statement with the problem mentioned afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks ルール as the object that is or is not understood clearly in sentence わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies わかりません and shows the level of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: わかりません is the main predicate. It states the problem that prevents the speaker from playing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.why: を marks the game the speaker wants to try, while が marks the content that is not clearly understood. やってみたいんですが puts the wish first and then uses が to move to the reason or obstacle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If やってみたい is replaced with やりたい, the sentence only means wanting to play and loses the sense of wanting to try the experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is placed after わかりません, the sentence changes direction and the opening is no longer a soft introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily always translate が as “but” and miss the soft opening nuance of が in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t82-q9.tokens.12.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.vi: I want to watch this movie, but I still have not watched it because I do not have time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the movie as the object of 見たい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: たい expresses a wish, while んですが serves as a soft opening before the following situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks time as the subject of the state ない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: なくて is the connecting form of ない and shows the reason for not having watched it yet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: まだ modifies 見ていません and shows that the action is still incomplete up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: Vていません describes an action that has not happened or has not been completed at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.cn: Vます omits ます＋たい＋んです＋が; Aい omits い＋くて; Vて＋いません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.why: The wish is stated first with たいんですが. Then が gently shifts to the situation that prevents it. 時間がなくて gives the reason, while まだ combines with 見ていません to confirm that the movie has not been watched up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 時間がないので, the sentence gives the reason more directly and formally, with less of the soft connecting nuance of なくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.kobun.tip: With an adjective ending in い, ない must be changed to なくて when connecting a reason; do not use ないで in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q10.tokens.11.m: not have; because there is no
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.vi: When I did something bad, my father scolded me severely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the thing done in the condition clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: すると connects a condition with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: In a passive sentence, に refers to the person who performs the action affecting the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: きびしく is the adverbial form and modifies the scolding action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: しかられました is the polite past passive form. It says that the speaker was scolded by their father.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.why: すると makes doing something bad the condition leading to the result. The sentence uses the passive because the speaker is affected, while 父に refers to the person who scolds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with たら, the sentence focuses on a more specific condition rather than a general rule or usual result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q5.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person who performs the action usually goes with に, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vi: I do not know how to prepare for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects よしゅう with 仕方, creating a phrase that means how to prepare for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks 仕方 as the thing that is or is not understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.vi: do not understand, do not know
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: わかりません is the polite negative form of わかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.why: よしゅうの 仕方 is a noun phrase in which の connects the content with the method. With わかる, the thing understood usually acts as the subject and goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: よしゅうをしません means not preparing for class, which is different from not knowing how to prepare for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 仕方, but わかる usually uses が to mark the thing that is understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q1.tokens.4.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vi: There is a restaurant inside that building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies 建物 and refers to something far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 建物 with 中 to identify the inside of the building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the location where the restaurant exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that exists at that location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is used to talk about the existence of an object or a place, not a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.why: The phrase あの建物の中に identifies the location first. Then レストランが states what exists there. The pattern location に ＋ thing が あります is the basic word order for saying “what exists where”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the phrase usually refers to the place where an action takes place, not the location where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If います is used, the noun referring to what exists must be a person or an animal instead of a restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q10.kobun.tip: In an existence sentence, the location goes with に and the existing thing goes with が; で is not used in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vi: There is a small forest near the university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 大学 with そば to modify the location そば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the location where the small forest exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the existing thing in the sentence with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q11.kobun.why: The location is stated first with そばに, and then the existing thing is marked with が. あります is used for things other than people and animals that exist in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with います, the subject must be a person or animal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use あります for people or animals; these subjects usually go with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vi: I take a walk around the pond.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 池 with まわり to form the phrase “around the pond”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を indicates the area or route through which the speaker walks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q12.kobun.why: 池のまわり forms the place “around the pond”, while を marks the area passed through during the walk. さんぽします is the main predicate in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence emphasizes the place where the activity happens, not the route taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q12.kobun.tip: With movement verbs such as “to take a walk”, を can indicate the route or area of movement, not only the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vi: This is a park for the city’s residents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は states ここ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 市民 with ため to indicate the intended person or group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ための modifies こうえん and shows the purpose or the person who benefits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a noun sentence and identifies ここ as a park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.why: ここは is the topic, while 市民のための comes before こうえん to modify “park”. The pattern Nのための N describes something intended for or serving a person or group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 市民のために is used, the phrase usually modifies an action and means “do something for the residents”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q13.kobun.tip: Distinguish ための + noun from ために + verb: の connects to a noun, while に usually connects to an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vi: This elevator cannot carry eight or more people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.sk: この Nは + number以上は + Vません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the elevator being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は states エレベーター as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks the stated quantity as a limiting condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: のれません is the polite negative form of 乗る and expresses that someone cannot get on or use the elevator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.why: このエレベーターは states the limited subject, while 八人以上は states the quantity that creates the restriction. のれません expresses that it is impossible to get on the elevator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 八人まで, it means “up to eight people”, so eight people are still allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q14.kobun.tip: 以上 includes the number before it; 八人以上 means eight or more people, not more than eight people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vi: Please turn up the volume a little.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks 音 as the thing being adjusted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 大きく is the く form of the adjective 大きい and modifies the action of making the sound louder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the action して with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.why: 音を is the thing being adjusted, and 大きくして expresses making the sound louder. The pattern Vてください comes at the end of the sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vてもいいです, the sentence asks about or gives permission for an action, so it is no longer a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vていただけますか is used, the request becomes more formal and sounds more like a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q15.kobun.tip: Do not connect 大きい directly to して; an adjective ending in い must change to 大きく before する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vi: My son has become a university student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は states むすこ as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the result or state reached after a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる and expresses a completed change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.why: むすこは is the topic, while 大学生に indicates the new state reached by the subject. なる combines with に to express a change into another noun or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Nである, it only states that someone is a student and does not emphasize the process of becoming one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vことになりました is used, it expresses a decision or arrangement that has been made, not a direct change in status.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q16.kobun.tip: With なる, a noun or adjective な usually goes with に; do not use を to indicate the result of a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.vi: Does this express train go to Kyoto?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun that follows and means “this”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きますか forms a polite question about going to the stated place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.why: The noun topic comes before は, followed by the destination with へ, and then the verb 行きます. The question form か is placed at the end to ask about the topic’s direction of travel.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is replaced with に, the sentence still indicates the destination, but focuses more strongly on the place to be reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may easily misuse を or に, but direction of travel is usually marked with へ or に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q18.kobun.vi: I stick a stamp on the envelope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the thing or place affected by the sticking action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing being stuck on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: はります is the polite present form of the verb はる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q18.kobun.why: The affected surface or object goes with に, while the thing being stuck on goes with を. The natural order is the affected place or object first, followed by the object and the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence may be understood as indicating the place or means of the action, not the thing being stuck on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q18.kobun.tip: Do not translate に here mechanically as “into”; it marks the surface or object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.vi: I borrowed a book at the library of the neighboring city.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies 市 and identifies the neighboring city.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 市 with としょかん and shows a relationship of belonging or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the borrowing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing being borrowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: かりました is the polite past form and shows that the borrowing was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.why: The phrases の successively connect the modifiers from “neighboring” to “city”, and then from “city” to “library”. After the place marked with で, 本を is the object and かりました is the main action in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of で, the sentence emphasizes the source or place from which the book was obtained rather than the place where the action occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q19.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit の between nouns, causing the modifier chain such as となりの市のとしょかん to be incorrectly separated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vi: I prepare tea in the kitchen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.sk: Place で + N の + N を + します
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the preparation takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects おちゃ with したく, showing what is being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks したく as the object of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: します combines with the noun したく to form a verb phrase used as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.why: The place where an action takes place goes with で, while the preparation is the object of します, so it goes with を. の connects おちゃ with したく to identify what is being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: 台所にいます indicates existence in the kitchen, not an action performed there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for an action's location, but the place where an action is performed must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q20.kobun.vi: I have absolutely no strength left.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: ぜんぜん modifies a negative predicate and emphasizes that there is none at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks something that does not appear or does not exist in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: 出ません is the polite negative form of 出る, expressing that strength does not appear or does not take effect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q20.kobun.why: ぜんぜん comes before the predicate to add a degree of negation. 力が is the grammatical subject, while 出ません expresses that strength does not appear or does not take effect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If あまり is used, the sentence means “not ... very much,” which is weaker than ぜんぜん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q20.kobun.tip: ぜんぜん usually goes with a negative predicate; a positive form should not be used in this basic pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person whose feelings or preferences are being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object judged to be liked in the structure 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, expressing a preference or positive feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q21.kobun.why: The person with the preference is stated as the topic with は, while the liked content goes with が. 好き is an な adjective, so its polite ending is です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced by を, the sentence no longer follows the basic structure 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 興味があります is used, the meaning changes to “be interested in,” which is more objective than 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say 旅行を好きです, but the object of 好き usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.vi: The next express train will arrive at 3 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies 急行, identifying the next express train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the train being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates when the train will arrive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 来ます is the polite form of 来る, expressing an arrival according to a schedule or expectation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.why: つぎの modifies the noun 急行, and the whole phrase then becomes the topic with は. A specific time comes before the verb and goes with に to identify when the train will arrive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used after 3時, the sentence does not fit the way a single event's time is expressed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q22.kobun.tip: For a specific time such as 3時, use に; do not use で out of habit from translating Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.vi: Because I had a headache, I went to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the body part with the symptom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a cause with a result and means “because.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle へ indicates the direction of movement to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行く is in the polite past form and expresses an action that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.why: The symptom phrase comes first, followed by ので to give the reason for going to the hospital. が marks the subject with the painful condition, while へ marks the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので replaces から, the sentence still means “because,” but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of が in the symptom pattern, making the sentence less natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q24.kobun.vi: The water supply has broken down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object that enters a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the verb 壊れる with the pattern てしまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: てしまいました expresses that something has been completed, often with a sense of regret or being unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q24.kobun.why: 水道が is the subject of the broken state. The verb in the て form connects with しまいました to emphasize that the event has completely happened and is regrettable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If てしまいました is replaced by ています, the sentence only describes the condition of being broken and does not emphasize that the problem occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may understand しまう as meaning only “finish doing,” but in this sentence it also carries the sense that the event was unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before the noun to modify the movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the movie as the object being watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 見ました is the polite past form of 見る and states the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q25.kobun.why: The adjective おもしろい comes directly before 映画 to describe the movie. を connects that noun with the verb 見ました, forming the relationship “watch a movie.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If おもしろそうな映画 is used, the meaning changes to “the movie seems interesting,” which is only a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the adjective after the noun as in Vietnamese, but Japanese puts the adjective before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vi: My mother is in another room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.sk: N は + N の + Place に + います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states my mother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 別 with へや to modify へや.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates where the mother exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: います expresses the existence of a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.why: The topic comes first with は, followed by the place phrase expanded with の. Because the sentence says where the mother is, へや goes with に and the predicate uses います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence says that the mother works in another room, emphasizing an action rather than only a place of existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit の between 別 and へや, but 別の部屋 is what means “another room.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vi: What is there in Japan's industry?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.sk: N の + Scope には + どんな N が + ありますか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with 工業 to limit the scope of the industry being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the scope of existence, while は presents that scope as a contrastive topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: どんな modifies もの and asks about the type or features of things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the things that exist within the scope being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ありますか creates a question about the existence of objects or events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.why: The phrase にほんの工業には sets the scope first, and then どんなもの asks what types of things exist within that scope. あります is used because もの refers to non-living things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: 何がありますか asks directly what exists, while どんなものがありますか emphasizes the type or form of those things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で in にほんの工業には, but an existence sentence needs に; は only adds the sense of stating a scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vi: I want to work at a newspaper office.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: たい is added after the ます form of a verb to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.why: The sentence puts the person who wants to work in the topic position, then states the place where the action takes place with で. はたらきたいです expresses the speaker’s own desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes a decided plan or intention, not just a desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に with a workplace, but the activity of working uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.vi: I said “Take care of yourself” to a friend who had a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.sk: N を ＋ Vた ＋ N に ＋ 「quoted speech」と ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb ひく in the phrase かぜをひく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: ひいた comes before 友だち to modify “friend.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person receiving the speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the quoted content after 言いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 言いました is the main predicate and takes the quoted content with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.cn: Quoted sentence／word ＋ と ＋ 言う・思う・聞く
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.why: ひいた comes before 友だち to modify “friend who had a cold.” The speech is put in quotation marks and connected to 言いました with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: ように言う is used to convey a request or instruction, while と言う quotes the content of speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that someone does something for someone else. It is not used to quote someone’s exact words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q11.kobun.tip: When reporting speech, Vietnamese speakers may easily omit と; in Japanese, と must be used before 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.vi: My daughter is more than 5 centimeters taller than me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: より states the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects むすめ with ほう to form the phrase “my daughter’s side.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ほうが marks the side chosen as higher in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: This phrase states the difference in height.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the object that has the characteristic 高い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: 高い is the predicate describing height and combines with です to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.why: わたしより is the comparison standard, while むすめのほうが is the side judged to be higher. The difference is placed before the noun being compared in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also makes a comparison, but it makes N1 the topic and does not emphasize N2 as のほうが does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it gives the meaning “about the same as N1,” so it no longer means higher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.tip: より usually comes after the comparison standard, while のほうが comes after the object judged to be higher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q9.kobun.cn: N1 より N2 のほうが ＋ Aい／Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.vi: You seem to be completely used to Japanese culture now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 日本 with ぶんか to form the noun phrase “Japanese culture.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the object that the speaker has become used to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: もう shows that the change of state was complete by the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: すっかり modifies なれた and emphasizes being completely used to it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.ch.4.vi: seem to be used to it, right?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: ようですね expresses a judgment based on signs and adds a gentle sense of confirmation for the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ ようだ; ようですね is used at the end of a sentence to make a guess and gently confirm it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.why: The object marked by に comes before なれた because this verb means being used to something. もう and すっかり both modify the state of being used to it, while ようですね makes the statement a softer judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If なれたみたいですね is used instead, the meaning is almost the same, but it is more conversational and informal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use を with なれる; the object that one is used to must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q15.tokens.5.m: became used to; got used to
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.vi: Thanks to Mr. Hayashi, I was able to leave the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects Mr. Hayashi’s name with おかげ to form a phrase showing help from someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks a cause that brings a positive result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: A dictionary-form verb comes before こと to turn it into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the action of leaving the hospital into a noun; が marks the thing that can be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: できました expresses an ability that was achieved in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.why: おかげで states the positive cause leading to the result. The action たいいんする is turned into a noun with こと, then combined with できました to express “was able to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If せいで is used instead, the cause has a negative feeling or leads to an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: The potential form Vられる also expresses ability, but the structure ことができる is clearer and more neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place こと after できる; in this structure, ことが comes before できる to turn the action into something that can be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ことができる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.vi: Because I hated studying, my mother often scolded me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is disliked in the expression べんきょうがきらい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: きらい is a な adjective and serves as the predicate of a clause describing a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: だった is the past form of きらいだ; ので connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the person who performs the scolding action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: 叱られました is the polite past passive form of 叱る and shows that the speaker received the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ だったので; Vない-removeない ＋ れる・られる; Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.why: The reason is given first with ので, followed by the result that happened often. The sentence uses the passive because the speaker received the action, while 母に indicates the person who caused it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 母が叱りました is used, the focus shifts to the mother as the person who scolds, and no longer emphasizes the person being scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q6.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person who performs the action usually goes with に, not が as the subject of an active sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.vi: This road is crowded on Saturdays because everyone goes home by car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ N で ＋ V辞書形 ＋ ため、＋ Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies 道 and identifies the road being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the road the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: This time phrase shows when the crowded condition occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: みんな is the subject performing the action of going home, even though が is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the means of transportation used to go home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: ため connects the reason to the result stated in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: 混んでいる describes the road as being crowded or congested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.why: 道は is the topic. The sentence then states the time and the subject causing the crowding. くるまで and かえるため explain the means and the reason, while 混んでいる is the resulting condition that continues to exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ため is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more natural in conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: から gives a direct, more conversational reason and often clearly shows the speaker's personal view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に after a means of transportation, but a means of transportation must be used with で in くるまで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.tokens.11.m: be doing; be in a state
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの＋ため（に）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.vi: As expected, winter sweaters and hot coffee are necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: やっぱり expresses a view that matches what the speaker predicted or felt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase modifies セーター and states the type or purpose of the sweater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle と connects セーター and コーヒー, showing that both are things that are necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: あつい comes before コーヒー to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: Particle が marks the things judged to be necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: ひつようです is the predicate that states the necessity of the nouns before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.why: The two nouns セーター and コーヒー are connected by と because both have the role of necessary things. The adjective あつい comes directly before コーヒー to limit the meaning of that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the sentence emphasizes or contrasts the topic, while が directly presents the thing that is necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.tip: The adjective ending い comes directly before a noun and does not take の, so the phrase is あついコーヒー.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q10.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ N; N と N; N が ＋ ひつようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.vi: Because I practiced hard, I think I can certainly win the match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the action of practicing and shows how it is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies れんしゅうしました and emphasizes practicing well or a lot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: れんしゅう combines with しました to form the verb “practice.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: から comes after a past clause to give the reason for the statement that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: きっと modifies 思います and shows a high level of confidence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: Particle に indicates the situation or competition in which the winning is aimed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: と marks the content being thought or believed and connects clause かてる with 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.ch.7.n: 思います is the final predicate and takes the quoted content before と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ から; normal clause ＋ と ＋ 思います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.why: The reason clause with から comes before the conclusion. The content “can win” comes before と, followed by 思います, following the word order for expressing a thought or judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If れんしゅうしましたので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective, while から is more direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If the sentence ends with かてるでしょう, it becomes a direct prediction and no longer emphasizes that it is the speaker's thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q18.kobun.tip: Before と, 思います uses the plain form, such as かてる, not the polite form かてます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.vi: I really like walking past the bakery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects パンや with the noun 前 to modify 前.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the place that the speaker passes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns とおる into a noun, while が marks the thing that is liked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: だいすきです functions as the predicate and states the degree of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.why: The phrase とおるのが is nominalized to become the subject of だいすきです. Particle を in まえをとおる marks the route being passed, not an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing のが with ことが still expresses a preference, but the tone is slightly more objective and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: Using に does not correctly express passing by a place; for a route being passed, を must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に instead of を in patterns showing a route being passed, such as 道を歩く or まえをとおる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ のが ＋ 好きだ・大好きだ・嫌いだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.vi: Please tell me your opinion about this job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies しごと and identifies the job being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: について marks the topic of the opinion; と before について in the given sentence is unnecessary and does not form a standard connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects あなた with 意見 and indicates who owns the opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks 意見 as the content that the listener is asked to state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects きかせる with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: てください is used to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.why: について sets the topic first, and then 意見を presents the content that is requested. In the given sequence, とについて is an unnecessary form; the natural structure is しごとについて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If について is replaced with によると, the meaning will be “according to some source,” not “about some topic.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is used to ask about a topic, while the current sentence uses きかせてください to ask the listener to share an opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.tip: Do not combine とについて; use Nについて directly to say “about N.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q9.kobun.cn: N ＋ について; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.vi: It has started to rain. Let's put up an umbrella.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the event taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: ふって is the て form of ふる, combined with くる to express an event that begins and continues toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing used in the action of さす.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう is attached to the polite form of a verb to make an invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる; Vます remove ます ＋ ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.why: 雨が states the phenomenon as the subject, then ふってきました describes the rain beginning to fall and continuing to the present. かさを is the object of さす, while ましょう turns the statement into a suggestion to act together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 雨がふっています, it only says that the rain is falling, without emphasizing its beginning or its progress toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If かさをさしましょうか is used, it becomes a question asking whether help should be offered or asking for the listener's opinion, making it softer than a direct invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand てくる as only meaning “come,” but in this sentence it also expresses a change that has begun to appear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.vi: It was decided that the year-end party would be held on December 15.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the expected time when the event will take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form of a verb + ことに nominalizes it, while に connects with なる in the decision pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ことになりました expresses a decision or result that has been determined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.why: The date comes first to state the time, and the event goes with を as the object of おこなう. The phrase おこなうことに なりました expresses the content that has been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes that the subject decides to do something, rather than describing a decision that has already been formed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: It only indicates a plan or expected schedule, without emphasizing the result of the decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ことになる with ことにする: なる focuses on a decision or determined result, while する focuses on a person actively making the decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形（肯定・否定）＋ことになる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q14.kobun.vi: I put the winter blanket in the built-in closet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ふゆよう with ふとん, creating the phrase “blanket for winter”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the blanket as the item being stored.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place where the blanket is stored.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q14.kobun.why: ふゆようの modifies ふとん, forming a complete object. を marks the item being stored, while に marks the destination of the action しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Using で emphasizes the place where the action happens, but for putting something into a place, に is more natural.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use で for every location, while に is used for the place or destination where an object is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.vi: That train is an express train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies 電車, referring to the identified train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents 電車 as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 急行 is a noun used as the predicate with です; よ emphasizes the information being conveyed to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.why: その comes before 電車 to modify the noun. 電車は states the topic, while 急行です forms a noun-predicate statement; よ adds a tone of informing the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: が makes 電車 the emphasized subject, instead of only stating it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: ですよね changes the tone to confirmation or waiting for the listener to agree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t1-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit は and directly combine the noun with です without clearly stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q1.kobun.vi: I scolded the children's mischief severely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の indicates the possessive relationship between 子どもたち and いたずら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The form く of the adjective い modifies the verb しかりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q1.kobun.why: の creates a possessive phrase, を marks what was scolded, and きびしく shows how the action was performed. The past-tense predicate comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If きびしい is used before a noun, it modifies the noun; here, きびしく is needed to modify the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep the adjective い before the verb, but they need to change きびしい into きびしく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.vi: I made a plan for next year at yesterday's meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.sk: Time の ＋ N で ＋ N の N を ＋ Vた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きのう with the noun かいぎ, creating the phrase “yesterday's meeting”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the context or place where the plan was made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the plan as the object being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: たてました is the polite past form of 立てる, used in the fixed combination 計画を立てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.why: The time and context phrases come before the object, while the verb comes at the end of the sentence. 計画を立てる is a fixed combination used to express making a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定を決める is used, it emphasizes deciding a schedule or intention, not creating a plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate each word of 立てる as “raise”, but in 計画を立てる it must be understood as “make a plan”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.vi: Let's think more deeply about this problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: この directly modifies the noun もんだい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the problem as the object of the act of thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: もっとふかく modifies かんがえて, indicating the degree of thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects 考える with みる, creating a pattern for trying an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: みましょう is the Vてみましょう pattern, expressing an invitation or suggestion to try doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.why: を marks the object of thought, while もっとふかく indicates the manner and degree of the action. Vてみましょう comes at the end of the sentence to suggest trying to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてください, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to do something and no longer has the meaning of inviting both people to try it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle を before the object or understand みる as “look”, but in the Vてみる pattern it means “try”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q11.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ みる／みます／みましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.vi: Looking at the family photo, I remembered my grandmother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects かぞく with しゃしん to show that the photo belongs to the family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the photo that was seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the act of looking with the act of remembering that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects おばあさん with こと to identify the content that was remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the content remembered in 思い出す.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: ました expresses a completed action politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.why: しゃしんをみて is the action that leads to the result おばあさんのことをおもいだしました. The whole phrase おばあさんのことを is used as the specific content of the verb 思い出す.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This sentence is also correct but focuses directly on the grandmother, while おばあさんのこと emphasizes things related to her.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことを is omitted, the sentence is shorter but does not clearly state the content being remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q12.kobun.tip: 思い出す usually goes with を; do not use the particle に to mark the person or event being remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.vi: Since we are hungry, let’s eat something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the part that is in the hungry state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the suggestion to eat in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: なにか is the indefinite object of 食べる, so particle を is omitted in spoken language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう attaches to the polite form of a verb to make an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.why: The clause describing hunger comes before から to give the reason. After the comma is a suggestion using ましょう; なにか is the object, but を is omitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective, while から is more direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say おなかをすいた, but the hungry state uses おなかがすく with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.vi: I should get married so that my parents can feel reassured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the object who is made to feel reassured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The causative verb shows that the parents are made to feel reassured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: ために connects to the preceding clause to show the purpose of the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The past form comes before ほうがいい to make advice about what should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ほうがいい expresses advice or an option judged to be better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.why: The purpose phrase comes first, followed by the action that is advised. The pattern Vたほうがいい is used to give gentle advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced, the meaning changes to advice not to get married.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is stronger and has a stronger sense of obligation than ordinary advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake ほうがいい for something used only for comparison, but in this pattern it expresses advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.tokens.8.m: option; thing that should be done
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q16.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ほうがいいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.vi: Because I missed the last train, I had no choice but to take a taxi.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.sk: Time point に ＋ Vなかったから、＋ N を ＋ V辞書形 ＋ しか ＋ ないです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time or object that must be reached or caught in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I did not make it in time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the cause to the result stated afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the taxi as the object taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: 拾いました is the polite past form of 拾う; however, しか does not connect naturally after this form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: ないです creates a negative meaning and usually goes with しか to say that only one option remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.why: The first part gives the reason with から, and the second part gives the only option with しか～ない. However, the given sequence contains 拾いましたしか, which does not follow the connection rule; the natural structure is タクシーを拾うしかないです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか～ない is replaced with だけ, the sentence only expresses the limit “only” and does not suggest that no other option remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.tip: しか always needs to go with a negative form and comes after the dictionary form or a noun. It does not come after 拾いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.tokens.2.m: did not make it in time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q17.kobun.cn: V辞書形・N ＋ しか ＋ ないです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.vi: I am trying not to show my feelings outwardly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects to the following noun to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the feelings as the object of the action of showing them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows the direction or place where the feelings are brought out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative clause with ように shows the goal of the effort.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: しています shows a habit or effort that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.why: The object to control is the feelings, while おもてに shows the direction in which the feelings are brought out. ように connects the negative goal with しています, creating the meaning of trying to keep from doing that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes the purpose more clearly and does not focus on the process of trying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern describes a decision not to do something, not a habit that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use ようにする directly after a noun; the action must be changed into a verb form, which here is ださない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q18.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ ように ＋ する
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.vi: Receiving an award like this is a great honor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: ような comes before a noun to modify it and show its type or quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the thing received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns the action into a noun, while は makes the whole act of receiving the award the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: たいへん is an adverb that modifies the degree of the following adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.why: The act of receiving the award is turned into a noun with こと and then made the topic with は. たいへん modifies the degree of the adjective describing the honor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことは is replaced with のは, the basic meaning is similar, but the tone is closer to everyday speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ことが is used, the action becomes the subject or object being evaluated, not the topic contrasted with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit こと when turning a verb into a noun, making the Vいただく part unable to function naturally as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q19.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ こと ＋ は ＋ Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.vi: The park is lively because there are people viewing the cherry blossoms.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle は presents the park as the place being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle を marks the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before 人 to modify the people viewing the flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows the cause or agent that makes the park lively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.why: The clause さくらをけんぶつする comes before 人 to identify which people they are. The phrase 人で gives the cause, and then にぎやかです serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced with 人がいて, the sentence emphasizes that people exist in the park instead of classifying them by their action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: 人によって means depending on the person or as carried out by the person, so it does not fit the meaning of a cause that makes the park lively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put the describing clause after 人, but Japanese puts さくらをけんぶつする before the noun being modified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.vi: I asked the staff member where the shoe section was.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person being asked or the person providing information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject whose location is being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the shop section exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: か changes a direct question into the content of an indirect question that follows the verb 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 聞く is in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, while the information to be found is placed before 聞きました. か keeps the question content but changes it into an indirect clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If used directly, this would be an independent question and could not be placed unchanged before 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding のか gives the question a stronger sense of asking for an explanation or emphasizing the content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.tip: In an indirect question, do not put ですか after the clause; use the plain form and end with か.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q20.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + 普通形 + か + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q21.kobun.vi: A man fell down on the train, which startled everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects でんしゃ with 中, creating the phrase "inside the train".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the event happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject experiencing the state of falling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the action of falling with the event that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q21.kobun.why: The phrase でんしゃの中で gives the location, and 男の人が identifies the person experiencing the state of falling. The て form connects the earlier event with everyone's reaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use を to mark the person who falls; the subject of the action usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.vi: I went to visit my senior who was in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects にゅういんする with いる to describe the state of being in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.ch.1.vi: to be in the state of
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: いる combines with a verb in the て form to show an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects せんぱい with おみまい and identifies the person being visited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.ch.3.vi: to visit someone in the hospital
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.why: にゅういんしている modifies せんぱい and shows that the senior was in the hospital. おみまいにいきました expresses that the purpose of going was to visit someone in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern were used, it would mean finishing the activity first and then going, so it would no longer describe the state of being in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q22.kobun.tip: Do not understand ている here as referring to an action in progress; with にゅういんする, it mainly refers to the state of being in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.vi: That is a good idea. Let’s do that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective いい comes before the noun to evaluate the idea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is used at the end of a sentence to confirm or share an opinion with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: そう replaces the content just suggested and modifies しましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form, used to suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.why: The first sentence evaluates the suggestion, while the second uses そう to refer back to the content just mentioned. しましょう changes the agreement into a suggestion to act together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If こう is used, the speaker emphasizes the specific method they are pointing out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If どう is used, the sentence becomes a question about what to do instead of agreement with the suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.tip: そう in そうしましょう does not mean 'seems'; it replaces the content 'that way' just mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q23.kobun.cn: そう + する + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.vi: This morning, I made a sandwich lunch box and had my child take it along.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: けさ indicates the time when the cooking or preparation took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects サンドイッチ with おべんとう to indicate a lunch box containing a sandwich.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the lunch box as the object being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects the action of making the lunch box with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the person for whom something is prepared or the person made to carry it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: もたせました describes making or letting the child carry the lunch box.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.why: The lunch box is the object of つくる, and then the て form connects it to the action of having the child carry it. に marks the person who performs the action in the causative structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes making or asking the child to carry it themselves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding あげました highlights that the speaker did it as a favor for the child.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q24.kobun.tip: Distinguish に in the causative pattern from を for the object: the person performing the action usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q25.kobun.vi: The sea in my hometown is very beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: 「ふるさとの」 modifies 「うみ」, meaning the sea in one's hometown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」 presents 「うみ」 as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い serves as the predicate, and 「です」 is added to make the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q25.kobun.why: The phrase 「ふるさとの」 comes before the noun to identify which sea. 「は」 makes the sea in one's hometown the topic, and the adjective 「うつくしい」 then describes the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were replaced in this sentence, the meaning would still be beautiful, but it would focus more on ordinary cleanliness or visual attractiveness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that an adjective ending in い, such as 「うつくしい」, can stand directly before 「です」 without adding 「な」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.vi: I decided to take the entrance exam for that university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to indicate an object far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects だいがく with にゅうし to create a modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the exam as the object of taking the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: V辞書形 combines with ことにする to express the decision to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: しました changes the pattern ことにする into the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.why: The phrases あの and だいがくの respectively modify the head noun にゅうし. V辞書形 + ことにしました changes the action of taking the exam into the content of the decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ことになる is used, it means that taking the exam was decided because of circumstances or by someone else, without emphasizing the speaker's decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: The expression 受験する still describes the decision to take the exam, but it uses a more specific verb instead of 受ける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse ことにする with ことになる; the first pattern emphasizes that the speaker made the decision themselves.
