default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことにする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.vi: Since I am now a third-year university student, I have to think about the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I am a third-year university student
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the reason to the main clause that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the noun しょうらい with こと to describe こと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content being thought about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb uses the negative form なくては to create an obligation pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.ch.5.vi: not being allowed not to do it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: なくてはいけません expresses the meaning of having to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with なので. The content that needs to be considered is marked by を. The pattern なくてはいけません comes at the end to show obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it keeps the meaning of obligation, but makes the tone more formal and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to not needing to think about it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake なくてはいけません for a negative meaning, but the whole pattern means that one must do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q4.kobun.cn: Vない形＋なくては＋いけない／いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.vi: From here to the company, I need to change lines.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: まで marks the endpoint, while は states the range being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks something that exists; のりかえる describes ひつよう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: あります acts as the predicate and states that the need exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.why: から and まで identify the starting and ending points of the route. The phrase のりかえるひつようが is the subject of あります, creating a structure that talks about necessity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence emphasizes that the speaker must change lines, rather than simply saying that it is necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If はありません is used, the meaning changes to not needing to change lines.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate 必要がある mechanically as “there is a need”; in this sentence, it should be understood as “need to”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.vi: Although the time was short, I received a lot of help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective い comes before あいだ to describe the period of time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.ch.1.vi: although it was a short period
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: でしたが connects two clauses with a concessive or mildly contrasting relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: いろいろと describes the help that was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に goes with お世話になる to refer to the care or help that the speaker received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました completes the expression お世話になる in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.why: The first clause limits the time and uses が to lead into thanks in the second clause. お世話になる is a fixed expression in which に marks the state or help that the speaker received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used, it means that the speaker cared for or helped someone else, which is the opposite of receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.tip: お世話になる must use に, not を; this is a polite way to talk about receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.tokens.8.m: usually fill in 世話: help, care
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q6.kobun.cn: N ＋ でしたが; N に ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q7.kobun.vi: I stack plates with the same shape.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the phrase おなじかたち with the noun おさら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the plates being stacked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite-form verb ます is the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q7.kobun.why: The phrase おなじかたちの comes before おさら to describe the type of plates. おさらを is the object, while かさねます is the main action at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q7.kobun.tip: The describing phrase must come before the noun; do not place おさら before おなじかたちの as in English word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.vi: The dog that was in a traffic accident is still alive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に goes with あう to describe what happened to the dog.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: あった is a clause that describes いぬ, giving the meaning “the dog was in an accident.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes いぬ the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: まだ describes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 生きています is the ています form expressing the state of still being alive; the original text in the exercise also has います at the end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる／います; Vた ＋ N to create a clause that describes a noun
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.why: The clause こうつうじこにあった comes before いぬ to identify which dog. After stating the topic with は, まだ combines with 生きています to show that the state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 生きました is used, the meaning focuses on having lived or survived at a certain time, without emphasizing that the dog is still alive now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q8.kobun.tip: The describing clause must come before the noun; do not put あった after いぬ as in the usual Vietnamese word order.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.vi: There are no particularly serious problems with this report.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: には makes レポート the scope being considered and states the topic with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: とくに modifies the phrase おおきなもんだい and emphasizes the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: おおきな comes before a noun to describe the problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes もんだい the topic being negated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.ch.5.vi: there is not; there are no
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.why: には identifies the report as the scope being considered. Then もんだいは states the object being negated. おおきな modifies もんだい, while とくに emphasizes that there is no significant problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, it simply gives the objective information that there is no problem, with less topic emphasis than は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If しかありません is used, the meaning changes to “there is only,” which is opposite to complete negation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t100-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may leave out は after もんだい, but は clearly expresses “as for the problem, there is none.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q1.kobun.vi: I gather everyone and then hold a meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks everyone as the people being gathered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of gathering with the action of holding a meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the meeting as the object of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q1.kobun.why: みんなを is the object of 集める, while かいぎを is the object of する. The form て connects the two actions in the order in which they happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using this pattern clearly emphasizes the order: "after gathering everyone, hold a meeting."
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q1.kobun.tip: Do not mistake みんなを for the subject; the particle を shows that everyone is the object being gathered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.vi: If you do not feel well, you should skip school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the condition that is described as bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 悪い serves as the predicate of the conditional clause and describes the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates a point in time, while は makes that situation the topic of the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the place or activity that is skipped in the expression がっこうをやすむ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: やすんだ in the past form modifies ほう and creates a pattern for giving advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: Vたほうがいい is used to advise someone to do an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: いいですよ completes the advice pattern and makes the sentence sound softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.why: The clause 悪いときは gives the condition first, followed by the recommended action. 具合が悪い uses が because 具合 is the condition being evaluated, while やすむ goes with を in the expression for skipping school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vないほうがいい, the meaning changes to advice not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: べきだ expresses a stronger obligation and is less gentle than ordinary advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say がっこうでやすむ, but for the meaning of skipping school, you must use がっこうをやすむ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: こちらの modifies 商品 and refers to the product on this side or the product being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the product as the object of the action of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ごらんに is the first part of the supplied sequence and connects to the honorific expression that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ご覧になる is the honorific form of 見る, while てください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.why: The demonstrative phrase comes before the noun, を marks the product being viewed, and then the honorific expression and request follow. The input sequence repeats ごらんにご覧になってください; if the whole sentence is kept unchanged, this repetition makes the sentence unnatural in standard Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 見てください, it is still a request to look, but it no longer has an honorific tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: ご覧ください is a shorter respectful request and does not use the structure ご覧になる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.tip: Do not divide ご覧になる into ご覧てください; change なる to なって before ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q11.kobun.cn: ご覧になる → ご覧になってください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I was able to meet the person I had wanted to meet for a very long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.sk: 時点 に + N から + Vたかった + N に + past potential form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the time when the person was successfully met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of an extended period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: あいたかった modifies 人 and expresses a wish to meet that had continued from the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person whom the speaker met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: あえました is the polite past potential form of あう and emphasizes that the speaker finally managed to meet the person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.cn: Vたかった + N; N に + potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.why: The time period and the wish come before the noun 人 to form a modifying clause. に after 人 marks the person met, while あえました emphasizes that the meeting was successfully achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If と会いました is used, it only states that the speaker met that person and does not emphasize successfully meeting them or achieving the wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding やっと emphasizes the waiting or difficulty before finally being able to meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after 人, but with あう, に must be used to indicate the person met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.vi: After moving house, I will greet the neighbors.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks moving house as the object of した.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: Vた comes before あと to indicate an action that was completed earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: あと connects the completed clause with the action that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person receiving the greeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks あいさつ as the content of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: します is the main predicate and describes the action of greeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.why: The moving-house clause comes before あと to establish the time. Then, に indicates the person being addressed and を indicates the greeting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with てから also means "after," but emphasizes that the later action starts from the time the earlier action ends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before あと when you want to say that the earlier action has been completed; use Vた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.vi: Compared with when I first started, I have become much better at skiing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents スキー as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects さいしょ with ころ to modify the time point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the point used for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: くらべると connects the comparison part with the evaluation result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: This is an adverb that modifies the degree of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective うまい changes into an adverbial form to modify なりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: なりました describes a change of state over time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.why: The initial time point is given as the standard for comparison, and then くらべると leads to the present evaluation. うまく is the adverbial form that goes with なる to express becoming better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this, the comparison meaning stays almost the same, but the expression is more formal and concise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily keep the adjective うまい before なる, but it must be changed to うまく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.vi: I really like this scarf because it feels soft.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the scarf being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the scarf the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い directly modifies てざわり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: で connects the scarf's feature with the feeling of liking it in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: だいすきです is the predicate that states the speaker's feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.why: The scarf is introduced as the topic, and the soft feature describes how it feels to touch. で connects this feature with the comment that the speaker likes it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If Nが好きだ is used, the sentence simply says that the speaker likes the scarf, without stating the feature that is the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q15.kobun.tip: Do not connect the adjective い to a noun with な; the adjective い directly modifies the noun, as in やわらかいてざわり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.vi: I sent a fax to the overseas branch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a place with the following modified noun ししゃ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place or recipient receiving the sent document.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being sent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: おくりました is the predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first to identify the recipient's location, followed by the item sent and the verb. に indicates the destination, while を indicates the object of the sending action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: へ can also indicate the direction of sending, but に sounds more natural when the place or recipient is emphasized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse に and で; use に for the recipient's location, while で usually indicates a means such as ファックスで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.vi: For me, she is the only special person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: にとって indicates the evaluator's position or viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that she is the person being evaluated from my viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects a quantity phrase with the modified noun そんざい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な modifies そんざい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: そんざいです is a noun predicate, concluding that she has special meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.why: にとって puts the viewpoint at the beginning of the sentence, then は states the person being evaluated. The phrases たったひとりの and とくべつな respectively modify the noun used as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with に対して, the meaning focuses on the direction or the object affected, not the viewpoint of the evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also means “when viewed from N's side,” but it emphasizes the way of looking or the comment more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate にとって as “for,” but this pattern indicates a viewpoint: “for N” or “from N's point of view.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.vi: I want to make use of my volunteer experience in my future work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun ボランティア with the following noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the experience as the object being made use of.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns これから into a modifier for しごと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the field or target where the experience is applied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: いかしたい consists of the verb いかす in the desire form and expresses the speaker's wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.why: The phrase ボランティアのけいけん creates a noun phrase meaning volunteer experience, and then を marks the object of いかす. に indicates the place or field where the experience is used, while 〜たいです expresses a desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the sentence emphasizes the wish to make the experience more useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q18.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use を for work, but with いかす, に is needed to indicate the place or field of application.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q19.kobun.vi: My younger brother went out to play again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the younger brother is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the purpose of going out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: でかけました is the main predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q19.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and then また adds the meaning of repetition. The pattern Vますにでかける combines the purpose with the action of going out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also means going out to play, but it uses 行く to emphasize the action of going somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q19.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in あそびに as a location; here に indicates purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.vi: There are only a pen and some materials on the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 「つくえの」 modifies 「うえ」 and indicates the position on the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: 「に」 indicates the place of existence, while 「は」 limits the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 「と」 connects 「ペン」 with the next noun in the list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 「しか」 means “only...,” and must be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 「ありません」 is the polite negative form of 「あります」, creating the structure pair 「しか～ない」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.why: 「つくえのうえに」 identifies the place of existence, while 「は」 focuses on that range. The two nouns are connected by 「と」, and 「しか～ありません」 expresses the limited amount: only two things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「だけ」 is used, it also means “only...,” but 「だけ」 does not have to be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「ばかり」 is used, the nuance is “all” or “almost only,” without the strong limit expressed by 「しか」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q2.kobun.tip: A common mistake is to use 「しか」 with an affirmative sentence; you must say 「しかありません」 or use a corresponding negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.vi: After confessing my feelings, I was able to receive a good reply.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: て connects the action of confessing with the action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: いい modifies the noun へんじ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the reply as the thing received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: こと turns the action もらう into a noun, while が marks the action as possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: できました is the predicate of the pattern Vることができる in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.why: て connects two actions in order, with the confession happening first. The phrase もらうこと turns the action of receiving into a noun phrase, which combines with できる to express ability or successful completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If the potential form is used, the sentence is shorter but does not emphasize the nominalized action structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern describes something being decided or becoming a certain way, not something that can be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.tip: Learners may easily omit こと in the pattern できる, but the verb must be nominalized with Vること.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ことができる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.vi: If you do not hurry, you will be late for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects a condition いそがない with a result that will certainly follow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the target or event toward which being late is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: おくれます is the main predicate, while よ emphasizes the warning to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes before the result. The verb in negative form combines with と to state a natural or certain result if the condition is not carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this pattern keeps a similar conditional meaning, but the tone is more formal and more hypothetical.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern usually states a specific condition or time, so it is less certainly warning-like than と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use the past tense before と in this usual conditional pattern; use the dictionary form or the present negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q21.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + と
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.vi: From next month, I will learn to drive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.sk: Time point から + NのNを + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から marks the starting point of the learning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun くるま with noun うんてん, creating the phrase 'driving a car'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks what is being learned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb まなびます is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.why: The starting time is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state the time reference. The phrase NのN clarifies what is being learned, and を connects it to the verb まなびます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with まで, the meaning changes from 'starting next month' to 'until next month'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q22.kobun.tip: から marks the starting point, not the deadline; therefore, it cannot be translated as 'until next month'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.vi: I hope this material will be useful for research.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun しりょう that follows immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the material as the subject that is useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the purpose or field in which the material is useful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: と connects clause 役立つ with いいですね in a pattern that expresses a wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: いいですね expresses a wish or hope that something will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.why: が marks the material as the subject of 役立つ, while に indicates the field in which the material is useful. Clause 役立つと comes before いいですね to create the meaning 'I hope that...'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If いいです is used instead of いいですね, the sentence is still a wish, but it has less of a shared or agreement-seeking tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is more formal and emphasizes a prayer or earnest wish. It is often used in writing or speeches.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.tip: Do not translate と in といいですね as 'and'; the whole phrase expresses a wish or hope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形 + といいですね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.vi: I learn a local dance for the festival.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects おまつり with ため to create a purpose phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: ために indicates the purpose of the learning action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the dance as the object of ならいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ならいます is the main predicate in the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.why: ために comes after a noun with の to state the purpose. The object of learning is marked by を and placed directly before the verb ならいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also indicates purpose, but it is usually used with ability, a state, or a desired result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern modifies the noun that follows, so it does not connect directly to a verb like ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.tip: When ために has a purpose meaning after a noun, the learner must use の: Nのために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q24.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ために／Nの + ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.vi: My one-year-old son is walking faster and faster.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the age with むすこ to modify the son.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the son is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the verb あるく into a noun, and が marks walking as the subject of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: どんどん modifies rapid and continuous progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: The い adjective changes to the く form before なりました to express becoming faster.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.why: むすこは is the topic, while あるくのが速くなる describes the change in walking speed. どんどん comes before 速くなりました to emphasize rapid improvement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes a quality changing into a new state, here meaning becoming fast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: Emphasizes beginning to have the ability or habit of doing an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.vs.2.d: Describes gradual change step by step, with a gentler and more even tone than どんどん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q25.kobun.tip: Before なる, the い adjective must change to the く form; do not say 速いなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.vi: I went to the airport to meet my foreign friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.sk: N の + N を + Vます omit ます + に + N へ + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: 「がいこくの」 modifies 「ゆうじん」, indicating a friend from a foreign country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The linking form 「Vます omits ます＋に」 and expresses the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 「へ」 indicates the direction or destination of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 「いきました」 is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.why: The object 「ゆうじんを」 comes before the purpose phrase. 「むかえに」 states the reason for going, 「くうこうへ」 states the destination, and finally 「いきました」 completes the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If the purpose phrase is replaced with this pattern, the sentence has a clearer and more formal meaning of going in order to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use 「を」 for purpose in this pattern; purpose uses the form that omits 「ます」＋「に」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.vi: I put the flowers I received in the middle of the table.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A verb in the past form comes before a noun to modify 「おはな」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 「テーブルの」 modifies 「まんなか」, identifying the middle of the table.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 「に」 indicates the location where the object is placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 「おきました」 is the completed action of placing something in the polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.why: Clause 「もらった」 comes before 「おはな」 to clarify which flowers they are. 「を」 marks the object being placed, 「に」 marks the location, and the verb 「おきました」 ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the focus shifts to the state of an object having been placed and still being in that position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q4.kobun.tip: English learners may easily confuse 「に」 and 「で」; the place where an object exists or is placed uses 「に」, while 「で」 usually indicates the place where an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.vi: Becoming a television announcer is her dream.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: 「テレビきょくの」 modifies 「アナウンサー」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 「に」 indicates the result or role that will be reached with the verb 「なる」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 「の」 turns the action 「なる」 into a noun, while 「が」 marks it as the subject being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 「かのじょの」 modifies 「ゆめ」 and shows whose dream it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 「です」 politely connects the subject 「なるのが」 with the predicate noun 「ゆめ」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.why: 「アナウンサーになる」 describes changing into a profession or role. Adding 「の」 turns the whole action into a noun, so 「が」 marks it as the dream stated in the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「のが」 is replaced with 「ことが」, the basic meaning stays the same, but the tone becomes more objective and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q5.kobun.tip: With 「なる」, the result goes with 「に」; do not use 「を」 as when marking a direct object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.vi: I do not know whether it suits your taste, but please help yourself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 「に」 indicates the object or standard that the food should suit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: 「かどうか」 turns the clause 「あう」 into an indirect question meaning whether or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 「が」 connects the previous sentence to the invitation that follows, creating a soft and modest tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: 「どうぞ」 is used to politely invite or encourage the listener to accept, eat, or do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.why: 「おくちにあう」 describes food suiting the listener's taste. The phrase 「あうかどうか」 makes the content something that is known or unknown, and then 「が」 softly connects it to the invitation 「どうぞ」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 「か」 is used, the sentence usually asks about one choice or specific content, without emphasizing the pair meaning whether or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「のか」 is used, the sentence has a stronger tone of wanting to know or wondering about a reason or situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.tip: 「かどうか」 already means whether or not, so 「ですか」 is not added immediately after it in an indirect question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ かどうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the information being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な modifies the information that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the basis or means that makes it possible to trust something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: This is a verb in the potential form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q7.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first with は, and then the adjective な modifies the noun. The particle で connects the basis with the ability to trust at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If を is used, the noun becomes the thing directly trusted instead of the basis for evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を to mean “trust something,” but で here emphasizes the basis or means.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.vi: The house was completely burned down in a fire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that made the house burn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the house as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 全部 modifies the result of burning and shows that it burned completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 焼けてしまいました describes an event that has been completed, often with a sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.why: The phrase showing the cause comes before the topic, followed by the degree 全部 and then the predicate. 焼ける is an intransitive verb, so the house is described as entering a burned state by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 焼きました, the subject has burned something, emphasizing the action of the person who did it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with 焼ける, but 焼ける cannot take the object を because it is intransitive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the homework the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ほとんど modifies the verb and shows that the level of completion is nearly complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q9.kobun.why: The topic comes first, and the adverb showing degree comes before the predicate to modify the result of completion. おわりました is in the polite past form and shows that the homework has progressed up to now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with あまり, it usually means not much and often goes with a negative sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with まったく, the degree becomes complete, often leading to the meaning of not finishing anything at all when used with a negative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t101-q9.kobun.tip: Do not translate ほとんど as completely; it usually means almost or most.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.vi: Last night, I went to hear a concert for the first time in a long while.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Adverb ＋ Nを ＋ Vます形＋に ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the point in time when the action occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern Vます＋に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 行く in the polite past form is the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.why: The phrase コンサートを is the object of 聞く, while 聞きに comes before いきました to state the purpose of going. The particle に in 聞きに indicates purpose, not location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning is still going to listen, but the purpose is stated more clearly and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q1.kobun.tip: Do not use を after 聞きに; the purpose pattern is Vます形＋に＋行く／来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.vi: Everyone is sitting around the heater and talking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: みんな is the subject performing the actions in the sentence, although が is omitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the heater as the object used as the reference point for the action 囲む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of surrounding with the action of talking in the same flow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks はなし as the content of the action する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: して connects the verb する with います to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the pattern ています and describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.why: みんな is the shared subject of the two actions. The two verbs in the て form connect the actions in sequence, while ています is placed at the end to show that the state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: ながら emphasizes two actions happening at the same time by the same subject, while て here connects actions naturally in sequence or as part of a description.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q10.kobun.tip: Do not omit て before います when describing an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.vi: Nice to meet you. I am Satō from Tanaka Electric.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This greeting is used when meeting someone for the first time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects a company name with a person's name to show where the person belongs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the name given in a self-introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 申します is a humble predicate used to give one's name or say what one says.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.why: The sentence begins with a greeting, then states the place of belonging with の and uses と to mark the name before 申します. 申します comes at the end because it is the main verb of the self-introduction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used to introduce one's name in a humble and polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with と言います, it still introduces a name, but the tone is more ordinary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q11.kobun.tip: Do not translate と as “and” in the name-introduction pattern ～と申します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.vi: I take an express train to the airport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a type of train with the noun 電車.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the vehicle or object that the speaker gets on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of taking the train with the action of going to the airport.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the destination of the verb いきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.why: The train-type phrase comes before 電車, に marks the vehicle used, and て connects the vehicle with the main action. に in くうこうに shows the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: へ also shows the direction toward the airport, but it emphasizes direction rather than the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: で marks the means of transport, while に in 電車に乗る is used with the verb 乗る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use 電車で乗る; you must say 電車に乗る, but 電車で行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q12.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; N に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.vi: I do not like it because I feel embarrassed speaking in front of other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 人 with 前 to form a phrase meaning in front of other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the action はなす takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the verb はなす into a noun, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the cause はずかしい with the conclusion いやです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.why: The phrase 人の前で identifies where the action takes place. はなすのは turns “speaking” into the topic, and then から gives the reason for the conclusion いやです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: が makes speaking the subject of the feeling of embarrassment, without emphasizing it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: と expresses that speaking causes embarrassment, with a conditional or natural-result meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.tip: Do not confuse のは with のが: のは marks the topic, while のが usually marks the subject of a feeling or ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ のは ＋ Aい／Aなだ ＋ から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.vi: Teacher Tanaka is studying modern Asian history.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Teacher Tanaka the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects アジア with the noun meaning history.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ている shows that the study is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.why: は identifies the person performing the action, の forms the phrase “the history of Asia,” and を marks the object of study. ています shows that the activity is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: について emphasizes that Asia is the topic of the study, without creating a possessive relationship like の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 研究しました, the meaning changes to having finished studying it in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q16.kobun.tip: In this sentence, を goes with the object of study, while は goes with the researcher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.vi: That family restaurant is open 24 hours.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies the noun ファミリーレストラン and identifies one specific restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the restaurant the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The duration phrase adds information about the state of operation that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: This is a noun predicate that says the restaurant operates for the stated duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.why: あの identifies a specific restaurant, and は makes the restaurant the topic. 24じかん comes before the predicate to state the operating duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes the action or state of being open, so it is more natural when talking about current operation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: だけ limits it to “only 24 hours,” making the meaning narrower than the original sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q17.kobun.tip: 24じかん here is the operating duration, not the time “at 24 o'clock.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.vi: I still remember my parents' wedding anniversary well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects りょうしん with けっこんきねんび to show that the anniversary belongs to the parents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the wedding anniversary as the object being remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies おぼえる and emphasizes remembering firmly and carefully.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb おぼえる with います to form the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern ている, showing a remembered state that continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.why: The phrase の identifies whose anniversary it is, and を marks the object being remembered. しっかり modifies the verb, while ている shows that the remembered state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: じっくり emphasizes working for a long time and carefully; it does not necessarily mean remembering firmly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: 覚えておく emphasizes remembering something in advance for later use, unlike a state of remembering now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q18.kobun.tip: ている does not always refer to an action in progress; with おぼえる, it usually refers to a remembered state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q19.kobun.vi: The train is very crowded during rush hour.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun with the noun でんしゃ to modify “train.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: たいへん modifies the crowded state that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 込む changes to the form ている to describe an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q19.kobun.why: The phrase NのN identifies the type of train, は makes the train the topic, and the adverb たいへん modifies the predicate. The Vている form is suitable for describing the current crowded condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q19.kobun.tip: Learners may easily understand ている as meaning only “be doing,” but in this sentence it describes a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.vi: A moment ago, I received a phone call from my teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nから ＋ Nが ＋ ありました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: This word refers to a time close to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から indicates the source or person making the call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the event being said to have happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ありました is the predicate, expressing existence or an event that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.why: The sentence uses ありました to report that a phone call happened. The source of the call comes before から, while the phone call is the subject used with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning changes to “I actively called the teacher.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q2.kobun.tip: With ありました, an event that appears or happens usually goes with が, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.vi: When people focus on their work, they no longer notice things around them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the object that the focus is directed toward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition or situation with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects まわり with こと to form the phrase “things around.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that becomes no longer clearly visible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: The form なく connects a negative adjective with なる to show a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.why: しごとに集中する indicates the direction of focus toward work. The pattern と connects a situation with a natural result, while なくなる describes changing into a state where something can no longer be seen or recognized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: たら indicates a more specific condition or time, without emphasizing a natural result like と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: 見えません indicates a state of not being able to see, while 見えなくなります emphasizes the change that leads to that state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use a negative adjective directly before なる; change it into the form なくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形＋と; Aい＋と; Aな＋だと; N＋だと
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.vi: I am going to the beach for fun, wearing sandals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item being worn or carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of putting on sandals with the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward the sea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverbial form あそぶ combines with に to indicate the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.why: を marks the sandals being worn, and て connects the preparatory action with the action of going. へ indicates the direction toward the sea, while あそびにいきます expresses that the purpose of going is to have fun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: に also indicates a destination and emphasizes a more specific destination than へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: ために also indicates a purpose, but it is more formal and emphasizes the goal more than the pattern of verb stem ます + に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.tip: Before 行く, the purpose must use the form without ます, such as あそびに, not あそぶに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q21.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; Vます-stem ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q22.kobun.vi: The company’s lunch break is one hour.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q22.kobun.sk: N の N は ＋ Time period です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の creates a possessive phrase, while は marks the whole phrase as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: です connects the topic with information explaining its duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q22.kobun.why: 会社の昼休み is the noun phrase “the company’s lunch break,” placed first by は. The duration comes after です to explain how long the topic lasts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is used, the sentence emphasizes that the period exists or is available, rather than stating its duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate の as “of” in every situation, but here it only shows a modifying relationship between two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.vi: After the age of 50, physical strength gradually decreases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the point that is passed, while と connects the condition with a result that usually occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks physical strength as the subject undergoing the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: だんだん modifies the process of decreasing that happens slowly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: おちます is the main predicate, expressing that physical strength decreases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.why: The clause beginning with 50さいをすぎると is placed at the beginning to state a condition or time point. After と comes a natural result that usually occurs: physical strength gradually decreases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: It emphasizes a condition that happens first or a more specific assumption, and does not necessarily describe a result that always repeats.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: It is based on information or an assumption that has been given, and talks about that case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q23.kobun.tip: と in a conditional pattern usually goes with a natural or repeated result; it is not used to express a direct command.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.vi: The convenience store employee’s service is very cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects コンビニ with the following noun to show a belonging relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の continues to modify たいおう, creating a multi-level noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks service as the subject that has the quality stated at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い acts as the predicate, and です adds a polite tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.why: The two phrases の gradually narrow the scope: コンビニ modifies てんいん, and then てんいん modifies たいおう. が connects this noun phrase with the adjective used as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used, the employee becomes the topic, and the focus changes from the service to talking about the employee in general.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate each の mechanically as “of”; identify the central noun at the end of the phrase as たいおう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.vi: I decided that I would quit smoking starting tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.sk: Time point から ＋ N を ＋ V普通形 ＋ と ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the action やめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: と quotes the content of the decision; やめる is in the dictionary form because it comes before と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.why: から sets the starting point, and たばこを is the object of やめる. The content of the decision comes before と, and then きめました expresses that the act of deciding has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If やめようと is used, the sentence emphasizes the intention “decided to quit,” instead of stating quitting smoking as specific content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.tip: Do not change やめる into やめます before と in the structure for quoting the content of a decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q25.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ と ＋ 決める
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.vi: Raising children to become respectable adults is not simple.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being raised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な modifies おとな and states the resulting condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the result or state that the object is made to become.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb plus の turns the whole action into a noun, and then は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective な modifies こと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: こと nominalizes the previous content, while では places it in a negative evaluation structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: ないです creates a polite negative expression at the end of a sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.why: The action of raising children is nominalized by のは to make it the topic of the comment. おとなに comes after the object and shows the result of raising the child, while ではない denies the comment that it is simple.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this pattern, the basic meaning does not change, but the expression is more formal and direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q3.kobun.tip: When saying that you make someone or something become a certain state, use Nを Nに V, not Nを Nで V.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.vi: I am looking forward to my overseas trip next month.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects a time expression with the noun 海外旅行, forming the phrase “next month’s trip.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object that is being looked forward to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に appears in the fixed pattern 楽しみにする and indicates a state or something that is anticipated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て of する connects with います to create a pattern that expresses an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: います completes the pattern ています and expresses that the state of looking forward to something is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.why: The time noun connects to the trip through の, and then を marks what is anticipated. 楽しみにしている is a fixed pattern that expresses looking forward to an event or activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning focuses more on expectations or waiting for a result than on excitement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in 楽しみにしている as “at”; the whole phrase is a fixed pattern meaning “to look forward to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q4.kobun.cn: Nを + 楽しみに + している
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.vi: I had a very difficult time because I lost an important document.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective な comes before and modifies the noun しょるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object that was lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of losing something with the result or state described afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: たいへんでした is a polite past predicate that describes the state after losing the document.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.why: The adjective comes before the noun to identify the type of document, while を marks the lost item. The form て connects an earlier cause or event with the state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer, and the sentence sounds more directly explanatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect the two clauses with と; in this sentence, the form て creates a natural connection between the event and the state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.vi: Pointing at another person with your finger and talking is rude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person being pointed at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で shows the means used to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of pointing at someone with the action of talking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Verb + の turns an action into a noun, and then は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: This is a predicate that evaluates the previous action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.why: 人を marks the object of the pointing action, while ゆびで shows the means. The two actions are connected with the て form before the whole action is nominalized and evaluated with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ながら is used, the two actions are understood to happen at the same time, without emphasizing that one happens before the other.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q6.kobun.tip: で shows the means, such as a finger, while を marks the person being pointed at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.vi: I boarded the Shinkansen that departed at 9 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.sk: Time + Nの + Vehicle に + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This noun phrase modifies the train and shows its departure time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the vehicle that the speaker boards.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: のりました is a polite past-tense predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.why: ９じしゅっぱつの comes before しんかんせん to modify the train. The verb のる combines with に to indicate the vehicle that the speaker boards or the object they get onto.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If で行く is used instead, the focus is on traveling by Shinkansen, not on the action of boarding the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q7.kobun.tip: With のる, use に to mark the vehicle boarded; do not use で simply because it translates as “by.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.vi: Because my feet were cold, I could not sleep at night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.sk: N が + Vて + 時間 + negative potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a cold state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects a previous cause or state with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: よる indicates the time when the inability to sleep occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ねむれません is the polite negative form of the potential form ねむれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.why: The clause あしがひえて gives the cause first, and then the negative potential form expresses the result: being unable to sleep. よる comes before the predicate to specify the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If て is replaced with ので, the cause is stated more clearly and the sentence sounds more explanatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q8.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ひえて with ひやして: ひえる means becoming cold by itself, while ひやす means making something else cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.vi: Today’s homework is difficult, so I cannot finish it even after a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects きょう with the noun しゅくだい to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes today’s homework the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to くて to connect the cause or state with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.ch.3.vi: even after a long time, still not
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: This adverb modifies できません and emphasizes that it is difficult to achieve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: できません is a negative predicate expressing that the homework cannot be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.why: は makes the homework the topic, and then むずかしくて connects the difficult quality with the result of being unable to do it. なかなか is used with a negative form to express that the desired result still cannot be achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If あまり is used instead, it means being unable to do much or not being good at it, so the feeling is weaker than “being unable to finish it despite trying for a long time.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t102-q9.kobun.tip: なかなか in this meaning usually appears with a negative form; do not simply translate it as “very.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.vi: Please store this snack at a suitable temperature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before the noun おかし to identify the item being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the snack the topic of the instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な modifies おんど, so な must be kept.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the condition or method of storage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects 保存する with ください to create a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after the て form of a verb to express a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.why: The topic おかし is stated first, while おんどで indicates the storage condition. The phrase ほぞんしてください is placed at the end to turn the content into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 適切な is used instead, the meaning is still “suitable,” but the tone is more formal and precise than 適当な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q1.kobun.tip: Do not omit な after the adjective な when it comes directly before a noun, as in てきとうなおんど.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.vi: We will develop the resources lying dormant underground.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the place where the resources exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause ねむっている comes before a noun to modify しげん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the resources as the object being developed or exploited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: かいはつします is the main predicate and shows a polite action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.why: ちかに identifies where the resources exist. ねむっている modifies しげん, while を connects this noun to the action かいはつします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてある is used, the sentence describes a state intentionally created by someone, which does not fit natural resources.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a continuing state. Here, it figuratively means that the resources remain dormant underground.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often understand ている as simply doing something, but with 眠っている it describes a state that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.vi: Please do not take books outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle へ shows direction, while の connects this phrase to the noun 図書 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects としょ to もちだし and shows the act of taking books outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks taking the books outside as the object of ごえんりょください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ください makes a polite request; ご comes before a noun to create a formal expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.why: The directional phrase そとへ comes before の to modify としょ, forming “books to take outside.” This noun phrase is the object of を, followed by ご〜ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence directly means “please do not take the books outside,” making the prohibition or prevention clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is also a polite request, but it is usually more formal and has the nuance of “please refrain.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may mistake への for a single particle. In fact, it is へ showing direction, combined with の to modify the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.vi: He will certainly keep his promise, so please do not worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb modifies the action of keeping the promise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb まもります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the reason clause to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: ないで connects the negative verb to the request ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: ないでください expresses a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.why: The topic is introduced first, followed by the object and the main action. から explains the reason and leads to the request しんぱいしないでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason remains the same, but the tone becomes softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also asks someone not to do something, but it is more formal and has a stronger reminder-like tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place から at the end of the previous sentence and forget that it must connect to a result clause or a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から; Vないで + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.vi: The host said: “Thank you for the wonderful performance.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The part in parentheses shows who says the thank-you sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: すばらしい modifies えんそう, forming a noun phrase that expresses an evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ありがとうございました is a polite past-tense expression of thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.cn: Aい + N; お+Vます omits ます+ました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.why: The speaker's role name appears outside the quotation, while the words inside the quotation marks are the speech itself. The adjective comes before the noun to evaluate the performance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning becomes “an enjoyable performance,” focusing more on the feeling of enjoyment than on praising its quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often put adjectives after nouns, but Japanese puts すばらしい before えんそう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.sk: N の + N を + Quantity + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects コンサート to チケット to modify the type of ticket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the ticket as the object that was reserved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: まい is a counter used for thin objects such as tickets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: しました is the polite past form, showing that reserving the tickets has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.why: の identifies the tickets as belonging or relating to the concert. The object comes before the quantity, followed by the verb meaning “reserve” at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 買いました, it means that the tickets were bought, without necessarily emphasizing advance reservation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If the quantity changes, only the number of tickets changes; the sentence structure stays the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may confuse まい with ひき or ほん; tickets and paper use the counter まい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.vi: When I searched online, I understood the truth.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the means used for searching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: てみる shows trying something, while たら connects a condition or time to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the noun ほんとう with こと to modify the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks what was realized or understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.why: The means phrase comes before the searching action. After trying to search, the result is stated with the pattern Nがわかる, where が marks what was understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたら is used alone, the sentence only states a condition or time, without emphasizing the idea of trying as in てみたら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If the sentence ends with Vてみる, it only means trying something and does not show that a result occurred afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use をわかる, but わかる usually goes with が to mark what was understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q17.tokens.2.m: blank for the word to fill in
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: おだやかな is an adjective な placed before a noun to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects タイプ with 人, forming a noun phrase meaning “type of person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that is liked in the pattern 人がすきです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.why: The adjective おだやかな modifies タイプ, and then タイプの人 forms the complete object. With すきです, the liked object usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: The use of を here does not fit the basic pattern すきです; use Nがすきです instead.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If タイプの is omitted, the meaning changes to “a gentle person,” directly describing personality, without the nuance of “type of person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.tip: Do not translate from English into your first language and then use を; remember the pattern Nがすきです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q18.kobun.cn: Aなな ＋ Nの ＋ Nがすきだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.vi: Please tell me the answer to this quiz.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to refer to something near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects クイズ with the noun 答え, showing a possessive relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the answer as the object being asked about or requested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て combines with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.why: この クイズのこたえ form a noun phrase, while を marks what should be told. The pattern Vてください comes at the end to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vてもらえますか, the request becomes a softer, more tentative question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q19.kobun.tip: Do not use に to mark what is being asked about; the object of おしえる usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.vi: Every evening, I face my desk and try hard to study.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.sk: Time に ＋ N に ＋ Vて ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎晩 indicates the time or repeated time of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object or direction that the speaker faces.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: 向かって is the て form of むかう, connecting posture or direction with the action of studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content carried out together with がんばる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects がんばる with います to create a continuous form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: います completes the pattern Vています and describes an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.why: 毎晩 places the time at the beginning of the sentence, while つくえにむかって describes the direction or posture while studying. がんばっています shows that the effort is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If 座って is used instead, the sentence only says that someone sits down or sits at the desk. It does not emphasize facing the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q2.kobun.tip: 向かって goes with に to show a direction or target, and does not use を as with an ordinary object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.vi: Athlete Tanaka has a shoulder problem, so he will not play.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents athlete Tanaka as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the body part affected in the phrase かたをこしょうする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The て-form connects the shoulder problem with the following action or result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates participation in or direction toward the match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.why: は places the topic at the beginning of the sentence. The condition かたをこしょうする is connected with て to explain the reason or background for not taking part in the match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of て, the cause is expressed more clearly and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: を is not suitable here because に marks the match that the speaker does not take part in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q20.kobun.tip: When saying that someone will not take part in an event, learners may easily use を, but the usual pattern is eventに出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.vi: The clock hand has passed one o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects とけい with 針, showing that the hand belongs to the clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the clock hand as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を goes with 回る to indicate the time marker that the hand has passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.why: The phrase とけいの針 identifies the subject as the clock hand. With 回る, the time marker goes with を to express that the hand has moved past that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, the sentence only emphasizes when the action happened, not the idea of passing one o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern says that the time is already past one o’clock. It does not directly describe the movement of the hand.
