default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q21.kobun.tip: Not every time marker uses に; with 回る in the meaning of passing a time marker, を is the suitable particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.vi: I asked Mr. Tanaka why he took time off from work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the person being asked or the person providing information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the workplace from which someone took time off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause やすんだ modifies 訳, while を marks the reason as what was asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きました is the main predicate and describes the action of asking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.why: 会社をやすんだ modifies 訳, so it is placed directly before the noun 訳. The person being asked goes with に, while the content being asked about goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 理由 is used instead of 訳, the meaning is still “reason,” but the expression is more direct and formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q22.kobun.tip: When a clause modifies a noun, do not add の between the verb やすんだ and the noun 訳.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.vi: Because I have not heard a detailed explanation, I do not understand clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the content that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The て-form connects hearing with the state of not having heard enough that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: Vていない shows that something has not been done, while ので connects this clause to the following result as a cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies わかりません and indicates the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.why: を marks the content that was heard, and then the て-form connects the action of hearing with the state of not having heard. ので puts the reason first, followed by the result of not understanding clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still states the cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: Vなかったので means that something was not heard in the past, while Vていないので emphasizes that it still has not been heard up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.kobun.tip: Do not mistake Vていない for simple past negation; this pattern usually emphasizes an unfinished state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q23.tokens.8.m: do not understand, do not know
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.vi: Because it is raining heavily, I am staying home today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the natural phenomenon that is the subject of the adjective ひどい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い keeps the form ひどい before ので to connect the reason with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that today is the time range of the conclusion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place where the speaker exists with the verb います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.why: The clause 雨がひどいので states the reason first. Then, 今日を sets the time topic, and 家にいます expresses where the speaker is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still means because, but から is usually more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: で is not suitable with います when talking about a place of existence; such places usually use に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q24.kobun.tip: Distinguish にいます, meaning where something exists, from で, meaning where an activity takes place; in this sentence, at home uses 家にいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.vi: On weekends, I sometimes go to watch movies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.sk: N は + Adv + N を + Vます-removeます + に + 行きます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that the weekend is the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: This is an adverb modifying the action of going to watch a movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the movie as the object of watching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: The removed form ます of 見ます combines with に to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: いきます is the main verb and expresses going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます + に + 行く・来る・帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.why: たまに modifies the whole action. The phrase 見にいきます uses the removed form ます of 見ます before に to state the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 映画を見ます, the sentence only says “watch a movie” and loses the meaning of going somewhere to watch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use 見ますに; remove ます first, then connect に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.vi: If it rains tomorrow, there will be no choice but to cancel the barbecue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.sk: Time + Nだ・Aなだ + ったら + Nを + Vする + しかない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase sets the context for the condition that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: だったら connects the hypothetical condition with the result; the noun あめ uses the shortened polite past form だったら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the activity that will be canceled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ちゅうしする is a compound verb combining the noun 中止 with する, and it is the main action in the phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: しか goes with the implied negative in ない to express that only one option remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.why: The condition あめだったら comes first to state a hypothetical situation. Then, を marks the object being canceled, while しかない limits the choice to exactly one action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 中止しなければなりません, the sentence has a stronger sense of being required to cancel than “there is no other choice.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only states that the result will happen; it does not emphasize that the speaker has no choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.tip: しか must always be used with a negative form such as ない; do not use しかない with an ordinary affirmative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q3.kobun.cn: Nだ・Aなだ + ったら／Vた形 + ら／Aいかったら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.vi: Choose a convenient day for everyone to hold the reunion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the reunion is the topic to be decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows ownership or a connection with 都合.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 都合のいい is a phrase modifying 日, in which の connects the noun with the adjective いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いい modifies 日, creating the meaning of a convenient or suitable day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the day chosen as the time for the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: しましょう is the polite volitional form, used to suggest deciding together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.why: The phrase みんなの都合のいい日 is built from the inside out to identify a day that suits everyone's schedule. に attaches to the chosen day, while しましょう expresses a suggestion to agree together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 都合のよい, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the tone is more formal than いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q4.kobun.tip: In the phrase 都合のいい日, いい comes directly before 日 and must not be placed の after いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.vi: I applied a protective film to protect my phone screen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects スマホ with がめん to show that the screen belongs to the phone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the screen as the object being protected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ために shows the purpose of applying the film; the verb before it uses the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object applied to the screen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: はりました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.why: The object to be protected is stated first, and then the clause まもるために explains the purpose. The main action はりました comes at the end of the sentence and takes ほごフィルム as its object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ように, the sentence usually emphasizes a goal or a state to be achieved, while ために directly states the purpose of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.tip: For a purpose carried out actively by the subject, use the dictionary-form verb before ために.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + ために
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.vi: After changing my study method, my grades improved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object that is changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects the preceding condition or time point with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that improves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: あがりました is the polite past form of あがる, expressing a result that has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.why: かえたら makes the act of changing a condition or earlier point. The grades are the subject of the result, so they take が, while あがりました expresses a natural increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If かえると is used, the sentence emphasizes that the result usually follows inevitably whenever the method is changed, rather than one specific change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If かえてから is used, the sentence only shows the time sequence “after changing” and does not clearly carry a conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q6.kobun.tip: Distinguish あがる from あげる: あがる increases on its own, while あげる requires the subject to actively increase something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.vi: The day before the business trip, I put my clothes into the suitcase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.sk: N の + Time に + N を + N に + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しゅっちょう with ぜんじつ to identify the day before the business trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates when the action of putting in the clothes took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item put into the suitcase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination where the clothes are put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.why: The phrase の identifies the day before as belonging to the business trip. The first に indicates the time, を indicates the item being moved, and the second に indicates the place receiving the action いれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the suitcase is understood as a tool or means, not as the destination receiving the clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 入りました is used, the clothes become the subject that goes in by themselves or are put in, without stressing that the speaker carried out the action of putting them in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q7.kobun.tip: With いれる, the object usually goes with を and the destination goes with に; do not switch these two particles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.vi: As November began, it became quite cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the starting point of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects a time point with the state that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb modifies the degree to which it becomes cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to the form く to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました indicates that a change has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.cn: Aい drops い + くなる; Vて is used to connect clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.why: The time point comes first, followed by the background event, and then the changed state. The adjective さむい must change to さむく before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means “probably” and no longer emphasizes the degree of coldness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the final result after a process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often keep the adjective い unchanged before なる, but they must change い to く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.vi: In this exam, scores of 80 or below are defined as failing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the exam is the scope of the rule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 以下 indicates the range not exceeding 80 points, and は states the standard being considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content defined or regarded as failing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: とします describes setting or defining a rule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.why: しけんは sets the general scope, while 80てんいかは states the specific standard. The conclusion ふごうかく is placed before とします to create the “define as” structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 以上 is used instead, the range will be 80 points or higher, and the meaning of the rule will change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If ふごうかくになる is used, the sentence only says that the result becomes a failure and does not have a rule-setting nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t103-q9.kobun.tip: 以下 includes the point of 80, not only scores below 80.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.vi: My senior is always very kind to me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states that the senior is the person performing the kind action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb いつも modifies the action してくれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: 親切に changes the adjective な into a state or manner, and then して connects it with くれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: くれます shows that the senior’s action benefits the speaker or the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.why: いつも comes before a verb phrase to show frequency. してくれます combines the action with the idea that the speaker receives help or a benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 親切にします is used instead, the sentence only says that the senior behaves kindly and does not emphasize a benefit for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate くれます simply as “give”; in this pattern, it emphasizes that the action benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q1.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる・くれます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.vi: Since this is my first time here, could you show me around?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it is my first time
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 案内して is the て form, connecting the action of guiding with いただけませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: いただけませんか is a polite way to make a request, in which the speaker humbly receives help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.why: The reason はじめてですから is placed before the request to explain the situation. The form て connects 案内する with いただけませんか, creating a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: It is also a request, but it is more casual and less humble than いただけませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It is still polite, but it focuses on the speaker receiving help and is less formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.tip: Do not translate いただけませんか as simple negation; the whole pattern is a very polite way to ask for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + いただけませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.vi: I gave 1,000 yen and received 120 yen in change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.sk: Amount を + Vて + Amount の + N を + もらいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the amount of money given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of giving money with the action of receiving change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the amount of money with the noun for change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the change as what is received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: もらいました describes the speaker receiving the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.cn: Vて connects actions in order; NのN shows a modifying relationship; Nをもらう describes receiving an item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.why: The money given is the object of だす, and then the form て connects it to the receiving action. の makes 120 yen a modifier of おつり, while を marks the amount received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this replaces もらいました, the sentence is more objective and emphasizes receiving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often omit の in the phrase “120 yen in change,” but Japanese requires 120えんの before おつり.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.vi: I think I will catch the 9 o’clock Shinkansen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the time with the noun 新幹線.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the object that must be caught in the pattern 間に合う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the content of the speaker’s judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 思います is the main predicate and expresses a thought or prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to modify the train. The verb 間に合う uses に for the object that must be caught, and then と connects the predicted content with 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence changes from a present thought to a thought held in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after the train, but 間に合う goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形 + と + 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.vi: I hit my foot against the corner of the table, so it hurts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.ch.0.vi: against the corner of the table
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the corner with the table, while に marks the point that the foot hits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the foot as the body part affected by ぶつける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the event of hitting the foot with the pain that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 痛いです is the main predicate. It states the condition of the foot or the speaker after the impact.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.why: The place of impact takes に, and the affected body part takes を. The form て links the earlier cause with the painful result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: ぶつかって is used when the subject hits another object, while ぶつけて emphasizes making a body part hit an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for 足; with ぶつける, the object or body part being hit usually takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q14.kobun.cn: N に + N を + Vて + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.vi: That shop is selling accessories such as necklaces and earrings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: あの modifies お店 and refers to a shop far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the shop the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: や lists one example from the group of items being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: などの modifies アクセサリー and means accessories such as earrings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks accessories as the items being sold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects the verb うる with います to form a pattern expressing an ongoing selling activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: います completes the pattern ています and expresses an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.why: は makes the shop the topic. Then や and などの name types of accessories. を marks the goods being sold, while ている expresses an ongoing selling activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 売ります is used, the sentence only says that the shop sells accessories. It does not emphasize that the activity is happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If と replaces や, the list is understood as complete, including both necklaces and earrings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q15.kobun.tip: や does not simply connect two fixed nouns; it usually shows that the list includes other things as well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.vi: My older brother is wearing a blue tie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the older brother the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: あおい comes before and directly modifies ネクタイ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the tie as the item being worn or fastened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: しめて is the て form of しめる and connects with います in the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ている expresses the current state created by tying the tie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.why: The adjective あおい comes before a noun to modify it, while を marks the tie as the object of しめる. しめています expresses the current state of the person who has tied the tie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If しめました is used instead, the sentence only says that the tie was tied in the past. It does not emphasize the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q16.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い comes directly before a noun, without adding の after あおい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q17.kobun.sk: N は + N が + ability V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person with the ability as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the activity or object that キムさん can perform.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: できます is a predicate showing that someone can do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q17.kobun.why: In the ability structure with できる, the person with the ability takes は, while the activity or field that can be performed takes が. Therefore, テニスができます means that Kim can play tennis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If テニスをします is used instead, the sentence only says that Kim plays tennis. It does not state that he has the ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q17.kobun.tip: With できます, を is not used for the activity that can be performed; が is usually used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q19.kobun.sk: Time は + N が + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks snow as the subject of the falling action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: ふりました is the polite past-tense predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q19.kobun.why: The time is placed first as the topic. Then the natural subject of the weather event takes が. ふりました uses the past tense because the event happened last night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ゆうべに is used, the sentence sounds less natural because time words such as ゆうべ usually do not need に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q19.kobun.tip: Do not automatically add に after every time word; ゆうべ is often used directly with は or as an adverbial phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.vi: That mountain is reflecting its shape on the surface of the lake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies 山 as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.ch.1.vi: on the surface of the lake
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates where the mountain scene is reflected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being reflected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ています shows an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.why: 山は is the topic, みずうみに indicates the place of reflection, and すがたを is the object of the verb うつす. The verb uses the ています form to express an ongoing reflective state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: With this pattern, the focus shifts to the state of the image being reflected on the surface of the lake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q2.kobun.tip: Learners may easily confuse に with で; in this sentence, に indicates the place where the image exists or appears, without emphasizing the place where the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q20.kobun.vi: I went to the hospital because I had a cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle で indicates the reason for going to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle に indicates the destination of the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: いきました is a movement verb in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q20.kobun.why: The reason comes first with で, the destination follows with に, and then comes the verb いきました. This order links the reason with the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced by なので, the reason is presented more clearly as an explanatory clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q20.kobun.tip: Distinguish で, which marks the reason, from に, which marks the destination; do not use the same particle for these two roles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.vi: I use a computer to create documents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle を marks the tool or object being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of using a computer with the action of creating documents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: Particle を marks the object being created.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: つくります is the main predicate, showing the action of creating a document.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.why: The object or tool of the first action goes with を, and then the form て connects it to the main action. The document is the direct object of つくります, so it also goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If パソコンで is used, the computer is stated directly as the means, without emphasizing a sequence of actions through the form て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q21.kobun.tip: The form て here connects two actions; it does not express the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun and modifies もんだい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は indicates the thing being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective やさしい and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: やさしいです is the polite form of an adjective ending in い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q22.kobun.why: この directly modifies the noun, は makes that noun the topic, and とても comes before the adjective to increase its degree. The adjective ending in い ends the sentence with です in polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If 人 is added after やさしい, the meaning changes to a person who is kind or gentle, not an easy problem.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q22.kobun.tip: やさしい can mean easy or kind; you need to use the noun it modifies to understand the correct meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.vi: I go from here to the movie theater by bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point of the journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: まで marks the ending point of the journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: いきます is the main predicate and shows the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.why: から and まで identify the starting point and ending point in that order. で adds the means of transportation, and いきます expresses the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If バスに乗ります is used, the focus is on getting on the bus, not directly on going to a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If まで is replaced by へ, the sentence only shows the direction toward the movie theater and does not emphasize the final point of the journey.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q23.kobun.tip: で shows the means of transportation, while に or へ shows the destination; で is not used to mark the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the person receiving the call.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the noun used with the verb かける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: かけました is the polite past form of かける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q24.kobun.why: The person receiving the call goes with に, while 電話 is the object of the action and therefore goes with を. The verb かける changes to ました to show that the action was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is still to make a phone call, but the verb する is used instead of the phrase 電話をかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q24.kobun.tip: Do not say 電話にかける; the natural pattern is 電話をかける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.vi: There are eight eggs in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.sk: N に + N が + number + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows where the eggs exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists and is being counted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: あります expresses the existence of an object; やっつ is the general counter for eight objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.why: The place comes first, followed by the existing object, the quantity, and the verb あります. For objects without a special counter, やっつ is used as a general counter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, 八個 also means eight objects, but it counts them with 個.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use やっつ for dates or for objects with special counters, such as 本 and 枚.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.vi: I paid at the checkout counter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects レジ with ところ to modify the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で shows where the payment action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: ました expresses a completed action in polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.why: レジのところで identifies the place, おかねを is the object, and はらいました is the main predicate. The particle で is suitable because payment is an action performed at a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with に, the sentence can easily mean going toward or going to the checkout counter, so it is less natural than で when talking about the place of payment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often use に for every place, but a place where an action takes place usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.vi: Please do not disturb my studies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 勉強 with 邪魔 and shows that the disturbance is related to studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks 邪魔をする as the action that must be stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: しないで connects the negative form of する with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ください changes the previous statement into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.why: 勉強の邪魔をする is a verb phrase meaning to disturb someone's studies. The form しないでください makes that action negative and creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If only しないで is used, the sentence still means "do not do it," but the tone is more casual and less complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also asks someone not to do something, but it is softer and has the tone of a reminder or a suggestion to try.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.tip: Do not separate じゃまをする into the meaning "do a disturbance"; it is a fixed verb phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q4.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to indicate the work being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the work is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が emphasizes the person who directly performs the work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: いたします is the humble form of します, used for the speaker's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.why: The work is made the topic with は, while the person performing it is identified with が. いたします is placed at the end of the sentence to show the speaker's humble action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If します is used, the basic meaning is still to do, but the humble and polite tone is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use いたします to describe another person's action; it is a humble form used when speaking about one's own action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q5.kobun.cn: N を + いたします
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.vi: Mr. or Ms. Suzuki is kind and serious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that Suzuki is the person being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い changes to くて to connect the first quality with the following one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: まじめな directly modifies 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a noun sentence and confirms that Suzuki is a person with the qualities stated earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.why: やさしくて connects two qualities that both describe Suzuki. まじめな comes before 人 because the adjective な must keep な when modifying a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used, the sentence has a contrastive or unfinished tone, rather than simply listing two qualities.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget な after the adjective な when it comes before a noun, but まじめな人 is the correct form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q6.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくて; Aな ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.vi: You must follow the library rules.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects としょかん with きそく, showing that the rules belong to the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the rules as the object of the action of following them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: まもらないと creates a condition with the negative form ない and connects it with いけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: いけません completes the pattern meaning “must do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.why: The rules are the object of まもる, so they are used with を. The pattern Vないといけません means that if someone does not do something, it is not allowed, which is equivalent to saying that they must do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It also expresses an obligation, but it is more formal and stronger than ないといけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses that something must not be done, which is the opposite of the requirement to follow the rules in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.tip: Do not mistake ないといけません for “must not do.” The whole phrase means “must do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q7.kobun.cn: Vない形 ＋ と ＋ いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.vi: My older brother made a strange face and made me laugh.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the older brother as the person who performs the series of actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: へんな modifies 顔, forming the phrase “strange face.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を goes with 顔をして to express having or making a certain facial expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: して connects the facial state with the action of making someone laugh.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: In a causative structure with an intransitive verb, を marks the person who is made to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: わらわせました is the causative form of わらう, meaning “make someone laugh.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.why: The phrase 顔をして describes the state or manner before stating the result. わたしを is the person affected by the causative form わらわせました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this sentence were used, it would mean that I laughed by myself, without the meaning that my older brother made me laugh.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.tip: English learners may easily understand わたしを as an ordinary object, but with an intransitive causative verb, it usually refers to the person who is made to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q8.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ N; Vて; Vる → Vさせる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.vi: Because it was hot, I lowered the air conditioner temperature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the cause あつかった with the action that follows; あつい changes to the past form あつかった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects エアコン with 温度, showing that the temperature belongs to the air conditioner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the temperature as the object being lowered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 下げました is a past transitive verb, showing that the subject actively reduced the temperature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and connects to the result with ので. 温度を is the object, while 下げました is the active action of making the temperature decrease.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: から also gives a reason, but it is usually more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: 下がりました is an intransitive verb, meaning that the temperature decreased or had decreased by itself, without emphasizing the person who adjusted it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.tip: Distinguish 下げる from 下がる: one means actively lowering something, while the other means that something decreases by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t104-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.vi: It is certain that his birthday is January 1.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the noun たんじょうび.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the clause that identifies the date.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: なのは turns the noun clause into a topic to be commented on with たしかです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: たしかです is the predicate that states the certainty of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.why: The clause たんじょうびが1月1日だ is nominalized with のは to serve as the topic. Because the preceding part is a noun, use なのは, not なのだは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only states the information directly and no longer has the comment-like meaning that the information is certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit な before のは after a noun or adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t106-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のは
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.vi: My friend asked me to help with moving house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: In the passive sentence, に refers to the person who made the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: ように marks the content of the indirect request and goes with 言われました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: いわれました is the polite past passive form of 言う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.why: The person who makes the request is used with に in a passive sentence. The action to be performed uses the dictionary form and connects with ように to create an indirect request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this form, the request becomes more direct and conversational, with the meaning of asking the listener to do something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the speaker in a passive sentence; the speaker usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t107-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ように ＋ 言う／言われる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.vi: The person standing over there is my husband.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the location of the person who is standing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 connects the verb 立つ with いる to create a continuing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: のは turns the phrase 立っている into the topic explained at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の modifies the noun しゅじん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: しゅじんです is the predicate identifying who the person standing there is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 立っているのは is moved to the front as the topic, and the answer about the topic is わたしのしゅじんです. に indicates the location, while ている describes the state of standing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this form, 人 clearly states that the subject is a person, while のは emphasizes the whole thing being pointed out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q10.kobun.tip: Do not translate 立っている as the action of standing up; in this sentence, it means the state of standing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.vi: The graduation ceremony will be held tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.sk: Time expression に ＋ N が ＋ passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This part only indicates when the event takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the graduation ceremony as the event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the passive form and expresses that the graduation ceremony will be held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.why: The time expression comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the event as the subject with が. The passive predicate emphasizes that the graduation ceremony is the event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あります, the sentence only says that there will be a graduation ceremony tomorrow, without emphasizing the act of holding it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use あります for every case meaning “there is,” but when talking about an event being held, the passive form should be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.vi: Mr. Kimura returned to the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ past V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Mr. Kimura as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place to which Mr. Kimura returned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb in the past tense, showing that the action of returning has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the destination or place of return with に, and then a verb showing movement. もどる emphasizes returning to the place that was left.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 帰りました, the sentence leans toward returning home or to a familiar place, while もどりました emphasizes returning to the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q12.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate に as “come” in every case; with もどる, に marks the place of return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.vi: My younger brother was warned by my uncle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N に ＋ past passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は shows that my younger brother is the person affected in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: In a passive sentence, に indicates the person who performs the warning action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: されました is the past passive form of ちゅういします, showing that the younger brother is the person affected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.why: The affected person is made the topic with は, while the person performing the action goes with に. The passive form is suitable because the sentence focuses on the younger brother, not the uncle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active sentence is used, the uncle is the person performing the action, and the younger brother is the person being warned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t111-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in a passive sentence with the object; here, に indicates the person who causes the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.vi: I finally reached the mountaintop at about 12 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Adverb ＋ N の N に ＋ past V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: This part indicates the approximate time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: やっと modifies the verb and emphasizes a result achieved after difficulty or waiting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects やま with うえ, forming the noun phrase “the top of the mountain”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the place that the speaker reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: つきました is the polite past form of つく, showing that someone arrived at the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.why: The time and adverb come first to set the context and express the meaning “finally.” The phrase やまのうえ is the destination, so it goes with に, followed by the verb つく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If やっと is replaced with ようやく, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the tone is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q20.kobun.tip: With つく, the destination usually goes with に, not を as when talking about passing through a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.vi: Recently, I have not had a chance to meet him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N に ＋ V辞書形 ＋ N が ＋ ありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: This part modifies the whole event and indicates a time close to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the object of the verb あう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form あう comes before and modifies the noun きかい, creating the meaning “a chance to meet him.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the chance as something that exists or does not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります, expressing nonexistence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.why: The verb あう comes before きかい to modify this noun. The whole phrase “a chance to meet him” acts as the subject with が, and then ありません expresses that there is no chance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 会っていません, the sentence says that the speaker has not met him for some time, without directly saying that there was no chance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t117-q6.kobun.tip: When a verb comes before a noun to modify it, do not add の between the verb and the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q11.kobun.sk: Time interval おきに ＋ N を ＋ します
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: 一日おきに indicates repeated frequency: the action is done once every other day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks cleaning as the object of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the predicate, expressing an action performed as a habit or on a repeated schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q11.kobun.why: The phrase 一日おきに comes at the beginning to state the cycle of the action. The noun そうじ is the object with を, combining with します to form the verb “clean.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 二日に一回, the sentence also means once every two days, but directly states the number of times within the period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q11.kobun.tip: 一日おきに means “every other day,” not “every day”; the action happens on alternating days.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.kobun.vi: You have worked hard. I will leave first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: This is a fixed greeting used to acknowledge another person’s hard work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: さきに is an adverb showing that someone does something before others.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The expression しつれいします politely asks permission to leave first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.kobun.why: おつかれさまです is a suitable opening greeting in a school or work setting. さきに modifies the action しつれいします, showing that the speaker leaves first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this expression is used, the sentence is more direct and simply announces that I will leave first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate しつれいします only as “sorry,” but in this context it should be understood as a polite request for permission to leave.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q12.tokens.0.m: you have worked hard; thank you for your work
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.vi: It is very unusual for him to take photos.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the action of taking photos.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being photographed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb とる combines with の to turn the clause into a noun phrase, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective めずらしい is the predicate and evaluates his taking photos as something that rarely happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.why: The clause かれが写真をとる is nominalized with の so that it becomes the subject of the comment. は marks the whole “act of him taking photos,” and then めずらしいです gives the evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a description of low frequency, with a milder meaning than “very unusual” in the original sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の in the pattern Vのは, so the clause before it is not clearly made the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ のは ＋ Aいです／Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.vi: The illness has improved quite a lot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Degree ＋ Aく ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject whose state is changing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: だいぶ modifies よくなりました and shows a significant degree of improvement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: よく is the adverbial form of よい, modifying なりました to express a state becoming better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる, expressing a change into a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ くなる／Aな ＋ になる／N ＋ になる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.why: びょうきが is the subject of the change, while よくなりました shows that the illness has changed to a better state. だいぶ comes before the adverb to add the degree of improvement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If 少しずつ is used, the sentence emphasizes the process of improving little by little rather than the degree of improvement achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 非常に is used, the degree is emphasized more strongly and has a more formal tone than だいぶ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t123-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may say よくになりました, but an adjective ending in い must change to the form く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t127-q19.kobun.why: せんもん is a compound word referring to a specialized field. The two parts are separated here to show all the vocabulary in the question, not because they are normally used as two independent words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t127-q19.kobun.tip: Do not guess the meaning of せん or もん separately; remember せんもん as a compound word meaning “specialized field”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: うんてん is the noun part that forms a compound word with する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: する combines with the noun うんてん to form the verb “to drive”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q11.kobun.why: うんてん is a noun meaning the act of controlling a vehicle. It combines with する to form a verb for an action. The whole word うんてんする can be conjugated as a group 3 verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: When 運転が好きです is used, the sentence talks about liking the activity of driving, without directly emphasizing the act itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily separate うんてん and する as two separate verbs, but together they form one compound verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.vi: to come, go, or be present
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.ch.0.vi: to come, go, or be present
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: おいで is the vocabulary part meaning come, go, or be present in an honorific expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: になる forms the fixed honorific expression おいでになる, used to show respect for another person's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.why: おいでになる is a fixed honorific expression in which になる does not have its usual meaning “to become.” The specific meaning is come, go, or be present, depending on the context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If these verbs are used instead, the basic meaning is still similar, but the respectful tone is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: いらっしゃる is also an honorific form of come, go, and be present, but it is an independent honorific verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.kobun.tip: Do not translate になる in おいでになる as “to become”; the whole phrase must be understood as an honorific pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t134-q12.tokens.2.m: to become; used in an honorific pattern
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t139-q9.kobun.why: あやまる is a verb describing the action of apologizing; when used with に, the person receiving the apology is stated clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t139-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 謝罪する also means to apologize, but it is more formal and more businesslike.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t139-q9.kobun.tip: Do not confuse あやまる with あやまち, because あやまち means a mistake, not the act of apologizing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t139-q9.tokens.0.m: to apologize; to make a mistake
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vi: My younger brother, who is five years younger than me, is very cute.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.sk: Number of years + 下の + N + とても + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase comes before 弟 as a modifier and shows that the younger brother is five years younger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: 弟 is understood as the subject being described in the following part; the given sentence has no particle that clearly marks the topic or subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective かわいい and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: かわいいです is the predicate formed by an adjective ending in い, in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.why: 5さい下の comes before 弟 to limit and describe the younger brother. 弟 is the person being described, and とても increases the degree of かわいい; in the given sentence, the topic particle after 弟 is omitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding は after 弟 makes the sentence structure more natural and makes the topic clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: が emphasizes that the younger brother who is five years younger is the cute person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t16-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget the particle は or が after the subject noun; in standard writing, they should say 弟は or 弟が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vi: This carrot is thin, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this carrot is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い keeps its basic form to act as the predicate before ですね.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is used to make a comment and wait for the listener's agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.why: The topic phrase comes first, followed by an adjective describing the carrot's feature. ですね is placed at the end to turn the comment into a gentle confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes negative: this carrot is not thin or slender.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily add だ after the adjective い, but 細い already acts as the predicate, so 細いだ is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vi: There are few shops nearby, so it is quite inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the shops exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the shop as the subject whose quantity is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 少ない changes to 少なくて to connect the situation of having few shops with the result of inconvenience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: 不便 is an adjective な, combined with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.cn: Aいくて + Aなで/Nで + result clause
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.why: The place is stated first, followed by the subject 店が and the state 少なくて. The final part states the result of having few shops with the adjective な 不便です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer: because there are few shops, it is inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the sentence expresses contrast: although there are few shops, it is inconvenient, or another idea follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use 少ないで; when the adjective い is connected with て, it must change to 少なくて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vi: This apartment is spacious, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that this apartment is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective い keeps its basic form to act as the predicate before ですね.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ですね is used to make a comment and wait for agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.why: The apartment phrase is made the topic with は, and then 広い directly describes its feature. ですね stands at the end to create a gentle confirmation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means: this apartment is not spacious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q6.kobun.tip: Do not add だ after 広い because the adjective い can directly end the clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vi: The train we will take is an express train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person performing the action 乗る in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: のる comes before 電車 to modify the train we will take.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the train being described is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 急行 acts as a noun predicate and states the type of train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: です connects the noun 急行 with the topic in a polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.why: The clause わたしたちがのる comes before 電車 to identify which train it is. After は, the noun 急行 acts as the description, and です ends the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If のった is used, the meaning changes to the train that we took.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If の is used, the sentence only means our train and does not emphasize the action of riding the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.tip: A modifying clause in Japanese comes before the noun, so のる is not placed after 電車 as in the familiar English expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.tokens.2.m: to ride; to get on a train
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t19-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形 + N; N は + N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vi: There is a dog behind the apartment building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects マンション with 裏側 to create the noun phrase “the back of the apartment building.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where the dog exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: います is the polite form of いる, used for people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.why: The phrase マンションの裏側 creates the location, and then に identifies the place where something exists. いぬが is the subject, and います is the predicate suitable for animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is used instead, the sentence is for objects or other inanimate things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often use あります for animals, but animals must be used with います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t23-q2.kobun.cn: Nの + 場所に + Nが + いる／います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q21.kobun.vi: I will submit the documents to the office.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place or recipient receiving the submitted documents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the documents as the direct object of 出します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: だします is a polite verb that states the main action of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q21.kobun.why: The recipient or receiving place is used with に, the documents are used with を, and the verb だします ends the sentence. This order makes clear who receives what and what the action is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced by で, the office becomes the place where the action takes place, with no longer an emphasis on it being the place where documents are received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q21.kobun.tip: Distinguish に as the place or recipient, while で is the place where the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.vi: If it rains, the sports day will be canceled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the sports day is the topic of the announcement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: 雨の場合は states the condition under which the event happens, while は emphasizes that case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the result or state that the event changes into.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: なります politely describes changing into the state 中止.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.why: The topic うんどうかいは is stated first. Then the condition 雨の場合は limits the situation in which it applies. The phrase 中止に combines with なります to describe changing into a canceled state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ときは, the sentence refers only to the time or situation of rain, with a less formal and less rule-like conditional meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with なら, the sentence has a hypothetical meaning based on the information or condition given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.tip: After 場合, の is usually used with nouns such as 雨の場合, and は is not omitted when emphasizing the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q22.kobun.cn: Nの + 場合(は); Nに + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.vi: When night comes, the harbor becomes quiet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the state occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: なると connects a condition with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the harbor is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: しずかです shows the present state of being quiet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.why: 夜に sets the time point, while なると creates the condition “when it becomes.” Then, 港は is the topic and しずかです is the state described about the harbor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is omitted after 夜, 夜になると can still be understood as “when night comes,” but the separation of the time point is less clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle に after a noun showing time, but 夜に is the expression to remember in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify 番組.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that this program is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: おもしろいです is the adjective predicate い in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q24.kobun.why: この must come directly before the noun to form the phrase “this program.” That phrase is made the topic with は, and the adjective おもしろい describes the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: これ means “this one” and can stand alone. It does not stand directly before 番組 like この.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use この alone as a pronoun. Before a noun, use この, while the independent form is usually これ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.vi: My current job still involves limited experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects いま with しごと to form the phrase “current job.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the current job is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ adds the meaning of a state that has not reached the desired level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that has the characteristic 浅い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: 浅い modifies 経験 and connects with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.why: いまのしごとは states the topic, while けいけんが浅い describes the level of experience of that topic. が comes before the adjective to mark the noun as having the characteristic “limited, shallow.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 少ない emphasizes the small amount of experience, while 浅い emphasizes that the experience is not deep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t28-q25.kobun.tip: 浅い should not be translated only as “shallow.” When talking about 経験, it usually means “not deep, still limited.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.vi: Write the numbers from 1 to 10 vertically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the number range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the endpoint, while の connects this range with ばんごう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the numbers as the objects being written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the direction or arrangement used when writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: かきます is the main verb in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.why: The phrase 1から10までの defines the range of ばんごう. ばんごうを is the object of the action, while 縦に shows how the writing is arranged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 横に, the meaning changes to writing horizontally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t30-q9.kobun.tip: に in 縦に does not indicate a place. Here, it shows the direction or way of performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to identify the temple being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that that temple is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the adjective ふるい and emphasizes the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ふるいです is the adjective predicate い, describing the temple.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q9.kobun.why: あのてら forms the noun phrase “that temple,” and then は makes this phrase the topic. とても comes before the adjective to add the degree “very.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 古くて would connect the characteristic “old” to another clause, rather than ending a simple statement like ふるいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t36-q9.kobun.tip: The adjective い, such as ふるい, comes directly before です; do not add な between them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: This number phrase combines with 10 to form a calculation that modifies こたえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the calculation 3かける10 with the noun こたえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that the result of the calculation is the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 30です is the conclusion, determining the value of the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q15.kobun.why: 3かける10 forms a calculation, and の turns the whole phrase into a modifier for こたえ. こたえは states the object being identified, while 30です gives its value.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This phrase is easily understood as “the answer to the problem consisting of 3 and 10,” without clearly stating multiplication.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t54-q15.kobun.tip: かける means “multiply” in a calculation, not the verb 掛ける meaning to hang or make a phone call in this context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.vi: This coat looks expensive, but it is not that expensive in fact.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the coat being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks コート as the topic of the two contrasting clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 高い drops い and connects with そうに to modify 見えます, describing how something appears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: そんなに shows degree and is often used with a negative form to say that something is not to that extent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: 高い changes to 高くない to form the polite negative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.cn: Aい drop い ＋ そうだ; そんなに ＋ negative; clause ＋ が ＋ clause
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.why: The first clause describes an outward impression with そうに見える, while the second clause denies the degree with そんなに〜ない. が is placed between the two clauses to create contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, it sounds more objective and formal, with less emphasis on a direct impression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If あまり高くない is used, it means not very expensive, but it does not contrast with an implicitly known price level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may incorrectly connect 高いそうに; they must drop い before そう and use 高そうに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.vi: I have always liked Japan, from childhood until now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with とき to form a phrase referring to a time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point of a period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: まで marks the ending point of a period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: ずっと modifies the state 好きでした and emphasizes continuity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the object of liking in the structure 好きだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 好きでした is the adjective predicate な in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ とき; N時点 ＋ から〜まで; ずっと ＋ predicate; Aな ＋ でした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.why: ときから and 今まで create a time period, while ずっと shows that the state continues throughout that period. With 好き, the object usually goes with が rather than を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Using を here is unnatural; 好き usually chooses が to mark the object of liking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If changed to the present tense, the sentence only says that the speaker likes Japan now and does not emphasize a state continuing from the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with 好き because it is translated as “like,” but the standard structure is Nが好きだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.vi: Because their faces look alike, I think those two people may be siblings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that has the similar feature in the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason clause to the statement that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: たぶん modifies the whole statement and expresses a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: あの comes before 二人 to identify the two people being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: は states 二人 as the topic of the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the content that 思います is thought or judged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: 思います is the main predicate and takes the quoted content with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ ので; N ＋ だと ＋ 思う; たぶん ＋ clause expressing a guess
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.why: The clause with ので gives the basis first, and then the speaker makes a guess. The content being thought is きょうだいだ, so it is connected to 思います with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If たぶん is omitted, the sentence is still a personal opinion, but the speaker sounds less cautious about the guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget だ before と when the quoted content is a noun or an adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.vi: Christmas is coming soon, so I have to think about presents.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: もうすぐ modifies the time クリスマス and indicates that something will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the reason to what needs to be done in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks プレゼント as the object of 考える.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ないと is a shortened form of ないといけない and expresses an obligation to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with ですから. At the end of the sentence, ないと omits いけない but still keeps the meaning that something must be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, the meaning of obligation stays the same, but the expression becomes more formal and complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes only advice about what should be done, so it is weaker than an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ないと as only expressing a condition, but at the end of a sentence it is often a shortened form meaning that something must be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q13.kobun.cn: Nです ＋ から; Vない ＋ と（いけない）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.vi: Recently, the number of apartments with tatami rooms has been decreasing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん indicates the period in which the change is observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 畳 with 部屋 to form the noun phrase 畳の部屋.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 部屋 with the clause ある, preparing to modify アパート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause 部屋のある modifies アパート, meaning an apartment that has that room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks アパート as the subject whose number is decreasing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: 少ない changes to 少なく and connects with なる to express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.cn: Aい drop い ＋ くなる; Nのある ＋ N; Nの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.why: The phrase 畳の部屋のあるアパート is placed before が to describe the type of apartment being discussed. 少なくなる expresses a change in quantity from many to few.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced in this sentence, it emphasizes more strongly that the present state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only describes something as few and does not state the process of becoming fewer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may separate the phrase 部屋のある incorrectly; the whole clause modifies アパート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.vi: I compared the two and bought the cheaper one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the two objects being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the comparison action to the purchase action that follows.
