default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective clause 安い modifies ほう, while を marks the item that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 買う uses the polite past form to end the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.why: The two items come first with を because they are the objects of the comparison. The phrase 安いほうを means “the cheaper side/item” and is the object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほう is replaced with もの, the meaning becomes “a cheap item,” and the sense of choosing one of the two items is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that ほう must come after a description such as 安いほう to indicate the more suitable side or choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.vi: My hometown has changed completely compared with 10 years ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the hometown as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と marks the point used to compare the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies かわって and emphasizes the degree of change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects かわる and しまいました in the same predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました expresses that the event has been completed, often with a sense of regret or something happening against one's plans.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.why: １０年前と creates the point of comparison, while すっかり adds the degree of change. かわってしまいました combines the form て with しまう to emphasize that the change has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If かわりました is used, the sentence only says that it changed. The tone is weaker and does not emphasize the degree of completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with かわりませんでした, the meaning changes to “did not change.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate しまう only as “finish doing,” but in this sentence it also gives the sense that the change happened completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q16.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます／しまった／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.vi: Preparing dinner every day is hard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The frequency adverb modifies the whole action of preparing dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks dinner as the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the action したくする into a noun, while は presents that action as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な with たいへんです forms the predicate and evaluates the action mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.why: The phrase ばんごはんをしたくする is nominalized with の so that it can be the topic with は. Then たいへんです gives a comment about the whole task of preparing dinner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: ことは can also nominalize an action, but it usually has a more general or formal tone than のは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put は after まいにち, but in this sentence は must attach to の to present “preparing” as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ のは ＋ Aな／Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.vi: Among fruits, I like grapes the most.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: では limits the comparison to the group of fruits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the item chosen as the most liked one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: This adverb modifies すきです and shows the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: 好きです is the adjective predicate な and expresses a preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.why: では sets the scope as “among fruits,” then が marks the selected fruit. いちばん comes before 好きです to create the meaning “like the most.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing では with の中で still indicates the scope, but the specific meaning is “inside the group of fruits.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with 好き, but 好きです usually uses が to mark the preferred item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.vi: In the morning, my mother always wakes me up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the morning as the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The frequency adverb modifies the action of being woken up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the person who performs the action in the structure てもらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: Vて＋もらいます expresses that the speaker receives help from their mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.why: 母に performs the action, while the speaker receives the benefit, so おこしてもらいます is used. あさは puts the time at the beginning of the sentence, and いつも adds frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression only states that the mother wakes someone up. It does not clearly show that the speaker receives help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: 起こされます is passive and emphasizes being woken up rather than gratitude or benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in てもらう with the receiver, but に here only indicates the person who helps.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.tokens.6.m: receive the favor of someone doing something for you
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q19.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もらう／もらいます／もらった／もらいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q20.kobun.vi: Tomorrow is my older sister's wedding ceremony.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents tomorrow as the time being announced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the owner to the noun 結婚式 that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun phrase combines with です to form the predicate and end the sentence politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q20.kobun.why: あしたは identifies the time being discussed. あねの shows possession and directly modifies the noun けっこんしき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If が結婚します is used, the meaning is that the older sister will get married, without focusing on the wedding ceremony.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit の or use が between あね and けっこんしき, but the relationship “my sister's wedding ceremony” requires の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.vi: Because I could speak English, I was able to enter this company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks English ability as the condition leading to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the result and follows the plain form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or organization that the speaker joins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 入れました is the polite past potential form and expresses that the speaker was able to enter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first with ので, followed by the place of entry with に and the result 入れました. The particle に is suitable because the company is the place or organization that the speaker enters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with から, the sentence still states a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use を with a place one enters, but 入る usually uses に to indicate the place or organization that someone joins.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q21.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.vi: Because I like this job, I want to continue doing it forever.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object evaluated as liked in the structure すきだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects the reason to the result, with から following the polite ending of the adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: たい is attached to the verb stem to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.why: The reason comes before から, while the speaker's desire appears at the end of the sentence with つづけたいです. が marks the object of the feeling of liking, not the subject of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If つづけたいです is replaced with つづけます, the sentence only says that the action will continue; it no longer means wanting to continue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with すきですが. The basic pattern is Nがすきです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.vi: The air conditioning at the company is too strong, so it is cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets the company as the topic area for commenting on the condition inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the strong feature in this clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: つよくて is the て form of the adjective い, connecting the air conditioner's feature with the cold state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: さむいです is the main predicate, stating the result or final feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.why: かいしゃは sets the scope of the comment, while れいぼうが is the subject of the feature つよい. The て form connects the cause-related feature with the feeling さむい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If つよくて is replaced with つよいので, the cause-and-effect relationship is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect two い adjectives with と, but when connecting い adjectives, they must change them to the くて form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.vi: I want to research medicine for sick people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun びょうき with 人たち to modify those people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 人たち with ため, identifying the intended target.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ために indicates the purpose or beneficiary of the research action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks medicine as the object being researched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: たい is attached after the verb stem けんきゅうし to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.why: The modifying phrase びょうきの人たち comes before ために to identify the intended people. Next comes the object くすりを, followed by the desired verb at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ように is used, the sentence focuses more on a goal or achieved state, rather than directly emphasizing the beneficiary as ために does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place ために after a verb, but in this sentence ために comes after the noun naming the target.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q24.kobun.cn: Nの ＋ ために; Vます-stem ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with 専門, showing that the specialty belongs to the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the specialty the topic explained at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with the noun giving the explanation and creates a polite ending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q25.kobun.why: わたしの modifies せんもん, forming a noun phrase that becomes the topic with は. The noun けいざい comes after です to state what the specialty is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the sentence emphasizes that the identified specialty is economics instead of simply stating the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically translate の as “of” in every case, but here it only shows a modifying relationship between two nouns.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.vi: I want to learn about the culture and history of European countries.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nの ＋ Nや ＋ Nが ＋ Vます形 omit ます＋たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun before it with the modified noun after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: の creates a modifying phrase for ぶんかやれきし.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: や connects the nouns listed as the content the speaker wants to learn about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the content to be learned in the structure しりたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: たい is attached to the ます form of the verb to express the speaker's desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.cn: Vます形 omit ます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.why: The two phrases の identify the scopes as Europe and countries, respectively. や connects the content the speaker wants to learn about, while が marks the content linked to 知りたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: と lists all the items, while や gives only a few examples, such as culture and history.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: を知りたい can be used to state the object the speaker wants to learn about, but the expression with が is also very natural in this pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mechanically use を after every noun naming an object, but 知りたい often goes with が when emphasizing what someone wants to learn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.vi: This summer was terribly hot, so many people collapsed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: の modifies なつ, identifying the summer as belonging to this year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this year's summer the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い comes before あつさ to modify the degree of the heat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the cause that led many people to fall or collapse.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The past-tense clause comes before 人 to modify the people who collapsed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the subject of 多かった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: 多かった is the past form of the adjective 多い, stating the number of people who collapsed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ さ; Vた ＋ N; Nで indicates the cause
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.why: なつは states the topic, and then あつさで gives the cause. The clause たおれた comes before 人 to identify the group of people, and then 多かった serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also states a cause, but usually directly connects a complete clause and sounds softer as an explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: から states a direct and more conversational cause than で in a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse で, which indicates a cause in あつさで, with で, which indicates a place or means.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.vi: First, cut the vegetables very finely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: はじめに is an adverb showing the order of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks vegetables as the object being cut.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The く form of the adjective い modifies how the action 切る is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: てください is used to politely ask or request the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.why: The adverb はじめに is placed at the beginning to show the order. After the object やさいを, こまかく describes the degree of cutting, while てください gives a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Vなさい is also a request, but it has the tone of a higher-status person instructing someone below them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Vてもいいです asks about or gives permission for an action; it is not a request for someone else to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate てください as “please” in every case, but its actual tone also depends on the relationship and context.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.vi: I had a date today, but I could not go because of unexpected work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes today the topic of the first clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: having a date but being unable to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun しごと to describe the work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: で shows that the work is the reason the speaker cannot go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けない changes to 行けなく to connect with なる, showing a change into a state of being unable to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: なりました completes the pattern 行けなくなりました and describes a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.cn: V可能形ない形 + く + なる; Aな + な + N; Nで shows the cause
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.why: The first clause states the plan, and が creates a contrast with the following situation. The phrase きゅうなしごとで states the cause, while 行けなくなりました describes the change from being able to go to being unable to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 行けませんでした only says that the person could not go, without stressing a change from being able to go to being unable to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: 行かないことになりました usually suggests that a decision or arrangement was made not to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q6.kobun.tip: Do not say 行けないなりました; before なる, ない must be changed to なく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.vi: I treasure and take good care of the mug that my friend gave me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the source or the person who gave the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause 友だちからもらった comes before マグカップ to describe the mug.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the mug as the object being treasured and cared for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: だいじに modifies しています and shows the state or manner of caring for the mug.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: ている in しています describes a state that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.cn: Vて + いる; Vた + N to create a clause that modifies a noun
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.why: 友だちからもらった is a modifying clause placed before マグカップ. After stating the object with を, だいじにしています describes the present state of keeping and treasuring it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 大切にする is close in meaning to 大事にする and usually emphasizes valuing or protecting something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: もらっている focuses on receiving or having received something as a state, not on treasuring the mug.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ています as describing an action in progress, but here it emphasizes a state that is being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.vi: At the restaurant's checkout counter, the two people paid separately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects レストラン with レジ and shows that the checkout counter belongs to the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the payment takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: 二人 is the subject performing the action, although particle が is omitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: べつべつに modifies はらいました and shows how the two people paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the money as the object being paid.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: はらいました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.cn: Aな + に to create an adverb; Nで indicates a place
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.why: The place phrase レストランのレジで comes first. 二人 is the subject, べつべつに describes the manner, お金を is the object, and はらいました ends the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: 一緒に would change the meaning to the two people paying together instead of paying separately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: それぞれ also means separately for each person, but it usually emphasizes each individual more than べつべつに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q8.kobun.tip: Do not omit に in べつべつに; a noun or adjective な usually needs に to function as an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.vi: I will never forget the pleasant experiences in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: での combines で, which indicates a place, with の to modify 経験.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective directly modifies 経験.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: は states that 経験 is the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: けっして is used with a negative predicate to emphasize the meaning of absolutely not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite negative form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.why: The phrase にほんでのたのしいけいけん is placed before は to make it the topic. けっして comes before the negative predicate to emphasize the degree of negation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence sounds more conversational and emphasizes not doing anything at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 必ず is used, the meaning changes to definitely doing or remembering something, so it is no longer negative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t71-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that けっして usually has to be used with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.vi: On TV, earthquake news is broadcast many times a day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.sk: Nで + Time periodに + Number of timesも + Nの + Nを + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means or channel through which the broadcast is carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に identifies the period used to count the number of broadcasts.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: も follows a number of times to emphasize that the number is higher than expected or that something is repeated many times.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects じしん with ニュース and shows the content of the news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the news report as the object being broadcast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: しています is the ている form of ほうそうする and describes broadcasting that is continuing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.why: テレビで states the means, followed by the time and frequency of broadcasting. The phrase じしんのニュースを is the complete object and comes directly before the predicate ほうそうしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に for means, but the means or channel used to perform an action usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.vi: When no one in the family was at home, a burglar broke into my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the state of being absent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: だれも combines with the negative form to indicate that there is not anyone at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: いない is the negative form of いる and is used for people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: ときに indicates the time when the main event occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the agent that caused the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: 入られました is the polite past passive form and describes the speaker being adversely affected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.why: The clause かぞくがだれもいないときに identifies the time. After that, どろぼうに states the agent, while 入られました is the event the speaker had to suffer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only emphasizes that something happened unwillingly and does not clearly show the passive structure of being affected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse に in a passive sentence with に, which indicates a place or time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.vi: Could you please exchange the shirt I bought here a moment ago?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: さっき modifies the buying action that happened earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the place where the buying action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: かった is the plain past form of 買う. It comes before a noun to modify シャツ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the item being exchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the verb とりかえる with もらう to express asking someone else to do something for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: もらえませんか is a polite way to make a request. It means asking the listener to do something for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.why: The clause さっきこちらでかった comes before シャツ to identify which shirt. シャツを is the object of とりかえる, while Vてもらえませんか changes the exchange action into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the question asks for permission to exchange the shirt yourself, not to ask someone else to exchange it for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the request is more direct and less gentle than もらえませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand もらう as simply “receive,” but here it expresses having someone else do something for you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q13.kobun.cn: Vて + もらえませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.vi: On cold days, I also enjoy coordinating outfits with gloves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: さむい modifies 日 to form a phrase meaning “cold days.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes cold days the setting or topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects てぶくろ with おしゃれ and shows that the fashion is related to gloves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: も replaces を and adds the meaning “also” to the thing being enjoyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: たのしみます is the main predicate in the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.why: さむい modifies 日 to create a weather setting. The phrase てぶくろのおしゃれ is the thing being enjoyed, while も adds the meaning “also.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If の is replaced with について, the phrase means “about glove fashion,” putting more focus on the topic than on the modifying relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle の between the two nouns and say てぶくろおしゃれ directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.vi: Saying that Tokyo has the highest prices in the world is a slight exaggeration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject described as having high prices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: で limits the scope of the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies 高い to create a superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the adjective 高い in the descriptive clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: 高い is the predicate of the quoted clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: というのは turns the entire preceding clause into a topic for comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: な connects オーバー with 話 and modifies the noun 話.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.ch.7.n: 話です is the main predicate and evaluates the content stated earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.why: The clause 東京が世界で一番物価が高い is placed before というのは to turn it into the content being evaluated. オーバーな話です is the concluding evaluation of that content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence focuses on drawing a conclusion from the earlier information, rather than evaluating a statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If のは is used directly, the tone is more natural in spoken language, but it does not emphasize the meaning “saying that” as much as というのは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place いちばん before the whole phrase in the wrong position. Here, it modifies 高い within the scope of せかいで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nだ + というのは + N だ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.vi: I think the person who painted such a large picture in just one day is amazing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the time needed to finish the painting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: こんなに modifies 大きな and emphasizes its large size.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 大きな comes before え to modify the noun directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the thing that was painted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: かいた is the plain past form. It comes before 人 to modify the person who painted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: は makes the person who painted the object being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: と marks the quoted comment before おもいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.ch.7.n: おもいます is the main predicate showing the speaker's thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.why: The phrase かいた人 forms “the person who painted,” with the preceding clause modifying 人. After this topic, すごいとおもいます states the speaker's comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes more objective and cautious, like a statement believed to be true.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence expresses a guess or degree of certainty instead of directly saying “I think.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use すごいなとおもいます in every situation. と comes after the comment content and is the standard structure with おもう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q23.kobun.cn: 普通形 + と + 思います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.vi: Because the air conditioner's sound seems unusual, let's ask someone to check it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects エアコン with 音 and shows that the sound comes from the air conditioner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject described as unusual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the reason with the proposed action in the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.ch.3.vi: let's ask someone to check it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてもらいましょう expresses a suggestion to ask someone to do something for us together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason using ですから. After the comma comes a suggestion to deal with the problem; みてもらいましょう shows that the speaker suggests asking someone else to check it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to check it directly, without the shared-suggestion meaning of ましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, it means trying to check it ourselves together, not asking someone else to do it for us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate もらう as “receive,” but Vてもらう here means having someone else do the task for us.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.tokens.9.m: have someone do it for you
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q24.kobun.cn: Aなですから、/Aいですから、/V普通形から、 + Vて + もらいましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.vi: After studying seriously, my grades improved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes the adjective な まじめ into an adverb modifying 勉強した.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects the action 勉強した with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object whose state has changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: よい changes to よく to connect with なる, showing that something has become better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: なりました is the polite past form of なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.cn: Vた形 + ら; Aい drop い + く + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.why: The べんきょうしたら part states the condition or time that leads to the result. 成績 is the subject that changes, while よくなりました expresses the result of becoming better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてから is used, the sentence emphasizes the order: the result comes only after studying is finished. It does not have as clear a conditional meaning as たら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only describes a change into a new state. It does not state a study condition by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t78-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers often keep よい before なる, but it must change to よくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.vi: The famous actor died from an illness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase modifies the noun はいゆう that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the action of dying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the cause of death.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 亡くなる is changed into the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.why: The phrase ゆうめいな comes before はいゆう to modify the person being discussed. はいゆうが is the subject, while びょうきで states the cause of 亡くなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence means that the actor is no longer there or has disappeared. It does not necessarily mean that the actor has died.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q1.kobun.tip: いなくなる should not be used to talk about a deceased person when you want to be polite and clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.vi: If I return home late, I will buy food at the supermarket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks returning home late as the stated condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb なる combines with おそく to express a change into a late state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 場合は makes a hypothetical case the topic and condition of the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action of buying or eating food takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks ごはん as the object of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: 買います is the main predicate and states the action that will be done in that case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.why: The clause おそくなる modifies 場合, forming the condition “the case of returning home late.” After the comma comes the corresponding action, with で showing the place and を showing the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: ときは refers generally to a time or situation, while 場合は emphasizes a specific hypothetical case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 場合 as a noun that stands alone. It usually needs a preceding clause to modify it, and は states the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + 場合は
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.vi: Whenever I look at this photo, I remember my city.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: Vると connects a condition or natural reaction: whenever the first action is done, the following result occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object being remembered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 思い出す is in the polite form and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.why: The dictionary form of the verb 見る combines with と to state a natural reaction after an action. Both 見る and 思い出す take an object marked by を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence becomes a more specific condition and no longer has the meaning of a natural reaction whenever one sees something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q11.kobun.tip: Do not change 見る into the た form before と in a pattern that expresses a repeated reaction; use 見ると.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.vi: Because this station is small, express trains do not stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents this station as the topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a reason with a result; after an い-ending adjective, 小さいので is used directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は presents the express train as the topic discussed in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: とまりません is the negative predicate, showing that the express train does not stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.why: は introduce the place and the topic to be explained in order. ので connects the reason 小さい with the result とまりません in a reason–result relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から keeps almost the same meaning of reason, but the expression becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily add な after an い-ending adjective; the correct form is 小さいので, not 小さいな所以.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.tokens.8.m: does not stop / does not call at
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q13.kobun.vi: Because many people saw me when I fell, I was very embarrassed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of 見られる, namely, the act of being seen by other people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the agent who performs the action of seeing in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 見られて is the passive form of 見る and connects to the following clause with て, expressing a cause or situation that leads to an emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 恥ずかしかった is an い-ending adjective in the past tense and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q13.kobun.why: The clause 見られて comes first to state the situation that caused the emotion in the following clause. The sentence uses に to mark the agent in the passive sentence, while て connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for the person performing the passive action, but the agent in a passive sentence usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.vi: I have just finished eating, but I am already very sleepy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the food as the object of the verb 食べる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたばかりで describes an action that has just been completed and connects it to a present state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: 眠い is an い-ending adjective that serves as the predicate and is made polite with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.why: 食べたばかりで is placed first to state an action that has just happened, and 眠いです then states the present condition. The particle を marks the food that was eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the moment just after eating rather than a general feeling that has just occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If 食べている is used, the meaning is that the person is eating, not that the person has finished eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ばかり with a quantity meaning; in the pattern Vたばかり, it means just having done something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q14.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ばかりだ／です／で／なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.vi: My apartment is near the station, but the sound of cars is very loud.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes “my apartment” the topic and introduces two contrasting features.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から marks the reference point used to judge distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ですが connects two contrasting comments: it is near the station, but the sound of cars is loud.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the sound of cars as the subject causing the state of being loud.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: うるさいです is an adjective predicate that describes the speaker’s impression of the sound of cars.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.why: えきから sets the reference point for the adjective ちかい. ですが connects a positive feature with an unfavorable comment, while が marks the sound of cars as the subject of the state of being loud.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: けど also connects contrasting ideas, but it is more casual than ですが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: のに shows a stronger contrast with expectations, like “although it is near the station, it is still noisy.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に after ちかい; when saying that something is near a place, use から to mark the reference point for distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q15.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ ですが; V普通形・Aな・N ＋ ですが
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.vi: Teacher Tanaka is a good teacher who always teaches with great dedication.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes Teacher Tanaka the topic of the sentence being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies ねっしんに and shows the degree of dedication.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The に form of the な adjective changes it into an adverb that modifies おしえてくださる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The modifying clause comes before いい先生 and describes the teacher as someone who teaches the speaker or learners with dedication.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: いい directly modifies the noun 先生.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: 先生です is a noun predicate that concludes that the person being discussed is a good teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.why: The parts とても and ねっしんに modify the teaching action. The clause おしえてくださる comes before the noun to describe 先生, and then 先生です serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: 教えてくれる describes someone teaching the speaker in a friendly way, while くださる shows respect for the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a modifying clause after a noun; in Japanese, おしえてくださる must come before 先生.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q16.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ に; Vて ＋ くださる; V普通形 ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.vi: About how much money is needed to rent an apartment in Tokyo?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で marks the place where the apartment rental takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb かりる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form of a verb + のに expresses purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: This phrase asks for an approximate amount of money needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 必要ですか is the predicate asking how much money is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.why: The place comes first, and the rental object comes before the verb. のに connects the action かりる with the meaning of purpose, while いくらぐらい asks about the amount of money needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is used with its contrastive meaning, it must connect two contrasting clauses and no longer means “to rent.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: ために also expresses purpose, but it is more formal and often emphasizes the goal more strongly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand のに here as “but,” while after a dictionary-form verb it can mean “to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.vi: I thought the test was difficult, but in fact it was not that difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the test the topic of the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content that is thought or predicted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: と思っていました expresses a previous thought, while が connects it to a result that differs from the prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: それほど combines with a negative form to reduce the degree being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ありませんでした is the past negative form of それほどでもない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.why: The first clause states a previous thought. Then が signals that reality was different from the prediction. それほど goes with a negative form to say that the degree was not as high as expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あまり〜ない, it means “not very ...,” which is milder and does not necessarily refer to a degree mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: と思います expresses a present thought, while と思っていました expresses a thought that existed earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use それほど with an affirmative sentence to mean “not that much”; this pattern usually requires a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ と思っていました; それほど ＋ ではない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.vi: Two years ago, even when I watched TV, I could not understand any Japanese at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N を ＋ Vて＋も ＋ N が ＋ Adv ＋ V past negative
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は sets a time point as a topic for comparison or for giving information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb 見る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: 見ても is the form て＋も, connecting to the meaning “even if I watch it, I still ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the object understood in the pattern わかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ちっとも modifies わかりません and usually goes with a negative sentence to emphasize a zero degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: わかりませんでした is the polite past negative form of わかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.why: The time point is placed at the beginning with は, followed by an action expressing a concession with ても. The subject of わかる uses が, while ちっとも combines with a negative form to create the meaning “understand nothing at all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あまり, the degree of “not understanding much” is milder and less emphatic than ちっとも.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ちっとも with an affirmative sentence, but this pattern must go with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.vi: There was a car and motorcycle accident near my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects いえ with ちかく, creating a place phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates where an event takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と connects 車 with the noun バイク in a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の connects バイク with 事故, forming a phrase about an accident involving a motorcycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: 事故が is an existing event in the pattern 事故がありました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ありました describes the existence or occurrence of the accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.why: いえのちかくで identifies the location, and then 車とバイクの事故 forms the subject of the sentence. あります is used to say that an event occurs or exists at that location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence emphasizes the accident happening rather than the existence of an accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use に to indicate where an event occurs in this pattern; the location of an event usually goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.vi: This place is usually quiet, but there are really a lot of people today, aren't there?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.sk: Timeは + Aななのに + Timeは + Adv + Nが + Aいですね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は contrasts the usual state with today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective な uses なのに to connect a concessive clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes today the contrasting topic with いつも.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ずいぶん modifies 多い and emphasizes that the number of people is higher than expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the thing whose quantity is described as large.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.ch.5.vi: there are really many, aren't there
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: 多い is the predicate, while ね adds a tone of shared confirmation or surprise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.why: いつもは and 今日は create a contrast in time. のに connects the usual state with the opposite reality, while ずいぶん adds degree to the adjective 多い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: けれども also connects two contrasting ideas, but it expresses “even so” less strongly than のに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: After a dictionary-form verb, のに can mean “for the purpose of,” but here it connects two contrasting clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.tip: With the adjective な, you must use なのに, rather than connecting it directly with なに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q20.kobun.cn: Aな + なのに; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + のに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.vi: If you like Japanese food, how about sushi or tempura, for example?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the thing judged to be いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: なら turns the statement いい into a condition for making a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: たとえば signals that specific examples will follow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: や connects representative nouns in an incomplete list.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes the suggested food the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: どうですか asks for an opinion or suggestion about the foods just mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first to identify the listener's preference. たとえば introduces examples, and や connects sushi and tempura as representative choices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: たら can also state a condition, but it is usually connected to a more specific situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: と expresses a natural or certain result, so it is less suitable than なら when making a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.tip: や does not mean “and” for the whole list; it only gives a few representative examples.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q21.kobun.cn: N・Aな + なら; V普通形・Aい + なら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.vi: If you like sake, let's drink together next time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.sk: Nが + Aななら + Time + Adv + Vますomitます+ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object that is liked in the pattern すき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: なら connects a condition based on the listener's preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase indicates the planned time to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: いっしょに adds the manner of doing the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb changes to the ましょう form to make an invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.cn: N・Aな + なら; Vますomitます + ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.why: The condition about preference comes before the invitation. こんど states the time, いっしょに states with whom or in what way, and ましょう expresses the invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: ましょうか turns an invitation into a question asking for an opinion or offering help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: たいです expresses only the speaker's wish and does not directly invite the listener to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q22.kobun.tip: With the adjective な, such as すき, use すきなら, not すきいなら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.vi: Please do not make noise in a loud voice late at night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the time when one should not make noise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the manner or means of carrying out the action 騒ぐ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: 騒がないでください uses the negative form ない+でください to ask someone not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.why: に sets the time context, while で describes the manner of making noise. The verb 騒ぐ changes to the ない form and connects with でください to make a request not to do that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Vなくてもいい means “it is okay not to do,” so it only allows a choice and does not directly ask someone not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.tip: 騒ぐ is a group 1 verb, so ぐ changes to が when forming the ない form: 騒がない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q23.kobun.cn: Vない形 + でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.vi: I think the meeting starts at one o'clock tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.sk: Nは + Adv + Timeから + Nだと + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes tomorrow the topic concerning the meeting schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: たしか modifies the whole statement and shows that the speaker remembers it but is not completely certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the meeting's starting time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: だと marks the reported content of the judgment after the noun かいぎ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: おもいます is the main predicate and expresses the speaker's thought or guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.why: あしたは sets the time range, and １時から identifies the starting time. The content かいぎだ is quoted with と before おもいます, turning it into the speaker's judgment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: でしょう also expresses a guess, but it usually seeks agreement from the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: かもしれません expresses a stronger possibility of uncertainty than たしかと思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.tip: Before とおもいます, nouns and adjectives な must keep だ, rather than becoming Nとおもいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + と思います
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.vi: Tomorrow is not convenient for me, but the day after tomorrow works.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks tomorrow as the time topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the state being described as inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: んですが connects the inconvenient situation with contrasting information in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.ch.3.vi: if it is the day after tomorrow
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: なら presents the day after tomorrow as a condition or point of reference for judging convenience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.why: The sentence makes tomorrow the topic and then clearly states that it is inconvenient. The pattern んですが connects this to a contrasting condition, in which the day after tomorrow is presented as a more suitable time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing んですが with けれども emphasizes connecting two contrasting clauses and has less of a soft introductory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use は instead of が in つごうがわるい, which makes the subject of the state incorrect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q3.kobun.vi: I will report the news from Vietnam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting place of the news or reporting activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content being reported.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the predicate and forms the verb レポートする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q3.kobun.why: から is placed first to state the source or place from which the information is sent. ニュース goes with を because it is the content affected by レポートします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is talking about the news, without the tone of reporting or giving a report.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake から for marking the recipient, but in this sentence it marks the starting point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.vi: I am sad because my favorite pair of earrings has gone missing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing that was lost or disappeared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the result and follows the past form of なくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends a polite sentence with the adjective い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.why: だいすきな comes before イヤリング to describe the earrings. Clause なくなったので gives the reason, and the main clause then expresses the emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning is because I forgot, not because the item disappeared or was lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake なくなった for “forgot,” but this word describes an object that is no longer there or has been lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.vi: This is the fashion from the time when my mother was a high school student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the thing being presented or explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense clause comes before the noun and modifies 時代.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 時代 with ファッション and indicates the period belonging to it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: です is a polite noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.why: Clause こうこうせいだった comes before じだい to identify which period is meant. の connects the noun referring to the period with ファッション, while これは introduces the whole topic being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ころの, the meaning focuses more on the time when my mother was still a student, without emphasizing an era.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese places this clause before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q6.kobun.vi: Because I can walk again, I will leave the hospital tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: ようになる expresses gaining a new ability, while ので connects the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase indicates when the following action will take place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: します is the predicate of the noun-based verb たいいんする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q6.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason for gaining the ability to walk. ので connects the reason with the result, and then あした comes before the predicate to specify when the speaker will leave the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only states the reason that walking is possible and does not emphasize the process of gaining that ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out ように, but あるけるようになった is what expresses becoming able to walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.vi: Because my friend became ill, I went to visit them in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result and means “because..., so...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.ch.2.vi: to visit someone who is ill
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行く is in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first, followed by the result. お見舞いに 行く use に to indicate the purpose of going to visit the sick friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still means “because..., so...,” but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after お見舞い, but the pattern for indicating purpose is お見舞いに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.vi: Because I am starting to feel hungry, I will prepare dinner soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the hungry state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I am starting to feel hungry
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: すいてきた expresses the beginning of a hungry state, while から connects the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb します is the main predicate and describes the action of preparing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.why: The reason clause comes before から, followed by the action being performed. そろそろ modifies the time of preparation, while を marks dinner as the object of 準備します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the subject of hunger; here, おなかが uses が because the stomach is the subject of the state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q8.kobun.cn: Vて + くる; V普通形 + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.vi: While the washing machine is spinning, I will clean the room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the washing machine as the subject of the spinning action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The phrase あいだに indicates the period during which another action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the room as the object being cleaned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb そうじします is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.why: The clause describing an ongoing state comes before あいだに to set the time reference. The room-cleaning action comes after it and takes を because the room is the object of the cleaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 間は emphasizes the entire period, while あいだに emphasizes an action that happens during that period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse あいだに with あいだは; に is suitable when talking about an action that happens during a period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.tokens.3.m: may be a spelling error for いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t83-q9.kobun.cn: Vている + あいだに; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + あいだに
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.vi: I tried making the dish that had been introduced on television.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.sk: N で + past passive V + N を + Vて + みる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means or place where information is introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: This clause modifies りょうり, while されていた expresses the state of having been introduced in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the dish as the object of the making action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb つくる to the pattern みる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: みました comes after the て form to create the pattern meaning “try doing something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.why: テレビで states the source or means of the introduction. The clause しょうかいされていた comes before りょうり to modify the dish, and then つくってみました expresses trying to make it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しょうかいされている, the sentence refers to a dish that is being introduced now or currently, without emphasizing a past state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If つくってみせます is used, the meaning changes to definitely doing something to show or prove it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistakenly understand みる as “see,” but after Vて it means “try doing.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q1.kobun.cn: Vて + みる; V普通形 + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.vi: I bought green clothes that suited my mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person for whom the clothes are judged to be suitable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: あう comes before ふく to modify the clothes that suit my mother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects a color name with ふく to modify the clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the clothes as the item bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 買いました is the main predicate and describes a completed buying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.why: 母にあう and みどりの both come before ふく to state the clothes' features and color, respectively. ふくを is the direct object of 買いました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 母に似合う is used, the meaning is that the clothes look good or suit my mother in appearance, which is more natural when talking about clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If 母のためのふく is used, the sentence only says that the clothes are for my mother, not necessarily that they suit her.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse にあう with に似合う. にあう emphasizes suitability, while に似合う emphasizes appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q10.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + N; Nの + N; Nに合う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q11.kobun.vi: I decided to choose this wallet as a Mother's Day gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic that was decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the object that is chosen or decided on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q11.kobun.why: The topic is placed first with は, and then に marks the item chosen. きめました is the main predicate and expresses a completed decision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q11.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に in this pattern with に, which indicates a location; here, に indicates the object that was decided on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q12.kobun.vi: I received a poster of a star I really like.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: な connects the adjective な with the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects スター with ポスター, creating a relationship of ownership or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q12.kobun.why: だいすきな modifies スター, while スターの further modifies ポスター. ポスターを is the direct object of もらいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 好きな, the tone is softer and only means “like,” without emphasizing “really like.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q12.kobun.tip: The adjective な must have な when it comes directly before a noun, as in だいすきなスター.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.vi: If we leave now, we will probably make the 3 o'clock movie.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: なら presents a condition or hypothetical situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the time of 3 o'clock with the noun えいが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the event that must be reached in time in the pattern 間に合う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: でしょう comes after the plain form to express a mild guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.why: 今なら sets the condition first, while 3時のえいが indicates a specific movie showing. えいがに combines with 間に合う to indicate making it in time for an event, and でしょう gives the sentence a guessing tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with かもしれない, the level of certainty is lower, close to “it may be.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 間に合う; an event or time that someone makes in time usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（だ）・N（だ）+でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.vi: Planning fun activities is very enjoyable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あそび with よてい and indicates the content of the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb かんがえる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the clause かんがえる into a noun, while は makes that action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.why: よていをかんがえる is the clause about making a plan. Add の to nominalize the whole clause, then use は as the topic for the comment たのしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is replaced with が, the focus shifts to the action being enjoyable, instead of presenting the action as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.tip: のは does not mean “of”; here, の turns the entire preceding clause into “the act of ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q14.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形・Vた形+のは+Aい／Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.vi: Please catch the bear that came down from the mountain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle から marks the starting point of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: This clause modifies くま; てくる shows movement toward the speaker or the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the act of catching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: 捕まえてください uses the て form together with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.why: The clause 下りてきた comes before くま to identify which bear. を marks the bear as the object being caught, while てください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vてもらえますか, the sentence sounds gentler and asks whether the listener can help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ください; the correct request pattern is the て form ＋ ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.vi: Japan's service industry is being introduced overseas.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with サービスさんぎょう to modify the industry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the introduction takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: されています is the passive form combined with ています, expressing a state of being introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.why: にほんの modifies the service industry. Because the service industry is the object being introduced, it becomes the subject with が and uses the passive form; がいこくで indicates the place where this happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with しょうかいしました, the subject has introduced the service industry, so the sentence is no longer passive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.tip: When the subject receives the effect of an action, learners may easily use the active form instead of Vられる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q16.kobun.cn: Nが＋場所で＋V受身形＋ています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.vi: The apartment building's elevator is stopped because of an earthquake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that made the elevator stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects マンション with エレベーター to show a possessive relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the object that is in a stopped state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ています describes the current state resulting from the stopping action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.why: じしんで gives the cause, while マンションのエレベーターが is the subject affected. とまっています emphasizes that the elevator is still stopped now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with とまりました, it only says that the elevator stopped and does not emphasize its current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q17.kobun.tip: Vている here does not describe an action in progress, but the remaining state after the elevator stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.vi: When you wear that outfit, you look about five years younger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the act of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb + と shows a natural result that occurs when the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: くらい indicates the perceived degree of change in age.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the く form to modify 見えます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 見えます describes the appearance as it is perceived; よ emphasizes the information being conveyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.why: After the object を comes the action きる, followed by と, which connects the condition with the natural result みえます. わかく comes before 見えます to describe an appearance that is about five years younger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence becomes a more specific condition and no longer emphasizes a natural result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If ようです is used instead of 見えます, the sentence emphasizes a guess that the person looks younger rather than a direct impression of appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 見ます instead of 見えます, but 見える describes visible appearance, not the act of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.vi: Whatever she wears, she is as cute as a doll.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks what she wears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The form ても connects to the following clause with a concessive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective い changes to the くて form to connect with the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle の connects a noun with よう to create a comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: ようです expresses a comparison, meaning to look similar to or like something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.cn: Vて形＋も; Aい drops い＋くて; Nの・V普通形＋ようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.why: かのじょは is the topic, and なにを is the object of the act of wearing. きても creates the meaning “whatever she wears,” and then かわいくて connects the characteristic with the comparison にんぎょうのようです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with みたいです, the comparison has almost the same meaning but sounds more casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that なにをきても needs を to mark what is being worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.vi: I like rice more than bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person making the comparison or expressing the feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: より marks the object used as the comparison standard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: のほうが marks the side rated higher in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: すきです is the adjective predicate な, stating the speaker's preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.why: パンより is the comparison standard, while こめのほうが is the chosen side. This pattern places the preferred object before the adjective expressing preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a question asking which of two objects is preferred, rather than a statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with パンほどすきではありません, it means not liking bread to a certain degree, with a weaker meaning and a different structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily reverse the positions, but in 〜より〜のほうが, the object rated higher must go with のほうが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q2.kobun.cn: N1より ＋ N2のほうが ＋ Aなです; N1より ＋ N2のほうが ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.vi: Recently, I have gained a little weight, so I do not eat cake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Degree ＋ Vて形 ＋ くる ＋ ので ＋ N を ＋ Vません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん identifies the period when the change occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ちょっと slightly reduces the degree of weight gain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: てくる shows a gradual change up to the present, while ので connects the cause with the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the food affected by the action of eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 食べる in the polite negative form expresses the decision not to eat.
