default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.why: さいきん and ちょっと add the time and degree of the change ふとってきた. This phrase combines with ので to give the reason, followed by the action ケーキを食べません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is stated more directly and sounds more subjective and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 太っている is used, the sentence only describes the state of being fat, without emphasizing the process of becoming fat up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.tip: With ので, verbs and adjectives ending in い use the plain form; they are not connected with the polite form です・ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q20.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ くる; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.vi: Not only the body, but mental health is also very important; let us value both.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は presents the body as the first topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: はもちろん is used to say that the first topic is obvious, and then add the following topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の connects こころ with けんこう, forming the phrase “mental health.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も adds mental health to the scope being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう expresses an invitation or advice to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.cn: Nはもちろん、Nも; Aな＋にする; Vます omit ます＋ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.why: 体はもちろん presents the body as obvious, while こころのけんこうも adds mental health. The phrase たいせつにしましょう changes the evaluation “important” into a call to value it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If だけでなく〜も is used, it emphasizes “not only 〜 but also 〜,” and is more formal and direct than はもちろん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q21.kobun.tip: も should not be translated mechanically as only “also”; here, it adds another object to the same scope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.vi: Because I have lived alone for a long time, I can also clean and cook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.sk: Time ＋ State で ＋ Vているので ＋ Nも ＋ Nも ＋ できます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: ずっと emphasizes a period that continues without interruption.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the state or situation in which someone lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: している describes an ongoing state, while ので connects the reason with the ability in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: も marks another task that the speaker is able to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: も is placed in parallel with そうじも, meaning that the speaker can also cook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: できます is the predicate showing the ability to do the tasks mentioned earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.why: ずっと一人で生活している describes a long-lasting situation and gives the reason for the present ability. The two nouns そうじ and りょうり both take も to show that both tasks can be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If たり〜たりする is used, the sentence only lists things that are usually done, without emphasizing the ability to do them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.tip: できる usually goes with noun + が, but when listing objects to mean that both this task and that task can be done, も can also be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q22.kobun.cn: Vている ＋ ので; Nも ＋ Nも
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.vi: Because my current house is cramped, I want to move to a larger place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ Aい ＋ ので ＋ Aい ＋ N に ＋ Vます omit ます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: 今の modifies いえ, forming the phrase “the current house.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は presents the house as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the result; the adjective い stays unchanged before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ひろい modifies ところ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に marks the place to which someone moves.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: たい is attached to the connective form 用 of a verb to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋なので・N＋なので; Vます omit ます＋たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.why: 今のいえは presents the object being evaluated, while せまいので gives the reason. The destination for moving house uses ところに, and then ひっこしたいです expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason is more direct and subjective, while ので sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: ほしいです is used for wanting to have a thing or object, so it cannot directly replace the desire to move house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に in the wrong position; に comes after the destination, not after the person who wants to move.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.vi: To give the room a spring-like look, I changed the curtains to a light green color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The form らしく changes the noun はる into an adverb, modifying the whole action of changing the curtains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects へや with the noun カーテン, forming a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the item that is changed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective うすい modifies グリーン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle に indicates the result or new state after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb かえる is in the polite past form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.why: The phrase はるらしく comes at the beginning of the sentence to state the general manner or purpose of the action. The item being changed goes with を, while the new color goes with に to show the result of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence emphasizes being like spring rather than a spring style or atmosphere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を before the new color, but the result after かえる usually uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.vi: The train is quiet on Sunday morning, isn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase goes with は to state the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that has the state of being uncrowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 空く in the ています form describes the train’s current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ね is used to confirm or share an observation with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.why: The time phrase is placed at the beginning as the topic. Then が marks the train as the object with the state. 空いています describes the condition of being uncrowded, not just a temporary action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means being open or free, not a vehicle with few passengers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q25.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 空く・すく with 開く・あく; they have different readings and different meanings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q3.kobun.vi: My grandmother was hospitalized because she was ill.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the grandmother as the person who performed the action of being hospitalized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the cause that led to hospitalization.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 入院する is changed to the polite past form しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q3.kobun.why: The subject comes first with が, the cause comes next with で, and the main action comes at the end of the sentence. This order clearly shows the relationship between the cause and the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 病気なので expresses the cause with a complete and softer clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand で as indicating a place, but in this sentence で indicates the cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q4.kobun.vi: I am receiving a great deal of help from my landlord.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: には both introduces the topic or target and emphasizes the person receiving the help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the degree of the help received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: お世話になる is a fixed expression meaning to receive care or help from someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q4.kobun.why: The person receiving the help is marked by には, while お世話になっています forms the fixed predicate. とても comes before the predicate phrase to increase the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern says more directly that someone helps you, while お世話になる is more polite and has a broader meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say お世話をなっています, but the correct phrase is お世話になる, and を is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.vi: My younger sister is currently on a diet, so she does not eat sweets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces the younger sister as the topic of both clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: いま adds the time of the dieting state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 中で connects the current state to the following result or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks sweets as the object that is not eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べません is the polite negative form for the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.why: ダイエット中で presents the background state and then connects it to the action of not eating sweets. を clearly identifies what is affected by 食べません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ダイエット中だから is used, the cause-and-effect relationship is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ダイエット中なのに is used, the sentence expresses contrast or surprise, such as still eating sweets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 中で as a place, but in ダイエット中で it indicates an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q5.kobun.cn: N中だ → N中で; Vます → Vません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.vi: I was complimented on my beautiful handwriting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Aな だと ＋ past passive V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject that has the stated feature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content of the compliment; きれいだ is a noun-adjective clause ending in だ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 褒められました is the polite past passive form of 褒める, expressing that the speaker received the compliment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.why: The clause 字がきれいだ states what was praised, and と connects that content to the verb 褒められる. The passive form shows that the speaker received the compliment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning would be that someone said the handwriting was beautiful, focusing more on the comment than on the act of complimenting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を after the praised content, but this structure uses と to introduce the content of the compliment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.vi: My current job does not offer opportunities to use Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今 with しごと to modify the job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: は introduces the current job as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks Japanese as the object being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: つかう comes before きかい to modify the opportunity to use Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the opportunity as something that exists or does not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ありません is the negative predicate of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.why: 今の modifies しごと, while にほんごをつかう modifies きかい. Therefore, きかいがありません means that the opportunity does not exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 少ない is used, the sentence says that opportunities are few, rather than saying that there are none at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If は replaces が, the contrast or emphasis on the topic of opportunities becomes clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect つかう with しごと, but the phrase つかうきかい must be understood as “opportunity to use.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ V; Nの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.vi: Although it was a difficult exam, I was very surprised when I came first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: むずかしい directly modifies しけん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: のに connects to the following clause to show a result contrary to what the previous clause suggests.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: になって expresses the change to first place and uses て to connect to the emotional result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: びっくりしました is the main predicate and states the emotion caused by the unexpected result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.why: のに creates a contrast between the difficult exam and coming first. になって connects the state of achieving first place with the reaction びっくりしました using the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If のに is replaced with けれども, the sentence only expresses mild contrast and does not emphasize that the result goes against expectations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ので, the sentence expresses a cause-and-effect relationship, which does not fit the surprise caused by the unexpected result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand のに as “although,” but this pattern also emphasizes that the result is contrary to what would normally be expected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.vi: After graduating from high school, I will become a university student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the school as the object of graduating from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects the earlier action of graduating with the state of becoming a student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the result or new state after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: なります expresses the change into the state stated before に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.why: そつぎょうして places the action first, followed by Nに + なります to express the result of changing into a university student. The particle に indicates the destination of the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 大学生にします is used, the subject actively decides or causes someone to become a student.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern naturally describes a change of state without emphasizing who causes it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を before なります, but a change of result always goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t84-q9.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ V; Nに ＋ なる; Aい → Aく ＋ なる; Aな ＋ に ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.vi: There are many interesting places in Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle には indicates a place and adds the limited-scope meaning “in Japan.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: おもしろい modifies ばしょ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the place where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies the number of places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is a predicate that shows the existence of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.why: にほんには defines the place range, while ばしょが is the existing subject. おもしろい comes before ばしょ to modify it, and たくさん shows that there are many.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If あります is replaced with います, the sentence is suitable only for people or animals, not places.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.tip: In existence sentences, Vietnamese speakers may easily use は for an existing object; the basic structure is placeに Nが あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q1.kobun.cn: Nに＋は; Aい＋N; Nが＋あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.vi: I have just come home and finished eating dinner a little while ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the destination of the returning action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 帰ってきて connects the returning action with the speaker’s current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: さっき modifies the action of eating and shows that it happened just recently.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks dinner as the object of the verb 食べた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: Vたところです describes an action that finished immediately before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.why: 帰ってきて connects the returning action to the next clause. さっき shows the time, while Vたところです emphasizes that eating has just finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 食べたところです is replaced with 食べたばかりです, the meaning is still “have just finished eating,” but the time period can be wider.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand ところ as a place, but in Vたところです, it is a pattern for an action that has just finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.vi: Before going out, did you close the window?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause Vる前に shows the time before which the following action must happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing that is closed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is in the polite past form and ends with か to form a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.why: The phrase 出かける前に sets a time before closing the window. The object comes before the verb, and を shows that the window is affected.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence asks about closing the window after going out, so the time order is reversed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used here, the sentence only refers to the time of going out and does not emphasize doing it before going out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 前に with a past-tense verb; before 前に, the dictionary form 出かける is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.vi: I go upstairs on the escalator while looking at the sales area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: に shows the means of transport or the object used to perform のる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: のって uses the て form to connect riding the escalator with going upstairs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the sales area as the object being viewed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 見ながら connects two actions that happen at the same time, with looking as the secondary action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: に shows the direction of 行きます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.why: のって connects using the escalator with the main action. 見ながら places looking before 行きます to show that the two actions happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If のって is replaced with のってから, the sentence emphasizes finishing the escalator ride before doing the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If 見ながら is replaced with 見つつ, the simultaneous meaning remains, but the expression is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for direction, but for a direction toward 上, に must be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.vi: Choose the correct answer from these four choices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.sk: この ＋ Quantity ＋ Nの中から ＋ Nを ＋ Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase 中から shows the range or source of the choice, meaning that one answer is selected from four choices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase is the object being chosen, and を marks the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The form ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.why: The phrase 中から limits the range of choices, and then the object comes before the verb えらぶ. The form ましょう turns the sentence into an instruction or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence directly asks the listener to choose an answer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used here, the sentence has a softer tone of invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit the particle から after 中; only 中から clearly shows selecting something from a range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.vi: For my family’s health, I am increasing the amount of vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects nouns and shows that the health being discussed is the family’s health.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: のために shows the purpose or reason for the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks vegetables as the object whose amount is increased.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: Aくする describes making the degree or quantity become greater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.cn: Nのために ＋ N ／ Aい omit い ＋ くする
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.why: The phrase のために states the purpose before the action. やさいを is the object, while 多くしています describes actively increasing the amount of vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the following phrase will be a noun used for that purpose, not an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used here, the sentence will say that vegetables are good for health, without emphasizing the purpose of eating more vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may translate 多くしています as simply meaning “many”; くしています emphasizes actively making the quantity increase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.vi: This snack is not a gift; it is for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes this snack the topic for contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ではなくて negates the noun before it and connects to additional information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun 用 shows the purpose of use and combines with です to form the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.why: は makes the snack the topic, then ではなくて denies the interpretation that it is a gift. 用です states the use or intended user of the snack.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence will emphasize the purpose or beneficiary, rather than directly meaning that it is intended for personal use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used here, the sentence will mean that it is intended or designed for a particular group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 用 as the noun 用事; in N用, 用 shows the purpose or intended user.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q16.kobun.cn: Nではなくて + N用だ／です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.vi: I made a cake, but unfortunately it failed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of making.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects the completed action of making the cake with the opposite result in the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: 失敗する combines with てしまう to express an unintended result or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.why: The object of the action comes before を, and the clause が then states a result opposite to what was intended. てしまいました emphasizes that the failure happened against the speaker's wishes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only states the failure and reduces the sense of regret or unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit て in てしまう, but the verb must first be changed to the て form before connecting it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q17.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう／しまいます／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.vi: I am interested in foreign films.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic of the sentence is the person who has the interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 外国 with えいが to modify it and show possession or type.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the object toward which the interest is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that exists in the pattern 興味がある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate and expresses that the interest exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.why: は identifies the person being discussed, の identifies the type of film, and に marks the object of the interest. 興味がある uses が to mark the interest that exists in the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the meaning is still interest, but the tone is more formal and suggests a longer-term concern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use を after the object in this pattern; you must say Nに興味があります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.vi: Please come at exactly 9 o'clock tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that tomorrow is the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: かならず modifies 来てください and emphasizes that the person must come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the specific time of the action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to make a polite request or ask someone for a favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.why: あしたは sets the time context, かならず emphasizes the requirement, and ９時に identifies the exact time to come. The pattern 来てください turns the statement into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If 来てください is replaced with 来なければなりません, the sentence changes from a request to the meaning that the person must come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily put に after かならず, but に must come after the time point ９時.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.vi: This cake is really soft, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: この must come before a noun to identify the cake being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は states ケーキ as the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the degree of the following adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: 柔らかい is an adjective ending in い. It acts as the predicate and can come directly before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: ね creates a tone of confirmation or agreement with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.why: The topic ケーキは is stated first, and then とても increases the degree of the adjective. 柔らかい keeps the adjective ending in い before ですね.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern means that something looks soft, based on an impression rather than a direct statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q2.kobun.tip: 柔らかい is an adjective ending in い, so it does not change into 柔らかくです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.vi: I was deeply moved when I heard the story of the dog that waited forever for its owner.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.sk: Time から + N を + V辞書形 + N の + N を + Vて + Adv + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: まで marks a time limit, while いつまでも expresses something continuing without end.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person being waited for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: A clause in the dictionary form comes before 犬 to modify the dog.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 犬 with 話 to show a story about or belonging to the dog.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the story as the object being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: 聞いて connects the action of hearing with the feeling that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.6.n: とても modifies 感動しました and increases the degree of being moved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.ch.7.n: 感動しました is the main predicate and states the speaker's feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.why: The clause まつ comes before 犬 to describe the dog, and then 話を聞いて states the direct cause of the feeling. The て form connects the two actions in the order of hearing and then feeling moved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, 待っている emphasizes the ongoing state of waiting instead of giving a general description with the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a modifying clause comes before the noun, so you must say まつ犬, not 犬まつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q20.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + N; Vて + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.vi: Excuse me, could you lend me some change?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: こまかい modifies お金 and creates the noun phrase “loose change.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks money as the object being lent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: かして is the て form of かす. It connects the verb “lend” with a pattern for asking someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてもらえませんか is used to make a polite request with a gentle tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.why: こまかい comes before お金 to create the noun phrase “loose change,” and then を marks the item being borrowed. かしてもらえませんか is a polite and gentle way to ask the listener to lend something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If かしてもらえませんか is replaced with 貸してくれませんか, the request is still polite but focuses more on the listener doing something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If 貸していただけませんか is used, the expression is more formal and respectful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say お金こまかい, but the adjective must come before the noun: こまかいお金.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q21.tokens.6.m: could you ask someone to do ...?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.vi: I asked Mr. Hayashi to do the work, but unfortunately he refused.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: たのみました is the predicate of the first clause, while が connects it to the opposite idea that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The passive form ことわられて shows that the speaker received the refusal; て connects with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました expresses that the event has been completed, often with a sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, while the work being requested goes with を. が connects two clauses with an opposite relationship, and then the passive form combines with てしまう to state an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If only 断られました is used, it only states that the person was refused and does not emphasize the regret expressed by しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers can easily use を after a person's name, but the person being asked a favor must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q22.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; V受身て + しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.vi: I hear that in this country, about 25% of people keep pets such as dogs and cats.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.sk: N では + quantity ぐらいの + N が + example などの + N を + Vている + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: では indicates the range or location being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: ぐらい shows an approximate level, while の connects the percentage to the noun 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that makes up about 25 percent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: や gives an incomplete list, and など adds the meaning “and so on”; together, they modify ペット.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the object being kept.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: ている describes the continuing state of keeping pets.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: そうです comes at the end of a sentence to pass on information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.why: では limits the location and the subject of the statistics. The percentage phrase comes before 人, while 犬やネコなどのペット clarifies the type of pets; そうです at the end of the sentence shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: そうな must come before a noun and means “seems,” so it cannot directly replace そうです at the end of this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.tip: Do not confuse そうです, which reports information, with そうです, which describes appearance; their positions before nouns and their meanings are different.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.vi: Choose the book you want to borrow at the library, then bring it to the reception desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the book is chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: たい attaches to the verb stem and modifies 本, creating the meaning “the book you want to borrow.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the book being chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action of choosing with the next action in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: に indicates the place where the book is brought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: もって is the て form of もつ and connects the action of bringing with 来てください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: てください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます + たい; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.why: The clause かりたい modifies 本, so it comes directly before 本. The two actions, えらんで and もって, use the て form to connect them in sequence, while に indicates the destination for bringing the book.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 選びます is used, the sentence becomes a statement or a direct command and no longer connects naturally to the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q24.kobun.tip: When modifying a noun, put the clause before the noun: かりたい本, not 本 before かりたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.vi: The mother is worried about the father who is working alone abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the father is working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the state or circumstances in which an action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause comes before 父 to modify it and identify which father is meant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object that 母 is worried about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes 母 the topic of the main sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: 心配する is a verb that expresses emotion; ています shows that the worried state is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.why: The clause 外国で一人ではたらいている comes before 父 to describe the father. 父を is the object of 心配する, while 母は is the person made the topic of the main sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used for 父, the meaning becomes “the father is worried,” changing the subject of the emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression emphasizes “being worried about the father’s situation” and is more complete and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q25.kobun.tip: In Japanese, the person who is worried uses は or が, while the person being worried about usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.vi: This bread is a little hard but very tasty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before パン to identify the bread being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks パン as the topic of the two following comments.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ちょっと reduces the degree of 固い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: が connects two clauses with opposite meanings; 固い is the predicate of the first clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the degree of おいしい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: おいしいです is the main predicate and gives a positive evaluation of the bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.why: The sentence states the first feature, then uses が to shift to an opposite feature. Both adjectives act as predicates for the same topic, パンは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing が with けれども still means “but,” but the tone is more complete and slightly more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q3.kobun.tip: が connects two clauses and must come after the first clause; でも cannot be placed immediately after 固い to connect them in this way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.vi: The top of the table is dirty, so please clean it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects テーブル with 上, creating a phrase meaning the top of the table.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the top as the place that is dirty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the request that follows; 汚い is an adjective ending in い, so it connects directly with ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: きれいに is the adverbial form of the adjective な and indicates the state that should be achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください makes a polite request; here, it means “please make it clean.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.why: The first clause states the condition and reason, then ので connects it to the request. きれいに indicates the result to be achieved, while してください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used instead of ので, the reason becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern changes a direct request into a softer, more polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.tip: きれい is an な adjective, so when it modifies a verb, it must change to きれいに, not きれいく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.vi: To me, he is an important and special person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks him as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: にとって indicates the standard or viewpoint used for making an evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な changes な to で to connect with the next quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: とくべつな modifies 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends a noun sentence and confirms the evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.why: かれは is the topic, while わたしにとって identifies the person who sets the evaluation standard. The two qualities are connected by たいせつで, and then とくべつな modifies 人です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If に対して is used, it usually refers to the object of an action or attitude. It is less natural than にとって when saying “to me” as a viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out な before a noun; とくべつな人 must be used because とくべつ is a な adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q5.kobun.cn: Nにとって; Aな+で; Aな+な+N; N+です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.vi: This sentence is complex and very difficult to understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.sk: N は + Aなで + とても + Vます removes ます + にくいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks this sentence as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: ふくざつで is the connecting form of the adjective な. It links the first comment to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies the degree of difficulty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: わかりにくい forms a word by joining the connective form 用 of わかる with にくい, and then です ends the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.cn: Aな+で; Vます removes ます+にくいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.why: この文は presents the subject of the comment, and ふくざつで connects the quality “complex” with the result “difficult to understand.” とても increases the degree, while わかりにくい expresses that understanding is difficult to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with わかりづらいです, the meaning is still “difficult to understand,” but the tone is more conversational and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily connect the adjective な with な; when connecting two clauses, で must be used, as in ふくざつで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.vi: Because I have never been to Okinawa, I definitely want to try going there once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: こと turns having gone into a noun, while が marks the subject of the negative experience pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ないので connects the reason to the following clause, meaning because I have never done it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ぜひ modifies the desire 行ってみたい and emphasizes the wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 行ってみたい combines the て form with みたい to express the desire to try doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.why: The phrase 行ったことがない expresses an experience that has never happened. Then ので gives the reason for the desire 行ってみたい. ぜひ comes before the desire pattern to emphasize the intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence still says that the person has never been there, but the tone is more polite and neutral.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse ことがない with a negative statement about a present action, but this pattern refers to an experience that has never happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.vi: On Sundays, I usually relax at home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets Sunday as the time reference and topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: たいてい modifies the following action and indicates a usual frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the resting action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ゆっくり modifies 休んでいます and indicates how the action is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 休んでいます uses the ている form to express an ongoing state or habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.why: The time reference is placed at the beginning with は, followed by the frequency and the place of the action. ゆっくり comes directly before the verb to describe how the person rests.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If そろそろ is used, the meaning changes to “it is almost time to do something,” so it no longer describes a regular habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q8.kobun.tip: で in いえで indicates the place where the action happens, not に, which indicates the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.vi: As for homework, after I get home, I try to do it right away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks homework as the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination of the action of returning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 帰ったら uses a past-tense verb together with たら to state a condition or time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: できるだけ modifies the action of doing it right away and indicates maximum effort.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: やっています uses the ている form to express an action that is usually done or is currently being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.why: 帰ったら places the time condition before the main action. できるだけ and すぐ add the level of effort and the time when the homework is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If できるだけ is replaced with なるべく, the meaning is still “try as much as possible,” but the tone is slightly softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 帰ったら is replaced with 帰ってから, the sentence emphasizes doing it only after returning home, rather than emphasizing a condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate たら only as “if,” but in this sentence it mainly indicates the time after returning home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t85-q9.tokens.4.n: verb in the たら form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q1.kobun.vi: The view from this room is wonderful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: からの modifies 景色 and shows where the view is seen from.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: は marks 景色 as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q1.kobun.why: The phrase このへやからの comes before 景色 to identify the source or viewing position. After the topic is stated with は, the adjective すばらしい gives a comment about the view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes the view that can be seen from the room, with a clear sense of visibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression only says that it is the room's view; it does not emphasize the viewpoint “from the room.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q1.kobun.tip: からの must be placed before the noun it modifies, not after 景色.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q10.kobun.vi: The laundry got wet because of the rain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause that made the laundry wet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object affected by the state of being wet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 濡れる is used in the て form with しまいました, expressing an unwanted or regrettable event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q10.kobun.why: The phrase showing the cause comes before the affected subject, followed by the state that happens to the laundry. The Vてしまう pattern emphasizes that the result is complete and has a regretful feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 濡れました, it only says that the laundry got wet, without emphasizing that the event was unwanted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate で as "by", but in this sentence で indicates the cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.vi: During the hike, I walked a lot in the mountains, so I became a little tired.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the context or activity in which the walking takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 山 with 中, forming the phrase “inside the mountain”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を indicates the route or space that the speaker passes through.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: たくさん modifies the action あるいて, showing that the person walked a lot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: て-form connects the walking action with the tired state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 少し modifies the following state and makes its degree less strong.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: This is the main predicate, describing the state after the walking activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.why: で sets the activity context, while を marks the space that is passed through. The two actions are connected by て, and the result or later state is given at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If あるいて、 is replaced with あるきながら, the sentence emphasizes that the two actions happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q11.kobun.tip: を does not always indicate an object; with movement verbs such as 歩く, it can indicate a place or route that is passed through.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.vi: If I practice every day, I will surely become better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 每日 modifies the practice action and shows its frequency.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: すれば is the conditional form of する, connecting the condition with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: きっと modifies the prediction and shows that the speaker believes the result will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The adverbial form of じょうず comes before なる to indicate the state after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: なる describes a change from the current state to a better state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: でしょう is placed at the end of the sentence to soften a judgment or prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first and states what needs to be done, while the following clause states the predicted result. きっと increases the level of certainty, while でしょう makes the prediction softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vと is used, the result has a more natural or inevitable feeling, so it is less suitable for predicting ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Vたら expresses a more specific condition and can also mean "after", while すれば is suitable for a general condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.tip: With the adjective な before なる, it must change to the adverbial form with に; do not use the original form じょうず.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q12.kobun.cn: Vば ＋ Aなに ＋ なる ＋ でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.vi: I want to attend tomorrow’s party.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nに ＋ Nする omit する ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: あしたの modifies パーティー and identifies the party as taking place tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the event that the speaker wants to attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 参加する changes into 参加したい to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.cn: Nする omit する ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.why: The phrase あしたのパーティー identifies the event, and に marks the object of the action of attending. たい is attached to the ます form of the verb to express desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 参加するつもりです, it means that the speaker plans to attend and has more certainty and a clearer plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q13.kobun.tip: With the verb する, remove する and add したい; do not say 参加するたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.vi: Before work, please cut your fingernails and come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects アルバイト with 前, while に indicates the time by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 手 with つめ, forming the phrase “the fingernails of the hand”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the fingernails as the object of the cutting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: て-form connects the cutting action with the following action of going or coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: てください is a polite request, while ね makes the tone softer and more familiar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence and states what must be done before going to work. The two actions, cutting the fingernails and coming, are connected by て in the order they are performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If きってからきてください is used, the sentence emphasizes more clearly that the cutting must be finished before coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If きらないでください is used, the meaning changes to “please do not cut them”, which is completely opposite to the current request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.tip: Vてください is a polite request, not an invitation to do something together like Vましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q14.kobun.cn: Nの前に／Vて＋ください／Vて＋くる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.vi: After watching Kunimoto, I looked up the names of the flowers blooming in the yard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being watched.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: て-form connects the watching action with the following action of looking something up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the flowers exist or are blooming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: さいている modifies 花 and describes the flowers blooming in the yard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 花 with 名前, forming the phrase “the names of the flowers”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the flower names as the object being looked up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: しらべました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.why: 見て、 connects the watching action with the looking-up action in sequence. The clause さいている comes before 花 to modify the flowers, while 名前を is the direct object of しらべました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見て is replaced with 見たあとで, the sentence emphasizes that the looking-up action happens after the watching has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If さいてある is used, the sentence describes a state deliberately arranged by someone, so it does not fit flowers blooming naturally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q15.kobun.tip: A clause before a noun must directly modify that noun; therefore, さいている is placed immediately before 花.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.vi: Her teeth became weak, so she cannot eat hard food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the grandmother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the part that is becoming weak.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective よわい changes to the form よわくなって to connect the cause or development to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: もの is modified by the adjective かたい, while が marks what cannot be eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べられません is the negative potential form, expressing that someone cannot eat something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.why: The sentence first states who is being discussed, then describes the change in the teeth, which leads to the result that hard food cannot be eaten. が marks the teeth and the object as the subjects of the two clauses, respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it means that the person does not eat or use the item, without emphasizing the inability to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 食べません instead of 食べられません, which removes the meaning of inability to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.vi: There is a mistake in the composition. Please correct it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the range or place where the mistake exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: あります describes the existence of a non-living thing or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the form く to modify the verb 直してください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください makes a request or asks the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.why: The first clause identifies where the mistake is, while the second clause requests that it be corrected. ただしく comes before 直してください to show how the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If ただしく is removed, it still means “please correct it,” but it does not clearly request that it be corrected properly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q17.kobun.tip: When changing the adjective い into an adverb, Vietnamese learners may easily keep the ending い instead of changing it to く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q18.kobun.vi: I look in the mirror and check my clothes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the mirror as the object being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of looking with the next action of checking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the clothes as the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q18.kobun.why: The two actions are arranged in order using the form て: first look in the mirror, then check the clothes. を is used for the objects of both 見る and チェックする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見ながら is used instead, it means looking and checking at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use に after the object with 見る; the object being looked at usually goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.vi: If I have the chance, I want to work abroad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the chance as the condition for something to occur.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: あったら is the たら form of ある, used to state a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows where the action of working takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: はたらきたい expresses the speaker’s wish, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first, followed by the wish to be carried out when the condition occurs. で shows the place of はたらく, while たい attaches to the form of the verb after removing ます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If なら is used, the sentence has a hypothetical meaning based on information or a topic already introduced.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If と is used, the sentence usually describes a natural or inevitable result rather than a personal wish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に with a workplace, but the place where an action occurs must use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q19.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aい・Aなだった・Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.vi: I thought it would become cold today, but in fact it was not that cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets today as the time reference for the prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content being thought; さむくなる is the く form of the adjective い before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: と思いました states a past thought, while が connects it to a result contrary to the prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: そんなに modifies an adjective and usually goes with a negative form to say that something does not reach that level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: さむくなかった is the negative past form of the adjective い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: です completes the polite expression at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.cn: Aい remove い ＋ くなる; V普通形 ＋ と思う; そんなに ＋ negative
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.why: と puts the predicted content inside the verb おもう. が connects the prediction to the opposite reality, while そんなに combines with the negative form to reduce the degree of “not that cold.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with あまり can also mean “not very cold,” but あまり focuses on a generally low degree, while そんなに usually compares it with a level that has been mentioned or imagined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: こんなに means “to this extent,” referring to a level closer to the speaker, so it does not fit the contrastive meaning “to that extent” in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget to change the adjective い into the く form before なる: さむくなる, not さむいなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.vi: I study every day, but my Japanese still does not improve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.sk: Time phrase ＋ Vていますが ＋ N が ＋ なかなか ＋ Aなに Vません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence to show how often the studying happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: the person studies, but the desired result has not been achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks Japanese as the object being evaluated for its level of improvement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: なかなか goes with a negative form to emphasize that the result is difficult to achieve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: になりません expresses a change into a good state, but here it is negated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.why: The sentence uses studying as the background, then uses が to shift to a result contrary to expectations. なかなか combines with the negative form to highlight very slow or unrealized progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If あまり〜ません is used, it means “not very good,” which is weaker and does not necessarily suggest that the person has tried for a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q20.kobun.tip: なかなか in this pattern must go with a negative form; it should not simply be translated as “quite” or “very.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.vi: Every year, when April comes, the cherry blossoms planted in the garden bloom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nになると ＋ Place に ＋ Vた ＋ Nの ＋ Nが ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The frequency phrase identifies when a repeated event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: になると shows that the event in the following part occurs whenever this time or condition comes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates where the trees were planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: うえた is a clause that modifies さくら, meaning that the cherry tree was planted in the garden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle の connects さくら with 花 and identifies the type of flower being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the flower as the subject of the blooming action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.why: になると creates a natural, repeated time-and-result relationship. The phrase うえたさくらの successively modifies 花: the cherry trees planted in the garden are the flowers that bloom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is used, the sentence only refers to the time of April and does not emphasize that the event regularly happens as soon as that time arrives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If たら is used, the condition is more flexible and may refer to only one occasion, without clearly expressing a repeated pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place に after さくら, but にわに is the phrase that indicates where the trees were planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q21.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい・N/なAだ ＋ と
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.vi: Because I had something I wanted to discuss, I asked which day was convenient for the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The verb form たい modifies こと and creates the meaning “something I want to discuss.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the matter that exists in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the result that follows and means “because.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 先生 with the noun that follows and expresses ownership or connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject being judged as convenient or inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: いい modifies 日 in the phrase 都合がいい日.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the day as the information being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb 聞く is in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.why: The clause あるので gives the reason first, followed by the information being asked about. The phrase 都合がいい日 uses a descriptive clause to modify 日, while を marks the day as the object of 聞きました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still expresses a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression also means a convenient day, but it uses のいい instead of the structure 都合がいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the wrong order and say 日都合がいい; the modifying clause must be placed directly before the noun 日.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋なので / N＋なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.vi: Because I am not very good at singing, I feel embarrassed when I sing in front of everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the topic is the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object being judged as not skillful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I am not very good
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: じゃない negates the adjective な, while ので connects the reason to the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects みんな with 前 and creates the phrase “in front of everyone.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the place where the singing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: の turns うたう into a noun meaning “singing,” and は makes this action the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective 恥ずかしい serves as the predicate and expresses the speaker’s feelings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.why: The reason for not being good at singing is placed first with ので. の turns うたう into a noun so that the whole action of “singing in front of everyone” becomes the topic of 恥ずかしいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Changing は to が emphasizes singing as the object that causes embarrassment, instead of presenting it as a contrasting topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: The negative form changes the meaning to “do not feel embarrassed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget の when they want to turn a verb into a noun before は or が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋なので / N＋なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.vi: When buying a 900-yen book, if you pay 1,000 yen, the change is 100 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.sk: Nの Nを ＋ V辞書形とき ＋ Amount of money ＋ V辞書形と ＋ Nは ＋ Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the price with 本 and creates the noun phrase “a 900-yen book.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the book as the thing being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: 買う modifies とき and creates a phrase indicating the time when the purchase is made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The money phrase indicates the amount of money paid, even though を is omitted in this expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: と connects the action of handing over money with the natural result, which is the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle は makes the change the topic explained at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: です connects the topic おつり with the value identified as 100 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.why: とき identifies the situation when buying the book, while と expresses the natural calculation result when 1,000 yen is handed over. は introduces the change, and then です states the corresponding amount.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If 買うとき replaces 買ったら, the meaning changes to “after buying” or “if one has bought it,” rather than simply “when buying.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If 出せば is used, the sentence has a hypothetical conditional tone and emphasizes the natural result less than 出すと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse とき with たら; とき indicates a time, while たら usually states a condition or a sequence after completion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q24.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい・N/なAだ ＋ とき; V辞書形・Aい・N/なAだ ＋ と
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.vi: This restroom is broken, so please use the restroom over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the action of using.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください makes a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.why: The topic comes first, followed by the reason with から. The object of the action uses を, while Vてください expresses a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので keeps the reason unchanged but makes the tone softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use を with the person performing the action; を here marks the object or place being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q25.tokens.5.m: be doing; be in a state
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.vi: Please come and visit. I will show you around the neighborhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ぜひ emphasizes an invitation or the speaker's wish for the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に after the noun あそび indicates the purpose of 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 来てください uses the てください form to make a polite invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person who directly performs the guiding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the place or area being shown around.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: あんないします is the main predicate of the second sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.why: あそびに comes before 来てください to state the purpose of coming. In the next sentence, が identifies the guide, while を marks the place or area where the tour takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: あそびに来ます only describes “coming to visit” as a statement, not as a direct invitation like あそびに来てください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.tip: The purpose of going or coming usually uses noun + に, not を: あそびに来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q3.kobun.cn: N + に + 行く・来る; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.vi: I was very happy to receive a birthday present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the present was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the present that was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects receiving the present with the feeling that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 嬉しい changes to the polite past form to describe the feeling at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first, followed by the object received, and then the clause て connects the reason or situation with the feeling. もらう describes the speaker receiving something from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If the present form is used, the sentence describes current happiness or a general feeling, without focusing on happiness that happened in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for the present and を for the time, but here に indicates the time, while を indicates the object received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.vi: Because of the earthquake, the book that was on the bookshelf fell down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the reason that caused the book to fall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the book was.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: あった comes before 本 to modify the noun meaning the book that was on the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thing that fell by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: おちました is an intransitive verb, so the book is the subject with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.why: The phrase 本だなにあった comes before 本 to form a clause that modifies the noun. Because おちる is an intransitive verb, the falling object uses が, while で states the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: 本を落としました means that someone dropped the book, with を marking the affected object; the present sentence only says that the book fell by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q5.kobun.tip: Do not use を with おちる; the object that falls by itself is the subject and uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.vi: Inside the school is a no-smoking area. Since this is a rule, let us follow it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 学校 with 中, forming the phrase “inside the school”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the place being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and states the condition of the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the object being explained the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ですから connects the reason clause with the advice that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.why: The phrase 学校の中 states the place, and は makes that place the topic. The clause ルールですから gives the reason, followed by まもりましょう as suitable advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes the prohibition “must not do,” instead of stating a rule and then advising people to follow it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は instead of が in every position, but は here states the topic or place being explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + から／Aな・N + だ + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q7.kobun.vi: Today was warm. The temperature was 25 degrees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the time the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: あたたかい changes to あたたかかった to describe a past state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: でした is the polite past form of です, stating the temperature being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q7.kobun.why: 今日は makes the time the topic, followed by a sentence describing the weather. The next sentence adds the specific number for the temperature.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If でした is replaced with です, the sentence states the current temperature instead of a temperature identified in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q7.kobun.tip: An adjective ending in い must change い to かった in the past; do not add でした directly after the present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.vi: When writing a letter, write in careful handwriting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the letter as the object of the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: とき follows the dictionary form 書く to create a time clause; は makes that time the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ていねいな modifies 字 and uses the な form before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the means or method used for the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 書きましょう is the polite suggestion form of 書く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.why: The clause 書くときは places the situation “when writing a letter” before the instruction. で shows the method, while ましょう turns the writing action into a suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 書いたとき is used, the meaning is “when the writing is finished,” emphasizing that the previous action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書きながら is used, the meaning is “while writing...,” describing two actions happening at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.tip: Before とき, the verb usually takes the dictionary form when describing an action that has not happened yet or a regular action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形＋とき／Aい＋とき／Aな＋な＋とき／N＋の＋とき
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.vi: I will have my hair cut at a barbershop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the hair-cutting action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the hair as the object being cut.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: Vて + もらいます expresses that the speaker has someone do something for them or provide a service.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.why: で identifies the place providing the service, and を identifies the hair being affected. The structure きってもらいます emphasizes that the speaker receives the haircut service from a staff member.
