default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vてあげます is used, the subject is the person who does something for someone else, which is the opposite of the speaker receiving a service.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてくれます is used, the focus is on someone else doing the action for the speaker, not on the speaker actively asking for or receiving a service.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t86-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate もらいます as receiving an object, but in the pattern Vて形もらいます it means having someone do something for them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.vi: It has been snowing continuously since last night.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of a period.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: ずっと modifies an action that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the phenomenon that is occurring.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Vています expresses an action or phenomenon that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.why: The starting time comes before the adverb showing continuity. The subject of the phenomenon takes が and ends with the ています form to emphasize that the state continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If まで is used, it means that the snow falls until a certain point, not that it starts falling from that point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding 前から emphasizes that the period began a long time ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q1.kobun.tip: から indicates the starting point, while まで indicates the ending point; do not confuse these two particles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.vi: My country is trading with Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし to 国 and shows possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 国 the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: と indicates the partner carrying out the trading activity together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content of the activity in 貿易をしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: しています describes a trading activity that is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.why: わたしの modifies 国 to identify which country. と states the partner, while 貿易をしています is the verb phrase describing the trading activity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q10.kobun.tip: と in this sentence indicates a partner in the activity, not と, which connects two nouns to mean “and.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.vi: Mr. Kim is listening carefully to the teacher's words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person carrying out the listening action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 先生 to 話 and shows whose words they are.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: まじめに modifies 聞いています and shows how the person listens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞いています uses the ている form to express an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.why: 先生の話 forms a noun phrase meaning “the teacher's words,” and then を marks this phrase as the object being heard. The adverb まじめに comes before the verb to describe how the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with よく, the sentence emphasizes how well or how often the person listens, rather than the serious attitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q11.kobun.tip: The adjective な must change to the に form when modifying a verb, but the adjective い usually changes い to く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I went to the hospital to get a haircut.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.sk: 時点 ＋ N を ＋ Vます removes ます ＋ に ＋ N へ ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence to show when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks hair as the object of the cutting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The linking form ます removes ます from きります and combines with に to show purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction of movement toward the place mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く and matches きのう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.cn: Vます removes ます ＋ に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.why: きりに states the purpose of traveling and comes before the place and the verb 行きました. へ marks the direction toward a place, while the past form matches the time reference “yesterday.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ために, the sentence still shows purpose, but the tone is more formal and its use is broader.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q12.kobun.tip: Do not use the basic form きりますに; remove ます first, then connect に to create the purpose pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q13.kobun.vi: Mr. Nakagawa is a quiet person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person being described in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: おとなしい comes before 人 to modify this noun directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: です ends a noun sentence and gives a polite statement about the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q13.kobun.why: は puts the person being described at the beginning of the sentence. おとなしい is an adjective before 人 that describes the type of person, and 人です makes it the noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with おとなしいです, the sentence only says that Mr. Nakagawa is quiet. It does not emphasize calling him “a quiet person.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q13.kobun.tip: The adjective い directly modifies the noun, with no な added between them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.vi: There is an interesting TV program on tonight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase shows when the program will be broadcast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: おもしろい comes before the noun phrase to describe the program.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects テレビ番組 to ほうそう and shows what is being broadcast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the broadcast as the subject that exists in sentence あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: あります expresses existence, while よ adds a tone of informing or emphasizing something to the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.why: おもしろい modifies テレビ番組, while テレビ番組のほうそう is the noun phrase serving as the subject of あります. よ at the end of the sentence shows that the speaker is informing the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 放送します, the sentence changes from “there is a program being broadcast” to “they will broadcast a program,” focusing on the person carrying out the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q14.kobun.tip: When あります is used to say that an event or program takes place, the noun naming the event usually goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q15.kobun.vi: I am sad because I cannot meet my friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q15.kobun.sk: N に + negative potential-form V なくて + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person being met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The negative potential form 会えない combines with なくて to connect the reason to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q15.kobun.why: The phrase 友だちに is the object used with 会う. 会えなくて connects the reason to the emotion さびしい at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If used in this sentence, the reason sounds clearer and more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use を with 会う; the person being met usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q16.kobun.vi: Thanks to that, I have gradually become used to my new job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase おかげさまで states a positive reason or expresses polite thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the object that the speaker is gradually adapting to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: なれてきました describes a state of becoming used to something that has developed up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q16.kobun.why: おかげさまで begins with a positive reason. The object of adaptation goes with に, while てくる emphasizes gradual change up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only says that the speaker has become used to it, without emphasizing the gradual process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q16.kobun.tip: Distinguish に in 新しいしごとに from で; に only marks the object of なれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.vi: The family next door is arguing very loudly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: となりの modifies かぞく, meaning the family next door.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the manner or means of the arguing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: ています describes an action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.why: となりの comes before a noun to identify which family. 大きなこえで describes how they are arguing, while しています shows that the event is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence describes an event that happened and ended in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q17.kobun.tip: Do not confuse で, which shows the manner in 大きなこえで, with が, which marks the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.vi: I have a habit of waking up at 6 o’clock every morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.sk: N は + time に + V辞書形 + N が + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: まいあさ indicates the repeated time of the habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the time of waking up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: A dictionary-form verb comes before a noun to modify the habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks what the speaker has.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.why: おきる directly modifies しゅうかん, so it is placed before the noun. The time phrase goes with に, and the whole phrase then becomes the subject of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only states a regular action and does not emphasize that it is a habit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q18.kobun.tip: A modifying clause comes before the noun and does not add の after the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.vi: Everyone discussed it together and then gave flowers to the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the people who take part in the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects discussing with giving a present in sequence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the person receiving the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the item being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.why: そうだんして is placed first to show the preparatory action. With プレゼントする, the receiver goes with に and the present goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sequence after discussing is emphasized more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q19.kobun.tip: Remember to distinguish に, the receiver, from を, the item being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.vi: If you think you are at fault, you should apologize immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject judged to be at fault.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.ch.1.vi: to be bad; to be at fault
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content of the thought that follows the adjective わるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: たら connects a hypothetical condition to the advice in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: すぐに modifies 謝ったほうがいい and indicates when to apologize.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: Vたほうがいいです uses the past form to give advice about what should be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.why: わるいとおもったら creates a condition based on the speaker’s thoughts. After the condition, Vたほうがいいです gives specific advice, with the timing added by すぐに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Vるべきだ expresses a stronger duty or recommendation than the softer advice of ほうがいい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern advises against doing the action, which is the opposite of the advice to apologize in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use the dictionary form before ほうがいい; for advice about what should be done, Vたほうがいいです is usually used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.tokens.8.m: way; thing that should be done
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q2.kobun.cn: Vた形＋ほうがいいです; Vた形＋ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.vi: What will you give to celebrate your friend’s wedding?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の shows possession or a connection to the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: けっこんの modifies おいわい and identifies the type of present or celebration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the purpose of giving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the present being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: あげますか creates a polite question about the act of giving.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.why: The two phrases の identify, respectively, which friend and which congratulatory occasion. おいわいに states the purpose, while 何を is the gift and comes before あげますか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: When replaced, the purpose of the congratulations is expressed more clearly and formally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q20.kobun.tip: Do not translate に in おいわいに as a place; here, に only indicates purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q21.kobun.vi: Who will you invite to the wedding?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place or event toward which the inviting action is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person as the object of the inviting action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb しょうたいします forms the predicate; か turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q21.kobun.why: The event phrase comes first, followed by the invited person with を, and then the main verb. か at the end asks about a plan or action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this pattern, the meaning would be introducing someone, not inviting them to attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse を with に; the invited person goes with を, while the event or destination goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.vi: The child was very happy because they received their favorite snack.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the child as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: すきな modifies おかし, while を marks the snack that was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the action of receiving with the happy state in the next clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: よろこんでいました expresses a happy state that continued in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.why: The topic comes first, the received item goes with を, and then もらって connects to the emotional state. The form ていました emphasizes that the happy state continued at that past time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is used, the sentence leans toward a condition or an inevitable result, so it is less natural for connecting two successive events.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.tip: もらって should not be translated as two equal actions; here, it provides the background for the happy state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q22.kobun.cn: Vて + いる（過去: Vていました）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.vi: I want to score 80 points or more on the next test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies テスト, forming the phrase “the next test.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the context or place where the score is achieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: This phrase is the score that the speaker hopes to achieve.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: とりたい is the たい form of とる and expresses the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.why: The test context comes before the score goal, followed by とりたい to express the desire. 以上 comes after the number to set a minimum threshold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with まで, the meaning would be up to a maximum of 80 points, which is opposite to wanting at least 80 points.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ごろ, the meaning would be around 80 points, without specifying a minimum.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q23.kobun.tip: 以上 means “from that level upward,” not simply “more than” a number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.vi: Because the school is far away, I try to leave home as early as possible every morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that has the characteristic of being far away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause clause with the result; とおい keeps the adjective い before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase comes before the action to show a regular time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: なるべく modifies はやく and shows the greatest effort possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: はやく is the adverbial form and modifies the action of leaving home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the place of departure in the use of 出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: 出ます is the main predicate and describes leaving home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first with ので, followed by the time, degree, and manner of the action. 出る combines with を to indicate that the starting point is home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If なるべく is replaced with できるだけ, the meaning is almost unchanged, but the emphasis on what can be done becomes clearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 早く as an independent adjective; before a verb, the adjective い must change into the adverbial form く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい + ので/Aな・N + なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the initial number to which another number is added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the number being added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary form 足す combines with と to state the result that occurs when the addition is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the result or state reached after the calculation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: なります is the main predicate and describes the result of the calculation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.why: The initial number goes with に, the added number goes with を, and then 足すと creates the condition for stating the result. The result 100 goes with に because なります expresses a change into a value.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If たら is used, the sentence has a hypothetical or “after adding” meaning and is less like a general rule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If ば is used, the sentence emphasizes the condition needed to obtain the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q25.kobun.tip: With なります, the result usually goes with に; を is not used to mark the value after a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.vi: Because the taste is a little weak, please add a little more salt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object described as having a weak taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result and has a gentle explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: もう少し modifies the action 入れて and indicates the amount to add.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks salt as the thing being added.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: 入れてください uses the form て + ください to make a polite suggestion or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.why: The clause 薄いので gives the reason first, and then states the action that should be taken. Salt is the direct object of 入れる, so it goes with を, while てください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives the reason, but the expression becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If しょっぱい is used, the meaning changes to salty, which is opposite to the state of being weak in taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse ので and のでください; ので only connects the reason, while a request must use the separate pattern てください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.vi: Since there are 20 people in this class, please divide them into four groups of five and then play a game.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this class the topic of the information that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the information about the number of people with the suggestion to form groups.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ずつ shows equal division by unit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ４つの modifies グループ and shows the number of groups.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: になって connects the state of becoming groups with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the game as the object of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: しましょう is a polite volitional form used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.why: Information about the class size provides the basis for dividing the groups. ５人ずつ shows that each unit has five people, while になって describes becoming groups before carrying out the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: ごとに emphasizes each separate group or interval and is less natural than ずつ when talking about dividing people equally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: なってから emphasizes playing after the groups have been formed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ずつ as “each,” but in this sentence it should be understood as dividing people equally among the groups.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q4.kobun.cn: N・Aい・Aな・V普通形 + ですから／から; 数量 + ずつ; Nに+なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.vi: You may use the pens here, but after using them, please put them back here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the pens exist.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ある modifies ペン and identifies the pens as being here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the pens as the objects being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: てもいい expresses permission, while が connects to a contrasting idea or the next condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: Vた+後で indicates the time after an action; は makes that time the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates where the object should be returned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: 戻してください uses the form て+ください to politely ask someone to put something back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.why: The first clause allows the use of the pens identified by the clause ここにある. Then, つかった後は sets the time point, and 戻してください states what should be done after using them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaces the first expression, the meaning becomes that using them is not allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: 使ったら戻してください emphasizes the condition “if you use them, put them back,” rather than simply saying after using them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may omit は in 後は, but は emphasizes the time “after using them” as the topic of the reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q5.kobun.cn: Vて+もいい; Vた+後で／後は; Vて+ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q6.kobun.vi: I am planning a family trip during the winter vacation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the time when the action is planned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being planned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: しています describes the planning process as currently underway.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q6.kobun.why: The time is placed at the beginning of the sentence with に. The planned content goes with を, followed by the verb 計画する in the しています form to show that the plan is being prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予定です is used, the focus is on an existing schedule or plan, without emphasizing the planning process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q6.kobun.tip: With 計画する, the planned content usually goes with を, not が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.vi: I am interested in Japanese movies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 日本 with えいが and indicates a movie that belongs to or is related to Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the object of the interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: あります combines with 興味があります to express having concern or interest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.why: The topic is the speaker, the object of interest goes with に, and 興味がある is the fixed expression for “be interested.” 日本のえいが creates the noun phrase “Japanese movies.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 関心があります also means being concerned, but it is more formal and suggests deeper concern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 好きです directly says that the speaker likes Japanese movies, rather than simply saying they are interested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 興味, but the correct pattern is 興味がある+Nに.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner with 趣味 and creates the meaning “my hobby.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the hobby the topic for explaining the information that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks novels as the object of the action of reading.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: V辞書形+こと nominalizes an action, while です is used to define what the hobby is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.why: The hobby is presented as the topic, and the action of reading is nominalized with こと to form the explanation. Novels are the object of 読む, so they go with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: のです has an explanatory or emphatic nuance and does not simply define the hobby.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 読んでいます means “am reading” and does not express that “the hobby is reading.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget こと when turning the verb 読む into a noun before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形 + こと; Nは+Nです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.vi: I am working part-time at a nearby shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects ちかく with 店 and creates a phrase that modifies 店.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the part-time work takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of しています in the phrase アルバイトをしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: しています describes an activity currently being carried out or the speaker's current job.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.why: は sets the topic at the beginning of the sentence, then の modifies the place. で shows where the action takes place, while を connects with しています to say that the person is doing that work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t87-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show the place where the action takes place; use で in this case.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.vi: I listened to a lecture by a famous teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうめいな modifies 先生 and uses な because it is an な adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 先生 with 講義 and shows that it is the teacher's lecture.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the lecture as the object being listened to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 聞きました is the main predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.why: The modifying phrases come before the head noun 講義: ゆうめいな modifies 先生, while 先生の modifies 講義. The verb 聞きました comes after the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use this sentence, the teacher is the person who gives the lecture, not the person who listens to it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q1.kobun.tip: When there are several modifying phrases, identify the head noun first; here, 講義 is the object that goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.vi: The bread sold at this store is very soft.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows where the bread is being sold in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause うっている comes before パン to modify it and show which bread is meant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes パン the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies 柔らかい and shows the degree of softness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: 柔らかいです is the い adjective predicate that describes the bread's quality.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.why: The clause うっている comes directly before パン to limit which bread is being discussed. After stating the topic with は, とても modifies the adjective that describes the soft state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 売る, the sentence focuses on the store selling bread in the future or as a usual activity, rather than on the state of selling it now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with ある, the sentence says that bread is present at this store, but not necessarily that it is being sold there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q10.kobun.tip: Learners may put the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always puts うっている before パン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.vi: No matter how much I scold him, my son still does not eat vegetables.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら shows the repeated degree of the scolding action in a concessive pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: しかっても is a concessive condition clause that connects to the unchanged result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes むすこ the topic of the stated result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks やさい as the food being eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 食べません is the polite negative predicate, showing that the result is still not eating.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.why: いくらしかっても creates the concessive clause and comes before the main result. むすこは states the person being discussed, and やさいを is the object of 食べません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that the result does not change, no matter how much the scolding increases.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace it with と, the sentence can mean that the result happens whenever someone scolds him, so it no longer has the meaning of “even though...still.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.tip: Learners may translate ても as “if,” but in いくら〜ても it means “no matter how much...still.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q11.kobun.cn: Vて形＋も・Aい＋くても・Aな＋でも・N＋でも
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.vi: Because I am full, I cannot eat everything.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks おなか as the subject that is in a full state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: なので connects the reason to the result and sounds softer and more explanatory than だから.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぶ modifies the action 食べる and refers to all of the food.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: の changes 食べる into a noun meaning the act of eating, while は makes that act the topic being judged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: 無理です is a predicate that judges eating everything to be too difficult or impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with なので. Then のは nominalizes the action of eating everything and makes it the object of evaluation. 無理です acts as the predicate concluding that the action cannot be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If you replace なので with から, the reason is stated more directly and sounds more conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If you replace 無理です with 食べられません, the sentence focuses on being unable to eat, possibly because of ability or circumstances.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.tip: Learners may leave out の in 食べるのは, but の is necessary to turn the verb into “the act of eating” before making it the topic with は.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい＋ので・Aな/N＋なので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this milk the topic of the taste perception.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: へんな modifies あじ and describes the kind of taste being perceived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks あじ as the sensation recognized through します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: します combines with a word for a sense to express that something has a certain smell or taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.why: このぎゆうにゅうは states the thing being perceived, while へんな comes before あじ to modify the taste. The pattern Nがします is used to describe a smell or taste perceived from the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use あります, the sentence only says that something has a taste or a taste quality. It is less natural than します when describing a taste sensation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If you use になります, the sentence says that the taste becomes strange, focusing on a change rather than only on the current perception.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q13.kobun.tip: Learners may use あります for every meaning of “have,” but smells and tastes usually go with します in Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.vi: Dinner is ready, so let's eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks dinner preparation as the subject of the completed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason to the result or suggestion in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう attaches to the polite form of a verb to express an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.cn: Vます形＋ました＋から; Vます形 omit ます＋ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.why: The phrase meaning dinner preparation is the subject of できました. The clause with から gives the reason, and then ましょう gives an invitation to eat together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので makes the reason sound softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q14.kobun.tip: Learners may use から as a separate word, but it must be attached directly to the correctly formed reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.vi: Let's make a reservation at the restaurant we will go to tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb 行く comes before the noun to modify the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects レストラン with the following noun and creates a relationship between the restaurant and the reservation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks 予約 as the object of the verb します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: しましょう expresses a suggestion to make a reservation together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.why: あした行く modifies レストラン, so the verb stays in dictionary form and comes before the noun. 予約をします forms a verb phrase with 予約 as its object, and then ましょう turns the statement into an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This phrase refers to the restaurant we will go to tomorrow, not to going to a restaurant that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is an invitation to go to the restaurant. It does not express making a reservation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.tip: Do not change the verb that modifies a noun into the polite form; use the dictionary form, such as 行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q15.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + N; Nの + N; Nを + します
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.vi: I want to drink coffee, so please boil some water for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks coffee as the object of the verb 飲みます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason for drinking coffee to the request to boil water in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks water as the object of the boiling action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows the form て to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.why: Coffee is the object being drunk, while water is the object being boiled. から gives the reason for the request, and てください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: ので also gives a reason, but it usually sounds gentler and more objective than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: ましょう is an invitation to do something together, not a request for the listener to do something for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; a request must use the form て.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q16.kobun.cn: Vます形 + から; Vて + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.vi: A: A hamburger and coffee, please. B: Yes, I understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: と connects the items ordered in the same request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: This noun continues the list of requested items.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: お願いします is used to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: かしこまりました is a polite reply confirming that the request has been received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.why: The items are listed with と and then followed by お願いします to make a polite order. The server replies with an honorific expression confirming that the request is understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use ください, it is still a polite request, but it is more direct than お願いします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: わかりました also means that you understand, but it is less respectful than かしこまりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q17.kobun.tip: と in this sentence connects the listed items. It is not と, which is used for quotations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.vi: I am looking for an apartment with rent of no more than 50,000 yen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks rent as the information described in the modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: 以下の sets the rent limit and modifies アパート.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the apartment as the object of the search.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects さがす with います to create the progressive tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: います after the form て shows that the action is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.why: The clause やちんが5万円以下の comes before アパート to identify the type of apartment being sought. を marks the apartment as the object, while ている shows that the search is in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: 未満 means that the amount has not reached that level, so 50,000 yen is not included.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: 以上 changes the limit to that amount or higher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.tip: 以下 includes the exact limit, so 50,000 yen still meets the condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q18.kobun.cn: N以下の + N; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.vi: The window broke, so I asked someone to repair it for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the window as the subject experiencing the broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause; てしまった shows that the breaking was completed and often adds a sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て of なおす connects the verb for repairing with もらいました to express receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: Vて + もらいました shows that the speaker received help from someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.why: The window is the subject of the broken state, not the person who actively broke it. ので gives the cause, and then the structure Vて + もらう expresses that the speaker asked someone else to repair it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: から gives a more direct and slightly stronger reason than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: 直しました means repairing it oneself. It does not show that someone else was asked to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.tip: Vて + もらう does not mean doing something oneself and then receiving it; it emphasizes that another person did it as help for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q19.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; V普通形 + ので; Vて + もらう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q2.kobun.vi: I overslept in the morning, so I arrived late for class.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て connects this action to the result that follows, creating a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the target of being late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q2.kobun.why: The first clause gives the cause, while ちこくしました is the result that happened afterward. に attaches to the thing for which someone is late, namely 授業.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but the explanation sounds clearer and gentler.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q2.kobun.tip: Do not understand して as meaning only “do and then”; in this sentence, it connects the cause to the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.vi: Today is my birthday, so I will decorate the table with flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that today is the topic and time reference of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause to the action in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the flowers are placed or displayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the flowers as the object being decorated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 飾ります is the main predicate and uses the polite present form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.why: The sentence first states the time, then gives the reason, and finally states the place, object, and action. ので connects the cause to the result naturally and more gently than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に, which indicates where an object is placed, with で, which indicates where an action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.vi: I hung a calendar on the classroom wall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the classroom with the wall and shows a possessive or belonging relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates where the calendar is hung.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the calendar as the object being hung.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: かけました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.why: The phrase の shows that the wall belongs to the classroom. Use に for the place where an object is received, and を before the verb for the object being acted on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used after かべ, that place is understood as where the hanging action happens, without stressing the exact hanging point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use で instead of に when you mean that an object is placed or hung in a certain position.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.vi: It is dark here at night, so it is very scary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this place the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: よる shows the time when the dark state occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the reason to the scary feeling in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: こわいです is an adjective predicate in the polite form い.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.why: The sentence makes the place the topic, adds a time, and then gives the reason before stating an evaluation. The adjective い comes before から without needing to add だ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds more objective and softer than with から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.tip: With the adjective い, do not add だ before から: say くらいから or くらいですから.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.vi: The train arrived at the station a little while ago.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.sk: N が + Time + N に + Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the train as the subject that completed arriving at the station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: さっき modifies the verb and shows when the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: に shows where the train arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: つきました is the predicate in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.why: The subject comes before が, the time comes before the verb phrase, and the station is the destination, so it takes に. This order makes clear where and when the train arrived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If へ is used, the sentence focuses more on the direction toward the station than on the exact destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q23.kobun.tip: When the verb つく refers to arriving at a place, it usually uses に, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.vi: There is an empty seat here. Would you like to sit down?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ここ with せき to modify the seat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the seat as the subject that is currently empty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: あいています describes the empty state, while から connects the reason to the invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.ch.3.vi: would you like to sit down
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ませんか creates a polite invitation or suggestion in question form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.why: The sentence first identifies the seat and then gives its empty state as the reason. The pattern ませんか turns sitting down into a polite invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ましょうか is used, the speaker actively suggests doing something together or helping to do it, rather than simply inviting the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If てもいいですか is used, the sentence becomes a request for permission to sit, not an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.tip: ませんか in this sentence does not simply express negation; it is usually used to invite or suggest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q24.kobun.cn: Vて + います; V普通形 + から; Vます-stem + ませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.vi: Tokyo is crowded. In addition, the trains are packed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Tokyo the topic of the first comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks people as what is being described in terms of number.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 多いです is the adjective predicate い, describing that there are many people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: それに adds information in the same direction as the previous sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the train as the subject whose crowded condition is being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: こんでいます describes the train as being crowded or packed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.why: The first sentence makes Tokyo the topic and describes the number of people. それに adds a similar comment, and the second sentence then uses が to state the subject and ています to describe an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If そして is used, the sentence only links events in order or adds neutral information. It does not stress the meaning of “in addition” as それに does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If でも is used, the next sentence will contrast with the fact that Tokyo has many people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q25.kobun.tip: それに adds an idea in the same direction; do not use it when the next idea contrasts with the previous one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q3.kobun.vi: I said “I’m leaving now” to my family and went outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the listener of the speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the directly quoted content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects the action of speaking with the following action of going outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q3.kobun.why: The listener comes before に, the spoken content is placed in quotation marks and takes と. 言って、 connects the speech with the action of going outside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If と伝えて is used, the nuance is more formal, meaning “convey” or “inform,” rather than simply speaking directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use に to mark the content of a sentence; quoted content must go with と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.vi: It was a real shame that I could not play soccer on a rainy day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the rainy day the topic and context of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that is said to be impossible to do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: できなくて is the negative form connected to 残念でした, giving the reason for the feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 残念 is the adjective な, so its polite past form is でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.why: は sets the context of “a rainy day,” while が marks playing soccer as impossible. The clause できなくて comes before 残念でした to explain the reason for the regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason “could not play” is stated more directly and clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q4.kobun.tip: With an adjective な such as 残念, do not say 残念い; the polite past form is 残念でした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.vi: I received change from the staff member, but it was 20 yen short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who provides or gives something in the structure もらう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing received by the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: が connects two contrasting clauses: the speaker received change, but the amount was still short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The quantity phrase is the subject of 足りませんでした and shows the amount of money that was missing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: 足りませんでした is the polite past negative form of 足りる, expressing that the amount of money was insufficient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.why: The structure もらう marks the person who gives as に and the thing received as を. が creates a contrast between having received change and the fact that the amount was still short.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If しかし is used, the contrast is stronger and it often begins a new clause or sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q6.kobun.tip: 足りない means “not enough,” so the missing amount usually comes before the verb without needing を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.vi: Please choose your favorite color from these.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: で limits the range used for choosing and comparing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies 好きな色 and shows the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な comes before the noun 色 to modify the chosen color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the color as the object of the action of choosing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてください is placed at the end of a sentence to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.why: この中で defines the range of choice, while いちばん shows the highest degree. すきな comes directly before いろ to form the noun phrase “favorite color”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with えらびましょう, the sentence becomes an invitation to choose together rather than a request for the listener to choose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q7.kobun.tip: 好き is an な adjective, so 好きな色 must be used, not 好きい色.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.vi: That shirt looks nice. It suits you very well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: その modifies シャツ and identifies the shirt being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: シャツ is the topic introduced first, and 、 marks the pause before the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: いいです is the predicate expressing an evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: ね is used to seek the listener’s agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies 似合っています and shows the degree of suitability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: 似合っています uses the form ている to describe the current state of suiting the wearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: よ emphasizes information that the speaker wants to tell the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.why: The first sentence introduces the shirt and gives an opinion, while the second uses とても to increase the degree and makes 似合っています the predicate. ね adds an agreement-seeking tone, while よ emphasizes the information being stated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence only says that the shirt will or usually does suit someone, without emphasizing the current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced here, the sentence only says that the shirt is beautiful, without saying whether it suits the wearer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 似合います as a verb meaning that an object suits another object only, but this pattern usually says that a person or appearance suits clothing, a hairstyle, or a color.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.vi: I put on a hat and tried looking in the mirror.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the hat as the item being worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects putting on the hat with the following action of looking or checking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the tool used to perform the action of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 見てみました combines 見る with てみる to express having tried looking, in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.why: ぼうしを is the object affected by かぶる, and then かぶって connects to the next action. かがみで indicates the means, while Vてみました expresses trying to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced here, the sentence only means that the person looked, without the meaning of trying to look.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t88-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand で as a location, but in this sentence かがみで indicates a tool: looking with a mirror.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.vi: Please carry this luggage to the next room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies the noun that follows and means “this”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the item being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the noun となり with the following noun for a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the destination of carrying the item.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb はこぶ changes to the て form to connect with ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.why: The item is marked by を, while the destination is marked by に. The verb in the て form combines with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with Vなさい, the sentence has a stronger and less gentle command-like tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for an object and を for a destination, but in this sentence を is the item being carried and に is the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.vi: When you take time off work, please contact the company.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks しごと as the object of 休む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 休む in the dictionary form comes before とき to indicate a time; は makes this situation the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the recipient of the contact.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 連絡してください uses the noun 連絡 combined with する, with する omitted, and then connects it with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.why: The phrase 休むときは places a time condition at the beginning of the sentence. 会社に identifies the place or recipient to contact, while してください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing 休む with 休んだ indicates the time after taking time off or after the break has finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing に with へ can indicate direction toward the company, but に is more natural when referring to the recipient of the contact.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ときは as a separate verb, but とき must come after the clause that modifies the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q10.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形 + とき; Vて形 + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.vi: Excuse me, may I sit here?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase opens the conversation and attracts attention before asking a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place of the sitting posture or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: すわっても is the て form + も, creating a permission-question pattern meaning “even if I sit.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: かまいませんか asks whether the previous action would cause a problem, meaning that it asks for permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.why: ここに identifies the place, and then すわってもかまいませんか creates a permission question. This pattern expresses permission politely and indirectly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is almost the same, but すわってもかまいませんか is slightly more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is usually an invitation or suggestion not to sit, rather than a permission question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.tip: Do not connect すわる directly to かまいません; change it to the て form, then add も.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q11.kobun.cn: Vて形 + も + かまいませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.vi: A: Shall we go shopping together on Saturday? B: I have something to do on Saturday, so it may be a little difficult…
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.sk: Time + いっしょに + Nに行きませんか; Nは + Nが + あるので + ちょっと……
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: どようび states the time of the invitation and is separated by a comma.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: いっしょに modifies the action of going shopping and shows that it is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the purpose of going in the pattern Nに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きませんか is a negative question form used to make an invitation or suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: は makes どようび the topic of B's reply.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks ようじ as the subject of the state ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: あるので connects the reason to the refusal at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: ちょっと, together with the ellipsis, creates an indirect refusal and lets the listener understand the rest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.why: A uses Nに行きませんか to invite B to go shopping. B sets the time as the topic, gives the reason that there is something to do, and uses ちょっと…… to refuse softly instead of directly saying no.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still gives a reason, but the explanation is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: 行きましょう is an invitation or decision to go together, not an inviting question like 行きませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ちょっと as meaning only “a little,” but in conversation it is often a polite way to refuse when used with an ellipsis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q12.kobun.cn: Nに + 行きませんか; V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.vi: The soccer match will start at 1 p.m.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.sk: Time noun から + N の + N が + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: から marks the starting point in time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects noun サッカー with noun 試合 to modify “match.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that will start.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.why: The time phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the noun phrase that acts as the subject. The verb はじまります describes an event that starts by itself, so が is used for 試合.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with まで, the meaning changes to “until 1 p.m.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse から, meaning “from,” with に, which only indicates when an event takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q14.kobun.vi: I do not know the rules of this game well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects このゲーム with ルール, creating the phrase “the rules of this game.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb 知りません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: よく modifies 知りません and shows the degree of knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q14.kobun.why: The possessive phrase comes before the object, while よく comes before the verb to show degree. ルールを is what is not known, so it takes the particle を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing よく with あまり～ません emphasizes “do not know much,” often suggesting that the person knows very little.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q14.kobun.tip: Do not place よく after the verb; this adverb usually comes before the verb it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.vi: Let's compete to see who can do it best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who does the activity best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies うまく and creates the meaning “best.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: うまく is the adverbial form of うまい and modifies できる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: か closes the indirect question clause and makes it the subject of the competition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.cn: Wh-question word + V plain form + か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.why: The clause だれが～できるか states what the competition is about. The main verb きょうそうしましょう then gives the invitation to compete together. うまく comes before できる to describe how the action is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Adding どうか asks “whether someone can do it,” so the focus is no longer on who does it best.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.kobun.tip: Do not use だれを when asking who performs the action; the person doing the action in this clause uses が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q15.tokens.4.m: can do; be able to do
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.vi: If we win this match, let's celebrate together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the situation or event in which the winning result is determined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects the assumed condition to the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the group of people who perform the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first and is separated by a comma. みんなで shows that the celebration is done together, while ましょう creates an invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If なら is used, the sentence has a tone based on information or an assumption stated earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: If と is used, the result is usually natural or automatic, so it does not fit an invitation to celebrate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change the verb to the past form before たら: 勝つ → 勝ったら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q16.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aかった形・Aな/Nだった + ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.vi: Because of the large earthquake, the bookcase fell over and I was injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: 大きな comes before a noun and directly modifies 地震.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the cause that made the bookcase fall over.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the falling event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the bookcase falling over with the result of being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the noun けが in the phrase けがをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: て connects けがをする with the auxiliary verb しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.ch.6.n: しまいました expresses a completed event with a feeling of regret or something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.why: で gives the cause. Then the subject and the main event are connected by て. The phrase けがをしてしまいました describes the unintended result of being injured.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the present form says that the regrettable event will happen or will be completed, instead of saying that it has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: Using ていました only describes a state or action continuing in the past; it does not emphasize regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q17.kobun.tip: Do not translate で as “by” in this sentence; after a noun naming an event, で indicates the cause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q18.kobun.vi: I planted many flowers in the garden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the flowers are planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: たくさん modifies 花 and indicates the number of flowers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the flowers as the objects being planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q18.kobun.why: The place comes before the object, followed by the main verb. With 植える, the thing being planted takes を, while the planting location takes に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, the sentence only emphasizes where the action takes place, not the fixed place where the plant is planted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q18.kobun.tip: With verbs such as 植える, mark the location with に; do not automatically use で for every action in a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.vi: This pond is deep, so please do not play around here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the pond as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason to the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the place where the playing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ないでください expresses a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.why: The sentence first describes the pond, then uses ので to explain the reason for the request. で identifies the place where people should not play.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and conversational than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.tip: English learners may easily use で as a general location marker, but here で indicates the place where the playing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.vi: If you leave the bag at the entrance, it will get in the way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the bag is placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing affected by おく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects a condition with the result that usually follows immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the state or result that something becomes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: なる expresses a change into the state じゃま; よ is used to remind or inform the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.why: 入口に is the place where the item is put, while かばんを is the item being put there. The clause おくと states a natural condition, and then じゃまになる expresses the result of becoming an obstruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence only states the condition “if you leave it there” and does not emphasize the result that usually happens automatically.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use を in じゃまになる; the state after なる usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Aい・N/Naだ ＋ と
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.vi: It has started to get a little cold, so let us turn on the heater.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: 少し modifies the degree of becoming cold.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.ch.1.vi: because it has started to get cold
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: てきた expresses the gradual appearance of a cold state, while ので connects the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being turned on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ましょう expresses an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.why: The first clause describes a change moving toward the present and gives the reason for the suggestion in the following clause. を connects the device noun with the verb meaning “turn on.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ていく is used, the change is viewed as continuing from the present into the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may easily translate てくる as “come,” but in this sentence it only indicates a change that began and has progressed toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q20.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くる; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.vi: If there is a word I do not know, I will look it up in the dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: The plain-form clause comes before and modifies ことば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the word or expression as something known or unknown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: たら turns あった into the hypothetical condition “if there is.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the tool or means used for looking something up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate, stating the action performed when the condition occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.why: わからないことば is a noun phrase in which the preceding clause modifies the noun. たら states the condition, while で indicates the means used for looking it up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is used, the sentence only indicates the time “when there is a word I do not know,” without emphasizing a condition as たら does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.tip: English learners may easily place で before the object to be looked up, but here で must go with the tool じしょ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q21.kobun.cn: Vた・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.vi: I accidentally forgot to submit my homework to the teacher.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who receives the submitted homework.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the homework as the object of submitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the phrase だす into a noun, and を marks it as the object that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects わすれる with しまう to create a pattern expressing an accidental action or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: しまいました shows that the action was completed and often carries a sense of regret or something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.why: 先生に and 宿題を indicate the recipient and the thing submitted, respectively. The phrase だすのを is nominalized to become the object of わすれる, and then てしまいました emphasizes that the event happened accidentally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with わすれました, the sentence only says that the person forgot, with a weaker sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.tip: English learners may easily omit の before を, but the dictionary-form verb must add の so that the whole action can be the object of わすれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q22.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形 ＋ の; Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.vi: The Chinese characters in the newspaper are difficult, so I can hardly read them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は ＋ Aいくて ＋ 副詞 ＋ negative potential-form V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun 新聞 with 漢字 to indicate the Chinese characters belonging to the newspaper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the Chinese characters in the newspaper as the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the adjective with the result in the following clause, creating a cause-and-effect or state-and-result relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ほとんど modifies 読めません and is often used with a negative form to mean “hardly.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: 読めません is the negative potential form, expressing the inability to read.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.cn: Aい ＋ くて; negative potential V: Vえます・Vえません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.why: 新聞のかんじ forms the noun phrase “the newspaper’s kanji,” which is made the topic with は. The adjective is connected with て to lead to the result of being unable to read, while ほとんど lowers the degree in a negative direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If あまり is used, the meaning is “cannot read much,” usually emphasizing that the amount is small.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 読めません as “do not read,” but it is the negative potential form: “cannot read.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.vi: In the future, I want to do work that is useful to people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nの ＋ V辞書形 ＋ Nが ＋ Vたいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: しょうらい indicates the time or period of the desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 人 with やくにたつ to indicate the people who benefit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb phrase in the dictionary form comes before and modifies しごと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks work as the object of desire in the pattern 仕事がしたい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: たい attaches to the verb stem to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.cn: Vます remove ます ＋ たいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.why: やくにたつ comes before しごと to modify “work.” In 仕事がしたい, が marks what the speaker wants, while たい expresses the desire to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing を with が is still natural in ordinary speech, but the focus shifts to the work as the object of する.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily separate 人の役に立つ into two unrelated ideas, but the whole phrase modifies 仕事.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.vi: It takes one hour to travel from home to the graduation ceremony hall.
