default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.sk: Nから ＋ Nまで ＋ Duration ＋ かかる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: まで indicates the endpoint of the route.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The duration phrase shows the time required.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: かかります expresses the time needed to travel from the starting point to the endpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.why: The sentence places the starting point first, the endpoint next, and then gives the duration and the verb かかります at the end. から and まで form a pair meaning “from … to …”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: へ indicates a direction toward something, but does not emphasize the endpoint of the route as まで does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: にかかる usually refers to the money or time needed for a specific task.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit まで or use に instead of から when they want to state the full route from one place to another.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.vi: Because this door is broken, please do not touch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ので connects the cause with a request; こわれている expresses a broken state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object toward which the touching action is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative form ないで combines with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: Vないでください is a polite way to request “please do not do V.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first and is connected with ので. The object of 触る uses に, while 触らないでください creates a prohibition or request not to touch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ください is omitted, the sentence still means “do not touch,” but becomes more direct and less polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern expresses a prohibition or rule more strongly than the request in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.tip: The verb 触る goes with に to indicate the object being touched; を is not used as a direct translation from Vietnamese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ ので; Vないで ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.vi: I received a travel souvenir from Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person giving the gift or the source from which the speaker receives it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun りょこう with おみやげ, showing the type or source of the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the gift that is received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: もらいました is the polite past form of もらう, expressing that the speaker received something from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.why: In the pattern もらう, the receiver is usually the omitted subject, the giver is marked with に, and the received item is marked with を. The phrase りょこうのおみやげ is formed with の to modify the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing に with から still indicates the source of the received item, but emphasizes “receive from” a person or place more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: あげる reverses the relationship, meaning that the speaker gives Tanaka a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q4.kobun.tip: The direction of giving and receiving must be identified before choosing もらう or あげる; もらう is viewed from the receiver’s perspective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.vi: Because of the snow, the train was delayed, so I arrived late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause of the train being delayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject of the first clause: the train was delayed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: 遅れる changes to the て form to connect a cause or sequence of events with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ちこくする changes to the て form to connect with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてしまいました expresses a completed action, often with a feeling of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.why: ゆきで states the cause, 電車が is the subject of the delay, and 遅れて connects it to the result ちこくしてしまいました. The て form links the actions, and しまいました emphasizes the unfortunate result that occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vていました is used instead, the sentence only describes a state or action in progress, without a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: The present or future form says that an action will be completed or will happen unintentionally, not that it has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate てしまう simply as “finish”; in this context, it also expresses something unintended and regrettable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.vi: I was singing when someone told me, “You are too noisy.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb うたう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: うたう changes to the て form to combine with いる and express an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ていたら creates the situation “while doing something,” leading to an event that happens afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content of quoted speech or a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: されました is the polite past passive form, showing that the speaker received the warning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.why: うたを is the object of the singing action, while うたっていたら creates the time point “while singing.” The warning is placed in quotation marks and connected with と, after which the passive verb shows that the speaker was warned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes an action that is in progress when another event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vたら is used, the meaning may shift to “after finishing singing” or “if one sings,” without clearly emphasizing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.vs.2.d: This pattern clearly states who gives the warning with に, while the current sentence focuses on the content of the warning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget と before the quoted content and may confuse the passive されました with the active 注意しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q6.kobun.cn: Vている + たら; 「～」と + 言う・思う・注意する; V受身
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.vi: Has the key that was lost yesterday been found yet?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This clause modifies かぎ and shows which key it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes かぎ the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: もう modifies the predicate and shows that finding it may already have happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: みつかりました is the polite past form of みつかる; か turns the whole sentence into a question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.why: The clause きのうなくした comes before かぎ to modify the noun. は states the topic, while もう comes before the predicate to ask whether the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing もう with まだ emphasizes that it still has not been found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a structurally equivalent shortened form, but it does not clearly state when きのう happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q7.kobun.tip: English speakers may place a modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese places きのうなくした before かぎ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.vi: At the stairs, I hit my head all over.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: すべて is an adverb that modifies what follows and is separated by a comma.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks あたま as the object affected by the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: うちました is the polite past form of the verb うつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.why: で states the place of the action, the adverb comes before the verb phrase to modify it, and を connects the object to the verb うちました. The comma keeps the pause boundary in the given sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with さわりました means touching the head, not hitting the head.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with とりました means that あたまを is understood as something taken or held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q8.kobun.tip: English speakers may use に for a place, but the place where an action happens usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.vi: This restaurant is very good, so please be sure to come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes このレストラン the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: ですから connects a reason to the advice or request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜひ modifies the suggestion and shows that the speaker wants the listener to do it for sure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 行って is the て form of 行く. It combines with ください to make a polite request; ね makes the tone softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.why: The clause おいしいですから gives the reason first, and then ぜひ emphasizes the advice. 行ってください is a request pattern that suits inviting the listener to the restaurant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still gives the reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing 行ってください with 行きましょう changes it into an invitation to go together, rather than a request for the listener to go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form 行くください; change the verb to the て form: 行ってください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t89-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(だ)・N(だ) + から; Vて形 + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the address should be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks 住所 as the object of the writing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いて is the て form used to connect a verb to ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください makes a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.why: ここに identifies the location of the action, and 住所を is what is written. The verb uses the て form before ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 書きます only says that someone will write or writes politely; it does not directly ask the listener to write.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: 書いてもいいです asks about or gives permission to write; it is not a request to write.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q6.kobun.tip: English speakers may use を for a place. In this pattern, the place of writing usually uses に, while the thing being written uses を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vi: A small light can be seen over there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the light can be seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 小さな comes before a noun to modify 光.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks 光 as the thing seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 見えます describes the state of the light entering the field of vision, without emphasizing the viewer's intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.why: あそこに sets the spatial context. 小さな modifies 光, while 光が makes it the subject of 見えます and describes something that naturally enters the field of vision.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: 光を見ます describes the speaker actively looking at the light.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: 光が見られます emphasizes the ability or conditions that make it possible to see the light.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q7.kobun.tip: English speakers may confuse 見えます with 見ます; 見えます means seeing something naturally, while 見ます means looking at it actively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vi: What will you do during the New Year's holiday?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 正月 with 休み, creating the noun phrase “New Year's holiday.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time or period when the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the activity to be done as the content of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: しますか creates a polite question about an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.why: 正月の休み creates a noun phrase connected with the New Year's holiday. 休みに states the time, while 何を is the unspecified object of します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: は makes the New Year's holiday the topic, giving the question a contrastive tone or emphasizing that holiday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 何か asks whether someone will do something, not what specific activity they will do.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q8.kobun.tip: English speakers may translate に as “to”; in this sentence, に indicates time and means “during the period.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vi: There are five people in my family.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.sk: N の + N は + people counter です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: の expresses the possessive relationship between わたし and 家族.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 家族 the speaker's topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: 五人 forms a quantity predicate with です to say that the family has five members.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.why: わたしの家族 is a noun phrase in which の shows possession. 家族は is the topic, while 五人です states the number of family members.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: が emphasizes that my family itself is the identified subject, but this expression is less natural when only stating the number of members.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: います is used to say that five people exist or are present, instead of using a noun as the predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t9-q9.kobun.tip: English speakers may use 五つ to count people, but Japanese uses the people counter 人, which is 五人 here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.vi: Excuse me, but please tell the teacher that I will be a little late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が connects a polite opening with the request that follows and does not necessarily express strong contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.ch.1.vi: that I will be a little late
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content of the message being conveyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person who receives the information being conveyed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: 伝えてください uses the て form together with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.why: The information to report comes before と, the recipient goes with に, and 伝えてください ends the sentence to express a request. This order makes clear what to report and to whom.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the request becomes more formal and humble.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence is still a request but more casual ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を with the recipient, but the person receiving the message must go with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.vi: I went to visit a friend who was in the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The clause before it modifies 友だち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the friend to the noun お見舞い, which refers to the person being visited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.ch.2.vi: go to visit a sick person
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main verb and describes a completed action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.why: The clause にゅういんしている comes directly before 友だち to identify which friend. お見舞いに行く is the phrase showing that the purpose of going was to visit a sick person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Nを見舞う uses the verb “visit N” directly, while お見舞いに行く emphasizes going somewhere to visit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: Nのために行く means going for N’s benefit and does not clearly state the purpose of visiting a sick person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use を after お見舞い when expressing the purpose of going; the natural pattern is お見舞いに行く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q10.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ N; Nの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the topic being commented on in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the object that has the characteristic うまい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: うまい is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate, and です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q12.kobun.why: The pattern Nは Nが Aい is used to describe a characteristic of a person or thing in a specific area. Here, は states the person being discussed, while が marks the area being evaluated as 歌.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means singing well, but is more polite and neutral うまい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes the ability to perform the action of singing, rather than making only a general comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use を after 歌, but with ability-related evaluative adjectives such as うまい, they need to use が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.vi: I was very embarrassed because the teacher scolded me in front of everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the scolding took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the person who performs the action in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects being scolded with the feeling that happened afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the adjective and shows the degree of the emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: はずかしい changes to the past form はずかしかった to express the feeling at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.cn: Vて: Vて形; Aいかった: remove い ＋ かったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.why: The place phrase comes first, followed by the person who performs the passive action with に. The clause しかられて connects the cause or situation with the feeling はずかしかった at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: It states the cause-and-effect relationship more clearly, equivalent to “because the teacher scolded me.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: It has a contrasting meaning: “although the teacher scolded me...”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for a place, but the place where the action occurs must use で; に here indicates the person who scolded someone in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to modify としょかん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the library is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: でも after a question word creates the inclusive meaning “everyone” and makes the person the possible user.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: できます expresses the ability to perform the action 利用.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.why: The topic としょかんは comes first, and then だれでも shows the range of possible users. できます comes at the end to express the ability or permission to use the library.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Only someone can use it; it does not mean everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes permission—“everyone is allowed to use it”—rather than ability.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.tip: Do not confuse だれでも with だれか; でも has an inclusive meaning, while か refers to one unspecified person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q14.kobun.cn: N＋でも; Nを利用する → Nが利用できます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.vi: After waiting for 30 minutes, I finally managed to get on the bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.sk: Duration ＋ Vて ＋ やっと ＋ Nに ＋ polite past potential V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The duration phrase comes before the verb to show how long the speaker waited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the action of waiting with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: やっと modifies the following clause and shows that the result was achieved after time or difficulty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the vehicle or object that the speaker gets on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: のれる is the potential form of のる, while ました expresses a result that has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.cn: Vて; potential V: Vる → Vえます; Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.why: The duration and the waiting action create the background, then やっと emphasizes the result achieved after waiting a long time. With のる, に marks the bus as the vehicle that was boarded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: It is close in meaning to やっと, but is usually more formal and emphasizes a result achieved after many difficulties.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: It means immediately, so it removes the feeling of having waited a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate のれました as “got on,” but the potential form のれる must be understood as “managed to get on.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.vi: Sweet cake goes very well with tea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective comes before ケーキ to modify the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: には combines with に to indicate the object that matches は, stating the object and creating a contrastive nuance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing judged to be suitable for the cake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: あう expresses a good match or harmonious combination between two objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.why: The object being considered is ケーキには, while おちゃが is the thing that matches it. The verb あう uses が for the suitable item and に for the object it suits.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes actively pairing tea with cake, rather than simply saying that the two go well together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: It focuses more on looking suitable than on taste or combination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q16.kobun.tip: With あう, do not use を for おちゃ; the suitable item goes with が, while the object it suits goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.vi: There is a party tomorrow, but I have something to do, so I cannot go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Nがありますが、＋ N は ＋ Nがありますから ＋ negative potential verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two clauses with a contrasting or shifting relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the speaker the topic of the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.ch.3.vi: because I have something to do
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: から comes after the clause to give the reason why the speaker cannot go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 行けません is the polite negative potential form, meaning that someone cannot go.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nだ ＋ から; negative potential V: Vえません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.why: The first clause states that there is a party, while が changes to the speaker’s contrasting situation. から connects the reason for being busy with the conclusion 行けません at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: It also shows a reason, but it is softer and more objective than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: It only contrasts having something to do with being unable to go. It does not clearly show a cause-and-effect relationship like から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place から after 行けません, but when the reason comes first, から must stand at the end of the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.kobun.vi: Before playing a game, we decided the rules.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the main action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing that was decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.kobun.why: The time expression するまえに comes before the main action. ルールを is the object of the verb at the end of the sentence, so it takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, it means deciding the game rules after playing the game.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.kobun.tip: Do not confuse に in まえに with を; に only indicates time, while を marks the object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q18.tokens.7.m: decided together (possibly a writing error for きめあってた)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.vi: After eating rice, I became sleepy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the food that was eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: Vたら connects a condition or time with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the form く to combine with なる and express a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: なる expresses a change to a new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.why: The clause 食べたら states the time or condition before the state changes. 眠くなる uses the く form of the adjective 眠い to say that the person became sleepy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: Vてから emphasizes that the later action happens after the earlier action is completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: Aいので would mean “because someone is sleepy...,” showing a reason rather than a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.tip: The adjective い must change to く before なる; do not say 眠いなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q19.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら; Aい → Aいく ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.vi: There is a test tomorrow. Therefore, I will study today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.sk: Time、 ＋ Nがあります。 ＋ それで ＋ Timeは ＋ Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates when the test takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: あります describes the existence of a thing that is not a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: それで connects the cause in the previous sentence with the result in the following sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes today the topic or time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: べんきょうします is the main predicate and states the action that will be done today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.why: The first sentence gives the reason that there is a test tomorrow. Then それで connects it to studying today as a logical result. は highlights today as the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning “therefore” is clearer and more direct. It is often used in conversation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the relationship between the two sentences becomes a contrast, so the cause-and-effect logic is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use それで to mean “after that” in every situation, but here it must connect a cause with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.vi: I have already forgotten what I studied yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The time expression modifies the studying action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form modifies こと and creates a relative clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns the studied content into a noun, while を marks the object that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: もう emphasizes that the action happened before the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the verb 忘れる with しまう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: てしまいました shows that the action has been completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unintended result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.why: きのうならった modifies こと, so it comes before this noun. ことを is the whole object of 忘れる, while てしまう emphasizes that the forgetting has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: Vていました shows a continuing state or action in the past and does not emphasize regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q20.kobun.tip: Do not separate こと from the preceding clause; the whole きのうならったこと is the object used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.vi: That new building is a department store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: あの comes before a noun to point to something far from both the speaker and the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective directly modifies ビル.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes ビル the topic explained at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: です connects the predicate noun with the topic politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.why: あの and あたらしい modify ビル respectively. ビルは states the topic, while デパートです says what that topic is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Using が emphasizes which building is the department store instead of stating a general topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q21.kobun.tip: The adjective い comes directly before the noun and does not need an extra の.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.vi: Somewhere, the sound of a baby crying can be heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where a sound comes from or is perceived.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects あかんぼう with the noun phrase that follows and shows possession or another relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies こえ and creates the meaning “the sound of crying.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the sound that is heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: する in the pattern 音がする expresses the perception of a sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.why: どこかで indicates where the sound is perceived. なく comes before こえ to modify the sound, while こえがします describes hearing that sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: Nを聞く emphasizes that the subject actively listens to a sound, rather than simply perceiving a sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: Nが聞こえる emphasizes that a sound can be heard, while Nがする emphasizes the feeling that the sound is coming from somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q22.kobun.tip: For sounds, use 音がする or 声がする; do not use を as when saying that you listen to an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.vi: Since coming to Japan, I have continued to live in this house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わたし the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the destination of 来る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: Vてから marks the starting point for counting time in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ずっと emphasizes that the state has continued without interruption.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: この comes before a noun to refer to a house near the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the place where someone exists or lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: The form て connects 住む with いる to show an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.ch.7.n: ています describes a state that has continued up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.why: 来てから sets the starting point. Then ずっと shows that living in this house has continued without interruption. に is used both for the destination with 来る and for the place of residence with 住む.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: Vたあとで only says that something happened after an action was completed. It does not emphasize a state continuing from that point to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: Vている only describes living there. It does not show when the state began.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.tip: Do not use で with 住む; a place of residence usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q23.kobun.cn: Vて + から; Vて + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.vi: Because I could not answer a simple question, I felt very embarrassed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective やさしい modifies the noun しつもん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the object of the action of answering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ～られなくて expresses that someone cannot do something and connects it to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: とても modifies the adjective 恥ずかしい and shows the degree of the emotion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 恥ずかしい changes to the polite past form 恥ずかしかったです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.why: The phrase that marks the object comes before the verb meaning “answer.” Then the ～なくて form connects the cause to the emotion. The adjective 恥ずかしい is the predicate at the end of the sentence and is changed to the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～なくて is replaced with ～ないで, the sentence tends to mean “not doing that, and then...,” without emphasizing the cause as strongly as the current sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake ～なくて for simply meaning “not do,” but here it connects the cause to the emotional result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.vi: Yamada: “Has your older brother recovered from his illness?” Tanaka: “Yes, thankfully, he has recovered.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The speaker’s name comes before 「 to begin the dialogue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the owner with the noun びょうき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the older brother’s illness the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies なりました and shows a change toward a better state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: なりましたか forms a polite question about a change of state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: The next speaker’s name opens the reply with 「.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: はい is a response word that confirms the question just asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.ch.7.n: おかげさまで is a fixed reply that shows a good result due to help or good luck.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.why: The question first sets びょうきは as the topic, then uses よくなりました to ask whether the illness has improved. The reply uses a fixed expression suitable for reporting good news and showing gratitude.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 元気になりましたか is used, the question directly asks whether a person or animal has become healthy again, instead of focusing on the condition of the illness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate よく as “usually,” but in よくなりました it means “become better or healthier.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.vi: I wrote and submitted a report about the Asian economy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: について indicates the topic covered by the report.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the report as the object that was written and submitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: 書いて uses the て form to connect the action of writing with the action of submitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: 出しました is the final predicate and shows that the submission was completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.why: について states the topic of the report, while を marks the report as the object of the whole series of actions. The て form connects two consecutive actions: writing first and then submitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is placed before レポート, the expression is more formal and directly modifies the noun “report.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is used instead, the sentence only lists representative actions and does not emphasize the order of writing and then submitting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use “and” between two verbs, but Japanese usually uses the て form to connect consecutive actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.vi: I felt uncomfortable because an unfamiliar person said rude things to me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.sk: Relative clause + Nに + Nなことを + V受身て、 + Nが + Aいかったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: しらない comes before 人 to modify it and identify the person as unfamiliar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the agent in the passive sentence, meaning the person who said the rude words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: 失礼な modifies こと and uses な because it is an な adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ことを is the content of what was said and is the object of 言われる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: 言われて is the passive form connected to the emotional result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the mood described by わるかったです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: わるかったです states an emotional condition in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.why: The sentence uses the passive voice to place the speaker in the position of being affected by the words. The clause 言われて gives the cause first, and then 気分がわるかったです gives the emotional result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If the sentence is changed to the active voice, the focus shifts to the person who spoke instead of the person affected by the words.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with ので, the cause-and-effect relationship is clearer, but the explanatory tone is softer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に in a passive sentence with に, which only marks a place; here に marks the person who caused the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this machine the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: 新しい modifies 技術 and shows that the technology being used is new.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the technology as the subject being used in the machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: つかわれています is the continuous passive form and describes technology currently being applied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.why: は states the machine as the topic, while が marks the technology being applied in the machine. The passive form emphasizes that the technology is being used, without needing to name the user.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence changes to the active voice, and the subject using it must be understood as the machine or its operator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes “can be used,” without stating that the technology is currently being applied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse が and を in a passive sentence; the object being used usually goes with が in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q5.kobun.cn: Nが + Vられる／Vられています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.vi: When the schedule is decided, I will inform you by email or phone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of what is being decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a condition or the time when the following action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: か is placed after a noun to state one of the choices.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: または connects equivalent choices and means “or.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the means used to give information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.why: The conditional clause comes first and states the time that serves as the basis for the main action. The phrase メールか、または電話で lists two possible means of giving information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: それとも is usually used in questions with choices, so it is less natural than または in this statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it would mean “and then,” so it would no longer show a choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と to connect two choices, but for the meaning “or,” they need to use か or または.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.tokens.2.m: if it has been decided, when it has been decided
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q6.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aかった形・Nだった形・Aなだった形 + ら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.vi: Check once more to see whether it is wrong before submitting it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: まちがっていないか creates the content to be checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ないか changes the question “is it or not?” into the content being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: もう modifies the checking action and expresses doing it one more time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: てから connects the action that must be completed first with the following action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: 出して in the て form connects with ください to create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.why: The content to be confirmed comes before か, and then てから shows that the checking must be completed before submission. ください makes the reminder polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Vたあとで also means “after,” but it only states the order and does not emphasize that the earlier action must be completed first as てから does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: Vないか means “whether ... or not” in this sentence, not an invitation such as “shall we ...?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate てから as “and,” because this pattern requires the first action to be completed before the next action is done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.vi: Because I carry heavy things every day, my arms have become thicker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.sk: Frequency + Aい + N を + Vていて + N が + Aいく + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 毎日 indicates how often the carrying action happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: おもい modifies the noun にもつ that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the thing being carried.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the carrying action with the following state or result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject whose state changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The form く connects the adjective with なる to express a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: なりました expresses a change that has already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + く + なる; Vて形 + いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.why: The phrase showing frequency and cause comes first, while the arm is the subject of the change. The adjective changes to the く form to combine with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This form is incorrect because なる must be used with the adjective ending い in the form く.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: くする expresses that the subject makes something change, while くなる indicates that something becomes that way by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t90-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use おもいなる directly, but they must change い into く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.vi: Because I had a nightmare last night, I could not sleep well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.sk: Time は + Aい + N を + Vて + Adv + V可能形ませんでした
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the time the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: こわい modifies ゆめ, while を marks the dream that was seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects seeing the dream with the result of not sleeping well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies ねむれませんでした and shows the degree of sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ねむれる in the polite past negative form expresses being unable to sleep well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.why: The time is stated at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the object of seeing. The て form connects a cause or an earlier event with the result of being unable to sleep.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見て is replaced with 見たので, the cause-and-effect relationship becomes clearer, and the sentence sounds more directly explanatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 見て as “and saw,” but here it connects a cause with a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.vi: She bought souvenirs from abroad and brought them back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who bought and brought back the souvenirs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から indicates the starting point or the place from which the souvenir was brought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the thing that was bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the て form connects buying with bringing something back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: きました expresses movement toward the speaker or the reference location after buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.why: が states the person who acts, から states the starting point, and を marks the souvenir. 買ってきました connects buying with 来る to express buying something elsewhere and bringing it back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it were used in this sentence, the direction of movement would be away from the speaker or toward another place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If it were used in this sentence, it would only mean “after buying,” without the idea of bringing the souvenir back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand 来る as only meaning “come,” but in 買ってくる it means doing something and then bringing the result back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q10.kobun.cn: Vて + 来る; Vて + 来ます・来ました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.vi: That child is always making their parents worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: は states the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the person affected by the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を is omitted in this expression, while this phrase states what is caused.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: かけています is the ている form of かける and expresses repeatedly causing that situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.why: The phrase for the affected person comes first, followed by the worrying content and the verb かける at the end of the sentence. ばかり emphasizes repetition in one direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ばかり with だけ gives more of a “only” meaning, with less of a complaining or repeated-action tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q11.kobun.tip: English learners may forget that に here indicates the person who is made worried, not a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q12.kobun.vi: A hotel will be built here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the location where the structure will be built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 建てます is the polite form of 建てる, indicating the action of building.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q12.kobun.why: The location comes first, the object being built comes next, and then the verb 建てます ends the sentence. に is suitable because this is the place where the structure will be built.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence emphasizes the place where the building activity happens rather than the location of the structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q12.kobun.tip: Do not habitually use で to translate “build at”; for the destination of 建てる, に is the natural particle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q13.kobun.vi: As expected, he did not come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: やはり modifies the whole clause and shows that the result was as predicted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that he is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ませんでした is the polite negative past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q13.kobun.why: やはり comes first to cover the whole statement, the topic comes in the middle, and the negative past predicate comes last. This order makes it clear that the actual result matched the prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with やっと, the sentence means “in the end, he did not come,” without the meaning of “as expected.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q13.kobun.tip: やはり does not mean “did”; the past tense is shown by ませんでした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.vi: I like people who have big dreams.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person who has the feeling or preference in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object that is possessed or held in the phrase 持っている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause もっている comes before 人 to modify that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the liked object in the structure 好きです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: 好きです is the predicate that expresses a feeling or preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.why: The clause 夢を持っている comes before 人 to identify which people are meant. Then 人が is the object of 好きです, while わたしは is the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with 持つ describes people with dreams in general, while 持っている emphasizes the state of having them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.tip: In Japanese, a modifying clause must come before the noun. It does not come after 人 as it does in English.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q14.kobun.cn: Aい + N / N を + Vている + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.vi: I still do not know clearly whether I will attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: か comes after a clause and turns its content into an uncertain choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: The negative clause parallels the previous clause and creates the choice pair か…か.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: まだ shows that, up to now, the decision has still not been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: はっきり modifies わかりません and indicates how clear the understanding is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: わかりません is a polite negative predicate that presents an undetermined conclusion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.why: The two contrasting clauses, しゅっせきするか and しないか, come before わかりません as the content to be determined. まだ and はっきり add the time and the level of uncertainty, respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If かどうか is used, the sentence only asks yes or no in a binary form. It does not directly state the two sides, attending and not attending.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use the past form in the two parts か…か when asking whether someone will attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.vi: War always takes the lives of many people. It is a very painful thing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the situation or context in which an event happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase たくさんの modifies the noun ひと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject affected by the action なくなります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb なくなる is in the polite form ます and describes an event that happens regularly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle は makes the event just mentioned the topic of the next sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.ch.7.n: The adjective 悲しい comes before こと to modify the event being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.ch.8.n: こと turns the content 悲しい into a noun, while です ends the sentence in a polite style.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.why: The first sentence gives the situation with で, then places the affected people with が before the predicate. The second sentence uses は to refer to the whole event again and 悲しいことです to evaluate it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the sentence means that it is something joyful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, the sentence tends to mean that it is something strange or unusual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q17.kobun.tip: English learners may use は instead of が in the first sentence, even though が is the particle that marks the affected person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.vi: There was only one vacant room left in the Japanese inn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.sk: N の + N が + Numberだけ + Vていました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun りょかん with the noun へや to indicate a room belonging to the inn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the room as being in the described state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: だけ limits the number of rooms to one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: あいていました is the past progressive form and describes the room's vacant state at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.why: The phrase りょかんのへや identifies the type of room, while が marks the room as the object with the vacant state. ひとつだけ comes before the predicate to limit the number of rooms, and ていました shows that this state existed in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, it means that someone opened a door or something else, not that the room was vacant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used, it means that something was closed or being closed, which is the opposite of having space available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q18.kobun.tip: English learners may mistake あく for “open,” but 空く in this sentence means “become vacant” or “have space available.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.vi: A hat is hanging on the wall by the entrance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects げんかん with かべ to identify the wall as belonging to the entrance area.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place where the object is hanging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the hat as the object in the hanging state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern てあります describes the result of an intentional action that remains unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.why: The place に comes before the object が, forming a structure that describes an object existing at that place. かけてあります emphasizes that someone hung the hat and that it is still in that state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If かけています is used, the sentence only describes an action or state in progress. It does not emphasize a prepared result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with this form, the meaning is that the hat has been placed on the wall or there, not hung.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand あります as simply meaning “there is,” but てあります also shows that the state is the result of an intentional action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.vi: To attend the meeting at 10 o’clock, I have to leave home early.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the time for the noun かいぎ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the event that the speaker will attend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb modifies ため, forming the purpose phrase “in order to attend.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ためには states the purpose and the necessary condition for achieving it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: はやく modifies the action of leaving home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the place of departure with the verb でる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: The conditional form でなければ combines with なりません to express obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: なければなりません indicates that something definitely must be done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.why: The phrase ためには puts the purpose first and then states the action needed to achieve it. The pattern ～なければなりません changes the condition “if one does not do it” into an obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ～ために is used instead of ～ためには, the sentence only states the purpose and has less of the meaning “to achieve this purpose, it is necessary to...”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If the obligation pattern is replaced with ～なくてもいい, the meaning changes to “it is okay not to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change ない to なければ before なりません; the plain-form verb cannot be followed directly by なければなりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの + ためには; Vない形－い + ければ + なりません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.vi: Her face looks very much like her father’s.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes her the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が identifies the specific part, the face, rather than the whole person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the person used as the standard for comparing similarity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: よく modifies 似ています and shows a high degree of similarity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: 似ています is the ている form of 似る and describes a state of being similar.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to talk about her, but uses が to limit the point of similarity to her face. With 似る, the object of comparison is used with に, while よく comes before the predicate to show the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this form, the meaning becomes “identical” or “the same thing,” which is stronger than the similarity expressed by 似ています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with this form, the meaning becomes “correct” or “suitable,” not similarity in appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use と for the object of comparison, but 似ています is used with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.vi: People aged 18 or older, please buy an adult ticket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the age as the topic and the scope of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun おとな to the noun that follows and modifies the type of ticket.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being bought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: てください connects to a verb to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.why: The age phrase comes at the beginning of the sentence and is marked with は to state who the request applies to. おとなの modifies きっぷ, while かってください expresses a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: Expresses a range from N upward, including N itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the meaning becomes from N downward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake 以上 for meaning only “greater than,” but this pattern usually includes the stated limit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.vi: This is the dictionary I received from my teacher when I graduated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the object being introduced the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 卒業 with とき to identify the time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: とき indicates when the dictionary was received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the person who gives the object in the structure いただく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: The clause いただいた comes before じしょ to modify the dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: です ends the sentence and confirms that the object being introduced is a dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.why: The time phrase comes before the main clause to state when the gift was received. いただいたじしょ is a modifying clause before the noun, in which に indicates the giver and いただいた shows the receiver’s humble way of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the focus shifts to the teacher as the person who gave the dictionary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the meaning is still “received from the teacher,” but the polite and humble tone is weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place the modifying clause after the noun, but Japanese always places いただいた before じしょ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q22.kobun.cn: Vた形 + N; N に + いただく
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.vi: I have almost no chance to speak Japanese.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: なかなか is used with a negative sentence to express that something is difficult to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object of the verb はなす.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase はなす modifies きかい, while が marks the subject of existence or nonexistence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ありません is the polite negative form of あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.why: The clause はなす modifies the noun きかい, forming the phrase “a chance to speak Japanese.” The structure Nがありません is used to say that something does not exist or is not available.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with this form, the meaning is still “not often,” but the tone is milder and more neutral than なかなか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate なかなか as “quite,” but in a negative sentence it usually means “hardly” or “almost not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.vi: Because the TV was not working properly, I took it to be repaired.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テレビ with ぐあい and indicates the TV’s condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the condition being described as abnormal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the purpose of taking the TV away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: だしました is the main action, meaning to take an object to a repair shop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.why: The phrase テレビのぐあい is the topic described by おかしい. ので connects the cause before it with the action of taking the TV for repair after it, while に states the purpose of taking it away.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the reason is stated more directly and conversationally than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: ために usually indicates an objective purpose or cause and does not naturally replace ので in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may use に to mean “to,” but in 修理に出す, に indicates the purpose “take it away to repair it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.vi: I went straight up to the rooftop by elevator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means of transportation used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: まっすぐ modifies the upward movement and shows how it was done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: まで marks the endpoint of the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: あがりました is the polite past form of the verb あがる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.why: で states the means, まっすぐ states how the movement was made, and まで marks the final destination. The verb あがりました comes at the end to complete the polite past statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: に can indicate a destination, but it does not emphasize the final limit as strongly as まで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: へ focuses more on the direction toward the place than on the endpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q25.kobun.tip: Do not use で to indicate the destination; で indicates the means here, while the final place uses まで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka always uses polite speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the person who performs the action as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: いつも modifies つかいます and indicates how often the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective な needs な when it comes before the noun ことば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the speech being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: つかいます is the main predicate and describes the habit of using speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.why: The person performing the action is marked by は, and the frequency adverb comes before the verb phrase. The adjective な must keep な before a noun, while the object of つかいます goes with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If ていねいに話します is used, the focus shifts to speaking politely, not to the type of speech being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q3.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily omit な before a noun and say ていねいことば; the correct form is ていねいなことば.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.vi: That day was a very enjoyable day.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks a specific day as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies たのしい and indicates the degree of enjoyment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective たのしい modifies the noun いちにち.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: いちにちでした is a polite past noun predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.why: The day is introduced as the topic at the beginning. Then とても increases the degree of the adjective. The adjective comes before the noun to describe the day, while でした ends the polite past noun sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 楽しかったです is used, the sentence directly says “that day was enjoyable,” instead of using the structure “was an enjoyable day.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q4.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily place とても after the adjective, but in Japanese とても must come before the word showing degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.vi: My father is a bus driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects バス to the following noun and creates a phrase that modifies the occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun 運転手 combines with です to form the predicate and describe an occupation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.why: The sentence uses は to introduce the person being discussed and の to show possession or modification between two nouns. です comes after the occupation noun to end the polite sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning changes to the negative: my father is not a bus driver.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily omit the particle の and say バス運転手, but the basic pattern requires バスの運転手.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q5.kobun.cn: N は ＋ N の ＋ N です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place or position toward which the action of sitting is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is used in the て form to connect with ください and create a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: ください comes after a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q6.kobun.why: The place or position いすに comes before the verb. The verb かける changes to the て form and then combines with ください to create a polite invitation or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the invitation becomes softer and more formal, with the feeling of asking for the listener’s agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q6.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily translate に as “on the chair,” but に here marks the place to sit, not an object placed on the chair.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.vi: I ran, so I caught the 9 o’clock train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: A verb in the たら form creates a conditional clause or shows a time before the following clause occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects 9時 with 電車 and identifies the train that leaves at 9 o’clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the object that the action of catching on time is directed toward in 間に合う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 間に合いました is a polite past predicate and states the result that occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.why: The clause はしったら comes first to state the condition or time leading to the result. The phrase 9時の電車に is the object of 間に合う, because this verb usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning is only “after running,” without emphasizing a conditional relationship or result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used in the sentence, it has a more general conditional meaning and is less natural than たら when talking about something that already happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily use を with 間に合う to mean “catch what,” but the correct pattern is Nに間に合う.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q7.kobun.cn: Vた・Vなかった ＋ ら; Aい ＋ かったら; Aな・N ＋ だったら
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.vi: I could not do the English test at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.sk: N の N は ＋ ぜんぜん ＋ past negative V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the name of a subject or language with テスト to modify the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes テスト the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぜん modifies the predicate and usually goes with a negative sentence to emphasize a degree of zero.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: できませんでした is the polite past negative form of できる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.why: The phrase えいごのテスト identifies the type of test, while は makes the whole phrase the topic. ぜんぜん comes before the negative predicate to emphasize that the result was almost zero.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning is weaker: “could not do much” or “was not very good.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern still means not at all, but it uses the present tense or describes a habit instead of something that could not be done in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.tip: English-speaking learners may easily use ぜんぜん with an affirmative sentence, but at the basic level this word usually goes with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q8.kobun.cn: ぜんぜん ＋ Vない・Aくない・Nではない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.vi: I accidentally caused a traffic accident on a motorcycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the means used to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the verb おこす.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb in the て form connects the action of causing the accident with the pattern てしまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: てしまいました describes a completed action with a sense of regret or something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.why: The means marker で comes before the object and verb. おこしてしまいました combines the form て with しまう to show that the accident happened and that the speaker regrets it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If the unintended meaning is removed and only Vました is used, the sentence only reports that an accident was caused. It does not emphasize regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used in the sentence, the meaning becomes doing something beforehand or preparing it in advance, so it does not fit an accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate で as “at,” but in this sentence で indicates the means of transport: by motorcycle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t91-q9.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; Vて + しまいます・しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.vi: No matter how short of money you are, you must never steal other people's things.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら begins a concessive condition and emphasizes a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject as being absent in the condition clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ない changes into なく and connects with ても to create the meaning “even if there is none.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: けっして usually goes with a negative predicate to emphasize prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects ひと with もの and indicates something that belongs to someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks the thing as the object of stealing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: ては connects the verb with いけません to create a prohibition pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: いけません in the pattern てはいけません expresses prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.why: いくら～なくても creates the concessive clause at the beginning, while the main clause uses けっして～てはいけません to emphasize an absolute prohibition. の identifies the owner of the thing, and を marks the thing being taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the meaning changes to “even if ..., it is allowed,” which is opposite to the prohibition expressed by てはいけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a request not to do something, which is weaker than a prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget that てはいけません always means “must not,” not just “should not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q1.kobun.cn: Vて・Aいくて・Aなで・Nで + も; Vて形 + は + いけません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.vi: In my country, men wear skirts during festivals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects わたし with くに to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: では states the scope and topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects おまつり with とき to modify the time expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: とき indicates the time when the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: の modifies ひと and creates a phrase referring to men.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: は states that men are the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: を marks the item worn in the action はきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: This is the main predicate and describes the action of wearing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.why: The time phrase おまつりのとき comes before the subject and predicate to state the setting. は marks the topic, while を marks the item being worn.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If では is replaced with において, the sentence becomes more formal and more literary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit を before the item being worn and use は instead of を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.vi: When I tried reading it, many things made me say, “So that's how it is.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The form て connects the action よんで with みる to create the pattern for trying to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: と connects a condition or time with the result discovered afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks a quoted exclamation or thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: This clause modifies こと and indicates what makes the reader think なるほど.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: こと turns the previous content into a noun, and が marks the thing being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 多かった is the predicate and describes a large quantity in the past.
