default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.cn: Vて + みる; exclamation or thought + と + 思わせる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.why: よんでみる describes trying to read, while みると leads to the realization that follows. The phrase なるほどとおもわせる modifies こと, and then ことが becomes the subject of 多かった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If と思う is used, the subject directly thinks that thought. It does not emphasize that the story made the reader think so.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If と感じる is used, the sentence only states the reader's feeling, with a weaker sense of being persuaded by the content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate と as “and,” but here と marks the content that is thought or said.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q11.tokens.5.m: make someone think, make someone feel
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.vi: This is a rare species of fish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes これ the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective directly modifies しゅるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects しゅるい with さかな to create the phrase “species of fish.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: です ends the noun sentence and identifies this as a species of fish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.why: めずらしい comes before しゅるい to describe the quality of the fish. の connects the noun しゅるい with さかな, while です completes the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If “rare fish” is said directly without using しゅるい, the sentence is shorter and does not emphasize that it is a species.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the adjective after the noun, but Japanese adjectives come before the nouns they modify.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.vi: The house was completely destroyed by fire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the cause or circumstances that led to the burning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the thing affected by the burning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぶ modifies the burning action and emphasizes that it was complete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: 焼けてしまいました describes an event that has been completed, often with a sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.cn: Vて + しまう; Vてしまいました in the polite past form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.why: かじで states the cause, and いえが is the object that enters the burning state. ぜんぶ comes before the verb to show degree, while てしまう emphasizes the unintended completed result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 焼きました is used, the sentence changes to mean that someone actively burned or roasted the house. It is no longer a state in which the house burned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If しまいました is omitted, the sentence only states that it burned, reducing the sense of regret or something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake 焼ける for the active verb “to burn,” but this verb describes an object entering a burned state by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.vi: No matter how many times I search, I still cannot find the wallet that should have been placed here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: いくら combines with ても to emphasize the degree, no matter how much one does something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: ても connects a concessive clause with a result that does not change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the wallet was put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: はずの connects a certain belief with さいふ and creates a clause modifying the wallet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the wallet as the thing that is found or not found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: みつからない describes a state in which something cannot be found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.why: いくら～ても creates the concessive clause before the result. はずのさいふ identifies the wallet that the speaker is certain was placed here, while が marks the wallet as the subject of みつからない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If はずだ is used at the end of a sentence, the speaker confirms the prediction; はずの here modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 置いたと思う, the level of certainty decreases because it is only a thought or guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use はずの as an independent predicate, but this form must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q14.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ はずの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.vi: In summer, cold beer really is the best, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes summer the topic and sets the scope of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: やっぱり adds a confirming feeling based on familiar experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: ひえた modifies ビール, while を marks beer as the object being drunk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns のむ into a noun, and が marks drinking beer as the thing being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: いちばん modifies いい and creates the meaning of the highest degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: ですね ends the sentence with a feeling of agreement or shared experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.why: ひえたビールをのむ is an action nominalized with の, and then が marks that action as the thing being evaluated. いちばん いい expresses the highest degree, while ですね creates a feeling of agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If 飲むことが is used, it still means “drinking,” but it sounds more neutral and formal than のが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If いい is replaced with おいしい, the focus changes from “the best” to good taste.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand のが as “of,” but here の turns the verb into a noun so it can be the subject of evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q15.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ のが ＋ いちばん ＋ Aい; Aい ＋ ですね
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.vi: There is only one snack left in the corner of the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.sk: Nの ＋ Nに ＋ Nが ＋ Quantityだけ ＋ Vて ＋ いました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun れいぞうこ to the following noun showing location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に shows the location where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing left in the refrigerator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: だけ limits the quantity to one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: のこって is the て form of のこる, and it connects to いました to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: ています expresses an ongoing state; いました puts that state into the polite past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.why: The phrase showing location comes before the subject to state where something exists. が marks the item as remaining, while だけ emphasizes that there is only one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If しか～ない is used, it also means “only one,” but it must be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that に here shows the place where something exists, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q16.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いる・います・いました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.vi: Ichiro's father is probably coming here soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the owner to the noun おとうさん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person performing the action of coming here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: もうすぐ modifies an action that will happen soon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the destination of the movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: おいでになる is the honorific form for the mentioned person's action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: はずだ expresses a well-founded guess; です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.why: The subject is marked with が, followed by the time もうすぐ and the destination ここに. はずです comes at the end of the sentence to conclude that the person's arrival is predicted with certainty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with でしょう, it is only a weaker prediction and does not emphasize firm evidence like はずです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with かもしれません, the level of certainty decreases, meaning that the person may come.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with the destination, but the movement verb for going or coming to a place uses に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q17.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの ＋ はずだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.vi: The company is looking for someone with the skills to repair airplanes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject that is looking for someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being repaired in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: 修理する comes before 技術 to modify “skills”; を marks the skills that the person has.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: もっている modifies ひと, forming the phrase “a person who has the skills”; を marks the person being sought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: さがして is the て form, connecting the main verb to います to show an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: ています expresses an action that is currently being performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.why: The clause 修理する技術 modifies 技術, while もっているひと modifies ひと. The two uses of を mark the object being repaired and the person the company is looking for, respectively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If 修理した is used, it means “the skills that repaired something,” changing the modifying relationship and sounding unnatural in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place a modifying clause after a noun, but Japanese always places it before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q18.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ N; Vて ＋ いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.vi: I plan to give a fountain pen to celebrate my friend's acceptance into university.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に goes with 合格する to show the place or examination that the learner passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ごうかくした modifies おいわい; に shows the purpose of giving the gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the gift being given.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: あげよう is the volitional form, and と quotes the content of the intention before おもいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: おもいます is the main verb and expresses the speaker's thought or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.why: ごうかくした modifies おいわい, forming the reason or occasion for giving the gift. The pattern Vようとおもいます places the intention immediately before the verb おもいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with Vつもりです, it also expresses a plan, but the tone states the plan more directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with Vたいです, it only expresses the desire to give something and does not emphasize a decision or plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake に in お祝いに for a time, but here it shows purpose: to celebrate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q19.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Nに + V意向形と + おもう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.vi: When teaching, the teacher was very strict, but normally he was a very gentle person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: とき shows a point in time, while は sets a time frame for comparison with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い comes before the noun せんせい to describe that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: でした forms a polite past noun predicate, while が connects two contrasting clauses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: は states a second situation for comparison with the time of teaching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective い directly describes the noun ひと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: でした is a noun predicate and ends the sentence in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.why: ときは and ふだんは create two situations placed side by side. が connects two contrasting clauses: strict when teaching but gentle in everyday life.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is replaced with けれども, the contrast remains, but the expression is more complete and slightly more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If ときには is used, the sentence means “sometimes” and no longer clearly states a comparison time frame like ときは.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit は after とき, so the meaning “specifically while teaching...” is not emphasized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形 + とき; Aい + N; Nでしたが、
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.vi: Everyone who sees that cow for the first time laughs because it has a very funny face.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: その describes the noun うし that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the cow that is seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: はじめて describes 見た and indicates the first time that person sees it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: みた comes before ひと to describe the person who has seen the cow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: は identifies the group of people mentioned in the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: みんな describes the act of laughing and refers to the whole group.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.7.n: ほんとうに describes the adjective おもしろい and emphasizes its degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.8.n: おもしろい comes before かお to describe the face.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.9.n: を marks the appearance being shown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.10.n: して connects the phrase かおをしている with the explanation of the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.ch.11.n: ～ていますから gives the reason why everyone laughs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.why: The phrase うしをはじめてみた comes before ひと to identify the people who see the cow for the first time. The next sentence uses から to explain why everyone laughs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If はじめて is replaced with 初めに, it means “first” and no longer expresses seeing something for the first time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective, but the cause remains the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate から as “from,” but after a clause it usually means “because.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q20.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Nをしている; 普通形 + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.vi: As expected, slightly bitter draft beer tastes better, doesn’t it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: やはり describes the whole sentence and shows a conclusion that matches a prediction or preference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: すこし describes にがい and indicates the degree of bitterness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: にがい comes before ビール to describe the type of beer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the type of beer described as tasty.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: おいしい is the predicate; ですね adds a tone of confirmation or agreement with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.why: にがい comes before ビール to limit the type of beer being evaluated. The subject ビールが comes before the predicate おいしい, while やはり states a conclusion that matches the existing impression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with からい, the beer tastes spicy or hot, not bitter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If おいしい is replaced with うまい, the meaning is still “tasty,” but the expression is more conversational and casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake にがい for “spicy,” while にがい means “bitter” and からい means “spicy.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q21.kobun.cn: 程度副詞 + Aい; Aい + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I took an exam for international students.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: きのう indicates the time when the action occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun りゅうがくせい with しけん to describe the exam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the exam as the object of the verb うけました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: うけました is the polite past form of うける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.why: The time expression comes at the beginning, followed by the noun phrase りゅうがくせいのしけん as the object. The verb うけました ends the sentence and shows that the action has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: This describes taking or sitting an exam, a test, or using a service.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: With this pattern, the meaning changes to receiving or accepting an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q22.kobun.tip: It is necessary to distinguish うける in 受ける from うけとる in 受け取る; adding と changes the meaning to receiving something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.vi: Try comparing prices to see which store is cheaper.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: どの comes before the noun みせ to ask which store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject being asked about in the question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: か changes the clause やすい into an indirect question and connects it to the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: てみる expresses trying to do something, while て connects to the request ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: てください creates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.why: The clause どのみせがやすいか states what needs to be determined, and then ねだんをくらべてみてください asks the listener to try comparing prices. The particle を marks price as the object of the action くらべる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If のか is used, the indirect question more strongly emphasizes finding out which store is cheap.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If みて is omitted, only the request to compare remains, without the nuance of “trying.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that てみる must be used with a verb in the て form, and cannot connect directly to the dictionary form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q23.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ みる ＋ Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.vi: The sky has gradually become brighter. It seems that the rain has also stopped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject whose state is changing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective ending in い changes to the く form to connect with なって.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: なって connects an adjective with 来る and describes a change that is progressing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: てきました shows that the change has taken place and has progressed up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: も adds the rain to the subject being discussed, meaning “also.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: やんだ is the past form of やむ, used for rain or an event that is stopping.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: ようです expresses a judgment based on an observed sign.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.why: あかるくなってきました describes the change from dark to bright as it progresses up to the present. The next sentence uses やんだようです because the speaker guesses that the rain has stopped from the sign that the sky is bright.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If なりました is used, it only says that the sky became bright, without emphasizing the process of change up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: そうです usually conveys information that was heard, while ようです focuses on a guess based on the observed situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate てくる as “go to,” but in this sentence it only indicates a gradual change toward the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q24.kobun.cn: Aいく ＋ なる ＋ Vてくる; V普通形・Nの ＋ ようです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q25.kobun.sk: N の N倍 は ＋ Number です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the number 8 with the number of times it is calculated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents 5倍 as the topic to be explained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: です connects the topic with the calculation result in a polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q25.kobun.why: The structure ８の５倍 only means an amount equal to five times 8. は makes the result to be explained the topic, while です states that the result is 40.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If this expression is used, the focus shifts to multiplying 8 by 5.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake 倍 for an ordinary counting unit; in this pattern, it means “... times.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 connects the act of speaking with the act of apologizing that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: あやまりました is the main action in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q3.kobun.why: Direct speech is placed in quotation marks and connected with と. いって in the て form connects the act of speaking with the main action, あやまりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only says that the speaker said “sorry,” without additionally emphasizing the act of apologizing through あやまりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is added, the sentence emphasizes that the act of apologizing happened after saying “sorry.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use と with the meaning “and,” but in this sentence と marks the quoted speech content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q3.kobun.cn: N ＋ と ＋ Vて形; Vて形 ＋ V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.vi: I heard that an old man was bitten by a dog in the park and suffered greatly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the place where the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person affected by the event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the agent in a passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the て form connects the event of being bitten with the following state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです at the end of a sentence shows that the information was heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.why: The place is mentioned first, followed by the person affected and the agent in the passive sentence. The て form connects the event of being bitten with the result of suffering, while そうです adds the meaning that the information was heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing it with this expression means “I heard that” or “it seems that,” but the guessing nuance is stronger.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に as a place marker; in this passive sentence, に indicates that the dog is the agent that caused the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.vi: Recently, I have gained weight because I have not had time to exercise.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb phrase modifies 暇 and indicates the time for exercising.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject of the state of not having something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the cause with the result in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: てくる describes a gradual change up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.why: The phrase うんどうする modifies 暇, forming the meaning “time for exercising.” ないので states the cause, while ふとってきました describes the result as a gradual change up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still indicates the cause, but the expression is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If ふとっていきます is used, it emphasizes that the weight gain will continue from the present onward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q5.kobun.tip: てくる should not be translated as “come”; in this pattern, it indicates a change progressing up to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.vi: My baby's weight is about 4000 grams.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the noun showing the owner with the noun 赤ちゃん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 赤ちゃん with the noun 体重 and shows possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: は introduces the weight as the topic to be described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ぐらい follows an amount to show an approximate level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.why: The two phrases の identify which family the baby belongs to and whose weight is being discussed. は makes the weight the topic, while だいたい and ぐらい both show that the number is only an estimate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ぐらい with ほど also indicates a degree, but it is usually used to emphasize a limit or a level reached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out one of the two particles の, but both are needed to connect the relationships “my baby” and “the baby's weight.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I heard a very useful story from Mr. Sato.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N に ＋ Adv ＋ V辞書形 ＋ N を ＋ humble V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person or source from whom the speaker heard the story.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: This clause comes before おはなし to modify the story.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the content that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the main predicate and uses the speaker's humble expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.why: The clause やくにたつ comes before おはなし to modify the story. を marks the content that was heard, while に identifies the person providing or serving as the source of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 聞いた is used, the meaning is still “heard,” but the humble nuance is lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern has the speaker as its subject, so it means that Sato said it, not that I heard it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q7.kobun.tip: Do not translate うかがった as “asked” in every case; with おはなしを, it humbly means “heard the story.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.vi: I always book plane tickets one month in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.sk: Adv + Time に + N の + N の + Vて + おく
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the time when the tickets are booked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 飛行機 with the ticket-booking phrase and identifies the type of ticket or booking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of the action しておきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects booking the tickets with おく and shows advance preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: ておきます describes doing something in advance to prepare for the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.why: The time of booking comes before the object of the action. 予約をしておきます combines the form て with おく to emphasize that the tickets are booked in advance as preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 予約をしています is used, the sentence only says that the speaker is booking tickets or usually books tickets. It does not emphasize advance preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 予約をしてから is used, it means doing something else after booking the tickets, not preparing them for the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t92-q9.kobun.tip: Do not understand おきます here as “put down”; in ておく, it means doing something in advance or preparing it beforehand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.vi: “I’m sorry, but could you finish this work by tomorrow?” “Yes, I understand.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: が softens the opening before making a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: までに indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: この modifies the noun しごと that comes immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the work as the object of the action of doing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.4.vi: could you do it for me
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: ていただけませんか politely asks whether the listener can do it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: はい confirms the request and begins the reply.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: 承知しました is a polite predicate showing that the speaker understands and accepts the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.why: The deadline あすまでに comes before the object and action to limit the completion time. ていただけませんか uses humble, polite language to ask someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It is also a request, but it is less polite than ていただけませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It is still a polite request, but it sounds more direct and common.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily understand いただく as only meaning “receive,” but in this pattern it makes the request humble and polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q1.kobun.cn: Vて + いただけませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka asked Yan, “Do you know that person’s name?”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the person who performs the action of asking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the person being asked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: あの modifies the noun that follows and also opens the quoted speech.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the noun かた with the noun なまえ to show possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the name as the object known.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the predicate of the quoted question and ends with ですか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: と marks the whole preceding sentence as the content of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.cn: Normal quotation + と + 言う・聞く・思う; inside the question, use Vます・Aい・Aな・Nです + か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.why: The person being asked goes with に, and the question content is placed in quotation marks and connected to the verb きく by と. なまえを is the object of ごぞんじですか, so it uses を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If について is used, the sentence focuses more on the topic being asked about than on quoting the exact question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If かどうか is used, the question of whether something is true is reported indirectly, without keeping the original question in quotation marks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily forget と after the quoted sentence when using きく or いう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.vi: The view seen from the hotel window was wonderful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ホテル with まど to modify “window.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause comes before the noun けしき and modifies that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the view as the subject that has the quality of being wonderful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The い adjective changes to the past tense with かった to describe an experience that was seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.why: The phrase みたけしき forms a clause that modifies けしき, so the description must come before the noun. から gives the starting point of the line of sight, while が marks the view as the subject of the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: で emphasizes the place where the action of looking happens, while から emphasizes the starting angle of the view.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: 見る refers to a view that is usually seen or will be seen, without emphasizing a view that has already been seen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the modifying clause after the noun, as in Vietnamese, but Japanese puts it before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q11.kobun.cn: Vた + N; Aい + かったです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.vi: There is plenty, so please do not be shy and eat a lot.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason with the advice or request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks えんりょ as the object of doing or not doing something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: Vないで connects with the following action and means not doing the first action before doing the next one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: ください expresses a request, while ね makes the tone softer and friendlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason, and the second gives advice. しないで means not carrying out the action of being hesitant, and then たべてください is used to ask the listener to eat.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with なくて, the sentence focuses more on stating a reason or a state of not doing something, so it is less natural than ないで in this advice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: ように emphasizes a goal or a reminder to avoid something, so its nuance differs from directly telling someone not to be shy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use ないでください for the whole sentence, but here しないで only connects two actions, and ください goes with たべて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ から; Vないで; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.vi: In the United States, houses with a swimming pool in the yard are not rare, or so I hear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: では states the scope and place being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place where the swimming pool exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the thing that exists in the yard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: ある comes before うち and modifies houses with swimming pools.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: は introduces the group of houses with the feature mentioned in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: ない negates the adjective めずらしい, creating the meaning “not rare.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: そうです comes at the end of a sentence to report information heard from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ そうです; before そうです in reported speech, the adjective な and noun keep だ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.why: The clause ある modifies うち, so it comes directly before the noun. では limits the comment to the United States, while そうです shows that this is reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: そうだ can be the casual form of reported information, while そうです is more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: ようです expresses an inference based on signs or circumstances, not simply something heard from another person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand そうです as “looks like,” but after a complete clause it usually means “I hear.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: は indicates the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: いそがしい changes to the past tense with かった to talk about a condition during today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q14.kobun.why: きょうは sets the time period as the topic, while ずいぶん adds degree to the adjective. Since the busy condition occurred during the day, the past form いそがしかった is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: だいぶ also indicates quite a high degree, but it often emphasizes a change or an achieved level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: とても means “very” and is stronger, without necessarily having the evaluative nuance of ずいぶん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q14.kobun.tip: Learners may easily forget to change い to かった when an adjective ending in い describes a past state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.vi: I do not understand very well. Could you explain it in a little more detail?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason for not understanding with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: An adjective ending in い changes to く to modify the verb せつめいする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: This noun is the content of the requested explaining action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects せつめいする with いただけませんか to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: いただけませんか is a humble and polite way to ask for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason for not understanding, followed by a request for an explanation. こまかく is an adverbial form that modifies せつめいして, while ていただけませんか makes the request very polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern is also a request, but it is more casual and direct than ていただけませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is a polite request, but it does not show as much humility as ていただけませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.tip: Learners may easily use こまかいせつめい, but when it modifies a verb, it must change to こまかく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q15.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いただけませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.vi: The ball I threw has flown into the neighbor’s garden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: なげた is a clause that modifies ボール, while が marks the subject of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects となり with the following modified location noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the ball enters.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the verb はいる with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: ～てしまいました expresses a completed action, often with a sense of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.why: The clause なげた modifies ボール to identify which ball it is. に marks the place where the ball enters, while the form て connects the action はいる with a pattern showing that something happened unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used instead, the sentence would describe doing something first or preparing it in advance, without the sense that it happened by mistake.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.tip: Learners may easily forget that ～てしまう can express not only completion but also regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q16.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.vi: Because it is dangerous, please do not touch this machine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: から connects the reason clause with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: この comes before a noun to identify the machine being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the object of the touching action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: Vないで connects with ください to make a request not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes the statement a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and is connected with から. The verb さわる goes with に to mark the object being touched, and then Vないでください makes a request not to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a polite way to ask someone not to do something, and it is softer than a direct prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If this were used instead, the sentence would have a stronger prohibitive tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.tip: In this basic pattern, do not use を with さわる; the object being touched usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q17.kobun.cn: Vない ＋ で ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.vi: I have never experienced such a large earthquake before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: こんな comes before an adjective and noun to state a degree or quality like the one being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: おおきい directly modifies the noun じしん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the earthquake the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたことが nominalizes an experience, while が marks something that has never happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません negates the existence of that experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.why: The adjective phrase comes before じしん to describe the earthquake, and then は makes it the topic. The pattern Vたことがありません expresses never having experienced doing that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If this were used instead, the sentence would mean having experienced it at least once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning is similar, but it emphasizes experience more than having done something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.tip: In this pattern, こと does not have the separate meaning “thing”; it helps turn the verb into a noun referring to an experience.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q18.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ことが ＋ ある／あります／ありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.vi: Because the small bird flew away, I went from house to house in the neighborhood to look for it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Vた ＋ ので ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Quantity ＋ ずつ ＋ Vて ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the first clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects a past reason to the search action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects きんじょ with うち to modify the houses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the range of houses visited one by one.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: ずつ shows equal division by each unit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: The て form connects going from house to house with searching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: This is the main predicate and ends the chain of actions in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.why: The clause にげたので states the cause before the result. を marks the houses visited, ずつ shows that they were visited one by one, and the て form connects going around with the purpose of searching.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes slightly more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てから is used, the meaning is that the speaker searched only after going around, so it is no longer a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.tip: ずつ comes after a quantity to mean “each...” or “one by one”; it does not come before the quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.vi: There is a stereo and a table placed in the reception room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates where the objects are located.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: や lists the stereo together with other objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the objects as being in a placed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects おく with あります to describe a state in which someone has arranged something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: あります is the predicate showing that an object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.why: The location goes with に, while the objects existing in that location go with が. Vてあります shows that the objects are in a state of having been intentionally placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If ています is used, the focus is on an action or an ongoing state, rather than on the result of arranging something as with てあります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If only あります is used, the sentence only says that objects are there; it does not show that they have already been placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for objects because they think of it as a location; in this sentence, the objects are the subject, so が is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies しごと and identifies the work being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this work the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the person who performed the action やった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: んですか creates a question that expresses a desire to know or confirm the situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the person who performed the action in the answer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: いたしました is the predicate and uses the humble form of しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.why: The question introduces the topic with は and asks who performed the action with が. The answer uses が to identify the person who did it and the humble form いたしました to show politeness toward the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If only ですか is used, the question simply asks for information and has less of an explanatory tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a respectful form used for another person's action. It is not used to speak humbly about one's own action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.tip: When speaking about something you did to a person who deserves respect, use humble language such as いたしました instead of a respectful form that honors the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい ＋ んです／んですか; Aな・N ＋ な ＋ んです／んですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.vi: I walked on the sand by the coast without wearing shoes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the item worn on the feet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: Vないで connects the state of not wearing shoes with the walking action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects かいがん with すなはま to identify which sandy beach.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects すなはま with うえ to create the phrase “on the sandy beach.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: を indicates the route or surface that the speaker travels across.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.why: Vないで describes the state of not wearing shoes while walking. を in うえを is not an ordinary object marker; it indicates the surface or route traveled across.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with ～ずに, the meaning “without...” remains almost the same, but the style is more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding ください turns this phrase into a request for someone not to do that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q21.kobun.tip: With movement verbs such as あるく, を can indicate a place or route traveled across, not only an object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.vi: There was an interpreter at the reception desk of the international conference venue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun phrase with the following noun for a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows that the reception desk belongs to the conference venue.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates where the person being discussed exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects the occupation with the noun ひと to form the phrase “interpreter.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the person who is present at the reception desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: いました is the polite past form of います, used for people or animals.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.why: The noun phrases gradually narrow the scope from the international conference to the venue and then to the reception desk. に states the place of existence, が marks the person who exists there, and いました completes the existence sentence for a person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is used, the sentence emphasizes the place where an action occurs, such as working at the reception desk, rather than mere existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で instead of に in an existence sentence; remember that いる・ある goes with に when saying that someone or something is somewhere.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.vi: Because my English test score was poor, my father scolded me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 英語 with テスト to form the phrase “English test.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects テスト with 点 and shows that the score belongs to the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the score as the subject being evaluated as good or bad.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: わるかった is the past form of an adjective, connected to ので to state the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: に marks the person who performs the scolding action in the passive sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: しかられました is the polite past passive form of しかる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.why: The test score phrase is the subject of the evaluation わるい. ので connects the reason to the result, while the passive sentence shows that the speaker is affected by being scolded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the basic meaning of the reason stays the same, but the expression is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget the particle に in passive sentences; the person performing the action is usually marked by に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.vi: I think it is time to summarize the content of today's meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 本日 with 会議, identifying the meeting as taking place today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects 会議 with 内容, identifying the content to be summarized.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the content affected by the verb まとめる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: まとめたい expresses a desire, and と marks the content being thought about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: おもいます is the main predicate and takes the whole preceding clause as the content of the thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.cn: Vます形 omit ます ＋ たい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.why: そろそろ modifies the whole sentence and shows that the suitable time is approaching. The meeting content is the object of まとめる, while まとめたいとおもいます makes the speaker's desire sound softer and more polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If まとめるつもりです is used, the sentence emphasizes a firmer intention instead of a thought or desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate とおもいます as only thinking in one's mind; here it also softens the expression of a desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.vi: This pond is quite deep, so be careful not to fall in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the pond is the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the comment about depth with the warning to be careful in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ように connects the negative form with guidance intended to prevent falling in.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ください creates a polite request based on the て form of the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.why: The previous clause gives the pond's feature as the reason, and then から leads to the warning. ないように expresses the purpose of preventing something unwanted, and then てください turns the warning into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with おちないでください, the sentence only asks someone not to fall, without emphasizing prevention as ように does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ないでください in every situation; ように is more suitable when describing a measure to avoid a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.vi: We are engaged in the export trade of various types of underwear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the subject of the activity being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: いろいろな modifies the noun したぎ that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects underwear with the exported content and creates a modifying noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: A dictionary-form verb comes before a noun to modify the following noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects 貿易 with しごと, showing the type of work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: を marks work as the object of しています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: しています describes an activity or job that is currently being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.why: The sentence places several modifying parts before しごと: quantity, the exported item, and the trade field. Then しごとを makes it the object of しています, expressing the meaning of doing this work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this structure is used, the grammatical relationship is clearer: the work is exporting underwear, without emphasizing the trade field.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If shortened this way, it only means doing trade work and does not specifically mention underwear as the product.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate each の as “of,” but の in this sequence is mainly used to connect nouns into a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ N; Nの ＋ N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.vi: This shirt has no buttons at all, so it is very easy to put on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: は states that the shirt is the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the buttons as what is being discussed in the clause saying they are absent.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: ぜんぜん is used with a negative form to emphasize complete absence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ついて is the て form of つく, connected to いない to create a negative state form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: ので connects the reason to the result; いない negates the state of buttons being attached to the shirt.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: きやすい is formed from きる by removing る and adding やすい, expressing that an action is easy to perform.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので; Vます-omitます ＋ やすい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.why: The clause saying there are no buttons comes before ので to give the reason, while きやすいです is the result. The topic of the whole sentence is marked by は, while が identifies the part that is absent as ボタン.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ぜんぜん with affirmative sentences, but in this pattern it must be used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.vi: I think forcing someone to work as much as 16 hours a day is terrible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase indicates the period of time spent working.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: も follows a quantity to emphasize that the number is larger than usual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.ch.2.vi: the act of forcing someone to work
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: は marks the whole phrase はたらかせるの as the topic; の turns the act of forcing someone to work into a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: と marks the content being evaluated or thought about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: 思います is the main verb and takes the quoted content marked by と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.why: The action phrase はたらかせる is nominalized by の and then made the topic with は. The evaluation “terrible” is placed before と, and then 思います expresses the speaker's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 働いてもらう, the meaning changes to asking or having someone work, which is less forceful than the compulsory meaning of はたらかせる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.tip: Do not translate も in 16じかんも as only “also”; here it emphasizes that the quantity is excessive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形・Vた形 + のは; Aい + と + 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.vi: When I got home, it was already completely dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the destination of the action つく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ついた is the past form of つく and modifies とき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: には marks a point in time and adds emphasis to the time reference.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks 日 as the subject of the state of being dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: くれていました describes a state that had formed and still existed at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.why: The time of getting home is placed before ときには as the reference point. The state of darkness uses ていました because it had already happened or was still present when the speaker got home.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If には is omitted and only とき is used, the sentence simply states an ordinary time and has less emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse くれる in 暮れる with a giving-and-receiving verb; here it only refers to sunset or becoming dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.tokens.11.m: was; a state that had continued
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q7.kobun.cn: Vた・V辞書形 + とき; N + のとき; Vている・Vていた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.vi: I heard that the thief who stole 300 million yen from the bank had been arrested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the stolen money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The money phrase is the object that was stolen, even though を is omitted in the modifying clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The clause ぬすんだ comes before and modifies 泥棒, identifying which thief it was.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the thief as the subject of the arrest.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: つかまった is the main predicate and describes the thief entering a state of being arrested.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです comes at the end of the sentence to report information that was heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.why: The phrase ぬすんだどろぼう is a clause modifying the noun 泥棒, so the verb comes before the noun. Then どろぼうが becomes the subject of つかまった, while そうです turns the whole sentence into reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: When そうだ means appearance, it usually follows the linking form of a word that shows a sign or appearance, and it does not mean “I heard that” as it does in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.tip: A modifying clause in Japanese comes before the noun, so ぬすんだ is not placed after どろぼう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.vi: There are also quite many days in winter when the temperature falls below 0 degrees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents winter as the topic for comparison or comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the result or level reached in the structure になる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: なる describes a change to the state of being below 0 degrees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: も is attached to 日 to include days with this feature in the scope of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: おおいです is the main predicate and comments on the number of days.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.why: れいどいかに なる form a clause modifying ひ, meaning days when the temperature falls below 0 degrees. も adds these days to the comment, while おおいです is the predicate of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If より低い is used, the sentence compares the temperature with another reference point instead of describing a change to a level below 0 degrees.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.tip: With になる, the new level or state usually comes before it with に; を is not used in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t93-q9.kobun.cn: N・Aな + に + なる; Aい + です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.vi: This is the piano that my father chose for me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the object being introduced as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の shows ownership or a connection with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: ために indicates the person who benefits from choosing the piano.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the person who performs the action of choosing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: This clause modifies ピアノ, while くれた shows that the action benefited the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: です concludes that the object being introduced is a piano.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.why: The clause ちちがえらんでくれた comes before ピアノ to modify the piano. ために identifies the beneficiary, while が identifies the father as the person who performed the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If changed to 選んでもらった, the focus shifts to the speaker receiving help with choosing the piano.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand くれる as simply “give”; in this structure, it emphasizes that the action benefits the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.vi: I ran from the station so that I would not be late for work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place or time at which being late is considered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.ch.1.vi: so as not to be late
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: Vないように expresses the purpose of avoiding an unwanted situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: から indicates the starting point of the running action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: はしりました is the main predicate and uses the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.why: かいしゃに identifies the place to reach on time, while おくれないように states the purpose of running. えきから adds the starting point, and then はしりました completes the main action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with this, the sentence emphasizes a more deliberate purpose, while ように is usually used for moving toward or avoiding a state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern only means not doing an action; it does not directly express purpose like ように.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ように when expressing the purpose of avoiding something; use a negative form such as おくれないように.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q10.kobun.cn: Vない形＋ように; V辞書形・Vない形＋ように
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.vi: For women, working while raising children is very difficult.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.sk: N が + Vます omit ます + ながら、＋ N を + V辞書形 + のは + Aなです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject who both works and raises children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: ながら connects two actions that happen at the same time; the main action is in the following part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being raised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: の turns the verb phrase into a noun, while は makes the whole activity of raising children the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: たいへんです is the predicate that evaluates how difficult the activity is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.cn: Vます omit ます＋ながら; V辞書形・Vない形・Vた形＋のは
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.why: 働きながら states the accompanying action, while 育てるのは turns raising children into the topic to be evaluated. The particle を identifies children as the object of 育てる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ながらも is used, the sentence has a contrastive meaning, such as “even though she works, she still raises children.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern lists typical actions and does not emphasize that the two actions happen at the same time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q12.kobun.tip: ながら must attach to the verb stem without ます, so use はたらきながら instead of はたらくながら.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.vi: I thought there was no one as good as him, so I married him.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: ほど sets him as the level used for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes the group of good people the range for denying existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: と marks the quoted content of the thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: おもって connects the thought with the marriage action that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: けっこんしました is the main action in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.why: かれほどいいひとはいない creates a negative comparison, meaning that no one is as good as him. The thought comes before と, and then 思って connects the reason or decision with the marriage action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If ほど is replaced with のように, the sentence only says that someone is like him. It does not stress the highest degree in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: だけ means only and narrows the range. It does not create a negative comparison like ほど.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.tip: The pattern Nほど～ない must have a negative predicate; removing いない loses the meaning “no one is as good.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q13.kobun.cn: N＋ほど＋～ない; 普通形＋と思う／と思って
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects daughter with the marriage event and shows possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the event that has been decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: きまった expresses that the decision has been settled; んですよ is used to announce and emphasize the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: This is a congratulatory phrase used in response to good news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ございます makes the congratulations formal and polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.why: In the announcement, 娘の結婚 is the subject of what has been decided, and が marks that subject. んですよ adds an explanatory tone, while the reply おめでとうございます is a polite formula suitable for good news.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If this expression is used, the focus changes to relief or happiness about a good result, not a direct congratulations.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression is used to wish a sick person a quick recovery, so it does not fit news about a daughter's marriage.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.tip: Do not use おめでとうございます to congratulate someone who is sick; this phrase is for happy events such as marriage, graduation, or birthdays.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q14.kobun.cn: Vた普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな＋んです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.vi: Many people who work in Tokyo live in the suburbs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: には marks the place presented as the range of existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the place toward which the commuting or traveling is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: かよう comes before ひとたち to modify the group of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject of the action of living.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: たくさん modifies the number of people living there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: すんでいます expresses the state of living or residing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.why: The location is introduced first with には, and then the clause かよう modifies ひとたち. The subject ひとたちが performs the predicate すんでいます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Using へ emphasizes the direction of commuting to Tokyo rather than a fixed destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes people who live in Tokyo, not people who work or commute to Tokyo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may place たくさん after the verb, but in this sentence たくさん comes before すんでいます to modify the number of people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.vi: I hear that the police are currently investigating the cause of the traffic accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: いま indicates the time when the action is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates where the investigation is taking place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being investigated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: しらべている is the ている form and describes an action in progress.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: そうです comes at the end of the sentence to pass on information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.why: The time and place come before the object of the investigation. しらべている shows that the investigation is in progress, while そうです turns all the previous information into reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: This means that the investigation seems to be happening based on a guess or signs, and is not necessarily information heard from someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: The question form asks again about reported information instead of stating it as reported information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.tip: Do not confuse そうです, which reports information, with そうです, which means “seems.” After a verb in the plain form, this pattern usually reports 聞.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ（丁寧形:そうです）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.vi: The new stereo has very good bass.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: あたらしい comes before ステレオ to modify the stereo.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the stereo as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: ひくい modifies おと and describes sound with a low pitch.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks sound as the thing being judged positively.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: すごく modifies いい to increase the degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: いいです is the predicate commenting on the quality of the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.why: The sentence makes ステレオ the topic, then identifies its sound with おとが. The two adjectives come before nouns to form modifying phrases, while すごく modifies the evaluation いいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: とても also means very, but its tone is more neutral and formal than すごく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: も shows that the sound is also good, in addition to another feature already mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use いいな to modify おと; the adjective いい must change to いい音, without adding な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.vi: This test was especially easy, so it may be okay.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: こんどの modifies テスト and identifies which test it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents this test as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: とくに emphasizes how easy the test was.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason in the first clause with the conclusion in the second; だった is the past form of the adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: だいじょうぶ is the content being guessed in the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: かもしれない comes at the end of the sentence to express possibility without making a firm statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason with ので, while the second gives an uncertain conclusion with かもしれない. とくに comes before the adjective to limit and emphasize the degree of ease.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: から also gives a reason, but more directly and strongly than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: でしょう expresses a well-founded prediction or hopes that the listener will agree, with a stronger tone than かもしれない.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.tip: With the adjective な, な must be used before ので, while だったので is used for the past form as in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹＋な・N＋な ＋ ので; V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹・N ＋ かもしれない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.vi: He does everything with great enthusiasm, so he will quickly become good at it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes him the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: なんでも refers to anything he actively does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb that modifies やる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the cause in the first clause with the result in the second clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: すぐ modifies なる and shows the time needed to reach the new state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: に marks the state reached after なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: なる is the main predicate; んですよ adds an explanatory and emphatic tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.why: なんでも states the broad range of what he does, while ねっしんに describes how he does it. The cause clause uses やるので, followed by すぐじょうずになる to express the result achieved quickly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: Without よ, the sentence is still explanatory, but it has less emphasis for the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.tip: With なる, the target state uses に: 上手になる, not 上手をなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q19.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹＋な・N＋な ＋ ので; Aな語幹＋に ＋ なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.vi: I am checking now whether this river is safe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the river as the object being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: か turns the adjective into the content to be determined in an indirect question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: どうか combines with か to express whether something is true or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: ています describes an action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.why: あんぜんかどうか is the complete content being checked and comes before the verb しらべる. かどうか creates an indirect question with two possibilities, true or not true, while ています emphasizes the ongoing process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If only あんぜんか is used, the sentence usually needs context or a following part; かどうか clearly expresses whether it is safe or not.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily add な before かどうか with the adjective な; here, あんぜんかどうか is used, not あんぜんなかどうか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ かどうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.vi: An entrance ceremony will be held, so please prepare chairs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the event being held.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason in the first clause with the request in the second clause; おこないます is the polite form of おこなう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the item that needs to be prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: Vてください is used to politely ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.why: The event is stated as the object of おこないます. This clause gives the reason with から, and the request then uses よういしてください to state what needs to be prepared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective than から.
