default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: This changes a direct request into a polite question asking someone to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form おこなうから in a sentence that keeps a polite style; おこないますから fits してください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から（丁寧形：Vます・です＋から）; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.vi: The road is slippery because of the rain, so please be careful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: で shows the cause that makes the road slippery.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject that has the slippery state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: やすい follows the verb form with ます removed to show a quality that makes something easy to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: なっています shows that it has become this way, while から connects it to the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: てください creates a polite request or reminder.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.why: The cause phrase comes first, followed by the subject and the road's state. から connects the cause with the reminder at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the sentence still gives a reason, but sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use を after あめ when saying that rain is the cause; the cause here goes with で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.vi: Because my friend will come, I went to the airport to pick them up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the person who performs the action of coming.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause clause with the speaker's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: へ shows the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: に attaches to the form with ます removed to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: いきました is the main predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.why: The clause about the friend coming is placed first to give the reason. へ shows the destination, while に after むかえ shows the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If ために is used, the purpose is emphasized more formally than with に after the form with ます removed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q22.kobun.tip: With the pattern Vます形語幹＋に行く, do not keep ます before に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.vi: When taking a plane, everyone is worried at first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the means of transport or the object that the speaker boards.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: とき attaches after a verb to show when the main action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: は makes the initial time the topic of comparison or comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: でも after a question word creates the broad meaning everyone or anyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.why: The phrase のるとき identifies the time, while さいしょは limits the comment to the initial stage. だれでも gives the subject the general meaning of everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If you say のるときは, the focus is on the whole time of flying, not only the beginning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.kobun.tip: だれでも is not a question; in a statement, it means everyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q23.tokens.2.m: to get on (an airplane, train, or vehicle)
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.vi: “Please take this copy to the principal’s office.” “Yes, I understand.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.sk: この N を + N に + Vてください。 + Polite reply
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the thing being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the thing that is requested to be transferred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the thing is received or its destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the verb with ください to form a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: ください completes the polite request pattern Vてください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: This is an independent reply that politely shows acceptance of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.why: The first sentence states the thing to be transferred and the receiving place, then ends with a request. The second sentence is an independent turn used to confirm that the request has been received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If you reply with お願いします, the speaker is asking the other person to do it, not confirming that they understand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use どういたしまして as a reply to a request; this expression is mainly used after someone says thank you.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.vi: Because a strange person was looking inside my house, I reported it to the police.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: へんな modifies the noun for the person that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person performing the action of looking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects うち with the following noun to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the area or place toward which the action of looking is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ている indicates an action in progress, while ので connects that situation to the reason for reporting it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the recipient of the information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.ch.6.n: しらせました is the main predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.why: The clause about looking inside the house states the event and reason first. Then けいさつにしらせました expresses the action of reporting it. に marks the place or person receiving the information, not the place where the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason sounds more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q25.kobun.tip: With しらせる, the recipient of the information usually goes with に, not を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.vi: Because the ship shook violently, everyone felt sick.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject experiencing the shaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb ひどく modifies ゆれた and shows the degree of shaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause to the result and follows the past plain form of the verb, ゆれた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: みんな is the subject of the uncomfortable state in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the noun that is the subject of the adjective わるく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective わるい changes to わるく to connect with なりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: なりました expresses a change of state and combines with わるく to form わるくなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first, followed by the result. わるい uses the form わるく to connect with なる and express that the mood changed to a bad state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing ので with から still states the cause, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If わるくしました is used, it means that someone made the mood become bad, not that it changed state by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use わるいなりました, but the adjective ending い must change to わるく before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・ Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.vi: I have never been to Mount Fuji.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.sk: N は + Number of times も + N へ + Vた + ことがありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes わたし the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いちども goes with a negative form to emphasize that the number of times is zero.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action いった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: Vたこと turns the experience into a noun, while が marks the content negated by ありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ありません completes the negative experience pattern Vたことがありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.why: The destination comes before the experience phrase. いちども combines with the negative form to mean never, not even once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to あります, the sentence says that the speaker has been there before.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern refers to something that has still not been done up to now. It does not emphasize past experience like たことがありません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.tip: いちども must be used with a negative form; do not use it with an affirmative sentence to say that something happened once.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q4.kobun.cn: Vた + ことがありません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.vi: May in Japan is a season when the greenery is very beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects にほん with 5がつ to form the phrase “May in Japan.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes 5がつ the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has the feature うつくしい in the modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: うつくしい modifies きせつ to form a phrase describing a season when the trees are very beautiful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: です ends the noun sentence and identifies 5月 as a season with the feature stated earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.why: The phrase にほんの 5がつ identifies the time and scope. The clause みどりがうつくしい comes before きせつ to modify the noun きせつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If は is used after みどり, it becomes an independent statement about the greenery or trees, and does not directly modify きせつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: うつくしくて is used to connect to another clause, so it cannot naturally come before the noun きせつ as it does here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily omit the particle が in the phrase みどりがうつくしい, which removes the subject of the adjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.vi: The important items have been put away in the desk drawer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: だいじな is a na-adjective ending in な that comes before a noun もの to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes もの the topic, while the object's location is stated afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrases の connect the desk to the drawer, and then the drawer to なか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に shows the place where something is kept, and いれて is the て form used to connect with あります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: Vてあります describes the result of an intentional action that is still being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.why: The place where the object is kept comes before the verb. The pattern Vてあります emphasizes that the object is in the state of having been placed there by someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 入れています is used, the subject is carrying out the action of putting something away, without emphasizing the arranged result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Vておきます means doing something in advance or as preparation, while Vてあります describes a result that already exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.kobun.tip: Do not translate あります simply as “have”; in Vてあります, it only describes the resulting state of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q6.tokens.9.n: the て form of the verb
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.vi: I threw a ball, and the window glass broke.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks ボール as the object being thrown.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: たら connects a condition or an event that occurs after the action なげた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects まど with ガラス and identifies the type of glass being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks ガラス as the thing affected and broken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: われて is the て form of われる, connecting the broken state with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: Vてしまいました describes an event that has been completed and often carries a feeling of regret or something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.why: The throwing action comes first as the condition or cause leading to the result. ガラス goes with が because it is the thing that broke, not a person who intentionally broke it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vると is used, the result is presented as something certain or automatic, with less emphasis on a specific event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If しまい is omitted, the sentence only says that the glass broke, without the feeling of an accident or regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を with ガラス, but with われる, the broken object usually becomes the subject and goes with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q7.kobun.cn: Vた + ら; Vて + しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.vi: I checked carefully, but there does not seem to be anything strange.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies しらべました and shows the degree of checking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: が connects two clauses with a slight shift from the checking to the comment that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: べつに usually goes with a negative form to deny that there is anything noticeable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: へんな is a na-adjective ending in な that comes before ところ to modify it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: は sets ところ as the area being commented on and combines with the negative form at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: ようです expresses a judgment based on the observed situation, while よ makes the statement softer and directs it toward the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.why: が connects the checked information with the conclusion. へんなところ is a noun phrase, while ないようです comes at the end to state that there seems to be nothing unusual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: そうです often relies on appearance or direct signs, while ようです is more about guessing from the situation observed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: わけではありません is used for limited negation and does not have the meaning of guessing found in ないようです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.tip: べつに usually needs to be used with a negative form; it should not be used alone to simply mean “especially.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + ようだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.vi: No matter what you ask him to do, he cannot do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the person who is assigned or asked to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content of the causative action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: させても is the causative form combined with ても, meaning “even if he is told to do something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: だめ describes an unsuccessful or unacceptable result; なんです is used to explain and emphasize.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.why: かれに is the person affected by the causative action, while なにを is what he is asked to do. The clause させても presents a concession, and then だめなんです concludes that the result is still unacceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is replaced with it, the meaning becomes “be allowed to do,” which is opposite to the inability or ineffectiveness expressed by だめです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern also expresses permission and does not carry the sense that something is unacceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake てもいい for “even if he does it, it is okay,” but in this sentence てもだめ means “even if he does it, it is not okay.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.tokens.4.m: make someone do, force someone to do
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t94-q9.kobun.cn: Vて形 + も + だめだ／だめなんです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.vi: Yesterday, my grandfather suddenly went to the hospital because he was ill.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase comes first to set the time for the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the person who experienced going to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the cause that led to the hospital admission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: きゅうに modifies the verb and shows that the action happened unexpectedly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate, using the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.why: The time is stated first, followed by the subject, the cause, and the unexpected manner of the action. The past predicate comes at the end to complete the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 病気になって is used, the sentence emphasizes the process of becoming ill before going to the hospital.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q1.kobun.tip: で in びょうきで shows the cause, not the place where the hospital admission happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.vi: When I was young, I often argued with my younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This time phrase sets the time for the whole event, while の connects 子供 with ころ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: よく modifies the action that follows and shows how often it happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: と identifies the person who took part or interacted in the argument.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun けんか as the object of しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: しました is the polite past form of する and ends the action けんかをする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.why: The time phrase comes first to set the background, and then よく shows the frequency. The fixed pattern けんかをする uses を for the action and と for the person involved in the interaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is used, it is easily understood as scolding or one-way action toward the younger brother, so it is less natural than と in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 話をしました, the meaning changes from arguing to talking with the younger brother.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に after the person they are talking to, but for a two-way interaction such as けんかする, と is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.vi: Recently, CDs have become very popular, so records hardly sell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は sets the present period as the topic of comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks CDs as the item that occurs in large numbers in the first clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: おおくて is the て form of the adjective おおい, connecting a reason or condition to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes レコード the comparison topic against CDs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: ほとんど modifies 売れません and shows that something happens very rarely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: うれません is the polite negative form of 売れる, meaning that something cannot be sold or does not sell well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.cn: Aい omit い ＋ くて
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.why: The first clause states that there are many CDs, and then the form て connects it to the result in the following clause. は in レコードは creates a contrast with CDs, while ほとんど reduces the degree of the negative action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If て is replaced with ので, the cause-and-effect relationship becomes clearer and softer, but it must be connected in the form おおいので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Using あまりうれません also means that something does not sell much, but it usually has the meaning “not ... very much,” which is weaker than ほとんど.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse おおくて with おおいで; an adjective ending in い changes い into くて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.vi: I have already finished almost all of my homework, so I feel relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the homework the topic of the completed state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: もう adds a time meaning and shows that the homework has already been done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ほとんど modifies the action phrase that follows and shows the degree to which it has been done.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: やってしまいましたから consists of Vてしまいました and expresses completion, while から connects the reason to the conclusion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: あんしんです is the conclusion and states the relieved feeling caused by the previous clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.why: The homework is presented as the topic, and then もう and ほとんど show the time and degree of completion. The Vてしまいましたから phrase gives the reason, while あんしんです is the resulting state or feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is replaced with ので, the reason sounds softer and more objective, but the main meaning remains that the homework is almost finished, so the speaker feels relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If もう is replaced with まだ, the meaning becomes “still not,” which is opposite to the idea of being almost finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate から as “from,” but in this structure から follows a clause and shows the reason “because ... , so ...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.tokens.4.m: do; the て form of やる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q13.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます／しまいました ＋ から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.vi: The luggage gets in the way when sitting, so please put it on the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The verb before とき modifies the time when the event occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: とき indicates the time when sitting becomes inconvenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.2.vi: because it gets in the way
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the reason to the request to put the luggage on the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the luggage the topic of the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: の connects the shelf with the noun うえ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: に marks the place where the luggage is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: The form て connects the verb with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: ください comes at the end of the sentence to express a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.why: The sentence first states the situation, then uses から to give the reason for the request. The luggage is marked as the topic by は, while に shows where to put it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので still gives a reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に in the wrong position; for a place of putting or moving to, に comes directly after the place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・N/Aな＋です＋から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.vi: Yesterday I lost the entrance key, so I was really troubled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks yesterday as the time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the entrance with the key.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the key as the object that was lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the action of losing something with the resulting troubled state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: ほんとうに modifies the degree of the troubled state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The polite past-tense verb is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.why: The sentence puts the time reference first, followed by the affected object and the action that caused the result. The form て at なくして connects the reason with the state こまりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: Using ので states the cause more clearly and does not merely connect two consecutive actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q15.kobun.tip: Do not mechanically translate て as “and”; in this sentence なくして means “because I lost it, I became troubled.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.vi: The hotel fee is high, so I am worried about whether I have enough money.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the hotel fee as the subject that has the feature of being expensive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the high price with the content of the worry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks money as the subject being considered for whether it is enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: か turns the preceding clause into the content of an indirect question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: どうか combines with か to create the pattern “whether ... or not.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: しんぱいです is the predicate that states the speaker’s feeling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.why: The clause saying that the hotel fee is high comes first and gives the reason through ので. The thing being worried about is placed in the indirect question clause かどうか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with かもしれない, the sentence expresses the possibility that the money is not enough rather than worry about whether it is enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.tip: With nouns and な adjectives, な must be added before ので, but い adjectives such as たかい remain unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q16.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・N/Aな＋な＋ので; V普通形＋かどうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.vi: I plan to stop in Paris first and then go to London.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: さきに shows the order of the action that will happen first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place of the stop, while the form て connects it to the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: それから modifies the order of the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: へ marks the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun よてい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.ch.5.n: よていです acts as the predicate and shows a planned schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.why: The sentence arranges two destinations in order: stop in Paris first, then go to London. The verb いく comes directly before よてい to modify the plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vたあとで is used, the sentence emphasizes that going to London happens after stopping in Paris.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q17.kobun.tip: へ shows the direction of travel, while に in パリに寄る marks the place of the stop.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.vi: When I met my middle school friend again after a long time, I saw that they had become much prettier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: に changes the phrase 久しぶり into an adverbial phrase showing when the person was met again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the school level to the noun とき.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: ときの modifies friend and means a friend from middle school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the person who was met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The form たら connects a condition or time with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: すっかり modifies the degree of the change in appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective な changes to the form に to show the state achieved after the change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.7.n: The form て of なります connects the change to いた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.ch.8.n: いた shows that the beautiful state already existed when they met again.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.why: The clause あったら sets the point of “meeting again,” and the sentence then describes the result of the change. The structure Aなに なる shows becoming beautiful, while ていた shows that this state had formed before the speaker saw the person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is used, the sentence only states the time of meeting and does not emphasize a condition or the situation in which the change was noticed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a gradual change or a result achieved after a process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.tip: The adjective な must change to に before なる; do not say きれいなになる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q18.kobun.cn: Vた形・Aい・N/Aな＋だった＋ら; Aな＋に＋なる; Vて＋いる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.vi: “I am going on a trip starting tomorrow.” “Have a safe trip.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: から shows the starting time of the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: へ marks the direction or purpose of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: いきます is the predicate of the first statement, and the closing quotation mark ends the quotation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks 気 in the fixed expression 気をつける; the form て connects the warning with the farewell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: いっていらっしゃい is said when seeing someone off and wishing them a safe return.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.why: The first statement gives the starting time and direction. The reply uses 気をつけて as a warning, then uses the pattern for seeing someone off, いっていらっしゃい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: This is what the person leaving says to ask permission or announce that they are leaving, not what the person staying says when seeing someone off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a greeting for customers entering a shop, so it is not suitable for seeing someone off.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q19.kobun.tip: Do not separate 気をつけて into the separate meanings of its words; the whole expression has the fixed meaning “be careful.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.vi: In summer, sandals are indeed cooler than shoes, aren't they?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は introduces summer as the topic being compared.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects サンダル with ほう and forms a phrase showing the side or choice that is preferred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: ほうが marks the object seen as having the stronger degree in the comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: より names the object used as the basis for comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: すずしい is the adjective predicate, while ですね adds a mild confirming tone and seeks agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.why: The sentence puts summer first as the topic, then names two objects for comparison. The phrase サンダルのほうが is the side rated higher, while くつより is the comparison point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If only より is used without ほうが, the sentence can still make a comparison, but the contrast between the two sides is less clear.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with this pattern changes the meaning to “not as ... as the object mentioned.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q2.kobun.tip: English learners may mistake より for a word meaning “more” and forget that the object rated higher usually goes with ほうが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.vi: Because the instructions for using the machine were very good, I understood them clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects this noun to the way of using it and creates a modifying phrase for what follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.ch.1.vi: the instructions for how to use it
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the content judged to be good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: とても modifies よかった and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: ので connects the reason to the result; よかった is the past form of the adjective いい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: よく modifies わかりました and shows the degree of understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.why: A long noun phrase acts as the subject, followed by よかったので to give the reason. The result, わかりました, comes after the comma and is modified by the adverb よく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.tip: English learners may confuse ので with the way of giving the reason for a noun, but with adjectives な and nouns, な must be used before ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q20.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.vi: Let's compete at the sports field to see which side is faster.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the object being asked about in the comparison clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: か turns clause はやい into an indirect question and makes it the content of the competition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: で shows the place where activity きょうそう takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the activity that is proposed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.ch.4.n: しよう is the volitional form of する, used to invite or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.why: The clause はやいか states what needs to be determined and comes before the main activity. The place uses で, while きょうそう is the object of しよう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If かどうか is used, it only asks whether something is fast and no longer means choosing which side is faster.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.tip: Do not use に to show where the competition takes place; because the activity happens at a place, use で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q21.kobun.cn: 疑問詞・文普通形 ＋ か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.vi: The lesson starts now. Please open page 49 of the textbook.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object being started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects テキスト to the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the page that needs to be opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: て connects the action ひらく to the request pattern ください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: ください follows the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.why: The first sentence announces the start of the lesson. The second identifies the material and page to open, then uses てください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the request sounds softer and more tentative.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q22.kobun.tip: Do not use the dictionary form before ください; a request must use the verb in the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.vi: He does not study English at all, so he cannot speak it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes him the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: ちっとも emphasizes a zero degree and is used with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the language being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: しないんだから gives the reason with the speaker's feeling that it is obvious.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: はなせる modifies はず and creates content that should supposedly be possible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: はずがない expresses a strong negative conclusion based on a reason or evidence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.ch.6.n: ない completes the pattern はずがない and denies the possibility stated before it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.why: The first part gives the basis for the negative conclusion and is connected by んだから. はなせる comes before はず to show possibility, and then はずがない strongly denies that possibility.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If わけがない is used instead, the negative meaning is also strong, but it focuses more on the firm conclusion that the situation is impossible.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: If かもしれない is used instead, the sentence becomes a much weaker guess about what may happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.tip: ちっとも must always be used with a negative form; it is not used with an affirmative verb in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ んだから; V可能形 ＋ はずがない
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.vi: Enough food has already been prepared, so it is fine to eat as much as you want.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the food the topic being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: じゅうぶん modifies 用意してあります and shows the degree of preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb 用意する with あります to express a state that has been prepared in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the reason to the result; あります indicates a state of existing or being maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: いくら modifies the clause たべても and shows an unlimited degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: ても connects a concessive condition to the conclusion だいじょうぶです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.why: The first part states that the food has already been prepared and uses から to give the reason. いくら combines with ても to express an unlimited concessive meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If どれだけ〜ても is used instead, the meaning of being allowed to have any amount is emphasized more in terms of degree or quantity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.tip: てある emphasizes a state intentionally prepared by someone, rather than simply food that exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.tokens.4.n: verb する in the て form
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q24.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ある; Vて・Aいくて・Aなでも・Nでも ＋ も
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.vi: I will call you right away, so please sit in this chair and wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: すぐ modifies よびます and indicates the time just before calling.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the explanation to the instruction that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects こちら to the noun いす and identifies the designated chair.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the place or object toward which the sitting posture is directed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: かけて is the て form of かける and connects the action of sitting to the request おまちください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: お＋the connective form＋ください creates a polite request; おまちください means please wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.why: から connects the advance notice to the instruction for the listener. に identifies the chair to sit in, and the two actions かけて and おまちください are connected by the て form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If 座ってください is used instead, the request is more direct and does not use the expression 掛ける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If お待ちいただけますか is used instead, the sentence becomes more formal and sounds more like a request for permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.tip: Do not translate かける mechanically as “hang”; in the context of a chair, いすにかける means sit down.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q25.kobun.cn: Vます ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.vi: I thought it might not be okay, and as expected, I really lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: だめ is an な adjective that becomes the content predicted in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: かもしれないと marks the quoted content of the thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: おもっていたら combines the past ている form with たら to indicate the time when an event occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: やっぱり modifies the result that follows and shows that it matches the earlier prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: まけて uses the て form to connect the main verb to しまった.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: しまった describes a completed event, often with a feeling of regret or something happening unintentionally.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.why: The predicted content is placed before とおもう as the object of thought. After おもっていたら, the actual result appears; やっぱり connects that result to the initial prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern often emphasizes an event that happens immediately after the speaker realizes or thinks something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 結局 is used, the sentence only emphasizes the final result and does not clearly show that it matches the prediction as やっぱり does.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate たら as always meaning if, but in this sentence おもっていたら means while or just after thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.tokens.4.m: if one is; while one is
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ かもしれない; Vた形 ＋ ら; Vて形 ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.vi: That area is under construction now, so it is dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes the place あそこ the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: いま identifies the time of the state being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the construction state to the conclusion that it is dangerous through a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: きけん is the predicate, while よ emphasizes the information the speaker wants the listener to notice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.why: The sentence first states the place and time, then gives the reason that construction is in progress. から connects the reason to the conclusion that the following clause is dangerous.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Replacing から with ので makes the way of stating the reason softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Replacing it with が changes the cause relationship into a contrast or opens into an unfinished idea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から as a separate word, but it must connect directly after the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな/Nだ ＋ から; N・Aな ＋ ですから
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.vi: Because the wind was too strong, the umbrella broke.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the wind as the subject that creates the strong state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective つよかった to show a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: つよかった is the past form of the adjective and combines with ので to state a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the umbrella as the object affected by the change in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: こわれて uses the て form to connect the broken state with しまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: しまいました shows that the event has been completed and suggests regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.why: The first clause gives the strong wind as the cause, while the second clause gives the result affecting the umbrella. ので connects the reason in a softer way, and てしまう emphasizes the unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and conversational.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If しまいました is omitted, the sentence only reports that the umbrella broke and reduces the sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that the adjective い must first change to the past form つよかった before connecting with ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな/Nな ＋ ので; Vて形 ＋ しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.vi: There is no time left, so hurry up.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: もう shows that, at the present time, there is no time left.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks time as something that exists or does not exist in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: ありませんから gives the reason for the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: いそいでください uses the てください form to make a polite request or ask someone for help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.why: The sentence puts the reason, that there is no time left, first and then states the request. から connects the reason with a polite command, while てください makes the request less forceful.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern changes the direct request into advice that the person should hurry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern means that we should hurry together, rather than asking the listener to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use the plain form before ください, but the verb needs to change to the て form, such as いそいでください.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな/Nだ ＋ から; Vて形 ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.vi: Because my friend has moved to a new apartment, I plan to visit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the friend as the person who moved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: あたらしい directly modifies アパート, which comes immediately after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: に marks the destination of the action ひっこした.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ひっこしたので states that moving house is the reason for the plan in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: に attaches to the form without ます あそび to show the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: いくつもりです expresses an intention that the speaker already has.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.why: The sentence first states what happened to the friend and the destination, then uses ので to explain the reason for the plan. The form あそびに + いく shows the purpose, while つもりです puts the intention at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes an intention that is still being formed or a softer way of speaking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a schedule or arranged plan more than a personal intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily mistake に in あそびにいく for a place marker, but here it shows the purpose of going to visit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな/Nな ＋ ので; Vます-stem ＋ に ＋ 行く; V辞書形 ＋ つもりだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q8.kobun.vi: Hokkaido is in the north of Japan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes Hokkaido the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects Japan with the north, while に shows the location where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is a predicate showing the existence or location of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q8.kobun.why: The sentence puts the place being discussed first, then uses の to identify the location and に to show where it exists. あります ends the sentence by saying where a place is located.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If に is replaced with で, it usually changes to the place where an action happens rather than showing a location of existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use で instead of に when saying where a place is located.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.vi: “I lost my wallet.” “That is not good.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the wallet as the object affected by the action of losing it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: なくして is the て form of なくす and connects the action of losing it with the following pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: ～てしまいました describes a completed action, often with a sense of regret or something unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: それは makes the event just heard the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: いけませんね is a comment showing concern or sympathy for the listener’s situation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.why: The first sentence states the object first, then uses the て form to connect it with しまいました, creating a pattern that expresses an unintended action or regret. The second sentence makes that event the topic and gives a sympathetic response.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If only the ordinary past form is used, it simply reports that the event happened and has a weaker sense of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the reply emphasizes that the situation is difficult or serious rather than simply saying “that is not good.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand しまいました as only meaning “did,” but this pattern often also suggests regret or an unintended event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t95-q9.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう／しまいます／しまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.vi: I want to carefully pass Japanese culture on to the children.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: に marks the recipient of the action of passing something on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun にほん with the following noun to show possession or belonging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the content being passed on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective な drops な and adds に to modify the verb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The form て connects the action of passing something on with the next part.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: と marks the content of the desire to be repeated in 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The final verb expresses an opinion in a soft and polite way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.why: The recipient comes before the content being passed on; this content goes with を. つたえて connects with いきたい and creates the meaning of wanting to continue the action in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used here, the sentence emphasizes that the passing on is done in advance to prepare for a certain purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence only directly expresses a desire and loses the soft tone of 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that だいじに must use に to change the adjective な into an adverb.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.vi: I’m hungry, aren’t I? Shall we eat something?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: 「が」marks the body part that is in the described state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: 「すきました」describes the state of the stomach becoming empty; 「ね」is used to gently confirm this with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: 「なにか」is the object being eaten; in casual speech, particle 「を」can be omitted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: 「ましょうか」is used to invite someone or suggest doing something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.why: The first sentence states the current condition and 「ね」creates empathy with the listener. The second sentence uses the volitional form 「ましょうか」to suggest eating together, while 「なにか」is the object of 「たべる」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「食べませんか」is used, the invitation sounds more polite and tentative, while 「食べましょうか」sounds more like a direct suggestion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may mistake 「おなかがすく」for “an empty stomach,” but the whole phrase naturally means “to be hungry.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.vi: Because I continued practicing tennis every day, I became much better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.sk: Time expression ＋ Nの ＋ Nを ＋ Vたので ＋ 副詞 ＋ Aなに ＋ なりました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This time expression shows how often the practice happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: 「の」connects 「テニス」with 「れんしゅう」and identifies the type of practice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: 「を」marks practice as the object of 「つづける」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: 「ので」connects the cause to the result; the past-form verb shows that the practice happened earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: This degree adverb modifies 「じょうず」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: 「じょうず」changes to 「じょうずに」to connect with 「なる」and show the achieved state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: 「なる」describes a change from not being good at something to being good at it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.why: The time expression and object come before the verb 「つづけた」to clarify what was practiced and for how long. 「ので」states the cause, while 「Aなに＋なる」expresses the result of becoming better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「ので」is replaced with 「から」, the reason sounds more direct and subjective; 「ので」sounds softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget that the adjective なmust use 「に」before 「なる」, so they say 「じょうずになる」rather than 「じょうずくなる」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.vi: Have you finished preparing for the trip?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」connects 「りょこう」with 「したく」and describes the preparations for the trip.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: 「は」makes the preparations the topic of the question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: 「もう」shows that something was completed before now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: 「済みましたか」asks whether the preparations have been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.why: 「りょこうのしたく」is a noun phrase meaning the preparations for the trip, made the topic with 「は」. 「もう」combines with a past-tense verb to ask whether they have been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If the question uses 「まだですか」, the focus shifts to confirming that it is still unfinished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand 「すむ」only as “to live,” but in 「したくがすむ」it means that the preparations are finished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.vi: I plan to meet a friend at a coffee shop at around 8 tonight.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: This time expression shows the planned time of the meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: でindicates the place where the meeting will happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: にindicates the person the subject will meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies 予定and creates the meaning of a plan to meet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: 予定ですexpresses a plan or a fixed schedule.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.why: The time, place, and object components come before the verb in that order. The dictionary-form verb modifies 予定to describe a plan for the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If つもりですis used, it emphasizes personal intention more, while 予定ですusually suggests a schedule or a specific plan.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.tip: The place of the meeting uses で, while the person being met uses に; these two particles cannot be exchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q13.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ 予定だ／Nの ＋ 予定だ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.vi: “Excuse me, could you finish this work by tomorrow?” “Yes, I understand.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: がconnects the opening apology to the request that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: までにindicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: をmarks the object of やる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: やってis the てform used to connect with いただけませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: いただけませんかcreates a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: 承知しましたis a polite predicate used to accept a request or confirm understanding.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.why: までにsets the time limit, while をmarks the work to be done. The てform connects the verb やるwith いただけませんかto create a respectful request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the request becomes more direct and less formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is still a polite request, but it has a more casual tone than いただけませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate までにas “by the day,” but this pattern emphasizes that the task must be completed before that deadline.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q14.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ いただけませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.vi: Since it is your child’s birthday, I think I will send a toy as a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: のconnects こどもwith the noun for birthday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: なのでconnects a noun-based reason to the action in the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: をmarks the item being sent as a gift.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: てconnects the action of sending with あげる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The volitional form あげようcombines with とto create the content of 思います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: と思いますexpresses the speaker’s thought or intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.why: The two phrases のrespectively show the relationship between the friend and the child and between the child and the birthday. なのでstates the reason, Vてあげるshows doing something for another person’s benefit, while the volitional form + と思いますexpresses the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If なのでis replaced with から, the reason is stated more directly and does not need the noun + なform.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: ためにusually expresses an objective purpose or cause and is less natural than なのでin this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.tip: Vてあげるis used only when the speaker does something beneficial for another person; it should not be used freely for actions done for oneself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.tokens.9.m: will give / will do something for someone
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q15.kobun.cn: N・Aな ＋ なので／Vて ＋ あげる／V意向形 ＋ と ＋ 思う
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.vi: There are many kinds of children's toys available in the nearby park.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ちかく to the noun that follows and modifies “park.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: には marks a place as the topic and adds a contrastive emphasis.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: いろいろな directly modifies the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the object as being in a state where it has already been placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.ch.4.n: おいて is the て form of おく and connects with あります in the pattern Vてあります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.ch.5.n: あります combines with Vて to describe a state created by someone's action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.why: The place is moved to the front with には, followed by the object that is already placed there. The pattern Vてあります emphasizes that the result of placing something still remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence only describes an action in progress or a current state. It does not emphasize that someone has placed something there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse Vてあります with Vてありますか, which only means simple existence, while this pattern emphasizes the result of an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the person being discussed in the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the content acted on by the verb うつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: の turns the verb うつ into a noun, while が marks that action as the subject being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: はやい is an adjective ending in い used as the predicate, and it is made polite with です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.why: The action うつ is nominalized with の so that it can be the subject with が. The adjective はやい evaluates the speed of performing that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If のは is used, the action becomes the topic for explanation or contrast instead of being the direct subject of the evaluation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.tip: Do not use を directly before はやい; first nominalize the verb with の and then use が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q17.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ のが ＋ Aい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.vi: You may freely use the objects placed on the shelf.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the objects are placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: おいて is the て form of おく and connects with ある to create the pattern Vてある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: The phrase たなにおいてある modifies もの and describes the state of the objects.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the objects that are allowed to be used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: じゆうに is an adverbial form that modifies how the objects are used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: ても connects the verb with いい to create a way of asking for or giving permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.ch.6.n: いいですよ ends the sentence and confirms that the action is allowed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.why: The clause たなにおいてある comes before もの and modifies the objects. After stating the object, the pattern Vてもいいです expresses permission.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence changes from giving permission to prohibiting the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.tip: てもいいです means that the action is allowed, not the concessive meaning “even if you do it, it is fine” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q19.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ ある; N ＋ に; Vて形 ＋ もいい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.vi: I have kept a diary since last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time から ＋ N を ＋ Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: は identifies the topic as the person writing the diary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: から marks the starting point of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of つける in the expression meaning “keep a diary.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: ている describes an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.why: きょねんから comes before the verb to state the starting point, while ています shows that the diary-writing state continues. にっきを is the object used with を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern can describe an action happening at the moment of speaking, but in this sentence it emphasizes that the action has continued since last year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with the simple past, the sentence would only say that the diary was written or that the writing happened in the past. It would no longer express continuation to the present.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may translate つける as “attach” and miss the fixed expression にっきをつける, which means “keep a diary.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.vi: Whenever I look at the sea, I always remember my childhood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being looked at.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: Vると connects a conditional clause or a situation that usually leads to the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: いつも modifies the action おもいだす and indicates repetition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: こどもの modifies ころ and identifies the time period being mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the memory being recalled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the main predicate and describes recalling something from the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.why: The clause うみをみると states a situation that happens regularly, followed by the result おもいだします. こどものころ is used as a noun phrase and takes を because it is the object of remembering.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence would focus on a one-time condition or assumption and would not emphasize a naturally repeating result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence would only state the time “when looking at the sea” and would not clearly show a regular cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q20.kobun.tip: Do not translate と as “and” in this sentence; it connects a situation with the result that usually follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.vi: I was very disappointed because I lost the last match of my student life.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase の modifies さいご and identifies the final one during student life.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: さいごの modifies しあい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the match that the speaker lost.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects a preceding cause or situation with the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: とても modifies the adjective ざんねん.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: でした is the polite past form of です, describing feelings after an event has happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.why: The phrases がくせいせいかつのさいごのしあい form a long noun phrase, in which the phrases の successively modify the noun that follows. まけて connects losing the match with feelings of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the cause-and-effect relationship would be clearer, and the sentence would sound more objective and explanatory.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, the sentence would only emphasize the time order, “after losing,” without emphasizing the cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q22.kobun.tip: Do not mistake に in 試合に負ける for a place; here, it indicates the object of winning or losing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.vi: I am going out shopping now. Shall I buy something and bring it back?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the starting point of an action that is about to happen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the purpose of going out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: でかけます is the main predicate of the first sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: なにか is the unspecified object of the action of buying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: かって is the て form of かう, connecting with きましょうか to express doing something and then bringing it back.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.ch.5.vi: shall I buy it and bring it back
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: ましょうか makes a polite offer or asks for the listener’s opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.why: The first sentence gives the time and purpose before the verb 出かける. The second sentence uses てくる to express buying something and returning with it, together with ましょうか to make an offer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vませんか is used, the sentence invites the listener to do the action together, instead of offering to do it for or on behalf of the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.tip: ましょうか usually means “Shall I do it for you?”, and does not necessarily invite the listener to do it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q23.kobun.cn: Nに + 出かける; Vて形 + くる; Vます語幹 + ましょうか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.vi: Thank you for treating me so kindly during the time we have just spent together. Not at all.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies あいだ and indicates the period of time being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the period of time as the topic of the thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: に changes the adjective な into an adverb, showing how the other person treated the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects して with いただく in a pattern expressing receiving help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: ていただく expresses that the speaker received a kind action from the other person, then connects to the thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: ありがとうございました is a polite thank-you in the past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.6.n: いいえ gently rejects the previous thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.ch.7.n: どういたしまして is a fixed response to thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.why: The period of time is given first with は, followed by a description of how the other person treated the speaker using しんせつにしていただく. The form ていただいて connects the action received with the thanks at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If used here, the sentence would mean “all right/no need anymore,” not a response to thanks.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence changes to mean “thanks to...,” and is usually used to describe a good result caused by someone’s help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ありがとう to respond to thanks, but the suitable response is どういたしまして.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.tokens.2.m: the period of time just passed
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q24.tokens.6.m: receive help; have someone kindly do something
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.vi: I have been keeping a diary since the New Year holidays this year.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.sk: N の + Time から + N を + Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects ことし with the time noun おしょうがつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.ch.1.vi: since this year’s New Year holidays
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: から indicates the starting point for keeping a diary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object of the verb つける.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the main verb with います to form the pattern ている.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: ています expresses an action that began earlier and is still continuing now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.why: から places the starting point before the object and action. にっきを is the object of つける, while つけています shows that this habit is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes that the action is continuing, unlike Vました, which only reports an action that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If V始める is used, the focus is on the starting time, without emphasizing that the action is still continuing now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q25.kobun.tip: Do not understand つける as meaning only “attach”; with 日記をつける, this verb means to record or write a diary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.vi: I heard that long ago this area stretched all the way to the other side and used to be the sea.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.sk: Time + N は + Range まで + Nだった + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A time word placed at the beginning of the sentence to identify when the event happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は identifies the area being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: It modifies the range over which the place extends.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.ch.3.vi: all the way to the other side
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: まで indicates the final limit of the range.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: だった is the past form of the noun うみだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: そうです follows a clause to show that the information was heard from another source.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.why: むかし is placed at the beginning to state the time, while は limits the topic to this area. まで expands the range, and then だったそうです combines the past form of the noun with the information-reporting pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: After the plain form, as in this sentence, it means “I heard that”; after the verb form without ます, it can instead mean “seems about to.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with this pattern, the sentence would still express an inference based on information, but the source of the information would sound less direct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily confuse そうです for reported information with そうです for appearance; look at the form directly before the pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな + だ・N + だ + そうだ
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.vi: The road was crowded, so I am sorry for making you wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.sk: N が + Vている ので + おVます形 without ます + せして + すみません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the state こんでいる and also states the cause in the preceding clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects こんで with いた to create the state of being crowded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the cause with the apology in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The form て connects the action that made someone wait with the apology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: This is an apology at the end of the sentence, directed to the person who had to wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.cn: Vている + ので; お + Vます形 without ます + せする + て
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first because of ので, while the action that made the listener wait comes directly before the apology. こんでいた describes the road as being crowded at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the cause-and-effect relationship remains, but the explanation is usually more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If お is omitted, the sentence is still understandable, but it loses the polite nuance of apologizing to someone who had to wait.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から in every situation; for a polite apology, ので usually creates a softer tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.vi: It smells so good, doesn't it? What are you cooking?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective いい directly modifies the noun におい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks what is sensed in the pattern においがする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: します combines with a noun for a sense to describe a perceived smell; ね seeks agreement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: どんな modifies a noun to ask about its type or characteristics.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the food being cooked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects つくる with いる to create the progressive form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: ているんですか asks about an ongoing situation, with a nuance of wanting to know more clearly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.why: においがする is a fixed expression for sensing a smell and is not used with を. In the question, どんな comes before りょうり, while つくっている expresses the act of cooking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If いい is omitted, the sentence only states that there is a smell and does not judge it as pleasant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If どんな料理 is replaced with 何, the question focuses more on “what someone is doing” than on the type of dish.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily say においをします, but the pattern that only expresses a smell is においがします.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.tokens.11.m: short form of の, emphasizing explanation
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q5.kobun.cn: Vて + いる + のですか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.vi: This village also got electric lights 20 years ago and became brighter.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.sk: この N にも + Time まえに + N が + Vて + Aいくなりました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: この modifies むら to identify a specific place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the place where an event occurs, while も adds the meaning “also.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The time phrase modifies まえに to form the time reference “20 years ago.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the time when the electric lights were installed.
