default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: が marks the subject that changes to a state of being on or bright.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The form て connects the state of the lights being on with the result that the village became bright.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective い changes to あかるく and then combines with なりました to express a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.cn: Aい remove い + く + なる; Vて + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.why: に comes after a place and time to identify where and when an event occurs; も adds the meaning “also.” でんとうがついて states that the lights were turned on, and then あかるくなりました states the resulting change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If あかるくなりました is replaced with あかるいです, the sentence only describes a bright state and does not express a change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern is not used with the adjective い to show a change that happens by itself; あかるくなりました is needed because the light makes the place become bright.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily keep あかるい before なる, but い must change to く: あかるくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.vi: Because there is a doll picture drawn on it, this is probably a child's handkerchief.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: 「の」 connects the noun before it with the noun 「絵」 to form a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: 「が」 marks the picture as the object being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: 「書いて」 uses the て form to connect with 「ある」, creating a pattern that describes a prepared state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: 「から」 connects the reason clause with the conclusion that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective comes before the noun 「子」 to modify the child.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: 「でしょう」 is placed at the end of the sentence to show a mild guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.why: The clause 「絵が書いてある」 states that a doll picture has been drawn on the handkerchief, and then 「から」 gives the reason for the guess. 「でしょう」 is placed at the end because the speaker is only guessing that it is a child's handkerchief.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 「そうだ」, the sentence focuses more on appearance or information heard from someone else and does not have the polite guessing nuance of 「でしょう」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily forget that 「から」must come after the entire reason clause, not only after a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q7.kobun.cn: Vて + ある; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + から; V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + でしょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.vi: Walk straight along this road for about 50 meters, and you will see a large shrine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.sk: Nを + 副詞 + Quantityぐらい + V辞書形と + Aな + Nが + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: 「この」comes before the noun 「みち」to specify which road is being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: 「を」marks the road that the speaker follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb modifies the verb 「あるく」 and shows how to walk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: 「ぐらい」shows the approximate length of the distance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: 「と」connects a condition with the natural result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: 「大きな」comes before the noun 「じんじゃ」to modify the shrine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: 「が」marks the shrine as the thing that appears in the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: 「あります」expresses the existence of an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.why: 「みちを」marks the route being followed, while 「まっすぐ」shows how to walk. The pattern 「Vると」connects walking about 50 meters with the natural result of there being a large shrine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「たら」 is used, the sentence has a more hypothetical conditional nuance, while 「と」emphasizes a result that usually occurs when the action is performed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use 「に」with a distance, but here 「50メートルぐらい」is an approximate quantity, so 「ぐらい」is used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.vi: Put important things in the drawer and lock it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: 「は」makes important things the topic of the instruction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects putting something in with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: 「を」marks the key as the object of the verb 「かける」.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The て form connects 「かける」with 「おく」, creating an action that is performed and maintained.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: 「Vておく」expresses doing something in advance or keeping that state unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.why: The topic 「だいじなものは」is handled through two consecutive actions: putting it in the drawer and then locking it. 「ておく」shows that the locking is done in advance to keep the items safe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「Vている」is used, the sentence only describes an ongoing or existing state and does not emphasize doing something in advance as preparation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t96-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate 「ておく」as only “did,” but this pattern also means doing something in advance or keeping a state unchanged.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.vi: Because the streets in Tokyo are crowded, it would be better to take the subway.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: は marks Tokyo as the topic being commented on.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject in the crowded state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: こんで is the て form of こむ and connects the state to the reason clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: ていますから gives the reason supporting the advice that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks the means of transportation chosen for use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: りようした modifies ほう and creates a phrase expressing what should be chosen.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: ほうが points to the option judged to be better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: ほうがいい expresses advice; よ makes the advice softer and more casual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.why: The clause with から places the reason before the advice. The phrase Vたほうがいい uses the past form of the verb before ほうがいい to suggest an option that should be taken.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this form is used instead, the sentence becomes advice not to use the subway.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern makes the advice stronger and gives it a sense of obligation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q1.kobun.tip: Do not translate ほうがいい mechanically as “a good direction”; the whole phrase means “it would be better to do something.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.vi: Because I heard it is an interesting movie, I definitely want to see it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective modifies the noun えいが.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: と marks the content that was heard; だ connects the noun えいが with the quoted content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason heard with the desire to watch the movie in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb that emphasizes a strong desire or request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: たい is attached to the continuative form of a verb to express the speaker’s desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.why: The phrase えいがだと聞いた states the content of the information heard, while ので turns that information into a reason. ぜひ comes before 見たい to emphasize the desire to watch it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If たぶん is used, the sentence only means “might want to watch it,” which is weaker and less determined.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If そうだ is used, the sentence can express heard information more directly, but the quotation structure changes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use たい for another person; in this sentence, 見たいです expresses the speaker’s own desire.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q10.kobun.cn: Nだと + V; Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; Vます-stem + たい
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.vi: Get off at the next station, then transfer to the bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: つぎの modifies えき and creates the phrase “the next station.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: で marks the place where the speaker gets off the train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The て form connects getting off with transferring to the bus.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に marks the means of transportation or object that the speaker transfers to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: 乗り換えてください is a polite request pattern in which てください comes at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.why: えきで indicates where to get off, and the て form connects this to the next action. に in バスに indicates the means of transportation or route being transferred to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If 取り替える is used, it means replacing or changing an object, not transferring between vehicles.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: If Vてもいいです is used, the sentence asks about or permits transferring instead of asking the listener to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.tip: Do not use を with the vehicle after 乗り換える; the vehicle being transferred to usually goes with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q11.kobun.cn: Vて + ください; Vて、V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.vi: Because someone showed me the way, I thanked them.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the object of the verb おしえて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 connects おしえる with もらった and creates a sequence of actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: もらった expresses receiving help, while ので connects the reason with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the object of いいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb いう uses the polite past form to end the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.why: The phrase おしえてもらった expresses that the speaker received help from another person. ので connects the reason before it with the act of thanking after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason remains the same, but the tone becomes more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If おかげで is used, the sentence emphasizes the good result thanks to the help, rather than simply stating the reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake もらう for the person who gives help, but in the pattern Vてもらう, the subject is the person who receives help.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q12.kobun.cn: Vて + もらう・もらった; V普通形 + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.vi: While talking with a friend, I left the store and it had already become completely dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: と indicates the person who performs the action はなす with the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: て形 connects the action of talking with いて.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ていて expresses an ongoing state and then connects it to leaving the store.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the place left in 店を出る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: たら connects a condition or time with the next action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: すっかり modifies the state of becoming dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective い changes to く to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: なって connects the change of state with いた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.ch.8.n: ていた shows that the dark state already existed at that time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.cn: Vている; Vた + ら; Aい remove い + く + なる; Vている・Vていた
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.why: ていて sets the conversation as the background, while たら points to the time just after leaving the store. すっかり adds degree to くらくなっていた and emphasizes that it was completely dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is used, the sentence only states the time of leaving the store, and the conditional nuance of たら becomes weaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If すっかり replaces もう, the sentence emphasizes that it was already dark, rather than emphasizing complete darkness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may forget to change the adjective い into the く form before なる: くらいなる is incorrect; it must be くらくなる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.vi: Please study in advance the kanji you will study tomorrow.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: あした indicates the time of studying in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The clause べんきょうする comes before and modifies かんじ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object to be studied in advance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects よしゅうする with おく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: ておく shows that an action is done beforehand to prepare for a later time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: ください changes a request into a polite favor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.why: べんきょうするかんじ is a noun phrase in which the clause before it modifies かんじ. ておく shows that the studying is completed beforehand to prepare for tomorrow's lesson.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, it means please review it in advance, that is, study the content again rather than study it beforehand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: If おいて is omitted, the sentence only asks someone to study and does not emphasize preparing beforehand.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ておく simply as “did,” but this pattern emphasizes doing the action beforehand for a later purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q14.kobun.cn: Vて + おく + ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.vi: I have not felt well since yesterday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the starting point of the unwell condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects からだ with ぐあい, forming the phrase “the condition of the body.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject that has the state わるい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: わるいです is the predicate and describes an unhealthy physical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.why: The phrase きのうから sets the time reference, while からだのぐあいがわるい describes the state that began at that point. が marks the condition being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced, the sentence refers to a body part or the body being painful, not to a general condition of feeling unwell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced, it means not liking something or finding it unsuitable, which does not fit a physical condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse わるい with いたい; わるい refers to a bad or unhealthy condition, while いたい refers to pain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.vi: I am praying that my father's illness will get better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: の shows that びょうき belongs to the father.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks what is hoped for: that the illness will get better.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.ch.2.vi: so that the illness will get better
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: ように connects the desired result with the verb 祈る.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: ている indicates that the action of praying is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.why: The clause びょうきがなおるように states what the speaker hopes will happen. ように connects that hope with 祈っています, the continuing action of praying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with ために, the sentence may sound like the purpose of an action; ように is more natural for expressing a hope.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: ようだ expresses similarity or a guess, not a prayerful hope like ように.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse ように in a prayer with ようだ; ように connects a wish here, not a guess.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q16.kobun.cn: V辞書形・ない形 + ように + V
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.vi: Which pair of gloves is the cheapest?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.ch.0.n: どの directly modifies the noun after it to ask about a choice.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the item being chosen in the comparison question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: いちばん modifies the adjective and creates a superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that has the feature やすい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: やすい is the adjective い used as the predicate, while ですか changes the sentence into a polite question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.why: どのてぶくろが asks which pair of gloves is being considered. The clause ねだんがやすい evaluates the price of that pair, and いちばん comes before the adjective to show the cheapest price.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If やすい is replaced with 高い, the sentence will ask which pair of gloves is the most expensive.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.vs.1.d: If 少ない is used, the sentence will ask about a small quantity, not the price level.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate ねだんがやすい as “little price”; in Japanese, やすい expresses “cheap price.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.vi: The restaurant is on the fifth floor. You should take the elevator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that the restaurant is the topic whose location is being identified.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates where the restaurant exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: あります is the existence predicate for an object or place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: 行った is the past form placed before ほう to modify the choice of method.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.ch.5.n: Vたほうがいい gives advice to choose that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.ch.6.n: いいですよ ends the advice with a gentle, friendly tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.why: The first sentence identifies the location using は, に, and あります. The second uses で to state the means of transportation, then uses Vたほうがいい to advise taking the elevator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるほうがいい is used, the advice can still be understood, but Vたほうがいい is a clearer advice pattern meaning “should do.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with Vなければならない, the sentence will mean that one must take the elevator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use に for means of transportation; transportation takes で, while に here only indicates the fifth-floor location.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q18.kobun.cn: Vた + ほうがいい; N + で; N + に + あります
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.vi: Yamada: Would you like a little more rice? Tanaka: No, I have had enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: ごはん is the content asked about in the offer; this part is spoken by やまだ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: もうすこし modifies the amount of rice being offered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: いかがですか is a polite way to ask what the listener wants.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: いいえ rejects the previous offer and begins the reply.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.ch.4.n: もう shows that the amount has reached a sufficient level and no more is needed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.ch.5.n: 結構です means that no more is needed when responding to an offer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.why: The question uses いかがですか to make a polite offer. The answer places もう before 結構です to show that the amount is enough and refuse more.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, it can mean “it is okay” or “no problem,” without directly emphasizing that the speaker has eaten enough.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, it means “I do not need it,” but the tone is more direct and less gentle.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 結構です as “always very good,” but after an offer it usually means “I have had enough” or “I do not need any more.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q19.kobun.cn: N は ＋ いかがですか／もう ＋ 結構です
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.vi: In the morning, I ate bread spread with apple jam.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: あさ indicates the time when the action of eating takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects りんご with the noun ジャム, forming the phrase “apple jam”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the jam as what is spread or dipped.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the action of using jam with the action of eating bread.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: を marks パン as the direct object of たべました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: たべました is the main predicate and describes a completed action in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.why: あさ sets the time context, and then ジャムをつけて describes how the bread was prepared. Both ジャム and パン have を because they are respectively the objects of つける and たべる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This expression emphasizes that the bread is the surface or object receiving the jam, with に indicating that surface or object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This expression states more clearly that the jam is spread on the bread before it is eaten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for both nouns, but the direct objects of つける and たべる both use を in this structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.vi: She has a facial expression that looks as if she is about to cry.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.sk: N は ＋ いまにも ＋ Vます remove ます ＋ そうな ＋ N を ＋ しています
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: は states that she is the person showing the described expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.1.vi: right now, on the verge of
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: いまにも modifies an expression for something that is about to happen immediately.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.2.vi: looks as if she is about to cry
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: Vます removes ます and combines with そうな to modify the noun that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks the noun used with the expression 顔をしている, indicating an expression on the face.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.4.n: て形 connects する with います in a pattern describing an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.ch.5.n: ています describes her current state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.cn: Vます removes ます ＋ そうだ; Vます removes ます ＋ そうな ＋ N; Vている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.why: いまにも combines with 泣きだしそうな to describe something that is about to happen immediately. This phrase comes before かお to modify the face, and then 顔をしています describes the expression.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vるそうだ is used, it means that someone is said to cry, not a judgment based on appearance.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If 泣き出すような顔 is used, the sentence focuses more on a face that looks like it is about to cry, with a clearer comparison.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily keep 泣きます and add そうな, but ます must be removed: 泣きそうな.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q20.tokens.3.m: looks as if she is about to cry
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.vi: I went to the hospital to visit my friend who was ill.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: へ indicates the direction or destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects 友だち with お見舞い, showing that the person being visited is related to the friend.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.ch.2.vi: to visit someone who is ill
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: Noun ＋ に indicates the purpose of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 行きました is the main predicate in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.why: へ marks the hospital as the destination, while に after お見舞い indicates the purpose of going. の shows the relationship between the friend and the visit.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used, the meaning focuses on going for N’s benefit or purpose, not on a specific activity name.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily omit に before 行く, but a noun showing purpose, such as お見舞い, needs to be used with に.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q21.kobun.cn: N に ＋ 行く／来る／帰る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.vi: You cannot go to Tokyo Station by this train. Please change trains at the next station.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates the means of transportation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: へ marks Tokyo Station as the destination.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: こと turns 行く into a noun, while は makes going to Tokyo Station the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: できません negates the ability to go by this train.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: で indicates the place where the train change takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: 乗り換えてください uses the て form with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.why: The first sentence uses で to indicate the train being used and へ to indicate the destination. 行くこと nominalizes the action and combines with できません to deny ability; the second sentence uses で to indicate the place for changing trains and Vてください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If が is used instead of は, it only states impossibility, while は adds a contrastive or emphatic nuance to going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used in the second sentence, it means that changing trains is required, which is stronger than the request to change trains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for means of transportation, but transportation must use で; に usually indicates a destination or purpose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q22.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことはできない／Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.vi: I met a friend from elementary school again after a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 小学校 with 友だち, showing that they are friends from elementary school.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: と indicates the person participating together or the person met.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: ひさしぶりに modifies 会いました, showing that the meeting took place after a long time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: 会いました is the 会う verb in the polite past tense.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.why: の identifies the relationship between elementary school and the friends. と goes with 会う to indicate the person met, while ひさしぶりに comes before the verb to show that a long time had passed since the previous meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If また is used, the sentence only means meeting again, without emphasizing that a long time has passed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.vs.1.d: 久しぶりだ is a comment on the state of not meeting for a long time, while 久しぶりに directly modifies the action of meeting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に with the person met, but 会う goes with と; に in ひさしぶりに indicates the manner or time of the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.vi: I listened to the principal speak in the school auditorium.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 学校 with 講堂, forming the phrase "school auditorium".
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action of listening takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の indicates the owner or speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the content being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: 聞きました is the main predicate, used in the polite past form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.why: The place phrase 講堂で comes before the object and verb to state where the action happens. 話を聞く is a natural combination in which 話 is the content being heard.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If で is replaced with に, the sentence focuses on a destination or existence, so it is less suitable than で for the action of listening.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use に for every place, but the place where an action takes place usually uses で.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.vi: Please decide which one to choose.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the chosen option in the pattern どちらにする.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: か turns the question content into a clause that serves as the object of 決める.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: 決めて is the て form. It connects with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows a verb in the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.why: The clause どちらにするか states what must be decided, so it comes before 決める. The form てください comes at the end to make the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If どちらにしますか is used, the sentence directly asks the listener what to choose instead of asking them to decide.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: Adding を clearly marks the whole question clause as the object of 決める, but を is naturally omitted in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.tip: Do not always translate か separately as "whether or not"; here, か turns the whole clause into the content to be decided.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q25.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 + V普通形 + か
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.vi: I think this sweater was probably bought in Italy.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: この comes before a noun to identify the sweater being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the sweater as the topic of the statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: たしか adds a level of certainty to the whole statement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: で indicates where the buying took place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the content that the speaker remembers and guesses.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: おもいます is the main predicate and takes the content before と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.why: The place is used with で, and the content of the thought comes before とおもう. たしか makes the statement less absolute, which suits an opinion that is not completely certain.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence emphasizes that the thought has continued from the past until now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with はずだ, the sentence expresses stronger, evidence-based reasoning rather than a personal thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.tip: The clause before とおもう uses the plain form, not the polite form かったです directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N + とおもう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.vi: He studied very hard and finally became an excellent doctor.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.sk: N は + Adverb + Vて + Adverb + Aな + N に + なりました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents 彼 as the topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: This phrase modifies べんきょうして and shows how he studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the studying action with the result that followed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: とうとう modifies なりました and emphasizes the result after a process.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: りっぱな directly modifies いしゃ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: に indicates the state or profession reached after なります.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: なりました is the main predicate and describes a completed change.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.why: The first part describes the process of studying, and the second part describes the result. With なりました, the new profession or state comes before に; the adjective な must keep な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If なる is replaced with する, it means making someone or something become that profession or state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: This pattern emphasizes a gradual change in ability or habits, not only becoming a profession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.tip: Do not omit な in りっぱないしゃ; the adjective な needs な before a noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q4.kobun.cn: Aなな + N; N + に + なる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.vi: After the typhoon, the trees had fallen because of the wind.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects たいふう with あと to identify an event that happened after the typhoon.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: あと indicates the time that provides the background for the main clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the cause that made the tree fall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the trees as the subjects affected and left in a fallen state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: たおれていました uses the ている form in the past to describe the state of the trees after they had fallen and remained that way.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.why: The time phrase after the typhoon is placed at the beginning to set the scene, while で states the cause. The structure Vていました focuses on the remaining state after the trees fell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with てしまう, the sentence emphasizes an unintended event or a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: With Vた, the sentence only states that the trees fell, without emphasizing that the state still continues.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q5.kobun.tip: で in this sentence indicates the cause "because of the wind," not the place where the action happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.vi: Every morning, the clock bell rings at 6 o'clock.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.sk: Frequency + Time に + N の + N が + Vます
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the time when the bell rings.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects とけい with ベル to show possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the subject that produces the sound.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.why: The frequency phrase comes first, followed by the time with に. ベルが is the subject, while 鳴ります is the predicate describing the sound made by the bell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 着く, the meaning becomes "arrive," which does not fit a bell as the subject.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q6.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 鳴る with an action performed by a person; this word is often used for bells, phones, or ringing sounds.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.vi: Because I started working around noon, today's work was left unfinished.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.sk: Time から + Vたので + N の + N が + Vてしまいました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: から indicates the time when the work started.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the cause with the result and sounds softer and more explanatory than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects きょう with the noun しごと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: が marks the work as what remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいました describes an action that was completed but whose result also carries regret or was unintended.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.why: The cause clause comes first with ので, and the result comes after it with しごとが as the subject. てしまいました shows that the work is finished in terms of time, but the remaining result is unwanted.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the reason becomes more direct and stronger, with less softness in the explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 残っています is used, the sentence only says that the work remains unfinished and does not emphasize regret like てしまいました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate てしまう simply as "finished doing," but in this sentence it also expresses regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q7.kobun.cn: Vた・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので; Vて + しまう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.vi: I opened the box. Immediately afterward, rare fruits came out from inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the box as the object that was opened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: すると connects the following event to the previous action in the order they occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: から indicates the place or starting point from which something comes out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: An adjective placed before a noun to modify くだもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: が marks the fruit as the thing that appeared from inside.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: The て form connects 出る with 来る to describe movement continuing toward the speaker or a reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.cn: すると: previous clause。すると、following clause; Vて + 来る
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.why: The first sentence states the action of opening the box, and すると signals that the result happened immediately afterward. から indicates the starting point, while 出てくる describes something coming out and moving toward the viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If それで is used, the relationship focuses more on a result or cause and effect, without stressing that the event happened immediately afterward.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 出ていく is used, the fruit is viewed as moving away from the reference point.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t97-q8.kobun.tip: Do not translate てくる simply as “come”; with movement verbs, consider the direction of movement compared with the speaker or viewpoint.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.vi: I woke up late, so I ended up being late for work.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the content of the action して.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: て connects waking up late with the event that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place or destination where the speaker was late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: て connects the state of being late with the regrettable result at the end of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: てしまいました shows that an event was completed with a feeling of regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason. Then に marks the place where the speaker was late. てしまいました ends the sentence with the idea that something happened against the speaker's wishes.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence changes to mean that something will unfortunately happen or will be completed in the future.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only describes an ongoing state and does not stress regret.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out に in a phrase showing where they were late, such as しごとにおくれる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.vi: Let's definitely have a meal together next time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.sk: Time ＋ Adverb ＋ Together に ＋ Nを ＋ Vましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: This word identifies the time or occasion that the invitation refers to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: ぜひ modifies the invitation and emphasizes the wish to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: に creates an adverb showing that the action is done together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: を marks しょくじ as the action carried out during しましょう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: ましょう expresses an invitation to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.cn: Vます-stem ＋ ます ＋ ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.why: The time expression comes first to state the occasion. ぜひ emphasizes the wish, while いっしょに shows that the speaker and listener will do it together. The object comes before しましょう to complete the content of the invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence becomes a gentler invitation in question form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence only states the speaker's wish and does not directly invite the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q10.kobun.tip: Learners may easily translate しましょう as “do immediately”; in this sentence, it is an invitation for an upcoming occasion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.vi: Sorry, I do not feel well, so I will go home first.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the state described in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.ch.2.vi: because I do not feel well
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects a reason with a result and means “because”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the order or time of carrying out an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite form and is the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.why: The sentence first states the condition, then uses ので to give the reason for going home first. 先に is placed before the verb to emphasize the order of actions.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of から, the sentence still means “because,” but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use から in every situation, but ので is usually softer and more polite when giving a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q11.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.vi: Cars do not often pass along this road.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: は makes this road the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the vehicle or thing that performs the action of passing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: あまり is used with a negative predicate to show a low degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is in the polite negative form and is the main predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.why: The sentence makes the road the topic and then identifies cars as the subject of the action. あまり comes before the negative verb to describe something rare or not usual.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern emphasizes low frequency or degree. It does not simply mean complete negation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q12.kobun.tip: あまり should not be translated as “very”; in a negative sentence, it usually means “not very” or “not often.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.vi: It is hot, isn't it? Shall we turn on the air conditioner?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: ですね is placed at the end of a sentence to confirm or share a feeling with the listener.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the air conditioner as the object that is turned on or used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょうか is used to make a suggestion or ask whether to do the action together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.why: The first sentence shares information about the weather or temperature. The second suggests a suitable solution. を marks the air conditioner as the object of the action 入れる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vませんか is used, the invitation sounds gentler and asks whether the listener wants to do it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: If か is omitted, the sentence becomes a suggestion or decision to do it together, rather than a question asking for the listener's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q13.kobun.tip: 入れる means “turn on” for a device in this context, not only the physical meaning “put in.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.vi: I went to bed late last night, so I am sleepy today.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: ゆうべ indicates the time when the action of sleeping occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: おそく is the adverb form of the adjective おそい and modifies ねた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects a past cause with a present result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes today the time reference being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: 眠い is an adjective ending in い. It combines with です to speak politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.why: The cause clause comes before ので and uses the past form because the sleeping happened in the past. The present result is stated after that, with 今日は as the time topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: から also indicates a cause, but it is usually more direct than ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: 寝なかったので means “because I did not sleep,” so the cause is quite different from sleeping late.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.tip: The adverb form of the adjective い is made by changing い to く. Therefore, say おそくねた, not おそいねた.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q14.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.vi: This winter is relatively warm. That is good, isn't it?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 今年 with the noun ふゆ to modify “winter.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: は makes this winter the topic of the comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: わりあい modifies an adjective and shows a fairly high or relative degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い changes to ～くて to connect with the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: よかった expresses a mild feeling of relief or happiness about the result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.why: 今年のふゆ identifies the time and the thing being discussed. あたたかくて connects the weather condition with the feeling よかった, creating the relationship “It is warm, so that is good.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with あたたかかったので, the sentence emphasizes that the warm winter is the reason for feeling good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, the two parts have a contrasting or unfinished meaning instead of connecting ideas in the same direction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q15.kobun.tip: When an adjective ending in い is connected with て, い must change to くて. Do not use あたたかいて directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.vi: I invited my friend to my house.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.ch.0.n: を marks the person who was invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: に indicates the destination of the invitation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: 招待する is a verb in group サ変. It changes to 招待しました to describe a completed action politely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.why: The invited person takes を, while the place they are invited to takes に. The verb 招待する comes at the end of the sentence and uses the polite past form to complete it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: 誘いました means to ask someone to join an action or to invite them, while 招待しました emphasizes inviting someone to a place or event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.vs.1.d: 呼びました means to call or ask someone to come, but it does not necessarily show the formal hospitality expressed by 招待しました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q16.kobun.tip: Do not use に for the invited person in this pattern. The invited person is the object, so it takes を.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.vi: Because my leg hurt, I went up to the second floor by escalator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the body part that is in a painful state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the painful condition with the action of going up by escalator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: で indicates the means used to perform the action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: へ indicates the direction or destination of the action 上がる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite past form and serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.why: The clause 足がいたかったので states the cause first. The sentence then indicates the means with で, the destination with へ, and ends with the verb 上がりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ２かいに is used, the sentence still indicates the destination but sounds more neutral, while へ emphasizes the direction of movement.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If から is used, the reason sounds more direct and more personal to the speaker than with ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use で to indicate the destination. で is the means here, while the direction toward the second floor is expressed by へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q18.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.vi: I put the important things in the desk drawer.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: な connects だいじ with もの, while は makes the whole phrase “important things” the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects つくえ with ひきだし to show that the drawer belongs to the desk.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: に indicates the place where the object is put and stored.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: 入れる is a transitive verb that describes putting an object into a place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.why: The phrase だいじなものは is the object presented as the topic. つくえのひきだしに identifies the place where it is stored, and then 入れました describes putting the object there.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If ひきだしに is replaced with ひきだしで, で indicates the place where the action occurs, not the place where the object is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.vs.1.d: If しまいました is used, the sentence emphasizes storing or putting something away, rather than the act of putting it in as expressed by 入れました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q19.kobun.tip: With the verb 入れる, the place receiving the object usually takes に. Do not confuse it with で, the particle that indicates the place where an action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.vi: I do not know which side will win in the next match.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects a word showing order with the noun しあい.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the situation in which winning or losing takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: が marks the subject being asked about in an indirect question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: か turns the preceding clause into the unknown content of わかりません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: This is the main predicate and takes the whole question clause as its content.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.why: The phrase どちらがかつか is a question inserted as the content of わかりません. が marks the winning side, while か closes the indirect question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a direct question with a guessing tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with とおもいます, the sentence expresses the speaker's opinion or prediction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use は instead of が in this indirect question clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.tokens.9.m: do not know; am not sure
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q2.kobun.cn: 疑問詞 ＋ V普通形 ＋ か ＋ わかりません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.vi: It is already dark, so everything became dark.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject whose state changes to darkness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: The form て connects the event of nightfall with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い changes to the form く to connect with なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: なりました indicates that a change of state has occurred.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.why: The first clause states an event that happened earlier, and the next clause describes the changed state. The adjective い must change to く before なる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If this expression is used, the focus is on the state becoming dark, without directly stating that the cause is nightfall.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q20.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily keep the adjective い unchanged before なる, but it must change くらい to くらく.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.vi: I am still waiting for your reply.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects あなた to the following noun and shows possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being awaited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: ずっと modifies an action that continues over time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: The form ている shows that the action started earlier and is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.why: The possessive phrase comes before the object, while ずっと emphasizes the long duration. まっています shows that the waiting is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If the simple past form is used, the sentence only says that the person waited; it does not emphasize that the waiting is still happening now.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q21.kobun.tip: ずっと should not be translated simply as 'very'; here, it emphasizes continuous duration.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.vi: Because there is a police station nearby, I think this place is safe.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the location where something exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the thing that exists with ある.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: ので connects the reason to the statement in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes ここ the topic being described.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: と marks the content of the statement being thought.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.ch.5.n: おもいます is the main verb and takes the quoted content before と.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.why: The first clause gives the reason, while ここはあんぜんだとおもいます is the main statement. と connects the content 'safe' to the verb of thinking.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If そうです is used instead, the sentence gives information heard from someone else rather than the speaker's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If でしょう is used, the sentence expresses a guess or a mild confirmation without directly saying 'I think'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.tip: With an adjective な such as あんぜん, あんぜんだと must be used before とおもう, not あんぜんなと.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q22.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋だ・N＋だ ＋ とおもう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the person who is studying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects コンピューター with 技術 and identifies the field of the technology.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content being studied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: ている shows that the studying is in progress or continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q23.kobun.why: The phrase コンピューターのぎじゅつ forms a compound noun meaning technology related to computers. This phrase is the object of べんきょうしています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If the past form is used, the sentence only says that the person finished studying or studied in the past.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q23.kobun.tip: の connects two nouns in a 'about/belonging to' relationship; it should not be translated mechanically as two nouns placed next to each other.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.vi: Because a car suddenly came out from the corner of the road, I was startled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 道 with かど, creating the phrase 'corner of the road'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.ch.1.vi: from the corner of the road
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から shows the starting point of the car.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the car as the subject that appears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: きゅうに modifies how the car appears.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The past form 出てきた combines with ので to give the reason for the reaction.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.ch.5.n: This is the main predicate and shows the feeling caused by the preceding event.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.why: The phrase showing the starting point comes before the subject, followed by the adverb showing suddenness. ので connects the reason the car appeared with the result that the speaker was startled.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced by から, the meaning is almost the same, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: If とき is used, the sentence only states when the car came out and does not emphasize the cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.tip: Do not use から to show the starting point in かどから and then understand it as 'because'; here, から means 'from'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.vi: A very beautiful flower picture is hanging on the wall of that room.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects the room with the wall being discussed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the place where the picture is hanging.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective い comes before 花 to modify that noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: の connects 花 with え, creating the phrase 'picture about flowers'.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the picture as the thing in a hung state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.ch.5.n: てありました describes the remaining state caused by someone intentionally hanging the picture earlier.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.why: The location かべに comes before the hung object, while えが is the grammatical subject of the state. てある emphasizes the result of an intentional action and that the state still remains.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If ていました is used, the sentence only describes a state or an action in progress and does not emphasize a result prepared by someone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.vs.1.d: If the passive form is used, the focus shifts to the picture being hung, usually implying that the person who did it is not mentioned or is unimportant.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.tip: てある is used with an object arranged intentionally; it should not be confused with ている when emphasizing a prepared result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q25.kobun.cn: Vて形＋ある（あります・ありました）
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.vi: You are tired, aren't you? Let's take a short break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: ね is used to share the feeling that the listener is tired.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: This adverb modifies the length of the break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: ましょう is placed at the end of a sentence to make an invitation or suggestion to do something together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.cn: Vます-removeます ＋ ましょう
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.why: The first sentence confirms the current condition, and the second gives a suitable suggestion. しばらく comes before the verb to limit the length of the break.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If this is used instead, the sentence becomes a request for the listener to rest and no longer means doing it together.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If this is used instead, the suggestion becomes softer and takes the form of asking for the listener's opinion.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand ましょう as a command; in fact, this pattern usually includes the speaker as well.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.vi: Please write your name on the back of this card.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: このカードの modifies 裏 and identifies which card the back belongs to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the place where the name is written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the content to be written.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: 書いて is a form of て. It connects with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: ください makes the request polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.why: 裏に shows where to write, while 名前を is the content of the writing action. The structure Vてください is placed at the end to express a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: With で, 裏 is understood as the place where the activity takes place, but に is more natural when simply indicating where to put the writing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 書きましょう is used, the sentence becomes an invitation to write together instead of a request for the listener to write.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q4.kobun.tip: Distinguish に, which indicates the destination or the place where the result is put, from で, which indicates the place where the activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.vi: Because putting a bicycle here would get in the way, please do not put it here.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place where the action takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the object being placed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: と connects the dictionary form of a verb with the inevitable result of doing that action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: because it gets in the way
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: から connects the cause with the request in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: ないでください expresses a request for the listener not to do something.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.why: The place goes with に, while the bicycle is the object of おく, so it goes with を. The conditional clause uses と to state a natural result, and then から gives the reason for the request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If と is replaced with たら, the sentence has a more specific hypothetical meaning and does not stress an inevitable result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If only ないで is used, the sentence becomes a short reminder, “do not put it,” and lacks the polite request meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse に and で. With the verb おく, に indicates the place where an object is put.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.tokens.10.m: do not put, do not place
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ と; Vない形 ＋ でください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.vi: Is there any interesting television program?
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: 何か comes before a noun phrase to indicate an unspecified object.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective comes before the noun to modify “program.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects テレビ with the noun ばんぐみ and identifies the type of program.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes the interesting television program the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: ありませんか politely asks whether the object exists.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.why: The parts before ばんぐみ gradually narrow the object: something, interesting, and related to television. は states the object being sought, while ありませんか creates a polite question about existence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If ありますか is used, the question is more neutral and does not have the mild suggesting tone of ありませんか.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 知りませんか, the question asks whether the listener knows of a good program.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the adjective after the noun, but Japanese places おもしろい before ばんぐみ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q6.kobun.cn: 何か ＋ Aい ＋ N ＋ は ＋ ありませんか
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.vi: Please check whether this address is correct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the content being checked.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: かどうか turns the preceding clause into the content “whether...”.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the verb 調べる with ください to make a request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: ください follows the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.why: 住所が is the object to be verified, while ただしいかどうか is the content of the check. This phrase serves as the complement of 調べて, and then ください completes the polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If only か is used, the sentence usually asks directly or needs clearer context; かどうか emphasizes the two possibilities, correct or incorrect.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If について is used, it means “check about this address,” so it no longer directly asks whether it is correct.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.tip: かどうか must follow a clause and is usually understood as “whether... or not.” Do not translate か separately as “ah.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q7.kobun.cn: 普通形 ＋ かどうか ＋ Vてください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 子ども with きょういく, while は marks this phrase as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: とても modifies the adjective that follows and shows a high degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: だいじです is the adjective predicate な in polite form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q8.kobun.why: The phrase 子どものきょういく is grouped into one topic with は. とても comes before the predicate to increase the degree, while です makes the sentence polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If だいじです is replaced with 大切です, the basic meaning is still “important,” but the tone may be more formal.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q8.kobun.tip: With な adjectives such as だいじ, do not add な before です.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.vi: Because I cannot do it alone, please help me.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: で indicates a state or manner, while は emphasizes the condition of doing something alone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason before it with the request after it.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: て connects the verb 手伝う with ください to make a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: ください is placed after the て form to ask the listener to perform an action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.why: The phrase 一人ではできません states the condition and reason why the action cannot be done, and then から leads to the request for help. The て form combines with ください to turn 手伝う into a polite request.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used, the reason sounds softer and more objective than から.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the request becomes a more polite and softer question.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use てください as a strong command; context and tone of voice determine the level of politeness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t98-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nだ ＋ から; Vて ＋ ください
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.vi: I am waiting for a reply to my work email.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects しごと with メール to modify the type of email.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects メール with へんじ to indicate the reply to the email.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: を marks the object being waited for.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: まって います is the form て＋います. It expresses an ongoing action.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.why: The two consecutive の phrases create a chain of modifiers: a work email, then the reply to that email. へんじを is the direct object of まっています.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern has an action as its subject, something that is being waited for, not an object or information.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If the past form is used, it no longer means waiting at the present time.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate each の as “of,” causing them to misunderstand a long chain of modifiers.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q10.kobun.vi: I was relieved because the lost wallet was found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: This clause modifies さいふ and shows which wallet it is.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the wallet as the subject that was found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The form て connects the wallet being found with the result that the speaker felt relieved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q10.kobun.why: なくした modifies さいふ, while が marks the wallet as the object that was found. The form て connects the previous reason or event with the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 見つけて is used, the subject must be the person who found the wallet, not the wallet itself being found.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q10.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse 見つかる, meaning “was found,” with 見つける, meaning “found an object.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.vi: I will invite the people who helped me to the wedding ceremony.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: に indicates the place or event that the invited person will go to.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: お世話になる is a fixed expression; に marks the care or help that the speaker received.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: なった in the past form comes before 人 to modify that person.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The clause before 人 identifies the object, while を marks the people who are invited.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: しょうたいします is the main predicate and describes the action of inviting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.why: The clause おせわになった comes before 人 to identify which people they are. 人を is the direct object of しょうたいします, while に in けっこんしきに indicates the place or event being approached.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If お世話をした人 is used, it means the people who took care of or helped someone else.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: If 人に is used, に refers to the person receiving the invitation in a different expression. It is not a natural replacement for the object 人を in this sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily place the relative clause after the noun; Japanese puts the modifying part directly before 人.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nの + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.vi: I understood the general reason for the accident.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects じこ with げんいん, creating the phrase “the reason for the accident.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the reason as the content that was understood.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: 大体 modifies わかりました and shows that the understanding is general or incomplete.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.why: じこのげんいん forms a noun phrase in which じこ modifies げんいん. 大体 comes before わかりました to limit the level of understanding to “generally.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: If 全部 is used, it means that the whole reason was understood completely.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: 全然 usually goes with a negative form and means “not understand at all.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q13.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 大体 as an independent noun, but in this sentence it works as an adverb modifying わかりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.vi: Because it exceeded the budget, the plan was not approved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the budget as the object that was exceeded.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: ので connects the reason in the first clause with the result in the second clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: その modifies きかく and refers to the plan just mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は makes the plan the topic of the comment in the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The past negative form describes the result that the plan was not approved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.why: よさんをオーバーしたので is a clause showing the reason and comes before the result. そのきかくは makes the plan the topic, while とおらなかったです describes the result that it was not approved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is replaced with から, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is more direct and subjective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: If です is omitted, the sentence becomes shorter and more casual, while the main meaning stays the same.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily confuse を and は in this sentence: を goes with the object that was exceeded, while は marks the plan as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q15.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな + ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.vi: It is fine to throw away that magazine.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.ch.1.n: は presents the magazine as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.ch.2.vi: even if you throw it away
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vて+も shows that doing something is acceptable.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.ch.3.n: かまいません expresses permission or the absence of objection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.why: ざっしは presents the thing being discussed, while すててもかまいません says that throwing it away is permitted. The particle も in this pattern means “also” and creates a permissive tone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the meaning becomes “You must not throw it away.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily mistake てもかまいません for a prohibition, but this pattern actually means “it is fine to do it.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q16.kobun.cn: Vて + もかまいません
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q17.kobun.vi: The new mobile phone is very easy to use.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q17.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects the noun けいたいでんわ with the noun after it to show ownership or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q17.kobun.ch.2.n: は presents the way of using it as the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q17.kobun.ch.4.n: 簡単 is an adjective ending in な and combines with です to form a polite predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q17.kobun.why: The phrase あたらしいけいたいでんわのつかいかた is organized with the modifying parts before the main noun. は marks the whole “way of using it” as the topic, and the predicate 簡単です then gives a comment.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q17.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 便利です, the sentence emphasizes convenience rather than only simplicity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q17.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put the adjective after the noun, but in Japanese the modifying part must come before the noun it modifies.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.vi: Because this is a secret, I will never tell anyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.ch.0.n: は presents the matter being discussed as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.ch.1.n: から connects the reason clause with the result; です keeps the expression polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.ch.2.n: けっして modifies the negative verb いいません to emphasize that the speaker will never tell anyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the person being told, while は adds emphasis or contrast.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.ch.4.n: いいません is the predicate in the polite negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.why: これは presents the topic, and then から gives the reason for not telling anyone. けっして must be used with a negative predicate, while 人には clearly identifies the person being told.
