default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.vs.0.d: If ですから is replaced with なので, the reason usually sounds softer and more objective, but the main idea is still not telling anyone.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.vs.1.d: If あまり is used, the negative meaning is weaker and means “not say much” or “not really say.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.tip: Do not use けっして with an affirmative sentence; this pattern almost always goes with a negative form.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q18.kobun.cn: N・Aな + ですから; V普通形・Aい + から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.vi: You must not bully weak people.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.ch.0.n: よわい modifies 人 and identifies the person being bullied.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks the person affected by the act of bullying.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.ch.2.n: Vては is the connecting part of the prohibition pattern Vてはいけません.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.ch.3.n: いけません completes the pattern used to express something that is forbidden.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.why: よわい comes before 人 to modify the person affected, while を marks the object of いじめる. The Vてはいけません pattern places the action before いけません to show a prohibition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is used in this sentence, the statement sounds softer, like a request not to do that.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q19.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily understand は in てはいけません as the topic, but here it is a fixed part of the prohibition pattern.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.vi: Because I am worried, my heart is restless.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: で is the connective form of the adjective な. It connects the worried state to the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: が marks the subject described as being restless.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: さわいで is the て form of さわぐ. It connects with います to express an ongoing state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: います completes the ています pattern and shows that the state is still continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.why: ふあんで states the condition or reason at the beginning of the sentence. むねが is the subject of the condition さわいでいます, while ています shows that the feeling is continuing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This pattern also gives a reason, but it is more direct and subjective than ふあんで.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: The past form only says that the heart was restless at a certain time. It does not emphasize the present state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use くて with all adjectives, but adjectives な must connect with で when expressing a reason or joining sentences.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q2.tokens.5.m: to be present, to be in a place
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 田中さん with the following noun and shows possession or a related connection.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.ch.1.n: いちばん modifies すきなきせつ and creates a superlative meaning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.ch.2.n: は states the favorite season as the topic being asked about.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.ch.3.n: いつ asks about a time, while ですか makes the question polite.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.why: The phrase 田中さんのいちばんすきなきせつ combines the modifiers before the main noun きせつ. は makes the main noun the topic, while いつ asks for the needed information about that topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.vs.0.d: If 何ですか is used, asking which season or the name of the season is still natural, but it does not emphasize asking about a point in time as much as いつ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.vs.1.d: If が is used, the sentence becomes more like a subordinate clause or an indirect question. は is more suitable for stating the topic directly.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.tip: Do not separate いちばん from 好きな. The whole phrase modifies the noun 季節.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q20.kobun.cn: Nの + いちばん + Aな + N
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.vi: I am sad because the pet I once loved very much has died.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.ch.0.n: だいすきだった uses the past form to modify ペット and shows that it was a pet the speaker once loved very much.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.ch.1.n: に marks the object that caused the unfortunate experience in the affected passive structure.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.ch.2.n: しなれて is the て form of the passive structure. It connects the pet's death with the feeling of sadness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.ch.3.n: 悲しいです is the predicate expressing the emotion that arises after the event in the previous clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.why: The relative clause だいすきだった comes before ペット to identify the pet being mentioned. に marks the related object in the affected passive sentence, while しなれて connects the cause with the emotion 悲しいです.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.vs.0.d: If ペットが死んで is used instead, the sentence only states that the pet died and places less emphasis on the pain suffered by the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.vs.1.d: If ペットを亡くして is used, the sentence sounds more natural in formal speech and shows that the speaker lost a pet.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily translate に as “with,” but in the affected passive, に can mark the person or thing that causes a sad experience for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q21.kobun.cn: V受身形のて形 + Aいです
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.vi: Thank you for the other day. Thanks to you, my health has improved.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.sk: Time は ＋ Thanks。＋ Cause phrase ＋ N は ＋ Aくなる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.ch.0.n: は states the period or occasion being mentioned as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.ch.1.n: ありがとうございました is a polite expression of thanks for something that happened.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.ch.2.n: おかげさまで is a fixed phrase that gives a good reason or support leading to a result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.ch.3.n: は makes たいちょう the topic of the following clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.ch.4.n: よくなる describes a change to a better state, while ました shows that the change has been completed.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.cn: Aい → Aくなる; おかげで ＋ result
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.why: The first sentence uses は to state the occasion being thanked. In the second sentence, おかげさまで gives the help as a good cause, while よくなりました describes the health changing to a better state.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.vs.0.d: If おかげさまで is replaced with せいで, the cause has a negative meaning or leads to an unwanted result.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.vs.1.d: If よくしました is used, it means that someone actively made the health or thing better, unlike a state that changed by itself.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q22.kobun.tip: With adjectives ending in い, such as よい, change them to よく before なる: よくなりました.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.vi: Because I live in the suburbs, transportation is not very convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the place where someone lives.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the verb すむ with the auxiliary verb います.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.ch.2.n: から connects the cause with the result that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は states that transportation is the topic being evaluated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.ch.4.n: あまり is usually used with a negative sentence to show that the degree is not high.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.ch.5.n: ではないです creates the polite negative predicate of the adjective な.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.why: The reason clause comes first and ends with から, followed by a comment about transportation. は marks the topic, while あまり combines with the negative form to express that it is not very convenient.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.vs.0.d: If から replaces ので, the meaning of the reason is almost unchanged, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use あまり with an affirmative sentence, while its basic use is with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q23.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ から
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.vi: Because I cannot drink alcohol, I ordered a non-alcoholic drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.sk: N が ＋ negative V可能形 ＋ ので、Nの ＋ ない ＋ N を ＋ Vました
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object that someone can or cannot drink.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.ch.1.n: The negative potential form combines with ので to state a reason.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.ch.2.n: の connects the noun アルコール with the modifier that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.ch.3.n: ない modifies のみもの and shows that the drink contains no alcohol.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the thing that was ordered.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.why: The reason for using ので comes before the action of ordering the drink. The phrase アルコールのない is a clause modifying のみもの, so the description comes before the noun.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.vs.0.d: If から is used, the reason is stated more directly and subjectively than with ので.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.vs.1.d: This still means a drink without alcohol, but it emphasizes the state of having no alcohol with が.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily place the modifier after the noun, following Vietnamese word order, but Japanese places アルコールのない before のみもの.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.tokens.6.m: does not exist; there is not
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q24.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなな・Nな ＋ ので
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.vi: I had absolutely no idea about the test.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects テスト with こと to form a noun phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.ch.1.n: こと turns the preceding content into a noun, while は marks it as the topic.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.ch.2.n: ぜんぜん modifies a negative predicate to emphasize a zero degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.ch.3.n: しらなかったです is the polite past negative form of しる.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.why: The phrase テストのこと is made the topic by は. The adverb ぜんぜん comes before the negative predicate to completely deny knowing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with まったく, it also means “not at all,” but the emphasis is stronger and it can be used in written language.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q25.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use ぜんぜん with an affirmative sentence, but at the basic level this word usually goes with a negative predicate.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q3.kobun.vi: I will leave out the detailed explanation.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object being left out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q3.kobun.why: The noun used as the object comes before を, followed by the verb expressing the main action. The sentence ends with the polite form します.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 小さい, it means “small,” not “detailed” or “minor.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 細い, it means “thin or slender,” usually describing shape or thickness.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q3.kobun.tip: こまかい should not always be translated as “small”; in explanations, it usually means “detailed.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.vi: My mother makes breakfast for me in the kitchen every morning.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Time ＋ N で ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ くれる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the mother as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: 毎朝 indicates a repeated time, while で indicates the place where the action occurs.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the food being made.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The て form connects action つくる with くれます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: くれます expresses that another person does something beneficial for the speaker or the speaker’s side.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.why: The topic 母 comes first, followed by the time and place where the action occurs. The object あさごはん goes with を, and then つくってくれます shows that the mother does it for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with つくります, it only says that the mother makes breakfast and does not emphasize the benefit for the speaker.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily leave out くれます, which removes the meaning of “doing something to help or for me.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q4.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれる・くださる
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.vi: Since this happens often, there is no need to be surprised.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: よく modifies ある and indicates something that often happens.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: ある comes before こと to modify こと with a relative clause.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: ですから connects the reason stated before it with the conclusion that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: おどろく modifies 必要, forming the phrase “the need to be surprised.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は makes “the need to be surprised” the topic so that it can be negated.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.ch.5.vi: does not exist; there is not
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: ありません negates the existence of 必要, meaning that it is not necessary.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.why: よくあること forms the noun phrase “something that often happens,” followed by ですから to state the reason. おどろく comes before ひつよう to modify it, while はありません negates the necessity.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If ので is used instead of ですから, the sentence still gives a reason, but the tone is softer and more objective.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If わけではありません is used, the meaning becomes “it is not necessarily...,” rather than directly saying “it is not necessary.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.tip: おどろく should not be placed after ひつよう; the verb must come before the noun to form a modifying phrase.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.tokens.9.m: does not exist; there is not
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な／の ＋ ですから
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.vi: I completely forgot my mother’s birthday.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects 母 to the following noun and shows possession.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the thing that was forgotten.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: すっかり modifies わすれました and emphasizes the state of forgetting everything.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.why: 母のたんじょうび is the noun phrase meaning “my mother’s birthday,” and it is the object of わすれる. すっかり comes before the verb to add the meaning of complete degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If はっきり is used, it means “clearly,” not the degree of forgetting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If しっかり is used, it means “surely” or “carefully,” which is opposite to the idea of completely forgetting.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use すっかり as an adjective; this word usually comes before a verb to show degree.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.vi: I feel unwell because I get carsick.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the cause leading to the condition that follows.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject that is in a bad condition.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective 悪い serves as the predicate and describes the condition of 気分.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.why: The cause phrase with で comes first, followed by the subject of the condition with が. 悪い is the adjective serving as the predicate for 気分, meaning that the feeling or physical condition is not good.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If replaced with 病気です, it means “being ill,” which is stronger and is not limited to simply feeling unwell.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with 元気です, the meaning changes to “healthy” or “feeling energetic.”
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q7.kobun.tip: 気分が悪い should not always be translated as “bad mood”; in this sentence, it usually refers to physical discomfort.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q8.kobun.vi: I go to the second floor by using the escalator.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the means of transportation or route being used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The て form connects the action of using the escalator with the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of the action of going.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q8.kobun.why: The means of transportation comes before を, followed by the て form to connect it with the main action. The destination goes with に and comes directly before いきます.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If エスカレーターで行きます is used, で directly marks the means of transportation, so the structure connecting two verbs with the て form is not used.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese speakers may easily use を for the destination; with いきます, the destination must go with に or へ.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.vi: Volunteer activities are being carried out actively throughout the country.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Scope で ＋ Aな に ＋ V受身ている
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: が marks the subject of the action being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: で indicates the scope or place where the activity takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: さかんに modifies おこなわれています and shows that the activity commonly takes place.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The passive form おこなわれる combines with ています to describe an activity that is being carried out.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.why: The doer of the activity comes first, the place where it takes place goes with で, and さかんに modifies how the activity is carried out. おこなわれています uses the passive form because the activity is carried out by a doer who does not need to be mentioned.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If 盛んだ is used, it only describes a state of development and does not directly modify the verb おこなう.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with 静かに, the sentence means that the activity is carried out quietly, not that it is widely developing.
default.q.2026_mojigoi_n4-t99-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily put に in the wrong position; here, さかんに comes directly before the verb to show how the activity takes place.
